== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 02 K/AG/1985 establishes an important legal principle regarding the marriage requirements for an adult woman holding the status of a widow. The Supreme Court outlined that for the validity of a marriage involving a woman [age removed] who is a widow, parental consent is not required, and guardianship is not absolute or strictly mandatory under Islamic Law.

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiff ([Party C]) filed a lawsuit for marriage annulment (fasid marriage) at the Brebes Religious Court against Defendant I ([Party A]) and Defendant II ([Party B]). The lawsuit was grounded on the premise that the marriage between Defendant I and Defendant II—solemnized on October 12, 1981, under Marriage Certificate No. 323/49/VI/1981—was conducted without parental consent and utilized an invalid guardian. The Brebes Religious Court (Decision No. 471/1984) and the Surakarta High Religious Court (Decision No. 27/1984) both granted the claim and annulled the marriage. Dissatisfied with these rulings, Defendants I and II filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:''' For the validity of a marriage of an adult woman [age removed] holding widow status, parental consent is not required, and the issue of guardianship is not absolute or strictly necessary. Because the relevant lineage guardian (wali nasab) explicitly stated no objection to the marriage, the marriage performed is valid according to Islamic Law.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition of Petitioners (1. [Party A], 2. [Party B]); annulling the Surakarta High Religious Court Decision No. 27/1984 and the Brebes Religious Court Decision No. 471/1984; and Independently Adjudicating by rejecting the Plaintiff's claim in its entirety.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 38 K/AG/1990 establishes a landmark legal rule regarding the *broken marriage* principle and the *no-fault divorce* doctrine within Islamic Civil Law. The Supreme Court outlined that under the divorce ground specified in Article 19 letter f of Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975, the emphasis lies solely upon the objective fact that the marriage itself has broken down and that no reasonable hope for reconciliation remains, without necessitating an inquiry into who bears fault for the continuous disputes and quarrels.

== Case Background ==

The Petitioner / Petitioner for Cassation (Drs. Fachrizal bin H. Lindau St. Rajo Ameh, a civil servant at Itwilkab Padang Pariaman) filed a petition for divorce (*cerai talak*) against his wife, the Respondent / Respondent for Cassation ([Party A]) at the Pariaman Religious Court. The couple married on September 9, 1984, and were blessed with one child. The Petitioner argued that frequent disputes arose due to the Respondent's groundless jealousy, culminating in an incident where the Respondent left the shared marital domicile, taking along all of the Petitioner's personal furnishings and documents.

The Pariaman Religious Court (Determination No. 39/P/1989 dated June 5, 1989) granted the divorce talak petition. However, the Padang High Religious Court (Decision No. 20/1989 dated December 12, 1989) annulled the Pariaman Religious Court determination and rejected the divorce petition on the grounds that the quarrels were instigated by the husband himself. Dissatisfied with the appellate ruling, the Petitioner filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# When the grounds for divorce under Article 19 letter f of Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975 are proven, this is directed purely at the marriage itself (the objective fact that the marital bond has broken down and that no hope for harmonious reconciliation exists) without questioning who is at fault for the continuous disputes and quarrels.
# Marriage is not merely an ordinary contract to cohabit as husband and wife, but rather a *miitsaaqan gholiidhan* (sacred covenant, Article 2 of the KHI), the dissolution of which must not be measured by attributing fault to either party.
# Attributing the breakdown of a household to the fault of a single party is inappropriate. Assigning fault when harmony can no longer be expected generates adverse psychological and social impacts upon both parties and their descendants in the future.
# This foundational rationale underpins the statutory rule that divorce procedural costs are consistently charged to the party filing the petition/lawsuit (Article 89 paragraph (1) of Law No. 7 of 1989), rather than being assessed against the losing party as is customary in general civil litigation.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation (Drs. Fachrizal bin H. Lindau St. Rajo Ameh); Annulling the Padang High Religious Court Decision No. 20/1989 dated December 12, 1989; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Granting the Petitioner's petition; (2) Granting authorization to the Petitioner to pronounce talak against the Respondent ([Party A]) before a session of the Pariaman Religious Court; (3) Ordering the Petitioner to pay *iddah* maintenance amounting to Rp 300,000 to the Respondent; (4) Ordering the Petitioner to provide maintenance for their 1 (one) child until adulthood; (5) Charging procedural costs at first instance (Rp 34,500), appellate level (Rp 16,500), and cassation level (Rp 20,000) to the Petitioner.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 004K/AG/1979 establishes an essential legal rule regarding divorce procedures under national marriage law. The Supreme Court outlined that since the enforcement of Law No. 1 of 1974 jo. Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975, a divorce initiated by a husband (talak) must be performed in front of a session of the local Religious Court / Mahkamah Syar'iyah. Unilateral pronouncements of talak outside the court session without valid legal grounds are considered "wild talak" (*talak liar*) that fail to comply with statutory provisions.

== Case Background ==

The Defendant for Cassation / Original Petitioner ([Party B]) unilaterally pronounced talak outside the court against his wife, the Petitioner for Cassation / Original Respondent ([Party A]), on December 4, 1977, accusing her of using witchcraft. [Party B] subsequently petitioned the Padang Panjang Religious Court to legalize the divorce. The Padang Panjang Religious Court / Mahkamah Syar'iyah (Decision No. 03/1978) rejected the divorce petition and declared [Party B]'s talak pronouncement as a "wild talak" due to non-compliance with legal procedures. However, the Provincial Religious Court / Mahkamah Syar'iyah in Padang (Decision No. 1/1978) annulled the first-instance decision and legalized the pronouncement of the first talak. Dissatisfied with the appellate ruling, [Party A] filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:''' Since the enactment of Law No. 1 of 1974 jo. Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975, a divorce executed by a husband (talak) must be conducted before a session of the local Religious Court / Mahkamah Syar'iyah. A husband's act of pronouncing talak outside the court session fails to fulfill the grounds and requirements for divorce under applicable laws and regulations, thus categorizing such a talak pronouncement as a wild talak (*talak liar*).
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition filed by Plaintiff for Cassation [Party A]; annulling the Provincial Religious Court / Mahkamah Syar'iyah Decision in Padang No. 1/1978 dated March 9, 1978; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Rejecting the divorce petition from [Party B] against his wife [Party A] due to a lack of legal grounds and requirements for divorce; (2) Establishing and classifying [Party B]'s talak pronouncement toward his wife [Party A] as a wild talak (*talak liar*) for failing to conform to prevailing statutory provisions; (3) Ordering the Petitioner / Defendant for Cassation to bear all procedural costs.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 5 K/TUN/1992 dated January 21, 1993, establishes three fundamental legal principles in State Administrative Court Procedure:
1. '''Lawsuit Time Limit (Article 55 of Law No. 5 of 1986):''' The 90-day period is calculated from the time the Plaintiff realistically becomes aware of the issuance of the administrative decision that prejudices their interests.
2. '''Status of the Defendant Party (Article 83 of Law No. 5 of 1986):''' The joinder or designation of a third party as a "Co-Defendant" (*Turut Tergugat*) upon the Plaintiff's sole initiative is procedurally improper and impermissible within the State Administrative Court.
3. '''Administrative Judges' Review Powers / Ultra Petita:''' State Administrative Judges possess the authority to annul or review decisions or determinations of Administrative Bodies or Officials that contravene existing legal frameworks, even if not specifically pleaded in the Plaintiff's petitory relief (*ultra petita*), in order to uphold legal order and rectify administrative aberrations.

== Case Background ==

The Plaintiffs (Mrs. D binti A, Mrs. YR binti ZAS, Moh. R bin Moh. S) filed a lawsuit at the Jakarta State Administrative Court (PTUN) against the Head of the National Land Agency (BPN) as Defendant I and the Governor of DKI Jakarta as Defendant II, seeking the annulment of the Land Allocation Permit (SIPPT) and Building Use Rights (HGB) Certificates No. 116/KS and No. 138/KS covering a disputed 7,100 m² plot of land on Jalan HAS / KS, Central Jakarta (formerly Ownership Certificate No. 60/G belonging to the late ZAS). The Jakarta PTUN and Jakarta High State Administrative Court rulings involved the joinder of third parties as Co-Defendants and Intervening Defendants (PT JS and PT SGM). The parties subsequently filed cassation petitions to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The time limit for filing a lawsuit under Article 55 of Law No. 5 of 1986 must be calculated from the moment the Plaintiff becomes aware of the prejudicial decision.
# Under Article 55 and Article 83 of Law No. 5 of 1986 alongside its official elucidation, it is impermissible for a Plaintiff on their own initiative to implead a private individual or legal entity as a Defendant (vide Article 1 point 6 of Law No. 5 of 1986) either as a Co-Defendant or an Intervening Defendant.
# Even if the original Plaintiffs did not explicitly request it in their petitum, the Supreme Court / Administrative Judge may consider and adjudicate upon any decisions or determinations that conflict with prevailing legal order. Restricting the judge's review power solely to the object of dispute raised by the parties is improper, as disputed objects frequently must be evaluated in relation to parts of administrative decisions that were not formally contested (*ultra petita*).
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petitions from Petitioner for Cassation I (Head of BPN), Petitioner for Cassation II (Governor of DKI Jakarta), Petitioner for Cassation III (PT JS and PT SGM), and Petitioner for Cassation IV (Mrs. D binti A et al.); Annulling the Jakarta High State Administrative Court Decision No. 13/B/1991/PT.TUN.JKT jo. Jakarta State Administrative Court Decision No. 010/G/1991/PTUN-Jkt; and Independently Adjudicating: Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part, declaring invalid/annulling the sale-and-purchase deed, SIPPT, HGB Certificates No. 116/KS and No. 138/KS, and ordering the original Defendants to pay court costs.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 10 K/AG/1981 dated January 20, 1982, establishes an important legal principle regarding the absolute jurisdictional limits of Religious Courts in disputes involving joint marital property. The Supreme Court outlined that matters concerning the division of gono-gini goods (joint marital property) fall under the authority of the District Court (General Judiciary) rather than the Religious Courts.

== Case Background ==

The Petitioner / Defendant for Cassation ([Party A]) filed a petition for divorce (talak) against his wife, the Respondent / Plaintiff for Cassation ([Party B]) at the Wates Religious Court, citing domestic disputes and alleged disobedience by the wife. The Wates Religious Court (Determination No. 169/1979 dated June 13, 1979) rejected the Petitioner's divorce petition. On appeal, the Surakarta Islamic High Court (Decision No. 03/1980 dated April 14, 1980) annulled the Wates Religious Court determination and granted [Party A]'s request to pronounce talak. [Party B] filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court, raising objections concerning household disputes, maintenance claims, and requesting that jointly acquired marital property be divided equally.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:''' Matters concerning the division of gono-gini goods fall within the competence of the District Court; therefore, the Islamic High Court committed no error in law by omitting the division of marital property from its ruling on the divorce petition. Objections raised by the Petitioner for Cassation regarding the evidentiary evaluation of facts cannot be reviewed at the cassation level.
* '''Ruling:''' Rejecting the cassation petition filed by the Plaintiff for Cassation ([Party B]) with a modification to the dispositive portion of the Surakarta Islamic High Court Decision No. 03/1980, such that the full order reads: (1) Accepting the appellant's appeal; (2) Annulment of Wates Religious Court Determination No. 169/1979; (3) Independently Adjudicating: (a) Granting the petitioner's request to pronounce talak; (b) Ordering the Wates Religious Court to reopen sessions to witness [Party A]'s talak pronouncement to [Party B]; (4) Ordering the Plaintiff for Cassation / Respondent to bear procedural costs.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 10 K/Pdt/1984 establishes an important legal principle in Civil Procedure Law regarding the formal requirements of third-party opposition (*derden verzet*). The Supreme Court outlined that an opposition (*derden verzet*) filed by a wife against the execution of a judgment ordering her husband to vacate a property is inadmissible (*niet ontvankelijke verklaard*), because a wife who resides together with her husband in the disputed object does not qualify as a pure, independent third party separate from the principal case.

== Case Background ==

The Opponent (Mrs. Inarti, wife of Eng Kie Men) filed a third-party opposition (*derden verzet*) at the Surabaya District Court against the execution of the Surabaya District Court judgment No. 80/1978 Pdt. jo. Surabaya High Court No. 565/1980 Pdt. jo. Supreme Court No. 355 K/Sip/1981. The judgment of the principal case had ruled in favor of the late Mrs. Sumiati's lawsuit and ordered Eng Kie Men (Mrs. Inarti's husband) to vacate and surrender the house and land located at Jalan Raya Arjuno No. 142, Surabaya. Mrs. Inarti argued that the house and building situated on state land belonged to her personally based on Grant Deed No. 124 dated May 28, 1977, issued by Liauw Kon Tjin, rather than her husband. The Surabaya District Court (No. 423/1981/G) and the Surabaya High Court (No. 5/1983 Perdata) granted Mrs. Inarti's opposition and cancelled the execution. Dissatisfied with this ruling, the heirs of the late Mrs. Sumiati and Kastamin filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:''' The Opponent is the wife of the defendant in the contested judgment against which the opposition is directed. Because the Opponent is the wife of the original Defendant I who continues to jointly occupy the disputed house and land, and given that the evidentiary grant documents were already examined and rejected during the principal lawsuit, the Opponent does not constitute a pure third party (*derden*). The third-party opposition (*derden verzet*) filed by the defendant's wife is consequently declared inadmissible.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from the Petitioners for Cassation (heirs of the late Sumiati and Kastamin); Annulling the Surabaya High Court Decision No. 5/1983 Perdata dated June 30, 1983, and the Surabaya District Court Decision No. 423/1981/G dated July 12, 1982; and Independently Adjudicating: Declaring the opposition filed by the Opponent (Mrs. Inarti) inadmissible (*niet ontvankelijke verklaard*), and ordering the Respondent for Cassation / Opponent to bear the procedural costs.

== Overview ==
Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 124 K/AG/1991 dated January 23, 1993, establishes fundamental Islamic Civil Procedure jurisprudence regarding the relative jurisdiction of courts: An exception concerning the relative jurisdiction of a court (domicile or territorial jurisdiction of the Religious Court) must be raised by the Respondent / Defendant at the first hearing. If the Defendant fails to attend the first hearing and does not raise an exception of relative competence, the Religious Court where the Plaintiff filed the lawsuit has full authority to try the case, and the High Religious Court is not justified in annulling the Religious Court's judgment solely on grounds of relative competence.

== Case Background ==
The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation ([Plaintiff], residing in [address removed]) filed a divorce suit against her husband, the Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation ([Defendant], residing in [address removed]), at the Klaten Religious Court. Both were married on December 10, 1977, at the Office of Religious Affairs (*KUA*) of Ketandan Sub-District, Klaten, and were blessed with 2 children. The marriage deteriorated due to continuous quarrels over financial issues, physical abuse by the Defendant, expelling the Plaintiff back to Klaten, and failing to provide maintenance for more than 6 consecutive months.

The Klaten Religious Court (Decision No. 614/1990 dated August 27, 1990 AD / 6 Shafar 1411 AH) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit by default (*verstek*) because the Defendant failed to appear despite being summoned properly, and declared a single *Khul'i* divorce pronounced by the Defendant against the Plaintiff with a compensation (*iwadl*) of Rp 50. However, the Semarang High Religious Court (Decision No. 24/G/1991 dated April 29, 1991 AD) annulled the Klaten Religious Court judgment and declared the decision null and void on the grounds that the Klaten Religious Court had exceeded its territorial relative jurisdiction (deeming the Plaintiff to be domiciled in [address removed]). Dissatisfied with the appellate ruling, the Plaintiff ([Plaintiff]) filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The Semarang High Religious Court committed an error in applying the law by failing to provide proper legal considerations when annulling the Klaten Religious Court judgment.
# The Original Plaintiff was in fact domiciled in [address removed]; concerning the relative competence of the court, such an exception should have been raised by the Respondent for Cassation / Original Defendant at the first hearing.
# Because the Respondent for Cassation / Original Defendant failed to raise an exception of relative competence at the first hearing, sufficient grounds exist for the Supreme Court to grant the Original Plaintiff's cassation petition, annul the Semarang High Religious Court decision No. 24/G/1991, and uphold the Klaten Religious Court decision No. 614/1990 dated August 27, 1990 AD, which was accurate and correct.

* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation [Plaintiff]; Annulling the Semarang High Religious Court decision dated April 29, 1991 AD / 14 Shawwal 1411 AH, No. 24/G/1991; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Declaring that the Defendant was properly summoned to appear at trial but failed to attend; (2) Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit by default (*verstek*); (3) Declaring a single *Khul'i* divorce of Defendant ([Defendant]) over Plaintiff ([Plaintiff]) with an *iwadl* amounting to Rp 50 (fifty rupiahs); (4) Ordering the Plaintiff to pay first-instance court costs amounting to Rp 26,500 (twenty-six thousand five hundred rupiahs); (5) Ordering the Appellant to pay appellate-level court costs amounting to Rp 10,500 (ten thousand five hundred rupiahs); (6) Ordering the Petitioner for Cassation to pay cassation-level court costs amounting to Rp 20,000 (twenty thousand rupiahs). *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court Cassation Panel of Justices on Monday, December 28, 1992, and pronounced on Saturday, January 23, 1993 AD, by Prof. H. Busthanul Arifin, SH. [Junior Chairman], H. Masrani Basran, SH., and H. Amiroeddin Noer, SH. [Associate Justices]).*

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 14 K/Mil/1987 dated September 30, 1987, establishes an essential legal rule regarding the prerequisites for imposing the death penalty. The Supreme Court outlined that for an individual sentenced to death, no mitigating factors may exist, and all judicial considerations must be strictly aggravating. If a Judge's considerations cite mitigating factors (such as the Defendant's past service and contributions to the State), the imposition of the death penalty is legally improper (*onvoldoende gemotiveerd*) and must be commuted to life imprisonment.

== Case Background ==

The Defendant, [Defendant] (Sergeant / Sertu NRP. 406266, MPP Status Denma Kodam III/Siliwangi), was charged with the premeditated murder of Sergeant Samuel Bulung (a Kopassus/RPKAD member) on May 3, 1983, arising from a dispute and fear that his intimate relationship with the victim's wife would be exposed. The Defendant was also charged with murdering Jhoni Parorongan (son of Sergeant Samuel Bulung) in the early hours of May 4, 1983, because Jhoni demanded the return of his parents' debt money managed by the Defendant, and the Defendant feared prior murder exposure. Furthermore, the Defendant embezzled and sold the victims' belongings (a Toyota Kijang car and a Honda GL motorcycle). The Bandung Military Court II-09 (Decision No. PTS-44-15/MAHMIL II-09/AD/K/III/1986) and the Jakarta High Military Court II (Decision No. PTS-04/BDG/K-AD/MMT-II/VIII/1986) sentenced the Defendant to death and ordered his dismissal from the armed forces. The Defendant subsequently filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:''' For any individual sentenced to death, there can be no mitigating factors, and all considerations must be aggravating. Because the considerations of the Jakarta High Military Court II Judge explicitly noted mitigating circumstances regarding the Defendant (taking into account the Defendant's past contributions and services to the State), the imposition of the death penalty was legally improper (*onvoldoende gemotiveerd*). Consequently, the death sentence must be annulled and commuted to life imprisonment. Additionally, the additional penalty of revoking the right to wear service medals/honors imposed by the *judex facti* is unwarranted as it is unregulated under the Military Criminal Code (KUHPM).
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation ([Defendant]); Annulling the Jakarta High Military Court II Decision No. PTS-04/BDG/K-AD/MMT-II/VIII/1986 and Bandung Military Court II-09 Decision No. PTS-44-15/MAHMIL II-09/AD/K/III/1986; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Declaring Defendant [Defendant] legally and convincingly proven guilty of the criminal offenses of "Premeditated Murder," "Murder preceded by another criminal offense committed with intent to evade punishment," and "Embezzlement"; (2) Sentencing the Defendant to Principal Penalty: Life Imprisonment, and Additional Penalty: Dismissal from military service coupled with the revocation of the right to enter the Armed Forces.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 15 K/AG/1980 dated November 25, 1981, establishes two essential legal principles:
1. '''Continuous Quarreling as Grounds for Fasakh:''' Proven facts sufficiently demonstrating continuous quarreling that can no longer be reconciled require the Plaintiff's lawsuit to have her marriage to the Defendant annulled (*fasakh*) to be granted.
2. '''Cassation Procedure in Religious Courts:''' Pursuant to Article 40 of Law No. 14 of 1970 jo. Law No. 1 of 1950, final judgments rendered by the Islamic High Court / Provincial Mahkamah Syar'iyah may be brought via direct cassation before the Supreme Court.

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiff ([Party A] / Siti Hawa) filed a lawsuit for marriage annulment (*fasakh*) against her husband, the Original Defendant (A. Rahman), at the Kualasimpang Religious Court / Mahkamah Syar'iyah. The couple married in 1960 and had six children. However, starting in 1976, frequent quarrels broke out, with the Defendant failing to provide financial support, accusing the Plaintiff of theft/robbery, and committing physical abuse (beating) on February 6, 1979. The Kualasimpang Religious Court / Mahkamah Syar'iyah (Decision No. 48/1979) granted the lawsuit and annulled the marriage. However, the Provincial Religious Court / Mahkamah Syar'iyah of Aceh in Banda Aceh (Decision No. 77/1979) overturned the first-instance ruling and declared the marriage to remain valid. The Plaintiff subsequently filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:''' Proven facts sufficiently demonstrating "continuous quarreling that can no longer be reconciled" warrant the granting of the plaintiff's lawsuit to annul (*fasakh*) her marriage to the defendant. The Provincial Mahkamah Syar'iyah of Aceh in Banda Aceh erred in concluding that insufficient grounds existed for a divorce.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition filed by the Plaintiff for Cassation ([Party A]); Annulling the decision of the Provincial Mahkamah Syar'iyah of Aceh in Banda Aceh dated November 17, 1979, No. 77/1979; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Accepting the Plaintiff's lawsuit; (2) Annulling (*fasakh*) the marriage between Defendant (A. Rahman) and Plaintiff ([Party A]); (3) Ordering the Defendant in cassation / original defendant to pay all court costs across all levels of jurisdiction.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Judicial Review Decision No. 01 PK/Mil/2003 adjudicates a military criminal case involving the Defendant, SERTU [Defendant], who was charged with unauthorized bigamy under Article 279 paragraph (1) item 1 of the KUHP. The Supreme Court annulled the prior rulings of the lower instances following the discovery of new evidence (novum) demonstrating that the contracted secondary marriage was legally invalid under religious law due to a failure to meet essential pillars (namely, the absence of a lawful marriage guardian and qualified witnesses). Because the marriage was invalid, the statutory elements of the crime under Article 279 KUHP were unfulfilled, resulting in the Defendant's complete acquittal and full rehabilitation.

== Case Background ==

The Defendant, SERTU [Defendant] (NRP 64040970, BASATSABHARA Poltabes Ujung Pandang), was charged with committing the crime of "Entering into a marriage knowing that an existing marriage constitutes a valid legal impediment" under Article 279 paragraph (1) item 1 of the KUHP. At the first instance, the Military Court III-16 Ujung Pandang sentenced the Defendant to 3 months of imprisonment and dismissal from the armed forces/police service. On appeal, the High Military Court III Surabaya modified the sentence to 4 months of imprisonment alongside dismissal. The Supreme Court subsequently rejected the Defendant's cassation petition. The Defendant then filed a Petition for Judicial Review (PK) accompanied by new evidence (novum) in the form of a Marriage Statement Letter, proving that the informal marriage with Witness II, Yuniar, was invalid due to the absence of a guardian and witnesses.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:''' Because the Defendant's marriage to Yuniar was invalid due to the absence of a lawful Guardian and Witnesses, the elements of the charge under Article 279 were unfulfilled, requiring the annulment of the Supreme Court decision jo. the High Military Court II Surabaya decision jo. the Military Court III-16 Ujung Pandang decision.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the petition for judicial review from the Judicial Review Petitioner / Convict [Defendant], SERTU NRP 64040970; Annulling the Supreme Court Decision No. 43 K/MIL/1998, High Military Court III Surabaya Decision No. PTS/425/BDG/MMT.III/K/POL/IX/1997, and Military Court III-16 Ujung Pandang Decision No. PUT/032-K/MM II-16/VII/1997; and Adjudicating Independently: Declaring Defendant [Defendant], SERTU NRP 64040970 not legally and convincingly proven guilty as charged; Acquitting the Defendant from all charges; Restoring the Defendant's rights in capacity, position, honor, and dignity (rehabilitation); and Charging all judicial costs across all levels of jurisdiction to the State.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 22 K/Mil/1992 dated January 8, 1994, establishes an important legal precedent in Military Justice regarding the proof of peacetime desertion and the formal requirement for adequate legal reasoning (*motivering*) in sentencing:
1. '''Unauthorized Absence / Peacetime Desertion (Article 86 item 1 of the KUHPM):''' The criminal offense of "intentionally committing desertion in peacetime" is proven when a Defendant abandons their unit without permission from their Commander or Superior for 19 consecutive days while the country is not in a state of war and units nationwide are not on alert status.
2. '''Legal Defect in Sentencing Considerations (Onvoldoende Gemotiveerd):''' The appellate court ruling (Medan High Military Court I) was annulled by the Supreme Court due to an error in law resulting from insufficient consideration (*onvoldoende gemotiveerd*) regarding the grounds and basis for sentencing, leading the Supreme Court to independently adjudicate the case.

== Case Background ==

The Defendant, [Defendant] (Police Sergeant / Serda Pol/Nrp. 64100480, Sabhara Member of the South Padang Sector Police, Padang Sub-Resort Police), was brought before the Padang Military Court I-03 under three cumulative charges:
1. '''First (Article 266(1) of the KUHP):''' Causing false statements to be entered into an authentic deed (marriage deeds at the Office of Religious Affairs (*KUA*) in Lubuk Kilangan Subdistrict, Padang, and KUA Pacet, Cipanas) by claiming to work as a student/private employee and maintaining an unmarried/single status.
2. '''Second (Article 279(1) item 1 of the KUHP):''' Contracting a secondary marriage without the permission of the first wife ([Party B]) or the authorization of the competent Superior in accordance with marriage regulations for ABRI/POLRI personnel, with Yulia Dewi Arjuna.
3. '''Third (Article 86 item 1 of the KUHPM):''' Committing unauthorized absence (desertion) from his unit at the South Padang Sector Police starting from July 22, 1989, to August 10, 1989 (approximately 19 days) to travel to West Java with Yulia Dewi Arjuna.

The Padang Military Court I-03 (Decision No. PUT/74/K/POL/IX/1990 dated September 11, 1990) sentenced the Defendant to 1 year and 6 months of imprisonment. On appeal, the Medan High Military Court I (Decision No. PUT/B-11/K/POL/MMT-I/VI/1991 dated June 26, 1991) modified the sentence to a Principal Penalty of 1 year of imprisonment alongside an Additional Penalty of dismissal from military/POLRI service. The Defendant subsequently filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The criminal offense of "intentionally committing desertion in peacetime" (Article 86 item 1 of the KUHPM) is proven because the Defendant abandoned his unit without permission from his Unit Commander or designated Superior for 19 days, whereas at that time the country was not at war and military units across all regions were not placed on alert.
# The Medan High Military Court I misapplied the law because it insufficiently considered (*onvoldoende gemotiveerd*) the penalty imposed. Therefore, the decision of the Medan High Military Court I must be annulled, and the Supreme Court shall independently adjudicate the *a quo* case.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation Defendant [Defendant], Serda Pol/Nrp: 64100480; Annulling the Medan High Military Court I Decision No. PUT/B-11/K/POL/MMT-I/VI/91 dated June 26, 1991, and the Padang Military Court I-03 Decision No. PUT/74/K/POL/IX/1990 dated September 11, 1990; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Declaring Defendant [Defendant] legally and convincingly proven guilty of the crimes of: I. Causing false statements to be entered into an official deed regarding facts that should be proven by that deed, with intent to use that deed; II. Contracting a secondary marriage while knowing that an existing marriage constitutes a valid legal impediment; III. Intentionally committing desertion in peacetime; (2) Sentencing the Defendant to Principal Penalty: Imprisonment for 1 (one) year, and Additional Penalty: Dismissal from Military/POLRI Service; (3) Crediting the period of arrest and detention already served by the Defendant in full against the sentence imposed; (4) Ordering that evidence items remain attached to the case file; (5) Ordering the Petitioner for Cassation / Defendant to pay court costs amounting to Rp 2,500.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 234 K/Pdt/1992 dated December 20, 1993 (deliberated on June 10, 1993), establishes two fundamental civil and customary land law jurisprudence principles:

* '''Letter C / Tax Records Are Not Proof of Ownership:''' Recording a person's name in the Village Letter C Book or as a taxpayer (Ipeda/PBB) does not constitute proof of land ownership (*bukti hak milik*), but merely indicates a person's obligation to pay tax on the land under their control. Recording the name of an uncle or guardian while the true land owner is an infant does not alter the status of the land's ownership.
* '''Legal Capacity to Perform Legal Actions Under Customary Law:''' According to Customary Law (referring to Supreme Court Decision No. 53 K/Sip/1952 dated June 1, 1955), a person who has reached the age of 15 (fifteen) years is deemed to have reached majority and is legally competent to perform legal transactions (such as purchasing rice fields).
* '''Transfer of Rights by a Non-Owner:''' Because an uncle or guardian is not the lawful owner of rice fields inherited by their ward, a land purchase transaction executed by such uncle to a third party is invalid and null and void (*nemo plus juris ad alium transferre potest quam ipse habet*).

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation ([Party D], represented by counsel L.L. Korassa, S.H.) filed a lawsuit against the Original Defendants / Respondents for Cassation (Defendant I: [Party E], Defendant II: Sunaryo, Defendant III: Tjahyono alias Siong, Defendant IV: [Party C] alias Ibu [Party A], and Co-Defendant: [Party F] [Plaintiff's sibling]) at the Jember District Court. The object of the dispute consisted of a plot of rice field measuring approximately 1.034 Ro / 0.952 Ha (Parcel No. 25, Petok No. 403 / Letter C No. 613 S.II) in Sumberjeruk Village, Kalisat Sub-District, Jember Regency.

The disputed rice field was originally purchased by the Plaintiff's late birth mother ([Party B], born [details removed]) from [Party G] on May 6, 1934. In 1938, [Party B] passed away shortly after giving birth to the Plaintiff ([Party D]). The infant Plaintiff was subsequently raised by his uncle and aunt, namely [Party A] ([Party B]'s biological brother) and his wife [Party C] (Defendant IV). For tax payment convenience, the rice field was recorded under the name of [Party A] in the Village Letter C Book. After [Party A] passed away in 1979, the rice field was controlled and unlawfully claimed to have been purchased by [Party E] (Defendant I) from [Party A] in 1975, and was subsequently farmed by Sunaryo (Defendant II) and Tjahyono (Defendant III).

The Jember District Court (Decision No. 26/Pdt.G/1990/PN.Jr. dated December 10, 1990) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part, declared the disputed rice field to be the inherited property of the late [Party B], affirmed that the sale and purchase between [Party B] and H. [Party G] on May 6, 1934, was valid, and declared the possession by Defendants I, II, and III to be unlawful. However, the Surabaya High Court (Decision No. 129/Pdt/1991/PT.Sby. dated April 20, 1991) annulled the Jember District Court judgment and ruled in favor of Defendant I on the grounds that the land was recorded under the name of [Party A] in the Village Letter C Book of 1942/1946. The Plaintiff filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The cassation objections raised by the Petitioner for Cassation ([Party D]) are well-founded because the Surabaya High Court erred in applying the law, wherein the legal reasoning of the Surabaya High Court was contradictory and improperly treated the Village Letter C Book as evidence of ownership.
# Under prevailing law, the Village Letter C Book does not constitute proof of ownership, but merely points to the party obligated to pay taxes on the land under their control. Because the Petitioner for Cassation was an infant at the time and raised by his uncle ([Party A]), it was natural for taxes to be paid by and registered under [Party A]'s name, which does not denote [Party A] as the owner.
# The Petitioner for Cassation successfully proved ownership of the disputed rice field through Exhibit P-1, reflecting the land sale from H. [Party G] to [Party B] (the Plaintiff's mother) on May 6, 1934, corroborated by witness testimonies and acknowledged by Defendant IV (the widow of the late [Party A]). Under Customary Law, [Party B]—born [details removed]—was deemed an adult (ex Supreme Court Decision No. 53 K/Sip/1952) and legally competent to execute legal actions.
# Because [Party A] was not the owner of the disputed rice field, the sale and purchase transaction between [Party A] and Respondent for Cassation I (Defendant I / [Party E]) concerning the disputed rice field on July 7, 1975, is invalid and null and void.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation: [Party D]; Annulling the Surabaya High Court decision dated April 20, 1991, No. 129/Pdt/1991/PT.Sby; and Independently Adjudicating: IN CONVENTION: IN EXCEPTION: Rejecting Defendant I's Exception; IN THE PRINCIPAL CASE: (1) Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part; (2) Declaring that the disputed rice field in its entirety is the lawful inherited property of the late [Party B] / birth mother of the Plaintiff and Co-Defendant; (3) Declaring that the sale and purchase between the late [Party G] and the late [Party B] regarding the disputed rice field on May 6, 1934, is lawful under the law; (4) **Declaring null and void all documents and deeds—including the sale and purchase deed / transfer records—concerning the disputed rice field executed between [Party A] and [Party E] (Defendant I);** (5) Declaring that the control and cultivation of the disputed rice field by Defendant I, Defendant II, and Defendant III without the Plaintiff's consent is unlawful; (6) Ordering Defendants I, II, III, and anyone deriving rights from them to vacate and surrender the disputed rice field to the Plaintiff free from any encumbrances; (7) Rejecting the remainder of the Plaintiff's lawsuit; (8) Ordering the Respondents for Cassation to pay court costs across all levels of jurisdiction (assessed at Rp 20,000 at the cassation level). *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court on Thursday, June 10, 1993, and pronounced on December 20, 1993, by the Cassation Panel of Justices: H. Soeharto, SH. [Presiding Judge], H. Asikin Kusuma Atmadja, SH., and Soedarmadji, SH.).*

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 25 K/AG/1984 dated October 31, 1984, establishes two fundamental legal principles in Islamic Civil Law and Civil Servant Divorce Regulations:

* '''Prohibition of Conditional Judgments:''' An appellate religious court's dispositive order commanding the religious court to open a session to witness the talak pronouncement only after obtaining authorization from the appellant's superior official (pursuant to Government Regulation No. 10 of 1983) and the opinion of the BP.4 and close family is legally impermissible because it renders the judicial decision conditional (*menggantung*).
* '''Conditions for Talak Validity under Islamic Law:''' A talak pronouncement uttered by a husband in a state of anger and in the absence of two (2) just witnesses is legally invalid under Islamic law.

== Case Background ==

The Respondent for Cassation / Original Petitioner ([Husband], a Perhutani employee, [age removed]) filed a petition for authorization to pronounce talak against his wife, the Petitioner for Cassation / Original Respondent (Mrs. [Wife], [age removed]), at the Blora Religious Court. The couple married in 1949/1959 and were blessed with 6 children. In 1974, the Petitioner contracted a secondary marriage (polygamy) with [Second wife] without proper procedural consent, triggering domestic discord that led the Petitioner to abandon the shared marital domicile for 8 years. The Petitioner had also previously uttered a unilateral talak while angry and without the presence of witnesses.

The Blora Religious Court (Determination No. 161/1982 dated October 13, 1982) rejected the Petitioner's divorce petition because the marital dispute arose from the Petitioner's own actions and all children and both wives desired reconciliation. However, the Surakarta High Religious Court (Decision No. 12/1983 dated June 14, 1983) annulled the Blora Religious Court determination and granted the divorce authorization with a conditional order linking the execution of talak pronouncement to civil servant superior authorization (PP No. 10 of 1983) and BP.4 opinions. Mrs. [Wife] subsequently filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The dispositive order of the High Religious Court commanding the Religious Court to witness the appellant's talak pronouncement upon securing superior authorization and BP.4 opinions is legally unjustified.
# A talak uttered by a husband while angry, unaccompanied and unwitnessed by two just witnesses, is deemed invalid under Islamic religious law.
# Because the domestic discord stemmed from the Petitioner's improper polygamy and his abandonment of the joint domicile, whereas the first wife, the 6 children, and even the second wife all desired to reconcile and preserve household harmony, the Petitioner's divorce petition lacks valid legal grounds and must be rejected.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation [Wife]; Annulling the Surakarta High Religious Court decision dated June 14, 1983, No. 12/1983; and Independently Adjudicating: Rejecting the divorce petition filed by Petitioner [Husband], and ordering the Respondent for Cassation / Petitioner to pay all procedural costs across all levels of jurisdiction.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 02 K/AG/2001 establishes the legal principle that any marriage entered into by an individual who already has a wife must be accompanied by authorization from the Religious Courts and the consent of the first wife, as stipulated under Articles 3, 9, 24, and 25 of Law No. 1 of 1974. A polygamous marriage conducted using false information regarding marital status and domicile, and executed without the first wife's consent or Religious Court authorization, is null and void, rendering any marriage certificate issued by the Office of Religious Affairs (KUA) legally ineffective.

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiff ([Party A]) filed a marriage annulment lawsuit at the Sungai Penuh Religious Court against her husband, Defendant I (Muhammad Nasir bin H. Abdurrahman / H. Ciduk), and Defendant II ([Party B]). The Plaintiff and Defendant I had been legally married since 1963 and had four children. However, on June 14, 1998, Defendant I contracted a marriage with Defendant II at the KUA of Kayu Aro Subdistrict, Kerinci Regency, without the Plaintiff's consent, without polygamy authorization from the Religious Courts, and using falsified personal data. The Sungai Penuh Religious Court (Decision No. 112/Pdt.G/1998/PA.Spn) granted the Plaintiff's claim and annulled the marriage. However, the Jambi High Religious Court (Decision No. 10/Pdt.G/1999/PTA.Jb) overturned the Religious Court's decision and declared the Plaintiff's claim inadmissible. Consequently, the Plaintiff filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:''' A marriage contracted by an individual who already has a wife should be accompanied by authorization from the Religious Courts as mandated by Articles 3, 9, 24, and 25 of Law No. 1 of 1974. Because the marriage between Defendant I and Defendant II was carried out using false information concerning the status of the first wife and the defendants' domiciles, and lacked the first wife's consent and Religious Court authorization, the marriage must be annulled and the Kayu Aro KUA marriage certificate declared legally void and non-binding.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition of Petitioner [Party A]; annulling the Jambi High Religious Court decision No. 10/Pdt.G/1999/PTA.Jb dated December 6, 1999; and independently adjudicating: (1) Granting the Plaintiff's claim; (2) Annulling the marriage between Defendant I (Muhammad Nasir bin H. Abdurrahman / H. Ciduk) and Defendant II ([Party B]) solemnized on June 14, 1998; (3) Declaring Marriage Certificate No. 043/14/VI/1998 dated June 14, 1998, recorded by the Kayu Aro KUA, to be legally ineffective and non-binding; (4) Imposing procedural costs.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 02 K/MIL/2002 establishes an essential legal precedent within the military judiciary concerning proportionality and sentencing objectives. The Supreme Court affirmed that the sentence handed down by the Judex Facti (High Military Court), which included an additional penalty of dismissal from service, was excessively harsh and failed to properly accommodate the core objectives of sentencing. The Defendant's expression of remorse and 15 years of dedicated service in the Indonesian National Police (Polri) served as mitigating factors. Consequently, elements prioritizing public order, public safety, and rehabilitation must take precedence, resulting in the annulment of the additional dismissal penalty and the reinstatement of a standard imprisonment term.

== Case Background ==

The Defendant, [Defendant] (Brigadier Police Officer NRP 67040328, Member of Dalmas, Directorate of Sabhara, Bali Regional Police), was charged with assault violating Article 351 paragraph (1) of the KUHP. The incident occurred on June 26, 2000, in Denpasar, where the Defendant took offense at remarks made by Witness I (Mr. [Witness]) at a gambling site and struck Witness I in the face once, resulting in an inner lower lip laceration and chin abrasion as confirmed by the Visum et Repertum.

The Denpasar Military Court III-14 (Decision No. PUT/01-K/MM.III-14/POL/I/2001) sentenced the Defendant to 10 months of imprisonment. On appeal, the High Military Court III Surabaya (Decision No. PUT/11-K/MMT.III/BDG/POL/VII/2001) modified the verdict, sentencing the Defendant to 7 months of imprisonment alongside an additional penalty of dismissal from military/police service. The Defendant subsequently filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:''' The sentencing imposed by the Judex Facti (High Military Court) disregarded sentencing objectives by being overly punitive, failing to account for the Defendant's remorse as a mitigating circumstance. Elements encompassing public order, public safety, and rehabilitation must be prioritized as weighed by the Judex Facti, rendering the High Military Court's decision subject to annulment.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition of the Petitioner / Defendant [Defendant]; annulling the decision of the High Military Court III Surabaya dated July 2, 2001, No. PUT/11-K/MMT.III/BDG/POL/VII/2001; and adjudicating independently: Declaring the Defendant legally and convincingly proven guilty of the criminal act of "Assault," and sentencing the Defendant to 10 (ten) months of imprisonment.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 33 K/Mil./1985 establishes an important legal principle in Criminal Procedure Law regarding the material requirements for the validity of an indictment. The Supreme Court outlined that if the Public Prosecutor / Military Prosecutor fails to include or formulate one of the core material elements of a criminal offense (such as the element of "causing potential loss" in the crime of document forgery under Article 263 paragraph (1) of the KUHP), the indictment is deemed not formulated with precision, clarity, and completeness as mandated by Article 143 paragraph (2) letter b of the KUHAP. This omission results in the indictment being declared **null and void** (*batal demi hukum*) pursuant to Article 143 paragraph (3) of the KUHAP.

== Case Background ==

The Defendant ([Party B], Corporal / Koptu-AD Nrp. 467187, Bamin Si 32 Yonif 731/BS) was charged with document forgery (Article 263 paragraph (1) of the KUHP) for altering the effective date (*t.m.t.*) of his Corporal rank and that of Witness I (Koptu [Party A]) on photocopies of their Appointment Extracts from 1976/1975 to 1974. This act was committed so that the Defendant would fulfill the minimum 8-year Corporal rank seniority requirement to participate in the Short Non-Commissioned Officer Candidate Selection (*Secaba Singkat*) for the 1983/1984 Fiscal Year at the Army Finance Education Center (*Pusdikku*) in Bandung.

The Ambon Military Court III-18 (Decision No. PUT/23/III-18/IX/1985 dated September 30, 1985) ruled that the Defendant was not legally proven guilty of document forgery and released the Defendant from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*). Dissatisfied with this acquittal ruling, the Military Prosecutor filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:''' Aside from the cassation arguments raised by the Petitioner for Cassation, the Supreme Court held that the Military Prosecutor's indictment in the *a quo* case was not formulated with precision, clarity, and completeness as required by Article 143 paragraph (2) letter b of the KUHAP, because the Prosecutor failed to formulate the element of "the use of such document could cause a loss" as one of the core material elements of document forgery (Article 263(1) of the KUHP). This omission prevented the court from examining the Defendant's case properly based on the indictment. Consequently, pursuant to Article 143 paragraph (3) of the KUHAP, the Military Prosecutor's indictment must be declared null and void.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation Military Prosecutor at Military Prosecutor's Office III-18; Annulling the Ambon Military Court III-18 decision dated September 30, 1985, No. PUT/23/III-18/IX/1985; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Declaring the Military Prosecutor's indictment null and void, alongside all trial proceedings conducted based on that indictment; (2) Charging all procedural costs across all levels of jurisdiction to the State.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Judicial Review Decision No. 034 PK/Pdt/1984 establishes two fundamental legal principles in Civil Procedure Law and Civil / Agrarian Law:
1. '''Civil Procedure Law (Judicial Review Novum):''' Grounds for a petition for judicial review are justified when the Petitioner for PK submits new documentary evidence (*novum*) from competent authorities (Directorate General of Immigration of the Ministry of Law and Human Rights and the Royal Netherlands Embassy) proving that the grantor held Dutch citizenship at the time the grant was executed.
2. '''Civil / Land Administration Law:''' A grant deed executed by a foreign national whose assets in Indonesia have fallen under or been directly controlled by the State (pursuant to Emergency Law No. 3 of 1960) is null and void (*batal demi hukum*) because it was executed without legal entitlement (*without valid causa*). Consequently, decisions rendered by the Governor of DKI Jakarta and the Director General of Agraria / Minister of Home Affairs (including Building Use Rights / HGB Certificates) predicated upon such a grant are unlawful and possess no legal force.

== Case Background ==

The Petitioners for Judicial Review / Original Plaintiffs (Haji Bahasan Pohan and Nn. Otje Lie) were lawful occupants and tenants of land and buildings formerly under *Eigendom Verp.* No. 16482 & 16483 located at Jalan Raden Saleh No. 44, Central Jakarta, pursuant to Housing Occupancy Permits (*SIP B*) issued in 1953 and 1956. Original Defendant II (Ny. [Party A]) claimed the land and house based on Grant Deed No. 22 dated February 4, 1961, from Herman Zadrach Maarten Apitulay and Grant Acceptance Deed No. 93 dated July 18, 1961. Based on this grant, Original Defendant III (Director General of Agraria / Minister of Home Affairs) issued Decree No. SK.170/HGB/DA/71 and HGB Certificates No. 90/Cikini & 91/Cikini in 1972 under the name of Original Defendant II, while Original Defendant I (Governor of DKI Jakarta) issued an eviction order against the Plaintiffs.

The Central Jakarta District Court granted the Plaintiffs' lawsuit (Decision No. 201/1980 G). However, the Jakarta High Court reversed the district court ruling (Decision No. 278/1981 *PT. Perdata*), and the Supreme Court at the cassation level rejected the Plaintiffs' cassation petition (Decision No. 3053 K/Sip/1982). The Plaintiffs subsequently filed for Judicial Review (*Peninjauan Kembali*) incorporating *novum* in the form of official letters from the Director General of Immigration and the Dutch Embassy confirming that the grantor had become a Dutch citizen as of June 11, 1960.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# Based on new documentary evidence (*novum*) from competent immigration and diplomatic institutions, it is conclusively proven that the grantor (Herman Zadrach Maarten Apitulay) became a Dutch citizen on June 11, 1960.
# Because the grantor held Dutch citizenship as of June 11, 1960, pursuant to Emergency Law No. 3 of 1960, all of his estate assets in Indonesia were directly placed under State control (P3MB). Consequently, the grant executed via Notarial Deed by Jan Cartian In't Hoot dated February 4, 1961, and the Grant Acceptance Deed dated July 18, 1961, are null and void (*batal demi hukum*) because the grantor no longer possessed the legal authority to grant those assets.
# State Administrative official decrees (issued by the Governor of DKI Jakarta and the Director General of Agraria / Minister of Home Affairs) alongside HGB Certificates No. 90 & 91/Cikini issued upon the foundation of such void grants are unlawful and declared to have no legal force.
# Considering that the disputed land and buildings remain under State control, Original Plaintiffs I & II as lawful tenants/occupants possess the right to apply to purchase the land/house from the State.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the Petition for Judicial Review from Petitioner for PK (Haji Bahasan Pohan and Nn. Otje Lie); Annulling the Supreme Court decision dated August 15, 1983, Reg. No. 3053 K/Sip/1982 jo. Jakarta High Court Decision No. 278/1981 jo. Central Jakarta District Court Decision No. 201/1980 G; and Independently Re-Adjudicating: (1) Granting the lawsuit of Plaintiffs I and II in part; (2) Declaring the appellate decision of Defendant I (Decree of the Governor of DKI Jakarta No. Kpts. Banding-012/UP/DKI/II/1980) devoid of legal force; (3) Declaring null and void Grant Deed No. 22 dated February 4, 1961, by Notary Jan Cartian In't Hoot (Rotterdam) and Grant Acceptance Deed No. 93 dated July 18, 1961, by Notary Noezar (Bandung); (4) Declaring Defendant III's Decree No. SK.170/HGB/DA/71 dated June 5, 1971, devoid of legal force; (5) Declaring HGB Certificates No. 90/Cikini and No. 91/Cikini of 1972 under the name of Defendant II devoid of legal force; (6) Declaring Plaintiffs I and II entitled to apply to purchase the land/house located at Jalan Raden Saleh No. 44, Central Jakarta; (7) Rejecting all other and remaining claims.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision Reg. No. 395 K/Pid/1995 (dated September 29, 1995) is a landmark decision (*putusan monumental*) in criminal law and human rights in Indonesia. The Supreme Court annulled the decisions of the Medan District Court and Medan High Court, which had convicted Dr. [Defendant], S.H., M.A. (General Chairman of the Central Executive Board of the Indonesian Prosperous Workers Union / SBSI) on charges of incitement (Articles 160 & 161 of the Criminal Code) in connection with labor demonstrations in Medan on April 14, 1994.


The Supreme Court outlined a primary sociological/teleological legal principle: Judges must interpret statutes sociologically and teleologically, following the evolution of social-political order, democracy, and freedom of association, rather than merely deducing textually and abstractly from colonial-era statutory norms. Calls for strikes and the struggle for freedom of association to advocate for workers' welfare constitute lawful rights and do not amount to the criminal offense of incitement (*ophitsing*) ex Article 160 of the Criminal Code. Acts of violence or riots occurring during mass demonstrations beyond the organizational leadership's intent fall outside the Defendant's criminal liability. The Defendant was declared not proven guilty, acquitted of all charges (*vrijspraak*), and his rights, standing, and dignity were restored (rehabilitation).


== Executive Summary ==


The central legal principle established in this landmark decision is that labor advocacy and strike calls cannot be criminalized as incitement under colonial-era laws when evaluated through a modern sociological and democratic lens.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Statutory interpretation must account for concrete societal developments rather than rigid abstract deductions.
* Freedom of association and peaceful labor organizing are protected rights, not crimes of incitement.
* Organizational leaders lack criminal liability for spontaneous excesses or riots occurring outside their control.


== Case Background ==


The Defendant, Dr. [Defendant], S.H., M.A. (General Chairman of SBSI), was charged with continuous incitement (Articles 160 jo. 64 and Article 161 of the Criminal Code) regarding a national strike call and labor demonstrations in Medan on April 14, 1994, demanding a minimum wage hike to Rp 7,000/day and freedom of association. 


The mass demonstration turned riotous and caused property damage. 


The Medan District Court (Decision No. 966/Pid.B/1994/PN.Mdn) sentenced him to 3 years imprisonment. The Medan High Court (Decision No. 188/Pid/1994/PT.Mdn) increased the sentence to 4 years imprisonment. 


The Defendant subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

| '''2'''
| '''Not an Incitement Offense:''' The Defendant's actions advocating for labor rights and SBSI cannot be classified as incitement.
| Supreme Court consideration: "it cannot be said that the Defendant's action was incitement, especially in an era where efforts to foster the role and function of socio-political organizations are actively pursued..."
| 0395K_PID_1995.pdf [Passages 1, 28]
|-
| '''3'''
| '''Separation of Demonstration Excess Liability:''' Excess riots/casualties during the Medan demonstration fell outside the Defendant's control.
| Supreme Court consideration: "...besides the demonstration in Medan on April 14, 1994, whose excesses caused casualties, it is outside the Defendant's responsibility."
| 0395K_PID_1995.pdf [Passages 1, 28]
|-
| '''4'''
| '''Acquittal and Rehabilitation Order:''' The Defendant was acquitted of all charges and his dignity and rights were restored.
| Adjudicating Directly Ruling: "Declaring the Defendant Dr. [Defendant], SH. MA. not legally and convincingly proven... Acquitting the Defendant... Restoring the Defendant's rights..."
| 0395K_PID_1995.pdf [Passages 6, 29]
|-
| '''5'''
| '''Annulment of Judex Facti Decisions:''' The Supreme Court annulled the Medan District Court (3 years) and Medan High Court (4 years) sentences.
| Annulled Medan High Court Decision No. 188/Pid/1994/PT.Mdn dated January 16, 1995, and Medan District Court Decision No. 966/Pid.B/1994/PN.Mdn dated November 7, 1994.
| 0395K_PID_1995.pdf [Passages 1, 4, 5, 6, 29]
|}


== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Teleological / Sociological Interpretation of Article 160 of the Criminal Code (Incitement) ===


The procedural issue questioned whether formal formal-offense incitement provisions (Article 160 of the Criminal Code) enacted during Dutch colonial rule could be applied rigidly and textually to labor union activities demanding freedom of association and fair wages.


The Supreme Court ruled that they could not. Statutes serve as references for problem-solving rather than exclusive sources of law. In an era of openness and democratic enforcement, expressing workers' aspirations via SBSI cannot be construed as criminal incitement.


=== Boundaries of Individual Criminal Responsibility ===


The issue questioned whether organizational leaders bear criminal liability for riots or anarchy occurring spontaneously during mass demonstrations involving tens of thousands of workers.


The Supreme Court ruled they do not. Elements of *mens rea* and incitement must be proven directly from the Defendant's actions. Accidental anarchy outside official organizational instructions falls outside the scope of the Defendant's criminal liability.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the *Judex Facti* (Medan District & High Courts) misinterpret the element of "inciting" (inciting to commit criminal offenses) under Article 160 jo. Article 64 of the Criminal Code and Article 161 of the Criminal Code by applying a textual-abstract interpretation without considering the sociological context of democratic development and freedom of association?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the *Judex Facti* misinterpreted the law. Consequently, the decisions of the Medan High Court and Medan District Court are annulled.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Medan District & High Courts) ===


Examination of speech contents, strike circular letters dated January 28, 1994, establishment meetings of SBSI Branch Boards in Medan, and the chronological timeline of the 20,000-worker demonstration on April 14, 1994, in Medan, which escalated into public facility destruction.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
1. The *Judex Facti* misconstrued the elements of incitement under Article 160 of the Criminal Code.
2. In statutory interpretation, judges must account for concrete societal problems and democratic/openness development rather than deducing from abstract logic of archaic laws.
3. SBSI's labor advocacy and freedom of association activities are lawful and do not constitute incitement offenses.
4. Riots arising during the April 14, 1994 demonstration in Medan were collateral excesses beyond the Defendant's control or responsibility.
5. The Supreme Court annulled the lower court rulings and directly acquitted the Defendant (*vrijspraak*) while rehabilitating his reputation.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation ('''Dr. [Defendant], SH. MA.'''), annulled Medan High Court Decision No. 188/Pid/1994/PT.Mdn in conjunction with Medan District Court Decision No. 966/Pid.B/1994/PN.Mdn, and Adjudicated Directly: Declaring that the Defendant Dr. [Defendant], SH. MA. is not legally and convincingly proven guilty of the First and Second charges; Acquitting the Defendant of all charges; Restoring the Defendant's rights in capacity, standing, and dignity (rehabilitation); and charging court costs across all judicial instances to the State.


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Criminal Code (KUHP) Articles 160, 161, 64:''' Public incitement and distribution of incriminatory writings.
* '''1945 Constitution Article 28:''' Freedom of association, assembly, and expression of thoughts orally and in writing.
* '''Doctrine of Sociological Interpretation (*Teleologische Interpretatie*):''' Law should serve evolving community needs (*living law*).


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* Dr. [Defendant] served as the legitimate and active General Chairman of SBSI advocating for workers' rights (demanding a minimum wage of Rp 7,000/day, repeal of Manpower Ministerial Decree No. 01/MEN/1994, and freedom of association).
* The Defendant issued a Strike/Demonstration Appeal Letter dated January 28, 1994, and a Speech Transmittal Letter.


=== Not Established / Unproven ===


* It was unproven that the Defendant intentionally instructed or incited workers to commit violence, destruction, or crimes during the April 14, 1994 demonstration in Medan.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Paradigm Shift in Criminal Cassation Review: This decision represents a historical milestone in judicial independence (*Judex Juris*) protecting human rights defenders and labor activists from criminalization by authoritarian regimes via rubber-stamp articles (*haatzaai artikelen* / incitement laws).


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Can demands for freedom of association and labor strike calls be prosecuted under incitement laws (Article 160 of the Criminal Code)?'''


'''A:''' No. Based on Supreme Court Landmark Decision No. 395 K/Pid/1995 (Dr. [Defendant] Case), workers' rights advocacy and strike calls organized by labor unions do not constitute criminal incitement offenses. The Supreme Court emphasized that Article 160 of the Criminal Code must be interpreted sociologically and teleologically in alignment with democratic principles and freedom of association, and organizational leaders cannot be held criminally liable for demonstration riots occurring beyond their control.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 39 K/Pid/1984 dated August 28, 1984, establishes a vital legal principle drawing a sharp distinction between the criminal offense of fraud (Article 378 of the KUHP) and civil legal relationships. The Supreme Court affirmed that the legal relationship arising between the Defendant and the witness/victim constitutes a civil relationship in the form of a sale and purchase agreement subject to a 1 (one) month deferred payment term, which cannot be interpreted or criminalized as the crime of fraud under Article 378 of the KUHP. Payment delays or defaults (*nakoming*) in a commercial transaction cannot serve as a justification or be manipulated into constituting the element of trickery required for fraud.

== Case Background ==

The Defendant, [Defendant] ([age removed], trader/farmer, residing in [address removed]), was brought before the Kendal District Court under two alternative/cumulative charges:
* '''Primair (Article 378 of the KUHP):''' With intent to unlawfully benefit oneself, purchasing 10 kg of dried cloves belonging to witness [Witness] at a price of Rp 15,000/kg (totaling Rp 150,000) under the promise that payment would be remitted the following month (August 1981). However, after selling the cloves to a third party, the proceeds were not paid to witness [Witness] but instead utilized by the Defendant to purchase stink beans (*jengkol*).
* '''Subsidair (Article 372 of the KUHP):''' Embezzlement of the clove property belonging to witness [Witness].

The Kendal District Court (Decision No. 28/1981/Kts.Kdl. dated August 23, 1982) declared the Defendant legally proven guilty of the criminal offense of "fraud" and sentenced him to 5 (five) months of imprisonment. The Semarang High Court (Decision No. 32/1983/Pid/PT.Smg. dated July 29, 1983) upheld the Kendal District Court decision in its entirety. The Defendant subsequently filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The *judex facti* misapplied the law by interpreting the legal relationship established between the Defendant and witness [Witness] as the criminal offense of fraud under Article 378 of the KUHP.
# The legal relationship occurring between the Defendant and witness [Witness] is a civil relationship structured as a sale and purchase agreement with a payment term of 1 (one) month.
# The Defendant's willingness to purchase at a price higher than the market rate and his subsequent default on payment (*nakoming*) cannot serve as grounds or be manipulated to constitute the element of trickery formulated under Article 378 of the KUHP.
# Although the acts charged against the Defendant are factually proven, such acts do not constitute a crime or a petty criminal offense (rather representing a civil dispute/relationship); hence, the Defendant must be released from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*).
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation [Defendant]; Annulling the Semarang High Court decision dated July 29, 1983, No. 32/1983/Pid/PT.Smg. and the Kendal District Court decision dated August 23, 1982, No. 28/1981/Kts.Kdl.; and Independently Re-Adjudicating: (1) Declaring that the acts charged against Defendant [Defendant] are proven, but that such acts do not constitute a crime or a misdemeanor; (2) Releasing the Defendant from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*); (3) Charging procedural costs across all levels of jurisdiction to the State.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 03 K/MIL/2001 establishes a crucial legal precedent regarding the evidentiary standards of official authority in bribery offenses. The Supreme Court affirmed that the statutory element of acting "contrary to authority or obligations concerning public interest" was unproven, as the authority and obligation to select and nominate the candidate for Regent of Bantul rested with the Bantul Regency Regional House of Representatives (D DPRD Tk. II Bantul), rather than Soeharto in his capacity as Chairman of the Dharmais Foundation. Consequently, the bribery charges were legally unestablished, resulting in the complete acquittal of the Defendant and the restoration of his honor and dignity.

== Case Background ==

The Defendant, [Defendant] (Colonel Art. NRP 22083 / 22093, former Regent of Bantul for the 1991–1996 term), was charged with giving bribes or inducing an official (Article 209 paragraph 1 item 1 of the KUHP / Article 2 of Law No. 11 of 1980) in connection with his efforts to be nominated and reappointed as Regent of Bantul for the 1996–2001 term. The Defendant was accused of issuing a letter of commitment to donate Rp 1,000,000,000 (one billion rupiahs) to the Dharmais Foundation, chaired by President Soeharto, to secure approval for his reappointment.

The Jakarta High Military Court II (Decision No. PUT.07-05/K-AD/MMT.II/VII/1999) sentenced the Defendant to 9 months of imprisonment. On appeal, the Supreme Military Court in Jakarta (Decision No. PUT/03/MMA/BDG/II/2000) modified the ruling, sentencing the Defendant to 6 months of imprisonment and a fine of Rp 10,000,000. The Defendant subsequently filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:''' Because the element contrary to the authority or obligation to appoint the Defendant as Regent fell outside the jurisdiction and responsibility of Soeharto as Chairman of the Dharmais Foundation—resting instead within the authority and obligation of the Bantul Regency Regional House of Representatives (DPRD) to conduct elections and nominate candidates—the elements of the bribery offense were not legally proven, rendering the Supreme Military Court's decision subject to annulment.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition of the Petitioner / Defendant [Defendant]; annulling the decisions of the Supreme Military Court Jakarta No. PUT/03/MMA/BDG/II/2000 and the High Military Court II Jakarta No. PUT.07-05/K-AD/MMT.II/VII/1999; and adjudicating independently: Declaring the Defendant not legally and convincingly proven guilty of the charges under the Primary, Subsidiary, or Secondary indictments; acquitting the Defendant of all charges; and restoring the Defendant's capacity, position, honor, and dignity (rehabilitation).

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Judicial Review Decision No. 03 PK/Mil/2005 annuls the ''in absentia'' ruling rendered by the Medan Military Court I-02 against Defendant Sergeant Major (Serda) [Defendant]. The Supreme Court granted the Petition for Judicial Review after discovering a manifest error committed by the Judex Facti. The Defendant had never deserted from Korem 023/KS Sibolga; pursuant to official transfer orders issued by superior authorities, the Defendant had been officially reassigned to Korem 031/WB in Batam. Furthermore, the Medan Military Court I-02 lacked jurisdiction to try a Defendant stationed outside its legal territory without a valid transfer of authority.

== Case Background ==

The Defendant, [Defendant] (Serda Nrp. 534920, Ba Kima Korem-023/KS), was charged with peacetime desertion under Article 87 paragraph (1) item 2 jo. paragraph (2) of the KUHPM, on the grounds of allegedly abandoning Unit Korem 023/KS Sibolga without authorization starting October 1, 1999. On March 24, 2003, the Medan Military Court I-02 rendered an ''in absentia'' decision (Decision No. PUT/67-K/MM.I-02/AD/III/2003) declaring the Defendant guilty and sentencing him to 2 years and 8 months of imprisonment alongside an additional penalty of dismissal from military service.

The Defendant filed a Petition for Judicial Review (PK) presenting evidence that he was never stationed at Korem 023/KS Sibolga during the contested period; rather, pursuant to the Regional Military Commander I/BB Order (Sprin/1578/X/1999) jo. Commander of Yonif Linud-100/PS Order (Sprin/166/XI/1999), the Defendant had been officially reassigned to a new duty station at Korem 031/WB based in Batam as of October 29, 1999.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:''' The grounds for judicial review are justified due to a manifest error committed by the Judex Facti, given that the Defendant never committed the criminal offense as charged by the Military Prosecutor. Since October 29, 1999, the Defendant never abandoned service, was actively serving at Korem 031/WB, and was never stationed at Korem 023/KS Sibolga. The Medan Military Court I-02 lacked competence to try TNI personnel operating outside its territorial jurisdiction absent a valid delegation of authority from another competent military court.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the petition for judicial review from Petitioner [Defendant]; annulling the Medan Military Court I-02 decision dated March 24, 2003, No. PUT/67-K/MM.I-02/AD/III/2003; and Adjudicating Independently: (1) Declaring Defendant [Defendant], Serda Nrp. 534920 not legally and convincingly proven guilty of the criminal offense of "peacetime desertion"; (2) Acquitting the Defendant of all charges; (3) Restoring the Defendant's rights in capacity, position, honor, and dignity (rehabilitation); (4) Charging all procedural costs across all levels of jurisdiction to the State.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 41 K/Pdt/1990 dated February 27, 1992, establishes a landmark legal rule regarding the protection and limits of civil liability for judicial officials (Judges, Registrars, Bailiffs, and Courts). The Supreme Court affirmed that judicial apparatus acting in the performance of technical judicial duties or judicial power cannot be sued civilly (as Defendants/Respondents). Actions by judicial officials that exceed boundaries or violate authority can only be subjected to administrative oversight and supervisory measures by higher judicial bodies (the High Court or the Supreme Court). Furthermore, regarding judicial administration actions tainted by legal defects, a civil lawsuit for nullification may only be brought by naming the party acquiring rights from such action as the Defendant, and not the Judge, Bailiff, Registrar, or Court concerned.

== Case Background ==

The Objector / Petitioner for Cassation ([Party A]) filed an auction execution third-party opposition (*perlawanan eksekusi lelang*) at the Ambon District Court against the Respondents: the State of the RI cq. Chairman of the Ambon District Court (Respondent I), Registrar of the Ambon District Court (Respondent II), Government of the RI cq. Minister of Finance cq. Director General of Taxation cq. Class II Auction Office of Ambon (Respondent III), and Sonny Waplau (Respondent IV / auction purchaser). The opposition was filed against the seizure and auction of Ownership Land Right No. 41 (Certificate No. 58/1973) in Ambon Municipality pursuant to Ambon District Court Chairman Determination No. 03B/1984-P/Deed No. 4/PN.AB/Eks. jo. No. 03C/1984-P/Deed No. 4/PN.AB/Eks. to execute a *Grosse Akte* of Debt Acknowledgement with Mortgage Power of Attorney No. 4 of 1981. The Objector argued that executing an auction of immovable property without first seizing movable property violated Article 208 of the RBg / Article 197 of the HIR.

The Ambon District Court (Decision No. 02/Pdt.G/Plw/1987/PN.AB dated April 9, 1988) rejected the Objector's opposition. The Maluku High Court in Ambon (Decision No. 2/Pdt/1989/PT.Mal. dated June 16, 1989) upheld the Ambon District Court decision. The Objector subsequently filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# Pursuant to Supreme Court Circular Letter (SEMA) No. 9 of 1976, jurisprudence, and public policy (*public policy*), any judicial apparatus acting in the execution of technical judicial duties or judicial power cannot be sued in a civil capacity.
# Actions by judicial apparatus that violate or exceed legally permitted authority may be brought before higher judicial institutions (the High Court or the Supreme Court) for supervisory action.
# Regarding judicial administration actions containing legal/juridical defects, a civil lawsuit for nullification may be filed, provided the party named as Defendant is the party deriving rights from such action, rather than the Judge, Bailiff, Registrar, or Court in question.
* '''Ruling:''' Rejecting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation [Party A]; Ordering the Petitioner for Cassation / Objector to pay cassation-level court costs amounting to Rp 20,000 (twenty thousand rupiahs).
