== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 04 K/MIL/2000 establishes a crucial legal principle regarding the relationship between criminal charges (embezzlement/land encroachment) and civil ownership disputes (*prejudisieel geschil*). The Supreme Court affirmed that where land parcel ownership status remains unclear and constitutes a civil dispute falling under the authority of Civil Judges within the General Judiciary, neither the element of "unlawfulness" nor the ownership of another's property under Articles 372 and 385 of the KUHP can be legally proven. Consequently, Military Judges lack the authority to convict the Defendant prior to the resolution of ownership status within the General Judiciary, leading to the Defendant's complete acquittal of all charges.

== Case Background ==

The Defendant, [Defendant] (Sergeant Major / Serda Nrp. 572356, Babinsa Koramil 1403-15 Malili), was charged with embezzlement (Article 372 of the KUHP) or land encroachment/sale of inherited land (Article 385 item 1 of the KUHP) in Ujung Pandang between 1990 and 1991, following a report filed by witness-complainant [Party B] Dg. Bollo. The Defendant had controlled and managed inherited land originating from his grandfather (Djaenang / Djamu bin Laikang) based on provisional registration evidence and family lineage records. The Military Court III-16 Ujung Pandang sentenced the Defendant to 4 months and 15 days of imprisonment. On appeal, the High Military Court III Surabaya annulled that decision while independently adjudicating the case and sentencing the Defendant to 4 months and 15 days of imprisonment under Article 372 of the KUHP. The Defendant subsequently filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:''' Because the element of ownership—specifically who owns the land parcel—remains unclear and constitutes a civil dispute falling under the competence of Civil Judges within the General Judiciary rather than Military Judges, the criminal charges under Articles 372 and 385 of the KUHP are unproven, requiring the Defendant's total acquittal.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner [Defendant], Serda Nrp. 572356; Annulling the High Military Court III Surabaya Decision No. PTS/401/BDG/MMT.III/K/AD/II/1998 and the Military Court III-16 Ujung Pandang Decision No. PUT/027-K/MM.III-16/AD/VI/1996; and Adjudicating Independently: Declaring Defendant [Defendant] not legally and convincingly proven guilty of the criminal offense as charged; Acquitting the Defendant of all charges; Restoring the Defendant's rights in capacity, position, honor, and dignity (rehabilitation); and Charging all procedural costs across all levels of jurisdiction to the State.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 04 K/Pdt.Pen/2009 establishes the constitutional legal principle that the Supreme Court and the General Judiciary lack the legal authority to evaluate, correct, or review decisions rendered by other judicial bodies such as the Constitutional Court (MK). Although the Supreme Court acknowledged the Petitioner's plight regarding disqualification from regional elections resembling a form of "civil death," the Supreme Court, in exercising its jurisdiction, cannot exceed the powers conferred upon it by statute.

== Case Background ==

The Petitioner (H. [Party A], SH., paired with H. Hartawan) won the South Bengkulu Regency regional election for the 2009–2014 term with 51.7% of the vote based on South Bengkulu KPUD Decree No. 59 dated December 10, 2008. The losing candidates (Reskan Effendi and Drh. Rohidin Mersyah, MMA.) filed a lawsuit at the Constitutional Court (Register No. 57/PHPU.D-VI/2008). In its decision dated January 8, 2009, the Constitutional Court nullified the regional election results by law (*void ab initio*) and ordered a revote excluding H. [Party A]'s ticket due to a 1985 criminal record. The Petitioner subsequently petitioned the Manna District Court to declare Constitutional Court Decisions No. 57/PHPU.D-VI/2008 and No. 4/PUU-VII/2009 null and void as if they never existed. The Manna District Court (Determination No. 02/Pdt.P/2009/PN.Mn dated May 11, 2009) declared the Petitioner's request inadmissible (*niet ontvankelijke verklaard*). Dissatisfied with this determination, the Petitioner filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The Supreme Court holds no authority to evaluate and review decisions of the Constitutional Court.
# Although the Supreme Court empathizes with the Petitioner's situation—where prohibition from participating in regional elections effectively results in civil death—the Supreme Court, while executing its functions as a General Judiciary institution, cannot correct or review decisions from other judicial bodies like the Constitutional Court because statutory law grants no such power.
# Regarding the enjoyment and loss of civic rights, the established legal maxim dictates that "No punishment shall result in Civil Death or the loss of all civil rights."
* '''Ruling:''' Rejecting the cassation petition filed by Petitioner H. [Party A], SH. (thereby upholding Manna District Court Determination No. 02/Pdt.P/2009/PN.Mn).

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 55 K/TUN/1992 dated November 25, 1993, establishes an important legal principle regarding the basis for assessing the validity of State Administrative Decrees and the authority of Administrative Officials in issuing Building Permits (*Izin Mendirikan Bangunan / IMB*):

* A building that was originally erected without a Building Permit (*IMB*), notwithstanding subsequent sales of the land and structure to a third party who subsequently applies for an *IMB* over that structure, remains an unlawful structure in its origin.
* The action of the Mayor in refusing the Plaintiff's application for an *IMB* does not constitute an arbitrary or unlawful act. The granting or refusal of an *IMB* falls entirely within the authority of the State Administrative Official, and no arbitrariness or abuse of authority for extraneous purposes (*detournement de pouvoir*) occurred in this matter.

== Case Background ==

The Respondent for Cassation / Original Plaintiff ([Plaintiff]) purchased a 335 m² plot of land at Lorong Kuningan Lama No. 187/B/2, 17 Ilir Subdistrict, Palembang, from Koesmanto Wirahadikusuma pursuant to 5 Sale and Purchase Deeds (subsequently split into Ownership Land Certificates No. 1684 through 1688 / 17 Ilir). The Plaintiff subsequently filed an *IMB* application on October 14, 1991 (Agenda No. 352/0510/1991) to continue construction on an existing 5-unit shop structure located on the premises. The application was refused by the Petitioner for Cassation / Original Defendant (Mayor of the Level II Municipality of Palembang) via Letter No. 640/0030/44/II dated December 9, 1991, on the grounds that an unpermitted building stood upon the land and that Supreme Court Decision No. 966/K/Pdt/1985 remained unexecuted.

The Plaintiff challenged the refusal decree at the Palembang State Administrative Court (*PTUN*). The Palembang *PTUN* (Decision No. 01/PTUN/G/PLG/1992 dated April 25, 1992) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in its entirety and annulled the *IMB* refusal letter. The Medan High State Administrative Court (*PTTUN*) (Decision No. 26/BDG.G.PL/PT.TUN/1992 dated August 18, 1992) upheld the Palembang *PTUN* ruling. Dissatisfied with these decisions, the Mayor of Palembang filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# A structure originally erected without a Building Permit (*IMB*), even if the land and structure are subsequently sold and transferred to a third party who applies for an *IMB*, remains an unpermitted and rule-violating structure.
# The Mayor's action in refusing the Plaintiff's application to issue an *IMB* does not constitute arbitrary or unlawful conduct.
# The issuance or refusal of an *IMB* is entirely within the discretion and authority of the State Administrative Official, and the refusal in this case was sufficiently reasoned; the Supreme Court finds no arbitrariness or misuse of authority for improper purposes (*detournement de pouvoir*).
# The fact that the Plaintiff purchased the land following a final and binding civil judgment altered the status of land ownership, but this remains distinct from the Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation's authority regarding an *IMB* for a structure that was unlawful from its inception.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation MAYOR OF LEVEL II MUNICIPALITY OF PALEMBANG; Annulling the Medan High State Administrative Court decision dated August 18, 1992, No. 26/BDG/PLG/PT.TUN/1992 jo. Palembang State Administrative Court decision dated April 25, 1992, No. 01/PTUN/G/PLG/1992; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Rejecting the Plaintiff's lawsuit; (2) Ordering Respondent for Cassation ([Plaintiff]) to pay all court costs across all levels of jurisdiction (assessed at Rp 50,000 at the cassation level).

|}

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Judicial Review (*Peninjauan Kembali / PK*) Decision No. 55 PK/PID/1996 dated October 25, 1996, establishes fundamental jurisprudence and legal standards regarding two critical legal aspects:

* **Authority of the Public Prosecutor to File for Judicial Review:** The Public Prosecutor / Prosecutor's Office, acting in representation of State and public interests, possesses the right and authority to file a petition for Judicial Review (*PK*) against a Supreme Court cassation ruling that acquitted a Defendant of the charges, in the name of upholding the law, justice, and the public interest.
* **Proof of Incitement Offenses (Articles 160 & 161 of the KUHP):** A series of acts committed by the Defendant (General Chairperson of the Central Executive Board of the Indonesian Prosperous Labor Union / SBSI)—consisting of public speeches, strike calls, speech texts, and written circulars provoking worker masses to stage unauthorized demonstrations resulting in riots and property damage in Medan—legally and convincingly satisfy the elements of continuous incitement (Article 160 jo. Article 64 paragraph (1) of the KUHP) and disseminating inciting writings (Article 161 paragraph (1) of the KUHP).

== Case Background ==

The Defendant, Dr. [Defendant], SH, MA (General Chairperson of the Central Executive Board of SBSI), was charged with continuous oral and written incitement (Article 160 jo. Article 64(1) of the KUHP) alongside disseminating inciting writings (Article 161(1) of the KUHP). These acts were executed via leadership lectures in Pematang Siantar, the "Strike/Demonstration Call" circular, and SBSI central board circular letters provoking workers to strike, which culminated in a mass demonstration of approximately 20,000 workers in Medan on April 14, 1994, resulting in rioting, destruction of buildings, factories, and vehicles.

The Medan District Court (Decision No. 966/Pid.B/1994/PN.Mdn dated November 7, 1994) sentenced the Defendant to 3 years of imprisonment. The Medan High Court (Decision No. 188/Pid/1994/PT.Mdn dated January 16, 1995) enhanced the sentence to 4 years of imprisonment. Upon cassation, the Supreme Court (Decision Reg. No. 395 K/Pid/1995 dated September 29, 1995) annulled the lower and appellate court rulings and acquitted the Defendant of all charges. The Head of the Medan State Prosecutor's Office, acting as Public Prosecutor, subsequently filed a petition for Judicial Review (*PK*) to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* **Ratio Decidendi:**
# The Public Prosecutor, acting in representation of State and Public interests, is entitled to file a petition for Judicial Review (*PK*) against a Supreme Court cassation decision that acquits a Defendant.
# The previous Supreme Court cassation decision Reg. No. 395 K/Pid/1995 contained manifest error/mistake (*kekhilafan/kekeliruan yang nyata*) because it disregarded applicable positive criminal law provisions (Articles 160 and 161 of the KUHP) and acquitted the Defendant despite the material acts of incitement having been proven legally and convincingly at trial.
# Grounded upon the Supreme Court's own reasoning and the well-founded reasoning of the *Judex Facti*, the Supreme Court declared sufficient evidence legally and convincingly establishing that the Defendant is guilty of continuous incitement (Article 160 jo. Article 64(1) of the KUHP) and disseminating inciting writings (Article 161(1) of the KUHP).
* **Ruling:** Granting the petition for Judicial Review from Petitioner for PK Head of Medan State Prosecutor's Office / Public Prosecutor; Annulling the Supreme Court decision dated September 29, 1995, Reg. No. 395 K/Pid/1995; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Declaring Defendant Dr. [Defendant], SH, MA legally and convincingly proven guilty of committing the criminal offenses of: "Publicly inciting orally and in writing to commit a criminal offense, to disobey lawful commands issued pursuant to statutory regulations and to disobey statutory provisions, committed as a continuous act" and "Publicly disseminating inciting writings to incite persons to commit a criminal offense, to fail to comply with lawful commands issued pursuant to statutory regulations, and to disobey statutory provisions with intent that the contents of the inciting writings become publicly known"; (2) Sentencing the Defendant to imprisonment for a term of 4 (four) years; (3) Crediting the period of detention already served by the Defendant in full against the sentence imposed; (4) Ordering that evidence items remain attached to the case file; (5) Ordering the Defendant to pay procedural costs across all levels of jurisdiction (assessed at Rp 2,500 at the PK level).

|-

|}

== Overview ==
Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 63 K/Pdt/1987 dated August 15, 1988, establishes settled jurisprudential legal rules regarding commercial transactions paid using empty *Bilyet Giro* instruments and the determination of moratory interest damages:

* '''Breach of Contract via Empty Bilyet Giro:''' In cases where a Defendant pays for purchased goods using a *Bilyet Giro* that turns out to have no funds (*kosong*), such conduct is classified as a breach of contract (*wanprestasi*), and the Defendant incurs a debt or loan obligation toward the Plaintiff equal to the purchase price of the goods.
* '''Moratory Interest of 6% per Annum:''' Regarding damages for payment delays that were not previously agreed upon, the amount of damages is calculated based on the statutory moratory interest rate of 6% (six percent) per year, calculated from the date the lawsuit is registered at the District Court until the debt is paid in full.

== Case Background ==
The Original Plaintiff / Respondent for Cassation (Susanto / Soesanto) sold goods in the form of cigarettes to the Original Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation ([Party A]) valued at Rp 5,352,500. For this transaction, the Defendant paid using 10 (ten) pieces of *Bilyet Giro* issued by Bank Surya Indonesia, Surabaya Central Office, totaling Rp 5,352,500. However, upon presentation for clearing, all of the *Bilyet Giro* instruments turned out to have no funds (*kosong*). Although the Plaintiff repeatedly issued verbal and written reminders and demands, the Defendant failed to settle the debt.

The Plaintiff filed a breach of contract lawsuit at the Surabaya District Court (Case No. 406/Pdt/G/1984/PN.Sby). The Surabaya District Court rendered a decision on February 18, 1985, granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part, declaring the Defendant in breach of contract, ordering the Defendant to pay the debt of Rp 5,352,500 in cash, and declaring the security confiscation valid and enforceable. Dissatisfied with the ruling, the Surabaya High Court (Decision No. 393/Pdt/1986/PT.Sby dated July 23, 1986) amended the appellate judgment by adding an order for interest amounting to 1.5% per month starting from May 1984. The Defendant ([Party A]) subsequently filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# When a Defendant pays for the purchase price of goods using a *Bilyet Giro* that proves to have no funds (*kosong*), it signifies that the Defendant has committed a breach of contract and holds a debt or loan obligation toward the Plaintiff equal to the price of such goods.
# Regarding damages for the buyer's delay in payment, such damages constitute compensation based on unagreed interest, namely 6% per annum in accordance with established settled jurisprudence of the Supreme Court.
# The *judex facti* ruling of the Surabaya High Court setting interest at 1.5% per month in the absence of a prior agreement lacks legal basis and contradicts settled Supreme Court jurisprudence, and must therefore be annulled.

* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation [Party A]; Annulling the Surabaya High Court decision dated July 23, 1986, No. 393/Pdt/1986/PT.Sby and the Surabaya District Court decision dated February 18, 1985, No. 406/Pdt/G/1984; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part; (2) Declaring that the Defendant has committed a breach of contract (*ingkar janji*) toward the Plaintiff; (3) Ordering the Defendant to pay a debt to the Plaintiff amounting to Rp 5,352,500 (five million three hundred fifty-two thousand five hundred rupiahs) in cash and in a lump sum; (4) Declaring that the security confiscation executed by the Substitute Bailiff of the Surabaya District Court on September 14, 1984, pursuant to the determination dated September 12, 1984, is valid and enforceable; (5) Ordering the Defendant to pay damages of 6% per annum to the Plaintiff from the date the lawsuit was registered at the District Court until the debt is paid in full; (6) Rejecting the remainder of the Plaintiff's lawsuit; (7) Ordering the Petitioner for Cassation to pay procedural costs across all levels of jurisdiction (assessed at Rp 20,000 at the cassation level).

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 06 K/PID.HAM.AD HOC/2005 establishes a crucial legal standard regarding the application of mandatory minimum criminal penalties for gross violations of Human Rights (HAM) and the principles of superior/command responsibility. The Supreme Court affirmed that the Ad Hoc High Human Rights Court committed an error in law and exceeded its authority by sentencing the defendant below the statutory minimum penalty prescribed by law (imposing a 5-year prison sentence against a statutory minimum threshold of 10 years). Imposing sentences below statutory minimums in a determinate sentencing system creates an adverse precedent that undermines legal certainty and the sense of justice.

== Case Background ==

The Defendant, [Defendant] (Former Deputy Commander of the Pro-Integration Fighters / PPI and Commander of the Aitarak Group), was charged under the doctrine of superior responsibility pursuant to Article 42 paragraphs (2)(a) and (b) jo. Article 7(b), Article 9(a) and (h), and Article 37 of Law No. 26 of 2000 on the Human Rights Court. The Defendant was accused of failing to exercise effective control over subordinates who carried out a systematic attack against the civilian population in Dili, East Timor, on April 17, 1999, including the attack on the residence of Manuel Viegas Carrascalao, which resulted in the deaths of 12 civilians and injuries to several others. The Ad Hoc Human Rights Court at the Central Jakarta District Court sentenced the Defendant to 10 years of imprisonment. The Ad Hoc High Human Rights Court of Jakarta modified the ruling by reducing the sentence to 5 years of imprisonment. Dissatisfied with this decision, both the Public Prosecutor and the Defendant filed cassation petitions.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:''' The Ad Hoc High Human Rights Court misapplied the law and exceeded its competence by imposing a lighter sentence below the statutory minimum threshold (namely a 5-year prison term, whereas the minimum threat under Article 37 jo. Article 42(2) jo. Article 9 of Law No. 26 of 2000 is 10 years of imprisonment). Sentencing below the statutory minimum within a determinate sentencing framework establishes a detrimental precedent that obstructs the fulfillment of sentencing objectives—namely utility, justice, and legal certainty.
* '''Ruling:''' Declaring the cassation petition filed by Petitioner for Cassation [Defendant] inadmissible; Granting the cassation petition filed by the Ad Hoc Public Prosecutor at the Attorney General's Office of the RI; Annulling the Jakarta Ad Hoc High Human Rights Court Decision No. 02/PID.HAM/AD.HOC/2004/PT.DKI; and Independently Adjudicating: Declaring Defendant [Defendant] legally and convincingly proven guilty of committing "GROSS HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS IN THE FORM OF CRIMES AGAINST HUMANITY," and sentencing the Defendant to 10 (ten) years of imprisonment.

|}

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Judicial Review Decision No. 06 PK/TUN/2008 rejects the Petition for Judicial Review (PK) filed by the Minister of Forestry of the Republic of Indonesia against the Oil Palm Plantation Cooperative (KPKS) Bukit Harapan concerning the annulment of the principle approval for oil palm plantation management within the Register 40 Padang Lawas Forest Area. The Supreme Court affirmed that divergent legal interpretations between a PK petitioner and the Judex Juris cannot be categorized as a judicial error or a manifest mistake. Furthermore, a criminal conviction against an individual (Darianus Lungguk Sitorus) is irrelevant to invalidating an administrative decision that granted valid permits to a cooperative legal entity.

== Case Background ==

Indigenous communities in Luhat Simangambat and Luhat Ujung Batu (North Sumatra) partnered with PT Torganda and established the Oil Palm Plantation Cooperative (KPKS) Bukit Harapan to manage oil palm plantations in former customary/ulayat land areas. The Minister of Forestry issued Letter No. 1680/Menhut-III/2002 dated September 26, 2002, granting principle approval for managing a 23,000-hectare area. However, on October 13, 2004, the Minister of Forestry issued Letter No. S.419/Menhut-II/2004, unilaterally revoking the principle approval. KPKS Bukit Harapan filed an annulment lawsuit at the Jakarta State Administrative Court (PTUN). The Jakarta PTUN granted the Plaintiff's claim, but the Jakarta High State Administrative Court overturned the ruling. At the cassation level (Decision No. 134 K/TUN/2007), the Supreme Court reversed the appellate decision and granted KPKS Bukit Harapan's claim. The Minister of Forestry subsequently filed a Petition for Judicial Review citing a manifest error regarding lawsuit time limits and newly discovered evidence (*novum*) in the form of criminal cassation decision No. 2642 K/Pid/2006.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# Differences in opinion or legal interpretation within a PK memorandum between a PK Petitioner and the Judex Juris (the Supreme Court's cassation decision) essentially constitute a divergence in legal interpretation and therefore cannot be deemed or categorized as a judicial error or manifest mistake under Article 67 letter f of Law No. 5 of 2004.
# Administrative negligence by an Administrative Official in dispatching an administrative decision to a citizen, which causes a shift in the lawsuit filing timeframe, constitutes an administrative fault and must not become a burden that prejudices the Plaintiff's rights as a seeker of justice.
# The criminal verdict against Darianus Lungguk Sitorus (Director of PT Torganda) cannot be linked or connected to the lawful legal actions of KPKS Bukit Harapan as a distinct legal entity that obtained valid permits from an Administrative Official.
* '''Ruling:''' Rejecting the petition for judicial review from the PK Petitioner: THE MINISTER OF FORESTRY OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA; Ordering the PK Petitioner / Defendant to pay judicial review examination costs amounting to Rp2,500,000 (two million five hundred thousand rupiahs).

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 76 K/AG/1992 dated October 23, 1993, establishes fundamental jurisprudence and legal standards in Islamic Grant Law and Inheritance: A grant (*hibah*) exceeding 1/3 (one-third) of the total area of the disputed object or estate owned by the grantor, given to one child without the consent of the other heirs, is contrary to legal rules and void by law. The Supreme Court affirmed that parental grants of property to a child must take into account principles of fairness among children and the one-third maximum limit to avoid prejudicing the rights of other legal heirs.

== Case Background ==

The late H. Saman bin Nasiman (passed away on July 24, 1987) was married 3 times during his lifetime and left behind 2 surviving wives (Hj. Saodah and Hj. Salamah), 4 biological children, and 2 grandchildren from a predeceased child. On May 10, 1986, the late H. Saman bin Nasiman granted a plot of land measuring 949 m² (pursuant to Girik C No. 692) located in Kampung Kapuk, Klender, East Jakarta, to one of his sons, the late [Party B] (Grant Deed No. 325/1.711.1/86). This grant was executed without the consent of the other legal heirs and consumed 949 m² out of the deceased's total land estate of approximately 1,340 m², leaving only about 391 m² for all remaining legal heirs.

[Party A] (alongside other heirs acting as Plaintiffs) filed a lawsuit seeking the cancellation of the grant and a distribution of inheritance at the East Jakarta Religious Court. The East Jakarta Religious Court (Decision No. 272/G/1990 dated July 17, 1990) granted the Plaintiffs' lawsuit and declared the 949 m² land grant invalid and void. However, the Jakarta High Religious Court (Decision No. 47/1990/PTA.JK dated March 25, 1991) annulled the East Jakarta Religious Court decision and declared the lawsuit inadmissible due to formal defects concerning power of attorney. Dissatisfied with the appellate ruling, the Plaintiff ([Party A]) filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The disputed object, namely the granted land measuring 949 m², exceeded one-third of the total land area owned by the late H. Saman bin Nasiman (out of a total area of 1,340 m²); hence, the granted surface area violated statutory legal provisions.
# The act of granting the vast majority of land to a single child without the consent of the other legal heirs generates inequity and disharmony in sibling/heir relations, which runs counter to Islamic teachings (as reflected in the Hadith of the Prophet SAW narrated by Nu'man bin Bashir, which commands fairness among children).
# The Jakarta High Religious Court committed an error of law by treating this matter as a voluntary jurisdiction (*voluntair*) case and dismissing the lawsuit on technicalities of power of attorney formalities lacking legal grounds. Therefore, the Jakarta High Religious Court decision must be annulled, and the Supreme Court independently re-adjudicates the case by upholding the East Jakarta Religious Court judgment.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation [Party A]; Annulling the Jakarta High Religious Court decision dated March 25, 1991, No. 47/1990/PTA.JK; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit; (2) Declaring that the grant by the late H. Saman bin Nasiman to the late [Party B] over a plot of land measuring 949 m² in Kampung Kapuk RT 008/05, Klender Village, East Jakarta, dated May 10, 1986, is invalid and void by law; (3) Determining the lawful heirs and the entire estate of the late H. Saman bin Nasiman; (4) Ordering the proportional distribution of inheritance among each legal heir in accordance with Islamic inheritance law; (5) Declaring valid and enforceable the Security Confiscation (*Conservatoir Beslaag*) placed by the East Jakarta Religious Court; (6) Ordering the Defendant to surrender land controlled in excess of their lawful share to the Plaintiff; (7) Ordering the Defendant to pay court costs across all levels of jurisdiction.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 86 K/Pid/1982 dated March 31, 1983, establishes two important legal principles in Material Criminal Law and Criminal Procedure Law:

* '''Criminal Procedure Law (Examination of Similar Indictments):''' Because the primary charge (Article 317 of the KUHP — Defamation via False Complaint) and the secondary charge (Article 311 of the KUHP — Defamation) are of a similar nature, functioning as alternative or primary-subsidiary charges, once the primary charge has been proven, the secondary charge does not need to be further examined or considered.

* '''Crime of Defamation via Complaint (Article 317 KUHP):''' The Defendant's act of intentionally submitting a false complaint or notification letter to the Police alleging that another person had embezzled his bus fleet, despite knowing that the buses had been legally sold and that National Police Crime Laboratory (*Labkrim*) examinations confirmed the authenticity of the Defendant's signature, while refusing to retract the complaint, legally and convincingly satisfies the elements of the crime of defamation via false complaint under Article 317 of the KUHP.

== Case Background ==

The Defendant, [Defendant], [age removed], Director of PT Solo Express and residing in [address removed], was brought before the Surakarta District Court facing two alternative charges:

* '''Primary Charge (Article 317 of the KUHP):''' Intentionally submitting and handing over a false complaint/notification letter to Police Precinct (*Komres*) 951 Surakarta containing allegations that witnesses [Witness] / Sutjipto Santoso had embezzled 4 (four) bus vehicles belonging to him, whereas the Defendant knew or should reasonably have suspected that such allegations were false, with the intent to prompt Police investigation against the witnesses.

* '''Secondary Charge (Article 311 paragraph (1) of the KUHP):''' Writing down defamation/libel against witness [Witness] by accusing him of embezzling 4 buses.

The Surakarta District Court (Decision No. 432/1977/Pid.B. dated December 11, 1979) declared the Defendant guilty of the crime of defamation via complaint and sentenced him to 4 (four) months of imprisonment.

The Semarang High Court (Decision No. 67/1980/Pid/PT.Smg. dated October 22, 1980) annulled the Surakarta District Court judgment and acquitted the Defendant of all legal prosecutions (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*) on the grounds that the Defendant's complaint was aimed at reclaiming his rights over the buses.

Dissatisfied with the Semarang High Court ruling, the Public Prosecutor at the Surakarta State Prosecutor's Office filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# Because the primary charge (Article 317 of the KUHP) and secondary charge (Article 311 of the KUHP) are of a similar nature, these charges ought to be treated as alternative. Therefore, with the primary charge having been proven, the secondary charge requires no further consideration.

# The Semarang High Court erred and lacked sufficient legal reasoning (*onvoldoende gemotiveerd*) because it based its ruling solely on the Defendant's appellate memorandum without examining or investigating the factual testimonies of witnesses, sales receipt evidence, and the findings of the National Police Crime Laboratory (*Labkrim*).

# Trial facts proved that the Defendant knew the buses had been sold to witness [Witness] under receipts signed by the Defendant himself, with the authenticity of the signature positively confirmed by Labkrim. Although advised by the Police to retract his complaint, the Defendant refused to do so and persisted in accusing the witness of embezzlement. Such conduct was found to constitute defamation via false complaint.

* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation, Public Prosecutor at the State Prosecutor's Office in Surakarta; annulling the Semarang High Court decision dated October 22, 1980, No. 67/1980/Pid/PT.Smg.; and independently adjudicating:

# Declaring that Defendant '''[Defendant]''' is guilty of committing the crime of: "Defamation via Complaint (*Memfitnah dengan pengaduan*)".

# Sentencing him accordingly to 4 (four) months of imprisonment.

# Ordering the Petitioner for Cassation to pay court costs at this level amounting to Rp 2,500 (two thousand five hundred rupiahs).

== Overview ==

Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 90 K/AG/1992, dated 30 September 1993, established jurisprudence and a standard guideline for formulating judgments in divorce cases before the Religious Courts.

The Supreme Court held that the operative part of a divorce judgment based on continuous disputes and discord (*syiqaq*), where the plaintiff's divorce claim is granted, must be formulated accurately and according to the established judicial wording:

'''“Declaring that one ba'in sughra talaq has fallen from the Defendant ([Party A]) upon the Plaintiff ([Party B]).”'''

The Supreme Court corrected the wording used by the Palembang High Religious Court because it was not formulated according to the established standard, particularly the use of the expression "divorcing" and the specification of a particular date from which the divorce was stated to take effect.

== Case Background ==

The original Plaintiff / Respondent in Cassation, [Party B], [age removed] and a farmer, filed a divorce petition against her husband, the original Defendant / Petitioner in Cassation, [Party A], [age removed] and a farmer, before the Lubuk Linggau Religious Court.

The parties were legally married on 6 February 1982 in Megang Sakti II Village, Musi Rawas, as recognized by Lubuk Linggau Religious Court Decision No. 191/G/1991/PA.LLG, and had two children. Since April 1991, they had lived separately because of continuous disputes and discord. The Plaintiff alleged that the Defendant had behaved harshly toward the Plaintiff's child from a previous relationship, had been dishonest concerning financial matters and agricultural harvest proceeds, and had frequently ridden together with another woman.

The Lubuk Linggau Religious Court, through Decision No. 192/G/1991/PA.LLG dated 17 October 1991, granted the Plaintiff's divorce claim and pronounced one ba'in sughra talaq.

The Palembang High Religious Court, through Decision No. 35/G/1991/PTA.Plg dated 16 March 1992, upheld the Lubuk Linggau Religious Court's decision but changed the operative wording to:

'''"Divorcing the Plaintiff, [Party B], from the Defendant, [Party A], with one ba'in sughra talaq effective from 17 October 1991."'''

The Defendant subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# Objections raised by the Petitioner in Cassation concerning the assessment of evidence constituted an appreciation of factual circumstances and therefore could not be reconsidered at the cassation level pursuant to Article 30 of Law No. 14 of 1985.

# The operative part of the Palembang High Religious Court's judgment, which stated ''"Divorcing the Plaintiff... from the Defendant... with one ba'in sughra talaq effective from 17 October 1991,"'' was considered insufficiently precise in formulating the judgment.

# In accordance with Islamic civil law and the established principles governing Religious Court judgments, the proper formulation of the operative part of a divorce judgment must expressly state:

'''“Declaring that one ba'in sughra talaq has fallen from the Defendant ([Party A]) upon the Plaintiff ([Party B]).”'''

# Accordingly, the cassation petition was rejected, with a correction to the operative part of the Palembang High Religious Court's judgment.

* '''Ruling:''' The Supreme Court rejected the cassation petition of the Petitioner in Cassation, '''[Party A]''', while correcting the operative part of Palembang High Religious Court Decision No. 35/G/1991/PTA.Plg dated 16 March 1992 in conjunction with Lubuk Linggau Religious Court Decision No. 192/G/1991/PA.LLG dated 17 October 1991, as follows:

# Granting the appeal petition of the Appellant.

# Correcting the operative part of the Lubuk Linggau Religious Court judgment dated 17 October 1991, No. 192/G/1991/PA.LLG, so that it reads:
## Granting the Plaintiff's claim.
## '''Declaring that one ba'in sughra talaq has fallen from the Defendant ([Party A]) upon the Plaintiff ([Party B]).'''
## Ordering the Plaintiff to pay the court costs at the first-instance level in the amount of Rp 56,500 (fifty-six thousand five hundred rupiah).

# Ordering the Appellant to pay the court costs at the appellate level in the amount of Rp 13,500 (thirteen thousand five hundred rupiah).

# Ordering the Petitioner in Cassation to pay the court costs at the cassation level in the amount of Rp 20,000 (twenty thousand rupiah).

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 1020 K/Pdt/1986, dated September 29, 1987, established three fundamental family civil law and divorce procedural law rules:


First, Divorce Grounds for Continuous Disputes (Article 19 letter f of PP No. 9 of 1975): In a marriage, when continuous disputes and quarrels occur between husband and wife with no hope of reconciliation, acknowledged by the Defendant (Wife) and corroborated by witness testimonies, a divorce lawsuit filed by the Plaintiff (Husband) must be granted.


Second, Inadmissibility of Cumulating Joint Property Distribution and Wife Maintenance Claims: Claims for living maintenance for a wife pending remarriage and joint property (*gono-gini*) distribution cannot be cumulatively joined within a divorce lawsuit (reconvention claims for property distribution in divorce proceedings are inadmissible / NO), but must instead be brought via separate, independent lawsuits after the divorce judgment attains final and binding legal force (referring to Supreme Court Decision No. 692 K/Sip/1981).


Third, Obligation to Formulate Divorce Registration Dictums: When a District Court grants a divorce lawsuit, the verdict dictum (*dictum*) must include a mandatory order: "Ordering the Substitute Registrar or designated official to transmit a copy of this decision to the Civil Registrar at the place where the divorce occurred so that the divorce judgment can be registered".


== Executive Summary ==


The central legal principles established in this decision govern the procedural separation of divorce actions from joint property disputes and mandate strict registration compliance in judicial divorces.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Continuous marital discord without reconciliation prospects satisfies statutory grounds for dissolving marriages.
* Joint property (*gono-gini*) and post-divorce maintenance claims cannot be attached to divorce actions and require separate lawsuits.
* Divorce judgment dictums must expressly command court registrars to transmit copies to civil registries for official registration.


== Case Background ==


The Original Plaintiff / Respondent for Cassation ('''[Husband]''') filed a divorce lawsuit against the Original Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Wife]''') at the Pekalongan District Court based on Marriage Certificate No. 32/1984 dated March 24, 1984, citing continuous disputes and quarrels (Article 19 letter f PP No. 9 of 1975). The Defendant filed a reconvention counterclaim demanding the return of personal property (gold jewelry/Rp 1,680,000.—), joint property distribution (*gono-gini* amounting to Rp 5,000,000.— & 1 kg of gold), and living maintenance of Rp 300,000.— per month. 


The Pekalongan District Court (Decision No. 79/Pdt.G/1984/PN.Pkl dated March 25, 1985) granted the convention divorce lawsuit and declared the reconvention counterclaim inadmissible (NO). The Semarang High Court (Decision No. 443/1985/Pdt/PT.SMG dated September 23, 1985) affirmed the Pekalongan District Court decision. The Petitioner for Cassation subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Inadmissibility of Cumulating Joint Property (*Gono-Gini*) and Wife Maintenance Claims in Divorce Proceedings (Article 24 paragraph 2 PP No. 9 of 1975 & Article 41 Law No. 1 of 1974) ===


The primary issue was whether a reconvention counterclaim filed by a Wife/Defendant demanding joint property distribution (Rp 5,000,000.— and 1 kg of gold) and post-divorce living maintenance (Rp 300,000.—/month) can be examined and adjudicated together with a divorce lawsuit filed by her Husband.


The Supreme Court held that it is Inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO). Pursuant to Supreme Court Standing Jurisprudence (as affirmed in Supreme Court Decision No. 692 K/Sip/1981 dated September 21, 1981), claims for joint property distribution and post-divorce wife maintenance cannot be joined with divorce lawsuits, but must instead be brought through separate, independent lawsuits after the divorce action is decided and attains final binding legal force. This ensures clarity of subject matter and avoids evidentiary complexity regarding property ownership during divorce trials.


=== Rectification of Divorce Verdict Dictums (Mandatory Registration Dictum ex Article 35 PP No. 9 of 1975) ===


District or High Court verdict dictums granting divorces are legally incomplete if they omit orders directing registration with the Civil Registrar. The Supreme Court on cassation is authorized to rectify such verdict dictums by adding mandatory clauses commanding registrars to transmit copies to civil registries.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the *Judex Facti* (Semarang High Court & Pekalongan District Court) err in formulating the divorce verdict dictums by omitting orders transmitting decision copies to the Marriage Registrar, and was the dismissal of the joint property reconvention counterclaim in the divorce proceedings legally correct?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the *Judex Facti* correctly dismissed joint property reconvention claims (mandating separate lawsuits ex Supreme Court Decision No. 692 K/Sip/1981), but the divorce verdict dictums were incomplete. The Supreme Court rejected the Petitioner for Cassation's cassation while rectifying the verdict dictums to include mandatory orders directing the Substitute Registrar to transmit divorce decision copies to the Civil Registrar.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Pekalongan District Court & Semarang High Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning the marriage of [Husband] and [Wife] on March 24, 1984 (Deed No. 32/1984); frequent verbal quarrels triggered by trivial matters (such as preparing soto babat); household separation where Defendant returned to her parents' home in Batang starting November 1984; witness testimonies ([Party C], Leginem, Enggawati Sutanto, Sugiasih Juwono, Kwan Tsu Bie, Suwarni, Sutedjo); and property claims (personal jewelry/cash Rp 1,680,000.— and joint property cash Rp 5,000,000.— & 1 kg gold).


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The *Judex Facti* correctly granted the convention divorce lawsuit because continuous disputes were proven, acknowledged by the Defendant, and corroborated by family witness testimonies.
# The *Judex Facti* correctly declared joint property and maintenance reconvention claims inadmissible (NO) because joint property distribution and post-divorce maintenance claims cannot be joined with divorce lawsuits, requiring separate independent lawsuits pursuant to Supreme Court Decision No. 692 K/Sip/1981.
# However, the appellate verdict dictums were incomplete for omitting divorce registration mandates. The Supreme Court rejected the Petitioner for Cassation's cassation while rectifying the verdict dictums to add mandatory orders transmitting divorce decision copies to the Civil Registrar.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court ruled: Rejecting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Wife]''') while rectifying the ruling of Semarang High Court Decision No. 443/1985/Pdt/PT.SMG dated September 23, 1985, which affirmed Pekalongan District Court Decision No. 79/Pdt.G/1984/PN.Pkl. dated March 25, 1985, to read: IN CONVENTION: 1. Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit entirely; 2. Declaring according to law that the marriage between [Husband] and Defendant [Wife] is dissolved by divorce; 3. Ordering the Substitute Registrar or designated official to transmit a copy of this decision to the Civil Registrar at the place where the divorce occurred so that the divorce judgment can be registered; IN RECONVENTION: Declaring the reconvention lawsuit inadmissible; IN CONVENTION AND RECONVENTION: Ordering the Petitioner for Cassation / Original Defendant to pay court costs across all judicial instances (cassation court costs set at Rp 20,000.—).

* '''Supreme Court Standing Jurisprudence:''' Supreme Court Decision No. 692 K/Sip/1981 (September 21, 1981): Prohibition of cumulating joint property distribution (*gono-gini*) claims with divorce lawsuits.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* Marriage between [Husband] and [Wife] solemnized on March 24, 1984, was dissolved by divorce.
* Continuous marital disputes and quarrels were proven, acknowledged by the Defendant, and corroborated by family witnesses, leaving no hope of reconciliation.
* Substitute Registrar of Pekalongan District Court was ordered to transmit divorce decision copies to the Civil Registrar at the place where the divorce occurred for official registration.


=== Not Established / Inadmissible (Separate Lawsuit Required) ===


* Reconvention claims concerning joint property distribution (Rp 5,000,000.— cash & 1 kg gold) and wife maintenance allowance (Rp 300,000.—/month) were unexamined in this divorce proceeding and declared inadmissible (NO), requiring separate civil lawsuits.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Separation of Divorce Actions from Joint Property Lawsuits: This landmark ruling establishes family procedural certainty in Indonesia: divorce proceedings must be fully finalized until attaining binding legal force before joint property distribution (*gono-gini*) and post-divorce maintenance disputes can be brought via separate independent lawsuits.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Can claims for joint property distribution (*gono-gini*) and ex-wife maintenance be joined within a single divorce statement of claim at a District Court?'''


'''A:''' No, they cannot be joined (*Requires Separate Lawsuits*). Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 1020 K/Pdt/1986 (in conjunction with Supreme Court Decision No. 692 K/Sip/1981), claims for a wife's living maintenance and joint property distribution (*gono-gini*) cannot be joined together with divorce lawsuits. Joint property distribution claims in divorce proceedings must be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO), and may only be brought through separate independent civil lawsuits after the divorce judgment attains final and binding legal force.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 1029 K/Pdt/1992, dated July 29, 1993, established a customary land law and inheritance rule concerning the inheritance rights of childless widows over the ancestral or pre-marriage assets (*harta asal/bawaan* / *harta pusaka*) of their late husbands:


A widow who has no children from her marriage with her late husband HAS NO RIGHT over the ancestral/pre-marriage assets (*harta asal/bawaan* / *harta pusaka*) of her late husband originating from the husband's bloodline or parents that have not yet been partitioned. Pursuant to Customary Law and the Marriage Law, such ancestral assets revert and fall to the direct bloodline/blood relatives of the late husband (his biological siblings and their descendants). The widow is entitled solely to joint property (*gono-gini*) acquired during her marriage with her late husband.


The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation (Widow [Widow]) in part, annulled Maluku High Court Decision No. 55/Pdt/1991/PT.Mal in conjunction with Ambon District Court Decision No. 153/Perd.G/1989/PN.Ab, and adjudicated afresh by declaring the Plaintiff, Defendant I, and Defendant II as lawful heirs of their respective husbands, while rejecting the Plaintiff's claim for a 1/3 share of the ancestral land belonging to her late husband's lineage.


== Executive Summary ==


The central legal principle established in this decision is that childless widows cannot inherit pre-marriage ancestral estates (*harta asal*) from their husband's family line, preserving lineage integrity while protecting spousal joint property rights.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Unpartitioned ancestral estates (*harta asal*) remain within the husband's direct bloodline and do not pass to childless widows.
* Spousal inheritance rights for childless widows are strictly limited to marital joint property (*gono-gini*).
* Lower court judgments dismissing whole lawsuits are subject to partial correction to recognize spousal heir status while denying ancestral estate claims.


== Case Background ==


The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation ('''Widow [Widow]''') filed a lawsuit at the Ambon District Court against the Original Defendants / Respondents for Cassation (1. '''[Party B]''', 2. '''[Party A]'''). The Plaintiff sought a court declaration recognizing corporate/ancestral land in Saparua Village, inherited from the late Daniel Melianus [Party], as the property of the Plaintiff, Defendant I, and Defendant II in equal 1/3 shares, based on their status as widows/heirs of Daniel [Party]'s three sons ([Party D], Jan, and Dominggus [Party]). The Plaintiff had no children from the late [Party D] [Party]. 


The Ambon District Court (Decision No. 153/Perd.G/1989/PN.Ab dated January 31, 1991) dismissed the Plaintiff's lawsuit entirely on the grounds that childless widows possess no right over their husband's ancestral goods. The Maluku High Court in Ambon (Decision No. 55/Pdt/1991/PT.Mal dated October 29, 1991) affirmed the Ambon District Court decision. The Petitioner for Cassation subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Legal Standing and Inheritance Claims of Childless Widows Over a Husband's Ancestral/Pre-marriage Assets ===


The primary issue was whether a widow without children from her marriage with her late husband is entitled to claim an inheritance share (1/3 share) of ancestral land (*harta pusaka* / *harta asal*) originating from her late husband's parents or bloodline.


The Supreme Court held that she is Not Entitled. Pursuant to Customary Inheritance Law principles and Law No. 1 of 1974 on Marriage, ancestral or pre-marriage assets acquired by a late husband from his parents' bloodline that remain undivided must be maintained within the husband's original bloodline / blood relatives. A widow who bore no children from her late husband holds no rights over such ancestral assets. Her civil rights are strictly limited to joint property (*gono-gini* / marital earnings) acquired during the marriage.


=== Rectification of Judex Facti Decisions Dismissing Lawsuits Entirely ===


The Ambon District Court and Maluku High Court misapplied the law by dismissing the Plaintiff's lawsuit entirely. Although the Plaintiff possessed no right to share in ancestral land, establishing the Plaintiff's legal status as a lawful heir of her late husband ([Party D]) pursuant to Ambon District Court Determination No. 66/Pdt.P/1988/PN.Ab had to be recognized and granted in the judgment. Therefore, the Supreme Court annulled the lower court rulings and adjudicated afresh, granting the lawsuit in part.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the *Judex Facti* (Maluku High Court & Ambon District Court) misapply the law (*foutieve kepassing van het recht*) by dismissing the Plaintiff's lawsuit entirely without recognizing the Plaintiff's status as a lawful heir of her husband and without providing a juridical distinction between ancestral/heirloom assets and joint property (*gono-gini*) for a childless widow?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the *Judex Facti* misapplied the law. The Supreme Court annulled Maluku High Court Decision No. 55/Pdt/1991/PT.Mal in conjunction with Ambon District Court Decision No. 153/Perd.G/1989/PN.Ab and adjudicated afresh, granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part: declaring the Plaintiff, Defendant I, and Defendant II as lawful heirs of their respective husbands, while rejecting the claim for partition of 1/3 of the ancestral land.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Ambon District Court & Maluku High Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning the origin of the enterprise land in Saparua Village purchased by Daniel Marthinus [Party] and his wife [Party C] from Jan Latuharhary (exhibits P.II, T.I.3, T.I.4); pedigree of Daniel [Party]'s 3 sons ([Party D], Jan, and Dominggus [Party]); marriage of [Party D] to Widow Constanthina Athilda [Party] on January 4, 1972 (exhibit P.IV) without children; and physical control over the disputed land by Defendants I and II.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The *Judex Facti* erred by dismissing the lawsuit entirely without recognizing the Plaintiff's status as a lawful heir.
# Regarding the merits, the disputed land constituted pre-marriage ancestral property (*harta asal*) of the late Daniel Melianus [Party] that remained unpartitioned.
# Pursuant to customary law and marriage law, ancestral assets fall to the direct bloodline, and a childless widow has no right over her late husband's ancestral assets, though she retains rights over marital joint property.
# The Supreme Court annulled lower court rulings and adjudicated afresh, recognizing heir status while denying the ancestral land partition claim.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court ruled: Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation ('''Janda [Widow]'''); Annulling Maluku High Court decision dated October 29, 1991, No. 55/Pdt/1991/PT.Mal., which affirmed Ambon District Court decision dated January 31, 1991, No. 153/Perd.G/1989/PN.Ab.; and ADJUDICATING AFRESH: 1. Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part; 2. Declaring the Plaintiff, Defendant I, and Defendant II as lawful heirs, respectively, of [Party D], Jan [Party], and Dominggus [Party]; 3. Rejecting all other claims of the Plaintiff; 4. Ordering the Respondents for Cassation to pay court costs across all judicial instances (cassation court costs set at Rp 20,000.—).

* Defendant I ([Party B]) and Defendant II ([Party A]) were wives and lawful heirs, respectively, of the late Jan [Party] and Dominggus [Party].
* Disputed land in Saparua constituted pre-marriage ancestral/heirloom property left by the late Daniel Melianus/Marthinus [Party] that remained unpartitioned.

* Preservation of Customary Heirloom Integrity: This landmark ruling consistently upholds customary inheritance law doctrine in Indonesia: ancestral/pre-marriage assets from a husband's parents cannot pass out of the original family bloodline through marriages of widows without offspring, while safeguarding widows' full rights over marital joint property (*gono-gini*).


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Does a widow without children have the right to inherit ancestral land (*harta pusaka* / *harta asal*) belonging to her late husband?'''


'''A:''' No, she has no right. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 1029 K/Pdt/1992, a widow who has no children from her late husband has no right over her late husband's ancestral or pre-marriage assets originating from his parents' bloodline. Pursuant to Customary Law and the Marriage Law, such ancestral assets revert to the late husband's direct bloodline, whereas the widow is entitled solely to joint property (*gono-gini*) acquired during the marriage.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 1036 K/Pid/1989, dated August 31, 1992, established a material criminal law rule concerning the qualification of issuing bad checks known to be unfunded from the beginning as the crime of fraud (*Oplichting* ex Article 378 of the Criminal Code):


Because the Defendant consciously knew from the outset that the checks given to the victim witness lacked funds (*bad checks* / *cek kosong*), the charge of "Fraud" under Article 378 of the Criminal Code must be considered legally and convincingly proven. Handing over bad checks while persuading the victim witness to hand over cash—under the pretext of a discounted cash exchange—does not constitute a pure civil loan relationship, but rather constitutes fraudulent trickery (*oplichtingsmiddel*) satisfying all elements of Article 378 of the Criminal Code.


The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Public Prosecutor at the Lumajang State Prosecutor's Office, annulled the release ruling (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*) of the Surabaya High Court Decision No. 270/Pid/1988/PT.Sby, and adjudicated afresh by declaring the Defendant ([Defendant]) proven guilty of Fraud and sentencing her to 5 (five) months' imprisonment.


== Executive Summary ==


The central legal principle established in this decision is that issuing checks known to be unfunded at the time of delivery to induce cash transfers constitutes criminal fraud rather than civil contract default.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Delivering checks known from inception to lack sufficient funds satisfies the fraudulent trickery element (*oplichtingsmiddel*) of criminal fraud.
* Transactions disguised as discounted cash exchanges utilizing bad checks are criminal offenses rather than pure civil debt disputes.
* Appellate discharge rulings (*ontslag*) mischaracterizing fraudulent check transactions as civil matters are subject to reversal on cassation.


== Case Background ==


The Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation, '''[Defendant]''' ([age removed], housewife), was charged with fraud (Article 378 KUHP) for going to the home of witness [Witness] in July 1987 carrying three checks issued by BRI Lumajang Branch totaling Rp 8,000,000.—, promising they were funded, and asking for cash exchanges with a 10% discount (net received Rp 7,200,000.—). On August 15, 1987, the checks were rejected by BRI Lumajang because the balance was insufficient, and the Defendant knew from the outset that the checks were unfunded. 


The Lumajang District Court (Decision No. 64/Pid.S/1988/PN.Lmj dated June 23, 1988) convicted the Defendant to 5 months' imprisonment. The Surabaya High Court (Decision No. 270/Pid/1988/PT.Sby dated December 6, 1988) annulled the district court decision and released the Defendant from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag*) on the grounds that the matter constituted a civil loan dispute secured by checks. The Public Prosecutor at the Lumajang State Prosecutor's Office filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Construction of the Element "Fraudulent Trickery" (*Oplichtingsmiddel*) in Bad Check Fraud (Article 378 KUHP) ===


The primary issue was whether handing over post-dated checks or gyro checks by a debtor who consciously knows from inception that bank account balances are insufficient to induce a victim witness to hand over cash constitutes Criminal Fraud under Article 378 KUHP or merely a civil loan default dispute.


The Supreme Court held that it constitutes Criminal Fraud. Pursuant to criminal law doctrine (Arrest Hoge Raad of November 1, 1920) and Supreme Court Standing Jurisprudence (Supreme Court Decision No. 133 K/Kr/1973 of November 15, 1975), delivering checks known by the issuer from the outset to be unfunded or uncashable is qualified as fraudulent trickery (*oplichtingsmiddel*). A series of false statements and the delivery of fictitious payment instruments to induce a victim to surrender cash satisfies all elements of Article 378 KUHP, preventing qualification as a pure civil dispute.


=== Admissibility of Prosecutor's Cassation Against Release Rulings (*Ontslag van Alle Rechtsvervolging*) ===


The issue evaluated whether the Supreme Court on cassation is authorized to annul High Court judgments releasing a Defendant from all legal prosecutions on civil dispute grounds.


The Supreme Court held that it is Authorized. When a High Court mistakenly classifies criminal trickery facts as a pure civil relationship and issues a release ruling (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*), the Supreme Court must annul such decisions because the High Court misapplied the law (*foutieve kepassing van het recht*).


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the *Judex Facti* (Surabaya High Court) misapply the law (*foutieve kepassing van het recht*) by qualifying the Defendant's act of handing over 3 bad checks known from inception to be unfunded as a "pure civil loan dispute with collateral" and releasing the Defendant from all legal prosecutions?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the Surabaya High Court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court annulled Surabaya High Court Decision No. 270/Pid/1988/PT.Sby and adjudicated afresh, declaring Defendant [Defendant] proven legally and convincingly guilty of committing the crime of "Fraud" ex Article 378 KUHP and sentencing her to 5 months' imprisonment.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Lumajang District Court & Surabaya High Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning the exchange of 3 checks (No. CK. 0480426, CK. 0480427, CJ. 348957) totaling a nominal value of Rp 8,000,000.— by the Defendant to [Witness] in July 1987; granting a 10% commission/discount (Rp 800,000.—) resulting in net cash received of Rp 7,200,000.—; check rejection statements by BRI Lumajang Branch on August 15, 1987, due to insufficient balances; and utilization of funds by the Defendant to settle prior debts owed to third parties.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The appellate *Judex Facti* of Surabaya High Court misapplied the law by releasing the Defendant.
# Because the Defendant consciously knew from the outset that the checks given to the victim witness lacked funds (*bad checks*), the charge of fraud must be considered proven.
# Pursuant to Arrest Hoge Raad November 1, 1920, jo. Supreme Court Decision No. 133 K/Kr/1973, delivering checks known to be uncashable qualifies as trickery (*oplichtingsmiddel*) under Article 378 KUHP.
# The Supreme Court annulled the Surabaya High Court decision and adjudicated afresh, convicting the Defendant of Fraud (Article 378 KUHP) and sentencing her to 5 months' imprisonment.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court ruled: Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation ('''Public Prosecutor at the Lumajang State Prosecutor's Office'''); Annulling Surabaya High Court Decision No. 270/Pid/1988/PT.Sby dated December 6, 1988; and ADJUDICATING AFRESH: 1. Declaring Defendant [Defendant] proven legally and convincingly guilty of committing the crime of "Fraud"; 2. Sentencing the Defendant to a prison term of 5 (five) months; 3. Deducting the full period of detention served; 4. Ordering the return of 3 check evidence items to witness [Witness]; and charging cassation court costs amounting to Rp 2,500.— to the Defendant.


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Criminal Code (KUHP):''' Article 378: Crime of Fraud / *Oplichting* (Elements: Whoever, with intent to unlawfully benefit themselves or others, utilizing false names, false circumstances, trickery, or a series of false statements, induces someone to deliver goods or incur debts).
* '''Standing Jurisprudence & Criminal Doctrine:'''
  * Arrest Hoge Raad (HR) November 1, 1920 (NJ 1920 / W. 10650): Delivering checks known to be unfunded constitutes trickery (*oplichtingsmiddel*).
  * Supreme Court Decision No. 133 K/Kr/1973 (November 15, 1975): Issuing bad checks as persuasive instruments in fraud offenses.
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 jo. Law No. 8 of 1981 (KUHAP) jo. Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Authority to rectify legal misapplication errors regarding release (*ontslag*) rulings by *Judex Facti*.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* Defendant [Defendant] visited witness [Witness]'s home and handed over 3 BRI Lumajang Branch checks valued at Rp 8,000,000.—, requesting cash exchange with a 10% discount (net received Rp 7,200,000.—).
* The Defendant knew from the outset that the checks were unsupported by funds in her BRI Lumajang account (*bad checks*).
* All three checks were officially rejected by BRI Lumajang Branch on August 15, 1987, due to insufficient balances.
* Defendant's acts legally satisfied all elements of the crime of "Fraud" under Article 378 KUHP.
* The Defendant was sentenced to 5 months' imprisonment.


=== Not Established / Set Aside ===


* Surabaya High Court's considerations declaring the Defendant's acts to be a pure civil loan-guarantee dispute were annulled entirely by the Supreme Court.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Strict Distinction Between Civil Default and Bad Check Fraud: This landmark ruling establishes clear boundaries for banking and payment traffic in Indonesia: debtors cannot hide behind "civil dispute/loan" defenses when payments or collateral handed over consist of checks/giros known from inception to be unfunded.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Does issuing a bad check to pay debts or exchange cash constitute criminal fraud or merely a civil dispute?'''


'''A:''' It constitutes Criminal Fraud (Article 378 KUHP). Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 1036 K/Pid/1989 (in conjunction with HR November 1, 1920, & Supreme Court Decision No. 133 K/Kr/1973), when an individual consciously knows from the outset that a check delivered lacks funds (*bad check*), such action qualifies as fraudulent trickery (*oplichtingsmiddel*) under Article 378 KUHP, rendering the perpetrator criminally liable to imprisonment.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 1047 K/Pid/1992, dated November 29, 1994, established a fundamental material criminal and criminal procedural law rule concerning the crime of instigating the insertion of false statements into an authentic deed (Article 266 paragraph 1 KUHP) within inheritance distributions and the judicial evaluation of a Notary's retraction of trial testimonies:


The action of the Defendant ('''[Defendant]''') in compelling/instigating a Notary ([Notary]) to insert false statements deviating from a valid Testamentary Will into Partition and Distribution of Estate Deed No. 138 dated January 20, 1983—pretending that the Defendant was entitled to a 50% share of land and buildings comprising the Sophia Hotel, which the Will assigned exclusively to victim witness [Heir]—constitutes the crime of "Instigating the insertion of false statements into an authentic deed" ex Article 266 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code. A Notary witness retracting police interrogation statements at trial under the pretext of investigator pressure was dismissed by the Supreme Court as lacking common sense for a senior intellectual Notary, with proven actual losses resulting to the victim witness from disrupted Land Rights certificates issued by the Agrarian Office.


The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Public Prosecutor at the Surabaya State Prosecutor's Office, annulled the acquittal (*vrijspraak*) of Surabaya District Court Decision No. 1594/PID/S/1991/PN.Surabaya, and adjudicated afresh by sentencing the Defendant to 10 (ten) months' imprisonment with a 1 (one) year probation period.


== Executive Summary ==


The central legal principle established in this decision is that forcing notaries to falsify partition deeds contrary to clear testamentary wills is criminal fraud, and courts will reject unconvincing retractions of notarial police statements.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Coercing notaries to record terms diverging from authentic wills in estate partition deeds satisfies Article 266 KUHP.
* Retractions of police statements by senior notaries at trial without logical basis are rejected as incredible.
* Acquittals resting on flawed evidentiary evaluations are impure acquittals reviewable and reversible on cassation.


== Case Background ==


The Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation ('''[Defendant]''', [age removed], entrepreneur) was charged with instigating the insertion of false statements into an authentic deed (Article 266 paragraph 1 KUHP) for forcing Notary [Notary] to include a 50%-50% partition clause regarding land and buildings of Hotel Sophia at [address removed], Surabaya, within Estate Partition Deed No. 138 dated January 20, 1983. Pursuant to the Testamentary Will of the late R. [Testator] and RA. [Testator], Hotel Sophia was explicitly bequeathed to the Defendant's younger sibling (victim witness [Heir]). The Defendant refused to sign the partition deed unless given a 50% share. 


The Surabaya District Court (Decision No. 1594/PID/S/1991/PN.Surabaya dated September 26, 1991) acquitted the Defendant (*vrijspraak*) after accepting the Notary's retraction of police interrogation statements at trial. The Public Prosecutor at the Surabaya State Prosecutor's Office filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Judicial Evaluation of Notary Police Examination Minute (BAP) Retractions at Trial (Article 185 KUHAP) ===


The primary issue was whether Trial Judges are justified in accepting a Notary witness's retraction of police interrogation statements at trial on the grounds of receiving directions from investigators prior to examination.


The Supreme Court held that it is Unjustified. A Notary is a public official and senior intellectual figure who, logically, cannot be easily influenced or pressured by investigators. When a Notary's BAP retraction at trial contradicts common sense and lacks valid legal reasoning, while the initial BAP harmonizes with authentic documentary evidence (the testamentary will), the initial police interrogation minutes retain binding and valid evidentiary force.


=== Elements of "Instigating the Insertion of False Statements into an Authentic Deed" (Article 266 paragraph 1 KUHP) in Estate Partitions ===


An heir's action in threatening not to sign an estate partition deed to compel a Notary to alter the provisions of their late parents' Testamentary Will—such that the Notarial Deed contains a 50% partition clause inconsistent with the Will—perfectly satisfies all elements of the crime under Article 266 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the *Judex Facti* (Surabaya District Court) misapply the law (*foutieve kepassing van het recht*) by accepting the Notary's BAP retraction without a logical basis and acquitting the Defendant of Primary charges under Article 266 paragraph (1) KUHP, despite the act of instigating the Notary to alter the will causing losses to lawful Property Owners?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the Surabaya District Court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court granted the Public Prosecutor's cassation petition, annulled Surabaya District Court Decision No. 1594/PID/S/1991/PN.Surabaya, and adjudicated afresh, declaring Defendant [Defendant] proven legally and convincingly guilty of committing the crime of "Instigating the insertion of false statements into an authentic deed" ex Article 266 paragraph (1) KUHP and sentencing him to 10 (ten) months' imprisonment with a 1-year probation period.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Surabaya District Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning the opening of the safe deposit box of late R. [Testator] (died June 2, 1977) and RA. [Testator] (died June 2, 1980) at [address removed], Surabaya, 100 days post-demise; discovery of 2 Testamentary Wills (dated Sept 9, 1976, and 10 days prior to demise) assigning Hotel Sophia at [address removed], Surabaya, to [Heir]; drafting of Deed No. 138 dated January 20, 1983, by Notary [Notary]; Defendant's coercion demanding a 50% share; issuance of Land Ownership Certificates in the name of [Heir] by the Surabaya Agrarian Office; and forced auction proceedings over Hotel Sophia.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The *Judex Facti* of Surabaya District Court misapplied the law by acquitting the Defendant based on an illogical Notary BAP retraction. A senior intellectual Notary is not easily coerced by investigators.
# The Defendant coerced Notary [Notary] into inserting a 50%-50% partition clause in Deed No. 138 dated January 20, 1983, deviating from the valid Will.
# This acquittal constituted an impure acquittal reviewable and reversible via cassation ex Article 244 KUHAP.
# The Supreme Court annulled the Surabaya District Court decision and adjudicated afresh, sentencing Defendant [Defendant] to 10 months' imprisonment with a 1-year probation period.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court ruled: Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation ('''Public Prosecutor at the Surabaya State Prosecutor's Office'''); Annulling Surabaya District Court Decision dated September 26, 1991, No. 1594/PID/S/1991/PN.Surabaya; and ADJUDICATING AFRESH: 1. Declaring Defendant [Defendant] proven legally and convincingly guilty of committing the crime of "Instigating the insertion of false statements into an authentic deed regarding a matter whose truth must be established by such deed, with intent to use the deed as if its statements accord with the truth, causing losses"; 2. Sentencing the Defendant to a prison term of 10 (ten) months; 3. Stipulating that the sentence need not be served unless within a probation period of 1 (one) year the convict commits a criminal offense; 4. Ordering the return of evidence items to the heirs of witness [Heir]; and charging cassation court costs amounting to Rp 2,500.— to the Defendant.


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Criminal Code (KUHP):'''
  * Article 266 paragraph (1): Crime of instigating the insertion of false statements into an authentic deed.
  * Articles 264 paragraph (1) 1st & 55 paragraph (1) 1st: Subsidiary charges.
* '''Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP / Law No. 8 of 1981):'''
  * Article 185: Witness testimony and judicial evaluation of BAP retractions at trial.
  * Article 244: Cassation petitions over impure acquittals (*vrijspraak*).
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 in conjunction with Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Authority to annul acquittals misapplying the law.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* Testamentary Wills of late R. [Testator] and RA. [Testator] explicitly assigned Hotel Sophia at [address removed], Surabaya, to youngest child [Heir].
* Defendant [Defendant] forced Notary [Notary] to include a 50%-50% partition clause in Deed No. 138 dated January 20, 1983, deviating from the Will.
* The fake Notarial Deed was utilized by the Defendant to seize half the building, causing actual losses through contested auction proceedings over lawful ownership rights belonging to [Heir].
* The Defendant was sentenced to 10 months' imprisonment with a 1-year probation period.


=== Not Established / Reversal of Acquittal ===


* Defendant's defense and the Notary's BAP retraction claiming will alterations occurred upon family initiative or Notary discretion were set aside and annulled entirely by the Supreme Court.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Integrity of Notarial Authentic Deeds Against Inheritance Usurpation: This landmark ruling establishes strict guidelines for notarial practice and inheritance law: Notaries are prohibited from submitting to intimidation or threats by appearance-makers to alter valid Testamentary Wills, confirming prison sentences for individuals usurping inheritance via notarial deed manipulation.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Can forcing a Notary to alter the terms of a Testamentary Will within an Estate Partition Deed be prosecuted under Article 266 KUHP?'''


'''A:''' Yes, it is Prosecutable (Article 266 paragraph 1 KUHP). Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 1047 K/Pid/1992, the act of instigating or forcing a Notary to insert statements deviating from a valid Testamentary Will into an Estate Partition Deed qualifies as the crime of instigating the insertion of false statements into an authentic deed under Article 266 paragraph (1) KUHP. Notary BAP retractions at trial without logical legal grounds are dismissed by the Supreme Court.
