== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 1068 K/Pdt/2008, dated January 21, 2009, established three fundamental civil execution and legal protection rules for bona fide auction purchasers:


First, Legal Protection of Bona Fide Auction Purchasers (*Te Goeder Trouw*): Auction purchasers acquiring disputed objects based on Auction Minutes (*Berita Acara Lelang*) and Official Auction Reports (*Risalah Lelang*) issued pursuant to court judgments possessing final and binding legal force (*inkracht van gewijsde*) are bona fide auction purchasers and therefore MUST BE PROTECTED BY LAW.


Second, Immunity of Valid Execution Auctions Against Annulment: The annulment of an auction conducted pursuant to a judgment possessing final and binding legal force CANNOT BE ANNULLED.


Third, Damages Claim Mechanism for Third Parties (Alternative to Auction Annulment): In the event a subsequent conflicting judgment is rendered holding that the *inkracht* judgment is non-binding, such conflicting judgment cannot serve as grounds to annul the auction. The legal remedy available to injured parties is to CLAIM DAMAGES regarding the disputed object FROM THE AUCTION PETITIONER rather than annulling the auction.


The Supreme Court annulled Medan High Court Decision No. 211/Pdt/2006/PT.Mdn and adjudicated afresh by declaring the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).


== Executive Summary ==


The central legal principle established in this decision is that court-ordered execution auctions executed under binding judgments confer absolute legal protection on bona fide purchasers, precluding subsequent third-party annulments while restricting aggrieved parties to monetary damages claims against original execution petitioners.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Execution auction sales founded on binding judicial rulings (*inkracht*) are immune to subsequent judicial annulment.
* Winning bidders at execution auctions enjoy absolute legal status as bona fide purchasers (*te goeder trouw*).
* Subsequent conflicting judicial rulings cannot invalidate completed execution auctions; relief is strictly confined to damages claims against auction applicants.


== Case Background ==


The Original Plaintiff / Respondent for Cassation ('''[Party A]''') sued the Original Defendants / Petitioners for Cassation (heirs of the late Hassan Chandra) at the Medan District Court. The Plaintiff sought the annulment of the execution order and eviction execution dated February 3, 2005, over land and a house at [address removed], Medan. The Plaintiff based his claim on Medan High Court Decision No. 181/Perd/1983/PT.Mdn in conjunction with Supreme Court Decision No. 1245 K/Pdt/1984 dated May 31, 1990, which annulled a seizure in execution. The Defendants argued that Hassan Chandra was the lawful auction winner of the property pursuant to Execution Auction Report No. 330/Perd/PN.Mdn dated October 14, 1982, and Official Auction Minutes No. 46/1982–1983, executed pursuant to a binding judgment in Medan District Court Decision No. 330/Perd/1963/PN.Mdn in conjunction with Medan High Court Decision No. 343/Perd/1967/PT.Mdn in conjunction with Supreme Court Decision No. 1002 K/Sip/1971 dated July 23, 1973. 


The Medan District Court (Decision No. 45/Pdt.G/2005/PN.Mdn dated January 30, 2006) sustained the *Ne Bis In Idem* exception and declared the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible (NO). The Medan High Court (Decision No. 211/Pdt/2006/PT.Mdn dated December 14, 2006) annulled the district court decision and granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part. The Petitioners for Cassation subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Legal Protection of Bona Fide Auction Purchasers (*Te Goeder Trouw*) in Court Execution Sales (Articles 1338 & 1457 Civil Code jo. Vendu Reglement) ===


The primary issue was whether an execution auction purchaser acquiring land/housing based on official Auction Minutes and Official Auction Reports issued by the State Auction Office under District Court orders (founded on an *inkracht* judgment) can have ownership rights annulled by a third-party lawsuit.


The Supreme Court held that they Cannot Be Annulled. Auction purchasers acquiring disputed objects through official District Court execution auctions founded on judgments possessing final and binding legal force (*inkracht van gewijsde*) are categorized as bona fide auction purchasers (*te goeder trouw*). As winning bidders in official auctions, their ownership rights enjoy absolute legal protection (*rechtsbescherming van de koper te goeder trouw*), precluding the annulment of completed execution auctions.


=== Resolution of Conflicting Judgments Regarding Valid Execution Auctions ===


The issue evaluated legal consequences when a subsequent conflicting court judgment (Supreme Court Decision No. 1245 K/Pdt/1984) rules in favor of a third party ([Party A]) conflicting with the underlying auction execution judgment (Supreme Court Decision No. 1002 K/Sip/1971).


The Supreme Court held that subsequent judgments declaring underlying auction judgments non-binding cannot be utilized as legal grounds to annul execution auctions already completed. Execution auctions remain valid and binding. The legal remedy or sanction available to third parties injured by such auctions is to claim civil damages (*pembayaran ganti rugi*) from the Auction Petitioner (Creditor/Winning Party of Underlying Proceedings) rather than annulling the auction or dispossessing bona fide auction purchasers.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the *Judex Facti* (Medan High Court) misapply the law (*foutieve kepassing van het recht*) by annulling an execution auction founded upon an *inkracht* judgment No. 1002 K/Sip/1971, stripping bona fide auction purchasers (heirs of Hassan Chandra) of their rights, and ignoring *Ne Bis In Idem* exceptions / lawsuit inadmissibility properly applied by the Medan District Court?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the Medan High Court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court annulled Medan High Court Decision No. 211/Pdt/2006/PT.Mdn and adjudicated afresh, affirming Medan District Court considerations in Decision No. 45/Pdt.G/2005/PN.Mdn by declaring the Plaintiff's ([Party A]) lawsuit inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Medan District Court & High Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning initial ownership of the house/land at [address removed], Medan; issuance of Execution Auction Report No. 330/Perd/PN.Mdn and Official Auction Minutes No. 46/1982–1983 dated October 14, 1982, in the name of Hassan Chandra; execution of eviction by Medan District Court on February 3, 2005, pursuant to Chairman of Medan District Court Penetapan No. 17/Eks/2003/KP3N-46/1982/PN-Mdn; conflict between Supreme Court Decision No. 1002 K/Sip/1971 (auction basis) and Supreme Court Decision No. 1245 K/Pdt/1984 ([Party A]'s claim basis); and Defendants' *Ne Bis In Idem* exception.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The appellate *Judex Facti* of Medan High Court misapplied the law. Annulment of an auction conducted pursuant to a judgment possessing final and binding legal force is impermissible.
# The Petitioner for Cassation (Defendant) as an execution auction purchaser based on Auction Minutes and Official Auction Reports founded on an *inkracht* judgment is a bona fide auction purchaser (*te goeder trouw*) and must be protected by law.
# If subsequent conflicting judgments arise, they cannot serve as grounds to annul auctions; aggrieved parties are restricted to claiming damages over disputed objects from the Auction Petitioner.
# The Supreme Court annulled the Medan High Court decision and adjudicated afresh, declaring the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court ruled: Annulling Medan High Court Decision No. 211/Pdt/2006/PT.Mdn dated December 14, 2006, which had annulled Medan District Court Decision No. 45/Pdt.G/2005/PN.Mdn dated January 30, 2006; and ADJUDICATING AFRESH: Declaring the Plaintiff's ('''[Party A]''') lawsuit inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard*); and ordering the Respondent for Cassation / Plaintiff to pay court costs across all judicial instances.


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Civil Procedure Code (HIR / RBg):''' Provisions governing auction execution (Article 200 HIR / Article 215 RBg) and the *Ne Bis In Idem* principle.
* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata):''' Article 1338 (Binding Force of Agreements/Auctions) & Article 1457 in conjunction with *Vendu Reglement* (Auction Regulation Stb. 1908 No. 189).
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 in conjunction with Law No. 14 of 1985 in conjunction with Law No. 5 of 2004 on the Supreme Court:''' Authority to review legal application errors by *Judex Facti*.
* '''Supreme Court Standing Jurisprudence:''' Supreme Court Decisions No. 3215 K/Pdt/1992 & No. 1812 K/Pdt/1989: Doctrine of Legal Protection for Bona Fide Auction Purchasers (*Te Goeder Trouw*).


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* Hassan Chandra (late / predecessor of Petitioners for Cassation) was a bona fide auction purchaser of land and housing at [address removed], Medan, pursuant to Auction Report No. 330/Perd/PN.Mdn and Official Auction Minutes No. 46/1982–1983 dated October 14, 1982.
* The execution auction was conducted lawfully pursuant to court judgments possessing final and binding legal force (*inkracht van gewijsde*).
* Execution auctions completed under binding judgments cannot be annulled.
* Plaintiff [Party A]'s lawsuit seeking auction annulment and eviction cancellation was declared inadmissible (NO).


=== Not Established / Annulment Prohibited ===


* Supreme Court Decision No. 1245 K/Pdt/1984 held by the Plaintiff could not serve as legal grounds to annul the execution auction, serving solely as a basis for third-party damages claims against the Auction Petitioner.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Legal Certainty of Court Execution Auctions: This landmark ruling firmly closes legal loopholes frequently exploited to destabilize official court execution purchasers. The Supreme Court outlines absolute protection: bona fide auction purchasers cannot be sacrificed due to subsequent dynamics of conflicting judgments. Third-party losses must be channeled into civil damages claims against Auction Petitioners (pure financial reparation disputes).


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Can a District Court execution auction completed pursuant to an *inkracht* judgment be annulled if a subsequent conflicting judgment arises?'''


'''A:''' Cannot Be Annulled. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 1068 K/Pdt/2008, the annulment of an auction conducted pursuant to a judgment possessing final and binding legal force CANNOT BE ANNULLED. Execution auction purchasers are bona fide purchasers (*te goeder trouw*) protected by law. If a subsequent conflicting judgment arises, it cannot be used to annul the auction; aggrieved parties are restricted to CLAIMING DAMAGES from the Auction Petitioner.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 1076 K/Pdt/1996, dated March 9, 2000, established fundamental civil law rules concerning the judge's authority to correct and reduce personal loan interest rates and the validity of conservatory attachments (*conservatoir beslag*) in individual default cases.


Although freely agreed upon and stipulated by both parties in the Statement of Debt (*Surat Pengakuan Hutang*) that the borrower must pay an interest rate of 2.5% per month (30% per year), in the interest of fairness and equity, such interest rate must be adjusted (subject to judicial correction) to the prevailing interest rate at Government Banks, amounting to 18% per year calculated from the date the lawsuit was registered until full repayment. Furthermore, a Conservatory Attachment (*Conservatoir Beslag*) placed on the Defendant's assets to secure the recovery of a personal debt is valid and lawful under the law to prevent the Plaintiff's lawsuit from becoming illusory (*illusoir*).


The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation ([Party B]), annulled Surabaya High Court Decision No. 97/Pdt/1995/PT.Sby, and adjudicated afresh, sentencing the Defendant ([Party A]) to pay a principal debt of Rp 350,000,000.— plus 18% annual interest and declaring the conservatory attachment valid and valuable.


== Executive Summary ==


The central legal principle established in this decision is that freedom of contract regarding interest rates is subject to judicial correction based on fairness, capping excessive private loan rates at government bank standards, while affirming the full legality of conservatory attachments in private default disputes.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Excessive agreed private loan interest rates (e.g., 30% p.a.) can be judicially corrected and reduced to match prevailing government bank rates (18% p.a.).
* Conservatory attachments over debtor assets in private loan defaults are lawful and necessary to protect creditors from illusory judgments.
* Appellate court rulings improperly lifting attachments and stripping contractual interest entitlements are subject to reversal on cassation.


== Case Background ==


The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Party B]''', a resident of [address removed]) filed a lawsuit at the Malang District Court against the Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation ('''[Party A]''', a resident of [address removed]) concerning default on a money loan of Rp 350,000,000.— pursuant to a Statement of Debt dated August 10, 1988, bearing interest at 2.5% per month. Upon maturity on May 10, 1990, the Defendant issued 3 Bilyet Giro checks which were rejected by the bank due to insufficient funds. 


The Malang District Court (Decision No. 241/Pdt.G/1993/PN.Malang dated March 30, 1994) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit, ordering the Defendant to pay the principal debt plus 2.5% monthly interest and validating the conservatory attachment. The Surabaya High Court (Decision No. 97/Pdt/1995/PT.Sby dated July 18, 1995) annulled the attachment and removed the interest award on the grounds that the Plaintiff was not a licensed financial institution. The Petitioner for Cassation subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Limits of Freedom of Contract (Article 1338 Civil Code) and Judicial Correction Authority Over Exorbitant/Fictitious Interest Rates ===


The primary issue was whether an agreed personal loan interest rate of 2.5% per month (30% per year) is binding absolutely, or whether a Judge holds authority to reduce such interest rate based on equity and fairness.


The Supreme Court held that the Judge holds authority to correct it. Although the 2.5% monthly interest agreement was freely consented to in the Statement of Debt pursuant to Article 1338 of the Civil Code, the Supreme Court on cassation holds the authority to effect equitable corrections (*mewujudkan kelayakan & kepatutan hukum*). Personal loan interest rates must be adjusted to prevailing macroeconomic interest rates at Government Banks, amounting to 18% (eighteen percent) per year calculated from the date the lawsuit was registered at the District Court until full loan repayment.


=== Admissibility of Conservatory Attachment (*Conservatoir Beslag* ex Article 227 HIR / 261 RBg) in Personal Loan Default Disputes ===


The issue evaluated the validity of Conservatory Attachment (*Conservatoir Beslag*) orders over individual debtor assets in money-lending default proceedings executed outside official banking/financial institutions.


The Supreme Court held that they are Valid and Valuable. High Court considerations canceling/lifting conservatory attachments on grounds that the Plaintiff was not a licensed financial institution were qualified as a misapplication of law (*foutieve kepassing van het recht*). Conservatory attachments over movable and immovable property belonging to debtors are lawful under the law to secure execution of judgment enforcement so that creditor claims can be satisfied and lawsuits do not become illusory (*illusoir*).


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the *Judex Facti* of Surabaya High Court (Decision No. 97/Pdt/1995/PT.Sby) misapply the law (*foutieve kepassing van het recht*) by lifting conservatory attachments and deleting interest compensation on grounds that the Plaintiff was not an official financial institution, and what is the proper determination standard for interest rates?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the Surabaya High Court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court annulled Surabaya High Court Decision No. 97/Pdt/1995/PT.Sby and adjudicated afresh, affirming Malang District Court Decision No. 241/Pdt.G/1993/PN.Malang with rectifications: ordering the Defendant to pay 18% annual interest (matching Government Bank rates) and declaring the Conservatory Attachment (*Conservatoir Beslag*) over 3 vehicles and 10 land plots (*petok*) in Batu City valid and valuable.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Malang District Court & Surabaya High Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning the execution of the Statement of Debt dated August 10, 1988, valued at Rp 350,000,000.— between [Party B] and [Party A]; delivery of 3 Bilyet Giros (BG 055760 Rp 100 Million, BG 055762 Rp 200 Million, BG 055763 Rp 50 Million) maturing on May 10, 1990, which proved to be unfunded; and execution of the Attachment Minutes dated February 18, 1994, No. 241/Pdt.G/1993/PN.Malang in conjunction with No. 9/CB/1994/PN.Malang.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The appellate *Judex Facti* of Surabaya High Court misapplied the law by lifting conservatory attachments and eliminating Plaintiff's interest compensation.
# Conservatory attachments over Defendant's assets are lawful (Article 227 HIR) to ensure lawsuits do not become illusory (*illusoir*).
# Regarding interest quantum, although 2.5% per month (30% p.a.) was agreed, in the interest of fairness and equity, interest rates must be adjusted to prevailing Government Bank interest rates of 18% per year calculated from lawsuit registration.
# The Supreme Court annulled the Surabaya High Court decision and adjudicated afresh, affirming the Malang District Court ruling with rectified interest and validated conservatory attachments.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court ruled: Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Party B]'''); Annulling Surabaya High Court Decision No. 97/Pdt/1995/PT.Sby dated July 18, 1995, which had rectified Malang District Court Decision No. 241/Pdt.G/1993/PN.Malang dated March 30, 1994; and ADJUDICATING AFRESH: UNDER EXCEPTIONS: Rejecting the Defendant's exception; UNDER THE MERITS: 1. Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part; 2. Declaring that the Defendant is indebted to the Plaintiff in the amount of Rp 350,000,000.— (three hundred fifty million rupiahs); 3. Declaring that the Defendant has committed default towards the Plaintiff; 4. Ordering the Defendant to pay the debt to the Plaintiff amounting to Rp 350,000,000.— in cash and simultaneously; 5. Ordering the Defendant to pay interest to the Plaintiff amounting to 18% (eighteen percent) per year from the total debt calculated from the date the lawsuit was registered at Malang District Court until the Defendant settles the debt; 6. Declaring valid and valuable the conservatory attachment (*conservatoir beslag*) No. 241/Pdt.G/1993/PN.Malang jo. No. 9/CB/1994/PN.Malang dated February 18, 1994, over 3 vehicles and 10 land parcels (*petok*); 7. Rejecting all other claims of the Plaintiff; and ordering the Respondent for Cassation to pay court costs across all judicial instances (cassation court costs set at Rp 50,000.—).


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata):'''
  * Articles 1243 & 1244 (Default & Damages).
  * Article 1338 (Binding Force of Contracts).
  * Articles 1765 & 1767 (Loan Interest).
* '''Civil Procedure Code (HIR / RBg):''' Article 227 HIR / Article 261 RBg (Conservatory Attachment / *Conservatoir Beslag*).
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 in conjunction with Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Authority to rectify legal application errors by *Judex Facti*.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* Defendant [Party A] was proven legally and convincingly to have defaulted on a principal loan of Rp 350,000,000.— pursuant to the Statement of Debt dated August 10, 1988 (Exhibit P.1).
* Three Bilyet Giro checks delivered by the Defendant were proven unfunded.
* Defendant was ordered to pay the principal debt of Rp 350,000,000.— in cash simultaneously.
* Defendant was ordered to pay adjusted interest of 18% per year on the principal debt calculated from lawsuit registration at Malang District Court until full repayment.
* Conservatory attachments over 3 motor vehicles and 10 land parcels (*petok*) in Punten and Songgokerto Villages, Batu City, were declared valid and valuable.


=== Not Established / Adjusted ===


* Plaintiff's claims for 2.5% monthly interest (30% p.a.) and late penalties of Rp 50,000.— per day were rejected / reduced by the Supreme Court in the interest of equity and fairness.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Standard for Adjusting Personal Loan Interest Rates: This landmark ruling establishes crucial jurisprudence in Indonesian contract law: freedom of contract in setting personal interest rates is not absolute. Courts possess authority to trim excessive/burdensome private commercial interest rates and adjust them to official Government Bank interest rate benchmarks (18% p.a.).


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: What is the maximum threshold for personal loan interest rates recognized and granted by the Supreme Court in default lawsuits?'''


'''A:''' Adjusted to Government Bank Interest Rates (18% per year). Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 1076 K/Pdt/1996, although both parties agreed to a personal loan interest rate of 2.5% per month (30% per year), the Judge possesses authority to correct and adjust it to the official interest rate prevailing at Government Banks, amounting to 18% per year calculated from the date the lawsuit was registered at the District Court.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 1104 K/Pid/1990, dated February 27, 1993, established a fundamental material criminal law rule concerning the absence of negligence (*culpa*) in traffic offenses under Article 359 of the Criminal Code when a motor vehicle driver is operating lawfully on the correct lane:


A motor vehicle driver operating a vehicle orderly on the correct lane (left side/own lane) cannot be convicted on the grounds of negligence (*culpa* ex Article 359 KUHP) when an accident occurs resulting in a fatality because the victim (a bicycle rider) first grazed/struck another bicycle rider ahead, fell, and ricocheted to the right directly underneath/into the path of the Defendant's bus. Because the Defendant's actions did not satisfy the element of negligence (*culpa*), the Defendant must be acquitted of all charges (*vrijspraak*) and his honor and dignity restored.


== Executive Summary ==


The central legal principle established in this decision is that cautious drivers operating in their proper lanes are not criminally liable for traffic fatalities caused by third-party collisions that throw victims unexpectedly into their path.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Drivers operating lawfully in their correct lanes without violating traffic rules lack the necessary negligence (*culpa*) required for criminal liability under Article 359 KUHP.
* Intervening collisions caused by third parties that propel victims into ongoing traffic constitute unavoidable accidents beyond driver control.
* Lower court convictions of compliant drivers are subject to outright reversal on cassation, resulting in pure acquittals (*vrijspraak*).


== Case Background ==


The Original Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation, '''[Defendant]''' ([age removed], bus driver), was charged with negligence resulting in death (Article 359 KUHP) because on February 13, 1987, in Desa Kejawar, Banyumas, the bus he drove ran over a bicycle rider (victim [Victim]), causing his death. Trial evidence proved the Defendant was driving slowly (20–30 km/h) on his correct lane (left side). The victim fell and ricocheted into the bus's path because his bicycle first grazed/struck another bicycle rider ahead while attempting to overtake a truck. 


The Banyumas District Court (Decision No. 35/Pts.Pid.B/1987/PN.Bms dated March 23, 1988) convicted the Defendant to 6 months' imprisonment. The Semarang High Court (Decision No. 443/Pid/1989/PT.Smg dated September 14, 1989) enhanced the sentence to 8 months' imprisonment. The Defendant subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Construction of the Element of Negligence (*Culpa* ex Article 359 KUHP) in Traffic Accident Cases ===


The primary issue was whether a bus driver operating lawfully on their proper lane can be blamed or convicted of negligence (*culpa*) when a bicycle rider falls and ricochets under the bus wheels after colliding with another bicycle rider ahead.


The Supreme Court held that they Cannot Be Convicted (*Element of Culpa Unproven*). Negligence (*culpa*) requires a manifestation of carelessness or lack of vigilance whose harmful consequences could objectively be foreseen by the driver (*voorzienbaarheid*). When a driver travels slowly on their correct lane (left side) and an accident arises solely due to consecutive collisions among fellow bicycle riders causing the victim to suddenly ricochet into the bus path, the event constitutes a pure accident (*musibah* beyond the Defendant's control), leaving the element of negligence unproven. The Defendant must be granted a pure acquittal (*vrijspraak*).


=== Supreme Court Authority to Correct Judex Facti Errors in Evaluating Negligence (Judex Juris vs. Judex Facti) ===


The issue evaluated whether the Supreme Court on cassation is authorized to annul conviction rulings from District and High Courts that erroneously classify accidental factual events as legal negligence.


The Supreme Court held that it is Authorized. Assessing whether a sequence of facts satisfies the juridical construction of the element "due to his fault/negligence" (*culpa*) under Article 359 KUHP constitutes a question of law (*Question of Law*). When *Judex Facti* (Banyumas District Court and Semarang High Court) impose criminal penalties despite trial facts showing the driver operated on their lawful lane, *Judex Facti* are declared to have misapplied the law (*foutieve kepassing van het recht*).


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the *Judex Facti* (Semarang High Court & Banyumas District Court) misapply the law (*foutieve kepassing van het recht*) by considering the Defendant negligent under Article 359 KUHP, despite trial facts proving the Defendant traveled on his correct lawful lane and the victim ricocheted into the bus path due to colliding with another bicycle ahead?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the *Judex Facti* misapplied the law. The Supreme Court granted Petitioner for Cassation [Defendant]'s cassation petition, annulled Semarang High Court Decision No. 443/Pid/1989/PT.Smg in conjunction with Banyumas District Court Decision No. 35/Pts.Pid.B/1987/PN.Bms, and adjudicated afresh, declaring Defendant [Defendant] unproven legally and convincingly guilty of committing the crime violating Article 359 KUHP (Pure Acquittal / *Vrijspraak*).


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Banyumas District Court & Semarang High Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning the accident on Friday, February 13, 1987, around 06:30 WIB on the public road in Desa Kejawar, Banyumas; facts regarding Santoso Bus AA 2587 A traveling from Purwokerto to Semarang on an upgrade/downgrade road at 20–30 km/h; presence of 3 bicycle riders behind a truck; facts where the first bicycle overtook the truck, the second bicycle overtook, grazed the truck side and fell, and the third bicycle (victim [Victim]) collided with the second bicycle, ricocheting to the right of the road directly beneath the Defendant's bus; Visum et Repertum No. 331/250/6/III/1987 by Dr. Budi Santoso; and the Defendant's humanitarian assistance to the victim's family.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The appellate and district *Judex Facti* misapplied the law. The bus driven by the Defendant was on the correct lane (left side), whereas the victim fell because he was grazed by the bicycle ahead, causing him to fall to the right and be crushed by the Defendant's bus wheels.
# Because the Defendant traveled on his lawful lane and the accident arose from another bicycle collision, no element of negligence/culpa was proven against the Defendant under Article 359 KUHP.
# The Supreme Court granted the Defendant's cassation, annulled lower court rulings, and adjudicated afresh, declaring Defendant [Defendant] unproven guilty of violating Article 359 KUHP (Pure Acquittal / *Vrijspraak*) and restoring his rights, position, honor, and dignity.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court ruled: Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Defendant]'''); Annulling Semarang High Court Decision No. 443/Pid/1989/PT.Smg dated September 14, 1989, in conjunction with Banyumas District Court Decision No. 35/Pts.Pid.B/1987/PN.Bms dated March 23, 1988; and ADJUDICATING AFRESH: 1. Declaring Defendant [Defendant] not proven legally and convincingly guilty of committing the crime charged in the indictment; 2. Acquitting the Defendant therefore from such indictment; 3. Restoring the Defendant's rights in capacity, position, honor, and dignity; 4. Charging State finances with court costs across all judicial instances.


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Criminal Code (KUHP):''' Article 359: Crime of Negligence Causing the Death of Another (*Culpa*).
* '''Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP / Law No. 8 of 1981):'''
  * Article 191 paragraph (1): Pure Acquittal (*Vrijspraak*) when a Defendant's guilt is unproven legally and convincingly.
  * Articles 253 & 255: Authority of the Supreme Court to review legal application errors committed by *Judex Facti* on cassation.
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 in conjunction with Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Authority to Adjudicate Afresh (*Mengadili Sendiri*) criminal cassation cases.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* Defendant [Defendant] operated Santoso Bus AA 2587 A on his correct lawful lane (left side) at a reasonable speed (20–30 km/h).
* Victim [Victim] fell and ricocheted into the bus driver's lane due to consecutive collisions/grazing among fellow bicycle riders while attempting to overtake a truck.
* The Defendant possessed no physical space or avoidable opportunity to prevent running over the victim who suddenly ricocheted into his lane.
* The Defendant was established as UNPROVEN guilty of violating Article 359 KUHP and was acquitted of all charges.


=== Not Established / Set Aside ===


* Considerations of Banyumas District Court and Semarang High Court declaring the Defendant negligent/lacking vigilance were annulled entirely by the Supreme Court for lacking valid legal constructions of negligence (*culpa*).


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Legal Protection of Law-Abiding Drivers Against Accident Criminalization: This landmark ruling establishes a vital traffic criminal law doctrine in Indonesia: vehicle drivers who act prudently and remain on their proper lawful lanes must not be made "scapegoats" or criminalized for victim fatalities arising from the fault or collisions of third parties ricocheting into their path.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Can a bus driver traveling on their own lane be convicted of negligence (Article 359 KUHP) if a bicycle rider ricochets into their path due to colliding with another bicycle?'''


'''A:''' Cannot Be Convicted (*Mandatory Pure Acquittal*). Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 1104 K/Pid/1990, a vehicle driver traveling slowly on the correct lane (left side) is unproven to have committed negligence (*culpa* ex Article 359 KUHP) when a fatal accident arises because the victim ricocheted into the bus path after first grazing another bicycle rider. The absence of negligence requires the Defendant to be acquitted of all charges (*vrijspraak*).

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 110 K/AG/2007 dated December 7, 2007, establishes fundamental jurisprudence and legal rules regarding child custody (*hadhanah*): The primary consideration in matters of *hadhanah* is the welfare and best interests of the child, rather than solely determining who is normatively most entitled. Even though a child has not reached the age of 7 (seven) years or *mumayyiz* (which normatively under Article 105 letter a of the KHI falls under the mother's custody), if the mother frequently travels abroad making it unclear who will care for the child, whereas the child has been proven to live peacefully and securely with the father, then for the welfare of the child, the right of *hadhanah* is awarded to the father.

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiff / Respondent for Cassation ([Mother]) and Original Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation ([Father]) married on October 23, 1999, in Bandung and were blessed with a daughter named [Child] (born [details removed]). Continuous disputes occurred during roughly the last two years of the marriage. The Plaintiff filed a divorce suit and a claim for child custody (*hadhanah*) at the South Jakarta Religious Court.

The South Jakarta Religious Court (Decision No. 50/Pdt.G/2006/PA.JS dated July 27, 2006) granted the divorce with a single *ba'in shughra* pronouncement and awarded child custody (*hadhanah*) to the Defendant ([Father]). The Jakarta High Religious Court (Decision No. 105/Pdt.G/2006/PTA.JK dated December 20, 2006) annulled the South Jakarta Religious Court decision and designated the Plaintiff ([Mother]) as the holder of child custody. Dissatisfied with the appellate ruling, the Defendant filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# Regarding child custody, the inquiry is not merely who holds the primary entitlement, but rather whose care minimizes detriment to the child; priority must be given to the child's interests above all else.
# Based on facts revealed by the First-Instance Judge, the child would suffer more if placed under the mother's care because the mother frequently travels abroad without a clear arrangement for the child's supervision, whereas the child currently lives calmly and securely with the father (Petitioner for Cassation / Defendant).
# Even though the child is placed under the father's custody, this must not sever communication with the mother (Respondent for Cassation / Plaintiff); the mother retains the right to visit, assist in upbringing, and bestow affection upon the child.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation [Father]; Annulling the Jakarta High Religious Court decision dated December 20, 2006, No. 105/Pdt.G/2006/PTA.JK, which had annulled the South Jakarta Religious Court decision dated July 27, 2006, No. 50/Pdt.G/2006/PA.JS; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) In Provision: Declaring the Plaintiff's provision request inadmissible; (2) In Convention: In Exception: Rejecting the Defendant's exceptions in their entirety; In the Principal Case: 1. Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part; 2. Pronouncing a single *ba'in shughra* divorce of Defendant ([Father]) against Plaintiff ([Mother]); 3. Declaring the Plaintiff's claim under item 4 concerning child maintenance costs inadmissible; 4. Rejecting the remainder of the Plaintiff's lawsuit; (3) In Reconvention: 1. Granting the Plaintiff-in-reconvention's lawsuit in part; 2. Determining that the child named [Child], born [details removed], is placed under the custody (*hadhanah*) of the Plaintiff-in-reconvention ([Father]); 3. Ordering the Plaintiff-in-reconvention to provide the Defendant-in-reconvention, as her biological mother, the opportunity to meet and be with the child during school holidays or mutually agreed days; 4. Rejecting the remainder of the Plaintiff-in-reconvention's lawsuit; (4) In Convention and Reconvention: Assessing court costs in accordance with judicial level provisions.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 111 K/AG/1998 dated September 13, 1999, establishes important jurisprudence and legal principles regarding the qualification of ownership disputes in Islamic inheritance law and the formal requirements of inheritance lawsuits:

* '''Estate Disputes Among Family Members:''' In inheritance matters (*waris mal waris*), disputes concerning estate properties among heirs who share family ties do not constitute pure property ownership disputes, and thus fall under the absolute competence of the Religious Courts.
* '''Formal Defects in Inheritance Lawsuits:''' If, in an inheritance lawsuit, the Plaintiff merely requests to be declared as an heir, whereas witness testimonies at trial reveal that there are other entitled heirs (as also acknowledged by the Plaintiff), the Plaintiff's lawsuit must be declared inadmissible (*niet ontvankelijke verklaard*).

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation ([Party B], represented by his attorney Jawite) filed a lawsuit against the Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation ([Party C]) and 9 Co-Defendants at the Praya Religious Court. The object of the dispute consisted of the estate left by his late father ([Party A], who passed away around 1947), comprising wet rice fields measuring approximately 1.000 Ha and garden land measuring 0.0768 Ha in Banyu Urip Village, West Praya, Central Lombok. The Plaintiff claimed that in 1996, the Defendant (child of Amaq Gande / sibling of [Party A]) unilaterally took over control of the land.

The Praya Religious Court (Decision No. 45/Pdt.G/1997/PA.PRA dated May 21, 1997) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit and determined the distribution of inheritance. However, the Mataram High Religious Court (Decision No. 72/Pdt.G/1997/PTA.MTR dated October 13, 1997) annulled the Praya Religious Court decision, declared the lawsuit inadmissible, and ruled that the Praya Religious Court lacked jurisdiction on the grounds that the case constituted a property ownership dispute. Dissatisfied with the Mataram High Religious Court ruling, the Plaintiff ([Party B]) filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The Mataram High Religious Court erred in applying the law because disputes concerning estate properties among persons sharing family relations do not constitute property ownership disputes, but rather pure inheritance disputes (*waris mal waris*) falling within the absolute competence of the Religious Courts.
# Although this dispute falls within the competence of the Religious Courts, the Plaintiff in this lawsuit merely requested a declaration of his status as an heir, whereas witness testimonies indicated that there were other entitled heirs (a fact also acknowledged by the Plaintiff). Because all entitled heirs were not joined or accounted for in the proceedings, the Plaintiff's lawsuit must be declared inadmissible (*niet ontvankelijke verklaard*).
# Consequently, the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation is rejected with a modification to the phrasing of the Mataram High Religious Court's ruling.
* '''Ruling:''' Rejecting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation [Party B] with a modification to the phrasing of the Mataram High Religious Court decision dated October 13, 1997, No. 72/Pdt.G/1997/PTA.MTR jo. the Praya Religious Court decision dated May 21, 1997, No. 45/Pdt.G/1997/PA.PRA; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Accepting the Appellant's appeal; (2) Annulling the Praya Religious Court decision No. 45/Pdt.G/1997/PA.PRA; (3) Declaring the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible (*niet ontvankelijke verklaard*); (4) Ordering the Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation to pay court costs across all levels of jurisdiction (assessed at Rp 216,000 at the first instance, Rp 48,000 at the appellate level, and Rp 50,000 at the cassation level). *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Cassation Panel of Justices: Drs. H. Taufiq, SH., MH. [Presiding], H. Chabib Syarbini, SH., and H. Zainal Abidin Abubakar, SH.)*.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 1130 K/PID/1985, deliberated on October 29, 1987 and pronounced in an open court session on December 18, 1987, established an important rule of criminal procedural and substantive law concerning the distinction between an acquittal (''vrijspraak'') and a release from all legal prosecution (''ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging'') in a receiving-stolen-goods case under Article 480 of the Indonesian Criminal Code (KUHP).

The Supreme Court held that where one of the objective or subjective elements of Article 480 KUHP, particularly the element that the defendant "knew or should have suspected" that the goods originated from a crime, cannot be proven at trial, the defendant must be acquitted from the charge (''vrijspraak'') under Article 191 paragraph (1) KUHAP.

An ''ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging'' under Article 191 paragraph (2) KUHAP is applicable where the act charged against the defendant is materially proven, but the act does not constitute a criminal offense.

In this case, the defendant was considered a good-faith purchaser who did not know or suspect that the bicycle he purchased originated from a crime. The Supreme Court therefore corrected the lower court's ''ontslag'' judgment and entered an acquittal (''vrijspraak'').

== Executive Summary ==

The central legal principle is the distinction between:

* '''Acquittal (''Vrijspraak'')''' under Article 191 paragraph (1) KUHAP, where the defendant's guilt is not legally and convincingly proven because one or more elements of the charged offense have not been established; and
* '''Release from All Legal Prosecution (''Ontslag van Alle Rechtsvervolging'')''' under Article 191 paragraph (2) KUHAP, where the charged act is materially proven but the act does not constitute a criminal offense.

Because the prosecution failed to establish that [Defendant] knew or should have suspected that the bicycle originated from a crime, the element required under Article 480 KUHP was not proven.

The Supreme Court therefore held that the proper judgment was an acquittal (''vrijspraak''), not an ''ontslag''.

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Public Prosecutor of the Pematang Siantar District Prosecutor's Office, annulled Simalungun District Court Decision No. 137/Pid/B/1985/PN.SIM dated July 29, 1985, and adjudicated the case itself by acquitting [Defendant] from all charges and restoring his rights, position, honor, and dignity through rehabilitation.

== Case Background ==

The Defendant / Respondent in Cassation, '''[Defendant]''', [age removed], born [place removed], male, Indonesian citizen, and a farmer residing in [address removed], was charged with receiving stolen goods under Article 480 KUHP.

On June 3, 1985, [Defendant] purchased a blue women's Forever-brand bicycle from witness [Witness] for Rp 25,000.

The transaction took place during the daytime and was conducted openly. The initial payment was Rp 15,000, with the remaining Rp 10,000 to be paid after the bicycle documents were delivered.

The bicycle was subsequently established to have been stolen from witness [Witness B].

Witness [Witness B] had reported the bicycle missing on May 31, 1985. Witness [Witness] was arrested by the police on June 6, 1985.

The Simalungun District Court, through Decision No. 137/Pid/B/1985/PN.SIM dated July 29, 1985, released the Defendant from all legal prosecution (''ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging'').

The Public Prosecutor of the Pematang Siantar District Prosecutor's Office filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Claims, Evidence and Source Mapping ==

! No.
! Legal Statement / Fact
! Evidence / Judicial Consideration
! Source

| '''1'''

| The Supreme Court jurisprudence headnote and its reasoning establish that if the defendant did not know, suspect, or have reason to suspect that the goods originated from a crime, an element of Article 480 KUHP is not proven.

| 1130K_PID_1985.pdf

| 1130K_PID_1985.pdf

| 1130K_PID_1985.pdf

| 1130K_PID_1985.pdf

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==

=== Distinction Between ''Vrijspraak'' and ''Ontslag van Alle Rechtsvervolging'' ===

The principal procedural issue was whether a court may impose ''ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging'' where one of the essential elements of the charged criminal offense, particularly the subjective element of Article 480 KUHP, has not been proven.

The Supreme Court held that this was legally incorrect.

The two forms of judgment have different legal bases and consequences:

* '''Acquittal (''Vrijspraak'') — Article 191 paragraph (1) KUHAP:''' Applies where the defendant's guilt in relation to the charged act is not legally and convincingly proven because one or more elements of the offense have not been established.

* '''Release from All Legal Prosecution (''Ontslag van Alle Rechtsvervolging'') — Article 191 paragraph (2) KUHAP:''' Applies where the act charged against the defendant is materially proven, but the act does not constitute a criminal offense.

Because the Simalungun District Court found that the Defendant was a good-faith purchaser who did not know or suspect that the bicycle originated from a crime, the "should have suspected" element under Article 480 KUHP was not proven.

The appropriate judgment was therefore an acquittal (''vrijspraak'').

=== Cassation by the Public Prosecutor ===

The Supreme Court also considered the Public Prosecutor's cassation petition concerning the lower court's incorrect legal qualification of the judgment.

The Supreme Court held that the lower court had incorrectly applied the law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') in determining the appropriate form of judgment.

The Supreme Court therefore had authority to annul the lower court's decision and adjudicate the case itself.

== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law ===

'''Question:'''

Did the Simalungun District Court incorrectly apply the law by imposing ''Ontslag van Alle Rechtsvervolging'' under Article 191 paragraph (2) KUHAP when the subjective element of receiving stolen goods under Article 480 KUHP had not been proven?

'''Supreme Court Answer:'''

Yes.

The Simalungun District Court had incorrectly applied the law.

Where the defendant does not know, suspect, or have reason to suspect that goods originated from a crime, an element of Article 480 KUHP is not established.

The legal consequence is an acquittal (''Vrijspraak'') under Article 191 paragraph (1) KUHAP, rather than ''Ontslag van Alle Rechtsvervolging'' under Article 191 paragraph (2) KUHAP.

The Supreme Court therefore granted the cassation petition of the Public Prosecutor, annulled the Simalungun District Court judgment, and adjudicated the case itself by acquitting [Defendant].

=== Question of Fact ===

The factual issues concerned:

* The purchase of one blue women's Forever-brand bicycle on June 3, 1985 in Kp. Silau Bayu.
* The negotiated purchase price of Rp 25,000, reduced from Rp 30,000.
* Initial payment of Rp 15,000.
* Agreement to pay the remaining Rp 10,000 after the bicycle documents were delivered.
* Witness [Witness]'s statement that the bicycle documents were at his house.
* The fact that the transaction took place openly during the daytime.
* The theft of the bicycle from witness [Witness B].
* The arrest of witness [Witness] by Serbelawan Police Sector on June 6, 1985.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The ''judex facti'' at the Simalungun District Court incorrectly applied the law by characterizing the proper judgment as ''ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging''.

# Where the defendant does not know or suspect that goods originate from a crime, an element of Article 480 KUHP, particularly the "knew or should have suspected" element, cannot be established.

# Failure to establish an element of the charged criminal offense requires an acquittal (''vrijspraak'') under Article 191 paragraph (1) KUHAP.

# ''Ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging'' under Article 191 paragraph (2) KUHAP is applicable only where the charged act is proven but the act does not constitute a criminal offense.

# The Defendant's status as a good-faith purchaser was relevant to the failure to establish the required subjective element under Article 480 KUHP.

# The Supreme Court therefore granted the Public Prosecutor's cassation petition, annulled the Simalungun District Court decision, and adjudicated the case itself.

== Ruling ==

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the '''Public Prosecutor of the Pematang Siantar District Prosecutor's Office''' and annulled Simalungun District Court Decision No. 137/Pid/B/1985/PN.SIM dated July 29, 1985.

The Supreme Court then adjudicated the case itself:

# Declaring that the alleged offense committed by Defendant '''[Defendant]''' was not legally and convincingly proven.

# '''Acquitting the Defendant from the charges (''Vrijspraak'').'''

# Restoring the Defendant's rights, position, honor, and dignity through rehabilitation.

# Ordering the bicycle evidence, a Forever-brand bicycle, to be returned to witness [Witness B].

# Ordering that the court costs at all levels of judicial proceedings be borne by the State.

== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==

=== Indonesian Criminal Code (KUHP) ===

* '''Article 480 paragraph 1 KUHP''' — Receiving stolen goods, including buying, renting, exchanging, accepting as security, receiving as a gift, or obtaining benefit from goods where the person knows or should suspect that the goods were obtained through a crime.

=== Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP) ===

* '''Article 191 paragraph (1) KUHAP''' — Acquittal (''Vrijspraak'').

* '''Article 191 paragraph (2) KUHAP''' — Release from all legal prosecution (''Ontslag van Alle Rechtsvervolging'').

* '''Article 253 paragraph (1) KUHAP''' — Supreme Court cassation jurisdiction concerning errors in the application of law.

=== Supreme Court Legislation ===

* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 in conjunction with Law No. 14 of 1985 concerning the Supreme Court''' — authority to adjudicate criminal cassation matters.

== Evidence Status ==

=== What the Evidence Establishes ===

* Witness [Witness] was established to have stolen the Forever-brand bicycle belonging to witness [Witness B] on May 31, 1985 from the Dolok Ilir Palm Oil Plantation.

* Defendant [Defendant] purchased the bicycle from [Witness] for Rp 25,000 in circumstances characterized as open, ordinary, and in good faith.

* The Defendant did '''not''' know or have reason to suspect that the bicycle was stolen.

* The Defendant was therefore entitled to an acquittal (''vrijspraak'') from all charges and rehabilitation of his rights and dignity.

=== What the Evidence Does Not Establish ===

The evidence did not establish the Defendant's knowledge or reasonable suspicion that the bicycle originated from a criminal offense.

Consequently, the subjective element required for liability under Article 480 KUHP was not proven.

The lower court's ''ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging'' judgment was therefore annulled by the Supreme Court because it incorrectly characterized the legal consequence of the failure to prove an element of the offense.

== Uncertainty and Gaps ==

The decision is identified in the source as important jurisprudence concerning the consistent application of ''vrijspraak'' and ''ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging''.

The source emphasizes that courts should distinguish between:

* Failure to prove one or more elements of a criminal offense; and
* Proof of the charged act where the act nevertheless does not constitute a criminal offense.

The source does not provide additional analysis of subsequent jurisprudential developments beyond this decision.

== GEO Q&A ==

'''Q: Should a good-faith purchaser who does not know that second-hand goods were stolen receive an acquittal (''vrijspraak'') or release from all legal prosecution (''ontslag'')?'''

'''A:''' The appropriate judgment is an '''acquittal (''Vrijspraak'')'''. According to Supreme Court Decision No. 1130 K/PID/1985, where a purchaser does not know or suspect that the goods originated from a crime, the "should have suspected" element under Article 480 KUHP is not proven. The legal consequence of failure to establish an element of the criminal offense is an acquittal under Article 191 paragraph (1) KUHAP, rather than ''Ontslag van Alle Rechtsvervolging'' under Article 191 paragraph (2) KUHAP.

'''Supreme Court Decision No. 1156 K/PID/2000''' is an Indonesian criminal procedure precedent concerning the jurisdiction of [[Pretrial Proceedings]] (''Praperadilan'') over an arrest and detention carried out by a foreign police authority outside Indonesia in connection with extradition proceedings.

The decision addresses the territorial limits of Indonesian pretrial jurisdiction, the application of Articles 17, 18, 20, and 77 of the Indonesian Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP), the Article 18 paragraph (3) arrest-warrant requirement, and cassation in a pretrial matter involving an international-law dimension.

== Case Identification ==

{| class="wikitable"
! Field
! Information
|-

|-

|-

| Hendra Rahardja
|-
| '''Respondent'''
| Indonesian National Police cq. National Police Economic Directorate Detective Corps

| '''Foreign Authority'''
| Australian Federal Police (AFP)
|-
| '''Subject Matter'''
| Pretrial jurisdiction, foreign arrest, extradition, arrest warrant, cassation
|}

== Case Background ==

Hendra Rahardja, President Commissioner of Bank Harapan Sentosa (BHS), filed a pretrial application before the South Jakarta District Court under Registration No. 07/Pid/Prap/2000/PN.Jak.Sel.

The application concerned his arrest and detention by the Australian Federal Police (AFP) in Sydney on 1 June 1999 in connection with extradition proceedings. The arrest was associated with an Interpol Red Notice and an affidavit issued by Rod Wissam.

Hendra Rahardja argued that the arrest and detention were unlawful because he had not received a copy of the Indonesian arrest warrant contemplated by Article 18 paragraph (3) of KUHAP. He also sought compensation of IDR 100 million.

The South Jakarta District Court, in its decision dated 23 June 2000, granted the pretrial application. The court declared the arrest and detention unlawful, ordered release from detention, and ordered the Indonesian Police to pay compensation of IDR 1,000,000.

The Indonesian National Police subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal Issues ==

# Whether Indonesian pretrial proceedings have jurisdiction to examine an arrest and detention physically carried out by a foreign police authority outside Indonesian territory.
# Whether Articles 77, 17, 18, and 20 of KUHAP apply to an arrest conducted by the Australian Federal Police in Australia pursuant to extradition arrangements.
# Whether the obligation to provide a copy of an arrest warrant under Article 18 paragraph (3) KUHAP arises before or only after a physical arrest is carried out by Indonesian investigators.
# Whether a pretrial decision may be challenged through cassation where the proceeding involves an international-law dimension.

== Supreme Court's Reasoning ==

The Supreme Court held that the South Jakarta District Court, as ''Judex Facti'', had misapplied the law.

According to the Supreme Court, the pretrial jurisdiction established under Article 77 of KUHAP, together with Articles 17, 18, and 20, concerns the legality of arrests and detentions physically carried out by Indonesian investigators within Indonesian sovereign territory.

The Supreme Court distinguished such Indonesian enforcement action from an arrest carried out by the Australian Federal Police in Australia pursuant to extradition arrangements.

Accordingly, an Indonesian pretrial court does not have jurisdiction to review the legality of an arrest or detention physically carried out by the AFP in Australian territory.

=== Article 18 Paragraph (3) KUHAP ===

The Supreme Court also addressed the requirement concerning delivery of a copy of an arrest warrant under Article 18 paragraph (3) KUHAP.

The Court reasoned that the obligation to provide the relevant copy arises in connection with a physical arrest carried out by Indonesian police authorities.

Because the Indonesian Police had not physically arrested Hendra Rahardja at the relevant stage, the Court found that the statutory obligation under Article 18 paragraph (3) had not yet been triggered.

== Holding ==

The Supreme Court:

# Granted the cassation petition submitted by the Indonesian National Police cq. National Police Economic Directorate Detective Corps.
# Annulled the South Jakarta District Court decision dated 23 June 2000 No. 07/Pid/Prap/2000/PN.Jak.Sel.
# Adjudicated the matter itself.
# Rejected Hendra Rahardja's pretrial application in its entirety.
# Ordered the Cassation Respondent/Pretrial Petitioner to pay cassation-level court costs amounting to IDR 2,500.

== Ratio Decidendi ==

The central ratio decidendi may be summarized as follows:

'''Indonesian pretrial jurisdiction over the legality of arrest and detention under KUHAP is territorially connected to physical enforcement action by Indonesian investigators within Indonesian territory.'''

An arrest physically conducted by a foreign police authority outside Indonesia in the context of extradition proceedings is not, by itself, an arrest subject to review under Indonesian pretrial jurisdiction.

The procedural obligation under Article 18 paragraph (3) KUHAP concerning delivery of an arrest warrant is likewise connected to a physical arrest carried out by Indonesian police authorities. Where such physical arrest has not yet occurred, the obligation has not yet arisen.

== Legal Significance ==

The decision is relevant to:

* Criminal Procedure Law
* Pretrial Proceedings (Praperadilan)
* Territorial Jurisdiction
* Extradition Law
* International Criminal Cooperation
* Foreign Police Powers
* Arrest and Detention
* Cassation Procedure
* Article 18 paragraph (3) KUHAP

== Related Legal Instruments ==

* [[Law No. 8 of 1981 on the Criminal Procedure Code]] (KUHAP), particularly Articles 17, 18, 20, 77, and 244.
* [[Law No. 8 of 1994]] concerning ratification of the Indonesia-Australia Extradition Treaty.
* [[Law No. 7 of 1992 on Banking]], particularly Article 49.
* [[Law No. 14 of 1970]] in conjunction with [[Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court]].

[Party C]''' in connection with the business activities of ''Fa. Kalimantan Development Corporation'' (Fa. KDC). [Party A] originally claimed timber-cutting commissions of US$2.80 per cubic metre, valued at IDR 16,406,613.60, under a Cooperation Statement dated 10 September 1972 concerning an approximately 8,000-hectare forest concession area in Melak. H. [Party C] responded with a counterclaim seeking recovery of 50% of the alleged losses of Fa. KDC as of 31 August 1970. The counterclaim relied upon a balance sheet and profit-loss statement prepared by accountant Drs. [Party B]. The lower courts granted the counterclaim. The Supreme Court, however, held that the financial statement had not satisfied the contractual formalities prescribed by the partnership's constitutive documents because it had not been signed or approved by [Party A]. Accordingly, the partnership-loss counterclaim had not yet become procedurally ripe for adjudication and was therefore inadmissible. The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition, annulled the decisions of the lower courts, rejected the conventional claim, and declared the counterclaim inadmissible. == Case Identification == {| class="wikitable" ! scope="col" style="width: 25%;" | Field ! scope="col" | Information |- ! scope="row" | Case | [Party A] v. [Party C] | Cassation Respondent / Original Defendant / Counterclaim Plaintiff | Former Director of Fa. Kalimantan Development Corporation |} == Case Background == [Party A] brought an action before the Samarinda District Court concerning timber-cutting commissions allegedly payable under a Cooperation Statement dated 10 September 1972. The claimed commission rate was US$2.80 per cubic metre, with the claim calculated at IDR 16,406,613.60. The underlying transaction concerned an approximately 8,000-hectare forest concession area in Melak. H. [Party C] contested the claim and filed a counterclaim relating to losses allegedly incurred by Fa. KDC. The counterclaim sought 50% of the partnership losses as of 31 August 1970, consisting of: * IDR 11,478,725.78 in partnership losses; and * IDR 4,757,723 in personal-account amounts; for a total claimed amount of '''IDR 16,236,448.78'''. The counterclaim relied upon a Balance Sheet and Profit-Loss Statement prepared by accountant '''Drs. [Party B]'''. == Procedural History == === First Instance: Samarinda District Court === The Samarinda District Court decided Case No. 109/1983/Pdt.G/PN.Smda on 12 November 1984. The court: * rejected [Party A]'s conventional claim; and * granted H. [Party C]'s counterclaim. === Appeal: East Kalimantan High Court at Samarinda === The East Kalimantan High Court at Samarinda decided Appeal No. 33/Perd/1985/PT.KT.Smda on 24 October 1985. The High Court affirmed the first-instance decision. === Cassation: Supreme Court === [Party A] subsequently filed a cassation petition. The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition and annulled both lower-court decisions. {| class="wikitable" |+ Procedural timeline ! scope="col" | Stage ! scope="col" | Court ! scope="col" | Case Number ! scope="col" | Date ! scope="col" | Outcome |- | First instance | Samarinda District Court | 109/1983/Pdt.G/PN.Smda | 12 November 1984 | Conventional claim rejected; counterclaim granted |- | Appeal | East Kalimantan High Court at Samarinda | 33/Perd/1985/PT.KT.Smda | 24 October 1985 | First-instance decision affirmed |- | Cassation | Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia | 1176 K/Pdt/1986 | 26 January 1988 (deliberation); 29 February 1988 (pronouncement) | Cassation granted; lower decisions annulled; conventional claim rejected; counterclaim inadmissible |} == Legal Issues == The case raised the following principal legal issues: # Whether a partnership-loss claim may be judicially enforced before the partnership's required Balance Sheet and Profit-Loss Statement has been validly prepared and approved. # Whether Article 7 of the Deed of Establishment of Fa. KDC required the relevant financial statement to be prepared by a designated accountant and signed by both partners. # Whether an unsigned or unapproved balance sheet could constitute a sufficient legal basis for determining the amount of partnership losses. # Whether the counterclaim was premature and therefore inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard'' / NO). # Whether the lower courts had correctly applied the partnership agreement and applicable procedural law. == Partnership Agreement and Financial Statement Requirement == The Supreme Court's reasoning centered on '''Article 7 of Deed No. 5 concerning the establishment of Fa. KDC''', read together with the '''Joint Statement dated 15 January 1971'''. Under these arrangements, the partnership's financial statements were subject to formal requirements. The relevant Balance Sheet and Profit-Loss Statement had to: # be prepared by the designated accountant; and # be signed or approved by both partners. These requirements were legally significant because the financial statement was being relied upon to establish the partnership's financial position and allocate losses between the partners. == Supreme Court's Reasoning == === 1. Contractual Requirements Governed the Financial Statement === The Supreme Court treated the partnership's constitutive documents as establishing the formal requirements for determining the partnership's financial position. Article 7 of the Deed of Establishment, together with the Joint Statement of 15 January 1971, required the relevant financial statement to be prepared and approved according to the agreed procedure. === 2. The Balance Sheet Had Not Been Properly Approved === The Balance Sheet and Profit-Loss Statement prepared by Drs. [Party B] had not been signed or approved by [Party A]. Therefore, the financial statement had not acquired the contractual status necessary to establish the partnership's final financial position between the partners. === 3. The Partnership-Loss Claim Was Premature === Because the financial statement had not been completed and validated in accordance with the partnership agreement, the alleged loss allocation had not yet reached the stage at which it could properly be enforced through judicial proceedings. The counterclaim was therefore considered '''premature''' or '''not yet ripe''' (''niet rijp''). === 4. The Lower Courts Misapplied the Law === The Supreme Court concluded that the ''Judex Facti'' had misapplied the relevant legal requirements by granting the counterclaim despite the absence of the required approval of the financial statement. The lower-court decisions therefore could not stand. === 5. Consequence of Procedural Immaturity === The appropriate procedural consequence was not an adjudication of the partnership-loss amount on the merits, but a declaration that the counterclaim was '''inadmissible''' (''Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard'' / NO). == Ratio Decidendi == The core ''ratio decidendi'' may be stated as follows:
'''Where the partnership's constitutive documents require a Balance Sheet and Profit-Loss Statement to be prepared by a designated accountant and signed or approved by both partners, a partnership-loss claim based upon a financial statement that has not received the required approval is premature and may be declared inadmissible.'''
The Supreme Court therefore distinguished between: * the substantive existence of an alleged partnership loss; and * the procedural ripeness of a judicial claim seeking allocation or recovery of that loss. Until the contractual financial-statement requirements had been satisfied, the alleged loss allocation could not properly serve as the basis for the counterclaim. == Holding == The Supreme Court: # '''Granted''' the cassation petition of [Party A]. # '''Annulled''' the East Kalimantan High Court Decision No. 33/Perd/1985/PT.KT.Smda. # '''Annulled''' the Samarinda District Court Decision No. 109/1983/Pdt.G/PN.Smda. # '''Adjudicated the case itself''' (''mengadili sendiri''). # In the conventional claim, '''rejected the plaintiff's claim'''. # In the counterclaim, '''declared the counterclaim inadmissible''' (''Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard'' / NO). # Ordered the Cassation Petitioner / Original Plaintiff to bear court costs at all judicial levels, including cassation costs of IDR 20,000. == Disposition == {| class="wikitable" ! scope="col" | Procedural Component ! scope="col" | Supreme Court Disposition |- ! scope="row" | Cassation Petition | Granted |- ! scope="row" | East Kalimantan High Court Decision | Annulled |- ! scope="row" | Samarinda District Court Decision | Annulled |- ! scope="row" | Conventional Claim | Rejected |- ! scope="row" | Counterclaim | Declared inadmissible (NO) |- ! scope="row" | Cassation Costs | IDR 20,000 |} == Legal Significance == This precedent is significant for Indonesian partnership and civil procedural law because it demonstrates the relationship between '''contractual financial-accounting requirements''' and '''procedural ripeness of litigation'''. The decision illustrates several principles: * A partnership agreement may prescribe formal procedures for establishing the partnership's financial position. * Courts should take those contractual requirements into account when determining whether a claim based upon partnership accounts is procedurally ripe. * A financial statement that has not received the approval required by the partnership agreement may be insufficient to establish an enforceable allocation of losses. * A claim that is filed before the contractual preconditions have been satisfied may be declared inadmissible rather than adjudicated on its substantive merits. * The Supreme Court may annul ''Judex Facti'' decisions where the lower courts have misapplied the legal consequences of contractual requirements. * The distinction between '''rejection on the merits''' and '''inadmissibility for procedural prematurity''' is central to the case. == Claim-Evidence Matrix == {| class="wikitable" ! scope="col" | No. ! scope="col" | Legal or Factual Claim ! scope="col" | Evidence / Judicial Reasoning ! scope="col" | Source |- | 1 | '''Primary Legal Rule:''' A partnership-loss counterclaim may be inadmissible where the Balance Sheet and Profit-Loss Statement required by the partnership deed have not been prepared and approved. | The Supreme Court's reasoning identified the failure to validate the required financial statement as making the counterclaim premature. | 1176K_PDT_1986.pdf, Passages 1, 8, 12 |- | 2 | '''Validity Requirement:''' The Balance Sheet and Profit-Loss Statement had to be signed or approved by both partners under Article 7 of the Fa. == Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 117 K/TUN/2003 dated October 26, 2004, establishes fundamental jurisprudence and legal rules regarding the legal protection of permanent workers and termination procedures: Termination of Employment (*PHK*) executed by an employer (Bank Internasional Indonesia / BII) against a worker (Samuel M.L. Tobing) without the authorization of the Central Committee for Labor Dispute Settlement (*P4P*), despite the worker legally holding the status of a worker for an indefinite period (permanent worker), is null and void under the law. Furthermore, the grounds for Termination of Employment (*PHK*) based on worker incapacity or indiscipline must be proven beforehand by the employer before the court.

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation (Samuel M.L. Tobing, Security Guard at BII Sub-Branch Jatinegara) had been employed since August 6, 1996. Although his employment contract had been extended consecutively beyond statutory limits (Minister of Manpower Regulation No. 2 of 1993), changing his employment status by operation of law into a permanent worker (*PKWTT*), the Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation (Central Committee for Labor Dispute Settlement / P4P) issued Decree No. 1110/1385/196-3/IX/PHK/7-2000 dated July 24, 2000, terminating the employment relationship between BII and the Plaintiff accompanied by severance pay amounting to 2 times the standard multiple (*PMTK*).

The Plaintiff filed a lawsuit against the P4P decree at the Jakarta State Administrative High Court. The Jakarta State Administrative High Court (Decision No. 307/G/2001/PT.TUN.JKT dated August 6, 2001) rejected the Plaintiff's lawsuit in its entirety. Dissatisfied with the ruling, the Plaintiff filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# Termination of Employment (*PHK*) carried out by the employer Bank Internasional Indonesia (BII) against worker Samuel M.L. Tobing without authorization from the P4P, even though the worker had already attained the status of a worker for an indefinite period (permanent worker), is contrary to the law.
# The grounds for Termination of Employment (*PHK*) based on incapacity or indiscipline must be proven in advance at trial by the employer.
# The *Judex Facti* (Jakarta State Administrative High Court) committed an error in applying the law by upholding the P4P decree that legitimized termination without authorization and without proof of the worker's faults or indiscipline. Consequently, the appellate administrative ruling must be annulled, and the Plaintiff must be reinstated as a permanent employee.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation SAMUEL M.L. TOBING; Annulling the Jakarta State Administrative High Court decision dated August 6, 2001, No. 307/G/2001/PT.TUN.JKT; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in its entirety; (2) Declaring null and void under the law the Defendant's (P4P) Decree No. 1110/1385/196-3/IX/PHK/7-2000 dated July 24, 2000, concerning the Termination of Employment between Bank Internasional Indonesia (BII) Jatinegara Branch, Jakarta, and Samuel M.L. |}

== Overview ==
Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 119 K/Pid/1982 dated March 17, 1983 (pronounced on March 31, 1983), establishes fundamental Criminal Procedure jurisprudence regarding prosecutorial appeals against acquittals: An appeal cannot be lodged by the Public Prosecutor against a pure acquittal (*vrijspraak*), unless it can be proven that the acquittal is in fact an impure acquittal (*verkapte ontslag van rechtsvervolging*), which must be elaborated and proven by the Prosecutor within their appellate memorandum. If the Public Prosecutor fails to submit an appellate memorandum detailing or proving an impure acquittal, the Prosecutor's appeal must be declared inadmissible (*niet ontvankelijke verklaard*).

== Case Background ==
The Defendants ([Party C] [Defendant I] and [Party B] [Defendant II], alongside Nawar, Sjafri, and Zakaria) were brought before the Batusangkar District Court indicted on primary charges of premeditated murder (Article 340 jo. Article 55 of the KUHP) and subsidiary charges of severe maltreatment resulting in death (Article 351 paragraph (1) sub 3 jo. Article 55 of the KUHP) against the victim [Party A] / Bachrum alias Mendek on August 15, 1968, in Parak Pandan, Jorong Tanjung Pauh, Lintau Buo, Tanah Datar.

The Batusangkar District Court (Decision No. 101/1969/PN.BS dated August 26, 1971) ruled to acquit all Defendants of all charges (*vrijspraak*). Against this acquittal, the Public Prosecutor filed an appeal but never filed or submitted an appellate memorandum. The Padang High Court (Decision No. 34/1976/PT.Pdg dated November 23, 1976) nevertheless accepted the Prosecutor's appeal, annulled the Batusangkar District Court decision specifically regarding Defendants I and II, and independently adjudicated the matter by sentencing Defendants I and II to 4 (four) years of imprisonment each. Dissatisfied with the Padang High Court ruling, Defendant I and Defendant II filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The cassation objections raised by the Petitioners for Cassation (Defendants I and II) are well-founded, because the Padang High Court should not have accepted the Public Prosecutor's appeal.
# Against a judgment of acquittal (*vrijspraak*), an appeal cannot be lodged by the Prosecutor unless it can be proven that the acquittal is actually an impure acquittal (*verkapte ontslag van rechtsvervolging*), which the Prosecutor is obligated to detail and prove within their appellate memorandum.
# Because the Public Prosecutor in this case never filed an appellate memorandum detailing an impure acquittal, the Prosecutor's appeal must legally be declared inadmissible (*niet ontvankelijke verklaard*). The action of the Padang High Court in examining and annulling the District Court's acquittal without the presence of an appellate memorandum violates criminal procedure law.

* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioners for Cassation I. [Party C] and II. [Party B]; Annulling the Padang High Court decision dated November 23, 1976, No. 34/1976/PT.Pdg; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Declaring that the Public Prosecutor's appeal against Defendant I ([Party C]) and Defendant II ([Party B]) is inadmissible (*niet ontvankelijke verklaard*); (2) Charging procedural costs across all levels of jurisdiction to the State. *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Cassation Panel of Justices on Thursday, March 17, 1983, by R. Djoko Soegianto, S.H. [Junior Chairman], Ny. Dora Sasongko Kartono, S.H., and H. Syafiar, S.H., and pronounced on Thursday, March 31, 1983).*
