== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 11 K/AG/2001 establishes an essential legal precedent regarding the boundaries of competence and jurisdiction of Religious Courts in disputes concerning the division and deduction of civil servant (*PNS*) salaries. The Supreme Court affirmed that the rule allocating half (1/2) of a defendant's salary to a former wife pursuant to Article 8 of Government Regulation No. 10 of 1983 jo. Government Regulation No. 45 of 1990 constitutes a civil servant disciplinary regulation, rather than forming part of Religious Court procedural law. The administrative action taken by a government agency to suspend or disburse a civil servant's salary constitutes a State Administrative Decision (*KTUN*). Consequently, once the Religious Court rules on the invalidity of the marriage certificate serving as the basis for salary suspension, claims regarding the payment or deduction of civil servant salaries must be brought before the State Administrative Court (*PTUN*) and are inadmissible before the Religious Courts.

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiff (Mrs. [Party B]) was the former wife of the Original Defendant ([Party A], a civil servant teacher) who divorced on December 1, 1994, at the Cilacap Religious Court (Decision No. 1312/Pdt.G/1994/PA.Clp). The divorce ruling stipulated that the Plaintiff was entitled to receive half (1/2) of the Defendant's salary until the Plaintiff remarried. However, starting in April 1994, the Defendant halted the transfer of this salary portion by submitting a copy of Marriage Certificate Extract No. 60/1995 dated February 3, 1995, issued by the Office of Religious Affairs (*KUA*) of Bojong Picung Subdistrict, Cianjur Regency, which stated that the Plaintiff had remarried a man named [Party C].

The Plaintiff, claiming she had never remarried, filed a lawsuit at the Cilacap Religious Court (Decision No. 2288/Pdt.G/1998/PA.Clp) seeking to declare the Marriage Certificate fraudulent and void, and demanding that the Defendant pay salary arrears. The Cilacap Religious Court granted the lawsuit in part by nullifying the fraudulent marriage certificate, but rejected the salary payment claims on the grounds that the Plaintiff allegedly cohabited without marriage. The Semarang High Religious Court (Decision No. 27/Pdt.G/1999/PTA.Smg) overturned the Cilacap Religious Court decision and granted all of the Plaintiff's claims, including the right to 1/2 of the civil servant salary. The Defendant subsequently filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:''' The allocation of half (1/2) of a defendant's salary to a plaintiff as stipulated under Article 8 of Government Regulation No. 10 of 1983 jo. Government Regulation No. 45 of 1990 concerning Civil Servant Disciplinary Regulations does not form part of Religious Court procedural law. Because the suspension or disbursement of 1/2 of the defendant's salary by the employing agency constitutes a State Administrative Decision, once the marriage certificate in the ''a quo'' case is declared legally void and non-binding, the plaintiff's claim for the deduction of 1/2 of the defendant's salary must be submitted to the State Administrative Court and is inadmissible before the Religious Courts.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition filed by Petitioner for Cassation ([Party A]); Annulling the Semarang High Religious Court decision dated September 28, 1999, No. 27/Pdt.G/1999/PTA.Smg; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part; (2) Declaring that the Marriage Certificate issued by KUA Bojong Picung Subdistrict, Cianjur Regency No. 60/1995 dated February 3, 1995, is invalid and possesses no legal force; (3) Declaring inadmissible the remainder of the Plaintiff's lawsuit (claims regarding the payment/deduction of 1/2 of the civil servant salary); (4) Ordering the Plaintiff and Appellant to bear procedural costs.

Nanyan; [Witness]; Counter-Memorandum of Appeal; Religious High Court of Banda Aceh; Written Defamation; Article 310(2) KUHP; Publicity Element; ''Vrijspraak'' |- ! scope="row" style="text-align: left; vertical-align: top;" |Related Regulations |Criminal Code (KUHP) Articles 310(2) and 311; Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP) Article 191(1) |} '''Supreme Court Decision No. 1205 K/Pid/1985''' is an Indonesian criminal-law precedent concerning the offence of written defamation (''pencemaran nama baik'' / Article 310(2) of the Criminal Code) and, in particular, the requirement that the statement be made "with the intention that it be made known to the public". The decision establishes that statements containing sharp words or attacks on a person's reputation, when included in a Counter-Memorandum of Appeal (''Kontra Memori Banding'') addressed officially to the panel of judges of a Religious High Court as a self-defence document in judicial proceedings, do not satisfy the publicity element of Article 310(2) KUHP. Where the publicity element is not proven, the defendant cannot be convicted and must be acquitted (''Vrijspraak'', Article 191(1) KUHAP). == Executive Summary == Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. '''1205 K/Pid/1985''' (pronounced 23 June 1987; deliberated 21 April 1987) sets out a fundamental rule of substantive criminal law on the '''inapplicability of the offence of written defamation (Article 310(2) KUHP) to official documents filed in judicial remedy proceedings'''. Writings or statements containing sharp words or attacks on a person's good name that appear in a Counter-Memorandum of Appeal addressed officially to the panel of judges of the Religious High Court (''Pengadilan Tinggi Agama'', a self-defence document in judicial proceedings) '''do not satisfy the element "with the intention that it be made known to the public"''' under Article 310(2) KUHP. Because the element of dissemination or publicity to the public was not proven, the Defendants could not be convicted and had to be acquitted of all charges (''Vrijspraak'', Article 191(1) KUHAP). The Supreme Court granted the cassation petitions of the Defendants '''[Defendant II]''' and '''[Defendant I]''', annulled Banda Aceh High Court Decision No. 30/Pid.S/1985/PT.BNA and Banda Aceh District Court Decision No. 21/Pid.S/1985/PN.BNA, adjudicated the case itself, and '''acquitted the Defendants of all charges'''. == JPAIS Knowledge Object (MODE 1 — BHT Knowledge) == {| class="wikitable" ! scope="col" style="width: 25%;" |Field ! scope="col" |Value |- ! scope="row" |Object ID |JPAIS:PRECEDENT:1205K_PID_1985 |- ! scope="row" |Applicable Mode |MODE 1 — BHT Knowledge (Extract Verified Knowledge from Final Cases; ''BHT'' = ''berkekuatan hukum tetap'', final and binding) |- ! scope="row" |Title |Failure of the Publicity Element ("Intent to Make Known to the Public") under Article 310(2) KUHP in Self-Defence Statements Contained in a Judicial File (Counter-Memorandum of Appeal) |- ! scope="row" |Judicial Institution |Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia (''Judex Juris'') |- ! scope="row" |Registry Number |Reg. Nanyan |Witness / person targeted by the statements |Alleged to be immoral and to divide property according to the "law of his stomach" (''hukum perut'') |- ! scope="row" |[Witness] |Witness / person targeted by the statements |Alleged to be known as a gambling kingpin and criminal |} == Case Background == In a Counter-Memorandum of Appeal (''Kontra Memori Banding'') dated 17 August 1984, addressed to the Religious High Court (''Pengadilan Tinggi Agama'', PTA) of Banda Aceh, the Defendants wrote statements attacking the morals and reputation of two witnesses: * witness '''H.M. Nanyan''' was described as immoral and as dividing property according to the "law of his stomach" (''hukum perut''); and * '''[Witness]''' was described as known as a gambling kingpin and criminal. The document was prepared for the Defendants' self-defence in a legal dispute before the Religious High Court. The Defendants were prosecuted for defamation, and the lower courts convicted them. == Procedural History == === First Instance: Banda Aceh District Court === The Banda Aceh District Court decided Case No. 21/Pid.S/1985/PN.BNA. It convicted the Defendants under Article 311 KUHP (calumny) and imposed a three-month sentence with probation (''percobaan''). === Appeal: Banda Aceh High Court === The Banda Aceh High Court decided Case No. 30/Pid.S/1985/PT.BNA. It modified the sentence to two months' imprisonment without probation (''penjara murni''). === Cassation: Supreme Court === The Defendants filed a cassation petition. The Supreme Court granted the petition, annulled both lower-court decisions, adjudicated the case itself, and acquitted the Defendants. {| class="wikitable" |+Procedural timeline ! scope="col" |Stage ! scope="col" |Court ! scope="col" |Case Number ! scope="col" |Outcome |- |First instance |Banda Aceh District Court |21/Pid.S/1985/PN.BNA |Defendants convicted under Article 311 KUHP; three months with probation |- |Appeal |Banda Aceh High Court |30/Pid.S/1985/PT.BNA |Sentence modified to two months' imprisonment without probation |- |Cassation |Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia |1205 K/Pid/1985 |Cassation granted; lower decisions annulled; Supreme Court adjudicated itself; Defendants acquitted (''Vrijspraak''). Deliberated 21 April 1987; pronounced 23 June 1987 |} == Legal Issues == The case raised the following principal legal issues: # Whether words attacking a person's honour, contained in an official judicial document (a Counter-Memorandum of Appeal) addressed to the panel of judges of the Religious High Court, satisfy the element "with the intention that it be made known to the public" under Article 310(2) KUHP. # Whether written self-defence arguments submitted in an official file to the judges hearing the case may be criminalised as defamation. # Whether the ''Judex Facti'' (the Banda Aceh District Court and High Court) erred in applying the law by convicting the Defendants without the publicity element being established. == Supreme Court's Reasoning == === 1. The Publicity Element of Article 310(2) KUHP === The Supreme Court examined the element "with the intention that it be made known to the public" (''dengan maksud supaya diketahui umum'') in the offence of written defamation under Article 310(2) KUHP. === 2. The Statements Were Made in an Official Judicial Document === The words were written in a Counter-Memorandum of Appeal addressed officially to the panel of judges of the Religious High Court. The document was submitted through the official channel of judicial proceedings, in a closed manner, for the purpose of the Defendants' self-defence (''due process of law''). === 3. The Publicity Element Was Not Proven === Because the document was addressed solely to the Religious High Court and was not disseminated to the general public, the element of intentionally disseminating the statements so that they would be known to the public was not legally proven. === 4. Protection of the Right of Self-Defence in Judicial Proceedings === Every citizen or litigant is entitled to present arguments, responses, and defences before the court or through official judicial documents. The courts should not hastily criminalise written defence arguments as defamation, provided the arguments are submitted in official files addressed to the panel of judges hearing the case. === 5. The Lower Courts Misapplied the Law === The Banda Aceh District Court and High Court convicted the Defendants without examining whether the element of dissemination to the public was fulfilled. The Supreme Court held that this was an erroneous application of the law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht''). === 6. Consequence: Acquittal === Since an essential element of the offence was not proven, the Defendants could not be punished and were acquitted of all charges (''Vrijspraak'', Article 191(1) KUHAP). == Ratio Decidendi == The core ''ratio decidendi'' may be stated as follows:
'''Statements containing sharp words or attacks on a person's reputation that appear in a Counter-Memorandum of Appeal addressed officially to the panel of judges of the Religious High Court, as a self-defence document in judicial proceedings, do not satisfy the element "with the intention that it be made known to the public" under Article 310(2) KUHP. Where the publicity element is not proven, the defendant cannot be convicted and must be acquitted (''Vrijspraak'', Article 191(1) KUHAP).'''
The Supreme Court's considerations (p. 13), as recorded in the source, read in the original Indonesian:
"Terdakwa tidak terbukti melakukan tindak pidana dimaksud dalam pasal 310 (2) KUHP, karena kata-kata tersebut terdakwa tulis dalam surat kontra memori banding yang ditujukan kepada Pengadilan Tinggi Agama, tanpa maksud untuk diketahui oleh umum."
In English: ''The defendant has not been proven to have committed the offence referred to in Article 310(2) KUHP, because the defendant wrote those words in a counter-memorandum of appeal addressed to the Religious High Court, without the intention that they be made known to the public.'' == Holding == The Supreme Court: # '''Granted''' the cassation petitions of the Defendants [Defendant II] and [Defendant I]. # '''Annulled''' Banda Aceh High Court Decision No. 30/Pid.S/1985/PT.BNA. # '''Annulled''' Banda Aceh District Court Decision No. 21/Pid.S/1985/PN.BNA. # '''Adjudicated the case itself''' (''mengadili sendiri''). # '''Declared''' that the Defendants were not legally and convincingly proven guilty. # '''Acquitted''' the Defendants of the charge (''Vrijspraak''). == Disposition == {| class="wikitable" ! scope="col" |Procedural Component ! scope="col" |Supreme Court Disposition |- ! scope="row" |Cassation Petitions |Granted |- ! scope="row" |Banda Aceh High Court Decision No. 30/Pid.S/1985/PT.BNA |Annulled |- ! scope="row" |Banda Aceh District Court Decision No. 21/Pid.S/1985/PN.BNA |Annulled |- ! scope="row" |Adjudication |Supreme Court adjudicated the case itself |- ! scope="row" |Charge |Defendants acquitted (''Vrijspraak'') |} == Question of Law vs Question of Fact == === Question of Law (''Judex Juris'' / Supreme Court) === Whether the ''Judex Facti'' (Banda Aceh High Court and District Court) erred in applying the law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') by convicting the Defendants of defamation/calumny (Article 310(2) / Article 311 KUHP), although the statements were written in an official Counter-Memorandum of Appeal addressed to the Religious High Court without the intention that they be made known to the public. '''Supreme Court's answer:''' Yes, the ''Judex Facti'' erred in applying the law. The Supreme Court granted the cassation petitions, annulled Banda Aceh High Court Decision No. 30/Pid.S/1985/PT.BNA and Banda Aceh District Court Decision No. 21/Pid.S/1985/PN.BNA, adjudicated the case itself, and acquitted the Defendants. === Question of Fact (''Judex Facti'') === The factual matters underlying the case, as recorded in the Claim-Evidence Matrix, were: * The Defendants wrote statements about witnesses H.M. Nanyan and [Witness] in a Counter-Memorandum of Appeal dated 17 August 1984. * The document was addressed to the Religious High Court of Banda Aceh for the Defendants' self-defence in a legal dispute, and was not disseminated to the general public. * The Defendants were [Defendant II] (farmer) and [Defendant I] (farmer), both of Meunasah Tuha, Aceh Besar. == Legal Significance == This precedent is significant for Indonesian criminal law because it clarifies the '''publicity element''' of written defamation and protects '''self-defence in judicial proceedings'''. The decision illustrates several principles: * Defamatory content alone is insufficient for conviction under Article 310(2) KUHP; the element "with the intention that it be made known to the public" must also be proven. * Statements made in an official judicial document addressed to the judges hearing the case, for the purpose of self-defence, are not made with the intention that they be made known to the public. * Courts should not hastily criminalise written self-defence arguments submitted through official judicial channels. * The Supreme Court may annul ''Judex Facti'' convictions where the publicity element was not examined, and may adjudicate the case itself and acquit the defendants. * The failure of an essential element leads to acquittal (''Vrijspraak'') rather than a conviction with a reduced sentence. == Claim-Evidence Matrix == {| class="wikitable" ! scope="col" |No. ! scope="col" |Legal or Factual Claim ! scope="col" |Evidence / Judicial Reasoning ! scope="col" |Source |- |1 |'''Primary Legal Rule (publicity exception for judicial documents):''' Words in a Counter-Memorandum of Appeal addressed to the Religious High Court do not satisfy the element "with the intention that it be made known to the public" under Article 310(2) KUHP. |Yurisprudensi headnote (p. 9) and Supreme Court considerations (p. 13): the Defendants were not proven to have committed the offence under Article 310(2) KUHP because they wrote the words in a counter-memorandum of appeal addressed to the Religious High Court, without intent that they be made known to the public. |1205K_PID_1985.pdf, Passages 1, 13 |- |2 |'''Statements at Issue:''' The Defendants wrote that witness H.M. scope="row" style="text-align: left; vertical-align: top;" |Related Regulations |HIR / RBg provisions on Voluntary vs. Contentious Jurisdiction; Law No. 14 of 1970; Law No. 1 of 1950; Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court |} '''Supreme Court Decision No. 1210 K/Pdt/1985''' is an Indonesian civil-law precedent establishing three fundamental civil procedure rules concerning the prohibition of using voluntary jurisdiction (''voluntaire jurisdictie'') for land rights determinations, the legal consequences of nullifying such petitions, and the appropriate handling of third-party objections. The decision establishes that district courts have no statutory authority to determine ownership or land rights through unilateral petition procedures without a dispute. Consequently, such orders are null and void (''batal demi hukum''), requiring disputes over customary land boundaries to be brought via separate contentious civil suits. == Executive Summary == The dispute arose in Jayapura, Papua (Irian Jaya), where '''[Party A]''' (Ondoafi Hedam Ayapo) filed a voluntary petition (No. 118/PN/Pdt.P/1983) at the Jayapura District Court seeking recognition of customary land rights without a contesting opposing party. The district court granted the petition. '''[Party B]''' (Ondoafi Besar Yoka Hebeibulu) subsequently filed an objection (''verzet'') challenging the order because it overlapped with customary lands in Abepura-Sentani. The lower courts examined the objection, with the High Court ruling in favor of the challenger. The Supreme Court held that the lower courts exceeded their jurisdiction. Voluntary jurisdiction cannot be used to establish land titles or ownership rights. The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition, annulled the lower-court decisions, declared the original district court petition order null and void, and ruled that all examination proceedings regarding the objection were invalid, mandating that land disputes be settled through standard contentious lawsuits. == Case Identification == {| class="wikitable" ! scope="col" style="width: 25%;" |Field ! scope="col" |Information |- ! scope="row" |Case |[Party A] v. [Party B] |- ! scope="row" |Supreme Court Registry |1210 K/Pdt/1985 |- ! scope="row" |Decision Date |11 May 1987 (deliberation); 30 June 1987 (pronouncement) |- ! scope="row" |Court |Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia |- ! scope="row" |Jurisdiction |Civil Law / Civil Procedure |- ! scope="row" |Subject |Voluntary jurisdiction, land rights determination, nullity of judicial orders, customary land disputes |- ! scope="row" |Parties |[Party A] (Original Petitioner / Cassation Petitioner) and [Party B] (Challenger / Cassation Respondent) |- ! scope="row" |DDC |347.052 |- ! scope="row" |Stable ID |JPAIS:PRECEDENT:1210K_PDT_1985 |} == Parties and Procedural Positions == {| class="wikitable" ! scope="col" |Party ! scope="col" |Procedural Position ! scope="col" |Role |- ! scope="row" |[Party A] |Cassation Petitioner / Original Petitioner / Original Defendant (Respondent to the Objection, ''Terlawan'') |Ondoafi Hedam Ayapo (Customary Leader, Sentani, Jayapura) |- ! scope="row" |[Party B] |Cassation Respondent / Original Plaintiff / Challenger (''Pelawan'') |Ondoafi Besar Yoka Hebeibulu (Customary Leader, Sentani, Jayapura) |} == Case Background == [Party A] filed a voluntary petition (No. 118/PN/Pdt.P/1983) at the Jayapura District Court, which was granted on 5 December 1983, recognizing customary control and rights (including the right to control and inherit) over ''ulayat'' land in Ayapo and surrounding areas. [Party B] challenged this order by filing an objection (''verzet'' No. 22/Pdt/Plw/1984/PN.Jpr), arguing that the order unilaterally annexed customary lands belonging to the Yoka Hebeibulu community in Abepura-Sentani. The Jayapura District Court ruled that the land was jointly owned, and upon appeal, the High Court of Irian Jaya (Decision No. 55/Pdt/1984/PT.Jpr) modified the judgment to grant the land entirely to the challenger. [Party A] then filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court. == Procedural History == === First Instance: Jayapura District Court (Petition) === The Jayapura District Court issued Order No. 118/PN/Pdt.P/1983 on 5 December 1983, granting the voluntary petition for land rights. === Objection Proceeding: Jayapura District Court === The Jayapura District Court decided Case No. 22/Pdt/Plw/1984/PN.Jpr on 29 October 1984, ruling that the disputed land was jointly owned. === Appeal: High Court of Irian Jaya at Jayapura === The High Court of Irian Jaya decided Appeal No. 55/Pdt/1984/PT.Jpr on 2 January 1985, modifying the first-instance judgment and declaring the land to belong entirely to the challenger (''Pelawan''). === Cassation: Supreme Court === [Party A] filed a cassation petition. The Supreme Court granted the petition, annulled the lower-court decisions, and independently declared the initial voluntary petition order null and void. {| class="wikitable" |+Procedural timeline ! scope="col" |Stage ! scope="col" |Court ! scope="col" |Case Number ! scope="col" |Date ! scope="col" |Outcome |- |Voluntary petition |Jayapura District Court |118/PN/Pdt.P/1983 |5 December 1983 |Petition for customary land rights granted |- |Objection (''verzet'') |Jayapura District Court |22/Pdt/Plw/1984/PN.Jpr |29 October 1984 |Disputed land declared jointly owned |- |Appeal |High Court of Irian Jaya at Jayapura |55/Pdt/1984/PT.Jpr |2 January 1985 |Judgment modified; land declared wholly the Challenger's |- |Cassation |Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia |1210 K/Pdt/1985 |11 May 1987 (deliberation); 30 June 1987 (pronouncement) |Cassation granted; lower decisions annulled; petition order declared null and void; objection proceedings declared null and void |} == Legal Issues == The case raised the following principal legal issues: # Whether a district court has the authority to receive, examine, and grant petitions for land ownership or customary land rights through voluntary jurisdiction (''voluntaire jurisdictie'') without a contentious dispute. # What the legal consequences are when a district court issues a voluntary land rights order without statutory backing. # Whether third-party objections (''verzet'') can be filed against a voluntary judicial order or whether a separate contentious lawsuit is required. == Supreme Court's Reasoning == === 1. Inadmissibility of Voluntary Jurisdiction for Land Rights === Acting on its own legal grounds (''ambtshalve''), the Supreme Court ruled that district courts examining and deciding land rights petitions without an active dispute exercise voluntary jurisdiction without legal basis. There is no statutory provision authorizing district courts to grant land ownership or title via ex-parte petitions. Such applications should initially be declared inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard'' / NO). === 2. No Objection (''Verzet'') Lies against an Order on a Petition === Under civil procedure law, an objection (''verzet'') cannot be filed against an order issued on a petition. A party who considers its land rights affected by such an order therefore cannot use the objection procedure to challenge it. === 3. Nullity of the Voluntary Order and Subsequent Proceedings === Because the Jayapura District Court petition order lacked legal foundation, it was declared null and void (''batal demi hukum''). Consequently, all subsequent examination proceedings in the objection lawsuits handled by the district and high courts were also rendered null and void. === 4. Requirement of Contentious Civil Lawsuits === Customary land disputes and boundary conflicts between tribes cannot be resolved via ex-parte petitions or irregular objection procedures, but must be pursued through separate, contentious civil lawsuits (''gugatan perdata kontradiktur''). == Ratio Decidendi == The core ''ratio decidendi'' may be stated as follows:
'''District courts have no statutory authority to adjudicate land ownership or customary rights via voluntary petition procedures; any such order issued without legal basis is null and void (''batal demi hukum''), and any property or boundary disputes must instead be litigated through separate contentious civil lawsuits.'''
== Holding == The Supreme Court: # '''Granted''' the cassation petition of [Party A]. # '''Annulled''' the High Court of Irian Jaya Decision No. 55/Pdt/1984/PT.Jpr. # '''Annulled''' the Jayapura District Court Decision No. 22/Pdt/Plw/1984/PN.Jpr. # '''Adjudicated the case itself''' (''mengadili sendiri''): ## Declared that the Challenger (''Pelawan'') is the rightful challenger (''Pelawan yang benar''). ## Declared Jayapura District Court Petition Order No. 118/PN/Pdt.P/1983 dated 5 December 1983 to be '''null and void'''. ## Declared that the Jayapura District Court lacked authority to examine the original petition. ## Declared all examination proceedings by the district and high courts in the objection case (No. 22/Pdt/Plw/1984/PN.Jpr jo. No. 55/Pdt/1984/PT.Jpr) to be '''null and void'''. # Ordered the Cassation Respondent ([Party B]) to pay court costs at all judicial levels (cassation costs set at IDR 20,000). == Disposition == {| class="wikitable" ! scope="col" |Procedural Component ! scope="col" |Supreme Court Disposition |- ! scope="row" |Cassation Petition |Granted |- ! scope="row" |High Court Decision |Annulled |- ! over Land Petitions |Denied (District Court lacked authority) |- ! scope="row" |Cassation Costs |IDR 20,000 (payable by the Cassation Respondent) |} == Legal Significance == This precedent is a landmark ruling regarding civil procedure and agrarian law in Indonesia, establishing that: * Courts are strictly prohibited from issuing declaratory property titles or land rights through voluntary jurisdiction (''voluntaire jurisdictie''). * Ex-parte land petitions are an absolute procedural nullity. * No objection (''verzet'') lies against an order on a petition, and objection proceedings built on a void order are themselves void. * Land and customary rights (''hak ulayat'') disputes must be settled via contentious (adversarial) civil lawsuits (''gugatan kontradiktur''). == scope="row" style="text-align: left; vertical-align: top;" |Related Regulations |Civil Code (KUHPerdata) Article 1365; Law No. 40 of 1999 on the Press (Articles 7 and 15); AD/ART of PWI; Law No. 48 of 2009 on Judicial Power; Law No. 14 of 1985, Law No. 5 of 2004 and Law No. 3 of 2009 on the Supreme Court |} '''Supreme Court Decision No. 1222 K/Pdt/2010''' is an Indonesian civil-law precedent concerning the lack of authority of the general courts to examine internal disputes of the Indonesian Journalists' Association (''Persatuan Wartawan Indonesia'', PWI) and the inadmissibility of a claim for an unlawful act (''perbuatan melawan hukum'', PMH) under Article 1365 of the Civil Code (KUHPerdata). The decision establishes that a dispute between a PWI branch board and the PWI Central Board over the dismissal of the branch chair and the suspension of the branch cannot be assessed as an unlawful act, because such matters are regulated autonomously within PWI by its Articles of Association and Bylaws (AD/ART) and the Journalistic Code of Ethics. Such disputes must be resolved through PWI's own mechanisms, and a claim brought before the general courts is inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard'' / NO). == Executive Summary == The dispute arose between the Board of the PWI West Papua Branch (2006–2010) and the PWI Central Board. The branch board members sued the Central Board before the Manokwari District Court, seeking annulment of PWI Central Board Decree No. 576/PP-PWI/2008 dated 9 May 2008, which dismissed the Chair of PWI West Papua ([Party A]), temporarily suspended the branch board, and appointed a caretaker. They characterized the decree as an unlawful act under Article 1365 of the Civil Code. The PWI Central Board had dismissed [Party A] because he concurrently served as Head of Public Relations Section (''Kabag Humas'') of the West Papua Provincial Government, which it considered a violation of the AD/ART. The Manokwari District Court partially granted the claim and annulled the decree, and the Jayapura High Court affirmed the decision with a correction of the operative part. The Supreme Court held that the ''Judex Facti'' had erred in applying the law. The dispute could not be assessed as an unlawful act under Article 1365, because PWI regulates such matters autonomously through its AD/ART and Journalistic Code of Ethics and accounts for them at the PWI Congress. The dispute therefore had to be resolved through PWI's own mechanisms and did not fall within the authority of the general courts. The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition, annulled the lower-court decisions, and, adjudicating the case itself, declared the Plaintiffs' claim inadmissible (NO). == Case Identification == {| class="wikitable" ! scope="col" style="width: 25%;" |Field ! scope="col" |Information |- ! scope="row" |Case |Central Board of PWI et al. v. [Party A] et al. |- ! scope="row" |Supreme Court Registry |1222 K/Pdt/2010 |- ! scope="row" |Decision Date |Not specified in source |- ! scope="row" |Court |Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia |- ! scope="row" |Jurisdiction |Civil Law / Civil Procedure |- ! scope="row" |Subject |Absolute competence of the general courts, internal organizational dispute, unlawful act (Article 1365 Civil Code), inadmissibility |- ! scope="row" |Parties |Central Board of PWI, Usman Taufiq Divinubun and Angleng Murcana (Cassation Petitioners) and [Party A], Karsuhan, La Ode Mursidin and Deminikus Talakua (Cassation Respondents) |- ! scope="row" |DDC |347.012 |- ! scope="row" |Stable ID |JPAIS:PRECEDENT:1222K_PDT_2010 |} == Parties and Procedural Positions == {| class="wikitable" ! scope="col" |Party ! scope="col" |Procedural Position ! scope="col" |Role |- ! scope="row" |Central Board of PWI / Drs. Tarman Azzam |Cassation Petitioner / Original Defendant I |Central Board of the Indonesian Journalists' Association |- ! scope="row" |Usman Taufiq Divinubun |Cassation Petitioner / Original Defendant II |Role not specified in source |- ! scope="row" |Angleng Murcana |Cassation Petitioner / Original Defendant III |Role not specified in source |- ! scope="row" |[Party A], SH |Cassation Respondent / Original Plaintiff |Board of PWI West Papua Branch, 2006–2010 (Chair dismissed by the disputed decree) |- ! scope="row" |Karsuhan |Cassation Respondent / Original Plaintiff |Board of PWI West Papua Branch, 2006–2010 |- ! scope="row" |La Ode Mursidin |Cassation Respondent / Original Plaintiff |Board of PWI West Papua Branch, 2006–2010 |- ! scope="row" |Deminikus Talakua, SH |Cassation Respondent / Original Plaintiff |Board of PWI West Papua Branch, 2006–2010 |} == Case Background == The Original Plaintiffs ([Party A], SH; Karsuhan; La Ode Mursidin; and Deminikus Talakua, SH), the Board of the PWI West Papua Branch for 2006–2010, sued the Original Defendants (the PWI Central Board / Drs. Tarman Azzam; Usman Taufiq Divinubun; and Angleng Murcana) before the Manokwari District Court. The Plaintiffs sought annulment of '''PWI Central Board Decree No. 576/PP-PWI/2008 dated 9 May 2008''' on the Dismissal of the Chair of PWI West Papua ([Party A]), the Temporary Suspension of the Branch Board, and the Appointment of a Caretaker, which they considered an unlawful act under Article 1365 of the Civil Code. The PWI Central Board had dismissed [Party A] because he concurrently served as Head of Public Relations Section (''Kabag Humas'') of the West Papua Provincial Government, which was considered a violation of the AD/ART. The Manokwari District Court partially granted the claim and annulled the decree. The Jayapura High Court affirmed the decision with a correction of the operative part. The PWI Central Board et al. then filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court. == Procedural History == === First Instance: Manokwari District Court === The Manokwari District Court decided Case No. 08/PDT.G/2008/PN.Mkw on 14 November 2008. It partially granted the Plaintiffs' claim and annulled the PWI Central Board decree. === Appeal: Jayapura High Court === The Jayapura High Court decided Appeal No. 25/PDT/2009/PT.Jpr on 11 December 2009. It affirmed the first-instance decision with a correction of the operative part. === Cassation: Supreme Court === The PWI Central Board et al. filed a cassation petition. The Supreme Court granted the petition, annulled the lower-court decisions, adjudicated the case itself, and declared the Plaintiffs' claim inadmissible. {| class="wikitable" |+Procedural timeline ! scope="col" |Stage ! scope="col" |Court ! scope="col" |Case Number ! scope="col" |Date ! scope="col" |Outcome |- |First instance |Manokwari District Court |08/PDT.G/2008/PN.Mkw |14 November 2008 |Claim partially granted; PWI Central Board decree annulled |- |Appeal |Jayapura High Court |25/PDT/2009/PT.Jpr |11 December 2009 |First-instance decision affirmed with correction of the operative part |- |Cassation |Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia |1222 K/Pdt/2010 |Not specified in source |Cassation granted; lower decisions annulled; claim declared inadmissible (NO) |} == Legal Issues == The case raised the following principal legal issues: # Whether a dispute between the PWI West Papua Branch Board and the PWI Central Board over the dismissal of the branch chair and the suspension of the branch can be assessed as an unlawful act (PMH) under Article 1365 of the Civil Code. # Whether the general courts have authority to examine internal disputes of PWI that are governed by its AD/ART and Journalistic Code of Ethics. # Whether the ''Judex Facti'' (the Manokwari District Court and the Jayapura High Court) erred in applying the law by granting the claim. == Supreme Court's Reasoning == === 1. The Dispute Was Not an Unlawful Act under Article 1365 === The dispute between the PWI West Papua Branch Board and the PWI Central Board concerning the dismissal and suspension of the branch cannot be assessed as an unlawful act (''perbuatan melawan hukum'') under Article 1365 of the Civil Code. === 2. Internal PWI Matters Are Regulated Autonomously === Within the PWI organization, such matters are regulated autonomously by the Articles of Association and Bylaws (AD/ART) and the Journalistic Code of Ethics, and are accounted for at the PWI Congress. === 3. Resolution through PWI's Own Mechanisms; Outside the Authority of the General Courts === Disputes within the PWI organization must be resolved through PWI's own mechanisms and do not fall within the authority of the general courts. === 4. The Lower Courts Misapplied the Law === The ''Judex Facti'' (the Jayapura High Court and the Manokwari District Court) erred in applying the law by examining and granting the claim. === 5. Consequence: Inadmissibility === Adjudicating the case itself, the Supreme Court declared the Plaintiffs' claim inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard'' / NO). == Ratio Decidendi == The core ''ratio decidendi'' may be stated as follows:
'''A dispute between a PWI branch board and the PWI Central Board over the dismissal and suspension of the branch cannot be assessed as an unlawful act under Article 1365 of the Civil Code, because within PWI such matters are regulated autonomously by its AD/ART and the Journalistic Code of Ethics and accounted for at the PWI Congress; such internal disputes must be resolved through PWI's own mechanisms and do not fall within the authority of the general courts, so that a claim brought before them is inadmissible (NO).'''
== Holding == The Supreme Court: # '''Granted''' the cassation petitions of the Cassation Petitioners: (1) the Central Board of the Indonesian Journalists' Association, (2) Usman Taufiq Divinubun, and (3) Angleng Murcana. # '''Annulled''' Jayapura High Court Decision No. 25/PDT/2009/PT.Jpr dated 11 December 2009, which had corrected Manokwari District Court Decision No. 08/PDT.G/2008/PN.Mkw dated 14 November 2008. # '''Annulled''' Manokwari District Court Decision No. 08/PDT.G/2008/PN.Mkw (see the ratio, which names both lower-court decisions as annulled). # '''Adjudicated the case itself''' (''mengadili sendiri''): ## Declared the Plaintiffs' claim '''inadmissible''' (''Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard'' / NO). # Ordered the Cassation Respondents to pay court costs at all judicial levels (cassation costs set at IDR 500,000). == Disposition == {| class="wikitable" ! scope="col" |Procedural Component ! scope="col" |Supreme Court Disposition |- ! scope="row" |Cassation Petitions |Granted |- ! scope="row" |Jayapura High Court Decision No. 25/PDT/2009/PT.Jpr |Annulled |- ! scope="row" |Manokwari District Court Decision No. 08/PDT.G/2008/PN.Mkw |Annulled |- ! scope="row" |Plaintiffs' Claim |Declared inadmissible (NO) |- ! scope="row" |Cassation Costs |IDR 500,000 (payable by the Cassation Respondents, together with costs at all levels) |} == Legal Significance == This precedent is significant for Indonesian civil procedure and organizational law because it addresses the reach of the general courts over the internal affairs of a professional organization. The decision illustrates several principles: * A dispute between a branch board and the central board of PWI over dismissal and suspension cannot be assessed as an unlawful act (PMH) under Article 1365 of the Civil Code. * Where an organization regulates its internal affairs autonomously through its AD/ART and code of ethics and accounts for them at its congress, internal disputes are to be resolved through the organization's own mechanisms. * Such internal disputes do not fall within the authority of the general courts. * The Supreme Court may annul ''Judex Facti'' decisions that examine such a dispute and declare the claim inadmissible (NO). == Claim-Evidence Matrix == {| class="wikitable" ! scope="col" |No. ! scope="col" |Legal or Factual Claim ! scope="col" |Evidence / scope="row" style="text-align: left; vertical-align: top;" |Related Regulations |Criminal Code (KUHP) Articles 338 and 351(3); Law No. 8 of 1981 on the Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP), Article 244; Law No. 14 of 1970, Law No. 13 of 1965 and Law No. 14 of 1985 (Supreme Court) |} '''Supreme Court Decision No. 1295 K/Pid/1985''' is an Indonesian criminal-law precedent concerning the proof of the element of intent (''opzet'' / ''dolus'') in the offence of murder under Article 338 of the Criminal Code (KUHP), and the distinction between murder and maltreatment resulting in death under Article 351(3) KUHP. The decision establishes that intent to deprive another person of life can be proven from the type of instrument used and the location on the victim's body that was wounded, and that proof of intent does not require repeated stabs or the victim's instant death at the scene. It also confirms that an acquittal of a primary charge based on a mistaken interpretation of intent is a non-pure acquittal (''niet-zuivere vrijspraak'') against which the Public Prosecutor may file cassation. == Executive Summary == Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. '''1295 K/Pid/1985''' (dated 2 January 1986) sets out a fundamental rule of substantive criminal law on '''proof of the element of intent (''opzet'' / ''dolus'') in the offence of murder (Article 338 KUHP), based on the instrument of the crime and the vital organ of the victim that was attacked'''. Intent to deprive another person of life (''opzet'' under Article 338 KUHP) can be proven legally and convincingly from the type of instrument used to commit the offence (a lethal kitchen knife) and the location on the victim's body wounded by that instrument (the left chest, penetrating the vital organs of the heart and lungs). The Supreme Court expressly rejected the ''Judex Facti'' reasoning that intent to kill must be proven by several stabs or by instant death at the scene: for an expert, a single stab accurately aimed at a vital organ is sufficient to kill, and the fact that the victim did not die instantly does not eliminate the intent to kill. The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Public Prosecutor at the West Jakarta District Prosecutor's Office, annulled DKI Jakarta High Court Decision No. 61/Pid/1985/PT.DKI and West Jakarta District Court Decision No. 046/JB./Pid./1984/PN.JKT.BAR, and, adjudicating the case itself, '''declared the Defendant ([Defendant]) guilty of murder under Article 338 KUHP and sentenced him to 12 (twelve) years' imprisonment'''. == JPAIS Knowledge Object (MODE 1 — BHT Knowledge) == {| class="wikitable" ! scope="col" style="width: 25%;" |Field ! scope="col" |Value |- ! scope="row" |Object ID |JPAIS:PRECEDENT:1295K_PID_1985 |- ! scope="row" |Applicable Mode |MODE 1 — BHT Knowledge (Extract Verified Knowledge from Final Cases; ''BHT'' = ''berkekuatan hukum tetap'', final and binding) |- ! scope="row" |Title |Proof of the Element of Intent to Kill (''Opzet'') under Article 338 KUHP Based on the Type of Lethal Instrument and the Vital Organ Targeted, and Rejection of the Requirement of Repeated Stabs |- ! scope="row" |Judicial Institution |Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia (''Judex Juris'') |- ! scope="row" |Registry Number |Reg. [age removed]; born [place removed]; male; Indonesian citizen; vehicle assistant (''kenek''); Gang Jamblang I No. 5, RT 008/RW 05, Duri Urban Village, West Jakarta; recidivist |- ! scope="row" |[Victim] |Victim |Stabbed on 18 August 1984 in Gang Jamblang I, West Jakarta |} == Case Background == The Defendant, [Defendant] (a vehicle assistant), was charged primarily under Article 338 KUHP (murder) and subsidiarily under Article 351(3) KUHP (maltreatment resulting in death). The charge arose because on 18 August 1984 in Gang Jamblang I, West Jakarta, he stabbed the victim [Victim] in the left chest with a kitchen knife, penetrating the heart and lungs to a depth of 15 cm and causing the victim's death. The West Jakarta District Court acquitted the Defendant of the primary charge (Article 338) and sentenced him to five years' imprisonment under the subsidiary charge (Article 351(3)), reasoning that he stabbed only once and the victim did not die instantly. The DKI Jakarta High Court affirmed the decision while increasing the sentence to seven years' imprisonment. The Public Prosecutor at the West Jakarta District Prosecutor's Office then filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court. == Procedural History == === First Instance: West Jakarta District Court === The West Jakarta District Court decided Case No. 046/JB./Pid./1984/PN.JKT.BAR on 5 February 1985. It acquitted the Defendant of the primary charge (Article 338 KUHP) and sentenced him to five years' imprisonment under the subsidiary charge (Article 351(3) KUHP). === Appeal: DKI Jakarta High Court === The DKI Jakarta High Court decided Appeal No. 61/Pid/1985/PT.DKI on 17 June 1985. It affirmed the first-instance decision and increased the sentence to seven years' imprisonment. === Cassation: Supreme Court === The Public Prosecutor filed a cassation petition. The Supreme Court accepted and granted the petition, annulled both lower-court decisions, adjudicated the case itself, and convicted the Defendant of murder under Article 338 KUHP. {| class="wikitable" |+Procedural timeline ! scope="col" |Stage ! scope="col" |Court ! scope="col" |Case Number ! scope="col" |Date ! scope="col" |Outcome |- |First instance |West Jakarta District Court |046/JB./Pid./1984/PN.JKT.BAR |5 February 1985 |Acquitted of the primary charge (Art. 338 KUHP); convicted under the subsidiary charge (Art. 351(3) KUHP); five years' imprisonment |- |Appeal |DKI Jakarta High Court |61/Pid/1985/PT.DKI |17 June 1985 |Affirmed; sentence increased to seven years' imprisonment |- |Cassation |Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia |1295 K/Pid/1985 |2 January 1986 |Cassation granted; lower decisions annulled; Defendant convicted under Art. 338 KUHP; 12 years' imprisonment |} == Legal Issues == The case raised the following principal legal issues: # '''Proof of the element of intent (''opzet'' / ''dolus'') in murder (Article 338 KUHP) through objective indicators (lethal instrument and vital organ of the victim):''' whether stabbing a kitchen knife into the victim's left chest, penetrating the vital organs of the heart and lungs, satisfies the element of intent to kill under Article 338 KUHP, or amounts only to maltreatment resulting in death (Article 351(3) KUHP) because there was a single stab and the victim did not die instantly at the scene. # '''Admissibility of the Public Prosecutor's cassation petition against a non-pure acquittal (''niet-zuivere vrijspraak'', Article 244 KUHAP):''' whether the Public Prosecutor may file cassation against a ''Judex Facti'' decision acquitting the Defendant of the primary charge (Article 338 KUHP) and convicting him only under the subsidiary charge (Article 351(3) KUHP). == Supreme Court's Reasoning == === 1. Admissibility of Cassation against a Non-Pure Acquittal === The acquittal of the Defendant from the primary charge (Article 338 KUHP) by the ''Judex Facti'', based on a mistaken interpretation of the element of intent, is in essence a non-pure acquittal (''niet-zuivere vrijspraak''). In accordance with the Supreme Court's jurisprudence on Article 244 KUHAP, the Supreme Court has full authority at the cassation level to assess and annul such an acquittal so as to enforce the law correctly. The Public Prosecutor's petition was therefore admissible. === 2. Intent Can Be Proven from the Instrument and the Body Location === Intent to deprive another person of life can be proven by the instrument used to commit the offence and the place on the victim's body that was wounded by that instrument. === 3. The Kitchen Knife and the Vital Organs Struck === A kitchen knife is a lethal instrument (a ''notoir feit'', i.e. a matter of common knowledge). The stab to the victim's left chest penetrated the fifth rib, the left lung, the pericardium and the right lung to a depth of 15 cm, which proves the intent to kill. === 4. Rejection of the Repeated-Stab and Instant-Death Requirement === The Supreme Court did not agree with the ''Judex Facti'' view that intent to kill must be proven by several stabs. For an expert, a single stab accurately aimed at a vital organ is sufficient to kill. Nor does the fact that the victim did not die instantly mean that the Defendant lacked intent. === 5. The Lower Courts Misapplied the Law === The ''Judex Facti'' (the DKI Jakarta High Court and the West Jakarta District Court) erred in applying the law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') in qualifying the element of intent to kill. === 6. Consequence: The Primary Charge Was Proven === All elements of Article 338 KUHP were proven legally and convincingly. The Supreme Court therefore annulled the lower-court decisions and, adjudicating the case itself, convicted the Defendant of murder and sentenced him to 12 (twelve) years' imprisonment. == Ratio Decidendi == The core ''ratio decidendi'' may be stated as follows:
'''Intent to deprive another person of life (''opzet'' under Article 338 KUHP) can be proven legally and convincingly from the type of instrument used (a lethal kitchen knife) and the location on the victim's body that was wounded (the left chest, penetrating the vital organs of the heart and lungs). Proof of intent does not require several stabs or the victim's instant death: for an expert, a single stab accurately aimed at a vital organ suffices, and the victim's not dying at once does not eliminate the intent to kill.'''
The Supreme Court's considerations (p. 30), as recorded in the source, read in the original Indonesian:
"Kesengajaan untuk menghilangkan nyawa orang lain dapat dibuktikan dengan alat yang dipergunakan untuk melakukan tindak pidana tersebut dan tempat pada badan korban yang dilukai alat itu."
In English: ''Intent to deprive another person of life can be proven by the instrument used to commit the offence and the place on the victim's body wounded by that instrument.'' And, on the rejection of the repeated-stab requirement:
"Mahkamah Agung tidak menyetujui pertimbangan judex facti yang berpendapat untuk membuktikan niat/kesengajaan untuk menghilangkan nyawa orang lain harus terbukti dengan beberapa tusukan... Begitu pula korban tidak meninggal seketika, tidak berarti bahwa terdakwa tidak ada niat/kesengajaan..."
In English: ''The Supreme Court does not agree with the judex facti's view that, to prove the intent to deprive another person of life, this must be proven by several stabs... Likewise, the fact that the victim did not die instantly does not mean that the defendant lacked intent...'' == Holding == The Supreme Court: # '''Accepted and granted''' the cassation petition of the Cassation Petitioner, the Public Prosecutor at the West Jakarta District Prosecutor's Office. # '''Annulled''' DKI Jakarta High Court Decision No. 61/Pid/1985/PT.DKI dated 17 June 1985. # '''Annulled''' West Jakarta District Court Decision No. 046/JB./Pid./1984/PN.JKT.BAR dated 5 February 1985. # '''Adjudicated the case itself''' (''mengadili sendiri''): ## Declared the Defendant [Defendant] '''guilty''' of the offence charged in the primary charge, namely "murder" as described in Article 338 KUHP. ## Sentenced him accordingly to '''12 (twelve) years' imprisonment'''. ## Ordered that the time spent in detention be deducted in full. ## Ordered the Defendant to remain in detention. ## Ordered the Defendant to pay court costs at all judicial levels (cassation costs set at IDR 2,500). == Disposition == {| class="wikitable" ! scope="row" |Detention |Time in detention deducted in full; Defendant to remain in detention |- ! scope="row" |Cassation Costs |IDR 2,500 (payable by the Defendant, together with costs at all levels) |} == Question of Law vs Question of Fact == === Question of Law (''Judex Juris'' / Supreme Court) === Whether the ''Judex Facti'' (the DKI Jakarta High Court and the West Jakarta District Court) erred in applying the law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') by acquitting the Defendant of the primary charge under Article 338 KUHP and re-qualifying the offence under Article 351(3) KUHP on the assumption that intent to kill requires several stabs and instant death at the scene. '''Supreme Court's answer:''' Yes, the ''Judex Facti'' erred in applying the law. The Supreme Court granted the Public Prosecutor's cassation petition, annulled DKI Jakarta High Court Decision No. 61/Pid/1985/PT.DKI and West Jakarta District Court Decision No. 046/JB./Pid./1984/PN.JKT.BAR, and, adjudicating the case itself, '''declared the Defendant [Defendant] guilty of murder under Article 338 KUHP and sentenced him to 12 (twelve) years' imprisonment'''. === Question of Fact (''Judex Facti'' / West Jakarta District Court and DKI Jakarta High Court) === The facts examined by the ''Judex Facti'' were: * The stabbing occurred on Saturday, 18 August 1984, at about 20:30 WIB, in Gang Jamblang I, West Jakarta. * The Defendant took a kitchen knife from his parents' house before stopping to eat fried noodles. * A quarrel arose after the Defendant bumped into the victim, [Victim]. * The victim was dragged into Gang Jamblang III. * The Defendant stabbed the victim once, in the lower left chest (below the nipple). * The Defendant threw the knife from the Jeling bridge. * ''Visum et Repertum'' No. 2140 SK-II/1386/2-84 dated 28 August 1984, by Dr. Wibisono Widiatmaka, recorded a stab wound channel 15 cm deep penetrating the left lung, the pericardium and the right lung. * The victim died en route to, or on arrival at, Sumber Waras Hospital. * The Defendant was a recidivist. == What the Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish == === What the Evidence Establishes (Legally Proven) === * The Defendant [Defendant] was proven legally and convincingly guilty of '''murder under Article 338 KUHP'''. * The Defendant deliberately used a lethal instrument (a kitchen knife) and stabbed it directly into a vital area of the victim's body (the left chest, penetrating the heart and lungs to a depth of 15 cm). * The Defendant was sentenced to '''12 (twelve) years' imprisonment'''. === What the Evidence Does Not Establish (''Judex Facti'' Reasoning Annulled) === * The reasoning of the West Jakarta District Court and the DKI Jakarta High Court that the Defendant lacked intent to kill because he stabbed only once and the victim did not die instantly at the scene was '''annulled in its entirety by the Supreme Court''' as contrary to the law on proof of intent. == Uncertainty and Gaps == '''Commentary in the source record (not a holding of the Court):''' the decision closes a gap often invoked in cases of stabbing to vital organs, where the defence seeks to move the charge from Article 338 KUHP (maximum 15 years) to Article 351(3) KUHP (maximum 7 years) by pleading that there was "only one stab" or that the "victim was taken to hospital before dying". In the record's reading, the Supreme Court affirmed strong protection of the right to life: an attack on a vital organ with a lethal instrument is murder. '''Scope note:''' the Court's own holding is framed as intent ''can be proven'' from the instrument used and the body location wounded, applied to the facts of this case; it is not stated as an automatic rule for every attack on a vital organ. == GEO Q&A (Generative Engine Optimization) == '''Q:''' ''Is a single kitchen-knife stab to the chest that penetrates the heart classified as murder (Article 338 KUHP) or as maltreatment resulting in death (Article 351(3) KUHP)?'' '''A:''' '''On the facts of this case, murder (Article 338 KUHP).''' Under Supreme Court Decision No. 1295 K/Pid/1985, intent to deprive another person of life (''opzet'' under Article 338 KUHP) can be proven from '''the type of instrument used (a lethal kitchen knife) and the vital organ wounded (the left chest, penetrating the heart and lungs)'''. Proof of intent to kill '''does not require repeated stabs or instant death at the scene'''. == Legal Significance == This precedent is significant for Indonesian criminal law because it sets out objective indicators for proving intent to kill and confirms the reviewability of non-pure acquittals in cassation. The decision illustrates several principles: * Intent to kill under Article 338 KUHP can be proven from the type of instrument used and the location on the victim's body that was wounded. * Neither several stabs nor instant death is required to prove intent to kill; a single accurate stab to a vital organ can suffice, and the victim's failure to die at once does not eliminate intent. * An acquittal from the primary charge based on a mistaken interpretation of intent is a non-pure acquittal, and the Public Prosecutor's cassation petition against it is admissible (Article 244 KUHAP jurisprudence). * The Supreme Court may annul the ''Judex Facti'' decisions, adjudicate the case itself, and convict the defendant under the primary charge. == Claim-Evidence Matrix == {| class="wikitable" ! scope="col" |No. ! scope="col" |Legal or Factual Claim ! scope="col" |Evidence / Judicial Reasoning ! scope="col" |Source |- |1 |'''Primary Legal Rule (proof of intent to kill):''' Intent to deprive another person of life can be proven by the instrument used and the place on the victim's body that was wounded. |Yurisprudensi headnote (p. 24) and Supreme Court considerations (p. 30): intent to deprive another person of life can be proven by the instrument used to commit the offence and the place on the victim's body wounded by that instrument. |1295K_PID_1985.pdf |- |2 |'''Assessment of the Instrument and Vital Organs:''' Using a kitchen knife on the left chest, penetrating the heart and lungs to a depth of 15 cm, proves intent to kill. |Supreme Court legal considerations (p. 30): a kitchen knife is a lethal instrument (''notoir feit''), and a stab to the left chest penetrating the fifth rib, the left lung, the pericardium and the right lung to a depth of 15 cm proves intent to kill. |1295K_PID_1985.pdf |- |3 |'''Rejection of the Repeated-Stab and Instant-Death Requirement:''' Intent to kill does not require several stabs, and the victim's not dying at the scene does not eliminate intent. |Supreme Court considerations (p. 30): the Supreme Court did not agree with the ''Judex Facti'' view that intent to kill must be proven by several stabs; == Overview ==
Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 134 K/TUN/2007 dated June 19, 2007, establishes fundamental State Administrative procedural jurisprudence regarding the calculation of the time limit for filing a lawsuit:

* '''Calculation of State Administrative Lawsuit Time Limit (Article 55 of Law No. 5 of 1986 jo. Law No. 9 of 2004):''' For parties whose names are directly listed/addressed in a State Administrative Decree, the 90 (ninety) day time limit to file a lawsuit is calculated from the date the said Decree is physically received by the concerned party, rather than from the date it was merely known.
* '''Negligence in Delivering Decrees via Postal Mail (*Re-tour*):''' If a decree sent via postal mail by a State Administrative Official is returned (*re-tour*) to the sender and is never physically received by the Plaintiff, such negligence or failure in delivery cannot be imposed as a prejudicial burden upon the Plaintiff. The time limit calculation only commences once the Plaintiff physically receives the decree (such as during the preliminary examination at the State Administrative Court).
* '''Cancellation of Forest Management Principle Permits:''' The unilateral cancellation or withdrawal of an oil palm plantation management principle permit within a forest area by the Minister of Forestry, despite the community/cooperative having fulfilled all requirements and compensation obligations, violates the Principles of Good Governance (*AAUPB*), specifically the Principle of Legal Certainty and the Principle of Thoroughness (*Asas Kecermatan*).

== Case Background ==
The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation (Bukit Harapan Oil Palm Plantation Cooperative / KPKS Bukit Harapan, represented by Chairman Ir. Djonggi Sitorus) cooperated with PT Torganda (Darianus Lungguk Sitorus / D.L. Sitorus) to establish an oil palm plantation on customary lands of Luhat Simangambat and Luhat Ujung Batu within the Register 40 Padang Lawas area, South Tapanuli, North Sumatra. The Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation (Minister of Forestry of the Republic of Indonesia) issued Letter No. 1680/Menhut-III/2002 dated September 26, 2002, concerning the Principle Permit for Oil Palm Plantation Management covering an area of 23,000 hectares, subject to compensation payments for standing timber amounting to Rp 21,852,760,000 and IUPHHBK provisions. KPKS Bukit Harapan fulfilled these obligations through Statement of Undertaking Deed No. 145 dated April 25, 2003.

However, the Minister of Forestry unilaterally issued Letter No. S.419/Menhut-II/2004 dated October 13, 2004, withdrawing the principle permit and ordering the cessation of all activities. The decree was sent via postal mail but never arrived and was returned (*re-tour*) to the Ministry of Forestry. The Plaintiff only received the physical decree during the preliminary examination at the Jakarta State Administrative Court on February 9, 2006.

The Jakarta State Administrative Court (Decision No. 12/G/2006/PTUN-JKT dated July 12, 2006) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit and annulled the Minister of Forestry's decree. The Jakarta State Administrative High Court (Decision No. 151/B/2006/PT.TUN.JKT dated October 12, 2006) annulled the State Administrative Court's judgment and declared the lawsuit inadmissible on the grounds that it exceeded the 90-day time limit. KPKS Bukit Harapan subsequently filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The Jakarta State Administrative High Court erred in applying the law regarding the determination of the lawsuit filing time limit pursuant to Article 55 of Law No. 5 of 1986 jo. Law No. 9 of 2004. The calculation of the lawsuit filing time limit for a party addressed in a State Administrative Decree must be computed from the time the decree is physically received (*ontvangan*).
# Trial facts proved that the decree sent via postal mail by the Defendant to the Plaintiff was returned (*re-tour*) to the sender and was never received by the Plaintiff. The Plaintiff only received the physical decree *in litis* during the preliminary examination at the Jakarta State Administrative Court on February 9, 2006. The negligence of the Defendant as a State Administrative Official cannot be shifted as a prejudicial burden upon the Plaintiff as a seeker of justice.
# The Supreme Court concurs with the legal reasoning of the Jakarta State Administrative Court, which annulled the Minister of Forestry's Decree No. S.419/Menhut-II/2004 because the unilateral revocation of the principle permit without valid legal grounds violated the Principles of Good Governance (*AAUPB*).

* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation BUKIT HARAPAN OIL PALM PLANTATION COOPERATIVE (*KOPERASI PERKEBUNAN KELAPA SAWIT BUKIT HARAPAN*); Annulling the Jakarta State Administrative High Court decision dated October 12, 2006, No. 151/B/2006/PT.TUN.JKT, which had annulled the Jakarta State Administrative Court decision dated July 12, 2006, No. 12/G/2006/PTUN.JKT; and Independently Adjudicating: IN EXCEPTION: Declaring the Defendant's exceptions inadmissible in their entirety; IN THE PRINCIPAL CASE: (1) Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit; (2) Declaring null and void the Letter of the Minister of Forestry No. S.419/Menhut-II/2004 dated October 13, 2004, regarding: Application to Manage Plantations within Forest Area Register 40 Padang Lawas, North Sumatra Province; (3) Ordering the Defendant to revoke the Letter of the Minister of Forestry No. S.419/Menhut-II/2004 dated October 13, 2004; (4) Ordering the Respondent for Cassation / Defendant to pay court costs across all levels of jurisdiction, assessed at this cassation level at Rp 500,000 (five hundred thousand rupiahs). *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Cassation Panel of Justices on Tuesday, June 19, 2007, by Titi Nurmala Siagian, SH., MH. [Presiding Judge], Marina Sidabutar, SH., MH., and H. Imam Soebechi, SH., MH.).*

== Overview ==
Supreme Court Decision No. 136 K/TUN/2003 dated October 15, 2003, establishes fundamental jurisprudence and legal rules regarding the limits of State Administrative Court jurisdiction in civil service disputes: State Administrative Courts do not have the authority to determine the form or type of disciplinary punishment against a Civil Servant (*PNS*), as such authority rests entirely with the State Administrative Official. State Administrative judges are not justified in usurping the discretionary power of State Administrative Officials by altering or mitigating the imposition of civil servant disciplinary sanctions.

== Case Background ==
The Original Plaintiff / Respondent for Cassation ([Plaintiff], Junior Administrative Officer Class III/b, NIP [removed], former Civil Servant at the Regional Office of the Department of Justice and Human Rights of Maluku) was subjected to a disciplinary punishment of Honorable Discharge Not at Own Request (*Pemberhentian Dengan Hormat Tidak Atas Permintaan Sendiri*) as a Civil Servant pursuant to the Decree of the Minister of Justice of the Republic of Indonesia No. M.130-KP.05.07 of 1998 dated September 1, 1998. This punishment was imposed because the Plaintiff was proven to have committed a disgraceful act, namely cohabiting (*kumpul kebo*) without a valid marriage bond with a woman named [Third party] / [Third party] in Ambon (despite the Plaintiff already being married to Mrs. Halidjah and having 3 children), as well as being absent from work without legitimate reason for 81 working days (October 1996 to January 1997).

The Plaintiff pursued an administrative appeal to the Civil Service Advisory Board (*BAPEK*). BAPEK issued Decree No. 119/KPTS/BAPEK/2000 Jakarta dated July 27, 2000, upholding the Minister of Justice's decision. The Plaintiff subsequently challenged BAPEK's decree at the Jakarta State Administrative High Court (serving as the first-instance court for administrative appeal efforts pursuant to Article 48 jo. Article 51 paragraph (3) of Law No. 5 of 1986). The Jakarta State Administrative High Court (Decision No. 103/G/2001/PT.TUN.JKT dated November 28, 2001) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part, annulled BAPEK's decree, and ordered BAPEK to change the type of disciplinary punishment from discharge to a demotion in rank by one level for 1 year. Dissatisfied with the ruling, BAPEK filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The cassation objections raised by the Petitioner for Cassation (BAPEK) are well-founded because the Jakarta State Administrative High Court committed an error in applying the law in its considerations stating that BAPEK violated the principle of justice and ordering a demotion in rank by one level for 1 year.
# Pursuant to Article 7 of Government Regulation No. 30 of 1980, State Administrative Courts lack the authority to determine the form and type of disciplinary punishment imposed upon Civil Servants, as such authority belongs exclusively to the State Administrative Official.
# The conduct of the Plaintiff / Respondent for Cassation in cohabiting with another woman without marriage and being absent from work for 81 working days is legally proven to violate Article 2 letters c, g, h, w, x jo. Article 3 paragraph (1) letter a of Government Regulation No. 30 of 1980 jo. Government Regulation No. 10 of 1983 jo. Government Regulation No. 45 of 1990. The decisions of BAPEK and the Minister of Justice ordering honorable discharge not at own request are in accordance with the law and are not arbitrary, rendering the Jakarta State Administrative High Court judgment subject to annulment.

* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation CIVIL SERVICE ADVISORY BOARD (*BADAN PERTIMBANGAN KEPEGAWAIAN / BAPEK*); Annulling the Jakarta State Administrative High Court decision dated November 28, 2001, No. 103/G/2001/PT.TUN.JKT; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Rejecting the objection of [Plaintiff] as stated in his letter dated December 18, 1998; (2) Affirming the disciplinary punishment decision of the Minister of Justice No. M.130-Kp.05.07 of 1998 dated September 1, 1998, in the form of Honorable Discharge Not at Own Request as a Civil Servant imposed upon [Plaintiff], born [details removed], NIP [removed], Junior Administrative Officer, Class III/b, employee at the Regional Office of the Department of Justice and Human Rights of Maluku; (3) If [Plaintiff]'s salary was temporarily suspended, such salary shall be paid in accordance with prevailing laws and regulations; (4) [Plaintiff] is not granted pension rights as he fails to meet the requirements stipulated under prevailing laws and regulations; (5) This decision takes effect from the date of its enactment; Ordering the Respondent for Cassation to pay cassation-level court costs amounting to Rp 200,000 (two hundred thousand rupiahs). *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court on Wednesday, October 15, 2003, by the Cassation Panel of Justices: Prof. DR. Paulus E. Lotulung, SH. [Junior Chairman for State Administrative Chamber / Presiding Judge], Ny. Titi Nurmala Siagian, SH., and Widayatno Sastrohardjono, SH., MSc. [Associate Justices]).*

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:1378K PID 2000
wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 1378 K/Pid/2000}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 1378 K/Pid/2000''' (dated November 16, 2000) is an Indonesian criminal jurisprudence precedent on psychotropic offenses establishing legal rules regarding the qualification of **distributing psychotropics** (Article 60 paragraph (1) letter c of Law No. 5 of 1997) versus mere **possession/storage** (Article 62 of Law No. 5 of 1997).

== Executive Summary ==
The Defendant's actions in controlling and storing psychotropics in large quantities (353 ecstasy pills and 14 packages of methamphetamine), equipped with weighing instruments (electronic scales) and packaging materials (plastic bundles and aluminum foil), coupled with proven delivery of methamphetamine to a buyer (witness [Witness]) in exchange for cash, **do not merely constitute possession or storage** (Article 62 of Law No. 5 of 1997), but fully satisfy the elements of "distributing psychotropics in the form of drugs not registered with the government department responsible for health" ''ex'' Article 60 paragraph (1) letter c of Law No. 5 of 1997 on Psychotropics.

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Public Prosecutor at the Sleman District Attorney's Office, annulled the Yogyakarta High Court Decision No. 43/Pid/2000/PT.Y, and **independently adjudicated** (*mengadili sendiri*) by reinstating the considerations of the Sleman District Court Decision No. 15/Pid.B/2000/PN.SLMN, sentencing the Defendant ([Defendant]) to **6 (six) years** of imprisonment and a fine of **Rp 25,000,000** (twenty-five million rupiahs) with a subsidiary of 3 (three) months of confinement.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Differentiation of Legal Qualifications Between the Offense of "Distributing Psychotropics" and "Possessing/Storing Psychotropics" ===
''Does the control of psychotropics in large quantities (353 ecstasy pills and 14 methamphetamine packages) accompanied by weighing instruments (electronic scales), packaging materials, and proven delivery of goods in exchange for cash qualify merely as passive possession/storage (Article 62 of Law No. 5/1997)?''

'''Supreme Court Rule:''' It cannot be classified merely as storage (proven distribution). The Yogyakarta High Court erred in applying the law by narrowly interpreting the term "distributing" (*mengedarkan*). The sequence of trial facts—digital weighing instruments, commercial packaging tools, large-scale inventory supplies, and actual sales transactions to witness [Witness] for cash compensation—demonstrates conclusively that the Defendant operated commercial distribution activities, fulfilling the formulation of '''"distributing psychotropics in the form of drugs not registered with the Health Department"''' ''ex'' Article 60 paragraph (1) letter c of Law No. 5 of 1997.

=== 2. Admissibility of Witness [Witness]'s Testimony Tried in a Severed Case File (Crown Witness / De Cautelo) as Valid Evidence (Article 185 of KUHAP) ===
The High Court erred in disregarding witness [Witness]'s testimony on the grounds that she was tried in a separate case file (*splitsing*). Witness testimony given under oath during trial and corroborated by physical seizure evidence constitutes valid witness testimony ''ex'' Article 185 of the Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP) to prove distribution elements.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' (Yogyakarta High Court Decision No. 43/Pid/2000/PT.Y) err in applying the law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') by acquitting the Defendant of the Primary Charge under Article 60 paragraph (1) letter c of Law No. 5 of 1997 and reclassifying the offense under Article 62 of Law No. 5 of 1997, despite trial facts proving the presence of scales, packaging, and psychotropic sales transactions?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. The Yogyakarta High Court erred in applying the law. The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Sleman District Attorney's Office, annulled Yogyakarta High Court Decision No. 43/Pid/2000/PT.Y, and independently adjudicated by affirming the legal considerations of Sleman District Court Decision No. 15/Pid.B/2000/PN.SLMN: declaring Defendant [Defendant] legally and convincingly guilty of violating Article 60 paragraph (1) letter c of Law No. 5 of 1997 and sentencing her to 6 (six) years of imprisonment and a fine of Rp 25,000,000 subsidiary 3 (three) months of confinement.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Sleman District Court & Yogyakarta High Court) ===
Inspection of arrest and search facts on Friday, October 29, 1999, at 5:00 PM WIB at the Defendant's residence at [address removed], Sinduadi, Mlati, Sleman; seizure facts of 353 ecstasy pills (MDMA), 14 methamphetamine packages weighing ± 125.2 grams, 1 electronic scale, 4 boxes of aluminum foil, 7 bundles of plastic packaging, and Rp 1,600,000 in cash; BPOM DIY Laboratory Testing Report No. 05.05.5721/99 dated December 11, 1999, by Dra. Atiek Harwati, SU, Apt; as well as the sales transaction facts of transferring methamphetamine from the Defendant to witness [Witness] in exchange for Rp 1,150,000 in cash.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Law No. 5 of 1997 on Psychotropics ===

* '''Article 60 paragraph (1) letter c:''' Crime of distributing psychotropics in the form of drugs not registered with the Department of Health (punishable by a maximum of 15 years imprisonment and a maximum fine of Rp 200,000,000).
* '''Article 62:''' Crime of unlawfully possessing, storing, and/or carrying psychotropics (punishable by a maximum of 5 years imprisonment and a maximum fine of Rp 100,000,000).

=== Law No. 8 of 1981 (Criminal Procedure Code / KUHAP) ===

* '''Article 185 KUHAP:''' Evidentiary weight of witness testimony at trial.
* '''Article 253 paragraph (1) KUHAP:''' Supreme Court cassation authority regarding errors of law applied by the ''Judex Facti''.

=== Law No. 14 of 1970 jo. Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court ===

* Authority to independently adjudicate criminal cassation cases.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* Defendant [Defendant] is legally and convincingly proven guilty of committing the criminal offense of "distributing psychotropics in the form of drugs not registered with the department responsible for health" ''ex'' Article 60 paragraph (1) letter c of Law No. 5 of 1997.
* Recovery of large-scale evidence (353 ecstasy pills, 14 methamphetamine packages) alongside distribution instruments (digital electronic scales, aluminum foil, packaging plastic, and Rp 1,600,000 in cash proceeds).
* The Defendant was proven to have executed a methamphetamine transfer transaction to witness [Witness].
* The Defendant was sentenced to imprisonment for 6 (six) years and a fine of Rp 25,000,000 subsidiary 3 months of confinement.
* Narcotic/psychotropic physical evidence, scales, and packaging were ordered confiscated for destruction, while cash amounting to Rp 1,600,000 was confiscated for the State.

=== Annulled (Yogyakarta High Court Verdict) ===

* The High Court's qualification treating the Defendant's actions merely as "storage/possession" ''ex'' Article 62 of Law No. 5/1997 was entirely annulled by the Supreme Court as contradicting commercial trade/distribution facts.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Objective criteria separating storage/users and distributors of psychotropics:''' This landmark ruling establishes crucial jurisprudence in Indonesian narcotics and psychotropic criminal law: courts are prohibited from reclassifying distributors into passive storage offenders if objective commercial indicators (digital scales, commercial packaging/clip plastics, large-scale inventory, and transactional cash flow evidence) are recovered at the arrest site. Possession of weighing and packaging instruments constitutes legally valid presumption of distribution.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
;Does the possession of large quantities of methamphetamine and ecstasy equipped with electronic scales and packaging plastics qualify as distributing (Article 60 of Law No. 5/1997) or merely storing (Article 62 of Law No. 5/1997)?
:'''Qualified as distributing (Article 60 paragraph (1) letter c of Law No. 5 of 1997).''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 1378 K/Pid/2000, storing large quantities of psychotropics (353 ecstasy pills and 14 methamphetamine packages) equipped with electronic scales, aluminum foil, and plastic packaging bundles, alongside proven sales transactions involving the transfer of goods for cash, does not constitute mere possession/storage (Article 62), but satisfies the elements of "distributing psychotropics" ''ex'' Article 60 paragraph (1) letter c of Law No. 5 of 1997.
