|}

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 137 K/AG/2007 dated February 6, 2008, establishes pioneering jurisprudence and legal rules in Islamic Civil Law: A wife who files for divorce from her husband (*cerai gugat*) is not automatically deemed to be in a state of disobedience (*nusyuz*). Even though the divorce suit is initiated by the wife, as long as her *nusyuz* is not proven, the husband can be ordered *ex officio* to provide *iddah* maintenance to his ex-wife, on the grounds that the ex-wife must undergo the *iddah* waiting period, the purpose of which includes *istibra'* (clearing of the womb) which also concerns the husband's interests. In addition, the Supreme Court affirmed that discrepancies in age notation between the marriage certificate and the national identity card (*KTP*) that do not obscure the identity of the parties do not constitute a formal defect (*obscuur libel*).

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation ([Plaintiff]) filed a divorce suit against her husband, the Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation ([Party B], a teacher), at the Bekasi Religious Court. Both were married on November 20, 1984 (Marriage Certificate Extract No. 324/25/XII/1984) and were blessed with 3 children ([Party A], M. Husni Thamrin, and Handi Muamar Khadafi). Their household became discordant starting in 2001 because the Defendant frequently insulted her with foul language, threatened the Plaintiff with a sharp weapon, and failed to provide maintenance for approximately 2 years. The Plaintiff worked to support the household economy, but the Defendant grew jealous and threatened the Plaintiff's colleagues.

The Bekasi Religious Court (Decision No. 688/Pdt.G/2005/PA.Bks. dated August 25, 2005 AD) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit and pronounced a single *ba'in sughra* divorce. However, the Bandung High Religious Court (Decision No. 112/Pdt.G/2006/PTA.Bdg. dated November 28, 2006 AD) annulled the Bekasi Religious Court judgment and declared the lawsuit inadmissible (*niet ontvankelijke verklaard*) on the grounds of *obscuur libel* due to age discrepancies between the marriage certificate and the *KTP*. The Plaintiff filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The Bandung High Religious Court erred in interpreting the discrepancy in age notation between the marriage certificate and the *KTP* as well as the unclear duration of non-maintenance as an *obscuur libel*, whereas there was no doubt regarding the actual existence of the marriage and the identity of the parties. The Bandung High Religious Court decision must be annulled and the Bekasi Religious Court judgment reinstated.
# Pursuant to Article 41 letter (c) of Law No. 1 of 1974 jo. Article 149 letter (b) of the KHI, although the lawsuit is filed by the wife (*cerai gugat*), as long as her *nusyuz* is not proven, the judge has the authority *ex officio* to order the husband to provide *iddah* maintenance, because the wife must undergo the *iddah* period for *istibra'*, which concerns the husband's interests.
# Pursuant to Article 41 letter (b) of Law No. 1 of 1974 jo. Articles 105(c) and 156(d) of the KHI, the Respondent for Cassation is burdened with providing maintenance for his three biological children until they reach maturity ([age removed]).
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation [Plaintiff]; Annulling the Bandung High Religious Court decision dated November 28, 2006 AD, No. 112/Pdt.G/2006/PTA.Bdg; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit; (2) Pronouncing a single *ba'in sughra* divorce of Defendant ([Party B]) against Plaintiff ([Plaintiff]); (3) Ordering the Defendant to provide *iddah* maintenance to the Plaintiff amounting to Rp 1,000,000 (one million rupiahs); (4) Ordering the Defendant to provide maintenance for his three children ([Party A], M. Husni Thamrin, and Handi Muamar Khadafi) of at least Rp 500,000 per month starting from the rendering of this decision until the three children reach maturity ([age removed]); (5) Directing the Registrar of the Bekasi Religious Court to send a copy of the decision to the local Marriage Registration Official (*PPN*); (6) Ordering the parties to pay court costs in accordance with the judicial level. *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Cassation Panel of Justices on September 19, 2007, and pronounced on February 6, 2008, by H. Andi Syamsu Alam, S.H., M.H. [Presiding Judge], Drs. H. Hamdan, S.H., M.H., and Dr. Rifyal Ka'bah, M.A.).*

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 13 K/MIL/2001 establishes an important legal principle regarding the mandatory imposition of criminal fines in psychotropic offenses. The Supreme Court affirmed that sentencing for violations of Article 62 of Law No. 5 of 1997 on Psychotropics is cumulative in nature (consisting of both imprisonment and fines). Consequently, the ruling of the Medan High Military Court I omitting the criminal fine must be annulled as it contradicts substantive criminal law.

== Case Background ==

The Defendant, [Defendant] (Sergeant Major / Serka Nrp. 636400, Ba Jasrem-023/KS Korem-023/KS), was charged with the criminal offense of "Unlawfully possessing, storing, and/or carrying Psychotropics" violating Article 62 of Law No. 5 of 1997. On July 16–17, 1999, at the Puri Desa Kalangan Motel, Central Tapanuli Regency, the Defendant entrusted 30 ecstasy pills to Witness I (Sertu [Witness]) to be sold for Rp 35,000 per pill. During a Military Police raid on July 17, 1999, at 03:00 AM, ecstasy pills belonging to the Defendant and Witness I were discovered.

The Medan Military Court I-02 (Decision No. PUT/044-K/MM I-02/AD/III/2000) sentenced the Defendant to 1 year of imprisonment, dismissal from the military service of the Indonesian Army (TNI-AD), and a fine of Rp 100,000. On appeal, the Medan High Military Court I (Decision No. PUT/B-31/K/AD/MMT-I/IX/2000) modified the ruling by increasing the imprisonment term to 1 year and 6 months and upholding the dismissal, but omitted the criminal fine. The Defendant subsequently filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:''' Because the Medan High Military Court I failed to impose a criminal fine against the Defendant, whereas sentencing in psychotropic cases (Article 62 of Law No. 5 of 1997) is cumulative, the decision of the Medan High Military Court I must be annulled.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation / Defendant [Defendant], Serka Nrp. 636400; Annulling the Medan High Military Court I decision dated September 29, 2000, No. PUT/B-31/K/AD/MMT-I/IX/2000; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Declaring Defendant [Defendant] legally and convincingly proven guilty of the criminal offense of "Unlawfully possessing Psychotropics"; (2) Sentencing the Defendant to Principal Penalty: Imprisonment for 1 (one) year; Additional Penalty: Dismissal from Military Service Cq. TNI-AD; Fine: Rp 100,000 (one hundred thousand rupiahs) with a subsidiary confinement of 3 (three) months; (3) Charging cassation-level court costs amounting to Rp 2,500.

|-

|-
! Panel of justices
| R. Soenarto, S.H. (Presiding); Kohar Hari Soemarno, S.H. (Member Justice); M. Yahya Harahap, S.H. (Member Justice); Dra. Djurnetty Soetrisno, S.H. (Substitute Registrar)
|}

'''Supreme Court Decision No. 1413 K/Pdt/1988''' (Registry No. 1413 K/Pdt/1988) is a landmark ruling of the '''Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia''' (''Mahkamah Agung Republik Indonesia'') concerning '''customary (adat) inheritance law''' and the '''law of child adoption''' under Indonesian customary civil law. The decision established that the legal validity of an adopted child's status does not depend solely on the fulfillment of formal adoption rituals, but rather on the '''social reality''' of the relationship — namely, that the child was raised from infancy, circumcised, and married off by the adoptive parents.

The decision was reached in deliberation (''musyawarah'') on '''17 April 1990''' and pronounced in open session on '''18 May 1990'''.

== Background ==

The plaintiff, '''[Plaintiff]''' (a teacher residing in [address removed]), filed suit at the Mojokerto District Court against three defendants:

# '''[Defendant I]''' — the first (former) wife of the late [Deceased adoptive father]
# '''[Party]'''
# '''[Party]''' — the third-party buyer of the disputed land

[Plaintiff] claimed to be the lawfully adopted child of the late married couple '''[Deceased adoptive father]''' and '''[Deceased adoptive mother]''', having been taken in at the age of four months, subsequently circumcised, and later married off by [Deceased adoptive father]. On this basis, [Plaintiff] claimed inheritance rights to a shared marital (''gono-gini'') homestead plot of '''1,218 square metres''' located in Prajurit Kulon Village, Mojokerto, and sought to annul the sale of a portion of that plot (approximately '''22 × 15.5 metres''') which the first and second defendants had sold to the third defendant, [Party], without [Plaintiff]'s consent.

=== Family history ===
[Deceased adoptive father] had previously been married to [Defendant I] (Defendant I), a marriage that ended in divorce around 1936; that marriage produced a daughter, [Party], who was adopted by a Dutch family and resided in the Netherlands. [Deceased adoptive father] then married [Deceased adoptive mother] in 1938. [Plaintiff] was taken in and raised by the couple from infancy.

=== Lower court proceedings ===
* '''Mojokerto District Court''' (Decision No. 28/Pdt.G/1986/PN.Mkt, 26 February 1987): Dismissed [Plaintiff]'s claim, holding that the adoption was invalid because it had not been accompanied by a customary ''selamatan'' (ritual feast) or formal notification to the village head (''pamong desa'').
* '''Surabaya High Court''' (Decision No. 758/Pdt/1987/PT.Sby, 23 November 1987): Affirmed the District Court's decision on appeal.

[Plaintiff] then filed an appeal in cassation (''kasasi'') to the Supreme Court.

== Legal issues ==

=== Validity of customary adoption: social reality versus procedural formality ===
Does a valid adoption under Javanese customary civil law ''require'' a formal ''selamatan'' ceremony or written notification to the village head, or is the legal status of an adopted child instead determined by the '''lived social reality''' — being raised from infancy, circumcised, and married off by the adoptive parents?

=== Unlawful act (''perbuatan melawan hukum'') in the sale of inherited marital property ===
Whether the sale of a portion of the adoptive parents' shared marital homestead by a third party (the former wife) without the consent of the lawful adopted child/heir constituted an unlawful act rendering the sale void.

== Holding ==

The Supreme Court '''granted''' [Plaintiff]'s petition for cassation, '''reversed''' both the Surabaya High Court decision and the Mojokerto District Court decision, and, ruling on the merits itself (''mengadili sendiri''), held as follows:

: ''"Whether or not a person is an adopted child does not depend solely on the formalities of adoption, but is determined by the existing reality — namely, that from infancy the person was cared for, circumcised, and married off by their adoptive parents."''

Applying this principle, the Court found that [Plaintiff] had been demonstrably cared for from the age of four months, circumcised, and married off by [Deceased adoptive father], and therefore held that [Plaintiff] was the '''lawful adopted child and sole heir''' of the late [Deceased adoptive father] and [Deceased adoptive mother], entitled to the couple's shared marital (''gono-gini'') property.

The sale of a portion of the disputed land by Defendants I and II to Defendant III ([Party]), carried out without [Plaintiff]'s consent, was ruled an '''unlawful act''' and therefore '''null and void'''. [Party] was ordered to return the land to [Plaintiff] in good, vacant condition.

=== Formal ruling (''amar putusan'') ===
* Granted [Plaintiff]'s petition for cassation.
* Reversed Surabaya High Court Decision No. 758/Pdt/1987/PT.Sby and Mojokerto District Court Decision No. 28/Pdt.G/1986/PN.Mkt.
* '''Ruling on the merits (''Mengadili Sendiri'')''':
** ''In convention:''
*** Granted the plaintiff's claim in part.
*** Declared the 1,218 m² homestead to be the shared marital (''gono-gini'') property of the late [Deceased adoptive father] and [Deceased adoptive mother].
*** Declared [Plaintiff] to be the lawful adopted child/heir of the late couple, entitled to their estate.
*** Declared that Defendants I ([Defendant I]) and II ([Party]) had committed an unlawful act.
*** Ordered Defendants I and II to surrender the portion of land in their possession (approx. 0.015 hectares) to the plaintiff in good, vacant condition.
*** Declared the sale of the approximately 22 × 15.5 metre plot by Defendants I and II to Defendant III ([Party]) invalid and void.
*** Ordered Defendant III ([Party]), and anyone claiming rights through him, to return the land to the plaintiff in good, vacant condition.
*** Dismissed the remainder of the plaintiff's claims.
** ''In reconvention:'' Declared the counterclaim inadmissible.
** ''In convention and reconvention:'' Ordered the respondents in cassation to bear all costs of proceedings at every level (cassation fee: Rp 20,000).

== Reasoning (''ratio decidendi'') ==

The Supreme Court held that the lower courts (''Judex Facti'') had '''misapplied the law''' by requiring formal adat rituals — a ''selamatan'' ceremony or notification to the village head — as a precondition for a valid adoption. Indonesian customary law, the Court reasoned, is flexible and prioritizes '''lived social fact''' over rigid procedural formality. Because [Plaintiff] was shown to have been:

* taken in and raised from the age of four months,
* circumcised by his adoptive parents, and
* married off by his adoptive father, [Deceased adoptive father],

he had thereby acquired the legal status of a lawful adopted child, carrying with it reciprocal inheritance rights with his adoptive parents. The sale of part of the marital estate by the former wife and her co-defendant, without the consent of the rightful heir, was accordingly held to be an unlawful act voiding the transaction.

== Significance ==

The decision is regarded as a leading precedent in Indonesian customary (adat) inheritance and adoption law, reinforcing the principle — earlier articulated in Supreme Court Decision No. 849 K/Sip/1977 (3 July 1980) — that the validity of an informal (adat) adoption is determined by the '''factual, lived reality of care and upbringing''', rather than by compliance with customary ceremonial or administrative formalities. It protects the inheritance rights of adopted children who have been genuinely raised and cared for by their adoptive parents from being defeated on purely procedural or documentary grounds.

== Related jurisprudence and legislation ==

* '''Supreme Court Decision No. 849 K/Sip/1977''' (3 July 1980) — establishing that the validity of child adoption is determined by the social reality of care and upbringing from childhood.
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970''' in conjunction with '''Law No. 14 of 1985''' concerning the Supreme Court — providing the Supreme Court's authority to correct errors in the application of law by lower courts (''Judex Facti'').

|-
|345.02
|-
|Dra. Dhanie Saraswati, H. [Defendant], Authentic Deed, Marriage Extract Photocopy, Article 266 KUHP, Tambelang KUA, Vrijspraak, Acquittal, Bekasi District Court, Bandung High Court
|-
|Criminal Code Articles 266(1) and (2); Civil Code (BW) Article 1868; HIR Article 165; Minister of Religious Affairs Regulation No. 2 of 1990; Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP) Law No. 8 of 1981; Law No. 14 of 1985
|}

== Overview ==
Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 144 K/Pid/2000 dated August 21, 2000, establishes fundamental Criminal Procedure and Material Criminal Law jurisprudence concerning the qualification of authentic deeds in forgery crimes: A photocopy of a Marriage Extract (*Kutipan Akta Nikah* No. 29/9/V/1992 dated May 9, 1992, issued by the Office of Religious Affairs (*KUA*) of Tambelang Sub-District, Bekasi Regency) cannot be regarded as an authentic deed under Article 266 of the KUHP jo. Article 1868 of the Civil Code (BW) / Article 165 of the HIR, inter alia, because there is no original or minute of the deed (*minit akta*), it is not excerpted from the minute of the marriage deed in the Marriage Register Book, and it fails to satisfy the requirements of Minister of Religious Affairs Regulation No. 2 of 1990. Because an authentic deed constitutes a primary element of Article 266 of the KUHP, the failure to prove this element requires the Defendant to be acquitted of all charges (*vrijspraak*).

== Case Background ==
The Defendant (Dra. Dhanie Saraswati, MSc., [age removed], private employee) was brought before the Bekasi District Court under two alternative/cumulative charges:

* '''First Charge (Article 266 paragraph (1) of the KUHP):''' Ordering the entry of false statements into an authentic deed regarding an event whose truth must be established by that deed, namely the arrangement of a marriage with reporting witness H. [Defendant] at KUA Tambelang Bekasi (Marriage Extract No. 29/9/V/1992 dated May 9, 1992).
* '''Second Charge (Article 266 paragraph (2) of the KUHP):''' Using an authentic deed whose contents appear to conform to the truth for processing a child's passport in South Jakarta.

The reporting witness (H. [Defendant]) stated that he had never married the Defendant at KUA Tambelang and felt aggrieved by the issuance of the marriage extract. The Bekasi District Court (Decision No. 31/Pid.B/1998/PN.Bks dated August 7, 1999) sentenced the Defendant to 1 (one) year of imprisonment. The Bandung High Court (Decision No. 207/PID/1999/PT.Bdg dated November 10, 1999) upheld the Bekasi District Court judgment. Dissatisfied with the appellate ruling, the Defendant filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The *Judex Facti* committed an error in applying legal regulations (violating the law) because a photocopy of Marriage Extract No. 29/9/V/1992 dated May 9, 1992, issued by KUA Tambelang Bekasi cannot be regarded as an authentic deed under Article 266 of the KUHP read in conjunction with Article 1868 of the Civil Code (BW) or Article 165 of the HIR.
# The photocopy of the marriage extract does not constitute an authentic deed because: (a) It fails to comply with the requirements under Minister of Religious Affairs Regulation No. 2 of 1990; (b) There is no original copy or minute of the deed (*minit akta*); (c) It is not excerpted from the minute of the Marriage Deed contained in the Marriage Register Book of KUA Tambelang Sub-District.
# Because the authentic deed—which constitutes an essential element of the Public Prosecutor's indictment under both the first and second charges—is unfulfilled, the Defendant is not legally and convincingly proven guilty of committing the criminal offenses charged. Consequently, the Defendant must be acquitted of those charges (*vrijspraak*).

* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation / Defendant: Dra. DHANIE SARASWATI, MSc.; Annulling the Bandung High Court decision dated November 10, 1999, No. 207/PID/1999/PT.Bdg, which upheld the Bekasi District Court decision dated August 7, 1999, No. 31/Pid.B/1998/PN.Bks; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Declaring that Defendant Dra. DHANIE SARASWATI, MSc. is not legally and convincingly proven guilty of committing the criminal offenses charged in the first and second counts; (2) Acquitting the Defendant accordingly from said charges (*vrijspraak*); (3) Ordering the restoration of the Defendant's rights in capacity, position, honor, and dignity; (4) Determining the status of evidence items; (5) Charging procedural costs across all levels of jurisdiction to the State. *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Cassation Panel of Justices on Monday, August 21, 2000, by Ny. Marianna Sutadi, S.H. [Presiding Judge], Ida Bagus Widja, S.H., and Djufri Ramli, S.H.).*

[Party A]|court=Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia (Mahkamah Agung RI)|image=|imagesize=|caption=|full name=Registration No. 1459 K/Pdt/1986|date decided=9 September 1987 (pronounced in open session); deliberated 22 July 1987|citations=1459 K/Pdt/1986|judges=Prof. Z. Asikin Kusumah Atmadja (Presiding), Goenawan, T. Boestomi|prior actions=District Court of Jayapura, No. 37/Pdt/G/1985/PN.Jpr; High Court of Jayapura, No. 38/Pdt/1985/PT.Jpr|subsequent actions=|holding=Property acquired by one spouse as a gift is separate property ("''harta bawaan''") under Article 35(2) of Law No. 1 of 1974 on Marriage, and the owning spouse may validly dispose of it, including by donation, without the other spouse's consent.|keywords=marital property law; separate property; gift/donation; land conversion; Indonesian Marriage Law}}

'''''[Party D] and [Party C] v. [Party A]''''', Registration No. '''1459 K/Pdt/1986''', is a decision of the '''Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia''' (''Mahkamah Agung RI'') concerning the legal classification of property acquired by a spouse through a family gift ("''hibah''") during marriage, and the validity of that spouse's subsequent donation of the property without the consent of their spouse. The Court held that such property constitutes '''separate property''' ("''harta bawaan''") under Article 35(2) of Law No. 1 of 1974 on Marriage, and that the owning spouse retains full authority to deal with it, including by gift, without requiring the other spouse's approval.

== Background ==
The dispute concerned a shop known as ''Toko Eng Bo Ho'', located on Jalan A. Yani, Jayapura, standing on land originally registered as ''Recht van Opstal'' (Rvo) No. 15/1954, with an area of 903 m². The plaintiff, '''[Party A]''' (the second wife of Defendant I), brought suit in the Jayapura District Court against:

* '''Defendant I''': [Party D] (her husband)
* '''Defendant II''': [Party C] (Defendant I's son from his first marriage)

The plaintiff sought to annul Deed of Gift No. 594.4/01/1984, dated 10 February 1984, by which Defendant I had donated the disputed land and building to Defendant II. She argued that the property was '''joint marital property''' (''harta bersama''), having been formalized (via Building Use Right/HGB certificate No. 60) during her marriage to Defendant I, which began in 1972.

The defendants countered that the land had in fact been transferred to Defendant I by his elder brother, '''[Party E]''', in '''1961''' — when [Party E] was preparing to return to Hong Kong — long before Defendant I's marriage to the plaintiff. Defendant I had also been previously married to '''[Party B]''' (1958–1971). The plaintiff and Defendant I were married according to Islamic law on 27 May 1972 and divorced by ''talak'' on 28 August 1984.

=== Procedural history ===

* The '''District Court of Jayapura''' (No. 37/Pdt/G/1985/PN.Jpr, 23 October 1985) partially granted the plaintiff's claim.
* The '''High Court of Jayapura''' (No. 38/Pdt/1985/PT.Jpr, 28 November 1985) affirmed the District Court's decision, holding the gift invalid and the land to be joint marital property.
* Defendants I and II filed an appeal in cassation (''kasasi'') to the Supreme Court.

== Issues ==
The Supreme Court considered two principal questions:

# Whether land and buildings whose certificate of title (or land-right conversion) was formalized '''during''' the marriage automatically become '''joint marital property''' (''harta bersama''), where the underlying origin of the property was in fact a '''family gift''' predating the marriage.
# Whether the owner of such '''separate property''' (''harta bawaan'') may validly dispose of it — including by donation to a child from a prior marriage — '''without the consent''' of the other spouse.

A subsidiary procedural issue concerned whether a general civil court (''Pengadilan Negeri'') had jurisdiction to adjudicate a claim for spousal maintenance (''nafkah'') arising from a marriage and divorce conducted under Islamic law.

== Ruling ==
The Supreme Court '''granted''' the petition for cassation filed by [Party D] and [Party C], and '''annulled''' the decision of the High Court of Jayapura. '''Adjudicating the case itself''' ("''mengadili sendiri''"), the Court:

* '''In the exception''': Declared that the District Court of Jayapura lacked jurisdiction to hear the plaintiff's claim for maintenance (''nafkah''), that claim falling within the absolute competence of the Religious Court (''Pengadilan Agama''); declared the defendants' remaining exceptions inadmissible.
* '''On the provisional claim''': Rejected the plaintiff's provisional claim.
* '''On the merits''': Rejected the plaintiff's claim '''in its entirety'''; declared the conservatory attachment (''sita jaminan'') executed by the District Court of Jayapura on 22 July 1985 (No. 37/BA.Pdt.G/1985.PN.Jpr) to be '''without legal force''', and ordered its lifting.

== Ratio decidendi ==
The Court held that the High Court of Jayapura had '''misapplied the law'''. Under '''Article 35(2) of Law No. 1 of 1974 on Marriage''', property that either spouse acquires individually as a gift, present, or inheritance remains under that spouse's exclusive control, constituting '''separate property''' (''harta bawaan''), unless the parties agree otherwise. Because the disputed land originated from a gift by Defendant I's brother in 1961 — well before Defendant I's marriage to the plaintiff — it was properly classified as Defendant I's separate property, notwithstanding that formal certification or conversion of the land right took place during the marriage.

Consequently, under '''Article 36(2)''' of the same law, Defendant I possessed '''full legal authority''' to deal with that property, including donating it to Defendant II (his son from his first marriage), '''without requiring the plaintiff's consent'''. The Deed of Gift No. 594.4/01/1984 and the resulting Building Use Right (HGB) Certificate No. 545 in Defendant II's name were accordingly held valid.

The Court further held that the '''timing of formal registration or certificate conversion''' during a marriage does not, by itself, alter the underlying legal character of property whose true origin lies in a gift or inheritance predating that formalization; courts must examine the '''actual moment of original acquisition''', not merely the date administrative documentation was issued.

== Significance ==
The decision is cited as a leading authority in Indonesian marital property law for two linked propositions:

* Property whose '''substantive origin''' is a gift or inheritance retains its character as separate property (''harta bawaan'') under Article 35(2) of Law No. 1 of 1974, even where formal land certification occurs during the marriage.
* The owner of separate property has an '''unrestricted right''' under Article 36(2) to transact regarding that property — including by gift — without the consent of a spouse.

The case is also referenced for its holding on '''absolute competence''' (''kompetensi absolut''), confirming that maintenance claims arising from marriages solemnized under Islamic law fall exclusively within the jurisdiction of the Religious Courts, not the general civil courts.

== Parties ==

* '''Petitioners for cassation / Defendants''': [Party D] (Defendant I); [Party C] (Defendant II)
* '''Respondent in cassation / Plaintiff''': [Party A], of Kotaraja, Jayapura

== See also ==

* Law No. 1 of 1974 on Marriage (Indonesia)
* Basic Agrarian Law (Law No. 5 of 1960)
* Marital property law in Indonesia

== References ==

* Yurisprudensi Mahkamah Agung RI, ''Putusan No. 1459 K/Pdt/1986'', pp. 57–95.
* Law No. 1 of 1974 on Marriage, Arts. 35–36.
* Law No. 5 of 1960 on Basic Agrarian Regulations (UUPA).

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 145 K/TUN/2002 dated October 2, 2003, establishes fundamental jurisprudence and legal rules regarding the limits of judicial authority in civil service disciplinary execution disputes: Under Civil Service Laws, the determination of the effective date of a rank demotion sanction falls within the authority of the respective administrative official (State Administrative Official / BAPEK); however, an error by the State Administrative High Court in determining the effective date of the sanction does not invalidate the High Court's decision and can be remedied simply by amending its ruling.

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiff / Respondent for Cassation ([Party A], S.Sos., Civil Servant Head of PMD Section at the Poasia Sub-District Office, Kendari Municipality) was subjected to a disciplinary punishment of Dishonorable Discharge as a Civil Servant pursuant to the Decree of the Minister of Home Affairs No. 815.488.2701 dated July 15, 1998 jo. Decree of BAPEK No. 007/KPTS/BAPEK/2000 dated February 15, 2000. This punishment was imposed because the Plaintiff violated Government Regulation No. 30 of 1980 (having multiple wives / cohabiting without a valid marriage with two women named [Party B] and Waode Aziza). Regarding this violation, the Plaintiff had expressed remorse, received guidance from his direct superior (the Poasia Sub-District Head), both women signed statements declaring they would not make claims, and the first wife ([Party C]) divorced the Plaintiff at the Kendari Religious Court (Divorce Certificate No. 08/AC/1999/PA Kendari).

The Plaintiff filed a lawsuit against BAPEK's decree at the Jakarta State Administrative High Court. The Jakarta State Administrative High Court (Decision No. 45/G/2001/PT.TUN.JKT dated August 22, 2001) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part, annulled BAPEK's decree, and ordered BAPEK to change the disciplinary punishment to a Rank Demotion by one level for a maximum of 1 year effective as of February 15, 2000. Dissatisfied with the ruling, BAPEK filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The consideration of the Jakarta State Administrative High Court in altering the disciplinary sanction from dishonorable discharge to a rank demotion by one level for 1 year was accurate and correct, given the facts of administrative guidance and the Plaintiff's expression of remorse.
# The Jakarta State Administrative High Court committed an error in applying the law by determining the effective date of the rank demotion sanction (as of February 15, 2000), because under Civil Service Laws, determining the effective date of rank demotion is the prerogative of the respective administrative official (State Administrative Official / BAPEK).
# Nevertheless, this error does not invalidate the judgment of the Jakarta State Administrative High Court and can be sufficiently remedied by deleting the clause specifying the effective date of the sanction from the dispositive portion of the ruling.
* '''Ruling:''' Rejecting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation THE CHAIRMAN OF THE CIVIL SERVICE ADVISORY BOARD (*KETUA BADAN PERTIMBANGAN KEPEGAWAIAN*), with an amendment to the Jakarta State Administrative High Court decision dated August 22, 2001, No. 45/G/2001/PT.TUN.JKT concerning the 3rd dispositive item by omitting the phrase "as of February 15, 2000", so that the dispositive ruling reads as follows: (1) Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part; (2) Declaring null and void the Decree of the Defendant Number: 007/KPTS/BAPEK/2000 dated February 15, 2000; (3) Ordering the Defendant to issue a new decree altering the disciplinary punishment imposed upon the Plaintiff, [Party A], S.Sos., a Civil Servant at the Poasia Sub-District Office, Kendari Municipality, from dishonorable discharge not at own request as a Civil Servant to a Rank Demotion to the adjacent lower rank for a maximum of 1 (one) year; (4) Rejecting the remainder of the lawsuit; (5) Ordering the Petitioner for Cassation to pay cassation-level court costs amounting to Rp 200,000 (two hundred thousand rupiahs). *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court on Thursday, October 2, 2003, by the Cassation Panel of Justices: Prof. Dr. Paulus Effendi Lotulung, SH. [Junior Chairman for State Administrative Chamber / Presiding Judge], Iskandar Kamil, SH., and Ny. Chairani A. Wani, SH. [Associate Justices]).*

{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 1498 K/Pdt/2006}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 1498 K/Pdt/2006''' (dated January 23, 2008) is a landmark Indonesian civil procedure and land law jurisprudence precedent establishing three vital legal rules regarding the admissibility of photocopies of photocopies under specific circumstances, the burden of proof for land sale validity based on the principle of fairness (''billijkheid beginsel''), and the nullity of land transfer deeds executed under power of attorney originating from a deceased person.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established three primary legal principles:

# '''Admissibility of Photocopies of Photocopies (Article 1888 of the Civil Code):''' Under specific circumstances, documentary evidence in the form of a photocopy of a photocopy is admissible and assessable as valid evidence if used to support and reinforce the opposing party's admission (i.e., Respondent for Cassation / Defendant III / PT Pertamina Tbk.), which acknowledged that the disputed land originally belonged to the Petitioner for Cassation's / Plaintiff's parent (the late [Plaintiff's parent]).
# '''Burden of Proof for Land Transfer Validity (Billijkheid Beginsel):''' To prove whether the transfer or sale of the disputed land occurred correctly and validly under the law, pursuant to the principle of equity and fairness (''billijkheid beginsel''), the burden of proof rests upon the buyer (i.e., Respondent for Cassation / Defendant III), as the buyer is in a better position to prove the validity of the legal title and the chain of transfer transactions.
# '''Nullity by Operation of Law of Power of Attorney from a Deceased Person and Subsequent Transfers:''' A land transfer power of attorney dated June 13, 1970, from [Plaintiff's parent] to Defendant I is null and void and without legal force because the principal ([Plaintiff's parent]) was proven to have passed away in 1963. Consequently, Land Release Deed No. 25 dated June 20, 1970, and Agreement Deed No. 11 dated May 22, 1970, contain an absolute legal defect (''nemo plus iuris''), ordering Defendant III to return the 1,500 m² disputed land (Girik C No. 721) to the Plaintiff.

The Supreme Court granted the Plaintiff's ([Party A]) cassation petition, annulled the Jakarta High Court Decision No. 234/Pdt/2005/PT.DKI jo. Central Jakarta District Court Decision No. 164/Pdt.G/2004/PN.Jkt.Pst, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Evidentiary Weight of Documentary Evidence in the Form of a Photocopy of a Photocopy (Article 1888 of the Civil Code jo. Opposing Party Admission) ===
''Is the High Court justified in rejecting photocopy-of-photocopy evidence absolutely based on Supreme Court Decision No. 701 K/Sip/1976, even though such photocopies were used to support Defendant III's admission that the disputed land originally belonged to the Plaintiff's parents?''

'''Supreme Court Rule:''' Admissible (Exception to Photocopy Rules). The Jakarta High Court erred in applying the law by dismissing the Central Jakarta District Court's judgment without adequately evaluating the evidentiary context (''onvoldoende gemotiveerd''). The doctrine of Article 1888 of the Civil Code restricting photocopies is not absolute when a photocopy of a photocopy is presented to support the express admission of the opposing party (Defendant III). Because Defendant III acknowledged that the land originally belonged to [Plaintiff's parent], the existence of such photocopy evidence is valid and legally binding.

=== 2. Allocation of Burden of Proof Based on Equity (''Billijkheid Beginsel'' / Fairness Principle in Burden of Proof) ===
When disputed land is proven to have originally belonged to the Plaintiff's parents and the Plaintiff asserts that the land has never been validly compensated or sold, pursuant to the principle of fairness (''billijkheid beginsel''), the burden of proving that the land transfer occurred lawfully and in good faith rests upon the buyer (Defendant III), as the buyer is in a better position to command transaction documents.

=== 3. Unlawful Acts (Tort ex Article 1365 of the Civil Code) and Absolute Legal Defect of Land Transfers Originating from False Powers of Attorney (''Nemo Plus Iuris'') ===
The execution of a Power of Attorney dated June 13, 1970, in the name of [Plaintiff's parent]—who had already passed away in 1963—constitutes a tort embodying an absolute legal defect. Pursuant to the principle ''nemo plus iuris ad alium transferre potest quam ipse habet'' (no one can transfer greater rights than they possess), all derivative deeds originating from such fraudulent power of attorney (Land Release Deed No. 25 jo. Agreement Deed No. 11 jo. Amendment Deed No. 2) are null and void and without binding legal force.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
Did the Jakarta High Court err in applying the law of evidence (Article 1888 of the Civil Code) and issue an inadequately reasoned decision (''onvoldoende gemotiveerd'') by rejecting photocopy-of-photocopy evidence supported by Defendant III's admission while disregarding the absolute legal defect of a power of attorney executed by a deceased person?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. The Jakarta High Court erred in applying the law. The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of Plaintiff [Party A], annulled Jakarta High Court Decision No. 234/Pdt/2005/PT.DKI dated September 29, 2005, and independently adjudicated by adopting the reasoning of Central Jakarta District Court Decision No. 164/Pdt.G/2004/PN.Jkt.Pst: granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part, declaring the Plaintiff the lawful owner of Girik C No. 721 covering 1,500 m², and ordering Defendant III to return the disputed land.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Central Jakarta District Court & Jakarta High Court) ===
Examination of ownership facts regarding the inheritance land of the late [Plaintiff's parent] covering 2,280 m² (Parcel 55 a, Girik C No. 718) in Kampung Guji, Duri Kepa, Kebon Jeruk, West Jakarta; the 12-hectare land acquisition by Defendant III (Pertamina) in 1970; the issuance of subdivided Girik C No. 721 covering 1,500 m² in the name of [Plaintiff's parent]; facts concerning the death of [Plaintiff's parent] in 1963 based on Inheritance Distribution Deed No. 296/APW/1992/PA.JB and Certificate of Heirs dated May 8, 2003, corroborated by witness testimonies of [Party B] and Amsir bin H. Musa; the forgery of the Power of Attorney dated June 13, 1970, to Defendant I; the issuance of Land Release Deed No. 25 dated June 20, 1970, before Deputy Notary Ambrosius Sitompul, S.H.; Agreement Deed No. 11 dated May 22, 1970, jo. Amendment Deed No. 2 dated October 10, 1970, before Notary Januar Hamid, S.H.; and facts of land occupation by Defendant III since 1971.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===

* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata):'''
** Article 1888: Evidentiary weight of documentary evidence / photocopies.
** Articles 1328 & 1335: Nullity of agreements arising from false / prohibited causes (''causa'').
** Article 1365: Unlawful Acts (''Perbuatan Melawan Hukum'' / Tort).
** Article 834: Inheritance Rights (''Hereditatis Petitio'').
* '''Law No. 4 of 2004 jo. Law No. 14 of 1985 jo. Law No. 5 of 2004 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation authority & independent adjudication powers.

=== Doctrines & Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===

* ''Billijkheid Beginsel'' in Evidence: Placing the burden of proof upon the party best positioned to prove it (fairness in burden of proof).
* Principle of ''Nemo Plus Iuris'': Legal defects in foundational root titles vitiate the validity of all derivative rights.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* [Plaintiff's parent] alias Amit bin Kibi was legally proven to have passed away in 1963.
* The Power of Attorney dated June 13, 1970, in the name of the late [Plaintiff's parent] to Defendant I is forged and null and void.
* Land Release Deed No. 25 dated June 20, 1970, and Agreement Deed No. 11 dated May 22, 1970, jo. Amendment Deed No. 2 dated October 10, 1970, are null and without legal force.
* The Plaintiff ([Party A]) is the lawful owner of the disputed land under Girik C No. 721, Parcel 55 d, covering 1,500 m² in Duri Kepa, Kebon Jeruk, West Jakarta.
* Defendants I, II, and III are proven to have committed Tort (''Perbuatan Melawan Hukum'').
* Defendant III (PT Pertamina Tbk.) is ordered to return the original Girik C No. 721 and surrender the 1,500 m² disputed land to the Plaintiff unconditionally (if necessary, with State police assistance).

=== Rejected / Dismissed Claims ===

* Claims for material lease compensation of Rp 200,000/m²/year, compound profit of 3%, immaterial damages of Rp 1 Billion, and daily penalty fines (''dwangsom'') of Rp 3 Million/day were rejected by the Supreme Court.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Revision of Boundaries and Physical Area of Disputed Land on Site:''' This landmark ruling definitively affirms ownership rights over Girik C No. 721 covering 1,500 m². However, executing physical surrender of a 1,500 m² plot within an 8-hectare perimeter fenced and occupied by PT Pertamina Tbk. since 1971 requires physical verification (''konstatering'') by the National Land Agency (BPN) based on boundaries set forth in the court verdict.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
;Can photocopy-of-photocopy evidence be admitted in court, and who bears the burden of proof for a land sale when the seller's power of attorney turns out to be from a deceased person?
:'''Admissible, and the buyer bears the burden of proof (Billijkheid Beginsel).''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 1498 K/Pdt/2006:

* Documentary evidence consisting of a photocopy of a photocopy is admissible as valid evidence when used to support the opposing party's admission that the land originally belonged to the Plaintiff's parents.
* Pursuant to the principle of fairness (''billijkheid beginsel''), the buyer (Defendant) bears the burden of proving the validity of the land sale because the buyer is in a better position to prove it.
* A land transfer power of attorney executed by a deceased person is null and void by operation of law, making all derivative transfer deeds an absolute legal defect, obligating the buyer to return the land to the lawful heirs.

Pursuant to the fairness principle (billijkheid beginsel), the burden of proof for the validity of the land sale rested upon Defendant III. Trial proceedings established that [Plaintiff's parent] passed away in 1963, making the Power of Attorney dated June 13, 1970, forged and null and void. All derivative deeds (Deed No. 25 & Deed No. 11) contained an absolute legal defect (nemo plus iuris). Defendant III failed to prove its legal title lawfully. The Supreme Court granted Plaintiff [Party A]'s cassation petition, annulled the Jakarta High Court decision, and independently adjudicated by granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part and ordering Defendant III to return the 1,500 m² disputed land.",

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:1506K PDT 2002
wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 1506 K/Pdt/2002}} '''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 1506 K/Pdt/2002''' (dated September 23, 2004) is a foundational Indonesian contract and commercial sales jurisprudence precedent establishing fundamental rules regarding the binding force of a Purchase Order (PO) signed by both parties and the forfeiture of the right to object to goods' quality upon exceeding an agreed contractual complaint deadline:
"A Purchase Order (P.O.) signed by both binding parties constitutes an agreement thus acting as law binding both parties ''ex'' Articles 1320, 1338, 1457, and 1458 of the Civil Code. If the P.O. has agreed that complaints regarding goods' quality/grade must be submitted by the buyer no later than 1 (one) week after the goods are received, and the buyer has accepted delivery without written proof of objection/complaint within such 7 (seven) day deadline, then the buyer's action of withholding payment on the grounds that the goods are not according to specifications (rejected) is classified as Default (''Wanprestasi''). The buyer is ordered to pay in cash and in full the entire price of the ordered goods along with damages interest of 6% per annum."
The Supreme Court granted the Plaintiff's (PT Greges Jaya) cassation petition, annulled the Bandung High Court Decision No. 147/Pdt/2001/PT.Bdg jo. Bekasi District Court Decision No. 153/Pdt.G/2000/PN.Bks, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part, declaring PT Amindo Pacific Industries in default, and ordering the Defendant to pay damages of US$ 74,388.15 plus 6% annual interest. == Infobox == {| class="wikitable" |- ! Object ID | JPAIS:PRECEDENT:1506K_PDT_2002 |- ! Mode | MODE 1 — BHT KNOWLEDGE (Extract Verified Knowledge from Final Cases) |- ! Pipeline Stage | SOURCE (1506K_PDT_2002.pdf) → EVIDENCE (Supreme Court Jurisprudence 2004, pp. 105–118) → CLAIM (Binding Force of Purchase Order Ex Article 1338 jo 1458 Civil Code & Forfeiture of Quality Complaint Rights Past 7-Day Deadline) → KNOWLEDGE OBJECT (JPAIS Precedent Schema) → RELATIONSHIP (Annulment of Bandung High Court Decision No. 147/Pdt/2001/PT.Bdg & Bekasi District Court Decision No. 153/Pdt.G/2000/PN.Bks & Independent Adjudication Granting Default Damages of US$ 74,388.15) → GEO ANSWER → HUMAN VERIFICATION (Mark Cecep Mustafa) |- ! Judicial Institution | Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia (''Judex Juris'') |- ! Registry Number | Reg. No. 1506 K/Pdt/2002 |- ! Decision Date | September 23, 2004 |- ! Judicial Chamber | General Civil Law / Law of Obligations & Commercial Sales |- ! Panel of Justices | * Iskandar Kamil, S.H. (Junior Chairman of the Supreme Court / Presiding Judge) * Prof. Rehngena Purba, S.H., M.S. (Associate Justice) * Prof. Dr. H. Muchsin, S.H. (Associate Justice) * Sutedjo Bomantoro, S.H., M.H. (Substitute Registrar) |- ! Grapher & Verification | Mark Cecep Mustafa (Verified Knowledge Grapher) — '''Status: VERIFIED''' |} == Claims, Evidence, and Sources == {| class="wikitable" |- ! # !! Claim (Legal Statement / Fact) !! Evidence (Case File / Legal Reasoning) !! Source / Passage |- | 1 | '''Core Legal Principle (Binding Force of PO Ex Article 1338/1458 Civil Code):''' A Purchase Order signed by both parties constitutes a valid agreement binding as law. | Jurisprudence Headnote p. 105 & Supreme Court Reasoning pp. 105, 115: "A Purchase Order signed by both binding parties constitutes an agreement thus acting as law binding both parties." | 1506K_PDT_2002.pdf |- | 2 | '''Forfeiture of Quality Complaint Rights:''' The buyer failed to lodge objections within the agreed 7-day deadline in the PO, rendering payment withholding an act of default. | Supreme Court Legal Reasoning pp. 106, 115, 116: "Complaints regarding quality and others shall be made by the recipient of the goods no later than 1 week... There is no proof of objection during the 7 days of each goods delivery... thus the respondent for cassation is in default." | 1506K_PDT_2002.pdf |- | 3 | '''Delivery Facts & Payment Impasse:''' The Plaintiff shipped timber 7 times (Feb 26–Apr 11, 2000). Shipment I was paid (US$ 23,671.05), but shipments II to VII stalled, totaling US$ 74,388.15. | Claim Posita pp. 108, 109 & Reasoning pp. 105, 115: The Defendant received timber shipments I to VII but refused to pay the remaining order balance of US$ 74,388.15 on unreasonable grounds. | 1506K_PDT_2002.pdf |- | 4 | '''Error of Judex Facti District and High Courts:''' Bekasi District Court (No. 153/Pdt.G/2000/PN.Bks) and Bandung High Court (No. 147/Pdt/2001/PT.Bdg) erred in dismissing the Plaintiff's lawsuit entirely. | District Court Verdict p. 113 & High Court p. 114: The District and High Courts validated the Defendant's unilateral rejection of goods without considering the PO complaint deadline. | 1506K_PDT_2002.pdf |- | 5 | '''Obligation to Pay Damages Interest:''' The Defendant is ordered to pay outstanding arrears of US$ 74,388.15 plus 6% annual interest from the date the lawsuit was registered. | Supreme Court Verdict pp. 106, 117: "...ordering the respondent for cassation / original defendant to pay in cash and in full... the amount of US$ 74,388.15 and damages of 6% per annum calculated from the filing of the lawsuit..." | 1506K_PDT_2002.pdf |- | 6 | '''Validity of Protective Attachment:''' The protective attachment over 4 lathe machines, 3 Outo Sander machines, and 38.0654 m³ of timber at the Defendant's factory is declared valid and lawful. | Supreme Court Verdict pp. 106, 117: "Declaring valid and lawful the protective attachment against 4 units of lathe machines, 3 units of Outo Sander machines, and 38.0654 Mm³ of timber executed by the Bekasi District Court." | 1506K_PDT_2002.pdf |- | 7 | '''Identity of Parties:''' Petitioner for Cassation / Plaintiff: PT GREGES JAYA (Surabaya / H.M. Raharjo); Respondent for Cassation / Defendant: PT AMINDO PACIFIC INDUSTRIES (Cikarang, Bekasi). | Confirmed in decision identity p. 108. | 1506K_PDT_2002.pdf |} == Legal / Procedural Issues == === 1. Juridical Construction of a Purchase Order (P.O.) as a Binding Contract (''Pacta Sunt Servanda'' ex Article 1338 jo. Article 1458 of the Civil Code) === ''Does a Purchase Order (P.O.) issued and signed by both parties (buyer and seller) possess complete legally binding force as a commercial sales agreement contract?'' ==== Supreme Court Rule: Binding Perfectly as Law ==== Pursuant to Articles 1320, 1338, 1457, and 1458 of the Civil Code, a sales obligation is established and legally binding upon achieving consensus regarding goods and price, embodied in a P.O. signed by both parties. Terms stipulated in the P.O. become mandatory law adhered to by both parties (''pacta sunt servanda''). === 2. Forfeiture of the Right to Object to Goods Quality (Waiver of Quality Claims) Due to Exceeding the Contractual Complaint Deadline === ''Is a buyer who has physically accepted goods delivery permitted to withhold payment on the grounds that the goods fail to meet specifications (rejected), despite the P.O. having stipulated a maximum complaint deadline of 1 week and the buyer having failed to lodge a complaint within such deadline?'' ==== Supreme Court Rule: Quality Complaint Right Forfeited (Payment Obligation Enforceable) ==== If a P.O. establishes a clause requiring quality complaints to be submitted no later than 1 week after goods receipt, and trial evidence establishes that goods were received without written complaint notices within the 7-day window, the buyer is deemed to have accepted the goods properly, and the right to object is legally forfeited. Withholding payment based on subsequent unilateral rejection claims constitutes Default (''Wanprestasi''). === 3. Error in Judicando by Judex Facti in Assessing Commercial Trade Default === Bekasi District Court and Bandung High Court misapplied the law by setting aside the PO complaint deadline clause and validating unilateral payment cancellations by the buyer. The Supreme Court annulled the ''Judex Facti'' decisions and granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit to restore commercial contract legal certainty. == Question of Law vs Question of Fact == === Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) === Did the ''Judex Facti'' (Bandung High Court Decision No. 147/Pdt/2001/PT.Bdg jo. Bekasi District Court Decision No. 153/Pdt.G/2000/PN.Bks) err in applying the law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') by dismissing the Plaintiff's default lawsuit, despite the PO signed by the parties binding as law (Article 1338 of the Civil Code) and the Defendant's failure to raise quality objections within the agreed 7-day PO deadline? '''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. The ''Judex Facti'' erred in applying the law. The Supreme Court granted PT Greges Jaya's cassation petition, annulled Bandung High Court Decision No. 147/Pdt/2001/PT.Bdg jo. Bekasi District Court Decision No. 153/Pdt.G/2000/PN.Bks, and independently adjudicated by declaring PT Amindo Pacific Industries in default, ordering the Defendant to pay US$ 74,388.15 plus 6% annual interest, and declaring the protective attachment valid. === Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Bekasi District Court & Bandung High Court) === Examination of facts regarding the issuance of P.O. No. API-GSJ/1332000 dated February 13, 2000; delivery of Ramin S4S timber 7 times between February 26 and April 11, 2000; payment proof for shipment I amounting to US$ 23,671.05; receipt of shipments II through VII at the Cikarang Bekasi factory without quality complaint letters within 7 days; total outstanding invoice value of US$ 74,388.15; and attachment enforcement over lathe machines, Outo Sander machines, and timber at the Defendant's factory location. == Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge == === Civil Code (KUHPerdata) === * Article 1320: Requirements for Valid Agreements (Consensus, Capacity, Specific Object, Lawful Cause). * Article 1338: Principle of ''Pacta Sunt Servanda'' (Agreements act as law for the parties). * Articles 1457 & 1458: Sales Obligations and Timing of Contractual Formation. * Articles 1460, 1504, & 1507: Hidden Defects & Buyer's Obligation to Object Within Time Limits. === Law No. 4 of 2004 jo. Law No. 5 of 2004 jo. Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court === * Cassation authority and independent adjudication powers over civil cases. == What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish == === Established by Evidence === * Purchase Order No. API-GSJ/1332000 dated February 13, 2000, constitutes a valid and binding sales contract between PT Greges Jaya and PT Amindo Pacific Industries. * The Defendant (PT Amindo Pacific Industries) was proven to have received timber shipments (shipments I through VII) from the Plaintiff. * The Defendant never submitted written quality complaints or objections within the 1-week (7-day) deadline mandated in the P.O. * The Defendant was proven to have committed Default (''Wanprestasi'') by failing to pay outstanding timber price arrears valued at US$ 74,388.15. * The Defendant is ordered to pay in cash US$ 74,388.15 plus moratory interest of 6% per annum from the date the lawsuit was filed. * Protective attachment (''conservatoir beslag'') over 4 lathe machines, 3 Outo Sander machines, and 38.0654 m³ of timber belonging to the Defendant is declared valid and lawful. === Rejected / Dismissed Claims === * Claims for immaterial damages of Rp 500,000,000 and expected profits of 5%/month were rejected by the Supreme Court as insufficiently proven. == Uncertainties and Gaps == '''Execution of Foreign Currency (USD) Debt Collection Against Defendant Assets:''' This landmark ruling decisively provides certainty in international/domestic export-import commercial transactions denominated in USD by ordering the buyer to pay the contract currency nominal amount (US$ 74,388.15) alongside 6% interest. Upon execution, the protective attachment over factory machinery and timber inventory serves as real collateral guaranteeing fulfillment of such foreign currency obligations. == Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) == ;Does a Purchase Order (PO) bind as a valid agreement, and can a buyer refuse to pay for goods on grounds of poor quality after the complaint deadline has expired? :'''Purchase Orders bind validly, and buyers cannot refuse payment.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 1506 K/Pdt/2002: :* A Purchase Order (P.O.) signed by seller and buyer is a valid agreement acting as law for both parties ''ex'' Article 1338 jo. 1458 of the Civil Code. :* If a P.O. agrees on a maximum quality complaint deadline of 1 week after goods receipt, and the buyer accepts goods without filing written complaints within such 7-day deadline, the buyer's right to complain is legally forfeited. :* A buyer withholding payment past the complaint deadline is classified as committing Default (''Wanprestasi'') and is ordered to pay the full invoice value in cash plus 6% annual damages interest. == Structured Data (JSON-LD) == == Notes == Mark Cecep Mustafa — Verified Knowledge Grapher for human verification of structure, provenance, claim-evidence linkage, relationships, metadata, and citation readiness. '''Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 1542 K/Pid.Sus/2008''' (28 January 2009) is a landmark [[Indonesia]]n [[environmental law|environmental]] and [[criminal procedure|criminal procedure law]] ruling of the [[Supreme Court of Indonesia|Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia]] (''Mahkamah Agung RI''). The decision established three important legal principles: (1) the admissibility of cassation (''kasasi'') against a "non-pure acquittal" (''niet-zuivere vrijspraak'') under Article 244 of the Indonesian Code of Criminal Procedure (KUHAP); (2) the criminal liability of an operational manager (an "Acting Resident Manager") for corporate environmental pollution; and (3) an absolute prohibition on the disposal of foreign-origin hazardous and toxic waste (''limbah B3'') into Indonesia's environment.

The Court granted the cassation petition filed by the Public Prosecutor of the Batam District Attorney's Office, overturned the acquittal issued by the Batam District Court, and, ruling on the merits itself, convicted the defendant, '''[Defendant]''', of the crime of "environmental pollution," sentencing him to three years' imprisonment and a fine of Rp 30,000,000 (thirty million rupiah), with six months' imprisonment in lieu of payment.

== Background ==

The defendant, [Defendant] ([age removed], born [details removed]), served as Acting Resident Manager and head of the Hotel Batam View Beach Resort, operated by PT. Horizon Bandiar Bahru. Beginning in April 2003, the hotel had a waste-disposal contract with [Contractor] (of CV. Andi Bangun Wahana) to collect waste originating from the gambling/cruise vessel ''Leisure World'', which operated in international waters in the Strait of Malacca, and transport it by wooden ''pompong'' boat (12 tons, Yanmark 16 HP engine) to a waste collection site at Kampung Trai Nongsa, Batam, without an official permit.

The defendant, who took over operational leadership of the hotel from predecessors Svein Moldskred and Gerald Lim, approved continuation of the contract and approved an increase in the transport fee from SGD 100 to SGD 110 per trip in January 2006. Monthly payments of approximately USD 39,710 were made through the hotel's cashier, I Nyoman Suta Aryana.

On 27 January 2007, the Riau Islands Regional Police (Polda Kepri) raided the site. Forensic laboratory analysis by the Indonesian National Police Criminal Investigation Agency (Puslabfor Bareskrim Polri), recorded in Laboratory Report No. LAB.623/KTF/2007 (12 March 2007), found that solid waste samples (oil sludge and paint residue) contained zinc (Zn) at 58.50 mg/l and lead (Pb) at 9.42 mg/l, both exceeding the Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP) quality standards under Government Regulation No. 85 of 1999.

The defendant was charged, cumulatively/alternatively, under Article 41(1), Article 43(1), and Article 42(1) in conjunction with Article 45 and Article 20(2) of Law No. 23 of 1997 on Environmental Management, in conjunction with Government Regulation No. 85 of 1999, in conjunction with Article 55(1)(1) and Article 64(1) of the Indonesian Penal Code (KUHP).

== Trial court decision ==

The Batam District Court, in Decision No. 846/PID.B/2007/PN.BTM (4 June 2008), acquitted the defendant of all charges (''vrijspraak''), reasoning that he was not a member of the board of directors (''Direksi'') of PT. Horizon Bandiar Bahru and therefore could not be held criminally liable — an ''error in persona'' defense based on an interpretation of Article 103 of Law No. 40 of 2007 on Limited Liability Companies.

The Public Prosecutor of the Batam District Attorney's Office filed a petition for cassation with the Supreme Court.

== Issues ==

=== Admissibility of cassation against an acquittal ===
Whether the Public Prosecutor could file a cassation petition against a district court decision acquitting the defendant of all charges, and whether the Supreme Court had authority to overturn that acquittal.

=== Criminal liability of an operational manager ===
Whether an Acting Resident Manager/hotel manager who is not a member of the board of directors of the corporation can be held criminally liable for environmental pollution arising from the corporation's hazardous-waste transport contract.

=== Legal classification of the waste disposal ===
Whether the unlicensed transport of waste from a foreign-flagged vessel in international waters to a site on Indonesian soil constitutes unlawful "environmental pollution" under Indonesian law.

== Holding ==

=== Admissibility of cassation against a "non-pure" acquittal ===
The Supreme Court held that it has authority to review, examine, and overturn a district court's acquittal in the interest of law and justice where the acquittal was based on a mistaken interpretation of law (a "non-pure acquittal," or ''niet-zuivere vrijspraak''). The Court found that the Batam District Court had erred in treating the case as one of mistaken identity of the responsible party (''error in persona'') on the ground that the defendant was not a director of PT. Horizon Bandiar Bahru, when in fact the defendant, as Acting Resident Manager and head of the Hotel Batam View, held full operational control and actively approved the extension and fee increase of the hazardous-waste transport arrangement.

This holding relied on established Supreme Court jurisprudence, including Decisions No. 275 K/Pid/1983, No. 892 K/Pid/1983, No. 532 K/Pid/1984, and No. 449 K/Pid/1985, as well as Supreme Court Letter No. MA/Pemb/2651/83 and Ministry of Justice Decree No. M.14-PW.07.03 of 1983, on the admissibility of prosecutorial cassation against non-pure acquittals under Article 244 of the KUHAP.

=== Criminal liability of the operational manager ===
The Court held that a company's operational leader or manager who possesses full authority over operational activities, approves payments, and continues an unlicensed waste-transport contract from a foreign vessel to Indonesian soil is criminally liable, as the party responsible for the activity, for the resulting environmental pollution, under Article 20 in conjunction with Articles 41, 42, and 43, in conjunction with Article 45, of Law No. 23 of 1997 on Environmental Management.

The Court reasoned that criminal liability for corporate environmental offenses cannot be confined to a company's formally registered board of directors; any officer or manager who holds factual operational control over business activities and approves conduct that pollutes the environment may be held individually criminally liable as the party responsible for the activity.

=== Prohibition on disposal of foreign-origin waste ===
The Court held that Article 20 of Law No. 23 of 1997 absolutely prohibits any person or business entity from bringing in and disposing of waste — including hazardous and toxic waste such as oil sludge, used oil, and paint residue containing zinc (Zn) and lead (Pb) in excess of TCLP quality standards — originating from outside Indonesian territory (here, from the vessel ''Leisure World'' in the Strait of Malacca) into Indonesia's environment (here, the waste site at Kampung Trai Nongsa, Batam).

== Disposition ==

The Supreme Court:
# Granted the cassation petition of the Public Prosecutor of the Batam District Attorney's Office;
# Overturned Batam District Court Decision No. 846/PID.B/2007/PN.BTM of 4 June 2008;
# Ruling on the merits itself (''mengadili sendiri''):
#* Declared the defendant, [Defendant], legally and convincingly guilty of the crime of "Environmental Pollution";
#* Sentenced the defendant to three years' imprisonment and a fine of Rp 30,000,000 (thirty million rupiah), with six months' imprisonment in lieu of payment of the fine;
#* Ordered forfeiture and destruction of evidentiary items (used work equipment, hardened paint cans, used oil jerry cans, etc.) and forfeiture to the State of one 12-ton wooden ''pompong'' boat (Yanmark 16 HP engine); ordered return of receipts, invoices, and permit/contract documents to their rightful owners;
#* Ordered the defendant to bear the costs of proceedings at all levels (cassation costs: Rp 2,500).

== Legal provisions cited ==
* Law No. 23 of 1997 on Environmental Management (''Undang-Undang No. 23 Tahun 1997 tentang Pengelolaan Lingkungan Hidup''), Articles 20, 41, 42, 43, and 45
* Government Regulation No. 18 of 1999, as amended by Government Regulation No. 85 of 1999, on Management of Hazardous and Toxic Waste (B3)
* Law No. 8 of 1981 on the Code of Criminal Procedure (KUHAP), Articles 244 and 253(1)(a)
* Indonesian Penal Code (KUHP), Article 55(1)(1) and Article 64(1)
* Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court, as amended by Law No. 5 of 2004 and Law No. 3 of 2009

== Significance ==
The decision is frequently cited in Indonesian environmental and corporate criminal law for two propositions: first, that a prosecutor may seek cassation against an acquittal that rests on an erroneous legal interpretation (a "non-pure acquittal"), and second, that criminal liability for corporate environmental pollution extends beyond a company's formal board of directors to any manager or officer with factual operational control over the polluting activity.

{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 154 K/Pdt/2012}} '''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 154 K/Pdt/2012''' (dated May 31, 2012) is a fundamental civil law and marital property jurisprudence precedent established under Chief Justice Decree No. 45/KMA/SK/III/2014 concerning the Supreme Court Jurisprudence Compilation. It establishes vital rules regarding the legal standing (''persona standi in judicio'') of children to sue their parents over joint marital property (''harta gono-gini'') that has been gifted (''hibah''), the prohibition of unilateral revocation of gifts, and the qualification of default (breach of contract) and tort (''perbuatan melawan hukum'' / PMH) when parents sell gifted property. == Executive Summary == The Supreme Court established three primary legal principles: # '''Children's Right to Sue Parents Over Gifted Marital Property:''' "Children can sue their parents over joint marital property (''harta gono-gini'') that has been gifted to the children prior to the divorce of both parents." # '''Prohibition of Unilateral Gift Revocation:''' "A gift of joint marital property executed by both parents to their children cannot be withdrawn or revoked, except for reasons restrictively regulated under Article 1688 of the Civil Code (BW)." A unilateral Deed of Gift Revocation drawn up before a Notary is null and void (''nietig''). # '''Default and Tort Qualification of Parents:''' "Parents who fail to hand down joint marital property that has been gifted constitute a default, and the alienation or sale of such gifted joint marital property by parents to third parties without the children's consent constitutes an unlawful act (Tort / PMH)." The Supreme Court rejected the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation (H. [Party A]) and affirmed Surabaya High Court Decision No. 646/PDT/2010/PT.SBY dated January 9, 2011, ''jo.'' Banyuwangi District Court Decision No. 119/PDT.G/2008/PN.BWI dated August 6, 2009. That decision partially granted the Plaintiffs' (biological children) lawsuit, declared the Statement Letter of Marital Property Handover dated September 17, 1996, valid, declared the land sales to Defendants IV, V, and VI null and void, and ordered Defendants I and II to evacuate and surrender the disputed object to the Plaintiffs. == Infobox == {| class="wikitable" |- ! scope="row" | Object ID | JPAIS:PRECEDENT:154K_PDT_2012 |- ! scope="row" | Mode | MODE 1 — BHT KNOWLEDGE (Extract Verified Knowledge from Final Cases) |- ! scope="row" | Provenance chain | SOURCE (Yurisprudensi Part 1 [revisi].pdf / Supreme Court Jurisprudence Compilation SK KMA No. 45/KMA/SK/III/2014) → EVIDENCE (Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. Claim (Legal Statement / Fact) !! Evidence (Case File / Legal Reasoning) !! Source / Passage |- | 1 || '''Core Legal Principle (Children's Standing to Sue):''' Children have the right to sue parents over joint marital property gifted to them prior to parental divorce. || Headnote p. 1 & Legal Rule p. 9: "Children can sue their parents over joint marital property that has been gifted to their children before the divorce of both parents occurs." || Yurisprudensi Part 1 [revisi].pdf [Passage 8, 13, 18] |- | 2 || '''Core Legal Principle (Irrevocability of Gifts):''' Gifts of joint marital property cannot be unilaterally revoked except for restrictive reasons under Article 1688 Civil Code. || Legal Rule p. 9 & Supreme Court Reasoning pp. 8, 18: "A gift of joint marital property executed by both parents to their children cannot be withdrawn or revoked, except for reasons..." || Yurisprudensi Part 1 [revisi].pdf [Passage 17, 18, 44, 45] |- | 3 || '''Dismissal of Religious Court Marital Property Lawsuits:''' Marital property lawsuits between ex-spouses in Religious Courts are dismissed if property has been gifted to children, as ownership has transferred. || Legal Rule p. 9 & Reasoning pp. 8, 18: "A wife's lawsuit against her divorced husband over joint marital property gifted to their children is declared inadmissible by the religious court..." || Yurisprudensi Part 1 [revisi].pdf [Passage 17, 18, 44] |- | 4 || '''Default and Tort Qualification:''' Parents failing to surrender gifted marital property commit a default, and alienating such property constitutes a Tort. || Legal Rule pp. 9, 10 & Reasoning pp. 8, 19: "Parents who fail to hand down joint marital property that has been gifted constitute a default, and the alienation of joint marital property... is an unlawful act." || Yurisprudensi Part 1 [revisi].pdf [Passage 14, 18, 19, 24, 45] |- | 5 || '''Facts of Joint Gift Agreement:''' Defendant I (H. [Party A]) and Defendant III ([Party D]) signed a Statement Letter of Marital Property Handover on September 17, 1996, in favor of their children. || Posita pp. 1, 13, 29, 43 & Exhibit P-2 pp. 34, 43: Plaintiffs received gifts over Disputed Object I (garden SHM 290 measuring 6,450 m²) and Disputed Object II (yard & 3 houses SHM 777 measuring 1,470 m²). || Yurisprudensi Part 1 [revisi].pdf [Passage 13, 21, 23, 29, 34, 43] |- | 6 || '''Facts of Void Unilateral Revocation Deed:''' Deed of Gift Revocation No. 1 dated April 7, 2008, by Notary Heru Ismadi, S.H., executed unilaterally without Article 1688 Civil Code grounds, holds weak evidentiary force. || Reasoning pp. 8, 18, 25, 44: Unilateral gift revocation deed set aside as conflicting with Article 1688 of the Civil Code. || Yurisprudensi Part 1 [revisi].pdf [Passage 17, 18, 25, 44] |- | 7 || '''Facts of Void Sales to Third Parties:''' Defendants I & II sold portions of gifted land (350 m² & 1,063.50 m²) to Defendants IV, V, and VI without children's consent, rendering transactions null and void. || Reasoning pp. 8, 18, 24, 45: Sale of gifted land by Defendant I without Plaintiffs' consent constitutes a Tort and void transactions. || Yurisprudensi Part 1 [revisi].pdf [Passage 14, 18, 24, 45] |- | 8 || '''Supreme Court Rejection of Cassation:''' The Supreme Court rejected H. [Party A]'s cassation petition and affirmed lower court rulings favoring the gift-recipient children. || Supreme Court Verdict pp. 5, 20, 26: "ADJUDICATES: Rejecting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation: H. [Party A]; Ordering Petitioner... to pay court costs..." || Yurisprudensi Part 1 [revisi].pdf [Passage 16, 20, 26] |- | 9 || '''Identity of Parties:''' Petitioner for Cassation / Defendant I: H. [Party A] (Banyuwangi, represented by Counsel Oesnawi, S.H.); Respondents for Cassation / Plaintiffs: [Party B], KHOBAB, HURROTUL FA'IZAH (biological children); Co-Respondents: [Party C] (Defendant II), Ny. [Party D] (Defendant III / mother), Ny. SUDIYANI (Defendant IV), Ny. ASRIYAH (Defendant V), BUANG SAPI'IE (Defendant VI). || Confirmed in decision identity pp. 11, 20, 22, 28, 29. || Yurisprudensi Part 1 [revisi].pdf [Passage 13, 20, 28, 29] |} == Legal / Procedural Issues == === 1. Legal Standing (''Persona Standi in Judicio'') of Children Suing Parents Over Gifted Marital Property === ''Do biological children possess legal standing (''persona standi in judicio'') to file civil default and tort lawsuits against their biological parents who sell or refuse to surrender joint marital property formally gifted to them?'' '''Supreme Court Rule: Possesses Legal Standing / Lawful.'''
Biological children as lawful gift recipients (''receptive legatee'' / ''rechterhebbende'') hold the right to file civil lawsuits in District Courts against their parents. Once marital property gifts are agreed upon and executed by both parents prior to divorce, ownership instantly transfers to the children, granting them full legal standing to demand physical surrender and nullify unilateral parental transactions with third parties. === 2. Absolutism of the Irrevocability Principle of Gifts (''Irrevocability of Inter Vivos Gifts'' ''ex'' Article 1688 Civil Code) === ''Can parents (donors) unilaterally cancel or revoke marital property gifts transferred to their children via a Notarial Deed/Revocation Statement?'' '''Supreme Court Rule: Cannot Be Unilaterally Revoked.'''
Pursuant to Article 1688 of the Civil Code, a completed gift cannot be revoked or annulled unilaterally unless 3 exclusive conditions are met: # non-fulfillment of gift conditions, # recipient committing or assisting in crimes against the donor's life, or # recipient refusing maintenance when the donor falls into poverty. Unilateral Notarial Revocation Deeds executed without Article 1688 grounds are null and void (''nietig'') and hold no evidentiary force. === 3. Absolute Competence Jurisdiction & Division of Authority between Religious and General District Courts === Where a Religious Court in a joint marital property partition lawsuit between ex-spouses rules that property cannot be partitioned because it was validly gifted to children, such a ruling constitutes ''res judicata'', serving as the legal foundation for District Courts to grant children's lawsuits and qualify parental retention/sales as defaults and torts. == Question of Law vs Question of Fact == === Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) === Did the ''Judex Facti'' Surabaya High Court (Decision No. 646/PDT/2010/PT.SBY) and Banyuwangi District Court (Decision No. 119/PDT.G/2008/PN.BWI) correctly apply the law (''juiste toepassing van het recht'' ''ex'' Article 1688 Civil Code) in ruling that the marital property gift agreement dated September 17, 1996, could not be unilaterally revoked by Defendant I via Notarial Deed No. 1/2008, and declaring sales of gifted land to third parties unlawful? '''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. The ''Judex Facti'' reasoning was correct and aligned with the law. Marital property gifts to children cannot be unilaterally revoked, and selling gifted land without children's consent constitutes a Tort. The Supreme Court rejected H. [Party A]'s cassation petition and affirmed the lower court decisions. === Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Banyuwangi District Court & Surabaya High Court) === Verification of facts concerning the marriage and divorce of H. [Party A] & [Party D] pursuant to Banyuwangi Religious Court Decision No. 2134/Pdt.G/1996/PA.Bwi dated October 25, 1996; verification of the Statement Letter of Marital Property Handover dated September 17, 1996 (Exhibit P-2); verification of Banyuwangi Religious Court Decision No. 1730/Pdt.G/1998/PA.Bwi dated August 10, 1998, dismissing partition due to gifts; verification of Notarial Gift Revocation Deed No. 1 dated April 7, 1988, by Notary Heru Ismadi, S.H. (Exhibit T.I-3); verification of sales of portions of SHM No. 777/Ds. Sraten land (350 m² & 1,063.50 m²) to Defendants IV, V, and VI; and witness testimonies. == Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge == === Statutory Regulations === * '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata / BW):''' Articles 1243 (Default), 1365 (Tort), 1666, & 1688 (Rules & Conditions for Gift Annulment). * '''HIR (Herziene Inlandsch Reglement):''' Article 163 (Burden of Proof). * '''Law No. 7 of 1989 ''jo.'' Law No. 3 of 2006 ''jo.'' Law No. 50 of 2009 on Religious Courts:''' Jurisdiction over Marital Property (''Gono-Gini''). * '''Law No. 14 of 1985 ''jo.'' Law No. 5 of 2004 ''jo.'' Law No. 3 of 2009 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation Review Authority. === Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence === * '''Doctrine of ''Irrevocability of Inter Vivos Gifts'':''' Once a gift is perfected and accepted by the recipient, ownership transfers instantly and cannot be unilaterally withdrawn by the donor. * '''Complementary Jurisdiction Doctrine between Religious and General Courts:''' Religious Court rulings declaring property vested in children preclude re-litigation of marital property partitions and serve as absolute foundations for General Courts (District Courts) to enforce children's civil rights. == What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish == === Established by Evidence === * The Statement Letter of Marital Property Handover dated September 17, 1996, is '''PROVEN VALID AND LEGALLY BINDING'''. * The Plaintiffs ([Party B], Khobab, Hurrotul Fa'izah) are '''PROVEN TO BE THE LAWFUL OWNERS''' of Disputed Objects I and II. * Notarial Gift Revocation Deed No. 1 dated April 7, 2008, is '''PROVEN LEGALLY DEFECTIVE AND NULL AND VOID (''NIETIGE'')'''. * Sales of portions of the disputed objects by Defendants I & II to Defendants IV, V, and VI are '''PROVEN TO CONSTITUTE A TORT AND VOID TRANSACTIONS'''. * Defendants I and II are ordered to surrender Disputed Objects I and II peacefully and free of encumbrances to the Plaintiffs. * The Petitioner's cassation petition (H. [Party A]) is '''REJECTED ENTIRELY BY THE SUPREME COURT'''. === Dismissed Claims (Plaintiffs' Petitum) === * Claims seeking material damages of Rp 500,000,000, moral damages of Rp 75,000,000, and coercive daily fines (''dwangsom'') of Rp 500,000/day were '''REJECTED BY THE COURT''' as lacking legal grounds. == Uncertainties and Gaps == '''Protecting Children's Rights Against Parental Abuse of Power Over Gifted Assets:''' This landmark ruling establishes rigorous legal protection for children in Indonesia: parents are strictly prohibited from manipulating gifts previously granted to their children during divorce proceedings.
