'''Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 1572 K/Pid/2001''' (decided 31 July 2002) is a [[Indonesia|Indonesian]] [[criminal law]] precedent concerning [[Psychotropic substances|psychotropic substance]] possession offences under Law No. 5 of 1997 on Psychotropics. The [[Supreme Court of Indonesia|Supreme Court]] reversed an acquittal handed down by the Denpasar District Court and convicted the defendant, a Dutch national, of unlawfully storing methamphetamine ("''sabu-sabu''") found in a bathroom cabinet within her private bedroom suite. The decision is a leading authority on three points of Indonesian criminal procedure and substantive narcotics law: (1) the admissibility of cassation appeals against a "not-genuine acquittal" (''niet-zuivere vrijspraak''); (2) the doctrine that a household's principal occupant — the "master of the house" — is presumed to know of, and be criminally responsible for, contraband found in areas of the home under her exclusive daily control; and (3) the mandatory judicial duty to weigh circumstantial evidence (''alat bukti petunjuk'') under Article 188 of the Indonesian Code of Criminal Procedure (KUHAP).

== Background ==

=== Parties ===
The defendant, '''[Defendant]''', was a Dutch national (born [details removed]), a homemaker residing at [address removed], Kerobokan, Kuta, [[Badung Regency|Badung]], [[Bali]], Indonesia. She was prosecuted by the Public Prosecutor of the Denpasar District Attorney's Office (''Kejaksaan Negeri Denpasar'').

=== Facts ===
On Wednesday, 30 August 2000, at approximately 17:00 local time, police searched the defendant's residence in Kerobokan, Kuta. In a wall cabinet inside the bathroom attached to the defendant's bedroom — a room said to be used only by the defendant and her young child — officers found:
* two plastic bags containing crystalline methamphetamine, with a combined weight of 5.6 grams;
* one box of plastic clip (resealable) bags; and
* additional plastic and paper packaging materials.

Forensic testing by the Indonesian National Police's Criminalistics Laboratory (Laboratorium Forensik Polri, Denpasar branch), recorded in Official Report No. LAB: 159/KNF/2000 dated 29 September 2000, confirmed the crystalline substance to be methamphetamine, a Category II psychotropic substance under Law No. 5 of 1997.

The defendant denied knowledge of the drugs and asserted that they belonged to her husband, [Husband], who she said returned to the home only occasionally. She was charged, in the primary indictment, with unlawfully storing psychotropics under Article 62 of Law No. 5 of 1997, and, in the alternative (subsidiary) indictment, with failing to report psychotropic substance abuse under Article 65 of the same law.

=== Proceedings below ===
By Decision No. 534/Pid.B/2000/PN.Dps of 30 March 2001, the '''Denpasar District Court''' (''Pengadilan Negeri Denpasar'') acquitted the defendant of both the primary and subsidiary charges (a "''vrijspraak''"), accepting her denial of knowledge. The Public Prosecutor of Denpasar filed an application for [[cassation]] with the Supreme Court, arguing that the trial court had misapplied the rules of evidence.

== Issues ==

# '''Admissibility of cassation against an acquittal.''' Under Article 244 of KUHAP, cassation is generally not available against an acquittal. Was the Denpasar District Court's acquittal, however, a "not-genuine acquittal" (''niet-zuivere vrijspraak'') reviewable by the Supreme Court, on the ground that it rested on a misapplication of the law of evidence (Article 185(6) KUHAP) and a failure to set out the court's factual and evidentiary reasoning as required by Article 197(1)(d) KUHAP?
# '''Criminal responsibility of a household occupant ("master of the house") for contraband in private space.''' Could the defendant, as the principal occupant of the household, avoid criminal liability for methamphetamine found in a cabinet of her private ensuite bathroom merely by asserting that she did not know of it, or by attributing it to a husband who visited infrequently?
# '''Duty to evaluate circumstantial evidence.''' Did the trial court err in failing to weigh, as circumstantial evidence (''alat bukti petunjuk'') under Article 188 KUHAP, the layout of the bathroom, the presence of clip-seal packaging, and the testimony of the witnesses, in determining whether the element of "unlawfully storing psychotropics" under Article 62 of Law No. 5 of 1997 had been proven?

== Holding ==

The Supreme Court granted the Public Prosecutor's application for cassation, set aside the Denpasar District Court's decision, and, exercising its power to try the matter itself (''mengadili sendiri''), convicted the defendant.

=== On the admissibility of cassation ===
The Court held that the Denpasar District Court's acquittal was a "not-genuine acquittal" because it was the product of an erroneous application of the law of evidence under Article 185(6) KUHAP, compounded by the trial court's failure to set out, concisely, its findings of fact and its assessment of the evidence as required by Article 197(1)(d) KUHAP. Such a defect takes the decision outside the ordinary bar on cassation against acquittals in Article 244 KUHAP, and the Supreme Court accordingly had full authority to examine, review, and set aside the decision.

=== On the "master of the house" doctrine ===
The Court held that the bathroom in which the drugs were found was reached only through the defendant's own bedroom and was used, in the ordinary course, only by the defendant and her young child. As the household's principal occupant, who made daily, exclusive use of that private space, the defendant was, as a matter of law, presumed to know of — and to be responsible for — items kept in the bathroom cabinet, including the 5.6 grams of methamphetamine. A bare denial of knowledge, or an unsubstantiated claim that the drugs belonged to a husband who visited only occasionally, did not displace this presumption of knowledge and possession.

=== On circumstantial evidence ===
The Court held that a court may not disregard the cumulative and mutually consistent character of facts proven at trial — including the layout and limited access to the bathroom, the discovery of resealable packaging materials, and the testimony of witnesses (including police officers I Putu Suta, M. Rifai, and I Wayan Darmadi, and household staff Ni Komang Mersini and Aminadap Tualaka) — which together constituted valid circumstantial evidence (''alat bukti petunjuk'') under Article 188 KUHAP sufficient to prove the element of "unlawfully storing psychotropics" under Article 62 of Law No. 5 of 1997.

The Court also had regard to the defendant's prior record, noting that she had previously been convicted in a narcotics/psychotropics matter involving approximately 20,781 ecstasy tablets.

=== Disposition (''Amar Putusan'') ===
The Supreme Court:
# granted the cassation application of the Public Prosecutor of the Denpasar District Attorney's Office;
# set aside Denpasar District Court Decision No. 534/Pid.B/2000/PN.Dps of 30 March 2001;
# '''trying the case itself''', declared the defendant, [Defendant], lawfully and convincingly proven guilty of the offence of unlawfully storing psychotropic substances;
# sentenced her to one (1) year's imprisonment and a fine of Rp 200,000 (two hundred thousand [[Indonesian rupiah|rupiah]]), to be substituted by one (1) month's detention if unpaid;
# ordered that time already spent in pre-trial detention be credited in full against the sentence;
# ordered the confiscation and destruction of the physical evidence — two packets of methamphetamine (5.6 grams), one box of clip-seal plastic bags, one white paper wrapping, and a white plastic box; and
# ordered the defendant to bear the costs of both the trial and cassation proceedings (cassation costs: Rp 2,500).

== Ratio decidendi ==
The trial court had misapplied the law of evidence under Articles 185(6) and 197(1)(d) KUHAP; its acquittal was therefore a "not-genuine acquittal" and reviewable on cassation under Article 244 KUHAP. Because the bathroom in which the drugs were found was accessible only through the defendant's own bedroom and was used exclusively by the defendant and her young child, the defendant — as the household's principal occupant, exercising daily exclusive control over that space — was, as a matter of law, presumed to know of and be responsible for its contents. Assessed together with the circumstantial evidence admissible under Article 188 KUHAP, this presumption was sufficient to establish the defendant's intentional possession of the psychotropic substance.

== Applicable law ==

=== Statutes ===
* Law No. 5 of 1997 on Psychotropics (''Undang-Undang No. 5 Tahun 1997 tentang Psikotropika''), Article 62 (unlawfully possessing, storing, and/or carrying Category II psychotropic substances) and Article 65 (failure to report psychotropic substance abuse).
* Law No. 8 of 1981 on Criminal Procedure (KUHAP):
** Article 185(6) — limits on the evaluation of witness testimony and evidentiary consistency;
** Article 188 — circumstantial evidence (''alat bukti petunjuk'');
** Article 197(1)(d) — requirement that a criminal judgment set out its legal reasoning;
** Article 244 — cassation against acquittals.
* Law No. 14 of 1970, as amended by Law No. 14 of 1985, on the Supreme Court — power of the Supreme Court to try a matter itself (''mengadili sendiri'') on cassation.

=== Related doctrine ===
* '''Presumption of knowledge/custody in private premises''': possession of an illegal item in a private space with restricted access gives rise to a legal presumption that the principal occupant of that space controls, and is aware of, the item.
* '''Cassation against a "not-genuine acquittal"''': the Supreme Court may set aside an acquittal where the trial court has misapplied the law of evidence.

== Significance ==
The decision is frequently cited in Indonesian narcotics jurisprudence for the proposition that an occupant of a household cannot readily escape criminal liability for contraband found in personal living space — such as an ensuite bathroom or bedroom — merely by disclaiming knowledge or attributing ownership to another family member, where that space is under the occupant's exclusive day-to-day control.

== See also ==
* [[Law of Indonesia]]
* [[Indonesian Code of Criminal Procedure]]
* [[Drug possession]]
* [[Supreme Court of Indonesia]]

== References ==
* Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia, Decision No. 1572 K/Pid/2001 (31 July 2002), pp. 559–571.
* Denpasar District Court, Decision No. 534/Pid.B/2000/PN.Dps (30 March 2001).

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:1575K PID 1992
wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 1575 K/Pid/1992}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 1575 K/Pid/1992''' (dated January 7, 1993) is an Indonesian substantive and criminal procedure law precedent establishing a fundamental rule regarding the prohibition on cumulatively charging or sentencing a defendant as a principal perpetrator (''dader'' ''ex'' Article 187 of the Criminal Code / KUHP) and under the offense of omitting to report another's criminal conspiracy (Article 164 of the Criminal Code).

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established a primary legal principle:

* '''Incompatibility of Cumulative Sentencing Between Principal Perpetrators (Article 187 KUHP) and Failure to Report Conspiracy (Article 164 KUHP):''' Article 187 of the Criminal Code (Arson causing general danger) '''should not be cumulatively charged or sentenced together with Article 164 of the Criminal Code''' (Criminal Conspiracy / Failure to Report a Crime). Article 187 KUHP is intended for persons charged as the '''perpetrators''' (''dader'' / ''mededader''), whereas Article 164 KUHP is intended for persons charged merely with '''knowing''' that others are conspiring to commit a crime but failing to notify authorized officials. If defendants are legally and convincingly proven to be the principal perpetrators of arson (Article 187 KUHP), they '''cannot simultaneously be sentenced''' under Article 164 KUHP, and must therefore be '''acquitted''' of the charge under Article 164 KUHP.

The Supreme Court amended the verdict of the Kupang High Court Decision No. 50/PID/1992/PT.K ''jo.'' Ruteng District Court Decision No. 4/Pid.B/1992/PN.Rut by declaring the Defendants guilty of Arson ''ex'' Article 187 paragraph (1) ''jo.'' Article 55 paragraph (1) 1st of the Criminal Code, while '''declaring the Defendants not legally and convincingly proven guilty of and acquitting them from the Second Charge''' (Article 164 ''jo.'' Article 55 of the Criminal Code).

| '''Acquittal of Defendants from Article 164 KUHP:''' Perpetrators proven to commit arson under Article 187 KUHP must be acquitted of the charge under Article 164 KUHP.

| Confirmed in decision identity pp. 219, 229.
| 1575K_PID_1992.pdf

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Juridical Prohibition on Cumulative Charging Between Principal Perpetrators (''Dader'' ''ex'' Article 187 KUHP) and Omission Offenses (Article 164 KUHP) ===
''Is the Public Prosecutor justified in cumulatively charging and the Court sentencing a Defendant under Article 187 KUHP (as an arson perpetrator) and Article 164 KUHP (for knowing of an arson conspiracy without reporting to authorities)?''

==== Supreme Court Rule: Unjustified / Cumulative Qualification Void by Operation of Law ====
The Supreme Court outlined that Article 187 KUHP and Article 164 KUHP are mutually exclusive regarding legal subject qualifications. A person acting as a perpetrator (''dader'' / ''mededader'') who directly sets fire or orders houses burned ''ex'' Article 187 KUHP cannot possibly be classified as an outsider who merely "knew of another's conspiracy and permitted it" ''ex'' Article 164 KUHP. The omission offense under Article 164 KUHP applies exclusively to third parties who are not perpetrators. Consequently, combining the sentencing of both provisions by the ''Judex Facti'' constitutes an error in law (''error in judicando'').

=== 2. Limits of Cassation Review Authority Over Alibi Evidence Evaluations (Article 253 paragraph (1) of KUHAP) ===
Cassation grounds raised by Defendants I and VI claiming they were located elsewhere (Wontong Village) during the arson incident constitute factual evidentiary assessments falling under the exclusive domain of the ''Judex Facti'' and cannot be reviewed at the cassation level.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' (Kupang High Court Decision No. 50/PID/1992/PT.K ''jo.'' Ruteng District Court Decision No. 4/Pid.B/1992/PN.Rut) err in applying the law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') by cumulatively sentencing the Defendants under both Article 187 KUHP and Article 164 KUHP?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. The ''Judex Facti'' erred in applying the law. The Supreme Court granted the correction of the verdict, annulled the qualification of Article 164 KUHP, and independently adjudicated by declaring the Defendants guilty of violating Article 187 1st ''jo.'' Article 55 paragraph (1) 1st of the Criminal Code, while '''acquitting the Defendants from the Second Charge under Article 164 of the Criminal Code'''.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Ruteng District Court & Kupang High Court) ===
Examination of facts regarding the Rembong and Dimpong villagers' conspiracy meeting on September 28, 1991; the raid and arson attack on 22 residents' houses in Nggawut Village, Lawi Village, on Sunday, September 29, 1991, at 3:00 PM WITA; Defendant I ([Party B]) pouring gasoline/kerosene; Defendants II ([Party A]) & III (Nikolaus Kelau) retrieving fire from a kitchen; Defendants IV ([Party D]) & V (Romanus Harum) setting houses ablaze; Defendant VI ([Party C]) giving the command to "burn all houses"; seizure of physical evidence including zinc sheets, bamboo, beams, and burnt window glass; and evaluation of the alibis of Defendants I and VI.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===

* '''Criminal Code (KUHP):'''
** Article 187 1st: Arson Crimes Creating General Danger to Property.
** Article 164: Crimes of Knowing Criminal Conspiracies Without Reporting/Preventing Them.
** Article 55 paragraph (1) 1st: Complicity (Perpetrator / Co-perpetrator).
* '''Law No. 8 of 1981 (Criminal Procedure Code / KUHAP):''' Article 253 paragraph (1) letter a (Correction of Errors in Application of Law at Cassation Level).

=== Substantive Criminal Law Doctrines & Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===

* Principle of Subjective Qualification ''Ne Bis In Idem'': The principal perpetrator of a crime cannot simultaneously be sentenced as a party permitting that crime to occur.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* The Defendants are legally and convincingly proven to have committed the criminal offense of "Intentionally causing a fire that creates a general danger to property committed jointly"

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:1588K PDT 2001
wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 1588 K/Pdt/2001}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 1588 K/Pdt/2001''' (dated June 30, 2004; deliberated May 18, 2004) is a fundamental Indonesian land and civil law jurisprudence precedent establishing vital legal rules regarding the nullity by operation of law of land rights certificates issued prior to the date of the underlying deed of sale and purchase (''antedated certificates'') as well as the nullity of certificates issued without an application from the lawful owner.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established two primary legal principles:

# '''Nullity of Certificates Issued Prior to the Deed of Sale and Purchase (AJB):''' A land certificate issued prior to the deed of sale and purchase serving as its foundational legal title is contrary to the law and declared null and void. The issuance of SHM No. 93 on December 23, 1980, based on Deed of Sale and Purchase No. 479/JS/VII/1981 dated July 7, 1981, contradicts actual legal reality and bears a fatal legal defect.
# '''Nullity of Land Certificate Issuance Without the Lawful Owner's Application:''' The issuance of a land rights certificate without an official application filed by the respective lawful owner is illegal and possesses no binding legal force.

The Supreme Court granted the Plaintiff's ([Party A]) cassation petition, annulled the Bandung High Court Decision No. 214/Pdt/1999/PT.Bdg ''jo.'' Bale Bandung District Court Decision No. 47/Pdt.G/1998/PN.BB, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part, declaring the Defendants' actions unlawful, declaring that Hak Milik Certificate (SHM) No. 91 in the name of [Party B] — subsequently subdivided into SHM No. 92 (in the name of Ny. Siti Aminah) and SHM No. 93 (in the name of Sutisna and later transferred to Teddy Suhardjo) — contains legal defects and possesses no legal force, and declaring the disputed land to be the lawful property of the Plaintiff ([Party A]).

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Absolute Legal Defect in Land Certificate Issuance Due to Chronological Anomalies (Antedated Certificate) ===
''Is a land rights certificate (SHM No. 93 issued on December 23, 1980) valid under the law when trial evidence proves that the deed of sale and purchase (AJB No. 479/JS/VII/1981) serving as its foundational title was executed months/years later (on July 7, 1981)?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Unlawful and Void by Operation of Law.'''

The Supreme Court established that land certificates issued prior to the date of execution of the Deed of Sale and Purchase (AJB) represent a chronological anomaly contradicting the logic of land registration and the principle of publicity. Certificates issued without a valid foundational title at the time of issuance contain an absolute legal defect and must be declared null and void (''nemo plus iuris transferre potest quam ipse habet'').

=== 2. Nullity of Land Rights Certificate Issuance Without the Lawful Owner's Application ===
''Does the Land Office (BPN) possess the authority to issue land certificates in the name of third parties without an official application filed by the lawful holder of the foundational title/land?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Void and Legally Defective.'''

The issuance of land rights certificates (SHM Nos. 91, 92, 93) executed without an application filed by the lawful owner ([Party B]) stems from administrative manipulation/procedural defects, rendering all derivative certificates born therefrom devoid of binding legal force.

=== 3. Error in Judicando by Bandung High Court in Assessing Ownership Disputes ===
The Bandung High Court misapplied the law by intertwining the disputed land ownership dispute with the ownership matters of a weaving enterprise ("Munding Laya" / "Pergaruda"), whereas the core dispute focused purely on the validity of certification and land ownership in Blok Toblong, Majalaya.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' (Bandung High Court Decision No. 214/Pdt/1999/PT.Bdg) err in applying the law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') by setting aside the Bale Bandung District Court judgment and validating SHM No. 93, despite SHM No. 93 being proven to have been issued on December 23, 1980, preceding AJB No. 479/JS/VII/1981 dated July 7, 1981, and being issued without the lawful owner's application?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. The Bandung High Court erred in applying the law. The Supreme Court granted Plaintiff [Party A]'s cassation petition, annulled Bandung High Court Decision No. 214/Pdt/1999/PT.Bdg, and independently adjudicated by partially granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit, declaring SHM Nos. 91, 92, and 93 legally defective and without binding legal force, and declaring the disputed land to be the lawful property of the Plaintiff ([Party A]).

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Bale Bandung District Court & Bandung High Court) ===
Examination of facts regarding the 1960 land exchange between [Party A] and [Party B] (Letter C No. 1777 Parcel 103 S IV measuring 468 Tumbak exchanged for Blok Toblong Kohir 2315 Parcel 209 DI measuring 80 tumbak & 70 tumbak); facts of land possession and textile factory leasing by the Plaintiff since 1976; issuance of SHM No. 91 covering 1,995 m² in [Party B]'s name without [Party B]'s application; subdivision of SHM No. 91 into SHM No. 92 covering 1,120 m² in the name of Ny. St. Aminah and SHM No. 93 covering 875 m² in the name of Sutisna (Defendant I) then transferred to Teddy Suhardjo (Defendant II); mortgaging of SHM No. 92 at Bank Exim by Eddy Tuhfah; and examination of written exhibits and witnesses (including witness [Party B] confirming he never sold the land nor applied for certification).

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* Law No. 5 of 1960 on Basic Agrarian Regulations (UUPA).
* Government Regulation No. 10 of 1961 ''jo.'' Government Regulation No. 24 of 1997 on Land Registration: Material prerequisites for valid land rights certificate issuance (existence of valid foundational title/AJB and applications from right-holders).
* Civil Code (KUHPerdata): Articles 1320 & 1365 (Requirements for Valid Agreements & Tort / ''Perbuatan Melawan Hukum'').
* Law No. 14 of 1985 ''jo.'' Law No. 4 of 2004 ''jo.'' Law No. 5 of 2004 on the Supreme Court: Cassation authority & independent adjudication powers.

=== Doctrines & Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* Principle of ''Nemo Plus Iuris Transferre Potest Quam Ipse Habet'': No person can transfer rights exceeding what they possess. A defect in the foundational root title vitiates the validity of all subsequent certificate issuance chains.
* Land Registration Legal Certainty: Certificates stemming from manipulative procedures / without owner applications enjoy no legal protection.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* The Plaintiff ([Party A]) is the lawful owner of the disputed land in Blok Toblong, Parcel No. 209 D.I Kohir No. 2315 (currently Pelangi St., Rt.02/Rw.03, Majalaya Sub-District, Bandung Regency) based on a 1960 land exchange with [Party B].
* SHM No. 93 was proven to have been issued earlier (December 23, 1980) than Deed of Sale and Purchase No. 479/JS/VII/1981 (July 7, 1981), and is thus declared void and legally defective.
* SHM Nos. 91, 92, and 93 were issued without any application from the lawful owner ([Party B]), rendering them legally defective and devoid of binding legal force.
* The Defendants were proven to have committed Tort (''Perbuatan Melawan Hukum'').
* The occupation of approximately 875 m² of land utilizing SHM No. 93 by Defendants I and II constitutes an unlawful act.
* The protective attachment (''sita jaminan'') dated November 14, 1998, is declared valid and lawful.

=== Rejected / Dismissed Claims ===
* The Plaintiff's Provisionary claim was rejected by the Supreme Court.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Procedural Oversight of Land Certification by BPN:''' This landmark ruling provides an exceptionally robust legal precedent in Indonesia: the Land Office (BPN) is strictly prohibited from issuing land certificates without direct applications from lawful foundational titleholders or relying on antedated deeds of sale and purchase. Certificates born from reversed chronology and procedural defects are absolutely declared null and void by the courts.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
;Is a land certificate (SHM) valid if its issuance date precedes the date of the Deed of Sale and Purchase (AJB) serving as its foundational title, or if issued without the owner's application?
:'''Such certificates are invalid and void by operation of law.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 1588 K/Pdt/2001:
:* Land certificates issued prior to the underlying deed of sale and purchase contradict the law and are declared null and void.
:* The issuance of land rights certificates without official applications filed by lawful owners constitutes legally defective issuance possessing no binding legal force.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 15 K/MIL/1999 establishes an essential legal precedent within the military judiciary that narcotics abuse committed by Indonesian National Armed Forces (*TNI*) soldiers constitutes a grave crime that ruins families, the younger generation, and the state. The Supreme Court affirmed that sentences imposed on TNI soldiers proven guilty of narcotics crimes cannot be limited solely to imprisonment and fines, but must mandatorily include the additional penalty of dismissal from military service. The appellate court's omission of the additional penalty of dismissal lacked adequate justification from an educational, preventive, corrective, and repressive standpoint.

== Case Background ==

The Defendant (Second Lieutenant / Letda Inf. Agus Isrok, Deputy Commander of the Special Unit of Detachment 411 Group 4 Kopassus) was caught in flagrante delicto alongside Witness I ([Defendant]) on August 8, 1999, in Room 408 of the Travel Hotel, West Jakarta, by officers from the West Jakarta Metro Police. Upon searching, authorities discovered evidence consisting of 1.6 kg of methamphetamine (*sabu-sabu*), 27.6 grams of heroin (*putauw*), 6,218 ecstasy tablets, 25 strips of valium, marijuana, and a lighter containing methamphetamine crystals.

The Jakarta Military Court II-08 (Decision No. PUT/58-K/MM II-08/AD/VI/2000) sentenced the Defendant to 4 years of imprisonment, a fine of Rp 10,000,000, and the additional penalty of dismissal from military service. On appeal, the Jakarta High Military Court II (Decision No. PUT.34-14/BDG/K-AD/MMT-II/XI/2000) modified the sentence to 2 years of imprisonment and a fine of Rp 3,000,000, while VACATING the additional penalty of dismissal from the TNI-AD. The Military Prosecutor subsequently filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:''' Because the criminal offense committed by the defendant involves narcotics abuse—which is regarded by both society and the Government as a serious crime capable of destroying families, the younger generation, and the State—the penalty imposed on the defendant is insufficient when limited to imprisonment and a fine, but must also incorporate the additional penalty of dismissal from the Kopassus TNI membership; consequently, the decision of the Jakarta High Military Court II must be annulled.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition filed by the Petitioner for Cassation / MILITARY PROSECUTOR AT THE MILITARY PROSECUTOR'S OFFICE II-08 JAKARTA; Annulling the Jakarta High Military Court II Decision No. PUT.34-14/BDG/K-AD/MMT-II/XI/2000; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Declaring Defendant Letda Inf. Agus Isrok legally and convincingly proven guilty of the criminal offense of "unlawfully and without right possessing, storing for possession or supply, or controlling Category I Narcotics other than plants"; (2) Sentencing the Defendant to Principal Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 (two) years and a fine amounting to Rp 10,000,000 (ten million rupiahs) with a subsidiary confinement of 6 (six) months; (3) Additional Penalty: Dismissal from Military Service; (4) Charging all procedural costs across all levels of jurisdiction to the Respondent for Cassation / Defendant.

{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 1600 K/Pid/2009}} '''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 1600 K/Pid/2009''' (dated November 24, 2009) is a fundamental Indonesian criminal law and criminal procedure jurisprudence precedent establishing pivotal rules regarding the application of the '''Restorative Justice''' doctrine and the '''Principle of Balance''' in adjudicating family criminal matters (specifically between a mother-in-law and a daughter-in-law):
"In resolving a criminal case, if a Judge finds an effective resolution based on the principle of balance, a sense of justice, forgiveness, and benefits that are far greater if the respective criminal case is terminated due to the withdrawal of the case by the Complainant rather than continuing the case examination merely to fulfill legal formalities, '''THEN A JUDGE MAY MAKE A JUDICIAL BREAKTHROUGH BY DEVIATING FROM FORMAL LEGAL ASPECTS (CRIMINAL PROCEDURE LAW).'''"
Although the withdrawal of the complaint/report by the Complainant (Witness Victim Ny. [Complainant] / mother-in-law) exceeded the 3-month statutory deadline stipulated under Article 75 of the Criminal Code (KUHP), the Supreme Court outlined that peace, reconciliation, and forgiveness between the mother-in-law and daughter-in-law restored the disrupted legal balance and family ties (''restorative justice''). Forcibly examining a family criminal case in a rigid, formalistic manner would instead destroy family bonds and the best interests of the children/grandchildren. The Supreme Court granted the Defendant's ([Defendant]) cassation petition, annulled the Yogyakarta High Court Decision No. 01/PID/PLW/2009/PT.Y dated March 2, 2009, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by granting Ny. [Complainant]'s complaint withdrawal petition and declaring the prosecution of Case No. 317/Pid.B/2008 in the name of Defendant [Defendant] '''Inadmissible''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO). == Infobox == {| class="wikitable" |- ! Application of the Restorative Justice Doctrine and Principle of Balance in Family Criminal Matters === ''Is the Court justified in continuing criminal prosecution against a daughter-in-law based on her mother-in-law's report, even though the victim witness (mother-in-law) has explicitly withdrawn the complaint, forgiven the Defendant, and declared that family relations and legal balance have been restored?'' '''Supreme Court Rule: Unjustified / Prosecution Must Be Declared Inadmissible (NO).''' The Supreme Court outlined that the primary objective of Criminal Law is to restore legal balance disrupted by a criminal offense (''restorative justice''). In an internal family conflict between a mother-in-law (complainant) and daughter-in-law (Defendant), acts of forgiveness and complaint withdrawal by the victim represent a high-value restoration of balance. Facilitating conflict resolution satisfying the parties is vastly more effective and just than enforcing formal criminal penalties. === 2. Reach of Substantive Justice Over Complaint Withdrawal Time Limits (Article 75 KUHP) === ''Does Article 75 KUHP restricting complaint withdrawals to a maximum of 3 (three) months operate so rigidly as to bar the Court from granting complaint withdrawals filed after 3 months?'' '''Supreme Court Rule: Can Be Deviated From in Favor of Substantive Justice.''' The Yogyakarta High Court's ruling rejecting complaint withdrawals based on Article 75 KUHP was assessed by the Supreme Court as rigid and overly formalistic. Although complaint withdrawals occur beyond the 3-month deadline, Judges possess authority to execute a legal breakthrough by deviating from criminal procedure formalities if terminating the case delivers vastly greater benefits to justice and family harmony. == Question of Law vs Question of Fact == === Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) === Did the ''Judex Facti'' (Yogyakarta High Court Decision No. 01/PID/PLW/2009/PT.Y) err in applying the law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') by annulling the Yogyakarta District Court Judgment and ordering trial proceedings to continue, despite the Victim Witness (Defendant's mother-in-law) having filed a complaint withdrawal and forgiven the Defendant based on Restorative Justice? '''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. Yogyakarta High Court erred in applying the law by exhibiting rigidity and excessive formalism. The Supreme Court granted Defendant [Defendant]'s cassation petition, annulled Yogyakarta High Court Decision No. 01/PID/PLW/2009/PT.Y dated March 2, 2009, and independently adjudicated by granting Ny. [Complainant]'s complaint withdrawal petition and declaring the prosecution of Case No. 317/Pid.B/2008 in the name of Defendant [Defendant] inadmissible (NO). === Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Yogyakarta District Court & Yogyakarta High Court) === Examination of facts regarding the mother-in-law and daughter-in-law family relationship between Ny. [Complainant] and [Defendant]; facts of electronic business capital disbursement amounting to Rp 3,910,000,000 between April and October 2007; issuance of promissory notes/barter cheques unpayable at banks; submission of complaint withdrawal petition letter dated October 28, 2008, by Ny. [Complainant] read before the Yogyakarta District Court Panel of Judges on November 5, 2008; and the existence of the Defendant's 2 young children (complainant's grandchildren). == Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge == === Statutory Regulations === * '''Law No. 4 of 2004 / Law No. 48 of 2009 on Judicial Power:''' Article 28 paragraph (1) / Article 5 paragraph (1) (Judicial obligation to explore, follow, and comprehend living legal values and a sense of justice in society). * '''Criminal Code (KUHPerdata / KUHP):''' ** Article 75 KUHP: Complaint Withdrawal Time Limit Provisions. ** Article 378 ''jo.'' Article 64 paragraph (1) KUHP & Article 372 ''jo.'' Article 64 paragraph (1) KUHP: Continuous Fraud / Embezzlement Charges. * '''Law No. 8 of 1981 (Criminal Procedure Code / KUHAP):''' Procedural rules on prosecution and criminal case termination. === Legal Doctrines & Landmark Supreme Court Jurisprudence === * Restorative Justice Doctrine: Criminal case resolution focusing on restoring harmony and balance in relations among perpetrators, victims, and society. * Principle of Judicial Breakthrough: Judges possess rights to deviate from criminal procedure formalities if conflicting with substantive justice and forgiveness. == What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish == === Established by Evidence === * Victim Witness / Complainant (Ny. [Complainant]) was legally proven to have voluntarily withdrawn all legal complaints/charges against her daughter-in-law (Defendant [Defendant]) based on humanitarian grounds, family bonds, and grandchildren's futures. * Legal balance and family relationship harmony between Victim Witness and Defendant were proven fully restored. * Complaint withdrawal petition granted by the Supreme Court. * Criminal Prosecution of Case No. 317/Pid.B/2008 in the name of Defendant [Defendant] declared INADMISSIBLE (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO). * Court costs across all levels of jurisdiction charged to the State. === Annulled (Yogyakarta High Court Verdict) === * Yogyakarta High Court Decision No. 01/PID/PLW/2009/PT.Y annulling complaint withdrawals and ordering trial continuation was entirely annulled by the Supreme Court as rigid and overly formalistic. == Uncertainties and Gaps == '''Jurisprudential Discretion on Restorative Justice Implementation in Indonesian Criminal Procedure:''' This landmark ruling represents a historical milestone decision in Indonesian Supreme Court Jurisprudence adopting the Restorative Justice doctrine. It provides legal certainty that criminal prosecution formalities must yield to social balance restoration and family forgiveness, affirming that Judges must not remain "legislative captives" (''bouche de la loi'') when confronted with substantive justice. == Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) == ;Can a criminal case between a mother-in-law and daughter-in-law be terminated if the mother-in-law withdraws the complaint even if such withdrawal occurs after the 3-month deadline? :'''Can Be Terminated (Prosecution Declared Inadmissible).''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 1600 K/Pid/2009: :* Under the Restorative Justice doctrine and Principle of Balance, complaint withdrawals and forgiveness by a mother-in-law toward her daughter-in-law represent an invaluable restoration of legal balance. :* Although complaint withdrawals occur past the 3-month deadline (Article 75 KUHP), Judges possess authority to execute a legal breakthrough deviating from criminal procedure formalities in favor of substantive justice and family utility. :* The Supreme Court grants complaint withdrawals and declares criminal prosecutions inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO). == Notes == Mark Cecep Mustafa — Verified Knowledge Grapher for human verification of structure, provenance, claim-evidence linkage, relationships, metadata, and citation readiness. title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:1690K PID 1987
wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 1690 K/Pid/1987}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 1690 K/Pid/1987''' (dated November 26, 1987 / pronounced December 16, 1987) is an Indonesian criminal law and criminal procedure precedent establishing two fundamental rules regarding the authority of High Courts to issue detention orders at the appeal level ''ex'' Article 238 paragraph (2) ''jo.'' Article 27 of the Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP) and the sentencing of heroin trafficking crimes:

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established two primary legal principles:

# '''High Court Authority to Issue Detention Orders (Article 238(2) ''jo.'' Article 27 of KUHAP):''' A High Court's verdict ruling that "the High Court lacks the authority to issue a detention order against the Defendant" misapplies the law and is annulled by the Supreme Court. Pursuant to Article 238(2) ''jo.'' Article 27 of KUHAP, High Courts possess full authority to issue detention orders for the interests of appeal proceedings for a maximum period of 30 (thirty) days.
# '''Crime of Selling Heroin Narcotics (Article 23(5) ''jo.'' Article 36(5)(b) of Law No. 9 of 1976):''' The Defendant [Defendant] was legally and convincingly proven guilty of the crime of "unlawfully selling narcotics in the form of heroin" totaling 2 ''tail'' weighing 80,000 milligrams (80 grams) for Rp 900,000, and was accordingly sentenced to 20 (twenty) years of imprisonment and a fine of Rp 500,000 (five hundred thousand rupiahs) with a subsidiary of 6 (six) months of confinement, while the 80,000 mg heroin evidence was confiscated for destruction.

The Supreme Court granted the Defendant's ([Defendant]) cassation petition, annulled Jakarta High Court Decision No. 96/Pid./1987/PT.DKI dated May 16, 1987, regarding the detention portion, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by declaring the Defendant guilty of unlawfully selling heroin narcotics and sentencing him to 20 (twenty) years of imprisonment and a Rp 500,000 fine subsidiary 6 months of confinement.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. High Court Authority to Issue Detention Orders During Appeal Proceedings (Article 238(2) ''jo.'' Article 27 of KUHAP) ===
''Does a High Court possess authority to issue a detention order against a Defendant during the appeal examination period?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Full Authority.'''
The Jakarta High Court's verdict stating that "the High Court lacks authority to issue a detention order against the Defendant" misapplied the law. Pursuant to Article 238(2) ''jo.'' Article 27 of KUHAP, detention authority shifts to the High Court upon filing an appeal petition, empowering the High Court to issue detention orders for a maximum of 30 (thirty) days.

=== 2. Qualification of Elements for "Unlawfully Selling Heroin/Morphine Narcotics" (Article 23(5) ''jo.'' Article 36(5)(b) of Law No. 9 of 1976) ===
The Defendant's actions in fulfilling an order for 2 ''tail'' of heroin (80 grams) for Rp 900,000, agreeing upon a transaction location, and entrusting the evidence to witness [Intermediary] for handover to the buyer ([Buyer]) perfectly fulfilled all elements of the crime of "unlawfully selling narcotics in the form of heroin."

=== 3. Evidentiary Value of Defendant's Interrogation Record (BAP) Withdrawal at Trial (Article 188 ''jo.'' Article 189 of KUHAP) ===
Unilateral withdrawal of a Defendant's BAP statements under claims of fear/threats without supporting valid evidence fails to displace the correspondence of witness testimonies (buyer, intermediary, and arresting officers), instead acting as circumstantial evidence (''aanwijzing'') reinforcing the Defendant's guilt.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
Did the Jakarta High Court err in applying criminal procedure law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') by declaring that High Courts lack authority to issue detention orders, and how does this apply under Article 238(2) ''jo.'' Article 27 of KUHAP?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. Jakarta High Court erred in applying the law. The Supreme Court granted the Defendant's cassation petition, annulled Jakarta High Court Decision No. 96/Pid./1987/PT.DKI regarding the detention portion, and independently adjudicated by declaring that High Courts possess authority to detain Defendants ''ex'' Article 27 of KUHAP and sentencing Defendant [Defendant] to 20 (twenty) years of imprisonment and a fine of Rp 500,000 subsidiary 6 months of confinement.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / West Jakarta District Court & Jakarta High Court) ===
Examination of facts regarding the order of 2 ''tail'' of heroin (80,000 mg) by [Buyer] to the Defendant on October 7, 1983, at PB Nasional Alley, Jelambar, West Jakarta; delivery on October 8, 1983, via [Intermediary]; arrest by Polsek/Metro Jaya Regional Police officers (Sertu Supangat, Mayor Harry YN Montolalu, Letkol Syaeri); National Police Criminalistics Laboratory test results confirming the crystals tested positive for heroin; facts of the Defendant fleeing to Lampung until arrested on April 6, 1986; and the Defendant's prior criminal record resulting in a conviction in Medan for a marijuana case.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''Law No. 8 of 1981 (Criminal Procedure Code / KUHAP):'''
** Article 27: Detention Authority by High Courts (maximum 30 days).
** Article 238 paragraphs (2) & (3): Transfer of Detention Authority During Appeal Examinations.
** Articles 184, 185, 188, 189: Means of Evidence and Circumstantial Indicators of Defendant Guilt.
* '''Law No. 9 of 1976 on Narcotics:''' Article 23(5) ''jo.'' Article 36(5)(b).
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation and Independent Adjudication Powers.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* Defendant [Defendant] is legally and convincingly proven guilty of committing the crime of "unlawfully selling narcotics in the form of heroin."
* Physical evidence comprising 2 ''tail'' of heroin weighing 80,000 milligrams (80 grams) was proven to have been sold by the Defendant for Rp 900,000.
* High Courts possess authority to issue detention orders against Defendants at the appeal level ''ex'' Article 27 of KUHAP.
* The Defendant was sentenced to imprisonment for 20 (twenty) years and a fine of Rp 500,000 subsidiary 6 months of confinement.
* Physical evidence of 2 ''tail'' of 80,000 mg heroin was ordered confiscated for destruction.

=== Rejected / Dismissed Arguments ===
* The Defendant's alibi claiming residence in Lampung since September 1983 and allegations of police torture were rejected by the Court as contradicting witness testimonies and BAP circumstantial evidence.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Enforcement of High Court Detention Authority During Appeal File Transitions:''' This landmark ruling affirms certainty in Indonesian criminal procedure law: High Courts must not reject detention authority under the pretext that case dossiers have not been fully registered, because upon appeal declarations being officially lodged at the District Court, authority over the Defendant's detention status legally transfers to the High Court ''ex'' Article 238(2) of KUHAP.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
;Does a High Court possess authority to detain a defendant during appeal proceedings, and what is the prison sentence for selling 80 grams of heroin pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence?
:'''High Courts possess detention authority, and offenders face 20 years imprisonment.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 1690 K/Pid/1987:
:* Pursuant to Article 238(2) ''jo.'' Article 27 of KUHAP, High Courts possess full authority to issue detention orders against Defendants for appeal proceedings for a maximum of 30 days.
:* A Defendant proven to have unlawfully sold 80 grams (2 ''tail'') of heroin narcotics for Rp 900,000 is sentenced to 20 (twenty) years of imprisonment and a fine of Rp 500,000 subsidiary 6 months of confinement.

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:1695K PDT 1984
wikitext:
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 1695 K/Pdt/1984''' (dated May 23, 1986 / deliberation on April 18, 1986) is a fundamental Indonesian private international law and civil procedure jurisprudence precedent establishing pivotal rules regarding the enforceability of contractual agreements between Indonesian citizens and foreign citizens or legal entities, as well as inconsistencies between legal considerations and appellate judgments.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established two primary legal principles:

# '''Private International Law / Foreign Contract Law (Choice of Law & Territoriality):''' Agreements between Indonesian citizens and foreign individuals or legal entities cannot be automatically enforced upon legal relationships whose objects are located within Indonesian territory. In international commercial trade transactions (i.e., issuance of bills of exchange / import of cosmetic goods from the Netherlands to Indonesia), foreign private law or international commercial law cannot be applied automatically without regard for Indonesia's national legal order and the formal validity of representative authorities or powers of attorney.
# '''Inconsistency Between Appellate Legal Considerations and Judgment Verdict:''' If an appellate court explicitly states in its legal considerations that the Plaintiff's appeal petition is inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO) due to the absence of a special power of attorney to file an appeal, the appellate court should no longer examine and adjudicate the merits of the case or the reconvention claim. An appellate court's action in granting part of the merits despite such procedural bar constitutes a manifest contradiction between considerations and the final verdict, warranting annulment at the cassation level.

The Supreme Court granted the Petitioner for Cassation's ([Party B]) petition, annulled Jakarta High Court Decision No. 429/1981 PT. Perdata dated January 20, 1982, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by adopting Central Jakarta District Court Decision No. 66/1979 G dated November 5, 1979, which declared the Plaintiff's (General Cosmetics B.V.) lawsuit inadmissible (NO).

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Reach of Enforcement for Foreign Law / International Agreements Over Legal Objects Within Indonesian Territory (Jurisdiction & Choice of Law) ===
''Can commercial accounts receivable transactions based on bills of exchange issued by a foreign company (Netherlands) to an Indonesian merchant be automatically enforced in Indonesian Courts based on foreign commercial law?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Cannot Be Automatically Enforced.''' The Supreme Court established that civil law relationships involving foreign legal subjects and Indonesian citizens with objects/execution located in Indonesia do not automatically submit to foreign law or foreign binding structures without aligning with Indonesia's national legal order and applicable procedural laws.

=== 2. Separation Between Appeal Power of Attorney Qualification and Jurisdiction Over Merits (Legal Standing / Persona Standi in Judicio) ===
''Is an Appellate Court justified in adjudicating and granting part of the Plaintiff's lawsuit merits, when in its legal considerations the Appellate Court explicitly declared that the Plaintiff's appeal petition was inadmissible due to a legally defective power of attorney?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Unjustified / Procedural Legal Defect.''' If an appellant's appeal petition is declared inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO) due to a defective special power of attorney, the Appellate Court legally loses jurisdiction (''lack of jurisdiction'') to examine, consider, and adjudicate the merits or reconvention claims. An Appellate Court that nevertheless adjudicates the merits issues a verdict contradictory to its own considerations, requiring annulment by the Supreme Court.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Jakarta High Court (Decision No. 429/1981 PT. Perdata) err in applying civil procedure law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') by partially granting the merits of the lawsuit, whereas in its own considerations the Jakarta High Court established that the Plaintiff's appeal petition was inadmissible because the appeal power of attorney failed to meet formal requirements (''geen kualitas'')?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. Jakarta High Court erred in applying the law. The Supreme Court granted Petitioner for Cassation [Party B]'s petition, annulled Jakarta High Court Decision No. 429/1981 PT. Perdata dated January 20, 1982, and independently adjudicated by adopting Central Jakarta District Court Decision No. 66/1979 G dated November 5, 1979, which declared the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible (NO).

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Central Jakarta District Court & Jakarta High Court) ===
Examination of facts regarding commercial cosmetic export trade from General Cosmetics B.V. Amsterdam to Jakarta between 1970–1977; issuance of 9 commercial bills of exchange valued at N.Fl. 198,167.75; acceptance recording of bills by Defendants I & II; partial debt payments via Amsterdam-Rotterdam Bank N.V.; execution of non-payment protests (''protest van niet betaling'') via Notary H.E. Gewang, S.H., on January 11, 1979; examination of special power of attorney for appeal registration on November 13, 1979 ''jo.'' power of attorney dated January 3, 1980; and currency conversion calculations from Guilders to Rupiah based on Kenop 15 exchange rates (November 16, 1978: N.Fl. 1 = Rp 315).

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===

* '''HIR / RBg (Civil Procedure Law):''' Provisions on formal requirements of Special Powers of Attorney to file appeals and lawsuit formalities.
* '''Commercial Code (KUHD / W.v.K.):''' Articles 100, 127, 143, 147, 148 (Provisions on Bills of Exchange & Acceptance).
* '''Law No. 1 of 1950 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation authority and independent adjudication powers.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===

* Supreme Court Decision No. 46/K/Sip/1969 dated June 5, 1971: Separation of appeal examinations and special power of attorney formal requirements.
* Supreme Court Decision No. 701 K/Sip/1976 dated April 14, 1976: Photocopy evidence unmatchable with originals and contested by opponents lacks binding evidentiary force.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* The Plaintiff's (General Cosmetics B.V.) appeal petition failed to meet formal requirements (''geen kualitas'') because it lacked a valid Special Power of Attorney when the appeal petition was filed.
* The Jakarta High Court verdict adjudicating the merits manifestly contradicted its own legal considerations.
* The Plaintiff's (General Cosmetics B.V.) Convention Lawsuit is declared '''INADMISSIBLE''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).
* The Defendants' Reconvention Lawsuit is declared '''INADMISSIBLE''' (NO).
* Respondent for Cassation / Original Plaintiff ordered to pay court costs across all levels of jurisdiction (cassation assessed at Rp 20,000).

=== Annulled (Jakarta High Court Verdict) ===

* Jakarta High Court considerations ruling in favor of the Plaintiff and ordering Defendants I & II to pay N.Fl. 133,798.23 were entirely annulled by the Supreme Court due to procedural legal defects.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Application of Choice of Law and International Engagement Qualifications in Indonesia:''' This landmark ruling affirms the precautionary principle of Indonesia's private international law: foreign business actors cannot simply force their home country's commercial law or international bill documents without respecting representation formalities, authority validity, and civil procedure laws applicable within the jurisdiction where execution/objects are located (Indonesia).

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==

; Does a contract agreement between a foreign citizen and an Indonesian citizen automatically apply if its object is in Indonesia, and what is the legal consequence if appellate considerations declare an appeal inadmissible but the verdict rules on the merits?
: '''Does not automatically apply, and the appellate verdict is void by operation of law.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 1695 K/Pdt/1984:
:* Agreements between foreign citizens/legal entities and Indonesian citizens cannot be automatically applied to legal relationships whose objects are located within Indonesian territory.
:* If an Appellate Court in its considerations states that the Plaintiff's appeal petition is inadmissible due to a defective power of attorney, the Appellate Court lacks authority to adjudicate the merits. An appellate verdict that nevertheless adjudicates the merits contradicts its own considerations and is annulled by the Supreme Court, declaring the lawsuit inadmissible (NO).

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:1696K PID 2002
wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 1696 K/Pid/2002}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 1696 K/Pid/2002''' (dated May 28, 2003) is a landmark Indonesian banking corruption (misappropriation of Bank Indonesia Liquidity Support / BLBI funds) and criminal procedure jurisprudence precedent establishing three vital legal rules regarding the non-extinguishment of criminal unlawfulness by civil settlements or asset restitution, the admissibility of cassation petitions against impure acquittals (''niet-zuivere vrijspraak'' ''ex'' Article 244 of KUHAP), and the criminal liability of a President Commissioner in the management of BLBI funds.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established three primary legal principles:

# '''Civil Settlements / Asset Restitution Do Not Extinguish Criminal Unlawfulness:''' The actions of a President Commissioner (the Defendant) in signing the Master Refinancing and Note Issuance Agreement (MRNIA) and executing deeds for the surrender of all Bank Modern assets to the Indonesian Bank Restructuring Agency (IBRA / BPPN) / State as security for debt repayment constitute civil arrangements that cannot eliminate or extinguish the "criminal unlawfulness" (''wederrechtelijkheid'') of the corrupt misappropriation of BLBI funds causing financial losses to the State.
# '''Admissibility of Cassation Against Impure Acquittals (''Niet-Zuivere Vrijspraak'' ''ex'' Article 244 of KUHAP):''' The Supreme Court possesses full authority to review and annul a District Court acquittal when such acquittal is based on an erroneous legal interpretation (misinterpretation of unlawful acts) regarding the elements of the indicted corruption offenses.
# '''Criminal Liability of President Commissioners / Bank Executives:''' A President Commissioner who exercises factual control and approval authority over transactions exceeding Rp 10 Billion, and who approves the utilization of BLBI funds outside their designated purposes (for related-party credit expansion, promissory note purchases, import L/C settlements, etc.) in direct contravention of Bank Indonesia's strict prohibitions, bears joint criminal liability alongside the Board of Directors for corruption causing state financial losses amounting to Rp 169,472,986,461.54.

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Public Prosecutor at the Central Jakarta District Attorney's Office, annulled the Central Jakarta District Court Decision No. 1146/Pid.B/2001/PN.Jkt.Pst dated August 1, 2002, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by declaring the Defendant [Defendant] legally and convincingly guilty of committing the criminal offense of "Corruption committed jointly and continuously," sentencing the Defendant to 4 (four) years of imprisonment, a fine of Rp 20,000,000 (twenty million rupiahs) with a subsidiary of 4 (four) months of confinement, and ordering him to pay restitution (replacement money) amounting to Rp 169,472,986,461.54.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Existence of Criminal Unlawfulness (''Wederrechtelijkheid'') Regarding Civil Settlements and Asset Restitution (IBRA Restitution / MRNIA) ===
''Does signing a civil settlement agreement (MRNIA) and surrendering collateral assets by bank executives/shareholders to IBRA eliminate the criminal unlawfulness of misappropriating Bank Indonesia Liquidity Support (BLBI) funds?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Criminal Unlawfulness Persists and Is Not Erased.'''

The Supreme Court established that misappropriating BLBI funds in contravention of Bank Indonesia Supervisory Letters and Banking Laws constitutes a corruption offense committed at the moment of execution (''tempus delicti''). Subsequent civil settlement actions through the Master Refinancing and Note Issuance Agreement (MRNIA) or asset surrenders to IBRA represent manifestations of good faith in restoring state losses, but cannot eliminate or erase the criminal unlawfulness (''wederrechtelijkheid'') that had already been fully consummated.

=== 2. Supreme Court Cassation Competence Over Impure Acquittals (''Niet-Zuivere Vrijspraak'' ''ex'' Article 244 of KUHAP) ===
''Does the Public Prosecutor have the right to file a cassation petition against a Central Jakarta District Court decision acquitting the Defendant of BLBI corruption charges, and does the Supreme Court possess authority to annul it?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Admissible and Competent to Annul.'''

The acquittal of the Defendant by the Central Jakarta District Court based on an erroneous legal interpretation—treating BLBI fund misappropriation as a purely civil dispute—constitutes an impure acquittal (''niet-zuivere vrijspraak''). Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence ''jo.'' Article 244 of KUHAP, the Supreme Court possesses authority to examine and annul such acquittals in the interest of fair banking law enforcement.

=== 3. Factual Role and Criminal Liability Qualification of President Commissioners in Corporate Banking Crimes (Prudential Banking Principle) ===
A President Commissioner who does not merely exercise passive supervisory functions but holds factual control, approves credit/fund expansion transactions exceeding Rp 10 Billion, and ignores written Bank Indonesia warnings concerning the placement of BLBI funds into productive assets bears criminal liability (qualified as co-perpetration / ''mededader'') ''ex'' Article 1 paragraph (1) sub a ''jo.'' Article 28 ''jo.'' Article 34(c) of Law No. 3 of 1971 ''jo.'' Law No. 31 of 1999 ''jo.'' Article 55 paragraph (1) 1st of the Criminal Code (KUHP).

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (''Judex Juris'' / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' (Central Jakarta District Court No. 1146/Pid.B/2001/PN.Jkt.Pst) err in applying evidentiary law and substantive law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') by acquitting the Defendant on the grounds that the BLBI matter had been resolved civilly via MRNIA/IBRA, and how is the qualification of criminal unlawfulness determined?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. Central Jakarta District Court erred in applying the law. The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Public Prosecutor at the Central Jakarta District Attorney's Office, annulled Central Jakarta District Court Decision No. 1146/Pid.B/2001/PN.Jkt.Pst dated August 1, 2002, and independently adjudicated by declaring Defendant [Defendant] guilty of committing the criminal offense of Joint and Continuous Corruption, sentencing him to 4 years of imprisonment, a Rp 20 Million fine subsidiary 4 months of confinement, and imposing Restitution amounting to Rp 169,472,986,461.54.

=== Question of Fact (''Judex Facti'' / Central Jakarta District Court) ===
Examination of facts regarding debit balances / overdrafts of PT Bank Modern Tbk. at Bank Indonesia since October 20, 1997; receipt of Bank Indonesia Liquidity Support (Fasdis I, Fasdis II, and SBPUK) valued at Rp 1.79 Trillion; utilization of BLBI funds to purchase Promissory Notes of PT Total Central Finance USD 1.516.000 (Rp 5 Billion) and PT PLN Rp 11.9 Billion; disbursement of related-party credits to PT Jakarta Steel Perdana (Rp 9 Billion), PT Awani Modern Indonesia, PT Modern Putratama, and PT Gunung Sewu Kencana; settlement of import L/Cs for PT Masterina Keramika Pratama via Bank Hokindo USD 4,348,500; testimonies of Bank Indonesia officials (Onny Widjanarko, Fathoni Achmad, Sarwanto, Soedradjad Djiwandono, Miranda S. Goeltom, Aulia Pohan); and verification of MRNIA execution dated December 18, 1998, and asset encumbrances to IBRA.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''Law No. 3 of 1971 ''jo.'' Law No. 31 of 1999 ''jo.'' Law No. 20 of 2001 on Eradication of Corruption Crimes:''' Article 1 paragraph (1) sub a / Article 2 paragraph (1), Article 28, Article 34(c) (Additional Restitution Penalties).
* '''Law No. 7 of 1992 ''jo.'' Law No. 10 of 1998 on Banking:''' Article 49 paragraph (2) letter b (Liability of Bank Commissioners and Management).
* '''Law No. 8 of 1981 (Criminal Procedure Code / KUHAP):''' Article 244 (Cassation Against Impure Acquittals) & Article 191.
* '''Criminal Code (KUHP):''' Article 55 paragraph (1) 1st (Complicity) & Article 64 paragraph (1) (Continuous Act).

=== Legal Doctrines & Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* Doctrine of Criminal Law Independence from Civil Law: Civil dispute resolution or financial loss recovery subsequent to a crime does not halt criminal prosecution nor eliminate criminal culpability.
* Supreme Court Decision No. 2477 K/Pid/1988 dated March 20, 1993: Sentencing bank commissioners/management misusing credit for personal/group interests.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* Defendant [Defendant] is legally and convincingly proven guilty of committing the criminal offense of "Corruption committed jointly and continuously."
* Proven to have unlawfully disbursed and utilized Bank Modern BLBI funds outside their designated purposes, resulting in state financial losses amounting to Rp 169,472,986,461.54.
* Signing the MRNIA and surrendering assets to IBRA was proven not to erase the Defendant's criminal unlawfulness.
* The Defendant was sentenced to 4 (four) years of imprisonment, a Rp 20,000,000 fine subsidiary 4 months of confinement, and ordered to pay Restitution amounting to Rp 169,472,986,461.54.

=== Annulled (Central Jakarta District Court Verdict) ===
* Central Jakarta District Court considerations acquitting the Defendant on grounds that the matter was resolved civilly via IBRA were entirely annulled by the Supreme Court as erroneous application of evidentiary law and substantive corruption law.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Strict Separation Between Corporate Settlements (IBRA / PKPS) and Criminal Accountability (Corruption):''' This landmark ruling stands as one of the most vital legal precedent pillars in Indonesia handling the BLBI scandal: banking debt settlement policies through IBRA/PKPS schemes (MRNIA) constitute civil/administrative state law domains that cannot serve as an "immunity shield" to erase criminal corruption liability for the unlawful misappropriation of public moneys.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
;Can civil asset surrender to IBRA / MRNIA extinguish BLBI corruption crimes, and can a bank President Commissioner be penalized for BLBI fund misappropriation?
:'''Asset surrender does not extinguish crimes, and President Commissioners remain penally liable.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 1696 K/Pid/2002:
:* Signing the MRNIA and surrendering civil assets to IBRA cannot eliminate or erase the criminal unlawfulness (''wederrechtelijkheid'') of corrupt BLBI fund misappropriation that caused state financial losses.
:* A President Commissioner holding approval control over transactions exceeding Rp 10 Billion and approving BLBI fund utilization outside designated purposes (for related-party credit expansion and productive assets prohibited by Bank Indonesia) bears joint criminal liability alongside the Board of Directors.
:* The Supreme Court annulled the Central Jakarta District Court acquittal and sentenced Defendant [Defendant] to 4 years imprisonment, a Rp 20 Million fine, and Restitution of Rp 169.47 Billion.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 169 K/Pid/1988 dated March 17, 1988, establishes fundamental Criminal Procedure jurisprudence regarding the validity of court judgments: A High Court that fails to include complete details of the Defendant's identity (such as place and date of birth) and fails to state the Defendant's detention status in the dispositive portion of its judgment, as mandated by Article 197 paragraph (1) letters b and k of the KUHAP, renders the High Court judgment null and void (*van rechtswege nietig*) pursuant to Article 197 paragraph (2) of the KUHAP. The Supreme Court consequently annulled the High Court judgment and independently adjudicated the narcotics and maltreatment criminal case.

== Case Background ==

The Defendant ([Defendant], [age removed], entrepreneur, Sukabumi) was brought before the Cibadak District Court facing two charges:

* '''First Charge (Article 23 paragraph (3) jo. Article 36 paragraph (3) letter a of Law No. 9 of 1976 on Narcotics):''' Unlawfully possessing, storing to possess, or controlling narcotics consisting of 356.4 milligrams of marijuana and 10 BK pills on April 4, 1987, around Hotel Pondok Dewata, Pelabuhan Ratu.
* '''Second Charge (Article 351 paragraph (1) of the KUHP):''' Intentionally committing maltreatment against witness [Party B] using a machete (*golok*), resulting in a laceration on the lower right elbow. The maltreatment occurred because the Defendant, in a state of intoxication, was mobbed/pushed by a group of people, fled, and grabbed a machete belonging to a young coconut vendor by the roadside.

The Cibadak District Court (Decision No. 69/Pid.B/1987/PN.Cbd dated August 22, 1987) sentenced the Defendant to 10 months of imprisonment and a fine of Rp 200,000, subsidiary 3 months of confinement. The Bandung High Court (Decision No. 231/Pid/B/1987 dated October 21, 1987) amended the Cibadak District Court judgment by sentencing the Defendant to 1 (one) year of imprisonment and a fine of Rp 300,000, subsidiary 3 months of confinement. Dissatisfied with the Bandung High Court ruling, the Public Prosecutor at the Cibadak State Prosecutor's Office filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The Bandung High Court erred in applying the law because it failed to include the Defendant's complete identity (place/date of birth) and failed to state the Defendant's detention status in the dispositive portion of its judgment, as required by Article 197 paragraph (1) letters b and k of the KUHAP.
# Pursuant to Article 197 paragraph (2) of the KUHAP, the failure to satisfy the requirements under Article 197 paragraph (1) letters b and k of the KUHAP renders the Bandung High Court judgment null and void (*van rechtswege nietig*).
# Considering that the High Court has examined the case and in the interest of the principles of fast, low-cost, and simple judicial proceedings, the Supreme Court independently adjudicated the matter. Regarding the substance of the case, the first charge (narcotics) and second charge (maltreatment) were legally and convincingly proven. Taking into account mitigating circumstances (the Defendant is young, frank, supports small children, and committed the maltreatment out of fear of being mobbed), the Defendant is sentenced to 1 (one) year of imprisonment and a fine of Rp 300,000.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation: Public Prosecutor at the State Prosecutor's Office in Cibadak; Declaring null and void (*batal demi hukum*) the Bandung High Court decision dated October 21, 1987, No. 231/Pid/B/1987; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Declaring Defendant [Defendant] legally and convincingly proven guilty of committing the crimes of "Unlawfully possessing marijuana-type narcotics" and "Maltreatment"; (2) Sentencing the Defendant to 1 (one) year of imprisonment; (3) Ordering that the period of detention already served be deducted in full; (4) Sentencing the Defendant to pay a fine of Rp 300,000, subsidiary 3 (three) months of confinement; (5) Ordering that evidence items (356.4 grams of dried marijuana leaves, 10 BK pills, 1 machete) be confiscated for destruction; (6) Ordering that the Defendant remain in detention; (7) Ordering the Defendant to pay court costs across all levels of jurisdiction (cassation assessed at Rp 2,500). *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Cassation Panel of Justices on Wednesday, March 2, 1988, and pronounced in an open session on Thursday, March 17, 1988, by Soerjono, S.H. [Presiding Judge], Bismar Siregar, S.H., and Mohammad Djanis, S.H.).*

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 16 K/AG/2010 establishes a fundamental jurisprudence and legal standard regarding the protection of civil rights of a non-Muslim wife surviving her Muslim husband. The Supreme Court affirmed that although a spouse practicing a non-Islamic faith does not qualify as a direct heir under Islamic Inheritance Law, a non-Muslim wife who has dedicated herself through a long-standing marriage is entitled to a portion of her late husband's estate via the institution of compulsory testament (*wasiat wajibah*) equivalent to a wife's inheritance share, alongside her rightful half (1/2) share of the joint marital property (*gono-gini*).

== Case Background ==

The late Ir. Muhammad Armaya bin Renreng (a Muslim Testator) passed away on May 22, 2008. During his lifetime, he contracted a valid marriage with [Party A] (Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation) on November 1, 1990, pursuant to Marriage Certificate Extract No. 57/K.PS/XI/1990, living together harmoniously for 18 years. The Testator was survived by five Muslim heirs: his mother ([Party B]) and four siblings (Dra. Hj. Murnihati, Dra. Hj. Muliyahati, Djelitahati, and Ir. Arsal).

The Testator left behind joint marital assets consisting of: (1) A house and 216 m² plot of land at [address removed], Makassar; (2) A house and 100 m² plot of land at Kompleks BTN Tabariah G 11/13, Makassar (valued at Rp 70,000,000); and (3) A PT AIA Indonesia Life Insurance policy payout of Rp 50,000,000. The Muslim heirs filed an inheritance distribution lawsuit at the Makassar Religious Court. The Makassar Religious Court (Decision No. 732/Pdt.G/2008/PA.Mks) and the Makassar High Religious Court (Decision No. 59/Pdt.G/2009/PTA.Mks) upheld claims that ignored the non-Muslim wife's share. Dissatisfied with these rulings, the Defendant ([Party A]) filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:''' The marriage between the Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation and the Testator lasted for a considerable duration of 18 years, signifying a sustained period of dedication by the Defendant toward the Testator. Therefore, despite the Petitioner's non-Muslim status, it is equitable and just for her to receive her spousal rights, namely a 1/2 share of the joint marital property and a portion of the Testator's estate through the institution of compulsory testament (*wasiat wajibah*).
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition filed by Petitioner for Cassation [Party A]; Annulling the Makassar High Religious Court Decision No. 59/Pdt.G/2009/PTA.Mks and the Makassar Religious Court Decision No. 732/Pdt.G/2008/PA.Mks; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Declaring the Defendant ([Party A]) entitled to a 1/2 share of the joint marital property; (2) Declaring the Defendant entitled to a share of the inheritance estate via compulsory testament (*wasiat wajibah*) amounting to 15/60 parts of the total inheritance apportionment; (3) Establishing the shares of the other heirs (Mother receiving 10/60; 3 sisters receiving 7/60 each; and 1 brother receiving 14/60).

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 17 K/MIL/2004 dated June 29, 2004, establishes an important legal principle regarding the limits of criminal (military) court competence in disputes originating from civil debt-receivable relations. The Supreme Court affirmed that if the core issue in a case stems from a debt-receivable obligation involving collateral and mutual agreements to substitute collateral items between parties, the matter falls within the scope of civil jurisdiction. Consequently, the criminal court lacks the authority to adjudicate the case; thus, lower court rulings were annulled, and the Military Prosecutor's indictment was declared inadmissible (*niet ontvankelijke verklaard*).

== Case Background ==

The Defendant, [Defendant] (Pelda/Peltu Nrp. 523361, Ba Tilat Alin Den Pusdiktop, Pusdiktop Kodiklat TNI AD), was charged with the criminal offense of embezzlement violating Article 372 of the KUHP. The case originated from a debt-receivable transaction in September 2001, where Witness I ([Witness B]) and [Witness D] borrowed Rp 4,000,000 from the Defendant, providing 1 Daihatsu Zebra car (License Plate B-2269-AB) belonging to [Witness D] as collateral. Because [Witness D] failed to fulfill his repayment promise, the collateral was replaced with a Suzuki Jimny vehicle belonging to Witness II (Kopka [Witness A]), and later substituted again with 1 Nissan sedan (License Plate AD-8157-PA) belonging to Witness III (Mr. [Witness C]), accompanied by a written collateral exchange agreement dated October 1, 2001. Subsequently, the Defendant pledged the Nissan sedan to Witness IV (Mr. [Witness E]) for Rp 6,000,000 without the consent of Witness III.

The Yogyakarta Military Court II-11 (Decision No. PUT/40-K/MM.II-11/AD/IV/2003) sentenced the Defendant to 3 months of imprisonment under Article 372 of the KUHP. On appeal, the Jakarta High Military Court II (Decision No. PUT/47-K/BDG/MMT-II/AD/VIII/2003) annulled the Yogyakarta Military Court ruling, declared the Defendant not legally proven guilty, and acquitted him of all charges. The Military Prosecutor subsequently filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:''' Because the core issue in this case is a debt-receivable matter involving collateral (namely vehicles between the Defendant and Witness [Witness D], followed by a substitution of collateral belonging to Witness III pursuant to the written collateral agreement dated October 1, 2001), this matter falls within the scope of civil jurisprudence; hence, the criminal court lacks competence to adjudicate it.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation MILITARY PROSECUTOR AT MILITARY PROSECUTOR'S OFFICE II-11 YOGYAKARTA; Annulling the Jakarta High Military Court II decision dated August 7, 2003, No. PUT/47-K/BDG/MMT-II/AD/VIII/2003 and the Yogyakarta Military Court II-11 decision dated April 29, 2003, No. PUT/40-K/MM.II-11/AD/IV/2003; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Declaring the indictment of the Military Prosecutor at Military Prosecutor's Office II-11 Yogyakarta inadmissible; (2) Charging all procedural costs across all levels of jurisdiction to the State.
