title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:1804K PID 1988
wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 1804 K/Pid/1988}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 1804 K/Pid/1988''' (dated October 23, 1991 / pronounced February 12, 1992) is an Indonesian substantive criminal law precedent establishing a fundamental rule regarding the juridical qualification of complicity (''deelneming'') between "Ordering an Act" (''Doen Plegen'' ''ex'' Article 55 paragraph (1) 2nd of the Criminal Code / KUHP) and "Direct Perpetrator / Co-perpetration" (''Dader'' / ''Mededader'' ''ex'' Article 170 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code).

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established two primary legal principles:

# '''Doctrine and Requirements of ''Doen Plegen'' ("Ordering an Act"):''' In criminal law theory, the form of complicity known as "Ordering an Act" (''Doen Plegen'') implies that the direct perpetrator (''manus ministra'' / tool) cannot be held criminally liable (for example, due to a lack of mental capacity, being under duress or irresistible force, or lacking intent/culpability).
# '''Requalification of Community Leaders' Actions in Mass Riots:''' If trial facts prove that Defendants (the Village Head and the LKMD Chairman) did not merely shout instructions, but were physically present and personally or jointly carried out acts of violence and property destruction at the scene, their actions constitute direct execution (''Dader'' / ''Mededader''). Consequently, the proper legal qualification is Direct Perpetrator of Public Assault / Property Destruction ''ex'' Article 170 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code, and '''not''' "Ordering an Act" (''Doen Pleger'').

The Supreme Court granted the Defendants' (I, II, IV, V) cassation petition, annulled Maluku High Court in Ambon Decision No. 15/PID.B/1987/PT.MAL dated May 2, 1988 ''jo.'' Labuha District Court Decision No. 01/PTS/Pid/B/1986/PN.LBH dated March 21, 1987, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by declaring Defendants I, II, and V legally and convincingly guilty of committing the crime of "Publicly and jointly using violence against property" ''ex'' Article 170 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code (as direct perpetrators) and sentencing them to imprisonment of 4 (four) months (Defendant I), 5 (five) months (Defendant II), and 3 (three) months (Defendant V), respectively. Defendant IV ([Party E]) was found guilty of violating Article 406 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code (2 months imprisonment), while Defendants VI, VII, and VIII were acquitted of all charges with their reputations restored.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Construction of Complicity (''Deelneming'' ''ex'' Article 55 KUHP): Delineation Between ''Doen Plegen'' ("Ordering an Act") and ''Medeplegen'' / ''Dader'' ("Co-perpetration / Direct Perpetrator") ===
''Is a village official / community leader present at a mass riot who shouts instructions for destruction while physically participating in structural demolition appropriately qualified as a person who "ordered an act" (''doen pleger'')?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Inappropriate (Misapplication of Law).'''
The form of complicity known as ''Doen Plegen'' (Article 55 paragraph 1 2nd of the Criminal Code) requires the presence of an instrument (''manus ministra'') who cannot be penalized due to a lack of intent or culpability. If community members present at the scene are penally liable and the Defendant directly participates in the destruction physically, the Defendant's legal qualification is Direct Perpetrator / Co-perpetrator (''Dader'' / ''Mededader'' ''ex'' Article 170 paragraph 1 of the Criminal Code).

=== 2. Forfeiture of Public Prosecutor's Cassation Right Due to Procedural Default (Article 248 of KUHAP) ===
A Public Prosecutor who files a cassation petition but fails to submit a cassation memorandum/brief within the 14-day statutory deadline stipulated under Article 248 paragraphs (1) and (4) of KUHAP causes their cassation right to be forfeited by operation of law, resulting in the petition being declared inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

=== 3. Proving Public Assault / Property Destruction (Article 170(1) KUHP vs. Article 406(1) KUHP) ===
Joint actions in public places destroying houses and furnishings belonging victims fulfill all elements of Article 170 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code. Meanwhile, individual actions destroying kitchen utensils (pots/pans) outside the main mass riot are more appropriately qualified as individual property destruction offenses ''ex'' Article 406 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' (Ambon High Court Decision No. 15/PID.B/1987/PT.MAL ''jo.'' Labuha District Court Decision No. 01/PTS/Pid/B/1986/PN.LBH) err in applying substantive criminal law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') by sentencing Defendants I, II, and V as persons who "ordered an act" (''doen pleger''), despite facts proving they directly executed violent/destructive acts jointly with residents in the field?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. The ''Judex Facti'' misapplied the law. The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of Defendants I, II, IV, and V, annulled the ''Judex Facti'' decisions, and independently adjudicated by requalifying the actions of Defendants I, II, and V as Direct Perpetrators of Public Assault / Property Destruction offenses ''ex'' Article 170 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Labuha District Court & Ambon High Court) ===
Examination of facts regarding mass riot reactions on Tuesday night, May 21, 1985, through Wednesday early morning, May 22, 1985, in Amasing Kota Village, Labuha, Bacan, following a slashing incident perpetrated by victim witness [Party D]; shouting by Defendant I (Village Head) and Defendant II (LKMD Chairman) in front of the Koramil commander's house and market complex ("just dismantle that house, do not be afraid, I take responsibility"); physical destruction of 1 wooden/thatched-roof house and kitchen items (plates, glasses, stoves, thermoses, mirrors) belonging to Ny. Sarifah Sumampoh and [Party D]; and evaluation of individual roles of Defendants I through VIII.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''Criminal Code (KUHP):'''
** Article 55 paragraph (1) 1st & 2nd: Forms of Complicity (Perpetrator, Ordering an Act, Co-perpetration).
** Article 170 paragraph (1): Public and Joint Violence Against Persons or Property.
** Article 406 paragraph (1): Property Destruction Crimes.
* '''Law No. 8 of 1981 (Criminal Procedure Code / KUHAP):'''
** Article 248 paragraphs (1) & (4): Obligation to Submit Cassation Memorandums and Forfeiture of Cassation Rights.
** Article 253 paragraph (1) letter a: Cassation Grounds Due to Errors in Applying Law.
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Authority to independently adjudicate at the cassation level.

=== Doctrines & Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* Doctrine of Complicity (''Deelneming'' / ''Doen Plegen'' vs. ''Medeplegen''): ''Doen Plegen'' requires a blameless tool (''manus ministra'' / ''niet strafbaar''). If field perpetrators are penally liable and the instigator joins in executing acts in the field, the legal qualification is ''medeplegen'' / direct perpetrator (''dader'').

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* Defendant I ([Party A]), Defendant II ([Party B]), and Defendant V ([Party C]) are legally and convincingly proven guilty of committing the crime of "Publicly and jointly using violence against property" ''ex'' Article 170 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code (as direct perpetrators).
* Defendant IV ([Party E]) is legally and convincingly proven guilty of committing the crime of "Intentionally destroying property" ''ex'' Article 406 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code.
* Defendant I sentenced to 4 months imprisonment; Defendant II to 5 months imprisonment; Defendant IV to 2 months imprisonment; Defendant V to 3 months imprisonment.
*

{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 1816 K/Pdt/1989}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 1816 K/Pdt/1989''' (dated October 22, 1992) is a fundamental Indonesian land and civil law jurisprudence precedent establishing three vital legal rules regarding the criteria for a good faith purchaser (''good faith purchaser''), the validity of land certificate cancellations by Land Authorities / Minister of Home Affairs due to criminal forgery of root titles, and the formal qualification of the defendant's status (plurality of parties) in a certificate cancellation lawsuit.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established three primary legal principles:

# '''Criteria for a Good Faith Purchaser vs. a Negligent Purchaser:''' A land buyer cannot be classified as a good faith purchaser if the acquisition is executed negligently—specifically, when the buyer completely failed to examine the rights and status of the sellers regarding the disputed land at the time of the transaction. Consequently, a negligent buyer does not deserve legal protection in such a transaction (''bad faith / negligent purchaser'').
# '''Validity of Land Certificate Cancellation Based on Criminal Convictions for Root Title Forgery:''' In cases where the issuance of a land certificate contains cadastral technical errors or is based on criminal forgery / false statements in an authentic deed (Article 266 of the Criminal Code) proven by a legally binding criminal judgment, the Minister of Home Affairs / Land Authority is authorized to cancel such land certificate pursuant to Article 12 ''jo.'' Article 14 of the Minister of Home Affairs Regulation No. 6 of 1972. Such certificate cancellation is legally valid and does not constitute a Tort by the Government (''Onrechtmatige Overheidsdaad'').
# '''Formal Plurality of Parties Qualification in Land Certificate Cancellation Lawsuits:''' A lawsuit seeking the cancellation of a land certificate that joins the local Agrarian Office as Defendant II satisfies the formal requirements regarding parties, meaning the High Court erred in declaring the lawsuit inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO) solely because the original seller or central Minister of Home Affairs was not co-joined as a separate defendant.

The Supreme Court granted the Plaintiff's ([Party A]) cassation petition, annulled Palembang High Court Decision No. 83/Pdt/1988/PT.Plg dated February 27, 1989, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by upholding the substantive verdict of the Palembang District Court in '''Rejecting the Convention Plaintiff's Lawsuit in its Entirety''' and declaring the Reconvention Lawsuit Inadmissible (NO).

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Qualification and Legal Standards for Good Faith Purchasers in Land Transactions ===
''Can a buyer who purchases land before a Land Deed Official (PPAT) claim protection as a good faith purchaser if they failed to diligently examine the rights and origin status of the seller's land which ultimately originated from criminal forgery?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Not Protected by Law.'''
A buyer who executes a transaction without reasonable caution and diligence (''due diligence'') in examining the validity of the seller's foundational title is categorized as a negligent / bad faith purchaser. The principle of legal protection for good faith purchasers does not apply to negligent buyers.

=== 2. Validity of State Administrative Actions (Minister of Home Affairs / BPN Decrees) Canceling Land Certificates Based on Criminal Judgments ===
''Does a Decree issued by the Minister of Home Affairs / Land Authority canceling a Hak Milik Certificate based on an in-kracht criminal forgery judgment constitute a Tort by the Government (Onrechtmatige Overheidsdaad)?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Valid and Not a Tort.'''
Pursuant to Article 12 ''jo.'' Article 14 of Minister of Home Affairs Regulation No. 6 of 1972, Land Authorities possess administrative authority to cancel land certificates issued on the basis of cadastral technical errors or criminal forgery of documents / false statements (Article 266 of the Criminal Code). The issuance of such cancellation decrees is legally valid, and lawsuits seeking their annulment must be rejected.

=== 3. Formal Plurality Requirements for Defendants in Land Certificate Cancellation Lawsuits ===
Joining the local Agrarian Office as Defendant II satisfies formal party requirements to test the validity of a certificate cancellation action, meaning Courts must not declare lawsuits inadmissible (NO) solely because the original seller or central Minister of Home Affairs was not independently co-sued.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Palembang High Court (Decision No. 83/Pdt/1988/PT.Plg) err in applying civil procedure law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') by declaring the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible (NO) due to non-joinder, and how are the Plaintiff's status as a land buyer and the validity of the Minister of Home Affairs Decree qualified?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. Palembang High Court erred in applying civil procedure law. The Supreme Court granted Plaintiff [Party A]'s cassation petition, annulled Palembang High Court Decision No. 83/Pdt/1988/PT.Plg, and independently adjudicated by Rejecting the Convention Plaintiff's Lawsuit in its Entirety on the grounds that the Plaintiff was a negligent purchaser and the Minister of Home Affairs Decree canceling the certificate was legally valid.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Palembang District Court & Palembang High Court) ===
Examination of facts regarding the land and house purchase transaction covering 118 m² on Cek Syech St. RT 05 No. 203, Palembang, on September 2, 1974, between [Party A] and Mohamad Ali bin Nurdin and H. Abdul Hamid before Notary/PPAT Darbi, S.H.; issuance of SHM No. 169/18 Ilir dated April 24, 1976, GS No. 1217 in the name of [Party A]; Palembang District Court Criminal Judgment No. 684/1976/PN.Plg dated October 14, 1976, sentencing sellers to 6 months imprisonment for authentic deed forgery / Article 266 of the Criminal Code; issuance of Minister of Home Affairs Decree No. 550/Dja/1986 dated September 13, 1986; and actual physical possession of the land by heirs of [Deceased landowner] / [Heir] et al.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata):''' Articles 1320, 1338, 1365 (Torts / ''Perbuatan Melawan Hukum'').
* '''Criminal Code (KUHP):''' Article 266 paragraphs (1) & (2) (Authentic Deed Forgery / Directing False Statements to be Entered).
* '''Agrarian Regulations:''' Minister of Home Affairs Regulation No. 6 of 1972 (Articles 12 ''jo.'' 14) & Government Regulation No. 10 of 1961 / Government Regulation No. 24 of 1997 on Land Registration.
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation authority and independent adjudication powers.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* Doctrine of Good Faith Purchaser: Legal protection principles are granted exclusively to honest and diligent buyers. Negligent buyers / those failing to research seller ownership status enjoy no legal protection.
* Supreme Court Decision No. 383 K/Sip/1971 & Supreme Court Decision No. 1080 K/Sip/1973: Validity of certificates and scope of certificate cancellations resulting from root title forgery.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* The original sellers (Mohamad Ali bin Nurdin & H. Abdul Hamid) were proven to hold no rights over the disputed land and were convicted under Palembang District Court Decision No. 684/1976/PN.Plg for authentic deed forgery / Article 266 of the Criminal Code.
* The Plaintiff ([Party A]) was proven negligent in purchasing the land by failing to examine the status and rights of the sellers, thus failing to qualify for legal protection as a good faith purchaser.
* Minister of Home Affairs Decree No. 550/Dja/1986 dated September 13, 1986, canceling SHM No. 169/18 Ilir was proven legally valid and not a tort.
* The Convention Plaintiff's Lawsuit is '''REJECTED IN ITS ENTIRETY'''.
* Defendant I's Reconvention Lawsuit is declared '''INADMISSIBLE''' (NO).

=== Annulled (Palembang High Court Verdict) ===
* Palembang High Court considerations declaring the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible (NO) due to non-joinder were entirely annulled by the Supreme Court as erroneous applications of procedural law.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Standard of Due Diligence for Pre-PP No. 24 of 1997 Land Purchasers:''' This landmark ruling provides an exceptionally crucial legal precedent in Indonesia: Deeds of Sale and Purchase executed before Notaries/PPATs and Hak Milik Certificates do not automatically render buyers immune to legal challenges if initial transactions are executed negligently from unauthorized sellers. Buyers carry obligations to perform thorough examinations (''due care'') regarding physical and juridical histories of land prior to transactions.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
;Is a land buyer who purchases before a PPAT protected by law if the seller's foundational root title stems from document forgery, and can BPN/Minister of Home Affairs cancel such land certificate?
:'''Negligent buyers receive no legal protection, and BPN/Minister of Home Affairs possess authority to cancel certificates.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 1816 K/Pdt/1989:
:* Buyers failing to carefully examine the rights and ownership status of sellers are classified as negligent purchasers (''bad faith / negligent purchasers'') and deserve no legal protection, even if transactions occur before Notaries/PPATs.
:* If certificates are issued based on root titles proven forged via criminal judgments (Article 266 KUHP), the Minister of Home Affairs / BPN is authorized to cancel such land certificates ''ex'' Minister of Home Affairs Regulation No. 6 of 1972, and such cancellation is legally valid and not a tort.

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:1828K PID 1989
wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 1828 K/Pid/1989}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 1828 K/Pid/1989''' (dated July 5, 1990 / deliberation on May 17, 1990) is an Indonesian criminal procedure law precedent establishing fundamental rules regarding the limitation of pretrial (''praperadilan'') objects, the subjects entitled to claim pretrial compensation, and the mechanism for filing a Cassation in the Interest of Law by the Attorney General of the Republic of Indonesia (''ex'' Article 259 of KUHAP).

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established three primary legal principles:

# '''Cassation in the Interest of Law (Article 259 of KUHAP):''' A cassation petition filed by the Attorney General ex officio in the interest of law is not bound by statutory time limits, and a judgment rendered via cassation in the interest of law carries no legal consequences (meaning it cannot disadvantage or alter the legal status of the litigant parties).
# '''Limitation of Pretrial Objects (Article 77 of KUHAP) Regarding Seizure and Delay of Ship Departures:''' The seizure of a merchant vessel and the action of the Harbor Master (''Syahbandar'') / Investigator in delaying or prohibiting a ship from leaving port do '''not''' constitute objects of pretrial proceedings as exhaustively and limitatively stipulated under Article 77 of KUHAP. The prohibition against a vessel leaving port does not qualify as bodily detention under Articles 20 and 21 of KUHAP. The harbor master's action in delaying a vessel is a non-judicial administrative act.
# '''Subjects Entitled to Claim Pretrial Compensation (Article 95 of KUHAP):''' A shipowner who suffers losses due to administrative actions delaying a vessel's departure is '''not''' a subject entitled to claim pretrial compensation under Article 95 of KUHAP (the right to pretrial compensation under Article 95 of KUHAP is exclusively vested in suspects, defendants, or convicts arrested, detained, prosecuted, or tried without legal grounds or due to error).

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition in the interest of law filed by the Petitioner for Cassation (Attorney General of the Republic of Indonesia), annulled North Jakarta District Court Decision No. 02/Pra.Per./Pen.Pid./1988/PN.JU. dated October 10, 1988, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by '''Rejecting''' the Pretrial Petitioner's ([Defendant]) application while determining that this ruling carries no legal consequences pursuant to Article 259 paragraph (2) of KUHAP.

The cassation verdict... carries no legal consequences." || 1828K_PID_1989.pdf

The prohibition against a vessel leaving port is not detention as intended in articles 20 and 21 of KUHAP." || 1828K_PID_1989.pdf

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Limitative Principle of Pretrial Objects (Article 77 of KUHAP) Regarding Vessel Seizures and Departure Delays (Non-Judicial Administrative Actions) ===
''Can the action of the Harbor Master / Investigator in delaying the departure of a merchant vessel (MV Cherry Navee) in port or executing a property seizure be reviewed for legality via Pretrial proceedings ex Article 77 of KUHAP?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Not a Pretrial Object.'''
Pretrial authority under Article 77 of KUHAP is exhaustively and limitatively structured, restricted solely to: (a) reviewing the legality of arrests, detentions, investigation terminations, or prosecution terminations; and (b) compensation and/or rehabilitation for suspects, their families, or third parties. Property/vessel seizures and port departure delays by Harbor Masters pursuant to Port Regulations of 1925 constitute non-judicial administrative acts falling outside pretrial jurisdiction.

=== 2. Delineation of Pretrial Compensation Claim Subjects (Article 95 ''jo.'' Articles 79, 80, 81 of KUHAP) ===
''Is a shipowner (an external party / non-suspect) entitled to file a pretrial compensation application ex Article 95 of KUHAP concerning a vessel delay action?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Not Entitled.'''
Pursuant to Article 95 of KUHAP, the right to claim pretrial compensation is exclusively vested in suspects, defendants, or convicts arrested, detained, prosecuted, or tried without statutory grounds or due to misidentification/legal error. A shipowner whose property is subjected to administrative delay measures does not qualify as a legal subject entitled to claim compensation through pretrial channels.

=== 3. Nature and Legal Consequences of Cassation in the Interest of Law by the Attorney General (Article 259 of KUHAP) ===
A cassation petition in the interest of law may be filed by the Attorney General against all final judgments possessing legal force rendered by courts below the Supreme Court. Pursuant to Article 259 paragraph (2) of KUHAP, a cassation verdict in the interest of law must not prejudice or alter the legal standing of the litigating parties (carrying no legal consequences), functioning exclusively as a doctrinal precedent correction to preserve uniformity in the national application of law (''legal unification'').

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
Did the North Jakarta District Court (Decision No. 02/Pra.Per./Pen.Pid./1988/PN.JU.) err in applying criminal procedure law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') by granting the pretrial petition concerning the departure delay of MV Cherry Navee and ordering the Police to pay compensation, and how are the jurisdictional limits of pretrial defined under Articles 77 & 95 of KUHAP?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. North Jakarta District Court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court granted the Cassation in the Interest of Law filed by the Attorney General of the Republic of Indonesia, annulled North Jakarta District Court Decision No. 02/Pra.Per./Pen.Pid./1988/PN.JU., and independently adjudicated by Rejecting the Petitioner's Pretrial Application while determining that this ruling carries no legal consequences ''ex'' Article 259 paragraph (2) of KUHAP.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / North Jakarta District Court) ===
Examination of facts regarding the departure delay of merchant vessel MV Cherry Navee at Tanjung Priok Port on June 11, 1988, by the Harbor Master at the request of the National Police Economic Crimes Sub-Directorate; seizure of crew passports (witnesses [Party B] and Chit Thein Tun) and vessel logs; claims for operational financial losses amounting to USD 730,000 asserted by the Petitioner; and proof of administrative delay measures pursuant to Port Regulations of 1925 and Presidential Instruction No. 4 of 1985.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''Law No. 8 of 1981 (Criminal Procedure Code / KUHAP):'''
** Article 77: Exhaustive Pretrial Objects.
** Articles 79, 80, 81: Subjects Entitled to File Pretrial Applications.
** Article 95: Right to Pretrial Compensation.
** Article 259 paragraphs (1) & (2): Cassation in the Interest of Law by the Attorney General.
* '''Port Regulations of 1925:''' Article 23 paragraph (2) (Harbor Master Authority to Delay Vessel Departures).
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Authority regarding Cassation in the Interest of Law.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* Doctrine of Limitative Pretrial Objects: Pretrial institutions must not be expanded arbitrarily beyond coercive measures expressly enumerated under Article 77 of KUHAP.
* Non-Executorial Character of Cassation in the Interest of Law: Verdicts rendered in the interest of law operate purely as legal corrections (doctrinal/precedent corrections) without altering concrete civil/criminal rights adjudicated below.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* The Cassation Petition in the Interest of Law filed by the Attorney General of the Republic of Indonesia was granted by the Supreme Court.
* North Jakarta District Court Decision No. 02/Pra.Per./Pen.Pid./1988/PN.JU. dated October 10, 1988, was entirely annulled by the Supreme Court.
* The Pretrial Application filed by the Petitioner ([Defendant]) is '''REJECTED IN ITS ENTIRETY'''.
* Vessel delay and seizure actions are '''NOT''' pretrial objects.
* The Petitioner is '''NOT''' a subject entitled to claim pretrial compensation ''ex'' Article 95 of KUHAP.
* This cassation ruling is determined to carry '''NO LEGAL CONSEQUENCES''' ''ex'' Article 259 paragraph (2) of KUHAP.

=== Annulled (North Jakarta District Court Verdict) ===
* North Jakarta District Court's verdict declaring vessel seizure/detention unlawful and ordering the Police to pay Rp 500,000 in compensation was entirely annulled by the Supreme Court as contrary to KUHAP.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Separation of Pretrial vs. State Administrative Court (PTUN) / Tort Lawsuits (PMH):''' This landmark ruling establishes absolute legal clarity in Indonesia: third parties or property owners aggrieved by administrative actions of state officials (such as port departure delays by harbor masters) cannot invoke Pretrial proceedings. The proper legal recourse to test such administrative measures lies within the State Administrative Court (PTUN) or civil tort lawsuits against the Government (''Onrechtmatige Overheidsdaad'').

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
; Are merchant vessel seizures or port departure prohibitions objects of pretrial proceedings, and can shipowners claim compensation via pretrial?
: '''Not pretrial objects and ineligible to claim pretrial compensation.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 1828 K/Pid/1989:
:* Pursuant to Article 77 of KUHAP, pretrial objects are exhaustively limited (restricted solely to testing the legality of arrests, detentions, investigation/prosecution terminations, and suspect compensation). Vessel seizures and port departure delays by harbor masters are not pretrial objects.
:* Pursuant to Article 95 of KUHAP, the right to claim pretrial compensation belongs exclusively to suspects, defendants, or convicts. Shipowners do not qualify as subjects entitled to claim pretrial compensation.
:* The Supreme Court granted the Cassation in the Interest of Law (Article 259 of KUHAP) filed by the Attorney General, annulled the North Jakarta District Court verdict, and rejected the pretrial application without legal consequences for the parties.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 189 K/AG/1996 dated January 8, 1998, establishes important Islamic Civil Procedure jurisprudence concerning the assessment of vague lawsuits (*obscuur libel*): In joint property (*gono gini*) disputes, a High Religious Court decision that annuls a Religious Court judgment and declares the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible on the grounds of vagueness (*obscuur libel*), without providing complete argumentation and legal reasoning regarding its obscurity, constitutes an error in applying the law and must be annulled by the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court reinstated the Gorontalo Religious Court judgment, which granted the equitable division of joint property between former spouses.

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation ([Plaintiff], [age removed], merchant, residing in [address removed]) and the Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation ([Defendant], entrepreneur, Gorontalo) married lawfully in 1977 and divorced on May 24, 1994 (Gorontalo Religious Court Decision No. 28/Pdt.G/1994/PA.Gorontalo), and were blessed with 4 children ([Child], [Child], [Child], [Child]). The Plaintiff filed a lawsuit for the division of joint property acquired during the marriage (1977–1994), comprising a house in Tenda Village (SHM No. 44/1978), a multi-story house in Dolong, Central Sulawesi, a Vespa motorcycle, clove trees, a motorboat, and cash.

The Gorontalo Religious Court (Decision No. 80/Pdt.G/1994/PA.GTLO dated March 29, 1995 AD / 27 Shawwal 1415 AH) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part and stipulated an equitable division of the joint property at 1/2 share each. The Manado High Religious Court (Decision No. 17/Pdt.G/1995/PTA.Mdo dated December 28, 1995 AD / 5 Sha'ban 1416 AH) annulled the Gorontalo Religious Court decision and declared the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible (*niet ontvankelijke verklaard*) on the grounds that the lawsuit was vague (*obscuur libel*). The Plaintiff ([Plaintiff]) filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The Manado High Religious Court committed an error in applying the law by declaring the Petitioner for Cassation / Original Plaintiff's lawsuit unclear (*obscuur libel*) without providing argumentation regarding its obscurity, rendering the legal reasoning of the Manado High Religious Court incomplete (*onvoldoende gemotiveerd*).
# The *posita* and *petitum* of the Original Plaintiff's lawsuit detailed the evidence, locations, areas, and boundaries of the joint property objects acquired during the marriage, meaning the Gorontalo Religious Court acted correctly and accurately in considering and ruling upon the division of such joint property.
# Consequently, the Petitioner for Cassation's petition is granted, the Manado High Religious Court decision is annulled, and the Supreme Court independently adjudicates by upholding the Gorontalo Religious Court decision dated March 29, 1995, No. 80/Pdt.G/1994/PA.GTLO.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation [Plaintiff]; Annulling the Manado High Religious Court decision dated December 28, 1995 AD, No. 17/Pdt.G/1995/PTA.Mdo; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part; (2) Declaring that the disputed properties listed under ad. I, II, III, IV, VI, and VII of the lawsuit petition constitute the joint property of the Plaintiff and Defendant; (3) Allocating the Plaintiff's share of the joint property as the property listed under ad. I of the lawsuit petition and 1/2 (one-half) of the properties listed under ad. III, VI, and VII of the lawsuit petition; (4) Allocating the Defendant's share of the joint property as the property listed under ad. II of the lawsuit petition and 1/2 (one-half) of the properties listed under ad. III, VI, and VII of the lawsuit petition; (5) Ordering the Plaintiff and Defendant to divide the joint properties listed under points III, VI, and VII of the lawsuit petition into 1/2 (one-half) shares each; (6) Declaring that the security confiscation (*Conservatoir Beslag*) executed by the Bailiff of the Gorontalo Religious Court on September 22, 1994, No. 80/Pdt.G/1994/PA.Gtlo is valid and enforceable; (7) Rejecting the remainder of the Plaintiff's lawsuit; (8) Ordering the Plaintiff to pay first-instance court costs and ordering the Appellant to pay appellate-level court costs; Ordering the Petitioner for Cassation to pay cassation-level court costs amounting to Rp 50,000 (fifty thousand rupiahs). *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court on Thursday, January 8, 1998, by the Cassation Panel of Justices: H. Yahya Harahap, SH. [Junior Chairman / Presiding Judge], Drs. H. Taufiq, SH., and H. Chabib Sjarbini, SH.).*

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:1900K PID 2002
wikitext:
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 1900 K/Pid/2002''' (deliberated on July 15, 2004 / pronounced on September 23, 2004) is a landmark Indonesian corruption and criminal procedure jurisprudence precedent establishing pivotal rules regarding the status of the Governor of Bank Indonesia as state cashier / holder of government accounts in executing the disbursement of the Government Guarantee Program (Bank Bali Scandal / PT Era Giat Prima Cessie Case) and the Inadmissibility of Cassation Petitions Against Pure Acquittals (''vrijspraak'' ''ex'' Article 244 of KUHAP).

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established three primary legal principles:

# '''Status of the Governor of Bank Indonesia as State Cashier:''' The action of the Governor of Bank Indonesia (Defendant Dr. [Defendant]) in processing and dispatching the disbursement of Government Guarantee Program funds to settle PT Bank Bali's claim regarding BDNI amounting to Rp 904,642,428,369 was executed within the scope of fulfilling duties as a state cashier or administrator of government accounts pursuant to instructions from IBRA (''BPPN'', specifically Pande N. Lubis as Vice Chairman of IBRA). The Governor of Bank Indonesia possessed no authority to determine claim eligibility and acted solely as a governmental cashier.
# '''Absence of Joint Intent (''Bewustese Samenwerking'' / ''Medeplegen''):''' Because the Defendant's actions were performed based on official IBRA instructions and standard banking administrative duties, the element of "acting jointly" (''medeplegen'') was unfulfilled, negating any abuse of authority or criminal intent (''mens rea'') to enrich oneself or others.
# '''Inadmissibility of Cassation Against Pure Acquittals (Article 244 of KUHAP):''' The Public Prosecutor's cassation petition against the Jakarta High Court decision acquitting the Defendant of all charges (''vrijspraak'') was declared '''Inadmissible''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO), because the Prosecutor's cassation reasons merely repeated evaluations of evidentiary findings (appreciations of fact) and failed to establish the existence of an impure acquittal.

The Supreme Court declared the cassation petition filed by the Petitioner for Cassation, the Prosecutor at the Central Jakarta District Attorney's Office, '''Inadmissible''', and charged cassation court costs to the State.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Status and Limits of Legal Liability for the Governor of Bank Indonesia as State Cashier under the Government Guarantee Program (Presidential Decree No. 26/1998 ''jo.'' BI-IBRA Joint Decree) ===
''Can the Governor of Bank Indonesia, who dispatches the execution of bank claim payments based on official request letters from IBRA, be penalized for joint corruption (''medeplegen'') alongside IBRA management or bank shareholders?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Cannot Be Penalized.''' The Governor of Bank Indonesia acted solely as a state cashier / administrator of government guarantee accounts upon the official request of IBRA (''BPPN'', specifically Pande N. Lubis as Vice Chairman). Verification authority and claim eligibility determinations rested entirely with IBRA (the Ministry of Finance / IBRA). The Governor of BI's policy forwarding payment technical dispositions to the executing unit in accordance with written IBRA instructions constituted neither an unlawful act nor an abuse of authority.

=== 2. Limits of Public Prosecutor Cassation Admissibility Against Pure Acquittals (''Vrijspraak'' ''ex'' Article 244 of KUHAP) ===
''Does the Supreme Court possess authority to grant a Prosecutor's cassation petition against an acquittal when the Prosecutor's grounds relate exclusively to evidentiary evaluations (appreciations of fact)?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Lacks Authority / Must Be Declared Inadmissible (NO).''' Pursuant to Article 244 of KUHAP, cassation cannot be filed against an acquittal unless the Prosecutor proves that the acquittal constitutes an "impure acquittal" (''niet-zuivere vrijspraak''). Because the Public Prosecutor's cassation memorandum merely reiterated factual evidentiary evaluations (appreciations of fact), the Jakarta High Court's acquittal constituted a pure acquittal, requiring the Prosecutor's cassation petition to be declared '''Inadmissible''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'').

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
Did the Public Prosecutor's Cassation Petition from the Central Jakarta District Attorney's Office against Jakarta High Court Decision No. 78/PID/2002/PT.DKI satisfy the formal admissibility requirements for cassation ''ex'' Article 244 of KUHAP, and did the Jakarta High Court ''Judex Facti'' misapply the law?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' The Cassation Petition Fails to Satisfy Admissibility Requirements. The Jakarta High Court judgment constitutes a pure acquittal (''pure acquittal'') because its legal considerations were based on the unproven elements of abuse of authority and joint participation (''medeplegen''). The Public Prosecutor's cassation memorandum, which merely contained re-evaluations of factual evidence, is inadmissible on cassation ''ex'' Article 244 of KUHAP.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Central Jakarta District Court & Jakarta High Court) ===
Examination of facts regarding initial BDNI claim rejections by BI in September–October 1998; verification execution by BI and IBRA guarantee teams; meetings at Mulia Hotel Senayan on February 11, 1999, and May 26, 1999, attended by Pande N. Lubis, Tanri Abeng, A.A. Baramuli, Joko S. Tjandra, Setya Novanto, and Rudy Ramli; execution of Cessie Agreement No. 002/P-EGP/I-99 dated January 11, 1999; issuance of Minister of Finance Power of Attorney SR-176/MK.01/1999 dated May 31, 1999; signing of IBRA Letters No. PB-380/BPPN/0699 and PB-385/BPPN/0699 dated June 1, 1999, by Farid Haryanto / Pande N. Lubis; and the Governor of BI's disposition to UASP Head (Desmi Demas).

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===

* '''Law No. 3 of 1971 ''jo.'' Law No. 31 of 1999 on Eradication of Corruption Crimes:''' Article 1 paragraph (1) sub a / sub b, Article 28, Article 34(c).
* '''Law No. 8 of 1981 (Criminal Procedure Code / KUHAP):''' Article 244 (Prohibition of Cassation Against Pure Acquittals) & Article 197 paragraph (1) letter d.
* '''Law No. 23 of 1999 on Bank Indonesia:''' Duties of the Governor of BI in Managing State Treasury Accounts.
* '''Presidential Decree No. 26 of 1998 & Ministry of Finance-BI-IBRA Joint Decrees:''' Provisions on the Government Guarantee Program for Commercial Bank Obligations.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===

* Doctrine of Evidentiary Evaluation on Cassation: Evaluations of evidentiary results constituting appreciations of fact (''bewijswaardering'') fall within the exclusive domain of the ''judex facti'' and cannot be reviewed on cassation.
* Doctrine of Pure Acquittals: When a Prosecutor's cassation grounds merely repeat facts without demonstrating legal misinterpretations of statutory elements by the ''judex facti'', the cassation petition must be declared inadmissible.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* Defendant Dr. [Defendant] acted in his official capacity as State Cashier / Holder of Government Guarantee Accounts upon the official request of IBRA.
* The Public Prosecutor's Cassation Petition from the Central Jakarta District Attorney's Office is declared '''INADMISSIBLE''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).
* Jakarta High Court Acquittal Decision No. 78/PID/2002/PT.DKI dated August 12, 2002, possesses legal force (''inkracht van gewijsde'').
* The acquittal of Defendant Dr. [Defendant] from all corruption charges and the restoration of his dignity are affirmed by the Supreme Court.
* Cassation court costs are charged to the State.

=== Rejected / Dismissed Arguments ===

* The Public Prosecutor's argument that the Defendant engaged in joint criminal intent (''bewustese samenwerking'' / ''medeplegen'') to enrich Rudy Ramli / Joko S. Tjandra / PT Era Giat Prima was '''NOT PROVEN''' legally and convincingly.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Legal Protection for Monetary Authority Officials Executing State Cashier Functions:''' This landmark ruling establishes a monumental legal precedent in Indonesia: Monetary Authority Officials (Governors of Bank Indonesia) executing administrative state payment disbursement functions based on instructions from authorized governmental bodies (IBRA / Minister of Finance) cannot be criminalized for alleged corruption, provided such actions represent official duty performance devoid of criminal intent (''mens rea'') or personal conflicts of interest.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==

; Can the Governor of Bank Indonesia be penalized for corruption for processing bank guarantee claim payments upon IBRA instructions, and can Prosecutors challenge pure acquittals on cassation?
: '''The Governor of BI cannot be penalized, and Prosecutor cassations are inadmissible.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 1900 K/Pid/2002:

* The Governor of Bank Indonesia, who dispatches disbursements of Government Guarantee Program funds upon IBRA instructions, acts solely as a state/government cashier, committing neither unlawful acts nor abuse of authority (''medeplegen'').
* Pursuant to Article 244 of KUHAP, public prosecutor cassation petitions against pure acquittals (''vrijspraak'') that merely challenge factual evidentiary evaluations must be declared '''Inadmissible''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:1904K PDT 2007
wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 1904 K/Pdt/2007}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 1904 K/Pdt/2007''' (dated September 16, 2008) is a fundamental Indonesian family law and contract/civil law jurisprudence precedent establishing pivotal rules regarding the status of joint spousal liability for debts incurred during marriage, the legal consequences of divorce regarding debt repayment obligations, and the validity of conservatory attachments over joint marital property (''gono-gini'').

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established three primary legal principles:

# '''Joint Liability for Marital Debts (Articles 35 & 36 of Law No. 1 of 1974):''' A debt incurred by either spouse while a marriage is ongoing for business purposes or corporate operations serving as a family income source constitutes a joint debt (a burden upon joint marital property / ''gono-gini'').
# '''Divorce Does Not Extinguish Debt Repayment Obligations:''' Divorce does not result in either party being released from the obligation to pay debts incurred while still bound in marriage. Separation or divorce between a husband and wife does not sever civil legal bonds toward third parties concerning debts born during an intact marriage.
# '''Validity of Conservatory Attachments Over Joint Property (''Conservatoir Beslaag''):''' A conservatory attachment (''conservatoir beslaag'') placed upon joint marital property (''gono-gini'') owned by a husband and wife to guarantee the repayment of marital debts is valid and lawful.

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of Petitioner for Cassation I ([Party B]) and Petitioner for Cassation II ([Party A], Teguh Hertanto, Tanty Anggraini), annulled Semarang High Court Decision No. 205/PDT/2006/PT.SMG dated January 22, 2007, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by upholding the considerations of the Semarang District Court—declaring Defendant I ([Party B]) and Defendant II ([Party C]) in default (''wanprestasi''), ordering Defendant I and Defendant II to jointly and severally pay the remaining principal debt of Rp 787,500,000 along with a moratory interest of 6% per year, and declaring the conservatory attachment over the joint property valid and lawful.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Construction of Spousal Legal Liability for Marital Debts (Articles 35(1)-(2) ''jo.'' 36(1)-(2) of Law No. 1 of 1974) ===
''Is a wife (Defendant II) legally liable for debts incurred by her husband (Defendant I) for family expedition business capital while their marriage remained intact, notwithstanding her claim that she did not co-sign the loan agreement?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Jointly and Severally Liable.'''
Pursuant to Articles 35(1)-(2) ''jo.'' 36(1)-(2) of Law No. 1 of 1974 (interpreted ''a contrario''), all debts arising during marriage for family interests or corporate operations serving as joint income sources constitute joint debts binding both spouses.

=== 2. Legal Impact of Divorce on Third-Party Debt Obligations ===
''Does a subsequent divorce between a husband and wife release the former spouse from the obligation to repay debts incurred during marriage to third parties?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Divorce Does Not Release Debt Obligations.'''
A divorce occurring after a debt arises does not sever civil legal ties or release either party from the obligation to repay that debt to creditors/third parties. The former husband and wife must be ordered to pay such debts jointly and severally (''tanggung renteng'').

=== 3. Validity of Conservatory Attachments (''Conservatoir Beslaag'') Over Joint Property (''Gono-Gini'') ===
Conservatory attachment orders placed by District Courts over jointly owned land and buildings (''gono-gini'') to secure marital debt obligations are valid and lawful, precluding High Courts from unilaterally lifting such attachments.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (''Judex Juris'' / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Semarang High Court (Decision No. 205/PDT/2006/PT.SMG) err in applying family and civil law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') by releasing Defendant II from debt obligations and lifting conservatory attachments, despite such debts being incurred while Defendants I and II remained married?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. Semarang High Court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court granted the cassation petitions of Petitioner for Cassation I ([Party B]) and Petitioners for Cassation II ([Party A] et al.), annulled Semarang High Court Decision No. 205/PDT/2006/PT.SMG, and independently adjudicated by ordering Defendants I and II to jointly and severally pay remaining principal debt of Rp 787,500,000 plus 6% annual moratory interest, while declaring the conservatory attachment over joint property valid and lawful.

=== Question of Fact (''Judex Facti'' / Semarang District Court & Semarang High Court) ===
Examination of facts regarding loan agreements totaling Rp 1,000,000,000 between Defendant I and Plaintiffs between October 17, 1999, and February 9, 2003, for PT Bermuda Cemerlang Abadi capital; repayment totaling Rp 125,000,000 leaving a principal debt of Rp 875,000,000 (calculated in District Court / Supreme Court verdicts as Rp 787,500,000); marriage of Defendants I & II in 1989 and divorce judgment dated September 28, 2005 (Semarang District Court No. 132/Pdt/G/2005/PN.Smg); and verification of Conservatory Attachment Minutes No. 145/Pdt.G/2005/PN.Smg.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''Law No. 1 of 1974 on Marriage:'''
** Article 35 paragraphs (1) & (2): Marital Property and Debts.
** Article 36 paragraphs (1) & (2): Rights and Responsibilities Over Joint Property.
** Article 37: Consequences of Divorce on Joint Property.
* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata):''' Article 1282 (Joint and Several Liability) & Article 1338 (Principle of Freedom of Contract / ''Pacta Sunt Servanda'').
* '''HIR / RBg:''' Article 227 HIR (Conservatory Attachment / ''Conservatoir Beslaag'').
* '''Law No. 14 of 1985 ''jo.'' Law No. 5 of 2004 on the Supreme Court:''' Independent Adjudication Powers at Cassation Level.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* Doctrine of Joint Marital Debt Liability: Loans executed by either spouse for business capital whose proceeds sustain family economics automatically bind the other spouse as a joint ''gono-gini'' property debt.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* Business capital loan debts were incurred while Defendants I and II remained in an intact marriage (1999–2003) for family business interests.
* The 2005 divorce did not extinguish joint debt status toward the Plaintiffs/Creditors.
* Defendants I and II were proven in default (''wanprestasi'') and ordered to jointly and severally pay remaining principal debt of Rp 787,500,000 plus 6% annual moratory interest.
* Conservatory attachments (''conservatoir beslaag'') placed over joint property (''gono-gini'') are declared valid and lawful.

=== Annulled (Semarang High Court Verdict) ===
* Semarang High Court considerations releasing Defendant II from debt obligations and lifting conservatory attachments were entirely annulled by the Supreme Court as erroneous applications of family law.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Proving Actual Utilization of Loan Proceeds in Marital Debt Disputes:''' This landmark ruling provides an exceptionally clear legal precedent in Indonesia: spouses cannot evade family debt repayment obligations on formalistic grounds of failing to co-sign loan applications or having divorced. Provided loans are incurred during ongoing marriage and utilized to support family businesses/income, such debts legally bind both parties jointly and severally.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==

:* Divorce does not result in either party being released from obligations to pay debts incurred while bound in marriage pursuant to Articles 35 & 36 of Law No. 1 of 1974. Family business capital debts remain joint burdens, and former spouses are ordered to pay jointly and severally.
:* Conservatory attachments (''conservatoir beslaag'') placed over joint marital property (''gono-gini'') to secure marital debt repayment are valid and lawful.

{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 1974 K/Pdt/2001}} '''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 1974 K/Pdt/2001''' (dated September 29, 2003) is an Indonesian land and civil evidence law jurisprudence precedent establishing a fundamental rule regarding the evidentiary requirements for establishing signature forgery in land rights transfers / authentic Deeds of Sale and Purchase (AJB):
''"The transfer of land rights declared legally flawed due to signature forgery, rendering the land sale and purchase null and void, MUST BE PROVEN THROUGH AN EXAMINATION BY THE CRIMINOLOGY LABORATORY (NATIONAL POLICE LABKRIM) OR PURSUANT TO A CRIMINAL JUDGMENT DECLARING THE SIGNATURE FORGED."''
== Executive Summary == The Supreme Court affirmed that appellate courts are unjustified in annulling Deeds of Sale and Purchase (''Akta Jual Beli'' / AJB) and certificate name transfers solely based on visual signature comparison assessments conducted by judges without expert assistance. Because the Plaintiff failed to substantiate allegations of signature forgery via National Police Criminology Laboratory examination results or a legally binding criminal court judgment, the Plaintiff's lawsuit must be declared inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO). The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioners for Cassation ([Party C], S.H., Ny. [Party B], S.H., PT Puri Ayu Lestari, [Party D]), annulled Bandung High Court Decision No. 445/Pdt/1999/PT.Bdg dated June 29, 2000, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by declaring the Plaintiff's ([Party A], S.H.) Convention and Reconvention Lawsuit '''Inadmissible''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO). == Infobox == {| class="wikitable" |- ! Object ID | JPAIS:PRECEDENT:1974K_PDT_2001 |- ! Legal Standards for Proving Signature Forgery in Authentic Deeds / Land AJB (Article 1868 of the Civil Code / Civil Evidence Law) === ''Is an Appellate Court legally justified in declaring a signature within an authentic Deed of Sale and Purchase (AJB) forged solely based on visual observations made by judges in court without an examination by the National Police Criminology Laboratory or a criminal judgment?'' '''Supreme Court Rule: Unjustified / Evidentiary Defect.''' Evaluating the falsity of a signature on an authentic deed drawn before a Notary/PPAT must not rest upon the naked visual inspection of judges (judicial subjectivity). To prove a signature was forged, Civil Evidence Law mandates scientific proof in the form of National Police Criminology Laboratory (''Labkrim'') Examination Results or a legally binding criminal court judgment declaring the signature forged. === 2. Appropriate Cassation Verdict Qualification for Evidentiary Defects (Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard / NO) === When a Plaintiff grounds a lawsuit on the premise that a transfer of land rights is null and void due to signature forgery, yet fails to tender National Police Labkrim examination results or a criminal judgment into evidence, the lawsuit must be declared inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO). == Question of Law vs Question of Fact == === Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) === Did the ''Judex Facti'' Bandung High Court (Decision No. 445/Pdt/1999/PT.Bdg) err in applying the law of evidence (''foutieve toepassing van het bewijsrecht'') by annulling deeds of sale and purchase and land rights transfers based solely on visual judge comparisons of signatures, and what constitutes the legal evidentiary standard for signature forgery in civil disputes? '''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. Bandung High Court misapplied the law of evidence. The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioners for Cassation, annulled Bandung High Court Decision No. 445/Pdt/1999/PT.Bdg dated June 29, 2000, and independently adjudicated by declaring the Plaintiff's Lawsuit Inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO). === Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Tangerang District Court & Bandung High Court) === Examination of facts regarding land ownership covering 97,501 m² in Buaran and Pondok Benda Villages, Serpong, Tangerang; issuance of SHM Nos. 625 through 631, SHM Nos. 405 through 409, and customary land titles C.930, C.833, C.912, C.278, C.2151, C.2095; execution of AJB Nos. 1131/21/V/Serpong/1992 through 1137/27/V/Serpong/1992 before Notary [Party C], S.H., and AJB Nos. 658/24/V/Serpong/JB/1990 through 662/28/V/Serpong/JB/1990 before Notary Ny. [Party B], S.H.; name transfer procedures at Tangerang Regency BPN to [Party D] and subsequent transfer to PT Puri Ayu Lestari (SHGB Nos. 5956 and 5957); and visual signature matching conducted by the Bandung High Court panel. == Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge == === Statutory Regulations === * '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata / BW):''' Articles 1868, 1870, 1871 (Evidentiary Force of Authentic Deeds). * '''HIR / RBg:''' Provisions on Civil Procedural Law and Witness/Expert/Documentary Evidence. * '''Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation and Independent Adjudication Authority. === Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence === * '''Doctrine of Authentic Deed Falsity Proof:''' Authentic deeds drawn before Public Officials (Notaries/PPAT) possess complete evidentiary force (''volledig bewijskracht''). Rebuttal evidence attempting to defeat an authentic deed on grounds of signature forgery must be scientifically proven via Police Criminology / Forensic Laboratory testing or pursuant to a legally binding criminal judgment (''inkracht van gewijsde''). == What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish == === Established by Evidence === * The cassation petition filed by the Petitioners for Cassation ([Party C], S.H., Ny. [Party B], S.H., PT Puri Ayu Lestari, [Party D]) is granted by the Supreme Court. * Bandung High Court Decision No. 445/Pdt/1999/PT.Bdg dated June 29, 2000, is entirely annulled. * The Plaintiff's ([Party A], S.H.) Convention and Reconvention Lawsuit is declared '''INADMISSIBLE''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO). * Respondent for Cassation / Original Plaintiff ordered to pay court costs across all levels of jurisdiction (cassation assessed at Rp 200,000). === Unproven / Annulled Arguments === * The Plaintiff's allegation that his signature was forged in the AJBs was '''UNPROVEN''' due to the absence of National Police Criminology Laboratory examination results or a criminal judgment. * The Bandung High Court verdict declaring AJBs and certificate name transfers null and void while ordering Rp 2 Billion in damages was entirely annulled by the Supreme Court. == Uncertainties and Gaps == '''Separation Between Civil and Criminal Proof in Document Forgery:''' This landmark ruling establishes absolute legal clarity in Indonesia: in land disputes involving authentic deeds (Notary/PPAT AJBs), Plaintiffs cannot invalidate certificates or deeds merely by asserting unilaterally that "my signature was forged." Without scientific proof from the National Police Criminology Laboratory or a criminal court judgment declaring such signature forged, civil lawsuits must be declared inadmissible (NO). == Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) == ; What evidentiary requirements apply when someone seeks to cancel a land sale or certificate on grounds of signature forgery pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence? : '''Mandatory examination by a Criminology Laboratory or a Criminal Judgment.''' title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:1992K PDT 2000
wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 1992 K/Pdt/2000}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 1992 K/Pdt/2000''' (dated October 23, 2002) is an Indonesian civil procedure law jurisprudence precedent establishing two vital legal rules regarding the legal consequences of an appellate court's failure to consider defendant exceptions (''Onvoldoende Gemotiveerd'') and the formal validity requirements of a Special Power of Attorney (''Surat Kuasa Khusus'').

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established two primary legal principles:

# '''Imperfect Judgment (''Onvoldoende Gemotiveerd'') Resulting from Ignored Exceptions:''' If the ''Judex Facti'' (High Court) annuls a District Court judgment without reviewing and considering the exceptions raised by the Defendant, such High Court judgment must be declared incomplete (''onvoldoende gemotiveerd'') and null and void.
# '''Validity of a Special Power of Attorney Without Detailed Listing of All Defendant Names:''' The failure to exhaustively list every defendant's name in detail within a special power of attorney does not render the power of attorney void or invalid, provided the power of attorney clearly specifies the plaintiff's name, the basis of the lawsuit, the object of the lawsuit, and the name of Defendant I.

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioners for Cassation ([Party A] et al.), annulled Bandung High Court Decision No. 556/Pdt/1998/PT.Bdg dated December 23, 1998, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by ordering the Bandung High Court to examine and adjudicate the merits of the case (''pokok perkara''), while ordering the Respondents for Cassation / Original Defendants to pay cassation court costs amounting to Rp 100,000.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Legal Consequences of High Court Omission of Exception Considerations (Imperfection / ''Onvoldoende Gemotiveerd'') ===
''Is a High Court justified in annulling a District Court judgment without considering exceptions raised by the Defendant?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Unjustified / Procedural Defect.'''
A High Court judgment annulling a District Court judgment without examining and reviewing exceptions rejected or considered by the District Court constitutes an incomplete judgment (''onvoldoende gemotiveerd'').

=== 2. Formal Validity Parameters of Special Civil Powers of Attorney (SEMA No. 1 of 1971 / SEMA No. 6 of 1994) ===
''Does a Special Power of Attorney submitted by a Plaintiff become void or invalid solely because it fails to itemize the names and addresses of all Defendants (specifying only Defendant I et al.)?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Remains Valid.'''
A special power of attorney containing the Plaintiff's name, the legal basis of the lawsuit, the object of the lawsuit, and specifically naming Defendant I satisfies the requirement of specificity (''substansi spesifik''). The omission of detailed listings for every individual co-defendant does not render the special power of attorney void or invalid.

=== 3. Supreme Court Independent Adjudication Authority Remanding Cases for Adjudication on Merits ===
When a High Court erroneously renders an inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO) judgment based on power of attorney formalities, the Supreme Court possesses authority to annul such judgment and remand the case to the High Court to examine and adjudicate the merits (''remand for judgment on merits'').

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (''Judex Juris'' / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Bandung High Court (Decision No. 556/Pdt/1998/PT.Bdg) err in applying civil procedure law (''foutieve toepassing van het procesrecht'') by declaring the Plaintiff's Special Power of Attorney void and dismissing the lawsuit as inadmissible (NO) without considering exceptions?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. Bandung High Court misapplied civil procedure law. The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioners for Cassation ([Party A] et al.), annulled Bandung High Court Decision No. 556/Pdt/1998/PT.Bdg, and independently adjudicated by ordering the Bandung High Court to examine and adjudicate the merits of the case.

=== Question of Fact (''Judex Facti'' / Bandung District Court & Bandung High Court) ===
Examination of facts regarding family relationships among heirs of the late Ny. Idjah and late Dede Sukamaja; validity of Inheritance Rights Certificate Notarial Deed No. 1/KWI-I/1994 by Notary Siti Munigar Temmy Suhandy, S.H.; execution of the Deliberation Minutes Statement dated November 6, 1995, concerning inheritance distribution obligations of Rp 75,000,000 per person; gold conversion calculations for damages; physical possession of assets including the Kopo 333 Bandung residence, Cikutra/Bojongkoneng property, and shares in PT Saudara Tunggal Kemajuan; and conservatory attachment rulings (''conservatoir beslag'') No. 88/Pdt/G/1998/PN.Bdg.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''HIR / RBg:''' Special Power of Attorney Provisions (Article 123 HIR / Article 147 RBg) & Formal Lawsuit Requirements.
* '''Supreme Court Circular Letters (SEMA):''' SEMA No. 1 of 1971 & SEMA No. 6 of 1994 on Special Power of Attorney Formulation Guidelines.
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation Authority and Remand Remission Powers.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* Doctrine of ''Onvoldoende Gemotiveerd'' Judgments: Judgments omitting exception considerations or failing to supply adequate legal reasoning for annulments are null and void as incomplete (''onvoldoende gemotiveerd'').
* Doctrine of Power of Attorney Formal Flexibility: Specificity in powers of attorney is governed by the clarity of the dispute object and primary parties, rather than a rigid requirement to list every co-defendant.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* The Petitioners for Cassation's Special Power of Attorney dated April 7, 1999 / May 21, 1997, is '''VALID''' and satisfies civil procedure formalities.
* Bandung High Court Decision No. 556/Pdt/1998/PT.Bdg dated December 23, 1998, is legally defective (''onvoldoende gemotiveerd'') and annulled by the Supreme Court.
* Bandung High Court is legally ordered to examine and adjudicate the substantive merits of the inheritance dispute.
* Respondents for Cassation / Original Defendants ordered to pay cassation court costs amounting to Rp 100,000.

=== Unproven / Reserved (Awaiting High Court Merits Review) ===
* The Supreme Court has not adjudicated the substantive material merits of the inheritance dispute in this cassation instance, but has restored jurisdiction to the Bandung High Court to adjudicate the merits.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Special Power of Attorney Formalities vs. Access to Justice:''' This landmark ruling provides a critical procedural precedent in Indonesia: ''Judex Facti'' must avoid hyper-formalistic refusals of public lawsuits merely because a special power of attorney omits exhaustive typed listings of dozens of co-defendant names, provided the lawsuit identity, dispute object, and primary Defendants are clear. Rigid formalism ignoring exceptions produces legally defective (''onvoldoende gemotiveerd'') judgments.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
; Is a special power of attorney considered invalid if it fails to comprehensively list all defendant names, and what are the consequences if a court fails to consider exceptions?
: '''The power of attorney remains valid, and judgments omitting exception considerations are legally defective.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 1992 K/Pdt/2000:
* The omission of comprehensive listings for all co-defendant names within a special power of attorney does not render it void or invalid, provided it specifies the plaintiff, legal basis, dispute object, and Defendant I.
* If a High Court annuls a District Court judgment without considering the Defendant's exceptions, such judgment is classified as incomplete (''onvoldoende gemotiveerd'') and is annulled by the Supreme Court.

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:2064K PDT 1991
wikitext:
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 2064 K/Pdt/1991''' (dated February 28, 1994 / deliberation on February 24, 1994) is a fundamental Indonesian land and civil evidence law jurisprudence precedent establishing a crucial rule regarding the perfect evidentiary force (''volledig bewijskracht'') of Land Rights Certificates (''Sertifikat Hak Milik'') and the inability of witness testimonies grounded in conjecture or indication (''legenbewijs / aanwijzingen'') to defeat them.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established two primary legal principles:

# '''Perfect Evidentiary Force of Land Rights Certificates:''' A Land Rights Certificate (''Sertifikat Hak Milik'') issued by authorized land authorities in accordance with applicable legal procedures (e.g., Government Regulation No. 10 of 1961 on Land Registration) constitutes an authentic instrument possessing perfect evidentiary force (''volledig bewijskracht'').
# '''Witness Testimonies / Conjectures (''Legenbewijs / Aanwijzingen'') Cannot Overturn Certificates:''' An Appellate Court errs in applying the law of evidence when it overturns or invalidates a legally issued Land Rights Certificate solely by relying on witness testimonies providing conjecture or indications (''legenbewijs / aanwijzingen'') regarding past oral purchase transactions. Standalone witness testimonies are insufficient to break down authentic certificate evidence issued pursuant to legal procedure.

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioners for Cassation ([Party B], Wardinah, Warda — heirs of the late H. Tompo), annulled Ujung Pandang High Court Decision No. 112/Pdt/1991/PT.Uj.Pdg dated March 16, 1991, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by adopting Polewali District Court Decision No. 36/Pdt.G/1990/PN.Pol dated November 12, 1990—partially granting the Plaintiffs' lawsuit, declaring the disputed 8,273 m² rice field as the property of H. Tompo inherited by the Plaintiffs, and ordering the Defendant ([Defendant]) to surrender the disputed rice field.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Hierarchy of Land Evidentiary Force (Land Rights Certificate vs. Witness Testimony / ''Legenbewijs'') ===
''Can oral witness testimonies asserting that a land transaction occurred with other parties decades prior undermine the legal force of a Land Rights Certificate officially issued pursuant to Government Regulation No. 10 of 1961?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Cannot Overturn.''' A Land Rights Certificate represents an authentic instrument issued by authorized land authorities following measurement procedures, land history research, and unprotested public announcements. This certificate possesses perfect evidentiary force (''volledig bewijskracht''). Witness testimonies constituting conjecture or indications (''legenbewijs / aanwijzingen'') carry no legal weight capable of defeating the validity of such authentic certificates.

=== 2. Open Acknowledgment of Certificate Procedure Validity (''Praesumptio Iustae Causa'' / Estoppel) ===
A defendant who never raises objections during the land registration announcement process (3 months) and never legally files a lawsuit to cancel a certificate is deemed by law to acknowledge the validity of such land rights certificate.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (''Judex Juris'' / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Ujung Pandang High Court (Decision No. 112/Pdt/1991/PT.Uj.Pdg) err in applying the law of evidence (''foutieve toepassing van het bewijsrecht'') by setting aside Land Rights Certificate No. 7613252 in the name of H. Tompo and ruling in favor of the Defendant based solely on oral witness testimonies?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. Ujung Pandang High Court misapplied the law of evidence. The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioners for Cassation ([Party B] et al.), annulled Ujung Pandang High Court Decision No. 112/Pdt/1991/PT.Uj.Pdg dated March 16, 1991, and independently adjudicated by adopting Polewali District Court Decision No. 36/Pdt.G/1990/PN.Pol dated November 12, 1990, partially granting the Plaintiffs' lawsuit.

=== Question of Fact (''Judex Facti'' / Polewali District Court & Ujung Pandang High Court) ===
Examination of facts regarding the origins of the 8,273 m² rice field in Ugi Baru, Ugi Baru Village, Wonomulyo Subdistrict, Polewali Mamasa Regency, initially pawned by La Malappe in 1962 for Rp 25,000 to [Party A] & H. Tompo; subsequent purchase of the land in 1963 by H. Tompo for Rp 60,000; issuance of SHM No. 7613252 on April 11, 1983, in the name of H. Tompo; cultivation relationships maintained by the Defendant ([Defendant]) under a sharecropping arrangement until the passing of [Defendant's mother] in 1989; and testimonies of witnesses ([Party C], [Witness], [Witness], H. Siraja, Maddiwali, Rusdi).

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===

* '''Government Regulation No. 10 of 1961 on Land Registration (''jo.'' Gov. Reg. No. 24 of 1997):''' Articles 3, 6 (Announcement and Certificate Issuance Procedures).
* '''HIR / RBg:''' Article 164 HIR / Article 284 RBg (Civil Evidence Instruments: Authentic Documents, Witnesses, Presumptions, Confessions, Oaths).
* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata / BW):''' Articles 1867, 1868, 1870 (Evidentiary Force of Authentic Deeds / Certificates).
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Independent Adjudication Powers at Cassation Level.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===

* '''Doctrine of Certificate ''Volledig Bewijskracht'':''' Land certificates issued in accordance with procedure serve as binding and perfect authentic evidence instruments.
* '''Doctrine of ''Legenbewijs'' Inability to Defeat Authentic Deeds:''' Individual witness testimonies unsupported by counter-documentary evidence lack sufficient legal strength to defeat registered title rights established in certificates.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* The disputed 8,273 m² rice field in Ugi Baru Village is proven to be the property of H. Tompo based on Land Rights Certificate No. 7613252 dated April 11, 1983.
* The Plaintiffs ([Party B], Wardinah, Warda) are legally proven to be the biological heirs entitled to the disputed land.
* The Defendant ([Defendant]) is proven to have occupied the disputed rice field without right and committed a tort upon refusing to share harvests beginning in 1989.
* The Defendant is ordered to surrender the disputed rice field to the Plaintiffs.

=== Annulled (Ujung Pandang High Court Verdict) ===

* The Defendant's assertion that the disputed rice field belonged to his father ([Party A]) based on oral witness accounts was '''UNPROVEN''' in law and entirely annulled by the Supreme Court.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Protecting Legal Certainty for Registered Right Holders Against Oral Claims:''' This landmark ruling underscores legal certainty concerning land registration in Indonesia: Holders of Land Rights Certificates who acquire their rights lawfully through formal registration procedures remain protected from unilateral ownership claims grounded solely in oral testimony (''legenbewijs''). Rebuttal evidence attempting to shake a certificate must demonstrate procedural registration flaws or authentic documentary proof bearing equivalent evidentiary weight.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==

; Can oral witness testimonies cancel or undermine a Land Rights Certificate legally issued under the law?
: '''Cannot Overturn Certificates.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 2064 K/Pdt/1991:
:* A Land Rights Certificate issued by land authorities pursuant to prevailing land registration procedures (Gov. Reg. No. 10/1961) constitutes an authentic instrument possessing perfect evidentiary force (''volledig bewijskracht'').
:* Witness testimonies constituting conjecture or indications (''legenbewijs / aanwijzingen'') '''CANNOT DEFEAT THE PERFECT EVIDENCE''' of a Land Rights Certificate.
:* High Courts invalidating land certificates based solely on oral witness accounts commit errors in evidentiary law, leading to their judgments being annulled by the Supreme Court.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 208 K/TUN/1998 dated November 25, 1999, establishes fundamental jurisprudence and legal principles regarding absolute judicial competence in tax collection disputes: Objections or lawsuits against the implementation of tax collection Warrants of Execution (*Surat Paksa*) may only be submitted to the Tax Judiciary Board (BPSP/MPP). Prior to the establishment of the Tax Judiciary Board, such objections or lawsuits were to be submitted to the District Court pursuant to Article 23 paragraph (2) and its Elucidation of Law No. 9 of 1994 concerning Amendments to Law No. 6 of 1983 on General Provisions and Tax Procedures. Consequently, the State Administrative Court (PTUN/PTTUN) lacks the competence to adjudicate lawsuits challenging the execution of Warrants of Execution.

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiff / Respondent for Cassation (PT Natra Raya, represented by President Director Donald C. Loebach) filed a lawsuit against the Original Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation (Head of the Foreign Investment Tax Service Office / KPP PMA) at the Jakarta State Administrative Court. The lawsuit challenged the issuance of Warrant of Execution No. Print. 315/WPJ.06/KP.0208 dated September 5, 1995, for collecting tax arrears under tax assessment notices (SKP, SKPT, STP) for Income Tax and Luxury Goods Sales Tax. The Plaintiff argued that the Warrant of Execution was issued while objections or appeals regarding the underlying tax assessments were still being processed by the Directorate General of Taxes / Tax Advisory Board (MPP), meaning the tax debt did not yet possess permanent legal force (*in kracht van gewijsde*) and could not yet be collected via a Warrant of Execution.

The Jakarta State Administrative Court (Decision No. 159/G.TUN/1995/PTUN-JKT dated June 5, 1996) rejected the Defendant's exception, granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in its entirety, and annulled the disputed Warrant of Execution. The Jakarta State Administrative High Court (Decision No. 106/B/1997/PT.TUN.JKT dated November 12, 1997) upheld the Jakarta State Administrative Court judgment. Dissatisfied with the ruling, the KPP PMA filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court asserting the absolute competence exception.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The cassation objections raised by the Petitioner for Cassation regarding absolute competence are well-founded because the Jakarta State Administrative High Court committed an error in applying the law.
# Pursuant to Article 23 paragraph (2) and its Elucidation of Law No. 9 of 1994 concerning Amendments to Law No. 6 of 1983 on General Provisions and Tax Procedures, objections or lawsuits against the implementation of a Warrant of Execution may only be submitted to the Tax Judiciary Board. Before the Tax Judiciary Board was formed, such matters were submitted to the District Court.
# Because the State Administrative Court lacks absolute competence to examine and adjudicate disputes concerning the implementation of tax collection Warrants of Execution, the Defendant's exception must be sustained and the Plaintiff's lawsuit declared inadmissible (*niet ontvankelijke verklaard*).
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation HEAD OF THE FOREIGN INVESTMENT TAX SERVICE OFFICE (*KEPALA KANTOR PELAYANAN PAJAK PENANAMAN MODAL ASING*); Annulling the Jakarta State Administrative High Court decision dated November 12, 1997, No. 106/B/1997/PT.TUN.JKT and the Jakarta State Administrative Court decision dated June 5, 1996, No. 159/G.TUN/1995/PTUN-JKT; and Independently Adjudicating: IN EXCEPTION: Sustaining the Defendant's exception; IN THE PRINCIPAL CASE: Declaring the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible (*niet ontvankelijke verklaard*); Ordering the Respondent for Cassation (PT Natra Raya) to pay all court costs across all levels of jurisdiction (assessed at Rp 100,000 at the cassation level). *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Cassation Panel of Justices on Thursday, November 25, 1999, by H. Soeharto, SH. [Presiding Judge], Iskandar Kamil, SH., and Achmad Kowi AS., SH.).*
