== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 209 K/TUN/2004 dated October 14, 2004, establishes fundamental jurisprudence and legal rules regarding the validity of a plaintiff's legal standing / capacity in a dispute concerning a State Administrative Decree on corporate share transfers: A Limited Liability Company (*PT*) acting as a buyer of another Limited Liability Company (*PT*) lacks the legal capacity or standing to sue a State Administrative Decree concerning the target company being acquired, as long as the buying company has not fully paid the entire purchase price as stipulated.

== Case Background ==

Plaintiff I (PT Asianagro Abadi) and Plaintiff II (PT Pusakamegah Buminusantara) filed a lawsuit against the Minister of Justice and Human Rights of the Republic of Indonesia (Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation I) alongside [Party A] and Ngarijan Salim (Intervention Defendant II / Petitioner for Cassation II) at the Jakarta State Administrative Court. The object of the dispute consisted of the Decree of the Minister of Justice and Human Rights No. C-13525 HT.01.04 TH.2003 concerning the Approval of the Deed of Amendment of Articles of Association of PT Pusakamegah Buminusantara and the Receipt of Notification of Deed of Amendment of Articles of Association No. C-13526 HT.01.04 TH.2003 dated June 13, 2003.

Plaintiff I argued that it had purchased all shares of Plaintiff II pursuant to Agreement Deed No. 75 dated September 24, 1997. However, Plaintiff I had only paid a down payment / earnest money of Rp 3,000,000,000 out of the total share purchase price of Rp 17,000,000,000. The Jakarta State Administrative Court (Decision No. 150/G.TUN/2003/PTUN.JKT dated January 19, 2004) declared the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible. The Jakarta State Administrative High Court (Decision No. 42/B/2004/PT.TUN.JKT dated March 16, 2004) annulled the State Administrative Court's judgment and granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit. Dissatisfied with the ruling, Petitioner for Cassation I (Minister of Justice and Human Rights) and Petitioner for Cassation II ([Party A] and Ngarijan Salim) filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# Pursuant to Agreement Deed No. 75 dated September 24, 1997, PT Asianagro Abadi had not fully settled the entire purchase price for the shares of PT Pusakamegah Buminusantara amounting to Rp 17,000,000,000, having only paid Rp 3,000,000,000.
# As long as the entire purchase price stipulated in the agreement remains unpaid, PT Asianagro Abadi does not possess full rights as a buyer and has not become a lawful shareholder possessing the capacity or legal standing to act as a Plaintiff challenging a State Administrative Decree concerning PT Pusakamegah Buminusantara.
# Because PT Asianagro Abadi lacked capacity or standing to sue from the outset, the lawsuit filed by the Plaintiffs / Respondents for Cassation must be rejected.
# There was also an erroneous application of procedural law by the Registry of the Jakarta State Administrative Court in failing to provide an opportunity for inspection of case files (*inzage*) to Intervention Defendant II before transmitting the files to the High Court, violating procedural provisions under Article 126 paragraph (1) of Law No. 5 of 1986 (*fair trial*).
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioners for Cassation: (1) THE MINISTER OF JUSTICE AND HUMAN RIGHTS OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA, (2) [Party A] and NGARIJAN SALIM; Annulling the Jakarta State Administrative High Court decision dated March 16, 2004, No. 42/B/2004/PT.TUN.JKT jo. the Jakarta State Administrative Court decision dated January 19, 2004, No. 150/G.TUN/2003/PTUN.JKT; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Rejecting the Plaintiffs' lawsuit; (2) Ordering the Respondent for Cassation to pay cassation-level court costs amounting to Rp 500,000 (five hundred thousand rupiahs). *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court on Thursday, October 14, 2004, by the Cassation Panel of Justices: Prof. Dr. Paulus Effendie Lotulung, S.H. [Presiding Judge], Ny. Titi Nurmala Siagian, S.H., and Ny. Chairani A. Wani, S.H. [Associate Justices]).*

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 213 K/TUN/2007 dated November 6, 2007, establishes two fundamental jurisprudence and legal rules in State Administrative and Mining Law:

* '''Supreme Court Cassation Jurisdiction Over Regional Official Decrees in the Mining Sector (Article 45A paragraph (2) letter c of Law No. 5 of 2004):''' Because the operation of Mining Authorizations (*Kuasa Pertambangan*) is cross-sectoral between the Central Government and Regional Governments (ex Gov. Reg. No. 75 of 2001), a Regent's or Regional Official's Decree concerning Mining Authorization is not a purely regional decision whose scope is strictly limited to the local region. Consequently, the cassation restriction under Article 45A paragraph (2) letter c of Law No. 5 of 2004 does not apply, and the Supreme Court retains jurisdiction to examine the cassation petition.
* '''Duty of Prudence & Principle of Thoroughness of State Administrative Officials (AAUPB):''' Although under Government Regulation No. 75 of 2001 a State Administrative Official (Regent) has the authority to issue Mining Authorization decisions within their region, the official is obligated to exercise caution and thoroughly consider the existence of pre-existing mining areas held by other parties (in casu the Coal Mining Concession Agreement / PKP2B area of PT Arutmin Indonesia) to prevent mining area overlaps. The issuance of a Mining Authorization Decree without thoroughness violates the Principles of Good Governance (*AAUPB*), specifically the Principle of Thoroughness and the Principle of Prudence.

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation (PT Arutmin Indonesia) is the holder of rights over a coal mining area pursuant to a Coal Mining Concession Agreement (*PKP2B*) jo. Decree of the Director-General of General Mining No. 198/K/2014/DDJP/1995 dated May 5, 1995 (mining area code DU 322/Kalsel covering 12,473 ha).

However, the Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation (Regent of Tanah Laut) issued Decree No. 545.3.006/PU/DPE/2004 dated September 27, 2004, concerning the Grant of Coal Exploitation Mining Authorization (KW.106 TW.I) to Intervention Defendant II / Turut Respondent for Cassation (PT Surya Kencana Jorong Mandiri) covering an area of 203 ha in Kintap Kecil and Bukit Mulia Villages, Kintap Sub-District, Tanah Laut Regency, which turned out to overlap (*overlapping*) within PT Arutmin Indonesia's PKP2B concession area.

PT Arutmin Indonesia filed a lawsuit against the Regent of Tanah Laut's decree at the Banjarmasin State Administrative Court. The Banjarmasin State Administrative Court (Decision No. 15/G/2006/PTUN.BJM dated September 1, 2006) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in its entirety and annulled the Regent of Tanah Laut's decree. However, the Jakarta State Administrative High Court (Decision No. 176/B/2006/PT.TUN.JKT dated December 18, 2006) annulled the Banjarmasin State Administrative Court judgment and rejected the Plaintiff's lawsuit on the grounds of lawsuit duplication (*ne bis in idem*) and considering the decree to be regional in scope, thereby triggering the cassation restriction. PT Arutmin Indonesia filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# Regarding the restriction on cassation legal remedies pursuant to Article 45A paragraph (2) letter c of Law No. 5 of 2004, under Government Regulation No. 75 of 2001, the administration of Mining Authorizations is cross-sectoral between the Central and Regional Governments. A Regent's authority is derivative of national regulations; therefore, Mining Authorization decrees issued by a Regent are not subject to Article 45A paragraph (2) letter c of Law No. 5 of 2004, and the Supreme Court has jurisdiction to examine the cassation remedy filed by the Petitioner for Cassation.
# Regarding the ground of lawsuit duplication, under Law No. 11 of 1967 and Government Regulation No. 75 of 2001, Exploration Mining Authorizations and Exploitation Mining Authorizations are two distinct and independent mining business categories. Consequently, the Plaintiff's lawsuit challenging the Exploration Mining Authorization decree (Case No. 02/G/2006/PTUN.BJM) and the lawsuit challenging the Exploitation Mining Authorization decree (Case No. 15/G/2006/PTUN.BJM jo. 213 K/TUN/2007) do not constitute lawsuit duplication and do not amount to *ne bis in idem*.
# The State Administrative Official (Regent of Tanah Laut) was proven to have violated the Principles of Good Governance (*AAUPB*), namely the Principle of Thoroughness and the Principle of Prudence. The Defendant should have exercised caution and thoroughly considered pre-existing mining areas prior to issuing the disputed decree by first obtaining a clear picture of relevant facts and third-party interests (PT Arutmin Indonesia) to avoid legal issues arising from Mining Authorization area overlaps.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation: PT ARUTMIN INDONESIA; Annulling the Jakarta State Administrative High Court decision dated December 18, 2006, No. 176/B/2006/PT.TUN.JKT, which had annulled the Banjarmasin State Administrative Court decision dated September 1, 2006, No. 15/G/2006/PTUN.BJM; and Independently Adjudicating: IN EXCEPTION: Rejecting the Exceptions of the Defendant and Intervention Defendant II; IN THE PRINCIPAL CASE: (1) Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in its entirety; (2) Declaring null and void the Decree of the Regent of Tanah Laut No. 545.3.006/PU/DPE/2004 dated September 27, 2004, concerning the Grant of Coal Exploitation Mining Authorization (KW.106 TW.I) to PT Surya Kencana Jorong Mandiri issued by the Defendant; (3) Ordering the Defendant to revoke the Decree of the Regent of Tanah Laut No. 545.3.006/PU/DPE/2004 dated September 27, 2004; (4) Ordering the Respondent for Cassation / Defendant to pay cassation-level court costs amounting to Rp 500,000 (five hundred thousand rupiahs). *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court on Tuesday, November 6, 2007, by the Cassation Panel of Justices: Prof. DR. Paulus E. Lotulung, S.H. [Junior Chairman for State Administrative Chamber / Presiding Judge], H. Imam Soebechi, S.H., M.H., and Titi Nurmala Siagian, S.H., M.H. [Associate Justices]).*

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:2146K PDT 1986
wikitext:
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 2146 K/Pdt/1986''' (dated November 21, 1990) is a fundamental Indonesian civil procedure law jurisprudence precedent establishing vital rules regarding the legal standing of parties and the burden of proof in opposition proceedings against default judgments (''verzet'').

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established three primary legal principles:

# '''Fixed Standing of Parties in Default Opposition (''Verzet''):''' When an opposition (''verzet'') against a default judgment (''verstekingang'') is formally admissible, the original lawsuit must be re-examined while preserving the original standing of the parties: the Respondent in Opposition (''Terlawan'') remains the Plaintiff, and the Objector (''Pelawan'') remains the Defendant.
# '''Primary Burden of Proof Rests on the Original Plaintiff (''Actori Incumbit Probatio''):''' Once the Objector (Defendant) disputes the factual assertions of the original lawsuit, the primary burden of proof is first assigned to the Respondent in Opposition (Plaintiff) to prove the factual basis of their claim.
# '''Consequences of the Original Plaintiff's Failure of Proof:''' If the Respondent in Opposition (Plaintiff) fails to substantiate their claim—furthermore demonstrated by evidence that the compensation document / foundational root title submitted by the Plaintiff originated from document forgery punishable under criminal law—the Objector's opposition must be declared well-founded, the default judgment annulled, and the original Plaintiff's lawsuit rejected in its entirety.

The Supreme Court rejected the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation ([Party B]) with amendments to the Medan High Court ''jo.'' Medan District Court verdicts, and '''ADJUDICATED ANEW''' (''mengadili sekali lagi'') by declaring the Objector's (P. Krisman Nainggolan) opposition well-founded, annulling Medan District Court default judgment No. 663/Perd/1975/PN.Mdn dated March 1, 1976, and rejecting the original Plaintiff's ([Party B]) lawsuit entirely.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Civil Procedure Construction of Opposition Against Default Judgments (''Verzet'' ''ex'' Article 129 HIR / Article 153 RBg) ===
''What is the legal standing of parties and the procedural examination flow when an opposition (''verzet'') filed by the original Defendant against a default judgment is formally declared admissible?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Standing Remains Original.''' During an opposition (''verzet'') meeting formal criteria, the legal standing of the parties does not shift or reverse. The Respondent in Opposition (''Terlawan'') retains the standing of Original Plaintiff, and the Objector (''Pelawan'') retains the standing of Original Defendant.

=== 2. Application of the Burden of Proof Principle (''Actori Incumbit Probatio'' ''ex'' Article 163 HIR / Article 283 RBg) in ''Verzet'' ===
''Who bears the primary burden of proof after the Objector disputes the original lawsuit'' posita ''in default opposition proceedings?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Original Plaintiff Bears Primary Burden.''' Because the Objector fundamentally challenges the initial claims, pursuant to ''actori incumbit probatio'', the burden of proof is primarily assigned to the Original Plaintiff (Respondent) to establish title and root rights over the disputed object. If the Plaintiff's foundational documents prove fraudulent or defective (e.g., resulting in criminal convictions for document forgery), the original Plaintiff's lawsuit must be rejected in its entirety.

=== 3. Formulation of Supreme Court Cassation Verdicts (''Adjudicating Anew'' in ''Verzet'' Actions) ===
The Supreme Court corrected incomplete appellate formatting by formulating precise rulings: (1) declaring the Objector's opposition well-founded; (2) annulling the default judgment; and (3) Adjudicating Anew: Rejecting the original Plaintiff's lawsuit in its entirety.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (''Judex Juris'' / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Medan High Court ''jo.'' Medan District Court apply civil procedure and evidentiary law correctly regarding party standing and the burden of proof in default opposition (''verzet'') proceedings?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes, the ''Judex Facti'' correctly ruled in favor of the Objector because the original Plaintiff failed to prove ownership and possessed fraudulent root titles. However, because appellate formatting was incomplete, the Supreme Court rejected the Petitioner's cassation appeal with amended formatting and '''ADJUDICATED ANEW''' by declaring the Objector's opposition well-founded, annulling Medan District Court default judgment No. 663/Perd/1975/PN.Mdn, and rejecting the original Plaintiff's ([Party B]) lawsuit entirely.

=== Question of Fact (''Judex Facti'' / Medan District Court & Medan High Court) ===
Examination of facts regarding the entry of Medan District Court default judgment No. 663/Perd/1975/PN.Mdn on March 1, 1976; filing of opposition (''verzet'') No. 30/Vz/Perd/1976/PN.Mdn on November 16, 1976, by P. Krisman Nainggolan; physical possession and cultivation of a 1,350 m² parcel (13.5 m x 100 m) in Lorong III/VIII Tegal Rejo Medan by the Objector since 1956; verification of Criminal Judgment No. 91/KTS/1976 penalizing the Respondent ([Party B]) for forging land purchase/compensation documents; and evaluation of testimonies from witnesses ([Party A], Kapeller Sitompul, Siti Aminah).

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===

* '''HIR / RBg:'''
** Article 129 HIR / Article 153 RBg: Rights and Procedures for Default Opposition (''Verzet'').
** Article 163 HIR / Article 283 RBg: Burden of Proof Principle (''Actori Incumbit Probatio'').
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 1 of 1950 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation Authority and Verdict Formatting Powers.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===

* '''Doctrine of Party Standing in ''Verzet'':''' Default opposition proceedings do not constitute a novel lawsuit (nor introduce a new ''posita''), but rather function as a rebuttal / defense against a default judgment. Consequently, the legal positions of the original Plaintiff and original Defendant remain unvaried.
* '''Doctrine of Document Forgery Root Flaws:''' Compensation documents or land purchase deeds cancelled or proven to originate from document forgery pursuant to criminal judgments carry no civil evidentiary value (legally worthless).

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* The opposition (''verzet'') filed by the Objector (P. Krisman Nainggolan) is formally admissible and well-founded in law.
* The Respondent / Original Plaintiff ([Party B]) '''FAILED TO PROVE''' ownership or rights over the disputed land.
* The compensation documents / foundational titles submitted by the original Plaintiff originated from document forgery (Plaintiff was sentenced to 6 months probation pursuant to Criminal Case No. 91/KTS/1976).
* The Objector proved physical cultivation of the disputed land since 1956.
* Medan District Court Default Judgment No. 663/Perd/1975/PN.Mdn dated March 1, 1976, is '''NULL AND VOID'''.
* The original Plaintiff's ([Party B]) lawsuit is '''REJECTED ENTIRELY'''.

=== Rejected / Dismissed Arguments ===

* The original Plaintiff's assertion that he lawfully possessed or purchased the disputed land in 1963 was '''UNPROVEN''' in law.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Procedural Precision in Default Opposition (''Verzet'') Verdict Formatting:''' This landmark ruling establishes an essential procedural guideline for all Indonesian courts: during ''verzet'' examinations, judges must not misapprehend the Objector as a Plaintiff bearing initial burdens of proof. The primary burden remains firmly upon the Original Plaintiff. Sustaining a default opposition verdict requires explicitly rejecting or declaring inadmissible the Plaintiff's original lawsuit within the dispositive text.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==

; What is the legal standing of parties and the burden of proof in opposition proceedings against default judgments (''verzet'') pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence?
: '''Parties retain their original standing, and primary burdens rest on the Original Plaintiff.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 2146 K/Pdt/1986:
:* When an opposition (''verzet'') against a default judgment is formally accepted, the original lawsuit is re-examined while preserving original party standing: the Respondent remains the Plaintiff, and the Objector remains the Defendant.
:* Because the Objector disputes the original claims, pursuant to ''actori incumbit probatio'', the primary burden of proof rests on the Original Plaintiff (Respondent) to establish claims.
:* If the original Plaintiff fails to establish rights (e.g., foundational titles originate from document forgery), the opposition is sustained, the default judgment is annulled, and the original lawsuit is rejected in its entirety.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 216/K/TUN/2010 dated September 28, 2010, establishes fundamental jurisprudence and legal rules in State Administrative Law (Civil Service): Only the President of the Republic of Indonesia has the right and authority to dismiss and/or temporarily release a Civil Servant (*PNS*) holding a Principal Functional Position / Principal Widyaiswara (Rank IV/e) from and in their office. A Decree of the Minister of Finance temporarily releasing a Principal Widyaiswara of Rank IV/e contains a legal defect because it was issued outside of official authority (*onbevoegd* / *ultra vires*).

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiff / Respondent for Cassation (Drs. [Plaintiff], Ak., MA., a Civil Servant holding the Functional Position of Principal Widyaiswara, Main Supervisor rank, Rank IV/e at Financial Training Center II Palembang, BPPK) received a copy of the Decree of the Minister of Finance of the Republic of Indonesia No. 113/KMK.01/UP.11/2009 dated April 1, 2009, concerning the Temporary Release of the Plaintiff from the Functional Position of Principal Widyaiswara effective from October 1, 2008. The Plaintiff filed a lawsuit seeking the annulment of the decree at the Jakarta State Administrative Court.

The Jakarta State Administrative Court (Decision No. 81/G/2009/PTUN-JKT dated September 2, 2009) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in its entirety, declared the Minister of Finance's Decree No. 113/KMK.01/UP.11/2009 null and void, ordered the Defendant to revoke the decree, and ordered the Defendant to pay compensation of Rp 5,000,000 plus court costs. The Jakarta State Administrative High Court (Decision No. 251/B/2009/PT.TUN.JKT dated February 2, 2010) upheld the Jakarta State Administrative Court judgment. Dissatisfied with the ruling, the Defendant (Minister of Finance of the Republic of Indonesia) filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The *Judex Facti* (Jakarta State Administrative Court and Jakarta State Administrative High Court) were accurate and committed no error in applying the law, as the disputed object decree contained a legal defect.
# The Defendant (Minister of Finance of the Republic of Indonesia) lacked the authority to issue the disputed State Administrative Decree.
# Pursuant to Article 12 of the Joint Regulation of the Head of LAN and the Head of BKN No. 7 of 2005 and No. 17 of 2005, as well as Article 26 of the Regulation of the Minister of State Apparatus Utilization No. PER/66/M.PAN/6/2005, the official authorized to determine the temporary release from and in the position of Principal Widyaiswara is identical to the official authorized to determine temporary dismissal from and in the position of Principal Widyaiswara, namely the President of the Republic of Indonesia.
# Legal Principle: "Only the President has the right to dismiss and/or temporarily release Civil Servants holding Principal Functional Positions / Principal Widyaiswara (rank IV/e) from and in their office."
* '''Ruling:''' Rejecting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation THE MINISTER OF FINANCE OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA; Ordering the Petitioner for Cassation to pay cassation-level court costs amounting to Rp 500,000 (five hundred thousand rupiahs). *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court on Tuesday, September 28, 2010, by Dr. H. Imam Soebechi, S.H., M.H. [Presiding Judge], Dr. H. Supandi, S.H., M.Hum., and Prof. Dr. Ahmad Sukardja, S.H., M.A. [Associate Justices]).*

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 218 K/Pid/2004 dated July 14, 2004, establishes fundamental jurisprudence and legal rules regarding the separation of criminal and civil legal domains in land disputes: The *Judex Facti* erred in applying the law by failing to thoroughly consider the documentary evidence of land ownership presented at trial. Disputes concerning the validity and truth of land ownership between heirs and other parties claiming rights based on a power of attorney or agreement fall within the scope of Civil Court jurisdiction. If a Defendant's failure to execute a power of attorney to sell land constitutes a breach of contract (*wanprestasi*) rather than a criminal offense, the Defendant must be released from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*).

== Case Background ==

The Defendants (1. [Defendant], 2. Murhali bin Misin, 3. Murtabak bin Misin, 4. Rinan bin Misin) were brought before the West Jakarta District Court charged under Primary counts of Article 266 paragraph (1) jo. Article 55 paragraph (1) point 1 of the KUHP (ordering the insertion of false statements into an authentic deed) and Subsidiary counts of Article 385 paragraph (1) point 1 jo. Article 55 paragraph (1) point 1 of the KUHP (embezzlement of rights over immovable property / *Delict Stellionaat*). The case originated from a dispute over inherited land under Girik C.647 parcel 113b D.III in Kapuk Village, Cengkareng, West Jakarta. Reporting witness [Party B] claimed to have purchased the land from H. Mursahid bin Misin measuring 6,000 m² in 1992, but subsequent land measurement revealed an area of 8,342 m² (an excess of 2,342 m²). On February 1, 2000, the Defendants granted a power of attorney to [Party B] to sell the excess land, but on May 19, 2000, the Defendants together with Sutrisno sold the land themselves to another party via Notary Marlon Silitonga, SH.

The West Jakarta District Court (Decision No. 423/PID/B/2002/PN.JKT.BAR dated May 6, 2002) acquitted the Defendants of the Primary charge, but convicted them on the Subsidiary charge (Article 385 paragraph (1)e of the KUHP), sentencing each to 1 (one) year of imprisonment. The Jakarta High Court (Decision No. 64/PID/2003/PT.DKI dated May 23, 2003) upheld the West Jakarta District Court judgment. Dissatisfied with the ruling, the Defendants filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The *Judex Facti* erred in applying the law and failed to properly evaluate the documentary evidence submitted during trial.
# Pursuant to Supreme Court civil decision No. 4502 K/Pdt/1998, the Defendants ([Defendant], Murhali, Murtabak, Rinan) are the lawful owners of the disputed land and never sold it to witness [Party B]. Witness [Party B] was merely asked to handle the land case at the Supreme Court and borrowed the Defendants' land documents. Furthermore, [Party B] was himself convicted under cassation decision No. 1739 K/Pid/2002 for forging the land sale agreement.
# The power of attorney to sell land dated February 1, 2000, given by the Defendants to [Party B], when unexecuted by the Defendants, constitutes a breach of contract (*wanprestasi*) within the domain of civil law.
# Land ownership disputes fall within the absolute competence of the Civil Courts. Because the acts committed by the Defendants under the Subsidiary charge do not constitute a criminal offense, the Defendants must be released from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*).
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioners for Cassation / Defendants: 1. [Defendant], 2. MURHALI bin MISIN, 3. MURTABAK bin MISIN, 4. RINAN bin MISIN; Annulling the West Jakarta District Court decision dated May 6, 2002, No. 423/PID/B/2002/PN.JKT.BAR and the Jakarta High Court decision dated May 23, 2003, No. 64/PID/2003/PT.DKI; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Declaring that the acts of the Defendants (1. [Defendant], 2. Murhali bin Misin, 3. Murtabak bin Misin, and 4. Rinan bin Misin) as charged under the Subsidiary count do not constitute a criminal offense; (2) Releasing the Defendants from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*); (3) Restoring the Defendants' rights in capacity, position, honor, and dignity; (4) Determining the status of evidence items (sale agreement and receipt in the name of H. Mursahid seized from Sutrisno shall be destroyed, while other evidence items shall be returned to witness [Party B] or annexed to the file); (5) Charging cassation-level court costs to the State. *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court on Wednesday, July 14, 2004, by Prof. Dr. Paulus Effendie Lotulung, SH. [Presiding Judge / Session Chairman], Ny. Titi Nurmala Siagian, SH., and Ny. Chairani A. Wani, SH. [Associate Justices]).*

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Civil Review Decision Reg. No. 220 PK/Pdt/1986 dated October 30, 1986 (pronounced on December 16, 1986), represents a foundational landmark decision in Indonesian Intellectual Property Law (Trademark Law). The Supreme Court established pioneering legal principles holding that:

* '''Protection of International Well-Known Marks:''' The Republic of Indonesia is obligated to maintain international relations by respecting well-known marks belonging to foreign citizens or legal entities, even if they have not been registered at the Indonesian Office of Industrial Property Rights (Directorate of Patents and Copyrights). Indonesian entrepreneurs who are aware of an international well-known mark are prohibited from using or registering identical or similar marks, in order to protect Indonesian consumers from confusion and deception regarding the origin of goods.
* '''Judicial Error / Manifest Error (Article 67(f) of Law No. 14 of 1985):''' A rigid (formalistic) interpretation of Articles 8 and 10 of Law No. 21 of 1961 regarding the time limit for filing a trademark cancellation lawsuit—which allows the registration of a bad-faith imitation mark to remain valid—constitutes a judicial error or manifest error (legal oversight), serving as valid grounds for granting a Civil Review (*Peninjauan Kembali*).

== Case Background ==

The Petitioner for Civil Review / Original Plaintiff (Nike International Ltd., Oregon, U.S.A.) is the sole owner and first user globally and in Indonesia of the trademark and trade name "Nike" alongside the wing device (*swoosh*) for shoes and apparel. However, Respondent for Civil Review I / Original Defendant I ([Party A]) without authorization registered the "Nike" trademark and wing device at the Directorate of Patents and Copyrights under Registration No. 141589 on December 13, 1979, with bad faith to exploit the fame of the "Nike" mark.

The Plaintiff (Nike International Ltd.) filed a lawsuit seeking the cancellation of said trademark registration at the Central Jakarta District Court. The Central Jakarta District Court (Decision No. 315/1983 Pdt.G dated November 22, 1983) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in its entirety and annulled the trademark registration in the name of [Party A]. However, on cassation appeal, the Supreme Court (Decision No. 294 K/Pdt/1984 dated July 24, 1985) annulled the Central Jakarta District Court decision and declared the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible on formalistic grounds, holding that the Defendant's trademark registration had not yet been published in the Additional State Gazette (*Tambahan Berita Negara RI*), meaning the 9-month lawsuit time limit ex Article 10 of Law No. 21 of 1961 could not yet be calculated. Dissatisfied with the cassation ruling, Nike International Ltd. filed a petition for Civil Review (*PK*) to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# A rigid interpretation of Articles 8 and 10 of Law No. 21 of 1961 declaring the lawsuit time limit rule to be absolute is erroneous. The interpretation that the time limit under Articles 8 and 10 of Law No. 21 of 1961 is not absolute serves as a correction of a judicial error or manifest error pursuant to Article 67(f) of Law No. 14 of 1985.
# The Republic of Indonesia, as an independent nation, is obligated to maintain international relations by respecting trademarks belonging to foreign nationals. Indonesian entrepreneurs who are aware of a mark that is famous internationally—although unregistered or not yet registered in the general register of the Industrial Property Office, yet known in Indonesia—cannot use an identical mark, in order to protect Indonesian consumers from confusion as to whether such Indonesian goods originate from an imitated foreign manufacturer.
# Indonesian citizens manufacturing Indonesian-made goods are required to use clear brand names reflecting an Indonesian national identity and should, to the extent possible, avoid using brand names that resemble, let alone plagiarize, foreign brand names.
# Respondent for Civil Review I ([Party A]) was proven to have acted in bad faith by registering the "Nike" mark under Registration No. 141589, which is identical to the mark owned by Nike International Ltd. Consequently, the Civil Review petition is granted, the cassation decision No. 294 K/Pdt/1984 is annulled, and the Central Jakarta District Court judgment granting Nike's lawsuit is reinstated.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the civil review petition from Petitioner for Civil Review: NIKE INTERNATIONAL LTD.; Annulling the Supreme Court decision dated July 24, 1985, No. 294 K/Pdt/1984; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in its entirety; (2) Declaring the Plaintiff as the sole owner and first user in Indonesia of the trademark and trade name Nike, and therefore holding the exclusive right to use the trademark and trade name Nike in Indonesia; (3) Declaring that the Nike trademark registered under the name of Defendant I under Registration No. 141589 bears an overall similarity to the Plaintiff's Nike trademark (Exhibit P-1)... [and ordering the cancellation of registration No. 141589 from the General Trademark Register]. *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court on October 30, 1986, and pronounced on December 16, 1986).*

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:2249K PDT 1992
wikitext:
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 2249 K/Pdt/1992''' (dated June 22, 1994 / deliberation on May 23, 1994) is a fundamental Indonesian family and divorce law jurisprudence precedent establishing vital rules regarding the prohibition against husbands engaged in extramarital affairs or cohabiting with other women from filing for divorce on the grounds of continuous disputes (the guilty party doctrine / ''Damni Culpa dati reparation'' / Supreme Court Circular Letter No. 3 of 1981), alongside the custody rights (''hadhanah'') of minor children vested in the biological mother.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established two primary legal principles:

# '''Incompatibility of Spousal Infidelity as a Divorce Ground (The Guilty Party Doctrine):''' Marital disputes between a Plaintiff (husband) and Defendant (wife) caused by the Plaintiff's proven involvement and cohabitation with another woman as his mistress cannot serve as grounds for divorce under Article 19 letter f of Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975. The law does not grant the right to seek a divorce to a husband who serves as the primary cause or guilty party (''misconduct'') responsible for marital friction.
# '''Principle of the Best Interests of the Child & Maternal Custody (''Hadhanah''):''' Toddlers and minor children are, by operation of law, entitled to be raised and cared for by their biological mother (affirming Supreme Court Jurisprudence Nos. 239 K/Sip/1968, 102 K/Sip/1973, and 27 K/AG/1982), rather than being surrendered to a husband cohabiting with a mistress.

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation ([Wife]), annulled Semarang High Court Decision No. 792/Pdt/1991/PT.Smg dated April 3, 1992, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by affirming Semarang District Court Decision No. 12/Pdt/G/1991/PN.Smg dated July 30, 1991, which '''rejected the Plaintiff's (Drs. [Husband]) divorce lawsuit in its entirety'''.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Application of the Guilty Party Doctrine (''Damni Culpa dati reparation'' / SEMA No. 3 of 1981) in Divorce Actions under Article 19(f) of Gov. Reg. No. 9 of 1975 ===
''Is a husband who commits infidelity and cohabits with a mistress entitled to file a divorce lawsuit on grounds of continuous disputes provoked by his own misconduct?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Not Entitled (Lawsuit Must Be Rejected).''' Pursuant to the general legal maxim ''Nemo auditur propriam turpitudinem allegans'' and ''Damni Culpa dati reparation'' (in conjunction with Supreme Court Circular Letter No. 3 of 1981), the right to file a divorce lawsuit is granted exclusively to innocent parties. A husband engaging in infidelity constitutes the guilty party responsible for marital breakdown, and is thus legally denied the right to seek a divorce based on disputes he provoked.

=== 2. Protection of Minor Child Custody Rights (''Hadhanah'' under the Best Interests of the Child Principle) ===
''To whom should custody (''hadhanah'') of a toddler (approx. 3–[age removed]) be awarded when parents separate?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Awarded to the Biological Mother.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence (Nos. 239 K/Sip/1968, 102 K/Sip/1973, and 27 K/AG/1982), in the interest of emotional and moral development, toddlers and minor children must be placed in the custody of their biological mother, rather than surrendered to a father cohabiting with another woman.

=== 3. Joinder of Child Custody Claims in Divorce Proceedings (Article 24 of Gov. Reg. No. 9 of 1975) ===
Requests for child custody determinations represent direct legal consequences inseparable from divorce proceedings, permitting joinder and joint adjudication within a single divorce action.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (''Judex Juris'' / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Semarang High Court (Decision No. 792/Pdt/1991/PT.Smg) err in applying family law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') by granting a divorce lawsuit filed by a proven adulterous husband and awarding toddler custody to the guilty husband?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. Semarang High Court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court granted the wife's cassation petition ([Wife]), annulled Semarang High Court Decision No. 792/Pdt/1991/PT.Smg dated April 3, 1992, and independently adjudicated by affirming Semarang District Court Decision No. 12/Pdt/G/1991/PN.Smg dated July 30, 1991, which '''rejected the Husband's divorce lawsuit in its entirety'''.

=== Question of Fact (''Judex Facti'' / Semarang District Court & Semarang High Court) ===
Examination of facts regarding marriage on August 14, 1986 (Civil Registry Act No. 483/1986); birth of child [Child] on June 18, 1987; adultery and cohabitation of the husband (Drs. [Husband]) with a woman named [Third party] at Puri Anjasmoro Complex, Semarang; testimonies of witnesses (Pastor [Witness B], Muryani Teno, Nurhayatun, [Witness]); and verification of photographs depicting the child with [Third party].

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===

* '''Law No. 1 of 1974 on Marriage:''' Article 1 (Purpose of Marriage), Article 39 (Grounds for Divorce).
* '''Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975:''' Article 19 letter f (Continuous Dispute Grounds) & Article 24 (Interim Child Custody Measures).
* '''Supreme Court Circular Letter (SEMA):''' SEMA No. 3 of 1981 (Guilty Party Doctrine Barring Divorce Claims).
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 in conjunction with Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Independent Adjudication Powers at Cassation Level.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===

* '''Clean Hands Doctrine (Guilty Party Doctrine):''' Supreme Court Decision No. 1604 K/Pdt/1984 dated September 26, 1985, in conjunction with SEMA No. 3/1981 — A husband/wife serving as the primary catalyst for marital breakdown due to reprehensible acts or infidelity has no right to file for divorce.
* '''Toddler Custody Jurisprudence:''' Supreme Court Decisions Nos. 239 K/Sip/1968, 102 K/Sip/1973, and 27 K/AG/1982 — Minor children must be raised by their biological mothers.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* Original Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation ([Wife]) is proven innocent regarding marital breakdown.
* Original Plaintiff (Drs. [Husband]) is proven to have engaged in adultery and cohabitation with a mistress ([Third party]) at Puri Anjasmoro Complex, Semarang.
* The Original Plaintiff is the guilty party and thus barred from seeking a divorce.
* Toddler [Child] remains legally in the custody and guardianship of her biological mother.
* The Plaintiff's divorce lawsuit is '''rejected in its entirety'''.

=== Annulled (Semarang High Court Verdict) ===

* Semarang High Court considerations granting the divorce and awarding child custody to the original Plaintiff were entirely annulled by the Supreme Court as erroneous applications of family law.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Integrity of Marriage Institutions Against Dispute Manipulation (''Unclean Hands''):''' This landmark ruling establishes an exceptionally robust legal precedent in Indonesia preventing the manipulation of divorce law: spouses engaging in infidelity cannot deliberately instigate quarrels or abandon the marital home only to exploit self-created friction as grounds to seize divorce judgments in court. The law protects spouses who persevere in preserving family unity (''clean hands'').

Reg. No. 9 of 1975.
:* Pursuant to established Supreme Court Jurisprudence, minor children/toddlers must by operation of law be raised and cared for by their biological mothers, rather than surrendered to a father cohabiting with a mistress.

wikitext:
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 2356 K/Pdt/2008''' (dated February 18, 2009) is a fundamental Indonesian contract law and Intellectual Property (Trademark) jurisprudence precedent establishing that trademark purchase and settlement agreements executed under duress while detained in a police holding facility constitute Abuse of Circumstances (''Misbruik van Omstandigheden'') under Article 1320 of the Civil Code.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established two primary legal principles:

# '''Abuse of Circumstances (''Misbruik van Omstandigheden''):''' Trademark sale and settlement agreements signed by a trademark holder while under police detention resulting from criminal charges filed by an opposing party constitute an Abuse of Circumstances (''Misbruik van Omstandigheden'').
# '''Defective Consent under Freedom of Contract (Article 1320 of the Civil Code):''' Coercion and duress inside a detention facility extinguish freedom of will (''wilsvrijheid''), rendering the agreement legally defective and void/voidable for failing to satisfy the legal requirements for valid agreements under Article 1320 of the Civil Code.

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Plaintiff ([Party A]), annulled Semarang High Court Decision No. 45/Pdt/2008/PT.Smg dated March 17, 2008, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by partially granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit and declaring the Settlement Agreement and Trademark Purchase Agreement dated October 6, 2006, '''Null and Void''' (''Batal Demi Hukum'').

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Construction of Defective Consent (''Wilsgebreken'') and Abuse of Circumstances (''Misbruik van Omstandigheden'') in Contract Law ''ex'' Article 1320 of the Civil Code ===
''Do trademark purchase and settlement agreements executed while a party is detained by the police due to criminal charges brought by the opposing party possess legal validity?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Legally Defective / Null and Void.'''

Signing an agreement while detained by the police under criminal allegations from an adversary constitutes an Abuse of Circumstances (''Misbruik van Omstandigheden''). Such duress eliminates freedom of will (''wilsvrijheid''), meaning the agreement fails to satisfy the subjective validity requirements under Article 1320 of the Civil Code, rendering it null and void / voidable.

=== 2. Qualification of Criminal Process Abuse to Usurp Intellectual Property / Trademarks (Abuse of Legal Process / Bad Faith Pressure) ===
Filing criminal complaints against registered trademark holders to engineer detention, then exploiting that detention to coerce victims into surrendering or selling their trademarks through settlement agreements, qualifies as an abuse of criminal reporting to unlawfully misappropriate an opponent's civil/trademark rights.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (''Judex Juris'' / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Semarang High Court (Decision No. 45/Pdt/2008/PT.Smg) err in applying contract law (''foutieve toepassing van het perikatenrecht'') by upholding the Settlement Agreement and Trademark Purchase Agreement dated October 6, 2006, without accounting for the fact that the agreements were executed while the Plaintiff was in police detention?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. Semarang High Court misapplied contract law. The Supreme Court granted the Plaintiff's cassation petition ([Party A]), annulled Semarang High Court Decision No. 45/Pdt/2008/PT.Smg, and independently adjudicated by declaring the Settlement Agreement and Trademark Purchase Agreement dated October 6, 2006, Null and Void.

=== Question of Fact (''Judex Facti'' / Semarang District Court & Semarang High Court) ===
Examination of facts regarding registration of Trademark Certificate "ARISE SHINE CES" Registration No. 477275 dated May 22, 2001, in the name of [Party A]; copyright infringement criminal complaint filed on August 8, 2006, by Yayasan Hwa Ing Fonds & Lo Iwan Setia Dharma at Semarang City Police; Plaintiff's detention on October 5, 2006; execution of the trademark purchase deed for Rp 150 Million and delivery of a Rp 400 Million Giro Note on October 6, 2006, inside the detention facility; police report withdrawal on October 6, 2006; release from detention on October 7, 2006; and issuance of Semarang City Police SP3 on October 12, 2006.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===

* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata / BW):'''
** Article 1320 (Validity Requirements of Agreements: Consent, Capacity, Specific Object, Lawful Cause).
** Article 1321 (Defective Consent: Mistake, Duress, Fraud).
* '''Law No. 15 of 2001 ''jo.'' Law No. 20 of 2016 on Trademarks and Geographical Indications:''' Legal Protection for Registered Trademark Holders.
* '''Law No. 14 of 1985 ''jo.'' Law No. 5 of 2004 ''jo.'' Law No. 3 of 2009 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation and Independent Adjudication Powers.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===

* Doctrine of ''Misbruik van Omstandigheden'' (Abuse of Circumstances): A modern evolution of defective consent alongside duress (''dwang''), fraud (''bedrog''), and mistake (''dwaling''). It occurs when one party exploits an emergency, distress, or detention position of another party to secure disproportionate advantages.
* Jurisprudence on Agreements Invalidated by Criminal Duress: Agreements born from coercion involving threats or exploitation of criminal proceedings lack freedom of contract (''wilsvrijheid'') and are null and void.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* The Plaintiff ([Party A]) is proven to be the lawful holder of Trademark Certificate "ARISE SHINE CES" Registration No. 477275 dated May 22, 2001.
* The Settlement Agreement and Trademark Purchase Agreement dated October 6, 2006, were proven to have been executed while the Plaintiff was detained at the Semarang City Police facility.
* The execution of said agreements involved Abuse of Circumstances (''Misbruik van Omstandigheden'') and duress, rendering them '''NULL AND VOID'''.
* Semarang High Court Decision No. 45/Pdt/2008/PT.Smg is entirely annulled by the Supreme Court.
* The Plaintiff's lawsuit is partially granted.

=== Annulled (Semarang High Court Verdict) ===

* Semarang High Court considerations declaring the trademark purchase agreement valid and dismissing the Plaintiff's lawsuit were entirely annulled by the Supreme Court as erroneous applications of contract law.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Protecting Civil Rights Against Unfounded Criminal Extortion:''' This landmark ruling establishes an essential legal safeguard in Indonesian business and intellectual property practice: criminal complaints must not be weaponized as instruments of legal extortion (''legal duress'') to misappropriate intellectual property or civil assets. Any compromise agreement or asset transfer born under the pressure of criminal investigation detentions is legally defective as an abuse of circumstances (''misbruik van omstandigheden'').

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==

; Are trademark purchase or settlement agreements signed while a person is in police detention legally valid under the law?
: '''Invalid and Null and Void.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 2356 K/Pdt/2008:

* Purchase or settlement agreements executed under pressure and in a state of duress while detained by the police due to an opponent's criminal complaint constitute an Abuse of Circumstances (''Misbruik van Omstandigheden'').
* Such detention deprives the detained party of freedom of will (''wilsvrijheid''), meaning the agreement fails to satisfy the validity requirements under Article 1320 of the Civil Code and is '''NULL AND VOID / VOIDABLE'''.
* The Supreme Court annulled the Semarang High Court verdict, declaring the Settlement Agreement and Trademark Purchase Agreement dated October 6, 2006, null and void.

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:2399K PID SUS 2010
wikitext:
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 2399 K/Pid.Sus/2010''' (dated December 30, 2010) is a landmark Indonesian special criminal law jurisprudence precedent establishing vital rules regarding the harmonization of sentencing with public demands for justice and the proportionality of state financial losses in single-charge indictments under Article 2 paragraph (1) of the Anti-Corruption Law.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established three primary legal principles:

# '''Harmonization of Law with Public Sense of Justice:''' In exercising its judicial function, the Supreme Court may apply the law in concrete cases where actualization does not entirely align with the spirit and intent of the legislature (specifically regarding mandatory special minimum prison sentences of 4 years under Article 2 paragraph (1) of Law No. 31 of 1999 ''jo.'' Law No. 20 of 2001), harmonizing sanctions instead with the magnitude of arising state financial losses and public demands for justice.
# '''Proportional Justice for Minimal Defendant Benefits:''' When a Public Prosecutor brings a single-charge indictment under Article 2 paragraph (1) of the Anti-Corruption Law, yet the monetary value enjoyed by the Defendant ([Defendant] T) is extremely minor (amounting to only Rp 2,900,000 as a corporate name-borrowing fee), imposing the special minimum sentence of 4 years imprisonment would violate the sense of justice due to a drastic imbalance between the Defendant's act, the personal gains acquired, and the minimum criminal sanction.
# '''Non-Permissive Stance on Corruption:''' Although corruption crimes must never be treated permissively regardless of the quantum of state loss, High Courts and Judges must avoid imposing sentences that violate public fairness by harmonizing criminal sanctions against material justice and disproportionality.

The Supreme Court annulled West Kalimantan High Court Decision No. 195/Pid/2010/PT.Ptk dated September 3, 2010, ''jo.'' Singkawang District Court Decision No. 63/Pid.B/2010/PN.Skw dated June 22, 2010, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by imposing a proportional sentence harmonized with public expectations of justice.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Proportionality Principle of Criminal Sanctions (''Strafmaat'') and Harmonization of Material Justice Against Special Minimum Sentences (Article 2 paragraph 1 Anti-Corruption Law) ===
''Does the Cassation Panel of Judges possess authority to harmonize sentencing below or deviate from the special minimum sentence (4 years imprisonment)'' ex ''Article 2 paragraph (1) of the Anti-Corruption Law when a Defendant is proven to commit corruption but personal gains acquired are extremely small (Rp 2.9 Million)?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Authorized and Obligated to Harmonize.''' The Supreme Court emphasized that rigid application of the 4-year special minimum sentence against a Defendant who merely enjoyed a Rp 2.9 Million fee from a failed procurement violates public justice (disproportionality of punishment vs. culpability/gains). Judges possess authority to harmonize criminal sanctions by reconciling concrete state losses and public fairness.

=== 2. Juridical Dilemma of Single Indictments in Corruption Cases ===
When a Public Prosecutor brings a single indictment under Article 2 paragraph (1) of the Anti-Corruption Law without including subsidiary charges under Article 3, the judge's position becomes dilemmatic. Cassation judges must not permit material injustice simply due to rigid framing by prosecutors.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
Is the rigid application of the 4-year special minimum sentence ''ex'' Article 2 paragraph (1) of the Anti-Corruption Law against Defendant [Defendant] T (who received a fee of only Rp 2,900,000) legally correct, and what are the bounds of judicial discretion in harmonizing law with public justice?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Incorrect because it violates justice. The Supreme Court annulled West Kalimantan High Court Decision No. 195/Pid/2010/PT.Ptk ''jo.'' Singkawang District Court Decision No. 63/Pid.B/2010/PN.Skw and independently adjudicated by harmonizing a proportional sentence aligned with the Defendant's gains and public demands for fairness.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Singkawang District Court & West Kalimantan High Court) ===
Examination of facts regarding secretariat DPRD Singkawang clothing procurement for FY 2007 with a budget ceiling of Rp 64,948,000; appointment of [Co-defendant] as Procurement Committee Chairman; corporate name-borrowing by Defendant [Defendant] T and withdrawal of disbursed funds amounting to Rp 58,157,981; fee deduction of Rp 2,900,000 by [Defendant] T and remittance of Rp 55,257,981 to [Co-defendant] on January 2, 2008; total failure of uniform procurement; and BPK RI Pontianak Report No. 12.B/HP/XIX.PNK/05/2008 dated May 19, 2008, establishing fines of Rp 3,247,400 and total state loss of Rp 61,405,381.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===

* '''Law No. 31 of 1999 ''jo.'' Law No. 20 of 2001 on Eradication of Corruption Crimes:''' Article 2 paragraph (1) & Article 18 (Special Minimum Penalty & State Loss Restitution).
* '''Criminal Code (KUHP):''' Article 55 paragraph (1) 1st (Complicity / ''Medeplegen'').
* '''Law No. 48 of 2009 on Judicial Power:''' Article 5 paragraph (1) (Judge's Duty to Explore Values of Public Justice).

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===

* Doctrine of Sentencing Harmonization (''Strafmaat Aequitas''): The law must not be applied with rigid mechanicalism producing ''summum ius summa iniuria'' (rigid justice spawning extreme injustice).
* Jurisprudence on Small-Scale Corruption Proportionality: Sentencing must account for fault gradations, individual roles, and the real economic gains acquired by defendants.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* Defendant [Defendant] T was proven to have lent his corporate name and received procurement funds of Rp 58,157,981.
* Personal gains enjoyed by Defendant [Defendant] T were proven to amount to only Rp 2,900,000.
* Singkawang DPRD clothing procurement for FY 2007 suffered total failure, inflicting a state loss of Rp 61,405,381.
* Imposing the special minimum 4-year sentence was proven to violate public fairness.
* High Court and District Court decisions were annulled by the Supreme Court.

=== Unproven / Dismissed Arguments ===

* Defendant [Defendant] T was '''UNPROVEN''' to have enjoyed the entire project fund of Rp 58.15 Million, as the remaining Rp 55.25 Million was proven to have been entirely surrendered to [Co-defendant].

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Enforcing Small-Scale Corruption vs. Minimum Sentence Legal Certainty:''' This landmark ruling establishes a courageous judicial precedent in Indonesia: the Supreme Court affirms that the judiciary's function is upholding material justice, not merely serving as a mechanical translator of statutory text. In corruption cases charged under a single indictment of Article 2 paragraph (1) carrying a minimum 4-year threat, Cassation Judges possess the right to harmonize penalties to prevent tragic injustice for small-scale defendants.

== Overview ==
Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 250 K/Pdt/1984 dated February 27, 1986, establishes fundamental Civil Procedure jurisprudence regarding the criteria and limitations for executing settlement decisions (*Acte van Vergelijk*): A settlement decision or deed that fails to clearly state the definite obligations of the parties (in casu stating only that a debt of US$ 500,000 owed to a third party shall be discussed further until a proper resolution satisfying both parties is reached) cannot be forcibly executed (*non-executable*), and an execution confiscation (*sita eksekusi*) carried out based on such a settlement deed must be lifted or annulled.

== Case Background ==
The Petitioner for Cassation / formerly Objector / Appellee (PT Limasatu Sankyo Industri Pangan, presently PT Supermi Indonesia) filed an objection (*verzet*) at the East Jakarta District Court against the Respondent for Cassation / formerly Defendant-Objected / Appellant ([Party A]). The objection was filed against the execution of a confiscation on June 23, 1982, based on the East Jakarta District Court Determination No. 26/1982/Eks jo. No. 49/Anm/1981 jo. No. 1/T/1975 G dated June 9, 1982, targeting the Objector's factory assets and noodle-making machinery.

The execution confiscation was requested by the Defendant-Objected on the grounds that the Objector had not fulfilled Article 8 of Settlement Deed No. 1/1975 G dated June 30, 1975, concerning the management of a debt amounting to US$ 500,000 owed to a third party (Chori America Inc.). The Objector rejected the execution confiscation, arguing that all obligations under Settlement Deed No. 1/1975 G jo. Settlement Deed No. 240 a/76 P dated July 27, 1976, had been completely fulfilled and that there was no promise to pay the debt directly to the Defendant-Objected.

The East Jakarta District Court (Decision No. 130/JT/1982 G dated December 22, 1982) granted the Objector's objection in part, declared the Objector to be a rightful objector, and ordered the lifting of the execution confiscation over the Objector's factory assets and machinery. However, the Jakarta High Court (Decision No. 102/1983 PT. Perdata dated June 27, 1983) annulled the East Jakarta District Court judgment and rejected the Objector's opposition. Dissatisfied with the Jakarta High Court ruling, PT Limasatu Sankyo Industri Pangan (PT Supermi Indonesia) filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The Jakarta High Court erred in applying the law in evaluating the dispositive provisions of Settlement Deed No. 1/1975 G dated June 30, 1975, particularly Article 8.
# Although pursuant to guarantee deed No. 29 dated June 9, 1973, the Defendant-Objected's debt to Chori Company Ltd. amounting to US$ 500,000 was guaranteed by the Objector, the dispute between the Objector and the Defendant-Objected had been terminated through a settlement (Settlement Deed No. 1/1975 G dated June 30, 1975), wherein Article 8 stipulated that the settlement method regarding the Defendant-Objected's debt to Chori Company Ltd. amounting to US$ 500,000 would be discussed further until a resolution satisfying both parties was achieved.
# Because the matter concerning the debt to Chori Company Ltd. has not yet reached a settlement to date, under procedural law, the provisions of Article 8 are non-executable through Settlement Deed No. 1/1975 G because it remains unclear what is to be executed, as it requires further discussion; thus, the appropriate legal avenue for the Defendant-Objected is to file a lawsuit against the Objector in a new proceeding.
# Furthermore, the claim of Chori America Inc. was never assigned to the Defendant-Objected via a valid assignment (*cessie* pursuant to Article 613 of the Civil Code) that would give rise to the Defendant-Objected's right to directly claim the sum of US$ 500,000 from the Objector.
# Legal Principle: "A settlement decision/deed that fails to clearly state the obligations of the parties cannot be executed, and execution confiscation carried out based on such settlement deed must be lifted."

* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation PT LIMASATU SANKYO INDUSTRI PANGAN (presently PT SUPERMI INDONESIA); Annulling the Jakarta High Court decision dated June 27, 1983, No. 102/1983 PT. Perdata; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Granting the Objector's opposition in part; (2) Declaring that the Objector is a rightful objector (*Pembantah yang benar*); (3) Lifting the execution confiscation levied upon the movable and immovable properties of the Objector (consisting of noodle-making machinery, noodle-packaging machinery and accessories, diesel engine, office inventory, office and factory buildings, and the land underneath) based on East Jakarta District Court Determination No. 26/1982/Eks jo. No. 49/Anm/1981 jo. No. 1/T/1975 G dated June 9, 1982, executed on June 23, 1982; (4) Rejecting the remainder of the Objector's opposition; (5) Ordering the Respondent for Cassation ([Party A]) to pay court costs across all levels of jurisdiction (cassation assessed at Rp 20,000). *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court on Wednesday, February 5, 1986, and pronounced on Thursday, February 27, 1986, by H.R. Poerwoto S. Gandasoebrata, S.H. [Vice Chairman of the Supreme Court / Session Chairman], Yahya, S.H., and Samsoeddin Aboebakar, S.H. [Associate Justices]).*

|-
|Minister of Manpower Decree No. Kep-150/Men/2000 (Articles 18(1)(h),(k), 18(4), 22); Law No. 22 of 1957 on Labor Dispute Settlement; Law No. 9 of 1998 on Freedom of Expression in Public; Law No. 21 of 1900 on Labor Unions; Law No. 5 of 1986 on State Administrative Courts; Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court
|}

== Overview ==
Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 250 K/TUN/2002 dated October 23, 2002, establishes fundamental labor and employment jurisprudence:

* **Serious Misconduct and Termination Sanctions (Minister of Manpower Decree No. Kep-150/Men/2000):** Workers/laborers who commit unlawful acts categorized as serious misconduct under Article 18 paragraph (1) letters h and k of Minister of Manpower Decree No. Kep-150/Men/2000 (such as occupying hotel lobbies, conducting unprocedural demonstrations/without police notification ex Law No. 9 of 1998 & Law No. 22 of 1957, damaging facilities, and leaving the employer's property in a dangerous condition) may be subjected to the sanction of Termination of Employment (*PHK*).
* **Awarding Severance Pay for the Sake of Justice (Casuistic / Ex Aequo et Bono):** Although formally under statutory law workers who commit serious misconduct are not entitled to severance pay (Article 18 paragraph (4) of Minister of Manpower Decree No. Kep-150/Men/2000), the Supreme Court acting as *Judex Juris* deemed it necessary to uphold human rights and humanitarian considerations for workers during an economic crisis. Based on case-by-case justice (*casuistic*), terminated workers are granted severance pay amounting to 3 (three) times the provisions of Article 22 of Minister of Manpower Decree No. Kep-150/Men/2000.

== Case Background ==
The object of the dispute was the Decree of Defendant I / Central Committee for Labor Dispute Settlement (*P4P*) No. 602/358/63-5/IX/PHK/5-2001 dated May 1, 2001, concerning the authorization of termination of employment (*PHK*) between PT Swadharma Kerry Satya (Shangri-La Hotel Jakarta) and its workers (Abd. Rochim et al. / 414 persons). The dispute arose from demands raised by the Shangri-La Independent Labor Union (*SPMS*) regarding the distribution of service charges, pension funds, and human resource development. Following the suspension of the SPMS Chairman (Halilintar Nurdin), the workers staged a demonstration in the hotel lobby, occupied the hotel premises, refused to resume work, which resulted in a hotel lock-out and property damage.

The Jakarta State Administrative High Court (Decision No. 227/G/2001/PT.TUN.Jkt dated March 26, 2002) annulled the P4P decree and ordered the employer to reinstate the workers. Dissatisfied with the appellate ruling, P4P (Petitioner for Cassation I) and PT Swadharma Kerry Satya / Shangri-La Hotel (Petitioner for Cassation II) filed cassation petitions to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* **Ratio Decidendi:**

# The *Judex Facti* (Jakarta State Administrative High Court) committed an error in applying the law by ignoring authentic evidence—namely the South Jakarta District Court Decision No. 22/Pdt.G/2001/PN.Jkt.Sel. dated November 1, 2001 (jo. Jakarta High Court No. 195/Pdt/2002/PT.DKI), which had acquired permanent legal force—qualifying the workers' demonstration and actions at Shangri-La Hotel as an unlawful act (*onrechtmatige daad*).
# The actions of the workers failing to follow proper procedures (violating Article 6 paragraph (1) of Law No. 22 of 1957 and Law No. 9 of 1998 on freedom of expression in public without police notification), leaving employer assets in danger, and disregarding the Shangri-La Hotel Collective Labor Agreement (*KKB*) fall within the category of serious misconduct ex Article 18 paragraph (1) letters h and k of Minister of Manpower Decree No. Kep-150/Men/2000, thereby justifying the authorization of termination.
# Labor union advocacy pursued with good intentions does not justify using rough, impolite methods, hotel lobby occupation, or destructive actions causing harm to other parties.
# Although formally workers committing serious misconduct are not entitled to severance pay, the Supreme Court, based on considerations of justice (*ex aequo et bono*) upholding human rights and worker welfare during an economic crisis, established an award of severance pay equivalent to 3 (three) times the standard stipulated in Article 22 of Minister of Manpower Decree No. Kep-150/Men/2000.

* **Ruling:** Granting the cassation petitions from Petitioner for Cassation I (CENTRAL COMMITTEE FOR LABOR DISPUTE SETTLEMENT / P4P) and Petitioner for Cassation II (PT SWADHARMA KERRY SATYA / Shangri-La Hotel); Annulling the Jakarta State Administrative High Court decision dated March 26, 2002, No. 227/G/2001/PT.TUN.Jkt; and Independently Adjudicating: Declaring null and void the P4P Decree No. 602/358/63-5/IX/PHK/5-2001 dated May 1, 2001, insofar as it concerns severance pay, long-service awards, housing/medical compensation, and the names of the Plaintiffs alone; Ordering P4P to issue a new decree providing: (I) Authorizing the Employer PT Swadharma Kerry Satya / Shangri-La Hotel to terminate the employment (*PHK*) of the workers (60 persons) effective as of the end of January 2001; (II) Mandating the Employer PT Swadharma Kerry Satya to pay in cash severance pay amounting to 3 (three) times the provisions of Article 22 of Minister of Manpower Decree No. Kep-150/Men/2000 to workers who have not yet or are unwilling to accept termination; (III) Requiring the Employer to submit data of terminated workers to the Central Jakarta Municipal Manpower Office; (IV) Execution to be conducted under the supervision of Labor Inspectors; and ordering the Respondents for Cassation / Plaintiffs to pay cassation court costs amounting to Rp 200,000. *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court on Wednesday, October 23, 2002, by Prof. Dr. Paulus Effendi Lotulung, S.H. [Presiding Judge], Dr. H.M. Laica Marzuki, S.H., and Ny. Chairani A. Wani, S.H.).*

|Civil Code (BW) Articles 1320, 1338, 1365; HIR Article 178; Vendu Reglement (S. 1908 No. 189); Law No. 4 of 1996 on Mortgage Rights; Law No. 14 of 1970 jo. Law No. 4 of 2004; Law No. 14 of 1985 jo. Law No. 5 of 2004

== Overview ==
Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 252 K/Pdt/2002 dated June 11, 2004, establishes fundamental civil jurisprudence and legal rules regarding fabricated sales and the lack of good faith by auction winners: An auction winner is deemed to be acting in bad faith and is not entitled to legal protection if the auction winner turns out to be the creditor themselves who purchased the property at a price far below the appraised collateral value. Furthermore, a land/house sale and purchase transaction unaccompanied by actual delivery of the object and executed based on a fabricated debt-security arrangement must be declared legally flawed and null and void together with all its legal consequences.

== Case Background ==
The Original Plaintiffs / Petitioners for Cassation I (Ir. [Party A], M.Sc., subsequently succeeded by his heirs: Ny. [Party B], Komaruddin Brotoatmodjo, Taufik Hidayat Brotoatmodjo, Siti Nooraini Williamson, and Muhamad Seisar Reza) are the lawful owners of a plot of land and building under HGB No. 106/Bantarjati (currently HGB No. 93/Babakan) located at [address removed], Bogor. To process *eigendom* land documents in Jakarta, the Plaintiff borrowed Rp 1,500,000,000 from Defendant I (Ir. Theodorus Tedja Lawu) secured by the land certificate and executed a blank, uncompleted Sale and Purchase Deed form before Notary Ny. Mulyani Sjafei, SH (Defendant II). Defendant I defaulted by only handing over Rp 560,000,000, but unlawfully utilized the blank form to draft Sale and Purchase Deed No. 25/Bgr/Utara/II/JB/1995 dated February 24, 1995, priced at Rp 300,000,000 (whereas market value was Rp 2,000,000,000), subsequently transferring ownership rights and encumbering it as credit collateral until it was auctioned off by the Bogor State Auction Office. The execution auction winner was Defendant I (the creditor himself) via PT Alam Sari Lestari / Bank Bali at a heavily depressed price.

The Bogor District Court (Decision No. 13/Pdt/G/1999/PN.Bgr dated December 6, 1999) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part, annulled the Sale and Purchase Deed, the Power of Attorney to Sell, the Auction Minutes, and declared the certificate in the name of Defendant I / Bank Bali to have no legal force. However, the Bandung High Court (Decision No. 261/Pdt/2000/PT.Bdg dated October 19, 2000) annulled the Bogor District Court judgment. Petitioners for Cassation I (Plaintiff's Heirs) and Petitioner for Cassation II (Defendant I) filed cassation petitions to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The sale and purchase transaction between the Plaintiff/seller and Defendant I/buyer regarding the land and building under HGB No. 93/Babakan ([address removed], Bogor) was unnatural because it was unaccompanied by the physical delivery of the land and house to the buyer and was executed based on the completion of a blank sale and purchase deed form signed during the creation of a secured debt instrument. Therefore, the transaction constitutes a mere fabrication and must be declared legally defective together with all its legal consequences.
# The auction winner of the disputed object turned out to be the creditor himself (Defendant I) with a purchase price far below the collateral value. This demonstrates that the auction winner acted in bad faith and is consequently not entitled to legal protection.
# The *Judex Facti* (Bandung High Court) committed an error in applying the law; thus, the Bandung High Court decision is annulled, and the Supreme Court independently adjudicates by adopting the Bogor District Court's reasoning, which was accurate and correct.

* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioners for Cassation I (1. NY. [Party B], 2. KOMARUDDIN BROTOATMODJO, 3. TAUFIK HIDAYAT BROTOATMODJO, 4. SITI NOORAINI WILLIAMSON, 5. MUHAMAD SEISAR REZA) and Petitioner for Cassation II (IR. THEODORUS TEDJA LAWU); Annulling the Bandung High Court decision dated October 19, 2000, No. 261/Pdt/2000/PT.Bdg; and Independently Adjudicating: IN EXCEPTION: Rejecting the Defendants' exceptions in their entirety; IN THE PRINCIPAL CASE: (1) Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part; (2) Declaring valid and enforceable the security attachment (*conservatoir beslag*) executed by the Bailiff of the Bogor District Court on September 2, 1999, No. 13/Pdt/G/1999/PN.Bgr jo. No. 16/CB/Pdt/1999/PN.Bgr; (3) Declaring that the Plaintiff is the lawful owner of the land and building under HGB Certificate No. 106/Bantarjati / presently HGB Certificate No. 93/Babakan known as Jalan Ceremai No. 18, Bogor; (4) Declaring that Defendants I, II, and III have committed an unlawful act (*onrechtmatige daad*); (5) Declaring: (a) Null and void Sale and Purchase Deed No. 25/Bgr/Utara/II/JB/1995 dated February 24, 1995, between the Plaintiff and Defendant I together with all legal consequences arising therefrom; (b) Null and void and without legal force the Power to Mortgage and Power to Sell No. 133 dated March 30, 1995, together with its legal consequences; (c) Null and void the execution carried out based on Auction Minutes No. 279/1997-1998 dated October 7, 1997; (d) Null and void and without binding legal force HGB Certificate No. 93/Babakan Village dated March 15, 1996, in the name of Ir. Theodorus Tedja Lawu, now in the name of Bank Bali (Defendant IV); (6) Ordering all parties related to this case to restore conditions to their original state and reinstate the legal status of the disputed object under HGB Certificate No. 93/Babakan Village in the name of Bank Bali Jakarta Branch; (7) Ordering the Respondents for Cassation to pay court costs across all levels of jurisdiction (cassation assessed at Rp 200,000). *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court on Friday, June 11, 2004, by Prof. DR. Paulus E. Lotulung, SH. [Junior Chairman of the Supreme Court / Presiding Judge], Ny. Chairani A. Wani, SH., and Prof. DR. Valerine J.L.K., SH., MA. [Associate Justices]).*

== Overview ==
Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 253 K/AG/2002 dated March 17, 2004, establishes important Islamic Civil Procedure jurisprudence regarding claim joinder (*kumulasi tuntutan*) and the qualification limits of vague lawsuits (*obscuur libel*): The joinder of multiple claims by a plaintiff is justified as long as it combines a divorce claim with its legal consequences as stipulated under Article 86 of Law No. 7 of 1989, whereas other claims not regulated under said article should simply be declared inadmissible (*niet ontvankelijke verklaard*). The entire lawsuit of the Plaintiff should not be dismissed as inadmissible on the grounds of *obscuur libel* solely due to such joinder.

== Case Background ==
The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation ([Party A]) and the Original Defendant were lawfully married in 1978 and blessed with 4 children. During the marriage, joint properties consisting of movable and immovable assets were acquired. Disputes arose because the Original Defendant contracted another marriage without permission with another woman ([Party B]) and traveled to Mecca in 1995. The peak of the dispute occurred in November 2000 when the Original Defendant accused the Original Plaintiff of adultery, causing them to separate households, and the Defendant ceased providing maintenance.

The Original Plaintiff filed for divorce (*cerai gugat*), division of joint property, security attachment (*conservatoir beslag*), and annulment of the Original Defendant's marriage to [Party B]. The Mataram High Religious Court (Decision No. 50/Pdt.G/2001/PTA.Mtr dated August 20, 2001 AD / 1 Jumada al-Akhirah 1422 AH) declared the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible in its entirety on the grounds of a vague lawsuit (*obscuur libel*) due to the joinder of various claims. Dissatisfied with the ruling, the Petitioner for Cassation filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The joinder of multiple claims by a plaintiff is justified as long as it represents a combination of a divorce claim with its legal consequences regulated under Article 86 of Law No. 7 of 1989.
# Regarding other claims not governed by Article 86 of Law No. 7 of 1989, they should merely be declared inadmissible (*niet ontvankelijke verklaard*), and it does not follow that the Plaintiff's entire lawsuit must be declared inadmissible under the consideration of being a vague lawsuit (*obscuur libel*).
# In accordance with civil procedural principles under the HIR and RBg, a lawsuit is deemed to meet requirements if it states the parties, the factual basis (*posita*), and the petitory claims (*petitum*) supported by the factual basis.

* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation [Party A]; Annulling the Mataram High Religious Court decision dated August 20, 2001 AD, No. 50/Pdt.G/2001/PTA.Mtr; and Independently Adjudicating: Rejecting the Plaintiff's lawsuit, and ordering the Plaintiff to pay court costs across all levels of jurisdiction, assessed at the cassation level at Rp 200,000 (two hundred thousand rupiahs). *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court on Wednesday, March 17, 2004, by Drs. H. Syamsuhadi Irsyad, S.H., M.H. [Presiding Judge], Drs. H. Habiburrahman, M.H., and Dr. H. Hamdan, S.H., M.H. [Associate Justices]).*
