title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:2563K PDT 1988
wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 2563 K/Pdt/1988}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 2563 K/Pdt/1988''' (deliberated on March 1, 1990 / pronounced on March 15, 1990) is a fundamental Central Javanese customary inheritance law and marital property law jurisprudence precedent establishing vital rules concerning the inheritance rights of children from a first marriage over their father's share of property acquired during a third marriage (''gono-gini'' of the third marriage).

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established three primary legal principles:

# '''Cross-Marriage Inheritance Rights Over a Father's ''Gono-Gini'' Property:''' A child from a first marriage (Plaintiff: Ny. [Party C]) is legally entitled to inherit their father's share (the late H.R. Moh. Idris bin Alimarja) acquired during his third marriage, alongside the child from the third marriage (Defendant: Ny. Rr. Suratmi).
# '''Proportional Distribution of Third Marriage Joint Property (''Gono-Gini''):''' Property acquired during a third marriage constitutes joint marital property (''gono-gini'') between the father and the third wife, such that one-half (½) constitutes the deceased father's estate. This father's share is inherited equally by his two biological children (each receiving ¼ of the entire disputed estate / half of the half).
# '''Final Inheritance Distribution Ratio:''' Because the remaining ½ ''gono-gini'' share constitutes the absolute right of the third wife inherited entirely by her own biological child (Defendant), the final inheritance distribution ratio over the entire disputed object between the Plaintiff (child of the 1st wife) and the Defendant (child of the 3rd wife) is 1 to 3 (¼ share for the Plaintiff and ¾ share for the Defendant).

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation (Ny. [Party C] ''alias'' Ny. M. Sadali), annulled Semarang High Court Decision No. 161/Pdt/1988/PT.Smg dated June 8, 1988, ''jo.'' Kebumen District Court Decision No. 42/Pdt.G/1986/PN.Kbm dated October 8, 1987, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by declaring the disputed land and building as the estate of the late H.R. Moh. Idris subject to inheritance division at a 1 : 3 ratio, while ordering the Defendant to surrender ¼ of the disputed estate and pay damages of Rp 400,000 to the Plaintiff.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Legal Standing of Children from Preceding Marriages Over a Father's Estate Acquired in Subsequent Marriages (Central Javanese Customary Inheritance Law) ===
''Is a biological child from a first marriage barred (excluded) or stripped of inheritance rights over their father's share originating from the ''gono-gini'' property of the father's third marriage?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Not Barred (Fully Entitled).'''

Pursuant to Central Javanese Customary Law, when a man enters into multiple marriages (polygamy/successive marriages), ''gono-gini'' property acquired within each respective marriage is separate. However, the one-half (½) share belonging to the late father from the third marriage's ''gono-gini'' constitutes estate property (''karangwidda'' / inheritance) that must devolve upon ALL of his biological children across all marriages.

=== 2. Cross-Marriage Inheritance Distribution Formula (Half of the Half / 1 : 3 Ratio) ===
''What is the mathematical distribution formula over a single third-marriage ''gono-gini'' asset when a deceased father leaves 2 children (1 child from the 1st wife and 1 child from the 3rd wife)?''

'''Supreme Court Rule:'''

* The disputed ''gono-gini'' asset is split into two equal halves (½ father's share : ½ third wife's share).
* The father's ½ share is divided equally between his 2 biological children: Plaintiff receives ½ × ½ = ¼ share (25%), and Defendant receives ½ × ½ = ¼ share (25%).
* The third wife's ½ share is inherited entirely by her own biological child (Defendant) = ½ share (50%).
* Plaintiff's total share = ¼ share (25%); Defendant's total share = ¼ + ½ = ¾ share (75%). The final distribution ratio is therefore 1 : 3.

=== 3. Calculation of Rental Proceeds Compensation ===
A Plaintiff entitled to a ¼ share of the father's estate is entitled to claim compensation for rental/contract proceeds of the disputed building proportional to her share, amounting to ¼ of proven total rental receipts (i.e., ¼ × Rp 1,600,000 = Rp 400,000).

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (''Judex Juris'' / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' (Kebumen District Court No. 42/Pdt.G/1986/PN.Kbm & Semarang High Court No. 161/Pdt/1988/PT.Smg) err in applying customary law (''foutieve toepassing van het adatrecht'') by ruling that a child from the first wife has no right whatsoever to the father's ''gono-gini'' share acquired from a third marriage?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. The ''Judex Facti'' misapplied the law. The Supreme Court granted the Plaintiff's cassation petition (Ny. [Party C]), annulled the Semarang High Court ''jo.'' Kebumen District Court decisions, and independently adjudicated by holding that the Plaintiff is entitled to a ¼ share of her father's estate under a 1 : 3 inheritance distribution ratio against the Defendant.

=== Question of Fact (''Judex Facti'' / Kebumen District Court & Semarang High Court) ===
Examination of facts regarding marital genealogies of the late H.R. Moh. Idris bin Alimarja with Ny. [Party A] (1st wife), Ny. Roliyah (2nd wife), and Ny. [Party B] (3rd wife); births of Plaintiff (Ny. [Party C]) and Defendant (Ny. Rr. Suratmi); purchase of land & buildings on Parcel 41 Letter C 522 Panjer Kebumen in 1944 during the third marriage; leasing of the property to co-respondents (Exhibits TT.I/1 through TT.IV/1); and verification of rental proceeds valued at Rp 1,600,000.

=== Statutory Regulations ===

* '''Central Javanese Customary Law:''' Principles of Polygamous Marital Property Separation & Customary Equity in Biological Children's Inheritance (''Gono-Gini'' vs. ''Karangwidda'').
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation and Independent Adjudication Authority.

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:2580K PDT 1998
wikitext:
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 2580 K/Pdt/1998''' (dated January 26, 2001) is a fundamental Indonesian civil procedure jurisprudence precedent establishing crucial rules regarding the formal prerequisites of third-party opposition lawsuits (''derden verzet'') and the fundamental legal distinction between a formal legal demand letter (''somasi'') and court-ordered execution (''eksekusi pengadilan'').

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established three primary legal principles:

# '''Third-Party Opposition Based on a Demand Letter Is Inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO):''' A third-party opposition (''derden verzet'') filed against a District Court judgment solely on the grounds of a demand letter (''somasi'') or warning notice issued by legal counsel must be declared '''Inadmissible''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).
# '''Legal Rule That "A Demand Letter Does Not Equal Execution":''' An attorney or legal counsel's demand letter (''somasi'') constitutes an ordinary civil action and does not represent official court execution proceedings (''aanmaning'' or physical execution), because "a demand letter does not equal execution." Execution is an official legal act conducted strictly under the authority and official writ of the Chairman of the District Court.
# '''Unenforceability of Judgments Against External Parties:''' An initial civil lawsuit judgment (No. 183/Pdt.G/1995/PN.Jkt.Bar) that failed to join registered certificate holders (the Objectors) as parties to the action cannot be invoked as a valid legal basis for execution or for issuing a demand letter against such third parties.

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation (YAYASAN SAWERI GADING), annulled Jakarta High Court Decision No. 259/Pdt/1997/PT.DKI dated June 5, 1997, ''jo.'' West Jakarta District Court Decision No. 29/Pdt.G/1996/PN.Jkt.Bar dated July 3, 1996, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by declaring the Objectors' opposition in Convention Inadmissible (NO), and declaring Defendant I's opposition in Reconvention Inadmissible (NO).

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Qualification of Demand Letters (''Somasi'') vs. Court Execution in Third-Party Opposition (''Derden Verzet'' ''ex'' Article 195 paragraph 6 / Article 207 HIR) ===
''Can a warning notice or demand letter issued by winning counsel qualify as official court execution proceedings capable of serving as the legal basis for filing a third-party opposition (''derden verzet'')?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Not Execution.''' A demand letter dispatched by an advocate or legal counsel represents an ordinary civil action, not official court execution (''aanmaning'' or physical execution) falling under the statutory authority of the Chairman of the District Court. A demand letter does not equal execution. Consequently, an opposition filed solely on the basis of a demand letter is premature and inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

=== 2. Legal Consequences of Judgments Omitting Land/Certificate Holders as Parties ===
A District Court judgment (e.g., No. 183/Pdt.G/1995/PN.Jkt.Bar) that omits third-party HGB certificate holders as parties to the lawsuit cannot be utilized as a valid legal basis for execution nor as a foundation for issuing demand letters against such third parties.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (''Judex Juris'' / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Jakarta High Court (Decision No. 259/Pdt/1997/PT.DKI) err in applying civil procedure law (''foutieve toepassing van het procesrecht'') by partially granting the Objectors' opposition and examining substantive land ownership merits, whereas the opposition was filed prior to any official court execution process (relying solely on counsel's demand letter)?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. Jakarta High Court misapplied civil procedure law. The Supreme Court granted the Petitioner's cassation petition (Yayasan Saweri Gading), annulled Jakarta High Court Decision No. 259/Pdt/1997/PT.DKI ''jo.'' West Jakarta District Court Decision No. 29/Pdt.G/1996/PN.Jkt.Bar, and independently adjudicated by declaring the Objectors' opposition Inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

=== Question of Fact (''Judex Facti'' / West Jakarta District Court & Jakarta High Court) ===
Examination of facts regarding the issuance of Demand Letter No. SM.3/086/LAPD/XI/1995 dated November 13, 1995, by Yayasan Saweri Gading's counsel; issuance of SHGB Nos. 2248, 2156, 2414, 2219, and 2115/Tomang in the name of the Objectors over land/buildings in Tomang, Grogol Petamburan, West Jakarta; prior litigation history in Case No. 100/1973.G ''jo.'' No. 233 PK/Pdt/1981; proceedings in Case No. 183/Pdt.G/1995/PN.Jkt.Bar between Yayasan Saweri Gading and Ir. Drs. Naftali Wiryodiguno; and verification of ''Aanmaning''/Execution Writ No. 114/1995 Eks. ''jo.'' No. 183/Pdt.G/1995/PN.Jkt.Bar.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===

* '''HIR / RBg:''' Article 195 paragraph (6) HIR / Article 206 paragraph (6) RBg (Third-Party Opposition / ''Derden Verzet'' Against Execution).
* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata / BW):''' Article 1238 (Definition of Default / Demand Notices).
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation Authority and Independent Adjudication Powers.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===

* '''Doctrine of ''Derden Verzet'' Object Requirements:''' Third-party opposition (''derden verzet'') may only be filed once court execution of a judgment has commenced or been formally ordered (''aanmaning'' / execution writ / attachment) threatening third-party rights. Private demand letters do not constitute execution objects.
* '''Doctrine of Judgment Unenforceability Against External Parties:''' Civil judgments bind only participating parties (principle of relative civil judgment effects / ''ne bis in idem'' / party limits). Judgments disregarding registered certificate holders cannot be arbitrarily executed against them.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* The Objectors' opposition was filed solely on the basis of Demand Letter No. SM.3/086/LAPD/XI/1995 dated November 13, 1995, issued by Defendant I's counsel.
* A demand letter DOES NOT CONSTITUTE COURT EXECUTION, rendering the opposition premature / wrongly objected.
* West Jakarta District Court Decision No. 183/Pdt.G/1995/PN.Jkt.Bar omitted the Objectors as parties to the action.
* Jakarta High Court Decision No. 259/Pdt/1997/PT.DKI and West Jakarta District Court Decision No. 29/Pdt.G/1996/PN.Jkt.Bar are entirely annulled by the Supreme Court.
* The Objectors' opposition in Convention and Defendant I's reconventional opposition are declared '''INADMISSIBLE''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

=== Annulled (High Court Verdict) ===

* Jakarta High Court considerations reviewing and granting the Objectors' property ownership claims in the ''a quo'' opposition proceedings were annulled by the Supreme Court due to formal procedural defects (NO).

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Clear Boundaries Between Execution Opposition (''Derden Verzet'') and Tort Lawsuits (''PMH'') over Demand Letters:''' This landmark ruling establishes crucial procedural certainty in Indonesia: third parties receiving demand letters or vacation threats from lawyers must not hastily file ''derden verzet'' (execution opposition) because courts have not initiated official execution acts. If seeking legal remedy against disruptive demand letters, the proper recourse is an ordinary Tort Lawsuit (''Perbuatan Melawan Hukum'' / PMH), rather than execution opposition.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==

; Can a third-party opposition (''derden verzet'') be filed in court solely based on a demand letter issued by the winning party's lawyer?
: '''Inadmissible (NO).''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. No. 2580 K/Pdt/1998:
:* An opposition filed on the grounds of a demand letter against a District Court judgment (where Objectors were unjoined as parties) shall be declared inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).
:* A demand letter DOES NOT CONSTITUTE COURT EXECUTION (''aanmaning'' or physical execution), because "a demand letter does not equal execution." A demand letter is merely a private warning notice from legal counsel, not an official execution order issued by a court.
:* The Supreme Court annulled the Jakarta High Court decision and independently adjudicated by declaring the Objectors' opposition inadmissible (NO).

== Overview ==
Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 266 K/Ag/1993 dated June 25, 1994, establishes fundamental Islamic civil jurisprudence in divorce proceedings: The provisions of Article 19 letter f of Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975 are fulfilled if the *judex facti* considers that the grounds for divorce are proven without questioning who is at fault. If the court is convinced that the marriage has broken down (*broken marriage*), meaning the hearts of both parties are estranged, continuous disputes and quarrels without hope of reconciliation are established. Furthermore, the determination of *mut'ah* for the wife in the form of the entire shared matrimonial house and land is proper and just, taking into account the wife's standing and the husband's financial capacity.

== Case Background ==
The Petitioner for Cassation / formerly Petitioner / Appellee ([Husband]) filed a petition for permission to pronounce *talak* against the Respondent for Cassation / formerly Respondent / Appellant ([Wife]) at the South Jakarta Religious Court. The Petitioner and Respondent were married on December 25, 1985, at the Office of Religious Affairs (*KUA*) of Luhak 50 Kota Sub-District (Payakumbuh) and were blessed with no children. Since early 1991, disputes and estrangement arose due to differing life values, and both had lived separately for more than 1.5 years.

The South Jakarta Religious Court (Decision No. 473/Pdt.G/1992/PA.JS dated October 8, 1992) granted the Petitioner's request and granted permission to the Petitioner to divorce the Respondent. The Jakarta High Religious Court (Decision No. 03/1993/PTA.JK dated July 14, 1993) annulled the South Jakarta Religious Court judgment and rejected the Petitioner's request in its entirety on the grounds that the dispute originated from the Petitioner's involvement with another woman. Dissatisfied with the Jakarta High Religious Court ruling, the Petitioner filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The Jakarta High Religious Court erred in applying the law by failing to consider the actual facts occurring between the litigant spouses, where the Petitioner and Respondent had lived separately for more than 1 (one) year, and disharmony existed in their household.
# The grounds for divorce under Article 19 letter f of Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975 are solely directed at the marriage itself without questioning who is at fault. If the court is convinced that the marriage has broken down (*broken marriage*), it means the hearts of both parties are estranged, thereby fulfilling the requirements of Article 19 letter f of Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975.
# Regarding *mut'ah*, considering the wife's standing, the husband's financial capacity, and the Petitioner's offer submitted in the cassation memorandum, it is proper and just that *mut'ah* in the form of the entire house and land constituting the shared matrimonial residence located at [address removed], South Jakarta, be surrendered to the Respondent.

* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation: [Husband]; Annulling the Jakarta High Religious Court decision dated July 14, 1993, No. 03/1993/PTA.JK; and Independently Adjudicating: Affirming the South Jakarta Religious Court decision dated October 8, 1992, No. 473/Pdt.G/1992/PA.JS with amendments to the dispositive order to read as follows: (1) Granting the Petitioner's request; (2) Granting permission to the Petitioner ([Husband]) to pronounce *talak* against the Respondent ([Wife]) before the session of the South Jakarta Religious Court; (3) Ordering the Petitioner to surrender *mut'ah* in the form of the house and land at [address removed], Lebak Lestari Indah, Lebak Bulus Village, Cilandak Sub-District, South Jakarta, to the Respondent; (4) Ordering the Petitioner to pay court costs. *(Decided in the deliberation session of the Supreme Court on Saturday, June 25, 1994).*

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 266 K/AG/2010 dated July 12, 2010, establishes highly landmark and progressive Islamic civil jurisprudence regarding the division of joint property: A wife receives 3/4 (three-quarters) of the joint property and the husband receives only 1/4 (one-quarter), because the joint property was acquired entirely through the wife's own labor while the husband failed to provide maintenance for the wife and children for 11 years.

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiff / Respondent for Cassation (Ny. [Wife], Amd.Pd., Lecturer at Universitas Muhammadiyah Yogyakarta & Research Consultant) filed a divorce suit (*cerai gugat*) and a claim for the division of joint property against the Original Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation (Drs. [Husband], NGO worker in Solo) at the Bantul Religious Court. The Plaintiff and Defendant were married on April 8, 1995 (KUA Ketandan, Klaten) and blessed with 2 children. Since 1998, their household became discordant, marked by quarrels and physical/psychological abuse, culminating in the Defendant acting selfishly and harshly, and eventually expelling the Plaintiff on November 6, 2008. Furthermore, since 1997 (11 years / 132 months), the Defendant entirely failed to provide material or spiritual maintenance (*nafkah lahir maupun batin*) to his wife and children, forcing all family expenses and the acquisition of joint properties (immovable and movable assets) to be generated purely through the Plaintiff's own hard work.

The Bantul Religious Court (Decision No. 229/Pdt.G/2009/PA.Btl. dated August 20, 2009) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part, pronounced a single *ba'in sughra* divorce, and ordered the division of joint property at 3/4 share for the Plaintiff (Wife) and 1/4 share for the Defendant (Husband). The Yogyakarta High Religious Court (Decision No. 34/Pdt.G/2009/PTA.Yk. dated November 19, 2009) annulled the Bantul Religious Court judgment and independently adjudicated by retaining the 3/4 share for the Plaintiff and 1/4 share for the Defendant. The Defendant filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court arguing that joint property must be divided equally in half (1/2 share each).

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The Petitioner for Cassation's cassation argument that joint property within a marriage must be divided equally in half (1/2 share each) cannot be sustained, as the Yogyakarta High Religious Court did not err in applying the law.
# Based on evidence and facts established at trial, it was proven that the husband (Petitioner for Cassation) failed to provide maintenance from his earnings for 11 years (132 months), and all joint properties were acquired by the wife (Respondent for Cassation) through her own labor.
# In the interest of justice (*ex aequo et bono*), it is proper and just for the Plaintiff (Wife) to receive 3/4 (three-quarters) of the joint property and the Defendant (Husband) to receive 1/4 (one-quarter) of the joint property.
# The Supreme Court also found it necessary to amend the dispositive order of the Yogyakarta High Religious Court to comply with Article 84 of Law No. 7 of 1989 (as amended by Law No. 3 of 2006 and Law No. 50 of 2009) by ordering the Registrar of the Bantul Religious Court to send a copy of the decision to the Marriage Registration Official (*PPN*).
* '''Ruling:''' Rejecting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation: Drs. [Husband]; Amending the dispositive order of the Yogyakarta High Religious Court decision dated November 19, 2009, No. 34/Pdt.G/2009/PTA.Yk., which annulled the Bantul Religious Court decision dated August 20, 2009, No. 229/Pdt.G/2009/PA.Btl., so that the dispositive order in its entirety reads as follows: (1) Accepting the Appellant's appeal; (2) Annulling the Bantul Religious Court decision No. 229/Pdt.G/2009/PA.Btl.; INDEPENDENTLY ADJUDICATING: (a) Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part; (b) Pronouncing a single *ba'in sughra* divorce of Defendant (Drs. [Husband]) against Plaintiff (Ny. [Wife], Amd.Pd.); (c) Stating that the child [Child] remains under the custody (*hadhanah*) of the Plaintiff; (d) Ordering the Defendant to pay child maintenance amounting to Rp 750,000 per month; (e) Declaring that assets consisting of agricultural land under SHM No. 1132 & SHM No. 1133 in Klaten, SHM No. 07435 in Bantul, SHM No. 01797 in Sleman, Kijang car AB 1781 Z, Legenda motorcycle AD 4802 EV, Supra Fit motorcycle, and household furniture constitute joint property; (f) Declaring that the Plaintiff / Appellee is entitled to own 3/4 (three-quarters) of the joint property and the Defendant / Appellant is entitled to own 1/4 (one-quarter) of the joint property; (g) Ordering the Defendant and Plaintiff to divide the joint property, and if partition in kind is unfeasible, to sell it via public auction; (h) Directing the Registrar of the Bantul Religious Court to send a copy of the decision to the Marriage Registration Official (*PPN*); (i) Ordering the Petitioner for Cassation / Defendant to pay cassation-level court costs amounting to Rp 500,000 (five hundred thousand rupiahs). *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court on Monday, July 12, 2010, by Drs. H. Andi Syamsu Alam, S.H., M.H. [Presiding Judge], Drs. H. Hamdan, S.H., M.H., and Drs. H. Mukhtar Zamzami, S.H., M.H. [Associate Justices]).*

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:2678K PDT 1992
wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 2678 K/Pdt/1992}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 2678 K/Pdt/1992''' (dated October 27, 1994 / deliberation on September 15, 1994) is a fundamental civil procedural law jurisprudence precedent establishing a vital rule concerning the legal standing (''legitimasi persona standi in judicio'') of banking branch offices in civil legal relations.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established two primary legal principles:

# '''Persona Standi in Judicio of Bank Branch Offices:''' A bank branch office is an extension (''extension'') of the head office. Therefore, a bank branch office possesses legal standing (''persona standi in judicio'') to be sued and to sue in civil courts.
# '''Legal Capacity of Operational Managers:''' A lawsuit or objection directed against a Bank Branch Operational Manager acting on behalf of the Board of Directors pursuant to a Power of Attorney and Credit Agreement Deed is lawful and legally binding.

Where the Banda Aceh High Court (Decision No. 41/Pdt/1992/PT.Aceh) erred in applying the law by holding that a bank branch lacked ''persona standi in judicio'' without examining the material merits of the case, the Supreme Court annulled the High Court's decision and ordered the Banda Aceh High Court to reopen the trial to examine the merits of the case (''terugwijzing'').

| 2 || '''Capacity of Branch Operational Manager:''' A lawsuit directed against a Bank Branch Operational Manager acting for and on behalf of the Board of Directors pursuant to a credit agreement deed is lawful. || Headnote p. 285 & Supreme Court Reasoning pp. 288, 293: "...the lawsuit directed against [Party A] as Operational Manager... pursuant to the credit agreement deed... has legal standing in his capacity representing Bank Duta Lhokseumawe Branch, and therefore such lawsuit is lawful according to law." || 26678K_PDT_1992.pdf [Passage 2, 5, 8]

Board of Directors of Bank Duta Head Office). || Confirmed in decision identity pp. 285, 289, 295, 298. || 26678K_PDT_1992.pdf [Passage 2, 6, 10, 11]

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Legal Standing (''Persona Standi in Judicio'') of Bank Branch Offices in Civil Litigation ===
''Does a bank branch office of a legal entity (such as Bank Duta Lhokseumawe Branch) possess legal standing (persona standi in judicio) to act as a party sued or suing in a civil court?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Possesses Legal Standing / Lawful.'''
A bank branch office is an extension (''organ'' / ''extension'') of the head office. In credit obligation disputes executed at a branch office, the Branch Head / Operational Manager authorized by the Board of Directors possesses legal standing (''persona standi in judicio'') to represent the bank as either Plaintiff or Defendant/Opponent.

=== 2. Legal Consequences of Remanding a Case (''Terugwijzing'') When the Judex Facti Has Not Examined the Merits (''Bodem Zaak'') ===
Where a High Court (''Judex Facti'') misapplies formal law (e.g., erroneously holding that a party lacks ''persona standi in judicio'') without examining and deciding the material merits of the case (''bodem zaak''), the Supreme Court does not adjudicate the merits directly, but instead annuls the High Court's decision and orders the High Court to reopen the trial to examine the merits (''terugwijzing'') pursuant to the Supreme Court Law.

=== 3. Validity of Mortgage/Fiduciary Execution Prior to Final Tenor Maturity Due to Installment Default (Articles 1243, 1244 Civil Code) ===
A clause in a debt acknowledgment deed stipulating that failure to pay installments/interest for 2 consecutive months renders the entire debt immediately due and payable is valid and binding. Banks hold the right to petition for execution auctions of collateral without waiting for the final maturity tenor if the debtor is proven in default.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Banda Aceh High Court (Decision No. 41/Pdt/1992/PT.Aceh) err in applying civil procedural law (''foutieve toepassing van het procesrecht'') by holding that Bank Duta Lhokseumawe Branch was merely a branch lacking ''persona standi in judicio'' to be sued or sue?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. Banda Aceh High Court misapplied the law. A bank branch is an extension of the head office and possesses ''persona standi in judicio''. The Supreme Court granted [Party B]'s cassation petition, annulled Banda Aceh High Court's decision, and ordered Banda Aceh High Court to reopen the trial to examine the material merits of the case.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Lhokseumawe District Court & Banda Aceh High Court) ===
Verification of facts concerning the execution of Credit Agreement Deeds Nos. 183 (KIK Rp 24M) and 184 (KMKP Rp 6M) dated June 28, 1989, before Notary Ridwan Usman, S.H.; verification of installment default starting July 1990; verification of five formal collection minutes (Exhibits T.4 to T.8); and verification of the surrender of Freehold Title (SHM) No. 242 in the name of Muhammad Ali Nafiah as debt collateral.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''Law No. 7 of 1992 on Banking (''jo.'' Law No. 10 of 1998):''' Legal Status and Operational Rules of Bank Branch Offices.
* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata / BW):''' Articles 1243, 1244 (Default) & Article 1338 (Principle of Freedom of Contract / ''Pacta Sunt Servanda'').
* '''HIR (Herziene Inlandsch Reglement):''' Articles 118, 120 (Capacity to Appear in Court).
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation Review Authority & Order to Reopen Trials (''Terugwijzing'').

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* '''Doctrine of Branch Persona Standi in Judicio:''' Corporate/banking branch offices hold independent legal capacity to represent obligations created by such branch offices within their territorial jurisdiction.
* '''Doctrine of Terugwijzing (Remand of Case Files to Judex Facti):''' Where appellate review stops at formal exceptions/standing without touching the merits, the Supreme Court, upon annulling the appellate ruling, must remand the case for rehearing on the merits by the High Court.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* Bank Duta Lhokseumawe Branch is '''PROVEN TO POSSESS PERSONA STANDI IN JUDICIO''' to sue and be sued in civil courts.
* The auction objection lawsuit directed against [Party A] (Operational Manager) ''qq.'' Bank Duta is '''PROVEN LAWFUL UNDER CIVIL PROCEDURAL LAW'''.
* Banda Aceh High Court Decision No. 41/Pdt/1992/PT.Aceh is '''NULL AND VOID'''.
* Banda Aceh High Court is '''ORDERED TO REOPEN THE TRIAL TO EXAMINE THE MATERIAL MERITS OF THE CASE'''.

=== Unresolved Merits (Remanded) ===
* The merits of the auction objection regarding SHM No. 242 '''WERE NOT FINALLY DECIDED BY THE SUPREME COURT''' as the case was remanded to Banda Aceh High Court for re-examination of its substance.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Outcome of Merits Re-Examination at Banda Aceh High Court:''' This landmark cassation ruling focuses on resolving civil procedural law concerning the ''persona standi in judicio'' of bank branch offices. The substantive objection regarding the validity of the execution auction of SHM No. 242 prior to the 48-month tenor maturity was remanded for re-examination and judgment by Banda Aceh High Court via the remand (''terugwijzing'') mechanism.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
; Does a bank branch office possess legal standing (''persona standi in judicio'') to be sued and sue in civil courts pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence?
: '''Possesses Legal Standing / Lawful.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. No. 2678 K/Pdt/1992:
:* A bank branch office is an extension of the head office; therefore, a bank branch '''possesses legal standing (''persona standi in judicio'') to be sued and to sue''' in court.
:* Civil lawsuits or objections directed against a Bank Branch Operational Manager as the representative of the Board of Directors pursuant to credit agreements are lawful under civil procedural law.
:* Appellate rulings erroneously declaring bank branches unable to be sued are annulled, and appellate courts are ordered to reopen trials to examine case merits.

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:2773K PDT 2002
wikitext:
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 2773 K/Pdt/2002''' (dated May 19, 2004) is a landmark Indonesian arbitration law and legal time limit (''preclusieve termijn'') jurisprudence precedent establishing strict rules concerning the formal prerequisites and statutory deadlines for filing opposition or annulment petitions against Arbitral Awards pursuant to Article 71 of Law No. 30 of 1999 on Arbitration and Alternative Dispute Resolution.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established a primary legal principle:

* '''Arbitral Award Annulment Opposition Is Formally Defective When Filed Beyond the 30-Day Limit:''' Pursuant to Article 71 of Law No. 30 of 1999, an annulment petition against an arbitral award must be filed in writing within a maximum period of 30 (thirty) days calculated from the date the arbitral award is submitted and registered with the District Court Registrar.

Because the Sole Arbitral Award was pronounced on December 21, 1999, and registered at the South Jakarta District Court Registry on December 23, 1999, whereas the opposition/annulment petition was registered by the Objector (PT Angkasa Interland) on July 3, 2000 (well beyond the 30-day limit), the opposition petition was time-barred (''daluwarsa'') and formally defective.

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioners for Cassation (Petitioner I: Societe Auxiliaire D'enterprise International & PT Waskita Karya (Persero); Petitioner II: Soelistio, S.H.), annulled Jakarta High Court Decision No. 328/Pdt/2001/PT.DKI dated November 29, 2001, ''jo.'' South Jakarta District Court Decision No. 282/Pdt.G/2000/PN.Jak.Sel dated February 22, 2001, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by sustaining the Respondents' exception and declaring the Objector's opposition '''Inadmissible''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO) in Convention.

K. Santoso, S.H.
|Confirmed in decision identity pp. 53, 54.
|2773K_PDT_2002.pdf

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Mandatory Legal Nature of the Arbitral Annulment Deadline (''Preclusieve Termijn'' ''ex'' Article 71 of Law No. 30 of 1999) ===
''May an annulment or opposition petition against an arbitral award filed beyond the 30 (thirty) day limit from the registration of the award at the District Court still be examined on its merits by the District Court?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Unexaminable / Formally Defective.'''

The 30-day time limit established under Article 71 of Law No. 30 of 1999 represents a mandatory, absolute procedural deadline (''preclusieve termijn''). Filing an opposition or annulment petition beyond the 30-day mark from the registration of the arbitral award results in the lawsuit lapsing by operation of law due to being time-barred (''daluwarsa'') and formally defective, thus mandating dismissal as '''Inadmissible''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

=== 2. Duty of Judex Facti to Prioritize Formal Time-Bar Exceptions in Arbitration ===
District and High Courts that examine and adjudicate the substantive merits of an arbitral opposition without regard to the 30-day time-bar exception raised by Petitioners/Respondents commit an error in applying civil/arbitration procedural law (''error in iudicando'').

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' (South Jakarta District Court Decision No. 282/Pdt.G/2000/PN.Jak.Sel ''jo.'' Jakarta High Court Decision No. 328/Pdt/2001/PT.DKI) err in applying the law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') by annulling the Sole Arbitral Award dated December 21, 1999, whereas the opposition/annulment petition was filed by PT Angkasa Interland on July 3, 2000—exceeding the 30-day limit from the registration of the arbitral award on December 23, 1999, ''ex'' Article 71 of Law No. 30 of 1999?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. The ''Judex Facti'' misapplied the law. The Supreme Court granted the Petitioners' cassation petition, annulled the Jakarta High Court ''jo.'' South Jakarta District Court decisions, and independently adjudicated by Sustaining the Respondents' Exception and Declaring the Objector's Opposition Inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / South Jakarta District Court & Jakarta High Court) ===
Verification of the pronouncement date of the Sole Arbitral Award (December 21, 1999); verification of the registration date of the arbitral award at the South Jakarta District Court Registry (December 23, 1999); verification of the registration date of the opposition/annulment petition by PT Angkasa Interland (July 3, 2000); review of execution warning (''aanmaning'') writ history No. 06/Eks.Arb/2000/PN.Jak.Sel dated March 6, 2000; and verification of the arbitral panel composition (Prof. Dr. Sudargo Gautama, S.H., Ny. K. Santoso, S.H., Soelistio, S.H.).

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===

* '''Law No. 30 of 1999 on Arbitration and Alternative Dispute Resolution:''' Articles 70, 71 (Requirements and 30-Day Time Limit for Arbitral Award Annulment Petitions).
* '''Reglement op de Burgerlijke Rechtsvordering (RV):''' Articles 615 through 651 (Transitional Arbitration Provisions).
* '''Law No. 14 of 1985 ''jo.'' Law No. 4 of 2004 on Judicial Power ''jo.'' Law No. 5 of 2004 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation and Independent Adjudication Authority.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===

* Doctrine of Legal Certainty and Finality of Arbitral Awards (Final and Binding): Arbitral awards are final and possess permanent legal force. Court annulment proceedings represent an exceptionally strict, limited exception bound rigidly to the 30-day limitation period from registration.
* Doctrine of ''Preclusieve Termijn'': Statutory time limits prescribed for legal acts determine the survival or termination of rights to sue. Expiration of the 30-day window extinguishes the formal right of disputing parties to annul arbitral awards.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* The Sole Arbitral Award was validly pronounced on December 21, 1999.
* The Arbitral Award was officially registered at the South Jakarta District Court Registry on December 23, 1999.
* The opposition/annulment lawsuit was newly registered by the Objector (PT Angkasa Interland) at South Jakarta District Court on July 3, 2000.
* The opposition petition was proven to have been filed exceeding the 30-day time limit (time-barred / ''daluwarsa'').
* Jakarta High Court Decision No. 328/Pdt/2001/PT.DKI and South Jakarta District Court Decision No. 282/Pdt.G/2000/PN.Jak.Sel are '''NULL AND VOID'''.
* The Objector's (PT Angkasa Interland) opposition lawsuit is declared '''INADMISSIBLE''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

=== Annulled (District & High Court Verdicts) ===

* South Jakarta District Court and Jakarta High Court considerations annulling the Sole Arbitral Award were entirely annulled by the Supreme Court as the opposition lawsuit was formally defective due to expiration of time limits.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Enforcing Compliance with the 30-Day Time Limit in Commercial Arbitration Ecosystems:''' This landmark ruling reinforces legal certainty for businesses and arbitration institutions in Indonesia: losing parties in arbitration cannot freely file annulment lawsuits in district courts whenever they choose. The 30-day deadline from arbitral award registration represents an absolute condition precedent. Disregarding the 30-day limit causes annulment lawsuits to lapse by operation of law.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==

; What is the deadline for filing an arbitral award annulment petition at a District Court pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence and Law No. 30 of 1999?
: '''Maximum of 30 Days From Arbitral Award Registration.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. No. 2773 K/Pdt/2002:
:* Under Article 71 of Law No. 30 of 1999, an arbitral award annulment petition must be filed in writing within a maximum period of 30 (thirty) days calculated from the submission and registration of the arbitral award at the District Court Registrar.
:* Opposition/annulment petitions filed beyond the 30-day limit are classified as formally defective and time-barred (''daluwarsa'').
:* Courts receiving opposition petitions exceeding 30 days must sustain the Respondent's exception and declare the opposition '''Inadmissible''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 277 K/Pdt/1984 dated June 15, 1985, establishes important civil jurisprudence regarding immovable property lease disputes (house/shop): In lease agreements, the provisions of Article 1579 of the Civil Code (BW) apply, whereby the lessor cannot terminate the lease by stating an intention to personally use the leased property, unless otherwise agreed upon beforehand. Furthermore, late payment or non-payment of rent by the lessee does not constitute grounds for the automatic termination or cancellation of the lease agreement by operation of law (*demi hukum*), but rather serves as grounds to demand fulfillment of rent payment obligations.

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiffs / Respondents for Cassation ([Party A], Theodorus Tolen Kerans, Baltasar Leopold Kerans, Maria Dolorosa Kerans, and Hendrikus Kelelleng Kerans — the heirs of the late Sinyo Kerans) filed a lawsuit against the Original Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation ([Party B]) at the Larantuka District Court. The object of the dispute was a plot of house/shop (measuring 6 x 18 meters) situated on inherited yard land belonging to the late Sinyo Kerans in Postoh Village, Larantuka. The lease agreement had been ongoing since 1952 with the Plaintiffs' parents and continued from 1963 until May 1977 with the Plaintiffs. On January 1, 1977, the Plaintiffs requested the Defendant to vacate the house/shop because the Plaintiffs intended to use it themselves, but the Defendant ignored the request. Since June 1, 1977, the Defendant failed to pay rent, prompting the Plaintiffs to demand lease cancellation, eviction, and payment of rent arrears.

The Larantuka District Court (Decision No. 9/PN.Ltk/Pdt.G/1982/III dated February 14, 1983) granted the Plaintiffs' lawsuit in part: declaring the lease terminated by operation of law, ordering the Defendant to vacate the house/shop, and ordering rent payment. The Kupang High Court (Decision No. 60/PTK/1983/PDT dated October 12, 1983) amended the Larantuka District Court judgment: declaring the lease agreement to remain valid, rejecting the claims for lease termination and eviction because under Article 1579 of the BW the lessor cannot terminate the lease on the grounds of personal use. The Defendant ([Party B]) filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The *Judex Facti* of the Kupang High Court committed no error in applying the law and correctly considered that the lease relationship between the Plaintiffs and the Defendant was valid.
# Pursuant to Article 1579 of the Civil Code (BW), the lessor cannot terminate the lease by stating an intention to personally use the leased property unless such a right has been explicitly stipulated beforehand.
# The delay or failure of the lessee to pay rent constitutes grounds to demand the fulfillment of rent payment, but does not constitute grounds for the cancellation or termination of the lease agreement by operation of law.
# The Petitioner for Cassation's cassation objections regarding the evaluation of evidentiary facts cannot be considered at the cassation level (ex Law No. 1 of 1950 jo. Law No. 14 of 1970). Consequently, the Petitioner for Cassation's petition must be rejected.
* '''Ruling:''' Rejecting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation: [Party B]; Ordering the Petitioner for Cassation to pay cassation-level court costs amounting to Rp 20,000 (twenty thousand rupiahs). *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court on Wednesday, May 29, 1985, and pronounced in an open session on Saturday, June 15, 1985, by R. Harsadi Darsokusumo, S.H. [Presiding Judge], H. Amiroeddin Noer, S.H., and H. Masrani Basran, S.H. [Associate Justices]).*

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 27 K/AG/2002 dated February 26, 2004, establishes an important legal principle regarding the proof of land grants (*hibah*). The Supreme Court affirmed that anyone claiming rights over land based on a grant must be able to prove ownership of that grant pursuant to Article 210 paragraph (1) of the Compilation of Islamic Law (KHI). If land is acquired through a grant, the land title should be promptly transferred (*balik nama*) into the name of the grantee. If no title transfer takes place and a dispute subsequently arises, the legal status of the land remains unchanged (registered under the name of the grantor) unless a change in ownership status is conclusively proven.

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiff (Sahudin / Sanudin bin Taslim) filed a grant lawsuit at the Giri Menang Religious Court (Decision No. 76/Pdt.G/2000/PA.GM) against the Original Defendants ([Defendant I], [Defendant II], [Defendant III], and [Defendant IV]). The Plaintiff claimed ownership of an agricultural plot measuring approximately 17 *are* located in Subak Bali, Karang Petak Hamlet, East Pemenang Village, West Lombok, allegedly acquired via a grant from his uncle (Amaq Mali alias H. Abdul Hamid) approximately 40 years prior. Because the Plaintiff was illiterate and unsophisticated, the land title was never transferred and remained registered under Amaq Mali's name.

In 1999, the Defendants took over possession of the land. The Giri Menang Religious Court (Decision No. 76/Pdt.G/2000/PA.GM dated December 6, 2000) and the Mataram High Religious Court (Decision No. 24/Pdt.G/2000/PTA.Mtr dated July 9, 2001) granted the Plaintiff's claim in part and declared the grant legally valid. Dissatisfied with these rulings, the Defendants filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:''' Anyone who asserts a right to land based on a Grant must prove ownership of that Grant as intended by Article 210 paragraph (1) of the KHI, and if acquired via grant, the land title should immediately be transferred (*balik nama*) to the recipient. If this is not done and a dispute arises later, the land's status remains as it originally was unless a change in ownership status is definitively proven.
* The Plaintiff, as the party asserting rights to the land based on a grant from the late Amaq Mali alias H. [Defendant II's parent], failed to prove ownership of the grant under Article 210(1) of the KHI.
* If the late Amaq Mali had truly granted the land 40 years ago, the granted land should have been transferred into the Plaintiff's name. In reality, the land remains registered under Amaq Mali alias H. [Defendant II's parent] to this day.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from the Petitioners for Cassation ([Defendant I], [Defendant II], [Defendant III], and [Defendant IV]); Annulling the Mataram High Religious Court Decision No. 24/Pdt.G/2000/PTA.Mtr dated July 9, 2001, and the Giri Menang Religious Court Decision No. 76/Pdt.G/2000/PA.GM dated December 6, 2000; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Rejecting the Plaintiff's (Sahudin / Sanudin bin Taslim) lawsuit; (2) Ordering the Plaintiff to pay procedural costs across all levels of jurisdiction and in cassation amounting to Rp 200,000 (two hundred thousand rupiahs).

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Judicial Review Decision No. 27 PK/Pid/2003 establishes fundamental jurisprudence and legal standards regarding evidentiary standing in criminal charges of unfair competition (*cybersquatting* over domain names) and the limits of evidentiary admissibility. The Supreme Court affirmed that testimony regarding elements of deceiving the public or individuals whose statements were never directly heard before the trial court, but rather acquired secondhand from other witnesses receiving information or faxes, constitutes *Testimonium De Auditu* and consequently cannot be utilized as a valid legal instrument of proof.

== Case Background ==

The Defendant, [Defendant] (General Manager of International Marketing at PT Martina Bertho), was charged with registering the domain name Mustika-Ratu.Com via Network Solutions in the United States on October 7, 1999. This registration was accused of constituting unfair competition (Article 382 bis of the KUHP) and obstructing PT Mustika Ratu Tbk from conducting electronic commerce transactions with prospective overseas partners.

The Central Jakarta District Court (Decision No. 1075/PID.B/2001/PN.JKT.PST dated December 11, 2001) acquitted the Defendant of all charges (*vrijspraak*). However, at the cassation level (Decision No. 1082 K/Pid./2002 dated January 24, 2003), the Supreme Court overturned the district court ruling and sentenced the Defendant to 4 months of imprisonment under Article 382 bis of the KUHP. The Defendant subsequently filed a Petition for Judicial Review (*Peninjauan Kembali / PK*) on the grounds of manifest error by the cassation judges, who improperly relied on secondhand testimony from witnesses who heard rumors from prospective partners in Saudi Arabia and Malaysia (*testimonium de auditu*) alongside unverified fax evidence lacking original documentation.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The *judex facti* and cassation judgments committed an error in law within their legal reasoning by treating proof regarding the element of deceiving the public or an individual whose statement was never directly heard in court—where testimony was instead heard secondhand from others—as valid evidence. Such testimony must be categorized as *Testimonium De Auditu* and is therefore legally inadmissible as evidence.
# Fax communications originating from prospective partners in Saudi Arabia and Malaysia that were never presented as original documents, never confirmed through the Indonesian Embassy or Consulate General, and whose primary witnesses were never presented in court possess no valid probative value. Consequently, a manifest error/mistake (*kekhilafan/kekeliruan yang nyata* pursuant to Article 263 paragraph (2) letter c of the KUHAP) infected the prior cassation decision.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the Petition for Judicial Review from Petitioner for Judicial Review [Defendant]; Annulling the Supreme Court decision dated January 24, 2003, No. 1082 K/Pid./2002; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Declaring that the Convict is not legally and convincingly proven guilty of committing the criminal offense as charged by the Prosecutor / Public Prosecutor; (2) Acquitting the Convict of all charges; (3) Restoring the Convict's rights in capacity, position, honor, and dignity (rehabilitation); (4) Charging the procedural costs of the Judicial Review to the State.

|-
|Law No. 1 of 1974 on Marriage (Articles 39(2), 41); Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975 (Articles 19(f), 22); Compilation of Islamic Law (KHI) (Articles 116(f), 149, 152); Law No. 7 of 1989 on Religious Courts; Law No. 4 of 2004 on Judicial Power; Law No. 14 of 1985 jo. Law No. 5 of 2004 on the Supreme Court
|}

== Overview ==
Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 280 K/AG/2004 dated November 10, 2004, establishes very important Islamic civil jurisprudence regarding the consequences of divorce and the protection of children's future: "That when a divorce has occurred, the consequences of the divorce must be determined in accordance with minimum living requirements based on compliance and fairness, and to ensure certainty and the child's future, it is necessary to establish the husband's obligation to finance his children's maintenance." The Supreme Court annulled the Jakarta High Religious Court decision which had rejected the talak petition, granted permission to pronounce talak, and established obligations for mut'ah, iddah maintenance/maskah/kiswah amounting to Rp 25,000,000, and child maintenance of at least Rp 1,000,000 per month per child until the children reach the age of 21 (majority).

== Case Background ==
The Petitioner for Cassation / formerly Petitioner / Appellee (Abdullah [Father]) filed a petition for divorce talak against the Respondent for Cassation / formerly Respondent / Appellant ([Mother]) at the South Jakarta Religious Court. The Petitioner and Respondent were married on January 15, 1995 (recorded at PPN KUA Cilandak Sub-District) and blessed with 2 children: [Child A] (born [details removed]) and [Child B] (born [details removed]). Since October 2001, continuous disputes and quarrels arose triggered by differences of opinion and domestic incompatibility, leading them to separate beds and households for more than 1 year and 4 months.

The South Jakarta Religious Court (Decision No. 182/Pdt.G/2003/PA.JS dated June 11, 2003) granted the Petitioner's request, granted permission to pronounce *talak raj'i*, and ordered the Petitioner to pay iddah maintenance of Rp 20,000,000 and mut'ah in the form of a house at [address removed], South Jakarta, and a Caravelle car. However, the Jakarta High Religious Court (Decision No. 96/Pdt/2003/PTA.JK dated February 26, 2004) annulled the South Jakarta Religious Court judgment and rejected the Petitioner's request in its entirety. The Petitioner filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The Petitioner for Cassation's cassation objections are well-founded because the Petitioner and Respondent have lived separately in terms of house and bed for more than 1 year and 4 months due to continuous disputes, and reconciliation efforts through family members failed, meaning the household has irretrievably broken down (*broken marriage*) and satisfies the divorce grounds under Article 19 letter (f) jo. Article 22 paragraph (2) of Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975 jo. Article 39 paragraph (2) of Law No. 1 of 1974. The Jakarta High Religious Court's decision rejecting the talak petition must be annulled.
# The total value of maintenance, maskah, and kiswah during the iddah period determined by the *Judex Facti* is deemed insufficient to meet minimum living requirements, compliance, and fairness, prompting the Supreme Court to increase the amount to Rp 25,000,000 (twenty-five million rupiahs).
# Because both children remain under the custody (*hadhanah*) of the Respondent, to ensure certainty and the children's future, it is necessary to establish the husband's obligation to finance the children's maintenance of at least Rp 1,000,000 per month for each child until they reach the age of 21 (majority).

* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation: ABDULLAH [Father]; Annulling the Jakarta High Religious Court decision dated February 26, 2004, No. 96/Pdt/2003/PTA.JK; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Granting the Petitioner's request in its entirety; (2) Granting permission to the Petitioner (ABDULLAH [Father]) to pronounce a single *talak raj'i* against the Respondent ([Mother]) before the session of the South Jakarta Religious Court; (3) Ordering the Petitioner to pay to the Respondent: (a) Mut'ah in the form of a house located at [address removed], South Cipete Village, Cilandak Sub-District, South Jakarta; (b) Maintenance (*Nafkah, Kiswah, and Maskah*) during the iddah period amounting to Rp 25,000,000 (twenty-five million rupiahs); (c) Maintenance for 2 (two) children of at least Rp 1,000,000 (one million rupiahs) each per month from the time the Petitioner pronounces talak until the children reach the age of 21 (majority); (4) Directing the Registrar of the South Jakarta Religious Court to send a copy of the talak pronunciation determination to the Marriage Registration Official; (5) Rejecting the Petitioner's requests for anything further and otherwise; (6) Ordering the Petitioner to pay court costs across first instance, appellate, and cassation levels (cassation costs assessed at Rp 500,000). *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court on Wednesday, November 10, 2004, by the Cassation Panel of Justices: Drs. H. Andi Syamsu Alam, S.H., M.H. [Presiding Judge], Drs. H. Hamdan, S.H., M.H., and Drs. H. Abdul Manan, S.H., S.I.P., M.Hum. [Associate Justices]).*

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 283 K/TUN/1998 dated December 14, 2000, establishes very fundamental labor and state administrative jurisprudence: Pursuant to Article 116 of Government Regulation No. 30 of 1990, foundations operating in the field of higher education act as an extension of the government to carry out governmental affairs in the field of education. Consequently, the Committees for Labor Dispute Settlement (P4P/P4D) lack the authority to resolve disputes between lecturers and foundations operating in higher education, as such disputes do not constitute industrial relations but rather fall within the domain of educational relations.

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation (Yayasan Perguruan Dharma Agung / Institut Sains dan Teknologi TD. Pardede, represented by Chairperson Ny. [Plaintiff]. Siregar br. Pardede) filed a lawsuit against the Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation (Central Committee for Labor Dispute Settlement / P4-Pusat) at the Jakarta State Administrative High Court (No. 09/G/1997/PT.TUN.JKT). The object of the dispute consisted of the Decree of P4-Pusat No. 845/787/77-14/II/PHK/9-1996 dated September 30, 1996 (Letter No. TAR.951/M/KP4P/19 dated October 31, 1996) concerning the Termination of Employment (*PHK*) dispute between the Plaintiff and Prof. DR. J.A. Napitupulu, Msc. et al. (6 lecturers).

P4-Pusat altered the decision of the North Sumatra P4-Regional Committee No. 148/105-08/W2/PHK-VI/96 dated June 27, 1996, by declaring that the employment relationship of the lecturers was never terminated, while ordering the Employer (Foundation) to pay wages, holiday allowances (*THR*), and processing wages. The Plaintiff filed a state administrative lawsuit arguing that P4P/P4D lacked the authority to adjudicate disputes involving private higher education lecturers because the lecturers' legal relationship is governed by Government Regulation No. 30 of 1990 and pure civil status/transfer agreements. The Jakarta State Administrative High Court (Decision No. 09/G/1997/PT.TUN.JKT dated February 19, 1998) rejected the Plaintiff's lawsuit in its entirety. Dissatisfied with the Jakarta State Administrative High Court ruling, Yayasan Perguruan Dharma Agung filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The Jakarta State Administrative High Court committed an error in applying the law. The Plaintiff is a foundation operating in the field of higher education, which serves as an extension of the government to administer governmental affairs in education pursuant to Article 116 of Government Regulation No. 30 of 1990.
# Lecturers working at such foundations are educational staff specifically appointed for teaching duties within the higher education institutions under the foundation (ex Article 1 points 2, 3 jo. Article 29 paragraph (3) sub 1 of Gov. Reg. No. 30 of 1990).
# From these provisions, it is clear that the relationship between the Plaintiff and the workers (Prof. Dr. J.A. Napitupulu, Msc. et al.) does not constitute an industrial relations relationship, but rather an educational relationship between lecturers and universities within the Plaintiff's working environment.
# Disputes between the Plaintiff and the lecturers / Rector of Dharma Agung University do not fall within the authority of the Central Committee for Labor Dispute Settlement (Defendant) to resolve.
# The issuance of the disputed decree by the Defendant satisfies the legal defect criteria under Article 53 paragraph (2)(a) of Law No. 5 of 1986 because it was issued outside of official authority (*ultra vires*), and therefore must be declared null and void by operation of law.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation YAYASAN PERGURUAN DHARMA AGUNG (INSTITUT SAINS DAN TEKNOLOGI TD. PARDEDE); Annulling the Jakarta State Administrative High Court decision dated February 19, 1998, No. 09/G/1997/PT.TUN.JKT; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Declaring that the Defendant lacks the authority to resolve this case (Government Regulation No. 30 of 1990); (2) Declaring null and void by operation of law the Decree of the Defendant Number TAR.951/M/KP4P/19; (3) Ordering the Respondent for Cassation to pay all court costs across first instance, appellate, and cassation levels (assessed at Rp 100,000 at the cassation level). *(Decided in tabular deliberation of the Supreme Court on Thursday, November 30, 2000, and pronounced in an open session on Thursday, December 14, 2000, by H. German Hoediarto, SH. [Junior Chairman of the Supreme Court / Presiding Judge], Mangatas Nasution, SH., and Ny. Hj. Emin Aminah Achadiat, SH. [Associate Justices]).*

== Overview ==
Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 285 K/AG/2000 dated November 10, 2000, establishes important Islamic civil jurisprudence in wife-initiated divorce proceedings: "That due to continuous disputes that can no longer be reconciled, and living apart under different roofs due to the lack of approval from the families of both parties, the pronunciation of a divorce / *talak* (*talak satu ba'in sughra*) is permitted." The Supreme Court annulled the Medan High Religious Court decision which had rejected the Plaintiff's divorce lawsuit, and independently adjudicated by granting a single *ba'in sughra* divorce and ordering the Defendant to settle the unpaid dowry (*mahar*) debt owed to the Plaintiff.

== Case Background ==
The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation ([Party B]) and the Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation ([Party A]) were spouses married on September 1, 1998, registered at the Office of Religious Affairs (*KUA*) of Bandar Pasir Mandoge Sub-District, Asahan Regency (No. 078/02/IX/1998). From the marriage, they were blessed with a child named [Child].

The marital relationship between the Plaintiff and Defendant became discordant because from the beginning of the marriage it lacked the approval of both families. The Defendant never provided a proper residence, refused to work to earn a living, and all living expenses were borne by the Defendant's parents. Furthermore, the Defendant remained indebted for the dowry (*mahar* / *mas kawin*) amounting to Rp 500,000, which had not been paid to the Plaintiff. The Plaintiff and Defendant had lived separately under different roofs since March 1999, and family reconciliation efforts proved unsuccessful.

The Medan Religious Court (Decision No. 294/Pdt.G/1999/PA.Mdn. dated September 30, 1999) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part, pronounced a single *ba'in sughra* divorce, and ordered the Defendant to pay the dowry debt of Rp 500,000. However, the Medan High Religious Court (Decision No. 91/Pdt.G/1999/PTA.Mdn. dated December 15, 1999) annulled the Medan Religious Court judgment and dismissed the Plaintiff's lawsuit in its entirety, deeming that the household was not yet irretrievably broken (*broken marriage*). The Plaintiff filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The Medan High Religious Court insufficiently considered all facts occurring within the Plaintiff's and Defendant's household.
# Facts revealed at trial proved: (a) The marriage between the Plaintiff and Defendant lacked approval from the Plaintiff's family; (b) The Plaintiff and Defendant had lived in separate homes since March 1999; (c) The Plaintiff's parents attempted to reconcile the Plaintiff and Defendant but failed, making the household extremely difficult to maintain.
# Due to continuous disputes that could no longer be reconciled and living apart under different roofs resulting from the lack of approval by the families of both parties, sufficient grounds existed to grant the divorce lawsuit with the pronouncement of a single *ba'in sughra* divorce.
# It was proven that the Defendant had not paid the dowry (*mahar* / *mas kawin*) debt amounting to Rp 500,000 recorded in the marriage certificate, rendering it mandatory under the law for the Defendant to settle such dowry debt to the Plaintiff.

* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation [Party B]; Annulling the Medan High Religious Court decision dated December 15, 1999 AD, No. 91/Pdt.G/1999/PTA.Mdn.; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part; (2) Pronouncing a single *ba'in sughra* divorce of Defendant ([Party A]) against Plaintiff ([Party B]); (3) Ordering the Defendant to pay to the Plaintiff the unpaid dowry (*mahar*) amounting to Rp 500,000 (five hundred thousand rupiahs); (4) Declaring the remainder of the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible; (5) Ordering the Plaintiff to pay first-instance court costs amounting to Rp 161,500; (6) Ordering the Appellant to pay appellate-level court costs amounting to Rp 68,000; and assessing cassation-level court costs against the Petitioner for Cassation amounting to Rp 100,000. *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court on Friday, November 10, 2000, and pronounced in an open session on Wednesday, November 29, 2000, by the Cassation Panel of Justices: Drs. H. Taufiq, S.H. [Junior Chairman of the Supreme Court / Session Chairman], Drs. H. Syamsuhadi Irsyad, S.H., M.Hum., and Drs. H. Andi Syamsul Alam, S.H. [Associate Justices]).*

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:2916K PDT 1984
wikitext:
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 2916 K/Pdt/1984''' (dated July 30, 1986 / deliberation on July 3, 1986) is a fundamental Indonesian contract and property law jurisprudence precedent establishing the validity of agreements granting occupancy rights (''woningrecht'') over hire-purchase (''huurkoop'') housing to divorced wives maintaining widowhood status, along with the legal consequences thereof pursuant to Articles 1338 and 1320 of the Civil Code.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established two primary legal principles:

# '''Validity of House Occupancy Agreements for Divorced Wives in Widowhood:''' A written agreement (Exhibit P.1 / P.II) dated January 6, 1982, executed and signed by the Defendant (former husband: Drs. [Party C]) on the date of their divorce, granting the Plaintiff (former wife: [Party A]) and their biological child the right to occupy/inhabit the disputed house for as long as the Plaintiff remains unmarried (''janda''), is '''Valid and Binding as Law Between the Parties''' ''ex'' Article 1338 ''jo.'' Article 1320 of the Civil Code.
# '''Compatibility of Occupancy Transfers with Hire-Purchase (''Huurkoop'') Principles:''' Transferring house occupancy rights from the Defendant to the Plaintiff does not constitute a transfer of ownership (''eigendom'') over the house, nor does it violate hire-purchase (''huurkoop'') regulations. Although occupancy rights are transferred to the former wife, the legal obligation to remit monthly installment payments to the developer/bank (BTN) remains entirely with the Defendant (former husband) since the home legally remains the property of the Defendant.

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation ([Party A]), annulled Banda Aceh High Court Decision No. 38/Perd./1984/PT.BNA dated April 26, 1984, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by partially granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit, declaring the agreement dated January 6, 1982 valid, and ordering the Defendant to vacate the disputed house (Simple Housing Complex No. 66 Lingke, Banda Aceh) and surrender it to the Plaintiff to be inhabited with her child during her widowhood.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Application of the Principle of ''Pacta Sunt Servanda'' (Article 1338 ''jo.'' Article 1320 of the Civil Code) to Post-Divorce Housing Agreements ===
''Does a written agreement executed by a former husband granting house occupancy rights to his divorced wife during her widowhood possess binding legal force and immunity against unilateral revocation?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Valid and Binding.''' A written agreement executed voluntarily before witnesses upon divorce satisfies the validity requirements of agreements under Article 1320 of the Civil Code. Pursuant to Article 1338 of the Civil Code, such agreement serves as law between the parties (''pacta sunt servanda''), prohibiting the former husband from unilaterally revoking or repudiating the agreement.

=== 2. Legal Distinction Between Occupancy Rights (''Woningrecht'' / ''Usus'') and Ownership (''Eigendom'') in Hire-Purchase Schemes (''Huurkoop'') ===
''Does transferring occupancy rights over a hire-purchase house from a hire-purchaser (''huurkoper'') to a third party (former wife) violate prohibitions against title transfer in developer/BTN hire-purchase agreements?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Does Not Violate.''' Transferring occupancy rights (''woningrecht'') confers merely a right of use and enjoyment, not a transfer of ownership (''eigendom''). Consequently, a former husband's promise permitting his former wife and child to occupy the residence does not conflict with hire-purchase law (''huurkoop''). Ownership title remains with the former husband, and the obligation to service mortgage/installment payments to the creditor/bank remains firmly upon him.

=== 3. Application of Transitional Cassation Procedure Rules (Law No. 1 of 1950 ''vs.'' Law No. 14 of 1985) ===
When appellate notification and cassation filings occurred prior to the enactment of Law No. 14 of 1985, the governing time limits and procedures applied are those prescribed under Law No. 1 of 1950.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Banda Aceh High Court (Decision No. 38/Perd./1984/PT.BNA) err in applying contract and property law (''foutieve toepassing van het perikatan- en zakenrecht'') by declaring the Written Agreement dated January 6, 1982 invalid solely because the disputed house remained under an uncompleted hire-purchase arrangement with BTN/PT Mestika?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. Banda Aceh High Court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court granted the Plaintiff's cassation petition ([Party A]), annulled Banda Aceh High Court Decision No. 38/Perd./1984/PT.BNA, and independently adjudicated by declaring the Written Agreement dated January 6, 1982 '''Valid and Binding''', while ordering the Defendant to surrender the disputed residence in good condition for the Plaintiff and her child to inhabit during her widowhood.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Banda Aceh District Court & Banda Aceh High Court) ===
Examination of facts regarding marriage on August 6, 1963, and divorce on January 6, 1982; execution of the written agreement dated January 6, 1982 before witnesses; location and boundaries of the disputed house at Simple Housing Complex No. 66 Lingke, Banda Aceh (East: Alley III, West: Drs. Idrus, North: Ir. Hasan Suud, South: Hasbi Yacob, S.H.); hire-purchase status with PT Meusara Agung / PT Mestika / BTN over a 15-year period (1979–1994); and testimonies of witnesses ([Party B], Sarbini Bidin, Suryadi).

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===

* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata / BW):'''
** Article 1320 BW: Validity Requirements of Agreements (Consent, Capacity, Specific Object, Lawful Cause).
** Article 1338 BW: Principle of ''Pacta Sunt Servanda'' (Valid Agreements Serve as Law).
* '''Hire-Purchase Doctrine (''Huurkoop''):''' Mixed Contract Law of Lease and Purchase.
* '''Law No. 1 of 1950 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation and Independent Adjudication Authority.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===

* '''Doctrine of Post-Divorce Housing Protection for Former Wives and Children:''' Post-divorce settlement agreements guaranteeing housing for former wives in widowhood and biological children possess complete legal force and judicial protection.
* '''Doctrine of Occupancy Rights Independence from Hire-Purchase Status:''' Promising house occupancy rights to third parties requires no land/building title transfer, and thus requires no hire-purchase creditor consent provided installments continue to be serviced by the primary debtor.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* The Written Agreement dated January 6, 1982 (Exhibit P.1 / P.II) is '''PROVEN VALID, SATISFIES ARTICLE 1320 BW, AND BINDS THE DEFENDANT''' ''ex'' Article 1338 BW.
* The Defendant (Drs. [Party C]) is proven to have breached the agreement (default) by barring the Plaintiff from occupying the disputed house.
* The Plaintiff ([Party A]) is legally entitled to occupy/inhabit the disputed house with her child during her widowhood.
* The Defendant is ordered to vacate the disputed house and surrender it to the Plaintiff.
* The Defendant retains the ongoing obligation to pay hire-purchase mortgage installments to the developer/BTN.
* Banda Aceh High Court Decision No. 38/Perd./1984/PT.BNA is '''NULL AND VOID'''.

=== Dismissed Arguments ===

* The Defendant's argument that the agreement was invalid because the house remained under hire-purchase status was '''REJECTED IN LAW AND ANNULLED BY THE SUPREME COURT'''.
* The Plaintiff's prayer seeking full ownership rights (''hak milik'') over the residence was '''DISMISSED''' (awarded occupancy rights during widowhood only).

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Legal Certainty in Protecting Former Wives' and Children's Housing Rights Through Divorce Settlements:''' This landmark ruling establishes an exceptionally humane and robust legal precedent in Indonesia: courts protect the written commitments of former husbands who promise housing to former wives and children post-divorce. Former husbands cannot exploit administrative loopholes (such as uncompleted mortgage/hire-purchase statuses) to evict former wives and children from promised homes.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==

; Is an agreement between a former husband and wife granting house occupancy rights to a divorced wife during widowhood valid pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence?
: '''Valid and Binding Under Article 1338 of the Civil Code.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. No. 2916 K/Pdt/1984:
:* A written agreement executed by a former husband granting house occupancy rights to his former wife and child during widowhood is '''VALID AND BINDING AS LAW BETWEEN THE PARTIES''' ''ex'' Article 1338 ''jo.'' Article 1320 of the Civil Code.
:* Transferring hire-purchase (''huurkoop'') occupancy rights does not violate hire-purchase law because ownership (''eigendom'') of the home is not transferred.
:* The obligation to service mortgage installments to the bank/developer remains with the former husband, while the former wife is legally entitled to vacate and inhabit the residence during her widowhood.
