|Law No. 21 of 1961 on Trademarks (Articles 2(1), 10(1),(2)); Paris Convention (Articles 2, 6bis); Commercial Code (KUHD); Law No. 14 of 1970 on Judicial Power; Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court
|}

== Overview ==
Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 294 K/Pdt/1989 dated August 28, 1990 (pronounced on October 17, 1990), establishes two fundamental civil and commercial jurisprudence principles regarding trademark law:

* **Procedure for Alleging Bad Faith in Trademark Registration:** The existence of bad faith on the part of the registrant must be declared in a separate lawsuit concerning unfair competition (*oneerlijke concurrentie*) or an unlawful act (*onrechtmatige daad*), and cannot be simultaneously declared within a decision granting a petition for trademark registration cancellation (ex Article 10 paragraph (2) of Law No. 21 of 1961).
* **Scope of Trademark Protection Limited to Similar Goods:** Pursuant to Article 2 paragraph (1) of Law No. 21 of 1961, exclusive rights over a trademark apply and protect only the use of goods that are similar (*sejenis*) to the goods bearing such trademark. A registered cosmetics trademark cannot serve to cancel the registration of an identical word mark for dissimilar categories of goods (such as tobacco, cigarettes, food, and beverages).

== Case Background ==
The Original Petitioner / Respondent for Cassation (Chanel, Societe Anonyme, Neuilly/Seine, France) is the owner of the famous trademark "Chanel" registered in Indonesia under No. 133.821 on January 27, 1979, protecting goods in Class 3 (cosmetics/perfumery). However, the Original Respondent I / Petitioner for Cassation (Perseroan N.V. Sumatra Tobacco Trading Company, Pematang Siantar) registered the word mark "CHANEL" under No. 197.890 on September 13, 1985, to protect tobacco products, cigarettes, cigars, pipes, beverages, biscuits, and other food substances.

Chanel, Societe Anonyme filed a petition for the cancellation of trademark registration No. 197.890 at the Central Jakarta District Court (Case No. 323/Pdt/G.D/1988/PN.Jkt.Pst.) on the grounds of bad faith aimed at exploiting the fame of the "Chanel" mark. The Central Jakarta District Court (Decision dated October 31, 1988, No. 323/Pdt/G.D/1988/PN.Jkt.Pst.) granted Chanel's petition in its entirety, recognized Chanel as the first user, annulled the trademark registration in the name of N.V. Sumatra Tobacco Trading Company, and declared the existence of bad faith. Dissatisfied with the Central Jakarta District Court ruling, N.V. Sumatra Tobacco Trading Company filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* **Ratio Decidendi:**

# The cassation objections raised by the Petitioner for Cassation (N.V. Sumatra Tobacco Trading Company) are well-founded because the Central Jakarta District Court erred in applying the law, specifically misinterpreting the provisions of Article 10 paragraph (2) of Law No. 21 of 1961 on Trademarks.
# The District Court erred in granting the trademark cancellation petition while simultaneously declaring that Respondent I acted in bad faith, whereas such bad faith must first be established in a separate lawsuit or judgment regarding unfair competition (*oneerlijke concurrentie*) or an unlawful act (*onrechtmatige daad*) committed by Respondent I (as formulated in Supreme Court Decisions No. 3146 K/Pdt/1983 and No. 2932 K/Sip/1982).
# Pursuant to Article 2 paragraph (1) of Law No. 21 of 1961, exclusive trademark rights do not extend to all categories of goods, but apply strictly to categories of goods similar (*sejenis*) to the goods bearing the mark. The Petitioner for Cassation's trademark registration (tobacco, cigarettes, beverages, biscuits) does not overlap with or infringe upon the Respondent for Cassation's goods (Class 3 cosmetics).
# National trademark legislation (Law No. 21 of 1961) takes precedence over the Paris Convention, and national law does not recognize discrimination while limiting protection strictly to similar goods. Consequently, the cancellation petition filed by Chanel, Societe Anonyme must be declared inadmissible (*niet ontvankelijke verklaard*).

* **Ruling:** Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation: Perseroan N.V. SUMATRA TOBACCO TRADING COMPANY; Annulling the Central Jakarta District Court decision dated October 31, 1988, No. 323/Pdt/G.D./1988/PN.Jkt.Pst.; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Declaring the petition of the Petitioner (Chanel, Societe Anonyme) inadmissible; (2) Ordering the Respondent for Cassation / Original Petitioner to pay all court costs across first instance and cassation levels (cassation costs assessed at Rp 20,000). *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court on Tuesday, August 28, 1990, and pronounced in an open session on Wednesday, October 17, 1990, by Samsoeddin Aboebakar, S.H. [Presiding Judge], H. Roesli, S.H., and Gunawan, S.H. [Associate Justices]).*

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:2981K PDT 1984
wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 2981 K/Pdt/1984}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 2981 K/Pdt/1984''' (dated July 22, 1985 / deliberation on June 5, 1985) is a fundamental trademark law and civil procedure jurisprudence precedent establishing vital rules regarding the formal ripeness of trademark registration cancellation lawsuits pursuant to Law No. 21 of 1961 on Trademarks.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established a primary legal principle:

* '''Unpublished Trademarks in the State Gazette Supplement Do Not Constitute Trademark Actions:''' A lawsuit seeking the cancellation of a trademark registration filed before a District Court regarding a trademark registered with the Directorate of Patents and Copyrights, but not yet published in the Supplement to the Official Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia (''Tambahan Berita Negara Republik Indonesia'' / TBN RI), does '''not constitute a trademark action''' pursuant to Article 10 paragraph (1) of Law No. 21 of 1961.

Because the trademark "Ratu Ayu" had been registered under No. 167258 but lacked official publication in the State Gazette Supplement, the lawsuit was premature and formally defective, mandating dismissal as '''Inadmissible''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation (Ny. Dra. Martha Tilaar), annulled Central Jakarta District Court Decision No. 048/1984 G. dated July 25, 1984, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by declaring the Plaintiff's (PT Rama Pharmaceutical Industry) lawsuit '''Inadmissible''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Formal Ripeness Requirements for Trademark Cancellation Lawsuits (''Ripeness of Action'' ''ex'' Article 10 paragraph 1 of Law No. 21 of 1961) ===
''Does a district court possess jurisdiction to receive and adjudicate third-party trademark registration cancellation lawsuits concerning marks registered at the Patent Directorate but not yet published in the Supplement to the Official Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia (TBN RI)?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: No Jurisdiction / Premature Lawsuit.'''

Pursuant to consistent Supreme Court jurisprudence concerning Article 10 paragraph (1) of Law No. 21 of 1961, official publication in the Supplement to the Official Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia (TBN RI) constitutes a mandatory formal prerequisite (''conditio sine qua non'') for a trademark registration to be validly classified as a "trademark action" subject to judicial cancellation. Prior to publication in the State Gazette Supplement, registration remains publicly unperfected, rendering cancellation lawsuits premature and mandating dismissal as '''Inadmissible''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

=== 2. Scope of Cassation Admissibility Review ''Ex Officio'' ===
The Supreme Court possesses authority ''ex officio'' to annul district court decisions based on independent legal grounds (regardless of formal cassation objections raised by the Petitioner) upon discovering that the district court entertained a legally defective or premature lawsuit.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (''Judex Juris'' / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Central Jakarta District Court (Decision No. 048/1984 G.) err in applying procedural and trademark law (''error in iudicando'') by accepting, examining the merits of, and granting the cancellation lawsuit against trademark "Ratu Ayu" No. 167258, whereas said trademark registration had not been published in the State Gazette Supplement?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. Central Jakarta District Court misapplied the law. Trademark cancellation lawsuits concerning marks unpublished in the State Gazette Supplement are immature (premature) and do not constitute trademark actions ''ex'' Article 10(1) of Law No. 21 of 1961. The Supreme Court granted Dra. Martha Tilaar's cassation petition, annulled the District Court decision, and independently adjudicated by declaring the Plaintiff's (PT Rama Pharmaceutical Industry) lawsuit Inadmissible (NO).

=== Question of Fact (''Judex Facti'' / Central Jakarta District Court) ===
Examination of facts regarding registration of trademark "Ratu Ayu" No. 167258 on October 13, 1982, in the name of Ny. Dra. Martha Tilaar; cosmetics production permits from the Minister of Health No. 220/Menkes/Per/IX/76 dated June 5, 1981, and Directorate General of POM registration in 1982 in the name of PT Rama Pharmaceutical Industry; examination of trademark label evidence ("Ratu Ayu" ''vs.'' "Ratu Ayu Solo"); and verification of the non-issuance of publication for registration No. 167258 in the State Gazette Supplement.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''Law No. 21 of 1961 on Trademarks:'''
** Article 2 paragraph (2) (Declaratory System).
** Article 10 paragraph (1) (Registered Trademark Cancellation Lawsuits).
** Article 18 paragraph (1) letter b (Extinction of Trademark Registration Force).
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 13 of 1965 ''jo.'' Law No. 1 of 1950 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation and Independent Adjudication Authority.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* Doctrine of Trademark Ripeness (''Ripeness Doctrine in Trademark Law''): Trademark registrations become binding and litigable for cancellation before civil courts only when all administrative registration stages—including public publication in the Official Gazette / State Gazette Supplement—have been executed by the trademark registration authority.
* Established Jurisprudence on State Gazette Supplement Requirements: Supreme Court Decision No. 2981 K/Pdt/1984 serves as a landmark precedent under the regime of Law No. 21/1961 establishing that State Gazette Supplement publication is mandatory for trademark cancellation actions.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* Trademark Registration No. 167258 ("Ratu Ayu") in the name of Ny. Dra. Martha Tilaar '''HAS NOT BEEN PUBLISHED''' in the Supplement to the Official Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia (TBN RI).
* The trademark registration cancellation lawsuit filed by the Plaintiff is '''PREMATURE AND FORMALLY DEFECTIVE''' ''ex'' Article 10 paragraph (1) of Law No. 21 of 1961.
* Central Jakarta District Court Decision No. 048/1984 G. dated July 25, 1984, is '''NULL AND VOID'''.
* The Plaintiff's (PT Rama Pharmaceutical Industry) lawsuit is declared '''INADMISSIBLE''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

=== Dismissed / Unconsidered Arguments ===
* The substantive question of who qualifies as the first user (''first user'') entitled to the "Ratu Ayu" trademark and whether confusing similarity existed '''WAS NOT CONSIDERED BY THE SUPREME COURT''', as the lawsuit lapsed upon formal admissibility testing.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Importance of Rigorous Admissibility Checks Prior to Substantive IP Examination:''' This landmark ruling emphasizes the necessity of judicial discipline in testing formal lawsuit conditions (''admissibility check''). In intellectual property disputes, judges must not prematurely rush into investigating substantive unfair competition or confusing similarity before verifying that the disputed object has satisfied all statutory publication formalities.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
; Can a registered trademark cancellation lawsuit be entertained by a court if the mark has not been published in the State Gazette Supplement (TBN RI)?
: '''Inadmissible (NO).''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. No. 2981 K/Pdt/1984:
* Trademarks registered at the Directorate of Patents and Copyrights that remain unpublished in the State Gazette Supplement (TBN RI) do not qualify as "trademark actions" pursuant to Article 10 paragraph (1) of Law No. 21 of 1961.
* Trademark cancellation lawsuits filed prior to official State Gazette Supplement publication are categorized as premature and formally defective.
* The Supreme Court annulled the Central Jakarta District Court decision and independently adjudicated by declaring the Plaintiff's lawsuit Inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 2985 K/Pdt/2001}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 2985 K/Pdt/2001''' (dated January 29, 2004) is a fundamental civil procedure jurisprudence precedent establishing crucial rules concerning the formal validity of a Defendant's legal standing (''persona standi in judicio'') and formal procedural defects (''error in persona'') resulting from filing lawsuits against committees or institutions that have already been dissolved.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established a primary legal principle:

* '''Lawsuits Against Dissolved Entities Are Formally Defective (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO):''' "A lawsuit shall be declared inadmissible when, at the time the lawsuit is filed, the sued subject has already been dissolved beforehand."

Where plaintiffs file a civil lawsuit naming ad-hoc committees or bodies (such as the Regional Election Committee II / PPD II and the Election Supervisory Committee / PANWASLU of Bolaang Mongondow Regency) as Defendants, even though these committees were officially dissolved by law prior to the registration of the lawsuit at the District Court (dissolved on September 14, 1999, whereas the lawsuit was registered on September 27, 1999), the lawsuit suffers from a fatal defect regarding the legal subject and must be declared '''Inadmissible''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioners for Cassation (DPC PSII, DPD PAN, and DPD Partai Golkar of Bolaang Mongondow Regency), annulled Manado High Court Decision No. 173/Pdt/2000/PT.Mdo dated November 20, 2000, ''jo.'' Kotamobagu District Court Decision No. 42/Pdt.G/1999/PN.Ktg dated May 22, 2000, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by declaring the Plaintiffs' lawsuit '''Inadmissible''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Formal Validity Requirements for Defendant's Legal Standing (''Legitima Persona Standi in Judicio'' ''ex'' ''Error in Persona'') ===
''Can a civil lawsuit be entertained by a court when the legal subject or ad-hoc body arrayed as a Defendant has been officially dissolved by law prior to the registration of the statement of claim at the District Court Registry?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Inadmissible / Formally Defective.'''

A Defendant legal subject must possess valid juridical existence (''persona standi in judicio'') at the exact time a lawsuit is registered. Arraying a defunct or non-existent entity—such as an ad-hoc committee already dissolved—inflicts the lawsuit with a formal procedural defect known as ''error in persona'' (wrong subject / fictitious defendant). Consequently, courts are mandated to declare the lawsuit '''Inadmissible''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO) without examining the substantive merits.

=== 2. Duty of Judex Facti to Verify Legal Subject Existence Prior to Substantive Adjudication ===
District and High Courts that ignore exceptions regarding the dissolution of Defendant institutions and proceed to adjudicate the substantive merits commit an error in applying civil procedure law (''error in iudicando'').

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' (Kotamobagu District Court Decision No. 42/Pdt.G/1999/PN.Ktg ''jo.'' Manado High Court Decision No. 173/Pdt/2000/PT.Mdo) err in applying civil procedure law (''foutieve toepassing van het procesrecht'') by granting the Plaintiffs' lawsuit, whereas Defendant V (KPU/PPD II Bolaang Mongondow) and Defendant VII (PANWASLU Bolaang Mongondow) had been officially dissolved on September 14, 1999—prior to the registration of the lawsuit on September 27, 1999?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. The ''Judex Facti'' misapplied the law. Lawsuits filed against dissolved legal subjects are formally defective. The Supreme Court granted the Petitioners' cassation petition, annulled the Manado High Court ''jo.'' Kotamobagu District Court decisions, and independently adjudicated by declaring the Plaintiffs' lawsuit Inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Kotamobagu District Court & Manado High Court) ===
Verification of the dissolution date of PPD II Bolaang Mongondow under North Sulawesi PPD I Decree No. 44 of 1999 dated September 14, 1999; verification of the registration date of the Plaintiffs' statement of claim at Kotamobagu District Court on September 27, 1999; examination of PPD II Bolaang Mongondow Plenary Session minutes dated July 19, 1999 No. 310/PPD II-BM/VII/1999; and the allocation of the remaining 7 DPRD II Bolaang Mongondow seats from the 1999 General Election.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''HIR / RBg:''' Provisions concerning Formal Lawsuit Requirements & Legal Subject Exceptions (''Error in Persona'' / Non-Existent Defendant).
* '''Law No. 3 of 1999 on General Elections:''' Provisions governing the structure and operational lifespan of election organizing bodies (KPU, PPI, PPD, Panwaslu).
* '''Law No. 14 of 1985 ''jo.'' Law No. 5 of 2004 ''jo.'' Law No. 3 of 2009 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation Authority and Independent Adjudication Powers.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* '''Doctrine of ''Persona Standi in Judicio'':''' Judicial standing requires Defendants to retain active legal capacity at the time a lawsuit is filed. Ad-hoc bodies whose operational terms have expired and which have been officially dissolved lack ''persona standi in judicio''.
* '''Established Precedent on Dissolved Legal Subjects:''' Supreme Court Decision No. 2985 K/Pdt/2001 represents a landmark precedent establishing that lawsuits filed against bodies, organizations, or committees dissolved prior to suit registration must be declared Inadmissible (NO).

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* Defendant V (PPD II Bolaang Mongondow) and Defendant VII (PANWASLU Bolaang Mongondow) are '''PROVEN TO HAVE BEEN OFFICIALLY DISSOLVED PRIOR TO LAWSUIT REGISTRATION''' (dissolved on September 14, 1999; lawsuit registered on September 27, 1999).
* The Plaintiffs' lawsuit contains a '''FORMAL LEGAL SUBJECT DEFECT''' (''Error in Persona'').
* Manado High Court Decision No. 173/Pdt/2000/PT.Mdo and Kotamobagu District Court Decision No. 42/Pdt.G/1999/PN.Ktg are '''NULL AND VOID'''.
* The Plaintiffs' (DPC PNU & DPD PKB) lawsuit is declared '''INADMISSIBLE''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

=== Dismissed / Unconsidered Arguments ===
* The substantive validity of the local ''Stembus Accord'' and disputes concerning the allocation of the remaining 7 DPRD II seats '''WERE NOT CONSIDERED BY THE SUPREME COURT''', as the lawsuit lapsed upon formal legal-subject testing.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Importance of Rigorous Defendant Designation Diligence Involving Ad-Hoc Bodies:''' This landmark ruling establishes crucial procedural certainty in Indonesia: plaintiffs must meticulously verify the juridical existence status of entities designated as Defendants. Where disputes involve ad-hoc committees (such as election committees, procurement boards, or independent task forces) that have been dissolved, plaintiffs must not sue the defunct committee, but rather direct claims to the establishing legal entity or the definitive legal subject assuming its statutory responsibilities.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
; Can a civil lawsuit be entertained if the legal subject or institution sued has been dissolved prior to the registration of the lawsuit at the District Court?
: '''Inadmissible (NO).''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. No. 2985 K/Pdt/2001:
:* A lawsuit shall be declared inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO) if, at the time the lawsuit is filed, the legal subject or institution sued has already been dissolved beforehand.
:* Arraying an ad-hoc body or committee (such as PPD II or Panwaslu) officially dissolved prior to the lawsuit registration date constitutes a formal ''error in persona'' defect.
:* The Supreme Court annulled the High Court and District Court decisions and independently adjudicated by declaring the Plaintiffs' lawsuit Inadmissible (NO).

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Judicial Review Decision No. 29 PK/TUN/2001 dated July 31, 2003, establishes an important legal principle regarding the principles of proportionality and justice in imposing disciplinary sanctions upon Civil Servants (*PNS*). The Supreme Court affirmed that imposing the sanction of honorable dismissal not at one's own request (*pemberhentian dengan hormat tidak atas permintaan sendiri*) for disciplinary violations under Article 4a of Government Regulation No. 30 of 1980 is excessively severe, unjust, and contrary to procedural/formal law. A more appropriate and proportional form of sanction for such a violation is a disciplinary penalty consisting of a demotion in rank by one level for a maximum duration of 1 (one) year.

== Case Background ==

The Petitioner for Judicial Review / Plaintiff (Dra. [Plaintiff], Junior Administrative Officer / Rank III/a Employee of the Ministry of Finance of the RI) was subjected to disciplinary punishment in the form of honorable dismissal not at her own request pursuant to the Decree of the Minister of Finance No. 504/KMK.01/UP.7/1996, which was subsequently upheld by the Civil Service Advisory Board (*BAPEK*) Decree No. 174/KPTS/BAPEK/1997 dated November 25, 1997. The Plaintiff was accused of assisting her ex-husband ([Ex-husband]) in committing fraud/extortion against prospective applicants for civil servant recruitment at the Ministry of Finance for the 1995/1996 fiscal year. In reality, the Plaintiff had separated and legally divorced her husband, and the misuse of applicant file photocopies had been perpetrated by her ex-husband without the Plaintiff's knowledge.

The Jakarta High State Administrative Court granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit. However, at the cassation level (Decision No. 127 K/TUN/1999), the Supreme Court overturned the Jakarta High State Administrative Court ruling and dismissed the Plaintiff's lawsuit. The Plaintiff subsequently filed a Petition for Judicial Review (*Peninjauan Kembali*), arguing that a manifest error and mistake existed in the cassation decision.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:''' The honorable dismissal not at one's own request for disciplinary violations under Article 4a of Government Regulation No. 30 of 1980 contradicts procedural/formal laws because disciplinary violations under Article 4a of Government Regulation No. 30 of 1980 are more appropriately penalized with a demotion in rank by one level for a maximum period of 1 (one) year. Imposing the sanction of dismissal is exceedingly severe and fails to uphold a sense of justice for a civil servant who has served for a long duration and has never previously been subjected to disciplinary punishment.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the Petition for Judicial Review from Petitioner for Judicial Review Dra. [Plaintiff]; Annulling the Supreme Court decision dated November 25, 1999, No. 127 K/TUN/1999; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in full; (2) Declaring void the Defendant's (*BAPEK*) Decree dated November 25, 1997, No. 174/KPTS/BAPEK/1997; (3) Ordering the Respondent for PK / Defendant (*BAPEK*) to issue a new Decree containing: a. Modifying the disciplinary punishment against Dra. [Plaintiff] NIP [removed] from honorable dismissal not at her own request to a demotion in rank by one level for a maximum period of 1 (one) year; b. Reinstating and rehabilitating the Petitioner for Judicial Review as a Civil Servant at the Ministry of Finance of the RI along with all civil service rights; (4) Charging all procedural costs across all levels of jurisdiction to the State.

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:3114K PDT 1991
wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 3114 K/Pdt/1991}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 3114 K/Pdt/1991''' (dated November 28, 1992 / deliberation on November 12, 1992) is a fundamental civil law, evidentiary law, and Central Javanese customary inheritance law jurisprudence precedent establishing three core legal principles:

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established three primary legal principles:

# '''Violation of the Principle of ''Unus Testis Nullus Testis'' (Single Witness Rule):''' An appellate court errs in applying the law of evidence when validating the transfer or conveyance of disputed land from a deceased owner to his son-in-law (Defendant II) based solely on the testimony of a single witness without corroborating documentary evidence or other valid supporting proof. A single witness does not constitute legal witness testimony (''unus testis nullus testis'' ''ex'' Articles 171/174 HIR).
# '''No Prescription (''Daluwarsa'') in Customary Inheritance Claims:''' The right to claim a share of an estate under customary law (''hukum adat'') recognizes no statutory time limits and is not subject to prescription (''daluwarsa''). The High Court erred in dismissing an inheritance lawsuit merely because the land had been occupied by the defendants for 33 years.
# '''Determination of Joint Marital Property (''Gono-Gini'') from Land Right Conversions (UUPA):''' Communal/customary land (''tanah sanggan/norowito'') converted into Ownership Rights (''Hak Milik'') pursuant to Article 7 of the Conversion Provisions of Law No. 5 of 1960 (''UUPA'') ''jo.'' Minister of Agrarian Affairs Regulation No. 2 of 1960 in the year 1960 (during the husband's second marriage) constitutes joint marital property (''gono-gini'') of the second marriage. Consequently, the ½ share belonging to the late father ([Party G]) devolves as an inheritance estate to his biological children (the Plaintiffs), while the remaining ½ share constitutes the absolute right of the second wife ([Party A]), which is inherited entirely by her pre-marital child (''anak gawan'' / Defendant I).

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioners for Cassation ([Plaintiff I] & [Plaintiff II]), annulled Semarang High Court Decision No. 249/Pdt/1991/PT.Smg dated June 24, 1991, ''jo.'' Pati District Court Decision No. 97/Pdt.G/1990/PN.Pt dated January 17, 1991, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by partially granting the Plaintiffs' lawsuit, declaring ½ of disputed land Certificate C 1308 as [Party G]'s inheritance share devolving to the Plaintiffs, and ordering Defendants I and II to surrender ½ of the disputed land to the Plaintiffs.

== Claims, Evidence, and Sources ==

| 1 || '''Core Legal Principle (''Unus Testis Nullus Testis''):''' The testimony of a single witness unsupported by other evidence fails to meet the minimum evidentiary threshold. || Supreme Court Reasoning p. 119: "This opinion and conclusion cannot be maintained because it is based solely on the testimony of a single witness without support from other evidence... violating the principle of ''unus testis nullus testis''." || 3114K_PDT_1991.pdf
|-
| 2 || '''Core Legal Principle (Non-Prescription of Customary Inheritance):''' The right to claim an inheritance under customary law recognizes no time limits or prescription periods. || Supreme Court Reasoning p. 120: "Regarding the right to sue for inherited estate property under customary law, it recognizes no time limits and no prescription." || 3114K_PDT_1991.pdf
|-
| 3 || '''Agrarian Conversion Status (''Gono-Gini''):''' ''Norowito'' land converted into Ownership Rights in 1960 during the second marriage constitutes joint marital property (''gono-gini'') of the second marriage. || Supreme Court Reasoning p. 121: ''Sanggan/norowito'' land converted in 1960 (Article 7 Conversion Provisions of UUPA ''jo.'' Minister of Agrarian Affairs Regulation 2/1960) during marriage with [Party A], hence constituting second marriage ''gono-gini''. || 3114K_PDT_1991.pdf
|-
| 4 || '''Facts of [Party G]'s Family Genealogy:''' [Party G] married 1st [Party D] (divorced 1944), producing [Plaintiff I] & [Plaintiff II] (Plaintiffs I & II). Married 2nd [Party A] (bringing pre-marital stepchild [Party E] / Defendant I). [Party G] passed away in 1965, [Party A] in 1983. || Claim Posita pp. 109, 115, 120 & Reasoning p. 121: [Plaintiff I] & [Plaintiff II] are [Party G]'s biological children. [Party E] is [Party A]'s pre-marital child ([Party G]'s stepchild). || 3114K_PDT_1991.pdf
|-
| 5 || '''Contradiction of Village Book C Transfer Date vs. Death Date:''' Village Book C recorded a transfer date of April 26, 1966, whereas [Party G] passed away in 1965, rendering the alleged conveyance unproven. || Supreme Court Reasoning pp. 119–120: "Based on Exhibit P.1, the conveyance... is recorded on April 26, 1966. Conversely, according to witness testimonies... W. [Party G] passed away in 1965, which is highly illogical..." || 3114K_PDT_1991.pdf
|-
| 6 || '''Supreme Court Independent Verdict:''' The Supreme Court annulled Semarang High Court and Pati District Court decisions, partially granted the lawsuit, established ½ of the disputed land as [Party G]'s estate for the Plaintiffs, and ordered surrender. || Supreme Court Verdict pp. 113, 122: "Annulling Semarang High Court... and Pati District Court... Adjudicating Independently: Partially granting the lawsuit... Declaring ½ of the disputed property... devolving as inheritance estate to the Plaintiffs..." || 3114K_PDT_1991.pdf
|-
| 7 || '''Identity of Parties:''' Petitioners for Cassation / Plaintiffs: 1. [Plaintiff I], 2. [Plaintiff II] (Karangwetan Village, Pucakwangi, Pati); Respondents for Cassation / Defendants: 1. [Party E], 2. [Party B]. || Confirmed in decision identity pp. 115, 118, 122, 124, 128. || 3114K_PDT_1991.pdf
|}

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Evidentiary Formalities of Single Witness Testimony (''Unus Testis Nullus Testis'' ''ex'' Articles 171 / 174 HIR) ===
''Is an appellate court judgment valid under civil procedural law when it validates the transfer of disputed land solely upon the testimony of one witness without documentary corroboration or corresponding proof?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Invalid / Evidentiary Defect.'''
The High Court violated the principle of ''unus testis nullus testis'' (a single witness is not a witness ''ex'' Articles 171/174 HIR). Standalone single-witness testimony unsupported by other valid evidence fails to satisfy the minimum evidentiary threshold required to validate real property title transfers.

=== 2. Prescription (''Daluwarsa'') in Central Javanese Customary Inheritance Claims ===
''Can an inheritance partition lawsuit under customary law be dismissed or barred by prescription (''daluwarsa'') when the disputed land has been occupied by a defendant for 33 years?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: No Prescription.'''
The right to claim an inheritance partition under customary law recognizes no statutory time limits or prescription periods (''daluwarsa''). As long as a deceased parents' estate has not been legally partitioned among rightful heirs, the right of biological heirs to claim their inheritance shares remains valid regardless of how long the property has been occupied by others.

=== 3. Legal Status of ''Norowito/Sanggan'' Land Converted Under the Basic Agrarian Law (Article 7 Conversion Provisions of UUPA ''jo.'' Minister of Agrarian Affairs Regulation No. 2 of 1960) ===
''Does former ''norowito/sanggan'' land converted into Ownership Rights (''Hak Milik'') in the husband's name in 1960 qualify as joint marital property (''gono-gini'') of a second marriage or estate property of a first marriage?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Second Marriage Joint Property (''Gono-Gini'').'''
Because the factual conversion of customary ''norowito'' land into Ownership Rights occurred in 1960 (during the husband's marriage to his second wife, [Party A]), the land by operation of law constitutes joint marital property (''gono-gini'') of the second marriage. Consequently, the husband's ½ share constitutes the inheritance estate for all his biological children (the Plaintiffs), while the second wife's remaining ½ share is inherited entirely by her own biological child (Defendant I).

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Semarang High Court (Decision No. 249/Pdt/1991/PT.Smg) err in applying evidentiary and customary inheritance law (''error in iudicando'') by ruling in favor of Defendant II based on a single witness and holding that the Plaintiffs' inheritance claim was time-barred (''daluwarsa'')?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. Semarang High Court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of [Plaintiff I] and [Plaintiff II], annulled the Semarang High Court ''jo.'' Pati District Court decisions, and independently adjudicated by holding that ½ of disputed land Certificate C 1308 constitutes [Party G]'s estate which must be surrendered to the Plaintiffs as biological children.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Pati District Court & Semarang High Court) ===
Examination of [Party G] [Plaintiffs' parent]'s marital genealogy with [Party D] (1st wife, divorced 1944) and [Party A] (2nd wife, married 1945/1960); verification of the status of stepchild [Party E] (Defendant I, [Party A]'s child) and her husband [Party B] (Defendant II); verification of property location and boundaries for Certificate C 1308 covering ± 1 ''bahu'' in Karangwetan Village, Pucakwangi, Pati; verification of [Party G]'s death date (1965) versus Village Book C No. 1404 transfer recording date (April 26, 1966); and testimonies of trial witnesses ([Party C], Senen, Komari, [Party F]).

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''HIR (Herziene Inlandsch Reglement):''' Articles 171, 174 (Witness Evidentiary Principles / ''Unus Testis Nullus Testis'').
* '''Law No. 5 of 1960 on Basic Agrarian Principles (UUPA):''' Article 7 Conversion Provisions (Conversion of Customary / ''Norowito'' Land Rights).
* '''Minister of Agrarian Affairs Regulation No. 2 of 1960:''' Implementation of Land Rights

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:3176K PDT 1988
wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 3176 K/Pdt/1988}} '''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 3176 K/Pdt/1988''' (dated April 19, 1990 / deliberation on April 3, 1990) is a fundamental land law and civil evidentiary law jurisprudence precedent establishing vital rules concerning the legal standing of Ownership Rights Certificates (''Sertifikat Hak Milik'' / SHM) as absolute authentic proof of land ownership compared to Tax Receipts / ''Girik'' (''Letter C''): == Executive Summary == The Supreme Court established three primary legal principles: # '''Certificates as Authentic and Absolute Proof of Land Ownership:''' A plot of land that clearly possesses a land certificate (i.e., SHM No. 626/Pusaka Rakyat Village) '''cannot be freely transacted or acquired solely on the basis of a ''Girik'' letter''', but must be based on the relevant land certificate, which serves as authentic and absolute proof of ownership. # '''Legal Function of ''Girik'' Letters:''' A ''Girik'' or Letter C serves '''solely as a sign for paying taxes''' (''Petuk Pajak''), and does not constitute proof of ownership rights over land. The bearer or holder of a ''Girik'' cannot trade or clear land for which a certificate has already been issued in the name of another party. # '''Unlawful Acts by Developers / Purchasers Based on ''Girik'':''' A developer (i.e., PT Green Garden / Defendant I) that clears certified land solely based on a ''Girik'' letter from local residents or ''Girik'' holders who are not the certificate owners is classified as acting without rights / unlawfully (''perbuatan melawan hukum''). The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation (PT Astra International Inc.), annulled Jakarta High Court Decision No. 527/Pdt/1987/PT.DKI dated October 22, 1987, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by partially granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit, declaring the Plaintiff's rights over land SHM No. 626 based on Power of Attorney Deed No. 92 and Appointment Deed No. 93 valid under the law, declaring Defendant I without rights in building a road over the disputed land, and ordering Defendant I to surrender the disputed land to the Plaintiff. == Infobox == {| class="wikitable" |- ! scope="row" | Object ID | JPAIS:PRECEDENT:3176K_PDT_1988 |- ! scope="row" | Mode | MODE 1 — BHT KNOWLEDGE (Extract Verified Knowledge from Final Cases) |- ! scope="row" | Knowledge Pipeline | SOURCE (3176K_PDT_1988.pdf) → EVIDENCE (Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. {{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 3180/Pdt/1985}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 3180/Pdt/1985''' (deliberated on December 24, 1986 / pronounced on January 28, 1987) is a fundamental family and divorce law jurisprudence precedent establishing vital rules concerning the judicial interpretation of continuous disputes and irreconcilable differences (''onheelbare tweespalt'') pursuant to Article 19 letter f of Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975 ''jo.'' Article 1 of Law No. 1 of 1974.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established a primary legal principle:

* '''Focus on the Factual Reality of Continuous Disputes Rather Than Their Causes:''' "The concept of continuous disputes and irreconcilable differences (''onheelbare tweespalt'') is not focused on proving the underlying causes of the dispute, but rather on observing the factual reality that continuous disputes are indeed proven to exist to the extent that reconciliation is no longer possible."

Where the Palu High Court ruled that a husband's frequent drunkenness and returning home late "did not yet fall within the definition of continuous disputes and irreconcilable differences," the Supreme Court held that such reasoning was erroneous and misapplied the law. Under the ''broken marriage'' doctrine, once witness testimony proves that a couple is in constant discord, that the husband has abandoned the shared domicile, and that all hope of reconciliation is lost, the statutory requirements for divorce under ''onheelbare tweespalt'' are fully satisfied.

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation ([Party A]), annulled Palu High Court Decision No. 48/Pdt/1984/PT. Palu dated October 17, 1984 (which had overturned Palu District Court Decision No. 7/1984/Pdt.G dated May 19, 1984), and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by partially granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit, declaring the marriage dissolved due to divorce, granting custody of the four children to the Plaintiff, and ordering both parties to share living and educational expenses according to their respective financial capabilities.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Judicial Interpretation of Continuous Disputes and Irreconcilable Differences (''Onheelbare Tweespalt'' ''ex'' Article 19 letter f of Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975 ''jo.'' Article 1 of Law No. 1 of 1974) ===
''In a divorce lawsuit based on Article 19 letter f of Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975, must the court examine and prove the degree or severity of the underlying causes of a dispute (such as a husband's habit of drunkenness), or is it sufficient to prove the factual reality that continuous disputes have occurred with no hope of reconciliation?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Focus on the Factual Reality of Disputes.'''
The concept of continuous disputes and irreconcilable differences (''onheelbare tweespalt'') does not focus on proving the underlying causes of conflict, but rather on observing the factual reality that continuous disputes are proven to exist such that reconciliation is impossible. Judicial reasoning that questions whether an underlying cause meets a threshold of severity is erroneous.

=== 2. Evaluation of Witness Testimony in Divorce Disputes (Article 1908 BW / Articles 171–172 HIR / Article 22 paragraph 2 of Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975) ===
The testimonies of three witnesses under oath confirming that the parties' domestic life has broken down, frequent quarrels have occurred, and the Defendant has abandoned the shared home satisfy the minimum evidentiary threshold required to grant a divorce.

=== 3. Prohibition Against Raising New Legal Grounds (''Novum'') During Cassation Proceedings ===
Cassation objections introducing new facts or legal events never raised during first-instance or appellate examinations are classified as an inadmissible ''novum'' before the Supreme Court.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (''Judex Juris'' / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Palu High Court (Decision No. 48/Pdt/1984/PT. Palu) err in applying the law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') by dismissing the divorce lawsuit on the grounds that "frequent quarrels caused by the Defendant frequently returning home drunk do not fall within the definition of ''onheelbare tweespalt''"?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. Palu High Court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court granted the Petitioner's cassation petition, annulled Palu High Court's decision, and independently adjudicated by declaring the marriage between the Plaintiff and Defendant dissolved due to divorce.

=== Question of Fact (''Judex Facti'' / Palu District Court & Palu High Court) ===
Verification of marriage in Manado on March 4, 1968; birth of four children; facts regarding the Defendant's frequent drunkenness and late returns; the Defendant's sale of shared residential property without the Plaintiff's consent; and testimonies of witnesses [Party C], Nyoman Putu, and Petrus Wongkar.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''Law No. 1 of 1974 on Marriage:''' Article 1 (Purpose of Marriage) & Article 39 paragraph (2) (Grounds for Divorce).
* '''Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975 on the Implementation of Law No. 1 of 1974:''' Article 19 letter f (Grounds for Divorce: Continuous Disputes / ''Onheelbare Tweespalt'') & Article 22 paragraph (2) (Examination of Family / Close Relative Witnesses).
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 1 of 1950 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation and Independent Adjudication Authority.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* '''Doctrine of Broken Marriage:''' Where a marital relationship has factually broken down, affection has vanished, physical separation has occurred, and reconciliation efforts fail, the marital bond must not be forcibly maintained as it contradicts the essence and purpose of marriage under Article 1 of Law No. 1 of 1974.
* '''Established Precedent on ''Onheelbare Tweespalt'':''' Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 3180/Pdt/1985 serves as a landmark decision utilized as a primary authority by general civil courts and religious courts across Indonesia in assessing the validity of continuous-dispute divorce lawsuits.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* The Plaintiff and Defendant are proven to be lawful husband and wife married in Manado on March 4, 1968, and blessed with 4 children.
* Continuous disputes and irreconcilable differences (''onheelbare tweespalt'') causing domestic breakdown and irreconcilability are '''PROVEN AS A FACTUAL REALITY'''.
* The Defendant is proven to have abandoned the shared marital home and only occasionally visits the children.
* Palu High Court Decision No. 48/Pdt/1984/PT. Palu is '''NULL AND VOID'''.
* The marriage between the Plaintiff and Defendant is '''OFFICIALLY DISSOLVED DUE TO DIVORCE'''.
* Custody, care, and guidance of the four minor children remain with the Plaintiff.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 318 K/TUN/2000 dated March 19, 2002, establishes fundamental state administrative and land law jurisprudence: Pursuant to Article 45 paragraph (1) of Government Regulation No. 24 of 1997 on Land Registration, the Head of the Land Office is prohibited/not permitted to register the transfer of land rights if the land in question is currently the object of a dispute in court. The issuance of a new Freehold Title (*Sertifikat Hak Milik*) over land currently undergoing judicial proceedings and subject to a State Administrative Court suspension order constitutes an unlawful act violating the authority of a State Administrative Official (*ultra vires*), and consequently, such certificate must be declared null and void and without legal force.

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiffs / Petitioners for Cassation (1. Nyonya Taily Aida and 2. Hendra Santoso) are the lawful owners of 5 (five) plots of Freehold Land located in Dukuh Pakis Village, Karangpilang Sub-District (currently Dukuh Pakis Sub-District), Surabaya Municipality (SHM No. 90/Dukuh Pakis in the name of Ny. Taily Aida; and SHM Nos. 142, 143, 144, and 145/Dukuh Pakis in the name of Hendra Santoso). On June 30, 1998, the Minister of Agrarian Affairs / Head of BPN annulled the registration of the Plaintiffs' property rights by issuing Decree No. 8-XI-1998. Challenging said decree, the Plaintiffs filed a cancellation lawsuit at the Jakarta State Administrative Court (No. 072/G.TUN/1998/PTUN.Jkt), where the Chief Judge of the Jakarta State Administrative Court on September 3, 1998, issued an Order for the Suspension of Execution of Decree No. 8-XI-1998 prohibiting the transfer or encumbrance of the disputed land.

Although the Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation (Head of the Land Office of Surabaya Municipality) had official knowledge of the pending dispute at the Jakarta State Administrative Court and the aforementioned Suspension Order, the Defendant on October 23, 1998, nevertheless issued Freehold Title (SHM) No. 669/Dukuh Pakis in the name of Drs. Suladi Abdus Shomad over the Plaintiffs' disputed land. The Plaintiffs subsequently filed a lawsuit seeking the annulment of SHM No. 669 at the Surabaya State Administrative Court (Decision No. 152/G.TUN/1999/PTUN.SBY dated December 23, 1999), which granted the Plaintiffs' lawsuit in its entirety. However, the Surabaya State Administrative High Court (Decision No. 38/B/TUN/2000/PT.TUN.SBY dated May 16, 2000) annulled the Surabaya State Administrative Court judgment and declared the Plaintiffs' lawsuit inadmissible on the grounds that it was premature because the proceedings at the Jakarta State Administrative Court were still undergoing cassation review. Dissatisfied with the Surabaya State Administrative High Court ruling, the Plaintiffs filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The cassation objections raised by the Petitioners for Cassation are well-founded because the Surabaya State Administrative High Court (*PTTUN*) committed an error in applying the law.
# The Defendant (Head of the Land Office of Surabaya Municipality) was aware that the Decree of the Minister of Agrarian Affairs / Head of BPN annulling the Plaintiffs' SHM was being litigated at the Jakarta State Administrative Court (No. 072/G.TUN/1998/PTUN.Jkt jo. Jakarta State Administrative High Court No. 26/B.TUN/1999/PT.TUN.JKT) and remained under cassation review at the Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia.
# In those proceedings, the Jakarta State Administrative Court had issued an Order for the Suspension of Execution of the disputed object.
# Pursuant to Article 45 paragraph (1) of Government Regulation No. 24 of 1997, the Head of the Land Office is prohibited from registering a transfer of rights if the land in question is the object of a dispute in court.
# The Defendant's action in persisting to issue Freehold Title (SHM) No. 669/Dukuh Pakis in the name of Drs. Suladi Abdus Shomad over the disputed land violated Article 45 paragraph (1) of Government Regulation No. 24 of 1997. Therefore, pursuant to Article 51 paragraph (2)(c) of the State Administrative Court Law, the Defendant should not have issued said Freehold Title, and the certificate improperly issued must be declared null and void by operation of law.
# Legal Principle: "Pursuant to Article 45 paragraph (1) of Government Regulation No. 24 of 1997, the Head of the Land Office is not permitted to register a transfer of rights if the land in question is the object of a dispute in court."
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioners for Cassation: 1. Ny. TAILY AIDA and 2. HENDRA SANTOSO; Annulling the Surabaya State Administrative High Court decision dated May 16, 2000, No. 38/B/TUN/2000/PT.TUN.SBY; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Granting the Plaintiffs' lawsuit in its entirety; (2) Ordering the Defendant to halt all legal acts or actions as implementation of the State Administrative Decree concerning Freehold Title (SHM) No. 669/Dukuh Pakis in the name of Drs. Suladi Abdus Shomad; (3) Declaring null, void, and without legal force Freehold Title (SHM) No. 669/Dukuh Pakis in the name of Drs. Suladi Abdus Shomad; (4) Ordering the Defendant to revoke and declare void Freehold Title (SHM) No. 669/Dukuh Pakis in the name of Drs. Suladi Abdus Shomad; (5) Ordering the Defendant to strike off Freehold Title (SHM) No. 669/Dukuh Pakis in the name of Drs. Suladi Abdus Shomad from the land book register; (6) Ordering the Respondent for Cassation to pay all court costs across first instance, appellate, and cassation levels (assessed at Rp 100,000 at the cassation level). *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court on Tuesday, March 19, 2002, by Prof. Dr. Paulus Effendi Lotulung, S.H. [Junior Chairman of the Supreme Court / Presiding Judge], Ny. Emin Aminah Achadiat, S.H., and Ny. Asma Samik Ibrahim, S.H. [Associate Justices]).*

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:3191K PDT 1984
wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 3191 K/Pdt/1984}} '''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 3191 K/Pdt/1984''' (dated February 8, 1986 / deliberation on December 12, 1985) is a fundamental civil law jurisprudence precedent establishing vital rules concerning the legal qualification of a broken promise to marry following cohabitation without marriage (''begendaan'') as an Unlawful Act (''Perbuatan Melawan Hukum'' / Tort) pursuant to Article 1365 of the Civil Code. == Executive Summary == The Supreme Court established three primary legal principles: # '''Broken Promise to Marry as an Unlawful Act (Tort):''' The action of the Original Defendant (I Gusti Lanang Rejeg) in revoking and failing to fulfill his promise to lawfully marry the Original Plaintiff ([Plaintiff]), after previously persuading and bringing the Plaintiff to cohabit without marriage for 1 year and 4 months (December 20, 1981, to April 20, 1983) under the inducement of a marriage promise, constitutes an Unlawful Act (''Perbuatan Melawan Hukum'' / PMH) because it violates societal norms of decency and propriety. # '''Obligation to Pay Compensation for Reputational Restoration:''' Because the breach of promise violated the Plaintiff's subjective rights, damaged her honor and reputation as a school teacher, and breached moral and ethical standards, the Defendant is obligated to pay compensation for reputational restoration amounting to Rp 2,500,000 (two million five hundred thousand rupiahs). # '''Restriction on Claims for Cohabitation Living Expenses:''' Claims for compensation covering expenses incurred by the Plaintiff during un-solemnized cohabitation (amounting to Rp 1,465,160) must be rejected because such expenses were not previously agreed upon (''geen voorafgaande perakkoord''). The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation ([Plaintiff]), annulled the West Nusa Tenggara High Court in Mataram Decision No. 65/PDT/1984/PT.NTB dated July 26, 1984 (which had overturned Mataram District Court Decision No. 073/PN.Mtr/Pdt/1983 dated March 1, 1984), and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by partially granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit, declaring that the Defendant committed an Unlawful Act, ordering the Defendant to pay Rp 2,500,000 in reputational damages, and validating the attachment (''sita jaminan'') placed over the Defendant family's courtyard property. == Infobox == {| class="wikitable" |- ! scope="row" | Object ID | JPAIS:PRECEDENT:3191K_PDT_1984 |- ! scope="row" | Mode | MODE 1 — BHT KNOWLEDGE (Extract Verified Knowledge from Final Cases) |- ! scope="row" | Knowledge pipeline | SOURCE (3191K_PDT_1984.pdf) → EVIDENCE (Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. No. 3191 K/Pdt/1984, pp. 1–29) → CLAIM (Broken Promise to Marry Following Cohabitation Without Marriage Constitutes Tort Violating Decency and Propriety ''ex'' Article 1365 Civil Code) → KNOWLEDGE OBJECT (JPAIS Precedent Schema) → RELATIONSHIP (Annulment of NTB High Court Decision No. 65/PDT/1984/PT.NTB & Independent Adjudication Affirming Tort and Awarding Reputational Damages) → GEO ANSWER → HUMAN VERIFICATION (Mark Cecep Mustafa) |- ! scope="row" | Court | Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia (''Judex Juris'') |- ! scope="row" | Register number | Reg. No. 3191 K/Pdt/1984 |- ! scope="row" | Date | December 12, 1985 (Deliberation) / Pronounced in Open Court on February 8, 1986 |- ! scope="row" | Chamber / Subject | General Civil Law Chamber / Law of Torts (PMH) & Family / Decency Law |- ! scope="row" | Panel | * Ny. H. Poerbowati Djoko Soedomo, S.H. (Presiding Judge) * Th. Ketut Suraputra, S.H. (Associate Justice & Reading Session Chair) * H. Danny, S.H. (Associate Justice) * Fatimah Achyar, S.H. (Substitute Registrar) |- ! scope="row" | Grapher & Verification | Mark Cecep Mustafa (Verified Knowledge Grapher) — '''Status: VERIFIED''' |} == Claims, Evidence, and Sources == {| class="wikitable" |- ! # !! Claim (Legal Statement / Fact) !! Evidence (Case File / Legal Reasoning) !! Source / Passage |- | 1 || '''Core Legal Principle (Broken Promise to Marry is a Tort):''' Failure to fulfill a marriage promise after inducing un-solemnized cohabitation constitutes a tort violating public decency and propriety. || Headnote p. 1 & Supreme Court Reasoning p. 6: "...with the failure of the original defendant to fulfill his promise to marry the original plaintiff, the original defendant violated societal norms of decency and propriety, and such action by the original defendant constitutes an unlawful act..." || 3191K_PDT_1984.pdf [Passage 1, 6] |- | 2 || '''Rejection of Cohabitation Expense Claims:''' Claims for living expenses during cohabitation are rejected because they were not previously contracted or agreed upon. || Headnote p. 1 & Supreme Court Reasoning p. 7: "...whereas the compensation claim filed by the original plaintiff concerning all expenses incurred during cohabitation must be rejected because they were not previously agreed upon." || 3191K_PDT_1984.pdf [Passage 1, 7] |- | 3 || '''Facts of Marriage Promise and Cohabitation:''' The Defendant approached the Plaintiff (Dec 16, 1981), surrendered employment identification/Taspen cards and a Honda motorcycle, and promised to marry her customarily and religiously within 4 months. || Claim Posita pp. 2, 14, 15: Defendant persuaded Plaintiff to cohabit from December 20, 1981, to April 20, 1983, in Karang Pendem Cakranegara. || 3191K_PDT_1984.pdf [Passage 2, 14, 15] |- | 4 || '''Facts of Defendant's Repudiation:''' After 1 year and 4 months of cohabitation, the Defendant refused to marry the Plaintiff under the pretext that his family withheld approval. || Claim Posita pp. 2, 16 & Supreme Court Reasoning p. 6: Testimony of witness Drs. [Defendant] (Defendant's superior) confirmed that Defendant admitted making the promise but canceled it due to family disapproval. || 3191K_PDT_1984.pdf [Passage 2, 6, 16, 21, 22] |- | 5 || '''Error of NTB High Court ''Judex Facti'':''' NTB High Court (No. 65/PDT/1984/PT.NTB) erred in dismissing the lawsuit entirely on the reasoning that the Plaintiff was a widow bearing her own risks. || High Court Reasoning p. 12 & Supreme Court Reasoning p. 6: The Supreme Court annulled the High Court decision for misapplying the law. || 3191K_PDT_1984.pdf [Passage 4, 6, 12, 13] |- | 6 || '''Supreme Court Independent Verdict:''' The Supreme Court annulled NTB High Court's decision and independently adjudicated by partially granting the lawsuit, ordering the Defendant to pay Rp 2,500,000 in damages, and validating the attachment. || Supreme Court Verdict pp. 7, 8: "Annulling Mataram High Court decision... INDEPENDENTLY ADJUDICATING: Partially granting plaintiff's lawsuit; Declaring defendant committed an unlawful act; Ordering defendant to pay... Rp 2,500,000..." || 3191K_PDT_1984.pdf [Passage 7, 8] |- | 7 || '''Identity of Parties:''' Petitioner for Cassation / Original Plaintiff: [Plaintiff] ([age removed], Kindergarten Teacher, Central Lombok); Respondent for Cassation / Original Defendant: I GUSTI LANANG REJEG ([age removed], BP-7 Employee of NTB, West Lombok). || Confirmed in decision identity pp. 1, 9, 14. || 3191K_PDT_1984.pdf [Passage 1, 9, 14] |} == Legal / Procedural Issues == === 1. Legal Qualification of a Broken Promise to Marry (''Broken Promise to Marry'' ''ex'' Article 1365 Civil Code) Following Cohabitation Without Marriage === ''Does the action of a man who persuades a woman to cohabit without marriage (''begendaan'') for 1 year and 4 months under a promise of lawful marriage, but subsequently revokes that promise due to family disapproval, qualify as an Unlawful Act (Tort)?'' '''Supreme Court Rule: Constitutes an Unlawful Act (Tort).'''
Repudiating a marriage promise after inducing a woman to cohabit without marriage violates prevailing community standards of decency and propriety. Such conduct infringes upon the woman's subjective rights, damaging her honor and reputation (particularly in her professional capacity as a teacher) and satisfying all elements of an Unlawful Act under Article 1365 of the Civil Code. === 2. Conditions for Granting Claims for Living Expenses Incurred During Cohabitation === Financial expenditures or daily living expenses incurred by a woman during un-solemnized cohabitation cannot be recovered as material damages unless such expenditures were previously contracted or agreed upon (''geen voorafgaande perakkoord'') as debt obligations. === 3. Transitional Cassation Procedure Rules (Law No. 1 of 1950 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1970) === Prior to the enactment of Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court, the governing cassation procedure for the Supreme Court was Law No. 1 of 1950 insofar as it did not conflict with Law No. 14 of 1970 on Basic Judicial Power Provisions. == Question of Law vs Question of Fact == === Question of Law (''Judex Juris'' / Supreme Court) === Did the ''Judex Facti'' NTB High Court in Mataram (Decision No. 65/PDT/1984/PT.NTB) err in applying the law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') by dismissing the Plaintiff's lawsuit entirely based on the consideration that the Plaintiff was a widow acting at her own risk, whereas the Defendant was proven to have promised marriage and induced cohabitation? '''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. NTB High Court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court granted [Plaintiff]'s cassation petition, annulled the High Court decision, and independently adjudicated by declaring that the Defendant committed an Unlawful Act and ordering him to pay reputational damages of Rp 2,500,000. === Question of Fact (''Judex Facti'' / Mataram District Court & NTB High Court) === Verification of facts regarding the relationship between [Plaintiff] and I Gusti Lanang Rejeg from December 20, 1981, to April 20, 1983; delivery of collateral comprising Taspen Card, Karpeg, and a Honda motorcycle; verification of the Defendant's admission to his superior (Witness Drs. {{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 31 K/MIL/2013 & Military High Court Decision No. PUT/26-K/PMU/BDG/AD/XI/2010}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 31 K/MIL/2013''' (dated April 2, 2013) and '''Military Appeals Court Decision No. PUT/26-K/PMU/BDG/AD/XI/2010''' (dated November 8, 2010) are landmark special criminal law and military justice jurisprudence precedents compiled under the Supreme Court Jurisprudence framework. They adjudicate complex military criminal matters involving active soldiers' participation in transnational human smuggling, the abuse of superior authority over subordinates (''ex'' Article 127 of the Military Criminal Code / ''KUHPM''), failure to report incidents to superior commands (''ex'' Article 121 ''KUHPM''), and the imposition of dishonorable discharge from active military service (''pemecatan'').

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court and the Military Appeals Court established four primary legal principles:

# '''Human Smuggling by Military Personnel (Article 120 paragraph (1) Immigration Law ''jo.'' Article 55 Criminal Code):''' Active Indonesian National Armed Forces (''TNI'') personnel (such as regional military supervisors / ''Babinsa'') who organize, coordinate, and cooperate with smuggling syndicates to secure boats, escort, and smuggle illegal foreign migrants from the Middle East to Australia through Indonesian coastal waters are legally and convincingly proven guilty of Human Smuggling ''ex'' Article 120 paragraph (1) of Law No. 6 of 2011 on Immigration ''jo.'' Article 55 paragraph (1) point 1 of the Criminal Code. Defendants are sentenced to imprisonment, a Rp 500,000,000 fine, and an additional penalty of dishonorable discharge from TNI-AD active service.
# '''Abuse of Superior Influence Over Subordinates (Article 127 KUHPM):''' A District Military Commander (''Dandim'') who abuses the influence of his office and authority to persuade or order subordinates (military intelligence personnel) to conduct unauthorized or violent actions outside official duties, resulting in the death of a civilian (victim [Party B] at Lake Singkarak), fulfills the elements of Abuse of Influence ''ex'' Article 127 of the Military Criminal Code (''KUHPM'').
# '''Failure to Report to Superior Command (Article 121 KUHPM):''' A military unit commander who intentionally conceals or neglects the duty to report prominent incidents (such as the discovery of a corpse or subordinate criminal offenses) to the Resort Military Commander (''Danrem'') as the Superior Command is proven to violate Article 121 of the Military Criminal Code (''KUHPM'').
# '''Criteria for Dishonorable Discharge from TNI-AD Active Service (Article 26 KUHPM):''' Mid-ranking officers (Lieutenant Colonels) or Non-Commissioned Officers committing crimes that tarnish institutional dignity, destroy the harmonious bond between the military and the people (''kemanunggalan TNI-Rakyat''), and strip away soldierly integrity are deemed unfit to remain in military service and must be subjected to the additional penalty of discharge from active service ''ex'' Article 26 of the Military Criminal Code (''KUHPM'').

The Supreme Court rejected the cassation petitions of the Petitioners for Cassation / Defendants (Serda [Defendant], Kopka Karyadi, Peltu Susiali, Serka Khoirul Anam) in Decision No. 31 K/MIL/2013, affirming the primary prison sentences and the additional penalty of dishonorable discharge from TNI-AD active service.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Military Criminal Liability for Human Smuggling (Article 120 paragraph (1) Immigration Law No. 6 of 2011 ''jo.'' Article 55 Criminal Code) ===
''Can an active TNI soldier utilizing their position and facilities as a local military supervisor (''Babinsa'') to facilitate transit, transportation, and departure of illegal foreign immigrants be prosecuted under the Immigration Law and discharged from military service?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Prosecutable & Mandatory Discharge.'''
Participation by military personnel in international migrant smuggling syndicates constitutes a transnational organized crime damaging state sovereignty and military institutional standing. Such conduct fulfills the elements of Article 120 paragraph (1) of the Immigration Law ''jo.'' Article 55 of the Criminal Code, warranting prison terms, a Rp 500 million fine, and the additional penalty of dishonorable discharge from TNI-AD active service.

=== 2. Limits of Superior Authority Abuse Over Subordinates in Military Justice (Article 127 Military Criminal Code) ===
''Does an oral order or direction from a Unit Commander (''Dandim'') instructing subordinates to handle civilians outside official statutory authority qualify as the crime of abusing superior influence ''ex'' Article 127 of the Military Criminal Code (''KUHPM'')?''

'''Supreme Court / Military Appeals Court Rule: Fulfills Article 127 KUHPM Elements.'''
A military superior using positional influence to direct subordinates to commit unlawful acts (assault/unlawful detention) remains criminally liable for abusing official influence, even if executing subordinates are prosecuted separately.

=== 3. Indicators of Propriety for Additional Military Discharge Penalties (Article 26 KUHPM) ===
Dishonorable discharge from military service (''pemecatan'') is applied when crimes committed by soldiers reflect bad character, subvert military discipline and leadership, and destroy the harmonious bond between the military and the people (''Kemanunggalan TNI dengan Rakyat'').

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (''Judex Juris'' / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Surabaya Military High Court III (Decision No. 86-K/PMT.III/BDG/AD/XI/2012) and Madiun Military Court III-13 (Decision No. 42-K/PM.III-13/AD/VIII/2012) correctly apply the law (''juiste toepassing van het recht'' ''ex'' Article 120 Immigration Law) against the Defendant illegal immigrant smugglers?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. The ''Judex Facti'' correctly applied the law and committed no evidentiary errors. The Supreme Court rejected Serda [Defendant] ''et al.''{{'}}s cassation petition and affirmed 5–6 years' imprisonment, a Rp 500 million fine, and discharge from TNI-AD active service.

=== Question of Fact (''Judex Facti'' / Padang Military Court I-03, Medan Military High Court I, & Military Appeals Court) ===
Verification of facts concerning the arrest of victim [Party B] on damaged roads in Nagari Kacang, X Koto Singkarak Sub-district, on May 20, 2007; physical torture in the garage of the Solok Dandim official residence; corpse disposal in Lake Singkarak; corpse discovery by fisherman Yunasri Sutan Man Cayo on May 25, 2007; ''Visum et Repertum'' from Dr. M. Djamil Hospital, Padang, No. Ym.01.08.1.5.1035; and verification of operational fund flows for illegal immigrants amounting to Rp 120,000,000 at Juanda Airport, Surabaya.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''Law No. 6 of 2011 on Immigration:''' Article 120 paragraph (1) (Human Smuggling).
* '''Military Criminal Code (KUHPM):''' Article 26 (Additional Discharge Penalty), Article 121 (Failure to Report), & Article 127 (Abuse of Positional Influence).
* '''Law No. 31 of 1997 on Military Justice:''' Articles 130, 171, 173 (Military Modes of Proof & Evidence).
* '''Criminal Code (KUHP):''' Article 55 paragraph (1) point 1 (Complicity / ''Deelneming'') & Article 338 (Murder).

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* '''Doctrine of Zero Tolerance for Transnational Crimes by TNI Personnel:''' Military personnel involved in transnational syndicates (human smuggling/narcotics) must face absolute discharge to safeguard national sovereignty and institutional dignity.
* '''Doctrine of Superior Responsibility / Abuse of Authority (''ex'' Article 127 KUHPM):''' Military command is a trust for troop development; abusing command authority for criminal acts destroys military hierarchy and legal obedience.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* The Defendants (Serda [Defendant], Kopka Karyadi, Peltu Susiali, Serka Khoirul Anam) are '''PROVEN LEGALLY AND CONVINCINGLY GUILTY OF HUMAN SMUGGLING''' ''ex'' Article 120 paragraph (1) of the Immigration Law ''jo.'' Article 55 of the Criminal Code.
* Lt. Col. Untung Sunanto is '''PROVEN GUILTY OF ABUSE OF POSITIONAL INFLUENCE (Article 127 KUHPM) AND FAILURE TO REPORT (Article 121 KUHPM)'''.
* Defendants are sentenced to primary prison terms and a fine of Rp 500,000,000.
* Defendants are subjected to the additional penalty of '''DISHONORABLE DISCHARGE FROM TNI-AD ACTIVE SERVICE'''.
* Defendants' cassation petitions are '''REJECTED ENTIRELY BY THE SUPREME COURT'''.

=== Dismissed Indictment Charges (Primary Murder Charge) ===
* The primary indictment charging murder (''ex'' Article 338 Criminal Code ''jo.'' Article 55 Criminal Code) against Lt. Col. Untung Sunanto was '''PROVEN UNFOUNDED MATERIALLY''', as physical torture was spontaneous subordinate initiative driven by fear of reprimand over escaped detainees.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Integrity of Military Criminal Law Enforcement Against Organized Crime:''' This landmark ruling establishes strict boundaries for Indonesian Military Justice integrity: no tolerance or legal immunity exists for mid-ranking officers or NCOs abusing command authority or engaging in international human smuggling syndicates. Imprisonment and military discharge are absolute consequences for upholding troop discipline and national law.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
; Can active TNI personnel involved in illegal immigrant smuggling be discharged from military service and prosecuted under the Immigration Law pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence?
: '''Prosecutable & Mandatory Discharge.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. No. 31 K/MIL/2013:

* TNI personnel cooperating within illegal foreign immigrant smuggling syndicates are legally proven to commit Human Smuggling ''ex'' Article 120 paragraph (1) of Law No. 6 of 2011 on Immigration ''jo.'' Article 55 of the Criminal Code.
* Such transnational crimes damage institutional reputation and state sovereignty, warranting prison sentences, a Rp 500,000,000 fine, and the additional penalty of '''DISHONORABLE DISCHARGE FROM TNI-AD ACTIVE SERVICE'''.
* The Supreme Court rejected soldiers' cassation petitions and affirmed military discharge penalties.

== Overview ==
Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 325 K/Pid/1985 dated October 27, 1986, establishes fundamental criminal and civil jurisprudence regarding the separation between the criminal offense of fraud and civil disputes: An indictment stating solely that the Defendant sold a rice field for Rp 1,500,000, which land turned out to be non-existent, does not constitute the crime of fraud under Article 378 of the KUHP or any other criminal offense, but rather constitutes an ordinary civil matter. Consequently, even if proven to have been committed by the Defendant, the Defendant must be released from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*), and the Defendant's rights regarding capacity, position, honor, and dignity must be restored.

== Case Background ==
The Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation ([Defendant], [age removed], retired Notary, residing in [address removed]) was brought before the Simalungun District Court charged with committing the crime of fraud under Article 378 of the KUHP. The Public Prosecutor alleged that on July 16, 1973, the Defendant sold 6 hectares of rice field in Kampung Merayap-II, Tanah Jawa Sub-District, Simalungun Regency, for Rp 1,500,000 to Kongsi Lumbanraja. However, upon investigation, the sold rice field did not exist (it existed only on paper).

The Simalungun District Court (Decision No. 147/KTS/1983/PN-Sim dated June 12, 1984) sentenced the Defendant to 3 (three) months of imprisonment with a 6-month probation period. The Medan High Court (Decision No. 202/PID/1984/PT-MDN dated December 31, 1984) upheld the Simalungun District Court judgment. Dissatisfied with the ruling, the Defendant filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The formulation of facts (*feitelijke weergave*) in the Public Prosecutor's indictment fails to legally incorporate the elements of the crime of fraud under Article 378 of the KUHP, merely stating that the Defendant sold 6 hectares of rice field for Rp 1,500,000, which land turned out to be non-existent.
# What was charged does not constitute the crime of fraud under Article 378 of the KUHP or any other criminal offense, but rather represents an ordinary civil dispute.
# Because the charged act is proven but does not constitute a criminal offense, the Defendant must be released from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*), and his rights in capacity, position, honor, and dignity must be restored (*rehabilitation*).
# Legal Principle: "An indictment stating solely that the Defendant sold a rice field for Rp 1,500,000, which land turned out to be non-existent, does not constitute the crime of fraud under Article 378 of the KUHP or any other criminal offense, but rather constitutes an ordinary civil matter. Thus, even if proven to have been committed by the Defendant, the Defendant must be released from all legal prosecutions, and the Defendant's rights regarding capacity, position, honor, and dignity must be restored."

* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation [Defendant]; Annulling the Medan High Court decision No. 202/PID/1984/PT-MDN dated December 31, 1984, and the Simalungun District Court decision No. 147/KTS/1983/PN-Sim dated June 12, 1984; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Declaring that the act charged against Defendant [Defendant] is proven; (2) Declaring further that the proven act does not constitute a criminal offense; (3) Releasing Defendant [Defendant] from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*); (4) Restoring the Defendant's rights in capacity, position, honor, and dignity (*rehabilitation*); (5) Ordering that photocopies of documentary evidence remain annexed to the case file; (6) Charging court costs across all levels of jurisdiction to the State. *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court on Wednesday, October 8, 1986, and pronounced in an open session on Monday, October 27, 1986, by Palti Radja Siregar, S.H. [Supreme Court Justice / Session Chairman], R. Soebijantono, S.H., and H. Agus Djamili, S.H. [Associate Justices]).*

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:3263K PDT 1992
wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 3263 K/Pdt/1992}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 3263 K/Pdt/1992''' (dated June 30, 1994 / deliberation on April 15, 1994) is a fundamental civil law and civil procedure jurisprudence precedent establishing crucial rules concerning the legal standing (''persona standi in judicio'') of associations dissolved by the Government and the legal consequences of lawsuits filed by unauthorized entities.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established a primary legal principle:

* '''Dissolved Associations Have No Right to File Lawsuits:''' "An association that has been dissolved has no right to file a lawsuit."

Where the Christian Lyceum Association (''Perkumpulan Lyceum Kristen'' / PLK) filed a lawsuit seeking the eviction and vacation of the SMAK Dago school building complex ([address removed], Bandung), the Supreme Court held that PLK was not a legitimate name change or continuation of ''Het Christelijk Lyceum'' (HCL). Because ''Het Christelijk Lyceum'' was a prohibited foreign association officially dissolved by the Government pursuant to Government Regulation in Lieu of Law No. 50 of 1960 (''UU No. 50 Prp. Tahun 1960''), and PLK was not its lawful continuation, PLK lacked legal standing (''no legal standing'' / ''lack of persona standi in judicio''). Consequently, the lawsuit filed by PLK must be declared '''Inadmissible''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation (Foundation of the West Java Christian Middle School Educational Board / YBPSMK Jabar), annulled Bandung High Court Decision No. 218/Pdt/1992/PT.Bdg dated July 31, 1992, ''jo.'' Bandung District Court Decision No. 245/Pdt/G/1991/PN.Bdg dated April 29, 1992, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by declaring the Plaintiff's lawsuit in Convention and the Counterclaim in Reconvention both '''Inadmissible''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).
