|}

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Formal Standing Requirements (''Persona Standi in Judicio'') for Private Associations / Legal Entities (Law No. 50 Prp. of 1960) ===
''Does a local association (i.e., Perkumpulan Lyceum Kristen) possess legal capacity (legal standing) to sue for asset vacation and rent on behalf of a foreign association (i.e., Het Christelijk Lyceum) that has been officially dissolved by the Government of the Republic of Indonesia under statutory law?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Lacks Legal Standing / Formally Defective.'''
Foreign/Dutch associations dissolved by the Government under Law No. 50 Prp. of 1960 no longer retain juridical existence. A newly formed association claiming to be a continuation or name change of such prohibited association without valid legal basis lacks legal capacity (''lack of persona standi in judicio'') to file civil lawsuits before courts.

=== 2. Legal Consequences of Lawsuits Filed by Unauthorized Legal Subjects (''Error in Persona'' ''ex'' Lack of Standing) ===
Civil lawsuits filed by unauthorized legal subjects lacking entitlement as owners or rights-holders over disputed objects contain a formal defect regarding the legal subject (''error in persona''), requiring courts to declare the lawsuit '''Inadmissible''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO) without examining the substantive merits.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Bandung High Court (Decision No. 218/Pdt/1992/PT.Bdg) and Bandung District Court (Decision No. 245/Pdt/G/1991/PN.Bdg) err in applying civil procedure and organizational law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') by validating Perkumpulan Lyceum Kristen as a qualified Plaintiff entitled to sue YBPSMK Jabar, whereas the parent organization Het Christelijk Lyceum had been dissolved by the Government under Law No. 50 Prp. of 1960 and PLK was not its lawful continuation?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. The ''Judex Facti'' misapplied the law. Dissolved associations have no right to file lawsuits. The Supreme Court granted YBPSMK Jabar's cassation petition, annulled the lower court decisions, and independently adjudicated by declaring the lawsuits in Convention and Reconvention Inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Bandung District Court & Bandung High Court) ===
Verification of Exhibits T-14 and T-15 regarding the dissolution status of Het Christelijk Lyceum; inspection of the School Building Lease Agreement dated November 14, 1978; verification of physical possession over the SMAK Dago school complex at [address removed], Bandung, by YBPSMK Jabar; and testimonies of trial witnesses (T. Sumarna, Sahala Hamonangan Simatupang, Drs. Helmy Sukardi, Solias Pandi, Jo Soa Tedjayuana, Iwan Suwardi, Drs. Wahyu Kurnia, Margo Wahono, Soesanto Kartoatmodjo, Sasongko Endrawijaya).

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===

* '''Law No. 50 Prp. of 1960:''' Prohibition of Prohibited Foreign Organizations / Associations Established by or for Foreigners Without Diplomatic Relations.
* '''Dwikora Cabinet Presidium Regulation No. 5/Prk/1965:''' Reaffirmation of House/Land/Building Status Belonging to Former Dutch Legal Entities.
* '''HIR / RBg:''' Provisions on Formal Lawsuit Requirements & Legal Subject Exceptions (''Persona Standi in Judicio'' / ''Error in Persona'').
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation and Independent Adjudication Authority.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===

* '''Doctrine of Legal Entity ''Persona Standi in Judicio'':''' Only definitive legal subjects possessing valid juridical existence and legally recognized rights may act as Plaintiffs before courts.
* '''Established Precedent on Dissolved Associations:''' Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 3263 K/Pdt/1992 serves as a landmark decision establishing that organizations/associations officially dissolved by the State forfeit all private law rights, including the right to file civil lawsuits in court.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* ''Het Christelijk Lyceum'' (HCL) is '''PROVEN TO HAVE BEEN DISSOLVED BY THE RI GOVERNMENT''' pursuant to Law No. 50 Prp. of 1960.
* ''Perkumpulan Lyceum Kristen'' (PLK) is '''PROVEN NOT TO BE A NAME CHANGE OR LAWFUL CONTINUATION''' of ''Het Christelijk Lyceum''.
* The Plaintiff (Perkumpulan Lyceum Kristen) is '''PROVEN TO LACK LEGAL STANDING''' (''Lack of Persona Standi in Judicio'').
* Bandung High Court Decision No. 218/Pdt/1992/PT.Bdg and Bandung District Court Decision No. 245/Pdt/G/1991/PN.Bdg are '''NULL AND VOID'''.
* Both the Plaintiff's Convention lawsuit (PLK) and Counterclaim Reconvention lawsuit (YBPSMK Jabar) are declared '''INADMISSIBLE''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

=== Unconsidered Substantive Issues ===

* Ultimate ownership rights over land and buildings of the SMAK Dago complex at [address removed], Bandung, '''WERE NOT CONSIDERED BY THE SUPREME COURT''', as the lawsuit lapsed upon formal legal-subject testing.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Legal Certainty in Restructuring Assets of Former Prohibited Foreign Organizations:''' This landmark ruling establishes rigorous procedural and organizational certainty in Indonesia: courts must not permit factions or groups to invoke prohibited foreign organizations dissolved by national statute to claim or demand rent over strategic assets (such as school complexes). Any claims brought on behalf of dissolved organizations must be declared inadmissible (NO) due to the absence of a valid legal subject.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
; Does an association or organization officially dissolved by the Government under statutory law retain the right to file civil lawsuits in court pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence?
: '''No Right / Inadmissible (NO).''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. No. 3263 K/Pdt/1992:

* An association that has been dissolved has no right to file a lawsuit in civil court.
* Local associations claiming to be replacements or continuations of prohibited foreign associations dissolved ''ex'' Law No. 50 Prp. of 1960 lack legal capacity / legal standing (''lack of persona standi in judicio'').
* The Supreme Court annulled the lower court decisions and independently adjudicated by declaring the Plaintiff's lawsuit Inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 3277 K/Pdt/2000}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 3277 K/Pdt/2000''' (dated July 18, 2003) is a fundamental civil law and tort law (''Perbuatan Melawan Hukum'' / PMH) jurisprudence precedent establishing vital rules concerning the legal qualification of a broken promise to marry, the legal consequences of reimbursing living and educational expenses, and damages for reputational restoration ''ex'' Article 1365 of the Civil Code.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established three primary legal principles:

# '''Broken Promise to Marry Constitutes a Tort (PMH):''' "With the failure to fulfill a promise to marry, such action constitutes an unlawful act because it violates societal norms of decency and propriety."
# '''Obligation to Reimburse Living and Postgraduate Studies Expenses:''' Because the Original Defendant (Drs. [Defendant]) failed to fulfill his promise to marry the Original Plaintiff ([Plaintiff], B.A.) after initiating an intimate relationship and cohabiting as husband and wife without marriage, the Original Defendant is legally obligated to reimburse the Original Plaintiff for all expenses incurred to support the Defendant's living costs and graduate studies (Master's / S-2 program) amounting to Rp 7,500,000 (seven million five hundred thousand rupiahs).
# '''Reputational Damages and ''Ex Aequo et Bono'' Determination:''' A man who repudiates a marriage promise after damaging a woman's honor and reputation (a school teacher) before her family and community is ordered to pay Rp 10,000,000 (ten million rupiahs) in reputational restoration damages. The Supreme Court affirmed that damages do not need to be detailed meticulously in the ''petitum'' because, pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. No. 2559 K/Pdt/1986, judges possess the authority to determine damages ''ex aequo et bono''.

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation ([Plaintiff], B.A.), annulled Surabaya High Court Decision No. 51/PDT/1999/PT.SBY dated April 13, 1999 (which had overturned Surabaya District Court Decision No. 142/Pdt.G/1997/PN.SBY dated October 28, 1997), and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by partially granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in Convention, declaring that the Defendant committed a Tort, ordering the Defendant to reimburse living expenses of Rp 7,500,000 and pay reputational damages of Rp 10,000,000, while rejecting the Defendant's counterclaim in Reconvention.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Legal Qualification of a Broken Promise to Marry (''Broken Promise to Marry'' ''ex'' Article 1365 Civil Code) Following Intimate Cohabitation ===
''Does the action of a man (a university lecturer/graduate student) who persuades a woman to engage in sexual relations and cohabit regularly under a promise of marriage, but subsequently repudiates that promise unilaterally, qualify as an Unlawful Act (Tort)?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Constitutes an Unlawful Act (Tort).'''

Pursuant to the analogy of Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. No. 3191 K/Pdt/1984 (February 8, 1986), repudiating a marriage promise after cohabiting and engaging in sexual relations constitutes a violation of societal norms of decency and propriety. Such conduct inflicts moral and material injury upon the woman, giving rise to a claim for damages ''ex'' Article 1365 of the Civil Code.

=== 2. Right to Claim Reimbursement of Living Expenses and Postgraduate Studies Funding ===
A man who fails to fulfill his marriage promise is legally obligated to reimburse (make restitution for) all expenses incurred by a woman to support his daily living costs and educational pursuits (including Master's degree tuition) during their romantic relationship absent a valid matrimonial bond.

=== 3. Judicial Discretion in Determining Damages ''Ex Aequo et Bono'' (Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 2559 K/Pdt/1986) ===
Defendants or appellate courts cannot dismiss damage claims on the grounds that loss breakdowns are insufficiently specific or vague (''obscuur libel''). Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. No. 2559 K/Pdt/1986 (June 22, 1988), judges possess discretionary authority to determine fair and equitable damage amounts (''ex aequo et bono'') based on standards of fairness regarding the victim's suffering.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (''Judex Juris'' / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Surabaya High Court (Decision No. 51/PDT/1999/PT.SBY) err in applying the law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') by annulling the Surabaya District Court decision and declaring the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible (NO) on the grounds that damage breakdowns were vague, whereas breaking a marriage promise is a tort ''ex'' Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 3191 K/Pdt/1984 and judges possess authority to determine damages ''ex aequo et bono'' ''ex'' Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 2559 K/Pdt/1986?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. Surabaya High Court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court granted [Plaintiff]'s cassation petition, annulled Surabaya High Court's decision, and independently adjudicated by declaring that Defendant Drs. [Defendant] committed a Tort, ordering him to reimburse living/S-2 expenses of Rp 7,500,000 and pay reputational damages of Rp 10,000,000.

=== Question of Fact (''Judex Facti'' / Surabaya District Court & Surabaya High Court) ===
Verification of facts regarding the relationship between [Plaintiff], B.A. and Drs. [Defendant] starting November 12, 1993; facts concerning the marriage promise stated before the Plaintiff's parents on November 24, 1995; facts regarding the Defendant's regular overnight stays from Saturday to Monday and sexual relations; funding of the Defendant's S-2 graduate studies and daily living expenses by the Plaintiff; the Defendant's evasion starting October 1996; and the Defendant's counterclaim in Reconvention concerning defamation across mass media (Jawa Pos, Memorandum, Wanita Indonesia).

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata / BW):''' Article 1365 (Unlawful Acts / Tort), Article 1372 (Damages for Reputational Restoration), & Article 1320 (Agreement Validity Requirements).
* '''Law No. 1 of 1974 on Marriage:''' Principles and Purpose of Marriage.
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation and Independent Adjudication Authority.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* '''Supreme Court Decision No. 3191 K/Pdt/1984 (Feb 8, 1986):''' Landmark decision establishing that repudiating a marriage promise after inducing un-solemnized cohabitation constitutes a Tort violating societal decency and propriety.
* '''Supreme Court Decision No. 2559 K/Pdt/1986 (June 22, 1988):''' Landmark decision regarding judicial authority to determine damage amounts ''ex aequo et bono'' in tort cases.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* The Defendant (Drs. [Defendant]) is '''PROVEN TO HAVE PROMISED TO MARRY THE PLAINTIFF''' before the Plaintiff's parents on November 24, 1995.
* The Defendant is '''PROVEN TO HAVE REGULARLY STAYED OVERNIGHT AND ENGAGED IN SEXUAL RELATIONS''' with the Plaintiff like husband and wife without a marriage bond.
* The Defendant is '''PROVEN TO HAVE RECEIVED AND UTILIZED DAILY LIVING AND MASTER'S DEGREE STUDY FUNDING''' provided by the Plaintiff.
* The Defendant is '''PROVEN TO HAVE REPUDIATED HIS MARRIAGE PROMISE''' and disappeared irresponsibly.
* The Defendant's conduct is '''PROVEN TO CONSTITUTE AN UNLAWFUL ACT (TORT)''' violating community decency and propriety.
* The Defendant is ordered to reimburse all expenses incurred by the Plaintiff amounting to Rp 7,500,000.
* The Defendant is ordered to pay reputational restoration damages to the Plaintiff amounting to Rp 10,000,000.
* Surabaya High Court Decision No. 51/PDT/1999/PT.SBY is '''NULL AND VOID'''.

=== Dismissed Claims (Reconvention) ===
* The Defendant's counterclaim in Reconvention regarding mass media defamation was '''REJECTED ENTIRELY BY THE SUPREME COURT'''.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Legal Protection for Women Against Material and Moral Losses Caused by False Marriage Promises:''' This landmark ruling reinforces Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 3191 K/Pdt/1984 in Indonesian civil law: men who exploit women using marriage promises—including enjoying S-2 educational funding and living support—cannot evade civil liability. Courts affirm dual protections: the right to recover material investments made by victims (restitution) and the right to immaterial damages for the restoration of dignity and reputation.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
; Can living expenses and graduate school tuition funded by a woman for her boyfriend be recovered if the man repudiates his marriage promise pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence?
: '''Yes, Mandatory Reimbursement.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. No. 3277 K/Pdt/2000:
* Repudiating a marriage promise after intimate romantic relations is qualified as an Unlawful Act (Tort) ''ex'' Article 1365 of the Civil Code because it violates community norms of decency and propriety.
* A man who repudiates a marriage promise must reimburse (make restitution for) all expenses incurred by the woman to support his living costs and graduate studies (S-2) during the relationship.
* In addition to material expense reimbursement, the man is ordered to pay reputational restoration damages (''in casu'' Rp 10,000,000), the sum of which judges are authorized to determine ''ex aequo et bono''.

== Overview ==
Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 330 K/TUN/2001 dated May 10, 2002, establishes fundamental State Administrative Court procedure jurisprudence regarding statute of limitations (*kedaluwarsa* / lawsuit time limits): Because the objects of the lawsuit (Building Use Rights / *HGB* and Freehold Title / *SHM* certificates) were issued on average around 1987, whereas the lawsuit was only filed at the Bandung State Administrative Court on January 26, 2000, the lawsuit has exceeded the 90-day time limit stipulated under Article 55 of Law No. 5 of 1986. Consequently, the appellate *Judex Facti* reasoning dismissing the lawsuit on the merits must be annulled and replaced with a ruling declaring the Plaintiffs' lawsuit inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard*).

== Case Background ==
The Original Plaintiffs / Petitioners for Cassation (1. Adang Effendi, 2. Layim Adipraja, 3. Ny. Omi Tewi Adiwiria, 4. Ny. Nani Kalni Adipraja, 5. Hadis Surtana, 6. Achmad Memed, 7. Sapri, 8. Tata Setiawan, 9. Piping Dana Wiria, 10. Otong, 11. H. Soearli, 12. Odjh Huraedji, 13. Hj. Kona'ah, 14. Oting — substitute heirs of Nji Mas Siti Aminah / Nji Mas Entjeh / Osah) filed a lawsuit at the Bandung State Administrative Court against Defendant I (Head of the Land Office of Bandung Regency) and Intervention Defendant II (PT Adhi Dharma Bumi Indonesia Indah / certificate holders).

The object of the lawsuit sought the annulment of State Administrative Decrees in the form of Building Use Rights Certificate (HGB) No. 37/Cibeureum Village (covering 32,550 m² in the name of PT Adhi Dharma Bumi Indonesia Indah, later subdivided into 92 HGB certificates Nos. 41 to 132/Cibeureum Urban Village) as well as Freehold Title Certificates (SHM) Nos. 3365, 1862, 2060, etc., issued over land formerly under *Eigendom Verponding* Right No. 3323, parcel 50, covering 64,394 m² in Cibeureum Urban Village, South Cimahi Sub-District, Bandung Regency.

The Bandung State Administrative Court (Decision No. 04/G/2000/PTUN-BDG dated July 20, 2000) granted the Plaintiffs' lawsuit in part. However, the Jakarta State Administrative High Court (Decision No. 05/B/2001/PT.TUN.JKT dated February 19, 2001) annulled the Bandung State Administrative Court judgment and independently adjudicated by rejecting the Plaintiffs' lawsuit in its entirety. Dissatisfied with the Jakarta State Administrative High Court ruling, the Plaintiffs filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The cassation arguments are well-founded because the *Judex Facti* (Jakarta State Administrative High Court) committed an error in applying the law in its legal reasoning.
# The *Judex Facti* held that the Plaintiffs failed to substantiate their claims, requiring the lawsuit to be dismissed on the merits. Such reasoning cannot be sustained because the objects of the lawsuit (the certificates) were issued on average around 1987, whereas the lawsuit was only filed at the Bandung State Administrative Court on January 26, 2000.
# Consequently, the filing of the lawsuit exceeded the 90-day time limit prescribed under Article 55 of Law No. 5 of 1986 on State Administrative Courts.
# Therefore, the exception raised by Intervention Defendant II must be accepted, and the Plaintiffs' lawsuit must be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard*).
# Legal Principle: "Because the objects of the lawsuit were issued on average around 1987, whereas the lawsuit was filed at the Bandung State Administrative Court on January 26, 2000, it has exceeded the 90-day time limit stipulated under Article 55 of Law No. 5 of 1986."

* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioners for Cassation: 1. ADANG EFFENDI, 2. LAYIM ADIPRAJA, 3. NY. OMI TEWI ADIWIRIA, 4. NY. NANI KALNI ADIPRAJA, 5. HADIS SURTANA, 6. ACHMAD MEMED, 7. SAPRI, 8. TATA SETIAWAN, 9. PIPING DANA WIRIA, 10. OTONG, 11. H. SOEARLI, 12. ODJH HURAEDJI, 13. HJ. KONA'AH, 14. OTING; Annulling the Jakarta State Administrative High Court decision dated February 19, 2001, No. 05/B/2001/PT.TUN.JKT, which upheld the Bandung State Administrative Court decision dated July 20, 2000, No. 04/G/2000/PTUN-BDG; and Independently Adjudicating: IN EXCEPTION: Accepting the exception of Intervention Defendant II; IN THE PRINCIPAL CASE: Declaring the Plaintiffs' lawsuit inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard*); Ordering the Petitioners for Cassation to pay all court costs across all levels of jurisdiction, with cassation costs assessed at Rp 200,000 (two hundred thousand rupiahs). *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court on Friday, May 10, 2002, by Ny. Hj. Emin Aminah Achadiat, S.H. [Presiding Judge], Ny. Hj. Chairani A. Wani, S.H., and H. Benjamin Mangkoedilaga, S.H. [Associate Justices]).*

== Overview ==
Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 334 K/AG/2005 dated February 22, 2006, establishes important Islamic inheritance jurisprudence regarding formal procedural requirements for inheritance lawsuits: "Because both the substitute heirs and the heirs being replaced have passed away, the exact time of death of each must be clearly stated both in the statement of claim and in the court's factual findings (*konstatering*). If not, the lawsuit must be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO) for being vague (*obscuur libel*)."

== Case Background ==
The Propositus / Original Heir ([Deceased]) passed away in 1976 and during his lifetime contracted three marriages:

* First wife (Dg. Tija) gave birth to a son named [Party B] (who predeceased him, leaving behind wife [Party C] and two children: [Heir] and [Heir]);
* Second wife (Dg. Lu'mu) gave birth to a son named H. [Party A] (Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation);
* Third wife (Dg. Puji) gave birth to four children: Bahar, Sugi, Haris, and Said (Plaintiffs IV to VII).

The Plaintiffs ([Party C], [Heir], [Heir], Bahar, Sugi, Haris, and Said) filed a lawsuit against [Party A] at the Makassar Religious Court concerning the unilateral control and sale of 8 land parcels constituting the estate of the late [Deceased] in Makassar. The Makassar Religious Court (Decision No. 261/Pdt.G/2003/PA.Mks. dated September 10, 2003) granted the Plaintiffs' lawsuit in part. The Makassar High Religious Court (Decision No. 114/Pdt.G/2003/PTA.Mks. dated July 6, 2004) upheld the Makassar Religious Court judgment. The Defendant ([Party A]) filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The *Judex Facti* (Makassar Religious Court and Makassar High Religious Court) erred in applying the law / exceeded their judicial authority.
# Neither the factual foundation (*posita*) of the claim nor the court's factual findings (*konstatering*) revealed the year in which [Party B] passed away; if [Party B] predeceased the propositus [Deceased] (before 1976), positioning [Party B]'s children ([Heir] and [Heir]) as substitute heirs (*ahli waris pengganti*) is correct (entitling them to a 21/240 share).
# Conversely, if [Party B] was still alive at the time the propositus [Deceased] passed away in 1976, [Party B] was a direct heir, meaning his children inherited his share from him (yielding a 42/240 share rather than 21/240).
# The *Judex Facti* erred in adjudicating based on uncertain status regarding whether [Party B] was a direct heir or whether his children acted as substitute heirs; the decisive factor is whether [Party B] was alive when the propositus [Deceased] passed away in 1976.
# Because the date of death of the heirs or substitute heirs was not clearly stated in the claim or the court's findings, the lawsuit is deemed vague and must be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).

* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation: [Party A]; Annulling the Makassar High Religious Court decision dated July 6, 2004, No. 114/Pdt.G/2003/PTA.Mks. and the Makassar Religious Court decision dated September 10, 2003, No. 261/Pdt.G/2003/PA.Mks.; and Independently Adjudicating: Declaring the Plaintiffs' lawsuit inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard*); and ordering the Respondents for Cassation to pay court costs across all levels of jurisdiction, with cassation costs assessed at Rp 500,000 (five hundred thousand rupiahs). *(Decided in the deliberation meeting of the Supreme Court on Wednesday, January 18, 2006, and pronounced in an open session on Wednesday, February 22, 2006, by Drs. H. Andi Syamsu Alam, S.H., M.H. [Junior Chairman of the Supreme Court / Presiding Judge], Drs. H. Habiburrahman, M.Hum., and Dr. H. Abdul Manan, S.H., S.IP., M.Hum. [Associate Justices]).*

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:3428K PDT 1985
wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 3428 K/Pdt/1985}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 3428 K/Pdt/1985''' (dated February 26, 1990 / deliberation on February 5, 1990) is a fundamental civil evidentiary law jurisprudence precedent establishing vital rules concerning the legal standing and evidentiary value of out-of-court written statements compared to sworn witness testimony given in open court pursuant to Article 1895 of the Civil Code / Articles 171–172 of the HIR.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established a primary legal principle:

* '''Out-of-Court Statements Do Not Constitute Courtroom Witness Testimony:''' A written statement or acknowledgment executed outside of a court hearing (such as a statement made before the Police / ''Kosek Polri'') '''cannot be equated with sworn witness testimony given in open court''', and therefore possesses no binding evidentiary value (''bindende bewijskracht'') to prove kinship affiliation (''sekaum'') and rights over high ancestral property (''harta pusaka tinggi'').

Where the Padang High Court granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit and annulled the Koto Baru District Court decision based solely on exhibits P.3 through P.5 (police statements) treated as binding proof, the Supreme Court held that the High Court misapplied the law of evidence. Witness testimonies in open court failed to establish that the Plaintiff ([Party A] ''gelar'' Datuk Rajo Kuaso) and Defendant I ([Party B]) belonged to the same lineage, shared ancestral property, and shared burial grounds under Minangkabau customary law.

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioners for Cassation ([Party B], ''et al.''), annulled Padang High Court Decision No. 30/G/B/K/T/1985/PT.PDG dated March 14, 1985, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by affirming Koto Baru District Court Decision No. 33/G/B/K/T/1983/PN.Kbr dated November 5, 1984, which dismissed the Plaintiff's lawsuit entirely.

|}

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Evidentiary Weight of Out-of-Court Unsworn Statements vs. Courtroom Witness Testimony (Articles 1867, 1895 Civil Code / Articles 164, 171–172 HIR) ===
''Can a written statement or acknowledgment executed by parties outside of court (such as at a police station / Kosek Polri) be classified and evaluated by a court as binding witness testimony (''bindende bewijskracht'')?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Cannot Be Equated / Non-Binding.'''

Written statements executed outside of court possess value merely as private documents (''onderhands geschrift''). Such documents cannot be equated with witness testimony (''getuigenbewijs'') mandated by civil procedural law to be delivered under oath during open court proceedings. An appellate court that relies upon out-of-court statements as primary witness evidence commits an error in applying the law of evidence (''foutieve toepassing van het bewijsrecht'').

=== 2. Burden of Proof for Kinship Affiliation and High Ancestral Property Under Minangkabau Customary Law (Article 163 HIR / Article 1865 Civil Code) ===
A plaintiff asserting a shared lineage, common ancestral property, and shared burial grounds with a defendant bears the burden of proving blood ties or maternal lineages (''ranji'') lawfully through sworn witnesses in open court proceedings. Where trial witnesses fail to establish such blood ties and genealogical records do not substantiate shared lineage, lawsuits seeking to invalidate grants or sales of high ancestral property must be dismissed.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (''Judex Juris'' / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Padang High Court (Decision No. 30/G/B/K/T/1985/PT.PDG) err in applying civil evidentiary law (''foutieve toepassing van het bewijsrecht'') by evaluating Exhibits P.3 through P.5 (police station statements) as binding witness testimony to overturn the Koto Baru District Court decision?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. Padang High Court misapplied the law. Out-of-court written statements cannot be equated with sworn testimony in open court. The Supreme Court granted [Party B] ''et al.''’s cassation petition, annulled Padang High Court's decision, and independently adjudicated by affirming Koto Baru District Court's ruling dismissing the Plaintiff's lawsuit entirely.

=== Question of Fact (''Judex Facti'' / Koto Baru District Court & Padang High Court) ===
Verification of claims regarding shared lineage between [Party A] ''gelar'' Datuk Rajo Kuaso and [Party B] in Bawah Duku, Koto Baru, Kubung, Solok; inspection of disputed properties comprising fish pond land Sub A measuring 235 m<sup>2</sup> and orchard land Sub B measuring 1,070 m<sup>2</sup> in Guguk Dama, Koto Baru; examination of Grant Deed No. 24/PPAT/1983 and Sale Deed No. 73/PPAT/1982; preparation of Exhibits P.2 and P.4 at the Kubung Police Sector; and examination of 10 Plaintiff witnesses and 7 Defendant witnesses during Koto Baru District Court hearings.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''HIR (''Herziene Inlandsch Reglement''):''' Article 164 (Civil Modes of Proof), Articles 171, 172 (Requirements for Sworn Witness Testimony in Open Court).
* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata / BW):''' Articles 1867, 1895 (Documentary and Witness Evidence).
* '''Minangkabau Customary Law:''' Provisions concerning Head of Clan Managers (''Mamak Kepala Waris''), Allotted Customary Land (''Ganggam Bauntuk''), and Clan High Ancestral Property Rights.
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 1 of 1950 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation and Independent Adjudication Authority.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* '''Doctrine of Courtroom Testimony Validity:''' Only oral statements delivered by witnesses under oath during open court proceedings satisfy the legal qualification of witness evidence.
* '''Established Precedent on Out-of-Court Statements:''' Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 3428 K/Pdt/1985 serves as a landmark decision establishing that private out-of-court statements cannot replace courtroom witness testimony and possess no binding evidentiary force.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* Exhibits P.3 through P.5 are '''PROVEN TO BE MERELY OUT-OF-COURT WRITTEN STATEMENTS''' lacking validity as courtroom witness testimony.
* The Plaintiff ([Party A]) is '''PROVEN NOT TO SHARE LINEAGE OR ANCESTRAL PROPERTY''' with Defendant I ([Party B]).
* Padang High Court Decision No. 30/G/B/K/T/1985/PT.PDG is '''NULL AND VOID'''.
* Koto Baru District Court Decision No. 33/G/B/K/T/1983/PN.Kbr dated November 5, 1984, dismissing the Plaintiff's lawsuit is '''AFFIRMED BY THE SUPREME COURT'''.

=== Annulled High Court Reasoning ===
* Padang High Court considerations holding that Plaintiff and Defendant I shared lineage based on police station statements were '''ANNULLED ENTIRELY BY THE SUPREME COURT'''.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Legal Certainty in Civil Evidence Regarding Customary Claims via Private Instruments:''' This landmark ruling establishes strict civil procedural certainty in Indonesia: litigants disputing ancestral property or customary rights cannot rely on statements executed before non-judicial authorities (such as police stations or village officials) to establish kinship status or invalidate property transactions. Procedural law demands direct proof via sworn witnesses in court to ensure material truth.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
; Do written statements executed outside of court (such as at a police station) possess binding evidentiary force equivalent to courtroom witnesses pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence?
: '''No.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. No. 3428 K/Pdt/1985:
:* Written statements executed outside of court '''cannot be equated with witness testimony delivered under oath in open court'''.
:* Such statements represent merely private out-of-court documents lacking binding evidentiary force (''bindende bewijskracht'') to prove land rights or customary kinship affiliation.
:* An appellate court granting a lawsuit based solely on out-of-court statements commits an error in applying evidentiary law, resulting in Supreme Court annulment.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Judicial Review (*Peninjauan Kembali / PK*) Decision No. 34 PK/PID.HAM.AD HOC/2007 dated March 14, 2008, acquits [Defendant] (Former Deputy Commander of the Pro-Integration Fighters / PPI) of all charges of gross human rights violations in the form of crimes against humanity. The Supreme Court affirmed that clashes or attacks at the residence of Manuel Viegas Carrascalao on April 17, 1999, constituted spontaneous riots devoid of widespread or systematic planning, and that the Petitioner for PK, as a civilian superior, lacked *de jure* or *de facto* effective authority (*chain of command*) to prevent or halt the actions of militia mobs belonging to other factions (such as Besi Merah Putih / BMP).

== Case Background ==

The Petitioner for PK / Convict ([Defendant]) was charged with omission (*omissions*) regarding the militia mob attack on the residence of Manuel Viegas Carrascalao in Dili on April 17, 1999, which resulted in the deaths of 12 civilians following a mass rally by PAM Swakarsa. The Ad Hoc Human Rights Court at the Central Jakarta District Court sentenced the Petitioner to 10 years of imprisonment (Decision No. 04/PID.HAM/AD.HOC/2002/PN.JKT.PST). The Ad Hoc High Human Rights Court of Jakarta reduced the sentence to 5 years of imprisonment (Decision No. 02/PID.HAM/AD.HOC/2004/PT.DKI). However, upon cassation, the Supreme Court annulled the appellate ruling and reinstated the 10-year prison sentence (Decision No. 06 K/PID.HAM AD HOC/2005). The Petitioner filed for Judicial Review (*PK*) incorporating new witness testimonies (*novum* from Eduardo De Yesus, Boa Ventura, Victor Pilipe, and Dominggus Bondia) alongside the acquittal ruling of former East Timor Governor Abilio Osorio Soares as a *novum*.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# Disputes, clashes, or riots occurring spontaneously without detailed planning do not fulfill the elements of an organizational policy to commit widespread or systematic crimes against humanity.
# Individuals or groups involved or participating in disputes, clashes, or riots cannot be categorized as "civilian populations."
# The criminal responsibility of a civilian superior for the acts of subordinates committing crimes against humanity (*omission*) must be grounded upon the existence of *de jure* or *de facto* authority possessing a genuinely effective leadership hierarchy (*chain of command*), akin to military hierarchies. The Petitioner for PK, acting as a civilian superior, did not hold effective *de jure/de facto* authority over members of opposing militia factions (BMP) carrying out the attack.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the petition for judicial review from Petitioner for PK [Defendant]; Annulling the Supreme Court Decision No. 06 K/PID.HAM AD HOC/2005 jo. Ad Hoc High Human Rights Court Decision No. 02/PID.HAM/AD.HOC/2004/PT.DKI jo. Ad Hoc Human Rights Court at Central Jakarta District Court Decision No. 04/PID.HAM/AD.HOC/2002/PN.JKT.PST; and Re-Adjudicating: (1) Declaring that Petitioner for PK [Defendant] is not legally and convincingly proven guilty of committing the criminal offense charged by the Public Prosecutor; (2) Acquitting him of all charges; (3) Restoring the Convict's rights in capacity, position, honor, and dignity (rehabilitation); (4) Charging procedural costs across all levels of jurisdiction to the State.

== Overview ==
Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 353 K/AG/2005 dated July 7, 2006, establishes fundamental Islamic civil jurisprudence regarding out-of-court inheritance distribution determinations (*P3HP*): An out-of-court inheritance distribution deed (P3HP Deed) ex Article 107 of Law No. 7 of 1989 (as amended by Law No. 3 of 2006) must list all legal heirs. If it fails to do so, such a deed can be challenged and declared legally void (*batal demi hukum*) on the grounds of manifest error.

== Case Background ==
The Original Plaintiffs (Franciscus [Party] / [Child], [Child] [Party] / [Child], and [Child] Br [Party] / [Child]) are the children born from the lawful marriage of [Deceased father] [Party] (SGT [Party]) alias [Party] Gun Tjun and Angela alias Lie Wan Njong, solemnized on September 26, 1951, in Medan. On June 7, 2003, SGT [Party] passed away. When seeking to administer the late father's estate, the Plaintiffs discovered that the Medan Religious Court had issued an Inheritance Distribution Deed Determination No. 11/PPPHP/2003/PA.Mdn. dated June 16, 2003, designating Defendant I (Hj. [Party C]), Defendant II ([Party A]), and Defendant III ([Party B]) as the sole heirs of SGT [Party] based on Marriage Certificate Extract No. 115/IV/1987 from the Office of Religious Affairs (*KUA*) of Sunggal Sub-District.

Upon investigation at KUA Sunggal (Letter No. K211PW/01/106/2003), it was revealed that Marriage Certificate Extract No. 115/IV/1987 did not belong to SGT [Party] and Hj. [Party C], but rather to Budy Caroko and Sridarmi. The Plaintiffs subsequently filed a lawsuit seeking the annulment of the P3HP Deed at the Medan Religious Court. The Medan Religious Court (Decision No. 557/Pdt.G/2004/PA.Mdn. dated November 10, 2004) granted the Plaintiffs' lawsuit and declared Determination No. 11/PPPHP/2003/PA.Mdn. to be without legal force. However, the Medan High Religious Court (Decision No. 19/Pdt.G/2005/PTA.Mdn. dated March 7, 2005) annulled the Medan Religious Court judgment and ruled that the Religious Court lacked jurisdiction. The Plaintiffs filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The Medan High Religious Court erred in applying the law, because determinations concerning out-of-court inheritance property distribution fall within the judicial product of the Religious Courts pursuant to Article 107 of Law No. 7 of 1989.
# In the event of a manifest error within such a determination, it can be declared devoid of legal force. Therefore, the Medan Religious Court possessed the jurisdiction to examine and adjudicate the a quo case.
# Medan Religious Court Determination No. 11/PPPHP/2003/PA.Mdn. dated June 16, 2003, determined that the sole heirs of SGT Agus [Party] were the Defendants. wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 3574 K/Pdt/2000}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 3574 K/Pdt/2000''' (dated September 5, 2002) is a fundamental civil law and Islamic inheritance law jurisprudence precedent establishing two vital rules concerning the limitation of heirs' liability for a decedent's debts and the legal protection of a wife's separate property (''harta bawaan'') from attachment over a husband's debts.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established two primary legal principles:

# '''Heirs' Liability Limited to the Estate Value:''' An heir's liability for a decedent's debts is strictly limited to the amount or value of the decedent's estate (pursuant to Article 175 paragraph (2) of the Compilation of Islamic Law / KHI).
# '''Protection of a Wife's Separate Property from Attachments over Husband's Debts:''' A wife's separate property (''harta bawaan'') cannot be attached as collateral for her deceased husband's debts, as separate property does not constitute the deceased husband's estate.

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation (Ny. [Party B]), annulled Central Java High Court in Semarang Decision No. 586/Pdt/1999/PT.Smg dated February 28, 2000, ''jo.'' Magelang District Court Decision No. 28/Pdt.G/1998/PN.Mgl dated June 15, 1999, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by declaring the Plaintiff's lawsuit in Convention Inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO), ordering the lifting of the attachment (''sita jaminan'') over the land and house at [address removed], Magelang, and declaring the Counterclaim in Reconvention Inadmissible (NO).

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Limitations on Heirs' Liability for a Decedent's Debts / Obligations (Article 175 paragraph (2) of the Compilation of Islamic Law / KHI) ===
''Are heirs (wife and children) obligated to pay off all debts of a deceased debtor using their own personal or separate property if the decedent's estate is insufficient or unspecified in the lawsuit?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Limited Liability (''Intra Vires Hereditatis'').'''
Pursuant to Article 175 paragraph (2) of the Compilation of Islamic Law (KHI), an heir's liability for a decedent's debt is strictly limited to the amount or value of the estate left by the decedent. Heirs cannot be compelled to pay a decedent's debts exceeding the net value of the decedent's estate.

=== 2. Legal Protection of a Wife's Separate Property Against Attachment for Husband's Debts (Article 35 paragraph (2) & Article 36 of Law No. 1 of 1974 on Marriage) ===
''Can land and a house acquired by a wife prior to marriage (''harta bawaan'') be attached or sold by creditors to settle business debts incurred by her late husband?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Cannot Be Attached.'''
Separate property acquired by a wife prior to marriage remains under her exclusive control and ownership. Such property neither constitutes joint marital property (''harta bersama'') nor forms part of her late husband's estate. Consequently, conservatory attachments (''conservatoir beslag'') over a wife's separate property to satisfy a late husband's debts are null and void by operation of law and must be lifted by the court.

=== 3. Formal Defect in Petitum for Decedent Debt Lawsuits (''Obscuur Libel'' / Execution Defect) ===
A lawsuit demanding settlement of a late husband's debts from heirs without specifying and detailing the exact amount or value of the decedent's estate is classified as vague and defective, requiring courts to declare the lawsuit '''Inadmissible''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Semarang High Court (Decision No. 586/Pdt/1999/PT.Smg) and Magelang District Court (Decision No. 28/Pdt.G/1998/PN.Mgl) err in applying the law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') by ordering heirs to pay a late decedent's debt of Rp 114,500,000 and declaring valid an attachment over a wife's separate property home (SHM No. 348, [address removed], Magelang), whereas Article 175(2) KHI limits heirs' liability to estate value and Article 35(2) of Law No. 1 of 1974 protects separate property?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. The ''Judex Facti'' misapplied the law. The Supreme Court granted Ny. [Party B]'s cassation petition, annulled the lower court decisions, and independently adjudicated by declaring the Plaintiff's lawsuit Inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO) and ordering the lifting of the attachment over the Petitioner's separate property.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Magelang District Court & Semarang High Court) ===
Verification of the project cooperation/loan agreement dated October 2, 1996, amounting to Rp 114,500,000 between [Party A] and the late Singgih Sumarsono, S.H.; verification of the death of Singgih Sumarsono, S.H. during court proceedings; verification of SHM No. 348 in South Rejowinangun Sub-district in the name of Ny. [Party B] acquired prior to marriage with the decedent; and verification of the Magelang District Court Attachment Minutes dated December 16, 1998 (No. 28/Pdt.G/1998/PN.Mgl).

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''Compilation of Islamic Law (KHI):''' Article 175 paragraph (2) (Heirs' Liability Limited to Decedent Estate Value).
* '''Law No. 1 of 1974 on Marriage:''' Article 35 paragraph (2) (Separate Property Under Respective Control) & Article 36 paragraph (2) (Exclusive Rights Over Separate Property).
* '''HIR (Herziene Inlandsch Reglement):''' Article 227 (Conditions for Conservatory Attachment / ''Conservatoir Beslag'').
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 35 of 1999 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation and Independent Adjudication Authority.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* '''Doctrine of Limited Heirs' Liability (''Intra Vires Hereditatis''):''' Heirs bear no personal liability for a decedent's debts using personal assets. Decedents' debts are satisfied exclusively out of the decedent's estate pool (''boedel waris'').
* '''Doctrine of Separate Property Protection (Separation of Ante-Nuptial Property):''' Separate property acquired prior to marriage cannot be attached to satisfy obligations or debts incurred by a spouse without the separate property owner's explicit consent.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* The house and land under SHM No. 348 at [address removed], Magelang, are '''PROVEN TO BE THE SEPARATE PROPERTY OF NY. [Party B] (DEFENDANT I)''' acquired prior to marriage with the late Singgih Sumarsono, S.H.
* The wife's separate property is '''PROVEN NOT TO CONSTITUTE PART OF THE LATE HUSBAND'S ESTATE'''.
* Heirs' liability for the decedent's debts is '''PROVEN TO BE LIMITED SOLELY TO THE VALUE OF THE DECEDENT'S ESTATE''' ''ex'' Article 175 paragraph (2) KHI.
* The Plaintiff's lawsuit ''petitum'' is '''PROVEN FORMALLY DEFECTIVE''' for failing to clarify the decedent's estate value and targeting separate property.
* Semarang High Court Decision No. 586/Pdt/1999/PT.Smg and Magelang District Court Decision No. 28/Pdt.G/1998/PN.Mgl are '''NULL AND VOID'''.
* The Plaintiff's ([Party A]) lawsuit is declared '''INADMISSIBLE''' (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO).
* The attachment executed on December 16, 1998, over land/house SHM No. 348 is '''ORDERED TO BE LIFTED'''.

=== Annulled Judex Facti Rulings ===
* Lower court rulings ordering Defendants I through V to pay the loan and validating attachments over Defendant I's separate property were '''ANNULLED ENTIRELY BY THE SUPREME COURT'''.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Importance of Inventorying Net Decedents' Estates Before Filing Debt Lawsuits:''' This landmark ruling establishes a crucial civil procedural principle for creditors in Indonesia: when a debtor passes away, creditors cannot simply sue heirs and attach arbitrary assets occupied by a grieving family. Creditors must investigate and prove precisely what constitutes the net estate (''boedel waris'') of the late debtor. Targeting separate property or personal assets of heirs results in fatal formal defects, leading to lawsuit dismissal (NO) and the lifting of attachments.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
; Can a wife's separate property be attached to pay her late husband's debts, and what are the limits of heirs' liability for a decedent's debts pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence?
: '''Cannot Be Attached & Limited Liability.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. No. 3574 K/Pdt/2000:
* A wife's separate property (''harta bawaan'') '''cannot be attached as collateral for her late husband's debts''', as separate property does not form part of the late husband's estate.
* An heir's liability for a decedent's debt is '''strictly limited to the amount or value of the decedent's estate''' pursuant to Article 175 paragraph (2) of the Compilation of Islamic Law (KHI).
* Creditor lawsuits targeting a wife's separate property without clarifying estate value limits contain formal defects, prompting the Supreme Court to annul appellate rulings and independently adjudicate by declaring the lawsuit Inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'' / NO) and ordering the lifting of attachments.

wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 3597 K/Pdt/1985}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 3597 K/Pdt/1985''' (dated May 7, 1987 / deliberation on April 14, 1987) is a fundamental land law and contract law jurisprudence precedent establishing vital rules concerning the invalidity (''null and void'' / ''batal demi hukum'') of the legal institution of Sale and Purchase with a Right of Repurchase (''recht van wederinkoop'' ''ex'' Article 1519 of the Civil Code / BW) regarding land and houses under the Basic Agrarian Law (UUPA No. 5 of 1960) and Customary Law.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established a primary legal principle:

* '''Incompatibility of Sale and Purchase with a Right of Repurchase Regarding Land/Houses:''' "A sale and purchase with a right of repurchase constitutes a form of contract pursuant to Article 1519 ''et seq.'' of the Civil Code, whereas the sale and purchase of land and houses pursuant to the Basic Agrarian Law is governed by Customary Law (''Hukum Adat''), which does not recognize the form of sale and purchase with a right of repurchase. Therefore, the plaintiff's and defendant's agreement in this case is null and void (''batal demi hukum'')."

Where a Deed of Sale and Purchase (Deed No. 51), a Deed of Vacating Agreement (Deed No. 52), and a Deed of Right of Repurchase Agreement (Deed No. 53) were executed on the same date (September 12, 1983) before a notary, the Supreme Court qualified the legal relationship not as a valid land/house transaction, but as a disguised debt-transaction secured by collateral (''titip jaminan''). Because the true legal relationship was a debt-obligation and the repurchase agreement was null and void, the Plaintiff ([Party B]) did not qualify as the lawful owner of the disputed land and house ([address removed], South Jakarta), requiring the dismissal of all claims for eviction and contractual default penalties.

The Supreme Court rejected the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation ([Party B]) and ordered him to pay court costs. Consequently, Jakarta High Court Decision No. 154/Pdt/1985/PT.DKI ''jo.'' South Jakarta District Court Decision No. 216/Pdt/G/1984/PN.JS. (which dismissed the Plaintiff's lawsuit entirely) was affirmed upon cassation.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Legal Status of Sale and Purchase with a Right of Repurchase (''Recht van Wederinkoop'' ''ex'' Article 1519 of the Civil Code) Following the Enactment of UUPA No. 5 of 1960 ===
''Is an agreement for the sale and purchase of land and/or houses containing a clause granting the seller the right of repurchase (''wederinkoop'' ''ex'' Article 1519 Civil Code) valid and enforceable under Indonesian National Agrarian Law?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Null and Void (''Batal Demi Hukum'').'''
Pursuant to Article 5 of the Basic Agrarian Law (UUPA No. 5 of 1960), Indonesian land law is based on Customary Law (''Hukum Adat''). Under Customary Law, land transactions adhere to the principle of clear and cash (''terang dan tunai''), which does not recognize sales with a right of repurchase. Consequently, applying the institution of sale with a right of repurchase ''ex'' Article 1519 of the Civil Code to land and houses is null and void (''nietig van rechtswege'').

=== 2. Legal Qualification of Disguised Debt-Secured Transactions (Pawn-Like Disguise / Sham Sales) ===
Where a land/house transaction is executed as an absolute sale deed but is accompanied simultaneously by a repurchase agreement and a vacating agreement, courts must pierce the legal veil (''piercing the legal veil'') to determine the true intent of the parties (''partij bedoeling''). Where the substance of the legal relationship is a loan of money or commercial debt secured by a land certificate, the transaction constitutes a debt obligation secured by collateral, not a genuine sale.

=== 3. Limits of Cassation Review over Evidentiary Findings (''Judex Juris'' vs. ''Judex Facti'') ===
Evaluations of evidentiary findings concerning whether a transaction constitutes a genuine sale or a debt obligation represent factual appreciations (''feitelijke waardering'') falling within the exclusive authority of the ''judex facti'' and cannot be reviewed during cassation proceedings.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (''Judex Juris'' / Supreme Court) ===
Did a land/house sale and purchase agreement accompanied by a right of repurchase ''ex'' Article 1519 of the Civil Code remain valid under Indonesian land law following the enactment of UUPA No. 5 of 1960?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Invalid and null and void. Indonesian land law under UUPA is governed by Customary Law, which does not recognize sales with a right of repurchase. The Supreme Court rejected the Petitioner's cassation petition and affirmed the ''Judex Facti'' decision.

=== Question of Fact (''Judex Facti'' / South Jakarta District Court & Jakarta High Court) ===
Verification of facts regarding the execution of Deed of Sale and Purchase No. 51, Vacating Agreement Deed No. 52, and Repurchase Agreement Deed No. 53 on September 12, 1983, before Notary Lieke L. Tukgali, S.H.; verification of commercial supply relationships for ABC syrup/soy sauce between CV Food Industrial Corp. and the Defendant; the surrender of the land/house certificate at [address removed], South Jakarta (measuring 155 m<sup>2</sup>) as debt collateral; and dismissal of the Defendant's reconvention counterclaim regarding alleged military personnel intimidation.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''Law No. 5 of 1960 on Basic Agrarian Principles (UUPA):''' Article 5 (Customary Law as the Foundation of Agrarian Law) & Rules on Land Transactions (Clear and Cash Principle).
* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata / BW):''' Articles 1519 through 1532 (Contracts of Sale with a Right of Repurchase).
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 1 of 1950 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation and Legal Review Authority.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* '''Agrarian Customary Law Doctrine (Clear and Cash):''' Land sales under customary law instantly transfer land rights in a cash and open manner. Customary law does not recognize temporary title transfers recallable via repurchase clauses.
* '''Established Precedent Prohibiting Repurchase Sales on Land:''' Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 3597 K/Pdt/1985 serves as a landmark authority prohibiting the application of Article 1519 of the Civil Code to land/house objects in Indonesia, reaffirmed in subsequent Supreme Court rulings to prevent moneylenders from unlawfully seizing debtor lands through disguised mortgages.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* The agreement for the sale and purchase with a right of repurchase over the house at [address removed], South Jakarta, is '''PROVEN NULL AND VOID''' for violating UUPA and Customary Law.
* The true legal relationship between the Plaintiff and Defendant is '''PROVEN TO BE A DEBT OBLIGATION SECURED BY COLLATERAL''', not a genuine sale.
* The Plaintiff ([Party B]) is '''PROVEN NOT TO BE THE LAWFUL OWNER''' of the disputed land and house.
* The Plaintiff's claims demanding house vacation and default penalties of Rp 500,000/month are '''DISMISSED ENTIRELY'''.
* The Petitioner's cassation petition is '''REJECTED BY THE SUPREME COURT'''.

=== Dismissed Counterclaims (Reconvention) ===
* The Defendant's / Reconvention Plaintiff's damages claim of Rp 75,000,000 alleging military personnel intimidation was '''REJECTED AS LEGALLY UNFOUNDED'''.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Legal Protection for Debtors Against Sham Sales / Disguised Collateral Transactions:''' This landmark ruling establishes robust legal protection for debtors in Indonesia: creditors or lenders cannot enforce house vacation executions relying solely on a Sale Deed executed simultaneously with a Repurchase Deed. Courts dismantle such sham sales and declare them null and void to enforce the clear-and-cash principle in National Agrarian Law.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==

:* Sales and purchases with a right of repurchase (''recht van wederinkoop'' ''ex'' Article 1519 Civil Code) concerning land and houses are '''NULL AND VOID'''.
:* Pursuant to the Basic Agrarian Law

== Overview ==

Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 359 K/Pdt/1992, dated March 10, 1994, established a civil procedural law rule concerning the validity of a statement of claim signed by legal counsel.

The Supreme Court held that a statement of claim prepared and signed by legal counsel on December 3, 1988, while the Special Power of Attorney from the plaintiff was issued only on December 15, 1988, was formally defective.

At the time the statement of claim was signed, the recipient of the power of attorney had not yet been legally authorized to act as counsel for the plaintiff. Consequently, the statement of claim was considered procedurally defective and was required to be declared inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard'' / NO).

== Executive Summary ==

The central procedural principle established in this decision is that legal counsel may not validly sign a statement of claim before the Special Power of Attorney authorizing the counsel has been granted.

The relevant dates were:

* Statement of claim signed: '''December 3, 1988'''
* Special Power of Attorney issued: '''December 15, 1988'''

Because the Special Power of Attorney post-dated the signing of the statement of claim, the counsel had no legal authority to sign the claim on December 3, 1988.

The Supreme Court therefore treated the defect as a fundamental formal defect resulting in the claim being declared inadmissible (NO).

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation, '''[Party A]''', filed a civil lawsuit against '''Drs. PHS. Marpaung''' and other parties concerning the occupation, lease, and eviction of a house located at [address removed], Central Jakarta.

The plaintiff claimed ownership of the house, which had been purchased in 1957 and was associated with HGB Certificate No. 80/Matraman. The property was occupied by the Defendant on the basis of a Housing License (SIP / Military SIP).

The Plaintiff's statement of claim was drafted and signed by legal counsel on '''December 3, 1988'''.

However, the Special Power of Attorney authorizing the legal counsel to represent the Plaintiff was issued only on '''December 15, 1988'''.

The Central Jakarta District Court, through Decision No. 04/Pdt/G/VI/1989/PN.JKT.PST, and the Jakarta High Court, through Decision No. 314/Pdt/1991/PT.DKI, rejected the claims on the merits without addressing the formal defect arising from the date of the Special Power of Attorney.

The Plaintiff subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==

=== Formal Validity of the Special Power of Attorney ===

The principal procedural issue was whether an attorney could validly sign a statement of claim dated before the creation or issuance of the Special Power of Attorney.

The Supreme Court held that the attorney's authority was limited by the date on which the Special Power of Attorney was granted.

Signing the statement of claim before that date constituted an unauthorized act of representation and resulted in a fundamental formal defect in the claim.

=== Default, Tort and Lease Termination ===

The Defendant also raised an exception concerning an obscure claim (''obscuur libel'') based on the alleged combination of default (''wanprestasi'') and tort (''perbuatan melawan hukum'' / PMH).

The Central Jakarta District Court rejected the exception, considering the alleged default and unlawful acts to be interconnected as a unified basis for termination of the lease.

== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law ===

'''Question:'''

Does a statement of claim signed by legal counsel on December 3, 1988, on the basis of a Special Power of Attorney issued on December 15, 1988, satisfy the formal validity requirements of a civil lawsuit under HIR/RBg?

'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''

No.

The Supreme Court held that the issuance date of the Special Power of Attorney strictly determined the legal authority of the attorney-in-fact.

Because the statement of claim was signed before the Special Power of Attorney was issued, the counsel had not yet been legally authorized to act on behalf of the Plaintiff.

The statement of claim therefore contained a formal procedural defect and was required to be declared inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard'' / NO).

=== Question of Fact ===

The factual matters considered in the lower courts included:

* Ownership of HGB Certificate No. 80/Matraman.
* The issuance history of Jakarta Housing Office License No. 12/61 RK.D.III.
* Kodam V Jaya SIP No. 252-4/1984.
* Evidence concerning payment of house rent.
* The occupation of the house at [address removed]

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The ''judex facti'' misapplied the law by failing to address the formal defect in the Plaintiff's authority of representation.

# The statement of claim was drafted and signed by the Plaintiff's legal counsel on '''December 3, 1988'''.

# The Special Power of Attorney authorizing the counsel was issued only on '''December 15, 1988'''.

# On December 3, 1988, the recipient of the power of attorney had therefore not yet obtained legal authority from the Plaintiff to act as counsel.

# A legal counsel who has not yet received the relevant Special Power of Attorney has no authority to sign the Plaintiff's statement of claim.

# A claim signed without proper authorization contains a fundamental formal defect.

# The appropriate procedural consequence is that the claim must be declared inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard'' / NO).

== Ruling ==

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of '''[Party A]''' and annulled Jakarta High Court Decision No. 314/Pdt/1991/PT.DKI in conjunction with Central Jakarta District Court Decision No. 04/Pdt/G/VI/1989/PN.JKT.PST.

The Supreme Court adjudicated the matter afresh as follows:

# '''In Convention: In Exception'''
## Declaring the exceptions submitted by the Defendant and Co-Defendant I inadmissible.

# '''In the Merits'''
## Declaring the Plaintiff's claim inadmissible (NO).

# '''In Reconvention'''
## Declaring the counter-claim (reconvention claim) inadmissible (NO).

# '''In Convention and Reconvention'''
## Ordering the Petitioner for Cassation / Original Plaintiff to bear the court costs across all judicial instances.

== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==

* '''Article 123 HIR / Article 147 RBg''' — provisions concerning the requirements for granting a Special Power of Attorney to represent a party's interests before the court.

* '''Supreme Court Jurisprudence''' — a Special Power of Attorney issued after a statement of claim has been filed or signed may result in the claim being procedurally invalid and subject to dismissal as inadmissible (NO).

* '''SEMA No. 1 of 1971''' — concerning requirements relating to Special Powers of Attorney.

* '''SEMA No. 6 of 1994''' — concerning requirements relating to Special Powers of Attorney.

== Evidence Status and Gaps ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* Plaintiff's statement of claim dated '''December 3, 1988'''.
* Plaintiff's Special Power of Attorney dated '''December 15, 1988'''.
* Defendant Drs. PHS. Marpaung occupied a portion of the house at [address removed]V Jaya and the Jakarta Housing Office.

=== Not Established or Not Further Considered Due to the Formal Defect ===

The merits of the lease-payment dispute and allegations concerning unlawful acts, including unauthorized alterations to the building, were not further evaluated by the Supreme Court because the claim failed on the basis of the formal procedural defect.

=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===

The source records a typographical correction issue concerning the date of the statement of claim.

The Plaintiff had previously argued that the date appearing in the replication was a typographical error. The Supreme Court, however, verified that '''December 3, 1988''' was explicitly and physically printed on the original statement of claim.

== GEO Q&A ==

'''Q: Is a statement of claim valid if it is signed by legal counsel before the issuance date of the Special Power of Attorney?'''

'''A:''' No. According to Supreme Court Decision No. 359 K/Pdt/1992, a statement of claim signed by legal counsel before the issuance date of the Special Power of Attorney contains a formal procedural defect. At the time of signing, the recipient of the power of attorney had not yet been legally authorized to represent the Plaintiff. The claim must therefore be declared inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard'' / NO).

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 35 K/Pid/2002 dated March 6, 2002, establishes fundamental jurisprudence and legal standards regarding the admissibility of cassation petitions against pre-trial (*praperadilan*) rulings and the legality of detention actions executed by Joint Connected Investigation Teams (*Tim Penyidik Koneksitas*). The Supreme Court affirmed that pre-trial rulings concerning the legality or illegality of detention executed by a Joint Connected Investigation Team in corruption cases (involving suspects holding active military status alongside civilian parties) are subject to cassation before the Supreme Court. Furthermore, the detention of corruption suspects by a Joint Connected Investigation Team under the coordination of the Attorney General is legally valid.

== Case Background ==

The Suspect, Marshal Madya (Ret.) Prof. DR. Ir. Ginanjar Kartasasmita, was tried on allegations of corruption during the formulation of a Technical Assistance Contract (TAC) between Pertamina and PT Ustraindo Petro Gas during 1992–1993, at which time the suspect served as the Minister of Mines and Energy and held active military status.

The Suspect was detained at the Attorney General's Office Detention Center (*Rutan*) starting April 6, 2001, pursuant to Detention Warrant No. Prin-052/F/FJP/04/2001 dated April 17, 2001, effective from April 9, 2001, to April 28, 2001. The Suspect filed a pre-trial application at the South Jakarta District Court. The South Jakarta District Court (Decision No. 11/Pid.Prap/2001/PN.Jak.Sel. dated May 2, 2001) granted the pre-trial application and declared the detention illegal. Dissatisfied with the pre-trial ruling, the Petitioner for Cassation (ATTORNEY GENERAL OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA cq. JUNIOR ATTORNEY GENERAL FOR SPECIAL CRIMES) filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# Pre-trial rulings regarding the legality or illegality of detention executed by a Joint Connected Investigation Team in corruption cases allegedly committed by a suspect subject to trial within the Military Justice environment alongside suspects subject to trial within the General Court environment **are subject to cassation**.
# Pursuant to Article 26 jo. Article 27 of Law No. 3 of 1971 and provisions governing connected case investigations (Article 89 of the KUHAP / Article 198 of Law No. 31 of 1997), the Attorney General as Law Enforcer and Supreme Public Prosecutor possesses the authority to direct and coordinate investigations into connected corruption cases, including establishing Joint Connected Investigation Teams (comprising elements of the Prosecutor's Office, Military Police, and Military Prosecutors) and executing detentions. Detentions executed by such Joint Connected Investigation Teams are legally valid.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation ATTORNEY GENERAL OF THE REPUBLIC OF INDONESIA cq. JUNIOR ATTORNEY GENERAL FOR SPECIAL CRIMES; Annulling the South Jakarta District Court pre-trial decision dated May 2, 2001, No. 11/Pid.Prap/2001/PN.Jak.Sel.; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Declaring the detention of Pre-Trial Petitioner / Respondent for Cassation Marshal Madya (Ret.) Prof. DR. Ir. Ginanjar Kartasasmita executed by the Joint Connected Investigation Team (pursuant to Attorney General Decree No. Kep. 141/A/JA/04/2001 dated April 9, 2001) to be **legally valid**; (2) Ordering the Respondent for Cassation / Pre-Trial Petitioner to pay court costs amounting to Rp 2,500 (two thousand five hundred rupiahs).

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 363 K/Pdt/1984, dated July 30, 1985 (pronounced August 22, 1985), established jurisprudence and commercial/maritime transport legal principles concerning the exemption of a carrier from liability for cargo damage caused by force majeure or acts of God at sea.


The Supreme Court held that a carrier cannot be held liable for compensation for damage to cargo caused by an unavoidable disaster at sea, pursuant to Article 468 paragraph (2) of the Indonesian Commercial Code (KUHD).


== Executive Summary ==


The central legal principle established in this decision is that a maritime carrier is released from liability for cargo damage if the damage results from an inevitable sea disaster (*force majeure* / act of God) and the vessel is seaworthy.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* The carrier cannot be burdened with indemnity for cargo damage caused by unavoidable perils of the sea ex Article 468 paragraph (2) KUHD.
* Proof of a severe storm (Beaufort scale 7–8) in the Atlantic Ocean for 4 days and 4 nights constitutes an act of God.
* Assessment of factual maritime disaster evidence is the authority of the *judex facti* and cannot be re-examined at the cassation level.


== Case Background ==


The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation, '''P.T. Asuransi Afia Indonesia''', filed a lawsuit claiming damages amounting to US $ 104,317.00 against the Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation, '''P.T. Djakarta Lloyd''', concerning damage to cargo (contractors heavy equipment) belonging to Interimco Trading Co. Ltd. transported by the vessel *M.V. Hadji Agus Salim* from Canada to Indonesia.


The Plaintiff brought the lawsuit based on subrogation rights after paying an insurance claim under Subrogation Form No. 100568 dated July 19, 1978.


The Defendant contested the claim, arguing that the damage occurred due to a major storm of Beaufort scale 7–8 in the Atlantic Ocean lasting 4 days and 4 nights (*force majeure* / act of God) and that the vessel was seaworthy under Article 468 paragraph (2) KUHD.


Central Jakarta District Court Decision No. 64/1979 G and Jakarta High Court Decision No. 325/1983/PT.Perd rejected the Plaintiff's claim in its entirety. The Plaintiff subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.


== Claims, Evidence and Source Mapping ==

| 363K_PDT_1984.pdf
|}


== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Force Majeure / Act of God in Maritime Transport ===


The primary issue was whether a carrier is responsible for cargo damage caused by a Beaufort scale 7–8 ocean storm in the Atlantic that caused severe rolling and dislodgement of cargo from its lashings.


The legal rule established is that if the carrier proves that the damage arose from a maritime disaster that could not be prevented or avoided by the master and crew exercising maximum effort (*good seamanship*), the carrier is released from the obligation of indemnification.


=== Seaworthiness vs. Carrier Negligence ===


The issue evaluated whether the carrier was negligent in safeguarding the cargo. A vessel equipped with official maritime safety documents (Certificate of Nationality, Certificate of Perfection, Construction Safety Certificate) and proper stowage is deemed seaworthy, rendering damage from extreme storm turbulence a force majeure event.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the *Judex Facti* (Central Jakarta District Court & Jakarta High Court) misapply Article 468 paragraph (2) KUHD and international maritime transport regulations (Hague Rules) in releasing the Defendant from liability?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


No. The *Judex Facti* did not misapply the law. Exemption from compensation under Article 468 paragraph (2) KUHD was fully in accordance with applicable law.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / District & High Courts) ===


Evaluation of physical evidence including storm velocity and scale (Beaufort 7–8), vessel Logbook Extract (T-1), Marine Note of Protest (T-4), Survey Report by Toplis & Harding of Canada Ltd. (P-11), and vessel seaworthiness certificates (T-6, T-7, T-8, T-9).


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The *Judex Facti* did not misapply the law. Pursuant to Article 468 paragraph (2) KUHD, a carrier cannot be burdened with indemnity for cargo damage caused by unavoidable maritime disasters.
# It was proven that *M.V. Hadji Agus Salim* was in a seaworthy condition and that the damage was caused by extreme gale-force storms in the Atlantic Ocean constituting an act of God.
# Evaluation of evidentiary findings falls within the exclusive domain of the *Judex Facti* and cannot be examined in cassation proceedings.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court rejected the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation ('''P.T. Asuransi Afia Indonesia''') and ordered the Petitioner for Cassation to pay cassation court costs amounting to Rp 20,000.— (twenty thousand rupiahs).


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Commercial Code (KUHD) Article 468 paragraph (2):''' The carrier is obliged to compensate for damage caused to cargo, unless the carrier proves that the damage was caused by an unavoidable or unpreventable disaster.
* '''Commercial Code (KUHD) Article 506:''' Definition and function of the Bill of Lading (*Kognosemen*) as proof of receipt of goods.
* '''International Convention / Hague Rules (1924) Article IV Section 2:''' Exemption of carriers from liability for perils, dangers, and accidents of the sea.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* P.T. Asuransi Afia Indonesia paid a claim of $ 104,317.00 and received subrogation rights from Interimco Trading Co. Ltd. (P-1).
* Cargo transport (contractors heavy equipment) utilizing *M.V. Hadji Agus Salim* owned by P.T. Djakarta Lloyd (P-3/T-5).
* The vessel encountered strong gale storms of Beaufort scale 7–8 for 4 days and 4 nights (December 21–24, 1977) in the Atlantic Ocean, causing cargo to break loose and sustain damage (T-1, T-3, T-4).
* The vessel *M.V. Hadji Agus Salim* satisfied official seaworthiness requirements (T-6, T-7, T-8, T-9).


=== Not Established / Unproven ===


* The Plaintiff failed to prove any negligence or intentional fault on the part of the Defendant or the ship's Master in safeguarding the cargo.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* The Petitioner for Cassation attempted to argue in the cassation memorandum that a Beaufort scale 7–8 storm should have been anticipatable; however, the Supreme Court confirmed that technical evaluations concerning natural conditions and vessel maneuvers belong to the factual domain (*Judex Facti*) and cannot be re-examined during cassation review.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Must a sea carrier compensate for losses if cargo is damaged due to severe storms at sea?'''


'''A:''' No. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 363 K/Pdt/1984 in conjunction with Article 468 paragraph (2) KUHD, the carrier is exempted from the obligation of compensation if it proves that cargo damage was caused by a maritime disaster (*force majeure* / act of God / perils of the sea) that could not be prevented or avoided, provided the vessel was seaworthy.

{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 3641 K/Pdt/2001}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 3641 K/Pdt/2001''' (dated September 11, 2002) is a fundamental civil law and contract law jurisprudence precedent establishing vital rules concerning the limitation of the principle of freedom of contract (''pacta sunt servanda''), the doctrine of abuse of circumstances (''misbruik van omstandigheden''), and the legal consequences of executing contract deeds and debt recognitions inside police detention cells.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established two primary legal principles:

# '''Freedom of Contract Is Not Absolute:''' "Within the principle of freedom of contract, a Judge possesses the authority to examine and declare that the positions of the parties are unbalanced, such that one party is deemed unfree in expressing their will."
# '''Application of Standards of Propriety and Justice:''' "In open-ended contracts, legal values living within society aligned with propriety, justice, and humanitarianism may be applied as a means to modify terms agreed upon in a contract."

Where notary deeds (Deed Nos. 41, 42, and 31) containing a fictitious debt recognition amounting to Rp 215,837,852,000 and personal asset guarantees were presented by creditors/notary to a debtor ([Party A]) while he was detained in the Polda Metro Jaya detention cell, the Supreme Court qualified the transaction as arising from an abuse of circumstances (''misbruik van omstandigheden'' / ''abuse of circumstances''). The debtor lacked physical and psychological freedom to express his will, rendering the agreement null and void / subject to cancellation ''ex'' Article 1320 ''jo.'' Article 1338 of the Civil Code.

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation ([Party A]), annulled Jakarta High Court Decision No. 393/PDT/2000/PT.DKI dated November 21, 2000 (which had overturned South Jakarta District Court Decision No. 442/Pdt.G/1999/PN.Jak.Sel. dated May 11, 2000), and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by partially granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in Convention, declaring that the Defendants committed an Unlawful Act (Tort), declaring Notary Deeds Nos. 41, 42, and 31 along with their derivative transfer deeds null and void, ordering the return of the Plaintiff's land and building assets, and holding Defendants I and IV jointly and severally liable for material and moral damages, while rejecting the Reconvention counterclaim entirely.

| 2 || '''Core Legal Principle (Propriety and Justice):''' Values of propriety, justice, humanitarianism, and the prohibition of abuse of circumstances can modify agreed contract terms. || Headnote p. 41 & Supreme Court Reasoning pp. 42, 59: "...legal values referred to possess an influence that can be applied as a means regarding terms previously agreed upon in an agreement..." || 3641 K_PDT_2001.pdf
