== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Limitation of Freedom of Contract (''Pacta Sunt Servanda'' ''ex'' Article 1338 Civil Code) via the Doctrine of Abuse of Circumstances (''Misbruik van Omstandigheden'') ===
''Can a contract deed or debt recognition signed by a debtor/suspect inside a police detention cell under psychological pressure and promises of detention suspension from a creditor qualify as a valid, binding agreement ''ex'' Article 1338 of the Civil Code?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Invalid / Null and Void / Subject to Cancellation.'''
Freedom of contract is not absolute. Judges possess the authority to examine unbalanced bargaining power (''undue influence'' / ''unconscionability''). Executing deeds inside a police detention cell is qualified as a transaction arising from abuse of circumstances (''misbruik van omstandigheden'' / ''abuse of circumstances''). The debtor lacks free will (physical and psychological freedom impaired), rendering the consent defective (''defect of consent'') and requiring the cancellation of the contract deeds ''ex'' Article 1320 ''jo.'' Article 1338 of the Civil Code.

=== 2. Qualification of Unlawful Acts (Torts / PMH) for Fabricating Police Reports to Compel Contract Execution (Article 1365 Civil Code) ===
Utilizing police/investigative institutions unlawfully (fabricating banking/corruption criminal reports to detain a debtor) as an instrument of coercion or psychological pressure (''duress'' / ''coercion'') to force a debtor to execute debt recognition deeds and transfer personal assets qualifies as an Unlawful Act (Tort) ''ex'' Article 1365 of the Civil Code.

=== 3. Protection of Third Parties and Cancellation of Derivative Deeds (Chain of Title Nullity) ===
Where primary debt recognition and encumbrance deeds (Deeds Nos. 41, 42, and 31) are declared null and void due to defective consent, all derivative/successor deeds—such as Sale and Purchase Deed No. 1363, Sale and Purchase Binding Deed No. 163, and Rights Transfer Deed No. 36—likewise become null and void, possessing no binding legal force, requiring defendants to return all assets belonging to the Plaintiff.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Jakarta High Court (Decision No. 393/PDT/2000/PT.DKI) err in applying contract law (''foutieve toepassing van het verbintenisrecht'' ''ex'' Article 1338 Civil Code) by validating Notary Deeds Nos. 41, 42, and 31, whereas such deeds were executed by the Petitioner for Cassation ([Party A]) inside the Polda Metro Jaya detention cell under psychological pressure and abuse of circumstances?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. Jakarta High Court misapplied the law. Freedom of contract is not absolute, and signing deeds in a detention cell constitutes abuse of circumstances (''misbruik van omstandigheden''). The Supreme Court granted [Party A]'s cassation petition, annulled Jakarta High Court's decision, and independently adjudicated by declaring the notary deeds null and void and ordering Defendants to return all assets to the Plaintiff.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / South Jakarta District Court & Jakarta High Court) ===
Verification of facts regarding [Party A]'s detention in the Polda Metro Jaya Detention Center from May to December 1997 upon complaints filed by PT Bank Arta Prima / PT Bank Artha Graha; verification of Notary [Notary], S.H.'s entry into the detention cell to present Deeds Nos. 41 and 42 (Oct 29, 1997) and Deed No. 31 (Nov 26, 1997); verification of debt recognition amounting to Rp 215,837,852,000 and surrender of giro checks of Rp 20B and Rp 15B; verification of collateral assets comprising Permata Hijau plot Block A-5, 6, 7 measuring 4,500 m<sup>2</sup> and Four Seasons Park Apartment in Singapore; and verification of detention suspension applications (P-16, P-17) filed by Defendant I with the Prosecutor's Office/Police following deed execution.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata / BW):''' Article 1320 (Validity Requirements of Contracts / Freedom of Will), Article 1338 (Principle of Freedom of Contract / ''Pacta Sunt Servanda''), & Article 1365 (Unlawful Acts / Tort).
* '''Open Contract Doctrine:''' Application of Principles of Propriety, Justice, and Humanitarianism in Indonesian Contract Law.
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation and Independent Adjudication Authority.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* '''Doctrine of Abuse of Circumstances (''Misbruik van Omstandigheden''):''' Defective consent (''wilsgebrek'') is not limited to coercion (''dwang''), error (''dwaling''), or fraud (''bedrog''), but encompasses abuse of circumstances and unbalanced bargaining positions (''undue influence'' / ''abuse of circumstances'').

|-

|}


== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision Reg. No. 370 K/AG/1998 (dated March 17, 1999) established a religious civil procedural law rule regarding the formal validity of a statement of claim drafted by legal counsel:


The use of imprecise redactional phrasing in a statement of claim—such as the sentence "filing a divorce claim from brother/sister [Defendant]"—does not automatically render the statement of claim null and void or formally defective pursuant to Article 142 paragraph (1) and Article 147 paragraph (1) of the Revised Indonesian Regulation for the Outer Regions (RBg). Such an error in word choice must not be interpreted as counsel acting on behalf of the opposing party (the defendant). Furthermore, the physical presence of the Principal Plaintiff alongside legal counsel during the hearings tangibly proves a valid attorney-client representation relationship. Therefore, the claim cannot be declared obscure (*obscuur libel*) or inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).


== Executive Summary ==


The central procedural principle established in this decision is that minor drafting or grammatical errors in a statement of claim do not invalidate a lawsuit if the substantive intent is clear and the principal plaintiff is physically present in court to validate the representation.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Inaccurate phrasing or word choice by counsel does not constitute double representation or formal defect ex Article 142(1) & 147(1) RBg.
* The presence of the principal plaintiff at trial validates the proxy relationship.
* Substantive justice takes precedence over rigid procedural formalism.


== Case Background ==


The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation, '''[Plaintiff]''', filed for divorce against her husband, the Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation, '''[Defendant]''', at the Bengkulu Religious Court due to continuous disputes and domestic violence occurring on August 16, 1997. 


The Bengkulu Religious Court (Decision No. 102/Pdt.G/1997/PA.Bn) granted the divorce (*talak satu ba'in sughra*), awarded child custody (*hadhanah*) to the Plaintiff, and ordered the Defendant to pay child support of at least Rp 50,000.— per month. 


The Bengkulu High Religious Court (Decision No. 01/Pdt.G/1998/PTA.BN) subsequently annulled the religious court's decision and declared the claim inadmissible (NO) on the grounds that the counsel's phrasing contained the phrase "filing a divorce claim from brother [Defendant]," which it interpreted as a formal defect of dual representation under Article 142(1) and 147(1) RBg. 


The Petitioner for Cassation then filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.


== Claims, Evidence and Source Mapping ==

|-

| 370K_AG_1998.pdf [Passages 1, 8]
|-

| 370K_AG_1998.pdf [Passages 2, 6, 9]
|-

| '''Domestic Violence and Marital Breakdown Facts:''' Continuous quarrels and physical assault by the Defendant on August 16, 1997, were proven.
| Visum et Repertum Evidence No. Pol. B/061/X/1997/DOK-KES (August 18, 1997) and family witness testimonies.
| 370K_AG_1998.pdf [Passages 1, 5, 21]
|-
| '''4'''
| '''Child Custody (Hadhanah) for Non-Mumayyiz Child:''' Custody of the child named [Child] (born [details removed]) was granted to the Plaintiff (Mother).
| Application of Article 105 sub a in conjunction with Article 156 sub a of the Compilation of Islamic Law (KHI).
| 370K_AG_1998.pdf [Passages 3, 9, 24]
|-
| '''5'''
| '''Child Maintenance Support:''' The Defendant was ordered to pay child maintenance/hadhanah costs of at least Rp 50,000.— per month.
| Consideration of the Defendant's capacity as an Honorary Employee at the Bengkulu Public Works Regional Office and minimum child needs.
| 370K_AG_1998.pdf [Passages 3, 9, 24]
|}


== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Formal Validity of the Statement of Claim (Article 142(1) & 147(1) RBg) ===


The procedural issue questioned whether an editorial error—specifically including the word "from" in the phrase "filing a divorce claim from brother [Defendant]"—rendered the lawsuit legally defective or created a conflict of interest.


The Supreme Court ruled that such linguistic clumsiness is merely a drafting imperfection rather than a conflict of interest or double representation (*double representation*). The physical presence of the Principal Plaintiff alongside her counsel during the trial confirms the validity of the representation.


=== Substantive Justice over Rigid Formalism ===


The Bengkulu High Religious Court erred by relying strictly on rigid formalistic text interpretation without considering the substance and the physical presence of the principal parties. The Supreme Court corrected this methodology by upholding substantive justice.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===


'''Question:'''


Can grammatical interpretation of the word "from" in a statement of claim serve as a legal basis for declaring a lawsuit formally defective (*obscuur libel* / NO) under Article 142 paragraph (1) and Article 147 paragraph (1) RBg?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


No. Formalistic interpretation that disregards the actual presence of the principal plaintiff at trial constitutes a misapplication of procedural law by the *Judex Facti*.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Bengkulu Religious Court) ===


Evaluation of factual elements concerning marital discord, the domestic violence incident on August 16, 1997, Visum et Repertum evidence (P.4), separation of residence since August 20, 1997, and the mother's suitability for holding *hadhanah* rights over a child.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The *Judex Facti* of the Bengkulu High Religious Court misapplied the law. The use of the word "from" in the claim phrasing must not be interpreted as counsel acting on behalf of the Defendant.
# The presence of the Principal Plaintiff alongside her legal counsel during the first and second hearings at the Bengkulu Religious Court proves that the counsel validly represented the Plaintiff.
# The lawsuit is not obscure and satisfies all formal requirements.
# The Supreme Court annulled the High Religious Court decision and adjudicated the case directly by affirming the first-instance religious court decision.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Plaintiff]'''), annulled the Bengkulu High Religious Court Decision No. 01/Pdt.G/1998/PTA.BN, and adjudicated the matter afresh: In Convention: Granting the Plaintiff's claim in part; Declaring a single irrevocable divorce (*talak satu ba'in sughra*) of the Defendant ('''[Defendant]''') against the Plaintiff; Establishing child maintenance/hadhanah of [Child] under the Plaintiff (Mother); Ordering the Defendant to pay child maintenance of at least Rp 50,000.— per month; Rejecting all other claims; In Reconvention: Rejecting the reconvention claim; and assessing court costs accordingly.


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''RBg Article 142 paragraph (1) / Article 147 paragraph (1):''' Provisions regarding the validity of legal counsel representation at trial.
* '''Law No. 7 of 1989 Article 89:''' Assessment of court costs in matrimonial matters.
* '''Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975 Article 19 letter f in conjunction with Compilation of Islamic Law (KHI) Article 116 letter f:''' Grounds for divorce due to continuous disputes and quarrels (broken marriage).
* '''Compilation of Islamic Law (KHI) Article 105 sub a & Article 156 sub a:''' Maintenance and custody (*hadhanah*) of non-mumayyiz children belong to the mother.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* Valid marriage between [Plaintiff] and [Defendant] on March 23, 1995 (Marriage Certificate No. 183/12/III/95 KUA Selebar).
* Birth of daughter [Child] on July 27, 1996.
* Occurrence of physical assault/domestic violence on August 16, 1997, proven by Visum et Repertum No. Pol. B/061/X/1997/DOK-KES dated August 18, 1997.
* Presence of the Principal Plaintiff alongside her legal counsel ([Party C], S.H.) during the first and second hearings at the Bengkulu Religious Court.


=== Not Established / Rejected ===


* The Defendant's reconvention allegation that the Plaintiff committed adultery or infidelity was unproven at trial.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* The Bengkulu High Religious Court focused excessively on literal text interpretation of the claim without reviewing the case file holistically and ignoring the actual presence of the principal parties. The Supreme Court firmly corrected this methodological error in procedural legal interpretation.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Do typos or incorrect phrasing in a statement of claim render a divorce lawsuit legally defective and inadmissible (NO)?'''


'''A:''' No. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 370 K/AG/1998, editorial errors in a statement of claim (such as using the word "from" instead of "against") do not render a lawsuit legally defective ex Article 142(1) & 147(1) RBg. As long as the Principal Plaintiff is present alongside counsel at trial and the intent of the claim is clear, the lawsuit is valid and cannot be declared obscure (*obscuur libel*).

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision Reg. No. 370 K/Pdt/1984 (dated July 31, 1985) established a fundamental civil law rule concerning the evaluation of the evidentiary value of witness testimonies pursuant to Article 472 H.I.R.:


The High Court was declared to have misapplied the law of evidence when it based its decision on witness testimonies that were mutually uncorroborated, contradictory to one another, and of a *de auditu* nature. Such witness testimony cannot serve as a legal basis to establish the validity of a customary land sale (*jual beli tanah adat*), meaning the defendant's occupation of the land is deemed unlawful and the disputed land must be returned to the lawful heirs.


== Executive Summary ==


The central procedural principle established in this decision is that judicial decisions cannot rely on contradictory or *de auditu* witness statements when assessing the validity of land transactions.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* High Courts misapply evidentiary law when resting judgments on conflicting or secondhand (*de auditu*) testimonies ex Article 472 H.I.R.
* Administrative village records (Letter C entries) cannot establish ownership or valid title (*titulus*) without proof of the underlying legal transaction.
* Unlawful occupation requires returning property unconditionality to the rightful heirs.


== Case Background ==


The Original Plaintiffs / Petitioners for Cassation ([Party A], et al., heirs of the late Ki Sanrodji Rijun and Ni Sanrodji Rijun) filed a lawsuit against [Party B] and Ni [Party B] (Original Defendants I & II) at the Purbalingga District Court concerning the unlawful occupation of inherited rice field land under Letter C No. 442, Parcel No. 40 S.II, covering an area of approximately 400 *ubin* in Karanggambas Village. 


The Defendants claimed they purchased the land from the heirs' predecessor in 1965/1967 for Rp 40,000.—. 


The Purbalingga District Court (Decision No. 15/1979 Pdt.G) granted the Plaintiffs' claim. However, the Semarang High Court (Decision No. 318/1980/Pdt/PT.Smg.) annulled the district court's decision and rejected the return of the land, ruling that the sale was valid based on witness testimonies and village Letter C records. 


The Petitioners for Cassation subsequently appealed to the Supreme Court.


== Claims, Evidence and Source Mapping ==

| 370K_Pdt_1984.pdf [Passages 1, 6, 7]

| 370K_Pdt_1984.pdf [Passages 4, 7, 8]
|}


== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Evaluation of Evidentiary Value of Witness Testimony (Article 472 H.I.R.) ===


The procedural issue questioned whether a High Court could rule in favor of a defendant based on contradictory witness testimonies where a primary witness only heard accounts from third parties (*de auditu*).


The Supreme Court held that under Article 472 H.I.R., judges must evaluate the connectivity and consistency of witness statements against other trial facts. Testimonies that cancel each other out or rely on hearsay (*de auditu*) possess no evidentiary weight (*waarde van bewijs*) to legalize property transfers.


=== Material and Formal Requirements of Customary Land Sales ===


The Defendants alleged they purchased the land in 1965/1967 and updated village Letter C registry records. However, the village secretary testified he never witnessed the sale and only acted on the village head's instructions to alter records. The Supreme Court underscored that administrative book modifications without proof of a real underlying legal transaction are void *ab initio*.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the *Judex Facti* (Semarang High Court) violate evidentiary law ex Article 472 H.I.R. by treating a customary land sale as proven based on inconsistent, contradictory, and *de auditu* witness testimonies?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the *Judex Facti* misapplied the law of evidence. Consequently, the Semarang High Court decision must be annulled.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Purbalingga District Court & Semarang High Court) ===


Examination of the family lineage of the late Ki Sanrodji Rijun, physical possession history of the rice field in Karanggambas Village, and local witness statements (Village Head [Village Head], Secretary [Village Secretary], and [Party C]).


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The *Judex Facti* of the Semarang High Court misapplied evidentiary law under Article 472 H.I.R.
# The testimonies of Witness I, Witness II, and Witness III conflicted, with Witness II admitting to *de auditu* knowledge and lacking direct observation of the transaction.
# Witness statements lacking consistency and resting on hearsay hold no legal evidentiary value to establish land purchases.
# The Supreme Court annulled the High Court decision and adjudicated directly by affirming the District Court decision.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Party A]'''), annulled Semarang High Court Decision No. 318/1980/Pdt/PT.Smg., and Adjudicated Directly: Granting the Plaintiffs' claim in part; Declaring the Plaintiffs the lawful heirs of the late Ki Sanrodji Rijun and Ni Sanrodji Rijun; Declaring the disputed rice field the lawful property of the Plaintiffs; Declaring that Defendants I and II have unlawfully occupied the disputed land since 1974; Ordering Defendants I and II to vacate and surrender the disputed land unconditionally to the Plaintiffs (with police assistance if necessary); and assessing all court costs across all judicial instances against the Respondent for Cassation.


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''H.I.R. Article 472 / RBg Article 308:''' Judicial duty to weigh consistency and connectivity among witness testimonies.
* '''Testimonium De Auditu:''' Witness accounts derived from secondhand hearing cannot serve as direct evidence for legal events.
* '''Agrarian Law & Land Registration:''' Government Regulation No. 10 of 1961 Article 19; village administrative book entries do not create new rights when the underlying legal act (*titulus*) remains unproven.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* Plaintiffs ([Party A], Chamid, Misem, Slamet, Suryat, Maryun, Sirat, Tukiman, Suhad) are the lawful heirs of the late Ki Sanrodji Rijun and Ni Sanrodji Rijun (who passed away in 1974).
* The disputed object, Letter C No. 442, Parcel No. 40 S.II covering ± 400 *ubin* in Karanggambas Village, forms part of the unpartitioned estate.
* Defendants I ([Party B]) and II (Ni [Party B]) unlawfully occupied the disputed rice field since 1974.


=== Not Established / Unproven ===


* The Defendants failed to establish the occurrence of a valid customary sale contract for the disputed land from the late Ki Sanrodji Rijun.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* The Defendants argued that a written purchase receipt for Rp 40,000.— was lost by theft. However, they never submitted the document nor provided an official police loss report, leaving their acquisition claim entirely dependent on verbal testimonies proven legally defective under evidentiary rules.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Are contradictory and de auditu witness testimonies valid for judges to decide land sale disputes?'''


'''A:''' Invalid. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 370 K/Pdt/1984 in conjunction with Article 472 H.I.R., judges are prohibited from basing decisions on witness accounts that are mutually inconsistent, contradictory, or *de auditu* (secondhand hearsay). Such witness accounts carry no evidentiary value to validate land transactions.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision Reg. No. 371 K/Pdt/1984 (dated August 31, 1985) established two fundamental civil procedural law rules:


1. **Validity of Conservatory Attachment (*Conservatoir Beslag*):** A request for conservatory attachment may be submitted by the plaintiff and granted by the court throughout the ongoing proceedings, even if it was not included in the primary petition of the initial statement of claim, without violating the *ultra petita* principle ex Article 178 H.I.R.


2. **Defect of Parties (*Plurium Litis Consortium*):** A lawsuit seeking the annulment or execution of a land sale that fails to join the original seller (Sani bin Saari) as a Principal Defendant is incomplete and suffers from a defect of parties, requiring the lawsuit to be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).


== Executive Summary ==


The central procedural principles established in this decision govern the flexibility of ancillary attachment measures versus the absolute requirement to include all necessary parties in property transaction disputes.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Conservatory attachments can be validly requested via separate letters during trial without triggering *ultra petita*.
* The omission of the primary seller in property litigation results in a defective party structure (*plurium litis consortium*).
* Dismissal of the primary claim on procedural grounds automatically nullifies and lifts any provisional attachments.


== Case Background ==


The Original Plaintiff / Respondent for Cassation, '''[Party B]''', sued Ny. [Party A] and Moch. Sarwani Nur (Defendants I & II) at the South Jakarta District Court regarding a breach of contract (*wanprestasi*) concerning the handover of a 200 m² plot of land and a house in Tanjung Barat, Pasar Minggu, purchased by the Plaintiff under Deed of Sale No. 557/I.7/11.1/1980 from the original seller, Sani bin Saari. 


During the proceedings, the Plaintiff requested a conservatory attachment via a separate letter dated July 15, 1982, which the South Jakarta District Court granted. 


The South Jakarta District Court (Decision No. 123/JS/1982 G.) partially granted the Plaintiff's claim and validated the attachment. The Jakarta High Court (Decision No. 75/1983 P.T. Perdata) affirmed the district court's decision. 


The Petitioner for Cassation (Defendant I) subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.


== Claims, Evidence and Source Mapping ==

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Validity of Conservatory Attachment Requests During Proceedings (Ultra Petita ex Article 178 H.I.R.) ===


The procedural issue questioned whether judges violate the prohibition against *ultra petita* by granting a conservatory attachment requested by the Plaintiff mid-trial via a separate letter when it was omitted from the initial statement of claim's petitum.


The Supreme Court ruled that it does not violate *ultra petita*. Conservatory attachments serve to safeguard the disputed object from being transferred while proceedings are underway; thus, requests for attachment can be validly submitted at any time before a final judgment is rendered.


=== Defect of Parties (*Plurium Litis Consortium*) ===


The issue questioned whether a lawsuit for the annulment or execution of a land sale is valid without joining the original seller whose name appears in the deed of sale.


The Supreme Court ruled that it is invalid. The original seller (Sani bin Saari) is an essential party to the underlying legal transaction of the disputed land sale. Failing to join the original seller as a defendant renders the party structure incomplete (*plurium litis consortium*), introducing a formal procedural defect that requires the lawsuit to be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the *Judex Facti* misapply civil procedural law by granting a lawsuit that failed to join the original seller (Sani bin Saari) as a Principal Defendant?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the *Judex Facti* misapplied the law. A lawsuit with a defect of parties is formally incomplete and must be declared inadmissible (NO).


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / South Jakarta District Court & Jakarta High Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning the breach of contract (*wanprestasi*) for the handover of the 200 m² plot (Parcel No. 104a, Kohir C. 303, Block D.III in Tanjung Barat, Pasar Minggu), the Defendant's report to the military police (POM ABRI), and the execution of attachments over the land and house.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
1. The Petitioner for Cassation's objection regarding the conservatory attachment is unfounded, because attachments may be requested and granted throughout ongoing proceedings via separate petitions without violating Article 178 HIR.
2. The Petitioner for Cassation's objection regarding the defect of parties is well-founded. It was proven that Sani bin Saari is the owner and original seller of the disputed land. Failure to join Sani bin Saari as a Principal Defendant renders the Plaintiff's lawsuit incomplete (*plurium litis consortium*) and subject to dismissal as inadmissible (NO).
3. Because the lawsuit is inadmissible, the conservatory attachment placed on August 6, 1982, is declared invalid and must be lifted.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation ('''Ny. [Party A]'''), annulled Jakarta High Court Decision No. 75/1983 P.T. Perdata in conjunction with South Jakarta District Court Decision No. 123/JS/1982 G., and Adjudicated Directly: Declaring the Plaintiff's claim inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO); Declaring the conservatory attachment dated August 6, 1982, invalid and without value, and ordering its removal; and ordering the Respondent for Cassation / Original Plaintiff to bear the court costs across all judicial instances.


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''HIR Article 178 / RBg Article 189:''' The *Ultra Petita* principle prohibiting judges from granting relief beyond what is requested.
* '''HIR Article 227 / RBg Article 261:''' Provisions governing Conservatory Attachments (*Conservatoir Beslag*).
* ***Plurium Litis Consortium* Principle:** Lawsuits failing to involve all parties directly bound to the core legal transaction are incomplete and inadmissible.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* The Plaintiff ([Party B]) purchased the 200 m² land and house in Tanjung Barat for Rp 2,000,000.— pursuant to Deed of Sale No. 557/I.7/11.1/1980 dated March 26, 1980, from seller Sani bin Saari.
* The Plaintiff's Special Power of Attorney dated May 12, 1982, was validly registered at the South Jakarta District Court registry on July 1, 1982.
* The attachment request was submitted by the Plaintiff via a letter dated July 15, 1982, and the attachment report was drawn up by the Substitute Bailiff on August 6, 1982.


=== Not Established / Unproven ===


* The Plaintiff failed to establish perfect standing to sue over the disputed object without joining Sani bin Saari in the proceedings.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* The conservatory attachment executed by the South Jakarta District Court on August 6, 1982, was automatically rendered null, void, and illegal by the Supreme Court because the primary lawsuit was declared inadmissible (NO).


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Can a request for conservatory attachment (*conservatoir beslag*) be filed midway through trial if it was omitted from the initial lawsuit?'''


'''A:''' Yes. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 371 K/Pdt/1984, a request for conservatory attachment may be filed and granted by the court throughout ongoing proceedings via a separate petition, even if it was omitted from the initial lawsuit's petitum, without violating the *ultra petita* principle under Article 178 H.I.R.

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:3726K PDT 1985
wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 3726 K/Pdt/1985}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 3726 K/Pdt/1985''' (dated June 30, 1987 / deliberation on May 19, 1987) is a fundamental contract law and insurance law jurisprudence precedent establishing vital rules concerning the calculation of prescription periods (''daluwarsa'') for insurance claims by heirs, the legal standing of unilateral foreign-language guidebooks (''keyman books''), and the prohibition of awarding moratory interest on insurance claim demands.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established three primary legal principles:

# '''Calculation of Prescription Period for Insurance Claims:''' "The time period for submitting a claim against life insurance by the insured's heirs is calculated from the time such heirs become aware of the requirements for submitting the claim."
# '''Legal Status of Foreign-Language Keyman Books:''' The 3-month prescription period stipulated in an English-language keyman book unilaterally drafted by the insurance company (without mutual signatures) cannot be equated with an insurance policy and holds no binding legal force against an insured or heir who does not understand the foreign language.
# '''Prohibition of Interest on Insurance Claims (Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 939 K/Sip/1976):''' Insurance underwriting disputes do not constitute money-lending contracts; therefore, damage claims seeking interest (''in casu'' 18% per annum) over delayed insurance claim payments must be rejected.

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation (Ny. [Party A]), annulled Jakarta High Court Decision No. 191/Pdt/1985/PT.DKI dated July 13, 1985, ''jo.'' Central Jakarta District Court Decision No. 124/Pdt/G/1984/PN.JP dated October 9, 1984, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by partially granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit, declaring that the Defendant (PT Maskapai Asuransi Nasuha) committed a default (''wanprestasi''), ordering the Defendant to pay insurance claim proceeds amounting to US$ 100,000 under Policy No. 1.7.10.01003, and rejecting the remainder of the lawsuit (including interest/damages at 18%).

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Starting Point (''Dies A Quo'') for Calculating Life/Accident Insurance Claim Prescription Periods by Heirs ===
''When does the insurance claim submission period begin to run for heirs who were not directly involved when the policy was signed by the late insured?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Calculated from Heirs' Awareness of Claim Requirements.'''

Heirs cannot be burdened with a prescription period running from the occurrence of the event (''eventemen'') or unilateral rejection; rather, the prescription period begins to run only when the relevant heirs actually know and understand the claim submission requirements (i.e., after receiving a sworn translation of the insurance documents).

=== 2. Legal Status of Unilateral Foreign-Language Keyman Books vs. Insurance Policies (Articles 246, 255, 257 Commercial Code ''jo.'' Articles 1320, 1338 Civil Code) ===
''Do the exoneration/3-month prescription terms set forth in an English-language keyman guidebook unilaterally issued by the insurer bind the insured and heirs?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Non-Binding.'''

An insurance policy constitutes an authentic or private deed mutually agreed upon that marks the underwriting contract (Articles 255, 257 Commercial Code). A foreign-language keyman book unilaterally issued without the insured's signature serves merely as an internal guide for insurance personnel and cannot operate as a binding prescription clause against the insured/heirs ''ex'' Article 1320 ''jo.'' Article 1338 of the Civil Code.

=== 3. Awarding Moratory Interest for Delayed Insurance Claim Payments (Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 939 K/Sip/1976) ===
Insurance contracts are conditional underwriting contracts, not money-lending agreements. Consequently, courts are prohibited from ordering insurers to pay moratory interest (such as 18% per annum) over delays in disbursing claim proceeds.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (''Judex Juris'' / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Jakarta High Court (Decision No. 191/Pdt/1985/PT.DKI) err in applying the law (''foutieve toepassing van het recht'') by accepting the 3-month prescription exception based on an English keyman book and dismissing the insurance claim, and can moratory interest be imposed on insurance claim obligations?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. Jakarta High Court misapplied the law. Foreign-language keyman books are non-binding for claim prescriptions, and prescription for heirs runs from awareness of claim requirements. The Supreme Court annulled the lower court decisions and independently adjudicated by partially granting the principal claim of US$ 100,000 while rejecting the 18% p.a. interest claim pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 939 K/Sip/1976.

=== Question of Fact (''Judex Facti'' / Central Jakarta District Court & Jakarta High Court) ===
Verification of facts regarding the underwriting of Personal Accident Policy No. 1.7.10.01003 in the name of Drs. Muhammad Djan (Director of CV IMPA); the slip-and-fall accident on November 23, 1981, causing cerebral hemorrhage (cerebellar haematoma) and death on December 1, 1981, at Cikini/RSCM; PT Maskapai Asuransi Nasuha's unilateral rejection letter dated February 25, 1982; and the sworn translation of the Personal Accident Policy dated January 10, 1984 (Exhibit P-7).

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''Commercial Code (''Kitab Undang-Undang Hukum Dagang'' / KUHD):''' Article 246 (Definition of Insurance), Article 255 (Policies Must Be in Writing), Article 256 (Policy Contents), & Article 257 (Inception of Insurance Contracts).
* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata / BW):''' Article 1320 (Validity Requirements of Contracts), Article 1338 (Principle of Freedom of Contract / ''Pacta Sunt Servanda''), Articles 1950 & 1993 (Prescription).
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 1 of 1950 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation and Independent Adjudication Authority.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* '''Supreme Court Decision No. 939 K/Sip/1976 (Feb 24, 1976):''' Landmark decision establishing that moratory interest damages cannot be imposed on civil obligations arising outside of money-lending contracts.
* '''Doctrine of Protecting Insurance Consumers from Foreign Exoneration Clauses:''' Insurers cannot hide behind internal foreign-language guidebooks (''keyman books'') never agreed upon or understood by customers/heirs to extinguish death benefit obligations.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* Drs. Muhammad Djan is '''PROVEN TO BE INSURED UNDER PERSONAL ACCIDENT POLICY NO. 1.7.10.01003''' with PT Maskapai Asuransi Nasuha with US$ 100,000 coverage.
* The Insured is '''PROVEN TO HAVE DIED FROM AN ACCIDENT''' (slip-and-fall causing cerebral hemorrhage) on December 1, 1981.
* Ny. [Party A] is '''PROVEN TO BE THE LAWFUL HEIR AND BENEFICIARY''' entitled to claim policy proceeds.
* The Insurer's unilateral rejection and policy cancellation are '''PROVEN TO CONSTITUTE A DEFAULT (''WANPRESTASI'') / UNLAWFUL ACT'''.
* The English-language keyman guidebook is '''PROVEN TO HOLD NO BINDING LEGAL FORCE''' to enforce a 3-month prescription period against the Plaintiff.
* The Defendant is ordered to pay insurance claim proceeds of US$ 100,000 to the Plaintiff.
* Jakarta High Court Decision No. 191/Pdt/1985/PT.DKI and Central Jakarta District Court Decision No. 124/Pdt/G/1984/PN.JP are '''NULL AND VOID'''.

=== Dismissed Claims ===
* The claim seeking moratory interest of 18% per annum (amounting to US$ 72,000) was '''REJECTED BY THE SUPREME COURT''' pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 939 K/Sip/1976.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Protecting Heirs' Rights Against Concealed Prescription Clauses in Insurance Contracts:''' This landmark ruling establishes robust legal certainty for insurance policyholders in Indonesia: insurance companies are strictly prohibited from unilaterally canceling policies or rejecting death benefit claims from heirs while sheltering behind foreign-language guidebooks or attachments never agreed upon or understood by customers. The prescription period for heirs fairly commences only when heirs clearly understand claim requirements.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
; When does the prescription period for insurance claims begin to run for heirs, and does a foreign-language keyman book bind the insured pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence?
: '''From Heirs' Awareness of Claim Requirements & Keyman Book Non-Binding.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. No. 3726 K/Pdt/1985:

* The time period for submitting a life/accident insurance claim by heirs is calculated from the time such heirs become aware of the requirements for submitting the claim.
* An English-language keyman book unilaterally drafted by the insurance company cannot be equated with an insurance policy and does not bind the insured/heirs who do not understand it ''ex'' Article 255 of the Commercial Code ''jo.'' Article 1320 of the Civil Code.
* An insurer rejecting a claim is mandated to pay the full insurance proceeds (''in casu'' US$ 100,000), but moratory interest claims are rejected because insurance transactions are not money-lending agreements (Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 939 K/Sip/1976).

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:3783K PDT 1987
wikitext:
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 3783 K/Pdt/1987''' (Interlocutory Decision dated June 14, 1989 / Final Deliberation Decision dated November 21, 1989, pronounced on February 14, 1990) is a fundamental civil procedure and national land law jurisprudence precedent establishing vital rules concerning the Supreme Court's authority to issue Interlocutory Decisions (''Putusan Sela'') to conduct supplementary examinations (''aanvullend onderzoek'') at the cassation level, the impossibility of customary rights/girik titles arising over State Land originating from Former Private Eigendom under Law No. 1 of 1958, and the dismissal of land ownership claims based on forged inheritance decrees and fictitious girik titles.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established three primary legal principles:

# '''Authority of Supplementary Examination via Cassation Interlocutory Decisions:''' Before rendering a final decision, the Supreme Court is authorized to issue an Interlocutory Decision to conduct a supplementary examination (''aanvullend onderzoek'') executed directly by the Supreme Court to summon expert witnesses (Agrarian Service, Land Tax/Ipeda, Sub-district Head, Village Head, Notary, and Court Registrar) to ascertain the precise status/location of the disputed land and examine the material truth of evidence where the ''Judex Facti'' misapplied the law of evidence.
# '''Incompatibility of Customary/Girik Rights Over State Land Originating from Former Private Eigendom (Law No. 1 of 1958):''' Over State Land originating from Former Eigendom Verponding Nos. 3861 and 1959, which was affirmed as land directly controlled by the State pursuant to Law No. 1 of 1958, '''customary rights (such as girik titles / Ipeda tax assessments) cannot possibly attach'''.
# '''Lawsuits Based on Forged Inheritance Decrees and Fictitious Giriks Must Be Dismissed:''' Land ownership lawsuits grounded on rights-transfer deeds supported by Judicial Inheritance Decrees proven to be fictitious/forged (testimony of Special District Court Registrar of Jakarta [Party A]) and girik titles unrecorded in Ipeda land tax registers '''must be declared unproven and dismissed entirely'''.

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation (State of the Republic of Indonesia ''qq.'' Government of the Republic of Indonesia ''qq.'' Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Indonesia), annulled Jakarta High Court Decision No. 375/Pdt/1987/PT.DKI dated August 31, 1987, ''jo.'' South Jakarta District Court Decision No. 148/Pdt/G/1986/PN.Jkt.Sel. dated June 16, 1987, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by dismissing the original Plaintiff's lawsuit (Yayasan Pendidikan Wiraswasta Indonesia) entirely, declaring the conservatory attachment invalid, and ordering the lifting of the conservatory attachment.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Authority of the Supreme Court to Conduct Supplementary Examinations (''Aanvullend Onderzoek'') via Cassation Interlocutory Decisions (Law No. 14 of 1985 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1970) ===
''Does the Supreme Court at the cassation level possess the authority to issue an interlocutory decision to summon and examine witnesses, land administration officials, and review evidence directly during cassation hearings?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Authorized / Constitutional.''' Before rendering a final decision, the Supreme Court is authorized to issue an Interlocutory Decision to conduct a supplementary examination (''aanvullend onderzoek'') carried out by the Supreme Court itself. This step is undertaken to clearly ascertain the status and location of disputed land and uncover material truths where the ''Judex Facti'' is proven to have misapplied evidentiary law.

=== 2. Juridical Status of Customary/Girik Rights Over State Land Originating from Former Private Eigendom ''ex'' Law No. 1 of 1958 ===
''Can customary rights/giriks arise, be recognized, or be maintained over parcels of land designated as State Land originating from Former Private Eigendom pursuant to Law No. 1 of 1958?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Impossible / Incompatible.''' Over State Land originating from Eigendom Verponding/Private Eigendom which, pursuant to Law No. 1 of 1958 ''jo.'' Agrarian Minister Decrees, was affirmed as land directly controlled by the State, customary rights such as girik/Ipeda land titles cannot possibly attach.

=== 3. Legal Consequences of Land Ownership Lawsuits Based on Forged Inheritance Decrees and Fictitious Giriks ===
Notarial rights-transfer deeds grounded on judicial inheritance decrees proven to be fictitious/forged (pursuant to testimony from court registrars) and giriks unrecorded in PBB Ipeda registers are qualified as legally defective transactions conferring no ownership rights whatsoever. Land ownership lawsuits must be dismissed entirely, and conservatory attachments improperly placed over State assets must be lifted.

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Jakarta High Court (Decision No. 375/Pdt/1987/PT.DKI) and South Jakarta District Court (Decision No. 148/Pdt/G/1986/PN.Jkt.Sel.) err in applying agrarian evidentiary law (''foutieve toepassing van het bewijsrecht'') by granting land ownership lawsuits grounded on girik titles over State Land originating from Former Private Eigendom under Law No. 1 of 1958?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. The ''Judex Facti'' misapplied the law. Through an Interlocutory Decision and Supplementary Examination, the Supreme Court proved that the Plaintiff's inheritance documents were forged and giriks fictitious. The Supreme Court granted the Ministry of Finance's cassation petition, annulled Jakarta High Court's decision, and independently adjudicated by dismissing the Plaintiff's lawsuit entirely and ordering the lifting of the conservatory attachment.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Supreme Court via Supplementary Examination) ===
Examination of facts concerning land location at [address removed], Duren Tiga / Kalibata, Mampang Prapatan, South Jakarta, measuring 38,844 m²; examination of Registrar witness [Party A] concerning Inheritance Decrees Nos. 427/1962 G, 429/1964 G, and 417/1974 G; examination of South Jakarta Ipeda/PBB Service Office Head A. Rashid Kusnaini concerning Register C Nos. 140, 710, and 1440; examination of South Jakarta Land Office Head Drs. Sularso concerning Eigendom Verponding Nos. 3861 and 1959; and examination of rights releases to PT Jaya Real Estate / PT Jaya Realty and the Ministry of Finance RI.

* '''Law No. 1 of 1958 on the Abolition of Private Lands:''' Affirmation of State Land Status for Former Private Eigendom Directly Controlled by the State.

{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 3888 K/Pdt/1994}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 3888 K/Pdt/1994''' (dated June 19, 1996 / deliberation on May 8, 1996) is a fundamental land law, housing law, and civil evidentiary law jurisprudence precedent. It establishes vital rules concerning the lawfulness of house occupancy based on a Placement Permit (''Surat Izin Penempatan'' / SIP) issued by competent authorities, the qualification of Unlawful Acts (Tort / PMH), and the absence of legal grounds to demand property eviction and damages against lawful SIP holders.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established three primary legal principles:

# '''Tenants Based on Lawful SIPs Do Not Commit a Tort (PMH):''' "That the ''Judex Facti'' misapplied the law of evidence because the Petitioner for Cassation is the principal occupant of the disputed house, and the SIP obtained by him is lawful, fully compliant with requirements, and issued by the competent authority; hence, the Petitioner for Cassation is not proven to have committed an unlawful act."
# '''Absence of Legal Basis for Tort Damages and Eviction:''' "Because the Petitioner for Cassation is not proven to have committed an unlawful act, the claim for damages against the Petitioner for Cassation has no legal basis whatsoever and the quantum of such damages cannot be proven."
# '''Lawful Tenancy Status:''' A lawful SIP holder occupying a house ([address removed], Surabaya) since 1972 cannot be forcibly evicted on allegations of Tort. The building owner is entitled solely to reasonable house rent payments (fixed at Rp 2,000,000 per year for a 20-year period, totaling Rp 40,000,000).

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation ([Defendant I]), annulled Surabaya High Court Decision No. 741/Pdt/1993/PT.Sby dated February 19, 1994, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri''). It partially granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in Convention, declaring that the Plaintiff (Ny. [Party B]) is the lawful owner of the house at [address removed], Surabaya, and ordered Defendant I to pay rent of Rp 2,000,000 per year for 20 years (totaling Rp 40,000,000). It rejected the remainder of the Plaintiff's lawsuit (including claims for Tort, eviction, and coercive penalty fines / ''dwangsom''), and rejected Defendant I's Reconvention counterclaim entirely.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Qualification of House Occupancy Based on a Lawful Placement Permit (SIP) Issued by Government Housing Offices (PP No. 17 of 1963 ''jo.'' Housing Regulations) ===
''Can a citizen occupying rental housing based on an official Placement Permit (SIP) issued by the Regional Government Housing Office be qualified as committing an Unlawful Act (Tort) ''ex'' Article 1365 of the Civil Code?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Not an Unlawful Act (Tort).'''
Where an occupant occupies a disputed house based on a lawful Placement Permit (SIP) issued by a competent authority (Housing Office) in accordance with legal procedures and regularly pays rent, such occupancy is lawful and protected under housing law. The occupant is not proven to have committed an Unlawful Act (Tort).

=== 2. Limits on Building Owners' Rights Over State Land / Expired HGB Land (Presidential Decree No. 32 of 1979) ===
The owner of a building standing on HGB land whose term has expired (becoming Land Directly Controlled by the State ''ex'' Presidential Decree No. 32 of 1979) possesses no right to demand property eviction against a lawful SIP holder, but is entitled solely to demand reasonable house rent payments from the occupant.

=== 3. Quantification Requirements for Tort Damages Claims (Supreme Court Jurisprudence No. 1057 K/Sip/1973, No. 78 K/Sip/1973, No. 556 K/Sip/1980) ===
Claims for damages grounded on Tort must be supported by tangible proof of unlawful conduct and detailed quantification of material losses. Because Tort is unproven, claims for damages and coercive fines (''dwangsom'') must be rejected entirely.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (''Judex Juris'' / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' Surabaya High Court (Decision No. 741/Pdt/1993/PT.Sby) err in applying the law of evidence (''foutieve toepassing van het bewijsrecht'') by qualifying Defendant I's occupancy under a lawful SIP as an Unlawful Act (Tort) and ordering property eviction alongside damages and coercive fines (''dwangsom'')?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. Surabaya High Court misapplied the law. Lawful SIP holders issued by competent authorities do not commit Torts; hence, eviction and Tort damage claims lack legal grounds. The Supreme Court granted [Defendant I]'s cassation petition, annulled Surabaya High Court's decision, and independently adjudicated by ordering Defendant I solely to pay reasonable house rent amounting to Rp 2,000,000 per year for 20 years (totaling Rp 40,000,000) while rejecting eviction/Tort claims.

=== Question of Fact (''Judex Facti'' / Surabaya District Court & Surabaya High Court) ===
Verification of facts regarding the occupancy history of the house at [address removed], Surabaya, starting from Mr. Kwee Sing Lien (1946), Widow Kwee Sing Lien (1949), Kwee Tjien Kie (1952), up to [Defendant I] (1972); inspection of Sale and Purchase Deed No. 8/1972 dated April 10, 1972; verification of Placement Permit (SIP) No. 301/KRKP/72 dated September 13, 1972, and Renewal SIP No. 181.2/004/411.87/88 dated January 7, 1988; examination of National Police Forensic Laboratory Report No. Lab. 465/DE/VII/1975 concerning blank seal form usage; and verification of postal money orders for house rent payments.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''Government Regulation No. 17 of 1963:''' Principles of Implementing the Government Regulation in Lieu of Law on Housing.
* '''Presidential Decree No. 32 of 1979:''' Principal Policy Framework for Granting New Land Rights Originating from the Conversion of Western Rights (Status of Expired HGB Becoming State Land).
* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata / BW):''' Article 1365 (Unlawful Acts / Tort) & Provisions on Lease Agreements.
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation and Independent Adjudication Authority.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* '''Established Precedent on Tort Damage Proof (Supreme Court Decisions No. 1057 K/Sip/1973, No. 78 K/Sip/1973, No. 556 K/Sip/1980):''' Damage claims based on tort cannot be granted without detailed proof of valid and proven material losses.
* '''Doctrine of Official SIP Holder Protection:''' Individuals occupying housing under regional housing office supervision based on valid, unexpired official SIPs are protected under law and cannot be forcibly evicted via civil tort lawsuits.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* Defendant I ([Defendant I]) is '''PROVEN TO BE THE LAWFUL PRINCIPAL OCCUPANT''' of the house at [address removed], Surabaya, pursuant to a Placement Permit (SIP) issued by the Surabaya Municipal Housing Service.
* Defendant I is '''PROVEN NOT TO HAVE COMMITTED AN UNLAWFUL ACT (TORT)'''.
* The Plaintiff (Ny. [Party B]) is '''PROVEN TO BE THE LAWFUL OWNER OF THE HOUSE BUILDING''' ''ex'' Sale and Purchase Deed No. 8/1972.
* Defendant I is ordered to pay house rent to the Plaintiff amounting to Rp 2,000,000 per year for a 20-year period (totaling Rp 40,000,000).
* Surabaya High Court Decision No. 741/Pdt/1993/PT.Sby is '''NULL AND VOID'''.

=== Dismissed Claims ===
* The Plaintiff's claims seeking to qualify Defendant I's occupancy as a Tort, ordering property eviction, and imposing coercive penalty fines (''dwangsom'') of Rp 250,000/day were '''REJECTED ENTIRELY BY THE SUPREME COURT''' for lacking legal grounds.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Legal Certainty of Protecting Officially Permitted Occupants (SIP) Against Priority Rights Over State Land:''' This landmark ruling establishes strict housing law boundaries in Indonesia: district and high courts may not evict or penalize house occupants holding official Placement Permits (SIP) from Regional Governments on allegations of Unlawful Acts (Tort). Owners of former HGB buildings are entitled solely to reasonable rent payments, while priority rights applications over expired HGB State land must be resolved through agrarian administrative law mechanisms.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
; Can a house occupant holding an official Placement Permit (SIP) from a Regional Government Housing Office be sued for a Tort and forced to evict pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence?
: '''No.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. No. 3888 K/Pdt/1994:
:* Principal occupants residing in a house based on a lawful Placement Permit (SIP) issued by a competent authority (Housing Office) '''are not proven to have committed an unlawful act (Tort)'''.
:* Because tort is unproven, claims for house eviction, tort damages, and coercive fines (''dwangsom'') have no legal basis whatsoever and must be rejected.
:* The Supreme Court annulled the Surabaya High Court decision and independently adjudicated by ordering the occupant solely to pay reasonable house rent to the building owner.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Judicial Review (*Peninjauan Kembali / PK*) Decision No. 38 PK/Pid/2003 establishes important legal precedents regarding criminal judicial review concerning unlawful firearms/ammunition possession and premeditated murder. The Supreme Court ruled to release the Defendant (H. [Defendant]) from legal prosecution regarding the charge of evading execution in the Goro case (Charge IV), because the underlying execution ruling had previously been annulled via a prior Judicial Review, thereby negating material unlawfulness. However, regarding the offenses of firearms possession and the premeditated murder of Supreme Court Justice H.M. Syafiuddin Kartasasmita, SH (Charges I, II, and III), the Supreme Court upheld the conviction while reducing the prison sentence from 15 (fifteen) years to 10 (ten) years, taking into account principles of justice and the emotional distress experienced by the Defendant due to unfair treatment during prior legal proceedings.

== Case Background ==

The Defendant, H. [Defendant] alias [Defendant], was indicted upon four charges:
1. '''Charge I (Emergency Law No. 12/1951 jo. Article 55(1) item 1 of the KUHP):''' Complicity in unlawfully controlling, storing, and concealing various types of firearms and ammunition at Cemara Apartment, Jalan Cemara No. 23-25, Menteng, Central Jakarta;
2. '''Charge II (Emergency Law No. 12/1951):''' Unlawfully controlling, storing, and concealing firearms, ammunition, and explosives at a residence on Jalan Alam Segar III No. 23, Pondok Indah, South Jakarta;
3. '''Charge III (Article 340 jo. Article 55(1) item 2 of the KUHP):''' Instigating (*uitlokker*) R. Moulawarman al. Molla and Noval Hadad bin Harun to commit premeditated murder against Supreme Court Justice H.M. Syafiuddin Kartasasmita, SH;
4. '''Charge IV (Article 216(1) of the KUHP):''' Intentionally disobeying orders or thwarting the actions of public officials executing statutory regulations (evading/becoming a fugitive from the execution of the Goro case criminal judgment).

The Central Jakarta District Court (Decision No. 407/Pid.B/2002/PN.JKT.PST dated July 26, 2002) sentenced the Defendant to 15 (fifteen) years of imprisonment. The Defendant subsequently filed a petition for Judicial Review directly to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# Regarding Charge IV, because the Cassation Decision No. 1 K/Pid/2000 dated September 22, 2000, in the "Goro" case forming the basis of execution was annulled by the Supreme Court via Judicial Review No. 78 PK/Pid/2000 dated October 1, 2001, the Defendant's act of evading execution no longer possesses material unlawfulness (*materiele wederrechtelijk*). Such conduct does not constitute a criminal offense; hence, the Defendant must be released from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*) specifically with respect to Charge IV.
# Regarding Charges I, II, and III, the Supreme Court adopted the Central Jakarta District Court *judex facti* reasoning holding that the criminal elements were legally and convincingly proven. However, the *judex facti* failed in its legal reasoning to account for principles of justice regarding the Petitioner for PK, who suffered emotional distress due to unfair treatment during the Goro case execution. Pursuant to Article 263 paragraph (2) of the KUHAP and considerations of equity, the imposed sentence is modified and reduced to 10 (ten) years of imprisonment.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the petition for judicial review from Petitioner for PK H. [Defendant] alias [Defendant]; Annulling the Central Jakarta District Court Decision No. 407/Pid.B/2002/PN.JKT.PST dated July 26, 2002; and Independently Re-Adjudicating: (1) Declaring that the Defendant is proven to have committed the acts under Charge IV, but that such acts do not constitute a criminal offense; (2) Releasing the Defendant from legal prosecution regarding Charge IV, and restoring the Defendant's rights in capacity, position, honor, and dignity regarding Charge IV; (3) Declaring Defendant H. [Defendant] alias [Defendant] legally and convincingly proven guilty of committing the crimes of: I. Complicity in unlawfully controlling, storing, and concealing firearms and explosives; II. Unlawfully controlling, storing, and concealing firearms and explosives; III. Instigating (*uitlokker*) the commission of premeditated murder; (4) Sentencing the Defendant to imprisonment for a term of 10 (ten) years, with full credit for the period of detention and imprisonment already served; (5) Charging judicial review court costs amounting to Rp 2,500.

|-
| '''Related Regulations''' | HIR Article 178 paragraph (3) / RBg Article 189 paragraph (3) (Ultra Petita); HIR Article 227 / RBg Article 261 (Conservatory Attachment); Law No. 14 of 1970 on Basic Principles of Judicial Power (Article 40); Law No. 13 of 1965 in conjunction with Law No. 1 of 1950 on the Supreme Court

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision Reg. No. 394 K/Pdt/1984 (dated July 5, 1985) established a vital civil procedural law rule concerning the prohibition of placing conservatory attachments (*conservatoir beslag*) on property pledged as collateral for bank or state debts, alongside strict enforcement against *ultra petita* rulings (Article 178 paragraph (3) H.I.R.):


1. Assets already pledged as debt collateral to Bank Rakyat Indonesia (BRI) / State Banks cannot be subjected to conservatory attachments by individual creditors or other third parties.
2. The *Judex Facti* is prohibited from rendering decisions exceeding what is demanded (*ultra petita*), whether by establishing interest rates exceeding the petition claims or by adding obligations not requested by the Plaintiff.


== Executive Summary ==


The central procedural principles established in this decision govern the protection of preferential bank collateral rights against private attachments and reinforce the boundary of judicial relief within plaintiffs' explicit petitions.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Property encumbered as state bank credit collateral is immune to private conservatory attachments.
* Courts violate Article 178(3) HIR (*ultra petita*) by granting relief or interest rates higher than requested in the petition.
* Attachments remain valid solely over unencumbered assets not pledged to the state bank.


== Case Background ==


The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation, '''[Party A]''', sued Soekemi Saleh and Imam Sukarno Adiwidjojo (Defendants I & II), alongside BRI Gresik Branch and PUPN East Java (Defendants III & IV) at the Gresik District Court over breach of contract regarding the repayment of a Rp 2,500,000.— cash loan. 


The Plaintiff requested a conservatory attachment over the Defendants' assets. However, Defendants I & II had also secured a Rp 7,000,000.— credit facility from BRI Gresik Branch, pledging land and houses (SHM No. 6 Singosari Village and Model A No. 215/Kab/1973 Gumantar Village) as collateral. 


The Gresik District Court (Decision No. 40/1979/Pdt) and Surabaya High Court (Decision No. 771/1982 Perdata) partially granted the claim, validated attachments over all assets, and fixed interest rates. 


The Petitioner for Cassation subsequently appealed to the Supreme Court.


== Claims, Evidence and Source Mapping ==


{| class="wikitable"
! No.
! Legal Statement / Fact
! Evidence / Judicial Consideration
! Source
|-
| '''1'''
| '''Primary Legal Rule (Conservatory Attachment):''' Assets already pledged as debt collateral to BRI Gresik Branch cannot be subjected to conservatory attachments.
| Supreme Court consideration page 227: "...assets that have been pledged as debt collateral to Bank Rakyat Indonesia Gresik Branch cannot be subjected to conservatoir beslag;"
| 394K_Pdt_1984.pdf [Passages 1, 6]
|-
| '''2'''
| '''Primary Legal Rule (Ultra Petita):''' The *Judex Facti* violates Article 178 paragraph (3) H.I.R. when ruling beyond what is demanded (e.g., awarding 6% monthly interest when 5% was requested).
| Supreme Court consideration page 227: "this objection is justified, because the judex facti decided beyond what was demanded by the plaintiff..."
| 394K_Pdt_1984.pdf [Passages 5, 6]
|-
| '''3'''
| '''Debt & Agreement Facts:''' Defendant I borrowed Rp 2,500,000.— from the Plaintiff secured by movable and immovable property, alongside credit collateral at BRI Gresik.
| Private agreement in conjunction with Notarial Deed before Raden Hadiwido (October 16, 1976) & Evidence P.IV, P.V.
| 394K_Pdt_1984.pdf [Passages 2, 15, 16]
|-
| '''4'''
| '''Validity of Partial Conservatory Attachment:''' The attachment is declared valid and enforceable strictly regarding assets not pledged to BRI.
| Supreme Court Cassation Ruling: "Declaring valid and valuable the conservatoir beslag strictly regarding assets not pledged to Bank Rakyat Indonesia Gresik Branch;"
| 394K_Pdt_1984.pdf [Passage 7]
|-
| '''5'''
| '''Annulment of Judex Facti Decisions:''' Surabaya High Court Decision No. 771/1982 Perdata and Gresik District Court Decision No. 40/1979/Pdt were annulled by the Supreme Court.
| Cassation ruling dated July 5, 1985.
| 394K_Pdt_1984.pdf [Passage 7]
|}


== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Protection of Preferential Rights (*Droit de Préférence*) of State Banks Against Conservatory Attachments (Article 227 H.I.R.) ===


The procedural issue questioned whether immovable property encumbered with credit debt/collateral at a State Bank (BRI Gresik Branch) can be placed under a conservatory attachment (*conservatoir beslag*) by an individual unsecured creditor.


The Supreme Court ruled that it cannot. Assets pledged to secure credit at Bank Rakyat Indonesia (BRI) are protected from conservatory attachments initiated by third parties or unsecured creditors. Attachments remain valid solely over the Defendant's properties unencumbered by bank pledges.


=== Application of the Ultra Petita Principle (Article 178(3) H.I.R. / Article 189(3) RBg) ===


The issue questioned whether appellate courts violate procedural law by imposing interest rates exceeding the percentage petitioned by the Plaintiff.


The Supreme Court ruled that they do. Judges are strictly prohibited from granting relief beyond what is requested or ruling on matters unpetitioned (*ultra petita non petita*). The Plaintiff requested 5% monthly interest; thus, the Surabaya High Court's adoption of 6% constituted a procedural violation requiring annulment.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the *Judex Facti* violate Article 178 paragraph (3) H.I.R. by granting interest exceeding the petition and validating a conservatory attachment over BRI bank collateral?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the *Judex Facti* violated procedural law. Placing an attachment on BRI debt collateral is void/invalid, and granting interest exceeding the petition constitutes *ultra petita*.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Gresik District Court & Surabaya High Court) ===


Examination of the Rp 2,500,000.— debt agreement between [Party A] (Plaintiff) and Soekemi Saleh & Imam Sukarno Adiwidjojo (Defendants I & II), Notarial Deed of Raden Hadiwido dated October 16, 1976, Ownership Certificates (SHM No. 6 Singosari Village and Model A No. 215/Kab/1973 Gumantar Village) pledged to BRI Gresik Branch, and auction announcements by PUPN East Java Branch.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
1. The *Judex Facti* violated Article 178 paragraph (3) H.I.R. (*ultra petita*) by fixing an interest rate of 6% when the Plaintiff only claimed 5% per month, and by introducing unrequested obligations.
2. Furthermore, assets already pledged as debt collateral to Bank Rakyat Indonesia (BRI) Gresik Branch cannot be subjected to conservatory attachments (*conservatoir beslag*). Attachments are valid only for assets not pledged to BRI. The Supreme Court annulled the Surabaya High Court and Gresik District Court decisions.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Party A]'''), annulled Surabaya High Court Decision No. 771/1982 Perdata in conjunction with Gresik District Court Decision No. 40/1979/Pdt, and Adjudicated Directly: Granting the Plaintiff's claim in part; Declaring Defendants I and II in default; Declaring valid and valuable the conservatory attachment strictly regarding assets not pledged to Bank Rakyat Indonesia Gresik Branch; Ordering Defendants I and II jointly and severally to pay their debt of Rp 2,500,000.— plus 6% annual interest from October 1976 until fully paid; Rejecting all other claims; and ordering Defendants I and II to bear court costs across all judicial instances.


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''HIR Article 178 paragraph (3) / RBg Article 189 paragraph (3):''' The *Ultra Petita* principle prohibiting judges from ruling on unrequested matters or granting more than requested.
* '''HIR Article 227 / RBg Article 261:''' Provisions governing Conservatory Attachments (*Conservatoir Beslag*).
* '''Banking & Collateral Law:''' The preferential right (*droit de préférence*) of bank/state collateral holders takes precedence over concurrent creditors, preventing bank collateral assets from being attached by other creditors.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* Defendants I and II breached their contract regarding the principal debt of Rp 2,500,000.— owed to the Plaintiff.
* Land and buildings (SHM No. 6 Singosari Village and Model A No. 215/Kab/1973 Gumantar Village) were legally pledged as collateral to BRI Gresik Branch for a Rp 7,000,000.— credit facility.
* The Plaintiff claimed loan interest limited to 5% per month.


=== Not Established / Rejected ===


* The Plaintiff has no right to request a conservatory attachment (*conservatoir beslag*) over assets of Defendants I and II that serve as official debt collateral at BRI Gresik Branch.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Lower courts (Gresik District Court and Surabaya High Court) initially erred by ordering Defendants to settle BRI debts within private civil judgments. The Supreme Court corrected this by ruling that courts cannot add third-party debt settlement orders not requested in the Plaintiff's petitum.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Can land or buildings serving as credit collateral at BRI Bank be subjected to conservatory attachments (*conservatoir beslag*) by other parties?'''


'''A:''' No. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 394 K/Pdt/1984, assets already pledged as debt collateral to Bank Rakyat Indonesia (BRI) or State Banks cannot be subjected to conservatory attachments (*conservatoir beslag*). Conservatory attachments filed by individual creditors are valid and valuable solely over assets not pledged to the bank.

|-
| colspan="2" style="background: #2b6cb0; color: #fff; font-weight: bold; font-size: 90%; text-align: center;" |⚖️ JPAIS Metadata

|-
