|-
|347.07
|-
|[Party A], [Party E], [Party D], [Party C], [Party B], Simulated Sale and Purchase, Debt Security, Plurium Litis Consortium, Deficient Parties, Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard, Onvoldoende Gemotiveerd, Purwokerto District Court, Semarang High Court
|-
|Civil Code (KUHPerdata) Articles 1320, 1457; Law No. 14 of 1970 on Basic Principles of Judicial Power (Article 40); Law No. 13 of 1965 in conjunction with Law No. 1 of 1950 on the Supreme Court
|}

== Overview ==
Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 400 K/Pdt/1984, dated July 19, 1985, established a highly important civil procedural law rule concerning the formal defect of deficient parties (*plurium litis consortium*) in simulated transactions.

The Supreme Court held that if a land/house purchase agreement is inherently a simulated transaction to secure the repayment of a debt between the Plaintiff and a third party (the Defendant's son), the Defendant's son, who is the primary debtor, must be joined as a defendant. Failing to join the primary debtor as a defendant renders the Plaintiff's lawsuit deficient in parties (formally defective) and subject to dismissal as inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).

== Executive Summary ==
The central procedural principle established in this decision is that when a formal sale and purchase agreement masks an underlying debt-securing arrangement involving a third party, that third-party debtor is a necessary party to the litigation.

Key elements established in the adjudication:

* The substantive legal relationship of a simulated debt-security transaction requires joining the principal debtor as a defendant; failure to do so results in a formal defect (*plurium litis consortium*), rendering the claim inadmissible (NO).
* Courts must scrutinize the actual cause (*oorzaak*) of an agreement rather than relying solely on formal contract documentation.
* Lower courts (*judex facti*) that fail to examine underlying causes and witness testimonies commit flawed reasoning (*onvoldoende gemotiveerd*).

== Case Background ==
The Original Plaintiff / Respondent for Cassation, '''[Party D] ([Party C])''', filed a lawsuit at the Purwokerto District Court against the Original Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation, '''[Party A] ([Party E])''', seeking the eviction and surrender of land and a house under Ownership Certificate (SHM) No. 358 in Purwokerto Kidul based on a Sale and Purchase Deed dated June 6, 1981.

The Defendant resisted the claim, arguing that the deed was executed under pressure as a security guarantee for debts owed by his son, [Party B], to the Plaintiff. It was revealed during trial proceedings that the transaction was a simulated arrangement covering [Party B]'s debt. However, the Plaintiff did not join [Party B] as a party to the lawsuit.

The Purwokerto District Court (Decision No. 34/1981/Pdt.G) and the Semarang High Court (Decision No. 194/1982/Pdt/PT.Smg) granted the Plaintiff's claim. The Petitioner for Cassation subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Claims, Evidence and Source Mapping ==
{| class="wikitable"
!No.
!Legal Statement / Fact
!Evidence / Judicial Consideration
!Source
|-
|'''1'''
|'''Primary Legal Principle:''' A simulated legal relationship (child's debt) requires joining the child as a defendant; otherwise, the claim is formally defective (NO).
|Supreme Court Consideration: "...because the actual legal relationship is a debt-credit relationship between the original plaintiff and [Party B], the original defendant's son, but [Party B] was not co-defendant... the lawsuit is incomplete or defective and must be declared inadmissible;"
|400K_PDT_1984.pdf, Passages 1 and 6
|-
|'''2'''
|'''Existence of a Simulated Transaction:''' Land/house sale and purchase deeds No. 5 dated February 6, 1980, and June 6, 1981, were essentially securities for [Party B]'s debt to [Party D].
|Testimony of witnesses in court (Wongsogiono & Liong Tje Kwong) explaining [Party B]'s debt of Rp 25,700,000.- and the collateralization of certificates under his father's name ([Party A]).
|400K_PDT_1984.pdf, Passages 5, 6, 17, and 18
|-
|'''3'''
|'''Flawed Judicial Consideration (*Judex Facti*):''' The *Judex Facti* gave insufficient reasoning (*onvoldoende gemotiveerd*) by evaluating the sale deed solely on its formal terms.
|Supreme Court Consideration: The *Judex Facti* failed to evaluate the cause (*oorzaak*) of the agreement ex Article 1457 of the Civil Code and ignored real evidence of the debt-credit relationship.
|400K_PDT_1984.pdf, Passages 5 and 6
|-
|'''4'''
|'''Identity of the Parties:''' Petitioner for Cassation / Original Defendant: [Party A] ([Party E]); Respondent for Cassation / Original Plaintiff: [Party D] ([Party C]).
|Expressly stated in the identity sections of the Supreme Court, Semarang High Court, and Purwokerto District Court decisions.
|400K_PDT_1984.pdf, Passages 1, 8, 12, and 15
|-
|'''5'''
|'''Annulment Ruling:''' The Supreme Court annulled Semarang High Court Decision No. 194/1982/Pdt/PT.Smg and Purwokerto District Court Decision No. 34/1981/Pdt.G.
|Adjudicating afresh: "Declaring that the plaintiff's lawsuit is inadmissible."
|400K_PDT_1984.pdf, Passages 3, 7, 8, and 11
|}

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==

=== Construction of Simulated Agreements & Agreement Cause (Articles 1457 & 1320 Civil Code) ===
The issue evaluated whether the creation of a Sale and Purchase Deed before a Notary/PPAT is formally binding as a pure sale when the true cause (*oorzaak*) is a third-party debt security.

The Supreme Court ruled that it is not. Courts are obligated to examine the true legal cause of a transaction. If proven that a sale and purchase transaction is a simulated arrangement to secure third-party debt repayment, the primary binding obligation is debt-credit.

=== Deficient Parties (Plurium Litis Consortium) ===
The issue evaluated whether an execution/eviction lawsuit over a simulated purchase object is valid if the Plaintiff fails to join the principal debtor ([Party B]) who holds the primary debt obligation.

The Supreme Court held that it is invalid. Because the principal debtor ([Party B]) is the legal subject who created the debt obligation and surrendered collateral, failing to join [Party B] as a defendant renders the lawsuit formally defective (*plurium litis consortium*) and subject to dismissal as inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).

== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===
'''Question:'''

Did the *Judex Facti* (Semarang High Court & Purwokerto District Court) misapply evidentiary law and provide flawed reasoning (*onvoldoende gemotiveerd*) by ignoring the nature of the simulated transaction and failing to declare the lawsuit formally defective due to missing parties (*plurium litis consortium*)?

'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''

Yes. The *Judex Facti* misapplied the law. Disregarding the existence of the principal debtor ([Party B]) in a simulated sale case constitutes a fundamental breach of procedural law.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Purwokerto District & Semarang High Courts) ===
Examination of the history of Ownership Certificate (SHM) No. 358 in Purwokerto Kidul (area 413 m²), witness testimonies from Wongsogiono, Liong Tje Kwong, and Mashudi regarding [Party B]'s total loan (Rp 25,700,000.-), and the drafting process of Notary Sutardjo Sumoatmodjo's deeds.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The *Judex Facti* misapplied evidentiary law and provided insufficient reasoning (*onvoldoende gemotiveerd*) by evaluating the sale deed purely on formal grounds without considering the agreement cause (*oorzaak*) ex Article 1457 of the Civil Code and witness statements.
# It was proven that the disputed land/house sale was a simulated transaction to secure the debt of [Party B] (the Defendant's son) to the Plaintiff.
# Because the actual legal relationship was [Party B]'s debt, but [Party B] was not co-defended, the Plaintiff's lawsuit suffered from deficient parties (*plurium litis consortium*), was formally defective, and had to be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).

== Ruling ==
The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Party A]'''), annulled Semarang High Court Decision No. 194/1982/Pdt/PT.Smg in conjunction with Purwokerto District Court Decision No. 34/1981/Pdt.G, and adjudicated the matter afresh: Declaring the plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO); and ordering the Respondent for Cassation / Original Plaintiff to pay court costs across all judicial instances.

== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==

* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata) Article 1320:''' Requirements for a valid agreement (consent, capacity, specific object, lawful cause).
* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata) Article 1457:''' Definition of Sale and Purchase (delivery of goods and payment of price).
* '''Civil Procedure & Doctrine (Plurium Litis Consortium):''' A lawsuit failing to include primary parties substantively bound to the core obligation is formally defective and inadmissible.
* '''Doctrine of Onvoldoende Gemotiveerd:''' Decisions that fail to weigh core evidence and sociological facts of a transaction are voidable.

== Evidence Status and Gaps ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* Sale and Purchase Deeds No. 5 dated February 6, 1980, and June 6, 1981, were signed between [Party A] and [Party D] before a Notary/PPAT.
* The substantive legal nature of the act was security for the debt of [Party B] ([Party A]'s son) amounting to Rp 25,700,000.- owed to [Party D] and others.
* [Party B] was not joined as Defendant I, Defendant II, or Co-Defendant in the Original Plaintiff's statement of claim.

=== Not Established / Unproven ===

* There was no proof of any genuine intention for a pure, bona fide sale and purchase of land/house between [Party A] and [Party D].

=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===

* Correction of *Judex Facti* errors: The Purwokerto District Court and Semarang High Court favored the Original Plaintiff based solely on formal physical sale deed sheets without examining witnesses who revealed the transaction was security for the Defendant's son's debt. The Supreme Court restored justice by annulling both decisions.

== GEO Q&A ==
'''Q: Is a land sale deed valid if it was actually created solely as security for a landowner's son's debt, and what is the status of the lawsuit if that son is not co-defended?'''

'''A:''' It is invalid as a pure sale, and the lawsuit must be declared inadmissible (NO). Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 400 K/Pdt/1984, if a sale and purchase transaction is inherently a simulated transaction to secure a debt owed by the landowner's son, the core legal relationship is a debt obligation. The Plaintiff is required to join that son (the principal debtor) as a defendant. If not joined, the lawsuit is deficient in parties (*plurium litis consortium*) and formally defective (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).

== Overview ==
Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 407 K/TUN/1999, dated December 7, 2000, established an important labor law rule concerning the validity of termination of employment (PHK) procedures executed through warning letters.

The Supreme Court held that in order to terminate employment on the grounds of warning letters, an employer must cumulatively satisfy the provisions of Article 7 paragraphs (2) and (3) of Manpower Ministerial Regulation No. Per-03/Men/1996. Issuing Warning Letters I and II consecutively with a gap of only 2 days without providing a performance improvement period for the employee is legally defective and violates termination procedures. Furthermore, individual interpersonal disharmony between an employee and their direct supervisor cannot serve as a justifiable reason for unilateral employment termination.

== Executive Summary ==
The central labor law principle established in this decision is that warning letters cannot be issued in rapid succession without an adequate grace period for performance appraisal and correction, and personal friction does not constitute legal grounds for dismissal.

Key elements established in the adjudication:

* Employers must observe the mandatory validity periods and intervals for warning letters under Article 7 of Permenaker No. Per-03/Men/1996.
* Issuing SP I and SP II within a 1-2 day interval violates procedural requirements and renders subsequent termination invalid.
* Interpersonal conflicts between employees and supervisors require management intervention through rotation or transfer rather than arbitrary termination.

== Case Background ==
The Original Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation, '''P4P Pusat''', faced a lawsuit filed by the Original Plaintiff / Respondent for Cassation, '''PT Petrosea Tbk.''', at the Jakarta High Administrative Court concerning Central Committee for Labor Dispute Settlement (P4P) Decision No. 1488/1326/316-1/IX/PHK/9-1998 dated September 25, 1998.

The P4P decision had rejected the employer's request for permission to terminate the employment of worker '''[Plaintiff]''' (Tax Accountant) and ordered his reinstatement. The employer argued that [Plaintiff] was negligent in completing tax reconciliation duties and had been issued Warning Letter I (December 23, 1997) and Warning Letter II (December 24, 1997).

The Jakarta High Administrative Court (Decision No. 139/G/1998/PT.TUN.JKT) annulled the P4P decision and permitted the termination. The Petitioner for Cassation subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==

=== Formal Validity Requirements of Warning Letters (Article 7 Permenaker No. Per-03/Men/1996) ===
The issue evaluated whether issuing Warning Letters I and II consecutively within a 1–2 day interval is valid as a legal basis for imposing termination.

The Supreme Court held that it is invalid. Pursuant to Article 7 paragraphs (2) and (3) of Permenaker No. Per-03/Men/1996, each warning letter has a validity period of 6 months aimed at providing guidance and opportunity for the worker to improve performance. Issuing SP II only 1–2 days after SP I constitutes arbitrary action violating formal termination requirements.

=== Limits of Employment Disharmony as Grounds for Termination ===
The issue evaluated whether interpersonal conflict between an employee and a direct supervisor (*personal friction*) qualifies as "disharmonious employment relations" validating unilateral termination.

The Supreme Court held that it does not. Corporate management is obligated to pursue job rotation or unit transfer to address inter-individual conflicts. Invoking personal disharmony without adequate guidance violates the principles of balance and protection of vulnerable workers.

== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===
'''Question:'''

Did the *Judex Facti* (Jakarta High Administrative Court) misapply labor law (Article 7 of Permenaker No. Per-03/Men/1996 jo. Law No. 12 of 1964) by validating a termination action based on SP I and SP II issued consecutively within a 2-day interval?

'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''

Yes, the Jakarta High Administrative Court misapplied the law. Consequently, the appellate decision was annulled and the employer's lawsuit was rejected.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Jakarta High Administrative Court & P4P) ===
Examination of the chronological duties of Tax Compliance Reconciliation by [Plaintiff], the issuance of Ref. Letter 601/FIN/234 (SP I dated Dec 23, 1997) and Ref. Letter 601/FIN/237 (SP II dated Dec 24, 1997) by Hendrick U. Ibrahim, and unproven police reports concerning computer data.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The appellate *Judex Facti* misapplied the law. Under Article 7 paragraphs (2) and (3) of Permenaker No. Per-03/Men/1996, termination via warning letters must comply with applicable legal procedures.
# Issuing SP I and SP II with only a 2-day gap (December 23 and 24, 1997) failed to provide a reasonable guidance period for the worker.
# Furthermore, interpersonal disharmony between an employee and a direct supervisor cannot serve as grounds for unilateral termination.
# The Supreme Court annulled the Jakarta High Administrative Court decision and adjudicated afresh by rejecting PT Petrosea Tbk.'s lawsuit in its entirety.

== Ruling ==
The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation ('''PANITIA PENYELESAIAN PERSELISIHAN PERBURUHAN PUSAT / P4P'''), annulled Jakarta High Administrative Court Decision No. 139/G/1998/PT.TUN.JKT dated June 1, 1999, and adjudicated afresh: Rejecting the Plaintiff's (PT Petrosea Tbk.) lawsuit in its entirety; and ordering the Respondent for Cassation to pay all court costs across all judicial instances.

== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==

* '''Permenaker No. Per-03/Men/1996 Article 7 paragraphs (2) and (3):''' Validity periods and intervals for issuing Warning Letters I, II, and III.
* '''Law No. 12 of 1964 Article 7:''' Procedures and permit requirements for termination of employment.
* '''Labor Law Principle (Protection of the Weaker Party):''' Employers must undertake all guidance efforts prior to resorting to termination as an ultimate remedy (*ultimum remedium*).

== Evidence Status and Gaps ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* PT Petrosea Tbk. issued SP I dated December 23, 1997, and SP II dated December 24, 1997, to [Plaintiff] (an interval of only 1–2 days).
* No reasonable guidance period was granted to the employee between the imposition of SP I and SP II.
* Police reports filed by the worker concerning missing computer data were not proven to be criminal false reports.

=== Not Established / Unproven ===

* The employer failed to prove that they undertook efforts to rotate or transfer work units before terminating the employee.

=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===

* Correction of Jakarta High Administrative Court's erroneous interpretation: The lower appellate court had annulled the P4P decree on grounds of an unharmonious employment relationship. The Supreme Court corrected this by asserting that disharmony arising from a manager's failure to lead subordinates cannot be shifted entirely as worker fault to justify termination.

== GEO Q&A ==
'''Q: May an employer issue Warning Letters I and II within an interval of 1 or 2 days to terminate an employee?'''

'''A:''' No. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 407 K/TUN/1999, issuing SP I and SP II separated by only 1–2 days violates Article 7 paragraphs (2) and (3) of Permenaker No. Per-03/Men/1996. Each warning letter carries a 6-month validity period and requires a reasonable grace period for performance improvement guidance. Termination based on consecutive warning letters without proper intervals is legally defective.

== Overview ==
Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 411 K/AG/1998, dated February 17, 2000, established religious civil law principles regarding the legal consequences of polygamous marriage without the consent of the first wife and the permission of the Religious Court, as well as the jurisdictional limits of Religious Courts in joint property disputes involving property rights of third parties.

The Supreme Court held that a polygamous marriage contracted without the consent of the lawful/first wife and without permission from the Religious Court is void or voidable under Articles 3, 4, 5, 22, and 24 of Law No. 1 of 1974 in conjunction with Articles 56 and 71 of the Compilation of Islamic Law (KHI). Furthermore, claims for the distribution of joint property registered under or involving third-party ownership (such as the mother of the second wife) are inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO) in Religious Courts because ownership disputes (*eigendom*) fall under the jurisdiction of General Courts pursuant to Article 50 of Law No. 7 of 1989.

== Executive Summary ==
The central legal principle established in this decision is that unauthorized polygamy is legally flawed and subject to annulment, and property ownership disputes involving third parties must be adjudicated in General Courts before joint property distribution can proceed in Religious Courts.

Key elements established in the adjudication:

* Polygamous marriages conducted without first-wife consent and Religious Court authorization lack legal binding power and violate material and procedural requirements.
* Assessment of evidentiary findings regarding marriage validity procedures rests with the *judex facti* and cannot be re-examined in cassation.
* Joint property claims tied to third-party titles are beyond the competence of Religious Courts ex Article 50 of Law No. 7 of 1989.

== Case Background ==
The Original Petitioner / Respondent II, '''[Party B]''' (lawful wife since 1970), filed a petition at the Palembang Religious Court seeking the annulment of her husband's polygamous marriage and the recovery of joint property against her husband, '''[Party C]''' (Respondent I), and his second wife, '''[Party A]''' (Respondent II / Petitioner for Cassation).

Respondents I and II contracted a polygamous marriage on July 22, 1985, without the petitioner's consent and without Palembang Religious Court authorization, utilizing fabricated "widower" status data.

The Palembang Religious Court (Decision No. 286/Pdt.G/1997/PA.Plg) annulled the marriage and declared joint property claims registered under a third party (Ny. Martina / mother of Respondent II) inadmissible (NO). The Palembang High Religious Court (Decision No. 15/Pdt.G/1998/PTA.Plg) affirmed the ruling with modifications. The Petitioner for Cassation subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==

=== Validity Requirements of Polygamous Marriage (Articles 3, 4, 5 Law No. 1 of 1974 jo. Article 56 KHI) ===
The issue evaluated whether a second polygamous marriage contracted by a husband without the first wife's consent and without Religious Court approval possesses binding legal force.

The Supreme Court held that it possesses no binding legal force. Polygamous marriage without first wife and court consent violates material and procedural rules of Islamic marriage law in Indonesia, rendering the issued marriage certificate void and without legal power.

=== Jurisdiction of Religious Courts over Third-Party Property Rights (Article 50 Law No. 7 of 1989) ===
The issue evaluated whether Religious Courts have authority to examine and adjudicate joint property division claims where ownership certificates are registered under third parties (other than husband/wife).

The Supreme Court held they lack authority. Under Article 50 of Law No. 7 of 1989 on Religious Courts, if joint property disputes involve property rights (*eigendom*) registered under a third party (in this case, Respondent II's mother), ownership disputes must first be resolved through General Courts (District Courts).

== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===
'''Question:'''

Did the *Judex Facti* (Palembang High Religious & District Religious Courts) misapply religious civil law by annulling the unauthorized polygamous marriage certificate and declaring joint property claims under third parties inadmissible (NO) ex Article 50 of Law No. 7 of 1989?

'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''

No, the *Judex Facti* did not misapply the law. Assessment of polygamous registration status and document ownership is the authority of the *Judex Facti*. The Supreme Court merely refined the wording of the ruling.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Palembang Religious & High Religious Courts) ===
Evaluation of the marriage facts between [Party B] & [Party C] in 1970 (Marriage Book No. 105/1970), [Party C] & [Party A]'s polygamous marriage in 1985 (Marriage Certificate No. 511/95/VII/AR/IT.1/85), and inspection of shop-house/land certificates under Ny. Martina's name (SHM Nos. 856, 118, 2135, 194).

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The *Judex Facti* did not misapply the law. Evaluating evidentiary findings regarding polygamous procedure validity is the exclusive domain of the *Judex Facti* and cannot be reviewed in cassation.
# Polygamous marriages without first wife and Religious Court consent are void ex Articles 3, 4, and 5 of Law No. 1 of 1974 in conjunction with Article 56 of the KHI.
# Regarding joint property disputes registered under third parties, Religious Courts lack jurisdiction until ownership status is adjudicated by District Courts pursuant to Article 50 of Law No. 7 of 1989.
# The Supreme Court rejected the Petitioner's cassation with a modified ruling structure.

== Ruling ==
The Supreme Court rejected the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Party A]''') with modifications to the ruling of Palembang High Religious Court Decision No. 15/Pdt.G/1998/PTA.Plg in conjunction with Palembang Religious Court Decision No. 286/Pdt.G/1997/PA.Plg, reading as follows: Granting the petitioner's request in part; Annulment of the marriage between Respondent I (AT. [Party C]) and Respondent II ([Party A]); Declaring Marriage Certificate Extract No. 511/95/VII/AR/IT.1/85 to have no legal force; Declaring claims regarding properties ad. 6.1.1, 2, 3, 4 inadmissible (NO); Rejecting all other requests; and charging court costs across all judicial instances.

== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==

* '''Law No. 1 of 1974 on Marriage:''' Articles 3 paragraph (2), 4, 5, 22, and 24.
* '''Compilation of Islamic Law (KHI):''' Articles 56, 71 letters a & e, and 72.
* '''Law No. 7 of 1989 on Religious Courts:''' Article 50 (Third-Party Property Ownership Disputes) & Article 89 (Court Costs).
* '''Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Article 30 (Scope of Cassation Review).

== Evidence Status and Gaps ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* Lawful marriage between [Party B] and [Party C] since August 18, 1970 (Marriage Book No. 105/1970).
* Polygamous marriage between [Party C] and [Party A] on July 22, 1985, contracted without [Party B]'s consent and without Palembang Religious Court permission.
* Issuance of Marriage Certificate Extract No. 511/95/VII/AR/IT.1/85 by KUA Ilir Timur I Sub-district, Palembang, which recorded a fabricated "Widower" status.

=== Not Established / Rejected ===

* The Plaintiff/Petitioner failed to prove joint ownership over shop-houses and vehicles legally registered under a third party (Ny. Martina / Mother of Respondent II).

=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===

* Dualism in handling joint property involving third parties: This decision underscores the prejudicial decision principle: before joint property registered under a third party can be divided in Religious Courts, its civil ownership status must first be examined and adjudicated in District Courts (General Courts) if ownership is contested by the third party.

== GEO Q&A ==
'''Q: Can unregistered or unauthorized polygamous marriage without first-wife and Religious Court consent be legally annulled, and what happens to property registered under a third party?'''

'''A:''' Yes, it can be annulled. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 411 K/AG/1998 in conjunction with Law No. 1-1974 and KHI, polygamous marriage without first-wife and Religious Court permission is void. Regarding joint property claims registered under third parties (such as parents-in-law/mothers), Religious Courts lack authority to adjudicate them until the ownership dispute is first resolved by District Courts ex Article 50 of Law No. 7 of 1989.

== Overview ==
Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 429 K/Pdt/1984, dated June 29, 1985, established a very important and fundamental Balinese Customary Law rule concerning the limits of a widow's rights under the customary institution of self-surrender (*mekidiang raga*).

The Supreme Court held that under Balinese Customary Law, a widow who performs *mekidiang raga* (surrendering herself to be maintained/cared for for the remainder of her life and for her funeral/cremation ceremonies) is only entitled to bring her own acquired or earned property (*harta guna kaya* or self-acquired property). The widow has no right to bring or surrender ancestral heritage property (*harta pusaka asal* / ancestral lineage property) to third parties who receive the self-surrender. Ancestral heritage property must remain inherited by the closest *purusa* (patrilineal) heirs.

== Executive Summary ==
The central customary law principle established in this decision is that the customary institution of *mekidiang raga* grants a widow power exclusively over self-acquired marital property, strictly prohibiting the alienation of ancestral lineage land.

Key elements established in the adjudication:

* A widow performing *mekidiang raga* can only transfer *harta guna kaya*, not ancestral lineage assets (*harta pusaka asal*).
* Extinction of direct male heirs (*camput/putung*) triggers the reversion of ancestral land to collateral *purusa* line relatives rather than external caretakers.
* Appellate court misinterpretation of customary land transfer powers is subject to correction and annulment in cassation.

== Case Background ==
The Original Plaintiff / Respondent for Cassation, '''I Made Kakak Latri''', filed a lawsuit against the Original Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation, '''I Simpen''', at the Amlapura District Court concerning the possession of two parcels of rice field land in Subak Buisi, Banjar Telengan. The Plaintiff claimed the land was legally acquired from Ni Panggih (widow of I Tulak Panggih) who performed self-surrender (*mekidiang raga*) to the Plaintiff before the Head of Manggis Sub-district in 1967.

The Defendant contested the claim on the grounds that the disputed land was ancestral heritage property (*harta pusaka asal*) originating from ancestor I Gunung and that the Defendant was the closest legitimate *purusa* heir.

The Amlapura District Court (Decision No. 1/Pts.Pdt.G/1983/PN.Amlapura) rejected the Plaintiff's lawsuit. The Denpasar High Court (Decision No. 69/Pdt/1983/PTD) annulled the district court decision and granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit. The Petitioner for Cassation (I Simpen) subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Claims, Evidence and Source Mapping ==

|429K_PDT_1984.pdf, Passages 5, 18, and 24

|429K_PDT_1984.pdf, Passages 5, 23, and 25

|}

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==

=== Limits of Widow Rights in Balinese Customary Law Institution of Mekidiang Raga ===
The primary issue was whether under Balinese Customary Law a widow (Ni Panggih) lacking direct male descendants (*camput/putung*) has the right to surrender family/ancestral heritage land belonging to her late husband's lineage to a third party through the self-surrender institution (*mekidiang raga*).

The Supreme Court held that she has no such right. The institution of *mekidiang raga* authorizes a widow solely to bring and surrender *harta guna kaya* (joint marital property acquired through joint efforts during marriage). Ancestral heritage property (*kawitan*) remains the property of the *purusa* kindred and cannot be transferred to outsiders.

=== Protection of Purusa Heir Rights over Ancestral Heritage Land ===
The issue evaluated the ownership status of ancestral heritage land when a nuclear family experiences extinction of direct male lines (*camput/putung*).

The Supreme Court ruled that in cases of extinction (*camput*), ancestral heritage property reverts to and is inherited by collateral line *purusa* relatives sharing blood lineage (in *casu* I Simpen), rather than becoming property of the recipient of the *mekidiang raga*.

== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===
'''Question:'''

Did the Denpasar High Court misapply Balinese customary law by assuming that a widow's self-surrender (*mekidiang raga*) automatically transfers rights over all property, including ancestral lineage land belonging to her husband's ancestors?

'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''

Yes, the Denpasar High Court misapplied customary law. The High Court's ruling contradicted foundational principles of Balinese customary inheritance law. Consequently, the Denpasar High Court decision was annulled.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Amlapura District Court & Denpasar High Court) ===
Examination of the lineage genealogy of I Gunung, the marital status of I Tulak Panggih and Ni Panggih, the *mekidiang raga* execution before the Head of Manggis Sub-district on June 19, 1967 / November 28, 1967, Ni Panggih's cremation (*Ngaben*) ceremony on November 21, 1967, and the classification of origin for the 2 plots of rice fields in Subak Buisi.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The Denpasar High Court misapplied Balinese customary law. A widow executing *mekidiang raga* is only entitled to bring self-acquired property (*harta guna kaya*).
# A widow has no right to bring or surrender ancestral heritage land originating from her husband's ancestors to third parties.
# Because the disputed land was proven to be ancestral lineage property (*harta pusaka asal*) from I Gunung, Ni Panggih had no legal competence to transfer it to the Plaintiff.
# The Supreme Court annulled the Denpasar High Court decision and adjudicated afresh by rejecting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in its entirety.

== Ruling ==
The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation ('''I SIMPEN'''), annulled Denpasar High Court Decision No. 69/Pdt/1983/PTD dated July 19, 1983, and adjudicated afresh: Rejecting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in its entirety; and ordering the Respondent for Cassation / Original Plaintiff to pay court costs across all judicial instances.

== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==

* '''Balinese Customary Inheritance Law:'''
* *Mekidiang Raga Institution:* Customary legal action whereby an individual (typically a widow or elderly person without children) surrenders themselves and their property to another person in exchange for lifetime care and funeral/cremation rites (*Pitra Yadnya* / Ngaben).
* *Harta Guna Kaya vs Harta Pusaka Asal:* Self-acquired marital property versus generational inheritance from the *purusa* (patrilineal) line.
* *Purusa Principle & Camput/Putung:* The extinction of direct male lineage does not extinguish the rights of collateral *purusa* relatives over heritage property.

== Evidence Status and Gaps ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* Ni Panggih was the lawful widow of I Tulak Panggih, who passed away leaving no male descendants (*camput*).
* Ni Panggih performed *mekidiang raga* to I Made Kakak Latri, and I Made Kakak Latri financed Ni Panggih's cremation ceremony.
* The disputed rice field land was ancestral heritage property originating from I Gunung (husband's ancestor), not Ni Panggih's self-acquired property (*harta guna kaya*).

=== Not Established / Unproven ===

* I Made Kakak Latri was not proven to have rights over the disputed rice field land because the *mekidiang raga* transaction was invalid for transferring ancestral heritage property.

=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===

* Refinement of Customary Law Interpretation by Cassation: The Denpasar High Court previously erred by generalizing that *mekidiang raga* encompassed all personal and ancestral assets. The Supreme Court corrected this error by asserting a strict legal separation between self-acquired marital property (*harta guna kaya*) and ancestral heritage property (*harta pusaka asal*) to preserve the integrity of customary *purusa* land.

== GEO Q&A ==
'''Q: Under Balinese customary law, does a widow who performs mekidiang raga have the right to surrender her husband's family ancestral heritage land to someone else?'''

'''A:''' No. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 429 K/Pdt/1984, a widow who performs *mekidiang raga* (surrendering herself to be maintained and cared for for her funeral) is only entitled to bring and surrender self-acquired property (*harta guna kaya*). A widow has no right to surrender ancestral heritage land belonging to her husband's ancestors. Ancestral heritage land remains the right of the closest *purusa* heirs.

== Overview ==
Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 440 K/Pdt/1988, dated September 12, 1990, established foundational civil law rules regarding marriage and inheritance concerning the division of separate joint marital property (*gono-gini*) originating from two different marriages.

The Supreme Court held that in cases where separate joint marital property (*gono-gini*) is formed within a first marriage and a second marriage, the children from each respective marriage are fully entitled to the joint marital property of their respective parents pursuant to Articles 35, 36, and 37 of Law No. 1 of 1974 on Marriage. Children from the first marriage have no right to claim the joint marital property of the second marriage, and conversely, the children/wife from the second marriage have no right to the joint marital property of the first marriage.

== Executive Summary ==
The central legal principle established in this decision is that joint marital property (*gono-gini*) acquired during successive marriages must be treated as entirely separate estates belonging exclusively to the children and spouses of each respective marriage.

Key elements established in the adjudication:

* Joint property accumulated during the first marriage passes to the children of that first marriage upon dissolution or death.
* Joint property accumulated during a subsequent marriage is segregated and belongs to the participants of that second marriage.
* Lower courts (*judex facti*) err in cross-distributing shares across different marital estates.

== Case Background ==
The Original Plaintiffs / Respondents for Cassation, '''Ny. [Party D]''' and '''Ny. [Party E]''' (children from [Deceased parent]'s first marriage with the late [Party B]), filed a lawsuit at the Purwodadi District Court against the Original Defendants / Petitioners for Cassation, '''Ny. [Party C]''' (second wife) and her children ([Party F], [Party A], Subadi, Sumarto), concerning the control over all estate assets left by [Deceased parent].

The Plaintiffs sought a 3/4 share of the first marriage properties (Ad. A.1 to A.9) and a 1/4 share of the second marriage properties (Ad. B.1 to B.7). The Purwodadi District Court (Decision No. 41/Pdt.G/1986/PN.Pwi) and the Semarang High Court (Decision No. 388/Pdt/1987/PT.Smg) granted the lawsuit using this cross-distribution scheme. The Petitioners for Cassation subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==

=== Segregation of First and Second Marital Estates (Articles 35, 36, 37 Law No. 1 of 1974) ===
The primary issue was how inheritance and joint property should be divided when a husband enters into two successive marriages, each producing separate joint marital estates and offspring.

The Supreme Court held that joint property acquired during the first marriage is common property of the husband and the first wife. Upon the first wife's death, that joint property transforms into the inheritance of the children from the first marriage. Conversely, joint property acquired during the second marriage belongs to the husband and the second wife, forming the inheritance of the children/spouse from the second marriage.

=== Correction of Judex Facti Errors in Cross-Distributing Inheritance Portions ===
The issue evaluated whether the lower courts (*judex facti* - Purwodadi District Court & Semarang High Court) correctly ruled that the Plaintiffs (children of the 1st marriage) were entitled to a 3/4 share of the 1st marriage estate and 1/4 of the 2nd marriage estate, while the Defendants (2nd wife and children) received 1/4 of the 1st marriage estate and 3/4 of the 2nd marriage estate.

The Supreme Court held that this cross-distribution was legally incorrect, as the lower courts mistakenly commingled the inheritance of the first and second marital estates. Under national marriage law principles (Law No. 1 of 1974), first-marriage joint property is strictly segregated from second-marriage joint property.

== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===
'''Question:'''

Did the *Judex Facti* (Semarang High Court & Purwodadi District Court) misapply the law (Articles 35, 36, 37 of Law No. 1 of 1974) by dividing first- and second-marriage joint property through cross-shares (3/4 and 1/4 proportions) rather than strictly segregating them based on their marital origin?

'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''

Yes, the *Judex Facti* misapplied the law. Consequently, the appellate and district court decisions were annulled, and the Supreme Court adjudicated afresh in accordance with the principle of property segregation between first and second marriages.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Purwodadi District & Semarang High Courts) ===
Examination of specific asset details under Ad. A.1 to A.9 (dry agricultural land C Village No. 643 parcel 55, C No. 650, C No. 441 parcels 58, 59, 50, 102, water buffaloes, and traditional *pencu/limasan* houses) as first-marriage joint property, alongside assets Ad. B.1 to B.7 (land C No. 441 parcels 59, 50, 58, 27a, 72) as second-marriage joint property in Wolo Village, Penawangan, Grobogan.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The *Judex Facti* misapplied the law. Where separate joint property is formed in a first and second marriage, pursuant to subsidiary claims and Articles 35, 36, and 37 of Law No. 1 of 1974, children from each marriage are entitled to their respective parents' joint property estates.
# Plaintiffs I and II (children of the first marriage) are entitled to all first-marriage joint property (Ad. A.1 to A.9).
# Defendants (second wife and children of the second marriage) are entitled to all second-marriage joint property (Ad. B.1 to B.7).
# The Supreme Court annulled the lower court rulings and adjudicated afresh.

== Ruling ==
The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Petitioners for Cassation ('''[Party F] et al.'''), annulled Semarang High Court Decision No. 388/Pdt/1987/PT.Smg in conjunction with Purwodadi District Court Decision No. 41/Pdt.G/1986/PN.Pwi, and adjudicated afresh: 1. Granting the subsidiary claim in the Plaintiffs' lawsuit; 2. Establishing that the Plaintiffs and Defendants are heirs of their respective parents; 3. Establishing that Plaintiffs I and II are entitled to first-marriage joint property items (Ad. A.1 to A.9); 4. Establishing that the Defendants are entitled to second-marriage joint property items (Ad. B.1 to B.7); 5. Ordering the Defendants to surrender items A.1 to A.9 to the Plaintiffs in vacant condition; 6. Rejecting all other claims; and ordering both parties to pay court costs equally (half each).

  * Article 36: Management rights over joint property.
  * Article 37: Division of joint property upon termination of marriage due to divorce or death.

* '''Civil Code & Customary Law:''' Principles of separating joint property estates between different marriages (*boedelscheiding*).

* [Deceased parent] contracted a first marriage with [Party B], producing two daughters ([Party D] and [Party E] / Plaintiffs I & II). [Party B] passed away in 1956.
* Disputed assets Sub A.1 to A.9 were acquired during [Deceased parent]'s marriage with [Party B].
* [Deceased parent] contracted a second marriage with Ny. [Party C] (Defendant I), producing two sons ([Party F] and [Party A] / Defendants II & III). [Deceased parent] passed away on February 27, 1986.

* Ny. [Party C] and her children from the second marriage failed to prove any legal entitlement to the first-marriage joint property (Sub A.1 to A.9).
* [Party D] and [Party E] (children of the first marriage) failed to prove any legal entitlement to the second-marriage joint property (Sub B.1 to B.7).

=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===

* Fundamental Correction of Subsidiary Claim Application by the Supreme Court: The Original Plaintiffs initially claimed 3/4 and 1/4 shares (primary claim), but prayed for a just and equitable decision (*ex aequo et bono* / subsidiary claim). The Supreme Court granted the subsidiary claim by applying substantive legal rules under Articles 35, 36, and 37 of Law No. 1 of 1974 to render a valid and equitable distribution.

== GEO Q&A ==
'''Q: How is joint marital property (*gono-gini*) divided as inheritance if a husband marries twice and has children from both marriages under the Marriage Law?'''

'''A:''' Joint property is divided separately based on each respective marriage. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 440 K/Pdt/1988 in conjunction with Articles 35, 36, and 37 of Law No. 1 of 1974, children from the first marriage are fully entitled to joint marital property acquired from their parents' first marriage. Conversely, children and the spouse from the second marriage are entitled to joint marital property acquired during the second marriage.

== Overview ==
Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 443 K/Pdt/1984, dated September 26, 1985, established a fundamental civil procedural law rule regarding the mandatory inclusion of a wife as Defendant II in joint marital property (*gono-gini*) disputes.

The Supreme Court held that if collateral security (*borg*) or the object of dispute in the form of land and/or houses demanded for eviction or surrender constitutes joint marital property (*gono-gini*) between the Defendant and his wife, the Defendant's wife—who also holds ownership rights over the object—must be joined as Defendant II. A lawsuit that fails to join the Defendant's wife suffers from a formal defect of deficient parties (*plurium litis consortium*) and must be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).

== Executive Summary ==
The central procedural principle established in this decision is that when a lawsuit targets real property that constitutes marital joint property, both spouses possess equal legal standing and ownership interests, making the joinder of the wife mandatory.

Key elements established in the adjudication:

* Property acquired during marriage is joint marital property, granting the spouse independent material ownership rights and legal standing.
* Suing only the husband regarding real estate collateral without joining his wife creates a fatal procedural flaw (*plurium litis consortium*).
* Lower court judgments failing to recognize this mandatory joinder are subject to correction and dismissal as inadmissible on appeal and cassation.

== Case Background ==
The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation, '''[Party A]''', filed a lawsuit at the Tarakan District Court against the Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation, '''[Party B]''', concerning a default on a monetary loan of Rp 480,000.— based on a written agreement dated January 13, 1982, secured by land (*perwatasan* measuring 240 m²) and a house in Karang Balik, Tarakan. The Plaintiff sought the surrender and ownership transfer of the collateral land/house.

The Tarakan District Court (Decision No. 19/Pdt/1982/PN.Trk) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part. The East Kalimantan High Court in Samarinda (Decision No. 48/Perd/1983/PT.KT.Smd) annulled the district court decision and adjudicated afresh, declaring the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible (NO) because the collateral object constituted joint marital property (*gono-gini*) belonging to the Defendant and his wife, rendering the joinder of the wife as Defendant II mandatory. The Petitioner for Cassation subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==

=== Legal Standing Requirements for Defendants in Joint Marital Property Disputes ===
The primary issue was whether a lawsuit for the surrender and eviction of a house and land collateral pledged by a husband without explicit separate consent can be filed exclusively against the husband alone.

The Supreme Court held that it cannot. Under marriage law and civil procedural law, land and buildings acquired during marriage constitute joint marital property (*gono-gini*) between husband and wife. The wife possesses material ownership rights and equal legal accountability over such joint property. Therefore, when joint property becomes the subject of a dispute, the wife must be joined as Defendant II.

=== Deficient Parties (Plurium Litis Consortium) ===
The issue evaluated the legal consequence if a Plaintiff fails to involve the Defendant's wife in a joint property ownership lawsuit.

The Supreme Court held that the lawsuit is incomplete and defective (*plurium litis consortium*) and must be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).

== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===
'''Question:'''

Did the *Judex Facti* (East Kalimantan High Court in Samarinda) misapply civil procedural law when declaring the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible (NO) due to the failure to join the Defendant's wife as Defendant II in the joint property house/land dispute?

'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''

No, the *Judex Facti* did not misapply the law. The East Kalimantan High Court applied civil procedural law correctly. Consequently, the Plaintiff's cassation petition was rejected.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Tarakan District Court & East Kalimantan High Court) ===
Examination of the debt agreement evidence of Rp 480,000.— dated January 13, 1982, the land transfer deed of 240 m² dated August 18, 1978, in Karang Balik West Tarakan, and the marital status of [Party B] alongside joint ownership over the disputed house.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The appellate *Judex Facti* did not misapply the law. Because the house and land serving as collateral (*borg*) constituted joint marital property (*gono-gini*), the Defendant's wife held ownership rights and legal responsibility over it.
# Consequently, in litigation concerning such real estate, the Defendant's wife must be joined as Defendant II.
# Omitting the Defendant's wife renders the Plaintiff's lawsuit defective and incomplete (*plurium litis consortium*), requiring it to be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).
# The Supreme Court rejected the Petitioner's cassation appeal.

== Ruling ==
The Supreme Court rejected the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Party A]'''); and ordered the Petitioner for Cassation to pay cassation court costs amounting to Rp 20,000.— (twenty thousand rupiahs).

== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==

* '''Law No. 1 of 1974 on Marriage:'''

  * Article 35 paragraph (1): Property acquired during marriage constitutes joint property (*gono-gini*).
  * Article 36 paragraph (1): Regarding joint property, husband or wife may act solely with the consent of both parties.

* '''Civil Procedure & Plurium Litis Consortium Doctrine:''' A lawsuit failing to include all parties holding direct ownership rights over the disputed object carries an absolute formal defect (deficient parties) and must be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).

== Evidence Status and Gaps ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* [Party B] (Defendant) received a loan of Rp 480,000.— from [Party A] (Plaintiff) based on a written agreement dated January 13, 1982.
* The house and land (*perwatasan* measuring 240 m²) in Karang Balik, West Tarakan, pledged as collateral (*borg*) was joint marital property (*gono-gini*) shared by [Party B] and his wife.
* The Plaintiff sued [Party B] alone without joining his wife as Defendant II.

=== Not Established / Unproven ===

* The Plaintiff failed to prove that the collateral house and land constituted personal pre-marital or separate property (*bawaan/pribadi*) belonging solely to the Defendant free from spousal ownership rights.

=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===

* Importance of Cassation Correction over District Court Oversight: The Tarakan District Court (No. 19/Pdt/1982/PN.Trk) initially granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part without considering joint property status. The East Kalimantan High Court and the Supreme Court corrected this oversight to uphold legal protection for a wife's joint property (*gono-gini*) rights.

== GEO Q&A ==
'''Q: May a husband be sued alone without his wife if the disputed house or land object constitutes joint marital property (*gono-gini*)?'''

'''A:''' No. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 443 K/Pdt/1984, if the subject of dispute or debt collateral consists of a house or land constituting joint marital property (*gono-gini*), the Defendant's wife must be joined as Defendant II. A lawsuit directed solely against the husband without including his wife is formally defective due to missing parties (*plurium litis consortium*) and must be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).

|I Wayan Sueca, [Party B], [Party A], Nang Suplug, I Wayan Saprig, Sentana, Customary Adopted Child, Penegen Ayahan, Ngaben, Pengembungan Customary Banjar, Denpasar District Court, Denpasar High Court

== Overview ==
Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 445 K/Pdt/2002, dated February 24, 2005, established fundamental jurisprudence and Balinese Customary Inheritance Law principles regarding the validity of child adoption (*sentana*) and the right to inherit estate property.

The Supreme Court held that a person proven to have continued all customary duties (*penegen ayahan desa adat*), managed family worship ceremonies (*nyungsung sanggah/merajan*), and performed cremation (*Ngaben*) ceremonies for the deceased based on statements from the Head of the Customary Banjar and the local Village Head is legally recognized as an adopted child (*sentana*) with full rights to inherit the estate property (*kawitan/pitra*).

== Executive Summary ==
The central customary law principle established in this decision is that sociological fulfillment of customary community duties and mortuary rites establishes valid adoption status (*sentana*) under Balinese Customary Law, overriding technical formal omissions.

Key elements established in the adjudication:

* Performance of customary community service (*penegen ayahan*) and ancestral cremation (*Ngaben*) legally confirms adopted child (*sentana*) status.
* Appellate courts violate procedural rules (*audi et alteram partem*) by admitting new documentary evidence without granting opposing parties an opportunity to respond.
* District court judgments recognizing customary community validation of heirs are reinstated on cassation.

== Case Background ==
The Original Plaintiffs / Petitioners for Cassation, '''I Wayan Sueca''' and '''[Party B]''', filed a lawsuit at the Denpasar District Court against the Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation, '''[Party A]''', concerning the unlawful possession of pipil land plot No. 273, parcel 41b, measuring 3,850 m² in Subak Kedungu, Pererenan Village, Mengwi, Badung. The Plaintiffs claimed to be the lawful heirs of I Wayan Saprig (adopted child / *sentana* of Nang Suplug), who had performed the cremation of Nang Suplug and fulfilled all customary duties (*penegen ayahan*) of the Customary Village.

The Denpasar District Court (Decision No. 76/Pdt.G/2000/PN.Dps) granted the Plaintiffs' lawsuit in part. The Denpasar High Court (Decision No. 98/Pdt/2001/PT.Dps) annulled the district court decision based on evidence T.18. The Petitioners for Cassation subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Claims, Evidence and Source Mapping ==

!Evidence / Judicial Consideration

|Supreme Court Decision No. 445 K/Pdt/2002 legal rule: "A person continuing all obligations of the deceased according to the village head and Customary Banjar statements and cremating the deceased is proven to be an adopted child and entitled to inherit the estate property."
|445K_PDT_2002.pdf, Passage 1
|-
|'''2'''

|Evidence P.2 & P.3 (Statements from Pengembungan Customary Banjar Head & Pererenan Village Head) alongside customary citizen testimonies.
|445K_PDT_2002.pdf, Passages 1, 2, 9, and 11
|-

|Trial facts: Plaintiffs cremated Nang Suplug and I Wayan Saprig, managing the Customary Village and Banjar *penegen ayahan* duties.

|Ruling of the Supreme Court Cassation Decision pages 92 & 103: Granting the Plaintiff's cassation petition and validating ownership of pipil land No. 273, parcel 41b, measuring 3,850 m².
|445K_PDT_2002.pdf, Passages 3, 13, and 14
|}

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==

=== Validity of Adoption (Sentana) Under Balinese Customary Inheritance Law ===
The primary issue was whether someone adopted as a child (*sentana*) without modern formalization documents but who executes all customary duties (*penegen ayahan desa/banjar adat*), maintains ancestral shrines (*nyungsung sanggah/merajan*), and organizes decedent cremation ceremonies is legally recognized as a sole heir.

The Supreme Court held that it is valid under customary law. Based on the principles of *Desa Kala Patra* and *Dresta* in Balinese Customary Law, the sociological reality of being recognized by the Customary Banjar and Village Head as a continuation of lineage (*penegen ayahan*) and performing mortuary rites (*pitra yadnya*) perfectly proves adopted child (*sentana*) status with full rights to inherit the estate.

=== Violation of the Principle of Audi Et Alteram Partem in Civil Procedure ===
The issue evaluated whether an appellate court violates civil procedure by directly considering new documentary evidence (in *casu* T.18) submitted at the appellate level without granting opposing parties an opportunity to respond or examine the evidence.

The Supreme Court held that it does violate procedure. The lower appellate court's admission and consideration of evidence without granting the opposing party the right to be heard constitutes a serious procedural breach (*foutieve kepassing van het procesrecht*).

== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===
'''Question:'''

Did the Denpasar High Court misapply Balinese customary evidentiary law and civil procedure (*audi et alteram partem*) by disregarding Customary Banjar/Village recognition of I Wayan Saprig's *sentana* status and granting the appeal based on procedurally defective evidence T.18?

'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''

Yes, the Denpasar High Court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court annulled the Denpasar High Court decision and affirmed the District Court judgment favoring the Plaintiffs.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Denpasar District Court & Denpasar High Court) ===
Examination of Nang Suplug (deceased) & Men Suplug (deceased) genealogy, the formalization process (*pemerascitaan*) of I Nyoman Doble into I Wayan Saprig, I Wayan Sueca's (Plaintiff I) adoption by I Wayan Saprig, registration of pipil rice field land No. 273, parcel 41b, measuring 3,850 m² (38.50 ares) in Subak Kedungu, Pererenan Village, Mengwi, Badung, alongside cremation execution.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The appellate *Judex Facti* misapplied Balinese customary law and civil procedure. Pursuant to facts and Customary Banjar/Village statements (evidence P.2 & P.3), I Wayan Saprig was proven to be the customary duty successor (*penegen ayahan*) of Nang Suplug and executed cremation alongside the Plaintiffs.
# Consequently, adoption status (*sentana*) is legally proven, granting full inheritance rights.
# Furthermore, the High Court breached procedural law by considering evidence T.18 without granting Plaintiffs a right to reply (*audi et alteram partem*).
# The Supreme Court annulled the appellate decision and adjudicated afresh, affirming the District Court ruling.

== Ruling ==
The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Petitioners for Cassation ('''1. I WAYAN SUECA, 2. [Party B]'''), annulled Denpasar High Court Decision No. 98/Pdt/2001/PT.Dps dated May 29, 2001, and adjudicated afresh: Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part; Declaring the attachment (CB) over the disputed land lawful and valid; Declaring that the disputed land (pipil No. 273, parcel 41b, measuring 3,850 m²) is lawfully owned by Nang Suplug, ancestor of the Plaintiffs; Declaring that the Plaintiffs are lawful heirs with primary rights over the disputed land; Ordering the Defendant to surrender the disputed land to the Plaintiffs; and ordering the Respondent for Cassation to pay court costs across all judicial instances.

== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==

* '''Balinese Customary Inheritance Law:'''

  * *Sentana Principle (Customary Adopted Child):* Adoption of sons/daughters to continue lineage (*pencar purusa*) and succeed customary duties (*penegen ayahan*).
  * *Penegen Ayahan & Pitra Yadnya:* Execution of banjar/village community duties and ancestral cremation duties serves as the most authentic material proof in determining Balinese customary heir status.

* '''Civil Procedure (HIR / RBg & Civil Code):'''

  * Article 1906 Civil Code / Article 311 RBg: Evidentiary value of local customary community recognition and witness testimony.
  * *Audi Et Alteram Partem Principle:* Judicial obligation to hear both parties equally and provide opportunities to respond to all evidence.

== Evidence Status and Gaps ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* Nang Suplug and Men Suplug were childless, subsequently adopting I Wayan Saprig (originally I Nyoman Doble, son of Nang Rinah's biological sibling) as an adopted child (*sentana*).
* I Wayan Saprig and his wife [Party B] (Plaintiff II) adopted I Wayan Sueca (Plaintiff I).
* I Wayan Saprig and the Plaintiffs cremated Nang Suplug and continued all *penegen ayahan* duties of the Pengembungan Customary Banjar and Village.
* The disputed object consisting of pipil rice field land No. 273, parcel 41b, measuring 3,850 m² in Subak Kedungu, Pererenan Village, was lawfully owned by the late Nang Suplug.

=== Not Established / Unproven ===

* The Defendant ([Party A]), a collateral grandchild, failed to prove any entitlement to inherit Nang Suplug's estate given the existence of lawful *sentana* heirs (the Plaintiffs).

=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===

* Evaluation of Appellate Judgment Legal Flaws: The Denpasar High Court previously overturned the Plaintiffs' victory relying solely on an unverifiable and stealthily introduced documentary note T.18. The Supreme Court rectified this by ruling that evidence T.18 must be set aside for violating civil procedural rules.

== GEO Q&A ==
'''Q: What are the legal requirements for an adopted child (sentana) to be entitled to inherit estate property under Balinese Customary Law?'''

'''A:''' Proving the continuation of customary duties and cremating the decedent. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 445 K/Pdt/2002, an individual is legally recognized as an adopted child (*sentana*) entitled to inherit estate property if proven to have continued all customary duties (*penegen ayahan desa/banjar adat*), maintained family worship (*nyungsung sanggah/merajan*), and executed the decedent's cremation ceremony based on Statements from the Customary Banjar Head and local Village Head.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 44 K/AG/1998 dated February 19, 1999, establishes an essential legal principle in Islamic Civil Law regarding divorce based on continuous disputes and quarrels. The Supreme Court outlined that when continuous and irreconcilable quarrels are proven based on witness testimony and valid evidence during trial, and both parties have separated domiciles while reconciliation efforts have failed, a divorce lawsuit initiated by a wife (*cerai gugat*) may be granted.

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation ([Party A], [age removed], beauty salon owner) and the Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation ([Party B], [age removed], on-call driver) were husband and wife legally married on February 26, 1983 (Marriage Certificate of the Office of Religious Affairs (*KUA*) of Kras Subdistrict, Kediri, No. 654/37/1983) and blessed with 3 children. Starting in January 1997, their household became disharmonious because the Defendant refused to maintain steady employment, frequently became angry when advised to work, and arbitrarily forced the closure of the Plaintiff's salon business, leading to a police report filed at the Kras Sector Police (*Polsek*). The Plaintiff and Defendant subsequently separated their domiciles.

The Kediri Regency Religious Court (Decision No. 455/Pdt.G/1997/PA.Kab.Kdr dated June 11, 1997) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit and ruled for a divorce via single *raj'i talak*. However, the Surabaya High Religious Court (Decision No. 142/Pdt.G/1997/PTA.Sby dated October 7, 1997) annulled the Kediri Religious Court decision and rejected the Plaintiff's lawsuit on the grounds that witness statements lacked clarity and police report documents possessed no probative weight. Dissatisfied with the appellate ruling, the Plaintiff filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# Because continuous and irreconcilable quarrels have been proven based on witness testimony and evidence presented at trial, a decree granting a divorce between the Plaintiff and the Defendant is legally permissible.
# The Surabaya High Religious Court committed an error by issuing a ruling lacking adequate legal reasoning (*onvoldoende gemotiveerd*) and misapplying evidentiary rules when rejecting testimony from close neighboring witnesses and police report evidence that clearly demonstrated the existence of disputes and the forced closure of the Plaintiff's salon by the Defendant.
# Reconciliation efforts undertaken by the court and family proved unsuccessful, and the Defendant was unwilling to present family members or witnesses to pursue reconciliation; hence, the Plaintiff's cassation petition must be granted and the Surabaya High Religious Court ruling annulled.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation [Party A]; Annulling the Surabaya High Religious Court decision dated October 7, 1997, No. 142/Pdt.G/1997/PTA.Sby; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) In Exception: Rejecting the Defendant's exception; (2) In the Merits: 1. Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit; 2. Pronouncing a single *raj'i talak* by Defendant [Party B] against Plaintiff [Party A]; 3. Ordering the Plaintiff to pay first-instance court costs amounting to Rp 70,500 (seventy thousand five hundred rupiahs); 4. Ordering the Defendant-Appellee to pay appellate-level court costs amounting to Rp 48,000 (forty-eight thousand rupiahs).

Legal and procedural issues == === 4.1 Legal nature of land registration through PRONA after the Basic Agrarian Law (Law No. 5 of 1960) === * ''Does issuing a land-rights certificate through PRONA automatically change the original land's status to "state land", extinguishing the original owner's civil rights?''Passages 1, 10, 11, 18. * '''Supreme Court rule: it does not change the original status of the land.''' PRONA is a subsidised titling method, not a determinant of the land's original status. The Court granted [Party D]'s cassation, annulled the HC decision, and, adjudicating itself, '''upheld the DC decision declaring the grant valid, the land the Plaintiff's property, and ordering Defendants I and II to demolish the house and vacate the land'''.Passages 1, 2, 11, 12. === Question of fact (''Judex Facti'' / Manado DC and HC) === * Verification of SHM No. 463/Pakowa, Survey Letter No. 576/1982, in the name of [Party C];Passages 4, 24, 32. * Verification of Grant Deed No. 5944/M.S/20/1989 dated 11 August 1989 before PPAT Drs. John Marthen Solang;Passages 32, 39. * Verification of physical possession by [Party A] and [Party E] and construction of a concrete/timber house;Passages 25, 33, 34. * Verification of the receipt for compensation for cultivation rights from Petrus Makasenggehe;Passages 35, 37. * Examination of trial witnesses ([Party B], Robinson Sanger, Bobby Warbung, Hamid Luran, Herman Sengkey, Ruben Adu, Jootje Waworundeng, Iskandar Elias).Passages 33–38. == 6. Related knowledge and jurisprudence == === Legislation === * '''Law No. 5 of 1960 (Basic Agrarian Law, UUPA):''' Art. 19 (land registration) and Art. 20 (freehold). * '''Government Regulation No. 10 of 1961 / No. 24 of 1997:''' land registration rules and Land Deed Officials (PPAT). * '''Decree of the Minister of Home Affairs / State Minister for Agrarian Affairs on PRONA:''' implementation guidelines for the National Agrarian Operational Project. * '''Law No. 14 of 1970 in conjunction with Law No. 35 of 1999 and Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' cassation and self-adjudication powers. === Doctrine and landmark jurisprudence === * '''Doctrine of legal certainty in PRONA registration:''' PRONA does not cancel or deprive existing civil rights in customary or freehold land; it provides legal certainty through issuance of subsidised certificates. * '''Settled jurisprudence on the evidentiary value of PBB / ''girik'' / ''petuk'':''' PBB/Ipeda payment is not proof of freehold and cannot defeat a freehold certificate (SHM) lawfully issued by the National Land Agency. == 7. Uncertainty and gaps == === Legal certainty for PRONA certificate holders and PPAT grantees === This landmark ruling gives crucial legal certainty to the many recipients of PRONA land certificates in Indonesia: district and high courts may not annul PRONA certificates on the mistaken assumption that PRONA registration automatically equates to a grant of state land. A PRONA certificate issued by the National Land Agency (BPN) and transferred by official PPAT grant deed is valid and must be legally protected against encroachment by persons without right. == 9. == Overview ==

Supreme Court Judicial Review (*Peninjauan Kembali / PK*) Decision No. 45 PK/Pid/Ham.Ad Hoc/2004 dated November 4, 2004, establishes fundamental jurisprudence and legal standards regarding the application of the doctrine of superior/command responsibility in gross human rights violation cases. The Supreme Court affirmed that when direct subordinates (the Regent of Liquisa and the Regent of Covalima) have been declared not legally proven to have committed gross human rights violations based on final and binding Supreme Court decisions, the legal element of "criminal responsibility for gross human rights violations committed by subordinates" pursuant to Article 42 paragraph (2) of Law No. 26 of 2000 charged against the Governor as a Superior likewise fails to be proven. Furthermore, emotional affiliation cannot serve as proof of a superior-subordinate relationship or effective control.

== Case Background ==

The Convict / Petitioner for PK ([Defendant], Former Governor of Level I Region of East Timor) was charged with omission (*crime by omission*) regarding crimes against humanity perpetrated by his subordinates (Liquisa Regent Leonito Martins, Covalima Regent Drs. Herman Sedyono, and PPI Deputy Commander [name removed]) at the Liquisa Church Complex, Manuel Carrascalao's Residence in Dili, the Dili Diocese, Bishop Bello's Residence, and the Ave Maria Suai Church.

The Ad Hoc Human Rights Court at the Central Jakarta District Court sentenced the Convict to 3 years of imprisonment (Decision No. 01/Pid.HAM/ADHOC/2002/PN.JKT.PST). The Ad Hoc High Human Rights Court of Jakarta upheld the ruling (Decision No. 01/PID.HAM/AD.HOC/2002/PT.DKI). Upon cassation, the Supreme Court rejected the Defendant's cassation petition (Decision No. 04 K/Pid.HAM.Ad Hoc/2003). The Convict subsequently filed a petition for Judicial Review (*PK*) presenting *novum* in the form of Supreme Court Decisions No. 01 K/Pid/HAM Ad Hoc/2004 and No. 01 K/Pid.HAM/Ad Hoc/2004, which had acquitted Covalima Regent Drs. Herman Sedyono and Liquisa Regent Leonito Martins of all charges of gross human rights violations.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# There exists decisive new evidence (*novum*), namely Supreme Court Decisions No. 01 K/Pid/HAM Ad Hoc/2004 and No. 01 K/Pid.HAM/Ad Hoc/2004 possessing permanent legal force, wherein the Convict's subordinates (Covalima Regent Drs. Herman Sedyono and Liquisa Regent Leonito Martins) were declared not guilty and acquitted of all charges of gross human rights violations.
# As a direct juridical consequence, because the Regents alleged to have committed gross human rights violations were declared not proven guilty, the indictment element requiring "criminal responsibility for gross human rights violations committed by subordinates" under Article 42 paragraph (2) of Law No. 26 of 2000 against the Convict in his capacity as Governor (Superior) is likewise unfulfilled and unproven.
# Regarding [name removed] (PPI Deputy Commander), the *judex facti* erred in concluding that [name removed] was a subordinate of the Convict, given that *de jure* and *de facto* the Convict possessed no effective control or chain of command over [name removed]. Emotional ties cannot serve as a legal basis for establishing a superior-subordinate relationship.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the petition for judicial review from Petitioner for PK [Defendant]; Annulling the Supreme Court cassation decision dated April 1, 2004, No. 04 K/PID.HAM.AD HOC/2003 jo. Ad Hoc High Human Rights Court of Jakarta Decision No. 01/PID.HAM/AD HOC/2002/PT.DKI jo. Ad Hoc Human Rights Court at Central Jakarta District Court Decision No. 01/PID.HAM/AD HOC/2002/PH.JKT.PST; and Re-Adjudicating: (1) Declaring Convict [Defendant] not legally and convincingly proven guilty of committing the criminal offenses set forth in the First and Second Charges; (2) Acquitting the Convict of all charges; (3) Restoring the Convict's rights in capacity, position, honor, and dignity; (4) Ordering that the Convict be immediately released from the Penitentiary; (5) Charging all procedural costs across all levels of jurisdiction to the State. (Decision rendered by majority vote / *Dissenting Opinions* by Supreme Court Justices Artidjo Alkostar, SH., LL.M. and Prof. DR. Sumaryo Suryokusumo, SH., LL.M.).

== Overview ==
Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 464 K/Pid/1985, dated September 13, 1985, established a very important criminal procedural law rule regarding the limitation of legal remedies against Pre-trial (*Praperadilan*) decisions.

The Supreme Court held that pursuant to the standing jurisprudence of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia, a Pre-trial decision is not subject to cassation review. Consequently, a cassation petition filed by the Petitioner for Cassation ([Defendant]) against Padangsidempuan District Court Pre-trial Decision No. 10/Pra/1984/P.N.Psp must be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).

== Executive Summary ==
The central legal principle established in this decision is that pre-trial (*praperadilan*) determinations are final and closed to cassation review under established Supreme Court jurisprudence.

Key elements established in the adjudication:

* Pre-trial decisions cannot form the object of a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.
* Petitions challenging pre-trial rulings must be dismissed as inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).
* Expedited pre-trial timelines under the Criminal Procedure Code (*KUHAP*) reinforce their status as self-contained special remedies.

== Case Background ==
The Original Petitioner / Pre-trial Petitioner, '''[Defendant]''', filed a pre-trial application at the Padangsidempuan District Court against the Pre-trial Respondent (Head of South Tapanuli Police Resort et al.) regarding the legality of arrest and detention, accompanied by claims for damages and rehabilitation arising from actions of South Tapanuli Police personnel.

The Padangsidempuan District Court (Decision No. 10/Pra/1984/P.N.Psp dated March 4, 1985) ruled that the Pre-trial application had lapsed (*gugur*) pursuant to Article 82 paragraph (1) letter c of the KUHAP because the examination exceeded the 7-day statutory limit due to administrative delays concerning the Substitute Counsel's practicing permit. The Petitioner subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Claims, Evidence and Source Mapping ==

|Expressly stated in decision identity pages 64 and 71.
