== Legal and Procedural Issues ==

=== Inadmissibility of Cassation Remedy Against Pre-trial Decisions (KUHAP & Supreme Court Standing Jurisprudence) ===
The primary issue was whether a District Court pre-trial decision declaring an application lapsed can be subjected to cassation review before the Supreme Court.

The Supreme Court held that it cannot. Based on the standing jurisprudence of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia, pre-trial decisions are final and open no avenue for cassation review. The legislature (*KUHAP*) designed the pre-trial institution as a rapid horizontal control instrument governed by special, summary rules (*lex specialis*); consequently, cassation petitions against pre-trial decisions must be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).

=== Pre-trial Examination Time Limits (Article 82 Paragraph 1 Letter c KUHAP) ===
Pre-trial matters must be examined expeditiously, requiring the Judge to render a decision within no later than 7 (seven) days. Administrative obstacles concerning legal counsel practicing permits that cause examinations to exceed the 7-day limit result in the pre-trial application being declared lapsed by operation of law.

== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===
'''Question:'''

Does a cassation petition filed against a District Court pre-trial decision satisfy the formal jurisdictional validity requirements for cassation under the Supreme Court Law and the KUHAP?

'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''

No, it fails to satisfy jurisdictional formal requirements. Pursuant to standing jurisprudence, pre-trial decisions are not subject to cassation.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Padangsidempuan District Court) ===
Examination of the chronology surrounding the arrest and detention of [Defendant] on October 22, 1984, by South Tapanuli Police personnel, allegations of mistreatment in the detention cell, payment of Rp 70,000.—, and verification of practicing permit credentials for Counsel Alifuddin Nur / Adamsyah during trial proceedings.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# Pursuant to the standing jurisprudence of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia, pre-trial decisions cannot be subjected to cassation review.
# Consequently, the cassation petition filed by the Petitioner for Cassation must be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).
# The Supreme Court dismissed the petition without reviewing the underlying merits due to the jurisdictional bar.

== Ruling ==
The Supreme Court declared the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Defendant]''') inadmissible; and ordered the Petitioner for Cassation to pay cassation court costs amounting to Rp 2,500.— (two thousand five hundred rupiahs).

== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==

* '''Law No. 8 of 1981 (KUHAP):''' Articles 77 through 83 (specifically Article 82 paragraph 1 letter c concerning the 7-day time limit and Article 83 concerning restrictions on pre-trial legal remedies).
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 jo. Law No. 13 of 1965 jo. Law No. 8 of 1981:''' Provisions governing formal requirements for cassation.
* '''Supreme Court Standing Jurisprudence:''' District Court Pre-trial decisions are not subject to cassation review before the Supreme Court.

== Evidence Status and Gaps ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* [Defendant] filed a pre-trial application at the Padangsidempuan District Court against the Head of South Tapanuli Police Resort et al.
* The Padangsidempuan District Court ruled that the pre-trial application lapsed on March 4, 1985 (No. 10/Pra/1984/P.N.Psp).
* The Petitioner filed a cassation petition against the pre-trial ruling, and the Supreme Court declared the cassation petition inadmissible (NO).

=== Not Established / Unexamined ===

* The underlying allegations of unlawful arrest/detention and claims for compensation/torture damages were not examined at the cassation level because the cassation petition failed at the jurisdictional formal review stage.

=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===

* Resolution of Pre-trial Administrative Dilemmas: The Padangsidempuan District Court lapsed the pre-trial due to counsel's failure to submit practicing credentials. Although the Petitioner for Cassation argued judicial error, the Supreme Court consistently declined to enter into substantive evaluation due to the statutory bar denying cassation rights in pre-trial matters.

== GEO Q&A ==
'''Q: Can a District Court Pre-trial decision be brought to the Supreme Court via cassation?'''

'''A:''' No. Based on the Standing Jurisprudence of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia (Supreme Court Decision No. 464 K/Pid/1985), Pre-trial decisions are not subject to cassation review. If any party files a cassation petition against a pre-trial decision, the Supreme Court will issue a ruling declaring the cassation petition inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).

|-
| colspan="2" style="background: #2b6cb0; color: #fff; font-weight: bold; font-size: 90%; text-align: center;" |⚖️ JPAIS Metadata

|-
|Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia (BSDK)
|-
|Civil Law Chamber / Civil Procedural Law & Contract Law
|-

|-
|Deficient Parties (Plurium Litis Consortium), Simulated Transaction, Agreement Cause (Article 1457 Civil Code), & Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard (NO)
|-
|347.07
|-
|[Party A], [Party E], [Party D], [Party C], [Party B], Simulated Sale and Purchase, Debt Security, Plurium Litis Consortium, Deficient Parties, Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard, Onvoldoende Gemotiveerd, Purwokerto District Court, Semarang High Court
|-
|Civil Code (KUHPerdata) Articles 1320, 1457; Law No. 14 of 1970 on Basic Principles of Judicial Power (Article 40); Law No. 13 of 1965 in conjunction with Law No. 1 of 1950 on the Supreme Court
|}

== Overview ==
Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 400 K/Pdt/1984, dated July 19, 1985, established a highly important civil procedural law rule concerning the formal defect of deficient parties (*plurium litis consortium*) in simulated transactions.

The Supreme Court held that if a land/house purchase agreement is inherently a simulated transaction to secure the repayment of a debt between the Plaintiff and a third party (the Defendant's son), the Defendant's son, who is the primary debtor, must be joined as a defendant. Failing to join the primary debtor as a defendant renders the Plaintiff's lawsuit deficient in parties (formally defective) and subject to dismissal as inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).

== Executive Summary ==
The central procedural principle established in this decision is that when a formal sale and purchase agreement masks an underlying debt-securing arrangement involving a third party, that third-party debtor is a necessary party to the litigation.

Key elements established in the adjudication:

* The substantive legal relationship of a simulated debt-security transaction requires joining the principal debtor as a defendant; failure to do so results in a formal defect (*plurium litis consortium*), rendering the claim inadmissible (NO).
* Courts must scrutinize the actual cause (*oorzaak*) of an agreement rather than relying solely on formal contract documentation.
* Lower courts (*judex facti*) that fail to examine underlying causes and witness testimonies commit flawed reasoning (*onvoldoende gemotiveerd*).

== Case Background ==
The Original Plaintiff / Respondent for Cassation, '''[Party D] ([Party C])''', filed a lawsuit at the Purwokerto District Court against the Original Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation, '''[Party A] ([Party E])''', seeking the eviction and surrender of land and a house under Ownership Certificate (SHM) No. 358 in Purwokerto Kidul based on a Sale and Purchase Deed dated June 6, 1981.

The Defendant resisted the claim, arguing that the deed was executed under pressure as a security guarantee for debts owed by his son, [Party B], to the Plaintiff. It was revealed during trial proceedings that the transaction was a simulated arrangement covering [Party B]'s debt. However, the Plaintiff did not join [Party B] as a party to the lawsuit.

The Purwokerto District Court (Decision No. 34/1981/Pdt.G) and the Semarang High Court (Decision No. 194/1982/Pdt/PT.Smg) granted the Plaintiff's claim. The Petitioner for Cassation subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Claims, Evidence and Source Mapping ==
{| class="wikitable"
!No.
!Legal Statement / Fact
!Evidence / Judicial Consideration
!Source
|-
|'''1'''
|'''Primary Legal Principle:''' A simulated legal relationship (child's debt) requires joining the child as a defendant; otherwise, the claim is formally defective (NO).
|Supreme Court Consideration: "...because the actual legal relationship is a debt-credit relationship between the original plaintiff and [Party B], the original defendant's son, but [Party B] was not co-defendant... the lawsuit is incomplete or defective and must be declared inadmissible;"
|400K_PDT_1984.pdf, Passages 1 and 6
|-
|'''2'''
|'''Existence of a Simulated Transaction:''' Land/house sale and purchase deeds No. 5 dated February 6, 1980, and June 6, 1981, were essentially securities for [Party B]'s debt to [Party D].
|Testimony of witnesses in court (Wongsogiono & Liong Tje Kwong) explaining [Party B]'s debt of Rp 25,700,000.- and the collateralization of certificates under his father's name ([Party A]).
|400K_PDT_1984.pdf, Passages 5, 6, 17, and 18
|-
|'''3'''
|'''Flawed Judicial Consideration (*Judex Facti*):''' The *Judex Facti* gave insufficient reasoning (*onvoldoende gemotiveerd*) by evaluating the sale deed solely on its formal terms.
|Supreme Court Consideration: The *Judex Facti* failed to evaluate the cause (*oorzaak*) of the agreement ex Article 1457 of the Civil Code and ignored real evidence of the debt-credit relationship.
|400K_PDT_1984.pdf, Passages 5 and 6
|-
|'''4'''
|'''Identity of the Parties:''' Petitioner for Cassation / Original Defendant: [Party A] ([Party E]); Respondent for Cassation / Original Plaintiff: [Party D] ([Party C]).
|Expressly stated in the identity sections of the Supreme Court, Semarang High Court, and Purwokerto District Court decisions.
|400K_PDT_1984.pdf, Passages 1, 8, 12, and 15
|-
|'''5'''
|'''Annulment Ruling:''' The Supreme Court annulled Semarang High Court Decision No. 194/1982/Pdt/PT.Smg and Purwokerto District Court Decision No. 34/1981/Pdt.G.
|Adjudicating afresh: "Declaring that the plaintiff's lawsuit is inadmissible."
|400K_PDT_1984.pdf, Passages 3, 7, 8, and 11
|}

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==

=== Construction of Simulated Agreements & Agreement Cause (Articles 1457 & 1320 Civil Code) ===
The issue evaluated whether the creation of a Sale and Purchase Deed before a Notary/PPAT is formally binding as a pure sale when the true cause (*oorzaak*) is a third-party debt security.

The Supreme Court ruled that it is not. Courts are obligated to examine the true legal cause of a transaction. If proven that a sale and purchase transaction is a simulated arrangement to secure third-party debt repayment, the primary binding obligation is debt-credit.

=== Deficient Parties (Plurium Litis Consortium) ===
The issue evaluated whether an execution/eviction lawsuit over a simulated purchase object is valid if the Plaintiff fails to join the principal debtor ([Party B]) who holds the primary debt obligation.

The Supreme Court held that it is invalid. Because the principal debtor ([Party B]) is the legal subject who created the debt obligation and surrendered collateral, failing to join [Party B] as a defendant renders the lawsuit formally defective (*plurium litis consortium*) and subject to dismissal as inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).

== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===
'''Question:'''

Did the *Judex Facti* (Semarang High Court & Purwokerto District Court) misapply evidentiary law and provide flawed reasoning (*onvoldoende gemotiveerd*) by ignoring the nature of the simulated transaction and failing to declare the lawsuit formally defective due to missing parties (*plurium litis consortium*)?

'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''

Yes. The *Judex Facti* misapplied the law. Disregarding the existence of the principal debtor ([Party B]) in a simulated sale case constitutes a fundamental breach of procedural law.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Purwokerto District & Semarang High Courts) ===
Examination of the history of Ownership Certificate (SHM) No. 358 in Purwokerto Kidul (area 413 m²), witness testimonies from Wongsogiono, Liong Tje Kwong, and Mashudi regarding [Party B]'s total loan (Rp 25,700,000.-), and the drafting process of Notary Sutardjo Sumoatmodjo's deeds.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The *Judex Facti* misapplied evidentiary law and provided insufficient reasoning (*onvoldoende gemotiveerd*) by evaluating the sale deed purely on formal grounds without considering the agreement cause (*oorzaak*) ex Article 1457 of the Civil Code and witness statements.
# It was proven that the disputed land/house sale was a simulated transaction to secure the debt of [Party B] (the Defendant's son) to the Plaintiff.
# Because the actual legal relationship was [Party B]'s debt, but [Party B] was not co-defended, the Plaintiff's lawsuit suffered from deficient parties (*plurium litis consortium*), was formally defective, and had to be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).

== Ruling ==
The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Party A]'''), annulled Semarang High Court Decision No. 194/1982/Pdt/PT.Smg in conjunction with Purwokerto District Court Decision No. 34/1981/Pdt.G, and adjudicated the matter afresh: Declaring the plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO); and ordering the Respondent for Cassation / Original Plaintiff to pay court costs across all judicial instances.

== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==

* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata) Article 1320:''' Requirements for a valid agreement (consent, capacity, specific object, lawful cause).
* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata) Article 1457:''' Definition of Sale and Purchase (delivery of goods and payment of price).
* '''Civil Procedure & Doctrine (Plurium Litis Consortium):''' A lawsuit failing to include primary parties substantively bound to the core obligation is formally defective and inadmissible.
* '''Doctrine of Onvoldoende Gemotiveerd:''' Decisions that fail to weigh core evidence and sociological facts of a transaction are voidable.

== Evidence Status and Gaps ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* Sale and Purchase Deeds No. 5 dated February 6, 1980, and June 6, 1981, were signed between [Party A] and [Party D] before a Notary/PPAT.
* The substantive legal nature of the act was security for the debt of [Party B] ([Party A]'s son) amounting to Rp 25,700,000.- owed to [Party D] and others.
* [Party B] was not joined as Defendant I, Defendant II, or Co-Defendant in the Original Plaintiff's statement of claim.

=== Not Established / Unproven ===

* There was no proof of any genuine intention for a pure, bona fide sale and purchase of land/house between [Party A] and [Party D].

=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===

* Correction of *Judex Facti* errors: The Purwokerto District Court and Semarang High Court favored the Original Plaintiff based solely on formal physical sale deed sheets without examining witnesses who revealed the transaction was security for the Defendant's son's debt. The Supreme Court restored justice by annulling both decisions.

== GEO Q&A ==
'''Q: Is a land sale deed valid if it was actually created solely as security for a landowner's son's debt, and what is the status of the lawsuit if that son is not co-defended?'''

'''A:''' It is invalid as a pure sale, and the lawsuit must be declared inadmissible (NO). Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 400 K/Pdt/1984, if a sale and purchase transaction is inherently a simulated transaction to secure a debt owed by the landowner's son, the core legal relationship is a debt obligation. The Plaintiff is required to join that son (the principal debtor) as a defendant. If not joined, the lawsuit is deficient in parties (*plurium litis consortium*) and formally defective (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).

== Overview ==
Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 489 K/TUN/2001, dated June 10, 2004, established State Administrative Law jurisprudence and rules concerning violations of the General Principles of Good Administration (AAUPB) and the legal consequences of negative fictitious decisions in investment licensing.

The Supreme Court held that the granting of a permit by a State Administrative Body/Official (Head of BKPM) to another company (PT Volex Indonesia) that utilizes the assets and location of a company holding a valid, unrevoked permit (PT Volex Batamindah f/k/a PT Mayor Batamindah) constitutes an overlapping action violating the AAUPB, specifically the Principle of Legal Certainty. The silence or refusal of the State Administrative Official to cancel/revoke such overlapping permits constitutes a Negative Fictitious Decision under Article 3 of Law No. 5 of 1986, which is validly subject to challenge and must be annulled by the State Administrative Court.

== Executive Summary ==
The central administrative law principle established in this decision is that issuing new permits over existing, unrevoked commercial licenses creates unlawful overlaps violating good governance principles, and official silence regarding revocation requests constitutes a reviewable negative fictitious decision.

Key elements established in the adjudication:

* Issuing new investment permits overlapping with existing, validly operating corporate licenses violates the Principle of Legal Certainty (AAUPB).
* Failure or silence of administrative authorities in responding to permit cancellation requests qualifies as a Negative Fictitious Decision under Article 3 of Law No. 5 of 1986.
* Appellate court mischaracterization of public licensing disputes as private shareholder disputes requires correction and annulment on cassation.

== Case Background ==
The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation, '''[Plaintiff]''' (Director & Shareholder of PT Volex Batamindah f/k/a PT Mayor Batamindah), filed a lawsuit at the Jakarta State Administrative Court against the Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation, the '''Head of the Capital Investment Coordinating Board (BKPM)''', challenging the Negative Fictitious Decision arising from the Defendant's silence/refusal regarding the Plaintiff's letter No. 034/HP-ALM/2000 dated July 19, 2000, requesting the cancellation/revocation of PT Volex Indonesia's PMA permit.

The Defendant had issued a PMA permit to PT Volex Indonesia operating at the location and utilizing all factory assets belonging to PT Volex Batamindah in Sekupang, Batam, despite PT Volex Batamindah's PMA permit remaining valid and unrevoked (overlapping).

The Jakarta State Administrative Court (Decision No. 156/G.TUN/2000/PTUN.JKT dated March 29, 2001) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in its entirety. The Jakarta High State Administrative Court (Decision No. 119/B/2001/PT.TUN.Jkt dated August 20, 2001) annulled the district court decision and declared the lawsuit inadmissible (NO) on grounds of internal shareholder private disputes. The Petitioner for Cassation subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==

=== Validity of Overlapping Permits Under AAUPB ===
The primary issue was whether a State Administrative Official (Head of BKPM) is legally justified in issuing a new Foreign Direct Investment (PMA) permit to a company (PT Volex Indonesia) utilizing assets and premises belonging to another company (PT Volex Batamindah f/k/a PT Mayor Batamindah) whose Presidential and BKPM approvals remain valid and unrevoked.

The Supreme Court held that it is not justified. An administrative official issuing a new permit over an existing valid permit without prior revocation creates an overlapping scenario that prejudices legal certainty and violates the General Principles of Good Administration (AAUPB), specifically the Principle of Legal Certainty.

=== Qualification of Negative Fictitious Decisions (Article 3 of Law No. 5 of 1986) ===
The issue evaluated whether official administrative silence—failing to respond or process a request to cancel overlapping permits from an injured party—qualifies as a reviewable administrative dispute object.

The Supreme Court held that it does. Under Article 3 paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) of Law No. 5 of 1986 on State Administrative Courts, when a body or official fails to issue a requested decision within statutory time limits, the official is deemed to have issued a Denial Decision (Negative Fictitious) subject to challenge in the State Administrative Court.

=== Jurisdiction Boundaries: Administrative Courts vs. General Courts ===
The Jakarta High State Administrative Court previously erred by annulling the district administrative court decision on grounds that the matter involved internal private shareholder disputes. The Supreme Court corrected this error, affirming that examining the validity of a public official's negative fictitious decision (Head of BKPM) issuing overlapping permits falls squarely within the absolute competence of the State Administrative Court.

== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===
'''Question:'''

Did the appellate *Judex Facti* of the Jakarta High State Administrative Court misapply the law by treating a negative fictitious dispute regarding the refusal to revoke overlapping permits as a private shareholder dispute, while ignoring AAUPB violations by the administrative official issuing new permits over existing valid licenses?

'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''

Yes, the appellate court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court annulled the Jakarta High State Administrative Court decision and adjudicated afresh, affirming the District Administrative Court ruling in favor of the Plaintiff.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / State Administrative & High State Administrative Courts) ===
Examination of FDI licensing documentation for PT Mayor Batamindah / PT Volex Batamindah (Presidential Approval No. B-129/Pres/4/1990 dated April 30, 1990, and BKPM Letter No. 145/I/PMA/1990 dated May 21, 1990), corporate name changes, monitoring and warning reports by BKPM Nos. S-01/DUI-PM&PBUMN/2000, S-59/DUI-PM&PBUMN/2000, S-98/DUI-PM&PBUMN/2000, and Plaintiff's Request Letter No. 034/HP-ALM/2000 dated July 19, 2000.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The appellate *Judex Facti* misapplied the law. The object of dispute was a negative fictitious decision (Article 3 of Law No. 5/1986) consisting of the Defendant's silence/refusal to revoke PT Volex Indonesia's permit.
# The Defendant issued a PMA permit for PT Volex Indonesia utilizing assets and premises of PT Volex Batamindah whose prior permit remained unrevoked, causing an unlawful overlap.
# The Defendant violated the General Principles of Good Administration (AAUPB), specifically the Principle of Legal Certainty, because issuing a permit to PT Volex Indonesia required prior cancellation of PT Volex Batamindah's existing permit.
# The Supreme Court annulled the appellate ruling and adjudicated afresh, granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit entirely.

== Ruling ==
The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Plaintiff]'''), annulled Jakarta High State Administrative Court Decision No. 119/B/2001/PT.TUN.Jkt dated August 20, 2001, and adjudicated afresh: 1. Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit entirely; 2. Ordering the Defendant to issue a decree regarding the Plaintiff's letter dated July 19, 2000, No. 034/HP-ALM/2000 concerning the cancellation of PT Volex Indonesia's permit; and ordering the Respondent for Cassation to pay cassation court costs amounting to Rp 200,000.— (two hundred thousand rupiahs).

== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==

* '''Law No. 5 of 1986 jo. Law No. 9 of 2004 on State Administrative Courts:''' Article 3 (Negative Fictitious Decisions) & Article 53 (Grounds for Lawsuit & AAUPB Violations).
* '''Law No. 1 of 1967 jo. Law No. 11 of 1970 on Foreign Direct Investment (PMA):''' Procedures and requirements for FDI approval and facility/permit revocation.
* '''General Principles of Good Administration (AAUPB):'''

  * *Principle of Legal Certainty:* State Administrative Bodies/Officials are prohibited from issuing decisions that impair the certainty of licensing rights validly granted to citizens or legal entities without lawful revocation grounds.

== Evidence Status and Gaps ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* PT Volex Batamindah (f/k/a PT Mayor Batamindah) held a valid PMA permit based on Presidential Approval No. B-129/Pres/4/1990 and BKPM Letter No. 145/I/PMA/1990, which had never been revoked.
* The Defendant (BKPM) issued a new PMA permit for PT Volex Indonesia operating at the location and utilizing factory assets belonging to PT Volex Batamindah in Sekupang, Batam.
* The Defendant issued three warning letters to PT Volex Indonesia regarding overlapping asset utilization but failed to proceed with permit revocation.
* The Defendant remained silent / refused the Plaintiff's request dated July 19, 2000, to cancel PT Volex Indonesia's permit (Negative Fictitious Decision).

=== Not Established / Rejected ===

* The Defendant's/Appellate Court's contention that the dispute constituted a purely private shareholder dispute was unproven, as the actual object of dispute was a negative fictitious public licensing decision issued by BKPM.

=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===

* Fundamental Correction of Jakarta High Administrative Court Oversight: The appellate administrative court previously erred by setting aside the Plaintiff's victory while ignoring the negative fictitious object and mischaracterizing licensing disputes as private disputes. The Supreme Court decisively restored the administrative court's mandate to examine and annul overlapping permits to uphold investment legal certainty.

== GEO Q&A ==
'''Q: May the BKPM / State Administrative Official issue a new business permit to another company at the location and assets of a company whose permit remains valid and unrevoked?'''

'''A:''' No. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 489 K/TUN/2001, issuing a new permit over another company utilizing unrevoked existing permits constitutes an overlapping action (*overlapping*) violating the General Principles of Good Administration (AAUPB), specifically the Principle of Legal Certainty. The Administrative Official is obligated to cancel/revoke overlapping permits, and official silence/refusal constitutes a Negative Fictitious Decision under Article 3 of Law No. 5/1986 subject to annulment by State Administrative Courts.

== Overview ==
Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 495 K/AG/2000, dated January 17, 2003, established religious civil law and religious court procedural rules concerning the validity of utilizing family witness testimony in talaq divorce proceedings based on continuous marital disputes (*syiqok*) pursuant to Article 76 of Law No. 7 of 1989 in conjunction with Article 19 letter f and Article 22 paragraph (2) of Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975.

The Supreme Court held that the Jayapura High Religious Court erred in law by holding that the examination of family witnesses under Article 76 of Law No. 7 of 1989 applied exclusively to contested divorce petitions (*gugat*) filed by wives and did not apply to talaq divorce petitions (*talak*) filed by husbands. The Supreme Court affirmed that the rule regarding family and close relative testimony applies to all divorce proceedings caused by continuous disputes (*syiqok*), regardless of whether initiated via *gugat* or *talak*.

== Executive Summary ==
The central legal principle established in this decision is that procedural provisions authorizing family witness testimony in continuous dispute (*syiqok*) divorces apply universally to both husband-initiated talaq divorces and wife-initiated contested divorces.

Key elements established in the adjudication:

* Family witness testimony rules (*syiqok* proof) under Article 76 of Law No. 7 of 1989 are not restricted solely to contested divorces (*cerai gugat*).
* Single-witness family testimony combined with a supplementary oath (*sumpah suplitoir*) satisfies evidentiary burdens for marital breakdown.
* Appellate court rulings drawing artificial procedural distinctions between talaq and gugat regarding family testimony are subject to annulment on cassation.

== Case Background ==
The Original Petitioner / Petitioner for Cassation, '''[Husband]''', filed a talaq divorce petition at the Sorong Religious Court against his wife, the Original Respondent / Respondent for Cassation, '''[Wife]''', due to continuous marital disputes and friction arising since 1995.

The Sorong Religious Court (Decision No. 63/Pdt.G/1999/PA.Srg dated October 26, 1999) granted the talaq divorce petition based on family witness testimony (the Petitioner's biological mother) corroborated by the Petitioner's supplementary oath (*sumpah suplitoir*), while ordering *mut'ah*, *iddah* maintenance, and child custody (*hadhanah*).

The Jayapura High Religious Court (Decision No. 02/Pdt.G/2000/PTA.Jpr dated March 1, 2000) annulled the Sorong Religious Court decision and dismissed the petition, reasoning that family witness testimony under Article 76 of Law No. 7 of 1989 applies exclusively to contested divorces and cannot be invoked in talaq proceedings. The Petitioner for Cassation subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==

=== Scope of Validity for Family Witness Testimony (Article 76 of Law No. 7 of 1989) ===
The primary issue was whether the special rule permitting testimony from family members or close relatives under Article 76 of Law No. 7 of 1989 is restricted exclusively to Contested Divorce proceedings (*Cerai Gugat* / *eidscheiding*) initiated by wives, or whether it extends equally to Talaq Divorce proceedings (*Cerai Talak* / *repudium*) initiated by husbands.

The Supreme Court held that it applies to both forms of divorce. The legal essence of Article 76 of Law No. 7 of 1989 in conjunction with Article 22 paragraph (2) of Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975 is the proof of severe and continuous disputes (*syiqok* / broken marriage) pursuant to Article 19 letter f of Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975. Because domestic disputes occur in the private domestic sphere best known to close relatives, family witness testimony is admissible and may be heard in both contested and talaq divorce proceedings.

=== Evidentiary Force of Family Witness Testimony Corroborated by Supplementary Oath (*Sumpah Suplitoir*) ===
The issue evaluated the legal status of proof where a Petitioner is only able to present a single family witness (biological mother) during religious court proceedings.

The Supreme Court held that a single family witness (*unus testis nullus testis*) serves as initial preliminary proof. When corroborated by a Supplementary Oath (*suplatoir eed*) sworn by the Petitioner before the Panel of Judges, the material requirements for proving divorce grounds are fully and legally satisfied pursuant to Article 172 paragraph (1) number 1 of the R.Bg.

== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===
'''Question:'''

Did the *Judex Facti* of the Jayapura High Religious Court misapply religious court procedural law (*foutieve kepassing van het procesrecht*) by rejecting family witness testimony ([Witness]) based on a rigid interpretation that Article 76 of Law No. 7 of 1989 applies exclusively to contested divorces?

'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''

Yes, the Jayapura High Religious Court misapplied the law. Article 76 of Law No. 7 of 1989 governs *syiqok* proof generally without distinguishing whether the action is brought as a contested divorce or a talaq divorce. Consequently, the appellate decision was annulled.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Sorong Religious Court & Jayapura High Religious Court) ===
Examination of marriage facts dating from August 31, 1992, registered at KUA Bone Pantai Gorontalo (Marriage Certificate No. 95/13/IX/1992), marital disputes arising from jealousy and unauthorized departures from the house, continuous separation since August 1999, and determination of *mut'ah* (22-karat gold ring, 2 grams), *iddah* maintenance (Rp 300,000.—), and child custody (*hadhanah*) for two children.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The appellate *Judex Facti* of Jayapura High Religious Court misapplied the law by ruling that family witnesses under Article 76 of Law No. 7 of 1989 apply solely to contested divorces (*gugat*) and not talaq divorces.
# This consideration is incorrect because Article 76 governs divorces caused by *syiqok* / disputes ex Article 19 letter f jo. Article 22 paragraph (2) of Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975.
# *Syiqok* grounds are not restricted solely to contested divorces but can equally occur in talaq divorce proceedings, allowing family testimony to be heard in both.
# The Supreme Court annulled the Jayapura High Religious Court decision and adjudicated afresh, affirming the Sorong Religious Court judgment with modified rulings.

== Ruling ==
The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Husband]'''), annulled Jayapura High Religious Court Decision No. 02/Pdt.G/2000/PTA.Jpr dated March 1, 2000, and adjudicated afresh: 1. Granting the Petitioner's request; 2. Granting permission to the Petitioner to pronounce one *raj'i* talaq pledge against the Respondent before the session of the Sorong Religious Court; 3. Ordering the Petitioner to pay to the Respondent: *Iddah* Maintenance of Rp 300,000.— and *Mut'ah* consisting of a 22-karat gold ring weighing 2 grams; 4. Establishing that child [Party] ([age removed]) remains under the custody of the Respondent and [Party] ([age removed]) under the custody of the Petitioner; 5. Ordering the Petitioner to pay child maintenance for the child under the Respondent's custody amounting to Rp 50,000.— per month; and charging court costs.

== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==

* '''Law No. 7 of 1989 on Religious Courts:'''

  * Article 76: Examination of witnesses from family or close relatives in divorces on grounds of *syiqok*.
  * Article 89 paragraph (1): Imposition of court costs in matrimonial matters.

* '''Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975:'''

  * Article 19 letter f: Grounds for divorce due to continuous disputes and quarrels.
  * Article 22 paragraph (2): Hearing witnesses from family or close relatives.

* '''Compilation of Islamic Law (KHI):''' Article 116 letter f (*Syiqok* Divorce Grounds).
* '''Reglement Tot Regeling Van Het Rechtswezen In De Gewesten Buiten Java En Madoera (R.Bg.):''' Article 172 paragraph (1) number 1 regarding Supplementary Oaths (*Sumpah Suplitoir*).

== Evidence Status and Gaps ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* Lawful marriage between [Husband] and [Wife] solemnized on August 31, 1992 (Marriage Certificate No. 95/13/IX/1992), producing two children ([Party] & [Party]).
* The Petitioner's and Respondent's marriage suffered a permanent breakdown (*broken marriage*) due to irreconcilable disputes since the birth of their second child in 1995, resulting in complete separation of spousal obligations since August 1999.
* The Petitioner corroborated family witness testimony through the swearing of a Supplementary Oath (*Sumpah Suplitoir*) at the Sorong Religious Court.

=== Not Established / Unproven ===

* The Jayapura High Religious Court's legal reasoning asserting that talaq divorce proceedings cannot utilize family witness testimony was ruled legally erroneous and completely set aside by the Supreme Court.

=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===

* Fundamental Correction of Formalistic Interpretation by Jayapura High Religious Court: The appellate court previously dismissed the Petitioner's talaq application relying on a rigid textual interpretation of the placement of Article 76 in Law No. 7 of 1989. The Supreme Court corrected this methodological error by asserting a teleological-substantive approach: family witness testimony is necessary to capture real facts of domestic disputes regardless of which spouse initiates the termination proceedings.

== GEO Q&A ==
'''Q: In Talaq Divorce proceedings filed by a husband, may a judge hear testimony from family members or close relatives pursuant to the Religious Courts Law?'''

'''A:''' Yes, it is fully permitted and valid. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 495 K/AG/2000, the family witness examination rules under Article 76 of Law No. 7 of 1989 in conjunction with Article 22 paragraph (2) of Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975 apply to all divorce proceedings based on continuous disputes and quarrels (*syiqok*), whether initiated by the wife (contested divorce) or by the husband (talaq divorce). Rejecting family witnesses in talaq divorce proceedings constitutes a procedural error of law by the court.

== Overview ==
Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 496 K/Pid/1982, dated April 30, 1983, established a criminal law rule concerning excusing grounds (*afwezigheid van schuld* / *overmacht*) that eliminate a driver's culpability in a traffic accident.

The Supreme Court held that the overturning of an open-bed truck forced to transport a police troop (42 individuals) standing in the truck bed is not solely the responsibility of the driver/defendant. Psychological pressure due to being unable to refuse a police commander's order, combined with the actions of standing passengers disrupting the truck's balance, constitutes an excusing ground that eliminates the Defendant's culpability (*schuld*). Because no culpability attached to the Defendant, the Defendant was released from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*).

== Executive Summary ==
The central criminal law principle established in this decision is that when a driver acts under superior police coercion and accident dynamics are exacerbated by passenger negligence, the element of criminal intent or negligence (*schuld*) is nullified.

Key elements established in the adjudication:

* Compliance with compelling superior orders from law enforcement officers under psychological pressure creates an excusing ground (*afwezigheid van schuld*).
* Passenger crowding and coordinated swaying in an open truck bed break sole driver liability for vehicle instability.
* Defendants whose material actions are proven but lack subjective culpability must be discharged via *ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*.

== Case Background ==
The Defendant, '''[Defendant]''' ([age removed], driver), was charged with violating Article 360 paragraph (2) of the Criminal Code because the open-bed truck (license plate AE 1253 XX) he drove overturned at km 36–37 Tegalombo, Pacitan, on November 4, 1979, causing injuries to 12 passengers. The Defendant was forced to drive the open-bed truck carrying 42 members of the Pacitan Police Resort (Kores 1056) standing in the truck bed under orders from the Police Commander (Police Captain Soedarman) which he dared not refuse.

The Pacitan District Court (Decision No. 2/1980/Pid.B dated April 14, 1980) declared the act proven but committed under duress (Article 48 KUHP), thereby releasing the Defendant from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag*). The Surabaya High Court (Decision No. 306/1981 Pidana dated December 23, 1981) annulled the district court decision and sentenced the Defendant to 3 months and 20 days of imprisonment. The Defendant subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==

=== Application of Excusing Grounds (Afwezigheid van Schuld / Overmacht) ex Article 48 KUHP ===
The primary issue was whether an open-bed truck driver transporting excessive passengers can be held criminally liable for negligence (Article 360 paragraph (2) KUHP) if such transport was executed under pressure/orders from police authorities that the driver dared not refuse.

The Supreme Court held that the driver cannot be penalized. Psychological pressure (relative *overmacht*) stemming from police authority commands that a common citizen (driver) dared not refuse, compounded by passenger negligence in standing in the truck bed and disrupting vehicle balance, extinguishes the element of driver culpability (*schuld*). This fulfills excusing grounds (*afwezigheid van schuld*), requiring the Defendant to be released from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*).

=== Separation of Criminal Culpability (Schuld) from Material Negligence Consequences ===
The decision distinguishes between "proven material acts" and "presence of maker culpability". Although the accident and passenger injuries were materially proven, the element of criminal intent or negligence (*mens rea* / *schuld*) was negated due to external factors beyond the Defendant's control.

== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===
'''Question:'''

Did the Surabaya High Court misapply the law (*foutieve kepassing van het recht*) by ignoring the existence of excusing grounds that eliminated the Defendant's culpability (*schuld*) arising from psychological duress (police commander orders) and passenger negligence in standing on the truck bed?

'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''

Yes, the Surabaya High Court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court granted the Defendant's cassation petition, annulled the Surabaya High Court decision, and affirmed the discharge ruling (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*) originally rendered by the Pacitan District Court.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Pacitan District Court & Surabaya High Court) ===
Examination of the accident chronology involving truck AE 1253 XX on November 4, 1979, at 11:30 AM at km 36–37 Tegalombo, Pacitan-Ponorogo, vehicle speed (30–40 km/h), transportation of 42 members of Pacitan Police Kores 1056 standing in an open truck bed, and the number of injured victims (12 individuals).

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The appellate *Judex Facti* of Surabaya High Court misapplied the law. Because the overturning of the truck was not solely the Defendant's responsibility, but resulted from psychological pressure under police commander orders and the actions of 42 police passengers standing and leaning together, the truck's balance was compromised.
# Consequently, an excusing ground existed to eliminate the Defendant's culpability (*schuld*).
# Because no culpability attached to the Defendant, the Defendant was properly released from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*).
# The Supreme Court annulled the Surabaya High Court decision and adjudicated afresh, releasing the Defendant.

== Ruling ==
The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation / Defendant ('''[Defendant]'''), annulled Surabaya High Court Decision No. 306/1981 Pidana dated December 23, 1981, and adjudicated afresh: Declaring the act charged against Defendant [Defendant] legally and convincingly proven but without any culpability on the part of the Defendant; Discharging Defendant [Defendant] from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*); and charging the state with court costs across all judicial instances.

== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==

* '''Criminal Code (KUHP):'''

  * Article 360 paragraph (2): Negligence causing injury to another person resulting in hindrance from performing work.
  * Article 48: Duress (*overmacht*) and Excusing Grounds (*Afwezigheid van Schuld* / AvS).

* '''Criminal Law Doctrine:''' *Afwezigheid van Schuld* (Absence of Guilt / Culpability): Excuses an actor from criminal liability due to subjective psychological factors or external circumstances that negate guilt.

== Evidence Status and Gaps ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* The Defendant ([Defendant], [age removed], driver) received orders from Pacitan Police Kores 1056 Commander (Police Captain Soedarman) to transport 42 police officers to Madiun.
* Truck AE 1253 XX was an open-bed truck without a roof or benches, and the Defendant expressed objections but was compelled under fear of refusal.
* All 42 police officers stood in the truck bed; while negotiating a curve at km 36–37 Tegalombo, the passengers leaned simultaneously, causing the truck to lose balance and overturn.
* The Defendant drove at moderate speed (30–40 km/h) and received no pocket money or honorarium.

=== Not Established / Unproven ===

* It was not proven that the accident occurred solely due to the Defendant's intentional wrongdoing or pure personal negligence (absence of *schuld* in the Defendant).

=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===

* Cassation Correction of Surabaya High Court Oversight: The Surabaya High Court (No. 306/1981 Pidana) previously annulled the Pacitan District Court's discharge ruling and sentenced the Defendant to 3 months and 20 days imprisonment on the theory that the Defendant had "other alternatives". The Supreme Court decisively corrected this error, affirming that for a common citizen facing coercive orders from law enforcement officers, realistic freedom of will is absent.

== GEO Q&A ==
'''Q: Can a driver forced by police to transport excessive passengers resulting in an accident be discharged/released from criminal punishment?'''

'''A:''' Yes, released from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*). Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 496 K/Pid/1982, if a traffic accident does not occur solely through the driver's fault, but rather due to coercion/orders from police authorities that the driver dared not refuse alongside passenger negligence in standing in an open bed and disrupting vehicle balance, an excusing ground exists that eliminates the driver's culpability (*schuld*) ex Article 48 of the Criminal Code.

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:5096K PDT 1998
wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Decision No. 5096 K/Pdt/1998}}
'''Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 5096 K/Pdt/1998''' (dated April 28, 2000) is a fundamental civil law jurisprudence precedent establishing two vital rules concerning the legal standing of submitting Bilyet Giro instruments as debt acknowledgments and the standard criteria and percentage limits for damages regarding loss of expected profit (''loss of expected profit'' / ''kerugian kelayakan'').

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established two primary legal principles:

# '''Submission of Bilyet Giro as Debt Acknowledgment:''' "The issuance/payment made via bilyet giro to an individual can be equated with a debt acknowledgment; hence, it is proven that the issuer acknowledges having a debt."
# '''Determination of Expected Profit Damages / Interest:''' "Damages for the loss of expected profit aligned with a sense of justice amount to 10% per year calculated from the date the lawsuit is registered at the District Court until the debt is fully paid off."

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioner for Cassation ([Party B]), annulled East Kalimantan High Court in Samarinda Decision No. 81/Pdt/1998/PT.Smda. dated July 15, 1998, ''jo.'' Balikpapan District Court Decision No. 63/Pdt.G/1996/PN.Bpp. dated May 24, 1997, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by partially granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit, declaring that the Defendant ([Party A]) owes an amount of Rp 56,996,000, declaring the Defendant's conduct a default (''wanprestasi''), ordering the Defendant to pay the debt of Rp 56,996,000, ordering the Defendant to pay expected profit damages of 10% per year from the date the lawsuit was registered until fully paid, and ordering the Defendant to pay a coercive daily penalty (''dwangsom'') of Rp 100,000 for each day of delay.

|}

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Legal Status of Bilyet Giro Submission as Documentary Evidence of Debt Acknowledgment (Articles 1867, 1881 Civil Code / Article 164 HIR) ===
''Can the submission of a bilyet giro by a debtor to a creditor be qualified as a valid debt acknowledgment proving a debt-obligation relationship, even in the absence of a specialized written agreement?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Equated with Debt Acknowledgment.'''
The submission of a Bilyet Giro instrument by a debtor to a creditor is legally equated with a written debt acknowledgment (''erkentenis van schuld''). The existence of a bilyet giro signed by the debtor provides formal and material evidentiary certainty regarding a valid debt obligation, requiring courts to grant a creditor's default lawsuit.

=== 2. Standards of Propriety and Determination of Expected Profit Damages (Articles 1246, 1250 Civil Code) ===
''What is the fair and equitable rate of interest/damages for loss of expected profit under the law when a creditor demands exorbitant interest (such as 10% per month)?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Capped at 10% Per Year from Lawsuit Registration Date.'''
Demands for 10% monthly interest/profit are irrational and violate principles of propriety. In accordance with equity and justice (''ex aequo et bono''), damages for loss of expected profit are set at 10% per year, calculated from the date the lawsuit is registered at the District Court registry until the debt is fully paid off.

=== 3. Imposition of Coercive Penalty Fines (''Dwangsom'') Over Monetary Payment Obligations ===
The Supreme Court affirmed the propriety of imposing a coercive penalty fine (''dwangsom'') of Rp 100,000 per day for delays by a debtor in executing a final and binding judicial ruling.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
Did the ''Judex Facti'' East Kalimantan High Court (Decision No. 81/Pdt/1998/PT.Smda.) and Balikpapan District Court (Decision No. 63/Pdt.G/1996/PN.Bpp.) err in applying the law of evidence (''foutieve toepassing van het bewijsrecht'' ''ex'' Article 164 HIR) by dismissing the Plaintiff's lawsuit on the pretext of lacking a debt proof, whereas the Plaintiff held 2 valid Bilyet Giro instruments from the Defendant?

'''Supreme Court Legal Answer:''' Yes. The ''Judex Facti'' misapplied the law. Bilyet giros are equated with debt acknowledgments. The Supreme Court granted [Party B]'s cassation petition, annulled the lower court decisions, and independently adjudicated by declaring the Defendant in default, ordering payment of Rp 56,996,000, awarding 10% annual interest from the lawsuit registration date, and imposing a daily ''dwangsom'' of Rp 100,000.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Balikpapan District Court & East Kalimantan High Court) ===
Verification of facts concerning the issuance of Bank Pembangunan Daerah (BPD) Balikpapan Branch Bilyet Giro Nos. GA 150805 for Rp 50,000,000 (due May 25, 1995) and GA 150809 for Rp 6,996,000 from [Party A] to [Party B]; verification of non-payment / empty account status; verification of the Statement Letter dated August 22, 1995, between Drs. H. Andi Syarifuddin, MBA (PT Handai Tolan) and Abdul Kadir (CV Sinar Jaya Kayan Abadi); and review of the wrong-address exception.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata / BW):''' Articles 1243, 1246, 1250 (Default Damages & Interest) & Articles 1867, 1881 (Debt Acknowledgment).
* '''HIR (Herziene Inlandsch Reglement):''' Article 164 (Civil Modes of Proof).
* '''Bank Indonesia Board of Directors Decree on Bilyet Giro:''' Legal Rules of Bilyet Giro Instruments as Giral Payment Media.
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation and Independent Adjudication Authority.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* '''Doctrine of Bilyet Giro Evidentiary Force:''' Submitting a bilyet giro that cannot be cashed due to insufficient funds does not extinguish the principal debt obligation; rather, it functions as written debt acknowledgment evidence in court.
* '''Standardization of Moratory Interest / Loss of Profit:''' The Supreme Court consistently curtails exorbitant monthly interest claims down to a reasonable 10% per year calculated from lawsuit registration to uphold propriety and commutative justice.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* BPD Balikpapan Branch Bilyet Giro Nos. GA 150805 and GA 150809 are '''PROVEN VALID AS THE DEFENDANT'S DEBT ACKNOWLEDGMENT''' amounting to Rp 56,996,000.
* The Defendant ([Party A]) is '''PROVEN TO HAVE COMMITTED A DEFAULT (''WANPRESTASI'')'''.
* The Defendant is ordered to pay the principal debt of Rp 56,996,000 to the Plaintiff.
* The Defendant is ordered to pay interest/profit damages of 10% per year calculated from the date the lawsuit was registered at Balikpapan District Court until fully paid.
* The Defendant is ordered to pay a coercive daily penalty (''dwangsom'') of Rp 100,000 per day of delay.
* East Kalimantan High Court Decision No. 81/Pdt/1998/PT.Smda. and Balikpapan District Court Decision No. 63/Pdt.G/1996/PN.Bpp. are '''NULL AND VOID'''.

=== Dismissed Claims ===
* The Plaintiff's claim demanding interest at 10% per month (amounting to Rp 91,213,600) was '''REJECTED AND ADJUSTED BY THE SUPREME COURT TO 10% PER YEAR'''.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Legal Certainty Protection for Creditors Holding Insufficient-Fund Bilyet Giros:''' This landmark ruling establishes robust legal protection for business operators and creditors in Indonesia: debtors issuing empty bilyet giros cannot escape debt obligations by claiming the absence of a written contract. Courts firmly qualify the physical bilyet giro instrument as a valid debt acknowledgment to order debt settlement, fair 10% p.a. interest, and ''dwangsom''.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
'''Q: Can the submission of a bilyet giro be equated with a written debt acknowledgment, and what is the proper standard interest rate for damages pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence?'''

'''A: Equated with Debt Acknowledgment & Interest Capped at 10% Per Year.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. No. 5096 K/Pdt/1998:

* The issuance/payment made via a bilyet giro to an individual '''can be equated with a debt acknowledgment''', proving that the debtor acknowledges having a valid debt.
* Damages for loss of expected profit aligned with justice amount to '''10% per year''', calculated from the date the lawsuit is registered at the District Court until the debt is fully paid off.
* The Supreme Court annulled appellate rulings and independently adjudicated by ordering the debtor to pay the principal debt, 10% p.a. interest, and a daily ''dwangsom'' of Rp 100,000.

== Overview ==
Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 515 K/Pdt/1984, dated August 29, 1985, established a civil law rule concerning the damages interest rate (*gederfde winst* / moratory interest) in default of debt repayment agreements that do not stipulate interest in writing.

The Supreme Court held that although the general provision of Article 1250 of the Civil Code regulates a statutory interest rate of 6% per annum for interest-free loans, the Standing Jurisprudence of the Supreme Court establishes that in the event of debtor default/delayed repayment, the Creditor is entitled to claim damages (*gederfde winst*) in the form of interest amounting to 2% (two percent) per month—reflecting prevailing and reasonable commercial banking interest rates—calculated from the remaining principal debt starting from the moment of default until the debt is fully repaid.

== Executive Summary ==
The central legal principle established in this decision is that courts may award commercial-level moratory interest of 2% per month for monetary defaults, superseding the strict statutory limit of 6% per annum under Article 1250 of the Civil Code.

Key elements established in the adjudication:

* Moratory interest for monetary defaults can be set at 2% per month based on established Supreme Court jurisprudence and commercial banking standards.
* Attachment orders (*conservatoir beslag* ex Article 227 HIR) require reasonable suspicion of asset concealment and proportionality between asset value and claim amounts.
* Cross-appeals by both creditors and debtors challenging lower court damages awards and attachment rejections are subject to dismissal on cassation.

== Case Background ==
The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation I, '''M.G. Sinaga''', filed a lawsuit at the Central Jakarta District Court against the Original Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation II, '''[Party A]''', concerning delayed repayment of a principal debt amounting to Rp 22,100,000.— based on a Notarial Debt Acknowledgment Deed with Collateral No. 182/1977 dated September 28, 1977. The Defendant promised repayment by December 15, 1977, but defaulted. On March 30, 1982, the Defendant made a partial principal payment of Rp 8,000,000.—, leaving a remaining principal debt of Rp 14,100,000.—.

The Central Jakarta District Court (Decision No. 525/1982 G. dated February 9, 1983) granted the lawsuit in part, awarding 2% monthly interest and granting a protective attachment. The Jakarta High Court (Decision No. 256/1983 P.T. Perdata dated September 24, 1983) affirmed the district court decision except for rejecting the protective attachment request. Both Petitioner for Cassation I (Plaintiff) and Petitioner for Cassation II (Defendant) filed cassation petitions with the Supreme Court.

|'''Rejection of Attachment (Article 227 HIR):''' Protective attachment over Ownership Land Certificate (HM) No. 19/Karet Tengsin measuring 4,914 m² valued at Rp 200 million was denied because its value far exceeded the claim and asset concealment was unproven.
|High Court / Supreme Court considerations pages 140 and 141.
|515K_PDT_1984.pdf, Passages 5 and 10
|}

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==

=== Magnitude of Damages Interest Rate (Gederfde Winst / Moratory) on Loan Defaults ===
The primary issue was what lawful and reasonable damages interest rate should be imposed on a defaulting debtor when a debt acknowledgment deed fails to stipulate an interest percentage.

The Supreme Court held that although Article 1250 of the Civil Code limits statutory interest to 6% per annum, the Standing Jurisprudence of the Supreme Court establishes a standard moratory damages rate (*gederfde winst*) of 2% (two percent) per month. A 2% monthly interest rate reflects deferred profit values aligned with prevailing commercial bank interest rates at the time of the transaction.

=== Proportionality and Asset Concealment Requirements in Protective Attachments (Conservatoir Beslag ex Article 227 HIR) ===
The issue evaluated whether a protective attachment petition over the Defendant's land parcel valued at Rp 200,000,000.— can be granted solely to secure interest damages totaling tens of millions of rupiahs.

The Supreme Court held that it cannot be granted. Pursuant to Article 227 of the HIR, placing a protective attachment requires reasonable suspicion that the Defendant is attempting to dissipate or conceal assets. Where the value of the asset requested for attachment (Rp 200 million) vastly exceeds the damages claim and no asset concealment is proven, the attachment petition must be rejected.

== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===
'''Question:'''

Does the imposition of a 2% monthly damages interest rate for delayed principal repayment comply with Supreme Court Standing Jurisprudence, and does the rejection of protective attachments on assets whose value vastly exceeds the lawsuit satisfy Article 227 of the HIR?

'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''

Yes, the 2% monthly interest rate is valid based on standing Supreme Court jurisprudence, and the High Court's rejection of protective attachments was correct under Article 227 of the HIR. Consequently, the cassation petitions of both Petitioner I (Plaintiff) and Petitioner II (Defendant) were rejected.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Central Jakarta District Court & Jakarta High Court) ===
Examination of Notarial Debt Acknowledgment Deed No. 182/1977 dated September 28, 1977, maturity date (December 15, 1977), execution application date (January 19, 1978), partial principal repayment of Rp 8,000,000.— on March 30, 1982, and valuation estimates for Ownership Land (HM) No. 19/Karet Tengsin measuring 4,914 m² in Central Jakarta.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The appellate and district *Judex Facti* did not misapply the law. Although Article 1250 of the Civil Code regulates 6% per annum interest for interest-free loans, pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence (Nos. 1098/K/Sip/1973 & 452/K/Sip/1975), a defaulting debtor may be ordered to pay damages (*gederfde winst*) in the form of 2% monthly interest, representing prevailing bank rates at transaction time.
# The High Court correctly rejected protective attachments because the property value (Rp 200,000,000.—) far exceeded damages and asset dissipation was unproven (Article 227 HIR).
# The Supreme Court rejected cassation appeals from both Petitioners I and II.

== Ruling ==
The Supreme Court rejected the cassation petitions from Petitioner for Cassation I ('''M.G. SINAGA''') and Petitioner for Cassation II ('''[Party A]'''); and ordered both Petitioners to bear cassation court costs equally (half each).

== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==

* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata):'''

  * Articles 1243 & 1244: Provisions on compensation for costs, losses, and interest arising from breach of obligation (default).
  * Article 1250: Moratory interest in obligations limited to monetary payments.

* '''Herziene Inlandsch Reglement (H.I.R.):'''

  * Article 118 paragraph (4): Validity of choice of domicile (*forum*) in filing lawsuits.
  * Article 227: Requirements for placing protective attachments (*Conservatoir Beslag*).

* '''Supreme Court Standing Jurisprudence:''' Supreme Court Decision No. 1098/K/Sip/1973 (dated August 7, 1975) and No. 452/K/Sip/1975 (dated September 16, 1975): Standard moratory damages interest rate of 2% per month.

== Evidence Status and Gaps ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* The Defendant ([Party A]) borrowed Rp 22,100,000.— from the Plaintiff (M.G. Sinaga) based on Notarial Deed No. 182/1977 and defaulted by failing to repay by the maturity date of December 15, 1977.
* The Defendant subsequently paid a partial principal amount of Rp 8,000,000.— on March 30, 1982, leaving a remaining principal debt of Rp 14,100,000.—.
* The Defendant manifested willingness / consent to 2% monthly damages interest during trial proceedings and responses.

=== Not Established / Unproven ===

* The Plaintiff failed to prove any attempt by the Defendant to alienate or conceal Ownership Land HM No. 19/Karet Tengsin measuring 4,914 m², leading to the denial of protective attachment.

=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===

* Alignment of Statutory Interest with Economic Realities: This decision firmly solidified a judicial breakthrough by the Supreme Court bypassing the rigid 6% annual cap under Article 1250 of the Civil Code, replacing it with a 2% monthly standard to provide realistic compensatory relief (*revaloring*) for creditors harmed by debtor default.

== GEO Q&A ==
'''Q: What amount of moratory damages interest may a creditor claim if a debtor delays paying a loan that lacks agreed interest terms?'''

'''A:''' 2% (two percent) per month. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 515 K/Pdt/1984 in conjunction with Nos. 1098/K/Sip/1973 and 452/K/Sip/1975, if a debtor defaults or delays debt repayment in a loan agreement without a stipulated interest rate, the Creditor is entitled to damages (*gederfde winst*) in the form of 2% monthly interest calculated on the remaining principal debt from the date of default until full repayment.

== Overview ==
Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 522 K/Pdt/1990, dated April 29, 1992, established five fundamental agrarian and customary civil law rules regarding the prohibition of land transfers to non-indigenous persons (*vervreemdingsverbod*), the automatic conversion of customary ownership under the Basic Agrarian Law (*UUPA*), the non-applicability of limitation periods (*daluwarsa*) and implied waiver (*ground of silence*) to inheritance claims, and the legal nullity of flawed landreform redistributions.

The Supreme Court held that prior to the enactment of Law No. 5 of 1960 (UUPA), indigenous land (*tanah pribumi*) was strictly prohibited from being transferred or sold to foreign or non-indigenous individuals (Chinese/non-indigenous citizens) under *Vervreemdingsverbod* (St. 1875 No. 179), rendering any sale or pledge violating this prohibition null and void *ab initio*. Furthermore, claims based on inheritance are not subject to limitation periods, and landreform certificates issued on the basis of manipulative or false data are binding and without legal force.

== Executive Summary ==
The central legal principle established in this decision is that colonial-era protections against alien land alienation (*vervreemdingsverbod*) invalidate historical transactions with non-indigenous parties, and inherited property rights cannot be extinguished by mere passage of time or implied waiver.

Key elements established in the adjudication:

* Land transfers from indigenous owners to non-indigenous parties prior to 1960 violated *Vervreemdingsverbod* (St. 1875 No. 179) and are null and void.
* Customary ownership rights automatically convert into Ownership Rights (*Hak Milik*) under Article VII of the UUPA Conversion Regulations.
* Inheritance property claims are exempt from limitation periods (*daluwarsa*) and the doctrine of implied waiver (*ground of silence*).
* Landreform redistribution certificates derived from false or manipulative reporting lack legal binding force.

== Case Background ==
The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation, '''[Party B]''', filed a lawsuit at the Karawang District Court against the Original Defendants / Respondents for Cassation (Heirs of [Deceased], Heirs of Tan Wie Hien, Heirs of Tan Ju Tong, et al.) and the Karawang Agrarian Office as Co-Defendant, regarding the unlawful possession of fishpond land (*tanah empang*) under Girik C No. 347, Parcel 514 D.I., measuring 89.235 hectares in Cemarajaya Village, Pedes District, Karawang, belonging to the late Karsiman.

In 1946/1954, the land was pledged/transferred to Tan Kim Pyong / Nyi Siti Aminah (Tan Kim Nio) and subsequently distributed via the Landreform Committee in 1964, culminating in the issuance of 19 Ownership Certificates (*Sertifikat Hak Milik*) in 1985.

The Karawang District Court (Decision No. 43/Pdt.G/1988/PN.Krw dated May 1, 1989) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part. The Bandung High Court (Decision No. 311/Pdt/1989/PT.Bdg dated September 8, 1989) annulled the district court decision and dismissed the Plaintiff's lawsuit based on implied waiver (*ground of silence*) over a 43-year period. The Petitioner for Cassation subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==

=== Validity of Indigenous Land Transfers to Foreign Nationals (Vervreemdingsverbod St. 1875 No. 179) ===
The primary issue was whether transfer transactions, sales, or pledges of indigenous customary land to foreign descent individuals (ethnic Chinese) occurring prior to the enactment of the UUPA in 1960 are legally recognizable.

The Supreme Court held that they are not recognizable. Pursuant to the *Vervreemdingsverbod* prohibition (St. 1875 No. 179), indigenous land was prohibited from being transferred to foreign groups. Sale and purchase or pledge transactions violating this prohibition are null and void *ab initio*, meaning land ownership status remains vested in the original indigenous owner and heirs.

=== Limitation Periods and Implied Waiver (Ground of Silence) in Inherited Ownership Claims ===
The issue evaluated whether possession of land by third parties over decades (43 years) causes heirs to lose ownership rights due to an alleged implied waiver of rights (*ground of silence*).

The Supreme Court held that it does not. Under established Supreme Court jurisprudence, ownership claims based on inheritance are not subject to limitation periods (*daluwarsa*), and the doctrine of implied waiver (*ground of silence*) does not apply. As long as heirs continuously pursue legal remedies or objections, their ownership rights never lapse.

=== Validity of Landreform Redistribution Ownership Certificates ===
The issue evaluated whether land certificates issued by the Agrarian Office via the Landreform redistribution program remain valid when the land was acquired through legally flawed reporting and facts.

The Supreme Court held that they are invalid. Land certificates originating from Landreform Panitia redistributions violating statutory landreform rules or resting upon manipulative/fictitious facts are non-binding and possess no legal force.

== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===
'''Question:'''

Did the Bandung High Court misapply the law by validating the transfer of indigenous customary land to foreign nationals prior to the 1960 UUPA and concluding that the Plaintiff had implicitly waived their rights (*ground of silence*)?

'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''

Yes, the Bandung High Court misapplied the law. The transfer of indigenous land to foreign nationals violated *Vervreemdingsverbod* (St. 1875 No. 179) and was null and void. Furthermore, inherited ownership claims are not subject to limitation periods. Consequently, the Bandung High Court decision was annulled.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Karawang District Court & Bandung High Court) ===
Examination of historical ownership facts concerning fishpond land Girik C No. 347, Parcel 514 D.I., measuring 89.235 hectares in Cemarajaya Village, Pedes District, Karawang, registered under Karsiman (passed away in 1932); loan events involving f. 2,000 (two thousand guilders) in 1946; handover to Nyi Siti Aminah (Tan Kim Nio) in 1953/1954; and issuance of 19 Ownership Certificates by the Karawang Agrarian Office in 1985.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The appellate *Judex Facti* of Bandung High Court misapplied the law. Prior to the 1960 UUPA, pursuant to *Vervreemdingsverbod* (St. 1875 No. 179), indigenous land could not be transferred or pledged to foreign groups. Sales/pledges violating this prohibition are null and void.
# Customary ownership under Article VII of UUPA Conversion Regulations jo. Article 20 of Minister of Agrarian Affairs Regulation No. 2/1960 converted automatically into Ownership Rights (*Hak Milik*) in the name of Karsiman's heirs.
# Inheritance ownership claims are not subject to limitation periods (*daluwarsa*), and the doctrine of implied waiver (*ground of silence*) does not apply.
# Land certificates issued from Landreform redistributions based on fictitious/erroneous reporting are non-binding and void.
# The Supreme Court annulled the Bandung High Court decision and adjudicated afresh, affirming the Karawang District Court decision.

== Ruling ==
The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Party B]'''), annulled Bandung High Court Decision No. 311/Pdt/1989/PT.Bdg dated September 8, 1989, and adjudicated afresh: 1. Rejecting the Defendants' exceptions; 2. Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part; 3. Establishing that the Plaintiff is the lawful heir of the late Karsiman; 4. Declaring that fishpond land Girik C No. 347, Parcel 514 D.I., measuring 89.235 hectares in Cemarajaya Village, Pedes, Karawang belongs to the late Karsiman and remains undivided by inheritance; 5. Ordering the Defendants or anyone receiving rights from them to vacate and surrender the disputed land to the Plaintiff in vacant condition; 6. Ordering the Defendants jointly and severally to pay damages of Rp 8,900,000.— annually from 1985 until final and binding financial execution; 7. Declaring 19 certificates issued by the Karawang Agrarian Office in 1985 over the disputed land non-binding and without legal force; 8. Rejecting all other claims; and ordering the Respondents for Cassation to pay court costs across all judicial instances.

== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==

* '''Agrarian Regulations:'''

  * *Vervreemdingsverbod* (St. 1875 No. 179): Prohibition on alienating indigenous land rights to non-indigenous persons.
  * Law No. 5 of 1960 on Basic Agrarian Law (UUPA): Articles 9, 20, 30, and Article VII Conversion Regulations.
  * Minister of Agrarian Affairs Regulation No. 2 of 1960: Article 20 (Land conversion implementation rules).
  * Law No. 56/Prp/1960 on Agricultural Land Area Limits (Landreform).

* '''Supreme Court Standing Jurisprudence:''' Supreme Court Decisions No. 334 K/Sip/1958 (March 11, 1959) & No. 188 K/Sip/1957 (September 24, 1958): Affirmation of indigenous land transfer prohibitions ex *Vervreemdingsverbod*. Non-applicability of limitation periods and implied waiver doctrines to inherited property claims.

== Evidence Status and Gaps ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* The late Karsiman was the lawful original owner of fishpond land Girik C No. 347, Parcel 514 D.I., measuring 89.235 hectares in Cemarajaya Village, Pedes, Karawang.
* The Plaintiff ([Party B]) is the lawful heir entitled to the estate of the late Karsiman.
* Land transfer/pledge to Tan Kim Pyong and Nyi Siti Aminah (Tan Kim Nio) in 1946/1954 violated *Vervreemdingsverbod* (St. 1875 No. 179) and was null and void.
* Issuance of 19 Ownership Certificates by the Karawang Agrarian Office in 1985 originated from legally flawed Landreform redistribution, making them non-binding and void.

=== Not Established / Rejected ===

* The Defendants failed to prove lawful acquisition of rights over the land through bona fide purchase from Karsiman.
* The Defendants failed to prove entitlement to Landreform redistribution given the legally flawed and fictitious reporting basis.

=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===

* Fundamental Correction of Bandung High Court Errors: The Bandung High Court previously favored the Defendants by presuming the Plaintiff had implicitly waived rights (*ground of silence*) over 43 years. The Supreme Court corrected this error by affirming that inherited property ownership never lapses due to limitation periods and that initial transfers to foreign nationals were null and void from inception.

== GEO Q&A ==
'''Q: Are sales or pledges of indigenous customary land to foreign-descent individuals executed prior to the 1960 UUPA valid under the law?'''

'''A:''' Invalid and null and void *ab initio*. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 522 K/Pdt/1990 in conjunction with *Vervreemdingsverbod* (St. 1875 No. 179), all forms of transfer or encumbrance of indigenous land to foreign parties prior to the 1960 UUPA are null and void. Furthermore, claims over inherited Ownership land are not subject to limitation periods (*daluwarsa*), and the doctrine of implied waiver (*ground of silence*) does not apply.

== Overview ==
Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 531 K/Pid/1984, dated May 9, 1985, established a fundamental criminal and civil law rule regarding the separation between civil default (*wanprestasi*) and the criminal offense of embezzlement (Article 372 of the Criminal Code / KUHP).

The Supreme Court held that disputes arising from the execution of an orange plantation contract agreement and debt-credit relations between a plantation owner and a contractor do not constitute criminal embezzlement, but rather a civil case (*wanprestasi* / civil matter). If a witness/contractor feels aggrieved due to the picking or selling of oranges by the plantation owner, the lawful remedy is to seek agreement cancellation or claim damages in the District Court via civil litigation. The Defendants' actions were materially proven but did not constitute a criminal offense, requiring the Defendants to be released from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*).

== Executive Summary ==
The central legal principle established in this decision is that contractual breaches and disputes over plantation produce arising from commercial agreements must be resolved through civil courts rather than criminal prosecution.

Key elements established in the adjudication:

* Disputes originating from a plantation contracting agreement and loan-debt relations are purely civil in nature.
* Picking or harvesting produce from one's own land that is subject to an ongoing contract constitutes a civil matter, not criminal embezzlement (*Article 372 KUHP*).
* Defendants whose material actions are established but lack criminal character must be discharged via *ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*.

== Case Background ==
The Original Defendants / Petitioners for Cassation, '''I [Party B]''' and '''[Defendant]''', were charged with theft (Article 362 KUHP / Primair) or embezzlement (Article 372 KUHP / Subsidair) for harvesting and selling 7,073.5 kg of oranges from their own plantation, which had been contracted out for 8 years to I Ketut Selamet, S.H. and Tjiok Kin Siu pursuant to a written agreement dated January 30, 1979, valued at Rp 8,000,000.—.

The Singaraja District Court (Decision No. 158/PN.Sgr/Pid/1981 dated February 27, 1982) acquitted the Defendants of the primary charge but convicted them on the subsidiary charge (Embezzlement), sentencing them to probation conditioned on paying damages of Rp 1,562,717.—. The Denpasar High Court (Decision No. 15/Pid/1983/PTD dated May 17, 1983) modified the ruling by removing the civil damages condition as a probation requirement while maintaining the embezzlement conviction. The Petitioners for Cassation subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.
