== Legal and Procedural Issues ==

=== Qualification and Propriety Standards of Moratory Damages Interest Rate ===
The primary issue was what moratory damages interest rate courts may lawfully and properly impose in commercial debt-default disputes.

The Supreme Court held that the *Judex Facti* (Samarinda District and High Courts) erred in imposing a 5% monthly damages rate. Based on standards of fairness, propriety, and Supreme Court Standing Jurisprudence, the moratory damages rate for delayed debt repayment is set at 2% (two percent) per month.

=== Joint and Several Liability (*Hoofdelijkheid*) of Joint Venture Partners ===
The issue evaluated whether an individual acting as cashier/financial administrator (Defendant II) in a joint venture construction project shares joint and several liability (*hoofdelijkheid*) with the credit applicant (Defendant I) for building material debts owed to third parties.

The Supreme Court held that they do. Procurement of building materials for joint project purposes and the signing/handing over of payment checks by Defendant II prove a joint legal bond, making both Defendants jointly and severally liable (*hoofdelijk*) to settle the debt.

== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===
'''Question:'''

Did the imposition of a 5% monthly interest damages rate by the *Judex Facti* violate civil law principles of equity, and was the Petitioner for Cassation's challenge justified in correcting it to 2% per month?

'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''

Yes. The Supreme Court corrected the Samarinda High Court's ruling specifically regarding the damages interest rate, reducing it from 5% per month to 2% per month calculated from April 2, 1981, until full repayment.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Samarinda District Court & East Kalimantan High Court) ===
Examination of facts concerning the statement letter dated July 29, 1980 (evidence P.1), issuance of State Trading Bank (*BDN*) Check No. CCC 033292 dated December 27, 1979, for Rp 1,931,000.—, Notarial Deed Agreement No. 961/1979 dated July 25, 1979, and execution of attachment over Defendant II's residence on September 18, 1981.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The *Judex Facti* of East Kalimantan High Court and Samarinda District Court correctly ruled that Defendants I and II defaulted and shared joint and several liability.
# However, regarding the quantum of damages, the imposition of a 5% monthly interest rate by the *Judex Facti* required correction. Pursuant to standards of propriety and Supreme Court jurisprudence, fair and proper moratory damages interest in this case is 2% (two percent) per month.
# The Supreme Court rejected the Petitioner's cassation appeal while modifying the lower court rulings regarding interest rates.

== Ruling ==
The Supreme Court rejected the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Party A]'''), with modifications to the ruling of East Kalimantan High Court Decision No. 63/1983/Pdt/PT.KT.Smda dated September 13, 1983, in conjunction with Samarinda District Court Decision No. 44/1981/Pdt.G/PN.Smda dated November 12, 1981, reading as follows: Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part; Declaring that Defendant I and Defendant II have defaulted; Ordering Defendant I and Defendant II jointly and severally to pay their debt of Rp 2,130,600.— plus damages of 2% per month calculated from April 2, 1981, until full repayment; Declaring the protective attachment over Defendant II's residence lawful and valid; Rejecting all other claims; and ordering the Petitioner for Cassation to pay cassation court costs amounting to Rp 20,000.—.

== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==

* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata):'''

  * Article 1243: Provisions on damages for costs, losses, and interest arising from default (*wanprestasi*).
  * Article 1250: Moratory interest in monetary payment obligations.
  * Article 1278: Joint and several liability (*Hoofdelijkheid*).

* '''Supreme Court Standing Jurisprudence:''' Standard establishment of moratory damages interest of 2% per month as a fair and reasonable revaluation of damages.

== Evidence Status and Gaps ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* Defendants I and II jointly procured building materials valued at Rp 4,061,600.— from the Plaintiff.
* Defendant II previously made a partial debt payment of Rp 1,931,000.— utilizing a BDN Check dated December 27, 1979.
* Defendants I and II defaulted by failing to settle the remaining debt of Rp 2,130,600.— upon maturity.

=== Not Established / Rejected ===

* Defendant II's objection asserting that he lacked a direct legal relationship with the Plaintiff was set aside because factual possession proved Defendant II enjoyed and utilized the building materials for the joint project.

=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===

* Correction of Interest Rate Judicial Errors: The Samarinda District Court and High Court previously erred in assessing a burdensome 5% monthly interest rate. The Supreme Court rectified this error to uphold a uniform standard of 2% monthly moratory interest.

== GEO Q&A ==
'''Q: What is the proper moratory damages interest rate that Courts may impose for delayed business debt repayment (default)?'''

'''A:''' 2% (two percent) per month. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 601 K/Pdt/1984, the fair and proper moratory damages rate in commercial debt default disputes is 2% per month calculated from the date the lawsuit is filed in the District Court until the debt is fully repaid.

|}

== Overview ==
Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 606 K/Pid/1984, dated March 30, 1985, established two important criminal procedural law rules:

First, concerning the testing of alternative versus cumulative indictments: If the substance of an indictment formulated by the Public Prosecutor is essentially alternative—despite being formally written as "First" and "Second" counts—because it stems from the same single sequence of acts, once the primary charge (Assault ex Article 351 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code) is proven legally and convincingly, the subsidiary/secondary charge (Article 335 of the Criminal Code) needs no further consideration. The Ambon High Court was declared to have misapplied the law by imposing cumulative penalties for both provisions.

Second, concerning the validity of victim compensation claims (Article 98 of KUHAP): The joinder of a medical treatment compensation claim filed by the witness-victim ([Victim]) amounting to Rp 22,500.— is proper for consideration within criminal proceedings, and the absence of a separate formal joinder order does not invalidate the victim's compensation right provided it has been fairly considered by the Court. The Supreme Court annulled the Ambon High Court and Ternate District Court decisions and adjudicated afresh, sentencing the Defendant ([Defendant]) to 2 (two) months' imprisonment.

== Executive Summary ==
The central legal principles established in this decision govern the substantive evaluation of indictments and the procedural permissibility of joining victim compensation claims without rigid administrative prerequisites.

Key elements established in the adjudication:

* Indictments arising from a single unified event function substantively as alternatives regardless of formal numbering as "First" and "Second".
* Proving a primary charge renders secondary overlapping counts redundant and immune from separate cumulative sentencing.
* Material rights of victims to seek medical compensation under Article 98 of KUHAP are upheld even without prior separate administrative joinder rulings, provided claims are verified.

== Case Background ==
The Original Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation, '''[Defendant]''' ([age removed], store employee), was charged with Assault (Article 351 paragraph 1 KUHP / First Count) or Unpleasant Acts with Violence (Article 335 paragraph 1 KUHP / Second Count) against the witness-victim, '''[Victim]''', in Ternate on May 8, 1983. The Defendant had recorded a conversation without permission and engaged in a struggle, causing the victim to sustain neck muscle contusions. The witness-victim filed a compensation claim for medical expenses amounting to Rp 22,500.—.

The Ternate District Court (Decision No. 67/Pen.Pid.B/1983/P.N.Tte dated January 16, 1984) sentenced the Defendant to 3 months' imprisonment with a 6-month probation period and ordered the payment of Rp 22,500.— in compensation. The Ambon High Court (Decision No. 05/Pid/1984/P.T.Mal dated March 14, 1984) annulled the Ternate District Court decision and sentenced the Defendant cumulatively on both the First and Second counts to 2 months and 15 days' imprisonment. The Petitioner for Cassation subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Claims, Evidence and Source Mapping ==
{| class="wikitable"
!No.
!Legal Statement / Fact
!Evidence / Judicial Consideration
!Source
|-
|'''1'''
|'''Primary Legal Principle (Alternative Indictment):''' An indictment is alternative despite being written as First and Second; if the primary charge is proven, the subsidiary charge needs no further consideration.
|Supreme Court considerations pages 43, 47: "...the High Court misapplied the law by holding that the indictment charged against the defendant was cumulative whereas the substance of the indictment turned out to be alternative, although written as First and Second because the crime charged was the same... the subsidiary charge need no longer be considered;"
|606K_PID_1984.pdf, Passages 1 and 5
|-
|'''2'''
|'''Primary Legal Principle (Victim Compensation ex Article 98 KUHAP):''' Joinder of criminal victim compensation is proper for consideration without requiring a separate joinder ruling if already considered.
|Supreme Court consideration page 48: "...although in this case there was no joinder ruling between the (petitioner's) compensation claim and the criminal case, because it has been considered... such petition is proper to be granted;"
|606K_PID_1984.pdf, Passage 6
|-
|'''3'''
|'''Facts of Victim Assault:''' The Defendant ([Defendant]) held the arm, lifted the chin, and broke the neck of the victim ([Victim]) causing him to fall backward with neck muscle contusions.
|Posita of Indictment & Visum et Repertum dated May 10, 1983, pages 43, 44, and 54: Victim suffered neck muscle contusion injuries from blunt force trauma resulting in 5–7 days of work incapacity.
|606K_PID_1984.pdf, Passages 1, 2, and 12
|-
|'''4'''
|'''Tape Recorder Tug-of-War Incident:''' The fight was triggered by the Defendant recording conversations regarding the revocation of house sales without the witness-victim's permission.
|Witness & Defendant testimonies pages 44, 45, and 55: Tug-of-war over a black Sony tape recorder between the Defendant and the witness-victim.
|606K_PID_1984.pdf, Passages 2, 3, and 13
|-
|'''5'''

|606K_PID_1984.pdf, Passages 1, 8, and 11
|-

|Supreme Court Cassation Ruling pages 48 and 49: "Sentencing the defendant to a prison term of 2 (two) months... Granting the compensation petition/lawsuit of the witness... amounting to Rp 22,500.—"
|606K_PID_1984.pdf, Passages 6 and 7
|}

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==

=== Interpretation of Formal vs. Substantive Nature of Indictments (Alternative vs. Cumulative) ===
The primary issue was whether an indictment structured with numbering "First" and "Second" permits a High Court to convict a Defendant cumulatively under Article 351 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code and Article 335 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code when the material facts described originate from a single unified act (a tape recorder tug-of-war causing injury).

The Supreme Court held that it does not. The substantive nature of an indictment is determined by the substance of the acts charged (*material*), rather than solely by textual numbering (*formal*). Because the sequence of acts was essentially the same, the indictment was alternative. When the primary charge (Assault ex Article 351 paragraph (1) KUHP) is proven legally and convincingly, the court must not examine or impose cumulative penalties on the secondary charge (Article 335 paragraph (1) KUHP).

=== Procedure for Joining Criminal Victim Compensation Claims (Article 98 of KUHAP) ===
The issue evaluated whether a medical expense compensation claim filed by a criminal victim can be granted by the Supreme Court even if the First-Instance Judge failed to issue a specific administrative joinder ruling order.

The Supreme Court held that it can be granted. The absence of a separate formal administrative joinder ruling does not invalidate the material rights of a criminal victim under Article 98 of KUHAP, provided that reasonable medical receipts (amounting to Rp 22,500.—) have been examined, verified, and weighed during trial proceedings by the *Judex Facti*.

== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===
'''Question:'''

Did the Ambon High Court misapply criminal procedural law (*foutieve kepassing van het procesrecht*) by treating an alternative indictment as a cumulative indictment and imposing double punishment under both Article 351 (1) and Article 335 (1) of the Criminal Code?

'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''

Yes, the Ambon High Court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court annulled Ambon High Court Decision No. 05/Pid/1984/P.T.Mal and Ternate District Court Decision No. 67/Pen.Pid.B/1983/P.N.Tte, and adjudicated afresh by convicting the Defendant solely of Assault (Article 351 paragraph 1 KUHP) with a sentence of 2 months' imprisonment.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Ternate District Court & Ambon High Court) ===
Examination of the facts surrounding the physical struggle at witness-victim [Victim]'s residence on May 8, 1983, at 20:30 WIT, the Doctor's Visum et Repertum dated May 10, 1983 (neck muscle contusions), medical examination and medication receipts totaling Rp 22,500.—, and the return of evidence comprising 1 Sony tape recorder and audio cassettes to the Defendant.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The appellate *Judex Facti* of Ambon High Court misapplied the law. The High Court treated the indictment as cumulative, whereas its substance was alternative (despite being written as First and Second counts) because the underlying criminal events were identical.
# Once the primary charge (Assault ex Article 351 paragraph 1 KUHP) was proven, the subsidiary charge (Article 335 KUHP) required no further consideration.
# Regarding victim compensation, although no separate joinder order was issued, the medical compensation claim of Rp 22,500.— filed under Article 98 of KUHAP was valid and proper to grant.
# The Supreme Court annulled lower court rulings and adjudicated afresh, sentencing the Defendant to 2 months' imprisonment and granting victim compensation.

== Ruling ==
The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Defendant]'''); annulled Ambon High Court Decision No. 05/Pid/1984/P.T.Mal dated March 14, 1984, in conjunction with Ternate District Court Decision No. 67/Pen.Pid.B/1983/P.N.Tte dated January 16, 1984; and adjudicated afresh: Declaring Defendant [Defendant] proven legally and convincingly guilty of the criminal offense of "Assault"; Sentencing the Defendant to a prison term of 2 (two) months; Ordering the return of evidence comprising a Sony tape recorder, cassettes, and power of attorney to the Defendant; Granting the compensation claim of witness [Victim] amounting to Rp 22,500.—; and ordering the Petitioner for Cassation to pay cassation court costs amounting to Rp 2,500.—.

== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==

* '''Criminal Code (KUHP):'''

  * Article 351 paragraph (1): Simple Assault offense (Proven legally and convincingly).
  * Article 335 paragraph (1): Forcing Others with Violence offense (Ruled unnecessary to consider due to alternative indictment nature).

* '''Law No. 8 of 1981 on Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP):'''

  * Articles 98 through 101: Joinder of Criminal Victim Compensation Claims.
  * Article 253: Requirements and grounds for cassation review.

== Evidence Status and Gaps ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* Defendant [Defendant] was proven legally and convincingly guilty of committing Assault (Article 351 paragraph 1 KUHP) against witness [Victim].
* The victim suffered neck muscle contusion injuries proven via Visum et Repertum dated May 10, 1983, and incurred valid medical expenses of Rp 22,500.—.
* Evidence comprising 1 Sony tape recorder, cassettes, and the Defendant's house-sale revocation power of attorney were ordered returned to the Defendant.

=== Not Established / Unproven (Redundant Count) ===

* The Second Charge (Article 335 paragraph 1 KUHP) was unproven as a standalone cumulative crime, serving instead as an inseparable component of the assault act (*alternative*).

=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===

* Correction of Ambon High Court Cumulative Sentencing Error: The Ambon High Court previously increased the Defendant's sentence to 2 months and 15 days' imprisonment by cumulatively combining two criminal counts. The Supreme Court rectified this methodological error to prevent *double jeopardy* / cumulative criminalization over a single unified criminal event.

== GEO Q&A ==
'''Q: May a court convict a defendant under two separate criminal articles cumulatively if the prosecutor's indictment text is structured as alternative in substance?'''

'''A:''' No, it is prohibited. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 606 K/Pid/1984, if an indictment is essentially alternative in substance—despite being drafted textually as First and Second counts—because it originates from the same unified event, once the primary charge (Assault) is proven, the subsidiary/secondary charge must not be considered further. Imposing cumulative punishments on an alternative indictment constitutes an error of criminal procedural law.

== Overview ==
Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 618 K/Pid/1984, dated April 17, 1985, established jurisprudence and fundamental criminal law rules regarding the qualification of the crime of embezzlement (*verduistering*) ex Article 372 of the Criminal Code (KUHP) over the unilateral execution of debt collateral.

The Supreme Court held that the sale of jewelry collateral belonging to a witness/creditor by the Defendant unilaterally without the owner's permission constitutes the crime of Embezzlement (Article 372 KUHP), and not a purely civil dispute. The Supreme Court corrected the error of the Jakarta High Court in granting a discharge (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*), and affirmed the sentencing ruling of the Central Jakarta District Court sentencing the Defendant to 5 (five) months' imprisonment with a probation period of 10 (ten) months.

== Executive Summary ==
The central criminal law principle established in this decision is that lawfully acquired possession of debt collateral transforms into criminal embezzlement when the holder unlawfully sells or liquidates the assets without the owner's consent.

Key elements established in the adjudication:

* Unilateral disposal of debtor property pledged as security constitutes criminal embezzlement (*Article 372 KUHP*), overriding arguments of purely civil disputes.
* Initial lawful possession (*rechtmatig bezit*) converts into unlawful appropriation (*wederrechtelijke toe-eigening*) upon unauthorized sale.
* Appellate court discharges (*ontslag*) of creditors misusing collateral are subject to reversal and conviction on cassation.

== Case Background ==
The Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation, '''Ny. [Defendant]''' ([age removed], housewife), was charged with embezzlement (Article 372 KUHP) for selling three pieces of diamond-studded gold/platinum jewelry belonging to the witness, '''Ny. C. Sihombing Sitompul''', at Senen Market for Rp 1,500,000.— without the witness's permission. The jewelry had been handed over by the witness as security for a loan of Rp 1,300,000.— on September 21, 1979.

The Central Jakarta District Court (Decision No. 22/1983/Pid/Biasa dated November 22, 1983) convicted the Defendant and sentenced her to 5 months' imprisonment with 10 months' probation. The Jakarta High Court (Decision No. 10/Pid/1984 P.T. DKI dated March 22, 1984) annulled the district court decision and discharged the Defendant from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag*) on the grounds that the matter was purely civil. The Public Prosecutor at the Central Jakarta State Prosecutor's Office subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Claims, Evidence and Source Mapping ==
{| class="wikitable"
!No.
!Legal Statement / Fact
!Evidence / Judicial Consideration
!Source

|Supreme Court Jurisprudence Headnote & Considerations pages 1, 4: "The sale of collateral items belonging to the witness by the defendant without the witness's permission constitutes embezzlement."
|618K_PID_1984.pdf, Passages 1 and 4
|-
|'''2'''
|'''Collateral Possession & Sale Facts:''' The Defendant received 3 jewelry pieces (platinum diamond earrings, platinum diamond eternity ring, platinum diamond pendant) as loan collateral of Rp 1,300,000.— and sold them at Senen Market for Rp 1,500,000.— without the witness's permission.
|Posita of Prosecutor's Indictment & District Court considerations pages 1, 11, and 15: "...the defendant sold those items to several unknown persons at Senen Market without permission from the witness for a total price of Rp 1,500,000.—"
|618K_PID_1984.pdf, Passages 1, 2, 11, and 15
|-
|'''3'''

|Jakarta High Court considerations pages 2, 8 & Supreme Court considerations pages 3, 4: The Supreme Court evaluated that the Public Prosecutor's objection was justified because the Defendant's action met the elements of Article 372 KUHP.
|618K_PID_1984.pdf, Passages 2, 3, 4, and 8
|-
|'''4'''
|'''Cassation Sentencing Ruling:''' The Supreme Court annulled the Jakarta High Court decision and Adjudicated Afresh, sentencing the Defendant to 5 months' imprisonment with 10 months' probation.
|Supreme Court Cassation Ruling page 4: "Granting the cassation petition... Annulling the Jakarta High Court decision... Sentencing the defendant therefore to a prison term of 5 (five) months... probation for 10 (ten) months."
|618K_PID_1984.pdf, Passage 4
|-
|'''5'''

|Expressly stated in decision identity pages 1, 6, 10, and 16.
|618K_PID_1984.pdf, Passages 1, 6, 10, and 16
|}

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==

=== Transformation of Lawful Possession into Unlawful Appropriation (Wederrechtelijke Toe-Eigening) ex Article 372 KUHP ===
The primary issue was whether a recipient of debt collateral who lawfully possesses debtor jewelry (because it was handed over as security) can be criminally prosecuted for embezzlement if they sell the collateral without the owner's permission or agreement.

The Supreme Court held that they can be penalized. Initial lawful possession (*rechtmatig bezit*) of collateral transforms into the crime of embezzlement (*verduistering*) at the moment the Defendant executes an unauthorized transfer or sale without the owner's consent (unlawful appropriation).

=== Boundaries Separating Civil Legal Relations and the Criminal Offense of Embezzlement ===
The Jakarta High Court previously erred by assuming that the existence of an underlying loan-debt relationship extinguished criminal qualification. The Supreme Court corrected this by ruling that breaching the obligation to safeguard collateral by unlawfully selling it transcends civil dispute and satisfies all criminal elements of Article 372 of the Criminal Code.

== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===
'''Question:'''

Did the Jakarta High Court misapply the law (*foutieve kepassing van het recht*) by discharging the Defendant from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*) by characterizing unauthorized collateral sales as purely civil matters?

'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''

Yes, the Jakarta High Court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court annulled the Jakarta High Court decision and adjudicated afresh, declaring the Defendant proven guilty of the crime of Embezzlement (Article 372 KUHP).

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Central Jakarta District Court & Jakarta High Court) ===
Examination of facts regarding the handover of three types of diamond-studded gold/platinum jewelry belonging to witness Ny. C. Sihombing Sitompul to the Defendant on September 21, 1979, as loan collateral for Rp 1,300,000.—, issuance of a warning letter on December 15, 1981, sale of jewelry at Senen/Inpres Market in June 1982 for Rp 1,500,000.—, and failure to return the remaining cash balance of Rp 200,000.— to the witness owner.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The appellate *Judex Facti* of Jakarta High Court misapplied the law. The sale of the witness's collateral items by the Defendant without the witness's permission constitutes an act of intentionally and unlawfully appropriating property in one's possession other than through crime.
# This action satisfies all elements of the crime of Embezzlement as regulated and punishable under Article 372 of the Criminal Code.
# The Supreme Court annulled the Jakarta High Court decision and adjudicated afresh, sentencing the Defendant to 5 months' imprisonment with 10 months' probation.

== Ruling ==
The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation ('''Public Prosecutor at the Central Jakarta State Prosecutor's Office'''); annulled Jakarta High Court Decision No. 10/Pid/1984/P.T. DKI dated March 22, 1984; and adjudicated afresh: Declaring Defendant Ny. [Defendant] guilty of committing the crime of "Embezzlement"; Sentencing the Defendant to a prison term of 5 (five) months; Stipulating that the sentence need not be served unless a subsequent judge's order dictates otherwise on the grounds that the convict prior to the expiration of the 10 (ten) month probation period has committed a criminal offense; Ordering evidence documents to remain attached to the case file; and ordering the Respondent for Cassation to pay cassation court costs amounting to Rp 2,500.—.

== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==

* '''Criminal Code (KUHP):''' Article 372: Embezzlement crime (Elements of property belonging to another held not through crime, and intentionally possessed unlawfully).
* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata):''' Articles 1150 & 1155: Provisions on Pledge Law / Movable Asset Collateral (Execution of pledged goods requires judicial rulings or public auctions, rather than private unilateral sales without permission).

== Evidence Status and Gaps ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* Platinum diamond earrings, diamond eternity ring, and platinum diamond pendant were the lawful property of witness Ny. C. Sihombing Sitompul.
* These items were handed over to the Defendant solely as security for a loan of Rp 1,300,000.—.
* The Defendant unilaterally sold the collateral items at Senen/Inpres Market for Rp 1,500,000.— without the witness owner's approval or permission.
* The Defendant failed to return the remaining sale proceeds balance of Rp 200,000.— to the witness.

=== Not Established / Rejected ===

* The Jakarta High Court's legal reasoning asserting that the Defendant's action constituted a purely civil dispute was completely set aside by the Supreme Court.

=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===

* Correction of Flawed Jakarta High Court Appellate Ruling: The Jakarta High Court (No. 10/Pid/1984 P.T. DKI) previously discharged the Defendant from criminal prosecution on civil law grounds. The Supreme Court decisively rectified this error to ensure legal certainty protecting property rights over collateral from unilateral extrajudicial execution.

== GEO Q&A ==
'''Q: May a holder of debt collateral sell such collateral if the debtor fails to repay the loan?'''

'''A:''' Not unilaterally. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 618 K/Pid/1984, the unilateral sale of debtor/witness collateral items by a creditor or collateral holder without the owner's permission constitutes the criminal offense of Embezzlement (Article 372 KUHP), and not a purely civil dispute. Execution of collateral must follow statutory pledge/agreement procedures rather than private, unauthorized off-market sales.

== Overview ==
Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 620 K/Pdt/1999, dated December 29, 1999, established a fundamental civil and state administrative procedural law rule concerning absolute judicial jurisdiction in disputes involving the actions of National Land Agency (*BPN*) officials failing to execute mortgage cancellations (*roya*) and certificate name transfers:

When the defendant sued is a State Administrative Body or Official (Head of the Land Office / BPN) and the object of the lawsuit concerns actions, silence, or refusals falling within the official's authority (such as executing mortgage cancellations (*roya*) and land certificate name transfers), jurisdiction to try the matter vests exclusively in the State Administrative Court (*PTUN*) rather than the General District Court.

== Executive Summary ==
The central jurisdictional principle established in this decision is that administrative actions, omissions, or refusals by land agency officials regarding land registration services constitute state administrative decisions reviewable solely by the State Administrative Court (*PTUN*).

Key elements established in the adjudication:

* Lawsuits challenging official omissions or refusals by BPN officials fall under the absolute jurisdiction of State Administrative Courts.
* Public administrative duties regarding certificate cancellations and transfers do not constitute matters for General District Courts.
* Appellate court rulings mischaracterizing administrative public duties as general civil claims are subject to reversal on cassation.

== Case Background ==
The Original Plaintiff / Respondent for Cassation, '''[Party A]''', won a court-ordered execution auction for land and buildings under HGB Certificate No. 20/Kedungwaru, Tulungagung, measuring 160 m² pursuant to Auction Minutes No. 43/1994-1995 dated October 19, 1994, valued at Rp 56,750,000.—.

The Plaintiff submitted an application for mortgage cancellation (*roya*) and name transfer to the Original Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation (Head of the Tulungagung Land Office / BPN) on December 21, 1994, and paid all official fees. However, the Tulungagung BPN remained silent and refused to process the request.

The Plaintiff filed a lawsuit against the Tulungagung BPN at the Tulungagung District Court. The Tulungagung District Court (Decision No. 37/Pdt.G/1996/PN.Ta. dated April 15, 1997) granted the Defendant's exception and declared that the District Court lacked absolute jurisdiction. The Surabaya High Court (Decision No. 767/PDT/1997/PT.SBY dated March 12, 1998) annulled the district court decision and ruled that the District Court possessed jurisdiction to hear the case. The Petitioner for Cassation subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Claims, Evidence and Source Mapping ==

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==

=== Absolute Jurisdiction in BPN Service Disputes ===
The primary issue was whether a lawsuit filed by an auction purchaser against the Head of the Land Office (*BPN*) refusing or unwilling to process applications for mortgage cancellations (*roya*) and certificate name transfers falls under the authority of the General District Court or the State Administrative Court (*PTUN*).

The Supreme Court held that it falls under the authority of the State Administrative Court (*PTUN*). BPN officials failing to execute *roya* and name transfer applications—even when originating from judicial execution auction minutes—constitute public administrative duties. Official silence or refusal qualifies as a Negative Fictitious Decision (State Administrative Decision) ex Article 3 paragraphs (1) and (3) in conjunction with Article 1 number 5 of Law No. 5 of 1986. Consequently, the dispute is subject to the absolute jurisdiction of *PTUN*, and General District Courts lack jurisdiction to adjudicate.

=== Review of State Administrative Dispute Exceptions ex Article 2 letter e of Law No. 5 of 1986 ===
The Surabaya High Court previously erred by treating name transfer services for judicial execution auction results as "judicial/executive execution actions" excluded from *PTUN*. The Supreme Court corrected this, clarifying that name transfer and *roya* cancellation applications in BPN land registries constitute pure public administrative legal actions distinct from judicial auction proceedings, thereby falling outside the exclusions under Article 2 letter e of Law No. 5 of 1986.

== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===
'''Question:'''

Did the Surabaya High Court misapply the law (*foutieve kepassing van het recht*) by ignoring absolute jurisdictional boundaries and declaring that the General District Court had authority to try a lawsuit challenging BPN official actions?

'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''

Yes, the Surabaya High Court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation (Head of Tulungagung BPN), annulled Surabaya High Court Decision No. 767/PDT/1997/PT.SBY, and adjudicated afresh by sustaining the absolute jurisdiction exception and declaring that the Tulungagung District Court lacked authority to try the case.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Tulungagung District Court & Surabaya High Court) ===
Examination of facts concerning the auction purchase of HGB Certificate No. 20/Kedungwaru, Tulungagung, measuring 160 m² in the name of Pujo Basuki on October 19, 1994 (Auction Minutes No. 43/1994-1995), submission of *roya* and name transfer applications on December 21, 1994 (Registration Form 305/1994 No. 3608), Deutsche Bank AG *Roya* Statement Letter No. 1630/94/cbd/kd dated December 26, 1994, and Tulungagung District Court Evacuation Minutes No. 13/Pdt.Plks/1994/PN.Ta. dated July 24, 1995.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''

# The appellate *Judex Facti* of Surabaya High Court misapplied the law in its legal reasoning. The Plaintiff's original lawsuit was essentially directed against a State Administrative Body or Official (Tulungagung BPN), with the object of lawsuit concerning official actions/omissions falling within that official's authority (refusal/silence regarding *roya* and certificate name transfers).
# BPN's actions met the criteria for a Negative Fictitious Decision ex Article 3 paragraphs (1) and (3) jo. Article 1 number 5 of Law No. 5 of 1986.
# Therefore, jurisdiction to try the case rested with the State Administrative Court (*PTUN*), not the General District Court.
# The Supreme Court annulled the Surabaya High Court decision and adjudicated afresh, affirming the Tulungagung District Court's ruling that the District Court lacked jurisdiction.

== Ruling ==
The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation ('''MINISTER OF AGRARIA / HEAD OF BPN IN JAKARTA cq. EAST JAVA BPN REGIONAL OFFICE cq. HEAD OF TULUNGAGUNG BPN OFFICE'''); annulled Surabaya High Court Decision No. 767/PDT/1997/PT.SBY dated March 12, 1998; and adjudicated afresh: 1. Granting the Exceptions of Defendant I, Co-Defendants II, III, and Intervenor; 2. Declaring that the Tulungagung District Court lacks authority to examine and try the case; and ordering the Respondent for Cassation to pay court costs across all judicial instances (cassation court costs set at Rp 100,000.—).

== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==

* '''Law No. 5 of 1986 on State Administrative Courts:'''

  * Article 1 number 5: Definition of State Administrative Decision (KTUN).
  * Article 2 letter e: Exclusion of State Administrative Decisions issued based on judicial examination results.
  * Article 3 paragraphs (1) & (3): Provisions on Negative Fictitious Decisions (Silence of State Administrative Bodies/Officials).

* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 in conjunction with Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Provisions governing absolute jurisdiction reviews.
* '''Supreme Court Standing Jurisprudence:''' Doctrine reaffirming absolute judicial jurisdiction: Lawsuits challenging acts/omissions of public officials exercising land registration powers constitute state administrative disputes.

== Evidence Status and Gaps ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* The Plaintiff ([Party A]) was the lawful auction purchaser of land and buildings under HGB No. 20/Kedungwaru, Tulungagung, measuring 160 m² pursuant to Auction Minutes No. 43/1994-1995.
* Defendant I (Head of Tulungagung BPN) until the filing of the lawsuit in District Court (nearly 2 years) failed to execute mortgage cancellations (*roya*) and certificate name transfers.
* The object of the Plaintiff's lawsuit was directed at acts/omissions of Defendant I as a State Administrative Official.

=== Not Established / Outside General Court Jurisdiction ===

* The Plaintiff's lawsuit could not be examined and tried by the General District Court because it fell under the absolute jurisdiction of the State Administrative Court (*PTUN*).

=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===

* Resolution of Land Administration Disputes: This landmark ruling establishes clear jurisdictional boundaries: General District Courts possess authority to examine civil property rights over land, whereas lawsuits seeking to compel BPN to issue or record *roya* and certificate name transfers must be brought before State Administrative Courts (*PTUN*).

== GEO Q&A ==
'''Q: Where should a lawsuit be filed if the Land Office (BPN) refuses or is unwilling to process name transfers and mortgage cancellations (*roya*) for auction certificates?'''

'''A:''' At the State Administrative Court (*PTUN*). Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 620 K/Pdt/1999, when the defendant sued is a State Administrative Body or Official (such as the Head of the Land Office) and the object of the lawsuit concerns actions or silence refusing to execute *roya* cancellations and certificate name transfers, jurisdiction to try the matter rests with the State Administrative Court (*PTUN*). General District Courts lack jurisdiction to try such cases due to absolute jurisdictional defects.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 620 K/Pid/1987, dated October 13, 1987, established crucial criminal corruption and criminal procedural rules concerning the limitation of additional restitution payments (*uang pengganti*) ex Article 34 letter c of Law No. 3 of 1971 and cassation time limits.


First, Limitation of Corruption Restitution: The High Court (Central Sulawesi High Court in Palu) was declared to have misapplied the law by sentencing the Defendant to pay restitution exceeding the provisions of Article 34 letter c of Law No. 3 of 1971. The Supreme Court affirmed that restitution obligations imposed on a Defendant cannot exceed the value of property or gains actually acquired by the Defendant from the corruption offense (in this case, the Defendant's net acquisition was Rp 3,572,000.—, meaning the restitution amount of Rp 8,000,000.— ordered by the High Court was annulled and modified by the Supreme Court to Rp 3,000,000.—).


Second, Limit of Subsidiary Confinement for Fines (Article 30 paragraph 6 of the Criminal Code): Subsidiary confinement for fines cumulatively cannot exceed 8 (eight) months.


Third, Late Prosecutor's Cassation Memorandum (Article 248 paragraph 1 of the KUHAP): The cassation petition of the Public Prosecutor at the Donggala State Prosecutor's Office was declared inadmissible because the cassation memorandum was submitted past the 14-day time limit from the registration of the cassation petition.


== Executive Summary ==


The central legal principle established in this decision is that additional restitution (*uang pengganti*) in corruption cases must strictly reflect the actual unlawful financial gains received by the perpetrator, and procedural deadlines for filing cassation memorandums are absolute.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Restitution penalties cannot legally exceed the proven net proceeds acquired by the defendant from corrupt activities.
* Cumulative subsidiary confinement terms for unpaid fines are legally capped under the Criminal Code.
* Public prosecutors missing statutory 14-day filing windows for cassation memorandums suffer dismissal of their appeals as inadmissible.


== Case Background ==


The Defendant, '''[Defendant]''' ([age removed], Donggala Public Works employee / Technical Supervisor for Inpres Elementary School Project Unit I No. 5/1981 in Damsol District), was charged with continuous corruption and bribery (Article 1 paragraph 1 sub b / Subsidiary & sub c of Law No. 3 of 1971 jo. Articles 55, 64 of the Criminal Code) in the construction project of SD Inpres Unit I Sampaga and Ogoamas Teacher's Official Residence for Fiscal Year 1981/1982 in Damsol District. The Defendant acted as technical supervisor while executing the project unilaterally under company names CV Sinjai Putra and CV Setia Abadi, and fabricated physical progress reports for 100% disbursement when physical construction was only 53.39% and 0% complete. 


The Palu District Court (Decision No. 42/Pid/B/1984/PN. Dgl. dated May 13, 1985) sentenced the Defendant to 5 months' imprisonment and a Rp 6,000.— fine. The Central Sulawesi High Court in Palu (Decision No. 10/PID/B/1986/PT. Palu dated August 20, 1986) modified the sentence to 2 years' imprisonment, a Rp 3,000,000.— fine (subsidiary 6 months' confinement), and Restitution (*Uang Pengganti*) of Rp 8,000,000.— (subsidiary 6 months' confinement). Both the Public Prosecutor at the Donggala State Prosecutor's Office and the Defendant filed cassation petitions with the Supreme Court.


== Claims, Evidence and Source Mapping ==

| Jurisprudence Headnote & Supreme Court considerations pages 184, 192: "The High Court has misapplied the law by deciding to sentence the defendant to pay restitution not in accordance with the provisions of article 34.c of Law No. 3 of 1971 because restitution that may be obligated upon the defendant to pay must not exceed property acquired from corruption."

| Supreme Court considerations page 193: "...the amount acquired by the defendant from the criminal offense of corruption is Rp. 3,252,000.— + Rp. 320,000.— = Rp. 3,572,000.—"

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Maximum Limit of Additional Restitution Penalties ex Article 34 letter c of Law No. 3 of 1971 ===


The primary issue was the maximum amount of additional Restitution (*Uang Pengganti*) penalties that may be imposed upon a convicted corruption offender.


The Supreme Court held that the Central Sulawesi High Court in Palu misapplied the law. Pursuant to Article 34 letter c of Law No. 3 of 1971, additional restitution obligations imposed on a Defendant cannot exceed the value of property or gains actually acquired by the Defendant from the corruption offense. Imposing Rp 8,000,000.— in restitution when the Defendant's actual gain was only Rp 3,572,000.— constituted a legal defect. The Supreme Court corrected the restitution amount to Rp 3,000,000.— subsidiary to 3 months' confinement.


=== Maximum Limit of Subsidiary Confinement for Fines ex Article 30 Paragraph (6) of the Criminal Code ===


The *Judex Facti* of Palu High Court violated substantive law by imposing cumulative subsidiary fine confinements totaling 12 months (6 months + 6 months). Article 30 paragraph (6) of the Criminal Code strictly caps subsidiary fine confinement at a maximum of 8 (eight) months.


=== Lapses in Cassation Rights Due to Late Submission of Cassation Memorandums (Article 248 Paragraph 1 KUHAP) ===


When a Petitioner for Cassation (Public Prosecutor) submits a cassation memorandum beyond the 14-day statutory limit from the date the cassation petition is registered, pursuant to Article 248 paragraph (4) of the KUHAP, the right to appeal via cassation lapses and the petition must be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard*).


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the Palu High Court misapply the law (*foutieve kepassing van het recht*) by imposing Rp 8,000,000.— in restitution exceeding the Defendant's corruption proceeds (Rp 3,572,000.—) in violation of Article 34c of Law No. 3/1971, and imposing 12 months' cumulative subsidiary fine confinement in violation of Article 30(6) of the Criminal Code?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the Palu High Court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court annulled Palu High Court Decision No. 10/PID/B/1986/PT. Palu and adjudicated afresh, sentencing the Defendant to 1 year's imprisonment, a Rp 2,000,000.— fine (subsidiary 2 months' confinement), and Restitution of Rp 3,000,000.— (subsidiary 3 months' confinement).


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Palu District Court & Palu High Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning the appointment of [Defendant] as technical supervisor for the SD Inpres No. 5/1981 project in Damsol District, unilateral execution of projects utilizing CV Sinjai Putra and CV Setia Abadi, creation of fictitious physical progress reports, fund disbursement from BRI Palu Branch, and receipt of gratuities/gifts from contractors.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The Public Prosecutor's cassation petition is inadmissible because the memorandum was filed exceeding the 14-day time limit ex Article 248 paragraph (1) of the KUHAP.
# Regarding the Defendant's cassation appeal, the Palu High Court misapplied the law by sentencing the Defendant to pay Rp 8,000,000.— in restitution, exceeding the actual financial gains acquired from corruption (Rp 3,572,000.—). Pursuant to Article 34 letter c of Law No. 3 of 1971, restitution cannot exceed property acquired from corruption. Furthermore, cumulative subsidiary fine confinement violated Article 30(6) KUHP.
# The Supreme Court annulled the Palu High Court decision and adjudicated afresh, sentencing the Defendant to 1 year's imprisonment, a Rp 2,000,000.— fine (subsidiary 2 months), and Restitution of Rp 3,000,000.— (subsidiary 3 months).


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court ruled: 1. Declaring the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation / Public Prosecutor at Donggala State Prosecutor's Office inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard*); 2. Annulling Central Sulawesi High Court in Palu Decision No. 10/PID/B/1986/PT. PALU dated August 20, 1986; 3. Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation / Defendant ('''[Defendant]'''); and adjudicating afresh: Declaring Defendant [Defendant] proven legally and convincingly guilty of committing "Continuous Corruption"; Sentencing the Defendant to a prison term of 1 (one) year; Sentencing the Defendant to a fine of Rp 2,000,000.— subsidiary to 2 (two) months' confinement; Sentencing the Defendant to pay Restitution (*Uang Pengganti*) of Rp 3,000,000.— subsidiary to 3 (three) months' confinement; Deducting the full period of detention already served; and charging court costs.


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Law No. 3 of 1971 on Eradication of Corruption Offenses:''' Articles 1 paragraph 1 sub b, 1 paragraph 1 sub c (Article 418 KUHP), 28, and 34 letter c.
* '''Criminal Code (KUHP):''' Articles 30 paragraph (6) (Maximum Subsidiary Confinement Limit), 55 paragraph (1) 1st, and 64 (Continuous Offenses).
* '''Law No. 8 of 1981 on Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP):''' Articles 248 paragraphs (1) & (4) (14-day time limit for cassation memorandums).


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* Defendant [Defendant] was proven legally and convincingly guilty of committing corruption repeatedly as a continuous offense.
* Actual material gains acquired by the Defendant from corrupt activities amounted to Rp 3,572,000.—.
* The Public Prosecutor's cassation memorandum was submitted past the 14-day time limit, rendering the Prosecutor's appeal inadmissible.


=== Not Established / Modified on Cassation ===


* The prosecution failed to prove that the Defendant acquired Rp 8,000,000.— in proceeds from corruption, leading to the judicial reduction of the restitution penalty by the Supreme Court.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Restorative-Reparative Nature of Corruption Restitution: This landmark ruling establishes the fundamental special criminal law principle that Restitution (*Uang Pengganti*) is a state financial loss recovery instrument (*restitutive*) matching the perpetrator's actual material gain, rather than an arbitrary punitive fine or penalization exceeding proven financial gains.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: What is the maximum limit of additional Restitution (*Uang Pengganti*) penalties that a Judge may impose on a Convicted Corruption Offender under Law No. 3 of 1971?'''


'''A:''' A maximum equivalent to the value of property or financial gains actually acquired by the Convicted Offender from corruption. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 620 K/Pid/1987, additional restitution penalties ex Article 34 letter c of Law No. 3 of 1971 must not exceed the sum of money or property value genuinely acquired by the Offender from corrupt acts. Imposing restitution exceeding a defendant's net proceeds constitutes an error of law subject to reversal on cassation.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 626 K/Pdt/2002, dated November 29, 2004, established a fundamental civil procedural law rule concerning the validity and legality of a Special Power of Attorney (*Surat Kuasa Khusus*) legalized by a Court Registrar:


A special power of attorney to litigate in court legalized by a District Court Registrar as a public officer within the judicial environment is valid and possesses perfect legal legality. A High Court that declares a lawsuit inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard*) on the grounds that power of attorney legalization by a Registrar is invalid has misapplied civil procedural law. The Supreme Court annulled the Surabaya High Court decision and ordered the High Court to reopen proceedings to examine and adjudicate the substantive merits of the case.


== Executive Summary ==


The central procedural principle established in this decision is that court registrars function as authorized public officers whose legalization of special powers of attorney endows them with complete legal validity.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Special powers of attorney legalized by court registrars satisfy formal representation requirements in civil litigation.
* Appellate courts dismissing claims on formal defects regarding registrar-legalized powers commit reversible procedural errors.
* Appellate rulings failing to evaluate substantive merits require remand orders directing courts to reopen proceedings (*heropening van het onderzoek*).


== Case Background ==


The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation, '''[Party B]''', filed a lawsuit at the Jember District Court against the Original Defendants / Respondents for Cassation (1. Suli, 2. Wahab) concerning the seizure of wet-rice land (*sawah*) in Petung Village, Bangsalsari, Jember, purchased by the Plaintiff from Markali Bukani alias Pak Sapi'i in 1976. The Plaintiff was represented by his attorney, [Party A], based on a Special Power of Attorney dated February 24, 2000. 


The Jember District Court (Decision No. 70/Pdt.G/2000/PN.Jr. dated September 11, 2000) rendered a default judgment (*verstek*) granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part. The Surabaya High Court (Decision No. 982/Pdt/2000/PT.SBY dated March 21, 2001) annulled the district court decision and declared the lawsuit inadmissible (NO) on the grounds that the power of attorney legalized by the Registrar was invalid. The Petitioner for Cassation subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Legalization Requirements and Validity of Special Powers of Attorney to Litigate in Court ===


The primary issue was whether a Special Power of Attorney signed by the Principal and Attorney and legalized by a District Court Registrar is valid under civil procedural law.


The Supreme Court held that it is valid and binding. A District Court Registrar is a public officer (*public officer*) authorized within the judicial branch to legally legalize and record special powers of attorney. Registrar legalization provides legal certainty and formal authenticity for attorney representation, ensuring the power of attorney is valid and that lawsuits filed thereunder must be declared admissible.


=== Appellate Judicial Duty to Examine Substantive Merits (*Procesrecht*) ===


The issue evaluated the appropriate course of action for the Supreme Court when a High Court annuls a District Court decision solely on formalistic exceptions concerning powers of attorney that prove erroneous.


The Supreme Court annuls the High Court decision and adjudicates afresh by issuing a remand order directing the High Court to reopen proceedings (*heropening van het onderzoek*) to examine and decide upon the substantive merits left unexamined.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the Surabaya High Court misapply civil procedural law (*foutieve kepassing van het procesrecht*) by declaring the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible (NO) on grounds of invalidity of a power of attorney legalized by the Jember District Court Registrar?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the Surabaya High Court misapplied procedural law. Registrar legalization by a District Court public officer is valid. The Supreme Court annulled Surabaya High Court Decision No. 982/Pdt/2000/PT.SBY and Jember District Court Decision No. 70/Pdt.G/2000/PN.Jr., and adjudicated afresh by ordering the Surabaya High Court to reopen proceedings and adjudicate the substantive merits.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Jember District Court & Surabaya High Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning the purchase of wet-rice land in Petung Village, Bangsalsari District, Jember Regency, by [Party B] from Markali Bukani alias Pak Sapi'i in 1976; agricultural cultivation since 1976; allegations of forcible seizure by Suli and Wahab in December 1999; and verification of the Special Power of Attorney dated February 24, 2000, executed before the Jember District Court Registrar.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The appellate *Judex Facti* of Surabaya High Court misapplied civil procedural law. The Plaintiff was represented by an attorney pursuant to a Special Power of Attorney legalized by the Jember District Court Registrar.
# Because the Registrar is a Public Officer in Court, the legality of the power of attorney executed by the Registrar is justified and declared valid. Consequently, the Plaintiff's lawsuit must be declared admissible.
# Because the Surabaya High Court failed to examine the substantive merits, it was ordered to reopen proceedings and adjudicate the merits.
# The Supreme Court annulled lower court rulings and adjudicated afresh, ordering the Surabaya High Court to examine the merits.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Party B]'''); annulled Surabaya High Court Decision No. 982/Pdt/2000/PT.SBY dated March 21, 2001, in conjunction with Jember District Court Decision No. 70/Pdt.G/2000/PN.JR dated September 11, 2000; and ADJUDICATED AFRESH: 1. Ordering the Surabaya High Court to reopen proceedings and adjudicate the substantive merits of the case; 2. Ordering the Respondent for Cassation to pay court costs across all judicial instances (cassation court costs set at Rp 200,000.—).


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Herziene Inlandsch Reglement (H.I.R.) / RBg:''' Article 123 paragraph (1) regarding the right to act through legal counsel and registration/legalization of powers of attorney.
* '''Law No. 2 of 1986 in conjunction with Law No. 8 of 2004 on General Courts:''' Duties and functions of Registrars as Court Public Officers.
* '''Law No. 14 of 1985 in conjunction with Law No. 5 of 2004 on the Supreme Court:''' Authority to review procedural misapplications on cassation.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* The Special Power of Attorney dated February 24, 2000, executed by the Plaintiff ([Party B]) appointing his attorney ([Party A]), was officially legalized by the Jember District Court Registrar.
* The District Court Registrar is a lawful Public Officer in Court.
* The Surabaya High Court had not examined or adjudicated the substantive merits of the land dispute.


=== Not Established / Rejected ===


* The alleged invalidity or formal defect of the Plaintiff's Special Power of Attorney, as erroneously concluded by the Surabaya High Court, was unproven and set aside by the Supreme Court.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Pending Substantive Merit Examination: Because the Surabaya High Court directly dismissed the lawsuit as inadmissible (NO) without reviewing substantive proofs of land ownership (purchase from Markali Bukani), the Supreme Court ordered the Surabaya High Court to reopen appellate examination to substantively test the merits.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Is a Special Power of Attorney to litigate in Court legalized by a District Court Registrar valid under the law?'''


'''A:''' Valid and legally binding. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 626 K/Pdt/2002, a District Court Registrar functions as a Public Officer (*public officer*) within the judicial branch, making a Special Power of Attorney legalized by the Registrar fully valid and possessing complete legal force. Courts must not declare lawsuits inadmissible (NO) merely by challenging registrar legalization of powers of attorney.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 628 K/Pid/1984, dated July 22, 1985, established a fundamental criminal and civil procedural law rule concerning prejudicial questions (*prejudisial geschil* / civil disputes preceding criminal prosecution ex Article 385 of the Criminal Code / KUHP):


When the ownership status of land or buildings in a criminal land crime case (sale of land/buildings ex Article 385 paragraph 1 of the Criminal Code) remains the object of an ongoing civil dispute that has not yet attained final and binding legal force (*Inkracht van Gewijsde*), the High Court, prior to deciding upon the criminal merits (releasing or sentencing), must suspend or await the civil court decision determining the ownership status of the land and house until it possesses binding legal certainty.


The Supreme Court annulled Bandung High Court Decision No. 150/1983/Pid/PT.B and ordered the Bandung High Court to reopen proceedings and examine/adjudicate the criminal merits after the civil judgment attains final and binding legal force.


== Executive Summary ==


The central legal principle established in this decision is that criminal courts cannot prematurely adjudicate land offenses when the underlying civil property rights are actively being litigated, mandating a stay of proceedings (*prejudisial geschil*).


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Land offenses requiring proof of ownership cannot be finalized while civil ownership suits remain sub judice.
* Appellate courts discharging defendants prematurely without waiting for final civil outcomes commit procedural error.
* Appellate rulings must be annulled with remand orders directing courts to stay proceedings until civil finality is achieved.


== Case Background ==


The Original Defendants / Respondents for Cassation (1. '''[Defendant I]''', [age removed], merchant; 2. '''[Defendant II]''', [age removed], housewife) were charged with violating Article 385 paragraph (1) in conjunction with Article 55 paragraph (1) 1st of the Criminal Code for jointly selling house and building HGB No. 197/Panaragan [address removed], Bogor, to their child ([Child]) for Rp 9,000,000.— using an alleged forged Power of Attorney dated May 30, 1969. 


The Bogor District Court (Decision No. 74/1983/Pid/B/PN.Bgr. dated October 17, 1983) sentenced Defendant I to 6 months' imprisonment and Defendant II to 4 months' imprisonment. The Bandung High Court (Decision No. 150/1983/Pid/PT.B dated March 8, 1984) annulled the Bogor District Court decision and discharged the Defendants from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag*) on the grounds that the element of property belonging to another remained uncertain because civil ownership disputes had not attained final and binding legal force. The Public Prosecutor at the Bogor State Prosecutor's Office subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Prejudicial Questions (*Prejudisial Geschil*) in Land Crime Offenses (Article 385 KUHP) ===


The primary issue was whether a High Court is justified in discharging a Defendant from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*) under Article 385 of the Criminal Code on the grounds that the element of "property belonging to another" is unproven because underlying civil ownership disputes remain pending without final legal force.


The Supreme Court held that the Bandung High Court misapplied the law. When elements of a land crime depend upon resolving civil ownership rights currently examined in civil courts and lacking final legal force (*Inkracht van Gewijsde*), the High Court must not prematurely discharge or convict. The Court is legally mandated to suspend proceedings and await the final civil judgment establishing land/house ownership before reopening and deciding the criminal merits.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the Bandung High Court misapply procedural law (*foutieve kepassing van het recht*) by prematurely issuing a discharge (*ontslag*) ruling over an Article 385 KUHP criminal charge without suspending proceedings until a final civil judgment established ownership of HGB land No. 197/Panaragan [address removed], Bogor?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the Bandung High Court misapplied procedural law. The Supreme Court annulled Bandung High Court Decision No. 150/1983/Pid/PT.B and adjudicated afresh, ordering the Bandung High Court to reopen proceedings and decide the criminal merits after the civil ownership judgment attains final and binding legal force.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Bogor District Court & Bandung High Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning the execution of the Power of Attorney dated May 30, 1969, Sale and Purchase Deed No. 01/JBR/Pm.014/I/1980 to [Child] for Rp 9,000,000.—, forgery convictions of Wahir bin Satim (Notary employee), issuance of HGB Certificate No. 197/Panaragan in the name of [Party D] / Pang Siong Foe, and Judicial Review (*Peninjauan Kembali*) civil proceedings No. 62/PK/Perd/1981.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The appellate *Judex Facti* of Bandung High Court misapplied the law by declaring that the Defendants' acts did not constitute a crime because civil ownership status remained unsettled.
# However, instead of discharging the Defendants (*ontslag*), the High Court prior to deciding the criminal merits was legally obligated to suspend and await the civil court decision determining land and house ownership to ensure binding certainty (*prejudisial geschil*).
# The Supreme Court annulled the Bandung High Court decision and adjudicated afresh, ordering the Bandung High Court to reopen proceedings and adjudicate the criminal merits after the civil judgment attains finality.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation ('''Public Prosecutor at the Bogor State Prosecutor's Office'''); annulled Bandung High Court Decision No. 150/1983/Pid/PT.B dated March 8, 1984; and ADJUDICATED AFRESH: 1. Ordering the Bandung High Court to reopen proceedings and examine and adjudicate the merits of this case after the civil court decision determining the ownership status of land H.G.B. No. 197/Panaragan located at Jalan Merdeka No. 11A, Bogor, attains binding certainty; 2. Stipulating that appeal court costs be deferred until the High Court renders its final decision; 3. Charging cassation court costs to the State.


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Criminal Code (KUHP):''' Article 385 paragraph (1) (Stellionaat / Unlawful Land Sale), Article 55 paragraph (1) 1st.
* '''Criminal Procedure Doctrine:''' *Prejudisial Geschil* Doctrine (Civil Prejudicial Questions Deriving Criminal Matters).
* '''Law No. 8 of 1981 (KUHAP):''' Provisions governing Supreme Court Cassation Authority.
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 in conjunction with Law No. 13 of 1965:''' Judicial Power & Supreme Court.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* Defendants I and II sold house and building HGB No. 197/Panaragan [address removed], Bogor, to their child ([Child]) for Rp 9,000,000.— using a Power of Attorney dated May 30, 1969.
* Civil ownership status over land HGB No. 197/Panaragan [address removed], Bogor, between witness [Party D] and the Defendants remained an active subject of civil litigation undergoing processing without final legal force during criminal trial.


=== Not Established / Suspended Awaiting Finality ===


* Lawful civil ownership over the disputed land/house cannot be legally ascertained in criminal proceedings prior to a final and binding civil judgment (*inkracht*).


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Interdependence of Civil Law and Land Criminal Law: This landmark ruling establishes strict boundaries between land crimes (Article 385 KUHP) and civil land ownership disputes. Criminal prosecution must not preempt civil outcomes when property rights over land/buildings remain uncertain and contested in civil courts.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: May a criminal judge decide a land sale criminal case (Article 385 KUHP) if the civil ownership dispute over the land is still ongoing in court and lacks final binding force?'''


'''A:''' No, they may not. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 628 K/Pid/1984 (*prejudisial geschil*), if the ownership status of land/buildings in an Article 385 KUHP criminal case remains the object of an ongoing civil dispute without final binding force, the Court is mandated to suspend proceedings and await the civil court decision determining land ownership to attain binding certainty (*inkracht*) before examining and deciding the criminal merits.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Review Decision No. 634 PK/Pdt/2007, dated May 22, 2008, established fundamental labor law and absolute judicial jurisdiction rules:


General Courts (District Courts, High Courts, and the Supreme Court) lack authority to examine and adjudicate labor disputes / termination of employment (PHK) between employees/teachers and employers/school foundations. Labor disputes fall under the absolute jurisdiction (*kompetensi absolut*) of labor dispute settlement bodies (P4D and P4P ex Law No. 22 of 1957). Initiating repeated lawsuits in General Courts over labor disputes already adjudicated by P4D, P4P, and State Administrative High Courts constitutes an attempt to obscure legal certainty (*rechtszekerheid*), requiring such lawsuits to be dismissed entirely.


== Executive Summary ==


The central jurisdictional principle established in this decision is that labor and employment termination disputes are exclusively reserved for specialized labor tribunals, shielding them from collateral civil litigation in General Courts.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* General courts lack absolute jurisdiction over employment termination and labor compensation disputes.
* Filing civil tort lawsuits (*PMH*) in District Courts over matters already settled by labor panels undermines legal certainty.
* Erroneous cassation rulings upholding general court jurisdiction over labor matters are subject to reversal upon judicial review (*peninjauan kembali*).


== Case Background ==


The Original Plaintiff / Respondent for Review, '''Mrs. [Party B]''' (sports teacher), filed a lawsuit at the Tangerang District Court against the Original Defendant II / Petitioner for Review, '''The British International School''', and Original Defendant I / Co-Respondent for Review, '''[Party A]''' (Principal), concerning oral/written dismissal in January 1995. The Plaintiff alleged that the Defendants committed an Unlawful Act (*Perbuatan Melawan Hukum* / Article 1365 Civil Code) and claimed material damages of US$ 3,065/month and immaterial damages of Rp 500 million. 


The Tangerang District Court (Decision No. 152/Pdt.G/1997/PN.Tng dated March 11, 1998) dismissed the Plaintiff's lawsuit entirely. The Bandung High Court (Decision No. 524/Pdt/1998/PT.Bdg dated October 19, 1999) affirmed the Tangerang District Court decision. However, the Supreme Court Cassation Panel (Decision No. 3385 K/Pdt/2000 dated July 25, 2005) annulled the Bandung High Court decision and granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part. The British International School subsequently filed a Review petition (*Peninjauan Kembali*) with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Absolute Jurisdiction of General Courts vs. Specialized Labor Tribunals (P4D/P4P ex Law No. 22 of 1957 jo. Law No. 12 of 1964) ===


The primary issue was whether General Courts (District Courts, High Courts, Supreme Court) have absolute jurisdiction to adjudicate unlawful act (*PMH*) lawsuits (Article 1365 Civil Code) filed by employees/teachers over Employment Termination (*PHK*) and salary/compensation demands against employers/schools.


The Supreme Court held that General Courts lack absolute jurisdiction. Disputes arising from employment relationships, dismissal determinations, and severance/salary claims constitute pure labor disputes subject to the absolute jurisdiction of the Regional Labor Dispute Settlement Committee (P4D) and Central Labor Dispute Settlement Committee (P4P).


=== Protection of Legal Certainty (Res Judicata / Ne Bis In Idem) Over Labor Body & PTTUN Decisions ===


The issue evaluated the legal standing of civil lawsuits in District Courts when identical dismissal disputes have already been adjudicated by P4D, P4P, affirmed by the State Administrative High Court (*PTTUN*), and reviewed by the Supreme Court Administrative Chamber.


The Supreme Court held that relitigating labor disputes already adjudicated by P4D, P4P, and PTTUN within General Courts aims to obscure legal certainty (*rechtszekerheid*). The Review Panel is legally required to annul erroneous civil cassation rulings and dismiss the Plaintiff's lawsuit entirely.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judicial Review) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the Supreme Court Cassation Panel in Decision No. 3385 K/Pdt/2000 commit a judicial error or manifest mistake (*kekhilafan yang nyata* ex Article 67 letter f of Law No. 14 of 1985) by granting the Plaintiff's civil dismissal lawsuit, despite such disputes falling under the absolute jurisdiction of labor bodies (P4D/P4P) and *PTTUN*?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes. There was manifest judicial error at the cassation level. General Courts lack absolute jurisdiction over labor disputes. The Supreme Court granted the Review petition of The British International School, annulled Supreme Court Decision No. 3385 K/Pdt/2000, and ADJUDICATED AFRESH by rejecting the Plaintiff's lawsuit entirely.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Tangerang District Court, Bandung High Court, & Labor Bodies) ===


Examination of facts concerning Mrs. [Party B]'s employment as a sports teacher since September 1, 1988; workplace disputes and correspondence dated January 12 & 27, 1995; registration of dismissal/authorization with the Department of Manpower; Bandung P4D Decision dated August 21, 1996; Central P4P Decision dated May 1, 1997; and Jakarta State Administrative High Court Decision No. 60/G/1997/PT.TUN.JKT jo. Administrative Cassation Supreme Court No. 107/K/TUN/1999.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# Review grounds were justified due to manifest judicial error and mistake at the cassation level.
# The dispute between the Plaintiff and Defendants was a pure labor dispute falling within the absolute jurisdiction of P4D and P4P. General Courts (District Courts, High Courts, Supreme Court) lack authority to examine and adjudicate labor disputes.
# Furthermore, P4D, P4P, and PTTUN had already adjudicated the dispute. Relitigating the dispute in General Courts aims to obscure legal certainty, requiring dismissal.
# The Supreme Court granted the Review petition, annulled Cassation Decision No. 3385 K/Pdt/2000, and adjudicated afresh by rejecting the Plaintiff's lawsuit entirely.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court ruled: 1. Granting the Review petition from Petitioner for Review ('''THE BRITISH INTERNATIONAL SCHOOL'''); 2. Annulling Supreme Court Decision No. 3385 K/Pdt/2000 dated July 25, 2005; 3. ADJUDICATING AFRESH: Under Exceptions: Rejecting the Defendant's exceptions; Under Provision: Declaring the Plaintiff's provisional claims inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard*); Under the Merits: Rejecting the Plaintiff's lawsuit entirely; and ordering the Respondent for Review / Original Plaintiff to pay court costs across all judicial instances (Review court costs set at Rp 2,500,000.—).


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Law No. 22 of 1957 on Labor Dispute Settlement:''' P4D & P4P jurisdiction.
* '''Law No. 12 of 1964 on Dismissal in Private Enterprises:''' Authorization requirements for private sector dismissals.
* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata):''' Article 1365 (Unlawful Acts / *PMH* — Ruled inapplicable to bypass labor jurisdiction).
* '''Law No. 14 of 1985 in conjunction with Law No. 5 of 2004 in conjunction with Law No. 3 of 2009 on the Supreme Court:''' Article 67 letter f (Grounds for Judicial Review / Manifest Judicial Error).
* '''Supreme Court Standing Jurisprudence:''' Supreme Court Decision No. 807 K/Pdt/1988 (March 28, 1991): Limitation of General Court absolute jurisdiction in labor disputes.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* The dispute between Mrs. [Party B] and The British International School was a pure labor dispute arising from employment termination / conclusion of employment contracts.
* The dismissal dispute had been processed and adjudicated by competent bodies, namely Bandung P4D, Central P4P, and Jakarta State Administrative High Court (*PTTUN*).
* Manifest judicial error infected Supreme Court Cassation Decision No. 3385 K/Pdt/2000, which erroneously granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in General Courts.


=== Not Established / Inadmissible ===


* General Courts lack absolute jurisdiction to evaluate dismissal validity and award labor compensation damages under Article 1365 of the Civil Code.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Prevention of Forum Shopping in Employment Disputes: This landmark Review ruling establishes strict boundaries preventing forum shopping by employees or employers attempting to repackage dismissal/labor disputes as civil tort claims (*PMH*) in District Courts after losing before labor settlement boards or *PTTUN*.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Can a dismissed employee or teacher sue an employer or school in District Court based on Unlawful Acts (Article 1365 Civil Code)?'''


'''A:''' No, General Courts lack jurisdiction (*Absolute Jurisdiction Dismissed*). Based on Supreme Court Review Decision No. 634 PK/Pdt/2007, General Courts (District Courts, High Courts, Supreme Court) lack authority to examine and adjudicate labor disputes/dismissals. Labor disputes constitute the absolute authority of specialized labor dispute settlement bodies (P4D/P4P / Industrial Relations Court). Relitigating dismissal disputes already adjudicated by labor bodies in District Courts obscures legal certainty, requiring lawsuits to be dismissed.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 693 K/Pid/1986, dated July 12, 1986, established fundamental criminal law rules concerning the inclusion of lesser theft offenses within aggravated theft indictments (*gekwalificeerde diefstal*) and the conceptual separation between force as a preliminary instrument (*middel*) and force as the actual execution method of a theft:


In an indictment for aggravated theft (*gekwalificeerde diefstal*), lesser theft offenses are inherently included, *in casu* Article 363 paragraph (1) number 4 of the Criminal Code. Force under Article 365 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code refers to force functioning as an instrument (*middel*) to enable a desired outcome (a preliminary stage preceding the theft itself); whereas the act of pulling a gold necklace during a snatching (*penjambretan*) action constitutes the execution method/technique of the theft itself. Consequently, the Supreme Court corrected the qualification of the Defendants' acts to "theft committed by two or more allied persons" ex Article 363 paragraph (1) number 4 of the Criminal Code.


== Executive Summary ==


The central criminal law principle established in this decision is that street snatching (*penjambretan*) characterized by sudden property grabs without independent violence preceding the theft qualifies as aggravated joint theft rather than armed robbery or violent theft.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Aggravated theft indictments automatically encompass lesser included theft offenses under the criminal code.
* Physical force directly employed to seize property during a snatching constitutes execution methodology rather than independent instrumental violence (*middel*).
* Convictions misqualifying snatching as violent theft are subject to corrective modification on cassation.


== Case Background ==


The Original Defendants (Defendant I: '''[Defendant I]''', [age removed], recidivist; Defendant II: '''[Defendant II]''', [age removed]) were charged with theft with violence (Article 365 paragraphs 1, 2 sub 4 / Primary) or ordinary theft (Article 362 jo. 55 KUHP / Subsidiary) for riding together on a Yamaha L2G motorcycle and snatching a 24.5-gram gold necklace valued at Rp 280,000.— belonging to witness Ny. [Victim] on the Sambi-Bangak public road in Boyolali on August 31, 1985. 


The Boyolali District Court (Decision No. 175/Pid.S/1985/PN.Bi dated January 13, 1986) sentenced Defendant I and Defendant II to 1 year and 3 months' imprisonment each and confiscated the motorcycle. The Semarang High Court (Decision No. 32/Pid/S/1986/PT.Smg dated March 3, 1986) modified Defendant II's sentence to 10 months' imprisonment and ordered the return of the motorcycle to witness [Defendant IV]. Both the Public Prosecutor and the Defendants filed cassation petitions with the Supreme Court.
