== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Conceptual Difference Between Instrumental Force (*Middel*) vs. Execution Force (Material Act) in Theft Offenses ===


The primary issue was whether forcefully pulling a gold necklace from a victim's neck while riding a motorcycle (snatching / *penjambretan*) qualifies as Robbery/Theft with Violence (Article 365 KUHP) or Aggravated Joint Theft (Article 363 paragraph 1 number 4 KUHP).


The Supreme Court held that it qualifies as Article 363 paragraph (1) number 4 of the Criminal Code. Force under Article 365 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code must function as a preliminary instrument (*middel*) intentionally executed to enable or facilitate theft. When physical action (such as pulling a necklace) is the direct technique or method of seizing property, that action constitutes the execution of the theft itself.


=== Principle of Lesser Included Offense Inclusion (*Gekwalificeerde Diefstal*) ===


The issue evaluated whether a Judge may convict a Defendant under Article 363 paragraph (1) number 4 of the Criminal Code when the Public Prosecutor formulates a primary indictment using Article 365 of the Criminal Code.


The Supreme Court held that it is justified and lawful. In prosecuting aggravated theft (*gekwalificeerde diefstal*), a kindred lesser theft offense (in casu joint theft by two or more allied persons ex Article 363 paragraph 1 number 4 KUHP) is legally and automatically included (*inclusief*) within the scope of the indictment.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the *Judex Facti* (Semarang High Court & Boyolali District Court) misapply the law (*foutieve kepassing van het recht*) by qualifying a snatching incident as "theft with violence" (Article 365 KUHP) rather than "theft committed by two or more allied persons" (Article 363 paragraph 1 number 4 KUHP)?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the qualification of the acts in the lower courts' rulings required correction. The Supreme Court rejected the Petitioners' cassation appeals while modifying the judgment to declare the Defendants proven guilty of "theft committed by two or more allied persons" ex Article 363 paragraph (1) number 4 of the Criminal Code.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Boyolali District Court & Semarang High Court) ===


Examination of facts regarding the incident on August 31, 1985, at 08:00 WIB on the public road of Sambi-Bangak, Boyolali; the roles of Defendant I ([Defendant I]) operating the red Yamaha L2G motorcycle plate AD-3314-AD and Defendant II ([Defendant II]) as pillion rider who snatched the 24.5-gram gold necklace belonging to Ny. [Victim]; ownership of the motorcycle belonging to witness IV [Defendant IV]; and Defendant I's status as a recidivist.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The *Judex Facti* of Semarang High Court correctly returned the motorcycle evidence to its last holder, but erred regarding the qualification of the Defendants' acts.
# In aggravated theft indictments (*gekwalificeerde diefstal*), lesser thefts are automatically included (i.c. Article 363 paragraph 1 number 4 KUHP).
# Force under Article 365(1) KUHP serves as an instrumental precursor (*middel*) enabling theft, whereas pulling a necklace during snatching constitutes the execution method of the theft itself. Consequently, the acts constitute "theft by two or more allied persons" ex Article 363 paragraph (1) number 4 KUHP.
# The Supreme Court rejected the cassation appeals of the Prosecutor and Defendants while modifying the qualification in the appellate ruling.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court ruled: Rejecting the cassation petitions from Petitioner for Cassation I (Public Prosecutor at Boyolali State Prosecutor's Office) and Petitioner for Cassation II (Defendant I: [Defendant I] & Defendant II: [Defendant II]); Modifying the ruling of Semarang High Court Decision No. 32/Pid/S/1986/PT.Smg dated March 3, 1986, solely regarding the qualification of proven guilt and sentence adjustments, to read: Declaring Defendant I [Defendant I] and Defendant II [Defendant II] proven legally and convincingly guilty of committing the crime of "Theft committed by two or more allied persons"; Sentencing Defendant I to a prison term of 1 (one) year and 3 (three) months and Defendant II to a prison term of 10 (ten) months; Deducting the full period of detention served; Ordering the return of the motorcycle evidence to witness IV [Defendant IV]; and ordering Petitioners for Cassation II to pay cassation court costs amounting to Rp 2,500.—.


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Criminal Code (KUHP):'''
  * Article 363 paragraph (1) number 4: Theft committed by two or more allied persons (Proven legally and convincingly).
  * Article 365 paragraphs (1) & (2): Robbery / theft with violence (Qualification corrected by Supreme Court).
  * Article 55 paragraph (1) 1st: Complicity in criminal offenses.
* '''Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP / Law No. 8 of 1981):''' Article 253: Supreme Court cassation review authority over misapplications of law.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* Defendants [Defendant I] and [Defendant II] jointly and in alliance seized a 24.5-gram gold necklace belonging to witness Ny. [Victim].
* Yamaha L2G motorcycle plate AD-3314-AD was the lawful property of witness IV ([Defendant IV]) borrowed by the Defendants.
* Defendant I possessed a prior criminal record as a recidivist in embezzlement.


=== Not Established / Modified on Cassation ===


* The act of pulling the necklace during the crime was unproven as instrumental force (*middel*) preceding Article 365 KUHP, but established as the execution method of allied theft under Article 363 paragraph (1) number 4 KUHP.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Refinement of Adjudication Qualifications by the Supreme Court: The Supreme Court meticulously distinguished between dogmatic boundaries separating "force as a preliminary instrument before a crime" and "force as a method of property seizure", preventing misqualification errors in street snatching cases.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Is the act of snatching a gold necklace on a public highway qualified as robbery/theft with violence (Article 365 KUHP) or aggravated theft (Article 363 KUHP)?'''


'''A:''' It is qualified as Theft committed by two or more allied persons (Article 363 paragraph 1 number 4 KUHP). Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 693 K/Pid/1986, force under Article 365 of the Criminal Code must serve as a preliminary instrument (*middel*) enabling the commission of theft. In contrast, the act of pulling a necklace during snatching constitutes the technique or execution method of the theft itself. Furthermore, in aggravated theft indictments (*gekwalificeerde diefstal*), lesser included theft offenses are legally and automatically encompassed.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Review Decision No. 698 PK/Pdt/2001, dated February 27, 2003, established a foundational rule in Marine Insurance regarding the duty of disclosing material facts (*utmost good faith* / *non-disclosure*) pursuant to Article 251 of the Commercial Code (*KUHD*):


Legally, the insured has a legal obligation to disclose the true condition (*the whole truth*) of the vessel to be insured. If the insured intentionally conceals the true condition or provides incorrect disclosures during the conclusion of the insurance policy (such as hiding the fact that M.V. Lucky Fortune was formerly M.V. Bethesda 2, which had caught fire on December 16, 1990, and lacked valid classification from Bureau Veritas), the insurance contract is rendered void (*batal demi hukum* ex Article 251 KUHD), thereby resulting in the total rejection of the claim for Total Loss / Constructive Total Loss.


== Executive Summary ==


The central principle established in this decision is that failure to disclose vital historical and safety data regarding a vessel prior to policy issuance voids the marine insurance contract under statutory commercial law.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Insured parties are bound by an absolute duty of disclosure (*utmost good faith*) regarding vessel history and classification.
* Concealment of past structural damage or lack of valid classification renders insurance policies void *ab initio* under Article 251 KUHD.
* Erroneous cassation judgments ignoring statutory disclosure duties are subject to reversal upon judicial review (*peninjauan kembali*).


== Case Background ==


The Original Plaintiffs / Respondents for Review (1. '''Intercontinental Maritime Pte Ltd''', 2. '''PT Layar Sentosa Shipping Corporation''') sued the Original Defendant / Petitioner for Review, '''PT Wataka General Insurance''', at the South Jakarta District Court over the rejection of an insurance claim for M.V. Lucky Fortune Policy No. 01.81.92.00004 (Hull & Machinery US$ 1,000,000.— & Removal of Wreck US$ 250,000.—), which capsized and sank due to a typhoon at Tanjung Priok Port on January 28, 1993. The Defendant rejected the claim because the Plaintiffs failed to disclose material facts (*non-disclosure of material facts*) that M.V. Lucky Fortune was formerly M.V. Bethesda 2, which had suffered severe fire damage on December 16, 1990, and lacked Bureau Veritas classification. 


The South Jakarta District Court (Decision No. 88/Pdt.G/1995/PN.Jkt.Sel dated September 1, 1995) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part. The Jakarta High Court (Decision No. 240/Pdt/1996/PT.DKI dated August 14, 1996) annulled the district court decision and dismissed the lawsuit entirely. However, the Supreme Court Cassation Panel (Decision No. 916 K/Pdt/1997 dated October 14, 1999) annulled the Jakarta High Court decision and affirmed the South Jakarta District Court judgment. PT Wataka General Insurance subsequently filed a Review petition (*Peninjauan Kembali*) with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Duty of Disclosing Material Facts (Utmost Good Faith / Non-Disclosure) in Commercial Insurance (Article 251 KUHD) ===


The primary issue was whether a marine insurance contract is valid when an insured covers a vessel without disclosing material facts establishing that the vessel suffered a prior constructive total loss by fire and lost its official classification status from a rating agency (Bureau Veritas).


The Supreme Court held that the insurance contract is void (*nietig* / void *ab initio*) pursuant to Article 251 of the Commercial Code (*KUHD*). The insured is bound by an absolute duty to disclose the whole truth (*the whole truth*). Non-disclosure of material facts during policy conclusion violates the principle of utmost good faith, entitling the insurer to reject claims and rendering the contract void.


=== Review Panel Authority to Annul Cassation Rulings Due to Manifest Judicial Error (Article 67 letter f Law No. 14 of 1985) ===


The issue evaluated how the Supreme Court responds on Review when a prior Cassation Panel misinterprets evidence T.3 (survey/classification reports) and ignores the concealment of vessel classification status.


The Supreme Court on Review possesses authority to annul Cassation Decision No. 916 K/Pdt/1997 dated October 14, 1999, and adjudicate afresh by rejecting the Plaintiffs' lawsuit entirely due to manifest judicial errors committed in applying Article 251 KUHD.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judicial Review) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the Supreme Court Cassation Panel in Decision No. 916 K/Pdt/1997 misapply the law (*foutieve kepassing van het recht*) by ignoring Article 251 of the Commercial Code, which mandates contract nullification for insurance policies concluded while intentionally concealing material facts regarding vessel condition and classification?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the Cassation Panel committed a manifest error. The Supreme Court granted PT Wataka General Insurance's Review petition, annulled Cassation Decision No. 916 K/Pdt/1997, and adjudicated afresh by rejecting the Plaintiffs' lawsuit entirely.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / South Jakarta District Court, Jakarta High Court, & Review Panel) ===


Examination of facts concerning Marine Insurance Policy No. 01.81.92.00004 dated January 31, 1992, over M.V. Lucky Fortune (Hull & Machinery US$ 1,000,000.— & Removal of Wreck US$ 250,000.—); the capsizing and sinking of the vessel due to a typhoon at Tanjung Priok Port on January 28, 1993; verification of evidence T.3 proving M.V. Lucky Fortune was formerly M.V. Bethesda 2, which burned on December 16, 1990; Bureau Veritas suspension/revocation reports dated February 24–25, 1992; and adjuster reports by Zoreale, PT Suisindo, and PT Carsurin.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# Review grounds were justified due to manifest judicial error at the cassation level.
# Evidence T.3 established that M.V. Lucky Fortune was formerly M.V. Bethesda 2, which burned on December 16, 1990, and lacked valid Bureau Veritas classification upon insurance coverage.
# Under Article 251 KUHD, the insured has a strict duty to disclose the true condition of the vessel (*the whole truth*). Because the Plaintiffs intentionally concealed true conditions during policy conclusion, the insurance contract is void (*batal demi hukum*).
# The Supreme Court granted the Review petition, annulled Cassation Decision No. 916 K/Pdt/1997, and adjudicated afresh by rejecting the Plaintiffs' lawsuit entirely.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court ruled: Granting the Review petition from Petitioner for Review ('''P.T. WATAKA GENERAL INSURANCE'''); Annulling the Supreme Court decision dated October 14, 1999, No. 916 K/Pdt/1997; and ADJUDICATING AFRESH: Under Provision: Rejecting the Plaintiffs' provisional claims; Under the Merits: Rejecting the Plaintiffs' lawsuit entirely; and ordering the Respondent for Review to pay Review court costs amounting to Rp 500,000.—.


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Commercial Code (KUHD):''' Article 251: Duty of disclosure/material facts notification and threat of contract nullification for incorrect disclosures or concealment of facts.
* '''Law No. 14 of 1985 in conjunction with Law No. 5 of 2004 in conjunction with Law No. 3 of 2009 on the Supreme Court:''' Article 67 letter f (Grounds for Judicial Review due to Manifest Judicial Error / Mistake).


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* M.V. Lucky Fortune insured on January 31, 1992, was actually former M.V. Bethesda 2, which suffered total destruction by fire (*Constructive Total Loss*) on December 16, 1990.
* At policy conclusion on January 31, 1992, the vessel possessed no valid classification status from Bureau Veritas.
* Plaintiffs / Respondents for Review intentionally concealed vessel conditions and classification status from Defendant / Petitioner for Review during policy issuance.


=== Not Established / Void Contract ===


* Plaintiffs were unproven entitled to insurance compensation claims of US$ 1,000,000.— (Hull & Machinery) and US$ 250,000.— (Removal of Wreck) because the insurance contract was void *ab initio*.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Application of Utmost Good Faith in Marine Insurance: This landmark Review ruling establishes strict legal certainty for the national insurance industry: the duty of disclosure rests entirely on prospective insureds. Concealment of fatal vessel accident histories is intolerable even after policy issuance.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Must an insurer pay a claim if the insured intentionally conceals severe prior damage and lack of vessel classification when concluding a marine insurance policy?'''


'''A:''' No, the insurer is not obligated. Based on Supreme Court Review Decision No. 698 PK/Pdt/2001, pursuant to Article 251 of the Commercial Code (*KUHD*), the insured has a legal duty to disclose the true condition of the vessel (*the whole truth*). If the insured intentionally conceals material facts (such as past fire history and absence of valid classification certificates) during policy conclusion, the insurance contract is void (*void ab initio*), and the insurance company is entitled to reject all compensation claims.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 731 K/Pid/1984, dated May 27, 1985, established a criminal procedural law rule regarding the limits of applying the Rapid Examination Procedure (*Acara Pemeriksaan Cepat* ex Article 205 KUHAP) and the mandatory requirement of Summary Examination Procedures for defamation offenses under Article 310 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code:


The defamation offense regulated under Article 310 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code carries a maximum imprisonment threat of 9 (nine) months. Because the sentencing threat exceeds 3 (three) months of imprisonment, the case MUST NOT be examined via Rapid Examination Procedures (Article 205 KUHAP), but MUST instead be examined via Summary Examination Procedures (*Acara Pemeriksaan Singkat*). Prosecutions brought forward by National Police Investigators under the authority of the Public Prosecutor utilizing Rapid Examination Procedures for offenses under Article 310 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code are formally defective, resulting in the Prosecutor's/Investigator's prosecution being declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).


== Executive Summary ==


The central procedural principle established in this decision is that misdemeanor-style rapid examination procedures cannot be legally utilized for criminal offenses whose statutory imprisonment penalties exceed the 3-month threshold.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Offenses carrying maximum imprisonment terms exceeding 3 months are disqualified from rapid examination (*Tipiring*).
* Using rapid examination procedures for defamation offenses carrying up to 9 months' imprisonment constitutes a fundamental formal procedural defect.
* Prosecutions suffering from improper procedural classification must be dismissed as inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).


== Case Background ==


The Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation, '''[Defendant]''' ([age removed], Religious Teacher), was brought before the Kandangan District Court by National Police Investigators (Head of Hulu Sungai Selatan Police Resort 1303) under the authority of the Public Prosecutor utilizing Rapid Examination Procedures (Article 205 KUHAP). The Defendant was charged with violating Article 310 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code for shouting "thief, thief" at witness [Witness] who climbed a starfruit tree to catch the Defendant's chicken. 


The Kandangan District Court (Decision No. 801/1983/Pel. PN.Kgn dated August 22, 1983) convicted the Defendant and sentenced him to a fine of Rp 4,500.— subsidiary to 4 days' confinement. The Defendant directly filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Statutory Boundaries of Rapid Examination Procedures (Article 205 KUHAP) vs. Summary Examination Procedures (Article 203 KUHAP) ===


The primary issue was whether a simple defamation crime (Article 310 paragraph 1 KUHP) punishable by a maximum of 9 months' imprisonment can be filed and examined by a District Court utilizing Rapid Examination Procedures (*Tindak Pidana Ringan* / Tipiring).


The Supreme Court held that it cannot. Pursuant to Article 205 paragraph (1) of the KUHAP, Rapid Examination Procedures are exclusively reserved for minor offenses (*tindak pidana ringan*) punishable by imprisonment or confinement not exceeding 3 (three) months and/or fines up to Rp 7,500.—. Because Article 310 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code carries an imprisonment threat of up to 9 (nine) months, the case must mandatorily be examined via Summary Examination Procedures. Initiating rapid prosecution for this offense constitutes a procedural error resulting in dismissal of the prosecution as inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).


=== Protection of Defendants' Right of Appeal ===


Improper utilization of Rapid Procedures illegally strips the Defendant of the right to appeal to the High Court (because Rapid Procedure Tipiring judgments cannot be appealed ex Article 67 jo. Article 244 KUHAP). The Supreme Court corrected this procedural error to uphold *due process of law*.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the Kandangan District Court misapply criminal procedural law (*foutieve kepassing van het procesrecht*) by examining and deciding an Article 310 paragraph (1) KUHP case using Rapid Examination Procedures (Article 205 KUHAP)?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the Kandangan District Court misapplied procedural law. The Supreme Court annulled Kandangan District Court Decision No. 801/1983/Pel. PN.Kgn and adjudicated afresh by declaring the Investigator's/Public Prosecutor's prosecution inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Kandangan District Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning the shouting of "thief" by Defendant [Defendant] (Religious Teacher) on Saturday night, April 8–9, 1983, in Hamayang Village, Daha Utara, directed at witness [Witness] who climbed a starfruit tree in the Defendant's yard to catch his chicken.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The *Judex Facti* of Kandangan District Court misapplied criminal procedural law. The Petitioner's objection is justified. This case should have been examined via summary procedures because the Defendant was charged under Article 310 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code, which carries up to 9 months' imprisonment.
# Pursuant to Article 205 KUHAP, Rapid Examination Procedures only apply to minor offenses carrying maximum imprisonment/confinement of 3 months.
# Because prosecution via rapid procedures was formally defective, the prosecution by the investigator/Public Prosecutor is declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).
# The Supreme Court annulled the lower court ruling and adjudicated afresh.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Defendant]'''); annulled Kandangan District Court Decision No. 801/1983/Pel. PN.Kgn dated August 22, 1983; and ADJUDICATED AFRESH: Declaring the prosecution by the investigator under the authority of the Public Prosecutor / Commander of Hulu Sungai Selatan Police Resort 1303 inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard*); and charging the State with court costs across all judicial instances.


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Criminal Code (KUHP):''' Article 310 paragraph (1): Ordinary Defamation offense (Maximum imprisonment threat of 9 months or fine).
* '''Law No. 8 of 1981 on Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP):'''
  * Article 205: Rapid Examination Procedures for Minor Offenses (Maximum penalty threshold of 3 months' imprisonment/confinement).
  * Article 203: Summary Examination Procedures.
  * Articles 67 & 244: Direct Cassation Rights over Rapid Procedure Judgments.
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 in conjunction with Law No. 13 of 1965 on Judicial Power & Supreme Court.'''


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* The Defendant was brought to trial by Police Investigators under Article 310 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code utilizing Rapid Examination Procedures ex Article 205 KUHAP.
* The statutory sentencing threat of Article 310 paragraph (1) KUHP is a maximum of 9 months' imprisonment, thereby exceeding the *Tipiring* threshold of Article 205 KUHAP (maximum 3 months).
* The prosecution by the investigator/Public Prosecutor suffered from formal legal defects and was inadmissible.


=== Not Established / Unexamined on Merits ===


* The substantive merits of the defamation accusation were not examined by the Supreme Court because the criminal prosecution was rendered formally defective from the outset.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Importance of Procedural Categorization Order: This landmark ruling guarantees legal certainty ensuring law enforcement agencies (Investigators, Prosecutors, Courts) do not bypass procedural law for trial simplification, which risks sacrificing a Defendant's defense rights.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Can a defamation criminal case under Article 310 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code be examined via rapid trials (*tipiring*) by the Police and District Court?'''


'''A:''' No, it cannot. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 731 K/Pid/1984, Article 310 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code carries a maximum imprisonment penalty of 9 months. Because the sentencing threat exceeds 3 months' imprisonment, the case must mandatorily be examined via Summary Examination Procedures rather than Rapid Procedures (Article 205 KUHAP). If forced into Rapid Procedures, the Investigator's/Prosecutor's prosecution must be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 736 K/Pid/1988, dated October 25, 1990, established a criminal procedural law rule concerning the technique of drafting and formulating sentencing verdict dictums (*amar putusan pemidanaan*):


In a court's verdict dictum, it is sufficient to state that the Defendant is legally and convincingly proven guilty of committing a crime (e.g., "possessing, keeping, displaying, using, and providing for use measuring instruments, measures, scales, or equipment lacking a valid active verification stamp..."). The specific articles and laws violated DO NOT NEED to be listed within the verdict dictum itself (instead, they are to be included in the legal considerations section and the "Considering" (*Mengingat*) opening recitals).


== Executive Summary ==


The central procedural principle established in this decision is that criminal sentencing dictums (*amar*) must focus cleanly on declaring guilt and stating the crime's legal qualification, omitting repetitive statutory article citations which belong properly in the legal considerations.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Verdict dictums require declarations of proven guilt and descriptive crime qualifications rather than statutory article listings.
* Statutory citations must be confined to the legal considerations and opening recitals of the judgment.
* Lower court judgments including statutory articles within dictums are subject to corrective formatting modifications on cassation.


== Case Background ==


The Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation, '''[Defendant]''' ([age removed], Civil Servant), was charged with violating Article 25 sub b in conjunction with Article 32 paragraph (1) of Law No. 2 of 1981 on Legal Metrology for providing and using a 10 kg table scale lacking a valid active verification stamp for the year 1987 at his shop in Payakumbuh. 


The Payakumbuh District Court (Decision No. 73/S/38/1987/PN.Pyk dated October 31, 1987) convicted the Defendant, sentencing him to a fine of Rp 100,000.— subsidiary to 3 months' confinement and confiscating the scale, while incorporating contradictory phrasing and statutory articles within the verdict dictum. The Padang High Court (Decision No. 108/Pid.S/1987/PT.Pdg dated December 22, 1987) modified the dictum qualification. The Defendant subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.


== Claims, Evidence and Source Mapping ==


{| class="wikitable"

! Legal Statement / Fact
! Evidence / Judicial Consideration
! Source
|-
| '''1'''
| '''Primary Legal Principle (Verdict Drafting):''' In verdict dictums, it is sufficient to state crime qualifications; violated articles and laws need not be listed in the dictum.
| Jurisprudence Headnote page 181: "In the verdict dictum it is sufficient to state that the defendant is legally and convincingly proven guilty of committing a crime... The articles and laws violated need not be listed in the verdict dictum."
| 736K_Pid_1988.pdf, Passage 1
|-
| '''2'''
| '''Facts of Legal Metrology Violation:''' Defendant [Defendant] provided and used a 10 kg table scale at his shop in Payakumbuh lacking a valid verification stamp for 1987 (bearing only a 1982 stamp / "P" mark).
| District Court Posita & Witness [Witness], SH testimonies pages 183, 195, 196: Scale inspection on May 22, 1987, found a 10 kg table scale at Defendant's shop bearing only the "P" mark (1982 stamp), whereas the valid 1987 verification mark was "87".
| 736K_Pid_1988.pdf, Passages 3, 14, 15, and 16
|-
| '''3'''
| '''Error in Lower Court Dictum Formulation:''' Payakumbuh District Court included the term "crime/violation" (*kejahatan pelanggaran*) and cited Law No. 2/1981 articles within the verdict dictum, which was corrected by the Supreme Court.
| Supreme Court considerations pages 187, 191, and 192: The Supreme Court modified the Padang High Court and Payakumbuh District Court dictums by removing statutory article citations from the crime qualification within the verdict dictums.
| 736K_Pid_1988.pdf, Passages 4, 7, 11, and 12
|-
| '''4'''
| '''Dismissal of Defendant's Cassation:''' The Defendant's cassation grounds (concerning qualification, fine quantum of Rp 100,000.—, and verification intervals) were rejected because the *Judex Facti* did not misapply the law.
| Supreme Court considerations pages 186 and 187: "that these objections cannot be justified, because the High Court did not misapply the law;"
| 736K_Pid_1988.pdf, Passages 6 and 7
|-

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Format and Technical Formulation of Criminal Verdict Dictums (Judicial Drafting Technique) ===


The primary issue was whether a criminal sentencing judge is legally required to list statute section numbers and statutory names violated by the Defendant within the verdict dictum (*dictum*).


The Supreme Court held that it is unnecessary. The verdict dictum focuses on declaring the proven guilt of the Defendant along with the juridical qualification of the committed crime (e.g., "possessing, keeping, displaying, using, and providing for use measuring instruments, measures, scales, or equipment lacking a valid active verification stamp...") and imposing penalties. The legal basis of violated articles and laws belongs in the opening recitals (*Mengingat*) and legal considerations, eliminating any need to duplicate them inside the verdict dictum.


=== Qualification of Legal Metrology Offenses (Law No. 2 of 1981) ===


Using or providing weighing scales without valid verification stamps constitutes a legal metrology crime ex Article 25 sub b in conjunction with Article 32 paragraph (1) of Law No. 2 of 1981. Using contradictory phrasing such as "crime/violation" (*kejahatan pelanggaran*) in a District Court verdict dictum is a drafting error corrected by the Supreme Court.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the *Judex Facti* (Padang High Court & Payakumbuh District Court) err in formulating verdict dictums by including statutory article numbers and mixed terminology ("crime/violation") within the verdict dictums?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the dictum formulation required correction. The Supreme Court rejected the Defendant's cassation appeal while modifying the judgment to establish a revised dictum containing solely descriptive crime qualifications without statutory article citations.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Payakumbuh District Court & Padang High Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning the scale inspection (*UTTP*) on May 22, 1987, at the shop owned by Defendant [Defendant] at [address removed], Payakumbuh; seizure of 1 table scale with a 10 kg capacity bearing only a 1982 verification stamp ("P" mark) lacking the valid 1987 verification mark ("87"); and imposition of a fine of Rp 100,000.— subsidiary to 3 months' confinement.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The appellate and district *Judex Facti* did not misapply the law regarding the establishment of the Defendant's guilt.
# However, regarding the drafting technique of sentencing verdict dictums, the Supreme Court affirmed that in verdict dictums it is sufficient to state that the Defendant is legally and convincingly proven guilty of committing a crime (along with its descriptive qualification). Statutory articles and laws violated need not be listed in the verdict dictum.
# The Supreme Court rejected the Defendant's cassation appeal while modifying the judgment to establish a clean verdict dictum.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court ruled: Rejecting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Defendant]'''); Modifying the ruling of Padang High Court Decision No. 108/Pid.S/1987/PT.Pdg dated December 22, 1987, solely regarding considerations to read: Declaring Defendant [Defendant] proven legally and convincingly guilty of committing the crime of "Possessing, keeping, displaying, using, and providing for use measuring instruments, measures, scales, or equipment lacking a valid active verification stamp or alternatively accompanied by valid endorsement descriptions"; Ordering Petitioner for Cassation to pay cassation court costs amounting to Rp 2,500.—.


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Law No. 2 of 1981 on Legal Metrology:''' Articles 25 sub b and 32 paragraph (1) (Criminal Penalties for Scales/Measuring Instruments Without Valid Verification).
* '''Law No. 8 of 1981 on Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP):''' Article 197 (Mandatory Formal Requirements of Sentencing Judgments).
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 in conjunction with Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Authority to rectify judgment formulation errors.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* Defendant [Defendant] was proven legally and convincingly guilty of committing the crime of "possessing, keeping, displaying, using, and providing for use measuring instruments, measures, scales, or equipment lacking a valid active verification stamp".
* The 10 kg table scale seized at the Defendant's shop lacked a valid verification mark for 1987.
* The Defendant was sentenced to a fine of Rp 100,000.— subsidiary to 3 months' confinement, and the scale evidence was confiscated for the State.


=== Not Established / Modified on Cassation ===


* Listing statutory article numbers within verdict dictums was established as legally unnecessary and removed from the textual dictum.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Standardization of Criminal Verdict Dictum Formulations: This landmark ruling provides guidelines for judges across Indonesia to maintain neatness and standardization in verdict dictums: dictums contain crime qualifications and penalties, whereas statutory norms belong in recitals and considerations.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Is a judge required to write statutory articles within the criminal verdict dictum (*amar*) of a judgment?'''


'''A:''' No, it is unnecessary. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 736 K/Pid/1988, in a criminal verdict dictum it is sufficient to state that the Defendant is legally and convincingly proven guilty of committing a crime along with its descriptive qualification. Violated statutory articles and laws are to be stated in legal considerations and opening recitals (*Mengingat*), and need not be written inside the text of the verdict dictum.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 753 K/Pdt/2000, dated August 15, 2002, established a Batak customary law rule (Batak Toba) concerning the validity of land rights given as marriage gifts (*[Party A]* / *Ulos Nasora Buruk*):


The transfer of wet-rice fields (*sawah*) by parents (father and mother) to their newly married daughter as livelihood provision witnessed by customary elders (*pengetua adat*) is valid and justified under Batak Customary Law (*[Party A]*). The ownership rights over such rice fields constitute the lawful property of the daughter, making the unilateral occupation by her stepmother and children from another marriage without permission an Unlawful Act (*Onrechtmatige Daad*).


== Executive Summary ==


The central customary law principle established in this decision is that traditional property transfers from parents to newly married daughters as wedding provisions under customary witness oversight create absolute, legally protected ownership rights.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Rice fields gifted by parents to newly married daughters (*[Party A]*) under customary supervision are valid and legally binding.
* Subsequent attempts by stepfamily members to seize gifted customary marriage land constitute unlawful acts.
* Appellate court rulings dismissing substantiated customary property rights are subject to reversal on cassation.


== Case Background ==


The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation, '''[Party B]''', filed a lawsuit at the Pematang Siantar District Court against the Original Defendants / Respondents for Cassation (1. [Party C] — second wife of late Gading Panjaitan, 2. Marojahan Panjaitan, 3. Pungu Panjaitan). The Plaintiff alleged that a wet-rice field measuring ± 3 rante located in Dusun Panjaitan, Nagahuta Village, Siantar Marihat District, Pematang Siantar, belonged to her based on a marriage gift (*[Party A]* / *Ulos Nasora Buruk*) from her parents in 1968 witnessed by customary elders. However, since 1995, the Defendants had occupied and cultivated the rice field without permission. 


The Pematang Siantar District Court (Decision No. 14/Pdt.G/1998/PN.Pms dated December 3, 1998) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part. The Medan High Court (Decision No. 83/Pdt/1999/PT.Mdn dated June 2, 1999) annulled the district court decision and dismissed the Plaintiff's lawsuit entirely. The Petitioner for Cassation subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Validity of Ownership Rights over Rice Fields as Marriage Gifts (*[Party A]*) in Batak Customary Law ===


The primary issue was whether wet-rice fields given by parents to their newly married daughter as a marriage gift (*[Party A]* / *Ulos Nasora Buruk*), witnessed by customary elders, are legally binding and constitute the daughter's lawful ownership rights.


The Supreme Court held that they are valid and legally binding. Under Batak Toba Customary Law, transferring land/rice fields from parents to a newly married daughter as livelihood support (*[Party A]*) represents a parental gesture of affection executed under the oversight of customary elders. Such property rights cannot be arbitrarily revoked or unlawfully seized by other heirs or secondary spouses of the deceased parents.


=== Misinterpretation of Customary Law by Appellate Judex Facti (Medan High Court) ===


The Medan High Court erred by dismissing the Plaintiff's lawsuit on the grounds that the Plaintiff failed to prove her land acquisition. The Supreme Court ruled that the Medan High Court misapplied the law of evidence (*foutieve kepassing van het bewijsrecht*). Because the Plaintiff established the transfer of the ± 3 rante rice field through witness testimonies from the 1968 customary ceremony, the appellate court's skepticism toward the customary acquisition was legally flawed.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the Medan High Court misapply Batak customary law and the law of evidence (*foutieve kepassing van het recht*) by dismissing the Plaintiff's lawsuit, despite the gift of rice fields as a marriage gift (*[Party A]*) being proven validly under custom?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the Medan High Court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court annulled Medan High Court Decision No. 83/Pdt/1999/PT.Mdn and adjudicated afresh, declaring the Defendants' actions to be unlawful acts and confirming the Plaintiff's ownership over the disputed rice field.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Pematang Siantar District Court & Medan High Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning the transfer of the ± 3 rante rice field during the 1968 wedding ceremony in Dusun Panjaitan; pledging (*menggadaikan*) of the rice field by the Plaintiff to Oppu Si Ridwan Br. Simanjuntak in 1987; usurpation of rice field possession by Defendants I, II, and III starting in 1995; and physical boundary details of the disputed land.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The appellate *Judex Facti* of Medan High Court misapplied the law of evidence and Batak customary law. Based on evidence and testimonies, the transfer of the ± 3 rante rice field from the Plaintiff's late parents to the Plaintiff in 1968 witnessed by customary elders was established.
# Pursuant to Batak Customary Law, this gift served as parental affection for a newly married daughter as livelihood provision (*[Party A]*).
# Consequently, the Defendants' unauthorized occupation of the rice field constituted an unlawful act.
# The Supreme Court annulled the Medan High Court decision and adjudicated afresh, granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part, declaring ownership rights, ordering property surrender, and awarding damages.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Party B]'''); annulled Medan High Court Decision No. 83/Pdt/1999/PT.Mdn dated June 2, 1999; and ADJUDICATED AFRESH: 1. Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part; 2. Declaring that the Defendants committed an unlawful act (*Onrechtmatige daad*); 3. Declaring that the disputed rice field measuring ± 3 rante (East: Tumpal Br. Simanjuntak, West: Tirosma Br. Panjaitan, North: Bonder, South: Late Gading Panjaitan) is the right and property of the Plaintiff; 4. Ordering Defendants I, II, and III to surrender the disputed rice field to the Plaintiff in good, vacant condition free of encumbrances; 5. Ordering Defendants I, II, and III to pay damages amounting to 120 cans of local dry paddy per year starting from the registration of the case at the Pematang Siantar District Court; 6. Rejecting all other claims; and ordering the Respondents for Cassation to pay court costs across all judicial instances (cassation court costs set at Rp 100,000.—).


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Batak Toba Customary Law:''' Doctrine of *[Party A]* / *Ulos Nasora Buruk* / *Pauseang* / *Saba Bangunan*: Customary legal institutions governing land/rice field gifts from maternal/paternal relatives (*Hula-hula*) or parents to daughters/spouses as permanent, inviolable livelihood provisions.
* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata):''' Article 1365: Unlawful Acts (*Onrechtmatige Daad*) concerning unauthorized land possession.
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 in conjunction with Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Authority to rectify misapplications of law by the *Judex Facti*.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* The Plaintiff ([Party B]) received a gift of wet-rice land measuring ± 3 rante from her parents (late Gading Panjaitan and late Kamelia Br. Omppusunggu) in 1968 witnessed by customary elders.
* This gift institution is validly recognized under Batak Customary Law as *[Party A]*.
* The Defendants ([Party C], Marojahan Panjaitan, Pungu Panjaitan) occupied the disputed rice field without right and without the Plaintiff's permission starting in 1995.
* The Defendants were ordered to surrender the rice field in vacant condition and pay damages of 120 cans of local dry paddy per year starting from the initial district court filing.


=== Not Established / Set Aside ===


* The Defendants' argument asserting that the disputed rice field constituted estate property freely controllable by the second wife and her children was set aside and rejected by the Supreme Court.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Affirmation of Women's Land Rights Protection under Customary Law: This landmark ruling provides robust legal certainty safeguarding the civil property rights of Batak women over customary marriage gifts (*[Party A]*), dismantling unilateral claims by other heirs attempting to repossess marriage gift lands.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Is the gift of rice fields from parents to a newly married daughter ([Party A]) valid under Batak Customary Law?'''


'''A:''' Valid and legally binding. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 753 K/Pdt/2000, rice fields given by parents to a newly married daughter as livelihood provision (*[Party A]* / *Ulos Nasora Buruk*) witnessed by customary elders are justified and valid under Batak Customary Law. Such rice fields become the full property of the daughter, and unilateral occupation by other family members without permission qualifies as an Unlawful Act.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 75 K/AG/2003 dated May 14, 2004, establishes two fundamental legal rules in Islamic Civil Procedure Law and Islamic Grant Law:

* '''Scope of Application of Law No. 20 of 1947:''' Law No. 20 of 1947 is a specialized statute governing appellate proceedings (*peradilan ulangan*); hence, the provisions of Article 7 paragraph (1) of Law No. 20 of 1947 cannot be applied to the formal requirements for drafting or signing statements of claim (*surat gugat*) at the first-instance court level.
* '''Obligation to Detail Total Assets in Grant Lawsuits (Obscuur Libel):''' Before applying the provisions of Article 210 paragraph (1) of the Compilation of Islamic Law (KHI), which restricts grants to a maximum of one-third of the grantor's estate, a plaintiff is legally obligated to describe and detail the total overall assets belonging to the grantor within the statement of claim. If the statement of claim fails to specify or itemize the grantor's total estate, leaving it unclear whether the grant exceeds the one-third estate limit, the lawsuit is deemed obscure (*obscuur libel*) and must be declared inadmissible (*niet ontvankelijke verklaard*).

== Case Background ==

The married couple H. Tuganal and [Party B] passed away in 2001 in Tembilahan, Indragiri Hilir. Each brought children from prior marriages: H. Tuganal was survived by [Party A] and Zaidah, while [Party B] was survived by Susiati and Yuniasih. During his lifetime, H. Tuganal granted a plot of land measuring 147.6 m² complete with a wooden house located at Jalan Jend. Sudirman, Tembilahan, to his wife ([Party B]) on May 17, 2001, pursuant to which Building Use Rights Certificate (*HGB*) No. 558 was issued. Following the deaths of both H. Tuganal and [Party B], the land and house were occupied by H. Tuganal's children ([Party A], Zaidah, et al.).

Susiati and Yuniasih ([Party B]'s children / Plaintiffs) filed a lawsuit at the Tembilahan Religious Court. The Tembilahan Religious Court (Decision No. 20/Pdt.G/2002/PA.Tbh dated May 16, 2002) granted the Plaintiffs' lawsuit in part and declared H. Tuganal's grant to [Party B] valid. However, the Riau High Religious Court (Decision No. 27/Pdt.G/2002/PTA.Pbr dated August 24, 2002) annulled the Tembilahan Religious Court decision and declared the Plaintiffs' lawsuit inadmissible on the grounds of formal power of attorney signing defects pursuant to Law No. 20 of 1947. Dissatisfied with the appellate ruling, the Plaintiffs (Susiati and Yuniasih) filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# Law No. 20 of 1947 is a statute enacted for appellate-level proceedings; therefore, Article 7 paragraph (1) thereof cannot be applied to the drafting of statements of claim at the first-instance level.
# Prior to applying Article 210 paragraph (1) of the KHI, the Plaintiff must first establish the total aggregate amount of the grantor's estate to determine whether the contested grant exceeds the one-third limit of the grantor's assets.
# Because the statement of claim fails to clarify whether the disputed property constituted the sole asset of the grantor or whether other assets existed, making it impossible to ascertain whether the grant exceeded one-third of the grantor's estate, the lawsuit is legally obscure (*obscuur libel*) and must be declared inadmissible (*niet ontvankelijke verklaard*).
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioners for Cassation SUSIATI and YUNIASIH; Annulling the Riau High Religious Court decision dated August 24, 2002, No. 27/Pdt.G/2002/PTA.Pbr and the Tembilahan Religious Court decision dated May 16, 2002, No. 20/Pdt.G/2002/PA.Tbh; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Declaring that the Plaintiffs' lawsuit is inadmissible; (2) Declaring that the Confiscation Security (*Sita Jaminan*) executed by the Tembilahan Religious Court is invalid and devoid of legal force; (3) Ordering the Tembilahan Religious Court to lift the said Confiscation Security; (4) Ordering the Defendants to pay first-instance court costs amounting to Rp 1,623,500; (5) Ordering the Appellee to pay appellate-level court costs amounting to Rp 107,000; (6) Ordering the Petitioner for Cassation to pay cassation-level court costs amounting to Rp 500,000.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Judicial Review (*Peninjauan Kembali / PK*) Decision No. 78 PK/Pid/2000 annulled the Supreme Court Cassation Decision No. 1 K/Pid/2000 dated September 22, 2000, and acquitted the Petitioner for PK / Convict [Defendant] of all charges brought by the Public Prosecutor concerning the corruption case involving the asset swap (*ruilslag*) between the National Logistics Agency (Bulog) and PT Goro Batara Sakti. The Supreme Court established the legal rule that an individual serving as a Commissioner of a limited liability company cannot be held criminally liable for unlawful acts committed by the company's Board of Directors, and a Commissioner's approval given to the Board of Directors within the boundaries of supervisory authority pursuant to Law No. 1 of 1995 on Limited Liability Companies does not constitute a criminal unlawful act.

== Case Background ==

The Defendant, [Defendant] (President Commissioner / shareholder of PT Goro Batara Sakti), was indicted jointly with H.M. Ricardo Gelael (President Director of PT Goro Batara Sakti) and Prof. DR. Ir. Beddu Amang, MA (Head of Bulog) for committing corruption in annuity with the execution of the land/warehouse asset swap (*ruilslag*) belonging to Bulog in Kelapa Gading, North Jakarta, with replacement land assets in Marunda, North Jakarta, which caused financial losses to the State cq. Bulog amounting to Rp 95,407,486,000.

The South Jakarta District Court (Decision No. 198/Pid.B/1999/PN.Jak.Sel. dated October 14, 1999) ruled that the charged acts were proven but constituted a civil legal relationship (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging* / released from all legal prosecutions). Upon the Public Prosecutor's cassation appeal, the Supreme Court at the Cassation level (Decision No. 1 K/Pid/2000 dated September 22, 2000) annulled the South Jakarta District Court decision, independently adjudicated the matter, declared the Defendant guilty of continuous corruption, and sentenced him to 1 (one) year and 6 (six) months of imprisonment, a fine of Rp 10,000,000, and restitution of Rp 30,680,306,400. The Defendant subsequently filed a petition for Judicial Review (*PK*) to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# An individual who no longer holds office as a Commissioner of a company cannot be held accountable for unlawful acts committed by that company, let alone actions occurring prior to or during their tenure if outside personal operational execution.
# The legal act of *ruilslag* was executed by the Board of Directors of PT Goro Batara Sakti (Ricardo Gelael) acting for and on behalf of the company, whereas the Defendant served as President Commissioner whose fundamental function under the Deed of Incorporation jo. Article 100 of Law No. 1 of 1995 on Limited Liability Companies is to perform supervision over the management of the company run by the Board of Directors. A Commissioner does not manage the operational affairs of the company and cannot be held criminally liable for the actions of the Board of Directors.
# The approval granted by a Commissioner to the Board of Directors to execute certain legal actions does not contravene Article 100 paragraph (1) of Law No. 1 of 1995 on Limited Liability Companies, and no unlawful act was proven under Article 1(1) sub a jo. Article 28 of Law No. 3 of 1971 jo. Article 55(1) item 1 jo. Article 64(1) of the KUHP.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the petition for Judicial Review (*PK*) from Petitioner for Judicial Review / Convict [Defendant]; Annulling the Supreme Court decision dated September 22, 2000, No. 1 K/Pid/2000; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Declaring the guilt of Defendant [Defendant] regarding the acts charged against him NOT PROVEN legally and convincingly; (2) Acquitting the Defendant of all charges brought by the Public Prosecutor (*vrijspraak*); (3) Ordering the restoration of the Defendant's rights in capacity, position, honor, and dignity; (4) Ordering that evidence items in the form of documents be returned to the Public Prosecutor to be utilized in other proceedings; (5) Charging procedural costs in this Judicial Review examination to the State.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 792 K/Pdt/2002, dated January 3, 2003, established a fundamental law of obligations and settlement deed (*dading*) rule concerning the validity of settlement deeds signed by parties under criminal detention:


A settlement agreement agreed upon by both parties without coercion, where both parties possess legal capacity to contract, remains VALID and legally binding even though one party is under detention (detained on criminal charges). Lawful detention executed pursuant to judicial/penal authority (*jus/auctoritas judicis*) cannot be equated automatically with coercion (*dwang*) or abuse of circumstances (*misbruik van omstandigheden*) under Article 1320 in conjunction with Articles 1323–1327 and Article 1859 of the Civil Code, provided that the execution of the deed before a Notary is conducted freely and without unlawful physical or psychological coercion.


The Supreme Court annulled Bandung High Court Decision No. 69/Pdt/2001/PT.Bdg and adjudicated afresh by affirming the considerations and rulings of Bale Bandung District Court Decision No. 47/Pdt.G/2000/PN.BB, which rejected the lawsuit seeking the annulment of the settlement deed.


== Executive Summary ==


The central legal principle established in this decision is that lawful criminal detention does not deprive a detainee of legal capacity to enter into binding civil settlement contracts voluntarily.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Settlement deeds signed by detainees before a notary are fully valid if executed freely without unlawful coercion.
* Lawful judicial detention under criminal procedure does not constitute civil coercion (*dwang*) or abuse of circumstances.
* Appellate court rulings invalidating settlement deeds based on detention status commit reversible errors of law.


== Case Background ==


The Original Plaintiff / Respondent for Review ('''[Party A]''') filed a lawsuit at the Bale Bandung District Court against the Original Defendant I / Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Party B]'''), Co-Respondent I / Defendant II ([Party C]), and Co-Respondent II / Co-Defendant (Notary [Notary], S.H.). The Plaintiff sought the annulment of Settlement Deed No. 18 dated August 7, 1999, executed before Notary [Notary], S.H., arguing that the deed was signed while the Plaintiff was detained at Kebonwaru Detention Center on alleged embezzlement/fraud charges involving PT Bintang Laju Sentosa capital, thereby alleging coercion/abuse of circumstances (*misbruik van omstandigheden*). 


The Bale Bandung District Court (Decision No. 47/Pdt.G/2000/PN.BB dated September 5, 2000) rejected the Plaintiff's convention lawsuit entirely and granted the reconvention lawsuit in part, ordering the Plaintiff to pay remaining debt of Rp 100,000,000.—. The Bandung High Court (Decision No. 69/Pdt/2001/PT.Bdg dated May 9, 2001) annulled the district court decision and invalidated Settlement Deed No. 18. The Petitioner for Cassation ([Party B]) subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.


== Claims, Evidence and Source Mapping ==


{| class="wikitable"
! No.
! Legal Statement / Fact
! Evidence / Judicial Consideration
! Source
|-
| '''1'''

| Headnote & Supreme Court considerations pages 134, 135, and 151: "A Settlement Agreement agreed upon by both parties, without coercion and where parties are capable of making agreements, although one party is under detention status, such agreement is valid;"
| 792K_PDT_2002.pdf, Passages 1, 2, and 18
|-
| '''2'''
| '''Legal Capacity of Detainees (Article 1330 Civil Code):''' Accused individuals/detainees are not categorized as legally incapable subjects under the law to form agreements.
| Supreme Court considerations pages 135 and 151: "...based on witness testimonies... it is proven that a settlement occurred... without coercion... the respondent for cassation at the time of signing although under detention status was legally capable of making agreements, because he is not categorized as legally incapable as determined in Article 1330 of the Civil Code;"
| 792K_PDT_2002.pdf, Passages 2 and 18
|-
| '''3'''
| '''Lawful Detention Not Unlawful Coercion:''' Criminal detention pursuant to law/judicial orders (Article 20 KUHAP) does not constitute abuse of circumstances or civil coercion.
| Cassation Memorandum & Supreme Court considerations pages 146, 147, and 151: Detention of the Plaintiff was a lawful judicial action, and therefore cannot be equated with coercion (*dwang*) ex Articles 1323–1327 of the Civil Code.
| 792K_PDT_2002.pdf, Passages 13, 14, and 18
|-
| '''4'''
| '''Facts of Deed No. 18 Execution (Aug 7, 1999):''' Executed before Notary [Notary], S.H. pursuant to a prisoner temporary release (*bon*) permit from the Bale Bandung District Court Judge No. 292/Pid.B/1999/PN.BB.
| Posita & Documentary Evidence pages 138, 139, 158, and 173: Signing was conducted upon the Plaintiff's wife's request and judge's temporary release permit to settle before the Notary.
| 792K_PDT_2002.pdf, Passages 5, 6, 25, and 40
|-

| Supreme Court Cassation Ruling pages 135 and 152: "Annulling Bandung High Court decision... ADJUDICATING AFRESH... In Convention: Rejecting plaintiff's lawsuit entirely; In Reconvention: Granting reconvention lawsuit in part..."
| 792K_PDT_2002.pdf, Passages 2, 3, and 19
|}


== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Testing Vitiated Consent (*Misbruik van Omstandigheden* / Coercion) in Settlement Deeds Signed by Criminal Detainees ===


The primary issue was whether the execution of a Settlement Deed (*dading*) before a Notary by a Defendant under detention in a detention center is automatically void *ab initio* on the grounds of containing coercion (*dwang*) or abuse of circumstances (*misbruik van omstandigheden*) ex Articles 1320, 1323–1327, and Article 1859 of the Civil Code.


The Supreme Court held that it is not void / remains valid. Lawful detention executed by law enforcement agencies pursuant to the Criminal Procedure Code (*KUHAP*) constitutes a judicial act (*judicial action*) that cannot be qualified as unlawful coercion or abuse of circumstances. Individuals under criminal detention retain legal capacity (*bekwaamheit*) under Article 1330 of the Civil Code. When a settlement deed is read, agreed upon, and signed before a Notary without physical force or unlawful threats, the settlement agreement is valid and binding upon the parties.


=== Judicial Error by Appellate Judex Facti (Bandung High Court) ===


The Bandung High Court (Decision No. 69/Pdt/2001/PT.Bdg) misapplied the law by aprioristically institutionalizing criminal detention as civil coercion. The Supreme Court rectified this error, affirming party autonomy which remains fully effective even under criminal detention status.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the Bandung High Court misapply the law of obligations (*foutieve kepassing van het recht*) ex Article 1320 jo. Articles 1323–1327 and Article 1859 of the Civil Code by assuming that criminal detention status automatically negates free will and voids a Settlement Deed?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the Bandung High Court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court annulled Bandung High Court Decision No. 69/Pdt/2001/PT.Bdg and adjudicated afresh by affirming Bale Bandung District Court Decision No. 47/Pdt.G/2000/PN.BB, declaring Settlement Deed No. 18 dated August 7, 1999, valid and binding.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Bale Bandung District Court & Bandung High Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning business cooperation under PT Bintang Laju Sentosa (Deeds No. 3 dated May 18, 1990, and Sept 1, 1995); criminal fraud/embezzlement reports at Bandung Police Resort; detention of [Party A] at Kebonwaru Detention Center (June 10 to August 18, 1999); temporary prisoner release applications filed by the Defendant's wife ([Party D]); execution of Deed No. 18 at Notary [Notary], S.H.'s office; testimonies of witnesses ([Party D], Bambang Haryanto, Eddy Rahmad, Johan Kristianto, Jo Sauw Hong); and rejection of BDN/Bank Mandiri Check of Rp 100,000,000.— due to insufficient funds.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The appellate *Judex Facti* of Bandung High Court misapplied the law of obligations. Based on sworn witness testimonies, a settlement agreement was established between parties without coercion as defined under Article 1324 jo. Article 1859 Civil Code.
# The Respondent for Cassation ([Party A]) at the time of signing, although under criminal detention status, maintained full legal capacity under Article 1330 Civil Code to enter into contracts.
# Lawful detention for criminal investigation purposes under procedural law does not constitute coercion or abuse of circumstances invalidating deeds.
# The Supreme Court annulled the Bandung High Court decision and adjudicated afresh, rejecting the Original Plaintiff's convention lawsuit entirely and affirming the Bale Bandung District Court ruling.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Party B]'''); annulled Bandung High Court Decision No. 69/Pdt/2001/PT.Bdg dated May 9, 2001, which had annulled Bale Bandung District Court Decision No. 47/Pdt.G/2000/PN.BB dated September 5, 2000; and ADJUDICATED AFRESH: IN CONVENTION: Under the Merits: Rejecting the Plaintiff's lawsuit entirely; IN RECONVENTION: Granting the Reconvention Lawsuit / Defendant I Convention's lawsuit in part; Declaring that the Defendant in Reconvention is indebted to the corporation and ordering payment to Original Plaintiff I in Reconvention of remaining debt amounting to Rp 100,000,000.— out of a total debt of Rp 165,420,429.—; Declaring that the Defendant in Reconvention committed default or unlawful acts; Declaring the protective attachment (*sita jaminan*) orders and minutes null and void; IN CONVENTION AND RECONVENTION: Ordering the Respondent for Cassation / Original Plaintiff to pay court costs across all judicial instances (cassation court costs set at Rp 200,000.—).


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata):'''
  * Article 1320: Essential requirements for valid contracts (Consent, Capacity, Specified Object, Lawful Cause).
  * Articles 1323 through 1327: Vitiated consent due to Coercion (*Dwang*).
  * Article 1330: Legally Incapacitated Persons (Minors, under curatorship, etc. — Criminal detainees are not included).
  * Articles 1851 & 1859: Validity and Annulment of Settlement Deeds (*Dading*).
* '''Law No. 8 of 1981 on Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP):''' Article 20: Judicial detention authority for examination purposes.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* [Party A] signed Settlement Deed No. 18 dated August 7, 1999, before Notary [Notary], S.H., pursuant to an official temporary release permit (*bon*) from the Bale Bandung District Court.
* The execution of the settlement deed was performed voluntarily, read beforehand, and witnessed by independent witnesses without physical coercion or unlawful threats.
* [Party A] possessed legal capacity under Article 1330 Civil Code to execute contracts.
* The Defendant in Reconvention / [Party A] was proven to maintain remaining debt obligations of Rp 100,000,000.— owed to the corporation / Original Plaintiff I in Reconvention.


=== Not Established / Rejected ===


* The Convention Plaintiff's argument asserting that the execution of the settlement deed occurred under unlawful coercion (*dwang*) or abuse of circumstances (*misbruik van omstandigheden*) was unproven and set aside by the Supreme Court.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Strict Distinction Between Lawful Detention and Civil Coercion: This landmark ruling establishes a clear legal boundary: lawful criminal detention cannot be used by debtors or suspected offenders as a pretext to invalidate settlement deeds voluntarily signed to resolve civil obligations and business capital losses.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Is a settlement agreement signed before a Notary by a person detained in a detention center (*Rutan*) valid under civil law?'''


'''A:''' Valid and legally binding. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 792 K/Pdt/2002, a settlement agreement agreed upon by parties without coercion where parties possess legal capacity under the law is valid, even though one party is under criminal detention status. Lawful detention pursuant to criminal procedural law does not constitute coercion (*dwang*) or abuse of circumstances (*misbruik van omstandigheden*) invalidating settlement deeds.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 808 K/Pid/1984 established a fundamental criminal procedural law rule concerning the material requirements for the validity of a Public Prosecutor's indictment:


A Public Prosecutor's indictment that is imprecise, unclear, and incomplete regarding the description of criminal events, dates, locations, and the qualification of the charged offenses (*obscuur libel*) MUST BE DECLARED NULL AND VOID (*BATAL DEMI HUKUM*). The Public Prosecutor may not obscure civil debt-dispute matters involving collateral security (*borg*) into criminal embezzlement offenses without formulating factual elements of unlawful acts precisely, clearly, and completely.


== Executive Summary ==


The central procedural principle established in this decision is that blurring the lines between civil debt disputes and criminal offenses through defective, vague indictments renders the entire prosecution legally null and void (*batal demi hukum*).


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Indictments lacking precision, clarity, and completeness regarding dates, places, and legal qualifications are null and void under criminal procedure code provisions.
* Creditor possession of collateral stemming from loan agreements constitutes a civil matter rather than criminal embezzlement.
* Appellate and district judgments upholding deficient indictments are subject to complete reversal on cassation.


== Case Background ==


The Original Defendants (Defendant I: '''[Defendant I] alias [Witness] alias Ny. [Defendant]''', [age removed], merchant; Defendant II: '''[Defendant II]''', [age removed], merchant) were charged with embezzling diamond jewelry belonging to witness Ny. [Witness B] (Article 372 jo. 55 KUHP) and/or conducting unauthorized banking operations (Law No. 14/1967). Evidence established that the underlying legal relationship was a money loan agreement of Rp 1,000,000.— by Ny. [Witness B] to Defendant I secured by diamond jewelry. 


The Pati District Court (Decision No. 491/1981/Pid.S dated April 13, 1982) convicted Defendant I to 9 months' imprisonment and Defendant II to 1 year's imprisonment. The Semarang High Court (Decision No. 225/1982/Pid/P.T.Smg dated January 16, 1984) affirmed the conviction with modifications. The Defendants subsequently filed cassation petitions with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Material Requirements of Indictments and Consequences of Nullity (*Obscuur Libel* ex Article 143 KUHAP / Article 282 HIR) ===


The primary issue was whether a Public Prosecutor's indictment that obscures boundaries between civil loan-collateral disputes and criminal embezzlement—failing to describe the unlawful acts of each Defendant with precision, clarity, and completeness—is valid under the law.


The Supreme Court held that it is null and void (*Batal Demi Hukum*). A Public Prosecutor's indictment failing to precisely formulate crime elements, times, places, and specific roles of Defendants constitutes a substantially defective indictment (*obscuur libel*). Prosecutors are prohibited from framing civil loan contract disputes as criminal embezzlement without precise factual descriptions, requiring the indictment to be declared null and void.


=== Distinguishing Civil Default in Pledges/Collateral from Criminal Embezzlement (Article 372 KUHP) ===


Creditor possession of collateral (*borg*) arising from loan agreements constitutes possession based strictly on a pure civil relationship. Disputes regarding debt repayment, interest calculations, and collateral return must be resolved within the civil domain and cannot be criminalized as embezzlement.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Does a Public Prosecutor's indictment formulating criminal embezzlement imprecisely, unclearly, and incompletely over a secured loan dispute satisfy statutory criteria for nullity (*batal demi hukum*) ex Article 143 KUHAP / HIR?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes. The Supreme Court annulled the Semarang High Court and Pati District Court decisions, declaring the Public Prosecutor's indictment null and void (*batal demi hukum*).


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Pati District Court & Semarang High Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning the Rp 1,000,000.— loan by Ny. [Witness B] / Pak [Witness B] to Defendant I ([Witness]) secured by diamond jewelry belonging to Ny. Mitro which was subsequently substituted; delivery of ransom/deposit funds of Rp 1,400,000.— before Defendant II ([Defendant]); and the background of social unrest/racial issues in Tayu/Pati in 1980.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The *Judex Facti* of Semarang High Court and Pati District Court misapplied the law.
# The indictment formulated by the Public Prosecutor failed to formulate criminal facts with precision, clarity, and completeness regarding crime qualifications and the roles of individual Defendants, while obscuring a secured debt dispute into a criminal embezzlement charge.
# Pursuant to criminal procedural provisions (Article 143 KUHAP / Article 282 HIR), an imprecise, unclear, and incomplete indictment is Null and Void (*Batal Demi Hukum*).
# The Supreme Court annulled lower court rulings and declared the Public Prosecutor's indictment null and void.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Petitioners for Cassation (Defendant I: '''[Defendant I] alias [Witness] alias NY. [Defendant]''' and Defendant II: '''[Defendant II]'''); annulled Semarang High Court Decision No. 225/1982/Pid/P.T.Smg dated January 16, 1984, in conjunction with Pati District Court Decision No. 491/1981/Pid.S dated April 13, 1982; and ADJUDICATED AFRESH: Declaring the Public Prosecutor's Indictment Null and Void (*Batal Demi Hukum*); Ordering the return of evidence to those entitled; and charging the State with court costs across all judicial instances.


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Law No. 8 of 1981 on Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP) / HIR:''' Articles 143 paragraphs (2) & (3) KUHAP / Article 282 HIR regarding material indictment requirements (precise, clear, and complete) and the sanction of nullity (*batal demi hukum*).
* '''Criminal Code (KUHP):''' Articles 372 (Embezzlement) and 55 (Complicity).
* '''Supreme Court Standing Jurisprudence:''' Supreme Court Decision No. 885/K/Sip/1974 (November 26, 1975): Prohibition of forfeiture clauses (*janji milik terban* / automatic collateral execution) in loan agreements.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* The initial legal relationship between the victim witness (Ny. [Witness B]) and Defendant I ([Witness]) was a civil loan agreement of Rp 1,000,000.— secured by jewelry collateral (*borg*).
* The Public Prosecutor's indictment was formulated vaguely, imprecisely, unclearly, and incompletely regarding the alleged criminal acts.


=== Not Established / Nullified ===


* The prosecution failed to prove valid criminal embezzlement because the indictment suffered from formal and material legal defects from the outset.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Prevention of Criminalizing Secured Debt Disputes: This landmark ruling establishes strict boundaries preventing Courts and Public Prosecutors from allowing civil pledge/debt disputes to be dragged into criminal courts via imprecisely drafted indictments.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: What are the legal consequences if a Public Prosecutor's indictment fails to describe criminal acts with precision, clarity, and completeness?'''


'''A:''' Null and Void (*Batal Demi Hukum* / *Obscuur Libel*). Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 808 K/Pid/1984, a Public Prosecutor's indictment failing to state factual actions, times, locations, and crime qualifications with precision, clarity, and completeness is declared null and void. Prosecutors are prohibited from obscuring civil legal relationships (such as loans secured by collateral goods) into criminal embezzlement offenses without precise factual crime formulations.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 818 K/Pid/1984, dated May 30, 1985, established a material criminal law rule concerning the application of offense qualifications for homogenous offenses carrying lighter statutory penalties (*inclusief* / *generics-specifics*):


Although the offense prosecuted by the Public Prosecutor in the indictment is Ordinary Defamation / Slander ex Article 310 of the Criminal Code (KUHP), the Defendant can be found guilty and punished under Article 315 of the Criminal Code (Minor Defamation) if the material factual acts proven at trial fail to satisfy the element of specific attribution of acts (Article 310 KUHP), but instead constitute minor defamation. Because the offense under Article 315 KUHP is a homogenous (sejenis) yet lesser offense carrying a lighter statutory penalty than Article 310 KUHP, such verdict qualification modifications are lawful and affirmed by the Supreme Court without violating the boundaries of prosecution.


== Executive Summary ==


The central legal principle established in this decision is that courts may modify conviction qualifications from ordinary defamation to minor defamation when trial evidence proves general insults rather than specific false imputations, provided both crimes are homogenous.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Indictments charging ordinary defamation under Article 310 KUHP can support convictions under Article 315 KUHP for minor defamation if specific imputations are unproven.
* Homogenous offenses with lighter penalty ceilings permit judicial re-qualification without exceeding prosecutorial bounds.
* Cassation appeals challenging such modifications without showing substantive prejudice are dismissed while formal qualifications are corrected.


== Case Background ==


The Original Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation, '''[Defendant]''' ([age removed], journalist for Harian Analisa), was charged with defamation (Article 310 KUHP) for stating on December 16, 1978, at the Central Market of Medan that Himpunan Pedagang Indonesia (H.P.I.) Rayon I and its board members "smacked of Komando Jihad". 


The Medan District Court (Decision No. 978/KS/1979/PN.Mdn dated May 17, 1979) convicted the Defendant of defamation (Article 310 KUHP) and sentenced him to a fine of Rp 500.— subsidiary to 2 days' confinement. The Medan High Court (Decision No. 206/Pid/1983/PT.Mdn dated December 31, 1983) modified the sentence to 1 month's imprisonment with a 3-month probation period (Article 14a KUHP). The Defendant subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.
