== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Application of the Homogenous Lesser Offense Doctrine (*Inclusief* / *Generics-Specifics*) in Criminal Sentencing ===


The primary issue was whether a Judge is justified in convicting a Defendant under Article 315 of the Criminal Code (Minor Defamation) when the Public Prosecutor's indictment formulates sole prosecution under Article 310 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code (Ordinary Defamation / Slander).


The Supreme Court held that it is justified. When trial evidence fails to prove the specific element of "imputing a specific act to be made public" under Article 310 KUHP, but establishes elements of Minor Defamation under Article 315 KUHP, the Trial Panel holds the authority to sentence the Defendant under Article 315 KUHP. This is grounded on the principle that Article 315 KUHP is a homogenous (homogen) offense sharing core characteristics with Article 310 KUHP while carrying a lighter statutory penalty ceiling, ensuring that qualification adjustments do not violate fair trial principles or exceed prosecution boundaries.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the *Judex Facti* (Medan High Court & Medan District Court) commit a legal qualification error in their verdict dictums by declaring the Defendant guilty of "Defamation/Slander" (Article 310 KUHP), whereas utterances of "smacking of Komando Jihad" without specific act imputation constitute "Minor Defamation" (Article 315 KUHP)?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the lower courts' verdict qualifications required correction. The Supreme Court rejected the Defendant's cassation petition while modifying the judgment to declare the Defendant proven guilty of committing the crime of "Minor Defamation" ex Article 315 of the Criminal Code.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Medan District Court & Medan High Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning the incident on December 16, 1978, around 13:00 WIB at Wahab Merek Horas Kios, 2nd Floor, Mercu Buana Project, Medan Central Market; statements made by Defendant [Defendant] (journalist) regarding "H.P.I. Rayon I Central Market Medan and its board members smelling of Komando Jihad"; and resulting offense/grievance taken by H.P.I. board members (Sutan Lukman et al. and Wahab / Wong Peng Cun).


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The *Judex Facti* did not misapply the law regarding establishing guilt, but erred regarding verdict qualifications.
# The Defendant's acts did not satisfy the specific act imputation requirement ex Article 310 paragraph (1) KUHP, but constituted Minor Defamation ex Article 315 KUHP.
# Although Article 310 KUHP was charged, the Defendant could be found guilty under Article 315 KUHP because Article 315 KUHP constitutes a homogenous yet lesser offense carrying lighter statutory penalties than Article 310 KUHP.
# The Supreme Court rejected the Defendant's cassation petition while modifying the verdict qualification to "Minor Defamation".


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court ruled: Rejecting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation ('''[Defendant]'''); Modifying the ruling of Medan High Court Decision No. 206/Pid/1983/PT.Mdn dated December 31, 1983, and Medan District Court Decision No. 978/KS/1979/PN.Mdn dated May 17, 1979, solely regarding the formulation of proven guilt and qualification dictums to read: Declaring the Defendant legally and convincingly proven guilty of committing the crime of "Minor Defamation"; Ordering the Petitioner for Cassation / Defendant to pay cassation court costs amounting to Rp 2,500.—.


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Criminal Code (KUHP):'''
  * Article 310 paragraph (1): Ordinary Defamation / Slander offense (Imputing specific acts with intent to make public).
  * Article 315: Minor Defamation offense (Insults not amounting to slander).
  * Article 14a: Conditional Sentencing / Probation provisions.
* '''Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP / Law No. 8 of 1981):''' Article 253: Supreme Court cassation review authority over legal application errors.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* Defendant [Defendant] uttered public statements that H.P.I. and its board members "smacked of Komando Jihad" on December 16, 1978.
* These statements wounded the feelings and reputation of H.P.I. board members (Sutan Lukman and Wahab).
* The Defendant's acts legally satisfied elements of the crime of Minor Defamation under Article 315 of the Criminal Code.


=== Not Established / Modified on Cassation ===


* The Defendant was unproven to have imputed specific acts as required under the Slander offense of Article 310 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code, leading to the judicial re-qualification of the offense by the Supreme Court.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Flexibility of Verdict Qualifications Without Subsidiary Indictments: This landmark ruling provides vital guidance showing that scaling homogenous lesser offenses (*generics-specifics*) enables judges to correct sentencing qualifications for justice without forcing outright acquittals merely due to the absence of subsidiary indictment formulations.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: May a Judge convict a Defendant under Article 315 of the Criminal Code (Minor Defamation) if the Prosecutor solely charged Article 310 of the Criminal Code (Slander)?'''


'''A:''' Yes, it is permitted. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 818 K/Pid/1984, although ordinary defamation under Article 310 KUHP is charged in the indictment, the Defendant can be found guilty and punished under Article 315 KUHP (Minor Defamation) if proven acts constitute minor defamation without specific act imputations. This is permissible because Article 315 KUHP is a homogenous (homogen) offense carrying a lighter statutory penalty than Article 310 KUHP.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 829 K/Pdt/1991, dated December 10, 1993, established a civil procedural law rule concerning the completeness of parties in inheritance distribution lawsuits (*plurium litis consortium*):


In a lawsuit regarding an undivided estate/inheritance, all heirs of the decedent must be included in the lawsuit, either as Plaintiffs or as Defendants/Co-Defendants. If any heir (or lineage of heirs) is omitted from the lawsuit, the claim is formally defective due to missing parties (*plurium litis consortium*), and the original plaintiff's lawsuit must be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO). Consequently, the dismissal of the principal claim (convention) as inadmissible renders any counter-claim (reconvention) similarly inadmissible.


== Executive Summary ==


The central procedural principle established in this decision is that courts cannot adjudicate undivided inheritance distribution claims unless every single legal heir is properly joined as a party to the proceedings.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Undivided inheritance lawsuits require the joinder of all legal heirs to avoid formal defects (*plurium litis consortium*).
* Omitting any heir lineage invalidates the action, requiring courts to sustain missing-party exceptions and dismiss claims as inadmissible (NO).
* Dismissal of a main convention claim for defect of parties automatically carries over to dismiss dependent reconvention claims.


== Case Background ==


The Original Plaintiffs / Petitioners for Cassation (1. '''Ny. [Party D]''', 2. '''Ny. [Party B]''', 3. '''Achmad Sadjuri, BA''') sued the Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation ('''[Party A]''') and Co-Respondent for Cassation / Plaintiff II ('''Ny. H. Saebani alias Ny. Abdullahadi''') at the Klaten District Court concerning the distribution of the estate of the late Iman Ashari (who died in 1944), consisting of a house and yard (parcel 288/3) and 3 wetland parcels (blocks F, G, H / Letter C 117 / SHK Nos. 218, 219, 220, 221) in Dukuh Gatak, Kedungan Village, Pedan, Klaten. 


The Defendant raised an exception that the Plaintiffs' lawsuit was incomplete due to missing parties (*plurium litis consortium*) because the descendants of the late Ny. [Party C] (one of Iman Ashari's children) were not joined. The Klaten District Court (Decision No. 70/Pdt/G/1988/PN.Klt dated July 1, 1989) granted the convention lawsuit in part and the reconvention lawsuit in part. The Semarang High Court (Decision No. 560/Pdt/1989/PT.Smg dated March 26, 1990) affirmed the district court decision. The Petitioners for Cassation subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Formal Requirements for Inheritance Distribution Lawsuits (*Plurium Litis Consortium*) ===


The primary issue was whether an inheritance distribution lawsuit filed by a subset of heirs without joining all other heirs (either as Plaintiffs or Defendants) is valid under civil procedural law.


The Supreme Court held that it is invalid (*Formal Defect*). In inheritance disputes concerning undivided estates, every legal subject holding the status of an heir must be joined as a party to the action (*plurium litis consortium*). If an heir or a line of heirs is omitted from the lawsuit, the Defendant's exception regarding missing parties must be sustained, and the lawsuit must be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).


=== Binding Fate of Reconvention Claims Upon Inadmissibility of Convention Claims ===


The issue evaluated the legal standing of a counter-claim (*reconvention*) when the main claim (*convention*) is declared inadmissible (NO) due to subjective defects or missing parties.


The Supreme Court held that a reconvention claim filed in proceedings where the convention claim is dismissed as inadmissible due to a formal defect of missing parties (*plurium litis consortium*) must likewise be declared inadmissible (NO).


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the *Judex Facti* (Semarang High Court and Klaten District Court) misapply civil procedural law (*foutieve kepassing van het procesrecht*) by examining and deciding substantive merits and granting reconvention claims, despite the Defendant raising a well-founded exception that the lawsuit suffered from a formal defect of missing parties (*plurium litis consortium*) by failing to join descendants of the late Ny. [Party C]?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the *Judex Facti* misapplied the law. The Supreme Court annulled Semarang High Court Decision No. 560/Pdt/1989/PT.Smg in conjunction with Klaten District Court Decision No. 70/Pdt/G/1988/PN.Klt and adjudicated afresh by sustaining the Defendant's exception and declaring both convention and reconvention lawsuits inadmissible (NO).


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Klaten District Court & Semarang High Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning the pedigree of the late Iman Ashari (died 1944); the legal relationships of his children (Ny. [Party C], Ny. Asyiah, Bp. Abdullahadi, Ny. [Party B], Bp. [Party A]); control history over yard parcel 288/3 and wetland blocks F, G, H in Dukuh Gatak; issuance of SHK Nos. 218, 219, 220, and 221 in the name of [Party A]; and the failure to join children/descendants of the late Ny. [Party C] in the lawsuit.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The appellate and district *Judex Facti* misapplied civil procedural law. Because the lawsuit concerned an undivided estate, all heirs of the late Iman Ashari had to be joined either as Plaintiffs or Co-Defendants.
# In accordance with the Defendant's exception asserting that parties were incomplete (*plurium litis consortium*), the Plaintiffs' lawsuit had to be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).
# Furthermore, because the principal claim was declared inadmissible, the reconvention claim was likewise declared inadmissible.
# The Supreme Court annulled lower court rulings and adjudicated afresh, sustaining the Defendant's exception.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from the Petitioners for Cassation (1. '''Ny. [Party D] alias Ny. Syatibi''', 2. '''Ny. [Party B]''', 3. '''Achmad Sadjuri, BA'''); annulled Semarang High Court Decision No. 560/Pdt/1989/PT.Smg dated March 26, 1990, in conjunction with Klaten District Court Decision No. 70/Pdt/G/1988/PN.Klt dated July 1, 1991; and ADJUDICATED AFRESH: Under Exceptions: Sustaining the Defendant's exception; In Convention: Declaring the Plaintiffs' lawsuit inadmissible; In Reconvention: Declaring the Plaintiff in Reconvention's lawsuit inadmissible; and ordering the Petitioners for Cassation / Co-Respondent for Cassation to pay court costs across all judicial instances (cassation court costs set at Rp 20,000.—).


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Civil Procedure Code (HIR / RBg):''' Principle of *Plurium Litis Consortium*: Lawsuits must involve all interested parties so that judgments are enforceable and do not prejudice third-party rights. Article 136 HIR / Article 162 RBg: Filing and examining exceptions concerning incomplete or missing parties.
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 in conjunction with Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Authority of the Supreme Court to annul *Judex Facti* judgments misapplying procedural law on cassation.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* Disputed property constituted an estate left by the late Iman Ashari that had not been officially divided among all legal heirs.
* Late Ny. [Party C] was a biological child and legal heir of the late Iman Ashari with surviving descendants.
* Plaintiffs failed to include children/descendants of the late Ny. [Party C] in the statement of claim, either as Plaintiffs or Defendants.
* Plaintiffs' lawsuit suffered from a formal defect of missing parties (*plurium litis consortium*).


=== Not Established / Dismissed on Formalities ===


* Substantive merits concerning distribution shares and certificate validity were not examined by the Supreme Court because claims were dismissed as inadmissible at the formal exception stage.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Protection of Heirs' Legal Rights in Inheritance Disputes: This landmark ruling rigorously enforces procedural legal certainty requiring courts to refrain from dividing estates without joining all heir lineages, preventing future repetitive litigation (*ne bis in idem* / third-party opposition claims).


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Is an inheritance distribution lawsuit valid if any single heir is omitted from the lawsuit?'''


'''A:''' Invalid (*Formal Defect / NO*). Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 829 K/Pdt/1991, in lawsuits regarding undivided estates, all heirs must be included either as Plaintiffs or Defendants/Co-Defendants. If any heir is missed or unjoined, the lawsuit is deemed defective due to missing parties (*plurium litis consortium*) and must be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 830 K/Pid/2003, dated July 23, 2003, established a special criminal corruption law rule concerning the principle of sentencing proportionality and preventive/educative functions in corruption offenses involving trillions of rupiahs of Bank Indonesia Liquidity Assistance (*BLBI*) funds:


A 4-year imprisonment sentence imposed by the Jakarta High Court (*Judex Facti*) for joint corruption involving the misappropriation of BLBI funds amounting to Rp 1,291,530,307,776.84 (approximately Rp 1.291 Trillion) committed by a bank President Director ([Defendant]) was declared UNBALANCED and UNPROPORTIONAL given the gravity of corruption offenses punishable by maximum penalties of capital punishment, life imprisonment, or 20 years' imprisonment. The Supreme Court annulled the Jakarta High Court decision and enhanced the Defendant's sentence to 8 (eight) years' imprisonment, a fine of Rp 30,000,000.— subsidiary to 6 months' confinement, and an order to pay Restitution (*Uang Pengganti*) of Rp 1,291,530,307,776.84 to deliver educative, preventive, and equitable retribution.


== Executive Summary ==


The central legal principle established in this decision is that grand corruption involving trillions in state liquidity assistance requires severe, proportional sentences reflecting extraordinary crimes, rejecting lenient judicial discounts.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Light sentences (e.g., 4 years) for trillion-rupiah systemic banking corruption are unproportional and must be enhanced on cassation.
* Misappropriation of liquidity assistance funds for interbank debt settlements and fictitious instruments constitutes severe abuse of authority.
* Trillion-rupiah restitution orders must accompany prison enhancements to ensure state financial recovery.


== Case Background ==


The Original Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation, '''[Defendant]''' ([age removed], former President Director of PT Bank Umum Servitia Tbk), was charged with joint corruption (Law No. 3 of 1971 jo. Law No. 31 of 1999) involving the misappropriation of Bank Indonesia Liquidity Assistance (*BLBI*) funds amounting to Rp 988.26 Billion via 34 Credit Notes to Bank Sanho, issuance of fictitious Negotiable Certificates of Deposit (*NCD*) to Bank Dagang Bali (Rp 155 Billion) and Bank Eksekutif (Rp 127.1 Billion), and demand loan financing for PT Mitra Rona Wana Sejahtera (Rp 25.6 Billion), resulting in total state financial losses of Rp 1,291,530,307,776.84. 


The West Jakarta District Court (Decision No. 504/Pid.B/2001/PN.Jkt.Bar. dated March 11, 2002) sentenced the Defendant to 1 year's imprisonment, a Rp 30,000,000.— fine, and Restitution of Rp 1.291 Trillion. The Jakarta High Court (Decision No. 67/Pid/2002/PT.DKI dated August 12, 2002) modified the prison sentence to 4 years. Both the Defendant and the Public Prosecutor filed cassation petitions with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Proportionality Testing and Educative/Preventive Effects of Banking Mega-Scandal Corruption Penalties (BLBI) ===


The primary issue was whether a 4-year imprisonment sentence imposed by the Jakarta High Court upon a Defendant involved in BLBI fund misappropriation valued at Rp 1.291 Trillion satisfies principles of justice and sentencing objectives.


The Supreme Court held that it does not. Joint corruption involving Bank Indonesia Liquidity Assistance facilities causing trillion-rupiah state losses constitutes an extraordinary crime (*extraordinary crime*) punishable by maximum penalties of capital punishment, life imprisonment, or 20 years' imprisonment. Imposing overly lenient sentences (4 years) by the *Judex Facti* offends public sense of justice and violates sentencing objectives requiring educative, preventive, and equitable (*retributive & deterrent*) sanctions proportional to the economic damage inflicted upon the State.


=== Elements of Abuse of Authority and Unlawful Acts by Banking Directors in Disbursing BLBI Funds ex Article 1 paragraph 1 sub b of Law No. 3 of 1971 ===


Actions by a Bank President Director diverting Bank Indonesia liquidity facility funds under their supervision to settle related-party debt obligations (Bank Sanho), unlawfully issuing certificates of deposit (*NCD*) while the bank's current account was in debit balance, and disbursing fictitious loans are qualified as abuse of authority and pure unlawful acts harming State finances.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the *Judex Facti* (Jakarta High Court) misapply the law (*foutieve kepassing van het recht*) in determining sentencing quantum (*strafmaat*) by imposing a 4-year prison sentence unproportional to state losses of Rp 1.291 Trillion and maximum statutory corruption penalties?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the *Judex Facti* misapplied sentencing law. The Supreme Court annulled Jakarta High Court Decision No. 67/Pid/2002/PT.DKI in conjunction with West Jakarta District Court Decision No. 504/Pid.B/2001/PN.Jkt.Bar and adjudicated afresh by enhancing the Defendant's prison sentence from 4 years to 8 (eight) years and ordering Restitution of Rp 1,291,530,307,776.84.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / West Jakarta District Court & Jakarta High Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning Defendant [Defendant]'s position as President Director of PT Bank Umum Servitia Tbk; issuance of 34 Credit Notes valued at Rp 988,265,055,555.56 to Bank Sanho; NCD sales transactions to PT Bank Dagang Bali (Rp 155 Billion) and PT Bank Eksekutif (Rp 127.1 Billion); demand loan disbursements for PT Mitra Rona Wana Sejahtera (Rp 25.6 Billion); and total actual State financial losses of Rp 1,291,530,307,776.84.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The appellate *Judex Facti* of Jakarta High Court misapplied the law in determining sentencing quantum (*strafmaat*). A 4-year prison sentence imposed for trillion-rupiah BLBI corruption was unbalanced and unproportional to maximum statutory corruption penalties.
# *Judex Facti* should have imposed sentences possessing educative, preventive, and equitable effects proportionate to proven acts.
# The Supreme Court annulled lower court rulings and adjudicated afresh, enhancing prison terms to 8 years, imposing a fine, and ordering full restitution of Rp 1,291,530,307,776.84.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court ruled: Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation (Defendant '''[Defendant]'''); Annulling Jakarta High Court Decision No. 67/Pid/2002/PT.DKI dated August 12, 2002, in conjunction with West Jakarta District Court Decision No. 504/Pid.B/2001/PN.Jkt.Bar. dated March 11, 2002; and ADJUDICATING AFRESH: 1. Declaring Defendant [Defendant] proven legally and convincingly guilty of committing the crime of "Joint Corruption"; 2. Sentencing the Defendant to a prison term of 8 (eight) years; 3. Deducting the full period of detention served; 4. Sentencing the Defendant to a fine of Rp 30,000,000.— subsidiary to 6 months' confinement; 5. Sentencing the Defendant to pay Restitution to the State amounting to Rp 1,291,530,307,776.84 (one trillion two hundred ninety-one billion five hundred thirty million three hundred seven thousand seven hundred seventy-six rupiahs and eighty-four cents); 6. Forfeiting evidence land/buildings to the State; and charging cassation court costs amounting to Rp 2,500.—.

* '''Law No. 3 of 1971 in conjunction with Law No. 31 of 1999 on Eradication of Corruption Offenses:''' Articles 1 paragraph (1) sub b, 28, and 34 letter c.
* '''Criminal Code (KUHP):''' Articles 55 paragraph (1) 1st, 65 paragraph (1), and 1 paragraph (2).
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 jo. Law No. 35 of 1999 jo. Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Authority to review legal application and sentencing quantum errors on cassation.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* Defendant [Defendant] was proven legally and convincingly guilty of committing joint corruption.
* Total State financial losses caused by the Defendant's misuse of BLBI funds, NCDs, and fictitious loans amounted to Rp 1,291,530,307,776.84.
* The Defendant was sentenced to 8 years' imprisonment, a Rp 30,000,000.— fine (subsidiary 6 months), and Restitution of Rp 1,291,530,307,776.84.


=== Not Established / Rejected ===


* The Defendant's defense asserting that credit note withdrawals and NCD issuances were merely efforts to rescue the bank from depositor bank runs was dismissed and set aside by the Supreme Court because such acts were unlawfully executed while in debit balance.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Standardization of Banking Corruption Sentencing / BLBI: This landmark ruling serves as a vital precedent giving strict guidance to judges across Indonesia not to grant lenient discounts or overly light sentences for grand corruption, but to impose severe, proportional sentences to recover state funds and establish national deterrence.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Does the Supreme Court possess authority to enhance prison sentences for BLBI corruption offenders given overly lenient sentences by High Courts?'''


'''A:''' Yes, it possesses authority and the obligation. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 830 K/Pid/2003, a 4-year prison sentence imposed by a High Court upon a BLBI corruption offender involving Rp 1.291 Trillion ([Defendant]) was declared unbalanced and unproportional to the gravity of the crime. The Supreme Court is authorized to annul such decisions and enhance prison sentences to 8 (eight) years alongside Restitution of Rp 1.291 Trillion to deliver educative, preventive, and equitable penal sanctions.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 83 K/AG/1999 dated February 24, 2000, establishes essential jurisprudence and legal principles in Islamic Civil Procedure Law regarding the evidentiary standing of family/parental witnesses in divorce proceedings: In divorce lawsuits based on disputes and persistent quarrels (*syiqaq* / Article 19 letter f of Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975 jo. Article 116 letter f of the KHI), the father and mother of the Plaintiff or Defendant may be appointed and heard as witnesses pursuant to Article 76 paragraph (1) of Law No. 7 of 1989, which constitutes a *lex specialis* overriding the general restriction under Article 145 paragraph (1) of the HIR (*unus testis nullus testis*), when corroborated and synchronized with other supporting witness testimonies.

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation ([Plaintiff], Civil Servant/Teacher) filed a divorce suit against her husband, the Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation ([Defendant], Private Sector Employee), at the Semarang Religious Court. The couple married on June 26, 1983 (Marriage Certificate No. 103/24-VI/1983) and were blessed with 3 children ([Child], [Child], and [Child]). Their household experienced frequent disputes beginning from the pregnancy of their first child due to the Defendant's womanizing habits, heavy drinking, emotional volatility/physical abuse, and separation of domicile since May 1996, with the Plaintiff and children residing at [address removed].

The Semarang Religious Court (Decision No. 506/Pdt.G/1996/PA.Smg dated March 24, 1997) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part, pronounced a single *ba'in sughro* divorce, and awarded child custody (*hadhanah*) to the Plaintiff. However, the Semarang High Religious Court (Decision No. 57/Pdt.G/1997/PTA.Semarang dated January 12, 1998) annulled the Semarang Religious Court decision and dismissed the Plaintiff's lawsuit on the grounds that the testimony of the Plaintiff's father and mother was prohibited under Article 145 of the HIR and constituted only a single external witness (*unus testis nullus testis*). Dissatisfied with the appellate ruling, the Plaintiff filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# In divorce lawsuits grounded on disputes and quarrels (*syiqaq* ex Article 19 letter f of Government Regulation No. 9 of 1975), the father and mother may be appointed as witnesses and have their testimonies heard pursuant to Article 76 paragraph (1) of Law No. 7 of 1989, which acts as a *lex specialis* provision superseding the general rule of Article 145 paragraph (1) of the HIR.
# The Semarang High Religious Court committed an error of law by setting aside Article 76 paragraph (1) of Law No. 7 of 1989 and treating parental testimony as legally inadmissible. The testimony of the Plaintiff's parents, corroborated by another witness ([Witness]) and consistent documentary evidence, clearly demonstrated that the parties' marriage had irretrievably broken down (*broken marriage*) and could no longer be maintained.
# Regarding child custody (*hadhanah*), the Semarang Religious Court's ruling granting custody and upbringing of children who have not yet reached the age of discernment (*mumaiyiz*) to the mother is accurate and correct under Islamic law (Article 105 of the KHI).
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation [Plaintiff]; Annulling the Semarang High Religious Court decision dated January 12, 1998, No. 57/Pdt.G/1997/PTA.Semarang; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part; (2) Pronouncing a single *ba'in sughro* divorce of Defendant [Defendant] against Plaintiff [Plaintiff]; (3) Awarding child custody (*hadhanah*) of the children named [Child] and [Child] to the Plaintiff; (4) Declaring the remainder of the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible; (5) Ordering the Plaintiff to pay first-instance court costs (Rp 91,500); (6) Ordering the Defendant/Appellant to pay appellate-level court costs (Rp 48,000); (7) Ordering the Respondent for Cassation to pay cassation-level court costs (Rp 100,000).

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 863 K/Pid/1994, dated August 10, 1994, established two fundamental criminal and criminal procedural law rules regarding the discretion of *Judex Facti* over sentencing severity and the formatting of verdict dictums in repeat offenses (*recidive*):


First, Authority over Sentencing Severity (*Strafmaat*): Assessing the severity or leniency of a sentence is the exclusive authority of the *Judex Facti* (District and High Courts) and is not subject to cassation review, except when the *Judex Facti* imposes a sentence exceeding the statutory maximum or issues a sentence without sufficient legal reasoning. A 4-year and 6-month prison sentence imposed on a Defendant repeatedly using fake credit cards remains below the statutory maximum threat of 8 years (Article 263 paragraph 2 jo. Article 64 paragraph 1 jo. Article 486 KUHP), thus violating no laws.


Second, Formulation of Recidivism Elements (*Recidive*): When a convict commits a similar criminal offense within a 5-year period following a prior conviction (*recidive* ex Article 486 KUHP), such recidivism does not need to be formulated or included within the verdict dictum (*dictum*), but is sufficiently stated and weighed solely within the legal considerations section (*ratio decidendi*) of the judgment.


== Executive Summary ==


The central legal principles established in this decision govern the procedural boundaries of cassation review over sentencing discretion and streamline verdict drafting for repeat offenders.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Sentencing severity determinations by lower courts are unreviewable on cassation absent statutory excess or unreasoned judgments.
* Recidivism enhancements function as sentencing aggravation grounds rather than independent dictum qualifications.
* Appellate judgments including recidivism clauses inside verdict dictums are subject to corrective cleanup on cassation.


== Case Background ==


The Original Defendant / Petitioner for Cassation, '''[Defendant]''' ([age removed], housewife), was charged with repeated use of forged credit cards (Article 263 paragraph 2 jo. Article 64 paragraph 1 jo. Article 486 KUHP) for purchasing 4 fake BCA Gold Cards from Hendrik for Rp 1,500,000.— each and utilizing them to buy luxury goods at Nagoya Batam shops in August–September 1993, causing losses of Rp 9,213,400.— to BCA Batam Branch. The Defendant was a repeat offender (*recidivis*) previously convicted by Surabaya District Court (2 months' imprisonment) and North Jakarta District Court (55 days' imprisonment) for similar fake credit card offenses. 


The Batam District Court (Decision No. 82/Pid/B/1993/PN.Btm dated March 5, 1994) sentenced the Defendant to 4 years and 6 months' imprisonment. The Riau High Court in Pekanbaru (Decision No. 11/Pid/1994/PTR dated May 10, 1994) modified the judgment by incorporating the recidivism clause into the dictum. The Defendant subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Technical Formulation of Criminal Verdict Dictums in Repeat Offenses (*Recidive* ex Article 486 KUHP) ===


The primary issue was whether sentence enhancements arising from repeat offenses (*recidive*) within a 5-year period must be listed and formulated within the verdict dictum (*dictum*).


The Supreme Court held that it is unnecessary. Elements of recidivism under Article 486 KUHP constitute sentencing aggravation grounds (*strafverzwaringsgrond*) rather than independent dictum qualifications. Therefore, recidivism must be stated and weighed solely within the legal considerations (*ratio decidendi*), and need not be formulated inside the verdict dictum (*dictum*).


=== Limits of Supreme Court Cassation Review over Sentencing Severity (*Strafmaat*) ===


The issue evaluated whether the Supreme Court on cassation is authorized to review the severity or leniency of sentences (*strafmaat*) imposed by the *Judex Facti*.


The Supreme Court held that assessing sentencing severity is the absolute authority of the *Judex Facti* (District and High Courts) and is unreviewable on cassation. The Supreme Court may only correct sentences in two exceptional circumstances: (1) when *Judex Facti* imposes a penalty exceeding the statutory maximum threshold, or (2) when penalties are imposed without sufficient legal reasoning (*rederijk/motivering*).


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the *Judex Facti* (Riau High Court in Pekanbaru) err in formulating its verdict dictum by incorporating descriptive clauses concerning recidivism within the dictum text, and did the 4-year 6-month prison sentence violate statutory maximum thresholds under Article 263(2) jo. Article 64(1) jo. Article 486 KUHP?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the verdict qualification required cleanup by removing recidivism clauses from the dictum text. The Supreme Court rejected the Defendant [Defendant]'s cassation petition while modifying the judgment to establish a clean verdict qualification: "Intentionally using a forged document as if true and genuine whose use causes losses, committed multiple times as a continuous act". A prison sentence of 4 years and 6 months was declared lawful because it did not exceed the 8-year statutory maximum.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Batam District Court & Riau High Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning the purchase of 4 fake BCA Gold Cards by [Defendant] from Hendrik at Pub Kisme Hayam Wuruk, Jakarta, for Rp 1.5 million each; practicing forged signatures; transactions at Marina Store, Verina Store, and Sally Cosmetik Nagoya Batam on August 22 & September 4, 1993; losses of Rp 9,213,400.— to BCA Batam Branch; and prior criminal conviction records at Surabaya and North Jakarta District Courts.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The appellate and district *Judex Facti* did not misapply the law regarding establishing guilt and sentencing severity (*strafmaat*). Sentencing severity is the exclusive authority of *Judex Facti* unreviewable on cassation, barring statutory maximum violations or unreasoned rulings (strafmaat of 4 years 6 months remains below the 8-year maximum).
# However, regarding verdict formulation, the Supreme Court affirmed that when a convict commits a similar crime within 5 years (*recidive* ex Article 486 KUHP), such recidivism need not be formulated within the verdict dictum, but suffices in legal considerations.
# The Supreme Court rejected the Defendant's cassation appeal while modifying the verdict qualification.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court ruled: Rejecting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation / Defendant ('''[Defendant]'''); Modifying the ruling of Riau High Court in Pekanbaru Decision No. 11/Pid/1994/PTR dated May 10, 1994, in conjunction with Batam District Court Decision No. 82/Pid/B/1993/PN.Btm dated March 5, 1994, solely regarding considerations to read: Declaring Defendant [Defendant] proven legally and convincingly guilty of committing the crime of "Intentionally using a forged document as if true and genuine and not forged, the use of which causes losses, committed multiple times as a continuous act"; and ordering the Petitioner for Cassation / Defendant to pay cassation court costs amounting to Rp 2,500.—.

  * Article 263 paragraph (2): Crime of using forged or falsified documents.

=== Established by Evidence ===


* Defendant [Defendant] was proven legally and convincingly guilty of committing repeated offenses of using fake credit cards as a continuous act ex Article 263 paragraph (2) jo. Article 64 paragraph (1) KUHP.
* The Defendant was established as a repeat offender (*recidivis*) previously convicted by Surabaya District Court and North Jakarta District Court for fake credit card offenses.

* Clean Formulation of Criminal Verdict Dictums: This landmark ruling establishes technical judicial guidelines for all criminal courts in Indonesia to strictly distinguish between proven core offense qualifications (stated in dictums) and sentence aggravation factors such as recidivism (stated solely in legal considerations).

'''Q: Is the element of repeat offenses (*recidive*) required to be written inside the verdict dictum of a criminal judgment?'''


'''A:''' No, it is unnecessary. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 863 K/Pid/1994, when a convict commits a similar criminal offense within a 5-year period following a prior conviction (*recidive*), such recidivism does not need to be formulated inside the verdict dictum (*dictum*), but is sufficiently stated and weighed solely within the legal considerations section (*ratio decidendi*) of the judgment.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 880 K/Pdt/2003, dated January 29, 2004, established a fundamental civil and constitutional/political law rule concerning the absolute judicial jurisdiction of general courts over internal political party management disputes:


District Courts lack absolute jurisdiction to adjudicate political party management disputes, which constitute internal organizational matters and internal mechanisms of political parties. Disputes concerning the organizational leadership of political parties must be resolved through internal party mechanisms in accordance with the applicable Statutes and Bylaws (*AD/ART*) of the political party. The Supreme Court annulled Mataram High Court Decision No. 176/Pdt/2002/PT.Mtr in conjunction with Mataram District Court Decision No. 134/Pdt.G/2001/PN.Mtr, and adjudicated afresh by declaring the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).


== Executive Summary ==


The central jurisdictional principle established in this decision is that general courts must observe the doctrine of non-intervention in internal political party disputes, leaving leadership contests to internal party tribunals and statutory bylaws.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* General courts lack absolute jurisdiction (*kompetensi absolut*) to examine leadership disputes within political parties.
* Internal party disputes over regional leadership boards and regional congresses (*Musda*) must be settled via party *AD/ART* mechanisms.
* District court judgments accepting jurisdiction over internal party matters are subject to reversal on cassation, resulting in dismissal as inadmissible (NO).


== Case Background ==


The Original Plaintiff / Respondent for Cassation (Regional Leadership Board of Golkar Party West Lombok Result of Accelerated Musda VIII: Drs. TGH. Muchlis Ibrahim & H. Abdul Kasim) filed a lawsuit at the Mataram District Court against the Original Defendants / Petitioners for Cassation (1. West Lombok Golkar DPD Result of Musda VII: Lalu Koeshardi, SH & Raden Putra Kesuma, SH; 2. NTB Golkar DPD; 3. DPP Golkar). The Plaintiff sought legal recognition of the accelerated Musda VIII held on January 6, 2001, and the annulment of Interim Replacement (*PAW*) appointment decrees issued by Defendant II. 


The Defendants raised an exception that the Mataram District Court lacked absolute jurisdiction because leadership disputes constitute internal party affairs governed by *AD/ART*. The Mataram District Court (Decision No. 134/Pdt.G/2001/PN.Mtr dated July 20, 2002) rejected the exception and granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part. The Mataram High Court (Decision No. 176/Pdt/2002/PT.Mtr dated November 14, 2002) affirmed the district court decision with modifications. The Petitioners for Cassation subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Absolute Jurisdiction of General Courts over Internal Political Party Disputes ===


The primary issue was whether General Courts (District Courts, High Courts, Supreme Court) have legal authority to examine, adjudicate, and decide disputes concerning the validity of leadership boards and dual outcomes of Regional Congresses (*Musda*) of a political organization (*Political Party*).


The Supreme Court held that they lack authority (*Absolute Jurisdiction Dismissed*). Disputes concerning leadership validity, interim replacements (*PAW*), or Regional Congress (*Musda*) validity constitute internal organizational disputes and affairs of political parties. Resolution of such internal disputes must be pursued through forums and mechanisms stipulated within the Statutes and Bylaws (*AD/ART*) of the respective political party. General District Courts possess no jurisdictional competence (*kompetens absolut*) to try such matters, requiring the Plaintiff's lawsuit to be declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the *Judex Facti* (Mataram High Court & District Court) misapply the law or exceed their jurisdictional limits (*foutieve kepassing van het recht* / exceeding authority ex Article 30 of Law No. 14/1985) by accepting and adjudicating a civil unlawful act lawsuit concerning internal political party leadership validity?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the *Judex Facti* misapplied the law. Political party management matters are internal party affairs, rendering General Courts unauthorized to adjudicate. The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition of the Petitioners for Cassation, annulled Mataram High Court Decision No. 176/Pdt/2002/PT.Mtr in conjunction with Mataram District Court Decision No. 134/Pdt.G/2001/PN.Mtr, and adjudicated afresh by declaring the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible (NO).


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Mataram District Court & High Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning the vote of no confidence by 12 Sub-District Consultative Councils (*DPK*) of Golkar Party in West Lombok; execution of accelerated Musda VIII on January 6, 2001, at Jayakarta Hotel; election of Drs. TGH. Muchlis Ibrahim and H. Abdul Kasim; issuance of the Decree on Composition and Personnel of Interim Replacement (*PAW*) for West Lombok Golkar DPD by DPD I NTB (Decree No. Kep-003/DPD/GOLKAR/IV/2001); and the absence of written approval from the DPD I NTB Chairman in convening Musda VIII.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The *Judex Facti* of Mataram High Court and District Court misapplied the law and exceeded their jurisdictional authority.
# Pursuant to the Plaintiff's *posita*, the object of dispute concerned management matters constituting internal affairs of the respective political party.
# Under organizational and political legal principles, District Courts lack authority to adjudicate internal political party management disputes.
# The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition, annulled lower court rulings, and adjudicated afresh, declaring the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court ruled: Granting the cassation petition from Petitioners for Cassation (1. '''WEST LOMBOK GOLKAR DPD RESULT OF MUSDA VII''', 2. '''NUSA TENGGARA BARAT GOLKAR DPD''', 3. '''DPP GOLKAR'''); Annulling Mataram High Court Decision No. 176/Pdt/2002/PT.Mtr dated November 14, 2002, in conjunction with Mataram District Court Decision No. 134/Pdt.G/2001/PN.Mtr dated July 20, 2002; and ADJUDICATING AFRESH: Declaring Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard*); and ordering the Respondent for Cassation / Original Plaintiff to pay court costs across all judicial instances (cassation court costs set at Rp 500,000.—).


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Law No. 2 of 1999 on Political Parties:''' Provisions governing internal political party autonomy and party *AD/ART*.
* '''Civil Procedure Code (HIR / RBg):''' Absolute Jurisdiction Exceptions of District Courts.
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 jo. Law No. 35 of 1999 jo. Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Article 30 letters a & b (Cassation Grounds: Lacking jurisdiction, exceeding authority, or misapplying law).


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* The object of dispute filed by the Plaintiff (West Lombok Golkar DPD Result of Musda VIII) was purely an internal political party management dispute.
* District Courts lack absolute jurisdiction to adjudicate internal political party management disputes.
* Plaintiff's lawsuit was declared inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO) and Plaintiff was charged with court costs.


=== Not Established / Inadmissible ===


* The substantive validity of leadership claims between Musda VII Results and Musda VIII Results was neither examined nor adjudicated by the Supreme Court because Courts lack authority to try internal party disputes.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Principle of Judicial Non-Intervention in Internal Political Organization Disputes: This landmark ruling firmly establishes the internal party dispute doctrine (*internal party dispute*): general courts are barred from meddling in political party leadership affairs, fostering democratic maturity by compelling internal resolution through Party Tribunals / party *AD/ART* mechanisms.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Do District Courts have authority to adjudicate dual leadership disputes within internal political parties?'''


'''A:''' No authority (*Absolute Jurisdiction Dismissed*). Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 880 K/Pdt/2003, District Courts lack authority to adjudicate political party management disputes constituting internal party affairs. Political party organizational leadership disputes fall within the internal domain mandatorily resolved through mechanisms set forth in the party's Statutes and Bylaws (*AD/ART*), rendering lawsuits filed in District Courts inadmissible (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard* / NO).

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 91 K/TUN/2000 dated November 13, 2000, establishes fundamental jurisprudence and legal principles regarding the absolute competence of tax dispute adjudication. The Supreme Court outlined that pursuant to Article 37 of Law No. 19 of 1997 on Tax Collection via Warrant of Execution (*Surat Paksa*), a tax debtor's lawsuit against the implementation of a Warrant of Execution **may only be submitted to the Tax Dispute Resolution Board (BPSP)**. Consequently, the State Administrative Court (PTUN) **lacks absolute competence** to examine and adjudicate lawsuits concerning the implementation of tax collection Warrants of Execution.

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiff / Respondent for Cassation (PT Timor Putra Nasional, represented by President Director Drs. Suharto) filed a lawsuit at the Jakarta State Administrative Court against the Defendants (Head of Jakarta Type A Customs and Service Office, Tanjung Priok III, Tanjung Priok II, and Head of Jakarta Tanah Abang Tax Service Office). The lawsuit challenged the issuance of more than a dozen Warrants of Execution for the collection of import duties, VAT, and luxury goods sales tax arrears related to the Timor national sedan car program for the 1996 through 1998 tax years.

The Jakarta State Administrative Court (Decision No. 025/G.TUN/1999/PTUN.JKT dated July 19, 1999) granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in entirety and declared the Warrants of Execution null and void. The Jakarta State Administrative High Court (Decision No. 157/B/1999/PT.TUN.JKT dated December 9, 1999 / November 22, 1999) upheld the Jakarta State Administrative Court judgment. Dissatisfied with the ruling, the Defendants filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court raising an exception of absolute judicial competence.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The cassation objections raised by the Petitioners for Cassation are well-founded because the Jakarta State Administrative High Court committed an error in applying the law.
# Pursuant to Article 37 of Law No. 19 of 1997 on Tax Collection via Warrant of Execution, a tax debtor's lawsuit against the implementation of a Warrant of Execution "may only be submitted to the BPSP (Tax Dispute Resolution Board)" and therefore falls outside the jurisdiction of the State Administrative Court to examine and adjudicate.
# Under prevailing positive law, absolute competence to examine and adjudicate matters concerning tax collection via warrants of execution rests with the Tax Dispute Resolution Board (BPSP), as explicitly underscored in Article 37 of Law No. 19 of 1997 by the phrasing *"may only be submitted to the BPSP..."*.
# Such statutory formulation dictates that matters of tax collection via warrants of execution—regardless of whether viewed from tax administration or general tax law perspectives—cannot be handled by any judicial body other than the BPSP. Therefore, the Defendants' exception of absolute competence is sustained, and the Plaintiff's lawsuit is declared inadmissible.
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from the Petitioners for Cassation: I. HEAD OF JAKARTA TYPE A CUSTOMS AND SERVICE OFFICE; II. HEAD OF TANJUNG PRIOK III TYPE A CUSTOMS AND SERVICE OFFICE; III. HEAD OF TANJUNG PRIOK II CUSTOMS AND SERVICE OFFICE; IV. HEAD OF JAKARTA TANAH ABANG TAX SERVICE OFFICE; Annulling the Jakarta State Administrative High Court decision dated December 9, 1999, No. 157/B/1999/PT.TUN.JKT jo. the Jakarta State Administrative Court decision dated July 19, 1999, No. 025/G.TUN/1999/PTUN.JKT; and Independently Adjudicating: In Exception: Sustaining the Exceptions of Defendants I, II, III, and IV; In the Principal Case: Declaring the Plaintiff's lawsuit (PT Timor Putra Nasional) inadmissible (*niet ontvankelijke verklaard*); Ordering the Respondent for Cassation to pay all court costs across all levels of jurisdiction (assessed at Rp 100,000 at the cassation level). *(Decided by Cassation Panel of Justices: Prof. Dr. Paulus E. Lotulung, SH. [Presiding], Ny. Hj. Emin Aminah Achadiat, SH., and Ny. Hj. Asma Samik Ibrahim, SH.)*.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 935 K/Pdt/1998, dated December 21, 1999, established a fundamental civil procedural law rule concerning the evidentiary force of Supplementary Oaths (*Sumpah Suppletoir*) and the limits of judicial review authority over them at appellate and cassation levels:


Additional documentary evidence cannot invalidate the evidentiary weight of a supplementary oath (*sumpah suppletoir*) taken and sworn by a Plaintiff before a District Court, because a supplementary oath executed in this manner possesses perfect evidentiary force (*volledig bewijskracht*) and is not subject to re-examination or re-evaluation in appellate or cassation proceedings. Consequently, the out-of-wedlock biological relationship between the Plaintiff and Defendant resulting in the birth of a child was declared lawfully proven, and the Defendant's refusal to provide maintenance/housing was qualified as an Unlawful Act (*Onrechtmatige Daad* ex Article 1365 Civil Code).


== Executive Summary ==


The central procedural principle established in this decision is that once a trial court properly orders and administers a supplementary oath (*sumpah suppletoir*), its conclusive evidentiary effect cannot be undone by appellate courts relying on post-trial documentary challenges.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Supplementary oaths ordered to complete incomplete proof carry binding evidentiary force.
* Appellate and cassation tribunals lack authority to re-weigh or overturn sworn supplementary oaths using secondary documents.
* Fathers denying out-of-wedlock biological children and refusing support commit actionable unlawful torts requiring financial reparation.


== Case Background ==


The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation ('''Ny. [Plaintiff]''', acting for herself and her child '''[Child]''') filed a lawsuit at the South Jakarta District Court against the Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation ('''[Defendant]'''). The Plaintiff sought accountability from the Defendant for the birth of a daughter, [Child] (born [details removed]), resulting from an out-of-wedlock biological relationship, and requested housing and maintenance damages. 


The South Jakarta District Court (Decision No. 349/Pdt.G/1995/PN.Jkt.Sel dated March 26, 1996) ordered the Plaintiff to take a supplementary oath (*sumpah suppletoir*), and upon administration, granted the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part, declaring [Child] to be the biological child of the Defendant, finding the Defendant liable for unlawful acts, and ordering the Defendant to provide decent housing worth Rp 161,000,000.—. The Jakarta High Court (Decision No. 519/Pdt/1996/PT.DKI dated October 31, 1996) annulled the district court decision based on documentary evidence T.4. The Petitioner for Cassation subsequently filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.


== Claims, Evidence and Source Mapping ==

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Status and Evidentiary Value of Supplementary Oaths (*Sumpah Suppletoir* ex Article 155 HIR / Article 182 RBg / Article 1940 Civil Code) in Appellate and Cassation Review ===


The primary issue was whether a High Court on appeal possesses authority to annul or undermine the evidentiary value of a Supplementary Oath (*Sumpah Suppletoir*) administered to and sworn by a Plaintiff before the District Court trial using additional documentary evidence (photocopies) submitted by the Defendant.


The Supreme Court held that it lacks authority. A supplementary oath (*sumpah suppletoir*) ordered by a Trial Judge to complete preliminary proof that remains imperfect (*onvolledig bewijs*) possesses binding evidentiary force upon the judge. Once a supplementary oath is lawfully sworn by the burdened party before the court, that oath is immune to re-examination or re-evaluation in appellate and cassation proceedings. Additional documentary evidence submitted on appeal cannot serve as grounds to invalidate the truth sworn under oath.


=== Unlawful Acts (*Onrechtmatige Daad* ex Article 1365 Civil Code) for Breach of Paternal Duties Toward Out-of-Wedlock Biological Children ===


A biological father who refuses to recognize, protect, and provide decent housing and maintenance for his out-of-wedlock biological child commits an Unlawful Act (*Onrechtmatige Daad*) inflicting moral and material damages upon the mother and child.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the Jakarta High Court misapply the law of evidence (*foutieve kepassing van het bewijsrecht*) by setting aside legal facts perfectly proven via a Supplementary Oath sworn by the Plaintiff at the South Jakarta District Court?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the Jakarta High Court misapplied the law of evidence. The Supreme Court granted the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation Ny. [Plaintiff], annulled Jakarta High Court Decision No. 519/Pdt/1996/PT.DKI, and adjudicated afresh by affirming South Jakarta District Court Decision No. 349/Pdt.G/1995/PN.Jkt.Sel.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / South Jakarta District Court & Jakarta High Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning intimate out-of-wedlock relationships from 1973 to 1985; birth of a female child named [Child] on December 30, 1985; administration of Ny. [Plaintiff]'s supplementary oath at the South Jakarta District Court trial on February 15, 1996; existence of exhibit T.4 (letter dated April 27, 1983); and determination of decent housing damages amounting to Rp 161,000,000.—.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The appellate *Judex Facti* of Jakarta High Court misapplied the law of evidence. Additional documentary evidence T.4 submitted by the Defendant on appeal could not invalidate the supplementary oath administered to and sworn by the original Plaintiff before trial court sessions, because supplementary oaths are immune to appellate or cassation review.
# Furthermore, exhibit T.4 failed to prove that subsequent to its drafting, the original Plaintiff and original Defendant never engaged in biological relations.
# The Supreme Court granted the Plaintiff's cassation petition, annulled the Jakarta High Court decision, and adjudicated afresh by affirming the South Jakarta District Court ruling.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court ruled: Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation ('''NY. [Plaintiff]'''); Annulling Jakarta High Court Decision No. 519/Pdt/1996/PT.DKI dated October 31, 1996, which had annulled South Jakarta District Court Decision No. 349/Pdt.G/1995/PN.Jkt.Sel. dated March 26, 1996; and ADJUDICATING AFRESH: Under Exceptions: Rejecting the Defendant's exception; Under Provision: Rejecting the Plaintiff's provisional claims; Under the Merits: Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit in part; Declaring that the Defendant has committed an unlawful act (*Onrechtmatige daad*); Declaring that the minor child [Child] is the biological child of the Defendant resulting from his relationship with the Plaintiff; Ordering the Defendant to provide the Plaintiff and her child with a decent house for shelter valued at Rp 161,000,000.—; Rejecting all other claims; and ordering the Respondent for Cassation to pay court costs across all judicial instances (cassation court costs set at Rp 50,000.—).


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Civil Procedure Code (HIR / RBg / KUHPerdata):''' HIR Article 155 / RBg Article 182 / Civil Code Article 1940: Supplementary Oath (*Suppletoir Eed*).
* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata):''' Article 1365: Unlawful Acts (*Onrechtmatige Daad*).
* '''Law No. 1 of 1974 on Marriage:''' Article 43 paragraph (1) (Out-of-wedlock children).
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 in conjunction with Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Authority to review evidence application errors on cassation.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* Plaintiff Ny. [Plaintiff] took a Supplementary Oath (*Sumpah Suppletoir*) at the South Jakarta District Court trial on February 15, 1996, reinforcing preliminary proof.
* The child [Child] (born [details removed]) was proven legally and convincingly to be the biological child of Defendant [Defendant] resulting from his relationship with the Plaintiff.
* The Defendant committed an unlawful act and was ordered to provide a decent house valued at Rp 161,000,000.— to the Plaintiff and her child.


=== Not Established / Set Aside ===


* Exhibit T.4 (letter dated April 27, 1983) submitted by the Defendant failed to prove the absence of biological relations subsequent to its writing and lacked legal power to invalidate a sworn supplementary oath.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Legal Certainty of Supplementary Oaths (*Sumpah Suppletoir*): This landmark ruling guarantees procedural certainty ensuring that the sacred evidentiary weight of a supplementary oath ordered by a Trial Judge cannot be undermined or overturned by Appellate Judges merely through speculative secondary documents.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Can a supplementary oath (*sumpah suppletoir*) judgment rendered by a District Court be annulled by a High Court or the Supreme Court?'''


'''A:''' No, it cannot. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 935 K/Pdt/1998, additional documentary evidence cannot invalidate a supplementary oath (*sumpah suppletoir*) administered at the District Court, because supplementary oaths are immune to appellate or cassation review. Once a supplementary oath is lawfully sworn, the law treats the underlying legal relationship as perfectly proven and binding.

== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision No. 96 K/MIL/2006 dated May 31, 2007, establishes fundamental jurisprudence and legal rules regarding the application of excusing conditions (*alasan pemaaf*) in Military Criminal Law. The Supreme Court affirmed that even though the Defendant (a subordinate soldier) was proven to have committed an act violating Article 105 paragraph (1) of the KUHPM by uttering inappropriate threats against his superior, such an act is unpunishable because it arose from an uncontrollable emotional outburst triggered by a heinous act—the rape of the Defendant's wife committed by that same superior. This outburst constitutes a legal excusing condition, requiring the Defendant to be released from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*).

== Case Background ==

The Defendant ([Defendant], Serda Nrp. 634800, Personnel Administration Clerk at Ajen Rem 131/Stg) was brought before the Manado Military Court III-17 under the charge of violating Article 105 paragraph (1) of the KUHPM ("A military personnel who intentionally and with overt acts threatens a superior with violence"). On March 16, 2004, in front of the Sandi Room at Ma Korem 131/Stg, the Defendant approached the victim witness, First Lieutenant (*Lettu Inf*) [Witness], while pointing fingers and threatening: "You are the one who tied my wife's hands together with Sergeant Rustam; I will kill you, I have many family members."

The threats were triggered by the reality that the victim witness, Lettu Inf [Witness], had raped the Defendant's wife ([Victim] / Merry Ulaan) under firearm threat while binding her hands and covering her eyes and mouth with black duct tape. The victim witness Lettu Inf [Witness] was himself sentenced to 8 months of imprisonment and dishonorably discharged from the Indonesian Army (TNI AD) pursuant to a final and binding military court judgment.

The Manado Military Court III-17 (Decision No. PUT/35-K/PM.III-17/AD/V/2005 dated May 25, 2005) sentenced the Defendant to 7 (seven) months of imprisonment. The Surabaya Military High Court III (Decision No. PUT/52-K/PMT.III/BDG/AD/VI/2006 dated June 1, 2006) upheld the conviction. The Defendant subsequently filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# Although the Defendant is proven to have committed the acts described in the Military Prosecutor's indictment (uttering threats against a superior), the underlying causes of such acts must be taken into account.
# The Defendant's actions were caused by an uncontrollable emotional outburst resulting from the rape committed by his superior (Lettu Inf [Witness]) against the Defendant's wife. A similar reaction could happen to anyone experiencing the same traumatic event, impairing their ability to maintain self-control in accordance with their emotional surge.
# The emotional outburst resulting from the superior's heinous act constitutes an excusing condition (*alasan pemaaf*) under the law. Therefore, the *Judex Facti* erred in its considerations, and it is legally justified for the Supreme Court to annul the *Judex Facti* rulings and release the Defendant from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*).
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation / Defendant [Defendant], Serda Nrp. 634800; Annulling the Surabaya Military High Court III decision dated June 1, 2006, No. PUT/52-K/PMT.III/BDG/AD/VI/2006, which upheld the Manado Military Court III-17 decision dated May 25, 2005, No. PUT/35-K/PM.III-17/AD/V/2005; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Declaring that Defendant [Defendant], Serda Nrp. 634800 is proven to have committed the acts formulated in the Military Prosecutor's indictment, but that such acts are unpunishable; (2) Releasing the Defendant accordingly from all legal prosecutions (*ontslag van alle rechtsvervolging*); (3) Restoring the Defendant's rights in capacity, position, honor, and dignity; (4) Charging procedural costs across all levels of jurisdiction to the State. *(Decided in the Supreme Court deliberation meeting on May 31, 2007, by the Cassation Panel of Justices: German Hoediarto, S.H. [Presiding], M. Imron Anwari, S.H., SpN., M.H., and Timur P. Manurung, S.H.)*.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 972 K/Pid/2000, dated November 30, 2000, established fundamental material criminal law and criminal procedural rules concerning the proof of the element "unlawful ownership" (*memiliki secara melawan hukum*) in the crime of embezzlement (Article 372 KUHP) and the admissibility of cassation against impure acquittals (*niet-zuivere vrijspraak*):


When the element of unlawful ownership is proven, the Defendant is legally and convincingly proven guilty of committing the crime of "Embezzlement" as charged by the Public Prosecutor, and sentencing must be imposed. The Defendant's act of leasing out another party's warehouse without permission and utilizing the rental proceeds for personal use is qualified as realizing a decision to act as an owner (*zich toe-eigenen*). The existence of an ongoing civil dispute lacking final and binding legal force does not eliminate the unlawful nature of the Defendant's acts, because prior to any court ruling establishing the Defendant as lawful owner, the registered rights holder (SHGB) must remain regarded as the lawful owner. The Supreme Court annulled Southeast Sulawesi High Court Decision No. 04/Pid/2000/PT.Sultra and adjudicated afresh by sentencing the Defendant to 2 (two) months' imprisonment with a 4-month probation period.


== Executive Summary ==


The central legal principle established in this decision is that leasing another person's registered property without authorization and keeping the proceeds constitutes unlawful embezzlement (*zich toe-eigenen*), which cannot be excused by pending civil claims.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Unauthorized leasing of another party's registered property constitutes criminal embezzlement (*zich toe-eigenen*).
* Pending civil disputes lacking finality do not strip registered land rights holders of their lawful ownership status.
* Appellate judgments improperly acquitting defendants based on flawed legal interpretations of criminal elements constitute impure acquittals (*niet-zuivere vrijspraak*) reviewable on cassation under Article 244 KUHAP.


== Case Background ==


The Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation, '''[Defendant]''' ([age removed], entrepreneur), was charged with embezzlement (Article 372 KUHP) for leasing a warehouse in Jembatan Batu, Bau-Bau, on April 9, 1998, to [Lessee] for Rp 8,500,000.— per year without permission from witness [Party C] (the Defendant's younger sibling / lawful owner holding SHGB No. 91/1989) and utilizing the rental proceeds for his child's medical expenses in Surabaya. 


The Bau-Bau District Court (Decision No. 156/Pid.B/1999/PN.BB dated August 5, 1999) convicted the Defendant to 2 months' imprisonment with a 4-month probation period. The Southeast Sulawesi High Court in Kendari (Decision No. 04/Pid/2000/PT.Sultra dated March 4, 2000) annulled the district court decision and acquitted the Defendant (*vrijspraak*) on the grounds that the leasing act lacked unlawful intent because the warehouse involved a pending civil dispute regarding Irian Store. The Public Prosecutor at the Bau-Bau State Prosecutor's Office filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.

== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Construction of the Element "Unlawful Ownership" (*Zich Toe-eigenen*) in Embezzlement (Article 372 KUHP) ===


The primary issue was whether leasing a building/warehouse under a Building Land Rights Certificate (*SHGB*) registered in another person's name to a third party without the owner's permission, while using the rental proceeds for personal use, satisfies the element of "unlawful ownership" (*zich toe-eigenen*) under Article 372 of the Criminal Code.


The Supreme Court held that it satisfies the element. Pursuant to criminal law doctrine (Hoge Raad arrests of October 16, 1905, and March 26, 1906), the concept of "ownership" (*toe-eigenen*) refers to actions where a property holder controls or acts as if they are the owner of the property. When the Defendant leased another person's warehouse and received/enjoyed rental proceeds of Rp 8,500,000.— per year without the registered owner's consent, the Defendant manifested a concrete decision to exercise unlawful control over the property (*zich toe-eigenen*).


=== Admissibility of Prosecutor's Cassation Petition Against Impure Acquittals (*Niet-Zuivere Vrijspraak* ex Article 244 KUHAP) ===


The issue evaluated whether a Public Prosecutor's cassation petition is admissible against a High Court judgment acquitting a Defendant on grounds that the Defendant's acts related to an ongoing civil dispute.


The Supreme Court held that it is Admissible. When a lower court's acquittal (*vrijspraak*) rests upon a flawed interpretation of the criminal elements contained in the indictment (rather than a failure to prove material acts), the acquittal is categorized as an impure acquittal (*niet-zuivere vrijspraak*). The Supreme Court possesses authority to examine and correct such legal misapplications pursuant to Article 244 of the KUHAP.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the *Judex Facti* of Southeast Sulawesi High Court in Kendari misapply the law (*foutieve kepassing van het recht*) by narrowly interpreting the element of "unlawful ownership" under Article 372 KUHP and acquitting the Defendant on civil dispute grounds, despite SHGB No. 91 being validly registered in the victim witness's name?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the Southeast Sulawesi High Court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court annulled High Court Decision No. 04/Pid/2000/PT.Sultra and adjudicated afresh, declaring Defendant [Defendant] proven legally and convincingly guilty of committing the crime of "Embezzlement" ex Article 372 KUHP.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Bau-Bau District Court & Southeast Sulawesi High Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning the leasing of the Jembatan Batu warehouse in Wale Village, Buton Regency, on April 9, 1998, to witness [Lessee] (via Yanto Alexander) for Rp 8,500,000.— per year; documentary evidence of SHGB No. 91 of 1989 and original purchase receipts dated December 22, 1987, valued at Rp 27,500,000.— in the name of [Party C]; utilization of rental funds by the Defendant for his child's medical expenses in Surabaya; and civil reconvention lawsuit case files No. 29/Pdt.G/1997/PN.BB jo. No. 62/Pdt.G/99.PT.Sultra.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The appellate *Judex Facti* of Southeast Sulawesi High Court misapplied the law (constituting an impure acquittal reviewable via cassation ex Article 244 KUHAP).
# The element of unlawful ownership (*zich toe-eigenen*) was proven legally and convincingly because the Defendant realized a decision to act as owner by leasing out the warehouse without the lawful owner's consent and using rental proceeds for personal use.
# Prior to any court decision establishing the Defendant as owner, [Party C] remained legally regarded as the lawful owner pursuant to SHGB No. 91.
# The Supreme Court annulled the High Court decision and adjudicated afresh, convicting the Defendant of Embezzlement (Article 372 KUHP) and sentencing him to 2 months' imprisonment with a 4-month probation period.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court ruled: Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation ('''Public Prosecutor at the Bau-Bau State Prosecutor's Office'''); Annulling Southeast Sulawesi High Court Decision No. 04/Pid/2000/PT.Sultra dated March 4, 2000; and ADJUDICATING AFRESH: 1. Declaring Defendant [Defendant] proven legally and convincingly guilty of committing the crime of "Embezzlement"; 2. Sentencing the Defendant to imprisonment for 2 (two) months; 3. Stipulating that the sentence need not be served unless a final and binding court decision determines otherwise prior to the expiration of the 4-month probation period; 4. Ordering the return of evidence (SHGB Warehouse & rental receipts attached; original warehouse purchase receipt dated Dec 22, 1987, returned to [Party C]); and charging cassation court costs amounting to Rp 2,500.— to the Defendant.


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Criminal Code (KUHP):'''
  * Article 372: Crime of Embezzlement (Elements: Whoever, intentionally, unlawfully owns, property wholly or partly belonging to another, held lawfully).
  * Article 22 paragraph (1): Deduction of detention period.
* '''Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP / Law No. 8 of 1981):''' Article 244: Cassation petitions over judgments other than pure acquittals (*vrijspraak*).
* '''Criminal Doctrine & Jurisprudence:'''
  * Hoge Raad Arrests of October 16, 1905, and March 26, 1906: Juridical definition of *Zich Toe-eigenen* (Unlawful Ownership).
  * Supreme Court Decision No. 148/K/Kr/1969 (December 23, 1970): Conditional sentencing / probation.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* Defendant [Defendant] leased the warehouse in Jembatan Batu, Bau-Bau, on April 9, 1998, to [Lessee] for Rp 8,500,000.— per year.
* The disputed warehouse was proven to be the lawful property of witness [Party C] based on Building Land Rights Certificate No. 91 of 1989 and original purchase receipts dated December 22, 1987.
* Defendant leased the warehouse without consent from [Party C] and enjoyed rental proceeds for personal purposes.
* Defendant's acts satisfied all elements of the crime of "Embezzlement" under Article 372 KUHP.


=== Not Established / Set Aside ===


* Defendant's defense asserting that the warehouse constituted joint assets of Irian Store or immune to criminal liability due to pending civil disputes was set aside and rejected by the Supreme Court because the Defendant lacked valid ownership proof while SHGB registration remained validly vested in [Party C].


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Separation Between Civil Disputes and Criminal Liability: This landmark ruling establishes vital guidance ensuring that unadjudicated civil claims cannot serve as a "shield" to justify physical possession or unauthorized leasing of certified property without permission from registered owners.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Can someone who leases out a building under an SHGB registered in another person's name without permission be convicted of embezzlement (Article 372 KUHP) even if claiming the building is subject to a pending civil dispute?'''


'''A:''' Yes, they can be convicted. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 972 K/Pid/2000, leasing out another party's building/warehouse without permission and utilizing rental proceeds for personal use satisfies the element of "unlawful ownership" (*zich toe-eigenen*) under Article 372 KUHP. Prior to any final court decision establishing the Defendant as owner, the registered rights holder (SHGB) must remain regarded as the lawful owner.
