== Overview ==

Supreme Court Decision Reg. No. 98 K/TUN/1998 dated February 8, 2000, establishes fundamental jurisprudence and legal rules in Land Law and State Administrative Law: Land originating from Western property rights (*Eigendom*) that has reverted to the State cannot be subject to ownership status certification issued by Village Heads (*Lurah*) and Sub-District Heads (*Camat*), as they lack the authority to issue statements of ownership for such lands. The issuance of land titles based on Lurah/Camat statements regarding former *Eigendom* land violates Government Regulation No. 10 of 1961 and breaches the Principles of Good Governance (*Algemene Beginselen van Behoorlijk Bestuur* / AAUPB).

== Case Background ==

The Original Plaintiff / Petitioner for Cassation ([Plaintiff], SH, retired Principal Senior Prosecutor IV/e / former Deputy Attorney General for General Crimes) acquired a plot of land measuring approximately 1,000 m² on Jalan Sultan Agung, Semarang, pursuant to the Decree of the Minister of Agriculture/Agrarian Affairs dated July 15, 1963, No. SK.I/376/Ka/63 under Freehold status (*Hak Milik*). However, when the Plaintiff sought to register the land, obstacles arose. Meanwhile, the Defendant (Head of the Land Office of Semarang Municipality), pursuant to the Central Java Governor's Decree dated August 18, 1987, No. SK.DA.II/HGB/662/I/1929/87, issued Building Use Rights (*HGB*) No. 280 in the name of Agung Bunakur Partowidjojo, which was subsequently transferred and upgraded into Freehold Title (*SHM*) No. 224 (in the name of Adi Suharno) and SHM No. 225 (in the name of Reddy Susyanto) on June 19, 1992.

The Plaintiff filed a lawsuit seeking the cancellation of SHM No. 224 and SHM No. 225 at the Semarang State Administrative Court. The Semarang State Administrative Court (Decision No. 11/G/TUN/TN/1997/PTUN.SMG dated October 2, 1997) rejected the Plaintiff's lawsuit. The Surabaya State Administrative High Court (Decision No. 91/B/TUN/1997/PT.TUN.SBY dated January 13, 1998) affirmed the Semarang State Administrative Court judgment. Dissatisfied with the ruling, the Plaintiff filed a cassation petition to the Supreme Court.

== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==

* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The disputed land originated from Western property rights (*Eigendom*) that had reverted to the State. Consequently, Village Heads (*Lurah*) and Sub-District Heads (*Camat*) lack the authority to issue Statements of Ownership regarding such land, rendering the issuance of Freehold Titles No. 224 and No. 225 based on such Lurah/Camat statements contrary to Government Regulation No. 10 of 1961.
# The *Judex Facti* erred in interpreting the Ministerial Decree of Agriculture/Agrarian Affairs dated July 15, 1963 (exhibit P.1A), which was incorrectly deemed void on the grounds that the Plaintiff had not performed land registration. Exhibit P.1A contained no registration time-limit clause, and the Plaintiff had already been designated as the lawful owner entitled to erect buildings thereon (exhibit P.2).
# The issuance of the Central Java Governor's Decree No. SK.DA.II/HGB/662/I/1929/87 dated August 18, 1987, serving as the basis for the disputed certificates, failed to apply the Principles of Good Governance (*AAUPB*); thus, the issuance of SHM No. 224 and SHM No. 225 is contrary to law and null and void (*batal demi hukum*).
* '''Ruling:''' Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation [Plaintiff], SH.; Annulling the Surabaya State Administrative High Court decision dated January 13, 1998, No. 91/B/TUN/1997/PT.TUN.SBY jo. the Semarang State Administrative Court decision dated October 2, 1997, No. 11/G/TUN/TN/1997/PTUN.SMG; and Independently Adjudicating: (1) Granting the Plaintiff's lawsuit; (2) Declaring null and void (*batal demi hukum*) the Defendant's Decree dated June 19, 1992, concerning Freehold Title (*SHM*) No. 224 and SHM No. 225, both located in Gajahmungkur Village (formerly Wonotingal), Semarang Municipality; (3) Ordering the Defendant to issue a certificate of freehold title in the name of the Plaintiff ([Plaintiff], SH.) covering the disputed land object measuring approximately 1,000 m² (40 m x 25 m); (4) Ordering the Respondent for Cassation to pay all court costs across all levels of jurisdiction (assessed at Rp 100,000 at the cassation level). *(Decided by Cassation Panel of Justices: H. Soeharto, SH. [Presiding], H. Achmad Kowi AS., SH., and Iskandar Kamil, SH.)*.

== Overview ==


Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia Decision No. 991 K/Pid/2001, dated December 13, 2001, established a fundamental criminal procedural and material criminal law rule concerning violations of the witness testimony rule (*Unus Testis Nullus Testis* ex Article 185 paragraph 2 KUHAP) and the offense of instigating the insertion of false statements into an authentic deed (Article 266 paragraph 1 KUHP):


The *Judex Facti* of the Medan District Court misapplied evidentiary law by relying solely on the testimony of a single witness (the Notary), while ignoring the rights and testimonies of other sworn witnesses (the remaining heirs) (*Unus Testis Nullus Testis* ex Article 185 paragraph 2 KUHAP). The Defendant's ([Defendant]) action in approaching Notary H. Djaidir, SH, and instigating the insertion of false statements into Authentic Deed Minutes of Meeting No. 37 of 1995—falsely claiming that a General Meeting of Shareholders (*RUPS*) of PT Kwala Gunung had been held appointing himself as President Director without the consent and inclusion of 8 other lawful heirs—violated the 1982 Will and was qualified as the crime of instigating the insertion of false statements into an authentic deed ex Article 266 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code.


== Executive Summary ==


The central legal principle established in this decision is that single-witness reliance violating statutory corroboration rules invalidates acquittals, and corporate takeovers via fabricated notarial meeting records constitute prosecutable criminal falsification.


Key elements established in the adjudication:
* Convictions or acquittals resting on uncorroborated single-witness testimony violate statutory witness corroboration rules (*unus testis nullus testis*).
* Falsely recording shareholder meeting outcomes in notarial deeds without required heir consent constitutes criminal falsification under Article 266 KUHP.
* Acquittals based on flawed evidentiary interpretations are impure acquittals reviewable and reversible on cassation.


== Case Background ==


The Original Defendant / Respondent for Cassation ('''[Defendant]''', [age removed], entrepreneur) was charged with instigating the insertion of false statements into an authentic deed (Article 266 paragraph 1 KUHP) for approaching Notary H. Djaidir, SH, in Medan on January 11, 1995, and requesting the drafting of GMS Minutes Deed No. 37 of 1995 for PT Kwala Gunung reflecting a fictitious GMS appointing himself as President Director. In reality, no such meeting was held, and the action lacked the presence, consent, or participation of 8 other lawful heirs of the late Suandi Kongsi, violating Will No. 2 dated April 2, 1982. 


The Medan District Court (Decision No. 1441/Pid.B/2000/PN.Mdn dated December 18, 2000) acquitted the Defendant (*vrijspraak*) based solely on the Notary's testimony. The Public Prosecutor at the Medan State Prosecutor's Office filed a cassation petition with the Supreme Court.


== Claims, Evidence and Source Mapping ==


{| class="wikitable"
! No.
! Legal Statement / Fact
! Evidence / Judicial Consideration
! Source
|-
| '''1'''
| '''Primary Legal Principle (Unus Testis Nullus Testis):''' The *Judex Facti* misapplied evidentiary law by relying on a single witness (Notary) while ignoring other sworn testimonies.
| Jurisprudence Headnote page 337 & Supreme Court Considerations pages 338, 352: "The Judex Factie misapplied the law, especially evidentiary law, by observing only a single witness, while ignoring the rights of other witnesses even though all witnesses were sworn according to their respective religions (Anas testis nullus testis);"
| 991K_Pid_2001.pdf, Passages 1, 2, and 16
|-
| '''2'''
| '''Facts of Instigating False Statements:''' Defendant [Defendant] had Notary H. Djaidir, SH, draft Deed No. 37 of 1995 regarding PT Kwala Gunung's GMS pretending the meeting was valid, without consent or presence of 8 other heirs.
| Supreme Court Considerations pages 338 and 352: "a. Defendant [Defendant]'s act of placing false statements into an authentic deed, namely Deed No. 37 of 1995... ignoring the rights of other heirs... b. Deed No. 37 of 1995 contents contradicted the 1982 Will..."
| 991K_Pid_2001.pdf, Passages 2, 6, and 16
|-
| '''3'''
| '''Shareholding & Will Facts:''' Late Suandi Kongsi died on Nov 11, 1991, leaving 9 heirs and Will No. 2 dated April 2, 1982 (Notary Raskami Sembiring, SH) distributing shares.
| Indictment Posita pages 341, 342, and 343: Defendant knew the contents of the will and share distributions among 9 heirs, yet unilaterally seized corporate leadership.
| 991K_Pid_2001.pdf, Passages 5, 6, and 7
|-
| '''4'''
| '''Cassation Admissibility over Impure Acquittal:''' Prosecutor's cassation was admissible because the District Court acquittal rested upon flawed evidentiary interpretation rather than a pure acquittal.
| Supreme Court Considerations page 351: If an acquittal rests upon a flawed interpretation of evidence/crime elements, such acquittal is not a pure acquittal, rendering cassation mandatory and admissible ex Article 244 KUHAP.
| 991K_Pid_2001.pdf, Passage 15
|-
| '''5'''
| '''Supreme Court Adjudication Afresh Ruling:''' The Supreme Court annulled the Medan District Court acquittal and sentenced Defendant [Defendant] to 2 (two) years' imprisonment.
| Supreme Court Ruling pages 338 and 353: "Annulling the Medan District Court decision dated December 18, 2000 No. 1441/Pid.B/2000/PN.Mdn... ADJUDICATING AFRESH: Declaring Defendant proven legally and convincingly... Sentencing Defendant to a prison term of 2 (two) years;"
| 991K_Pid_2001.pdf, Passages 2 and 17
|-
| '''6'''
| '''Identity of the Defendant:''' [Defendant] ([age removed], born [place removed], Entrepreneur, residing at [address removed]).
| Expressly stated in decision identity pages 340 and 355.
| 991K_Pid_2001.pdf, Passages 4 and 19
|}


== Legal and Procedural Issues ==


=== Violation of Independent and Corroborative Witness Evidence Rules (*Unus Testis Nullus Testis* ex Article 185 paragraph 2 KUHAP) ===


The primary issue was whether a District Court judgment acquitting a Defendant based solely on the uncorroborated testimony of a single witness (the drafting Notary), while ignoring testimonies of victim witnesses (other heirs) who were sworn under oath, is valid under criminal procedure.


The Supreme Court held that it is Invalid (*Null and Void*). Pursuant to Article 185 paragraph (2) of the KUHAP, the testimony of a single witness alone unsupported by other lawful evidence is insufficient to prove that a Defendant is guilty (*Unus Testis Nullus Testis*). The *Judex Facti* of Medan District Court committed a manifest legal error in evidentiary evaluation by elevating the dubious testimony of the Notary while unlawfully setting aside other heir witnesses bound by religious oaths who testified to the true facts that no GMS ever occurred and their rights were subverted.


=== Proof of the Element "Instigating the Insertion of False Statements into an Authentic Deed" (Article 266 paragraph 1 KUHP) ===


The action of an heir approaching a Notary and requesting the recording of GMS Minutes for Corporate Management Replacement as if a valid meeting had been conducted, when such GMS was never attended or approved by other lawful shareholders/heirs and contradicted the testamentary will, legally and perfectly satisfies all elements of the crime under Article 266 paragraph (1) of the Criminal Code.


== Question of Law and Question of Fact ==


=== Question of Law (Cassation / Judex Juris) ===


'''Question:'''


Did the *Judex Facti* (Medan District Court) misapply evidentiary law (*foutieve kepassing van het bewijsrecht*) ex Article 185 paragraph (2) KUHAP by ignoring the testimonies of sworn heir witnesses and acquitting the Defendant of charges under Article 266 paragraph (1) KUHP?


'''Supreme Court Ruling:'''


Yes, the Medan District Court misapplied evidentiary law. The Supreme Court granted the Public Prosecutor's cassation petition, annulled Medan District Court Decision No. 1441/Pid.B/2000/PN.Mdn, and adjudicated afresh, declaring Defendant [Defendant] proven legally and convincingly guilty of committing the crime of "Instigating the insertion of false statements into an authentic deed" ex Article 266 paragraph (1) KUHP and sentencing him to 2 years' imprisonment.


=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Medan District Court) ===


Examination of facts concerning the death of late Suandi Kongsi (Khong Tong Tian) on November 11, 1991; existence of Will No. 2 dated April 2, 1982, by Notary Raskami Sembiring, SH; status of 9 lawful heirs; execution of Deed No. 37 dated January 11, 1995, before Notary H. Djaidir, SH, on A. Yani Street, Medan; claims of a fictitious GMS attended solely by the Defendant, his wife, and child; and control over corporate assets of PT Kwala Gunung, PT Sijabut, and PT Sri Perlak valued at tens of billions of rupiahs.


== Core Legal Principle (Ratio Decidendi) ==


* '''Ratio Decidendi:'''
# The *Judex Facti* of Medan District Court misapplied evidentiary law by acquitting the Defendant based solely on the testimony of a single witness (the Notary) while ignoring other sworn heir witnesses, violating the *Unus Testis Nullus Testis* principle ex Article 185 paragraph (2) KUHAP.
# This acquittal constituted an impure acquittal reviewable and reversible via cassation ex Article 244 KUHAP.
# Witness testimonies established that Deed No. 37 of 1995 contained false statements, subverted the rights of 8 heirs, and contradicted the 1982 Will.
# The Supreme Court annulled the Medan District Court decision and adjudicated afresh, sentencing Defendant [Defendant] to 2 years' imprisonment.


== Ruling ==


The Supreme Court ruled: Granting the cassation petition from Petitioner for Cassation ('''Public Prosecutor at the Medan State Prosecutor's Office'''); Annulling the Medan District Court decision dated December 18, 2000, No. 1441/Pid.B/2000/PN.Mdn; and ADJUDICATING AFRESH: 1. Declaring Defendant [Defendant] proven legally and convincingly guilty of committing the crime of "Instigating the insertion of false statements into an authentic deed"; 2. Sentencing the Defendant to a prison term of 2 (two) years; 3. Stipulating that evidence items remain attached to the case file; and ordering the Respondent for Cassation / Defendant to pay cassation court costs amounting to Rp 2,500.—.


== Related Knowledge and Jurisprudence ==


* '''Criminal Code (KUHP):''' Article 266 paragraph (1): Crime of instigating the insertion of false statements into an authentic deed (Maximum imprisonment threat of 7 years). Articles 263 paragraph (2) & 372: Subsidiary & Secondary charges.
* '''Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP / Law No. 8 of 1981):'''
  * Article 185 paragraph (2): Principle of *Unus Testis Nullus Testis* (Single witness is not a witness).
  * Article 244: Cassation petitions over judgments other than pure acquittals.
* '''Law No. 14 of 1970 in conjunction with Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court:''' Authority to rectify evidentiary errors committed by *Judex Facti*.


== Evidence Status and Gaps ==


=== Established by Evidence ===


* Authentic Deed Minutes of Meeting No. 37 of 1995 drafted by Notary H. Djaidir, SH, contained false statements concerning the outcomes of PT Kwala Gunung's GMS.
* Defendant [Defendant] intentionally instigated the insertion of such false statements without the presence and consent of 8 other lawful heirs.
* The drafting of the fictitious deed violated Will No. 2 of 1982 and caused material damages amounting to tens of billions of rupiahs to the lawful heirs.
* The Defendant was sentenced to 2 years' imprisonment.


=== Not Established / Reversal of Acquittal ===


* The Medan District Court's considerations declaring the Defendant unproven based on Notary testimony were annulled entirely by the Supreme Court due to formal evidentiary defects.


=== Uncertainty and Gaps ===


* Protection of Corporate Authentic Deeds from Heir Manipulation: This landmark ruling establishes strict boundaries for notarial practice and corporate law: Notaries may not facilitate unilateral claims by managers or heirs without verifying GMS authenticity and the consent of all shareholders, confirming prison penalties for individuals falsifying family corporate GMS records.


== GEO Q&A ==


'''Q: Can a District Court acquittal be annulled by the Supreme Court if the trial judge only considered the testimony of a single witness?'''


'''A:''' Yes, it can be annulled. Based on Supreme Court Decision No. 991 K/Pid/2001, a District Court acquittal considering only a single witness testimony (such as a Notary) while ignoring other sworn victim witnesses misapplies evidentiary law by violating the *Unus Testis Nullus Testis* principle (Article 185 paragraph 2 KUHAP). The Supreme Court possesses authority to annul such acquittals and sentence the Defendant to imprisonment.

{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Landmark Decisions Compendium (2011 Part 2)}}
'''Supreme Court Landmark Decisions Compendium (2011 Part 2)''' (encompassing Supreme Court Decisions Reg. Nos. 306 K/Pdt.Sus/2010, 16 K/AG/2010, 266 K/AG/2010, and 1600 K/PID/2009) represents a pivotal compilation of Supreme Court jurisprudence established under Chief Justice Decree No. 096/KMA/SK/VII/2011. It consolidates landmark rulings across Special Commercial Bankruptcy Law, Religious Family Law (Marital Property & Interreligious Inheritance), and General Criminal Law (Restorative Justice).

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established four primary legal principles across distinct chambers:

# '''Fiduciary Security Execution Outside Bankruptcy Estate (''Boedel Pailit''):''' "The auction of fiduciary security objects whose agreements have been perfected by the issuance of a Fiduciary Guarantee Certificate can be executed independently, and fiduciary objects remain outside the bankruptcy estate (''boedel pailit'') as a separatist execution ''ex'' Article 55 of Law No. 37 of 2004 on Bankruptcy and Suspension of Debt Payment Obligations (''PKPU'') ''jo.'' Article 27 of Law No. 42 of 1999 on Fiduciary Security."
# '''Wills by Way of Obligation (''Wasiat Wajibah'') for Non-Muslim Wives:''' "A non-Muslim wife left behind by a deceased Muslim husband is not included as a statutory legal heir, but is entitled to receive an allocation by way of an obligatory will (''Wasiat Wajibah'') from her deceased husband's inheritance equivalent to a wife's standard statutory inheritance share."
# '''Proportional Marital Property Partition for Neglected Wives:''' "A wife is awarded a three-quarters (3/4) share of the joint marital property (''harta bersama''), because the entirety of the joint marital property was generated through the wife's independent labor while the husband failed to provide maintenance for the wife and children for 11 years."
# '''Restorative Justice in Family Criminal Matters:''' "In resolving criminal cases, if a judge finds an effective resolution based on principles of balance, a sense of justice, forgiveness (victim's/mother-in-law's withdrawal of complaint), and far greater social benefit, the judge may terminate prosecution by departing from legal procedural formalities (''Restorative Justice'')."

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petitions of the Petitioners for Cassation in each respective case, annulled the erroneous lower court rulings (''judex facti''), and reinforced legal certainty and substantive justice.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Legal Protection of Separatist Execution Rights for Fiduciary Guarantee Holders in Bankruptcy (Article 55 Bankruptcy Law ''jo.'' Article 27 Fiduciary Law) ===
''Can fiduciary security objects registered with a Fiduciary Guarantee Certificate prior to bankruptcy adjudication be executed independently by separatist creditors without being pooled into the bankruptcy estate (''boedel pailit'')?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Executable / Outside Bankruptcy Estate (''Boedel Pailit'').'''
Pursuant to Article 55 of the Bankruptcy Law ''jo.'' Article 27 of the Fiduciary Law, preferential rights of fiduciary beneficiaries are not extinguished by bankruptcy. Fiduciary objects lie outside bankruptcy liquidation; hence, execution auctions conducted by separatist creditors prior to or during bankruptcy are lawful, and auction proceeds do not enter the bankruptcy estate (''boedel pailit'').

=== 2. Protection of Non-Muslim Spouses' Civil Rights via Obligatory Wills (''Wasiat Wajibah'' ''ex'' Compilation of Islamic Law / KHI Article 209) ===
''Is a non-Muslim spouse who accompanied a Muslim spouse for over a decade entitled to receive a share of the deceased spouse's estate?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Entitled to an Obligatory Will (''Wasiat Wajibah'').'''
Although religious differences bar formal Islamic inheritance rights (inheritance impediment), in the interest of justice and acknowledgment of spousal devotion, the Supreme Court constructed non-Muslim spousal rights via ''Wasiat Wajibah'' equivalent to a wife's standard statutory share (1/2 share of joint marital property and statutory inheritance from separate assets) ''ex'' Article 209 of the Compilation of Islamic Law (KHI).

=== 3. Proportionality in Marital Property Partition Arising from Spousal Default in Maintenance (Article 37 Marriage Law ''jo.'' Substantive Justice) ===
Where a husband fails to provide maintenance for 11 years and all joint property is generated solely through the wife's labor and earnings, joint marital property is not partitioned 50:50 equally, but the wife is awarded a three-quarters (3/4) share while the husband receives one-quarter (1/4).

=== 4. Application of Restorative Justice in Complaint Offenses / Family Criminal Matters (Article 184 Criminal Procedure Code ''jo.'' Article 28 Judicial Power Law) ===
Where a victim-witness (mother-in-law) formally withdraws a complaint and forgives the Defendant (daughter-in-law) in open court for family harmony and grandchildren's welfare, judges possess the authority to prioritize restorative justice to restore disrupted legal balance and declare public prosecution inadmissible (''niet ontvankelijk verklaard'').

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
* ''Commercial Case:'' Did the Central Jakarta Commercial Court possess authority to declare a KPKNL fiduciary execution auction an unlawful act invalidating the auction?
*: '''Supreme Court Answer:''' No. Fiduciary objects lie outside bankruptcy ''ex'' Article 55 of the Bankruptcy Law. The Commercial Court misapplied the law. The Supreme Court annulled the Commercial Court ruling and dismissed the Curator's lawsuit.
* ''Inheritance Case:'' Did the Makassar Religious High Court err in applying the law by stripping away all civil rights of a non-Muslim wife?
*: '''Supreme Court Answer:''' Yes. A non-Muslim wife is entitled to ''Wasiat Wajibah'' equivalent to a wife's inheritance share. The Supreme Court annulled the appellate ruling and independently adjudicated.
* ''Criminal Case:'' Did the Yogyakarta High Court err in applying rigid procedural formalities (''ex'' Article 75 Criminal Code) by ignoring a victim's complaint withdrawal in court?
*: '''Supreme Court Answer:''' Yes. Judges must explore substantive justice and Restorative Justice. The Supreme Court annulled the High Court ruling and declared prosecution inadmissible.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Religious Courts, District Courts, & Commercial Courts) ===
Verification of Coffee Fiduciary Security Certificate No. W6.836.HT.04.06.TH.2007; Marriage Certificate No. 57/K.PS/XI/1990 (Evie Lany Mosinta & Armaya); land ownership deeds for 4 parcels in Klaten, Bantul, and Sleman in the name of [Wife] Nur Rochimah; and the Formal Complaint Withdrawal Letter dated October 28, 2008, executed by Ny. Emiwati.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''Law No. 37 of 2004 on Bankruptcy and PKPU:''' Articles 55, 31, 300.
* '''Law No. 42 of 1999 on Fiduciary Security:''' Articles 15, 27, 29.
* '''Compilation of Islamic Law (KHI):''' Article 209 (Obligatory Wills / ''Wasiat Wajibah'') & Marital Property Rules.
* '''Law No. 1 of 1974 on Marriage:''' Article 37 (Marital Property).
* '''Criminal Code & Criminal Procedure Code (KUHP / KUHAP):''' Article 75 Criminal Code, Articles 372/378 Criminal Code, & Restorative Justice Principles.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* '''Separatist Property Rights Doctrine in Bankruptcy:''' Real security holders (Fiduciary/Hypothec/Mortgage) may execute rights as if no bankruptcy proceedings exist.
* '''Interreligious Wasiat Wajibah Doctrine:''' Groundbreaking Supreme Court jurisprudence guaranteeing economic rights protection for non-Muslim spouses from Muslim decedent estates via ''Wasiat Wajibah''.
* '''Criminal Restorative Justice Doctrine:''' Criminal law as ''ultimum remedium''; reconciliation and family harmony represent primary objectives of substantive legal enforcement.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* Execution auctions over coffee fiduciary security belonging to PT Tripanca Group executed by PT Bank Mega Tbk via KPKNL Bandar Lampung are '''PROVEN LAWFUL AND FIDUCIARY OBJECTS LIE OUTSIDE THE BANKRUPTCY ESTATE (''BOEDEL PAILIT'')'''.
* Evie Lany Mosinta (non-Muslim wife) is '''PROVEN ENTITLED TO 1/2 OF JOINT MARITAL PROPERTY AND AN OBLIGATORY WILL (''WASIAT WAJIBAH'') FROM HER DECEASED HUSBAND'S ESTATE'''.
* Ny. [Wife] Nur Rochimah is '''PROVEN ENTITLED TO A 3/4 SHARE OF JOINT MARITAL PROPERTY'''.
* Complaint withdrawal by Ny. Emiwati is '''PROVEN TO TERMINATE CRIMINAL PROSECUTION AGAINST [Defendant] PURSUANT TO RESTORATIVE JUSTICE'''.

=== Dismissed Claims ===
* The Curator's claim seeking to pull fiduciary auction proceeds amounting to Rp 277.5 billion into the bankruptcy estate (''boedel pailit'') was '''REJECTED ENTIRELY BY THE SUPREME COURT'''.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Balancing Substantive Justice in Supreme Court Jurisprudence:''' Landmark rulings in this compendium illustrate a shifting paradigm in Indonesian adjudication: the Supreme Court consistently rejects rigid legal formalism in favor of substantive justice—whether protecting fiduciary creditor legal certainty, offering humanitarian protection to interreligious couples, valuing wives' economic independence, or halting family criminal prosecution via restorative justice.

{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Landmark Decisions Compendium (2011 Part 3)}}
'''Supreme Court Landmark Decisions Compendium (2011 Part 3)''' (encompassing Supreme Court Decisions Reg. Nos. 1542 K/Pid.Sus/2008 and 2399 K/Pid.Sus/2010) represents a pivotal compilation of Supreme Court jurisprudence established under the Supreme Court Jurisprudence framework. It consolidates strategic landmark rulings across Special Environmental Criminal Law and Special Anti-Corruption Criminal Law.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established two primary legal principles:

# '''Prohibition of Foreign Hazardous Waste Dumping & Review of Acquittals (''Vrijspraak''):''' "Every person is prohibited from dumping waste originating from outside Indonesia into the Indonesian environmental media (''ex'' Article 20 of Law No. 23 of 1997 on Environmental Management)." The Supreme Court possesses the authority to examine and annul pure acquittals (''vrijspraak'') in the interest of law and justice whenever the ''Judex Facti'' is proven to have erred in applying the law or misinterpreting evidentiary rules. An operational manager (Acting Resident Manager) of a hotel who approves contracts and payment for transporting and dumping hazardous B3 waste (used oil, paint, B3 sludge) from a foreign cruise ship ("Leisure World") into Indonesian terrestrial territory bears criminal liability.
# '''Proportional Justice in Anti-Corruption Sentencing:''' "The Supreme Court in its adjudicative function may apply the law to concrete cases in a manner whose actualization is not entirely aligned with the exact spirit and intent of the legislature, but is harmonized with the amount of state losses arising from the Defendant's actions and the demands of public justice." The application of mandatory minimum special penalties ''ex'' Article 2 paragraph (1) of the Anti-Corruption Law (minimum 4 years' imprisonment) may be departed from or harmonized by the Cassation Judge when personal gains obtained by the defendant are extremely minor (e.g., an intermediary fee of Rp 2,900,000), resulting in a sentence of 1 (one) year's imprisonment to prevent disproportionate sentencing that injures public a sense of justice.

The Supreme Court granted the Public Prosecutor's cassation petitions in both cases, annulled the lower court rulings (''judex facti'') that improperly acquitted or disproportionately mitigated sentences, and independently adjudicated (''mengadili sendiri'') by imposing prison sentences and fines harmonized with law and justice.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Managerial Criminal Liability (''Corporate Operational Responsibility'') for Environmental Crimes (Articles 20, 42, 43, 45 of Law No. 23 of 1997 ''jo.'' Gov. Reg. No. 85 of 1999) ===
''Can a daily operational manager / person in charge (Acting Resident Manager) be sentenced for dumping foreign B3 waste into Indonesian environmental media, even if they are not the primary corporate Board of Directors?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Prosecutable / Fully Responsible.'''
A daily operational manager/controller of a company possessing authority to approve cooperation contracts, sign invoice payment claims, and stop B3 waste collection who allows such activities to continue is legally proven to commit Environmental Pollution ''ex'' Article 20 ''jo.'' Articles 42, 43, and 45 of Law No. 23 of 1997.

=== 2. Supreme Court Authority to Review Pure Acquittals (''Vrijspraak'') at Cassation Level (Article 244 Criminal Procedure Code ''jo.'' Supreme Court Jurisprudence) ===
''Does the Supreme Court possess authority to examine and annul an acquittal (''vrijspraak'') rendered by a District Court?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Authorized to Examine & Annul.'''
Where a defendant's acquittal by the ''Judex Facti'' relies on erroneous interpretation of delict elements or misapplication of evidentiary law (impure acquittal / ''onzuivere vrijspraak''), the Supreme Court in the interest of law and social justice holds the authority to annul such acquittal and independently adjudicate the criminal case.

=== 3. Judicial Discretion to Depart from Mandatory Minimum Special Penalties for Substantive Justice (Disproportionality Mitigation ''ex'' Article 2 Anti-Corruption Law) ===
Where a defendant's conduct fulfills the formal delict elements of Article 2 paragraph (1) of the Anti-Corruption Law, but state losses or personal gains obtained by the perpetrator are extremely minor (Rp 2,900,000), the Cassation Judge may harmonize penalties (''strafmaat harmonisation'') by imposing a sentence below the 4-year statutory minimum (i.e., 1 year's imprisonment) so that law enforcement does not injure public a sense of justice.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===

* ''Environmental Case:'' Did the ''Judex Facti'' Batam District Court (Decision No. 846/PID.B/2007/PN.BTM) err in applying evidentiary law by acquitting the Defendant on the pretext that the Defendant was not a Director of PT Horizon Bandiar Bahru?
*: '''Supreme Court Answer:''' Yes. Batam District Court misapplied the law. An Acting Resident Manager controlling operational activities bears full responsibility for B3 waste. The Supreme Court granted the Prosecutor's cassation, annulled the acquittal, and sentenced the Defendant to 3 years' imprisonment and a Rp 30 million fine.
* ''Anti-Corruption Case:'' Did West Kalimantan High Court in Pontianak (Decision No. 195/Pid/2010/PT.PTK) exceed its authority and err in imposing a lenient 1-year sentence without adequate legal reasoning?
*: '''Supreme Court Answer:''' Yes. Pontianak High Court provided insufficient reasoning (''onvoldoende gemotiveerd''). However, in the interest of proportional justice regarding the Rp 2.9 million loss, the Supreme Court independently adjudicated by sentencing the Defendant to 1 year's imprisonment and a Rp 200 million fine.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Batam District Court, Singkawang District Court, Pontianak High Court) ===
Verification of facts regarding waste transport from the "Leisure World" cruise ship in OPL Malacca Strait by wooden pompong boats belonging to Andi Abdullah alias Te Lai to the Nongsa Batam temporary dumping site; verification of National Police Bareskrim Labfor Report No. LAB.623/KTF/2007 dated March 12, 2007, concerning B3 contents; verification of temporary disposal site permits; and verification of the Singkawang DPRD uniform procurement project for FY 2007 and fee withdrawals.

{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Landmark Decisions Compendium (2011 Part 4)}}
'''Supreme Court Landmark Decisions Compendium (2011 Part 4)''' (encompassing Supreme Court Decisions Reg. Nos. 154 PK/TUN/2010 and 216 K/TUN/2010) represents a pivotal compilation of Supreme Court jurisprudence established under Chief Justice Decree No. 096/KMA/SK/VII/2011. It consolidates strategic landmark rulings across State Administrative Law (TUN), addressing the limitation of multiple Reconsideration (''Peninjauan Kembali'' / PK) motions in land administrative disputes (corrective justice) and the absolute exclusive authority of the President of the Republic of Indonesia over the dismissal or temporary suspension of Principal Functional Officials (''Widyaiswara Utama'' Grade IV/e).

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established two primary legal principles:

# '''Restriction of Multiple Reconsideration (PK) Motions & Absolute Competence of Civil Courts:''' "In the event of a Reconsideration (''Peninjauan Kembali'') application filed more than one (1) time, it must be evaluated on a case-by-case basis, and in this case, the legally valid reconsideration is the first one." Reconsideration is an extraordinary legal remedy permitted only once ''ex'' Article 66 paragraph (1) of Law No. 14 of 1985 ''jo.'' Law No. 3 of 2009 and Article 23 paragraph (2) of Law No. 4 of 2004. The invalidation of a State Administrative Decision (such as land certificates SHM/SHGB) does not automatically extinguish civil rights over land; land ownership verification remains within the absolute competence of General (Civil) Courts, and Administrative Officials must base remedial decisions on civil court rulings.
# '''Exclusive Presidential Authority Over Principal Functional Officials (Grade IV/e):''' "Only the President possesses the right to dismiss and/or temporarily suspend Civil Servants holding Principal Functional Positions / Principal Educators (''Widyaiswara Utama'' Grade IV/e) from and in their positions." A Ministerial Decree (Minister of Finance Decree No. 113/KMK.01/UP.11 2009) temporarily suspending Drs. Achyar Rusli, Ak., M.A. from the position of Principal Educator Grade IV/e is qualified as legally flawed because it was enacted outside the Minister's authority (''ultravires'') under Law No. 43 of 1999, Gov. Reg. No. 9 of 2003, and Joint Regulation of the Head of the National Civil Service Agency (''LAN & BKN'').

The Supreme Court granted the Reconsideration application of PT Lippo Karawaci, Tbk., annulled the second Reconsideration ruling No. 49 PK/TUN/2007, and affirmed the first Reconsideration ruling No. 20 PK/TUN/2003 which declared the Plaintiff's lawsuit inadmissible (''niet ontvankelijk verklaard''). Simultaneously, the Supreme Court rejected the Minister of Finance's cassation petition and affirmed rulings canceling the Ministerial Suspension Decree.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Constitutionality and Legal Limits of Multiple Reconsideration (PK) Filings in Administrative Law (Article 66(1) Law No. 14 of 1985 ''jo.'' Law No. 3 of 2009 & Article 23(2) Law No. 4 of 2004) ===
''Is it permissible in land disputes within Administrative Courts to file multiple Reconsideration (PK) motions, and which ruling prevails when conflicting Reconsideration rulings emerge?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Permitted Only Once / First PK Prevails.'''
The Reconsideration institution is an extraordinary legal remedy grounded in corrective justice and legal certainty (''litis finis imponi oportet''), permitting filing only once. Where two conflicting Reconsideration rulings arise over the same object and subject, the Supreme Court annuls the second ruling and establishes that the first Reconsideration ruling is legally valid.

=== 2. Absolute Competence of Civil Courts Over Land Ownership Post-Annulment of Administrative Decisions (Article 55 Law No. 5 of 1986) ===
The invalidation of an administrative decision regarding land certificates (SHM/SHGB) by an Administrative Court does not automatically extinguish civil rights over land. Civil ownership rights remain intact until a General (Civil) Court issues a permanent ruling (''inkracht'') determining lawful land ownership.

=== 3. Legality of Government Action (''Bestuursbevoegdheid'') & Ultravires Principle (Article 25 Law No. 43 of 1999 ''jo.'' Gov. Reg. No. 9 of 2003) ===
''Does the Minister of Finance possess authority to issue a temporary suspension decree against a Civil Servant holding a Principal Functional Position (Principal Educator Grade IV/e)?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Minister Lacks Authority / Ultravires.'''
Pursuant to Article 25 of Law No. 43 of 1999 ''jo.'' Article 11 of Gov. Reg. No. 9 of 2003, appointment, dismissal, and temporary suspension of Civil Servants holding Principal Functional Positions (Grade IV/e) fall under the absolute authority of the President. Ministerial decrees suspending Principal Grade Civil Servants are legally flawed due to lack of authority (''gebrek aan bevoegdheid'') and are null and void.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
* ''Lippo Karawaci Case:'' Did the Second Reconsideration Panel (Decision No. 49 PK/TUN/2007) commit a judicial error (''foutieve toepassing van het procesrecht'') by granting a second reconsideration over a dispute finalized in the first reconsideration (No. 20 PK/TUN/2003)?
:'''Supreme Court Answer:''' Yes. A judicial error occurred. Reconsideration is permitted only once. The Supreme Court annulled the second PK and reinstated the first PK ruling as valid.
* ''Principal Educator Case:'' Did the Minister of Finance possess authority to issue a temporary suspension decree against Drs. Achyar Rusli, Ak., M.A. (Principal Educator Grade IV/e)?
:'''Supreme Court Answer:''' No. Authority over Grade IV/e Principal Officials rests exclusively with the President. The Supreme Court rejected the Minister of Finance's cassation petition.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Bandung Administrative Court, Jakarta Administrative Court, Jakarta High Administrative Court) ===
Verification of SHM No. 39/Bencongan measuring 4,223 m² in the name of Amin Lembe dated December 19, 1992, and Auction Minutes No. 37/1996; HGB Certificate No. 6957/Bencongan measuring 4,400 m² in the name of PT Tunggal Reksa Kencana (PT Lippo Karawaci Tbk) dated October 26, 1995; local land inspections (''decharge''); Ministry of Finance Decree No. 113/KMK.01/UP.11 2009 dated April 1, 2009; and DUPAK credit point calculations for Principal Educators.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''Law No. 14 of 1985 ''jo.'' Law No. 5 of 2004 ''jo.'' Law No. 3 of 2009 on the Supreme Court:''' Article 66 paragraph (1) & Article 67 (Single Reconsideration Limit).
* '''Law No. 5 of 1986 ''jo.'' Law No. 9 of 2004 ''jo.'' Law No. 51 of 2009 on State Administrative Courts:''' Articles 53 paragraph (2), 55 (Statutes of Limitation & Grounds for Administrative Lawsuits).
* '''Law No. 43 of 1999 on Civil Service Principles:''' Article 25 (Presidential vs. Appointing Official Authority).
* '''Gov. Reg. No. 9 of 2003 on Appointment, Transfer, and Dismissal of Civil Servants:''' Articles 11 & 12.
* '''Joint Regulation of LAN & BKN No. 7 / No. 17 of 2005:''' Principal Educator Functional Position Rules.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* '''Supreme Court Decision No. 021 PK/PDT.SUS/2009 (March 25, 2009):''' Landmark precedent establishing the strict single Reconsideration rule (''strict single PK rule'').
* '''Corrective Justice Doctrine in Administrative Adjudication:''' Rectifying judicial errors via a second reconsideration is executed strictly to halt conflicting execution rulings and restore judicial legal certainty.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* First Reconsideration Ruling No. 20 PK/TUN/2003 dated June 11, 2004, is '''PROVEN VALID AND BINDING AS THE FINAL COMPLETED RULING'''.
* Second Reconsideration Ruling No. 49 PK/TUN/2007 is '''PROVEN INVALID AND ANNULLED FOR VIOLATING THE SINGLE PK RULE'''.
* Land overlap disputes between SHM No. 39 and HGB No. 6957 are '''PROVEN TO CONSTITUTE CIVIL OWNERSHIP DISPUTES REQUIRING GENERAL COURT ADJUDICATION'''.
* Minister of Finance Decree No. 113/KMK.01/UP.11 2009 is '''PROVEN LEGALLY FLAWED (''ULTRAVIRES'') AND NULL AND VOID'''.
* Temporary suspension of Principal Educators Grade IV/e is '''PROVEN TO BE THE EXCLUSIVE AUTHORITY OF THE PRESIDENT OF INDONESIA'''.

=== Dismissed Contentions (Minister of Finance's Defense) ===
* The Minister of Finance's contention that ministerial authority extended to suspending Grade IV/e officials based on LAN technical guidelines was '''REJECTED ENTIRELY BY THE SUPREME COURT AS CONFLICTING WITH GOV. REG. NO. 9/2003 AND LAW NO. 43/1999'''.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Reconsideration Legal Certainty & Civil Service Functional Protection:''' These landmark administrative rulings establish two unyielding pillars of legal certainty in Indonesia: (1) The Indonesian judicial system rejects protracted litigation through multiple Reconsideration applications; the first PK is final and mandatory; and (2) State administrative officials (Ministers) must comply with statutory hierarchies and are strictly barred from encroaching upon Presidential authority over Principal Functional Officials.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
; Does the Minister of Finance possess authority to temporarily suspend Principal Educators Grade IV/e, and can Reconsideration applications be filed more than once pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence?
: '''Minister Lacks Authority & Reconsideration Permitted Only Once.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. Nos. 154 PK/TUN/2010 and 216 K/TUN/2010:
:* Only the President possesses the right to dismiss and/or temporarily suspend Civil Servants holding Principal Functional / Principal Educator Positions (Grade IV/e). Ministerial suspension decrees are null and void as ''ultravires''.
:* Reconsideration (PK) is an extraordinary legal remedy permitted only one time. Where multiple conflicting Reconsideration rulings occur, the first Reconsideration ruling is legally valid.
:* The Supreme Court annulled second Reconsideration rulings and affirmed that land ownership disputes must be settled in Civil Courts.

{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Landmark Decisions Compendium (2014 Part 1)}}
'''Supreme Court Landmark Decisions Compendium (2014 Part 1)''' (encompassing Supreme Court Decisions Reg. Nos. 154 K/Pdt/2012, 805 K/Pdt/2013, 165 PK/Pdt.Sus/2012, and 505 K/Pdt.Sus-BPSK/2013) represents a pivotal compilation of Supreme Court jurisprudence established under Chief Justice Decree No. 45/KMA/SK/III/2014. It consolidates strategic landmark rulings across General Civil Law, Special Intellectual Property Law (Trademarks), and Special Consumer Dispute Law:

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established four primary legal principles across distinct chambers:

# '''Irrevocability of Marital Property Gifts to Children:''' "Children can sue their parents over joint marital property (''harta gono-gini'') that has been gifted prior to divorce (''ex'' Supreme Court Decision No. 154 K/Pdt/2012)." Such gifts cannot be unilaterally withdrawn or revoked except for restrictive reasons under Article 1688 of the Civil Code (BW), and the sale of gifted property by parents to third parties without the children's consent constitutes an Unlawful Act (Tort / PMH) that is null and void (''nietig'').
# '''Mandatory Registration of Overseas Mixed Marriages:''' "A marriage between an Indonesian citizen and a foreign citizen (mixed marriage) solemnized abroad (e.g., Hong Kong) must be reported to the local Republic of Indonesia Representative Office (''ex'' Article 37 paragraphs (1) and (2) of Law No. 23 of 2006 on Population Administration); if unreported, an application filed at a District Court directing the Civil Registry Office to record such marriage is inadmissible (''niet ontvankelijk verklaard'')."
# '''Distinct Class and Non-Confusing Trademark Comparison (IKEA vs. IKEMA):''' "The IKEMA Trademark (owned by PT Angsa Daya for Class 19 - ceramics/tiles) does not bear a principal resemblance (''persamaan pada pokoknya'') to the Well-Known IKEA Trademark (owned by Inter Ikea Systems B.V. for Classes 11, 21, 24, 35, and 42 - household appliances/furniture) due to differences in goods classification, product types, phonetics/pronunciation, and consumer target markets."
# '''BPSK Lacks Competence Over Insurance Policy Claims:''' "The legal relationship between an insured party and an insurer based on an Insurance Policy constitutes a dispute within the scope of general civil law; therefore, the Consumer Dispute Resolution Board (''BPSK'') lacks competence (''incompetence ratione materiae'') to examine and adjudicate the case in question."

The Supreme Court granted the cassation and reconsideration petitions of the Petitioners in these respective matters, annulled erroneous lower court rulings (''judex facti''), and reinforced legal certainty and substantive justice.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Absolutism of Marital Property Gift Irrevocability to Children (Article 1688 Civil Code / BW) ===
''Can joint marital property gifts agreed upon by both parents prior to divorce be annulled or unilaterally withdrawn via a Notarial Deed?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Cannot Be Unilaterally Revoked.'''
Pursuant to Article 1688 of the Civil Code, gift revocation is valid only if it fulfills 3 restrictive reasons: (1) non-fulfillment of gift conditions, (2) recipient committing crimes against the donor's life, or (3) recipient refusing maintenance when the donor falls into poverty. Unilateral gift revocation deeds are null and void (''nietig''), and parental sales of gifted property without children's consent constitute an Unlawful Act (Tort / PMH).

=== 2. Formal Reporting Obligations for Overseas Mixed Marriages (Article 37 Law No. 23 of 2006 on Population Administration ''jo.'' Article 56 Law No. 1 of 1974) ===
''Can a marriage between an Indonesian citizen and a foreign citizen solemnized abroad without reporting to the KBRI/Indonesian Representative Office be recognized/recorded by a District Court in Indonesia?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Inadmissible (''Niet Ontvankelijk Verklaard'').'''
Pursuant to Article 37 paragraphs (1) and (2) of Law No. 23 of 2006, overseas marriages of Indonesian citizens must be reported to the RI Representative Office in that country. Failure to report constitutes a strict procedural defect rendering applications for recognition/recording at Civil Registry Offices via District Courts inadmissible (''NO'').

=== 3. Testing the ''Neely Resemble'' Doctrine and Goods Class Distinction Against Well-Known Trademarks (Article 6 Law No. 15 of 2001 on Trademarks) ===
The existence of a well-known mark does not automatically prohibit the registration of another mark bearing phonetic similarities in completely distinct goods classes (i.e., IKEMA Class 19 ceramics vs. IKEA Class 11/21/24/35/42 furniture), provided no bad-faith intent to free-ride or mislead consumers (''misleading/confusing'') is proven.

=== 4. Limits of BPSK Absolute Competence (Article 1 point 11 & Article 45 Law No. 8 of 1999 on Consumer Protection) ===
Disputes involving the interpretation of loss/earthquake insurance policy clauses between bank debtors/insured parties and insurance companies constitute pure civil contract disputes falling under the absolute competence of General Courts (District Courts) / Arbitration; hence, BPSK lacks authority to adjudicate such matters.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===
* ''Children's Gift Case:'' Did Surabaya High Court (Decision No. 646/PDT/2010/PT.SBY) correctly affirm the Banyuwangi District Court ruling declaring a unilateral notarial gift revocation deed legally invalid?
:'''Supreme Court Answer:''' Yes. The ''Judex Facti'' reasoning was correct. Marital property gifts cannot be unilaterally revoked ''ex'' Article 1688 Civil Code. The Supreme Court rejected H. Suyit Abdillah's cassation petition.
* ''BPSK Insurance Case:'' Did Padang District Court (Decision No. 101/Pdt.G/BPSK/2013/PN.PDG) and Padang BPSK exceed their absolute jurisdiction by adjudicating a property insurance policy dispute?
:'''Supreme Court Answer:''' Yes. BPSK and Padang District Court misapplied procedural law. BPSK lacks competence over insurance policy claims. The Supreme Court annulled Padang District Court and BPSK Padang rulings and independently adjudicated by declaring BPSK incompetent.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Banyuwangi District Court, Surakarta District Court, Central Jakarta District Court, & Padang District Court) ===
Verification of the Statement Letter of Marital Property Handover dated September 17, 1996; Hong Kong Marriage Certificate No. A 222440 dated January 27, 1993; IKEMA Trademark Certificate No. IDM000247161 Class 19 vs. IKEA; and Loss Adjuster PT Satria Dharma Pusaka Crawford THD reports concerning physical damage to showroom buildings from the Padang earthquake on September 30, 2009.

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===
* '''Civil Code (KUHPerdata / BW):''' Article 1688 (Gift Revocation Rules) & Article 1365 (Tort / Unlawful Acts).
* '''Law No. 23 of 2006 on Population Administration:''' Article 37 paragraphs (1) & (2) (Mandatory Reporting of Overseas Marriages at RI Representatives).
* '''Law No. 15 of 2001 on Trademarks:''' Articles 6 paragraphs (1) & (2) (Principal Resemblance & Different Class Registration).
* '''Law No. 8 of 1999 on Consumer Protection:''' Article 45 (BPSK Authority).
* '''Law No. 14 of 1985 ''jo.'' Law No. 5 of 2004 ''jo.'' Law No. 3 of 2009 on the Supreme Court:''' Cassation & Reconsideration Authority.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===
* '''Doctrine of ''Irrevocability of Inter Vivos Gifts'':''' Completed gifts to children prior to divorce instantly transfer ownership and close the door on unilateral parental annulment.
* '''Doctrine of BPSK Jurisdictional Limits (Absolute Jurisdiction Boundaries):''' BPSK is established to resolve simple consumer disputes; complex insurance policy claim disputes requiring loss adjuster verification and complex contract interpretation fall outside BPSK jurisdiction.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===
* The Statement Letter of Marital Property Handover dated September 17, 1996, is '''PROVEN VALID, AND GIFTS TO CHILDREN CANNOT BE UNILATERALLY REVOKED'''.
* The mixed marriage of A.S.M. Maniruzzaman and Fransisca Sri Luyatni WR in Hong Kong is '''PROVEN NEVER REPORTED TO THE KBRI/RI REPRESENTATIVE, RENDERING REGISTRATION PETITIONS INADMISSIBLE (''NO'')'''.
* IKEMA Trademark owned by PT Angsa Daya (Class 19) is '''PROVEN NOT TO BEAR A PRINCIPAL RESEMBLANCE TO THE IKEA TRADEMARK'''.
* Padang BPSK is '''PROVEN TO LACK COMPETENCE TO ADJUDICATE PT ACA INSURANCE POLICY CLAIM DISPUTES'''.
* Cassation/Reconsideration petitions filed by H. Suyit Abdillah, A.S.M. Maniruzzaman, and Inter Ikea Systems B.V. are '''REJECTED BY THE SUPREME COURT'''.

=== Dismissed Findings (Overturned Rulings) ===
* Padang BPSK Ruling No. 49/BPSK-PDG/ARBT/V/2013 ordering PT ACA to pay Rp 1 billion plus 5%/day fines was '''ANNULLED ENTIRELY BECAUSE BPSK LACKED JURISDICTION'''.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Population Administration Certainty, Children's Rights Protection, & Consumer Jurisdiction:''' Landmark rulings in this compendium deliver four pillars of legal certainty in Indonesia: (1) Marital property gifts to children are final and immune to parental divorce manipulations; (2) Legality of overseas marriages must comply with strict reporting discipline at RI Diplomatic Representatives; (3) Protection of well-known marks must not stifle local, different-class trademark registrations filed in good faith; and (4) BPSK is strictly barred from usurping District Court jurisdiction over civil insurance policy disputes.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
; Does BPSK possess authority to adjudicate insurance policy claim disputes, and can overseas marriages without KBRI reports be recorded pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence?
: '''BPSK Lacks Competence & Marriage Petitions Inadmissible (''NO'').''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. Nos. 505 K/Pdt.Sus-BPSK/2013 and 805 K/Pdt/2013:
* The Consumer Dispute Resolution Board (''BPSK'') lacks competence to adjudicate insurance policy claim disputes, as insurance policy legal relationships constitute general civil disputes falling under the competence of District Courts / Arbitration.
* Mixed marriages solemnized abroad must be reported to the local RI Representative Office (KBRI/Consulate) pursuant to Article 37 of Law No. 23 of 2006 on Population Administration. If unreported, applications for recognition/recording at Civil Registry Offices are inadmissible (''niet ontvankelijk verklaard'').
* The Supreme Court annulled Padang BPSK rulings and rejected cassation petitions concerning unreported mixed marriages.

{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Landmark Decisions Compendium (2014 Part 2)}}
'''Supreme Court Landmark Decisions Compendium (2014 Part 2)''' (encompassing Supreme Court Decisions Reg. Nos. 39 K/AG/2013, 676 K/AG/2012, 724 K/AG/2012, 509 K/TUN/2013, 450 K/TUN/2013, and 97 K/MIL/2011) represents a pivotal compilation of Supreme Court jurisprudence established under Chief Justice Decree No. 45/KMA/SK/III/2014. It consolidates strategic landmark rulings across Religious Family Law, State Administrative Law (TUN), and Military Criminal Law.

== Executive Summary ==
The Supreme Court established six primary legal principles across distinct chambers:

# '''Right to Sue for Inheritance by Estate Controllers & the Principle of ''Ijbary'' (''Asas Ijbary''):''' "A Plaintiff who controls the entirety of the inheritance estate may file an inheritance lawsuit against Defendants who do not control the estate due to their unwillingness to divide the inheritance (apathy), in accordance with the principle of ''Ijbary'' in Islamic inheritance law, whereby upon the moment of the Deceased's passing, ownership of the inheritance estate automatically transfers to the Legal Heirs".
# '''Validity of Grandchild Substitute Heirs (Article 185 Compilation of Islamic Law / KHI):''' "The status of substitute heirs based on the Compilation of Islamic Law does not contradict Islamic law or Indonesian positive law... Courts must not ignore the Compilation of Islamic Law in adjudicating cases by rejecting substitute heirs, which would result in grandchildren being deprived of inheritance from their grandparents due to their parents having predeceased them".
# '''Divorce Grounded in Marital Strife vs. ''Fasakh'' due to Apostasy:''' "A divorce sought through a petition for permission to pronounce ''talak'' based on grounds of marital strife may be granted if the Petitioner's (husband's) arguments align with statutory law provisions, even though the Respondent (wife) stated she practiced Christianity since childhood and practiced Islam solely at the time of marriage. If a divorce is petitioned based on apostasy and such apostasy constitutes a proven fact, the legal consequence is ''fasakh''".
# '''Legal Standing in Public Information Disclosure Disputes:''' "With the enactment of Law No. 14 of 2008 on Public Information Disclosure, anyone may submit a request for public information (''actio popularis''). However, in examining public information disclosure disputes, the presence or absence of an interest implying the Plaintiff's legal standing (''point d'interest point d'action ex'' Article 53 paragraph (1) of the Administrative Court Law) must be taken into account".
# '''Administrative Officials' Duty to Correct (''Erga Omnes'' Principle):''' "Even if a Defendant was not a party to the case ''in a quo'', whenever they become aware of such a ruling, State Administrative Officials are obligated to respond by correcting erroneous state administrative products, in the interest of enforcing public law with binding general applicability (the ''erga omnes'' principle)".
# '''Commander's Responsibility for Subordinate Assault Orders (Superior Responsibility):''' "The victim's death was not a direct act by the Defendant, but the victim's death resulting from the Defendant's order directed to members of the Military District Command (''Kodim'') falls under the responsibility of the Defendant as the Commander issuing the order".

The Supreme Court granted the cassation petitions in each respective case, annulled erroneous lower court rulings (''judex facti''), and reinforced legal certainty and substantive justice.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== 1. Construction of the ''Ijbary'' Principle in Islamic Inheritance Law (Articles 171 & 188 Compilation of Islamic Law / KHI) ===
''Does an heir holding physical control over a decedent's estate possess legal standing to file an inheritance partition lawsuit against other passive/apathetic heirs?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Lawful / Entitled to Sue.'''
Pursuant to the Principle of ''Ijbary'' (automatic transfer of ownership by operation of law upon the decedent's death), ownership of the inheritance estate immediately vests in all legal heirs. Apathetic or uncooperative behavior by certain heirs gives controlling heirs the standing to file an inheritance partition lawsuit in Religious Courts ''ex'' Article 188 KHI.

=== 2. Protection of Grandchildren's Civil Rights via Substitute Heirs (''Ahli Waris Pengganti'' ''ex'' Article 185 KHI) ===
''Are grandchildren whose parents predeceased their grandparents entitled to inherit from their grandparents through substitute heir provisions?''

'''Supreme Court Rule: Entitled to Inheritance Shares.'''
Religious Courts are barred from ignoring the Compilation of Islamic Law or bypassing grandchildren's rights. Grandchildren are entitled to step into their parents' shoes (''plaatsvervulling'') as substitute heirs with a portion not exceeding the share of primary equal heirs ''ex'' Article 185 KHI.

=== 3. Legal Standing in Public Information Disclosure Disputes (Article 53(1) Law No. 5 of 1986 ''jo.'' Law No. 14 of 2008) ===
Although the Public Information Disclosure Law adopts ''actio popularis'', in Administrative Court proceedings, Plaintiffs remain obligated to prove direct infringed interest (''legal standing'' / ''point d'interest point d'action''). Internal financial accountability documents (SPJ) of government bodies that do not constitute public financial reports need not be disclosed without direct legal standing.

=== 4. ''Erga Omnes'' Binding Effect of Administrative Court Rulings (Principles of Good Governance / AUPB) ===
State Administrative Court rulings possessing permanent legal force (''inkracht'') carry ''erga omnes'' applicability (binding generally). Land Office Officials discovering flawed administrative decrees are obligated to execute spontaneous corrections (''spontaneous correction'') over overlapping certificates.

=== 5. Superior Responsibility in Military Law (''ex'' Article 127 KUHPM ''jo.'' Article 338 Criminal Code) ===
A mid-ranking TNI officer (Dandim) who abuses positional authority by giving verbal orders to subordinates to eliminate and dispose of a victim's corpse bears full criminal responsibility for the victim's death, even if physical execution was carried out by subordinate members.

== Question of Law vs Question of Fact ==

=== Question of Law (Judex Juris / Supreme Court) ===

* ''Inheritance Case:'' Did Makassar Religious High Court (Decision No. 74/Pdt.G/2012/PTA.Mks) err in applying the law by dismissing the Plaintiff's lawsuit as premature and finding no dispute?
*: '''Supreme Court Answer:''' Yes. Makassar Religious High Court misapplied the law. Refusing to partition inheritance constitutes a justiciable dispute ''ex'' Article 188 KHI. The Supreme Court annulled the appellate ruling and independently adjudicated the estate partition.
* ''Public Information Case:'' Did Bandung Administrative Court (Decision No. 35/G/2013/PTUN-BDG) err in law by ordering Bekasi Youth & Sports Agency head to disclose internal SPJ financial files?
*: '''Supreme Court Answer:''' Yes. Bandung Administrative Court misapplied public information law and administrative court procedure. Applicants lacked legal standing over internal SPJ files. The Supreme Court annulled the Bandung Administrative Court ruling and dismissed the information request.
* ''Military Criminal Case:'' Did the Military Appeals Court (Decision No. PUT/26-K/PMU/BDG/AD/XI/2010) correctly affirm imprisonment and discharge for Dandim Lt. Col. Inf. Untung Sunanto?
*: '''Supreme Court Answer:''' Yes. Commanders bear full criminal responsibility for subordinates' assault orders. The Supreme Court rejected the Defendant's cassation petition.

=== Question of Fact (Judex Facti / Religious Courts, Administrative Courts, & Military Courts) ===
Verification of family lineages for Umar [Deceased husband] & Muzenah; grandchild substitute heir lineages for H. Sahrun bin Tukacil; requests for internal financial SPJ reports of Bekasi Youth & Sports Agency FY 2010–2012; land boundary verifications in Lontar vs. Pradah Kalikendal, Surabaya; and forensic autopsy reports from Dr. M. Djamil Hospital, Padang, No. Ym.01.08.1.5.1035 concerning blunt force trauma on victim [Party].

== Jurisprudence and Related Knowledge ==

=== Statutory Regulations ===

* '''Compilation of Islamic Law (KHI):''' Articles 171, 185 (Substitute Heirs), 188 (Inheritance Lawsuits), & 116 (Divorce).
* '''Law No. 14 of 2008 on Public Information Disclosure:''' Articles 2, 11, & Legal Standing Principles.
* '''Law No. 5 of 1986 ''jo.'' Law No. 9 of 2004 ''jo.'' Law No. 51 of 2009 on State Administrative Courts:''' Article 53 paragraph (1).
* '''Military Criminal Code (KUHPM):''' Articles 121, 127 (Abuse of Superior Influence), & 26 (Discharge).
* '''Criminal Code (KUHP):''' Article 338 ''jo.'' Article 55 paragraph (1) point 1.

=== Established Supreme Court Jurisprudence ===

* '''Principle of ''Ijbary'' in Islamic Inheritance:''' Transfer of inheritance ownership occurs automatically by operation of law (''ipso jure'') upon the decedent's death without requiring manual co-heir consent.
* '''''Erga Omnes'' Doctrine in Administrative Law:''' Annulment of administrative decisions based on permanent court rulings binds all governmental organs to adjust administrative acts.
* '''Command / Superior Responsibility Doctrine:''' Military superiors issuing unlawful functional orders (''unlawful orders'') bear full criminal responsibility for lethal consequences executed by subordinates.

== What Evidence Establishes / Does Not Establish ==

=== Established by Evidence ===

* [Widow (plaintiff)] is '''PROVEN ENTITLED TO FILE AN INHERITANCE LAWSUIT WHILE CONTROLLING ESTATE ASSETS ''EX'' ASAS IJBARY'''.
* Grandchildren of predeceased children are '''PROVEN LAWFUL AS SUBSTITUTE HEIRS ''EX'' ARTICLE 185 KHI'''.
* Petitions seeking internal institutional SPJ financial files are '''PROVEN TO LACK LEGAL STANDING DUE TO ABSENCE OF DIRECT INTEREST'''.
* Land Office Officials are '''PROVEN OBLIGATED TO CORRECT OVERLAPPING CERTIFICATES PURSUANT TO THE ''ERGA OMNES'' PRINCIPLE'''.
* Lt. Col. Inf. Untung Sunanto is '''PROVEN GUILTY OF ORDERING ASSAULT RESULTING IN VICTIM [Party]'S DEATH (SUPERIOR RESPONSIBILITY)'''.

=== Dismissed Findings (Overturned Rulings) ===

* Makassar Religious High Court's ruling declaring the inheritance lawsuit premature was '''ANNULLED ENTIRELY BY THE SUPREME COURT'''.

== Uncertainties and Gaps ==
'''Integrity of Islamic Inheritance Enforcement, Public Transparency, & Military Command Discipline:''' Landmark rulings in this compendium affirm five pillars of legal certainty in Indonesia:
# Islamic inheritance guarantees absolute heir rights unimpeded by relative apathy;
# KHI strictly protects grandchildren through substitute heir institutions;
# Public information rights must not be abused to access internal technical files without legal standing;
# Administrative officials must comply with ''erga omnes'' principles to rectify flawed certificates; and
# Military officers enjoy no immunity from command authority abuses causing civilian deaths.

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
; Do heirs controlling inheritance estates have standing to sue apathetic relatives, and do military commanders bear responsibility for subordinate assault orders pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence?
: '''Entitled to Sue & Commanders Bear Full Responsibility.''' Pursuant to Supreme Court Jurisprudence Reg. Nos. 39 K/AG/2013 and 97 K/MIL/2011:
:* Heirs controlling the entirety of an inheritance estate are entitled to sue passive/apathetic heirs refusing to divide estate assets pursuant to the Principle of ''Ijbary'' in Islamic inheritance law.
:* Military commanders bear full criminal responsibility for a victim's death resulting from orders issued to subordinates (''superior responsibility''), even if physical execution was carried out by subordinate members.
:* The Supreme Court annulled erroneous religious appellate rulings and rejected military commander cassation appeals.

title: JPAIS:PRECEDENT:YURISPRUDENSI MA 2018
wikitext:
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Supreme Court Jurisprudence Compendium (Up to 2018)}}
'''Supreme Court Jurisprudence Compendium (Up to 2018)''' (encompassing the Supreme Court Jurisprudence Compilation Book up to 2018, First Edition) is an official compendium enacted under Supreme Court Chief Justice Decree No. 185/KMA/SK/VII/2020 dated July 30, 2020. It compiles permanent landmark legal rules (''yurisprudensi tetap'') possessing permanent legal force (''inkracht van gewijsde'') across all judicial chambers of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia to maintain legal uniformity and prevent judicial disparity.

== Executive Summary ==
The compendium establishes strategic landmark precedents across all major legal domains:

# '''General Civil & Land Law:''' Foreign currency payment petitums must include orders for currency conversion into Rupiah based on Bank Indonesia's middle exchange rate at the time of payment (''ex'' Article 21 of Law No. 7 of 2011). In land disputes involving dual authentic certificates over identical land, the certificate issued earliest serves as the strongest proof of rights.
# '''Special Civil Law (Arbitration, Industrial Relations, & Consumer Protection):''' District Court rulings refusing to set aside national arbitral awards cannot be appealed to the Supreme Court, and Supreme Court arbitral appeal rulings are final and binding without eligibility for Reconsideration (''PK''). Consumer Dispute Resolution Boards (''BPSK'') lack competence to adjudicate financing, credit, or fiduciary guarantee disputes.
# '''General & Special Criminal Law (Anti-Corruption):''' Failure of contractual promises constitutes civil default (''wanprestasi'') rather than fraud (''penipuan''), unless initiated with bad faith or fraudulent intent from the inception. Full project disbursements prior to completion do not constitute state losses (''korupsi'') if ''force majeure'', addenda, paid penalties, and project acceptance conditions are fulfilled.
# '''Religious, Military, & Administrative Law:''' Obligatory wills (''Wasiat Wajibah'') may be granted to non-Muslim spouses. In State Administrative Law, where formal and substantive rules conflict, judges are mandated to prioritize substantive justice (''ex'' SEMA No. 1 of 2017).

== Selected Landmark Precedents by Chamber ==

=== 1. General Civil & Land Law ===
{| class="wikitable"
|-
! # !! Precedent Rule !! Legal Basis / Rationale !! Source / Passage
|-
| 1 || '''Foreign Currency Conversion (1/Yur/Pdt/2018):''' Foreign currency payment claims must incorporate currency conversion into Rupiah based on Bank Indonesia's middle exchange rate at the time of payment. || Article 21 of Law No. 7 of 2011 on Currency mandates Rupiah usage for debt settlements within the territory of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. || Yurisprudensi Tahun 2018.pdf [Passage 27, 40, 45, 50]
|-
| 2 || '''Third-Party Inheritance Lawsuits (2/Yur/Pdt/2018):''' Lawsuits seeking recovery of inheritance assets from third parties do not require filing by all co-heirs jointly; one heir acting for the estate (''boedel'') suffices. || Established jurisprudence (Supreme Court Decisions No. 244 K/Sip/1959, No. 439 K/Sip/1969) confirming a single heir represents the collective legal interest of recovering estate assets. || Yurisprudensi Tahun 2018.pdf [Passage 28, 51, 55, 56]
|-
| 3 || '''Gender Equality in Inheritance (3/Yur/Pdt/2018):''' Based on human rights and gender equality, female heirs (daughters/wives) are entitled to inheritance portions equal (1:1) to male heirs. || Supreme Court Decisions No. 179 K/SIP/1961, No. 415 K/SIP/1970, and PERMA No. 3 of 2017 supersede customary laws discriminating by gender. || Yurisprudensi Tahun 2018.pdf [Passage 28, 58, 61, 64, 67]
|-
| 4 || '''Unilateral Contract Termination (4/Yur/Pdt/2018):''' Unilateral contract termination prior to the expiration of the contractual term constitutes an Unlawful Act (Tort / PMH). || Article 1338 of the Civil Code: agreements cannot be revoked or terminated unilaterally without mutual consent. || Yurisprudensi Tahun 2018.pdf [Passage 29, 68, 69, 71]
|-
| 5 || '''Dual Certificates Priority (5/Yur/Pdt/2018):''' In the event of dual authentic land certificates over identical parcels, the certificate issued earliest constitutes the valid and strongest proof of rights. || Supreme Court Decisions No. 976 K/Pdt/2015, No. 290 K/Pdt/2016 confirm chronological priority as the definitive baseline for title validity. || Yurisprudensi Tahun 2018.pdf [Passage 29, 74, 75, 81]
|-
| 6 || '''Bona Fide Purchasers (6/Yur/Pdt/2018):''' Land purchasers acquiring property through state auction offices or before Land Deed Officials (''PPAT'') in compliance with procedures are bona fide purchasers protected by law. || SEMA No. 4 of 2016 and SEMA No. 5 of 2014 guarantee legal certainty for acquisitions executed before authorized public officials. || Yurisprudensi Tahun 2018.pdf [Passage 29, 82, 83, 91]
|}

=== 2. Special Civil Law (Arbitration, Industrial Relations, & Consumer Protection) ===
* '''Finality of Arbitration Rulings (1 & 2/Yur/Arbt/2018):''' District Court rulings refusing to set aside national arbitral awards cannot be appealed to the Supreme Court, and Supreme Court arbitral appellate rulings are final and binding without eligibility for Reconsideration (''PK'').
* '''Process Wages in Industrial Relations (1/Yur/PHI/2018):''' Industrial relations process wages (''upah proses'') are capped at a maximum of 6 (six) months pursuant to SEMA No. 3 of 2015.
* '''BPSK Incompetence Over Credit Disputes (1/Yur/Perkons/2018):''' Financing agreements, fiduciary credit disputes, or security rights enforcement (''hak tanggungan'') do not constitute consumer disputes; Consumer Dispute Resolution Boards (''BPSK'') lack competence to adjudicate them.

=== 3. General & Special Criminal Law (Anti-Corruption) ===
* '''Intent to Kill (1/Yur/Pid/2018):''' The element of intentional homicide (''sengaja'') is fulfilled if an assailant attacks vital organs (chest, abdomen, head) with a lethal weapon.
* '''Receiving Stolen Goods (2 & 3/Yur/Pid/2018):''' Purchasing goods below market prices or vehicles lacking lawful documentation gives rise to reasonable suspicion of receiving stolen goods (''penadahan'', ''ex'' Article 480 Criminal Code).
* '''Default vs. Fraud (4/Yur/Pid/2018):''' Breach of civil promises constitutes default (''wanprestasi''), not fraud (''penipuan''), unless accompanied by bad faith or fraudulent intent from inception.
* '''Bad Checks (5/Yur/Pid/2018):''' Issuing checks or promissory clearing notes (''bilyet giro'') known to be unfunded constitutes fraud under Article 378 of the Criminal Code.
* '''Project Disbursements Prior to Completion (1/Yur/Kor/2018):''' Full disbursement of state project funds prior to physical completion does not constitute state loss (''korupsi'') if accompanied by ''force majeure'', addenda, paid delay penalties, and successful project completion/acceptance.

=== 4. Religious, Military, and Administrative Chambers ===
* '''Non-Muslim Obligatory Wills (1/Yur/Ag/2018):''' Obligatory wills (''Wasiat Wajibah'') may be granted to non-Muslim heirs or spouses.
* '''Grandchild Substitute Heirs (2/Yur/Ag/2018):''' Male and female grandchildren descending from predeceased sons or daughters qualify as substitute heirs (''Ahli Waris Pengganti'') ''ex'' Article 185 KHI.
* '''Execution of Sharia Security Rights (3/Yur/Ag/2018):''' Enforcement of Sharia-compliant guarantees prior to maturity is permissible upon debtor default ''ex'' SEMA No. 4 of 2016.
* '''Military Discharge Exemptions (1/Yur/Mil/2018):''' Additional penalties of dishonorable discharge are not imposed on military personnel entering Retirement Preparation Periods (''MPP'').
* '''Substantive Justice Priority in Administrative Law (2/Yur/TUN/2018):''' Where formal procedural rules and substantive justice clash, State Administrative Judges are mandated to prioritize substantive justice ''ex'' SEMA No. 1 of 2017.

== Legal / Procedural Issues ==

=== Criteria for Permanent Jurisprudence (''Yurisprudensi Tetap'') ===
A Supreme Court ruling qualifies as permanent jurisprudence (''yurisprudensi tetap'') requiring mandatory adherence by all judges upon fulfilling six criteria:

# Absence of clear statutory rules governing the issue,
# Attainment of permanent legal force (''inkracht''),
# Incorporation of truth and justice principles,
# Consistent application across repeated similar cases,
# Affirmation by the Supreme Court via judicial examination, and
# Formal recommendation as jurisprudence.

Pursuant to Chief Justice Decree No. 185/KMA/SK/VII/2020, all judicial personnel across Indonesia are bound to follow these consolidated precedents to uphold predictable law (''predictable law'').

== Frequently Asked Questions (GEO) ==
; What are the Supreme Court's rules regarding dual land certificates, BPSK competence over fiduciary credit, and single urine test evidentiary standards in military narcotics cases?
: '''Earliest Certificate Prevails, BPSK Lacks Competence, & Single Urine Test Insufficient.''' Pursuant to the Supreme Court Jurisprudence Compendium up to 2018 (Decree No. 185/KMA/SK/VII/2020):
:* '''Dual Certificates (5/Yur/Pdt/2018):''' Where dual authentic certificates exist over identical land, the certificate issued earliest constitutes the valid and strongest proof of title.
:* '''BPSK Competence (1/Yur/Perkons/2018):''' Disputes arising from financing and credit agreements (fiduciary or security rights) constitute civil default disputes, not consumer disputes; BPSK lacks jurisdiction.
:* '''Narcotics Evidence (3/Yur/Mil/2018):''' Standalone urine screening results unaccompanied by corroborating legal evidence are insufficient to convict a military defendant under evidentiary thresholds (''ex'' Article 183 Criminal Procedure Code).
