wikitext:
{{JPAIS Knowledge|id=JPAIS:REFORM-PROPOSAL:JPAIS-MED-REF-001|type=ReformProposal|title_id=Pelembagaan Majelis Mediasi Hibrida (Hakim dan Komisioner Mitra Ahli)|title_en=Institutionalization of Hybrid Mediation Panels (Judges and Expert Commissioners)|slug=jpa-med-ref-001-hybrid-mediation-panels|description_id=Reformasi mediasi peradilan mengadaptasi model Komite Konsiliasi Tripartit Jepang (Minji Chotei) ke dalam peradilan perdata dan niaga Indonesia di bawah Kerangka JPAIS.|description_en=Judicial mediation reform adapting the Japanese Minji Chotei tripartite conciliation committee model into Indonesian civil and commercial judiciary under the JPAIS Framework.|jurisdiction=Indonesia / Japan Comparative|legal_domain=Judicial Reform / Alternative Dispute Resolution / Civil Procedure|topics=Hybrid Mediation Panels, Minji Chotei, SIPP Integration, BSDK Training, Judicial Reform|status=Proposed (Co-Design & Pilot Stage)|language=bilingual (id/en)|authority=Mahkamah Agung Republik Indonesia / JICA KCCP|verification_status=VERIFIED|version=1.0}}

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

== Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas ==

* Entity ID: JPAIS-MED-REF-001
* Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa
* Ingestion Status: Confirmed

== Description / Deskripsi ==
Transforms Indonesian court-connected mediation by replacing the solo mediator model with a '''Hybrid Mediation Panel''' (''Majelis Mediasi Hibrida'') for high-value civil claims, commercial disputes, construction cases, and agrarian conflicts. The panel pairs 1 internal Judge Mediator (responsible for formal legal compliance and homologation enforceability) with 1 or 2 accredited Non-Judge Expert Commissioners (possessing technical expertise in engineering, accounting, business law, or customary practice).

== Problem / Masalah ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-001]]: Court mediation in general civil district courts suffers from structural ritualization (''tick-box formalism'') with stagnant success rates hovering between 8% and 12%.
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-002]]: Career judges suffer from severe role overload, simultaneously carrying adjudicative burdens and conducting superficial 15–20 minute mediation sessions[cite: 1].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-003]]: External non-judge professional mediators experience systemic exclusion from court-annexed mediation due to the absence of public budget compensation (DIPA), resulting in a zero-cost bias toward free judge mediators[cite: 1].

== Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ID-001]]: Mandatory universal court mediation under PERMA No. 1 of 2016 relies on a solo mediator model operating within a rigid 30+30 day post-filing window[cite: 1].

== Japanese Practice / Praktik Jepang ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-JP-001]]: Under the Civil Conciliation Act (1951), Japan utilizes tripartite Civil Conciliation Committees (''Chōtei Iinkai''—1 Conciliation Judge + 2 Professional Lay Commissioners) achieving success rates exceeding 45% to 50%[cite: 1].

== Gap / Kesenjangan ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-001]]: Absence of a primary statutory act providing permanent fiscal appropriations for non-judge conciliation commissioners[cite: 1].
* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-002]]: Lack of an autonomous judicial ADR governance directorate within the Supreme Court[cite: 1].

== Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan ==
Institutionalize Hybrid Mediation Panels mandatorily for commercial and land disputes exceeding Rp 200 million in metropolitan and class IA courts, and facultatively in class IB and II courts[cite: 1].

== Action / Aksi ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-001]]: Promulgate SK KMA pilot decree, establish steering committee, and configure SIPP workflow[cite: 1].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-002]]: Deploy Hybrid Panels across designated pilot courts and implement preliminary assessment protocols[cite: 1].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-003]]: Audit performance metrics and draft permanent PERMA[cite: 1].

== Pilot / Pilot Proyek ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-001]]: 6-month pilot across PN Jakarta Pusat, PN Surabaya, PN Sleman, PN Makassar, PA Jakarta Selatan, and PA Bandung[cite: 1].

== KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-001]]: Substantive Settlement Rate (SSR) $\ge 25\%$ in general courts and $\ge 60\%$ in religious courts[cite: 1].

== Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan ==
Issue Supreme Court Leadership Decree (SK KMA) and integrate expert commissioner rosters into SIPP and court fee surcharges[cite: 1].

== Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi ==
Promulgate revised PERMA on Integrated Mediation and Conciliation superseding PERMA No. 1 of 2016[cite: 1].

== Evidence / Bukti Empiris ==

* District court general civil mediation success rate ranges persistently between 8% and 12%[cite: 1].
* Japanese conciliation committees achieve >45–50% settlement rates[cite: 1].

wikitext:
{{JPAIS Knowledge|id=JPAIS:REFORM-PROPOSAL:JPAIS-MED-REF-002|type=ReformProposal|title_id=Analisis Komparatif Mediasi Peradilan di Indonesia dan Jepang|title_en=Comparative Analysis of Judicial Mediation in Indonesia and Japan|slug=jpa-med-ref-002-comparative-analysis-mediation|description_id=Studi komparatif terperinci mengenai kerangka hukum, efektivitas empiris, dan arsitektur reformasi struktural mediasi peradilan antara Indonesia dan Jepang dalam Kerangka JPAIS.|description_en=Detailed comparative study on legal frameworks, empirical effectiveness, and structural reform architecture of judicial mediation between Indonesia and Japan under the JPAIS Framework.|jurisdiction=Indonesia / Japan Comparative[cite: 2]|legal_domain=Judicial Reform / Alternative Dispute Resolution / Civil Procedure[cite: 2]|topics=Comparative Judicial Mediation, Minji Chotei, PERMA 1 of 2016, SIPP Integration, Tripartite Panels[cite: 2]|status=Proposed (Co-Design & Pilot Stage)[cite: 2]|language=bilingual (id/en)|authority=Mahkamah Agung Republik Indonesia / JICA KCCP[cite: 2]|verification_status=VERIFIED|version=1.0}}

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

== Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas ==

* Entity ID: JPAIS-MED-REF-002
* Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa
* Ingestion Status: Confirmed

== Description / Deskripsi ==
Evaluates judicial mediation through a comparative framework between Indonesia and Japan, addressing structural frictions such as Indonesia's low general civil settlement rates (<10%) versus Japan's high conciliation success (>50%) through the Chōtei system, and proposes actionable structural reforms[cite: 2].

== Problem / Masalah ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-001]]: General civil court litigation mediation in Indonesia suffers from structural ritualization, with nationwide settlement rates remaining under 10%[cite: 2].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-002]]: Indonesia relies on a single mediator operating within a strict short procedural window without public budget line items for non-judge compensation[cite: 2].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-003]]: Lack of institutional integration between preliminary evaluation, issue sorting, and trial resolution compared to the Japanese model[cite: 2].

== Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ID-001]]: Mandatory court-annexed mediation under PERMA No. 1 of 2016 and PERMA No. 3 of 2022 serves as an obligatory procedural step for civil filings[cite: 2].

== Japanese Practice / Praktik Jepang ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-JP-001]]: Japan's Civil Conciliation Act of 1951 utilizes specialized Conciliation Committees (Chōtei Iinkai) comprising a presiding judge and lay experts to resolve over 50% of petitions[cite: 2].

== Gap / Kesenjangan ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-001]]: Procedural formalism where litigants treat mediation as a routine delay rather than a substantive resolution space[cite: 2].
* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-002]]: Absence of state-funded compensation for external non-judge mediators and limited evaluative training[cite: 2].

== Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan ==
Implement tripartite conciliation panels, codify evaluative-facilitative hybrid protocols with a 10-day issue-sorting phase, institutionalize state budget allocations for non-judge compensation, and upgrade digital mediation infrastructure[cite: 2].

== Action / Aksi ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-001]]: Issue SEMA authorizing pilot procedures across four target courts (PN Jakarta Selatan, PA Jakarta Selatan, PN Surabaya, PA Sleman)[cite: 2].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-002]]: Deploy Tripartite Mediation Panels and mandatory 10-day issue-sorting protocols[cite: 2].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-003]]: Conduct mid-term empirical audits and finalize permanent PERMA revisions[cite: 2].

== Pilot / Pilot Proyek ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-002]]: 90-day multi-court pilot program across PN Jakarta Selatan, PA Jakarta Selatan, PN Surabaya, and PA Sleman[cite: 2].

== KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-002]]: District court settlement rate $\ge 25.0\%$; religious court settlement rate $\ge 55.0\%$; settlement duration $\le 18$ calendar days[cite: 2].

== Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan ==
Promulgate joint ministerial decrees and Supreme Court circulars to establish sustainable funding and operational guidelines for tripartite panels[cite: 2].

== Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi ==
Amend PERMA No. 1 of 2016 and PERMA No. 3 of 2022 to incorporate hybrid evaluative-facilitative protocols and digital infrastructure standards[cite: 2].

== Evidence / Bukti Empiris ==

* National religious court settlement rate stands at 39.85% while general district court civil settlement rate ranges between 6.8% and 7.4%[cite: 2].
* Japanese civil conciliation achieves >50% settlement rates across summary and district courts[cite: 2].

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

== Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas ==

* Entity ID: JPAIS-MED-REF-003
* Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa
* Ingestion Status: Confirmed

== Description / Deskripsi ==
Provides a comparative assessment of court case management between Indonesia and Japan, examining case intake, tracking, digital architectures (SIPP, EIS, e-Court, e-Berpadu vs. Japanese CCP amendments), and institutional bottlenecks, and proposes targeted administrative reforms and a 90-day pilot implementation plan[cite: 3].

== Problem / Masalah ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-001]]: EIS platform data aggregation masks granular non-compliance, forcing supervisory judges into manual audits across active SIPP case files[cite: 3].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-002]]: SEMA No. 1 of 2023 postal summons delivery failures in rural regions lead to undelivered notices, default judgments (verstek), and appellate remands[cite: 3].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-003]]: e-Berpadu digital criminal integration suffers from manual paper fallback exceptions during network downtime, causing data discrepancies with SIPP[cite: 3].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-004]]: Legacy criminal procedure (KUHAP Law No. 8 of 1981) creates statutory gaps and procedural challenges for electronic trials and digital evidence transfers[cite: 3].

== Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ID-001]]: Dual-track intake via e-Court (PERMA No. 1/2019, PERMA No. 7/2022) and e-Berpadu (PERMA No. 8/2022), tracked through SIPP and evaluated via EIS[cite: 3].

== Japanese Practice / Praktik Jepang ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-JP-001]]: Unified civil litigation processing under the 2022 Code of Civil Procedure Amendment, featuring front-loaded pre-trial issue organization (Preparatory Proceedings) and high pre-trial settlement rates via Chotei[cite: 3].

== Gap / Kesenjangan ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-001]]: Indonesia prioritizes strict administrative timelines (5-month SEMA target) and compliance scoring over pre-trial issue formulation, creating lower court trial compression[cite: 3].
* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-002]]: Japan's historical reliance on physical documentation slowed digital adoption, and judicial performance metrics risk "mediatory adjudication" pressures[cite: 3].

== Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan ==
Upgrade EIS to version 4.0 for granular anomaly detection, establish an address verification API bridge with Dukcapil and PT Pos, codify pre-trial issue formulation conferences into a new PERMA, and permanently codify digital procedures into primary legislation (RUU KUHAP and RUU Hukum Acara Perdata)[cite: 3].

== Action / Aksi ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-001]]: Form steering committee, deploy EIS 4.0 granular module, and establish API interoperability for postal verification[cite: 3].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-002]]: Execute 90-day pilot across five Class IA Khusus and Class IA District Courts (PN Jakarta Pusat, PN Surakarta, PN Surabaya, PN Makassar, PN Medan)[cite: 3].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-003]]: Monitor performance via automated dashboards, conduct mid-term reviews, and deliver national scaling blueprint[cite: 3].

== Pilot / Pilot Proyek ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-003]]: 90-day pilot program across PN Jakarta Pusat, PN Surakarta, PN Surabaya, PN Makassar, and PN Medan[cite: 3].

== KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-003]]: EIS audit time burden $< 1.5$ hours/week; summons delivery accuracy $> 92\%$; average civil duration $< 3.5$ months; e-Berpadu manual bypass $< 3\%$; pre-trial issue narrowing $> 80\%$; EIS compliance score $> 98.5\%$[cite: 3].

== Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan ==
Establish inter-agency steering committees between Mahkamah Agung, PT Pos Indonesia, and the Ministry of Home Affairs to streamline digital workflows and address verification[cite: 3].

== Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi ==
Promulgate a new PERMA mandating Pre-Trial Issue Formulation Conferences and pass legislative amendments to national procedural codes[cite: 3].

== Evidence / Bukti Empiris ==

* Indonesian Supreme Court handled 31,138 cases in 2024 with a 99.26% clearance rate, while lower courts registered 410,754 e-Court cases[cite: 3].
* Japanese district courts handle ~216,000 filings annually, with summary courts handling ~1.45 million filings and Chotei resolving over 50% of civil disputes[cite: 3].

{{JPAIS Knowledge|id=JPAIS:REFORM-PROPOSAL:JPAIS-MED-REF-004|type=ReformProposal|title_id=Analisis Komparatif Persiapan Sidang Perdata di Indonesia dan Jepang|title_en=Comparative Analysis of Civil Preparatory Proceedings in Indonesia and Japan|slug=jpa-med-ref-004-comparative-preparatory-proceedings|description_id=Analisis komparatif mendalam mengenai tahap persiapan persidangan perdata, tata kelola keaktifan hakim, pengungkapan bukti, dan sanksi preklusi antara Indonesia dan Jepang dalam Kerangka JPAIS.|description_en=In-depth comparative analysis on civil preparatory proceedings, active judicial management, evidence disclosure, and preclusion sanctions between Indonesia and Japan under the JPAIS Framework.|jurisdiction=Indonesia / Japan Comparative[cite: 4]|legal_domain=Judicial Reform / Civil Procedure / Alternative Dispute Resolution[cite: 4]|topics=Civil Preparatory Proceedings, Shakumeiken, Pre-Trial Evidence Disclosure, Preclusion Sanctions, Wakai[cite: 4]|status=Proposed (Co-Design & Pilot Stage)[cite: 4]|language=bilingual (id/en)|authority=Mahkamah Agung Republik Indonesia / JICA KCCP[cite: 4]|verification_status=VERIFIED|version=1.0}}

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

== Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas ==

* Entity ID: JPAIS-MED-REF-004
* Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa
* Ingestion Status: Confirmed

== Description / Deskripsi ==
Evaluates civil preparatory proceedings through a comparative framework between Indonesia and Japan, identifying systemic gaps in Indonesia's general civil courts (absence of mandatory pre-trial issue clarification, passive judicial roles, and low mediation success rates) and proposing the institutionalization of mandatory Pre-Trial Civil Examinations (Pemeriksaan Persiapan Perdata / PPP) modeled after Japan's CCP issue-arrangement framework[cite: 4].

== Problem / Masalah ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-001]]: General civil actions in Indonesian District Courts proceed with vague claims (obscuur libel) and broad denials due to a lack of preliminary issue clarification, leading to prolonged trials and low mediation success (1.4% to 5%)[cite: 4].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-002]]: Litigants experience surprise evidence submissions during main trial hearings because the legacy HIR/RBg procedural system lacks pre-trial document disclosure mechanisms[cite: 4].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-003]]: Indonesian civil trials suffer from unpredictable schedules and a lack of procedural preclusion sanctions for late submissions, causing frequent delays beyond SEMA's 5-month target[cite: 4].

== Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ID-001]]: Standard civil procedure under legacy HIR/RBg codes proceeds directly from initial appearances to PERMA No. 1 of 2016 mediation and serial written exchanges without a general pre-trial issue clarification stage[cite: 4].

== Japanese Practice / Praktik Jepang ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-JP-001]]: Japan's Code of Civil Procedure (CCP Act No. 109/1996) integrates issue and evidence arrangement proceedings (kozo chosei tetuzuki) via Preliminary Oral Arguments, Preparatory Proceedings, and Written Preparatory Proceedings supported by judicial clarification (shakumeiken) and binding trial plans[cite: 4].

== Gap / Kesenjangan ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-001]]: Statutory absence of active judicial clarification powers and mandatory pre-trial issue framing in general civil District Courts, contrasting with PTUN and Small Claims exceptions[cite: 4].
* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-002]]: Absence of pre-filing inquiry rights, mandatory pre-trial document disclosure rules, and formal inter-party information exchange mechanisms[cite: 4].

== Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan ==
Institutionalize mandatory Pre-Trial Civil Examinations (PPP) across all District Courts, adapt Japan's shakumeiken and inter-party inquiry rules into the E-Court framework, implement binding procedural calendars with strict preclusion sanctions, and establish a dual-track settlement mechanism post-issue clarification[cite: 4].

== Action / Aksi ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-001]]: Promulgate interim judicial pilot guidelines and configure SIPP/E-Court modules for issue matrix creation and digital pre-trial document management[cite: 4].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-002]]: Deploy mandatory PPP and digital evidence disclosure protocols across five Class IA Special District Courts (Central Jakarta, Surabaya, Medan, Bandung, Makassar)[cite: 4].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-003]]: Enforce binding procedural calendars, conduct mid-term reviews, and draft a permanent PERMA for nationwide rollout[cite: 4].

== Pilot / Pilot Proyek ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-004]]: 90-day multi-court pilot program across Central Jakarta, Surabaya, Medan, Bandung, and Makassar District Courts[cite: 4].

== KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-004]]: Interlocutory exceptions reduced by 40%; evidentiary sessions reduced by 30%; 100% issuance of pre-trial issue summaries; SEMA 5-month compliance rate $> 92.0\%$; commercial settlement success rate $> 25.0\%$[cite: 4].

== Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan ==
Issue Supreme Court Circulars establishing judicial performance evaluations based on effective issue-narrowing and active clarification enforcement during pre-trial phases[cite: 4].

== Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi ==
Promulgate a comprehensive PERMA on Civil Preparatory Proceedings, amend PERMA No. 7 of 2022 (E-Court) and PERMA No. 1 of 2016 (Mediation), and incorporate provisions into the draft Civil Procedure Code (RUU Hukum Acara Perdata)[cite: 4].

== Evidence / Bukti Empiris ==

* General district court civil mediation success rates range between 1.4% and 5%, while Japanese in-court settlement (Wakai) rates reach 36% to 37.1%[cite: 4].
* Japanese first-instance proceedings achieve an actual average duration of 9 to 14 months under active judicial case management[cite: 4].

{{JPAIS Knowledge|id=JPAIS:REFORM-PROPOSAL:JPAIS-MED-REF-005|type=ReformProposal|title_id=Analisis Isu dan Manajemen Bukti dalam Peradilan Indonesia dan Jepang|title_en=Issue and Evidence Management in Indonesian and Japanese Courts: Comparative Analysis, Institutional Gaps, and a Phased Pilot Model for Judicial Reform|slug=jpa-med-ref-005-issue-evidence-management|description_id=Analisis komparatif mendalam mengenai perumusan isu pra-sidang, pemetaan bukti terstruktur, alokasi beban pembuktian (Yoken-jijitsu-ron), pengungkapan dokumen, bukti digital, dan evaluasi putusan antara Indonesia dan Jepang dalam Kerangka JPAIS.|description_en=In-depth comparative analysis on pre-trial issue formulation, structured evidence mapping, burden of proof allocation (Yoken-jijitsu-ron), document disclosure, digital evidence, and judgment evaluation between Indonesia and Japan under the JPAIS Framework.|jurisdiction=Indonesia / Japan Comparative[cite: 5]|legal_domain=Judicial Reform / Civil Procedure / Evidence Law[cite: 5]|topics=Pre-Trial Issue Formulation, Structured Evidence Matrix, Yoken-jijitsu-ron, Document Production Orders, Digital Evidence Authentication[cite: 5]|status=Proposed (Co-Design & Pilot Stage)[cite: 5]|language=bilingual (id/en)|authority=Mahkamah Agung Republik Indonesia / JICA KCCP[cite: 5]|verification_status=VERIFIED|version=1.0}}

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

== Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas ==

* Entity ID: JPAIS-MED-REF-005
* Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa
* Ingestion Status: Confirmed

== Description / Deskripsi ==
Provides an exhaustive comparative assessment of issue and evidence management across six core procedural domains between Indonesia and Japan, identifying systemic gaps in Indonesia's piecemeal hearing model and proposing the institutionalization of a comprehensive Pra-Sidang and Evidence Modernization System modeled after Japan's CCP and LTRI doctrine[cite: 5].

== Problem / Masalah ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-001]]: Indonesian civil litigation suffers from trial fragmentation and unstructured document dumping because courts lack a pre-trial mechanism to crystallize issues and map documentary exhibits to material facts[cite: 5].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-002]]: Burden of proof allocation is unpredictable due to unguided judicial application of Roman maxims, and severe information asymmetry exists due to a lack of compulsory document disclosure mechanisms[cite: 5].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-003]]: District courts handle electronic records inconsistently, treating digital files as mere paper printouts requiring physical stamps (nazegelen), while civil judgments remain formalistic and opaque[cite: 5].

== Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ID-001]]: Civil adjudication relies on colonial-era codes (HIR/RBg) featuring sequential written exchanges (gugatan, jawaban, replik, duplik) and unstructured evidence submission without front-indexed mapping[cite: 5].

== Japanese Practice / Praktik Jepang ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-JP-001]]: Japan's Code of Civil Procedure of 1996 incorporates specialized preparatory proceedings (benron junbi tetsuzuki), evidence explanation schedules (shoko setsumeisho), document production orders (bunsho teishutsu meirei), and the Theory of Presupposed Ultimate Facts (Yoken-jijitsu-ron)[cite: 5].

== Gap / Kesenjangan ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-001]]: Absence of an interlocutory pre-trial hearing (pra-sidang) to bind contested issues, structured evidence explanation matrices, and systematic claim deconstruction doctrines[cite: 5].
* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-002]]: Lack of enforceable document production orders, cryptographic hash authentication standards for digital evidence, and structured evidentiary reasoning protocols in judgment drafting[cite: 5].

== Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan ==
Institutionalize a mandatory Pra-Sidang conference post-mediation, a Structured Evidence Matrix via e-Court, the Material Requisite Facts doctrine (Yoken-jijitsu-ron), targeted Document Production Orders with adverse inferences, cryptographic digital evidence standards, and reformed judgment templates[cite: 5].

== Action / Aksi ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-001]]: Promulgate Supreme Court Decree (SK KMA) authorizing the Pilot Pra-Sidang Program, finalize e-Court Evidence Matrix module, and publish the official Yoken-jijitsu Benchbook[cite: 5].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-002]]: Deliver 5-day professional certification courses for judges and registrars, deploy e-Court matrix into pilot registries, and mandate Pra-Sidang for all contentious civil and commercial cases[cite: 5].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-003]]: Monitor case progression via SIPP, submit bi-weekly operational reports to Ditjen Badilum, and publish the 90-day comprehensive pilot evaluation report[cite: 5].

== Pilot / Pilot Proyek ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-005]]: 90-day pilot program across commercial and general civil divisions at Central Jakarta District Court (PN Jakarta Pusat) and Surabaya District Court (PN Surabaya)[cite: 5].

== KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-005]]: Post-mediation judgment duration $\le 90$ calendar days; evidentiary hearings $\le 3$ sessions; factual claims resolved via stipulation $\ge 30\%$; pre-trial settlement $\ge 25\%$; evidence matrix compliance $100\%$; document production compliance $\ge 85\%$; digital stipulation rate $\ge 80\%$; cassation overturn rate $\le 15\%$[cite: 5].

== Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan ==
Issue Supreme Court Circular Letters mandating Minutes of Disputed Issues, structured burden allocation reasoning, and integration of judgment metrics into EIS[cite: 5].

== Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi ==
Promulgate comprehensive Supreme Court Regulations (PERMA) on Pre-Trial Case Management, Structured Evidence Explanation, Targeted Document Production, Digital Evidence Admissibility, and Judgment Reasoning, while codifying provisions into the Draft Civil Procedure Code[cite: 5].

== Evidence / Bukti Empiris ==

* Japanese preparatory proceedings and Yoken-jijitsu training reduced first-instance disposition times from 12.4 months to 9.2 months and achieved over 50% conciliation settlement rates[cite: 5].
* Indonesian civil trials suffer from prolonged multi-session evidentiary hearings that conflict with SEMA No. 2 of 2014's five-month disposition ceiling[cite: 5].

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

== Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas ==

* Entity ID: JPAIS-MED-REF-006
* Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa
* Ingestion Status: Confirmed

== Description / Deskripsi ==
Evaluates judicial training architectures through a comparative study between Indonesia and Japan, identifying systemic gaps in Indonesia's segmented professional training pipeline and proposing the Indonesian Competency-Based Judicial Training Model (J-CBTM) modeled after Japan's LTRI and Yoken Jijitsu doctrine[cite: 6].

== Problem / Masalah ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-001]]: Indonesian judicial training lacks a comprehensive outcome-based competency matrix and suffers from irregular recruitment cycles, curriculum compressions (65-week PPC Terpadu), and immediate solo judge appointments[cite: 6].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-002]]: Judgments display structural inconsistencies due to the absence of a standardized drafting taxonomy, while clinical apprenticeships lack pedagogical rigor and protected mentorship allocations[cite: 6].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-003]]: Assessment systems produce near 100% graduation rates without a rigorous practical gateway exam, and judicial education lacks binding continuing education tiers and AI governance frameworks[cite: 6].

== Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ID-001]]: Judicial training is administered autonomously by BSDK through Pusdiklat Teknis Peradilan, separating candidate judge education (PPC Terpadu) from prosecutors and private advocates[cite: 6].

== Japanese Practice / Praktik Jepang ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-JP-001]]: Japan administers unified legal training for judges, prosecutors, and attorneys through the Legal Training and Research Institute (LTRI / Shihō Kenshūjo) featuring a 12-month apprenticeship, Yoken Jijitsu methodology, and the high-stakes Nikai Shiken exit exam[cite: 6].

== Gap / Kesenjangan ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-001]]: Structural divergence between Japan's cohesive professional culture and Indonesia's segmented training model, coupled with the absence of a post-induction transitional collegiate bench requirement (Hanjiho equivalent)[cite: 6].
* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-002]]: Lack of a standardized analytical drafting taxonomy, blinded national qualifying exit examinations, and ethical boundaries for generative AI deployment in judicial operations[cite: 6].

== Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan ==
Establish the Indonesian Competency-Based Judicial Training Model (J-CBTM) featuring four progressive educational gates, a three-year transitional collegiate rank (Hakim Pertama Pratama), the DFKUM structured drafting doctrine, the UNKY gateway exam, and AI governance rules[cite: 6].

== Action / Aksi ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-001]]: Promulgate Supreme Court Regulations establishing the Judicial Competency Framework, structured drafting benchbooks, and the UNKY qualification exam[cite: 6].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-002]]: Deploy the J-CBTM pilot across designated jurisdictions, implementing protected mentorship allocations (SMYB) and unscripted trial simulations[cite: 6].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-003]]: Audit pilot training outcomes, evaluate UNKY inter-rater reliability, and submit permanent structural reform recommendations to the Supreme Court leadership[cite: 6].

== Pilot / Pilot Proyek ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-006]]: 90-day pilot program across trial simulation labs in Megamendung, pilot commercial courts in Jakarta and Surabaya, and appellate prep academies[cite: 6].

== KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-006]]: Evidentiary consensus $\ge 90\%$; new judge appellate reversal rate $< 5.0\%$; judgment page length reduced by $35\%$; UNKY inter-rater reliability (Kendall's W) $\ge 0.88$; AI citation verification accuracy $100\%$[cite: 6].

== Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan ==
Promulgate joint ministerial and Supreme Court decrees recognizing inter-agency training modules and establishing ethical AI governance protocols for judicial operations[cite: 6].

== Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi ==
Amend SK KMA guidelines on candidate judge induction, judgment drafting standards, promotional career gates, and digital trial conduct[cite: 6].

== Evidence / Bukti Empiris ==

* Japan's unified LTRI apprenticeship and Yoken Jijitsu methodology ensure uniform analytical baselines and high adjudication quality across the legal profession[cite: 6].
* National baseline appellate reversal rates for newly appointed Indonesian judges stand at 18.4% under compressed induction pipelines[cite: 6].

{{JPAIS Knowledge|id=JPAIS:REFORM-PROPOSAL:JPAIS-MED-REF-007|type=ReformProposal|title_id=Analisis Komparatif Sistem Manajemen Perkara Digital di Indonesia dan Jepang|title_en=Comparative Analysis of Digital Case Management Systems in Indonesia and Japan: Architectural Deficits, Lessons Learned, and an Adapted Modernization Framework|slug=jpa-med-ref-007-comparative-digital-case-management|description_id=Analisis komparatif mendalam mengenai arsitektur sistem manajemen perkara digital, desentralisasi SIPP vs mints cloud, interoperabilitas SPPT-TI, standar Akoma Ntoso, dan arsitektur referensi e-Peradilan Modern antara Indonesia dan Jepang dalam Kerangka JPAIS.|description_en=In-depth comparative analysis on digital case management architectures, decentralized SIPP vs mints cloud, SPPT-TI interoperability, Akoma Ntoso standards, and the e-Peradilan Modern reference architecture between Indonesia and Japan under the JPAIS Framework.|jurisdiction=Indonesia / Japan Comparative[cite: 7]|legal_domain=Judicial Reform / Court Administration / Legal Technology[cite: 7]|topics=Digital Case Management, SIPP Topology, mints Platform, SPPT-TI Interoperability, LegalDocML, e-Peradilan Modern[cite: 7]|status=Proposed (Co-Design & Pilot Stage)[cite: 7]|language=bilingual (id/en)|authority=Mahkamah Agung Republik Indonesia / JICA KCCP[cite: 7]|verification_status=VERIFIED|version=1.0}}

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

== Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas ==

* Entity ID: JPAIS-MED-REF-007
* Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa
* Ingestion Status: Confirmed

== Description / Deskripsi ==
Provides an exhaustive comparative assessment of digital court case management systems between Indonesia and Japan, examining technical topologies, e-filing onboarding, interoperability middleware (Puskarda/SPPT-TI vs. Japanese centralized platforms), cybersecurity governance, and proposing the cloud-native ''e-Peradilan Modern'' reference architecture and a 90-day pilot execution plan[cite: 7].

== Problem / Masalah ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-001]]: Indonesia's decentralized SIPP database topology suffers from asynchronous synchronization failures, packet loss in remote islands, concurrency conflicts, and manual EIS metric manipulation risks[cite: 7].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-002]]: Inter-agency criminal integration (SPPT-TI) experiences semantic divergence and identifier misalignments due to the lack of an immutable Master Person Index anchored to national identity numbers (NIK)[cite: 7].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-003]]: Court records are stored as unstructured binary PDF/DOCX files without machine-readable legal ontologies (LegalDocML), while decentralized servers expose vulnerabilities to web defacements and unmonitored scraping[cite: 7].

== Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ID-001]]: Decentralized IT infrastructure utilizing local SIPP database nodes across 800+ working units, synchronized upstream daily to central servers, combined with e-Court and e-Berpadu portals under Supreme Court regulations[cite: 7].

== Japanese Practice / Praktik Jepang ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-JP-001]]: Centralized cloud and server repository managed by the Supreme Court, operating under statutory amendments (Act No. 48 of 2022) with the "3e" framework (e-Court, e-Filing via mints, e-Case Management)[cite: 7].

== Gap / Kesenjangan ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-001]]: Reliance on autonomous judicial decrees (PERMA) rather than primary parliamentary legislation, creating legal friction, alongside asynchronous synchronization vulnerabilities and unstructured file storage[cite: 7].
* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-002]]: Absence of machine-readable legal schemas (Akoma Ntoso), unautomated personal identifiable information (PII) redaction exposing PDP law compliance risks, and digital divide barriers for pro-se litigants[cite: 7].

== Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan ==
Adopt the ''e-Peradilan Modern'' reference architecture: replace decentralized SIPP instances with a multi-tenant PostgreSQL cloud backbone, upgrade Puskarda into an Apache Kafka event mesh with an MPI Master Person Index, adopt OASIS LegalDocML (Akoma Ntoso) XML schemas, enforce BSrE hardware security module digital signatures, and institute automated PII redaction[cite: 7].

== Action / Aksi ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-001]]: Form multi-agency PMO (Supreme Court, BSSN, Komdigi, Polri, Kejaksaan), enact Supreme Court Pilot Decree, publish canonical LegalDocML schemas, and provision staging cloud environments[cite: 7].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-002]]: Deploy BPMN 2.0 workflow engine, integrate SIPP change-data-capture connectors, install PTSP self-service pro-se kiosks, and connect Puskarda 2.0 to local law enforcement registries[cite: 7].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-003]]: Cut over pilot court civil and criminal dockets to ''e-Peradilan Modern'', conduct MA-CSIRT/BSSN penetration testing, audit PII redaction accuracy, and deliver national scaling report[cite: 7].

== Pilot / Pilot Proyek ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-007]]: 90-day multi-agency pilot program across Central Jakarta District Court (PN Jakarta Pusat) and Surabaya District Court (PN Surabaya)[cite: 7].

== KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-007]]: Synchronization latency $< 5$ seconds; inter-agency handshake velocity $< 120$ minutes; LegalDocML parsing rate $\ge 95\%$; PDP PII redaction precision/recall $\ge 99.2\%$; pro-se completion $\ge 80\%$; zero unauthorized database modifications; instant appellate bundle compilation ($< 10$ minutes)[cite: 7].

== Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan ==
Establish high-level inter-agency steering committees and PMO oversight to govern master data management, cybersecurity telemetry, and legal-tech standardization[cite: 7].

== Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi ==
Codify electronic procedures directly within the forthcoming national Civil Procedure Code and promulgate joint ministerial data-sharing protocols under SPPT-TI[cite: 7].

== Evidence / Bukti Empiris ==

* Indonesia's e-Court registered 410,754 first-instance cases in 2024 and mandated electronic appellate transmission, but struggles with synchronization bottlenecks across 800+ local databases[cite: 7].
* Japan's statutory-backed mints platform and centralized e-Case Management establish a unified, high-integrity cloud repository taking full statutory effect on May 21, 2026[cite: 7].

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

== Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas ==

* Entity ID: JPAIS-MED-REF-008
* Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa
* Ingestion Status: Confirmed

== Description / Deskripsi ==
Evaluates judicial performance measurement and key performance indicator (KPI) architectures across the Indonesian and Japanese judiciaries, analyzing the operational distortions caused by uniform disposition targets (SEMA No. 2/2014) and proposing a balanced reform framework incorporating Differentiated Case Management (DCM), a Weighted Caseload System (CWM), an Appellate Durability Index, and independent blind survey platforms (ICUX)[cite: 8].

== Problem / Masalah ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-001]]: Uniform disposition deadlines (5-month SEMA No. 2/2014) and real-time EIS rankings create transactional compliance pressure, incentivizing metric gaming such as pre-registration delays and premature procedural dismissals (putusan NO)[cite: 8].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-002]]: Indonesian court workloads and backlogs are evaluated through raw numerical volume rather than complexity-weighted metrics, producing workload imbalances across jurisdictions[cite: 8].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-003]]: Current performance indicators treat all dispositions homogeneously, failing to evaluate substantive legal reasoning quality, while counter-side in-person customer satisfaction surveys (SKM/SPAK) suffer from social pressure and metric inflation[cite: 8].

== Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ID-001]]: Centralized digital monitoring framework administered by Badilum via SIPP and EIS v3, reinforced by court quality certification (AMPUH), enforcing uniform 5-month disposition ceilings[cite: 8].

== Japanese Practice / Praktik Jepang ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-JP-001]]: Decentralized qualitative oversight centered in the Supreme Court General Secretariat, operating under the Act on Expediting Trials (Act No. 107 of 2003) with flexible 2-year macro-targets and biannual empirical verification reviews[cite: 8].

== Gap / Kesenjangan ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-001]]: Absence of case complexity calibration, weighted caseload models, and substantive legal quality metrics within the executive monitoring framework[cite: 8].
* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-002]]: Lack of independent, blind sampling for public integrity perception surveys and structural integration of appellate durability into first-instance evaluations[cite: 8].

== Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan ==
Establish Differentiated Case Management (DCM) tracks (A, B, C) in SIPP, deploy a Weighted Caseload Allocation Module (CWM), integrate an Appellate Durability Module into AMPUH/EIS, transition customer satisfaction collection to an independent blind survey engine (ICUX) managed by Bawas, and execute a 90-day multi-court balanced pilot[cite: 8].

== Action / Aksi ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-001]]: Deploy DCM and CWM sub-routines in staging databases, decouple local PTSP survey collection, and establish automated WhatsApp/SMS blind survey delivery via Bawas (ICUX)[cite: 8].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-002]]: Process incoming civil and criminal dockets through active SIPP-DCM/CWM modules, enforce weighted caseload ceilings (40 active points/judge), and conduct bi-weekly exception tracking[cite: 8].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-003]]: Perform appellate quality audits on procedural dismissals (putusan NO), analyze econometric pilot data against baseline controls, and compile administrative reform reports for Supreme Court leadership[cite: 8].

== Pilot / Pilot Proyek ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-008]]: 90-day multi-court pilot program across Pengadilan Negeri Jakarta Pusat, Pengadilan Negeri Surabaya, and Pengadilan Negeri Sleman[cite: 8].

== KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-008]]: Milestone Timeliness Index $\ge 95\%$; adjournment interval $\le 10$ calendar days; caseload variance coefficient $\le 0.15$; weighted clearance ratio $1.0$ to $1.1$; appellate affirmance rate $\ge 85\%$; procedural dismissals $\le 5\%$ of civil dispositions; externalized integrity index $\ge 85\%$[cite: 8].

== Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan ==
Promulgate a revised Supreme Court Regulation superseding SEMA No. 2 of 2014 to institutionalize DCM tracks, weighted caseload allocations, and independent integrity evaluations[cite: 8].

== Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi ==
Upgrade EIS platform to version 4, revise AMPUH accreditation checklists (Areas II and VI), and enact Supreme Court Decrees governing ICUX blind surveys and the Judicial Decision Quality Framework[cite: 8].

== Evidence / Bukti Empiris ==

* Indonesian Supreme Court productivity ratios remain high (99.47% in 2023, 99.26% in 2024, 99.54% in 2025) under administrative speed enforcement, while first-instance courts resolved over 2.7 to 2.9 million cases annually[cite: 8].
* Japanese civil first-instance proceedings average 12.3 to 12.4 months under flexible 2-year statutory targets backed by intensive preparatory proceedings[cite: 8].

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

== Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas ==

* Entity ID: JPAIS-MED-REF-009
* Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa
* Ingestion Status: Confirmed

== Description / Deskripsi ==
Provides an exhaustive comparative assessment of evidence-based judicial policy frameworks between Indonesia and Japan, examining micro-data fragmentation, de-identification standards (SK KMA 2-144/2022), institutional research think-tanks (Pustrajak Kumdil vs. LTRI/Chōsakan), biennial trial expedition verifications, regulatory sandboxes (IJPL), and algorithmic governance for artificial intelligence[cite: 9].

== Problem / Masalah ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-001]]: Indonesian judicial data remains functionally fragmented across distributed SIPP databases, focusing on mechanical caseload accounting rather than structured longitudinal micro-data modeling[cite: 9].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-002]]: Manual anonymization under SK KMA 2-144/2022 creates inconsistent redaction standards, exposing protected identifiers or stripping out non-identifying substantive variables[cite: 9].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-003]]: Policy interventions lack institutionalized ex-post empirical evaluations, formal research judge corps, or controlled regulatory sandboxes prior to nationwide promulgation[cite: 9].

== Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ID-001]]: Institutionalized technological infrastructure (SIPP, e-Court, e-Berpadu, Direktori Putusan, Smart Majelis) paired with the restructured Center for Law and Judicial Policy Strategy (Pustrajak Kumdil under BSDK)[cite: 9].

== Japanese Practice / Praktik Jepang ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-JP-001]]: Centralized empirical governance operated by the General Secretariat and LTRI, supported by statutory biennial verification reports under the Act on Expediting Trials, Judicial Research Officials (Saibansho Chōsakan), and phased IT transformations[cite: 9].

== Gap / Kesenjangan ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-001]]: Absence of a centralized, queryable National Judicial Data Repository (NJDR), explicit statutory mandates for periodic empirical reviews, and formal operational integration of Pustrajak Kumdil research into Supreme Court chambers[cite: 9].
* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-002]]: Lack of automated algorithmic de-identification pipelines, formal judicial policy testing laboratories, and explicit ethical audit charters for artificial intelligence systems[cite: 9].

== Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan ==
Establish the National Judicial Data Repository (NJDR), deploy automated AI-driven de-identification pipelines, transform Pustrajak Kumdil into an empirical think-tank with Research Judges, institutionalize Biennial Trial Expedition Verification Reports, create the Indonesian Judicial Policy Laboratory (IJPL) sandboxes, and adopt an Algorithmic Governance Framework[cite: 9].

== Action / Aksi ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-001]]: Promulgate Supreme Court Regulation on Judicial Data Governance, execute a 90-day data cleaning and micro-data extraction pilot, and establish the Pustrajak Kumdil Research Fellowship[cite: 9].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-002]]: Deploy the IJPL sandbox in Surabaya for pre-trial disclosure protocols, roll out the MD-JPD dashboard, and integrate the advisory Simetris Precedent Analytics Engine in pilot criminal chambers[cite: 9].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-003]]: Conduct independent algorithmic audits, compile the Prototype Biennial Judicial Expedition Report, and submit policy recommendations to Supreme Court Chamber Plenaries[cite: 9].

== Pilot / Pilot Proyek ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-009]]: 90-day multi-court pilot program across PN Jakarta Pusat, PN Surabaya, PA Surabaya, PN Sleman, and PN Kisaran[cite: 9].

== KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-009]]: Anonymization accuracy $\ge 99.5\%$; micro-data structuring latency $< 24$ hours; policy brief adoption $\ge 75\%$; trial postponement reduction $\ge 25\%$; off-hours data batching reduced by $50\%$; pre-trial settlements increased by $25\%$; 100% algorithmic audit compliance[cite: 9].

== Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan ==
Issue Supreme Court Executive Orders and Regulations requiring empirical data briefs for all proposed Perma and SEMA regulations and institutionalizing Pustrajak Kumdil research integration[cite: 9].

== Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi ==
Promulgate comprehensive Supreme Court Regulations on Judicial Data Governance, Biennial Trial Expedition Verification, Experimental Judicial Sandboxes, and Algorithmic AI Governance[cite: 9].

== Evidence / Bukti Empiris ==

* Indonesian Supreme Court achieved 99.54% clearance in 2025 across 37,973 resolved cases, with first-instance courts handling over 2.8 million filings[cite: 9].
* Japan's statutory biennial verification reports (such as the 11th report in 2025) empirically track civil trial durations, showing 7.6% of civil first-instance cases exceeding two years[cite: 9].

{{JPAIS Knowledge|id=JPAIS:REFORM-PROPOSAL:JPAIS-MED-REF-010|type=ReformProposal|title_id=Analisis Komparatif Arsitektur Alternatif Penyelesaian Sengketa di Indonesia dan Jepang|title_en=Comparative Jurisprudential and Institutional Architecture of Alternative Dispute Resolution: Systemic Bottlenecks in Indonesia, Japanese Conciliation Models, and an Integrated Reform Framework (JPAIS)|slug=jpa-med-ref-010-comparative-adr-architecture|description_id=Analisis komparatif menyeluruh mengenai arsitektur alternatif penyelesaian sengketa (APS/ADR) mencakup mediasi peradilan, antarmuka arbitrase, gugatan sederhana (small claims), ODR, eksekusi putusan, dan akses terhadap keadilan antara Indonesia dan Jepang dalam Kerangka JPAIS.|description_en=Comprehensive comparative analysis on alternative dispute resolution (ADR) architectures covering court-connected mediation, arbitration interfaces, small claims, ODR, settlement enforcement, and access to justice between Indonesia and Japan under the JPAIS Framework.|jurisdiction=Indonesia / Japan Comparative[cite: 10]|legal_domain=Judicial Reform / Alternative Dispute Resolution / Civil Procedure[cite: 10]|topics=Tripartite Conciliation Panels, Order in Lieu of Settlement, Arbitration Annulment Screening, Pre-Action Settlement Ratification, SIPP-ODR Portal, Singapore Convention Implementation[cite: 10]|status=Proposed (Co-Design & Pilot Stage)[cite: 10]|language=bilingual (id/en)|authority=Mahkamah Agung Republik Indonesia / JICA KCCP[cite: 10]|verification_status=VERIFIED|version=1.0}}

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

== Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas ==

* Entity ID: JPAIS-MED-REF-010
* Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa
* Ingestion Status: Confirmed

== Description / Deskripsi ==
Evaluates alternative dispute resolution (ADR) architectures across six core domains between Indonesia and Japan, addressing structural bottlenecks such as Indonesia's low general civil mediation success rates (4.0%–4.08%) versus Japan's high conciliation efficiency (>50% general civil, >70% family/inheritance) through the Chōtei committee system, and proposes the Japan-Indonesia ADR Integration System (JPAIS) reform framework[cite: 10].

== Problem / Masalah ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-001]]: Court-connected mediation in Indonesia suffers from structural ritualization and negligible general civil settlement rates (4.0%–4.08%), driven by overloaded solo judge-mediators and uncompensated non-judge mediators[cite: 10].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-002]]: Arbitration interfaces face post-award delays, dilatory annulment actions under Article 70 of Law No. 30 of 1999 following CC Decision No. 15/PUU-XII/2014, and the lack of direct executory power for provisional measures[cite: 10].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-003]]: Small claims and electronic dispute resolution frameworks lack pre-litigation settlement ratification mechanisms and secure, integrated ODR virtual caucus portals, while mediated settlements encounter slow domestic execution and unratified cross-border enforcement (Singapore Convention)[cite: 10].

== Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ID-001]]: Governed by PERMA No. 1 of 2016, PERMA No. 4 of 2019 (Small Claims), PERMA No. 3 of 2022 (Electronic Mediation), PERMA No. 3 of 2023 (Arbitration Procedures), and Law No. 30 of 1999 on Arbitration and ADR[cite: 10].

== Japanese Practice / Praktik Jepang ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-JP-001]]: Governed by the Civil Conciliation Act (1951), Domestic Relations Case Procedure Act (2011), Arbitration Act (2003), and ADR Act (2004), utilizing tripartite Conciliation Committees (Chōtei Iinkai) and ex-officio Orders in Lieu of Conciliation (Article 17)[cite: 10].

== Gap / Kesenjangan ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-001]]: Reliance on a solo mediator model without multidisciplinary expert panels, evaluative settlement authority, or enforced bad-faith cost sanctions[cite: 10].
* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-002]]: Absence of summary screening for frivolous arbitral annulments, pre-action settlement ratification for small claims, mandatory default ODR portals, and statutory implementation for the Singapore Convention on Mediation[cite: 10].

== Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan ==
Establish Tripartite Conciliation Panels (Majelis Konsiliasi Tripartit) with judicial Orders in Lieu of Settlement (Penetapan Pengganti Perdamaian), specialized commercial arbitration supervision benches with 7-day screening, pre-action settlement ratification for small claims, default SIPP-ODR portals with BSrE signatures, domestic fast-track execution, Singapore Convention ratification, and subsidized lay conciliator allowances[cite: 10].

== Action / Aksi ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-001]]: Issue Supreme Court Implementation Decree establishing the JPAIS pilot program across 12 designated courts, configure SIPP-ODR portal, and accredit 120 Non-Judge Expert Commissioners[cite: 10].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-002]]: Deploy Tripartite Conciliation Panels, Rapid Small Claims Settlement Desks, and Specialized Commercial Arbitration Supervision Benches across pilot jurisdictions[cite: 10].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-003]]: Conduct empirical performance audits, track settlement and execution timelines, finalize draft permanent PERMAs, and submit statutory reform proposals to DPR[cite: 10].

== Pilot / Pilot Proyek ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-010]]: 90-day multi-court pilot program across 12 target courts (PN Jakarta Pusat, PN Surabaya, PN Medan, PN Bandung, PN Semarang, PN Denpasar, PN Kupang, PN Jayapura, PA Jakarta Selatan, PA Surabaya, PA Malang, PA Depok)[cite: 10].

== KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-010]]: General civil mediation success $\ge 25\%$; religious property/inheritance resolution $\ge 60\%$; mediation duration $\le 21$ calendar days; arbitral annulment disposal compliance $100\%$ ($>85\%$ frivolous claims dismissed in 7 days); small claims ratification $\le 3$ days; ODR commercial processing $\ge 50\%$; settlement execution writ issuance $\le 21$ calendar days[cite: 10].

== Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan ==
Promulgate joint ministerial decrees, Supreme Court circulars, and executive-legislative ratifications to establish sustainable funding for lay conciliators, ODR cryptographic standards, and international treaty enforcement[cite: 10].

== Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi ==
Promulgate revised PERMAs on Court-Connected Mediation and Conciliation, Small Claims Settlement Ratification, Electronic Mediation, and Arbitral Annulment Screening, alongside statutory revisions to Law No. 30 of 1999 and ratification of the Singapore Convention[cite: 10].

== Evidence / Bukti Empiris ==

* Indonesian general civil mediation success rates hover between 4.0% and 4.08%, while Japanese conciliation achieves $>50\%$ in general civil disputes and $71.8\%$ in inheritance property cases[cite: 10].
* Japanese Article 17 orders resolve 29.9% of inheritance division cases alongside 42.0% consensual accords within two to three sessions spanning approximately three months[cite: 10].

{{JPAIS Knowledge|id=JPAIS:REFORM-PROPOSAL:JPAIS-MED-REF-011|type=ReformProposal|title_id=Akses terhadap Keadilan di Indonesia dan Jepang|title_en=Access to Justice in Indonesia and Japan: Comparative Legal Frameworks, Systemic Deficiencies, and Empirical Reform Pathways|slug=jpa-med-ref-011-access-to-justice|description_id=Analisis komparatif menyeluruh mengenai akses terhadap keadilan mencakup keterjangkauan dan bantuan hukum (BPHN vs Hōterasu), keadilan geografis kepulauan, transformasi digital dan pengalaman pengguna, perlindungan kelompok rentan, akses disabilitas, penyelesaian gugatan sederhana, mediasi peradilan, serta transparansi informasi dan privasi data antara Indonesia dan Jepang dalam Kerangka JPAIS.|description_en=Comprehensive comparative analysis on access to justice covering affordability and legal assistance (BPHN vs Hōterasu), archipelagic geographic access, digital transformation and user experience, vulnerable user protections, disability access, small claims litigation, court-annexed mediation, and information transparency versus data privacy between Indonesia and Japan under the JPAIS Framework.|jurisdiction=Indonesia / Japan Comparative[cite: 11]|legal_domain=Judicial Reform / Access to Justice / Civil Procedure[cite: 11]|topics=Public Defender Stations, Tele-Justice Access Pods, Assisted Digital Filing, Trauma-Informed Courtrooms, Certified Sign-Language Interpreters, Automated Pseudonymization[cite: 11]|status=Proposed (Co-Design & Pilot Stage)[cite: 11]|language=bilingual (id/en)|authority=Mahkamah Agung Republik Indonesia / JICA KCCP[cite: 11]|verification_status=VERIFIED|version=1.0}}

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

== Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas ==

* Entity ID: JPAIS-MED-REF-011
* Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa
* Ingestion Status: Confirmed

== Description / Deskripsi ==
Provides an exhaustive comparative assessment of access to justice across eight core domains between Indonesia and Japan, addressing structural deficiencies such as Indonesia's fragmented legal aid reimbursement ceilings and archipelagic transit bottlenecks versus Japan's consolidated legal support corporation (Hōterasu), summary court network, and digital civil procedure transformation, and proposes an integrated reform framework[cite: 11].

== Problem / Masalah ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-001]]: Indonesian state-funded legal aid is structurally fragmented, geographically maldistributed, and fiscally constrained by retrospective reimbursement ceilings, forcing indigent litigants to rely on under-resourced non-governmental OBHs[cite: 11].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-002]]: Archipelagic geography, marine transit costs, and rugged terrain impose severe physical and financial barriers on rural populations reaching distant courts, while electronic litigation (*e-Court* and *e-Litigasi*) creates a digital divide that excludes self-represented and marginalized litigants[cite: 11].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-003]]: Vulnerable users face secondary trauma and gender bias, disabled and linguistic minorities encounter inaccessibility and lack of certified sign interpreters, small claims face procedural bottlenecks, mediation suffers from formalism, and public information transparency experiences inconsistencies under data privacy mandates (UU PDP)[cite: 11].

== Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ID-001]]: Governed by Law No. 16 of 2011 (BPHN/OBH), Perma No. 1 of 2014 (Posbakum), Perma No. 1/2019 and Perma No. 7/2022 (e-Court), Perma No. 3/2017 (Women/Children), PP No. 39/2020 (Disabilities), Perma No. 4/2019 (Small Claims), Perma No. 1/2016 (Mediation), and SK KMA No. 2-144/2022 (Public Information Standards)[cite: 11].

== Japanese Practice / Praktik Jepang ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-JP-001]]: Governed by the Comprehensive Legal Support Act (Hōterasu), Summary Court network (Kan'i Saibansho), CCP digital amendments taking full effect May 21, 2026, Crime Victims and DV Protection Acts, Act on Elimination of Discrimination against Persons with Disabilities, Small Claims track (Shōgaku Soshō), Civil Conciliation Act (Minji Chōtei), and APPI data privacy frameworks[cite: 11].

== Gap / Kesenjangan ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-001]]: Separation of courthouse advice from defense, episodic mobile court hearings, mandatory e-court portals without unrepresented paper support or open-court video displays, and lack of dedicated operational budgets for disability and trauma accommodations[cite: 11].
* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-002]]: Absence of intermediate legal professions (*shihō shoshi* equivalents), solo mediator capacity constraints, and manual clerk redactions leading to publication errors under data privacy statutes[cite: 11].

== Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan ==
Establish permanent Public Defender Stations (Sentra Advokat Publik) with salaried public advocates and DTKS automated fee waivers, deploy Tele-Justice Access Pods in island sub-districts, institutionalize assisted digital filing at PTSP desks with mandatory paper backup, implement automated vulnerability screening and UPTD PPA referrals, fund certified sign-language interpreters, introduce interactive small-claims form kiosks with active judicial guidance, form tripartite expert conciliation panels, and deploy AI-assisted automated pseudonymization and redaction pipelines[cite: 11].

== Action / Aksi ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-001]]: Promulgate joint ministerial and Supreme Court decrees (SKB Tiga Lembaga) establishing the National Public Defender Roster, remote archipelagic hearing SOPs, and disability/linguistic accommodation budgets[cite: 11].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-002]]: Deploy the 90-day multi-domain pilot across six targeted regional jurisdictions (Wamena, Saumlaki, Tahuna, Natuna, Talaud, Surabaya, Bandung, Padang, Denpasar, Mataram, Sleman, Kupang, Ambon)[cite: 11].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-003]]: Audit pilot performance metrics, evaluate representation rates and digital access, finalize permanent PERMA regulations, and submit statutory reform proposals to DPR[cite: 11].

== Pilot / Pilot Proyek ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-011]]: 90-day multi-domain pilot program across 14 designated first-instance jurisdictions spanning remote islands, urban centers, and regional trial courts[cite: 11].

== KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-011]]: Indigent civil representation $\ge 45\%$; mean prodeo processing duration $< 24$ hours; rural travel cost reduction $\ge 75\%$; self-represented digital initiations increased by $50\%$; vulnerability pre-trial assessment $100\%$; disability assessment completion $100\%$ with zero linguistic hearing postponements; small claims 25-day compliance $\ge 95\%$; mediation success $\ge 40\%$; automated PII masking precision $99.8\%$[cite: 11].

== Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan ==
Promulgate joint ministerial regulations, Supreme Court circulars, and executive-legislative framework codifications to establish permanent national budget appropriations for salaried public defenders, remote satellite terminals, and algorithmic privacy compliance[cite: 11].

== Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi ==
Promulgate comprehensive Supreme Court Regulations (PERMA) amending Perma No. 7 of 2022 (E-Court), Perma No. 4 of 2019 (Small Claims), Perma No. 1 of 2016 (Mediation), alongside unified regulations on Disability/Linguistic Accommodations, Trauma-Informed Courtrooms, and automated SK KMA 2-144/2022 pseudonymization[cite: 11].

== Evidence / Bukti Empiris ==

* Indonesia's e-Court registered 410,754 first-instance cases in 2024, but unrepresented individual litigants (*Pengguna Lain*) account for a negligible fraction due to strict onboarding barriers[cite: 11].
* Japan's Hōterasu operates with a central budget of JPY 32.1 billion, supporting 50 branches and salaried staff attorneys, while its amended CCP digital transformation culminates on May 21, 2026[cite: 11].

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

== Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas ==

* Entity ID: JPAIS-MED-REF-012
* Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa
* Ingestion Status: Confirmed

== Description / Deskripsi ==
Provides an exhaustive evaluation of peaceful conflict resolution in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, analyzing historical structural failures (Oslo incrementalism, Camp David 2000, regional normalization), stakeholder dynamics, third-party monitoring precedents (MFO Sinai, ILMG), and proposing an Integrated Peaceful Conflict Resolution Model (IPCRM) structured across a four-tier settlement framework and a 30-60-90 day peacebuilding pilot[cite: 12].

== Problem / Masalah ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-001]]: The diplomatic architecture of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict has repeatedly suffered from systemic vulnerabilities, severe power asymmetries, deferral of final-status issues, settlement expansion, and domestic political instability[cite: 12].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-002]]: International and bilateral mediation frameworks exhibit severe enforcement deficits and lack coercive mechanisms to enforce compliance with UN resolutions or interim treaty terms[cite: 12].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-003]]: Severe territorial fragmentation in the West Bank (Areas A, B, and C) and the political/geographic schism between the Palestinian Authority and Hamas paralyze unified governance and negotiation mandates[cite: 12].

== Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ID-001]]: While not a direct party to the conflict, Indonesia maintains consistent normative support for Palestinian statehood through international multilateral bodies (UN, NAM, OIC) and judicial proceedings (ICJ advisory opinions).

== Japanese Practice / Praktik Jepang ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-JP-001]]: Japan contributes via diplomatic mediation, humanitarian funding, and economic confidence-building initiatives (such as the Corridor for Peace and Prosperity initiative bridging Jericho and regional markets).

== Gap / Kesenjangan ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-001]]: Absence of binding final-status parameters in incremental peace frameworks, leaving processes vulnerable to irreversible facts on the ground and spoiler violence[cite: 12].
* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-002]]: Lack of robust, independent third-party monitoring and executive enforcement mechanisms equipped with independent civilian observer units and structured military-to-military liaison channels[cite: 12].

== Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan ==
Adopt the Integrated Peaceful Conflict Resolution Model (IPCRM) structured across four progressive tiers: Tier 1 (Immediate Ceasefire & Humanitarian Access), Tier 2 (Short-Term Confidence-Building Measures), Tier 3 (Medium-Term Negotiated Arrangements via hybrid international peacekeeping), and Tier 4 (Long-Term Settlement & Reconciliation featuring 1967 borders with 1:1 swaps, shared Jerusalem governance, and refugee compensation funds)[cite: 12].

== Action / Aksi ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-001]]: Deploy Phase 1 of the peacebuilding pilot (Days 1–30): implement simultaneous ceasefires, execute prisoner/hostage swaps under ICRC oversight, open border points for 500+ aid trucks daily, and stand up the Joint Ceasefire Coordination Cell (JCCC) in Cairo[cite: 12].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-002]]: Execute Phase 2 (Days 31–60): deploy advance civilian observers, unblock PA clearance tax revenues via BIS escrow accounts, reactivate joint technical utility boards, and enforce settlement freezes[cite: 12].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-003]]: Execute Phase 3 (Days 61–90): appoint a technocratic Palestinian municipal administrative council, convene regional steering committee talks, launch civil society dialogues, and formalize gender advisory boards under UNSCR 1325[cite: 12].

== Pilot / Pilot Proyek ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-012]]: 90-day peacebuilding pilot framework structured across three sequential phases (Ceasefire Stabilization, Verification Deployment, Transitional Governance)[cite: 12].

== KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-012]]: 100% halt in verified cross-border strikes; 500+ daily aid trucks entering Gaza; 100% Phase-1 hostage/prisoner execution; 100% transfer of withheld clearance tax funds via BIS escrow; zero new settlement construction starts; technocratic council operational in all municipalities[cite: 12].

== Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan ==
Establish executive mediation councils and international funding mechanisms to support regional stabilization, financial escrow accounts, and hybrid peacekeeping deployments[cite: 12].

== Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi ==
Promulgate UN Security Council resolutions mandating ceasefire phases, hybrid peacekeeping mandates, and international financial oversight frameworks[cite: 12].

== Evidence / Bukti Empiris ==

* Historical analysis reveals structural failures in Oslo (1993/1995), Camp David (2000), and Wye River (1998), contrasted with successful third-party verification models such as the Sinai MFO (active since 1981) and the Israel-Lebanon Monitoring Group (ILMG)[cite: 12].
* The 2024 UNSCR 2735 framework and the 2002 Arab Peace Initiative illustrate contemporary multilateral efforts and regional macro-settlement parameters[cite: 12].

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

== Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas ==

* Entity ID: JPAIS-MED-REF-013
* Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa
* Ingestion Status: Confirmed

== Description / Deskripsi ==
Provides comprehensive administrative guidelines and regulations for international participants attending JICA's Knowledge Co-Creation Program (KCCP) in Japan, detailing legal status, code of conduct, financial allowances, medical services, pre-departure checklists, and terminal navigation maps for major Japanese airports[cite: 13].

== Problem / Masalah ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-001]]: International participants navigating foreign legal systems, strict regulatory standards, and complex transportation hubs face potential compliance risks, health vulnerabilities, and administrative friction[cite: 13].

== Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ID-001]]: Official nomination and acceptance procedures through diplomatic/official channels connecting nominating governments with Japanese Embassies, JICA overseas offices, and domestic program partners[cite: 13].

== Japanese Practice / Praktik Jepang ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-JP-001]]: Standardized administration of international training programs under JICA's domestic and international operational guidelines, enforcing strict participant obligations and comprehensive support structures[cite: 13].

== Gap / Kesenjangan ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-001]]: Potential misunderstandings regarding strict Japanese laws concerning drug possession, copyright infringement, sexual harassment, and financial allowances management[cite: 13].

== Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan ==
Strict adherence to JICA KCCP operational guidelines, participant rules and regulations, health requirements, and standardized allowance management protocols[cite: 13].

== Action / Aksi ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-001]]: Complete pre-departure checklists (Checklists 1, 2, 3, 4), secure appropriate visas (Trainee/Scholar status), and prepare required reports and medical records[cite: 13].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-002]]: Observe JICA Center regulations, including return times, stay-out applications, fire prevention policies, and environmental guidelines[cite: 13].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-003]]: Utilize medical insurance cards, adhere to emergency/non-emergency care protocols, and complete arrival health examinations for stays exceeding six months[cite: 13].

== Pilot / Pilot Proyek ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-013]]: Standardized nationwide implementation across all JICA domestic training centers and partner institutions[cite: 13].

== KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-013]]: Zero regulatory infractions; successful completion of course curricula; maintenance of good health status throughout the program duration[cite: 13].

== Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan ==
Reinforce institutional capacity building, human resource development, and international friendship through reciprocal knowledge co-creation between Japan and partner countries[cite: 13].

== Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi ==
Strict compliance with Japanese laws, ordinances, JICA Center rules, and copyright regulations during the training period[cite: 13].

== Evidence / Bukti Empiris ==

* Over the past 60 years, more than 349,000 participants from 198 countries have participated in JICA's Knowledge Co-Creation Program, with approximately 10,000 annual participants across diverse development sectors[cite: 13].

{{JPAIS Knowledge|id=JPAIS:REFORM-PROPOSAL:JPAIS-MED-REF-014|type=ReformProposal|title_id=Penyempurnaan Standar Pengujian Yudisial untuk Putusan KPPU|title_en=Refining Judicial Review Standards for KPPU Decisions: Policy Bottlenecks, Due Process Protections, and Proposed Normative Strengthening of PERMA No. 3 of 2021|slug=jpa-med-ref-014-refining-judicial-review-kppu|description_id=Analisis komprehensif mengenai hambatan kebijakan (policy bottlenecks) dalam penerapan PERMA Nomor 3 Tahun 2021 tentang Tata Cara Pengajuan dan Pemeriksaan Keberatan Terhadap Putusan KPPU di Pengadilan Niaga, serta usulan reformasi norma pembuktian, Due Process of Law, dan peta jalan implementasinya.|description_en=Comprehensive analysis of policy bottlenecks in the implementation of PERMA Number 3 of 2021 concerning the procedure for filing and examining objections against KPPU decisions in Commercial Courts, alongside proposed evidentiary reforms, Due Process of Law protections, and an implementation roadmap.|jurisdiction=Indonesia[cite: 14]|legal_domain=Competition Law / Judicial Review / Civil Procedure[cite: 14]|topics=PERMA No. 3 of 2021, KPPU Decision Review, Due Process of Law, Economic Evidence, Commercial Court Reform[cite: 14]|status=Proposed (Co-Design & Pilot Stage)[cite: 14]|language=bilingual (id/en)|authority=Mahkamah Agung Republik Indonesia / Indonesian Competition Lawyers Association (ICLA)[cite: 14]|verification_status=VERIFIED|version=1.0}}

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

== Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas ==

* Entity ID: JPAIS-MED-REF-014
* Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa
* Ingestion Status: Confirmed

== Description / Deskripsi ==
Evaluates systemic policy bottlenecks arising from the application of Supreme Court Regulation (PERMA) No. 3 of 2021 governing objections to KPPU decisions in Commercial Courts, addressing issues such as the absolute ban on new evidence (novum), discrepancies in day-count definitions, unproportional bank guarantees, partial inkracht risks in joint conduct (cartel) cases, and the absence of specialized economic guidelines, while proposing a comprehensive two-track reform framework and ICLA normative recommendations[cite: 14, 16, 23, 24].

== Problem / Masalah ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-001]]: Absolute restriction on new evidence (novum) under Article 13(5) of PERMA 3/2021 violates defensive rights and *Due Process of Law*, especially when KPPU introduces economic analyses or penalty computations in final decisions without prior commission hearings[cite: 14].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-002]]: Procedural and administrative ambiguities—such as the conflict between PP No. 44/2021 (working days) and PERMA 3/2021 (calendar days), restrictive 14-day appeal windows from excerpts, non-proportional bank guarantees for non-monetary sanctions, and partial *inkracht* risks in multi-party cartel cases (e.g., 97 respondents)—create systemic legal uncertainty[cite: 16, 18, 23].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-003]]: Institutional capacity gaps, including an absence of formal standards for reviewing economic evidence (*economic evidence*) and econometric models, a deficit of certified competition law judges, and lack of secure data rooms or *inzage* access, reduce commercial courts to formalistic administrative "stamps"[cite: 17, 24, 27, 31].

== Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ID-001]]: Commercial Courts handle objections to KPPU decisions pursuant to PERMA No. 3 of 2021, operating under tight administrative timelines and restricted evidentiary review confines based solely on the KPPU dossier[cite: 14, 27, 28].

== Japanese Practice / Praktik Jepang ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-JP-001]]: Developed jurisdictions balance integrated administrative enforcement bodies (like the EU Commission or KFTC) with deep, substantive judicial scrutiny (*legality review with verification*) and robust protections for the equality of arms[cite: 27, 31].

== Gap / Kesenjangan ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-001]]: Disconnect between KPPU's integrated administrative model (investigating, prosecuting, and adjudicating simultaneously) and commercial courts' restricted review scope, which risks violating *audi et alteram partem* when review is reduced to a superficial "rubber stamp"[cite: 27, 28, 31].

== Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan ==
Implement a Two-Track Reform Approach: (1) Limited amendment of PERMA No. 3 of 2021 to harmonize day counts, relax novum restrictions when new economic models are introduced, provide proportional bank guarantees, and adopt confidentiality data rooms/inzage; (2) Issue dedicated Judicial Guidelines on Economic Analysis (*Pedoman Mengadili*) alongside mandatory continuous judicial certification and training[cite: 23, 24].

== Action / Aksi ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-001]]: Phase 1 (Q3 2026): Conduct public consultations on Draft Academic Papers (DIM) with MA, KPPU, and academics across 5 Commercial Court regions, finalizing the urgency text[cite: 16].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-002]]: Phase 2 (Q4 2026): Draft amendments to PERMA 3/2021, issue SK KMA guidelines for economic assessment (MSEJR), and structure Supreme Court circulars (SEMA) on PK and executory status[cite: 16].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-003]]: Phase 3 (Q1 2027): Upgrade SIPP and secure data rooms, and launch mandatory specialized economic training and certification programs for commercial judges[cite: 16].

== Pilot / Pilot Proyek ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-014]]: 5-Region Commercial Court Deployment across Jakarta Pusat, Surabaya, Medan, Makassar, and Semarang[cite: 16].

== KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-014]]: Net Impact Score of +7 for Option I reforms; 100% synchronization of working-day definitions; zero unjust procedural dismissals due to unproportional bank guarantees; complete adoption of economic evidence review standards across 5 Commercial Courts[cite: 16].

== Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan ==
Shift commercial court oversight from a mechanical *Crime Control* model (*assembly line*) to a rigorous *Due Process* model (*obstacle course*) that prioritizes substantive material justice and the protection of defensive rights[cite: 14, 16, 24].

== Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi ==
Promulgate an amended PERMA No. 3 of 2021, issue specialized SK KMA guidelines on economic analysis, and pursue long-term statutory harmonization via amendments to Law No. 5 of 1999 and the laws governing extraordinary legal remedies (Peninjauan Kembali)[cite: 16, 19, 23].

== Evidence / Bukti Empiris ==

* Empirical observations from ICLA and policy evaluations indicate that PERMA 3/2021 successfully established forum and procedural certainty, but current restrictions on new evidence and limited economic expertise risk reducing judicial review to a rubber stamp, especially in complex joint conduct cases like the 97-respondent online lending (pinjol) cartel[cite: 14, 17, 24, 27].
