== Summary / Ringkasan ==

== Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas ==

* Entity ID: JPAIS-MED-REF-015
* Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa
* Ingestion Status: Confirmed

== Description / Deskripsi ==
Synthesizes the August 2026 integrated Inventory of Issues (DIM) evaluating PERMA No. 3 of 2021 on procedures for filing and examining objections against KPPU decisions in Commercial Courts, covering 35 specific problem points distributed across 9 thematic issue groups (ranging from court jurisdiction, deadlines, formal requirements, examination stages, inspection scope, evidence/files, witnesses/experts, decisions/execution, to institutional support), plus 12 novel issues requiring regulatory incorporation[cite: 27].

== Problem / Masalah ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-001]]: Jurisdictional ambiguity for foreign respondents (foreign entities), conflicting day-count definitions between PERMA 3/2021 (calendar days) and PP 44/2021 (working days), and rigid filing deadlines tied to decision excerpts rather than complete copies create severe procedural barriers[cite: 27].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-002]]: Unproportional bank guarantees required without fines, multi-party joinder complexities (Turut Termohon), SIPP/e-Court multi-applicant tracking limitations, and uncertainties surrounding judicial review scope (*judex facti* assessment of economic analysis and relevant markets) impair substantive justice[cite: 27].
* [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-003]]: Evidentiary restrictions against new evidence (*novum*), lack of standards for indirect evidence and economic models, limited access to dossiers (*inzage*), absence of confidentiality data rooms, lack of online witness/expert examination frameworks (*hot tubbing*), and dual *inkracht* statuses in joint conduct cases hinder fair adjudication[cite: 27].

== Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ID-001]]: Commercial Courts examine objections against KPPU decisions pursuant to PERMA No. 3 of 2021, relying on decentralized SIPP tracking and tight administrative rules across designated regional courts[cite: 27].

== Japanese Practice / Praktik Jepang ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-JP-001]]: Comparative developed jurisdictions integrate specialized economic expertise, structured evidentiary testing, and comprehensive digital case management to ensure rigorous judicial review of administrative antitrust decisions[cite: 27].

== Gap / Kesenjangan ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-001]]: 23 problem points touch 14 existing articles of PERMA 3/2021, while 12 critical issues (such as partnership dispute pathways, economic evidence standards, confidentiality data rooms, and execution of non-monetary remedies) completely lack regulatory guidance[cite: 27].

== Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan ==
Execute comprehensive amendments to PERMA No. 3 of 2021 addressing the 35 DIM items: harmonize calendar/working days, introduce proportional bank guarantees, clarify Commercial Court scope over relevant markets and economic evidence, permit limited reciprocal new evidence, establish data rooms and *inzage* access, modernize online witness/expert examinations (*hot tubbing*), and streamline enforcement[cite: 27].

== Action / Aksi ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-001]]: Consolidate the August 2026 DIM across all eight internal court sources (Jakarta Pusat, Medan, Semarang, Surabaya, Makassar, and expert association papers)[cite: 27].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-002]]: Draft the Amending PERMA text targeting the 14 existing articles and incorporating provisions for the 12 unregulated new issue domains[cite: 27].
* [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-003]]: Upgrade SIPP and e-Court software modules to support multi-applicant bundling, big file management, and secure virtual proceedings[cite: 27].

== Pilot / Pilot Proyek ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-015]]: Multi-region Commercial Court deployment across Central Jakarta, Medan, Semarang, Surabaya, and Makassar[cite: 27].

== KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama ==

* [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-015]]: 100% harmonization of day-count definitions; zero improper dismissals due to unproportional bank guarantees; complete integration of economic evidence review standards across all Commercial Courts[cite: 27].

== Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan ==
Provide legal and procedural certainty for economic objection proceedings, closing procedural gaps while maintaining trial speed and institutional accountability[cite: 27].

== Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi ==
Promulgate an amended PERMA No. 3 of 2021, issue supplementary Supreme Court Circulars (SEMA) on case consolidation and extraordinary remedies, and align competition rules with the New Criminal Code (UU 1/2023)[cite: 27].

== Evidence / Bukti Empiris ==

* The August 2026 integrated DIM aggregates data and operational friction points from Commercial Court registries and expert association presentations across Jakarta, Medan, Semarang, Surabaya, and Makassar[cite: 27].

"1.0" } --- == Slide Presentation Breakdown: Amendment of PERMA No. 3 of 2021 (MA Corporate University Theme Colored Format) == === Slide 1 === * Main Title: INVENTORY OF ISSUES (DIM) * Subtitle: Key Issues for the Amendment of Supreme Court Regulation (PERMA) Number 3 of 2021 * Topic: Procedures for Filing and Examining Objections against KPPU Decisions in Commercial Courts * Presentation Note: This deck summarizes the integrated August 2026 DIM version containing 35 problem points regarding the application of PERMA 3/2021, grouped into 9 issue categories following the case management lifecycle. === Slide 2 === * Title: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY — Amendment Map on a Single Page * Key Statistics: * **35** Problem Points * **9** Issue Groups * **14** Potentially Amended Articles * **12** Unregulated New Issues * Articles Potentially Amended: Article 1 number 7 (Definition of days), Article 2 paragraph (4) (Inkracht status), Article 3 (Competence and deadlines), Article 4 (Bank guarantee obligation), Article 6 (Guarantee amount), Article 8 (Court appointment), Article 10 (Start of examination), Article 11 (Notification of decision), Article 12 (Mediation and evidence), Article 13 (Scope and evidence), Article 14 (Case duration), Article 15 (Witnesses and experts), Article 16 (Subsequent legal remedies), Article 21 (Standing of parties). * Potential New Issues to Include: (1) Legal remedies for partnership decisions; (2) Limits of authority between KPPU and other supervisory bodies; (3) e-Court and SIPP support for multiple Applicants; (4) Master case registry number post-consolidation; (5) Judicial review standards for economic analysis; (6) Confidentiality protection and data room mechanisms; (7) Summoning procedures for witnesses and experts; (8) Expert hot-tubbing; (9) Execution of non-monetary relief and asset data availability; (10) Courtroom facilities and human resource capacity; (11) Criminal law harmonization between Law 5/1999 and Law 1/2023 (New Criminal Code); (12) Socialization, periodic evaluation, and coordination. === Slide 3 === * Title: DIM STRUCTURE — Distribution of 35 Points across 9 Issue Groups * Heaviest Burden: Group C (Formal Requirements & Administration) and Group G (Witness & Expert Examination) each contain 5 points. * Unregulated Issues: 12 out of 35 points currently have no regulatory basis in PERMA 3/2021. * Structuring Flow: Grouping follows case stages, from adjudicating authority up to execution and institutional support. === Slide 4 === * Title: GROUP A — Court Jurisdiction and Competence * Point 1: Relative competence for foreign Respondents (Article 3 paragraph 2) — PERMA only regulates registry filings without clarifying forums for Respondents domiciled abroad, risking *niet ontvankelijke verklaard*. * Point 2: Legal remedies for partnership decisions (Unregulated) — KPPU Regulation 2/2024 states partnership decisions are final, yet courts continue to accept legal remedies. * Point 3: Authority limits between KPPU and other supervisory bodies (Unregulated) — Jurisdictional boundaries between KPPU and APIP, BPKP, LKPP, and State Administrative Courts (PTUN) regarding technical specifications remain unclear. === Slide 5 === * Title: GROUP B — Procedures and Deadlines for Filing Objections * Point 1: Conflict in day definitions (Article 1 number 7) — PERMA interprets days as calendar days, whereas Government Regulation 44/2021 mandates working days. * Point 2: Deadlines calculated from decision excerpts (Article 3 jo. Article 11) — Complete copies take up to 14 days to arrive, forcing memorial drafting without reviewing full legal reasoning. * Point 3: Simultaneous filing of declaration and memorial (Article 3 jo. Article 12) — Both must be filed within 14 calendar days, unlike cassation which separates them, while applicants must simultaneously arrange bank guarantees. === Slide 6 === * Title: GROUP C — Formal Requirements and Case Administration * Point 1: Bank guarantees for Respondents without fines (Article 4 paragraph 1 & Article 6) — Guarantees remain mandatory even when no monetary payment needs securing; amounts and refund mechanisms are unregulated. * Point 2: Status of Co-Respondents (Article 21 paragraph 2) — To avoid *plurium litis consortium*, other respondents are joined as parties, increasing costs and prolonging summons. * Point 3: e-Court and SIPP limitations (Unregulated) — Secondary objection filings for the same decision are frequently rejected; SIPP records only one petition per register. * Point 4: Master register number post-consolidation (Unregulated) — No legal basis exists for establishing a master case after multiple petitions are consolidated, risking breach of the 12-month limit. * Point 5: Delays in cross-forum court appointments (Article 8 paragraph 1) — Supreme Court Chief Justice appointment orders take too long to arrive, causing concurrent trials across Commercial Courts with risks of conflicting verdicts. === Slide 7 === * Title: GROUP D — Examination Timeframes and Stages * Point 1: Uncertainty of start timing (Article 10) — Timeframes are counted from the first hearing and dossier handover, even though parties may be absent or dossiers incomplete. * Point 2: Desynced minimum and maximum limits (Article 14 paragraph 1 jo. Article 15) — Cases must finish between 3 and 12 months, but judgments may be pronounced without waiting 3 months, causing ambiguity. * Point 3: Objection proceedings without mediation (Article 12) — PERMA omits mediation, whereas PERMA 1/2016 mandates court mediation, creating doctrinal debate. === Slide 8 === * Title: GROUP E — Scope and Standards of Objection Examination * Point 1: Commercial Court standing as *judex facti* (Article 13 paragraph 1) — Unclear whether panels must re-evaluate evidentiary sufficiency for every violation element or merely test KPPU reasoning reasonableness. * Point 2: Review of relevant market definitions (Article 13 paragraph 1) — No explicit authority to re-examine relevant market methodologies despite direct impacts on market share and dominance. * Point 3: Judicial review standards for economic analysis (Unregulated) — Economic analysis is not *self-proving*; tiered testing of methodology, data, assumptions, and alternative explanations is proposed. * Point 4: Transparency of fine calculation breakdowns (Article 10) — KPPU does not submit fine calculation details, preventing judicial review of formulas, aggravating, and mitigating factors. === Slide 9 === * Title: GROUP F — Evidence and Dossier Access * Point 1: Prohibition of new evidence (Article 13 paragraph 5) — KPPU decisions often contain facts and calculation methods absent from the Initial Report (LDP); limited reciprocal *novum* is proposed. * Point 2: Indirect evidence without guidelines (Article 12) — No quality standards or boundaries exist for *indirect evidence* aligned with Article 42 of Law 5/1999 or OECD guidelines. * Point 3: Limited access to files and investigation minutes / *inzage* (Article 13 paragraph 3 jo. Article 21 paragraph 2) — File inspection rights lack explicit adoption, causing informational asymmetry violating *audi et alteram partem*. * Point 4: Protection of business confidentiality (Unregulated) — Confidential info lacks protection in open hearings, whereas international practice utilizes two-version documents, data rooms, and confidentiality rings. === Slide 10 === * Title: GROUP G — Witness and Expert Examinations * Point 1: Criteria for submitting witnesses and experts (Article 13 paragraph 3 jo. Article 15) — Submissions are restricted to specific conditions; panel approval criteria lack clarity and written reasoning mandates. * Point 2: New witnesses or experts never previously submitted (Article 13) — Prohibitions lack clarity, causing divergent inter-panel applications and expanding proof beyond KPPU findings. * Point 3: Witness/expert summoning mechanism (Unregulated) — Unclear whether attendance is a party burden or court-summoned, leading to inconsistent trial practices. * Point 4: Online hearings / teleconferencing (Article 15) — Economic and industry experts often reside out-of-town or abroad, causing repeated adjournments due to lack of teleconferencing rules. * Point 5: Scope of expert testimony (Unregulated) — Experts are barred from discussing case merits, yet testimony is essential to test economic models; *hot-tubbing* is proposed. === Slide 11 === * Title: GROUP H — Judgments, Subsequent Legal Remedies, and Execution * Point 1: Inkracht status in multi-party cases (Article 2 ayat 4) — Some respondents accept final judgments while others pursue objections, confusing joint settlement remedies. * Point 2: Conflicting cassation verdicts on a single KPPU decision (Article 8 jo. Article 16) — Separated examinations have produced contradictory cassation verdicts, halting execution. * Point 3: Absence of Reconsideration / Peninjauan Kembali (Article 16 paragraph 2) — New evidence bans and law-only cassation reviews prevent the correction of newly discovered factual errors. * Point 4: Execution hurdles (Unregulated details) — Distrainable asset data is unavailable and relief is non-monetary; ordering KPPU to compile asset lists is proposed. === Slide 12 === * Title: GROUP I — Institutional Support, Capacity, and Harmonization * Point 1: Shortage of certified judges (Panel appointment) — Certified competition judges are extremely limited and fluctuate due to rotations, even in courts with the highest caseloads. * Point 2: Courtroom facilities and infrastructure (Unregulated) — Requires electronic trial facilities, big-file document management, and human resource upskilling. * Point 3: Criminal law harmonization (Unregulated) — Penal provisions in Law 5/1999 are misaligned with Law 1/2023 (New Criminal Code), particularly regarding corporate criminal liability and fines. * Point 4: Socialization, periodic evaluation, and coordination (Unregulated) — Severe regional caseload disparities require periodic evaluations, publication, and enhanced MA-KPPU coordination. === Slide 13 === * Title: DIRECTION OF REFINEMENT — Emerging Core Proposals * 1. Deadline Harmonization: Align days with PP 44/2021 and separate declarations from objection memorials. * 2. Proportional Bank Guarantees: Differentiate fined Respondents and clarify guarantee amounts and refunds. * 3. Scope Clarity: Affirm Commercial Court standing and relevant market review authority. * 4. Economic Review Standards: Establish tiered testing for methodology, data, assumptions, and alternatives. * 5. Limited New Evidence: Open reciprocal *novum* with written panel permission and reasoning. * 6. Dossier Access & Confidentiality: Adopt *inzage* with dual document versions and closed hearings. * 7. Modernization: Regulate online witness/expert hearings and e-Court/SIPP integration. * 8. Correction & Execution: Open Reconsideration (PK) under strict conditions and strengthen execution instruments. === Slide 14 === * Title: REFERENCES — Integration Sources for Inventory of Issues (August 2026) * 1–5. DIM Central Jakarta District Court (July 23, 2026), DIM Medan District Court, DIM Semarang District Court (2021–2026), DIM Surabaya District Court, Makassar District Court Presentation (2024–2026). * 6–8. Ine Ruky Presentation (Economic Analysis, August 2, 2026), ICLA Presentation (August 3, 2026), Prof. Ningrum Natasya Sirait Presentation (Comparison of KPPU PERMAs, August 3, 2026).

Confirmed == Description / Deskripsi == Provides an exhaustive assessment of global maritime security and crime trends from 2015 to the present, examining structural evolutions such as the post-2024 piracy resurgence (137 global incidents in 2025), the exponential expansion of the opaquely owned "Shadow Fleet" (1,300–1,481 active vessels financing state-backed conflict), Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb between 2024 and 2025, reaching 137 reported incidents characterized by low-level opportunistic boardings and increased firearm carriage in strategic chokepoints like the Singapore Straits. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-002]]: The proliferation of a parallel "Shadow Fleet" (1,300–1,481 aging, unrated tankers) operating outside international regulations enables systemic sanctions evasion, generating billions in state revenues while introducing severe marine pollution and environmental disaster risks. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-003]]: Kinetic non-state attacks in the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb Strait have forced commercial shipping diversions around the Cape of Good Hope, expanding global ton-mile demand by 6%, driving freight rate volatility, and threatening global supply chain inflation. == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-001]]: Regional maritime security in Southeast Asian chokepoints (SOMS) is maintained through coordinated law enforcement operations, such as Indonesian Marine Police interventions that dismantled active pirate syndicates in mid-2025. == Japanese Practice / Praktik Jepang == * [[JPAIS-MED-JP-001]]: Advanced maritime nations collaborate through international naval deployments, maritime domain awareness (MDA) sharing, and rigorous compliance verification mechanisms to secure vital sea lines of communication. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-001]]: Limitations in coastal state maritime domain awareness (MDA), unflagged or fraudulently flagged vessel registrations (Flags of Convenience), and unrated P&I insurance gaps that complicate high-seas enforcement against shadow fleets. * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-002]]: Absence of mandatory multi-agency verification frameworks for vessel insurance and ownership transparency across primary international trade corridors. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Establish mandatory insurance verification frameworks for commercial tankers transiting strategic straits, enforce stateless and fraudulent vessel interdiction protocols under UNCLOS, expand multilateral naval escorts and maritime domain awareness in high-risk chokepoints, integrate AI-driven container inspection at major container ports, and establish regional coastal state environmental liability funds. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-001]]: Implement mandatory P&I insurance verification for vessels transiting strategic regional chokepoints (e.g., Malacca and Singapore Straits). * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-002]]: Deploy AI-driven container inspection and cargo anomaly detection systems across primary domestic and regional container terminals. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-003]]: Expand public-private satellite AIS and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) monitoring to detect IUU fishing and dark shadow fleet transfers within national EEZs. == Pilot / Pilot Proyek == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-017]]: 90-day regional maritime security and shadow fleet monitoring pilot across the Straits of Malacca and Singapore (SOMS) approach corridors. == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-017]]: 100% verification compliance of transiting commercial tanker insurance credentials; $\ge 90\%$ reduction in undetected dark vessel transfers within pilot EEZ sectors; zero uninspected high-risk container imports in pilot ports. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Promulgate regional and national maritime security directives enhancing cooperative domain awareness, port state controls, and high-seas interdiction protocols. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Strengthen national maritime laws and port state control regulations to enforce compliance with IMO Assembly Resolution A.1192(33) regarding deceptive shadow fleet operations and unrated marine insurance. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * Global maritime crime incidents rose to 137 in 2025 (up from 116 in 2024), with the Singapore Straits accounting for 80 incidents (58% of global totals). * The active shadow fleet comprises 1,300 to 1,481 aging vessels, delivering 2.6 million barrels per day of sanctioned crude to China and financing major state defense budgets. == Related Entities / phenomenon, where capturing navies release armed suspects due to legislative omissions, human rights constraints, and high logistical costs[cite: 2]. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-006]]: Opaque corporate Ocean Affairs, and the Penal Code (KUHP) through multi-agency commands including BAKAMLA, KKP, and TNI-AL, though inter-agency operational overlaps persist[cite: 4]. == Japanese & Comparative Practice ultimate beneficial ownership[cite: 2]. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-004]]: Implement standardized regional transfer agreements supported by international judicial capacity-building[cite: 2]. gathering and authenticating digital evidence (AIS, VMS, SAR imagery, body-worn cameras) across common law and civil law jurisdictions. == Pilot / Pilot Proyek == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-020]]: 120-day regional harmonization pilot for digital evidence admissibility and port state verification across strategic maritime transit corridors[cite: 2]. == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * uninspected high-risk vessels entering participating port states[cite: 2]. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Promulgate cohesive national and multilateral maritime security policies aligning domestic penal codes with extraterritorial treaty obligations under UNTOC, SUA, and UNCLOS[cite: 2]. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Strengthen domestic statutory frameworks and port state control regulations to mandate ultimate beneficial ownership transparency and suppress shadow fleet operations[cite: 2]. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * UNCLOS Article 101 restricts piracy to high-seas two-ship scenarios, leaving territorial waters exposed to armed robbery[cite: 4]. * Over 1,300 to 1,481 active shadow fleet vessels operate globally outside regulatory frameworks, Entity ID: JPAIS-MED-REF-021 * Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa * Ingestion Status: Confirmed == Description / Deskripsi == Analyzes the codified governance of the global maritime domain under the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), the partition of ocean space into distinct jurisdictional zones (Internal Waters, Territorial Sea, Contiguous Zone, EEZ, Continental Shelf, and High Seas), typologies of maritime jurisdiction (Flag State, Coastal State, Port State, Universal, and Concurrent), and legal mechanisms for interstate criminal cooperation including the SUA Convention, *aut dedere aut judicare*, mutual legal assistance, and joint investigation frameworks. == Problem / Masalah == * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-007]]: Illicit actors exploit spatial boundaries and jurisdictional gaps between coastal State sovereignty and flag State high-seas exclusivity to evade interdiction. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-008]]: Traditional definitions of piracy under UNCLOS Article 101 impose restrictive cumulative criteria—requiring private ends, a two-ship scenario, and location on the high seas—which exclude single-ship mutinies, political terrorism, and armed robbery in territorial waters. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-009]]: Concurrent jurisdictional claims from multiple sovereign states create legal friction and require structured priority rules or extradition mechanisms. == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-021]]: Indonesia exercises absolute sovereignty over internal and archipelagic waters while navigating cooperative frameworks across regional straits for transboundary crime suppression. == Japanese & Comparative Practice / Praktik Perbandingan == * [[JPAIS-MED-JP-021]]: Global maritime nations utilize specialized bilateral shiprider agreements, port state control inspections under IMO conventions, and regional patrols to harmonize enforcement across boundaries. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-004]]: Disparities in domestic penal legislation, long-term detention capacity, and human rights safeguards (such as *non-refoulement* and prohibitions against sub-standard shipboard detention) complicate the prosecution and transfer of interdicted maritime offenders. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Adopt robust multilateral cooperation instruments, implement the 2005 SUA Protocols, streamline mutual legal assistance (MLA) workflows, and establish standardized regional prisoner transfer frameworks in alignment with international human rights standards. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-007]]: Operationalize bilateral shiprider agreements to enable seamless joint maritime law enforcement within overlapping EEZs. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-008]]: Harmonize domestic statutory definitions of maritime terrorism and transnational organized crime with the SUA Convention and UNTOC. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-009]]: Ensure all maritime interdictions and detentions strictly adhere to procedural due process and human rights obligations under international jurisprudence. == Pilot / Pilot Proyek == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-021]]: Implementation of a regional joint operational protocol for fast-track evidence sharing and mutual legal assistance across strategic maritime chokepoints. == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-021]]: 100% compliance with flag state consultation protocols during high-seas boardings; zero procedural challenges in domestic courts regarding maritime chain-of-custody or evidentiary admissibility. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Integration of UNCLOS spatial zoning principles with targeted suppression conventions to eliminate legal safe havens for transnational maritime criminals. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Enactment of comprehensive domestic legislation incorporating extraterritorial enforcement powers, port state control measures, and mandatory *aut dedere aut judicare* mechanisms. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * UNCLOS spatial partitioning successfully reconciles coastal economic rights with traditional high seas freedoms across six distinct zones. * The 2005 SUA Protocols successfully eliminate the two-ship and private ends requirements, providing an effective legal basis for prosecuting maritime terrorism. == Related Entities / Entitas Terkait == * {{JPAIS Relationship|relation=CREATED_BY|target=JPAIS:PERSON:CECEP-MUSTAFA|target_type=Person|label=Ingested and structured by Knowledge Grapher Cecep Mustafa}} * {{JPAIS Summary / Ringkasan == == Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas == * Entity ID: JPAIS-MED-REF-022 * Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa * Ingestion Status: Confirmed == Description / Deskripsi == Provides an exhaustive examination of comprehensive best practices in maritime criminal and casualty investigations, detailing jurisdictional frameworks under UNCLOS, pre-boarding intelligence and risk planning, tactical VBSS execution, BISI/EISI safety inspections, compartmentized vessel search methodologies, environmental and MARPOL evidence sampling, Voyage Data Recorder (VDR) binary extraction and hashing, seafarer human rights under IMO Resolution LEG.7(112), and unbroken chain of custody management. == Problem / Masalah == * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-010]]: Procedural errors during initial maritime boardings, crime scene isolation, or evidence recovery can permanently compromise judicial admissibility in shore-based courts. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-011]]: Volatile bridge audio and sensor data on Voyage Data Recorders (VDR) continuously overwrite older loops, risking the permanent loss of critical investigative evidence if emergency save mechanisms are delayed. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-012]]: Maritime environments expose crime scenes to salt spray, humidity, and soot, rapidly degrading trace biological and physical evidence unless immediate protective enclosures are established. == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-022]]: Multi-agency maritime enforcement units coordinate interdictions and shipboard inspections, requiring standardized protocols for digital forensics and evidence continuity. == Japanese & Comparative Practice / Praktik Perbandingan == * [[JPAIS-MED-JP-022]]: Advanced maritime jurisdictions deploy specialized boarding teams equipped with digital hashing tools and structured sector search grids to secure conviction-ready evidentiary packages. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-005]]: Inconsistent handling of chain-of-custody logs and failure to calculate cryptographic hashes (SHA-256) during digital extractions leave electronic evidence vulnerable to defense challenges regarding tampering. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Standardize end-to-end maritime investigation workflows across seven distinct phases—from pre-boarding intelligence to judicial handover—incorporating rigorous TFMA digital categorization and seafarer fair treatment protections. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-010]]: Mandate immediate activation of VDR emergency save functions and raw binary extraction using SHA-256 hashing protocols. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-011]]: Enforce strict sectorized search methodologies and IMO Resolution A.1091(28) crime scene containment guidelines. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-012]]: Maintain master evidence ledgers and dual-signature transfer manifests to guarantee an unbroken chain of custody. == Pilot / Pilot Proyek == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-022]]: 90-day specialized training program for maritime boarding officers focusing on advanced digital forensics, MARPOL oil sampling, and human rights compliance under IMO Resolution LEG.7(112). == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-022]]: 100% adherence to chain-of-custody documentation standards; zero evidentiary rejections in court due to digital corruption or mishandling; complete compliance with seafarer fair treatment guidelines. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Adoption of harmonized national guidelines for maritime crime scene management and digital evidence preservation aligned with UNODC and IMO frameworks. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Strengthening statutory provisions requiring mandatory VDR data preservation and standardized evidentiary reporting following maritime casualties or criminal allegations. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * Structured sector searches and BISI/EISI safety protocols significantly reduce tactical boarding risks and uncover hidden contraband compartments. * Cryptographic hash verification proves data integrity for digital extractions from VDR and ECDIS systems. == Related Entities / Entitas Terkait == * {{JPAIS handling exposes electronic records to suppression based on spoliation or lack of authentication. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-015]]: Historical judicial misapplications of expert testimony standards allowed expert overstatement and improper delegation of gatekeeping duties to juries. == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-023]]: Public prosecutors evaluate case files (berkas perkara) from investigators to ensure formal and material completeness before initiating judicial proceedings. == Japanese & Comparative Practice / Praktik Perbandingan == * [[JPAIS-MED-JP-023]]: Advanced jurisdictions implement strict prosecutorial discretion guidelines, rigorous pre-trial discovery mandates, and active judicial gatekeeping for expert evidence. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-006]]: Inadequate vetting of expert methodologies and unverified digital chain-of-custody protocols undermine conviction integrity in complex transnational trials. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Implement a standardized prosecutorial execution framework spanning charging discretion, duplicity/multiplicity checks, continuous discovery compliance, active FRE 702 gatekeeping, and structured OIA/MLAT international cooperation. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-013]]: Apply the two-step charging discretion model to verify probable cause and substantial federal interest before filing charges. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-014]]: Audit all digital evidence workflows against ISO/IEC 27037 identification, collection, acquisition, and preservation standards. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-015]]: Enforce amended FRE 702 preponderance standards, requiring proponents to establish expert reliability across all four statutory criteria. == Pilot / Pilot Proyek == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-023]]: 180-day prosecutor training initiative focusing on advanced digital evidence handling, FRE 702 methodological vetting, and complex indictment review workflows. == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-023]]: 100% compliance with *Brady*/*Giglio* continuous disclosure mandates; zero indictments dismissed for duplicity or multiplicity; 100% expert witness compliance with reliable application bounds under FRE 702(d). == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Institutionalization of rigorous internal review protocols (such as OCRS for RICO) and comprehensive departmental disclosure policies exceeding constitutional minimums. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Adoption of standardized statutory pleading rules and mandatory pre-trial evidentiary gatekeeping mechanisms for specialized scientific and technical testimony. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * Plea bargaining resolves 90 to 95 percent of federal criminal cases, requiring strict supervisory approval frameworks for specialized plea structures like *Alford* or *nolo contendere* pleas[cite: 4, 5]. * Amended FRE 702 successfully eliminates expert overstatement by enforcing an active judicial gatekeeping role under a preponderance of the evidence standard. == Related Entities / Entitas Terkait == * {{JPAIS gathering and judicial chain-of-custody protocols undermine successful prosecutions of transnational maritime criminals[cite: 6]. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Operationalize the evidentiary protocols[cite: 6]. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-018]]: Prioritize funding for non-cooperative tracking assets, including space-borne Synthetic Aperture Radar and commercial radio frequency evidentiary chain-of-custody gaps; measurable increase in successful judicial prosecutions resulting from intelligence-led interdictions[cite: 6]. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakanلاء == exercising adjudicative authority[cite: 7]. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-020]]: Environmental crimes involving oil pollution face defense challenges contending that hydrocarbons originated from urban runoff or natural seeps, requiring complex chemical fingerprinting to disprove[cite: 7]. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-021]]: Multi-jurisdictional shell companies and single-vessel special purpose vehicles registered under flags of convenience attempt to insulate beneficial owners from criminal exposure and civil liabilities[cite: 7]. == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * and biophysical HEA metrics to quantify marine ecological damages[cite: 7]. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-008]]: Traditional tort theories based on market property values fail to account for lost ecosystem services, complicating judicial quantification of environmental harm[cite: 7]. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Adopt a structured six-phase trial framework—spanning jurisdictional verification, evidence admissibility, scientific fact-finding, liability attribution, environmental remediation valuation via HEA, and prompt release balancing—to guide judicial decision-making in maritime crime[cite: 7]. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-019]]: Require multi-sensor data fusion and SHA-256 cryptographic hashing to verify digital tracking and navigation evidence[cite: 7]. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-020]]: Apply refractory biomarker diagnostic ratios (GC-MS) and stable isotope profiling (IRMS) to establish definitive pollution source attribution[cite: 7]. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-021]]: Utilize Habitat Equivalency Analysis (HEA) to calculate biophysical debits and scale compensatory ecological restoration orders[cite: 7]. == Pilot / Pilot Proyek == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-025]]: 120-day judicial training workshop on environmental forensics, HEA modeling, and ITLOS prompt release bond calculations for maritime judges[cite: 7]. == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-025]]: 100% judicial compliance with UNCLOS spatial zoning verification standards; zero unverified digital chain-of-custody admissions; precise biophysical scaling of all environmental restoration judgments[cite: 7]. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Harmonization of judicial approaches across regional maritime courts to ensure consistent application of international law of the sea standards and environmental accountability[cite: 7]. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Adoption of standardized forensic protocols for oil spill sampling (EN 15522) and corporate transparency mandates targeting beneficial ownership behind flags of convenience[cite: 7]. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * Stable carbon isotope ratios (IRMS) remain conserved during physical weathering processes, providing high-probability proof of origin even when 80% of spilled fuel has evaporated[cite: 7]. * Habitat Equivalency Analysis successfully replaces speculative monetary valuations with biophysical service-acre-year metrics[cite: 7]. == Related Entities / Entitas Terkait == * {{JPAIS It categorizes simulation designs into operational archetypes (systemic chain-of-justice simulations, adversarial micro-simulations, and appellate moots), evaluates adult learning frameworks including the Hampel Method and NITA experiential cycles, and details competency assessment rubrics[cite: 8]. == Problem / Masalah == * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-022]]: Traditional legal education relied heavily on anecdotal, lecture-based pedagogy rather than structured experiential learning, leaving practitioners unprepared for complex courtroom dynamics[cite: 8]. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-023]]: High-level courtroom advocacy is rendered ineffective if the underlying multi-agency investigative chain, intelligence gathering, or evidence handling is compromised[cite: 8]. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-024]]: Institutional divergences between active "hot bench" moot interrogations and formal judicial restraint complicate the realistic training of judges and advocates[cite: 8]. == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-026]]: Indonesian judicial and prosecutorial training incorporates case-based discussions and simulation modules to bridge investigative protocols with courtroom adjudication[cite: 8]. == Japanese & Comparative Practice / Praktik Perbandingan == * [[JPAIS-MED-JP-026]]: Leading institutions like the Singapore Judicial College utilize continuous career-long developmental tracks and 360-degree peer feedback to cultivate the "Learning Judge"[cite: 8]. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-009]]: Isolated trial advocacy training frequently fails to address systemic inter-agency operational gaps across the criminal justice chain[cite: 8]. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Adopt a diversified simulation architecture that aligns scenario scope with operational goals—utilizing NITA micro-performances for advocate mechanics, Hampel Method instruction for international tribunals, and UNODC multi-agency simulations for systemic chain-of-justice stress-testing[cite: 8]. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-022]]: Implement the NITA four-component critique formula (Headline, Playback, Fix, Rationale) during practical advocacy training[cite: 8]. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-023]]: Structure multi-agency operational simulations spanning the entire legal continuum from maritime interdiction to judicial trial[cite: 8]. * interscholastic simulation involving the M/V Pacific Dragon casualty[cite: 9]. == Problem / Masalah == * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-025]]: Admiralty litigation differs fundamentally from general civil litigation due to complex jurisdictional mechanisms, historical absence of jury trials in *in rem* proceedings, and statutory exceptions like the Saving to Suitors clause[cite: 9]. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-026]]: Modern maritime disputes require advocates to master both complex legal doctrines and digital marine forensics (AIS, VDR, ARPA radar), creating a dual-literacy demand that traditional legal curricula often fail to address[cite: 9]. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-027]]: Procedural friction between federal admiralty limitation injunctions (Supplemental Rule F) and state court personal injury claims demands sophisticated multi-forum strategic agility[cite: 9]. == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-027]]: Indonesian maritime legal education integrates statutory shipping regulations with practical navigation and casualty investigation standards to prepare practitioners for commercial admiralty disputes[cite: 9]. == Japanese & Comparative Practice / Praktik Perbandingan == * [[JPAIS-MED-JP-027]]: Advanced maritime legal training programs deploy experiential learning models combining technical navigation labs, expert witness management, and appellate moot court competitions[cite: 9]. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-008]]: Traditional law school curricula rarely provide structured, experiential training on laying evidentiary foundations for electronic marine telemetry and navigating technical expert testimonies under FRE 702[cite: 9]. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Implement a seven-module experiential curriculum spanning admiralty jurisdiction, personal injury, COGSA cargo carriage, Rule F limitation petitions, COLREGS collision forensics, expert witness management, and interscholastic appellate advocacy[cite: 9]. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-025]]: Integrate digital navigation and forensic labs into advocacy training, focusing on AIS telemetry, VDR audio authentication, and electronic chart plotting[cite: 9]. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-026]]: Execute simulated courtroom practicums and problem-based learning exercises modeled on complex historical maritime casualties[cite: 9]. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-027]]: Conclude training with a multi-stage capstone simulation (The M/V Pacific Dragon Casualty) combining trial advocacy and Supreme Court-formatted appellate argument[cite: 9]. == Pilot / Pilot Proyek == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-027]]: 14-week intensive maritime advocacy clinic incorporating technical navigation data labs, bench mooting workshops, and interscholastic competition preparation[cite: 9]. == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-027]]: 100% student proficiency in laying evidentiary foundations for digital marine telemetry; successful execution of complex limitation of liability and COGSA trial arguments[cite: 9]. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Advancement of specialized maritime legal education standards, aligning academic advocacy training with national competition requirements like the Judge John R. Brown Admiralty Moot Court Competition[cite: 9]. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Standardization of procedural rules governing multi-forum admiralty litigation, electronic evidence admissibility, and marine casualty investigations[cite: 9]. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * Experiential problem-based learning combined with technical navigation labs bridges the gap between theoretical admiralty law and high-stakes courtroom execution[cite: 9]. * Standardized 100-point rubric scoring and statistical scaling successfully eliminate grading variance in national appellate brief evaluations[cite: 9]. == Related Entities / Entitas Terkait == * {{JPAIS Relationship|relation=CREATED_BY|target=JPAIS:PERSON:CECEP-MUSTAFA|target_type=Person|label=Ingested and structured by high-value smuggling and security threats[cite: 10]. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-029]]: Prosecuting maritime offenses requires establishing precise legal foundations across diverse treaty frameworks, including UNCLOS Article 110, the SUA Convention, and MARPOL[cite: 10]. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-030]]: Complex evidence chains—ranging from digital GPS tracks and OWS electronic logs to cryptographic telemetry and contraband and prosecute offenders[cite: 10]. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-009]]: Gaps in flag state verification speed and coordination during high-seas interdictions risk allowing suspect vessels to scuttle or evade jurisdiction before boarding authorization is secured[cite: 10]. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Implement standardized operational case files and prosecutorial briefs across ten maritime crime domains, ensuring rigorous alignment with UNCLOS, SUA, and MARPOL enforcement standards[cite: 10]. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-028]]: Apply UNCLOS Article 110 right of visit and stateless vessel verification procedures during high-seas interdictions[cite: 10]. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-029]]: Enforce port state jurisdiction under UNCLOS Article 218 and MARPOL Annex I to prosecute oil record book fraud and OWS bypasses[cite: 10]. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-030]]: Integrate financial intelligence and corporate registry audits to dismantle front companies and trace ultimate beneficial ownership in sanctions and wildlife trafficking cases[cite: 10]. == Pilot / Pilot Proyek == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-028]]: 180-day multi-agency operational pilot deploying container risk-profiling algorithms and accelerated SUA flag-verification channels across regional transshipment hubs[cite: 10]. == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-028]]: interdictions[cite: 10]. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Harmonization of national prosecutorial strategies with international maritime law enforcement standards, ensuring robust legal finishes for complex maritime criminal cases[cite: 10]. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Strengthening domestic penal legislation to incorporate stateless vessel jurisdiction, universal suppression mandates under the SUA Convention, and strict port state controls[cite: 10]. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * Ten comprehensive case scenarios demonstrate the practical Provides an operational manual for designing, executing, and evaluating courtroom simulations, integrating spatial zoning and sightline geometry for judicial benches, bar tables, and witness stands, role-specific operational mandates, standardized time governance and evidentiary frameworks, media access protocols, and multi-factor performance evaluation architectures. == Problem / Masalah == * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-031]]: Immersive legal simulations require balancing realistic spatial design, procedural rigor, precise role definitions, and structured pedagogical evaluation to bridge theoretical jurisprudence with trial practice. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-032]]: Without standardized time management and clear evidentiary boundaries, courtroom simulations risk devolving into unstructured debates. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-033]]: Uncontrolled media access or improper participant decorum compromises trial fairness, witness integrity, and institutional simulation realism. == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-029]]: Indonesian judicial and advocacy training programs incorporate structured courtroom simulations and practical trial exercises to test evidentiary rules and procedural compliance. == Japanese & Comparative Practice / Praktik Perbandingan == * [[JPAIS-MED-JP-029]]: Leading international judicial colleges and training centers enforce strict spatial hierarchies, technological integration, and multi-factor grading rubrics during trial simulations. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-010]]: Informal or ad-hoc simulation planning often lacks standardized courtroom spatial zoning, rigorous time governance, and multi-dimensional evaluation rubrics. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Adopt a standardized courtroom simulation operations manual establishing precise architectural layouts, role mandates, time allocations, simplified evidence rules, media standing orders, and a four-phase debriefing framework. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-031]]: Configure simulated courtrooms with strict spatial segregation of judicial benches, bar tables, witness stands, and jury boxes. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-032]]: Enforce explicit time allocations and countdown timers across opening statements, cases-in-chief, and closing arguments. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-033]]: Execute a four-phase pedagogical debriefing immediately following trials to provide recursive feedback and systemic reflection. == Pilot / Pilot Proyek == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-029]]: 90-day institutional trial simulation pilot utilizing the operational manual's spatial zoning, countdown time governance, and 100-point multi-factor evaluation matrix. == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-029]]: 100% adherence to trial time allotments and media standing orders; zero spatial or decorum breaches; comprehensive completion of multi-factor evaluation rubrics. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Standardization of immersive simulation protocols across judicial training academies and advocacy clinical programs. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Adoption of formal media standing orders, administrative contempt enforcement rules, and expert qualification *voir dire* protocols within simulated court environments. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * Structured courtroom simulations bridge theoretical jurisprudence and practical trial advocacy, enabling participants to master statutory application and evidentiary mechanics. * Multi-factor evaluation rubrics and four-phase debriefing sessions transform experiential exercises into measurable competency-based learning. == Related Entities / Entitas Terkait == * {{JPAIS Grapher: Cecep Mustafa * Ingestion Status: Confirmed == Description / Deskripsi == Provides an exhaustive legal analysis of Indonesia's maritime security regime, evaluating structural, statutory, and institutional dynamics under Law No. 1 of 2023 (New KUHP), Constitutional Court Decision No. 15/PUU-XIX/2021, and sector-specific legislation. It examines international treaty compliance (UNCLOS, UNTOC, SUA), institutional coordination challenges between Bakamla, TNI AL, PSDKP KKP, Polairud, and KPLP, and outlines a legislative reform roadmap featuring the proposed Maritime Security Bill (*RUU Keamanan Laut*). == Problem / Masalah == * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-034]]: Co-existence of multiple agencies with overlapping mandates under Law No. 17 of 2008 on Shipping and Law No. 32 of 2014 on Maritime Affairs creates institutional friction that compromises state efficacy at sea. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-035]]: Bakamla lacks independent prosecution and comprehensive investigative authority under Law No. 32 of 2014, limiting its enforcement capacity despite its role as central patrol coordinator under PP No. 13 of 2022. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-036]]: Transnational syndicates exploit regulatory fragmentation and short investigation windows to execute IUU fishing, maritime smuggling, and environmental crimes. == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-030]]: Indonesia enforces maritime security through a fragmented multi-agency model involving Bakamla, TNI AL, Polairud, PSDKP KKP, KPLP, and Customs, recently modernized by the New KUHP and Constitutional Court asset recovery expansions. == Japanese & Comparative Practice / Praktik Perbandingan == * [[JPAIS-MED-JP-030]]: Unified coast guard models in Australia, Malaysia, and the United States consolidate civilian maritime law enforcement under a single agency to eliminate jurisdictional overlaps. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-011]]: Horizontal conflicts of norms between shipping and maritime affairs statutes prevent the realization of a cohesive single-agency multi-task enforcement framework. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Transition from a fragmented multi-agency model to a cohesive single-agency multi-task framework via the promulgation of the Maritime Security Bill (*RUU Keamanan Laut*), granting Bakamla autonomous investigative and prosecutive powers. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-034]]: Promulgate the Maritime Security Bill to establish Bakamla as the sole national coast guard and amalgamate KPLP assets. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-035]]: Operationalize PP No. 13 of 2022 and integrate financial intelligence networks following Constitutional Court Decision No. 15/PUU-XIX/2021. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-036]]: Establish an integrated National Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA) platform consolidating satellite AIS/VMS tracking and coastal radar feeds. == Pilot / Pilot Proyek == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-030]]: 120-year transitional integration pilot for regional maritime intelligence fusion centers and joint investigative teams targeting maritime money laundering. == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-030]]: Reduction of regulatory fragmentation factor ($R_f$) in the enforcement efficiency index; 100% inter-agency data sharing across maritime fusion nodes; increased successful prosecutions of corporate beneficial owners. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Harmonization of national maritime security policy through statutory consolidation, eliminating horizontal norm conflicts and strengthening state sovereignty in strategic sea lines of communication. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Enactment of the Maritime Security Bill and harmonization of criminal procedure codes to extend investigation windows for complex corporate and financial maritime crimes. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * Landmark case law, including *State v. Yotin Kuarabiab (MV Silver Sea 2)* and Constitutional Court Decision No. 15/PUU-XIX/2021, demonstrates the legal efficacy of DNA species profiling and PPNS money laundering investigations. * Mathematical modeling of the enforcement efficiency index ($E_{eff}$) proves that regulatory fragmentation ($R_f$) directly degrades operational outcomes regardless of operational capacity ($O_c$). == The imbalance between high certified judge capacity (6 judges) and extremely low case volume (1 case/6 years), compounded by under-optimized cross-island e-Court utilization. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Establish the Makassar Commercial Court as an Eastern Indonesia e-Court Digital Hub for KPPU objection trials and reform qualitative DIM reporting instruments. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-042]]: Drafting e-Court accessibility technical guidelines specifically for cross-island competition law cases in Eastern Indonesia. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-043]]: Regular training and economic evidence "hot-tubbing" simulations for the 6 Makassar commercial judges in collaboration with BSDK Mahkamah Agung RI. == Pilot / Pilot Proyek == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-031]]: Implementation of the Makassar Commercial Court as a Digital Hub for Business Competition Dispute Services in Eastern Indonesia. == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-033]]: 100% electronic trial processing (*e-Court*) for KPPU objection cases; dispute resolution duration $\le 60$ working days in alignment with national reform standards. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Optimization of mandatory full electronic trial provisions to reduce litigation costs for regional enterprises and enhance data synchronization between KPPU Regional Office VI Makassar and the court registry. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Refinement of Supreme Court DIM reporting mechanisms to map access-to-justice barriers objectively, even when real-time case data indicates This page records the empirical analysis of official judicial statistics and the Problem Inventory List (Daftar Inventaris Masalah / DIM) for business competition objection cases (Komisi Pengawas Persaingan Usaha / KPPU) at the Makassar Commercial Court at the Makassar District Court, covering the reporting period from 2021 through 2026. The primary dataset reveals a sustained administrative readiness—maintaining a specialized panel of 6 (six) certified competition law judges annually—contrasted with an extraordinarily low litigation density, recording only 1 (one) objection case across the entire 6-year period. The official DIM document dated 10 July 2026, signed by Court Leadership and the Registrar, officially records a status of "Nihil" (Nil). All structural entities, numerical records, and signatories have been ingested into the Knowledge Graph under the direction of Knowledge Grapher '''Cecep Mustafa'''. == Problem / Masalah == * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-034]]: Resource Over-Allocation vs. Low Caseload Density, where maintaining 6 specialized competition law judges continuously over 6 years to handle a single case (Case No. 1/Pdt.Sus-KPPU/2024/PN Niaga Mks) represents a severe imbalance in judicial workload distribution compared to high-density commercial courts. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-035]]: Geographic Disincentive & Access Barriers, where the near-absence of objection filings across Eastern Indonesia reflects significant geographic and logistical cost barriers for local business actors traveling to Makassar to challenge KPPU administrative sanctions. == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-034]]: The Makassar Commercial Court fulfills formal statutory requirements by maintaining a dedicated judicial roster of 6 certified judges, successfully adjudicating Case No. 1/Pdt.Sus-KPPU/2024/PN Niaga Mks to completion by issuing a judgment rejecting the objection without Supreme Court cassation escalation, while submitting periodic DIM reports recording procedural obstacles as "Nihil". == Japanese & Comparative Practice / Praktik Perbandingan == * [[JPAIS-MED-JP-034]]: In Japan (Tokyo High Court / JFTC), the court utilizes fully integrated electronic hearings (*online proceedings*) and circuit hearings to prevent geographic disincentives for business actors located in distant prefectures (e.g., Hokkaido or Okinawa), ensuring equitable access without requiring physical presence. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-034]]: The primary structural gap is the absence of an integrated digital filing incentive under PERMA No. 3/2021 tailored to regional commercial courts, where current reliance on physical court presence discourages regional enterprises from exercising their statutory right to judicial review. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Transform the Makassar Commercial Court into a specialized *e-Court Digital Center* for competition review across Eastern Indonesia and implement a flexible judicial deployment model where certified judges in low-density courts can be assigned virtually to support high-density commercial courts via cross-court electronic panels. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-034]]: Issue a Supreme Court Circular (SEMA) establishing full digital trial options for competition cases in regional Commercial Courts. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-035]]: Integrate cross-jurisdictional virtual judicial panels within the SIPP/e-Court architecture under BSDK oversight. == Pilot / Pilot Proyek == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-034]]: Implementation of the Makassar Commercial Court as a Digital Hub for Business Competition Dispute Services in Eastern Indonesia. == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-034]]: 100% adoption of electronic filing (*e-Court*) and remote evidentiary hearings for regional KPPU objections; dispute resolution duration $\le 60$ working days per case. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Re-evaluating judicial certification quotas based on empirical caseload density rather than static court status, alongside optimizing mandatory full electronic trial provisions to reduce litigation costs for regional enterprises. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Amending PERMA No. 3/2021 to explicitly mandate virtual trials for parties residing outside the physical seat of regional Commercial Courts and refining Supreme Court DIM reporting mechanisms. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * Official DIM document dated July 10, 2026, signed by the Chief Judge of Makassar District Court (Dr. I Wayan Gede Rumega, S.H., M.H.) and Registrar (Handri Mamudi, S.H., M.H.), combined with registration records for Case No. Summary / Ringkasan == == Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas == * Entity ID: JPAIS-MED-REF-035 * Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa * Ingestion Status: Confirmed == Description / Deskripsi == This page records the empirical analysis of official judicial statistics and the Problem Inventory List (Daftar Inventaris Masalah / DIM) for business competition objection cases (Komisi Pengawas Persaingan Usaha / KPPU) at the Semarang Commercial Court at the Semarang District Court, covering the reporting period from 2021 through 2026. The dataset presents a notable structural dynamic: while recording 0 (zero) incoming objection cases across the entire 6-year period, the court maintained a significant roster of certified competition law judges—peaking at 14 judges in 2021, readjusting to 5 judges between 2023 and 2025, and expanding to 8 certified judges in 2026. Furthermore, the accompanying DIM highlights critical technical-juridical bottlenecks in competition enforcement, including the lack of direct execution power, evidentiary barriers regarding digital data and indirect evidence, and the strict evidence lock under PERMA No. 3/2021. All structural entities and numerical data have been ingested into the Knowledge Graph under the direction of Knowledge Grapher '''Cecep Mustafa'''. == Problem / Masalah == * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-035]]: Resource Readjustment & Human Capital Imbalance, where maintaining a high allocation of certified judges (14 judges in 2021, stabilizing at 5–8 judges through 2026) alongside zero registered objection filings over six consecutive years reflects a structural misalignment in judicial resource allocation between regional Commercial Courts. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-036]]: Evidentiary & Structural Friction, where the comprehensive DIM submitted by the court emphasizes severe systemic gaps—including KPPU's lack of direct execution power (*irah-irah*), absence of subpoena powers during investigation, and the rigid prohibition against submitting new evidence (*novum*) at the Commercial Court level. == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-035]]: The Semarang Commercial Court maintains formal institutional readiness by ensuring a roster of 5 to 8 certified competition judges annually, processing objections against KPPU decisions strictly on the administrative record (*dossier*) within 14 days under PERMA No. 3/2021 without a mediation phase, while fine execution remains reliant on civil execution procedures through District Courts. == Japanese & Comparative Practice / Praktik Perbandingan == * [[JPAIS-MED-JP-035]]: In Japan (Tokyo High Court / JFTC), judicial review of Japan Fair Trade Commission decisions is concentrated in specialized panels at the Tokyo High Court, utilizing economic experts and a flexible evidentiary standard (*rule of reason* evaluation) rather than rigid civil evidence locks. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-035]]: The primary gap lies in the rigid application of the evidence lock (*Pasal 13 PERMA No. 3/2021*) and the 14-day statutory limit, which severely restricts business actors from submitting comprehensive economic counter-analyses when appealing KPPU decisions. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Enable certified judges stationed at low-caseload courts like Semarang to participate in virtual judicial panels (*e-Court*) supporting high-caseload centers like Central Jakarta, and modify PERMA No. 3/2021 to allow limited new documentary and expert economic evidence when KPPU decisions introduce novel market definitions or penalty calculations. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-035]]: Issue a Supreme Court Circular (SEMA) standardizing the definition of working days for objection filings and establishing guidelines for evaluating indirect economic evidence. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-036]]: Amend PERMA No. 3/2021 to incorporate specialized economic evidence procedures (*Hot Tubbing* expert testimony and confidential *Data Room* mechanisms). == Pilot Proyek / Pilot Projections == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-035]]: Semarang Commercial Court (Central Java Judicial Region) integration into the national virtual judicial pool via *e-Court*. == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-035]]: 100% integration of Semarang's certified competition judges into the national virtual judicial pool via *e-Court*; dispute resolution duration $\le 60$ working days per case upon docket entry. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Amending Law No. 5/1999 to clarify statutory phrases ("dapat mengakibatkan") and grant explicit direct execution mechanisms for KPPU administrative fines. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Establishing clear procedural rules for digital evidence and algorithmic market manipulation under updated Supreme Court regulations, alongside relaxing the evidence lock in PERMA No. 3/2021. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * Official caseload and DIM report document from Semarang Commercial Court (*data statistik KPPU_Pn_Niaga_Semarang.pdf*) covering the reporting period 2021–2026. == Related Entities / Entitas Inventaris Masalah / DIM) for business competition objection cases (Komisi Pengawas Persaingan Usaha / KPPU) at the Surabaya Commercial Court at the Surabaya District Court, covering the reporting period from 2021 through 2026. The primary dataset demonstrates an active judicial docket, recording three major objection cases (Case No. 1/Pdt.Sus-KPPU/2021/PN Sby, Case No. 1/Pdt.Sus-KPPU/2022/PN Sby, and Case No. 1/Pdt.Sus-KPPU/2025/PN Sby) with all three resulting in judgments favoring the petitioners in whole or in part (*dikabulkan / dikabulkan sebagian*). The accompanying DIM focuses on jurisdictional conflicts between KPPU and public procurement oversight bodies (LKPP, APIP, BPKP, PTUN) regarding specialized high-tech infrastructure procurement, taking the Gili Trawangan seawater desalination project as a central case study. All statistical entries, case records, judicial panel members, and issue inventories have been ingested into the Knowledge Graph under the direction of Knowledge Grapher '''Cecep Mustafa'''. == Problem / Masalah == * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-036]]: High Petitioner Success Rate, where in 100% of recorded objection cases (3 out of 3 cases between 2021 and 2026), the Surabaya Commercial Court overturned or modified KPPU's administrative decisions, underscoring intense judicial scrutiny of KPPU's evidentiary findings and market definitions. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-037]]: Overlapping Jurisdictional Friction in Specialized Procurement, highlighting a severe regulatory clash between KPPU's anti-monopoly mandates under Article 22 & Article 50 of Law No. 5/1999 and the authority of procurement officials (PPK, PA/KPA) and auditors (APIP, BPKP, LKPP) in high-tech, high-investment infrastructure projects. == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-036]]: The Surabaya Commercial Court actively reviews KPPU decisions across diverse economic sectors, maintaining specialized judicial panels composed of senior commercial judges who evaluate public utility concessions under civil procedural rules to determine whether technical specifications constitute legitimate efficiency choices or unlawful competition barriers. == Japanese & Comparative Practice / Praktik Perbandingan == * [[JPAIS-MED-JP-036]]: In Japan (Tokyo High Court / JFTC), public utility and high-tech infrastructure concessions subject to JFTC review are evaluated under formal inter-agency consultation guidelines between JFTC and government procurement agencies, utilizing a broad "rule of reason" test that explicitly factors in technical necessity and capital investment risks. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-036]]: The primary gap lies in the absence of a legal framework for KPPU to coordinate with LKPP/APIP before declaring a specialized direct-appointment procurement illegal, alongside overly narrow geographic market definitions (e.g., restricting the market definition to Gili Trawangan island rather than national specialized desalination capability). == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Establish a formal administrative gateway requiring KPPU to consult APIP/LKPP technical audits before issuing findings of bid-rigging on specialized direct-appointment procurements, and draft clear Supreme Court guidelines defining statutory exemption standards under Article 50 of Law No. 5/1999. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-036]]: Issue a Joint Decree/Circular between Mahkamah Agung, KPPU, and LKPP regulating evidentiary standards for technical procurement objections. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-037]]: Incorporate specialized market definition standards (national vs. localized geographic markets) into the upcoming PERMA Amendment. == Pilot Proyek / Pilot Projections == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-036]]: Surabaya Commercial Court (East Java & NTB Jurisdiction) pilot integration for specialized infrastructure procurement review. == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-036]]: 100% alignment between judicial market definition assessments and economic efficiency standards in infrastructure cases; resolution of objection cases within $\le 60$ working days per statutory standard. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Amending Law No. 5/1999 to provide explicit remedies for upstream procurement adjustments and clarify KPPU's jurisdiction relative to PTUN and APIP, alongside enhancing judicial training for Surabaya Commercial Court judges on complex public utility concessions and econometrics. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Promulgating inter-agency coordination rules between competition authorities and procurement oversight bodies to resolve administrative and judicial conflicts. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * Official court record and Problem Applying Herbert L. Packer's dual model framework (Crime Control vs. Due Process), ICLA identifies 10 formal filing issues, 7 substantive trial issues, and 8 administrative obstacles at the KPPU level. The submission urges the Supreme Court to transition from an administrative "assembly line" review to a comprehensive Due Process Model ("obstacle course"), given that administrative fines under Law No. 11/2020 (Job Creation Law) now reach up to 50% of net profit or 10% of total sales without nominal caps (e.g., SANY Heavy Industry truck cartel fine of Rp 449 billion, Google Play Billing fine of Rp 202 billion, and Fintech/Pinjol cartel fine of Rp 755 billion across 97 business actors). All legal analyses and proposed amendments to PERMA No. 3/2021 have been ingested into the Knowledge Graph under the direction of Knowledge Grapher Cecep Mustafa. == Problem / Masalah == * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-038]]: Strict Evidence Lock (Article 13(5) PERMA No. 3/2021), where prohibiting new documentary, witness, or expert evidence at the Commercial Court level forces judges to act merely as *judex juris* (reviewing administrative dossiers) rather than *judex facti*, preventing business actors from challenging novel market definitions or fine formulas introduced for the first time in KPPU's final decision. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-039]]: Inkracht Fragmentation in Joint Conduct Cases, where under Article 2(4) PERMA No. 3/2021, if only a subset of respondents files an objection, KPPU's decision becomes final and enforceable for non-appealing parties, producing contradictory legal outcomes where a shared contract clause is invalidated for appealing parties but legally binding on non-appealing co-parties in large-scale cartel proceedings. == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-037]]: Under current Supreme Court practice pursuant to PERMA No. 3/2021, objection review is confined to administrative dossiers barring new evidence; filing deadlines (14 days) are strictly enforced based on oral reading of decisions rather than physical receipt of complete copies; bank guarantees are demanded indiscriminately; and judicial review (*Peninjauan Kembali* / PK) is not explicitly regulated despite high-value precedents. == Japanese & Comparative Practice / Praktik Perbandingan == * [[JPAIS-MED-JP-037]]: Comprehensive international comparison across six jurisdictions shows that advanced legal systems—such as the UK Competition Appeal Tribunal (CAT), EU General Court, and Japan High Court—guarantee full merits review, independent economic evaluation, confidentiality rings, data rooms, and unrestricted access to investigative files (*Statement of Objections*). == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-037]]: Indonesia's PERMA No. 3/2021 remains stuck in a hybrid administrative review model lacking international standards of *due process*—specifically missing full merits review, limited evidence lock relaxation, formal access to file (*inzage*), and confidentiality ring mechanisms. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Adopt four foundational amendments to PERMA No. 3/2021: expand judicial review scope to full merits and relevant market definition (Article 13(1)); relax the evidence lock (Article 13(5)) to permit new expert and economic evidence; implement a two-stage filing model (Statement followed by Memory of Objection); and mandate full access to file (*inzage*) alongside confidentiality ring and data room protocols. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-038]]: Issue a Supreme Court Circular (SEMA) harmonizing the definition of "days" to working days, suspending execution against non-appealing co-respondents until final judgment, and exempting non-monetary sanction recipients from bank guarantees. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-039]]: Promulgate the comprehensive PERMA Amendment incorporating ICLA's proposed 8-stage case workflow. == Pilot Proyek / Pilot Projections == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-037]]: Central Jakarta Commercial Court pilot implementation handling major cartel objections (e.g., Fintech/Pinjol 97-party case). == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-037]]: 100% compliance with access to file (*inzage*) prior to substantive hearings; zero procedural dismissals (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard*) caused by relative competence or master case e-Court registration errors; adjudication within $\le 60$ working days. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Amending PERMA No. 3/2021 to explicitly establish Judicial Review (*Peninjauan Kembali* / PK) procedures based on new evidence (*novum*) and manifest error, aligned with Article 67 of Law No. 14/1985, alongside establishing a dedicated legal framework for partnership (*kemitraan*) appeals. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Restructuring administrative review procedures into an equitable adversarial framework that balances KPPU's enforcement authority with robust constitutional due process safeguards. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * Official position paper and policy submission document from the Indonesian Competition Lawyers Association (*ICLA_Permasalahan Praktik HPU di Pengadilan_Agust 2026.pdf*) presented by General Chairman Asep Ridwan, S.H., M.H., on 3
