Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas == * Entity ID: JPAIS-MED-REF-038 * Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa * Ingestion Status: Confirmed == Description / Deskripsi == This page records the empirical research findings and policy recommendations published in the monograph ''"Kewenangan Pengadilan Niaga dalam Mengadili Permohonan Keberatan atas Putusan Komisi Pengawas Persaingan Usaha Tidak Sehat"'' (ISBN 978-623-384-090-3), conducted by the Research and Development Center for Law and Justice (Puslitbang Kumdil MA RI) under lead researchers Dr. Ismail Rumadan, M.H. et al. The study evaluates the shifting of absolute jurisdiction over KPPU objections from District Courts to Commercial Courts pursuant to Article 118 of Law No. 11/2020 (Job Creation Law), PP No. 44/2021, SEMA No. 1/2021, and PERMA No. 3/2021. It identifies a profound procedural impasse caused by forcing a public-administrative enforcement mechanism into a private civil procedural framework (HIR/RBg), proposing the adoption of the United States Federal Trade Commission (FTC) judicial remand doctrine. All legal frameworks and comparative analysis data have been ingested into the Knowledge Graph under the direction of Knowledge Grapher '''Cecep Mustafa'''. == Problem / Masalah == * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-038]]: Eversion of Judex Facti Role & Evidence Lock, where while PP No. 44/2021 orders Commercial Courts to examine formal and substantive aspects, Article 13(5) of PERMA No. 3/2021 strictly prohibits petitioners from submitting new documentary evidence or *novum*, depriving judges of fact-finding authority and trapping them into passively confirming administrative records. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-039]]: Misalignment of Evidentiary Standards & Execution Deficit, where KPPU investigations rely on criminal-analogous evidence under Article 42 of Law No. 5/1999 while Commercial Courts apply civil evidence rules (Article 164 HIR), creating severe admissibility confusion, compounded by a lack of asset-tracing powers for PNBP fine execution. == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-038]]: Under current practice pursuant to SEMA No. 1/2021 and PERMA No. 3/2021, objections filed after 2 February 2021 are processed exclusively by the 5 regional Commercial Courts, bypassing formal court mediation and relying primarily on administrative dossier review, with Cassation judgments serving as final review as PERMA No. 3/2021 bars Judicial Review (*Peninjauan Kembali* / PK). == Japanese & Comparative Practice / Praktik Perbandingan == * [[JPAIS-MED-JP-038]]: International comparison evaluated in the Puslitbang Kumdil monograph highlights the United States Federal Trade Commission (FTC) model applying the **Judicial Remand Doctrine**, where appellate courts finding incomplete evidentiary records issue remand orders returning cases to agencies to re-examine facts without nullifying actions outright or touching substantive market merits. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-038]]: The primary gap is the absence of a dedicated **Commercial Court Procedural Law Act** (*UU Hukum Acara Peradilan Niaga*), where current reliance on civil code procedure (HIR/RBg) fails to accommodate quasi-judicial administrative reviews, leaving judges without statutory tools like remand power or specialized economic evidence evaluation rules. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Adopt the judicial remand doctrine by amending PERMA No. 3/2021 to authorize Commercial Court judges to issue a Remand Order (*Putusan Sela / Pengembalian Berkas*), re-align examination timeframes from 3–12 months back to a strict maximum of 60 working days, and relax the evidence lock for novel arguments introduced in KPPU final decisions. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-038]]: Issue a Supreme Court Regulation (PERMA Amandemen 3/2021) incorporating the remand mechanism and clarifying the 60-working-day trial cap. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-039]]: Draft a comprehensive Bill on Commercial Court Procedural Law (*RUU Hukum Acara Peradilan Niaga*) establishing specialized competition procedure. == Pilot Proyek / Pilot Projections == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-038]]: Central Jakarta Commercial Court pilot implementation evaluating remand order execution and trial duration reduction. == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-038]]: Reduction of average case disposal time to $\le 60$ working days; successful implementation of remand orders for incomplete administrative dossiers, reducing outright annulments based on minor procedural gaps. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Harmonizing PP No. 44/2021 and PERMA No. 3/2021 regarding the definition of working days and execution mechanisms for PNBP fines, alongside establishing specialized economic certification programs for Commercial Court judges in coordination with BSDK MA RI. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Promulgating specialized commercial court procedural rules that reconcile public administrative enforcement powers with private civil due process safeguards. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * Official research monograph titled *“Kewenangan Pengadilan Niaga dalam Mengadili Permohonan Keberatan atas Putusan Komisi Pengawas Persaingan Usaha Tidak Sehat”* (ISBN 978-623-384-090-3) published by Puslitbang Kumdil MA RI (2021) under lead researcher Dr. Ismail Rumadan, M.H. et al. == Related Entities / Entitas Navigation == * [[Main Page|Main Portal]] * * * --- == Summary / Ringkasan == == Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas == * Entity ID: JPAIS-MED-REF-039 * Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa * Ingestion Status: Confirmed == Description / Deskripsi == This page records the empirical multi-jurisdictional statistical compilation and Problem Inventory List (Daftar Inventaris Masalah / DIM) prepared for the inaugural Kick-Off Meeting of the Business Competition Law Working Group (Kelompok Kerja Hukum Persaingan Usaha) of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia, held in Jakarta on 3–4 August 2026. The comprehensive dataset synthesizes official caseload figures and judicial resource allocations across three core Commercial Court seats (Central Jakarta, Makassar, and Semarang) for the 2021–2026 reporting period. The statistics reveal extreme geographic centralization: Central Jakarta accounts for **98.7% of all incoming objection filings** (77 out of 78 total cases) and **96.7% of resolved decisions** (29 out of 30 total cases). Across all three jurisdictions, **63.3% of resolved objection cases resulted in judgments rejecting the objection** (19 cases), while **36.7% resulted in judgments granting or partially granting the objection** (11 cases). All structural entities, numerical matrices, and issue categories have been ingested into the Knowledge Graph under the direction of Knowledge Grapher '''Cecep Mustafa'''. == Problem / Masalah == * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-039]]: Extreme Geographic Asymmetry & Docket Concentration, where Central Jakarta handles over 98% of national competition objections, straining its 2 active presiding competition judges while regional courts in Semarang and Makassar maintain 14 to 6 certified judges with near-zero dockets. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-040]]: E-Court Technical Blockade for Multi-Petitioner Cases, where the compilation's DIM highlights that SIPP/e-Court architecture locks master case registration after the first petitioner registers, rejecting subsequent co-respondents in joint conduct cases and forcing separate, fragmented trials across different courts. == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-039]]: Competition objections are processed without formal court mediation (Article 12 PERMA No. 3/2021) relying on administrative dossier review, while SIPP/e-Court systems lack multi-petitioner consolidation features and suffer from norm conflicts between calendar days (PERMA 3/2021) and working days (PP 44/2021). == Japanese & Comparative Practice / Praktik Perbandingan == * [[JPAIS-MED-JP-039]]: In Japan (Tokyo High Court / JFTC), centralized review at the Tokyo High Court is paired with a unified digital case management system that automatically consolidates multi-party appeals against Japan Fair Trade Commission orders, preventing fragmented trials. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-039]]: The primary gap is the structural disconnect between PERMA No. 3/2021 procedural rules and SIPP/e-Court technical capabilities, alongside the rigid "evidence lock" (Article 13(5) PERMA No. 3/2021) that prevents judges from evaluating new economic counter-evidence. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Deploy an automated e-Court feature allowing multiple co-respondents filing objections against the same KPPU decision to link their petitions to a single Master Case Number, and re-allocate certified competition judges from low-density courts (Semarang and Makassar) to participate in virtual e-Court panels supporting Central Jakarta. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-040]]: Issue a Supreme Court Circular (SEMA) standardizing filing deadlines to "working days" and establishing guidelines for multi-petitioner e-Court registration. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-041]]: Promulgate PERMA Amandemen 3/2021 establishing limited evidence lock relaxation, specialized economic evidence procedures (*Hot Tubbing*), and explicit Judicial Review (*Peninjauan Kembali*) rules. == Pilot Proyek / Pilot Projections == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-039]]: Working Group on Competition Law (Pokja MA RI) pilot coordination across Central Jakarta, Makassar, and Semarang Commercial Courts. == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-039]]: 100% elimination of parallel trials arising from multi-petitioner e-Court registration errors; reduction of average objection trial duration to $\le 60$ working days per statutory standard. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Harmonizing PP No. 44/2021 and PERMA No. 3/2021 regarding working days, bank guarantee requirements, and execution of PNBP fines, alongside establishing formal inter-agency protocols between Mahkamah Agung, KPPU, and the Ministry of Finance (DJKN) for effective asset tracing and fine recovery. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Updating SIPP/e-Court system architecture to incorporate multi-petitioner master case linking and cross-jurisdictional virtual judicial panel assignments. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * Official Working Group Kick-Off Meeting compilation document (*Kompilasi Data dari P Niaga dan Draft DIM.pdf*) prepared for the Supreme Court of RI on 3–4 August 2026 in Jakarta. == Summary / Ringkasan == == Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas == * Entity ID: JPAIS-MED-REF-040 * Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa * Ingestion Status: Confirmed == Description / Deskripsi == This page records the detailed Problem Inventory List (Daftar Inventaris Masalah / DIM) matrix analysis synthesized from the official working document ''"Kompilasi Data Statistik Perkara dan Daftar Inventaris Masalah Penyelesaian Perkara Keberatan Terhadap Putusan Komisi Pengawas Persaingan Usaha di Pengadilan Niaga"'' (prepared for the inaugural Supreme Court Working Group Kick-Off Meeting on 3–4 August 2026 in Jakarta). Focusing on the empirical submissions from the Central Jakarta Commercial Court (Table 19) and the Semarang Commercial Court (Table 20), this page evaluates critical technical-juridical bottlenecks in PERMA No. 3/2021, including the prohibition against new witnesses/experts (*evidence lock*), the e-Court registration lockout in multi-petitioner cases (e.g., the Cooking Oil cartel trial), the total absence of a judicial appeal mechanism for MSME partnership (*kemitraan*) decisions, and the lack of confidentiality protections (*confidentiality rings*) for trade secrets during public court proceedings. All problem matrices, legal bases, and proposed solutions have been ingested into the Knowledge Graph under the direction of Knowledge Grapher '''Cecep Mustafa'''. == Problem / Masalah == * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-042]]: Infringement of Audi Alteram Partem via Information Asymmetry, where Article 13(3) of PERMA No. 3/2021 does not grant petitioners full access to KPPU investigation files (*BAP penyelidikan*) or witness identities, preventing effective defense preparation. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-043]]: Absence of Trade Secret Protections (*Confidentiality Rings*), where PERMA No. 3/2021 lacks mechanisms to protect sensitive corporate financial data and trade secrets disclosed during public Commercial Court hearings, exposing business actors to commercial harm. == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-040]]: Judges in Commercial Courts face contradictory procedures when handling new witness requests, with some panels permitting new experts and others strictly enforcing the evidence lock under Article 13(5) PERMA No. 3/2021, while SIPP/e-Court systems reject secondary filings in multi-party cartel cases, and partnership (*kemitraan*) dispute appeals are routinely dismissed for lack of jurisdiction (*Niet Ontvankelijke Verklaard*). == Japanese & Comparative Practice / Praktik Perbandingan == * [[JPAIS-MED-JP-040]]: In Japan (Tokyo High Court / JFTC), Japan Fair Trade Commission orders are evaluated under administrative litigation rules, permitting full review of relevant market definitions and indirect economic evidence via independent expert panels (*Concurrent Expert Evidence*), while the EU General Court implements formal **Data Room Procedures** and **Confidentiality Rings**. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-040]]: The primary structural gap is the rigid, dossier-based administrative review model under PERMA No. 3/2021, which lacks modern procedural tools such as e-Court multi-party consolidation, remote video expert testimony, confidentiality rings, and partnership appeal pathways. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Harmonize deadline calculations strictly to working days (*hari kerja*), relax the evidence lock (Article 13(5)) to permit new documentary and expert evidence whenever KPPU introduces novel market definitions or fine formulas in its final ruling, mandate e-Court Master Case Consolidation features for multi-petitioner filings, and establish explicit Commercial Court jurisdiction for MSME Partnership (*kemitraan*) appeals. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-040]]: Issue a Supreme Court Circular (SEMA) harmonizing working days, waiving bank guarantees for non-monetary remedies, and authorizing remote witness teleconferencing under PERMA No. 6/2022. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-041]]: Promulgate the PERMA Amandemen 3/2021 incorporating ICLA and Pokja DIM recommendations. == Pilot Proyek / Pilot Projections == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-040]]: Central Jakarta Commercial Court pilot implementation handling complex multi-party and high-tech cartel objections. == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-040]]: 100% elimination of e-Court registration lockouts for co-respondents; zero procedural dismissals of partnership (*kemitraan*) appeals based on jurisdictional ambiguity; adjudication completed strictly within $\le 60$ working days per statutory standard. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Amending Law No. 5/1999 and Law No. 20/2008 to grant explicit statutory rights of judicial appeal for all KPPU administrative decisions, including partnership enforcement and merger notification delays, alongside establishing formal inter-agency data-sharing protocols between Mahkamah Agung, KPPU, and Ministry of Finance (DJKN) for PNBP fine execution. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Restructuring administrative review procedures into an equitable adversarial framework that balances KPPU's enforcement authority with robust constitutional due process safeguards. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * Official Working Group compilation document (*Kompilasi Data dari P Niaga dan Draft DIM.pdf*) prepared for the Supreme Court of RI on 3–4 August 2026 in Jakarta, detailing Central Jakarta (Tabel 19) and Semarang (Tabel 20) DIM submissions. == Related Entities / Entitas Terkait == * {{JPAIS JPAIS-MED-REF-041 * Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa * Ingestion Status: Confirmed == Description / Deskripsi == This page records the empirical analysis of official judicial statistics and the 7-point Problem Inventory List (Daftar Inventaris Masalah / DIM) issued by the Central Jakarta Commercial Court on 23 July 2026, in response to Official Supreme Court Request Letter No. `23/KM.BIN/HK1.2/VII/2026` dated 9 July 2026 (signed by Chairman of the Development Chamber, Syamsul Ma'arif, S.H., LL.M., Ph.D.). Formally signed by the Chief of Central Jakarta Commercial Court, Dr. Husnul Khotimah, S.H., M.H., the dataset establishes Central Jakarta as the primary judicial hub for competition disputes in Indonesia, logging 78 incoming objection filings between 2021 and 2026 (peaking at 46 cases in 2026 alone). The report identifies critical procedural defects under PERMA No. 3/2021, including witness summoning disparities, SIPP software limitations in registering multi-petitioner actions, time-limit contradictions (3–12 months vs SEMA No. 2/2012), lack of court mediation, and the absence of asset-tracing mechanisms for fine execution. All structural entities, yearly caseload matrices, judicial rosters, and problem matrices have been ingested into the Knowledge Graph under the direction of Knowledge Grapher '''Cecep Mustafa'''. == Problem / Masalah == * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-046]]: Extreme Filing Surge vs Active Bench Allocation, where the sudden surge from 7 cases in 2025 to 46 cases in mid-2026 represents a 557% increase in caseload, while only 2 judges (Anton Rizal Setiawan, S.H., M.H., and Muhammad Firman Akbar, S.H., M.H.) actively preside over competition panels out of 15 listed judges, creating severe panel burnout and scheduling bottlenecks. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-047]]: SIPP Software Architecture Lockout & Witness Disparities, where the SIPP case tracking system cannot log more than one petitioner under a single case register number (blocking secondary co-respondents in multi-party cartel cases), while judicial panels exhibit inconsistent witness summoning practices due to ambiguous language in Article 13 of PERMA No. 3/2021. == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-041]]: Under current practice at Central Jakarta, competition objections bypass mediation entirely pursuant to Article 12 PERMA No. 3/2021, relying on administrative dossier review, with over 83% of resolved cases appealed to the Supreme Court via Cassation while trial panels face inconsistent rules regarding new witness hearings. == Japanese & Comparative Practice / Praktik Perbandingan == * [[JPAIS-MED-JP-041]]: In Japan (Tokyo High Court / JFTC), orders are reviewed under strict administrative record review (*substantial evidence rule*), prohibiting new witness testimony unless the JFTC arbitrarily refused to hear the witness during administrative proceedings, providing a model for restricting de novo evidentiary re-openings. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-041]]: The primary structural gap is the absence of explicit statutory authority for Commercial Court judges to order asset discovery during trial or mandate that KPPU submit certified asset schedules of respondents to enable effective civil execution, compounded by SIPP architectural rigidity. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Amend Article 13 of PERMA No. 3/2021 to explicitly restrict new witnesses/experts not presented at KPPU; abolish the minimum 3-month trial timeframe in Article 14(1) while retaining a 60-working-day cap; re-introduce court mediation under PERMA No. 1/2016; mandate in court judgment amars that KPPU attach certified asset schedules; and upgrade SIPP database schemas to support multi-petitioner master case registration. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-042]]: Issue a Supreme Court Circular (SEMA) standardizing witness summoning procedures and waiving minimum trial duration requirements. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-043]]: Deploy the SIPP Multi-Petitioner Update and promulgate the PERMA Amandemen 3/2021 incorporating Central Jakarta's 7-point DIM recommendations. == Pilot Proyek / Pilot Projections == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-041]]: Central Jakarta Commercial Court (High-Density Hub) implementation of SIPP multi-petitioner updates and standardized hearing protocols. == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-041]]: 100% SIPP recording compliance for multi-petitioner objection filings; reduction of average case trial duration to $\le 60$ working days; zero execution failures caused by missing asset inventories in final judgments. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Expanding judicial panel authority under PERMA No. 3/2021 to allow judges to order prosecution/KPPU evidence production or asset tracing reports during trial, alongside re-balancing judicial roster assignments at Central Jakarta District Court. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Updating SIPP/e-Court database architecture and revising PERMA No. 3/2021 provisions concerning evidentiary limits, trial timelines, and execution remedies. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * Official report document (*Laporan Data Statistik Perkara KPPU dan DIM Pengadilan Niaga Pada Pengadilan Negeri Jakarta Pusat.pdf*) signed by Dr. Husnul Description / Deskripsi == This page records the standardized adjudication framework and policy guidelines for KPPU objection proceedings, formulated pursuant to Supreme Court Directives Letter No. `23/KM.BIN/HK1.2/VII/2026` issued on 9 July 2026 by Chairman of the Development Chamber, Syamsul Ma'arif, S.H., LL.M., Ph.D., and the official technical submission delivered on 23 July 2026 by Chief of the Central Jakarta Commercial Court, Dr. Husnul Khotimah, S.H., M.H. The reform proposals focus on resolving three critical procedural bottlenecks in PERMA No. 3/2021: (1) eliminating the normative contradiction between the 3-to-12-month trial timeframe in Article 14(1) PERMA 3/2021 and the 5-month maximum case disposal limit under SEMA No. 2/2012; (2) re-integrating court-annexed mediation under PERMA No. 1/2016 into competition disputes to foster win-win commercial solutions; and (3) empowering Commercial Court judges to order asset discovery and mandate bailiff seizure (*sita jaminan*) for unpaid Non-Tax State Revenue (PNBP) administrative fines. All structural entities, legal analyses, and procedural guidelines have been ingested into the Knowledge Graph under the direction of Knowledge Grapher '''Cecep Mustafa'''. == Problem / Masalah == * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-048]]: Normative Timeframe Contradiction, where trapping judicial panels between the minimum 3-month rule in Article 14(1) PERMA No. 3/2021 and the 5-month maximum limit under SEMA No. 2/2012 causes unnecessary delays and administrative non-compliance. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-049]]: Adversarial Rigidity & Execution Impasse, where excluding mediation under Article 12 PERMA No. 3/2021 forces all objections into protracted litigation, while the absence of asset discovery powers and attached asset schedules renders court judgments unenforceable when non-compliant respondents conceal corporate assets. == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-042]]: Competition objection trials proceed strictly on administrative dossiers without a pre-trial mediation phase, resulting in an adversarial posture where over 83% of cases escalate to Supreme Court Cassation, while trial durations vary significantly across commercial courts due to conflicting timeline interpretations, and fine collection relies on District Court execution clerks lacking compulsory asset disclosure powers. == Japanese & Comparative Practice / Praktik Perbandingan == * [[JPAIS-MED-JP-042]]: In Japan (Tokyo High Court / JFTC), the court combines specialized judicial review with administrative enforcement mechanisms that mandate public financial disclosures, enabling swift asset attachment for unpaid administrative penalties, providing a benchmark for empowering Indonesian commercial courts with asset discovery and mediation tools. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-042]]: The primary gap is the lack of statutory provisions in PERMA No. 3/2021 authorizing Commercial Court judges to order asset discovery, mandate pre-trial mediation, and complete trials within a streamlined 60-working-day window. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Amend Article 14(1) of PERMA No. 3/2021 to delete the 3-month minimum trial timeframe, establishing a strict maximum disposal cap of 60 working days; revise Article 12 to permit court-annexed mediation under PERMA No. 1/2016; amend execution provisions to require KPPU to submit certified respondent asset schedules, empowering judges to include bailiff seizure orders (*sita jaminan*) in final amars; and issue binding guidelines clarifying witness summoning restrictions. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-042]]: Issue a Supreme Court Circular (SEMA) waiving minimum trial duration requirements and encouraging voluntary judicial mediation. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-043]]: Promulgate PERMA Amandemen 3/2021 incorporating Central Jakarta's 7-point DIM recommendations regarding trial timelines, mediation, and asset seizure. == Pilot Proyek / Pilot Projections == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-042]]: Central Jakarta Commercial Court (High-Density Hub) implementation of standardized adjudication guidelines. == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-042]]: 100% case disposal completed strictly within $\le 60$ working days; zero execution failures caused by missing corporate asset inventories in final judgments; successful implementation of court mediation for eligible commercial competition disputes. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Harmonizing SEMA No. 2/2012 and PERMA No. 3/2021 to ensure uniform trial management across all 5 Commercial Courts, alongside strengthening inter-agency cooperation between Mahkamah Agung, KPPU, and Ministry of Finance (DJKN) for PNBP fine execution and asset tracing. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Promulgating standardized adjudication guidelines that reconcile trial timelines, introduce court mediation, and establish enforceable execution remedies. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * Supreme Court Request Letter No. `23/KM.BIN/HK1.2/VII/2026` by Syamsul Ma'arif, S.H., LL.M., Ph.D. (9 July 2026) and Official Report by Dr. Husnul Khotimah, S.H., M.H. (Universitas Sumatera Utara). The study traces twenty years of procedural rulemaking by the Supreme Court of the Republic of Indonesia—from PERMA No. 1 Tahun 2003, PERMA No. 3 Tahun 2005, PERMA No. 3 Tahun 2019, to the current PERMA No. 3 Tahun 2021. It highlights major paradigm shifts, including the nature of objection petitions (from civil lawsuits to administrative review permohonan), trial duration limits (from 30 days to 3–12 months), definition of days (from working days to calendar days), and the absolute jurisdictional transfer from 412 District Courts to 5 specialized Commercial Courts pursuant to Article 118 of Law No. 11/2020 (Job Creation Law). All historical comparison matrices and normative evolutions have been ingested into the Knowledge Graph under the direction of Knowledge Grapher '''Cecep Mustafa'''. == Problem / Masalah == * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-050]]: Normative Oscillations in Time Management, where moving from a strict 30-day trial cap (PERMA 3/2005 and 3/2019) to an expanded 3-to-12-month window (PERMA 3/2021) created severe friction with general summary proceedings in Commercial Courts. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-051]]: Calendar Days Conflict & Strict Evidence Lock, where defining "days" as calendar days in PERMA No. 3/2021 conflicts directly with PP No. 44/2021 (specifying working days), and a total ban on new documentary evidence traps judges into acting as dossier checkers. == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-043]]: All competition objections are filed exclusively at 5 regional Commercial Courts via *e-Court* pursuant to PERMA No. 3/2021, requiring submission of legal power of attorney, petition, KPPU ruling copy, and a legalized bank guarantee, proceeding without court mediation and bypassing Judicial Review (*Peninjauan Kembali*). == Japanese & Comparative Practice / Praktik Perbandingan == * [[JPAIS-MED-JP-043]]: In Japan (Tokyo High Court / JFTC), specialized review of Japan Fair Trade Commission orders evolved over decades from administrative panel reviews to direct High Court litigation, establishing consistent evidentiary standards without shifting definitions of trial days, providing a benchmark for stable statutory procedural rules. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-043]]: The primary structural gap is the ongoing instability of procedural rules caused by relying on administrative Supreme Court Regulations (PERMAs) that frequently alter filing definitions, trial durations, and evidence admissibility standards without a unifying parliamentary statute. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Harmonize PERMA No. 3/2021 to restore "working days" as the uniform metric matching PP No. 44/2021; codify clear criteria permitting new documentary evidence when KPPU introduces novel market definitions or fine formulas; and replace the 3–12 month window with a strict maximum cap of 60 working days. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-043]]: Issue a Supreme Court Circular (SEMA) three-tier reform roadmap presented by competition law expert Prof. Dr. Ningrum Natasya Sirait, S.H., M.Li. (Universitas Sumatera Utara) at the inaugural Kick-Off Meeting of the Supreme Court Competition Law Working Group (Pokja MA RI) in Jakarta on 3 August 2026. Entitled *“Ruang Lingkup dan Intensitas Pemeriksaan Keberatan atas Putusan KPPU Oleh Lembaga Peradilan”*, the study analyzes the structural tension between KPPU's integrated quasi-judicial model (combining investigation, prosecution, and adjudication) and the restricted "dossier review" model (*pemeriksaan atas berkas*) enforced under Article 13 of PERMA No. 3/2021. Drawing from major precedent cases—including the Google Play Billing system decision (Rp 202.5 billion fine, finalized in March 2026), the SANY Heavy Industry truck cartel case, and the landmark Transjakarta tender collusion Judicial Review (*Peninjauan Kembali* No. 9/PK/Pdt.Sus-KPPU/2020 and PT Jakpro PK decision No. 43 PK/Pdt.Sus-KPPU/2025 decided on 3 November 2025)—the paper formulates a Three-Tier Policy Action Plan (Options A, B, and C) for Supreme Court reform. All structural entities and analytical frameworks have been ingested into the Knowledge Graph under the direction of Knowledge Grapher '''Cecep Mustafa'''. == Problem / Masalah == * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-052]]: Interpretive Ambiguity of Article 13, where PERMA No. 3/2021 generates three conflicting judicial interpretations—(1) full factual review with restricted source evidence; (2) pure administrative record checking; or (3) middle verification checking—causing severe judicial divergence across commercial courts. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-053]]: Risk of Uncorrectable Factual Errors & Conflicting Cassation Rulings, where Article 13(5) prohibiting *novum* and Article 16(2) barring Judicial Review (*PK*) leave no valve to correct factual errors, compounded by divergent Cassation rulings in joint conduct cases (e.g., PT Jakpro tender collusion). == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-044]]: Commercial courts review KPPU decisions strictly on administrative dossiers without pre-trial court mediation, leaving unredacted investigation file access (*inzage*) unregulated and partnership (*kemitraan*) disputes without explicit procedural frameworks. == Japanese & Comparative Practice / Praktik Perbandingan == * [[JPAIS-MED-JP-044]]: In Japan (Tokyo High Court / JFTC), the court formerly utilized a record-review model similar to Indonesia's, but abandoned it in 2015 in favor of full judicial examination after finding record-checking failed to provide meaningful oversight over JFTC administrative orders. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-044]]: The primary structural gap is that no comparative jurisdiction combines an integrated quasi-judicial agency, a strict record-review model, a total ban on new documentary evidence (*novum*), and a complete prohibition of Extraordinary Judicial Review (*Peninjauan Kembali*). == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Implement a Three-Tier Policy Action Plan: Option A (Immediate Executive Action via SEMA/PERMA covering Article 13 verification, *inzage* access, and working days harmonization); Option B (Intermediate Reforms introducing reciprocal *novum*, supplementary hearings before judges, and partnership appeals); and Option C (Long-Term Parliamentary Amendments to Law No. 5/1999, statutory PK codification, and expert *Hot Tubbing*). == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-044]]: Execute Option A immediately via a Supreme Court Circular or PERMA Amendment. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-045]]: Implement Option B and C reforms following Pokja MA RI evaluation and legislative coordination with DPR RI. == Pilot Proyek / Pilot Projections == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-044]]: Commercial Court pilot implementation handling major corporate competition objections under the Three-Tier Policy Framework. == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-044]]: 100% compliance with access to file (*inzage*) protocols for appealing respondents; zero conflicting Cassation rulings in multi-party joint conduct cases; adjudication completed strictly within $\le 60$ working days. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Harmonizing PERMA No. 3/2021 with Article 67(e) of Law No. 14/1985 to clarify Judicial Review (*PK*) availability for conflicting Cassation judgments, alongside submitting Option C policy proposals to Commission VI of DPR RI. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Codifying the Three-Tier Policy Action Plan into binding Supreme Court regulations and parliamentary statutes to resolve structural ambiguities in competition review. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * Keynote presentation document (*Ningrum_2026 agustus 2 Perubahan Perma.pdf*) authored by Prof. Dr. Ningrum Natasya Sirait, S.H., M.Li. Edisi Agustus 2026*), drafted pursuant to the National Institute of Public Administration (LAN RI) Executive Template (June 2026 Edition) by the Expert Team and Working Group on Competition Law Reform (*Tim Ahli & Kelompok Kerja Pembaharuan Hukum Persaingan Usaha Mahkamah Agung RI*). Addressed directly to the Leadership of the Supreme Court of RI (Chief Justice, Deputy Chief Justice for Judicial Affairs, Chairman of the Civil Chamber, and Chamber Chairmen), the Policy Brief synthesizes empirical findings from the August 2026 Problem Inventory List (DIM 2026) across all 5 Commercial Courts (Central Jakarta, Medan, Semarang, Surabaya, and Makassar), ICLA, academia, and economic experts. To resolve 35 core operational and legal issues, the document formulates a strategic Dual-Track Policy: (1) amending PERMA No. 3/2021 for procedural reform; and (2) issuing a Supreme Court Decree (KMA) on Adjudication Guidelines for Commercial Judges, backed by deep comparative research into Germany (Civil Law / GWB), Australia (Common Law / ACT), and Singapore (Regional Neighbor / CAB). All structural entities, policy matrices, stakeholder roles, and implementation roadmaps have been ingested into the Knowledge Graph under the direction of Knowledge Grapher '''Cecep Mustafa'''. == Problem / Masalah == * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-054]]: Normative Conflicts & Regulatory Disharmony, characterized by conflicting definitions of days between PERMA No. 3/2021 (calendar days) and PP No. 44/2021 (working days), absolute competence ambiguity regarding MSME Partnership (*kemitraan*) rulings under KPPU Reg No. 2/2024, and a lack of explicit forum rules for foreign respondents. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-055]]: E-Court Incompatibility & Evidentiary Complexity, where SIPP/e-Court architecture rejects secondary objection filings and lacks multi-petitioner consolidation features (triggering parallel trials and contradictory Cassation judgments), compounded by rigid evidence locks under Article 13(5) PERMA No. 3/2021 and a total absence of trade secret protections (*confidentiality rings*). == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-045]]: Objections are processed without pre-trial mediation (Article 12 PERMA No. 3/2021) or formal *inzage* rules, forcing judges to conduct dossier-bound reviews without economic expert evaluation tools, while SIPP/e-Court architecture lacks multi-petitioner master case features and bank JPAIS-MED-REF-047 * Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa * Ingestion Status: Confirmed == Description / Deskripsi == This page records the executive leadership policy brief dated August 2026 entitled *"Policy Brief untuk Pimpinan: Reformasi Hukum Acara dan Kelembagaan Pengadilan Niaga dalam Penanganan Keberatan Putusan Komisi Pengawas Persaingan Usaha"*. Addressed to the Leadership of the Supreme Court of RI, KPPU, and the Legislature (DPR RI/Government), the document evaluates five years of absolute jurisdictional transfer of KPPU objections from District Courts to Commercial Courts pursuant to Article 118 of Law No. 11/2020 on Job Creation and Law No. 6/2023. It identifies five critical operational bottlenecks: (1) public vs. private law incompatibility; (2) trial duration contradiction (3–12 months); (3) evidentiary restrictions (*evidence lock*); (4) geographical access disparities; and (5) limitations in fine execution and asset tracing. To establish legal certainty and a healthy investment climate, the policy brief formulates a Three Horizons Action Plan (2026–2028+). All structural entities, legal analyses, and strategic frameworks have been ingested into the Knowledge Graph under the direction of Knowledge Grapher '''Cecep Mustafa'''. == Problem / Masalah == * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-057]]: Public-Private Procedural Disorientation, where treating KPPU as a civil defendant (*Termohon Keberatan*) under HIR/RBg forces commercial judges to evaluate public administrative rulings using strict civil standard of proof (Article 164 HIR), creating profound friction with public/criminal evidentiary rules under Article 42 of Law No. 5/1999. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-058]]: Evidence Lock Paradox & Execution Impasse, where PERMA No. 3/2021 restricts new documentary evidence and turns commercial courts into mere dossier-checking bodies (*judex juris*), violating due process rights when KPPU introduces novel market definitions in final rulings, compounded by an inability to execute PNBP fines due to a lack of banking asset-tracing instruments. == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-047]]: Commercial courts examine objections without pre-trial mediation under PERMA No. 3/2021, restricting review strictly to administrative dossiers, while PNBP fine collection relies on conventional civil execution procedures (Article 196 HIR) that lack direct access to OJK or banking data. == Japanese & Comparative Practice / Praktik Perbandingan == * [[JPAIS-MED-JP-047]]: Comparative analysis reveals advanced international models: the United States FTC applies the **Judicial Remand Doctrine** to return incomplete dossiers; Australia's ACCC utilizes **Hot-Tubbing (Concurrent Expert Evidence)** for econometric testing; and Japan/Germany concentrate review in specialized higher courts with expert economic judges. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-047]]: The primary structural gap is the absence of a dedicated *sui generis* Commercial Court Procedural Law Act separate from HIR/RBg, alongside regulatory gaps regarding evidence lock relaxation, end-to-end e-Court integration, and delegated PNBP fine execution. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Execute a Three Horizons Action Plan: Horizon 1 (Short-Term 2026 — revise PERMA No. 3/2021 to relax evidence locks, establish a strict 60-working-day cap, and mandate end-to-end e-Court); Horizon 2 (Medium-Term 2027 — draft a Commercial Court Procedural Law Bill / Comprehensive PERMA, delegate PNBP fine execution to local district courts, and establish asset-tracing cooperation with OJK/banks); and Horizon 3 (Long-Term 2028+ — amend Law No. 5/1999, appoint specialized competition ad hoc judges, and expand Commercial Courts to strategic regional hubs). == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-048]]: Puslitbang Kumdil & Civil Chamber MA RI draft Academic Papers and PERMA revision texts during Year I (2026). * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-049]]: Supreme Court Registrar & KPPU integrate end-to-end e-Court systems and formulate PNBP Fine Execution Guidelines during Year II (2027). == Pilot Proyek / Pilot Projections == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-047]]: Implementation across all 5 Commercial Courts (Central Jakarta, Medan, Semarang, Surabaya, Makassar) under the Three Horizons Action Plan. == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-047]]: Year I (2026): Promulgation of updated PERMA; Year II (2027): 100% objection cases filed and examined via e-Court with average disposal duration $\le 60$ working days; Year III (2028+): Inclusion of Commercial Court Procedural Law Bill in the DPR RI Priority National Legislation Program (Prolegnas). == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Fundamental revision of technical adjudication guidelines for KPPU objections in the Supreme Court, strengthening inter-agency coordination between Mahkamah Agung, KPPU, Ministry of Finance (DJKN), OJK, and Ministry of Law and Human Rights. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Providing a clear legislative roadmap to resolve substantive and procedural conflicts arising from the absolute jurisdictional transfer under the Job Creation Law. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * Official JPAIS-MED-REF-048 * Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa * Ingestion Status: Confirmed == Description / Deskripsi == This page records the comprehensive synthesis of the Master Problem Inventory List (Daftar Inventarisasi Masalah / DIM) prepared for the amendment of Supreme Court Regulation No. 3 of 2021 (PERMA No. 3/2021) concerning the Procedures for Filing and Examining Objections against KPPU Decisions in Commercial Courts. Compiled in August 2026 under the auspices of the Agency for Legal and Judicial Strategy Development (BSDK Mahkamah Agung RI), this master synthesis integrates empirical and normative inputs from eight distinct primary sources: (1) PN Jakarta Pusat DIM & Statistics Report (23 July 2026); (2) PN Medan Internal DIM; (3) PN Semarang DIM & Statistics Report (2021–2026); (4) PN Surabaya DIM & Statistics Report; (5) PN Makassar Case Presentation (2024–2026); (6) Economic Analysis & Evidence Standards Paper by Ine Ruky (2 August 2026); (7) Practice Issues Submission by the Indonesian Competition Lawyers Association (ICLA, 3 August 2026); and (8) Comparative PERMA Trajectory Analysis by Prof. Dr. Ningrum Natasya Sirait (3 August 2026). The consolidated dataset identifies 35 specific problem points structured across 9 issue clusters, targeting 14 existing PERMA articles for amendment and identifying 12 novel legal issues currently lacking statutory coverage in PERMA No. 3/2021. All structural entities, issue distributions, and core reform proposals have been ingested into the Knowledge Graph under the direction of Knowledge Grapher '''Cecep Mustafa'''. == Problem / Masalah == * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-059]]: Administrative Overload in Groups C and G, where Groups C (Formal Requirements & Administration) and G (Witness & Expert Examination) represent the highest workload concentration, each containing 5 distinct problem points, causing litigation stalls due to administrative logjams (SIPP multi-petitioner lockouts, bank guarantee disputes) and procedural uncertainty surrounding expert/witness testimony. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-060]]: Information Asymmetry & Evidentiary Lock, where petitioners face severe information asymmetry due to restricted access to investigation dossiers (*BAP/inzage*) and missing protective *Data Rooms*, while Article 13(5) imposes a strict evidence lock prohibiting new documentary evidence even when KPPU introduces novel factual findings in final written decisions. == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-048]]: Objections are processed without pre-trial court mediation (Article 12) or formal *inzage* rules, forcing commercial judges to conduct dossier-bound reviews without economic expert evaluation tools, while SIPP and e-Court software architectures reject secondary objection filings against the same KPPU ruling, and bank guarantees are demanded indiscriminately. == Japanese & Comparative Practice / Praktik Perbandingan == * [[JPAIS-MED-JP-048]]: International comparative practices embodied in the 8 Core Reform Proposals include Germany's specialized *Kartellsenat* review, full *inzage* rights, and secure *Data Rooms* (GWB); Australia's **Hot Tubbing (Concurrent Expert Evidence)** for simultaneous expert economic testimony under court supervision (ACT); and Japan's structured judicial review over JFTC economic market definitions. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-048]]: The primary structural gap is that 12 out of 35 problem items (34.3% of all DIM items) currently have zero statutory coverage in PERMA No. 3/2021, leaving judges without procedural guidance on critical matters like MSME partnership appeals, economic analysis review standards, *Data Rooms*, and *Hot Tubbing*. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Implement the 8 Core Reform Proposals (*Usulan Pokok yang Mengemuka*): (1) Uniform Deadlines harmonized with PP No. 44/2021 (working days) and bifurcated memory submission; (2) Proportional Bank Guarantee restricted strictly to monetary fines; (3) Clear Review Scope affirming *judex facti* and relevant market re-examination; (4) Economic Testing Standards for methodology, data, assumptions, and alternatives; (5) Reciprocal Evidence Lock Relaxation; (6) File Access & Confidentiality (*inzage*, two-version documents, *Data Rooms*); (7) Trial Modernization (online video expert examination, e-Court master case consolidation); and (8) Corrective Mechanisms & Execution (strict Judicial Review / PK and bailiff asset tracing). == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-050]]: Draft and enact the comprehensive PERMA Amandemen 3/2021 incorporating the 8 Core Reform Proposals during Phase 1 (Short-Term / 2026). * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-051]]: Upgrade SIPP/e-Court architecture for Master Register Consolidation and promulgate KMA Adjudication Guidelines for Commercial Judges during Phase 2 (Medium-Term / 2027). == Pilot Proyek / Pilot Projections == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-048]]: Implementation across all 5 Commercial Courts (Central Jakarta, Medan, Semarang, Surabaya, Makassar) under the Master DIM Reform Package. == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-048]]: 100% resolution of the 12 unregulated novel issues in the amended PERMA text; 100% elimination of e-Court registration lockouts for multi-petitioner cartel objections; adjudication efficiency maintained strictly at $\le 60$ working days per case. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Comprehensive alignment of Supreme Court competition rules with PP No. 44/2021, Law No. 6/2023, and Law No. 1/2023 (New KUHP), alongside strengthening institutional capacity building for Commercial Court judges through specialized BSDK MA RI economic certification programs. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Promulgating an updated Supreme Court Regulation (PERMA) that systematically resolves all 35 operational and legal issues identified across the 9 DIM clusters. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * Master Problem Inventory List presentation document (*PPT Amandemen PERMA 3_2021*) synthesized by the Supreme Court Working Group and BSDK MA RI in August 2026, integrating inputs from 8 primary regional and Ruky on 2 August 2026. Entitled *“Judicial Review of Economic Evidence dari Sisi Ekonomi”*, the expert submission establishes that under Indonesia's Integrated Administrative Model—where the Commission for the Supervision of Business Competition (KPPU) combines investigative, prosecutorial, and adjudicative powers—judicial review of economic reasoning is not an impermissible expansion of court authority, but the essential institutional counterpart required under the Rule of Law. The study formulates a 3-tiered Minimum Standard of Economic Judicial Review (MSEJR), establishes a 5-point minimum test for relevant market definitions, sets strict quality thresholds for indirect evidence (*indirect evidence*) in cartel cases, and drafts concrete normative text for PERMA No. 3/2021. All analytical frameworks, international comparisons, and proposed regulatory articles have been ingested into the Knowledge Graph under the direction of Knowledge Grapher '''Cecep Mustafa'''. == Problem / Masalah == * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-061]]: Misapplication of Evidence Lock to Evolving Market Data, where Article 13(5) of PERMA No. 3/2021 bars new documentary evidence, preventing judges from considering updated market data (e.g., 2023 market entrance data disproving a 2021 KPPU market dominance finding) or counter economic analyses prepared to challenge novel penalty formulas introduced in KPPU's final decision. * [[JPAIS-MED-PROB-062]]: Unchecked Reliance on Low-Quality Indirect Evidence & Expert Scope Restriction, where cartel adjudications frequently rely on circumstantial evidence (such as parallel pricing) without testing whether price alignment stems from external market factors, while commercial courts routinely restrict economic experts to abstract theoretical statements. == Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini == * [[JPAIS-MED-ID-049]]: Commercial Court judges lack explicit methodological guidelines for testing KPPU's economic inferences, treating economic reports as unexaminable administrative findings, evaluating indirect evidence on a binary basis ("admissible vs. inadmissible") rather than testing inference strength, and barring economic experts from applying methodologies directly to case facts. == Japanese & Comparative Practice / Praktik Perbandingan == * [[JPAIS-MED-JP-049]]: International benchmark analysis across the United States (strict *Daubert* expert admissibility standards), the European Union (CJEU precedents requiring accurate, complete, and methodologically consistent data), Australia (Concurrent Expert Evidence / *Hot Tubbing*), and Japan (reasoned decision standards for JFTC methodology) demonstrates advanced judicial economic scrutiny. == Gap / Kesenjangan == * [[JPAIS-MED-GAP-049]]: The primary structural gap is the absence of explicit normative provisions in PERMA No. 3/2021 defining the Minimum Standard of Economic Judicial Review (MSEJR) and establishing quality thresholds for indirect evidence in cartel cases. == Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan == Establish a 3-tiered Minimum Standard of Economic Judicial Review (MSEJR) model, codify a mandatory 5-point relevant market minimum test, and incorporate five specific draft articles into PERMA No. 3/2021 covering economic analysis review standards, relevant market testing, reciprocal evidence lock relaxation, indirect evidence quality criteria, and expanded expert witness scope. == Action / Aksi == * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-052]]: Integrate the five economic adjudication draft articles into the ongoing PERMA No. 3/2021 amendment process under Supreme Court Working Group oversight. * [[JPAIS-MED-ACT-053]]: Develop joint BSDK MA RI and academic training programs to build judicial capacity in industrial organization and econometric evaluation. == Pilot Proyek / Pilot Projections == * [[JPAIS-MED-PILOT-049]]: Commercial Court pilot implementation handling complex cartel and market power objection proceedings applying MSEJR standards. == KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama == * [[JPAIS-MED-KPI-049]]: 100% compliance with Level 1 Minimum Standard of Economic Judicial Review (MSEJR) in all competition judgments; mandatory application of the 5-point relevant market test prior to evaluating market power or antitrust violations. == Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan == Incorporating economic proof as an integral component of competition law procedure, shifting Indonesian enforcement from a formalistic form-based approach to an effect-based analysis, and strengthening institutional capacity building via BSDK MA RI. == Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi == Codifying objective economic review standards and indirect evidence quality thresholds into binding Supreme Court regulations. == Evidence / Bukti Empiris == * Expert presentation document (*Presentasi Ine Ruky -2 Agustue 2026.pdf*) submitted by senior competition economist Ine Minara == Summary / Ringkasan ==

== ID ==
JPAIS:REFORM-PROPOSAL:KCCP-REF-001

== Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas ==

* Entity ID: KCCP-REF-001
* Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa
* Ingestion Status: Confirmed

== Problem & Gap Mapping / Pemetaan Masalah & Kesenjangan ==

* Baseline Problem (KCCP-PROB-001): Court-connected mediation in Indonesian general civil courts (Pengadilan Negeri) suffers from procedural ritualization, resulting in stagnant settlement success rates between 4.0% and 4.08%.
* Current Practice (KCCP-PRACT-ID-001): PERMA No. 1 of 2016 relies on a solo mediator model (a busy career judge or an uncompensated non-judge mediator) conducting brief facilitative sessions without evaluative authority.
* Institutional Gap (KCCP-GAP-001): Lack of multidisciplinary expert panels, absent evaluative settlement mechanisms when parties reach an impasse, and unenforced cost sanctions for bad-faith attendance.

== Comparative Legal Grounding / Landasan Hukum Komparatif ==

* Japanese Practice (KCCP-PRACT-JP-001 & KCCP-PRACT-JP-003): Under Articles 5, 6, and 17 of the Civil Conciliation Act (Minji Chōtei Hō, Act No. 222/1951), Japan utilizes 3-member Conciliation Committees (Chōtei Iinkai: 1 judge + 2 lay commissioners) and empowers courts to issue ex-officio Orders in Lieu of Conciliation (Chōtei ni kawaru kettei), achieving >50% settlement in civil cases and 71.8% in inheritance divisions.

== Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan ==

* Majelis Konsiliasi Tripartit: Institutionalize 3-member panels for commercial, property, and inheritance disputes exceeding Rp 500 million, pairing 1 certified Judge Mediator with 2 accredited Non-Judge Expert Commissioners (e.g., accountants, engineers, land valuers).
* Penetapan Pengganti Perdamaian: Authorize panels to issue a provisional evaluative settlement order upon negotiation deadlock. The order converts into a binding Settlement Deed (Akta Perdamaian) if no party files a formal objection within 14 calendar days.

== Execution Roadmap / Peta Jalan Eksekusi ==

* Phase 1 (Preparation / Persiapan): Promulgate a Chief Justice Decree (SK KMA), establish the Steering Committee, configure SIPP workflow modules, and train 120 expert commissioners.
* Phase 2 (Implementation / Implementasi): Deploy panels across the 6 designated pilot courts (KCCP-PILOT-001).
* Phase 3 (Evaluation / Evaluasi): Audit SIPP performance metrics and draft a permanent Supreme Court Regulation (PERMA).

== Pilot Scope & KPI Targets / Cakupan Pilot & Target KPI ==

* Pilot Courts (KCCP-PILOT-001): PN Jakarta Pusat, PN Surabaya, PN Medan, PA Jakarta Selatan, PA Surabaya, and PA Malang (90-day duration).
* Target KPIs (KCCP-KPI-001):

  * District Court (PN) General Civil Settlement Rate: \(\ge 25%\) (up from ~4.0%).
  * Religious Court (PA) Property/Sharia Banking Settlement Rate: \(\ge 60%\).
  * Average Mediation Duration: \(\le 21\) calendar days (down from 30 working days).

== Policy & Regulatory Impact / Dampak Kebijakan & Regulasi ==

* Administrative: Issue an SK KMA for pilot authorization and integrate lay expert rosters directly into SIPP.
* Regulatory: Promulgate a new PERMA on Integrated Court Mediation superseding PERMA No. 1 of 2016.
* Legislative: Submit amendments to the House of Representatives (DPR) for inclusion in the Draft Civil Procedure Code (RUU Hukum Acara Perdata).

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

* Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa
* Ingestion Status: Confirmed

== Integration with Judicial Education & Training (BSDK Kumdil) / Integrasi dengan Pendidikan & Pelatihan Yudisial ==
The comparative judicial training research highlights how adapting Japanese judicial education practices at the Legal Training and Research Institute (Shihō Kenshūjo) provides the pedagogical foundation required to operationalize KCCP-REF-001:

* Co-Mediation Simulation & Panel Leadership: Deploying 3-member Tripartite Panels requires shifting away from solo, purely facilitative mediation toward collaborative evaluative co-mediation. BSDK's In-Service Specialization Chamber conducts 20-hour clinical co-mediation workshops training judge mediators and accredited non-judge expert commissioners.
* Claim Deconstruction via the DFKUM Doctrine: Adapting Japan's Requirements-Facts Doctrine (Yōken Jijitsu) into the Substantive Elements and Causal Facts Doctrine (Doktrin Fakta Kausal dan Unsur Materiil / DFKUM). Training enables panel members to analyze pre-trial evidence disclosures and draft precise Orders in Lieu of Settlement (Penetapan Pengganti Perdamaian).
* Continuous Roster Governance & Certification: Tiered career accreditation under the Competency-Based Judicial Training Model (J-CBTM) with digital roster management integrated into SIPP.

== Implementation Mapping across Training Tiers / Pemetaan Implementasi Lintas Tingkat Diklat ==

* Pre-Service Induction (Pre-Service Apprenticeship Chamber): Doctrinal element mapping (DFKUM), preliminary issue clarification, and court-connected mediation procedures (Exit Credential: Basic Judicial Qualification).
* In-Service Specialization (In-Service Specialization Chamber): Co-mediation dynamics, financial/land dispute deconstruction, and drafting Penetapan Pengganti Perdamaian (Exit Credential: Certified Court Conciliator / Expert Commissioner Status).
* Court Leadership & Supervision (Leadership & Harmonization Chamber): Monitoring SIPP 14-day objection timers, auditing Substantive Settlement Rates (SSR), and evaluating panel performance (Exit Credential: Court Leadership Eligibility).

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

== Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas ==

* Entity ID: KCCP-REF-001 (Continuation Module)
* Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa
* Ingestion Status: Confirmed

== Description / Deskripsi ==
Reforms Indonesian court-connected mediation by establishing 3-member Tripartite Conciliation Panels (''Majelis Konsiliasi Tripartit'') for claims exceeding Rp 500 million, pairing 1 certified Judge Mediator with 2 accredited Non-Judge Expert Commissioners. The panel is empowered to issue a provisional "Order in Lieu of Settlement" (''Penetapan Pengganti Perdamaian''), which becomes a binding Settlement Deed (''Akta Perdamaian'') if no party objects within 14 calendar days.

== Problem / Masalah ==

* KCCP-PROB-001: Court mediation in general civil courts (''Pengadilan Negeri'') suffers from structural ritualization and stagnant success rates (~4.0%).

== Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini ==

* KCCP-PRACT-ID-001: Mandatory court mediation under PERMA No. 1 of 2016 relies on a solo mediator model (judge or uncompensated non-judge) conducting brief facilitative sessions without evaluative authority.

== Japanese Practice / Praktik Jepang ==

* KCCP-PRACT-JP-001 & KCCP-PRACT-JP-003: Under Articles 5, 6, and 17 of the Civil Conciliation Act, Japan utilizes 3-member Conciliation Committees (''Chōtei Iinkai''—1 judge + 2 lay commissioners) and empowers courts to issue ex-officio "Orders in Lieu of Conciliation" (''Chōtei ni kawaru kettei'').

== Gap / Kesenjangan ==

* KCCP-GAP-001: PERMA No. 1 of 2016 lacks multidisciplinary expert panels, evaluative settlement mechanisms, and enforced cost sanctions for bad-faith attendance.

== Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan ==
Institutionalize Tripartite Conciliation Panels for commercial, property, and inheritance disputes >Rp 500 million, and introduce judicial ''Penetapan Pengganti Perdamaian'' subject to a 14-day objection window.

== Action / Aksi ==

* KCCP-ACT-001: Promulgate SK KMA pilot decree, establish steering committee, configure SIPP workflow, and train 120 expert commissioners.
* KCCP-ACT-002: Deploy panels across 6 pilot courts and issue evaluative orders upon impasse.
* KCCP-ACT-003: Audit SIPP performance metrics and draft permanent PERMA.

== Pilot / Pilot Proyek ==

* KCCP-PILOT-001: 90-day pilot across PN Jakarta Pusat, PN Surabaya, PN Medan, PA Jakarta Selatan, PA Surabaya, and PA Malang.

== KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama ==

* KCCP-KPI-001: PN mediation success rate $\ge 25\%$; religious court property settlement $\ge 60\%$; duration $\le 21$ calendar days.

== Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan ==
Issue Supreme Court Leadership Decree (SK KMA) and integrate lay expert rosters into SIPP. Submit amendments to Draft Civil Procedure Code (''RUU Hukum Acara Perdata'') to DPR.

== Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi ==
Promulgate new PERMA on Court-Connected Mediation and Conciliation superseding PERMA No. 1 of 2016.

== Evidence / Bukti Empiris ==

* PN general civil mediation success rate hovers between 4.0% and 4.08%.
* Japanese conciliation achieves >50% settlement in general civil disputes and 71.8% in inheritance property cases.

* Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa
* Ingestion Status: Confirmed

== Empirical Grounding & Systemic Context / Landasan Empiris & Konteks Sistemik ==

* The Indonesian Baseline Problem (KCCP-PROB-001): Mandatory court-annexed mediation under PERMA No. 1 of 2016 operates as an obligatory procedural prerequisite before trial, recording nationwide general civil settlement success rates between 6.8% and 7.42% in District Courts (Pengadilan Negeri). Active judge mediators face heavy trial dockets, while external non-judge mediators lack dedicated state budget (DIPA) funding, resulting in high roster attrition and low success rates (e.g., 7.04% at Tangerang Religious Court).
* The Japanese Comparative Model (KCCP-PRACT-JP-001 & 003): Under the Civil Conciliation Act of 1951 (Act No. 222 of 1951), Japan’s Minji Chōtei framework consistently resolves over 50% of petitions. Japan utilizes Conciliation Committees (Chōtei Iinkai) comprising 1 presiding Conciliation Judge (Chōtei Kan-an) and 2 lay Conciliation Commissioners (Chōtei Iin) drawn from specialized backgrounds. Article 17 empowers courts to issue ex-officio Orders in Lieu of Conciliation (Chōtei ni kawaru kettei), which gain binding force if no party objects within two weeks.

== Core Reform Adaptation / Adaptasi Reformasi Inti ==

* Tripartite Conciliation Panels (Majelis Konsiliasi Tripartit): Pairs 1 certified Judge Mediator with 2 accredited Non-Judge Expert Commissioners for commercial, land, and property disputes exceeding Rp 500 million.
* Orders in Lieu of Settlement (Penetapan Pengganti Perdamaian): Authorizes panels to issue a provisional evaluative settlement order upon impasse, converting into a binding Settlement Deed (Akta Perdamaian) unless a party files an objection within 14 calendar days.
* State Budget Allocations: Establishes fixed per-case honoraria for certified non-judge mediators via a Joint Ministerial Decree (SKB) between the Supreme Court, Ministry of Law, and Ministry of Finance.

== Phased Implementation & Pilot Targets / Implementasi Bertahap & Target Pilot ==

* 90-Day Pilot Deployment (KCCP-PILOT-001): Executed across representative trial courts including PN Jakarta Selatan, PA Jakarta Selatan, PN Surabaya, and PN Sleman.
* Target Benchmarks (KCCP-KPI-001):

  * Increase District Court settlement rates to \(\ge 25.0%\).
  * Reduce average settlement duration from 30 days to \(\le 18\) calendar days.
  * Expand non-judge panel allocation to \(\ge 45.0%\) of pilot cases.

== Executive Summary & Institutional Alignment / Ringkasan Eksekutif & Penyelarasan Institusional ==

* Core Purpose: The entity KCCP-REF-001 (Tripartite Conciliation Panels and Orders in Lieu of Settlement) serves as the core operational bridge within the Japan-Indonesia ADR Integration System (JPAIS / JICA KCCP) framework, addressing the structural stagnation of court-annexed mediation in Indonesian general civil courts (Pengadilan Negeri) where settlement success rates hover between 4.0% and 7.42%.
* Japanese Model Adaptation: Drawing on Japan's Civil Conciliation Act (Minji Chōtei-hō, Act No. 222 of 1951) and IT transformation under Act No. 48 of 2022, KCCP-REF-001 introduces Tripartite Conciliation Panels (Majelis Konsiliasi Tripartit) and Orders in Lieu of Settlement (Penetapan Pengganti Perdamaian).

== Digital Architecture & SIPP Integration / Arsitektur Digital & Integrasi SIPP ==

* Automated Intake Triaging: Cases registered via e-Court with claims > Rp 500 million are automatically flagged by SIPP and routed to the Tripartite Pra-Sidang queue.
* Expert Roster Matching: SIPP matches case classifications with accredited expert commissioner tags.
* 14-Day Objection Clock: SIPP automates the tracking of the 14-calendar-day objection window following electronic service, sealing the final Akta Perdamaian if no objection is logged.
* Real-Time Analytics: Performance metrics feed into centralized executive dashboards tracking Substantive Settlement Rates and panel velocity.

== Core Operational Matrix / Matriks Operasional Inti ==

* Pilot Authorization: Supreme Court Leadership Decree (SK KMA) enacting a 90-day pilot across 6 courts (KCCP-PILOT-001: PN Jakarta Pusat, PN Surabaya, PN Medan, PA Jakarta Selatan, PA Surabaya, PA Malang).
* System Configuration: SIPP Module & e-Court Workflow Update to automate expert matching and 14-day objection timers.
* Capacity Building: BSDK Kumdil 20-Hour Clinical Certification training 120 Non-Judge Expert Commissioners.
* Legislative Reform: DPR RI Working Committee Brief (RUU Hukum Acara Perdata) codifying Penetapan Pengganti Perdamaian in statutory law.
* Performance Audit: SIPP Dashboard Metrics (KCCP-KPI-001) targeting District Court settlement \(\ge 25\%\) and duration \(\le 21\) calendar days.

{{JPAIS Knowledge|id=JPAIS:REFORM-PROPOSAL:KCCP-REF-001-KCCP-ENTITY|type=ReformProposal|title_id=Entitas KCCP-REF-001: Panel Konsiliasi Tripartit dan Penetapan Pengganti Perdamaian|title_en=KCCP-REF-001 Entity: Tripartite Conciliation Panels and Orders in Lieu of Settlement|slug=kccp-ref-001-kccp-entity-format|description_id=Format struktur lengkap entitas KCCP-REF-001 dalam kerangka JPAIS / JICA KCCP, merinci reformasi mediasi, perbandingan hukum Indonesia-Jepang, aksi pilot, KPI, serta entitas terkait.|description_en=Complete structural format of the KCCP-REF-001 entity within the JPAIS / JICA KCCP framework, detailing mediation reform, Indonesia-Japan legal comparison, pilot actions, KPIs, and related entities.|jurisdiction=Indonesia / Japan Comparative|legal_domain=Judicial Reform / Alternative Dispute Resolution / Civil Procedure|topics=KCCP Entity, Tripartite Conciliation, Minji Chotei, Mediation Reform, JPAIS Framework|status=Proposed (Co-Design / Pilot Stage)|language=bilingual (id/en)|authority=Mahkamah Agung Republik Indonesia / JICA KCCP|verification_status=VERIFIED|version=1.0}}

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

== Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas ==

* Entity ID: KCCP-REF-001
* Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa
* Ingestion Status: Confirmed

== Description / Deskripsi ==
Reforms Indonesian court-connected mediation by establishing 3-member Tripartite Conciliation Panels (''Majelis Konsiliasi Tripartit'') for claims exceeding Rp 500 million, pairing 1 certified Judge Mediator with 2 accredited Non-Judge Expert Commissioners. The panel is empowered to issue a provisional "Order in Lieu of Settlement" (''Penetapan Pengganti Perdamaian''), which becomes a binding Settlement Deed (''Akta Perdamaian'') if no party objects within 14 calendar days.

== Problem / Masalah ==

* KCCP-PROB-001: Court mediation in general civil courts (''Pengadilan Negeri'') suffers from structural ritualization and stagnant success rates (~4.0%).

== Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini ==

* KCCP-PRACT-ID-001: Mandatory court mediation under PERMA No. 1 of 2016 relies on a solo mediator model (judge or uncompensated non-judge) conducting brief facilitative sessions without evaluative authority.

== Japanese Practice / Praktik Jepang ==

* KCCP-PRACT-JP-001 & KCCP-PRACT-JP-003: Under Articles 5, 6, and 17 of the Civil Conciliation Act, Japan utilizes 3-member Conciliation Committees (''Chōtei Iinkai''—1 judge + 2 lay commissioners) and empowers courts to issue ex-officio "Orders in Lieu of Conciliation" (''Chōtei ni kawaru kettei'').

== Gap / Kesenjangan ==

* KCCP-GAP-001: PERMA No. 1 of 2016 lacks multidisciplinary expert panels, evaluative settlement mechanisms, and enforced cost sanctions for bad-faith attendance.

== Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan ==
Institutionalize Tripartite Conciliation Panels for commercial, property, and inheritance disputes >Rp 500 million, and introduce judicial ''Penetapan Pengganti Perdamaian'' subject to a 14-day objection window.

== Action / Aksi ==

* KCCP-ACT-001: Promulgate SK KMA pilot decree, establish steering committee, configure SIPP workflow, and train 120 expert commissioners.
* KCCP-ACT-002: Deploy panels across 6 pilot courts and issue evaluative orders upon impasse.
* KCCP-ACT-003: Audit SIPP performance metrics and draft permanent PERMA.

== Pilot / Pilot Proyek ==

* KCCP-PILOT-001: 90-day pilot across PN Jakarta Pusat, PN Surabaya, PN Medan, PA Jakarta Selatan, PA Surabaya, and PA Malang.

== KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama ==

* KCCP-KPI-001: PN mediation success rate $\ge 25\%$; religious court property settlement $\ge 60\%$; duration $\le 21$ calendar days.

== Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan ==
Issue Supreme Court Leadership Decree (SK KMA) and integrate lay expert rosters into SIPP. Submit amendments to Draft Civil Procedure Code (''RUU Hukum Acara Perdata'') to DPR.

== Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi ==
Promulgate new PERMA on Court-Connected Mediation and Conciliation superseding PERMA No. 1 of 2016.

== Evidence / Bukti Empiris ==

* PN general civil mediation success rate hovers between 4.0% and 4.08%.
* Japanese conciliation achieves >50% settlement in general civil disputes and 71.8% in inheritance property cases.

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

== Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas ==

* Entity ID: KCCP-REF-001
* Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa
* Ingestion Status: Confirmed

== Description / Deskripsi ==
Reforms Indonesian court-connected mediation by establishing 3-member Tripartite Conciliation Panels (''Majelis Konsiliasi Tripartit'') for claims exceeding Rp 500 million, pairing 1 certified Judge Mediator with 2 accredited Non-Judge Expert Commissioners. The panel is empowered to issue a provisional "Order in Lieu of Settlement" (''Penetapan Pengganti Perdamaian''), which becomes a binding Settlement Deed (''Akta Perdamaian'') if no party objects within 14 calendar days.

== Problem / Masalah ==

* KCCP-PROB-001: Court mediation in general civil courts (''Pengadilan Negeri'') suffers from structural ritualization and stagnant success rates (~4.0%).

== Current Indonesian Practice / Praktik Indonesia Saat Ini ==

* KCCP-PRACT-ID-001: Mandatory court mediation under PERMA No. 1 of 2016 relies on a solo mediator model (judge or uncompensated non-judge) conducting brief facilitative sessions without evaluative authority.

== Japanese Practice / Praktik Jepang ==

* KCCP-PRACT-JP-001 & KCCP-PRACT-JP-003: Under Articles 5, 6, and 17 of the Civil Conciliation Act, Japan utilizes 3-member Conciliation Committees (''Chōtei Iinkai''—1 judge + 2 lay commissioners) and empowers courts to issue ex-officio "Orders in Lieu of Conciliation" (''Chōtei ni kawaru kettei'').

== Gap / Kesenjangan ==

* KCCP-GAP-001: PERMA No. 1 of 2016 lacks multidisciplinary expert panels, evaluative settlement mechanisms, and enforced cost sanctions for bad-faith attendance.

== Proposed Adaptation / Adaptasi Usulan ==
Institutionalize Tripartite Conciliation Panels for commercial, property, and inheritance disputes >Rp 500 million, and introduce judicial ''Penetapan Pengganti Perdamaian'' subject to a 14-day objection window.

== Action / Aksi ==

* KCCP-ACT-001: Promulgate SK KMA pilot decree, establish steering committee, configure SIPP workflow, and train 120 expert commissioners.
* KCCP-ACT-002: Deploy panels across 6 pilot courts and issue evaluative orders upon impasse.
* KCCP-ACT-003: Audit SIPP performance metrics and draft permanent PERMA.

== Pilot / Pilot Proyek ==

* KCCP-PILOT-001: 90-day pilot across PN Jakarta Pusat, PN Surabaya, PN Medan, PA Jakarta Selatan, PA Surabaya, and PA Malang.

== KPI / Indikator Kinerja Utama ==

* KCCP-KPI-001: PN mediation success rate $\ge 25\%$; religious court property settlement $\ge 60\%$; duration $\le 21$ calendar days.

== Policy Implication / Implikasi Kebijakan ==
Issue Supreme Court Leadership Decree (SK KMA) and integrate lay expert rosters into SIPP. Submit amendments to Draft Civil Procedure Code (''RUU Hukum Acara Perdata'') to DPR.

== Regulatory Implication / Implikasi Regulasi ==
Promulgate new PERMA on Court-Connected Mediation and Conciliation superseding PERMA No. 1 of 2016.

== Evidence / Bukti Empiris ==

* PN general civil mediation success rate hovers between 4.0% and 4.08%.
* Japanese conciliation achieves >50% settlement in general civil disputes and 71.8% in inheritance property cases.

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

== ID ==
JPAIS:REFORM-PROPOSAL:KCCP-REF-001-SK-SIPP

== Entity Ingestion / Ingesti Entitas ==

* Entity ID: KCCP-REF-001 (SK & SIPP Specification Extension)
* Knowledge Grapher: Cecep Mustafa
* Ingestion Status: Confirmed

== Draft Supreme Court Leadership Decree / Rancangan Keputusan Pimpinan Mahkamah Agung ==

* Title: RANCANGAN SURAT KEPUTUSAN KETUA MAHKAMAH AGUNG REPUBLIK INDONESIA NUMBER: [XX]/KMA/SK/[MONTH]/2026 CONCERNING THE PILOT IMPLEMENTATION OF TRIPARTITE CONCILIATION PANELS AND ORDERS IN LIEU OF SETTLEMENT (MAJELIS KONSILIASI TRIPARTIT DAN PENETAPAN PENGGANTI PERDAMAIAN) IN SELECTED FIRST-INSTANCE COURTS
* First Dictum (Establishment of Panels): Establishes the Tripartite Conciliation Panel comprising 1 Certified Judge Mediator (Panel Chair) and 2 Accredited Non-Judge Expert Commissioners for claims > Rp 500 million.
* Second Dictum (Orders in Lieu of Settlement): Authorizes panels to issue provisional evaluative settlement orders (Penetapan Pengganti Perdamaian) upon impasse, which convert into binding Settlement Deeds (Akta Perdamaian) if no objection is filed within 14 calendar days.
* Third Dictum (Pilot Jurisdictions - KCCP-PILOT-001): 90-day pilot across 6 courts: PN Jakarta Pusat, PN Surabaya, PN Medan, PA Jakarta Selatan, PA Surabaya, and PA Malang.
* Fourth Dictum (Performance Metrics & System Integration): Mandates SIPP configuration for KPIs (PN settlement rate \(\ge 25.0%\), PA property settlement rate \(\ge 60.0%\), duration \(\le 21\) days) and certification of 120 Expert Commissioners by BSDK Kumdil.

== SIPP Technical & Workflow Specification / Spesifikasi Teknis & Alur Kerja SIPP ==

* Workflow Architecture: [e-Court Filing > Rp 500M] ──► [SIPP Auto-Triaging Engine] ──► [Tripartite Session (<= 21 Days)] ──► [Consensus -> Akta Perdamaian OR Impasse -> Penetapan Pengganti Perdamaian -> 14-Day Objection Clock -> Binding Deed or Trial].
* Key Technical Modules:

  * Automated Expert Matching Algorithm: Matches dispute classifications with accredited Expert Commissioner registry tags.
  * Objection Clock Module: Triggers an automated 14-day countdown upon electronic delivery of the Penetapan Pengganti Perdamaian via e-Court.
  * Audit Dashboard: Tracks real-time Substantive Settlement Rates (SSR) and panel performance across pilot courts.

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

=== Bahasa Indonesia ===
Peraturan Mahkamah Agung (PERMA) Nomor 2 Tahun 2025 merupakan instrumen hukum progresif yang memberikan panduan komprehensif bagi Hakim dan Aparatur Pengadilan dalam menyelenggarakan proses peradilan yang inklusif, nondiskriminatif, dan akomodatif bagi penyandang disabilitas. Peraturan ini mengintegrasikan perlindungan hak asasi manusia berdasarkan Konvensi Hak-Hak Penyandang Disabilitas (UNCRPD) ke dalam semua lingkungan peradilan (umum, agama, militer, dan tata usaha negara) untuk penanganan perkara perdata, pidana, perdata agama, jinayat, militer, dan tata usaha negara. Melalui mekanisme wajib seperti Identifikasi Awal dan Penilaian Personal, PERMA ini memastikan setiap hambatan personal diidentifikasi secara dini dan dipenuhi melalui penyediaan Akomodasi yang Layak dan Aksesibilitas.

=== English ===
Supreme Court Regulation (PERMA) Number 2 of 2025 is a progressive legal instrument providing comprehensive guidance for Judges and Court Apparatus to administer an inclusive, non-discriminatory, and accommodative judicial process for persons with disabilities. This regulation integrates human rights protections under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD) across all judicial jurisdictions (general, religious, military, and state administrative courts) for civil, criminal, Islamic family, jinayat, military, and state administrative cases. Through mandatory mechanisms such as Initial Identification and Personal Assessment, this PERMA ensures that any personal barriers are identified early and met through the provision of Reasonable Accommodation and Accessibility.

== Scope & Classification / Ruang Lingkup ==

; Lingkup Sistem Peradilan

* Peradilan Umum
* Peradilan Agama
* Peradilan Militer
* Peradilan Tata Usaha Negara
