== Abstract & Executive Summary ==
'''Improving the Procedure for Refugee Status Determination and Judicial Review in Korea''' is an official judicial policy research report published by the [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] (JPRI) of the Supreme Court of Korea (Research Series 2017-10). Co-authored by Research Fellows [[Lee, Hyeyoung]] and [[Pyo, Hyunduk]], the report presents a comprehensive analysis of the administrative refugee status determination (RSD) procedure conducted by immigration authorities under the [[Ministry of Justice (Korea)|Ministry of Justice]] and the subsequent judicial review proceedings handled by administrative courts.

Evaluating comparative asylum frameworks across eight international jurisdictions (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Germany, France, and Japan) as well as [[UNHCR]] and [[European Union|EU]] asylum directives, the report formulates a structural reform package designed to enhance both procedural fairness (*절차의 공정성*) and operational efficiency (*신속성·효율성*).

== Statutory & Legal Basis ==
The research was conducted under the 2017 Supreme Court Annual Research Plan. The analytical framework evaluates compliance and operational friction across several statutory and international instruments:

* '''[[Refugee Act (Korea)|Korean Refugee Act]] (Act No. 11298)''': Enacted February 10, 2012; effective July 1, 2013.
* '''[[Immigration Control Act (Korea)|Korean Immigration Control Act]]''' and '''[[Administrative Litigation Act (Korea)|Korean Administrative Litigation Act]]'''.
* '''[[Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees|1951 Refugee Convention]] & 1967 Protocol'''.
* '''[[Convention Against Torture]] (CAT)''', specifically Article 3 (Non-Refoulement).

== Policy Background & Problem Statement ==
Following the enactment of the stand-alone [[Refugee Act (Korea)|Refugee Act]] in 2012, asylum applications in South Korea surged from 2,896 in 2014 to 7,542 in 2016. First-instance administrative lawsuits contesting refugee status denials similarly rose from 423 cases in 2014 to 3,161 in 2016. Despite this volume, recognition rates remained exceptionally low compared to [[OECD]] averages, while appeal rates to the High Court (76.9%) and Supreme Court (71.3%) remained disproportionately high in 2016.

Key systemic bottlenecks identified include: 1. '''Airport Port-of-Entry Screening Bottlenecks''': Applicants receiving a non-referral decision (*불회부결정*) lack transparent appeal mechanisms and face prolonged isolation in Departure Waiting Rooms (*출국대기실*) without adequate legal protection. 2. '''Administrative Determination Flaws''': Inadequate interview recording, shortage of qualified certified interpreters, and overlapping duties between immigration enforcement personnel and asylum assessors. 3. '''Formalistic Administrative Appeals''': The [[Refugee Committee]] under the Ministry of Justice operates non-permanently and primarily conducts documentary reviews without mandatory oral hearings. 4. '''Four-Tier Fact-Finding Duplication''': The repetitive full fact-finding process (First-instance Administrative Assessment → Refugee Committee Review → First-instance Administrative Court → High Court) induces severe judicial backlog and creates opportunities for bad-faith applications intended solely to extend temporary stay status (G-1 visa).

== International Comparative Analysis ==
The study systematically evaluates eight comparative international legal frameworks:

* '''United States''': Structural bifurcation between affirmative RSD under [[USCIS]] and defensive proceedings under [[Executive Office for Immigration Review|EOIR]], incorporating the one-year filing deadline.
* '''United Kingdom''': Home Office triage routing coupled with the specialized two-tier tribunal system ([[First-tier Tribunal]] and [[Upper Tribunal]]).
* '''Canada''': Specialized quasi-judicial body—the [[Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada]] (IRB)—housing the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) and Refugee Appeal Division (RAD).
* '''France''': Autonomous first-instance administrative authority ([[OFPRA]]) paired with the specialized asylum court ([[CNDA]]).
* '''New Zealand''': Centralized Country Research Branch (CRB) model providing real-time Country of Origin Information (COI).

== Key Reform Recommendations ==
1. '''Airport Screening Reform''': Restrict non-referral decisions strictly to manifestly unfounded or fraudulent applications, issue formal written rationale, and guarantee a 3-day emergency appeal channel. 2. '''Mandatory Interview Recording & Separation of Functions''': Mandate audio/video recording of asylum interviews, grant applicants right of review over interview transcripts (*면접조서*), and strictly separate asylum assessor qualifications from immigration enforcement functions. 3. '''Establishment of a Quasi-Judicial Refugee Tribunal''': Reconstruct the passive Refugee Committee into an independent Quasi-Judicial Tribunal (*난민심판원*) featuring permanent adjudicators and mandatory oral hearings. 4. '''Judicial Evidentiary Paradigm Shift''': Transition from civil law foundationalism (demanding strict documentary proof) to a *coherentism* paradigm (*정합주의*), emphasizing overall narrative consistency, supported by a centralized national Country of Origin Information (COI) Center. 5. '''Differentiated Fast-Track Procedures''': Implement accelerated determination tracks for manifestly unfounded or repetitive claims lacking new factual grounds.

== Knowledge Graph Entities & Personnel ==

* '''Lead Authors''': [[Lee, Hyeyoung]] (Co-Lead), [[Pyo, Hyunduk]] (Co-Lead).
* '''Research Contributors''': [[Seo, Yongsung]], [[Choi, Yuna]].
* '''Issuing Body''': [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] (JPRI).
* '''Associated Entities Under Verification''': [[Cecep Mustafa]] (JPW-PERSON-CECEP) and [[Qonita Mutmainah]] (JPW-PERSON-QONITA) are designated as *Entity Identity Uncertain* due to their absence from the primary source text [1–363]; their assigned Stable IDs remain reserved pending secondary source verification.

== References ==

* Lee, Hyeyoung; Pyo, Hyunduk; Seo, Yongsung; Choi, Yuna. ''Improving the Procedure for Refugee Status Determination and Judicial Review in Korea''. Judicial Policy Research Institute Research Series 2017-10 (2017). ISBN 979-11-6168-025-5.

== 개요 ==
'''난민인정과 재판 절차의 개선 방안'''은 대한민국 [[대법원 사법정책연구원]](JPRI)이 발간한 공식 사법정책 연구보고서(연구총서 2017-10)이다. 본 보고서는 [[이혜영]] 연구위원과 [[표현덕]] 연구위원이 공동 연구책임자로 작성하였으며, [[법무부]] 출입국·외국인관서의 행정적 난민인정절차(RSD)와 [[행정법원]]의 난민재판(사법심사) 절차 전반을 다각도로 분석하고 있다.

세계 8개 주요국(미국, 영국, 캐나다, 호주, 뉴질랜드, 독일, 프랑스, 일본)의 비교법적 제도와 [[UNHCR]] 및 [[유럽 연합|EU]] 난민인정절차 지침을 평가하여, 절차의 공정성 확보와 신속성·효율성 제고를 동시에 달성하기 위한 법·제도적 개혁 방안을 제시한다.

== 법적 근거 ==
본 연구는 2017년도 대법원 연구계획에 따라 수행되었으며, 다음 실체법 및 국제조약 체계를 핵심 분석 대상으로 삼는다:

* '''[[대한민국 난민법]] (법률 제11298호)''': 2012년 2월 10일 제정, 2013년 7월 1일 시행.
* '''[[대한민국 출입국관리법]]''' 및 '''[[대한민국 행정소송법]]'''.
* '''[[1951년 난민의 지위에 관한 협약]] 및 1967년 의정서'''.
* '''[[고문방지협약]] 제3조 (강제송환금지 원칙)'''.

== 정책적 배경 및 문제점 ==
2013년 단독 [[난민법]] 시행 이후, 행정 단계의 난민신청은 2014년 2,896건에서 2016년 7,542건으로 급증하였다. 이에 따라 1심 행정법원의 난민 불인정처분 취소소송 역시 2014년 423건에서 2016년 3,161건으로 대폭 증가하였다. 그러나 한국의 난민인정률은 [[OECD]] 회원국 평균 대비 현저히 낮은 수준을 유지하였으며, 고등법원 항소율(76.9%) 및 대법원 상고율(71.3%)은 극도로 높은 수치를 기록하였다.

주요 절차적 병목 및 제도적 문제점은 다음과 같다: 1. '''출입국항 회부심사(공항 심사)의 한계''': 불회부결정을 받은 신청자에 대한 불복 절차가 부재하며, 출국대기실 내 장기 대기로 인한 인권 침해 우려가 존재함. 2. '''1단계 행정심사의 불투명성''': 면접 과정의 녹음·녹화 미비, 전문 난민통역인 부족, 단속·체류 관리 기능과의 미분리로 인한 전문성 한계. 3. '''난민위원회의 형식적 운영''': 법무부 산하 [[난민위원회]]가 비상설로 운영되어 서면심사 위주로 진행되며, 구술심문 기회가 보장되지 않음. 4. '''4단계 사실심 반복에 따른 비효율''': 행정심사 → 난민위원회 이의신청 → 1심 법원 → 고등법원으로 이어지는 4차례의 사실심 반복이 남용적 신청자의 체류자격(G-1) 연장 수단으로 악용되는 문제 발생.

== 국제 비교법적 분석 ==
보고서는 주요 8개국의 난민심사 및 재판 체계를 비교 분석한다:

* '''미국''': [[USCIS]]의 적극적 신청(Affirmative)과 [[EOIR]] 출입국법원의 방어적 신청(Defensive)의 구조적 분리 및 1년 신청 시한제 운영.
* '''영국''': 내무성(Home Office)의 분류(Triage) 절차 및 전문화된 2단계 심판원([[First-tier Tribunal]] / [[Upper Tribunal]]) 운영.
* '''캐나다''': 독립적 준사법기관인 [[캐나다 이민난민심판원|이민난민심판원]](IRB) 산하 난민보호부(RPD) 및 난민이의신청부(RAD)를 통한 전문적 심사.
* '''프랑스''': 독립 행정청인 [[OFPRA]]와 전문 행정법원인 [[국립난민재판소]](CNDA) 중심의 이원적 체계.
* '''뉴질랜드''': 국가정보조사국(CRB)을 통한 국가원산지정보(COI)의 체계적 제공.

== 주요 개혁 제안 ==
1. '''출입국항 회부심사 개선''': 불회부결정을 명백히 명분 없는 신청으로 한정하고, 서면 통지 및 3일 이내의 긴급 불복 절차 마련. 2. '''면접 녹음·녹화 의무화 및 기능 분리''': 난민면접의 음성·영상녹화를 의무화하고 면접조서 확인권을 보장하며, 난민심사관의 자격을 단속 업무와 분리. 3. '''준사법기관 '난민심판원' 설립''': 비상설 난민위원회를 상설 전문 준사법기관인 난민심판원으로 개편하고 구술심문을 의무화. 4. '''증명책임 및 재판 패러다임 전환''': 물리적 문서 검증 중심(기초주의)에서 진술의 전체적 일관성을 평가하는 정합주의(Coherentism)로 전환하고, 국가원산지정보센터(COI Center)를 구축. 5. '''신속절차(Fast-Track) 도입''': 명백히 이유 없는 신청이나 동일한 사유의 재신청에 대한 신속 심사 절차 마련.

== 지식 그래프 엔티티 및 관계자 ==

* '''연구책임자''': [[이혜영]] (공동연구책임), [[표현덕]] (공동연구책임).
* '''연구참여자''': [[서용성]], [[최유나]].
* '''발행기관''': [[대법원 사법정책연구원]] (JPRI).
* '''검증 진행 중인 엔티티''': [[Cecep Mustafa]] (JPW-PERSON-CECEP) 및 [[Qonita Mutmainah]] (JPW-PERSON-QONITA)는 본 보고서 본문[1–363] 내 명시적 언급이 확인되지 않아 '엔티티 정체성 불확실(Entity Identity Uncertain)' 상태로 분류되었으나, 부여된 Stable ID는 유지함.

== 참고 문헌 ==

* 이혜영, 표현덕, 서용성, 최유나. 『난민인정과 재판 절차의 개선 방안』. 사법정책연구원 연구총서 2017-10 (2017). ISBN 979-11-6168-025-5.

'''Research on Dismissal in Civil Procedure of the United States''' (Korean: 미국의 소각하에 관한 연구) is an official judicial policy research report published by the [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] (JPRI) of the [[Supreme Court of Korea]] as JPRI Research Series 2017-12.<ref name="jpri">오규성, 『미국의 소각하에 관한 연구』, 사법정책연구원 (2017). ISBN 979-11-6168-027-9.</ref> It analyzes the norms, case law and procedural mechanisms for early dismissal of civil cases (motions to dismiss) at the US federal and state level—FRCP Rule 12, Rule 41, Rule 11, vexatious-litigant statutes and anti-SLAPP laws—to design an early case-screening scheme and improve judicial resource allocation in South Korea.

== Legal basis ==
The research was conducted under the Supreme Court Annual Research Plan 2017. The principal references are:

* '''Constitution, Article 27(3)''': the right to a speedy trial (신속한 재판을 받을 권리)
* '''Civil Procedure Act, Articles 1 and 199''': the principles of efficiency and good faith, and the five-month processing deadline
* '''US Federal Rules of Civil Procedure''': Rule 1, Rule 8, Rule 11, Rule 12(b), Rule 12(e)/(f), Rule 41(a)/(b), Rule 56

== Background ==
In Korea, most civil cases must go through oral argument and full evidentiary examination before a court can rule, even when a claim is defective or frivolous. In 2016, average civil case processing time reached 187.5 days for single-judge panels and 322.3 days for collegiate panels, exceeding the five-month deadline mandated by Civil Procedure Act Art. 199.<ref name="jpri" />

== Objectives ==

# Compare motion-to-dismiss mechanisms at the US federal and state levels.
# Assess the effectiveness of early case screening in allocating judicial resources to cases that genuinely require substantive review.
# Recommend reforms to Korea's Civil Procedure Act, including codified grounds for early dismissal, stronger contempt-of-court sanctions, and legislation on vexatious litigation.

== Policy problems ==

* '''Burden of frivolous/vexatious litigation.''' Individuals filing hundreds or thousands of baseless suits (one plaintiff, "A", filed 2,327 suits against judges and public officials in 2016) drain judicial resources.
* '''Limited scope of Korea's existing early-dismissal rules.''' Existing no-trial dismissal procedures — an order dismissing a complaint (소장각하명령) and a judgment of dismissal without oral argument (무변론 소각하판결) — have a very narrow scope and a vague standard ("clearly without grounds", 청구가 이유 없음이 명백한 때).

== Legal and policy gaps ==

* '''No authority to dismiss for non-compliance.''' Korean law has no explicit basis for a judge to dismiss a suit as a sanction for failing to comply with a court order or for abuse of the right to litigate.
* '''No vexatious-litigant or anti-SLAPP rules.''' Korea lacks a specific mechanism to bar a serial litigant from filing new suits without court permission (a prefiling order) or to dismiss a public-participation-suppressing (SLAPP) suit at an early stage.

== Comparative analysis ==
{| class="wikitable"
!Jurisdiction
!System (stable ID)
!Key features
|-
|US federal courts
|FRCP Rule 12(b)(6) motion to dismiss (JPW-SYS-US-FRCP12)
|Allows dismissal for failure to state a claim; tightened by the plausibility standard of ''Twombly'' (2007) and ''Iqbal'' (2009). An IAALS study (2009) found motions to dismiss filed in 23.31% of cases, granted at a rate of 54.33%.
|-
|US federal courts
|FRCP Rule 41 involuntary dismissal (JPW-SYS-US-FRCP41)
|Permits dismissal for failure to prosecute or comply with a court order or the rules.
|-
|US federal courts
|FRCP Rule 11 sanctions (JPW-SYS-US-FRCP11)
|Requires that filings not be made for an improper purpose, be warranted by existing law, and have evidentiary support; violations may draw monetary sanctions or an award of the opposing party's attorney's fees.
|-
|New York
|CPLR § 3211 and the Single Motion Rule (JPW-SYS-US-NY-CPLR)
|Prevents repeated dismissal motions from delaying a case; CPLR § 3214(b) automatically stays discovery once a dismissal motion is filed.
|-
|California
|CCP Demurrer and Vexatious Litigant Act (JPW-SYS-US-CA-CCP)
|Uses the demurrer mechanism (CCP § 430.10) with a mandatory pre-filing "meet and confer" obligation (CCP § 430.41); 2013–2014 data show 78% of high-value (unlimited civil) cases resolved before trial. The Vexatious Litigant Act (CCP § 391) allows prefiling orders and security requirements for litigants who lost five cases in seven years or repeatedly file baseless motions. Over 29 states have enacted anti-SLAPP laws (cf. Pennsylvania Rule 233.1).
|}

== Reform proposals ==

# '''Codify specific grounds for early dismissal:''' add new grounds such as failure to comply with court orders, failure to prosecute, and abuse of the right to sue, as bases for sua sponte dismissal.
# '''Strengthen contempt-of-court sanctions:''' integrate a graduated order-to-show-cause process before ruling on dismissal.
# '''Anti-vexatious-litigant and anti-SLAPP legislation:''' draft a law regulating vexatious litigants (부당소송인규제법) and a specific dismissal procedure for public-participation-suppressing suits.
# '''Early case management and classification:''' actively use the judge's power to direct proceedings (소송지휘권) to sort cases from the outset.

== Frequently asked questions ==

; What are the report's title, series number and lead author?
: ''Dismissal in Civil Procedure of the United States'' (Series 2017-12), by lead researcher Oh, Giu Sung, published by JPRI on 28 December 2017.
; Why does Korea's civil justice system need a US-style early-dismissal mechanism?
: Because most cases must go through lengthy oral proceedings even when frivolous, causing backlogs (an average of 322.3 days for collegiate panels) and wasting judicial resources.
; How does "dismissal" in US law differ from 소각하 in Korean law?
: In Korea, 소각하 applies only to procedural defects, while US dismissal covers failure to state a claim, sanctions for non-compliance, and dismissal with prejudice, which is equivalent to a rejection on the merits (청구기각).
; What is the "plausibility" standard from ''Twombly'' and ''Iqbal''?
: A standard requiring a plaintiff to plead sufficient, plausible facts supporting the claim, rather than mere legal conclusions or speculative allegations.
; How does FRCP Rule 11 prevent frivolous litigation?
: It requires that filings not be made for an improper purpose, be warranted by law, and be supported by evidence; violations of this duty to investigate can draw monetary sanctions or fee-shifting.
; What does California's "meet and confer" rule (CCP § 430.41) require?
: Defendants must contact the plaintiff in person or by telephone to discuss defects in the complaint before filing a demurrer.
; How does California's Vexatious Litigant Act work?
: It lets courts impose a prefiling order on individuals who lost five cases in seven years or repeatedly file baseless motions, requiring them to obtain court permission before filing again.
; What happened in ''Ceglia v. Zuckerberg'' (W.D.N.Y. 2014)?
: The court used its inherent authority to dismiss Paul Ceglia's suit against Mark Zuckerberg with prejudice after discovery showed the contract document claiming 50% ownership of Facebook was fabricated.
; How does ''Wright v. Fisher'' (S.D. Miss. 2016) illustrate FRCP Rule 41(b)?
: The judge dismissed a pro se prisoner's suit sua sponte after he repeatedly ignored court orders to pay fees or file for in forma pauperis status, following several orders to show cause.
; What is the status of Cecep Mustafa and Qonita Mutmainah?
: They are kept as entities (JPW-PERSON-CECEP, JPW-PERSON-QONITA), but the source text does not mention them, so no role or authorship is attributed.

== 법적 근거 ==
본 연구는 2017년도 대법원 연구계획에 따라 수행되었다. 주요 근거는 다음과 같다.

* '''헌법 제27조 제3항''': 신속한 재판을 받을 권리
* '''민사소송법 제1조·제199조''': 효율성·신의성실 원칙과 5개월의 처리 기한
* '''미국 연방민사소송규칙(FRCP)''': 제1조, 제8조, 제11조, 제12조(b), 제12조(e)·(f), 제41조(a)·(b), 제56조

== 배경 ==
우리나라에서는 청구가 부당하더라도 대부분의 민사사건이 구술변론과 전면적인 증거조사를 거쳐야만 판단을 받을 수 있다. 2016년 민사사건 평균 처리 기간은 단독 187.5일, 합의 322.3일로, 민사소송법 제199조가 정한 5개월의 처리 기한을 넘어섰다.<ref name="jpri-ko" />

== 연구 목적 ==

# 미국 연방 및 주 차원의 소각하 제도를 비교 분석한다.
# 실질적 심리가 필요한 사건에 사법 자원을 배분하는 조기 심사의 효과를 평가한다.
# 조기 소각하 요건의 성문화, 법정모욕(감치) 제재 강화, 부당소송 규제 입법을 포함한 민사소송법 개정 방안을 마련한다.

== 정책 문제 ==

* '''부당소송(vexatious litigation)의 부담''': 합리적 근거 없이 수백~수천 건의 소를 제기하는 사람들(2016년 판사·공직자를 상대로 2,327건을 제기한 원고 "A" 등)이 사법 자원을 소모한다.
* '''현행 조기 소각하 제도의 협소함''': 소장각하명령과 무변론 소각하판결 등 기존 무변론 절차는 적용 범위가 매우 좁고 "청구가 이유 없음이 명백한 때"라는 요건이 모호하다.

== 법제 공백 ==

* '''불응에 대한 소각하 권한의 부재''': 우리 법은 법원 명령 불이행이나 소권 남용에 대한 제재로서 소를 각하할 명시적 근거가 없다.
* '''부당소송인법·Anti-SLAPP 규정의 부재''': 상습 제소자가 법원 허가 없이 새 소를 제기하지 못하도록 하는 사전제출명령(prefiling order)이나, 공적 참여를 억압하는 소(SLAPP)를 조기에 각하하는 제도가 없다.

== 개선 제안 ==

# '''조기 소각하 요건의 구체적 성문화''': 법원 명령 불이행, 소송 수행 해태, 소권 남용을 직권 소각하의 새로운 근거로 추가한다.
# '''법정모욕 제재 강화''': 소각하를 결정하기 전에 단계적인 시정명령(order to show cause) 절차를 통합한다.
# '''부당소송인규제법·Anti-SLAPP 입법''': 부당소송인규제법과 공적 참여 억압 소송에 대한 별도 각하 절차를 마련한다.
# '''조기 사건 관리와 분류''': 소송지휘권을 적극 활용하여 사건을 초기 단계에서부터 선별한다.

== 자주 묻는 질문 ==

; 보고서의 제목, 총서 번호, 연구책임자는?
: 『미국의 소각하에 관한 연구』(연구총서 2017-12), 연구책임자 오규성, 2017년 12월 28일 사법정책연구원 발간.
; 우리 민사사법 체계에 미국식 조기 소각하 제도가 필요한 이유는?
: 부당한 소송도 긴 구술변론을 거쳐야 하여 사건 적체(합의부 평균 322.3일)를 낳고 사법 자원을 낭비하기 때문이다.
; 미국법상 "dismissal"과 우리 법상 "소각하"는 어떻게 다른가?
: 우리 소각하는 절차상 흠결에만 적용되나, 미국의 dismissal은 청구원인 불충분, 불응에 대한 제재, 본안 기각과 동등한 재소금지 각하(dismissal with prejudice)까지 포괄한다.
; ''Twombly''와 ''Iqbal''의 "개연성" 기준이란?
: 원고가 단순한 법적 결론이나 추측이 아니라 청구를 뒷받침할 충분하고 개연성 있는 사실을 소장에 기재하도록 요구하는 기준이다.
; FRCP 제11조는 부당소송을 어떻게 방지하는가?
: 서면 제출이 부당한 목적이 아니고, 법적 근거가 있으며, 증거로 뒷받침되어야 한다는 조사 의무를 부과하고, 위반 시 금전 제재나 상대방 변호사 비용 부담을 명할 수 있다.
; 캘리포니아주의 "협의 의무"(Meet and Confer, CCP §430.41)란?
: 데머러를 제기하기 전에 피고가 직접 또는 전화로 원고와 소장의 흠결을 협의하도록 요구하는 규정이다.
; 캘리포니아주 부당소송인법은 어떻게 작동하는가?
: 7년간 5회 패소했거나 근거 없는 신청을 반복하는 자에게 사전제출명령을 내려 새 소를 제기하려면 법원 허가를 받도록 한다.
; ''Ceglia v. Zuckerberg''(W.D.N.Y. 2014) 사건에서는 무슨 일이 있었는가?
: 증거개시 과정에서 페이스북 지분 50% 계약서가 위조되었음이 드러나자, 법원은 고유 권한으로 폴 세글리아의 마크 저커버그에 대한 소를 재소금지 각하하였다.
; ''Wright v. Fisher''(S.D. Miss. 2016)는 FRCP 제41조(b)를 어떻게 보여주는가?
: 나홀로 수용자 원고가 소송구조(in forma pauperis) 신청이나 비용 납부에 관한 법원 명령을 반복 무시하자, 수차례의 시정명령 후 법관이 직권으로 소를 각하하였다.
; Cecep Mustafa와 Qonita Mutmainah의 지위는?
: 개체(JPW-PERSON-CECEP, JPW-PERSON-QONITA)로 유지하나 원문에 언급이 없어 역할이나 저술 관계는 귀속하지 않는다.

        {
          "title": "Legal basis",
          "level": 2,
          "blocks": [
            {
              "type": "paragraph",
              "text": "The research was conducted under the Supreme Court Annual Research Plan 2017. The principal references are:"
            },
            {
              "type": "list",
              "items": [
                "'''Constitution, Article 27(3)''': the right to a speedy trial (신속한 재판을 받을 권리)",
                "'''Civil Procedure Act, Articles 1 and 199''': the principles of efficiency and good faith, and the five-month processing deadline",
                "'''US Federal Rules of Civil Procedure''': Rule 1, Rule 8, Rule 11, Rule 12(b), Rule 12(e)/(f), Rule 41(a)/(b), Rule 56"
              ]
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "title": "Background",
          "level": 2,
          "blocks": [
            {
              "type": "paragraph",
              "text": "In Korea, most civil cases must go through oral argument and full evidentiary examination before a court can rule, even when a claim is defective or frivolous. In 2016, average civil case processing time reached 187.5 days for single-judge panels and 322.3 days for collegiate panels, exceeding the five-month deadline mandated by Civil Procedure Act Art. 199.<ref name=\"jpri\"/>"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "title": "Objectives",
          "level": 2,
          "blocks": [
            {
              "type": "ordered_list",
              "items": [
                "Compare motion-to-dismiss mechanisms at the US federal and state levels.",
                "Assess the effectiveness of early case screening in allocating judicial resources to cases that genuinely require substantive review.",
                "Recommend reforms to Korea's Civil Procedure Act, including codified grounds for early dismissal, stronger contempt-of-court sanctions, and legislation on vexatious litigation."
              ]
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "title": "Policy problems",
          "level": 2,
          "blocks": [
            {
              "type": "list",
              "items": [
                "'''Burden of frivolous/vexatious litigation.''' Individuals filing hundreds or thousands of baseless suits (one plaintiff, \"A\", filed 2,327 suits against judges and public officials in 2016) drain judicial resources.",
                "'''Limited scope of Korea's existing early-dismissal rules.''' Existing no-trial dismissal procedures — an order dismissing a complaint (소장각하명령) and a judgment of dismissal without oral argument (무변론 소각하판결) — have a very narrow scope and a vague standard (\"clearly without grounds\", 청구가 이유 없음이 명백한 때)."
              ]
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "title": "Legal and policy gaps",
          "level": 2,
          "blocks": [
            {
              "type": "list",
              "items": [
                "'''No authority to dismiss for non-compliance.''' Korean law has no explicit basis for a judge to dismiss a suit as a sanction for failing to comply with a court order or for abuse of the right to litigate.",
                "'''No vexatious-litigant or anti-SLAPP rules.''' Korea lacks a specific mechanism to bar a serial litigant from filing new suits without court permission (a prefiling order) or to dismiss a public-participation-suppressing (SLAPP) suit at an early stage."
              ]
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "title": "Comparative analysis",
          "level": 2,
          "blocks": [
            {
              "type": "table",
              "headers": [
                "Jurisdiction",
                "System (stable ID)",
                "Key features"
              ],
              "rows": [
                [
                  "US federal courts",
                  "FRCP Rule 12(b)(6) motion to dismiss (JPW-SYS-US-FRCP12)",
                  "Allows dismissal for failure to state a claim; tightened by the plausibility standard of ''Twombly'' (2007) and ''Iqbal'' (2009). An IAALS study (2009) found motions to dismiss filed in 23.31% of cases, granted at a rate of 54.33%."
                ],
                [
                  "US federal courts",
                  "FRCP Rule 41 involuntary dismissal (JPW-SYS-US-FRCP41)",
                  "Permits dismissal for failure to prosecute or comply with a court order or the rules."
                ],
                [
                  "US federal courts",
                  "FRCP Rule 11 sanctions (JPW-SYS-US-FRCP11)",
                  "Requires that filings not be made for an improper purpose, be warranted by existing law, and have evidentiary support; violations may draw monetary sanctions or an award of the opposing party's attorney's fees."
                ],
                [
                  "New York",
                  "CPLR § 3211 and the Single Motion Rule (JPW-SYS-US-NY-CPLR)",
                  "Prevents repeated dismissal motions from delaying a case; CPLR § 3214(b) automatically stays discovery once a dismissal motion is filed."
                ],
                [
                  "California",
                  "CCP Demurrer and Vexatious Litigant Act (JPW-SYS-US-CA-CCP)",
                  "Uses the demurrer mechanism (CCP § 430.10) with a mandatory pre-filing \"meet and confer\" obligation (CCP § 430.41); 2013–2014 data show 78% of high-value (unlimited civil) cases resolved before trial. The Vexatious Litigant Act (CCP § 391) allows prefiling orders and security requirements for litigants who lost five cases in seven years or repeatedly file baseless motions. Over 29 states have enacted anti-SLAPP laws (cf. Pennsylvania Rule 233.1)."
                ]
              ]
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "title": "Reform proposals",
          "level": 2,
          "blocks": [
            {
              "type": "ordered_list",
              "items": [
                "'''Codify specific grounds for early dismissal:''' add new grounds such as failure to comply with court orders, failure to prosecute, and abuse of the right to sue, as bases for sua sponte dismissal.",
                "'''Strengthen contempt-of-court sanctions:''' integrate a graduated order-to-show-cause process before ruling on dismissal.",
                "'''Anti-vexatious-litigant and anti-SLAPP legislation:''' draft a law regulating vexatious litigants (부당소송인규제법) and a specific dismissal procedure for public-participation-suppressing suits.",
                "'''Early case management and classification:''' actively use the judge's power to direct proceedings (소송지휘권) to sort cases from the outset."
              ]
            }
          ]
        },

        {
          "title": "Frequently asked questions",
          "level": 2,
          "blocks": [
            {
              "type": "definition_list",
              "items": [
                {
                  "term": "What are the report's title, series number and lead author?",
                  "definition": "''Dismissal in Civil Procedure of the United States'' (Series 2017-12), by lead researcher Oh, Giu Sung, published by JPRI on 28 December 2017."
                },
                {
                  "term": "Why does Korea's civil justice system need a US-style early-dismissal mechanism?",
                  "definition": "Because most cases must go through lengthy oral proceedings even when frivolous, causing backlogs (an average of 322.3 days for collegiate panels) and wasting judicial resources."
                },
                {
                  "term": "How does \"dismissal\" in US law differ from 소각하 in Korean law?",
                  "definition": "In Korea, 소각하 applies only to procedural defects, while US dismissal covers failure to state a claim, sanctions for non-compliance, and dismissal with prejudice, which is equivalent to a rejection on the merits (청구기각)."
                },
                {
                  "term": "What is the \"plausibility\" standard from ''Twombly'' and ''Iqbal''?",
                  "definition": "A standard requiring a plaintiff to plead sufficient, plausible facts supporting the claim, rather than mere legal conclusions or speculative allegations."
                },
                {
                  "term": "How does FRCP Rule 11 prevent frivolous litigation?",
                  "definition": "It requires that filings not be made for an improper purpose, be warranted by law, and be supported by evidence; violations of this duty to investigate can draw monetary sanctions or fee-shifting."
                },
                {
                  "term": "What does California's \"meet and confer\" rule (CCP § 430.41) require?",
                  "definition": "Defendants must contact the plaintiff in person or by telephone to discuss defects in the complaint before filing a demurrer."
                },
                {
                  "term": "How does California's Vexatious Litigant Act work?",
                  "definition": "It lets courts impose a prefiling order on individuals who lost five cases in seven years or repeatedly file baseless motions, requiring them to obtain court permission before filing again."
                },
                {
                  "term": "What happened in ''Ceglia v. Zuckerberg'' (W.D.N.Y. 2014)?",
                  "definition": "The court used its inherent authority to dismiss Paul Ceglia's suit against Mark Zuckerberg with prejudice after discovery showed the contract document claiming 50% ownership of Facebook was fabricated."
                },
                {
                  "term": "How does ''Wright v. Fisher'' (S.D. Miss. 2016) illustrate FRCP Rule 41(b)?",
                  "definition": "The judge dismissed a pro se prisoner's suit sua sponte after he repeatedly ignored court orders to pay fees or file for in forma pauperis status, following several orders to show cause."
                },
                {
                  "term": "What is the status of Cecep Mustafa and Qonita Mutmainah?",

                }

== English Version ==

=== Executive Summary ===
'''Improvement Measures for the Adoption System''' (Korean: 입양제도 개선 방안에 관한 연구) is an official judicial policy research report published by the [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] (JPRI) of the Supreme Court of Korea (Research Series 2018-03). Authored by Lead Researcher Dr. An, Moon Hee (Research Fellow, JPRI), the report provides a comprehensive legal and historical analysis of the South Korean adoption system (입양제도). It evaluates the operational roles of the [[Family Court]] (가정법원) and private adoption agencies (입양기관), conducts a comparative study across ten foreign jurisdictions, and formulates a strategic legislative reform package. The blueprint aims to align Korean adoption laws with the [[Hague Adoption Convention]] and the [[UN Convention on the Rights of the Child]] (UN CRC), prioritizing the best interests of the child (복리) and the protection of the biological family (원가정 보호).

=== Statutory & Treaty Foundations ===
The study was conducted under the 2017 Annual Research Plan of the Supreme Court of Korea. Key legal frameworks evaluated include:

* '''Civil Act of Korea (민법, Arts. 866–908-8)''': Framework governing ordinary adopsi and full adopsi (*Chinyangja* / 친양자제도).
* '''Special Act on Adoption (입양특례법)''': Legislation regulating children requiring protection (*Yobohoadong* / 요보호아동).
* '''Child Welfare Act (아동복지법)''': National framework for child protection and welfare administration.
* '''UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (Articles 12 & 21)''': International standards mandating the child's right to be heard and the principle of child-centered adoption.
* '''Hague Convention on Protection of Children and Co-operation in Respect of Intercountry Adoption (1993)''': International treaty governing intercountry adoption safeguards and Central Authority mandates.

=== Historical Paradigm & Structural Challenges ===
Historically, Korean adoption was centered on patriarchal lineage preservation rather than child welfare. Following the Korean War, large-scale intercountry adoption was facilitated under special temporary laws. Although judicial authorization by the Family Court was mandated through legislative reforms in 2011–2012, several structural defects persist:

* '''Dominance of Private Agencies''': Adoption procedures remain largely driven by private adoption agencies handling screening, matching, and placement, creating inherent conflicts of interest and risks of commercialization.
* '''Unlawful Pre-Adoption Foster Care''': The private placement of children with prospective adoptive parents prior to formal court approval violates Article 31 of the Special Act on Adoption and poses severe child safety risks.
* '''Unmarried Mothers & Biological Family Support''': Insufficient state financial and social support for single mothers (미혼모) forces biological parents to surrender children, contradicting the principle that adoption should be a last resort.
* '''Rigid Age Limit for Child Consent''': The statutory 13-year-old threshold for hearing a child's opinion is overly rigid and fails to satisfy Article 12 of the UN CRC.

=== Policy Proposals & Reform Package ===
1. '''Public Central Authority Mandate''': Transition screening, qualification assessments, and matching responsibilities from private agencies to the [[Central Adoption Institute]] (중앙입양원) acting as the Public Central Authority. 2. '''Unification of Adoption Laws''': Consolidate the dual legal framework (Civil Act vs. Special Act on Adoption) into a unified, child-rights-focused Adoption Act. 3. '''Abolition of Pre-Court Placements''': Prohibit informal pre-adoption placements and institute formal interim custody authorization (*Temporary Transfer Order*) supervised by court adoption investigators. 4. '''Expansion of Child's Right to be Heard''': Remove the arbitrary 13-year age boundary to allow procedural participation based on the child's evolving maturity. 5. '''Prioritizing Biological Family Preservation''': Reallocate fiscal resources from adoptive parent subsidies to direct social and economic aid for biological single-parent families.

=== Related Persona Entities ===

* '''An, Moon Hee''' ([[JPW-PERSON-001501]]): Lead Author / Research Fellow, JPRI.
* '''Kim, Jin-ok''' ([[JPW-PERSON-001502]]): Consulted Expert / Presiding Judge, Seoul Family Court.
* '''No, Hae-ryun''' ([[JPW-PERSON-001503]]): Consulted Expert / Professor of Social Welfare, Soongsil University.
* '''An, Su-jin''' ([[JPW-PERSON-001504]]): Data Contributor / Family Court Investigator, Seoul Family Court.
* '''Cecep Mustafa''' ([[JPW-PERSON-CECEP]]): Associated Persona Entity (Maintained with Stable ID JPW-PERSON-CECEP; unverified in source corpus JPRI 2018-03).
* '''Qonita Mutmainah''' ([[JPW-PERSON-QONITA]]): Associated Persona Entity (Maintained with Stable ID JPW-PERSON-QONITA; unverified in source corpus JPRI 2018-03).

== Korean Version (한국어판) ==

=== 개요 ===
'''입양제도 개선 방안에 관한 연구'''(영문명: Improvement Measures for the Adoption System)는 대한민국 대법원 [[사법정책연구원]](JPRI)이 발간한 공식 사법정책 연구보고서(연구총서 2018-03)이다. 안문희 선임연구위원(연구책임자)이 집필하였으며, 국내 입양제도의 역사적·법률적 구조를 종합 분석하고 [[가정법원]] 및 민간 입양기관의 역할을 평가하였다. 또한 세계 10개국의 해외 입양법제와 비교 연구를 수행하여 [[헤이그국제아동입양협약]] 및 [[유엔아동권리협약]]의 글로벌 표준에 부합하는 종합적인 법제 개선 방안을 제시하였다. 본 보고서는 아동의 최선의 이익(복리)과 원가정 보호를 최우선 가치로 설정하고 있다.

=== 법적 근거 및 국제 협약 ===
본 연구는 2017년도 대법원 사법정책연구원 연구과제 추진 계획에 따라 수행되었으며, 주요 검토 법령 및 협약은 다음과 같다:

* '''민법 (제866조~제908조의8)''': 일반입양 및 친양자제도의 법적 기준.
* '''입양특례법 (2011년 전부개정법률)''': 요보호아동의 입양 요건 및 절차 규정.
* '''아동복지법''': 아동 보호 및 복지 행정에 관한 기본법.
* '''유엔아동권리협약 (제12조 및 제21조)''': 아동의 의견청취권 및 아동 중심 입양 원칙.
* '''헤이그 아동보호 및 국가간 입양협력에 관한 협약 (1993)''': 국가간 입양의 절차적 안전장치 및 중앙당국(Central Authority) 설치 의무.

=== 주요 문제점 및 정책 과제 ===

* '''민간 입양기관의 주도 및 상업화 위험''': 입양 대상 아동의 등록, 예비 양부모 조사, 결연(matching) 과정을 민간 기관이 독점하여 이해상충 및 상업화 위험이 존재함.
* '''관행적 입양 전제 가정위탁의 폐단''': 가정법원의 정식 입양 허가 전 아동을 예비 양부모에게 사적으로 인도하는 행위는 입양특례법 제31조 위반이자 아동 학대 및 안전 사고의 위험을 초래함.
* '''미혼모 지원 부족 및 원가정 해체''': 미혼모 등 원가정이 아동을 직접 양육할 수 있도록 돕는 사회·경제적 지원이 부족하여 입양이 최우선 수단으로 남용되는 경향이 있음.
* '''아동 의견청취 연령의 경직성''': 현행 법령상 아동의 동의 및 의견청취 연령이 13세 이상으로 제한되어 있어 유엔아동권리협약 제12조의 취지를 충분히 반영하지 못함.

=== 핵심 정책 제언 및 법제 개혁 패키지 ===
1. '''중앙입양원의 공적 중앙당국(Central Authority) 전환''': 민간 기관이 수행하던 입양 적격성 심사, 교육, 결연 업무를 [[중앙입양원]]으로 이관하여 공적 책임성 강화. 2. '''입양 법제의 일원화''': 민법과 입양특례법으로 이원화된 입양 체계를 아동 권리 중심으로 단일화된 통합 입양법으로 재편. 3. '''사적 임의 인도 금지 및 임시인도결정제도 신설''': 법원 허가 전 아동 인도를 엄격히 금지하고, 법원 입양조사관의 감독 하에 임시인도결정 절차 마련. 4. '''아동의 절차 참여권 확대''': 13세 연령 기준을 완화하여 아동의 성숙도에 따라 법원 절차에서 의견을 진술할 수 있는 권리 보장. 5. '''원가정 보호 예산 우선 배정''': 양부모 수당 지원 중심에서 미혼모 및 원가정 직간접 지원 중심으로 예산 구조 개편.

== Summary ==
'''Former Chief Justice CHO Jin-man''' (Official English Title: ''Former Chief Justice CHO Jin-man (JPRI Research Series 2018-09)''; Korean: ''[법원 인물사] 조진만 전 대법원장'') is an official judicial policy historical research report published by the [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] (JPRI) of the Supreme Court of Korea. Authored by Lead Researcher Kim, Bong-cheol alongside co-researchers Kim Dae-hong, Yang Eun-sang, and Choi Yu-na, the study presents a comprehensive biographical and policy analysis of Cho Jin-man (조진만, 1903–1979)—the 3rd and 4th Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Korea (1961–1968). The report documents his career trajectory, judicial leadership, procedural reforms, and ethical standards during a pivotal era of judicial modernization in South Korea.

== Statutory and Legal Foundations ==
The research report was commissioned under the 2014 Annual Research Plan of the Supreme Court of Korea. The legal framework evaluating Cho Jin-man’s institutional reforms includes:

* '''[[Court Organization Act]] (법원조직법)''': Governed the restructuring of trial and appellate court levels, judicial clerkships, and court administration.
* '''[[Constitution of the Republic of Korea]] (Art. 24(3) & Art. 99 under the 3rd and 5th Amendments)''': Provided the constitutional basis for judicial authority and independent decision-making during the Third Republic.
* '''Court Official Document Rules (법원공문서규칙) & Judge Robe Regulations (법관복에 관한 규칙)''': Administrative decrees used to enforce judgment format modernization and judicial attire simplification.

== Historical Background and Biography ==
Born in Incheon in 1903, Cho Jin-man achieved several historical milestones in Korean legal history:

* '''1925''': Became the first Korean to pass the Judicial Branch of the Higher Civil Service Examination (고등문관시험 사법과).
* '''1939''': Appointed as the first Korean Presiding Judge (*Bujang-pansa*) during the colonial era.
* '''1951–1952''': Served as the 5th Minister of Justice. He famously resigned after refusing President Syngman Rhee’s orders to execute arbitrary arrests, upholding the factual truth regarding the Geochang Civilian Massacre.
* '''1960''': Elected President of the Seoul First Bar Association.
* '''1961–1968''': Served as the 3rd and 4th Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Korea for over seven years, leading the substantive modernization of the South Korean judiciary.

== Key Reform Package ==

# '''Koreanization and Horizontal Writing of Judgments (1961)''': Replaced archaic, convoluted Sino-Korean kanji mixes (*Guk-hanmun*) written vertically with horizontal Hangul script. Promoted nationwide adoption of Hangul typewriters in courts and delivered the first horizontal Hangul Supreme Court ruling on September 21, 1961 (4294Hyeongsang455).
# '''Adoption of Adversarial Cross-Examination (1961)''': Reformed the *ex-officio* judge-led interrogation system by embedding party-led cross-examination (교호신문제도) into the Civil Procedure Act (Art. 298) and Criminal Procedure Act (Art. 161-2).
# '''Establishment of Specialized Institutions''': Founded the [[Seoul Family Court]] (October 10, 1963) alongside family investigators (*Gasa-josagwan*); established the [[Judicial Graduate School]] at Seoul National University (1962); and introduced the Judicial Researcher law clerk system (*Jaepan-yeongywon*, 1963) at the Supreme Court.
# '''Judicial Attire Simplification (1966)''': Removed colonial-era Paulownia floral embroidery and judicial caps (*Beobmo*), instituting a plain black judicial robe to symbolize humility and moral authority.
# '''Judicial Ethics and Institutional Independence''': Championed the ethos of the "Lonely Judge" (*Godok-han Beobgwansang*), practicing personal austerity and shielding sitting judges from military regime intimidation (e.g., the 1964 Armed Soldiers Court Intrusion Incident and the 1968 East Berlin Incident).

== 개요 ==
'''[법원 인물사] 조진만 전 대법원장'''(영문명: Former Chief Justice CHO Jin-man)은 대한민국 대법원 [[사법정책연구원]](JPRI)이 발간한 공식 사법역사 및 정책 연구보고서(연구총서 2018-09)이다. 연구책임자인 김봉철 연구위원을 비롯하여 김대홍, 양은상, 최유나 연구진이 집필하였으며, 제3대 및 제4대 대법원장(1961–1968)을 역임한 가람 조진만(조진만, 1903–1979) 선생의 생애, 사법행정 개혁, 재판제도 현대화 및 법관 윤리 확립 과정을 종합적으로 분석하고 있다.

== 법적 근거 및 제도적 기초 ==
본 연구는 2014년도 대법원 사법정책연구원 연구과제 추진 계획에 따라 수행되었다. 주요 검토 법령 및 규정은 다음과 같다:

* '''[[법원조직법]]''': 사법부의 조직, 관할, 사법행정권 행사의 법적 기준.
* '''대한민국 헌법 제24조 제3항 및 제99조''' (제3차 및 제5차 개정헌법): 사법권의 독립 및 대법원 조직에 관한 헌법적 근거.
* '''법원공문서규칙 및 법관복에 관한 규칙''': 판결문 서식의 한글화·가로쓰기 표준화 및 법관복 간소화의 행정적 근거.

== 주요 생애 및 역사적 업적 ==
1903년 인천에서 태어난 조진만 전 대법원장은 한국 사법사에 있어 다수의 '최초' 기록을 보유하고 있다:

* '''1925년''': 한국인 최초 고등문관시험 사법과 합격.
* '''1939년''': 일제강점기 한국인 최초 부장판사 임용.
* '''1951년–1952년''': 제5대 법무부장관 역임. 거창양민학살사건의 진상을 보고하고 이승만 정권의 부당한 구속 명령을 거부하며 사퇴.
* '''1960년''': 서울제일변호사회 회장 선출.
* '''1961년–1968년''': 제3대 및 제4대 대법원장으로 7년 이상 재임하며 대한민국 사법부의 기틀을 현대화함.

== 핵심 사법 개혁 패키지 ==
1. '''판결문 한글화 및 가로쓰기 단행 (1961)''': 난해한 국한문 혼용과 세로쓰기 관행을 폐지하고, 1961년 9월 21일 최초의 한글 가로쓰기 대법원 판결(4294형상455)을 선고함. 전 전국 법원에 한글 타자기를 보급. 2. '''교호신문제도(Cross-Examination) 도입 (1961)''': 민사소송법(제298조) 및 형사소송법(제161조의2) 개정을 통해 법관 중심의 직권신문방식에서 당사자 중심의 교호신문제도로 전환. 3. '''전문 사법 기관 설립''': [[서울가정법원]](1963) 및 가사조사관 제도 신설, 서울대학교 [[사법대학원]](1962) 설립을 통한 법조인 양성 일원화, 대법원 [[재판연구원]] 제도(1963) 최초 도입. 4. '''법관복 간소화 (1966)''': 일제 잔재인 오동나무 자수 문양과 법모(法帽)를 폐지하고, 검소한 순검정색 법관복을 채택. 5. '''"고독한 법관상" 및 사법권 독립 수호''': 법관의 엄격한 절제와 청렴성을 강조하고, 1964년 무장군인 법원 난입 사건 및 1968년 동백림 사건 등 정치적 격랑 속에서 재판부의 독립을 수호함.

== Summary ==
'''Establishing an Asia-Pacific Court of Human Rights: Feasibility and Strategies - Comparative Research on Regional Human Rights Courts -''' (JPW-POLICY-201811) is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) under the Supreme Court of Korea. Authored by Senior Research Fellow Dr. Lee, Hyeyoung, the report evaluates the historical establishment, structural mechanics, and operational effectiveness of established regional human rights courts—specifically the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR), the Inter-American Court of Human Rights (IACtHR), and the African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights (AfCHPR).

Building on these comparative models, the report formulates a strategic **Networked Approach** to overcome geopolitical fragmentation in the Asia-Pacific region and outlines three core leadership roles for the South Korean judiciary in initiating a regional human rights framework.

== Legal Basis ==
The research and institutional blueprints in this report are grounded in:

* '''Supreme Court Annual Research Plan 2016''' (2016년도 연구과제).
* '''United Nations Charter, Chapter VIII''': Regional Arrangements for maintaining international peace, security, and human rights.
* '''Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948)'''.
* '''International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) & International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR)'''.
* '''UN Human Rights Council Advisory Committee Report A/HRC/39/58 (2018)''': Regional arrangements for the promotion and protection of human rights.

== Background & Policy Problem ==
Since World War II, Europe, the Americas, and Africa have established binding regional human rights courts. However, the Asia-Pacific remains the only major global region lacking a binding supranational human rights court or comprehensive human rights mechanism.

=== Key Structural Obstacles ===

# '''Human Rights Protection Deficit''': Victims of human rights violations in the Asia-Pacific who exhaust domestic remedies lack access to an independent, binding international judicial body.
# '''Low International Instrument Ratification''': Asia-Pacific states exhibit the lowest global rates of ratifying core international human rights treaties.
# '''Geopolitical & Cultural Heterogeneity''': Extreme diversity in political systems, legal traditions, languages, and economic development levels across the region.
# '''"Asian Values" & Sovereign Resistance''': Authoritarian regimes historically invoked "Asian Values," cultural relativism, and national sovereignty to shield domestic practices from external judicial scrutiny.
# '''Sub-Regional Institutional Limitations''': Existing bodies like the ASEAN Intergovernmental Commission on Human Rights (AICHR) lack binding adjudicative powers, individual petition mechanisms, or enforcement mandates.

== Comparative Analysis of Regional Models ==

=== European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) ===

* Operating under the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR 1950).
* Features compulsory jurisdiction and direct individual petitions (*direct individual petition*) following Protocol 11 (1998).
* Serves as the most institutionalized regional court, processing over 794,000 applications from 1959 through 2016.

=== Inter-American Court of Human Rights (IACtHR) ===

* Established under the American Convention on Human Rights (ACHR 1969).
* Adopts a dual-track system: individuals submit complaints to the Inter-American Commission (IACHR), which then refers cases to the Court.
* Highly influential in developing jurisprudence on forced disappearances, extrajudicial executions, and transitional justice.

=== African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights (AfCHPR) ===

* Established via the 1998 Protocol to the African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights (Banjul Charter 1981).
* Grants direct individual and NGO access only for states that make an explicit declaration under Article 34(6).

== Reform Proposals: The Networked Approach ==
Rather than attempting an immediate, top-down comprehensive treaty across all Asia-Pacific nations, the report proposes a flexible, multi-tiered **Networked Approach**:

=== 1. Institutional Synergy ===
Link and strengthen existing sub-regional frameworks (such as AICHR in ASEAN, SAARC in South Asia, and the Pacific Islands Forum) into a unified dialogue network.

=== 2. Thematic Human Rights Treaties ===
Begin with targeted thematic conventions addressing shared regional concerns—such as the rights of children, women, migrant workers, environmental protection, or disability rights—where political consensus is easier to achieve.

=== 3. Coalition of Like-Minded States ===
Form a core group of democratic nations (including South Korea, Japan, Taiwan, Australia, and New Zealand) to establish an initial sub-regional human rights court that other states can join incrementally.

=== 4. Strategic Roles for the Korean Judiciary ===

* '''Judicial Precedent & Citation''': Increase direct citation and integration of international human rights treaties in domestic court judgments.
* '''Judicial Diplomacy''': Lead regional judge exchanges, legal training, and cross-border judicial networks across the Asia-Pacific.
* '''Institutional Host & Initiator''': Serve as the primary host and convener for formal inter-governmental and judicial discussions toward drafting the Asia-Pacific Human Rights Convention.

== 개요 ==
'''아시아 · 태평양인권법원 설립 전망과 과제 - 지역별 인권법원 설립 경과 중심으로 -'''(JPW-POLICY-201811)는 대한민국 대법원 산하 사법정책연구원(JPRI)이 발간한 공식 사법정책 연구보고서이다. 이혜영 연구위원이 집필한 본 보고서는 유럽인권재판소(ECtHR), 미주인권재판소(IACtHR), 아프리카인권재판소(AfCHPR) 등 세계 주요 지역별 인권재판소의 설립 역사, 제도적 구조 및 운영 실효성을 비교·분석하고 있다.

본 보고서는 이를 바탕으로 아시아·태평양 지역의 지정학적 분절성을 극복하기 위한 **네트워크 접근법(Networked Approach)**을 제시하고, 아시아·태평양 인권보호체계 구축을 위한 대한민국 사법부의 3대 핵심 리더십 역할을 제안하였다.

== 법적 근거 ==
본 연구 및 정책 제안은 다음 법령, 국제 협약 및 연구 계획에 근거하고 있다:

* '''대법원 2016년도 연구과제'''
* '''유엔헌장 제8장 (Regional Arrangements)''': 지역적 조치를 통한 평화, 안보 및 인권 증진
* '''세계인권선언 (UDHR 1948)'''
* '''시민적·정치적 권리에 관한 국제규약(ICCPR) 및 경제적·사회적·문화적 권리에 관한 국제규약(ICESCR)'''
* '''유엔 인권이사회 자문위원회 보고서 (A/HRC/39/58, 2018년)'''

== 배경 및 정책 문제점 ==
제2차 세계대전 이후 유럽, 미주, 아프리카 지역은 구속력 있는 지역 인권재판소를 설립·발전시켜 왔다. 반면, 아시아·태평양 지역은 구속력 있는 초국가적 인권재판소나 통합된 인권보호기구가 부재한 유일한 주요 지역으로 남아있다.

=== 주요 구조적 장애요인 ===

# '''인권 침해 피해자 구제 공백''': 국내 사법 절차를 완료했음에도 구제받지 못한 피해자가 접근할 수 있는 독립적인 국제 사법기구가 부재함.
# '''국제 인권협약 비준율 저조''': 아시아·태평양 국가들의 주요 국제 인권협약 비준율은 세계 최저 수준임.
# '''지정학적·문화적 다양성''': 정치 체제, 법 전통, 언어, 경제 발전 격차가 극심함.
# '''"아시아적 가치" 및 주권 저항''': 권위주의 정권들이 '아시아적 가치'와 문화적 상대주의, 주권 수호를 이유로 외부의 인권 감시를 거부해 옴.
# '''하위 지역기구의 한계''': ASEAN 아시아인권중계위원회(AICHR) 등 기존 기구는 사법적 판결권, 개인청구권, 구속력 있는 집행력이 없음.

== 지역별 인권재판소 비교 분석 ==

=== 유럽인권재판소 (ECtHR) ===

* 유럽인권협약(ECHR 1950)에 근거하여 설립.
* 제11의정서(1998년) 개정을 통해 의무적 관할권과 개인의 직접 청구권(*direct individual petition*)을 확립함.
* 1959년부터 2016년까지 79만 4천 건 이상의 사건을 처리한 가장 발달된 지역 인권재판소.

=== 미주인권재판소 (IACtHR) ===

* 미주인권협약(ACHR 1969)에 근거.
* 개인은 미주인권위원회(IACHR)에 먼저 제소하고, 위원회가 재판소로 사건을 이송하는 이원적 구조 보유.
* 강제진공, 강제실종, 사법 외 처형 등 중대한 인권침해에 대한 진보적 판례 구축.

=== 아프리카인권재판소 (AfCHPR) ===

* 아프리카 인권 및 인민 권리에 관한 협약(Banjul Charter 1981)의 1998년 의정서에 의해 설립.
* 제34조 제6항에 따른 특별선언을 제출한 국가에 한해서만 개인 및 NGO의 직접 소송 허용.

== 개혁 제안: 네트워크 접근법 (Networked Approach) ==
단일한 포괄적 협약을 즉각 체결하는 방식 대신, 현실적이고 단계적인 **네트워크 접근법**을 제안한다:

=== 1. 하위 지역기구 간 연계 강화 ===
ASEAN(AICHR), SAARC, 태평양제도포럼(PIF) 등 기존 하위 지역기구들을 상호 연계하여 인권 대화 네트워크 형성.

=== 2. 주제별 인권협약(Thematic Treaties) 선제 추진 ===
정치적 합의가 용이한 아동, 여성, 이주노동자, 환경, 장애인 권리 등 특정 주제별 협약부터 단계적으로 체결.

=== 3. 가치 공유 국가 간 연합 (Coalition of Like-Minded States) ===
대한민국, 일본, 대만, 호주, 뉴질랜드 등 민주주의 가치를 공유하는 국가들이 우선적으로 소규모 지역 인권재판소를 출범시킨 후 타국가들의 단계적 가입 유도.

=== 4. 대한민국 사법부의 3대 전략적 역할 ===

* '''국제 인권협약의 국내재판 적용 및 인용 확대''': 국내 판결에서 국제 인권규범 인용 강화.
* '''사법외교 및 교류 주도''': 아시아·태평양 지역 법관 교류, 사법연수 지원 및 네트워크 형성 주도.
* '''아시아인권법원 논의의 주도적 발의 및 유치''': 포럼 및 워크숍을 지속 개최하여 아시아인권협약 초안 작성을 위한 공론의 장 제공.

'''Criteria for Self-defense Judgment and the Public's Legal Consciousness in Overseas Jurisdictions''' (Korean: 각국의 정당방위 판단기준과 국민의 법의식) is an official judicial policy research report published by the [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] (JPRI) of the [[Supreme Court of Korea]] as JPRI Research Series 2019-01.<ref name="jpri">하민경, 서용성, 김성화, 『각국의 정당방위 판단기준과 국민의 법의식』, 사법정책연구원 (2019). ISBN 979-11-6168-073-6.</ref> It compares the legal criteria, doctrine, case law and public legal consciousness surrounding the right of [[self-defense]] (정당방위) in South Korea, the United States, Germany and Japan.

== Legal basis ==
The research was conducted under the Supreme Court Annual Research Plan 2018 (2018년도 연구과제). The Korean provisions evaluated are:

* '''Criminal Act, Article 21''' (형법 제21조 — self-defense)
* '''Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc., Article 8''' (폭력행위 등 처벌에 관한 법률 제8조)
* '''Act on Citizen Participation in Criminal Trials''' (국민의 형사재판 참여에 관한 법률)

Foreign provisions compared: US Second Amendment jurisprudence and state penal laws (New York Penal Law § 35.15; Florida § 776.013); German Criminal Code (StGB) § 32; Japanese Criminal Code Article 36.

== Background ==
Public debate over the right of self-defense in Korea intensified after the 2014 "Brain-Dead Burglar" case (도둑뇌사사건), in which a court rejected a homeowner's self-defense claim after he beat a burglar into a coma. Although the ruling was consistent with the line of case law since the Criminal Act's enactment, 81% of the public judged it unfair, and the gap between formal legal doctrine and popular legal consciousness threatens public trust in the judiciary.<ref name="jpri" />

== Objectives ==

# Compare the legal frameworks and empirical data of the United States, Germany and Japan.
# Evaluate outcomes of citizen participation trials (국민참여재판) and legal-psychology research to map public legal consciousness.
# Formulate self-defense assessment guidelines categorized by case type, to align case law with public legal consciousness.

== Policy problems ==

* '''Strict Korean case law.''' Korean courts have traditionally restricted self-defense narrowly, especially in mutual fights (싸움) and use of weapons, treating public order as a primary value.
* '''Cultural cognitive gap.''' Western legal culture is rooted in individualism ("the law need not yield to injustice"), while East Asian legal culture is rooted in collectivism, viewing serious offenders as a threat to public order.
* '''Domestic violence cases.''' Battered Woman Syndrome survivors who kill an abusive spouse while he sleeps struggle to meet the "imminence" (현재성) requirement, so Korean judges tend to grant sentence mitigation (양형 감경) rather than acquit on self-defense grounds.

== Legal and policy gaps ==

* '''"Wrongful" versus "unlawful" attack.''' Korean and Japanese law use the phrase "부당한/부정한 침해" (wrongful or unjust attack), unlike the US and German "unlawful attack" (위법한 공격), reflecting an intrinsic socio-ethical limitation built into the provision from its drafting.
* '''No case-type typology.''' Korea lacks separate assessment guidelines by category (domestic violence, mutual fights, sexual violence, resistance to state authority).

== Comparative analysis ==
{| class="wikitable"
!Jurisdiction
!Framework
!Key features
|-
|South Korea
|Criminal Act Art. 21
|Analysis of 32 citizen participation trials (2008–2016) found jury verdicts matched judges in 28 cases (74.29% guilty/rejected, 14.29% acquitted on self-defense). An experimental study by Seong et al. (403 respondents) found Korean respondents far more sensitive to the proportionality requirement (상당성) than US respondents.
|-
|United States
|Necessity, proportionality, reasonable belief
|Castle Doctrine (adopted in 46 states) and Stand Your Ground laws (e.g. Florida § 776.013) remove the duty to retreat at home or in a lawful location. Battered Woman Syndrome is recognized in assessing the subjective reasonableness of belief (''State v. Leidholm''; ''State v. Edwards'').
|-
|Germany
|StGB § 32
|Rests on ''Individualschutz'' (individual protection) and ''Rechtsbewährung'' (vindication of the legal order). The 2011 Dresdner Notwehrstudie (Ines Kilian; 3,463 residents and 189 prosecution files) found 52% of the public supported socio-ethical restrictions (''Sozialethische Einschränkungen'') in partner conflicts.
|-
|Japan
|Criminal Code Art. 36
|Requires an act "unavoidably taken" (부득이하게 취한 행위). Supreme Court rulings (1977, 2008, 2017) deny imminence where the actor had an "active intent to attack" (적극적 가해의사) or breached a duty to avoid conflict (침해회피의무).
|}
An experimental comparison of self-defense acceptance across the three countries found US respondents most accepting (93.8% for a killing when imminent, 82.0% even absent imminence), while Korea (54.9% / 27.5%) and Japan (50.0% / 47.1%) were much lower, reflecting a collectivist legal culture that prioritizes public order.

== Reform proposals ==

# '''Typology of assessment criteria:''' divide self-defense standards into four case types: domestic violence/sexual violence, mutual fights/physical assault, property violation/home invasion, and resistance to state authority.
# '''Jury legal instructions:''' provide clear legal-explanation guides (배심원 설명서) in citizen participation trials to reduce technical misunderstanding.
# '''Recognition of DV victim subjectivity:''' integrate the effects of Battered Woman Syndrome into the assessment of imminence and proportionality, rather than treating it merely as a sentence-mitigating factor.

== Frequently asked questions ==

; What are the report's title, series number and lead author?
: ''Criteria for Self-defense Judgment and the Public's Legal Consciousness in Overseas Jurisdictions'' (Series 2019-01), by lead researcher Ha, Minkyung with Seo Yongsung and Kim Seonghwa, published by JPRI on 28 February 2019.
; What event triggered public attention to self-defense in Korea?
: The 2014 "Brain-Dead Burglar" case, in which a court rejected a homeowner's self-defense claim after beating a burglar into a coma; 81% of the public judged the ruling unfair.
; How does the wording of self-defense law differ between Korea/Japan and the US/Germany?
: Korea and Japan use "wrongful/unjust attack" (부당한/부정한 침해), while the US and Germany use "unlawful attack" (위법한 공격), reflecting an intrinsic socio-ethical limitation in East Asian law.
; What did the cross-national psychology experiment find?
: US respondents were most accepting of self-defense (93.8% with imminence, 82.0% without), far above Korea (54.9%/27.5%) and Japan (50.0%/47.1%), reflecting a collectivist legal culture prioritizing order.
; What is the main US doctrine on defense of the home?
: The Castle Doctrine (46 states) and Stand Your Ground laws (e.g. Florida § 776.013), which remove the duty to retreat at home or in a lawful location.
; How is Battered Woman Syndrome used in US trials?
: It broadens the assessment of "reasonable belief" from the subjective viewpoint of a long-term abuse survivor, as in ''State v. Leidholm'' and ''State v. Edwards''.
; What did the 2011 Dresdner Notwehrstudie find in Germany?
: A survey of 3,463 residents and 189 prosecution files found most Germans favor balancing interests (''Interessenabwägung'') and support socio-ethical restrictions, rather than the absolute ''Rechtsbewährung'' doctrine.
; How does Japan's Supreme Court limit imminence in fights?
: Rulings of 21 July 1977 and 26 April 2017 deny imminence where the actor had an "active intent to attack" or breached a duty to avoid conflict.
; What did the analysis of Korean citizen participation trials on self-defense find?
: Of 32 cases (2008–2016), juries agreed with judges in 28 (74.29% guilty, 14.29% acquitted on self-defense), suggesting juror consciousness generally aligns with judges when given legal instructions.
; What is the status of Cecep Mustafa and Qonita Mutmainah?
: They are kept as entities (JPW-PERSON-CECEP, JPW-PERSON-QONITA), but the source text does not mention them, so no role or authorship is attributed.

== 법적 근거 ==
본 연구는 2018년도 대법원 연구과제에 따라 수행되었다. 검토 대상 국내 규정은 다음과 같다.

* '''형법 제21조'''(정당방위)
* '''폭력행위 등 처벌에 관한 법률 제8조'''
* '''국민의 형사재판 참여에 관한 법률'''

비교 대상 외국 규정: 미국 수정헌법 제2조 관련 판례와 주 형법(뉴욕주 형법 제35.15조; 플로리다주 §776.013), 독일 형법(StGB) 제32조, 일본 형법 제36조.

== 배경 ==
우리나라의 정당방위 논쟁은 2014년 "도둑뇌사사건"을 계기로 크게 확산되었다. 이 사건에서 법원은 절도범을 구타하여 혼수상태에 이르게 한 집주인의 정당방위 주장을 받아들이지 않았다. 이 판결은 형법 제정 이래의 판례 흐름과 일치했음에도 국민의 81%가 부당하다고 평가하였고, 이러한 법 형식과 국민 법의식 사이의 간극은 사법 신뢰를 위협한다.<ref name="jpri-ko" />

== 연구 목적 ==

# 미국, 독일, 일본의 법체계와 실증 자료를 비교 분석한다.
# 국민참여재판의 결과와 법심리학 연구를 평가하여 국민의 법의식을 파악한다.
# 사건 유형별로 구분된 정당방위 판단 기준 지침을 마련하여 판례를 국민 법의식과 조화시킨다.

== 정책 문제 ==

* '''엄격한 국내 판례''': 우리 법원은 전통적으로 싸움과 흉기 사용 사건에서 정당방위를 좁게 인정하며, 공공질서를 우선 가치로 삼는다.
* '''문화적 인지 격차''': 서구 법문화는 개인주의("법은 불의에 굴복할 필요가 없다")에, 동아시아 법문화는 집단주의(중대 범죄자를 질서에 대한 위협으로 봄)에 뿌리를 둔다.
* '''가정폭력 사건''': 매맞는 여성 증후군을 겪는 피해자가 잠든 배우자를 살해한 경우 "현재성" 요건을 충족하기 어려워, 법원은 정당방위 무죄보다 양형 감경을 선택하는 경향이 있다.

== 법제 공백 ==

* '''"부당한" 침해와 "위법한" 공격의 차이''': 한국과 일본은 "부당한/부정한 침해"라는 표현을 사용하는 반면 미국과 독일은 "위법한 공격"이라는 표현을 사용하며, 이는 조문 제정 당시부터 내재된 사회윤리적 제한을 반영한다.
* '''사건 유형별 기준 부재''': 가정폭력, 싸움, 성폭력, 국가권력 저항 등 유형별로 구분된 판단 지침이 없다.

== 개선 제안 ==

# '''판단 기준 유형화''': 정당방위 기준을 가정폭력·성폭력, 싸움·물리적 폭행, 재산 침해·주거침입, 국가권력 저항의 4개 유형으로 구분한다.
# '''배심원 법률 설명''': 국민참여재판에서 기술적 오해를 줄이도록 명확한 배심원 설명서를 제공한다.
# '''가정폭력 피해자의 주관성 인정''': 매맞는 여성 증후군의 영향을 단순한 양형 감경 요소가 아니라 현재성·상당성 판단에 통합한다.

== 자주 묻는 질문 ==

; 보고서의 제목, 총서 번호, 연구책임자는?
: 『각국의 정당방위 판단기준과 국민의 법의식』(연구총서 2019-01), 연구책임자 하민경과 공동연구자 서용성·김성화, 2019년 2월 28일 사법정책연구원 발간.
; 국내에서 정당방위 논쟁이 확산된 계기는?
: 2014년 도둑뇌사사건으로, 절도범을 구타해 혼수상태에 빠뜨린 집주인의 정당방위 주장이 기각되었고 국민의 81%가 이를 부당하다고 평가하였다.
; 한국·일본과 미국·독일의 정당방위 문언은 어떻게 다른가?
: 한국·일본은 "부당한/부정한 침해"를, 미국·독일은 "위법한 공격"을 사용하며, 이는 동아시아법에 내재된 사회윤리적 제한을 반영한다.
; 3개국 비교 실험 결과는?
: 미국 응답자가 정당방위를 가장 폭넓게 인정했고(급박성 있을 때 93.8%, 없을 때도 82.0%), 한국(54.9%/27.5%)과 일본(50.0%/47.1%)은 질서를 중시하는 집단주의 법문화로 인해 훨씬 낮았다.
; 미국의 주거 방어 관련 주요 법리는?
: 46개 주가 채택한 캐슬 독트린과 플로리다주 §776.013 등의 스탠드 유어 그라운드 법으로, 주거나 적법한 장소에서의 후퇴 의무를 없앤다.
; 매맞는 여성 증후군은 미국 재판에서 어떻게 쓰이는가?
: 장기간 학대를 겪은 피해자의 주관적 관점에서 "합리적 믿음"을 넓게 판단하는 데 쓰이며, ''State v. Leidholm''과 ''State v. Edwards''가 그 예이다.
; 2011년 Dresdner Notwehrstudie의 주요 결과는?
: 주민 3,463명과 검찰 파일 189건을 분석한 결과 다수의 독일 국민이 이익형량(Interessenabwägung)과 사회윤리적 제한을 지지하며, 절대적 법질서 수호론과는 차이를 보였다.
; 일본 최고재판소는 싸움에서 급박성을 어떻게 제한하는가?
: 1977년 7월 21일과 2017년 4월 26일 판결에서 행위자에게 적극적 가해의사가 있거나 침해회피의무를 위반한 경우 급박성을 부정한다.
; 국민참여재판 분석 결과는?
: 32건(2008~2016) 중 28건에서 배심원과 판사의 판단이 일치했으며(74.29% 유죄, 14.29% 정당방위 무죄), 법률 설명이 주어질 경우 배심원의 법의식이 대체로 판사와 부합함을 보여준다.
; Cecep Mustafa와 Qonita Mutmainah의 지위는?
: 개체(JPW-PERSON-CECEP, JPW-PERSON-QONITA)로 유지하나 원문에 언급이 없어 역할이나 저술 관계는 귀속하지 않는다.

      },
      "lead": "'''Criteria for Self-defense Judgment and the Public's Legal Consciousness in Overseas Jurisdictions''' (Korean: 각국의 정당방위 판단기준과 국민의 법의식) is an official judicial policy research report published by the [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] (JPRI) of the [[Supreme Court of Korea]] as JPRI Research Series 2019-01.<ref name=\"jpri\"/> It compares the legal criteria, doctrine, case law and public legal consciousness surrounding the right of [[self-defense]] (정당방위) in South Korea, the United States, Germany and Japan.",

        }

        {
          "title": "Legal basis",
          "level": 2,
          "blocks": [
            {
              "type": "paragraph",
              "text": "The research was conducted under the Supreme Court Annual Research Plan 2018 (2018년도 연구과제). The Korean provisions evaluated are:"
            },
            {
              "type": "list",
              "items": [
                "'''Criminal Act, Article 21''' (형법 제21조 — self-defense)",
                "'''Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc., Article 8''' (폭력행위 등 처벌에 관한 법률 제8조)",
                "'''Act on Citizen Participation in Criminal Trials''' (국민의 형사재판 참여에 관한 법률)"
              ]
            },
            {
              "type": "paragraph",
              "text": "Foreign provisions compared: US Second Amendment jurisprudence and state penal laws (New York Penal Law § 35.15; Florida § 776.013); German Criminal Code (StGB) § 32; Japanese Criminal Code Article 36."
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "title": "Background",
          "level": 2,
          "blocks": [
            {
              "type": "paragraph",
              "text": "Public debate over the right of self-defense in Korea intensified after the 2014 \"Brain-Dead Burglar\" case (도둑뇌사사건), in which a court rejected a homeowner's self-defense claim after he beat a burglar into a coma. Although the ruling was consistent with the line of case law since the Criminal Act's enactment, 81% of the public judged it unfair, and the gap between formal legal doctrine and popular legal consciousness threatens public trust in the judiciary.<ref name=\"jpri\"/>"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "title": "Objectives",
          "level": 2,
          "blocks": [
            {
              "type": "ordered_list",
              "items": [
                "Compare the legal frameworks and empirical data of the United States, Germany and Japan.",
                "Evaluate outcomes of citizen participation trials (국민참여재판) and legal-psychology research to map public legal consciousness.",
                "Formulate self-defense assessment guidelines categorized by case type, to align case law with public legal consciousness."
              ]
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "title": "Policy problems",
          "level": 2,
          "blocks": [
            {
              "type": "list",
              "items": [
                "'''Strict Korean case law.''' Korean courts have traditionally restricted self-defense narrowly, especially in mutual fights (싸움) and use of weapons, treating public order as a primary value.",
                "'''Cultural cognitive gap.''' Western legal culture is rooted in individualism (\"the law need not yield to injustice\"), while East Asian legal culture is rooted in collectivism, viewing serious offenders as a threat to public order.",
                "'''Domestic violence cases.''' Battered Woman Syndrome survivors who kill an abusive spouse while he sleeps struggle to meet the \"imminence\" (현재성) requirement, so Korean judges tend to grant sentence mitigation (양형 감경) rather than acquit on self-defense grounds."
              ]
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "title": "Legal and policy gaps",
          "level": 2,
          "blocks": [
            {
              "type": "list",
              "items": [
                "'''\"Wrongful\" versus \"unlawful\" attack.''' Korean and Japanese law use the phrase \"부당한/부정한 침해\" (wrongful or unjust attack), unlike the US and German \"unlawful attack\" (위법한 공격), reflecting an intrinsic socio-ethical limitation built into the provision from its drafting.",
                "'''No case-type typology.''' Korea lacks separate assessment guidelines by category (domestic violence, mutual fights, sexual violence, resistance to state authority)."
              ]
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "title": "Comparative analysis",
          "level": 2,
          "blocks": [
            {
              "type": "table",
              "headers": [
                "Jurisdiction",
                "Framework",
                "Key features"
              ],
              "rows": [
                [
                  "South Korea",
                  "Criminal Act Art. 21",
                  "Analysis of 32 citizen participation trials (2008–2016) found jury verdicts matched judges in 28 cases (74.29% guilty/rejected, 14.29% acquitted on self-defense). An experimental study by Seong et al. (403 respondents) found Korean respondents far more sensitive to the proportionality requirement (상당성) than US respondents."
                ],
                [
                  "United States",
                  "Necessity, proportionality, reasonable belief",
                  "Castle Doctrine (adopted in 46 states) and Stand Your Ground laws (e.g. Florida § 776.013) remove the duty to retreat at home or in a lawful location. Battered Woman Syndrome is recognized in assessing the subjective reasonableness of belief (''State v. Leidholm''; ''State v. Edwards'')."
                ],
                [
                  "Germany",
                  "StGB § 32",
                  "Rests on ''Individualschutz'' (individual protection) and ''Rechtsbewährung'' (vindication of the legal order). The 2011 Dresdner Notwehrstudie (Ines Kilian; 3,463 residents and 189 prosecution files) found 52% of the public supported socio-ethical restrictions (''Sozialethische Einschränkungen'') in partner conflicts."
                ],
                [
                  "Japan",
                  "Criminal Code Art. 36",
                  "Requires an act \"unavoidably taken\" (부득이하게 취한 행위). Supreme Court rulings (1977, 2008, 2017) deny imminence where the actor had an \"active intent to attack\" (적극적 가해의사) or breached a duty to avoid conflict (침해회피의무)."
                ]
              ]
            },
            {
              "type": "paragraph",
              "text": "An experimental comparison of self-defense acceptance across the three countries found US respondents most accepting (93.8% for a killing when imminent, 82.0% even absent imminence), while Korea (54.9% / 27.5%) and Japan (50.0% / 47.1%) were much lower, reflecting a collectivist legal culture that prioritizes public order."
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "title": "Reform proposals",
          "level": 2,
          "blocks": [
            {
              "type": "ordered_list",
              "items": [
                "'''Typology of assessment criteria:''' divide self-defense standards into four case types: domestic violence/sexual violence, mutual fights/physical assault, property violation/home invasion, and resistance to state authority.",
                "'''Jury legal instructions:''' provide clear legal-explanation guides (배심원 설명서) in citizen participation trials to reduce technical misunderstanding.",
                "'''Recognition of DV victim subjectivity:''' integrate the effects of Battered Woman Syndrome into the assessment of imminence and proportionality, rather than treating it merely as a sentence-mitigating factor."
              ]
            }
          ]
        },

        {
          "title": "Frequently asked questions",
          "level": 2,
          "blocks": [
            {
              "type": "definition_list",
              "items": [
                {
                  "term": "What are the report's title, series number and lead author?",
                  "definition": "''Criteria for Self-defense Judgment and the Public's Legal Consciousness in Overseas Jurisdictions'' (Series 2019-01), by lead researcher Ha, Minkyung with Seo Yongsung and Kim Seonghwa, published by JPRI on 28 February 2019."
                },
                {
                  "term": "What event triggered public attention to self-defense in Korea?",
                  "definition": "The 2014 \"Brain-Dead Burglar\" case, in which a court rejected a homeowner's self-defense claim after beating a burglar into a coma; 81% of the public judged the ruling unfair."
                },
                {
                  "term": "How does the wording of self-defense law differ between Korea/Japan and the US/Germany?",
                  "definition": "Korea and Japan use \"wrongful/unjust attack\" (부당한/부정한 침해), while the US and Germany use \"unlawful attack\" (위법한 공격), reflecting an intrinsic socio-ethical limitation in East Asian law."
                },
                {
                  "term": "What did the cross-national psychology experiment find?",
                  "definition": "US respondents were most accepting of self-defense (93.8% with imminence, 82.0% without), far above Korea (54.9%/27.5%) and Japan (50.0%/47.1%), reflecting a collectivist legal culture prioritizing order."
                },
                {
                  "term": "What is the main US doctrine on defense of the home?",
                  "definition": "The Castle Doctrine (46 states) and Stand Your Ground laws (e.g. Florida § 776.013), which remove the duty to retreat at home or in a lawful location."
                },
                {
                  "term": "How is Battered Woman Syndrome used in US trials?",
                  "definition": "It broadens the assessment of \"reasonable belief\" from the subjective viewpoint of a long-term abuse survivor, as in ''State v. Leidholm'' and ''State v. Edwards''."
                },
                {
                  "term": "What did the 2011 Dresdner Notwehrstudie find in Germany?",
                  "definition": "A survey of 3,463 residents and 189 prosecution files found most Germans favor balancing interests (''Interessenabwägung'') and support socio-ethical restrictions, rather than the absolute ''Rechtsbewährung'' doctrine."
                },
                {
                  "term": "How does Japan's Supreme Court limit imminence in fights?",
                  "definition": "Rulings of 21 July 1977 and 26 April 2017 deny imminence where the actor had an \"active intent to attack\" or breached a duty to avoid conflict."
                },
                {
                  "term": "What did the analysis of Korean citizen participation trials on self-defense find?",
                  "definition": "Of 32 cases (2008–2016), juries agreed with judges in 28 (74.29% guilty, 14.29% acquitted on self-defense), suggesting juror consciousness generally aligns with judges when given legal instructions."
                },
                {
                  "term": "What is the status of Cecep Mustafa and Qonita Mutmainah?",
                  "definition": "They are kept as entities (JPW-PERSON-CECEP, JPW-PERSON-QONITA), but the source text does not mention them, so no role or authorship is attributed."
                }

            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "title": "정책 문제",
          "level": 2,
          "blocks": [
            {
              "type": "list",
              "items": [
                "'''엄격한 국내 판례''': 우리 법원은 전통적으로 싸움과 흉기 사용 사건에서 정당방위를 좁게 인정하며, 공공질서를 우선 가치로 삼는다.",
                "'''문화적 인지 격차''': 서구 법문화는 개인주의(\"법은 불의에 굴복할 필요가 없다\")에, 동아시아 법문화는 집단주의(중대 범죄자를 질서에 대한 위협으로 봄)에 뿌리를 둔다.",
                "'''가정폭력 사건''': 매맞는 여성 증후군을 겪는 피해자가 잠든 배우자를 살해한 경우 \"현재성\" 요건을 충족하기 어려워, 법원은 정당방위 무죄보다 양형 감경을 선택하는 경향이 있다."
              ]
            }

'''Ideal Management Plan for the Termed Civil Servant System: Focusing on the Judiciary's Termed Civil Servants''' (Korean: 임기제공무원제도의 바람직한 운영방안에 관한 연구 - 사법부 임기제공무원을 중심으로) is an official judicial policy research report published by the [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] (JPRI) of the [[Supreme Court of Korea]] as JPRI Research Series 2019-05.<ref name="jpri">서현웅, 『임기제공무원제도의 바람직한 운영방안에 관한 연구 - 사법부 임기제공무원을 중심으로 -』, 사법정책연구원 (2019). ISBN 979-11-6168-080-4.</ref> It analyzes personnel-practice problems in Korea's termed (fixed-term) civil servant system, evaluates the comparative legal frameworks of the United States, United Kingdom and Japan, and sets out operating guidelines and a legislative reform package to improve the management of termed employees across the judiciary.

== Legal basis ==
The research was conducted under the Supreme Court Annual Research Plan 2018. The principal references are:

* '''State Public Officials Act, Article 26-5''' (국가공무원법 제26조의5)
* '''Court Public Servants Rules, Articles 4-2, 24-2 and 24-3''' (법원공무원규칙)
* '''Public Officials Remuneration Regulation''' and the court staff pay rules (공무원보수규정)

== Background ==
The termed civil servant system was first introduced in Korea in 1998, after the IMF economic crisis, as the Contractual Civil Servant System (계약직공무원제도), to break the rigidity of the closed career (grade-based, 계급제) system, inject private-sector professionalism and increase personnel flexibility. In 2013, through a public-position structural reform, this contract system was folded into the general civil service category as the "Termed Civil Servant" to strengthen status security during the term and broaden position integration. As of December 2017, termed employees across all Korean government agencies numbered 12,588 (1.2% of all civil servants); the judiciary alone employed 569 termed employees (3.2% of its 17,736 civil servants), of whom 74.5% (424) were women.<ref name="jpri" />

== Objectives ==

# Analyze real-world personnel-practice problems facing termed employees in Korea and the judiciary.
# Evaluate the management mechanisms for termed staff in the United States, United Kingdom and Japan.
# Develop operating guidelines and draft amendments to the Court Public Servants Rules to protect termed employees' rights and prevent abuse of appointment power.

== Policy problems ==

* '''Status uncertainty and fear of reappointment.''' Initial terms are capped at five years; after five years, agencies often terminate the employee or run a new open recruitment for the same position.
* '''The "dummy applicant" phenomenon (들러리).''' When reappointment recruitment is held after five years, the experienced incumbent is almost always selected, so outside applicants serve only as formal, token competitors.
* '''Unconstitutional salary reset.''' Incumbents who are reselected for the same position through reappointment recruitment are often treated as new hires and have their salary reset to first-year levels, disregarding five years of accumulated experience.
* '''No promotion path and single-evaluator appraisal.''' Termed employees are barred from promotion. Performance appraisal is subjective and dominated by a single direct supervisor, with no participation right or feedback interview.

== Legal and policy gaps ==

* '''Ambiguous "outstanding performance" standard.''' Since 2015/2016, regulations have allowed extending a term to a total of ten years without new recruitment for employees with "outstanding performance" (탁월한 성과), but no clear quantitative or qualitative indicator defines this standard within the judiciary.
* '''No notice procedure or right to request extension.''' Agencies have no legal duty to give early notice of an approaching term expiry, and termed employees have no administrative right to apply for an extension evaluation.

Domestic practice: the Seoul Metropolitan Government and the National Assembly Secretariat (National Assembly Research Service/Budget Office) have already defined "outstanding performance" criteria based on average evaluation scores (e.g. average grade A or S) and multi-source peer evaluation.

== Reform proposals ==

# '''Define outstanding-performance criteria and protect salary:''' legislate objective evaluation-score standards and require preserving the prior salary (종전 연봉 보전) for employees reselected to the same position.
# '''Flexible initial terms:''' apply a flexible term scheme based on position characteristics, such as 2+3 years or 1+4 years, for ongoing (상시·계속적) work.
# '''Institutionalize an expectation right to request extension (기대권):''' require notice of expiry 80 days in advance, a right to apply for extension 60 days in advance, and an objection (이의신청) mechanism.
# '''Establish a Judiciary Termed Personnel Committee:''' a dedicated body to oversee recruitment, term extension and prevention of nepotism or abuse of appointment power.
# '''Allow conversion to permanent career status:''' permit termed employees managing ongoing, routine work to convert to general career civil servant status through a limited, non-competitive selection examination (비다수인대상채용).
