title: JPW-REPORT-018
wikitext: == ICC Annual Report to UNGA 2015/16 — Wiki Entry == '''Report of the International Criminal Court on its Activities in 2015/16''' is the ICC's official annual report to the UN General Assembly for the period 1 August 2015 to 31 July 2016, submitted pursuant to Article 6 of the Relationship Agreement between the United Nations and the ICC. == Summary == The report summarizes the ICC's judicial, prosecutorial, and institutional activities over the reporting period, recording four simultaneous trials, the conviction of Jean-Pierre Bemba, the inauguration of the Court's new permanent premises, El Salvador's accession, and continued obstacles to executing 13 outstanding arrest warrants. == Legal Basis == * [[Relationship Agreement between the United Nations and the International Criminal Court]]: Article 6, on the obligation to submit annual reports. * [[UN General Assembly Resolution 70/264]]: Paragraph 28. * [[Rome Statute]]: The judicial framework, and Article 115(b) on financing arising from UN Security Council referrals. == Background == Submission of this 71st annual report to the UN General Assembly reflects the accountability relationship and principal communication channel between the ICC and the UN, aimed at strengthening international law-enforcement cooperation. == Objectives == * Report on judicial and prosecutorial achievements across all active situations. * Report on operational efficiency and the inauguration of the new permanent premises in The Hague. * Strengthen the integration of international criminal justice into the UN's 2030 Agenda (SDG 16). == Key Provisions == * '''Prosecutorial Activity''': Management of 11 preliminary examinations and the opening of a full investigation in Georgia. * '''Judicial Decisions''': Conviction of Jean-Pierre Bemba (18 years' imprisonment); opening of the Ntaganda and Gbagbo/Blé Goudé trials; and confirmation of charges against Al Mahdi and Ongwen. * '''Institutional Development''': Relocation to new permanent premises (cost: €204 million); El Salvador's accession as the 124th State Party; and the establishment of the ICCBA. * '''Victim Assistance''': The Trust Fund for Victims (TFV) assisted over 300,000 victims in Uganda and the DRC. == Implementation == Carried out through close coordination among the Court's organs (Presidency, OTP, Registry), the UN, peacekeeping missions (such as MINUSCA), and civil society organizations. == Evidence == * Registration of 410 Article 15 communications. * Participation of 2,571 victims in proceedings, alongside TFV assistance to over 300,000 victims in Uganda and the DRC. * Submission of 724 visa requests and 224 cooperation requests by the Registry, and 380+ requests for assistance by the OTP. * El Salvador's accession as the 124th State Party on 3 March 2016. == Policy Issues == * Slow response by the UN Security Council to 14 findings of non-cooperation. * Challenges in executing 13 outstanding arrest warrants. * The need for UN financing under Article 115(b) of the Rome Statute for costs arising from Security Council referrals. == Relationships with Other Entities == * '''[[International Criminal Court]]''': Reporting institution. * '''[[United Nations General Assembly]]''': Recipient of the report. * '''[[Jean-Pierre Bemba Gombo]]''': Defendant in the Central African Republic I situation, convicted of crimes against humanity and war crimes and sentenced to 18 years' imprisonment on 21 June 2016. * '''[[Bosco Ntaganda]]''': Defendant in the Democratic Republic of the Congo situation, on trial before Trial Chamber VI since 2 September 2015. * '''[[Laurent Gbagbo]]''' and '''[[Charles Blé Goudé]]''': Defendants in the Côte d'Ivoire situation, whose joint trial opened before Trial Chamber I on 28 January 2016. * '''[[Ahmad Al Faqi Al Mahdi]]''': Defendant in the Mali situation, surrendered to the Court on 26 September 2015 on war crimes charges for directing attacks on historic and religious buildings in Timbuktu. * '''[[Dominic Ongwen]]''': Defendant in the Uganda situation, whose charges were confirmed by Pre-Trial Chamber II on 23 March 2016, with trial set to begin 6 December 2016. * '''[[Omar Hassan Ahmad Al Bashir]]''': President of Sudan, subject of two outstanding arrest warrants; findings of non-cooperation over the failure to arrest him were referred to the Assembly of States Parties and the UN Security Council after Djibouti and Uganda failed to execute the warrants. * '''[[Simone Gbagbo]]''', '''[[Sylvestre Mudacumura]]''', '''[[Walter Barasa]]''', '''[[Paul Gicheru]]''', '''[[Philip Kipkoech Bett]]''', '''[[Saif Al-Islam Gaddafi]]''', '''[[Ahmad Harun]]''', '''[[Ali Kushayb]]''', '''[[Abdel Raheem Muhammad Hussein]]''', '''[[Abdallah Banda]]''', '''[[Joseph Kony]]''', '''[[Vincent Otti]]''': Twelve other individuals with outstanding public arrest warrants during the reporting period. * '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': '''Not found in the title: JPW-REPORT-019
wikitext: == ICC Annual Report to UNGA 2020/21 — Wiki Entry (English) == '''Report of the International Criminal Court on its Activities in 2020/21''' is the ICC's official annual report to the UN General Assembly for the period 1 August 2020 to 31 July 2021, submitted pursuant to Article 6 of the Relationship Agreement between the United Nations and the ICC and UN General Assembly Resolution 75/3. == Summary == The report summarizes the ICC's judicial, prosecutorial, and institutional activities during the period, recording the conviction of Dominic Ongwen, confirmation of Bosco Ntaganda's sentence, the final acquittals of Gbagbo and Blé Goudé, the revocation of U.S. sanctions, a major change in ICC leadership, and progress on victim reparations. == Legal Basis == * [[Relationship Agreement between the United Nations and the International Criminal Court]]: Article 6, on submission of annual reports. * [[UN General Assembly Resolution 75/3]]: Paragraph 28. * [[Rome Statute]]: The judicial framework, including Articles 15, 18, 58, 70, and 75. == Background == Submission of this annual report to the 76th session of the UN General Assembly reflects the accountability relationship and principal communication channel between the ICC and the UN, aimed at strengthening the international criminal justice system. == Objectives == * Report on judicial and prosecutorial achievements across 14 active situations. * Address the operational challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic through hybrid trial mechanisms. * Report progress on implementing the Independent Expert Review (IER) process. == Key Provisions == * '''Prosecutorial Activity''': Opening of a new investigation in Palestine (March 2021); a request for authorization to investigate in the Philippines (May 2021); completion of 4 preliminary examinations (Iraq/UK, Nigeria, Ukraine, Philippines); and receipt of a new referral from Bolivia. * '''Judicial Decisions''': Conviction of Dominic Ongwen (25 years); confirmation of Bosco Ntaganda's conviction (30 years, plus a $30 million reparations order); the final acquittals of Gbagbo and Blé Goudé; vacating of the arrest warrant against Simone Gbagbo; and confirmation of charges against Ali Kushayb (31 counts) and Paul Gicheru (8 counts). * '''Institutional Development''': Election of Karim Khan (Prosecutor), Piotr Hofmański (ICC President), and Silvia Fernández de Gurmendi (ASP President). * '''Diplomatic Development''': U.S. revocation of Executive Order 13928 on 2 April 2021. == Implementation == Carried out through close coordination among the Court's organs (Presidency, OTP, Registry), the UN, the Trust Fund for Victims (managing 27 projects), and civil society organizations. The Court adopted hybrid proceedings and distributed work arrangements to maintain its judicial calendar despite the COVID-19 pandemic. == Evidence == * Participation of approximately 11,000 victims in ICC proceedings, with 2,300+ new victim applications registered. * Registration of 612 Article 15 communications (438 outside jurisdiction). * Transmission of 472 requests for assistance by the OTP and 222 principal cooperation requests by the Registry. * Ratification/accession to the Article 8 Amendments, the Crime of Aggression Amendments, and the 2019 Starvation Amendment by a number of States Parties. == Policy Issues == * Lack of UN Security Council response to 16 findings of non-cooperation. * Challenges in executing 12 outstanding arrest warrants. == Relationships with Other Entities == * '''[[International Criminal Court]]''': Reporting institution. * '''[[United Nations General Assembly]]''': Recipient of the report. * '''[[Dominic Ongwen]]''': Defendant in the Northern Uganda situation, convicted of 61 crimes against humanity and war crimes and sentenced to 25 years' imprisonment in May 2021 (on appeal). * '''[[Bosco Ntaganda]]''': Defendant in the DRC situation, whose conviction and 30-year sentence were confirmed by the Appeals Chamber on 30 March 2021, alongside a $30 million reparations order. * '''[[Laurent Gbagbo]]''' and '''[[Charles Blé Goudé]]''': Defendants in the Côte d'Ivoire situation, whose acquittals were finally confirmed by the Appeals Chamber on 31 March 2021. * '''[[Simone Gbagbo]]''': Former First Lady of Côte d'Ivoire, whose arrest warrant was vacated by Pre-Trial Chamber II on 19 July 2021, upon the Prosecutor's request, for failing to meet the Article 58 evidentiary threshold. * '''[[Alfred Yekatom]]''' and '''[[Patrice-Edouard Ngaïssona]]''': Anti-Balaka defendants (CAR II situation), whose trial began 16 February 2021 before Trial Chamber V. * '''[[Mahamat Said Abdel Kani]]''': Séléka defendant (CAR II situation), who surrendered and was transferred to ICC custody on 24 January 2021. * '''[[Al Hassan Ag Abdoul Aziz Ag Mohamed Ag Mahmoud]]''': Defendant in the Mali situation, whose trial continued before Trial Chamber X over crimes in Timbuktu. * '''[[Ali Muhammad Ali Abd-Al-Rahman]]''' ("Ali Kushayb"): Defendant in the Darfur, Sudan situation, whose 31 counts of war crimes and crimes against humanity were confirmed by Pre-Trial Chamber II on 9 July 2021. * '''[[Paul Gicheru]]''': Defendant in the Kenya situation, who surrendered in November 2020, with 8 counts of offences against the administration of justice confirmed on 15 July 2021. * '''[[Karim Asad Ahmad Khan]]''': ICC Prosecutor elected by the Assembly of States Parties for a nine-year term, taking office 16 June 2021. * '''[[Piotr Hofmański]]''': Judge elected President of the International Criminal Court on 11 March 2021 for a three-year term. * '''[[Silvia Fernández de Gurmendi]]''': President of the Assembly of States Parties, elected by acclamation for the 20th to 22nd sessions. * '''[[Joe Biden]]''' / US Administration: U.S. President who revoked Executive Order 13928 on 2 April 2021, ending economic sanctions and visa restrictions against ICC officials. * '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': '''Not found in the available sources.''' * '''[[Ferdi Raditya Akbar]]''': '''Not found in the available sources.''' == See Also == * [[International Criminal Court]] * [[United Nations General Assembly]] * [[Rome Statute]] == References == * United Nations General Assembly, "Report of the International Criminal title: JPW-REPORT-020
wikitext: == ICC Annual Report to UNGA 2022/23 — Wiki Entry == '''Report of the International Criminal Court on its Activities in 2022/23''' is the ICC's official annual report to the UN General Assembly for the period 1 August 2022 to 31 July 2023, submitted pursuant to Article 6 of the Relationship Agreement between the United Nations and the ICC and UN General Assembly Resolution 77/6. == Summary == The report summarizes the ICC's judicial, prosecutorial, and institutional activities during the period, recording the issuance of arrest warrants for Vladimir Putin and Maria Lvova-Belova, the final confirmation of Dominic Ongwen's sentence, the launch of the 2023–2025 Strategic Plans, the election of new Registrar Osvaldo Zavala Giler, and continued obstacles in executing 16 outstanding public arrest warrants. == Legal Basis == * [[Relationship Agreement between the United Nations and the International Criminal Court]]: Article 6, on submission of annual reports. * [[UN General Assembly Resolution 77/6]]: Paragraph 31. * [[Rome Statute]]: The judicial framework, including Articles 8, 18, 56, 61, and 93(10). == Background == Submission of this annual report to the 78th session of the UN General Assembly serves as the principal official communication channel between the ICC and the UN, strengthening international law-enforcement cooperation under the Rome Statute mandate. == Objectives == * Report on judicial and prosecutorial developments across active situations. * Report on alignment of the 2023–2025 Strategic Plans under the One Court principle. * Strengthen the complementarity framework and international cooperation with the UN and States Parties. == Key Provisions == * '''Prosecutorial Activity''': Continued investigations in Afghanistan, Venezuela I, and the Philippines; conclusion of investigations in Georgia, CAR II, and Guinea; receipt of a second referral from the DRC concerning crimes in North Kivu since 1 January 2022. * '''Judicial Decisions''': Arrest warrants for Vladimir Putin and Maria Lvova-Belova; final confirmation of Dominic Ongwen's sentence; determination of Ntaganda's estimated reparations liability at $31.3 million; termination of proceedings against Paul Gicheru and Al-Tuhamy Khaled following their deaths. * '''Institutional Development''': Election of Osvaldo Zavala Giler as Registrar; launch of the 2023–2025 Strategic Plans; adoption of the Policy on the Crime of Gender Persecution. * '''Victim Assistance''': The TFV assisted nearly 17,000 victims across 7 countries. == Implementation == Carried out through close coordination among the Court's organs (Presidency, OTP, Registry), the UN (including OLA, UNDP), field missions, and civil society organizations. The Court opened a field office in Ukraine under a 23 March 2023 agreement, and signed an operational cooperation framework with UNDP in October 2022. == Evidence == * Issuance of 534 written decisions and 227 hearings held by the Chambers. * Participation of over 15,000 victims in proceedings, with 8,900+ new victim application forms received. * TFV programs directly benefiting close to 17,000 individual victims in 7 countries. * Submission of 536 visa requests and 300 principal cooperation requests by the Registry, and 458 requests for assistance by the OTP. * Collection of €3.8 million in voluntary contributions from 32 States Parties for the TFV. == Policy Issues == * Lack of substantive UN Security Council response to 16 findings of non-cooperation. * Unacceptable threats against elected ICC officials in the course of their mandate. * Challenges executing 16 outstanding public arrest warrants. * The impact of active armed conflict in Sudan on the Darfur investigation. * A $2.5 million funding gap for reparations in the Lubanga case. == Relationships with Other Entities == * '''[[International Criminal Court]]''': Reporting institution. * '''[[United Nations General Assembly]]''': Recipient of the report. * '''[[Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin]]''': President of the Russian Federation, subject of an ICC public arrest warrant issued on 17 March 2023 over alleged war crimes involving the deportation and forcible transfer of children from occupied Ukrainian territory. * '''[[Maria Alekseyevna Lvova-Belova]]''': Commissioner for Children's Rights in the Office of the President of the Russian Federation, subject of an ICC public arrest warrant issued on 17 March 2023 over the alleged forcible transfer of Ukrainian children. * '''[[Dominic Ongwen]]''': Former Lord's Resistance Army (LRA) commander whose conviction and 25-year sentence were finally confirmed by the Appeals Chamber on 15 December 2022; the case is now at the stage of defining a representative sample for victim reparations. * '''[[Ali Muhammad Ali Abd-Al-Rahman]]''' ("Ali Kushayb"): Defendant in the Darfur, Sudan situation, whose trial on war crimes and crimes against humanity charges continued before Trial Chamber I, marking the ICC's first trial arising from a UN Security Council referral. * '''[[Osvaldo Zavala Giler]]''': Ecuadorian national elected by the judges on 10 February 2023 as ICC Registrar for a five-year term beginning 17 April 2023, succeeding Peter Lewis. * '''[[Paul Gicheru]]''': Defendant in the Kenya situation, whose proceedings were formally terminated by Trial Chamber III on 14 October 2022 following confirmation of his death. * '''[[Al-Tuhamy Mohamed Khaled]]''': Suspect in the Libya situation, whose proceedings were terminated by Pre-Trial Chamber I on 7 September 2022 following receipt of an official death certificate from Libyan authorities. * '''[[Joseph Kony]]''', '''[[Vincent Otti]]''', '''[[Mahamah Nouradine Adam]]''', '''[[Ahmad Harun]]''', '''[[Omar Al-Bashir]]''', '''[[Abdel Raheem Muhammad Hussein]]''', '''[[Abdallah Banda]]''', '''[[Walter Barasa]]''', '''[[Philip Kipkoech Bett]]''', '''[[Saif Al-Islam Gaddafi]]''', '''[[Mikhail Mayramovich Mindzaev]]''', '''[[Gamlet Guchmazov]]''', '''[[David Georgiyevich Sanakoev]]''', '''[[Sylvestre Mudacumura]]''': 14 other individuals with outstanding public arrest warrants. * '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': '''Not found in the available sources.''' * '''[[Ferdi Raditya Akbar]]''': '''Not found in the available sources.''' == See Also == * [[International Criminal Court]] * [[United Nations General Assembly]] * [[Rome Statute]] == References == * United Nations General Assembly, "Report of the International Criminal Court on its activities in 2022/23," {{Infobox report|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-314|canonical_name=Report of the International Criminal Court for 2012/13 / Verslag van het Internationaal Strafhof over 2012/13|official_name=Report of the International Criminal Court for 2012/13 (United Nations General Assembly Document A/68/314)|type=Official UN/ICC annual activity report / Officieel jaarverslag van de VN en het ICC|jurisdiction=International criminal law, International Criminal Court, United Nations / Internationaal strafrecht, Internationaal Strafhof, Verenigde Naties|institution=ICC, UN General Assembly, Office of the Prosecutor, Registry, Assembly of States Parties / ICC, Algemene Vergadering van de VN, Bureau van de Aanklager, Griffie, Vergadering van Verdragsstaten|legal_basis=Article 6 UN-ICC Relationship Agreement, UNGA Resolution 66/262 paragraph 19, Rome Statute / Artikel 6 Relatieovereenkomst VN-ICC, Resolutie 66/262 van de Algemene Vergadering lid 19, Statuut van Rome|document_code=A/68/314|reporting_period=1 August 2012 to 31 July 2013 / 1 augustus 2012 tot 31 juli 2013|date=13 August 2013 / 13 augustus 2013|status=Official, published / Officieel, gepubliceerd}}

'''Report of the International Criminal Court for 2012/13''' is the ninth annual report of the International Criminal Court (ICC) to the United Nations General Assembly. It covers the period from 1 August 2012 to 31 July 2013 and was transmitted by the UN Secretary-General to the General Assembly at its sixty-eighth session (UN Doc A/68/314, 13 August 2013).<ref name="icc">United Nations General Assembly, "Report of the International Criminal Court for 2012/13", UN Doc A/68/314, 13 August 2013.</ref>

'''Verslag van het Internationaal Strafhof over 2012/13''' is het negende jaarverslag van het Internationaal Strafhof (ICC) aan de Algemene Vergadering van de Verenigde Naties. Het beslaat de periode van 1 augustus 2012 tot 31 juli 2013 en werd door de secretaris-generaal van de VN voorgelegd aan de Algemene Vergadering tijdens haar achtenzestigste zitting (VN-doc. A/68/314, 13 augustus 2013).<ref name="icc" />

== Also known as / Ook bekend als ==

* UN Doc A/68/314
* ICC Annual Report 2012/13
* Laporan Tahunan CPI 2012/2013
* Ninth Annual Report of the ICC to the UN

== Summary / Samenvatting ==
'''EN:''' The report summarises the judicial, prosecutorial and institutional activities of the ICC during the reporting period. It records the surrender of Bosco Ntaganda, the acquittal of Mathieu Ngudjolo Chui, the opening of an investigation in Mali, the ratification by Côte d'Ivoire (122nd State Party), and the election of Herman von Hebel as Registrar.<ref name="icc" />

'''NL:''' Het verslag vat de gerechtelijke, vervolgings- en institutionele activiteiten van het ICC in de verslagperiode samen. Het vermeldt de overgave van Bosco Ntaganda, de vrijspraak van Mathieu Ngudjolo Chui, de opening van een onderzoek in Mali, de ratificatie door Ivoorkust (122e verdragsstaat) en de verkiezing van Herman von Hebel tot griffier.<ref name="icc" />

== Legal basis / Rechtsgrond ==

* '''Relationship Agreement UN-ICC / Relatieovereenkomst VN-ICC:''' Article 6 on the submission of the annual report. / artikel 6 over de indiening van het jaarverslag.<ref name="icc" />
* '''UNGA Resolution 66/262:''' paragraph 19. / lid 19.<ref name="icc" />
* '''Rome Statute / Statuut van Rome:''' judicial framework. / rechterlijk kader.<ref name="icc" />
* '''Regulation 55 of the Regulations of the Court / Regel 55 van het Reglement van het Hof:''' recharacterisation of the form of criminal responsibility, considered in the Katanga case. / herkwalificatie van de vorm van strafrechtelijke verantwoordelijkheid, overwogen in de zaak Katanga.<ref name="icc" />

== Background / Achtergrond ==
'''EN:''' Under Article 6 of the Relationship Agreement and paragraph 19 of Resolution 66/262, the Secretary-General transmits the ICC's annual report to the General Assembly. The report is a channel of transparency and communication between the Court and the United Nations.<ref name="icc" />

'''NL:''' Op grond van artikel 6 van de Relatieovereenkomst en lid 19 van Resolutie 66/262 legt de secretaris-generaal het jaarverslag van het ICC voor aan de Algemene Vergadering. Het verslag is een kanaal voor transparantie en communicatie tussen het Strafhof en de Verenigde Naties.<ref name="icc" />

== Objectives / Doelstellingen ==

* '''EN:''' To report on judicial and prosecutorial developments in the active investigations. / '''NL:''' Verslag doen van gerechtelijke en vervolgingsontwikkelingen in de lopende onderzoeken.<ref name="icc" />
* '''EN:''' To strengthen international cooperation on arrests, asset freezing and witness protection. / '''NL:''' Internationale samenwerking versterken bij arrestaties, het bevriezen van tegoeden en getuigenbescherming.<ref name="icc" />
* '''EN:''' To broaden membership of the Rome Statute and the Kampala amendments on the crime of aggression. / '''NL:''' Het lidmaatschap van het Statuut van Rome en de Kampala-amendementen over het misdrijf agressie uitbreiden.<ref name="icc" />

== Key developments / Belangrijkste ontwikkelingen ==

!Area / Terrein
!English
!Nederlands

|Bosco Ntaganda surrendered voluntarily to the Court on 26 March 2013 (situation in the DRC).<ref name="icc" />
|Bosco Ntaganda gaf zich op 26 maart 2013 vrijwillig over aan het Hof (situatie in de DRC).<ref name="icc" />
|-

|Kamer van Eerste Aanleg II sprak Mathieu Ngudjolo Chui op 18 december 2012 vrij van alle aanklachten. Hij vroeg later asiel aan in Nederland.<ref name="icc" />

|-

|The Prosecutor opened an investigation on 16 January 2013 after a government referral in July 2012.<ref name="icc" />
|De Aanklager opende op 16 januari 2013 een onderzoek na een verwijzing door de regering in juli 2012.<ref name="icc" />
|-
|Preliminary examinations
|A preliminary examination was opened into the attack on Gaza flotilla vessels (Comoros, Greece, Cambodia). Analysis advanced in Nigeria, Colombia, Afghanistan, Georgia, Guinea, Honduras and Korea.<ref name="icc" />
|Er werd een voorlopig onderzoek geopend naar de aanval op vaartuigen van de Gaza-vloot (Comoren, Griekenland, Cambodja). De analyse vorderde in Nigeria, Colombia, Afghanistan, Georgië, Guinee, Honduras en Korea.<ref name="icc" />
|-

|The confirmation hearing of Laurent Gbagbo was adjourned for additional evidence. The arrest warrant for Simone Gbagbo was unsealed on 22 November 2012.<ref name="icc" />
|De bevestigingszitting van Laurent Gbagbo werd aangehouden voor aanvullend bewijs. Het arrestatiebevel tegen Simone Gbagbo werd op 22 november 2012 openbaar gemaakt.<ref name="icc" />
|-
|Libya
|The Government of Libya filed admissibility challenges in the cases of Saif Al-Islam Gaddafi and Abdullah Al-Senussi. The challenge in the Gaddafi case was rejected.<ref name="icc" />
|De regering van Libië diende ontvankelijkheidsbezwaren in in de zaken van Saif al-Islam Kadhafi en Abdullah Al-Senussi. Het bezwaar in de zaak Kadhafi werd afgewezen.<ref name="icc" />
|-
|Kenya
|The trial of William Samoei Ruto and Joshua Arap Sang was set to begin on 10 September 2013, with continuous presence waived for Ruto. The trial of Uhuru Muigai Kenyatta was set for 12 November 2013 after the charges against Francis Kirimi Muthaura were withdrawn.<ref name="icc" />
|Het proces tegen William Samoei Ruto en Joshua Arap Sang zou op 10 september 2013 beginnen, met vrijstelling van voortdurende aanwezigheid voor Ruto. Het proces tegen Uhuru Muigai Kenyatta stond gepland voor 12 november 2013 nadat de aanklachten tegen Francis Kirimi Muthaura waren ingetrokken.<ref name="icc" />
|-

|The two arrest warrants against Omar Hassan Ahmad Al Bashir remain active. Pre-Trial Chamber II referred Chad's non-compliance to the UN Security Council and the Assembly of States Parties. Saleh Mohammed Jerbo Jamus was reported to have died.<ref name="icc" />
|De twee arrestatiebevelen tegen Omar Hassan Ahmad Al Bashir blijven van kracht. Kamer voor Vooronderzoek II verwees de niet-naleving door Tsjaad naar de VN-Veiligheidsraad en de Vergadering van Verdragsstaten. Saleh Mohammed Jerbo Jamus zou zijn overleden.<ref name="icc" />
|-
|CAR situation
|The trial of Jean-Pierre Bemba Gombo continued with the presentation of defence evidence.<ref name="icc" />
|Het proces tegen Jean-Pierre Bemba Gombo ging verder met de presentatie van bewijs door de verdediging.<ref name="icc" />
|-
|States Parties
|Côte d'Ivoire ratified on 15 February 2013 and became the 122nd State Party.<ref name="icc" />
|Ivoorkust ratificeerde op 15 februari 2013 en werd de 122e verdragsstaat.<ref name="icc" />
|-
|Officials
|Herman von Hebel (Netherlands) was elected Registrar on 8 March 2013 for five years and sworn in on 18 April 2013, succeeding Silvana Arbia. James Stewart (Canada) was elected Deputy Prosecutor on 16 November 2012 for nine years and sworn in on 8 March 2013. Judge Anthony T. Carmona (Trinidad and Tobago) resigned effective 18 March 2013.<ref name="icc" />
|Herman von Hebel (Nederland) werd op 8 maart 2013 voor vijf jaar tot griffier gekozen en op 18 april 2013 beëdigd als opvolger van Silvana Arbia. James Stewart (Canada) werd op 16 november 2012 voor negen jaar tot plaatsvervangend Aanklager gekozen en op 8 maart 2013 beëdigd. Rechter Anthony T. Carmona (Trinidad en Tobago) nam met ingang van 18 maart 2013 ontslag.<ref name="icc" />
|-
|UN cooperation
|The UN guidance on non-essential contacts with persons subject to ICC warrants was revised. UN missions provided 324 flights in support of ICC operations.<ref name="icc" />
|De VN-richtlijn over niet-essentiële contacten met personen tegen wie een ICC-bevel loopt werd herzien. VN-missies verzorgden 324 vluchten ter ondersteuning van ICC-activiteiten.<ref name="icc" />
|-
|Charles Taylor
|The former President of Liberia was held at the ICC detention facility in The Hague at the request of the Special Court for Sierra Leone (SCSL).<ref name="icc" />
|De voormalige president van Liberia werd op verzoek van het Speciaal Hof voor Sierra Leone (SCSL) vastgehouden in de detentiefaciliteit van het ICC in Den Haag.<ref name="icc" />
|}

== Implementation / Uitvoering ==
'''EN:''' The report describes activities carried out through close coordination among the organs of the Court (Presidency, Office of the Prosecutor and Registry), UN bodies such as MONUSCO, UNOCI, MINUSMA and OLA, and civil society organisations.<ref name="icc" />

'''NL:''' Het verslag beschrijft activiteiten die zijn uitgevoerd in nauwe coördinatie tussen de organen van het Hof (Presidium, Bureau van de Aanklager en Griffie), VN-organen zoals MONUSCO, UNOCI, MINUSMA en OLA en maatschappelijke organisaties.<ref name="icc" />

== Policy analysis / Beleidsanalyse ==
{| class="wikitable"
!Aspect
!English
!Nederlands
|-
|Background / Achtergrond
|Fact. The Secretary-General transmitted the ninth annual report under Article 6 of the Relationship Agreement and paragraph 19 of Resolution 66/262.<ref name="icc" />
|Feit. De secretaris-generaal legde het negende jaarverslag voor op grond van artikel 6 van de Relatieovereenkomst en lid 19 van Resolutie 66/262.<ref name="icc" />
|-
|Problem / Probleem
|Fact (per source). A fast-growing caseload with eight active investigations and eight preliminary examinations, twelve outstanding public arrest warrants (Uganda, DRC, Darfur, Libya, Côte d'Ivoire), and no follow-up by the Security Council on findings of non-cooperation.<ref name="icc" />
|Feit (volgens de bron). Een snel groeiende caseload met acht lopende onderzoeken en acht voorlopige onderzoeken, twaalf openstaande openbare arrestatiebevelen (Oeganda, DRC, Darfoer, Libië, Ivoorkust) en geen opvolging door de Veiligheidsraad van bevindingen van niet-medewerking.<ref name="icc" />
|-
|Legal or policy gap / Juridische of beleidsmatige lacune
|Fact (per source). No automatic enforcement mechanism for Security Council referrals, and a need for more witness relocation and enforcement-of-sentences agreements with active support from States Parties.<ref name="icc" />
|Feit (volgens de bron). Geen automatisch handhavingsmechanisme voor verwijzingen door de Veiligheidsraad en behoefte aan meer overeenkomsten over getuigenhervestiging en tenuitvoerlegging van straffen met actieve steun van verdragsstaten.<ref name="icc" />
|-
|Objectives / Doelstellingen
|Fact. Report on developments, strengthen cooperation, and widen membership of the Statute and the Kampala amendments.<ref name="icc" />
|Feit. Verslag doen over ontwikkelingen, samenwerking versterken en het lidmaatschap van het Statuut en de Kampala-amendementen uitbreiden.<ref name="icc" />
|-
|Implementation / Uitvoering
|Fact. Mali investigation, Gaza flotilla examination, Ntaganda's surrender, Ngudjolo's acquittal, Gbagbo hearing adjournment, election of the Registrar and Deputy Prosecutor.<ref name="icc" />
|Feit. Onderzoek in Mali, onderzoek naar de Gaza-vloot, overgave van Ntaganda, vrijspraak van Ngudjolo, aanhouding van de zitting Gbagbo, verkiezing van de griffier en de plaatsvervangend Aanklager.<ref name="icc" />
|-
|Evidence / Bewijs
|Fact. 122 States Parties, 716 victim participation applications and 722 reparations applications received by the Registry, 691 visa requests and 220 major cooperation requests sent by the Registry, 307 assistance requests by the OTP, and two new witness relocation agreements signed in Nuremberg.<ref name="icc" />
|Feit. 122 verdragsstaten, 716 aanvragen voor slachtofferparticipatie en 722 herstelaanvragen ontvangen door de Griffie, 691 visumaanvragen en 220 belangrijke samenwerkingsverzoeken verzonden door de Griffie, 307 bijstandsverzoeken van het OTP en twee nieuwe overeenkomsten over getuigenhervestiging ondertekend in Neurenberg.<ref name="icc" />
|-
|Impact / Effect
|Inference. Improves the operational effectiveness of international criminal justice through the surrender of a key accused, logistical cooperation with the UN and stronger transparency standards.
|Inferentie. Vergroot de operationele effectiviteit van de internationale strafrechtspleging door de overgave van een belangrijke verdachte, logistieke samenwerking met de VN en sterkere transparantienormen.
|-
|Reform or future direction / Hervorming of toekomstige richting
|Fact. Ratification of the Kampala amendments (seven States for aggression, nine for non-international war crimes) and an integrated single-page victim application form in the Ntaganda case.<ref name="icc" />
|Feit. Ratificatie van de Kampala-amendementen (zeven staten voor agressie, negen voor oorlogsmisdaden in niet-internationale conflicten) en een geïntegreerd eenpagina-aanvraagformulier voor slachtoffers in de zaak Ntaganda.<ref name="icc" />
|-
|Unresolved issues / Onopgeloste kwesties
|Fact. Twelve outstanding arrest warrants, Ngudjolo Chui's asylum application in the Netherlands, and no concrete Security Council action on the non-cooperation referrals concerning Al Bashir's travel.<ref name="icc" />
|Feit. Twaalf openstaande arrestatiebevelen, de asielaanvraag van Ngudjolo Chui in Nederland en geen concrete actie van de Veiligheidsraad op de verwijzingen wegens niet-medewerking rond de reizen van Al Bashir.<ref name="icc" />
|}

Policy Analysis == ; Background : Real estate constitutes the foundation of individual living and the core object of private property rights under Article 23(1) of the ROK Constitution, forming the core of property law (물권법). To protect property rights and guarantee transaction safety, public disclosure systems (공시제도) have evolved. In South Korea, a dual public disclosure system (이원적 부동산 공시제도) operates: the Judiciary (Supreme Court) manages the real estate registration system (부동산 등기제도) via court register books (부동산등기부) to reflect legal rights (권리관계), while the Executive branch (MOLIT & local governments) manages the cadastral/registration system (부동산 등록제도) via public cadastres (대장) to reflect physical property status (현황) and taxation. In 2013, Korean court registry offices (192 locations with 1,768 staff) processed over 10.69 million real estate registration cases (averaging 84.8 cases per registrar daily). ; Policy Problem : '''Potential Discrepancies Between Register Books and Cadastres''': Because court register books and executive cadastres are managed separately by different branches of government, discrepancies in physical descriptions or owner records frequently occur, reducing public disclosure credibility, creating unexpected transaction losses, and increasing litigation costs. : '''Dual Procedural Burden on Citizens''': Property owners must complete double administrative procedures (e.g., applying for use approval with local government heads and then separately filing building modification registrations with court registry offices within 1 month), incurring double fees and inconvenience. : '''Administrative Inefficiency''': Civil servants in both branches perform redundant manual double-entry and notification processing. : '''Executive Overreach & Unconstitutional Delegated Legislation''': The Executive branch launched a project (부동산 행정정보 일원화 사업) to merge 18 real estate records (15 MOLIT cadastral records + 3 court registration records) into a single Comprehensive Real Estate Register (부동산종합공부). The Executive promulgated Article 62-2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Surveying, Hydrographic Survey and Cadastre (측수지법 시행령 제62조의2), attempting to force the Judiciary to hand over court rights registration data to executive cadastral offices. ; Legal/Policy Gap : '''Unconstitutionality & Legal Invalidity of 측수지법 Enforcement Decree Article 62-2''': The parent statute (측수지법 Art. 76-3 No. 5) delegated only "other necessary matters" (ancillary details), NOT core judicial property rights data. By expanding this via executive decree to include court registration rights data, the decree exceeded delegated statutory authority (위임명령의 한계 일탈), rendering it legally void (무효) under Supreme Court En Banc precedent (2011Du30878). Furthermore, it directly conflicts with the Court Organization Act (Art. 9(3)) and Real Estate Registration Act (Art. 109(2)), which grant exclusive authority over registration data management and certificate issuance to the Judiciary. : '''Inherent Flaws of Record Unification''': Real estate registration rights data (갑구, 을구) contains highly complex legal relationships (trusts, provisional registrations, multiple attachments, mortgages) requiring quasi-judicial review by independent registrars (등기관). Summarizing or mixing complex rights data into an executive administrative certificate (부동산종합증명서) misleads the public, fails to replace legal register certificates (등기사항증명서), wastes budget, and violates the Separation of Powers (삼권분립). : '''Comparative Evidence Against Unification''': :* ''Germany'': In 2004 and 2006, the German Bundestag rejected agency unification bills (BT-Drucksache 15/3148 & 16/510) to merge ''Grundbuch'' (Courts) and ''Liegenschaftskataster'' (Executive) following unanimous opposition from the Federal Government, Federal Notaries Association (BNotK), and Judiciary, which cited the need to preserve independent judicial review, constitutive effect (''konstitutive Wirkung''), and public trust (공신력). :* ''Japan'': Japan's 1960 unification of register books and cadastres occurred because the Ministry of Justice's registry offices had already managed BOTH systems since 1950 (meaning there was no Judiciary vs. Executive division). After unification, Japanese registry offices suffered severe operational backlogs (taking 2+ weeks per registration), and local municipalities still had to maintain separate tax registers (고정자산과세대장). ; Objectives : Preserve the structural advantages and judicial independence of Korea's dual public disclosure system while resolving administrative discrepancies and double procedural burdens through practical, e-government technical linkage. ; Implementation & Proposed Reforms : '''Building Act Amendment (건축법 제39조 개정)''': Amend Article 39 of the Building Act to transform local government heads' registration commission from discretionary (등기촉탁을 할 수 있다) to MANDATORY (지방자치단체장의 등기촉탁 의무화) whenever building cadastre details change upon use approval. Simultaneously, abolish the civil fine penalty under Real Estate Registration Act Article 112 (과태료 규정 삭제). : '''Direct E-System Linkage (등기기록과 대장 전산시스템 연계)''': Create direct, seamless electronic cross-viewing links between the Court Internet Registry (대법원 인터넷등기소) and Executive Minwon24 (민원24) / cadastral systems, allowing citizens and officials to view and cross-check both records with a single click (one-click). : '''Real-Time Notification & Commission (실시간 통지와 촉탁)''': Upgrade court and executive computer networks to enable instant, automated transmission of registration and cadastral modifications between court registry offices and local government cadastral departments. : '''Automated System Updates (관련 정보의 자동 변경)''': Implement automated data synchronization so that when a change is entered in the primary source system (e.g., physical changes in cadastres or ownership changes in registers), the corresponding fields in the secondary system update automatically without manual re-entry. : '''Restriction of MOLIT's Project Scope''': Confine MOLIT's 부동산 행정정보 일원화 사업 strictly to the 15 executive cadastral records under MOLIT jurisdiction, excluding court registration rights records. == 5. MediaWiki Output == {{Infobox Judicial Policy|name=A Research on Methods for Improving Korea's Real Estate Records System|official_name=현행 이원적 부동산 공시제도의 발전 방안에 관한 연구|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-201412|issuing_authority=Judicial Policy Research Institute (사법정책연구원)|authors=Yang, Eunsang (양은상), Kim, Tae-ho (김태호)|publication_date=2014-12-30|report_series=연구보고서 2014-12|isbn=979-11-954206-1-2|legal_basis=ROK Constitution Art. 23(1); Civil Act Art. 186; Real Estate Registration Act; Building Act Arts. 22 & 39; Court Organization Act Arts. 2 & 9}} '''A Research on Methods for Improving Korea's Real Estate Records System''' is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. == Summary == This document is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. It comprehensively analyzes South Korea's dual real estate public disclosure system (이원적 부동산 공시제도) — under which the Judiciary (Supreme Court) manages the real estate registration system (부동산 등기제도) through court register books (등기부), while the Executive branch (Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport / MOLIT and local governments) manages the cadastral system (부동산 등록제도) through cadastral books (대장). It evaluates comparative studies and unification debates in Germany and Japan; diagnoses the legal defects, unconstitutionality, and technical limitations of the executive-led project to unify property records (부동산 행정정보 일원화 사업 / 부동산종합공부); and formulates practical improvement recommendations within the current dual framework through amendment of the Building Act (건축법), integration of e-government computer systems, and automated cross-system data updates. == Legal Basis == The legal frameworks analyzed include: * '''Constitution of the Republic of Korea''': Article 23(1) (Guarantee of Property Rights & the Private Property System). * '''Civil Act of South Korea (민법)''': Article 186 (Constitutive Principle of Property Rights Registration / 성립요건주의 / 형식주의), Article 268, Article 303(2), and Article 361. * '''Real Estate Registration Act (부동산등기법)''': Articles 7, 11, 12, 15, 19, 22, 29, 35, 36, 38, 41, 43, 48, 58, 62, 65, 66, 100, 107, 109(2), and 112. * '''Building Act (건축법)''': Article 22 (Use Approval), Article 38 (Building Cadastre / 건축물대장), and Article 39 (Registration Commission / 등기촉탁). * '''Act on Surveying, Hydrographic Survey and Cadastre (측수지법)''': Articles 64, 71, 76-2, 76-3, 84, 88, 89, and Enforcement Decree Article 62-2. * '''Court Organization Act (법원조직법)''': Article 2(3), Article 9(3), and Article 19. * '''Supreme Court Jurisprudence''': En Banc Decision No. 2011Du30878 (Dec 20, 2012) & No. 2006Du19693 (Mar 19, 2009) on the limits of executive delegation orders (위임명령의 한계 일탈). == Background == Real estate is the object of property rights underlying citizens' livelihoods and the national economy. South Korea operates a dual disclosure system in which the courts manage property rights (권리관계) and the executive government manages the physical status of property (현황) and taxation. In 2013, 192 court registry offices with 1,768 staff handled more than 10.69 million property registration cases. However, the existence of two separate systems has led to potential data discrepancies between the register book (등기부) and the cadastre (대장), dual procedures for citizens, and administrative inefficiency. == Objectives == # Diagnose the strengths and operational challenges of South Korea's dual property disclosure system. # Evaluate comparative studies and unification debates in Germany (Grundbuch vs. Liegenschaftskataster) and Japan (1960 Amendment). # Examine the unconstitutionality and legal defects of Article 62-2 of the Enforcement Decree of the 측수지법, which forces the merger of judicial registration data into the executive's 부동산종합공부. # Formulate practical and technical improvement recommendations within the dual framework without altering the judiciary's institutional structure. == Scope == * '''Ten-Country Comparative Study''': Germany, Japan, the Netherlands, France, Belgium, Austria, Slovenia, Greece, the US, and the UK. * '''Evaluation of the Executive Project''': Analysis of the 부동산 행정정보 일원화 사업 (15 MOLIT cadastral records + 3 court registration records). * '''Practical Reform Recommendations''': Amendment of the 건축법, e-government system linkage (대법원 인터넷등기소 & 민원24), real-time notification, and automated data updates. == Key Provisions == * '''Advantages of the Dual System & Separation of Powers''': Maintains the separation of authority between the Judiciary and the Executive to prevent centralization of property data in a single institution and to protect private property rights. * '''Unconstitutionality of Article 62-2 of the Enforcement Decree of the 측수지법''': Confirms that the Enforcement Decree Article 62-2 is '''null and void''' (무효) for exceeding the scope of parent-statute delegation (위임명령의 한계 일탈) and violating the MediaWiki Output == {{Infobox Judicial Policy|name=Research on Different Level Lecture Programs Conducted by Judges for Elementary, Middle, and High School Students (Appendix)|official_name=법관의 초·중·고등학생을 위한 수준별 강의안(별책)|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-201501-APP|issuing_authority=Judicial Policy Research Institute (사법정책연구원)|publication_date=2015-05-22|report_series=연구총서 2015-01-별책|isbn=979-11-86491-15-7|legal_basis=Act on Support for Law-Related Education Art. 2; Constitution of the Republic of Korea}} '''Research on Different Level Lecture Programs Conducted by Judges for Elementary, Middle, and High School Students (Appendix)''' is an official, practical guide published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) to help judges deliver tiered legal lectures to elementary, middle, and high school students. == Summary == This document is an official, practical guide published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) to help judges deliver tiered legal lectures to elementary, middle, and high school students. == Legal Basis == The development of this educational module is grounded in: * '''Act on Support for Law-Related Education''': Article 2. * '''Constitution of the Republic of Korea''': Provisions on the right to trial, separation of powers, judicial independence, and human rights. * '''School Violence Prevention and Countermeasures Act''': Articles 2 and 20. == Background == Many students perceive law and the courts as complicated, intimidating, or rigid. This manual was designed to address that barrier through a friendly, contextualized educational approach. == Objectives == # Help young people understand the judicial system and rational methods of dispute resolution. # Strengthen public trust in judicial institutions. # Provide judges with practical guidance for delivering material appropriate to students' developmental level. == Scope == The lecture modules are divided into three tiers: * '''Elementary level (Grades 4–6)''': Focuses on basic legal concepts as shared rules, symbols of justice (the Goddess of Justice and Haetae), human rights, and internet ethics. * '''Middle school level''': Focuses on legal classification, types of courts, court structure, and the right to trial. * '''High school level''': Focuses on in-depth understanding of civil and criminal procedure, constitutional rights guarantees, and real case analysis. == Key Provisions == * Standard time allocations: Elementary (43 minutes), Middle school (50 minutes), High school (65 minutes). * Alignment of material with the national curriculum (e.g., the "Law and Politics" subject in high school). * Provision of sample complaint documents, response letters, and copies of court judgments for case studies. == Implementation == Judges may use this module either when visiting schools directly or when receiving student visits to the courts. Interactive teaching methods such as quizzes, animated screenings, and shared reading exercises are recommended to maintain student concentration. == Policy Issues == Variation in comprehension levels among students, combined with limited classroom time, requires judges to exercise flexibility in trimming or selecting lecture topics. == Reform / Amendments == The manual provides condensed module variants as well as specialized civil-track or criminal-track options, allowing instruction to be adapted to field conditions. == Relationship to Other Entities == * '''Publisher''': Judicial Policy Research Institute & Supreme Court of Korea. * '''Exemplary Figure''': Kim Byung-ro (First Chief Justice of Korea). == See Also == * [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] * [[Act on Support for Law-Related Education]] * [[Kim Byung-ro]] == References == == 7. Policy Analysis == ; Background : Encouraging public participation and openness in judicial administration (사법행정 참여) is a foundational element for strengthening public trust in the courts. In South Korea, the judiciary has developed two main mechanisms for citizen participation: the Citizen Judicial Council (시민사법위원회) and the Citizen Judicial Participation Group (시민사법참여단), alongside online and offline communication mechanisms. ; Policy Problem : '''Operational Limitations of the Citizen Judicial Council (시민사법위원회)''': The Council often operates passively, focusing solely on plenary meetings (총회), and lacks subcommittees (분과위원회) or a steering committee (운영위원회) to sustain the practical implementation of its agenda. : '''Fragmented Participation in the Citizen Judicial Participation Group (시민사법참여단)''': This group, composed of over 100 ordinary citizens, lacks an independent governing body (자체 운영기구) and is entirely dependent on court management, limiting its function to online monitoring or blog commentary without a deeper consultative process. : '''Lack of Structured Dialogue and Feedback''': The dialogue mechanism between courts and local communities has not been systematically structured, and lacks standardized management guidelines, orientation programs, and in-depth interview-based methods for identifying issues. ; Legal/Policy Gap : The absence of standardized management guidelines for public participation administration and an integrated online/offline consultation platform to bridge judicial governance and the public. ; Objectives : Strengthen the systematization, implementation, specialization, and consolidation of public participation in Korea's judicial administration; activate subcommittees and steering committees; diversify member representation; build an online consultation/debate portal; and implement structured feedback methods (in-depth interviews, focus groups, orientation programs). ; Implementation & Proposed Reforms : '''Activation of Subcommittees & Steering Committee (분과위원회 및 운영위원회 활성화)''': Establish an executive steering committee and practical subcommittees within the Citizen Judicial Council to complement the plenary meeting function and realize judicial policy proposals. : '''Diversification & Representation of Membership (구성의 다변화)''': Expand external membership beyond well-known figures to include representatives from legal organizations, NGOs, arts/culture, religion, media, academia, women's organizations, and disability associations (10–30 members, 2-year terms; 1 year at Seoul Central District Court). : '''Digital Participation & Online Platforms (온라인 자문 및 커뮤니티 구축)''': Develop a dedicated website for online consultation, e-panels, and deliberative e-polling (숙의형 e-여론조사) to reach a broader range of stakeholders. : '''Issue Identification & Capacity-Building Methods''': Conduct in-depth interviews and focus groups with court users, staff, and participants; develop management guidelines; hold orientation programs; and establish online communities. == 5. It evaluates the development and operational status of public participation in South Korea's judicial administration — specifically the Citizen Judicial Council (시민사법위원회) and the Citizen Judicial Participation Group (시민사법참여단) — and examines court and community collaboration practices in the United States. In South Korea, courts operate two main channels: the Citizen Judicial Council, which focuses on policy advice, and the Citizen Judicial Participation Group, which focuses on online monitoring and publication. == Summary ==
This document is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of the Supreme Court of Korea. The study develops 7 level-differentiated mock trial scripts along with a comprehensive guidance manual for judges serving as instructors in middle and high school court experience programs. The initiative directly addresses the historical imbalance of mock trial materials—which heavily favored criminal cases—by balancing civil and criminal proceedings, aligning legal complexity with students' educational levels, and fostering legal literacy and public trust in the Korean judiciary.

== Legal Basis ==
The operational framework and guidelines analyzed in this report include:

'''Law-Related Education (LRE) Framework (법교육)''': A public legal education initiative designed to build legal awareness, civic responsibility, and critical thinking among secondary students.

'''Advanced Court Experience Program Guidelines (고급 법원체험프로그램)''': Internal court regulations governing student visits and mock trial execution supervised by judges acting as educational instructors (지도관).

== Background ==
Scripted mock trials have proven to be an effective law-related education tool for secondary students. However, traditional mock trial scenarios exhibited significant structural flaws:

Excessive reliance on criminal cases (형사 사건 편중 현상), which skewed student understanding of the broader judicial system and ignored civil litigation.

A lack of differentiation between the cognitive and legal educational levels of middle school versus high school students.

The absence of a standardized operational manual for judges conducting court experience programs.

== Objectives ==
Develop 7 level-differentiated mock trial scripts tailored for middle school (3 scripts) and high school (4 scripts) students.

Establish a quantitative balance between civil and criminal litigation in educational scenarios.

Formulate a standardized, 3-stage guidance manual for judges (법관을 위한 모의재판 지도안) leading mock trial programs.

== Scope ==
'''Middle School Scripts (3 Scenarios)''': 1 civil case and 2 criminal cases.

'''High School Scripts (4 Scenarios)''': 2 civil cases and 2 criminal cases.

'''Judicial Operational Manual''': A structured, 3-stage instructional guide (Pre-trial, Trial, and Post-trial) for judge-instructors.

== Key Provisions ==
'''Scenario Development Principles''':
 Clear level separation between middle and high school educational tiers.
 Topic selection based on real-world incidents and everyday situations to maximize engagement.
 A balanced mix of civil and criminal cases.
 Legal complexity set slightly above the students' current educational baseline.
'''Three-Stage Guidance Manual for Judges''':
 '''Pre-trial Stage (실시 전 단계)''': Scenario selection, script adaptation, time allocation, facility/prop preparation, student orientation, and role assignment.
 '''Trial Stage (실시 중 단계)''': Script execution, outcome prediction discussions, student opinion sheet completion, and mock citizen jury deliberations (국민참여재판 평의·평결).
 '''Post-trial Stage (실시 후 단계)''': Summary of procedural and legal outcomes by the judge, Q&A session, and in-depth debriefing.

== Implementation ==
Courts across South Korea implement these level-differentiated scripts and the judge's guidance manual within the Advanced Court Experience Program (고급 법원체험프로그램), directly supervised by active judges.

== Policy Issues ==
Over-concentration on criminal law in past educational materials.

Absence of a leveled curriculum adapted to the developmental stages of secondary students.

Lack of standardized instructional training for judges serving as educators.

== Reforms ==
Promulgation of 7 leveled mock trial scripts covering civil and criminal law.

Standardized 3-stage operational manual for judge-instructors.

Integration of citizen participation trial mechanisms (국민참여재판) into judicial education.

== Entity Relationships ==
'''Issuing Authority''': Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) / Supreme Court of Korea.

'''Lead Author''': Park, Weon-Keu (박원규) [Stable ID: JPW-PERSON-000057].

'''Unaffiliated Entities''': Cecep Mustafa [Stable ID: JPW-PERSON-UNKNOWN01] and Qonita Mutmainah [Stable ID: JPW-PERSON-UNKNOWN02] (Unidentified in source documentation; flagged as unaffiliated).

== Key Policy Improvements ==
'''Digital Distribution Standardization''': Integrating the 7 scripts into the Supreme Court portal as accessible e-books for secondary schools and regional courts.

'''Institutionalizing Citizen Jury Deliberations''': Embedding mock citizen jury voting and deliberation (국민참여재판 평의·평결) into high school criminal scenarios to foster understanding of participatory justice.

'''Judicial Instructor Training-of-Trainers (ToT)''': Developing periodic workshops based on the operational manual to maintain consistent instructional quality across district courts nationwide.

Policy Analysis == ; Background : Globalization, expanding international trade, and complex commercial transactions have heightened the demand for rapid, specialized, and flexible alternative dispute resolution (ADR) mechanisms. While arbitration is traditionally conducted by private arbitrators (attorneys, academics, industry experts) or institutional bodies like KCAB, sitting judge-run arbitration (법관에 의한 중재) represents a unique hybrid where active judicial officers conduct confidential, binding arbitration inside court facilities. Common law jurisdictions exhibit divergent approaches: England & Wales (Sec. 93 Arbitration Act 1996) and Scotland (Sec. 25 Arbitration Act 2010) permit sitting High Court / Commercial Court / TCC judges to serve as sole arbitrators, whereas US judicial ethics rules generally forbid judges from acting as arbitrators. ; Policy Problem : '''Unconstitutionality of Confidential Judge-Run Adjudication''': In Delaware, the Court of Chancery established a confidential business arbitration program in 2009 (10 Del. C. § 349). In ''Delaware Coalition for Open Government v. Strine'' (2012–2013), federal courts struck down the program, ruling that conducting confidential, binding trials led by active judges using state facilities and taxpayer-funded salaries violates the First Amendment Right of Public Access. : '''Violation of the Open Trial Principle in Korea''': ROK Constitution Article 109 guarantees that court trials and judgments shall be open to the public (재판공개의 원칙). Introducing confidential judge-arbitration would violate Article 109 and trigger fundamental constitutional challenges. : '''Creation of a "Two-Tier Justice System" & Public Distrust''': Critics and legal scholars argue that judge-arbitration creates an elitist "special door to the courthouse" where wealthy corporations receive secret, expedited justice from active judges, while ordinary citizens endure public, delayed litigation, undermining public trust in judicial equality (법 앞의 평등). : '''Ethical & "Current Official" Bias Risks (현관예우 / 現官禮遇)''': Allowing active judges to serve as private arbitrators or accept arbitration fees introduces severe conflicts of interest, perceived judicial bias, and risks of "current official favors." : '''No Net Reduction in Court Caseload''': Empirical and comparative data show that judge-arbitration does not reduce general court litigation volume or appellate burdens because commercial parties choosing arbitration would otherwise use private arbitration rather than trial courts. ; Legal/Policy Gap : ROK law contains no statutory authorization for sitting judges to act as arbitrators. Civil procedure and arbitration statutes strictly maintain the division between public judicial power and private arbitration. ; Objectives : Evaluate international judge-arbitration models; confirm the constitutional and procedural infeasibility of sitting judge-arbitrators in Korea; and design alternative, constitutionally sound court-connected ADR reforms. ; Implementation & Proposed Alternative Reforms : '''Rejection of Sitting Judge-Arbitrators''': Conclude that South Korea should not introduce sitting judge-arbitrators due to insurmountable constitutional, ethical, and public trust barriers. : '''Alternative 1: Promoting Retired Judges as Private Arbitrators (퇴직 법관에 의한 중재)''': Encourage retired senior judges with deep judicial expertise to register as private arbitrators with KCAB or conduct ad hoc arbitration, expanding private dispute resolution without compromising sitting judicial neutrality. : '''Alternative 2: Establishing Specialized Court Arbitration Benches (중재전담법관 / 중재전문재판부)''': Designate specialized arbitration judges/benches at major courts (such as Seoul Central District Court and Seoul High Court) to handle court-related arbitration support (enforcement judgments, set-aside petitions, interim measures, arbitrator appointment support) with high expertise and speed, modeled after Australia (List G in Victoria Supreme Court), Ireland, and Hong Kong. : '''Alternative 3: Court-Annexed Med-Arb utilizing Standing Mediators (상임조정위원을 활용한 조정-중재 프로그램)''': :* Establish a court-annexed Med-Arb program within Court Mediation Centers (법원조정센터) operating across 10 regional courts. :* Authorize 31 full-time Standing Mediators (상임조정위원 — senior legal professionals with 15+ years experience) to serve as arbitrators upon voluntary post-dispute consent by the parties (선 조정, 후 중재). :* Require a specific statutory amendment to the Arbitration Act authorizing courts to provide administrative and record-management support for Standing Mediator arbitration. ; Strine}} '''A Research on Judge-run Arbitration in the U.K., and the U.S., and the Possibility of Introducing Judge-Arbitrator''' is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. == Summary == This document is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. It comparatively analyzes the legal framework of judge-run arbitration (법관에 의한 중재) in England, Scotland, and the State of Delaware (US). It examines the landmark US ruling ''Delaware Coalition for Open Government v. Strine'' (3rd Cir. 2013), which held that confidential judge-run arbitration violates the First Amendment Right of Public Access; evaluates the constitutional barrier posed by Article 109 of the Korean Constitution (the Open Trial Principle); and formulates alternative policy recommendations, including promoting retired judges as private arbitrators (퇴직 법관에 의한 중재), establishing Specialized Arbitration Judges/Benches (중재전담법관 / 중재전문재판부), and an integrated Med-Arb scheme using Standing Mediators (상임조정위원) at Court Mediation Centers. == Legal Basis == The legal frameworks analyzed include: * '''Court Organization Act of South Korea (법원조직법)''': The legal basis for establishing the Judicial Policy Research Institute under the Supreme Court of Korea. * '''Constitution of the Republic of Korea''': Article 27(3) (Right to a Fair and Speedy Trial) and Article 109 (Open Trial Principle / 재판공개의 원칙). * '''Arbitration Act of South Korea (중재법)''': Articles 3, 6, 7, 12, 13, 14, 20, 29, 31, 41. * '''UK Arbitration Act 1996''': Section 93 (Appointment of Judges as Arbitrators in the Commercial Court & TCC) & Schedule 2. * '''Arbitration (Scotland) Act 2010''': Section 25 & Rule 26. * '''Delaware Law (US)''': Former 10 Del. C. § 349 & Chancery Rules 96-98 (struck down); the Delaware Rapid Arbitration Act (DRAA 2015 / 10 Del. C. § 5801-5812) & Revised Chancery Rules 96-98. * '''Landmark US Jurisprudence''': ''Delaware Coalition for Open Government v. Strine'' (894 F.Supp. 2d 493 (D. Del. 2012), affirmed 733 F.3d 510 (3d Cir. 2013)). == Background == The escalation of commercial disputes and the complexity of business transactions have driven demand for fast, expert Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) mechanisms. Common law countries take different approaches: England and Scotland allow sitting Commercial Court and TCC judges to act as sole arbitrators, while in the US, judicial ethics prohibit sitting judges from serving as arbitrators. Delaware's experiment with confidential judge-run arbitration (2009) sparked fierce debate and was ultimately struck down by US federal courts for violating the public's constitutional right to open access to justice. == Objectives == # Diagnose the legal framework and effectiveness of judge-run arbitration in England, Scotland, and the US. # Evaluate the implications of the ''Strine'' decision for confidential arbitration led by sitting judges. # Assess the compatibility of sitting judge arbitration with the Constitution and civil procedure of South Korea. # Formulate alternative judicial reforms to improve the effectiveness of commercial arbitration in Korea. == Scope == * '''Three-Jurisdiction Comparative Study''': England (Commercial Court & TCC Guide), Scotland (Court of Session & SAR Rule 26), and the US (Delaware Court of Chancery & DRAA 2015). * '''Constitutional & Ethical Issue Analysis''': The open trial principle (ROK Constitution Article 109 / US First Amendment), the right to equal justice, and the risk of "current official" bias (현관예우). * '''Alternative Policy Recommendations''': Retired judge arbitration, Specialized Judicial Arbitration Benches, and Standing Mediator Med-Arb. == Key Provisions == * '''Rejection of Sitting Judges as Arbitrators''': South Korea does not recommend appointing sitting judges as confidential arbitrators, as this would violate the open trial principle and create a "two-tier justice system." * '''Establishment of Specialized Arbitration Benches (중재전담법관 / 중재전문재판부)''': Allocates specialized judges at Seoul Central District Court and Seoul High Court to handle enforcement, set-aside, and arbitration support applications. * '''Standing Mediator Med-Arb Program (상임조정위원을 활용한 조정-중재)''': ** Utilizes 31 Standing Mediators (상임조정위원) across 10 Court Mediation Centers. ** Adopts a "mediation first, arbitration second" (선 조정, 후 중재) scheme based on the parties' voluntary agreement after a dispute arises. ** Requires a specific amendment to the Korean Arbitration Act to provide the legal basis for court administrative support. == Implementation == Courts encourage the registration of retired judges as arbitrators with KCAB (대한상사중재원), draft proposed amendments to the Arbitration Act for the role of Standing Mediators (상임조정위원), and strengthen mediation/arbitration courtroom infrastructure. == Policy Issues == * The potential conflict between confidential judge-run arbitration and Article 109 of the ROK Constitution (the Open Trial Principle). * Public perception of unfairness if large corporations gain access to a taxpayer-funded "special door" to confidential justice. == Reform / Amendments == # Rejection of appointing sitting judges as confidential arbitrators. # Establishment of Specialized Arbitration Judges/Benches (중재전담법관 / 중재전문재판부). # Enactment of an integrated Med-Arb Program at Court Mediation Centers (상임조정위원 Med-Arb). # Specific amendment to the Korean Arbitration Act for Med-Arb administrative support. == Relationship to Other Entities == * '''Issuing Institution''': Judicial Policy Research Institute & Supreme Court of Korea. * '''Lead Researcher''': Rhee Jae-Seok (이재석). * '''Related Institutions''': KCAB (대한상사중재원) & the Court Mediation Center (법원조정센터). == See Also == * [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] * [[Supreme Court of Korea]] * [[Korean Commercial Arbitration {{Infobox Judicial Policy|name=Standard Proposal for Legal Citation Methods [Draft]|official_name=법률문헌 등의 인용방법 표준안 [시안]|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-201512-ATT|issuing_authority=Judicial Policy Research Institute (사법정책연구원)|authors=Byun, Ji-young (변지영), Lee, Deok-hwan (이덕환), Yang, Si-hoon (양시훈), Gye, In-gook (계인국)|publication_date=2015-09-14|report_series=JPRI Research Series 2015-12 Attachment|isbn=979-11-86491-47-8|legal_basis=JPRI Research Framework & Research Ethics Guidelines}}

== Summary ==
This document is an official legal citation standard draft published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of the Supreme Court of Korea as supplementary material to JPRI Research Report 2015-12. The manual establishes unified, systematic rules for citing domestic court decisions, statutes, books, academic journals, public reports, digital documents, foreign legislation and case law across seven jurisdictions, and international law instruments. The standard is designed to prevent plagiarism, protect copyright, enforce research ethics, and ensure the reliability and traceability of South Korean legal research.

== Legal Basis ==
The operational framework and foundational authority analyzed in this report include:

* '''Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) Research Authority''': Published as the official attachment to JPRI Research Series 2015-12 ("Research on Legal Citation Methods").
* '''Research Ethics & Copyright Principles''': Grounded in principles of good faith citation, copyright protection, and the strict distinction between original analysis and referenced material.

== Background ==
With the rapid growth of legal research and the digitalization of legal literature, the absence of a uniform citation standard across academics, legal practitioners, and the judiciary created confusion, inconsistent citations, and potential research ethics risks such as plagiarism and self-plagiarism. A national standard proposal was required to unify legal citation practices in South Korea.

== Objectives ==
1. Prevent plagiarism and uphold research ethics in South Korean legal scholarship. 2. Ensure easy verification and source traceability for readers and researchers. 3. Establish unified citation conventions for domestic court decisions, statutes, digital literature, foreign laws, and international legal instruments.

== Scope ==

* '''General Citation Rules''': Footnote system (`각주방식`), direct and indirect quotations, re-citation rules (`재인용`), and short-form citations.
* '''Domestic Legal Materials''': Decisions of the Supreme Court, Constitutional Court, lower courts, quasi-judicial bodies, active statutes, former statutes (`구법`), and North Korean legal materials.
* '''Digital Literature & New Media''': Webpages, online news articles, blogs, and electronic databases.
* '''Foreign & International Law''': Legal systems across seven jurisdictions (United States, United Kingdom, Germany, France, European Union, Japan, and China), international treaties, ICJ/ICTY/ICTR precedents, UN documents, and WTO reports.

== Key Provisions ==

* '''South Korean Court Judgments''': Formatted as `[Court Name] [Date YYYY. M. D.] [선고] [Case Number] [Judgment Type]` (e.g., `대법원 1996. 4. 26. 선고 96다1078 판결`).
* '''Statutes and Regulations''': Formatted as `[Statute Name] [Article No.] [Paragraph No.] [Item No.]`.
* '''Digital Literature''': Mandatory inclusion of the complete URL alongside the last confirmation date in parentheses, e.g., `(YYYY. M. D. 확인)`.
* '''Secondary Sources''': Mandates direct verification of primary sources whenever possible; secondary citations require explicit attribution to both primary and secondary works using the tag `재인용`.

== Implementation ==
This draft standard serves as an official writing guideline for JPRI research reports, judicial journals, and official legal filings within the Supreme Court of Korea.

== Policy Issues ==

* Inconsistency in citation formatting across legal journals, law schools, and judicial institutions in South Korea.
* Absence of standardized citation conventions for digital materials, electronic resources, and online official publications.

== Reforms ==
1. Promulgation of the National Standard Draft for Legal Citation Methods (`법률문헌 인용방법 표준안`). 2. Standardization of rules governing digital and new media legal citations. 3. Alignment of foreign legal citations with the official standards of their respective jurisdictions (e.g., Bluebook, neutral citations, BVerfGE/BGHZ, J.O., OJ).

== Entity Relationships ==

* '''Issuing Authority''': Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) / Supreme Court of Korea.
* '''Research Team''': Byun, Ji-young (변지영) [Lead Researcher], Lee, Deok-hwan (이덕환), Yang, Si-hoon (양시훈), Gye, In-gook (계인국).
* '''Parent Report''': JPRI Research Series 2015-12 ("Research on Legal Citation Methods").
* '''Unaffiliated Entities''': Cecep Mustafa [Stable ID: JPW-PERSON-UNKNOWN01] and Qonita Mutmainah [Stable ID: JPW-PERSON-UNKNOWN02] (Unidentified in source documentation; flagged as unaffiliated).

== Key Policy Improvements ==
1. '''Official Adoption by Judiciary and Law Schools''': Formal integration of the JPRI draft standard into the style guides of law school journals and judicial publications nationwide. 2. '''AI-Based Automated Citation Validation Tool''': Developing an automated verification module within the judicial research portal to check footnote formats, URL access dates, and secondary citation tags (`재인용`). 3. '''Periodic Updates for Digital and Foreign Standards''': Establishing annual updates to maintain standard abbreviations, e-journal citations, and international neutral citation formats.

Policy Analysis == ; Background : Law enforcement search and seizure in South Korea faced long-standing public criticism due to overbroad, indiscriminate bulk search practices. Investigators routinely seized whole paper file collections or physical computer hardware and transferred them to police or prosecutorial offices, conducting covert, unconstrained data exploration over extended periods. ; Policy Problem : Bulk hardware and file seizures inflict massive operational disruption on corporations, violate fundamental constitutional rights to privacy and property, and risk converting specific crime warrants into unconstitutional general warrants ("fishing expeditions"). ; Legal/Policy Gap : Traditional Criminal Procedure Code provisions were constructed around tangible physical objects. Although the 2011 CPC amendment introduced Article 106(3) — establishing the output or copying of specific digital data as the mandatory default method — investigators frequently resorted to statutory exceptions, seizing physical storage media or entire disk images without proper ex-ante judicial limitations or ex-post controls. ; Objectives : Harmonize the dual imperatives of criminal procedure: maintaining effective truth-finding and societal security while strictly enforcing constitutional due process, proportionality, and the warrant requirement. ; Implementation : Formulated a comprehensive four-stage reform framework: :# ''Warrant Issuance Stage'': Implement substantial ex-ante hearings (examining affiants/investigators under oath), establish an Electronic Warrant (e-Warrant) system, introduce separate or phased search vs. seizure warrants, and impose explicit ex-ante method restrictions on warrant attachments. :# ''Execution Stage'': Enforce mandatory attendance and participation rights for suspects, defendants, and defense counsel during all off-site digital parsing, filtering, and copying phases. :# ''Post-Execution Stage'': Require mandatory return of warrants, detailed inventory lists, and non-relevant data deletion records to the issuing court; actively enforce and notify statutory return/temporary return rights under CPC Article 218-2. :# ''Trial Stage'': Apply the Exclusionary Rule (위법수집증거 배제법칙) rigorously under the Relevance Rule (관련성 원칙), rejecting attempts to import foreign "plain view" exceptions into digital search contexts. ; Evidence : Empirical analysis of 2014 ROK judicial statistics reveals that out of 181,067 search/seizure/inspection warrant applications (which saw a 91.7% issuance rate), only 380 court applications for the return or temporary return of seized items were filed nationwide. This stark disparity demonstrated that post-seizure remedy mechanisms were severely underutilized due to lack of explicit procedural notices. ; Impact : Directly shaped the Seoul Central District Court's revised warrant practice (effective August 1, 2015), which explicitly restricted digital seizure scope in warrant text, mandated detailed electronic inventory delivery, enforced the destruction of non-relevant data, and guaranteed full participation rights across all imaging and parsing phases. ; Evaluation : Serves as a foundational policy roadmap for digital evidence jurisprudence in Korea, reinforcing Supreme Court En Banc Decision 2011Mo1839 and entrenching the Relevance Rule as a non-negotiable constitutional check on state coercive power. ; Reform Recommendations : Institutionalize e-Warrant platforms, enact statutory obligations requiring immediate deletion of non-relevant digital data, mandate post-execution court return filings, and insert clear procedural remedy rights directly onto search warrant forms. ; Unresolved Issues : Resolving cross-border data access (trans-border remote searches) under cloud computing frameworks, establishing legal mechanisms for encryption key disclosure without infringing the privilege against self-incrimination, and managing judicial administrative workloads resulting from increased ex-ante and ex-post hearings. == 5.
