It comparatively analyzes search and seizure law in Japan, the United States, and Germany, and formulates comprehensive reforms to prevent bulk seizures and unrestricted seizure of electronic information. == Legal Basis == The legal frameworks analyzed include: * '''Constitution of the Republic of Korea''': Article 12 (Personal Liberty & Due Process), Article 16 (Warrant Doctrine & Inviolability of Residence), Article 17 (Privacy), Article 18 (Secrecy of Communications), Article 21 (Freedom of Expression), and Article 37(2) (Proportionality Principle). * '''Criminal Procedure Code of the Republic of Korea (형사소송법)''': Article 106 (Digital Data Output/Copy Principle), Article 109, Article 199(1) (Proportionality), Article 215 (Crime Relevance), Articles 216–218 (Warrant Exceptions), and Article 218-2 (Right to Return of Seized Items). * '''Protection of Communications Secrets Act (통신비밀보호법)''': Articles 3, 5, 6, 9-2, 9-3, and 13. == Background == Law enforcement practice in South Korea has historically involved bulk seizure of entire document collections or computer hardware without filtering for crime relevance. Such devices were brought to investigators' offices and analyzed covertly over extended periods, violating constitutional rights and disrupting business operations. == Objectives == # Balance the discovery of substantive truth (실체적 진실규명) with the protection of human rights and due process of law (적법절차). # Formulate judicial controls at the warrant issuance, execution, and post-execution stages of search and seizure. == Scope == * '''Comparative Study''': Japanese law (2011 CPC Amendment & Wiretapping Act), US law (4th Amendment, Fed. R. Crim. P. 41/4.1, SCA, Wiretap Act, CalECPA), and German law (Grundgesetz & StPO). * '''Main Focus''': Seizure of digital evidence (디지털 증거), the right of the examined party to be present (참여권), and ex-ante restrictions (사전적 제한). == Key Provisions == * '''Output/Copy Principle''': Seizure of digital data must be carried out by printing or copying the relevant files on-site (Article 106(3) of the Criminal Procedure Code). * '''Relevance Principle (관련성 원칙)''': Seizure is only valid for data with objective, subjective, and temporal relevance to the alleged crime. * '''Plain View Exception''': The report rejects extending the "plain view" doctrine to exploratory digital data searches. == Implementation == The report evaluates and supports the integrated warrant practice adopted by the Seoul Central District Court (effective August 1, 2015), which requires submission of detailed digital file inventories, deletion of irrelevant data, and guarantees the examined party's right to be present throughout all analysis stages. == Policy Issues == * The high warrant issuance rate (91.7% in 2014) stands in stark contrast to the low number of applications for return of seized items (only 380 cases nationwide). * Risk of digital examination being misused as a general warrant / fishing expedition. == Reform / Amendments == # Establishment of an Electronic Warrant (e-Warrant) System. # Substantive Pre-Issuance Review (examination of witnesses/investigators under oath). # Separate/Phased Warrant Issuance (분리/단계적 발부). # Statutory Obligation to Return and Delete Irrelevant Data Post-Execution. == Relationship to Other Entities == * '''Issuing Institution''': Judicial Policy Research Institute & Supreme Court of Korea. * '''Research Team''': Son Ji-young, Kim Joo-seok. * '''Related Judicial Practice''': Seoul Central District Court (서울중앙지방법원). == See Also == * [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] * [[Supreme Court of Korea]] * [[Digital Evidence Seizure Rules]] * [[Exclusionary Rule in South Korea]] == References == == 7. Policy Analysis == ; Background : Under South Korea's criminal justice system, summary procedures allow courts to impose fines, minor fines, or confiscations via written examination without formal public trials. In 1997, Article 457-2 was inserted into the Criminal Procedure Code, establishing the prohibition of reformatio in peius (불이익변경금지원칙) for formal trials requested by defendants following summary orders, meaning the court in a formal trial could not impose a heavier penalty than that in the summary order. ; Policy Problem : The introduction of Article 457-2 caused a massive surge in formal trial requests — increasing from 1.8% of summary orders in 1997 to 11.5% in 2014 (and over 14% in 2012). Defendants filed formal trials with a "nothing to lose" (밑져야 본전) mindset solely to delay fine payments, delay administrative license suspensions (especially in business offenses/영업범), or attempt to obtain a suspended sentence of imprisonment rather than a fine. ; Legal/Policy Gap : Formal trial cases represent over 30% of all single-judge criminal trial caseloads (고정사건). Because full trial proceedings with strict rules of evidence are applied to minor summary cases without the possibility of increasing the fine, judicial resources are severely distorted, causing trial delays and impairing the court's ability to conduct thorough trials for serious and complex criminal cases. ; Objectives : Reform the formal trial system to ensure that the constitutional right to trial is upheld without being abused for improper collateral purposes, restore the proper filtering function of summary orders, and establish an efficient, two-tiered criminal justice procedure. ; Implementation & Proposed Reforms : '''Abolition or Modification of Article 457-2''': Abolish the prohibition of reformatio in peius for formal trials, or restrict its scope. To protect defendants' rights upon abolition, implement safeguards: advance explanation/notice of summary procedures, pre-trial confirmation of intent, written decision procedure for fine-only appeals (similar to German StPO § 411(1)), restriction on pre-trial detention during formal trial, and mandatory written reasons when increasing sentence. : '''Summary Stage Reforms''': Expand summary order targets to include judgments of acquittal (무죄), dismissal of public prosecution (공소기각), and exemption of punishment (면소/형면제); enforce verified service locations to reduce public notice service (공시송달) rates which exceed 30%. : '''Trial & Fine Efficiency''': Introduce simplified evidence examination rules and simplified judgment drafting for formal trials; operationalize suspended fines (벌금형의 집행유예), installment/deferred fine payments, and community service in lieu of fine detention (노역장 유치). : '''Long-term Structural Reform''': Establish specialized summary courts (간이법원) or expand Rechtspfleger (사법보좌관) duties to handle minor criminal cases, expand electronic summary filing (전자약식절차), and introduce plea bargaining / summary disposal models. ; Evidence & Empirical Data : A nationwide survey of 328 district court judges revealed that 99.4% agreed on the need for formal trial procedure reform, with 93% supporting the abolition of Article 457-2. Judicial statistics showed that in 2014, out of 84,102 formal trial dispositions, 92% resulted in the same fine or withdrawal, with actual acquittal/dismissal rates at only 4.8%. == 5. MediaWiki Output == {{Infobox Judicial Policy|name=Research on Improvement Measures of the System of Motion for a Formal Trial|official_name=정식재판청구제도 개선 방안에 관한 연구|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-201608|issuing_authority=Judicial Policy Research Institute (사법정책연구원)|authors=Kim Hyung-jin (김형진), Ha Min-kyung (하민경)|publication_date=2016-03-28|report_series=연구총서 2016-08|isbn=979-11-86491-65-2|legal_basis=ROK Constitution Arts. 27(1), 27(3); ROK Criminal Procedure Code Arts. 448–458}} '''Research on Improvement Measures of the System of Motion for a Formal Trial''' is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. == Summary == This document is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. It comparatively and systematically analyzes problems within the system of motions for a formal trial against summary orders (약식명령), and formulates legal and practical reforms to prevent abuse of the right to trial and optimize judicial resource allocation. == Legal Basis == The legal frameworks analyzed include: * '''Constitution of the Republic of Korea''': Article 27(1) (Right to a Fair Trial) and Article 27(3) (Right to a Speedy Trial). * '''Criminal Procedure Code of the Republic of Korea (형사소송법)''': Article 448 (Summary Order Requirements), Article 449 (Request for Summary Order), Article 450 (Referral to Public Trial), Article 453 (Motion for Formal Trial), Article 455 (Dismissal Decision), Article 457 (Effectiveness of Summary Order), and Article 457-2 (Prohibition of Reformatio in Peius / 불이익변경금지원칙). * '''Act on Special Cases Concerning the Promotion, etc. of Legal Proceedings''' (소송촉진 등에 관한 특례법): Article 22. * '''Act on Use of Electronic Documents in Summary Procedure''' (약식전자문서법). == Background == The summary order procedure (약식절차) was designed to quickly resolve minor offenses through written examination without an open trial. However, since Article 457-2 of the Criminal Procedure Code took effect in 1997 — prohibiting the imposition of a heavier sentence in a formal trial requested by the defendant — the rate of formal trial motions surged from 1.8% (1997) to 11.5% (2014). == Objectives == # Restore the filtering function of the summary order procedure and prevent abuse of formal trial motions. # Ensure rational allocation of judicial resources so that serious and complex cases receive thorough examination (공판중심주의, trial-centered principle). == Scope == * '''Five-Country Comparative Study''': United States (Fed. R. Crim. P. 58 & Magistrate system), United Kingdom (Summary Trial & CJS Common Platform), Germany (StPO §§ 407–412 & Beschleunigtes Verfahren), France (Procédure simplifiée), and Japan (Summary Court & 在庁略式). * '''Empirical Survey''': A survey of 328 criminal judges across district courts in South Korea. == Key Provisions == * '''Reformatio in Peius Principle''': A defendant who files for a formal trial cannot be given a heavier fine than the original summary order (Article 457-2 of the Criminal Procedure Code). * '''Practical Impact''': Defendants exploit this procedure to delay payment of fines or administrative sanctions (영업범) without risk of a heavier penalty. == Implementation == The report proposes a four-stage reform: # Abolition or scope restriction of Article 457-2 of the Criminal Procedure Code. # Expansion of summary order eligibility to include acquittals (무죄), dismissal of prosecution (공소기각), and exemption from punishment (면소). # Simplification of judgment drafting and evidence examination for minor formal trial cases. # Optimization of suspended fines (벌금형의 집행유예), installment fine payments, and electronic summary filing (전자약식). == Policy Issues == * Single-judge caseloads (고정사건) exceed 30% of all first-instance criminal cases. * Of 84,102 formal trial cases in 2014, only 4.8% resulted in a substantive change (acquittal or exemption), indicating a high rate of non-substantive motions. == Reform / Amendments == * Abolition of the prohibition of reformatio in peius, paired with procedural safeguards (advance explanation, written procedures for fine challenges, and mandatory justification when increasing a sentence). * Establishment of specialized summary courts (간이법원) or expansion of Rechtspfleger (사법보좌관) authority. == Relationship to Other Entities == * '''Issuing Institution''': Judicial Policy Research Institute & Supreme Court of Korea. * '''Research Team''': Kim Hyung-jin, Ha Min-kyung. * '''Related Institutions''': National Assembly of the Republic of Korea & Constitutional Court of Korea. == See Also == * [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] * [[Supreme Court of Korea]] * [[Prohibition of Reformatio in Peius in Formal Trial]] * [[Electronic Summary Procedure]] == References == == 7. Policy Analysis == ; Background : With the rapid globalization, specialization, and digitalization of legal research in South Korea, legal literature produced by legal scholars, judges, prosecutors, attorneys, and students requires accurate, standardized, and easily retrievable citation formats. In 2015, the Judicial Policy Research Institute published a preliminary draft (법률문헌 등의 인용방법에 관한 연구 / Research Series 2015-12). To meet expanding academic and judicial requirements for citing foreign primary legal materials, JPRI updated and expanded the draft into the 2017 enlarged edition (증보판 / Research Series 2017-01), incorporating citation methods for 37 additional foreign jurisdictions (totaling 45 countries) and refined digital resource standards. ; Policy Problem : '''Absence of Unified National Legal Citation Standards''': Historically, South Korea lacked a standardized legal citation manual, causing fragmented practices across academic journals, courts, and law schools. : '''Inconsistent Access to Foreign & Digital Materials''': Globalization increased reliance on foreign statutes, judicial decisions, and online databases. Lacking clear rules for foreign citations or URL verification created confusion and verification delays. : '''Research Ethics & Plagiarism Risks''': Vague source attribution exposed legal scholarship to risks of idea theft, plagiarism (표절), double publishing (이중게재), and self-plagiarism (자기표절). ; Legal/Policy Gap : Korean legal research lacked an official, comprehensive manual regulating domestic primary/secondary sources, digital documents, international law, and foreign law across 45 countries. ; Objectives : Provide clear footnote citation rules (각주 인용 방식); distinguish direct versus indirect citations; prevent plagiarism; establish standard formats for domestic cases, statutes, books, periodicals, and public documents; provide jurisdiction-specific rules for 45 foreign countries; integrate European Case Law Identifiers (ECLI); and regulate digital media and international law citations while protecting authors' freedom of expression. ; Implementation & Standard Rules : '''General Principles''': Footnote-based system (각주 인용 방식). Short direct quotes (3 lines or less) use double quotation marks "..."; longer direct quotes use indented paragraphs without quotation marks. It establishes a national standard (표준안) for legal citation methods (인용방법) for domestic legal literature (법률문헌) — court decisions, statutes, books, journals, public reports, and digital documents — as well as foreign law across 45 countries and international legal materials (treaties, international courts, tribunals). It aims to foster a culture of responsible research, prevent plagiarism (표절), and ensure legal sources can be easily verified. == Legal Basis == The legal and methodological frameworks analyzed include: * '''Court Organization Act of South Korea (법원조직법)''': The legal basis for establishing the Judicial Policy Research Institute under the Supreme Court of Korea. * '''Research Ethics & Copyright Standards''': Academic writing guidelines to prevent plagiarism (표절), duplicate publication (이중게재), and self-plagiarism (자기표절). * '''International Citation Guides''': The Bluebook (19th ed.), the ALWD Citation Manual (4th ed.), OSCOLA (4th ed.), the AGLC (3rd ed.), and the McGill Canadian Guide (7th ed.). == Background == With the rapid globalization and digitalization of legal research in South Korea, legal literature produced by scholars, judges, prosecutors, and attorneys requires a uniform and accurate citation standard. In 2015, JPRI published a preliminary draft (Research Series 2015-12). To meet growing demand for citing foreign legal sources, JPRI updated that draft into an enlarged edition (증보판 / Research Series 2017-01), adding guidance for 37 new countries (45 total) and digital documents. == Objectives == # Establish general principles for footnote-based citation (각주). # Develop uniform citation standards for domestic Korean court decisions, statutes, books, and journals. # Provide specific foreign law citation rules for 45 countries and the ECLI (European Case Law Identifier) system. # Regulate the citation of digital documents, online news, and international law (UN, ICJ, ICC, ITLOS, ECHR, WTO). == Scope == * '''Domestic Legal Materials''': Case law (Supreme Court, Constitutional Court, lower courts), statutes (laws, enforcement decrees, supplementary provisions, former laws), monographs, periodical articles, theses, official reports, press releases, newspaper articles, presentations, and personal records. * '''Foreign Law (45 Countries)''': US, UK, Germany, France, Japan, China, Russia, Greece, South Africa, Norway, Netherlands, New Zealand, Taiwan, Denmark, Malaysia, Mexico, Belgium, Belarus, Vietnam, Brazil, Sweden, Switzerland, Spain, Singapore, Argentina, Ireland, Austria, Uzbekistan, Ukraine, Israel, Egypt, Italy, India, Indonesia, Chile, Kazakhstan, Canada, Kenya, Thailand, Finland, Philippines, Australia, Hong Kong, the EU/EC, and ECLI. * '''International Law''': International treaties, ICJ, ICC, ITLOS, PCA, ECHR, IACHR, AfCHPR, ICTY, ICTR, ECCC, MICT, UN documents, and WTO/GATT reports. == Key Provisions == * '''Direct vs. Indirect Quotation''': Direct quotes under 3 lines use double quotation marks ("..."); longer direct quotes use indented paragraphs without quotation marks. Indirect quotes must include 참조 or 참고. * '''Korean Court Decision Format''': Court Name | Date (YYYY. M. D.) | 선고 / 자 | Case Number | 판결 / 결정 (e.g., 대법원 1996. 4. 26. 선고 96다1078 판결.). * '''Korean Statute Format''': Statute Name | Article | Paragraph | Item (e.g., 부정경쟁방지 및 영업비밀보호에 관한 법률 제2조 제1호 (가)목.). * '''Book & Journal Format''': Author, | Title (Edition), | Publisher | (Year), | Page. == Implementation == This guide is applied throughout the judiciary, the Supreme Court, and JPRI, and serves as the reference standard for law schools and academic journals across South Korea. == Policy Issues == * The absence of a national citation standard, which caused inconsistency in legal writing. * The risk of research ethics violations arising from unclear attribution of foreign and digital primary sources. == Reform / Amendments == # National standardization of citation methods for domestic and foreign legal materials. # Adoption of the ECLI (European Case Law Identifier) system for European case law. # Standardization of citation for digital and internet documents. # Protection of copyright and prevention of plagiarism in legal research. == Relationship to Other Entities == * '''Issuing Institution''': Judicial Policy Research Institute & Supreme Court of Korea. * '''Research Team''': Byun Ji-young (변지영), Oh Se-yong, Gye In-guk, Lee Je-woo. == See Also == * [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] * [[Supreme Court of Korea]] * [[European Case Law Identifier]] * [[The Bluebook]] == References == == 7. Policy Analysis == ; Background : South Korea transitioned from a career judge system (직업법관제) to a career unification system (법조일원화) requiring significant legal experience before judicial appointment. Following the 2011 amendment to the Court Organization Act, minimum career requirements stepped up incrementally (3 years in 2013, 5 years in 2018, 7 years in 2022, and 10 years by 2026). Concurrently, national judge demographics experienced severe aging: the average judge age rose from 38.8 in 2003 to 42.6 in 2017 (and is projected to exceed 50 by 2030). ; Policy Problem : '''Imminent Chronic Shortage of Qualified Judicial Candidates''': Requiring 10 years of prior legal practice severely restricts candidate pools, making recruitment difficult and creating chronic judicial vacancies. : '''Accelerating Judge Resignations & Former Judge Privilege Controversies (전관예우)''': Most Korean judges resign long before reaching the statutory retirement age of 65 (only 6 judges reached statutory retirement between 2013 and 2017 out of hundreds of resignations) to open private law practices, triggering public distrust over judicial bias. : '''Inadequacy of Current Judicial Pension & Placement Structures''': Judges joining at older ages receive lower public official pensions (공무원연금), while frequent nationwide mandatory transfers (전보인사) discourage senior judges from remaining on the bench. : '''Limitations of Existing "Wonro-Beopgwan" (원로법관) Rules''': Introduced in Feb 2017 (Judicial Personnel Rules Art. 11-3) for judges with 30+ years experience, the rule merely assigned former court presidents to 1st-instance single-judge panels with standard full-time workloads without formal supernumerary status or workload reduction. ; Legal/Policy Gap : ROK law lacks a statutory supernumerary (정원 외) part-time senior judicial framework capable of retaining veteran judges past age 60 without occupying standard judicial quotas, allowing flexible caseload reductions, and providing stable pension-integrated compensation. ; Objectives : Mitigate judge shortages; reduce caseload pressures; abolish early resignation incentives; enhance judicial independence; and utilize veteran judicial expertise. ; Implementation & 4 Evaluated Reform Options : '''Option 1 (Creation of New Senior Judge Title)''': Establishing a new senior judge post (retiring at 68–70, part-time/reduced caseload, salary + pension). : '''Option 2 (Expansion of Exclusive Dedicated Judges / 전담법관)''': Extending retirement age to 68–70 for dedicated judges (modeled on Japan's Summary Court Judges). : '''Option 3 (Supernumerary Part-Time Judges)''': Adopting Canadian/UK supernumerary status with part-time schedules. : '''Option 4 (German-Style Pre-Retirement Part-Time Work)''': Work-hour reductions for judges aged 60+. : '''Final Recommended Framework (Author's Model)''': :* ''Eligibility'': Judges aged 60+ who completed two 10-year reappointments (20+ years service). :* ''Status & Quota'': Designated as Supernumerary Judges (정원 외 시니어판사), freeing up active judicial quota slots for new appointments. :* ''Workload & Schedule'': Part-time schedule (e.g., 3–4 days per week or 60%–80% standard caseload). :* ''Compensation & Pension'': Combined per diem/salary + pension drawing. ; Evidence & Empirical Data : '''US Federal Senior Judges''': Over 500 active senior judges handle 20%–25%+ of total federal civil and criminal cases. : '''Canada Supernumerary Judges''': 89% of eligible Canadian federal judges choose supernumerary status at age 65 or Rule of 80, representing 20% of the federal judiciary. : '''ROK Resignation Statistics''': Annual judge resignations averaged 50–60 judges (85 in 2011, 72 in 2012, 62 in 2013, 67 in 2014, 56 in 2015, 47 in 2016), whereas statutory 65-year-old retirements totaled only 6 judges between 2013 and 2017. == 5. MediaWiki Output == {{Infobox Judicial Policy|name=A Research on Senior Judge Program|official_name=시니어판사 제도에 관한 연구|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-201801|issuing_authority=Judicial Policy Research Institute (사법정책연구원)|authors=Seongjun Mo (모성준), Yongsung Seo (서용성), Yuna Choi (최유나)|publication_date=2018-11-02|report_series=연구총서 2018-01|isbn=979-11-6168-051-4|legal_basis=ROK Constitution Art. 105(3); Court Organization Act Art. 42; Judicial Personnel Rules Art. 11-3; US 28 U.S.C. § 371; Canada Judges Act s.28/42}} '''A Research on Senior Judge Program''' is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. == Summary == This document is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. It comprehensively analyzes the Senior Judge Program (시니어판사 제도) as a strategic solution to the judge shortage crisis and judge aging resulting from full career judicial unification (전면적 법조일원화, requiring 10 years of legal career experience by 2026); it addresses the early resignation of senior judges, which fuels controversy over former-judge favoritism (전관예우); evaluates senior/supernumerary/part-time judge schemes in 10 global jurisdictions (US, Canada, UK, Singapore, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Germany, Netherlands, Spain, Japan); and formulates concrete recommendations for enacting an out-of-quota part-time Senior Judge Program (정원 외 시간제 시니어판사) in South Korea. == Legal Basis == The legal frameworks analyzed include: * '''Constitution of the Republic of Korea''': Article 105(3) (10-Year Judicial Term). * '''Court Organization Act of South Korea (법원조직법)''': Article 42 (Minimum 10-Year Legal Career Requirement for Career Unification). * '''Judicial Personnel Rules (법원인사규칙)''': Article 11-3 (Senior Judge System / 원로법관제, effective February 2017). * '''United States Federal Code''': 28 U.S.C. § 371 (Retirement in Senior Status / Rule of 80). * '''Canada Judges Act''': R.S.C. 1985, c. J-1, s. 28 & s. 42 (Supernumerary Judges). * '''UK Constitutional Reform Act 2005''': Sections 38 & 39 (Acting Judges & Supplementary Panel). * '''Constitution of Singapore''': Article 95 (Senior Judges of the Supreme Court). * '''Japan Court Act (재판소법)''': Articles 44, 45, 50 (Summary Court Judges / 간이재판소 판사). == Background == The full implementation of career judicial unification in South Korea, requiring a minimum of 10 years of legal career experience by 2026, risks triggering a judge supply crisis, an increase in average judge age (projected to exceed 50 by 2030), and case backlogs. Meanwhile, most senior judges resign well before the statutory retirement age of 65 (only 6 judges retired naturally between 2013 and 2017, while 50–67 judges resigned annually) to open law practices, fueling accusations of ''jeongwan-yeowu'' (전관예우). The Senior Judge Program is needed to recruit and retain dedicated senior judges. == Objectives == # Address the chronic judge shortage crisis caused by full career judicial unification. # Prevent the early resignation of senior judges and curb ''jeongwan-yeowu'' controversies. # Analyze comparative senior/part-time judge schemes across 10 countries. # Design an out-of-quota part-time Senior Judge Program (정원 외 시간제 시니어판사) compatible with the Korean Constitution. == Scope == * '''Ten-Country Comparative Study''': ** '''United States''': 28 U.S.C. § 371 (Rule of 80), the California AJP, New York JHO, Indiana, Georgia. ** '''Common Law Systems''': Canada (Supernumerary Judges), UK (Recorders & Supplementary Panel), Singapore (Senior Judges), Hong Kong (Non-Permanent Judges). ** '''Civil Law Systems''': Taiwan (法官優遇制度), Germany (Altersteilzeit), the Netherlands (Rechter-plaatsvervanger), Spain, Japan (간이재판소 판사). * '''Evaluation of 4 Reform Options''': Option 1 (New Senior Judge Position), Option 2 (Expansion of Dedicated Judges), Option 3 (Supernumerary Part-Time Judges), Option 4 (German-Style Part-Time Work). == Key Provisions == * '''Eligibility Criteria''': Judges aged 60 and above who have completed two 10-year terms (20+ years of service). * '''Supernumerary Status''': Designated as "정원 외 시니어판사" (outside the active quota), freeing up new active judicial slots for recruitment. * '''Part-Time Workload''': A part-time schedule (3–4 days per week, or 60%–80% of the standard workload). * '''Compensation & Pension''': A combination of part-time per diem/salary and pension drawdown. == Implementation == The Supreme Court adopts a pilot scheme based on the Judicial Personnel Rules, proposes an amendment to the Court Organization Act for out-of-quota status, and adjusts the civil servant pension system accordingly. == Policy Issues == * A shortage of qualified judicial candidates due to the 10-year experience requirement. * Early resignation of senior judges fueling ''jeongwan-yeowu'' accusations. * Barriers posed by pension structure and mandatory regional transfer rotation (전보인사). == Reform / Amendments == # Enactment of the out-of-quota part-time Senior Judge Program (정원 외 시간제 시니어판사). # Freeing up active judge quota slots for new recruitment when a judge takes senior status. # Establishing a 60%–80% part-time workload standard and case-assignment flexibility. # Reform of the judicial pension system to ensure financial stability for senior judges. == Relationship to Other Entities == * '''Issuing Institution''': Judicial Policy Research Institute & Supreme Court of Korea. * '''Research Team''': Seongjun Mo (모성준), Yongsung Seo (서용성), Yuna Choi (최유나). == See Also == * [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] * [[Supreme Court of Korea]] * [[Rule of 80]] * [[Career Judicial Unification System]] == References == == 7. Policy Analysis == ; Background : Although the Constitutional Court of Korea holds ultimate authority to review the constitutionality of statutes (Article 111(1) of the ROK Constitution), the regular judiciary (ordinary courts) carries an inherent constitutional function through the resolution of concrete disputes and the application of the "Principle of Constitutional Interpretation of Statutes" (합헌적 법률해석의 원칙). When interpreting and applying the law, judges consistently limit, exclude, supplement, or correct the meaning of statutory provisions to align them with the Constitution, which substantially performs a norm-control function (규범통제). Therefore, ordinary courts require careful, systematic, and standardized benchmarks and standards for reviewing constitutionality (위헌심사기준). ; Policy Problem : '''Uncertainty and Inconsistency of Review Standards in Ordinary Courts''': Judges in ordinary courts often fail to explicitly articulate the standard or intensity of constitutional review (심사강도) in their legal reasoning, resulting in a lack of rigor in constitutional argumentation. : '''Divergence in Rulings Between Ordinary Courts and the Constitutional Court''': In norm-control constitutional complaint cases (헌바 cases under Article 68(2) of the Constitutional Court Act), there are cases where ordinary courts dismissed requests for constitutional review (위헌제청신청 기각), yet the Constitutional Court subsequently declared the same statutory provision unconstitutional (333 cases out of 6,606 petitions between 1988 and 2018, or 11.8% of substantively decided cases). : '''Passive Handling of Human Rights and Social Rights Cases''': The absence of a structured framework leads ordinary courts to tend to reject constitutional review petitions by merely citing "broad legislative discretion" without conducting precise, tiered scrutiny. ; Legal/Policy Gap : The absence of a comprehensive manual mapping general and specific standards of constitutional review (organized by type of constitutional right) specifically designed for the practical needs of judges in ordinary courts. ; Objectives : Provide detailed guidance on general review standards (proportionality, protection of trust, prohibition of retroactivity, prohibition of blanket delegation, and due process) as well as specific review standards (equality, freedom of occupation, property rights, and social rights); enhance the certainty and precision of constitutional analysis in ordinary courts; and ensure the effective protection of citizens' fundamental rights. ; Implementation & Core Review Framework : '''Definition of Standards of Constitutional Review (위헌심사기준의 의의)''': :* ''Scale/Method (척도 내지 방법)'': Substantive benchmarks such as the principle of proportionality (과잉금지원칙), the principle of equality (평등원칙), and the principle of protection of trust (신뢰보호원칙). :* ''Intensity of Scrutiny (심사강도)'': The level of strictness of review (strict scrutiny, intermediate scrutiny, rational basis test / 자의금지원칙) determined by the degree of legislative discretion and the importance of the right being restricted. : '''General Standards of Constitutional Review (일반적 위헌심사기준)''': :* ''Principle of Proportionality / Prohibition of Excessive Restriction (과잉금지원칙 — Article 37(2))'': Tests four tiered elements: (1) Legitimacy of Purpose (목적의 정당성), (2) Suitability of Means (수단의 적절성), (3) Minimal Restriction (피해의 최소성), and (4) Balance of Legal Interests (법익의 균형성). :* ''Principle of Protection of Trust (신뢰보호원칙)'': Derived from the Principle of the Rule of Law (''Rechtsstaat'' / 법치국가원리), weighing citizens' trust interests against the public interest sought through legal change. :* ''Prohibition of Retroactive Legislation (소급입법금지원칙 — Article 13)'': Distinguishes genuine retroactive legislation (진정소급입법 — generally prohibited) from non-genuine retroactive legislation (부진정소급입법 — tested via the principle of protection of trust). :* ''Prohibition of Blanket Delegation (포괄위임금지원칙 — Article 75)'': Promotes certainty and predictability in criminal and tax law. :* ''Principle of Due Process (적법절차원칙 — Article 12)'': Guarantees formal/procedural as well as substantive due process across all state actions. : '''Area-Specific Standards of Constitutional Review (개별적 위헌심사기준)''': :* ''Right to Equality (평등권 — Article 11)'': Determines whether differential treatment occurs among essentially similar groups (본질적으로 같은 것), then applies either the arbitrariness test (자의금지원칙) or strict proportionality review. :* ''Freedom of Occupation (직업의 자유 — Article 15)'': Applies the 3-Stage Theory (단계이론): (1) Restrictions on the exercise of an occupation (rationality review), (2) Restrictions on subjective qualifications (intermediate proportionality review), and (3) Restrictions on objective qualifications (strict proportionality review). :* ''Property Rights (재산권 — Article 23)'': Distinguishes content/limitation restrictions on property [Article 23(1)(2)] from expropriation [Article 23(3)], adopting the Separation Theory (분리이론) over the Boundary Theory (경계이론). :* ''Social Rights (사회적 기본권 — Article 34)'': Applies the Prohibition of Minimal Protection (과소보호금지원칙) and adopts Alexy's Principles Model (원칙모델), combining substantive and procedural review. ; Evidence & Empirical Data : Of the 6,606 헌바 cases filed with the Constitutional Court between 1988 and 2018, 333 cases (11.8% of substantively decided cases) were declared unconstitutional by the Constitutional Court after having previously been dismissed by ordinary courts. : This report conducts an in-depth analysis of 15 Constitutional Court decisions related to 과잉금지원칙, 3 decisions related to 신뢰보호원칙, 4 decisions related to 소급입법금지원칙, 4 decisions related to 포괄위임금지원칙, 3 decisions related to 적법절차원칙, 8 decisions related to 평등권, and 2 decisions related to 직업의 자유. MediaWiki Output == {{Infobox Judicial Policy|name=A Study on Standards of Constitutional Review for Constitutional Judgment of Court|official_name=법원의 헌법판단을 위한 위헌심사기준 연구|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-201808|issuing_authority=Judicial Policy Research Institute (사법정책연구원)|authors=Lee, Jong Youp (이종엽), Kim, Ju-kyung (김주경)|publication_date=2018-10-11|report_series=연구총서 2018-08|isbn=979-11-6168-053-8|legal_basis=ROK Constitution Arts. 37(2), 101, 103, 107, 111; Constitutional Court Act Arts. 41 & 68(2)}} '''A Study on Standards of Constitutional Review for Constitutional Judgment of Court''' is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. == Summary == This document is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. It systematically develops standards of constitutional review (위헌심사기준) for ordinary court judges performing constitutional adjudication (법원의 헌법판단) through the Principle of Constitutional Interpretation of Statutes (합헌적 법률해석의 원칙). The study analyzes general review principles (proportionality, protection of trust, prohibition of retroactivity, prohibition of blanket delegation, due process) and area-specific review standards (equality, freedom of occupation, property rights, social rights), and conducts a comparative empirical study of divergent rulings between ordinary courts and the Constitutional Court in 헌바 cases (norm-control cases under Article 68(2) of the Constitutional Court Act). == Legal Basis == The legal frameworks analyzed include: * '''Constitution of the Republic of Korea''': ** Article 101(1) (Judicial Authority Vested in Courts) & Article 103 (Judicial Independence Under the Constitution and Law). ** Article 107(1) (Court's Right to Request Constitutional Review / 위헌법률심판제청권) & Article 107(2) (Supreme Court's Authority for Final Review of Executive Orders/Dispositions). ** Article 37(2) (General Limitation Clause & Principle of Proportionality / 과잉금지원칙). ** Article 11(1) (Equality), Article 12 (Due Process), Article 13 (Prohibition of Retroactivity), Article 15 (Freedom of Occupation), Article 23 (Property Rights), Article 34 (Social Rights), and Article 75 (Prohibition of Blanket Delegation). * '''Constitutional Court Act (헌법재판소법)''': Article 41 & Article 68(2) (Norm-Control Constitutional Complaint Cases / 헌바 사건). * '''Court Organization Act (법원조직법)''': Article 2(3) & Article 15. == Background == Although the Constitutional Court holds final authority over judicial review of statutes, ordinary courts perform constitutional adjudication on a daily basis through constitutionally-aligned statutory interpretation (합헌적 법률해석). Interpreting statutes to align with the Constitution practically functions and has the same effect as norm control (규범통제). The lack of a structured review standard in ordinary courts frequently leads to the dismissal of constitutional review petitions that are later overturned by the Constitutional Court (reaching 11.8% of substantively decided 헌바 cases). == Objectives == # Map general and specific standards of constitutional review for ordinary court judges. # Improve the precision and rigor of constitutional argumentation in ordinary court rulings. # Empirically analyze the divergence in rulings between ordinary courts and the Constitutional Court to draw practical implications. == Scope == * '''General Review Standards''': 과잉금지원칙 (Proportionality), 신뢰보호원칙 (Protection of Trust), 소급입법금지원칙 (Prohibition of Retroactivity), 포괄위임금지원칙 (Prohibition of Blanket Delegation), and 적법절차원칙 (Due Process). * '''Area-Specific Review Standards''': 평등권 (Right to Equality), 직업의 자유 (Freedom of Occupation / 3-Stage Theory), 재산권 (Property Rights / Separation Theory), and 사회적 기본권 (Social Rights / Alexy's Model). * '''Empirical Study of 헌바 Cases''': Comparative analysis of 15–47 Constitutional Court decisions against prior dismissals of constitutional review petitions by ordinary courts. == Key Provisions == * '''Proportionality Test Structure (과잉금지원칙)''': Applies 4 tiered stages: Legitimacy of Purpose, Suitability of Means, Minimal Restriction (피해의 최소성), and Balance of Legal Interests (법익의 균형성). * '''Freedom of Occupation Review (단계이론)''': Applies rationality review for restrictions on the exercise of an occupation; intermediate proportionality review for subjective qualifications; and strict review for objective qualifications. * '''Property Rights Review (분리이론)''': Adopts the Separation Theory, distinguishing content/limitation restrictions on property (Article 23(1)(2)) from expropriation/compensation (Article 23(3)). * '''Social Rights Review (과소보호금지원칙)''': Applies the prohibition of minimal protection and combines substantive review with procedural control. == Implementation == This draft and research standard is applied as an official guideline for constitutional analysis by judges at all court levels in South Korea, as well as a reference for drafting petitions for constitutional review submitted to the Constitutional Court. == Policy Issues == * Lack of transparency in constitutional argumentation within ordinary court rulings. * Passive dismissal of constitutional review petitions by ordinary courts due to a tendency to over-rely on legislative discretion. == Reform / Amendments == # Standardization of a tiered constitutional review framework in ordinary courts. # Active application of constitutionally-aligned statutory interpretation (합헌적 법률해석의 활성화). # Strengthening procedural control in the review of social rights and property rights. == Relationship to Other Entities == * '''Issuing Institution''': Judicial Policy Research Institute & Supreme Court of Korea. * '''Research Team''': Lee, Jong Youp (이종엽) & Kim, Ju-kyung (김주경). == See Also == * [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] * [[Supreme Court of Korea]] * [[Constitutional Court of Korea]] * [[Principle of Proportionality]] == References == == 7. Policy Analysis == ; Background : Public trust in the judiciary is a core form of institutional trust (제도신뢰) and social capital (사회적 자본), functioning as an indispensable prerequisite for democratic governance, the rule of law, and fair economic competition. In South Korea, while the judiciary has implemented extensive institutional reforms to enhance public trust, public perception of judicial trust has often been evaluated as low or unstable. To formulate effective trust-building policies, a rigorous diagnostic assessment of how judicial trust is measured globally is required. ; Policy Problem : '''Glaring Contradictions Across International Indices''': South Korea presents a paradoxical profile across global metrics. In objective performance and efficiency metrics — such as World Bank Doing Business "Enforcing Contracts" where Korea ranked 1st–2nd globally, and CEPEJ/OECD 1st instance trial duration averaging 144 days (5th fastest among 33 OECD nations, vs OECD average 242 days and Italy 550+ days) — Korea achieves world-leading results. However, in direct perception surveys published in OECD's Government at a Glance (via Gallup World Poll), Korea ranked near the bottom among OECD nations (22%–29% trust, ranking 33rd–34th out of 34 OECD countries). Concurrently, WVS Wave 6 showed a 66.7% trust rate for Korea's courts (ranking 5th out of 15 OECD countries). : '''Flaws in Single-Item Binary Survey Instruments''': Direct trust surveys often rely on a single, ambiguous question ("Do you have confidence in the judicial system and courts?") with a binary "Yes/No" scale (e.g., OECD/Gallup). This binary format fails to capture nuanced public attitudes, introduces acquiescence bias (묵종 편향), and forces respondents into a binary choice without defining whether "judicial system" includes courts, prosecution, police, or the Ministry of Justice. : '''Over-Concentration on Technical Competence''': Historically, Korean judicial policies focused heavily on case processing speed, IT e-court infrastructure, and technical competence (능력), while neglecting qualitative trust factors such as benevolence/procedural respect (호의), integrity and fairness (성실성·일관성), and institutional openness/transparency (개방성). ; Legal/Policy Gap : Korean judicial policy lacked a multi-dimensional framework capable of distinguishing between objective operational performance and subjective trust perceptions, and lacked standardized survey instruments aligned with the OECD 2017 Trust Guidelines and TCPS standards. ; Objectives : Diagnose methodological causes of index discrepancies; adopt the OECD 2017 Trust Guidelines for survey design; apply the TCPS multi-dimensional framework (Ability, Benevolence, Integrity/Consistency, Openness); and design balanced short- and long-term judicial trust enhancement policies. ; Implementation & Proposed Statutory & Administrative Reforms : '''Methodological Survey Design Reform (OECD 2017 Guidelines Adoption)''': :* Replace binary Yes/No scales with 0–10 point Likert numerical scales anchored by clear verbal descriptors to eliminate acquiescence bias and allow nuanced statistical variance. :* Utilize computer-assisted self-interviewing (CASI/CAPI) to minimize social desirability bias (사회적 바람직성 편향). :* Precise item phrasing separating "courts" (법원) from 수사기관 (prosecution/police) to prevent conflation. : '''Multi-Dimensional Trust Enhancement Strategy''': :* ''Shift from Speed to Procedural Respect (호의·윤리성·헌신 / TCPS Area 1-4 & 3-1)'': Reorient courtroom management from pure disposition speed toward active listening, courteous treatment (친절·응답성·존경), and robust procedural participation. :* ''Strengthening Judicial Integrity & Independence (성실성·일관성 / TCPS Area 3 & 4-1)'': Enhance judicial ethics, transparency in case assignment, and independence from improper external or governmental influence. :* ''Expanding Openness & Information Transparency (개방성 / TCPS Area 1-1, 1-5, 4-4)'': Ensure open court proceedings, public disclosure of court decisions, clear judgment writing, public legal education, and affordable access to justice. : '''Conceptual Separation of Trust (신뢰) and Distrust (불신)''': Treat trust and distrust as conceptually independent and co-existing dimensions. Policy must actively target and eliminate specific drivers of distrust (e.g., perceived opacity, corruption) rather than assuming that increasing administrative efficiency will automatically diminish distrust. : '''Establishment of a Domestic Composite Judicial Trust Index''': Combine objective performance metrics (disposition times, cost ratios) with multi-item survey data across all TCPS performance areas to produce a balanced, scientifically valid domestic index. ; Evidence & Empirical Data : '''OECD vs. WVS Judicial Trust Discrepancy (South Korea)''': :* OECD (Government at a Glance via Gallup World Poll, 2-point Y/N scale): 2007 = 29% (ranked 33rd/34 OECD nations), 2012 = 22% (ranked 34th/34), 2014 = 27% (ranked 33rd/34). :* WVS (4-point Likert scale): Wave 1 (1982) = 78.0% (3rd/8 OECD nations), Wave 2 (1990) = 66.1% (1st/8), Wave 3 (1996) = 58.4% (7th/17), Wave 5 (2005) = 50.8% (14th/21), Wave 6 (2010) = 66.7% (5th/15). : '''WJP Rule of Law Index (South Korea 2010–2017)''': :* Overall Global Rank (2017): 20th out of 113 nations (Score 0.72). :* Civil Justice Rank (2017): 15th out of 113 (Score 0.74); Criminal Justice Rank (2017): 17th out of 113 (Score 0.70). :* Sub-factor strengths: Absence of corruption in civil justice (high score), effective enforcement, trial delay control. Sub-factor weaknesses: Perceived attorney fee burdens. : '''World Bank Doing Business "Enforcing Contracts" (South Korea)''': Ranked 1st globally in 2017 (2018 report) and 2nd globally in 2012–2014 and 2016–2018 (2019 report) among 190 economies. : '''CEPEJ / OECD Disposition Time''': 1st instance civil disposition time in South Korea averaged 144 days (5th fastest among 33 OECD countries, vs OECD average 242 days and Italy 550+ days). == 5. MediaWiki Output == {{Infobox Judicial Policy|name=A Comparative Study on Methods of Measuring Public Trust in the Judicial Systems and Courts|official_name=국제적인 사법신뢰도 측정방식에 관한 연구|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-201813|issuing_authority=Judicial Policy Research Institute (사법정책연구원)|authors=Han Seongsoo (한성수)|publication_date=2018-12-28|report_series=연구총서 2018-13|isbn=979-11-6168-063-7|legal_basis=Court Organization Act of South Korea; OECD Guidelines on Measuring Trust (2017); Trial Court Performance Standards (TCPS)}} '''A Comparative Study on Methods of Measuring Public Trust in the Judicial Systems and Courts''' is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. == Summary == This document is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. It comparatively and methodologically analyzes various international indices measuring public trust in the judiciary (사법신뢰). It diagnoses a fundamental contradiction in South Korea's scores (which rank 1st–2nd in the world for civil efficiency under the World Bank Doing Business index, yet fall near the bottom in binary OECD Gallup surveys); evaluates direct trust indices (the OECD's ''Government at a Glance'' & the ''World Values Survey'') as well as performance-component indices (the WJP Rule of Law Index, World Bank WGI/Doing Business, WEF GCI, and IMD WCY); and formulates survey methodology reforms based on the 2017 OECD Guidelines and a multidimensional TCPS-based policy strategy (Ability, Benevolence, Integrity/Consistency, Openness). == Legal Basis == The legal and methodological frameworks analyzed include: * '''Court Organization Act of South Korea (법원조직법)''': The legal basis for establishing the Judicial Policy Research Institute under the Supreme Court of Korea on January 1, 2014. * '''OECD Guidelines on Measuring Trust (2017)''': An international standard framework for national statistical agencies and researchers to measure interpersonal and institutional trust. * '''Trial Court Performance Standards (TCPS)''': A US NCSC/BJA framework establishing 5 performance areas (Access to Justice, Expedition/Timeliness, Equality/Fairness/Integrity, Independence/Accountability, Public Trust & Confidence) and 22 measurable standards. == Background == Public trust in the judiciary is a form of institutional trust (제도신뢰) and social capital (사회적 자본) that is essential to a democratic rule-of-law state. Although the Supreme Court of Korea has implemented various judicial reforms, international trust surveys show confusing and extreme variation. South Korea shows outstanding objective performance in trial speed and efficiency (averaging 144 days for first-instance civil cases), yet scores low on OECD Gallup binary Yes/No surveys (22%–29%). Meanwhile, the WVS Wave 6 survey recorded a 66.7% trust level (ranking 5th among OECD countries). == Objectives == # Diagnose the methodological causes behind the divergence in South Korea's international trust index scores. # Adopt the 2017 OECD Guidelines to improve judicial survey instrument design. # Apply the multidimensional TCPS framework, covering Ability (능력), Benevolence (호의), Integrity/Consistency (성실성·일관성), and Openness (개방성). # Formulate a balanced short- and long-term judicial policy strategy. == Scope == * '''Methodological Analysis of International Indices''': ** '''Direct Trust Indices''': The OECD's ''Government at a Glance'' (Gallup World Poll) and the World Values Survey (WVS Waves 1–6). ** '''Performance Component Indices''': The World Justice Project (WJP) Rule of Law Index, World Bank Doing Business & WGI, the WEF Global Competitiveness Index, and the IMD World Competitiveness Ranking. * '''TCPS Indicator Mapping''': Classifies the 22 TCPS performance standards into the 4 core factors underlying judicial trust. == Key Provisions == * '''Survey Design Reform (OECD 2017 Guidelines)''': ** Replaces the binary Yes/No scale with a 0–10 point Likert scale. ** Uses CAPI/CASI modes to reduce social desirability bias. ** Clarifies the survey's target object by separating the term "court" (법원) from other law enforcement institutions. * '''Separation of the Concepts of Trust (신뢰) and Distrust (불신)''': Recognizes trust and distrust as two independent dimensions that can coexist. * '''Multidimensional Policy Framework''': ** Shifts focus from mere trial speed (expedition) toward procedural fairness, attentiveness to litigants, and judicial ethics. ** Improves judicial information transparency and affordable legal access. == Implementation == Courts adopt a multidimensional 0–10 point Likert-based survey instrument, integrate TCPS indicators into an integrated Domestic Judicial Trust Index, and conduct public education programs on judicial performance. == Policy Issues == * The limitations of single-item binary surveys (the Gallup World Poll), which produce acquiescence bias and blur the boundaries between judicial institutions. * A historical policy imbalance overly focused on technical efficiency (ability) while neglecting qualitative factors (benevolence, integrity, openness). == Reform / Amendments == # Adoption of the 2017 OECD Guidelines on Measuring Trust in national judicial surveys. # Formulation of a Domestic Composite Judicial Trust Index based on TCPS. # Reorientation of judicial policy from pure efficiency toward procedural fairness and judicial ethics. # Independent management of distrust drivers. == Relationship to Other Entities == * '''Issuing Institution''': Judicial Policy Research Institute & Supreme Court of Korea. * '''Lead Researcher''': Han Seongsoo (한성수). * '''International Organizations''': OECD, WVSA, WJP, World Bank, WEF, IMD. == See Also == * [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] * [[Supreme Court of Korea]] * [[OECD Guidelines on Measuring Trust]] * [[Trial Court Performance Standards]] == References == == 7. Policy Analysis == ; Background : Globalization has led to a rapid increase in international population movements, with the registered foreign population in South Korea growing at an average annual rate of 8.5% to reach 2,180,498 by the end of 2017 (representing 4.21% of the total national population). Concurrently, criminal cases involving foreign suspects expanded exponentially, from 9,338 individuals in 2003 to 53,151 in 2016. When foreign nationals are subjected to physical detention in a foreign legal system, language barriers, cultural differences, and unfamiliar procedural rules create severe double hardship and impair defense rights. Under Article 36 of the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations (VCCR) — to which South Korea acceded on March 7, 1977 (in force April 6, 1977) — the receiving state is legally bound to inform detained foreigners of their right to consular advice without delay and notify the sending state's consular post upon request. ; Policy Problem : '''Lack of Judicial Focus & Institutionalization in ROK''': Historically, South Korean courts viewed consular notification primarily as an administrative function for police or immigration authorities, lacking court-specific procedural rules or systematic oversight during trial and warrant hearings. : '''Ineffective Rights Advice & Statutory Gaps''': Except for internal police/prosecution guidelines and the Immigration Control Act, South Korea's Criminal Procedure Code lacks explicit statutory provisions mandating judges or law enforcement to inform detained foreign suspects of their consular notification rights. : '''State Tort Liability Risks''': As demonstrated in Seoul Central District Court Decision 2017Gadan25114 (affirmed on appeal), law enforcement failure to inform a detained foreigner of consular notification rights constitutes an illegal breach of official duty (직무상 불법행위), subjecting the state to civil damage liability. : '''International Precedent and Remedy Tensions''': Landmarks in international jurisprudence (ICJ ''LaGrand'' and ''Avena'' decisions) affirm that VCCR Article 36 creates individual rights, requiring judicial review and reconsideration of convictions where non-compliance prejudiced the defendant. However, domestic courts in the US (''Sanchez-Llamas'', ''Medellín'') strictly apply procedural default rules, whereas German courts (BVerfG) treat VCCR violations as appealable procedural errors subject to evidentiary evaluation. ; Legal/Policy Gap : ROK law lacks unified statutory rules establishing court responsibility for verifying consular notification at warrant review (구속영장 실질심사), providing standardized multi-lingual advisement forms, and defining evidentiary or procedural remedies when rights are omitted. ; Objectives : Establish judicial rules (대법원 예규) for consular notification; mandate verification of consular notification during pre-trial detention hearings; implement standardized advisement forms for non-criminal detention (immigration, civil commitment); and define legal remedies for non-compliance. ; Implementation & Proposed Reforms : '''Institutionalizing Court Oversight at Warrant Review Stage''': Formalize warrant review practices (currently practiced informally at Seoul Central and Seoul Southern District Courts) requiring judges to verify whether law enforcement performed consular advisement, verbally advise the foreign suspect in open court, and grant brief adjournments for police to complete notification if omitted or if the suspect changes their mind. : '''Promulgation of Judicial Rules & Advisement Forms''': Draft comprehensive Supreme Court regulations (modeled after Japan's Supreme Court Circular) detailing: :* Categories of detention requiring notification (warrants, bench warrants, court-ordered civil/medical commitments). :* Mandatory verification for mandatory-notification treaty nations (e.g., China, Russia) regardless of suspect request. : '''Expansion to Non-Criminal Liberty Restrictions''': Extend consular advisement protocols to non-criminal detention, including immigration protection (보호), juvenile commitments, and involuntary mental health commitments. : '''Researching Judicial Remedies for Non-Compliance''': Establish guidelines for appellate review, evaluating whether unadvised statements should face evidentiary exclusion (증거배제) or whether procedural defects were cured by subsequent consular contact. ; Evidence & Empirical Data : '''Korean Foreigner Crime Statistics''': Foreign crime cases processed by ROK prosecution surged from 9,338 in 2003 to 53,151 in 2016. : '''ROK Mandatory Treaty Protocols''': Under ROK-China Consular Agreement (2014) Article 7, notification must occur within 4 days regardless of suspect request (unless immigration violation with written refusal). Under ROK-Russia Convention (1992) Article 39, notification is strictly mandatory without exception. : '''ROK Police KICS Workflow''': ROK police execute consular notification via KICS (형사사법정보시스템), printing automated "Consular Notification Request Confirmation" forms (영사기관 통보요청 확인서) and faxing notifications directly to foreign embassies. : '''State Tort Precedent''': In Seoul Central District Court Decision 2017Gadan25114 (affirmed 2018Na3969), an innocent foreign national misidentified by police was detained for 12 days without consular advisement; the court awarded state damages, holding police and prosecutors strictly liable for violating VCCR advisement duties. == 5. MediaWiki Output == {{Infobox Judicial Policy|name=A Research on Consular Notification in the Case of Detention|official_name=외국인 인신구속시 영사 통보에 관한 연구|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-201902|issuing_authority=Judicial Policy Research Institute (사법정책연구원)|authors=Sunmi Lee (이선미), Hyunbum Kim (김현범), Moonhee Ahnn (안문희), Junghyun Kang (강정현), Yongsung Seo (서용성)|publication_date=2019-03-29|report_series=연구총서 2019-02|isbn=979-11-6168-075-0|legal_basis=Vienna Convention on Consular Relations Art. 36; ROK Bilateral Consular Conventions (US, Russia, China); Immigration Control Act Arts. 54 & 63; Crime Investigation Rules Art. 241}} '''A Research on Consular Notification in the Case of Detention''' is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. == Summary == This document is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. It comprehensively, empirically, and comparatively analyzes the obligation of consular notification (영사 통보) and the right to advice (권리 고지) under Article 36 of the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations (VCCR) and bilateral consular treaties when foreign nationals are subject to physical detention (인신구속). It examines the law and practice of 6 countries (US, UK, Japan, China, Germany, France) as well as rulings by international courts (ICJ, IACHR); evaluates South Korean judicial practice; and formulates recommendations to institutionalize the role of Korean courts in guaranteeing the right to consular notification and to formulate judicial remedies for violations. == Legal Basis == The legal frameworks analyzed include: * '''Vienna Convention on Consular Relations (VCCR / 비엔나영사협약)''': Article 36(1)(b) (Consular Notification & Right to Advice), (c) (Right to Consular Visitation), and Article 36(2). South Korea acceded on March 7, 1977 (effective April 6, 1977). * '''ROK Bilateral Consular Conventions''': ** ROK–US Consular Convention (1963), Article 5. ** ROK–Russia Consular Convention (1992), Article 39 (Unconditional Mandatory Notification). ** ROK–China Consular Agreement (2014), Article 7 (Mandatory Notification Within 4 Days). * '''ROK Domestic Legislation & Regulations''': ** Immigration Control Act (출입국관리법) Articles 54 & 63, and Ministerial Rule Article 68 (Form No. 103). ** Guidelines on Handling Foreign National Crime Investigations (외국인범죄수사처리지침 — Ministry of Justice Instruction No. 1100). ** Crime Investigation Rules (범죄수사규칙 — Police Instruction No. 903), Article 241. ** Railway Special Judicial Police Investigation Rules, Article 53 & Maritime Police Rules, Article 254. * '''International & Domestic Jurisprudence''': ** ICJ Decisions: ''Breard'' (1998), ''LaGrand'' (2001), and ''Avena'' (2004). ** IACHR Advisory Opinion: OC-16/99 (1999). ** US Supreme Court Jurisprudence: ''Sanchez-Llamas v. Oregon'' (2006) and ''Medellín v. Texas'' (2008). ** South Korean State Tort Decision: Seoul Central District Court No. 2017Gadan25114 (Affirmed 2018Na3969). == Background == With the growing foreign population in South Korea (reaching 2.18 million in 2017, or 4.21% of the population) and a surge in foreign crime cases (53,151 cases in 2016), the physical detention of foreign nationals carries a risk of rights violations due to language and legal barriers. Under VCCR Article 36, the receiving state must inform detained foreign nationals of their right to consular notification without delay. However, South Korean courts have historically treated consular notification as an administrative police duty, without standardized judicial procedural rules. == Objectives == # Guarantee due process (적법절차) and the human rights of detained foreign nationals in accordance with VCCR Article 36. # Institutionalize the court's role at the warrant review (심문) stage to verify consular notification. # Draft Supreme Court Regulations (대법원 예규) and standardized multilingual rights notification forms. # Research forms of judicial remedy and civil compensation for violations of consular notification. == Scope == * '''Six-Country Comparative Study''': ** '''United States''': 28 CFR 50.5, 8 CFR 236.1 (58 mandatory-notification countries), Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure Rule 5(d)(1)(F), and state laws (Illinois, California, Oregon, Nevada, North Carolina, Florida). ** '''United Kingdom''': PACE Code C/H Section 7 and Prison Service Instruction PSI 52/2011. ** '''Japan''': 2014 Supreme Court Secretary-General Circular (平成26年 刑二第155号) and Osaka Police Regulation No. 28. ** '''China''': Supreme People's Court Judicial Interpretation (法释〔2012〕21号) and Ministry of Public Security Regulations No. 127 & 125. ** '''Germany''': StPO § 114b(2) Sentence 4, § 127(4), RiVASt § 135/136, and MiZi Part 2 Ch 1 Sec II § 5. ** '''France''': Ministry of Justice Circular DAP-PMJ4 (September 18, 2007). == Key Provisions == * '''Court Verification at the Warrant Review Stage (영장실질심사)''': Judges must verify police KICS documentation, verbally advise the foreign suspect of their rights, and briefly adjourn proceedings if notification has not yet been completed. * '''Standardization of Mandatory Bilateral Notification''': Applies special protocols for Chinese and Russian nationals, requiring automatic notification regardless of the suspect's request. * '''Expansion to Non-Criminal Detention''': Applies consular notification protocols to immigration detention (보호), juvenile detention, and involuntary psychiatric commitment. == Implementation == Courts adopt the KICS (형사사법정보시스템) multilingual notification form, while the Supreme Court develops an integrated handling guide for foreign national suspects. == Policy Issues == * The absence of an explicit provision on consular notification in the Korean Criminal Procedure Code. * The risk of state civil liability claims (state tort liability) arising from law enforcement negligence. == Reform / Amendments == # Enactment of Supreme Court Regulations (대법원 예규) on Judicial Consular Notification Procedures. # Standardization of consular notification verification at pre-trial detention hearings. # Formulation of judicial remedy rules and evidentiary evaluation standards. == Relationship to Other Entities == * '''Issuing Institution''': Judicial Policy Research Institute & Supreme Court of Korea. * '''Research Team''': Sunmi Lee (이선미), Hyunbum Kim, Moonhee Ahnn, Junghyun Kang, Yongsung Seo. * '''Related Agencies''': National Police Agency of Korea, Ministry of Justice, & the International Court of Justice (ICJ). == See Also == * [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] * [[Supreme Court of Korea]] * [[Vienna Convention on Consular Relations]] * [[International Court of Justice]] == References == == 7. Policy Analysis == ; Background : Korea's Civil Act adheres to a strict binary model of legal personality: only natural persons (''자연인'') and incorporated entities (''법인'') possess capacity of enjoyment of rights (''권리능력'', Civil Act Art. 3). However, millions of socially active organizations — such as clan associations (''종중''), religious bodies (''교회/사찰''), village/neighborhood associations (''동/리/마을회/노인회''), and alumni groups — operate as unincorporated associations (''법인 아닌 사단'') without registering as corporations. To accommodate practical economic necessity, procedural statutes explicitly accord them party capacity in litigation (Civil Procedure Act Art. 52) and real estate registration capacity (Registration of Real Estate Act Art. 26). ; Policy Problem : Unincorporated associations hold immense national wealth: official 2018 government data shows 383,720 registered associations owning 8,392 km² of land (representing 8.3% of Korea's total landmass), with clan associations owning 78.1% (6,096 km²) and religious bodies owning 12.8% (999 km²). Despite this massive economic footprint, there is '''no public register''' (''공시제도'') verifying their actual existence, corporate substance, or legal representatives. Consequently: :# ''Litigation Inefficiency'': Courts frequently conduct full trials only for appellate courts to overturn rulings due to lack of party capacity or invalid representative authority, causing severe waste of judicial resources. :# ''Transaction Insecurity & Invalidation'': Real estate transactions or mortgages executed under an association's name are routinely invalidated retroactively when lower-tier representative appointments or general meeting resolutions (''총유물 처분결의'') are later proven fraudulent or defective. :# ''Non-Contentious Hazards'': Non-contentious procedures like court deposits (''공탁'') or compulsory execution (''강제집행'') risk releasing funds to fraudulent self-proclaimed representatives without reliable verification tools. ; Legal/Policy Gap : Korea's Civil Act enforces an administrative permission system (''허가주의'', Art. 32) for non-profit incorporation, giving administrative agencies broad discretion. Associations actively avoid incorporation to evade state supervision, asset dissolution restrictions (Art. 80), and mandatory filing burdens. Furthermore, Civil Act Art. 275 mandates that association property be owned collectively (''총유'', ''chong-yu''), requiring general meeting resolutions for management and disposition (Art. 276). This creates an inherent structural conflict between procedural statutes treating them as quasi-corporations and property law treating their assets as collective member ownership. ; Evaluation of Alternative Reform Models :# ''Civil Act Incorporation Reform (준칙주의 / Normative Principle)'': Shifting non-profit incorporation from permission (''허가주의'') to normative registration (''준칙주의'' / ''인가주의''), as proposed in the 2004 and 2013 Civil Act Revision drafts. '''Evaluated as ineffective''' because as long as procedural laws grant real estate ownership and litigation standing without incorporation, associations have no financial or operational incentive to undergo corporate oversight. :# ''Single Special Law / Intermediate Corporation Model (중간법인법)'': Enacting a standalone special law modeled after Japan's 2001 Intermediate Corporation Act. '''Evaluated as a failure''' based on empirical evidence from Japan, where only 2,619 intermediate corporations were formed over four years due to compliance burdens and corporate tax exposure. :# ''Special Laws for Specific Groups (종중관리법 / 종교법인법)'': Enacting specific regulation for clan or religious bodies. '''Evaluated as politically complex''' due to deep-seated social resistance and constitutional issues surrounding religious freedom. ; Preferred Solution — Public Disclosure via Real Estate Registration Act Amendment : The report formulates a highly practical, immediate reform centered on the existing real estate registration identification number system: :# ''Statutory Enactment'': Insert '''Article 26-2''' into the Registration of Real Estate Act (''부동산등기법 제26조의2''). :# ''Court-Administered Register'': Establish an official '''Unincorporated Association Register''' (''법인 아닌 사단 등록부'') managed directly by court registration officers (''등기관'') rather than local municipal heads (''시장/군수/구청장''). :# ''Mandatory Notary Attendance'': Require notary public attendance and certification (''공증인 참석인증'') for general membership meeting resolutions and articles of association to guarantee procedural truthfulness and representative authenticity. :# ''Public Register Certificate'': Issue official '''Unincorporated Association Registration Certificates''' (''법인 아닌 사단 등록사항증명서'') disclosing: (a) Association Name, (b) Principal Office Address, (c) Registration Identification Number, (d) Representative Name and Address, and (e) Whether property disposition requires a general assembly resolution under Civil Act Art. 276(1). :# ''Protection of Bona Fide Third Parties'': Establish statutory protection ensuring that registered representative information cannot be contested against bona fide third parties (''선의의 제3자 보호''). ; Evidence : Official 10-year court registration statistics (2009–2018) reveal that unincorporated associations engage in '''18,719 to 29,585 real estate ownership registrations per year''' (accumulating 223,915 registrations over the decade). Implementation of the proposed court register would immediately capture nearly 20,000 active associations annually, creating an exhaustive public disclosure network covering virtually all property-holding unincorporated associations in South Korea. == 5. MediaWiki Output == {{Infobox Judicial Policy|name=A Study on the Methods of Public Disclosure of Unincorporated Associations|official_name=법인 아닌 사단의 공시방안에 관한 연구|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-201910|issuing_authority=Judicial Policy Research Institute (사법정책연구원)|authors=Lee Dong-sun (이동선), Kang Jeong-hyun (강정현)|publication_date=2019-12-18|report_series=연구총서 2019-10|isbn=979-11-6168-098-9|legal_basis=ROK Civil Act Arts. 3, 32, 275–277; Civil Procedure Act Arts. 51, 52; Real Estate Registration Act Arts. 26, 48, 49}} '''A Study on the Methods of Public Disclosure of Unincorporated Associations''' is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. == Summary == This document is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. It analyzes the legal status, comparative law (Germany, France, Japan), and practical problems concerning unincorporated associations (법인 아닌 사단), and formulates a concrete legal reform: the establishment of a court-administered "Unincorporated Association Register" (법인 아닌 사단 등록부). == Legal Basis == The legal frameworks analyzed include: * '''Civil Act of the Republic of Korea (민법)''': Article 3 (Capacity of Enjoyment of Rights), Article 32 (Permission Principle for Non-Profit Incorporation), Article 275 (Collective Ownership / 총유), and Articles 276–277 (Management and Disposition of Collective Property). * '''Civil Procedure Act of the Republic of Korea (민사소송법)''': Articles 51 and 52 (Capacity to be a Party in Court). * '''Registration of Real Estate Act (부동산등기법)''': Article 26 (Registration Capacity), Article 48 (Registration Details), and Article 49 (Registration ID Number Procedures). * '''Supreme Court Registration Directive No. 1621''': Directive on Business Processing regarding Registration Applications by Unincorporated Associations. == Background == In South Korea, hundreds of thousands of organizations — such as clan associations (종중), religious institutions (교회/사찰), and village associations (동/리/마을회) — do not register as incorporated bodies (법인), yet hold extensive rights over land (accounting for 8.3% of South Korea's total land area as of 2018). The absence of a public registration system (공시제도) has led to a high risk of representative fraud, invalidated land registrations, and overturned court judgments due to lack of legal party capacity. == Objectives == # Establish an effective and efficient public registration system to verify the existence of associations and the authenticity of their legal representatives. # Improve legal certainty in property transactions and reduce social costs and case burdens on the courts. == Scope == * '''Three-Country Comparative Study''': ** '''Germany''': Section 54 BGB (application of partnership rules) and Section 47 GBO (rejection of independent land registration capacity). ** '''France''': The 1901 Act on Non-Declared Associations (''associations non déclarées''). ** '''Japan''': The 2001 Intermediate Corporation Act (중간법인법) and the 2008 Non-Profit Corporation Reform (일반법인법). == Key Provisions == * '''Enactment of Article 26-2 of the Real Estate Registration Act''': Requires court registration officers (등기관) to maintain an "Unincorporated Association Register." * '''Notary Authentication (참석인증)''': Requires notary attendance and certification of general membership meetings and articles of association to guarantee representative authenticity. * '''Registration Certificate (법인 아닌 사단 등록사항증명서)''': Contains the association's name, office address, registration number, representative's name/address, and a clause on general assembly consent for disposal of collectively owned property (Civil Act Article 276(1)). * '''Protection of Bona Fide Third Parties (선의의 제3자 보호)''': Guarantees that registered representative information cannot be challenged by conflicting internal claims. == Implementation == Transfers registration authority from local government heads (시장/군수/구청장) to district courts/court registry offices (등기소) so that verification is conducted rigorously by legal professionals and integrated with the land registration system. == Policy Issues == * The failure of Japan's model (중간법인법) shows that relaxing incorporation requirements (준칙주의) alone is insufficient if associations lack tax or operational incentives to submit to state oversight. * Uncertainty in representative verification during non-contentious procedures such as court deposits (공탁) and compulsory execution (강제집행). == Reform / Amendments == * Establishment of a court registration system for unincorporated associations. * Mandatory notary authentication for general meetings and articles of association. * Issuance of official registration certificates for legal and court transactions. == Relationship to Other Entities == * '''Issuing Institution''': Judicial Policy Research Institute & Supreme Court of Korea. * '''Research Team''': Lee Dong-sun, Kang == Summary ==
'''A Study on the Federal Assembly System of Switzerland: Focusing on the Legislative Process''' (`JPW-REPORT-201915`) is an official judicial policy publication issued by the [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] (JPRI) under the [[Supreme Court of Korea]]. Authored by Dispatched Senior Research Fellow Choi, Yong-hoon, the report presents a comprehensive legal and structural analysis of the Swiss Federal Assembly (연방의회).

The study examines the bicameral structure with perfectly equal powers, the militia parliament principle (민병제 의회), mandatory public consultation procedures (입법협의절차), direct democracy veto mechanisms via popular initiatives and referendums, four-year legislative planning, ex-ante and ex-post legislative evaluation, and the democratic election and supervision of federal judges by the United Federal Assembly (양원합동회의 연방법관 선출). Based on these observations, the report outlines 10 core institutional characteristics and 9 strategic legal reforms for the Republic of Korea.
