== Legal Basis ==
The policy report grounds its comparative analysis in statutory frameworks, constitutional mandates, and federal ordinances:

* '''Federal Constitution of the Swiss Confederation (SR 101.1)''':
** ''Articles 136–142'': Political Rights, Popular Initiatives, and Referendums.
** ''Articles 143–147'': General Provisions, Eligibility, Incompatibility, and Consultation.
** ''Articles 148–173'': Federal Assembly Organization, Procedure, Powers, and the Militia Principle.
** ''Articles 174–187'': Federal Council and Federal Administration.
** ''Articles 188–191c'': Federal Supreme Court and Judicial Authorities.
* '''Federal Act on the Federal Assembly / Parliament Act (ParlA / SR 171.10)''': Articles 22, 26, 27, 28, 29, 35, 44, 52, 56, 61, 70, 74, 84, 86, 88–91, 94a, 115, 116, 120, 123, 141, 146, and 147.
* '''Federal Act on the Consultation Procedure / Consultation Procedure Act (CPA / SR 172.061)''': Articles 2–7, 13, 15, and 21.
* '''Government and Administration Organisation Act (GAOA / SR 172.010)''': Articles 7c, 7d, 32, 36, 51, and 57a–57g.
* '''Publications Act (PublA / SR 170.512)''': Article 7(1).
* '''Federal Court Act (BGG / SR 173.110)''': Articles 1, 4, 15, 74, and 82.

== Background & Policy Problems ==
1. '''Lack of Comprehensive Understanding of Swiss Institutions''': In South Korea, the Swiss political and judicial framework has often been understood piecemeal, lacking systematic analysis regarding its bicameral equality, lawmaking procedures, public consultation, and inter-branch judicial relations. 2. '''Deficits in ROK Legislative Quality and Impact Assessment''': Lawmaking in the ROK National Assembly frequently faces criticism for rushed proceedings, brief legislative notice periods (40 days), superficial bill explanatory notes, and the absence of an integrated ex-ante and ex-post regulatory evaluation system across the legislature and executive branch. 3. '''Democratic Legitimacy of Judicial Appointments''': Appointments of Supreme Court Justices in South Korea rely heavily on proposals from the Chief Justice and nomination by the President, prompting calls for greater democratic legitimacy, representative diversity, and parliamentary scrutiny.

== Key Institutional Features & Comparative Findings ==

* '''Supreme Position of the Federal Assembly''': The Federal Assembly is designated as the highest authority in the Confederation, subject to the rights of the people and cantons (Art. 148(1)). It elects the 7 members of the Federal Council and federal judges, yet neither can the legislature pass a vote of no confidence against the government, nor can the executive dissolve parliament.
* '''Militia Parliament Principle (민병제 의회)''': Members of Parliament serve part-time (50%–70% commitment) during four annual 3-week sessions while retaining their primary civilian professions, rooting governance in active civic participation.
* '''Perfect Bicameral Equality (양원제)''': The National Council (200 members representing the population) and the Council of States (46 members representing the 26 cantons) possess fully co-equal statutory authority. Disputes are handled via a Parliamentary Shuttle (`왕복심의`) limited to 3 rounds, followed by a 26-member Joint Conciliation Committee (`양원조정협의회`).
* '''Mandatory Consultation Procedure (입법협의절차)''': Under the CPA, draft bills, major treaties, and impactful policies must undergo a minimum 3-month public consultation gathering feedback from cantons, political parties, economic associations, and civil society to mitigate referendum veto risks.
* '''Comprehensive Bill Dispatches (Dispatch / Botschaft)''': Government-sponsored bills must include an extensive official explanation covering economic, social, environmental, human rights, gender equality, and EU law compatibility assessments.
* '''Constitutional Legislative Evaluation (입법평가)''': Article 170 of the Federal Constitution mandates the evaluation of the effectiveness of federal measures, supported empirically by the central ARAMIS research database.
* '''Parliamentary Election of Federal Judges''': The United Federal Assembly elects approximately 200 federal judges based on Judicial Committee recommendations, maintaining party proportions, language representation (German, French, Italian), gender, and regional balance while preserving adjudicative independence.

== Policy Recommendations for South Korea ==
1. '''Extension of Legislative Notice Periods''': Extending ROK legislative notice from 40 days to at least 3 months, mirroring the Swiss Consultation Procedure. 2. '''Standardization of Comprehensive Bill Explanation Dispatches''': Mandating thorough impact reports for proposed bills covering socio-economic effects and rights impact. 3. '''Codification of Legislative Evaluation''': Amending the National Assembly Act to formalize ex-ante and ex-post regulatory evaluations. 4. '''Democratic Legitimacy in Judicial Appointments''': Enhancing transparency and parliamentary involvement in the nomination and confirmation of Supreme Court Justices.

* '''공보법 (PublA / SR 170.512)''': 제7조 제1항.
* '''연방법원법 (BGG / SR 173.110)''': 제1조, 제4조, 제15조, 제7조4, 제82조.

== 정책 배경 및 문제점 ==
1. '''스위스 의회·사법제도에 대한 이해 부족''': 한국에서는 스위스의 양원제, 입법절차, 국민투표, 사법부 구성에 대해 단편적인 정보만 알려져 있어, 제도 전반에 대한 체계적·비교법적 연구의 필요성이 제기됨. 2. '''입법 품질 및 규제영향평가 한계''': 대한민국 국회의 입법 과정은 졸속 심의, 짧은 입법예고 기간(40일), 형식적인 법률안 제안설명서, 사전·사후 입법평가 체계의 미비라는 문제점을 안고 있음. 3. '''대법관 선출의 민주적 정당성 이슈''': 대법관 제청권이 대법원장에 집중되고 대통령이 임명하는 구조로 인해, 사법부 구성의 다원성과 민주적 정당성을 강화할 필요성이 지속적으로 논의됨.

== 주요 제도적 특징 및 분석 결과 ==

* '''연방의회의 최고기관성''': 연방의회는 연방의 최고기관으로 규정되며(헌법 제148조 제1항), 연방내각위원(7명)과 연방법관(~200명)을 선출함. 다만 불신임권이나 의회해산권은 존재하지 않음.
* '''민병제 의회 (Militia Parliament)''': 의원이 본업을 유지하면서 연 4회, 회기당 3주씩 파트타임(50%~70%)으로 의정 활동에 참여하는 전통적 시민참여 모델.
* '''완전한 권한 동등의 양원제''': 국민을 대표하는 연방하원(200석)과 26개 칸톤을 대표하는 연방상원(46석)이 완전히 동등한 권한을 가짐. 의견 불일치 시 최대 3회의 왕복심의(`왕복심의`) 후 양원조정협의회(`양원조정협의회`)를 거침.
* '''입법협의절차 (Consultation Procedure)''': CPA에 따라 모든 법안은 최소 3개월간 26개 칸톤, 정당, 경제단체 등의 의견을 수렴하는 공표·서면 협의를 거쳐 국민투표 거부권을 예방함.
* '''법률안 제안설명서 (Dispatch / Botschaft) 내실화''': 정부 제출 법안은 경제, 사회, 환경, 인권, EU법 적합성 평가를 포함한 수십~수백 페이지의 상세 설명서를 첨부해야 함.
* '''헌법상 입법평가 명문화''': 헌법 제170조에 법률의 실효성 평가(effectiveness evaluation) 의무를 규정하고, ARAMIS 연구 데이터베이스를 통해 사후 평가를 체계적으로 관리함.
* '''양원합동회의의 연방법관 선출''': 양원합동회의(United Federal Assembly)가 사법위원회의 검증을 거쳐 정당 비율, 언어(독일어·프랑스어·이탈리아어), 성별, 지역을 고려하여 연방법관을 선출함.

== 대한민국 법제 개선을 위한 제언 ==
1. '''입법예고 기간 연장''': 현행 40일의 입법예고 기간을 스위스 입법협의절차와 같이 최소 3개월 이상으로 연장. 2. '''법률안 제안설명서 내실화''': 단순 개요를 넘어 사회·경제적 영향 및 기본권 침해 여부를 종합 평가하는 보고서 작성 의무화. 3. '''국회 입법평가 규범화''': 국회법 개정을 통해 사전·사후 입법평가 절차를 법제화. 4. '''대법관 선출의 민주적 정당성 제고''': 대법관 후보자 추천 및 국회 인사청문회 과정에서 의회의 실질적 검증과 다원적 대표성 확보.

== Summary ==
'''A Study on the Improvement of Family Relations Registration System with a Focus on the Certificate by Registration''' (`JPW-REPORT-201918`) is an official judicial policy research publication issued by the [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] (JPRI) under the [[Supreme Court of Korea]]. Authored by Research Officer Lee, Hye-jeong, the report evaluates South Korea's family relations certification system (등록사항별 증명제도) under the [[Act on Registration of Family Relations]].

The study examines the tension between personal privacy rights (informational self-determination) and public disclosure principles, analyzes comparative civil status models across 8 jurisdictions (Vietnam, Japan, Hong Kong, United States, Canada, Germany, United Kingdom, Sweden) alongside international frameworks (ICCS Conventions No. 1, 16, 34 and EU Regulation 2016/1191), evaluates national empirical survey data from 12,343 registration officers, and formulates 3 core policy proposals: (1) expanding customizable options under the Specific Certificate system (특정증명서), (2) establishing penal and administrative sanctions against third parties who excessively demand detailed certificates (상세증명서), and (3) expanding English and multi-language certificates (영문증명서).

== Entity Identity & Metadata ==

* '''Stable ID''': `JPW-REPORT-201918`
* '''Canonical Name''': A Study on the Improvement of Family Relations Registration System with a Focus on the Certificate by Registration
* '''Official Korean Name''': 가족관계등록제도의 개선방안에 관한 연구 - 등록사항별 증명서를 중심으로 -
* '''Entity Type''': Judicial Policy Research Report / Family Law & Civil Status Registration Reform Study
* '''Aliases''': JPRI Research Series 2019-18; Research Report 2019-18; 2019-18 가족관계등록제도의 개선방안에 관한 연구; Study on the Family Relations Registration System
* '''Issuing Authority''': Judicial Policy Research Institute (사법정책연구원 / JPRI) / Supreme Court of Korea (대법원)
* '''Publication Date''': Printed February 11, 2020; Published February 19, 2020
* '''ISBN / Registration''': 979-11-6168-114-6 95360 / Publication Registration No. 32-9741568-001323-01

== Legal Basis ==

* '''Constitution of the Republic of Korea''':
** ''Article 10'': Human Dignity, Worth, and Individual Rights.
** ''Article 17'': Right to Privacy and Informational Self-Determination (개인정보자기결정권).
* '''Act on Registration of Family Relations (Act No. 8435 / 가족관계등록법)''':
** ''Article 14'': Issuance of Certificates and Access Restrictions on Third Parties.
** ''Article 14(5)'': Mandate for Minimal Information Access & Prohibition of Excessive Third-Party Demands.
** ''Article 15'': Types of Certificates (Family Relations, Basic, Marriage, Adoption, Special Adoption) and Formats (General, Detailed, Specific).
** ''Articles 118 & 122'': Penal Provisions for False Notifications and Administrative Fines for Delays.
* '''Supreme Court Regulations & Practice Directions''':
** ''Supreme Court Regulations on Registration of Family Relations'': Article 21-2 (Specific Certificates for Parental Rights/Guardianship); Article 21-3 (Issuance of English Certificates, Effective Dec 27, 2019).
** ''Practice Direction on English Certificates'' (영문증명서지침, Effective Dec 27, 2019).
** ''Practice Direction on Specific Certificates'' (특정증명서의 작성에 관한 업무처리지침).
* '''Constitutional Court Decisions''': Decision 2015Hun-Ma924 (June 30, 2016 - unconsented issuance of certificates to siblings declared unconstitutional).
* '''International Treaties & Frameworks''': ICCS Conventions No. 1 (1956), No. 16 (1976), No. 34 (2014) on Multilingual Civil Status Extracts; EU Regulation 2016/1191 on Public Documents & Multilingual Standard Forms (MSF).

== Background & Policy Problems ==
1. '''Habitual Third-Party Over-demands for Detailed Certificates''': Despite the 2016 statutory amendment designating General Certificates (`일반증명서`) as the default standard, Detailed Certificates (`상세증명서`) accounted for 67.4% of total issuances between 2017 and 2019. Financial institutions, employers, and schools routinely require complete disclosures without specific justification. 2. '''Absence of Statutory Sanctions under Article 14(5)''': Article 14(5) instructs third parties to request minimal information and refrain from misuse, but lacks criminal penalties or administrative fines, turning the provision into an unenforceable warning. 3. '''Inflexible Specific Certificate Options''': The existing Specific Certificate (`특정증명서`) framework only covers parental authority and guardianship (Article 21-2), leaving applicants unable to selectively exclude non-relevant past personal histories (e.g., old divorces, deceased children, or estranged parents). 4. '''Administrative Burden for Abroad Usage''': Prior to the implementation of English Certificates (`영문증명서`) on December 27, 2019, citizens faced high costs and delays associated with private translation, notarization, and manual Apostille authentication.

== Key Findings & Policy Proposals ==

* '''Flexible Specific Certificate Framework''': Granting applicants customizable options to exclude deceased individuals (`사망자`), original registration base (`등록기준지`), or clan origin (`본`), select specific family members, and limit timeframes for past marriage/adoption records.
* '''Integrated Specific Certificates''': Proposing legislative amendments to establish an Integrated Specific Certificate (`통합 특정증명서`) and Use-Specific Certificates (`용도별 증명서`).
* '''Enforceable Third-Party Sanctions''': Establishing penal provisions (imprisonment or fines) and administrative fines for third parties that force the submission of Detailed Certificates without proven legal necessity.
* '''International Certificate Standards''': Expanding English Family Relations Certificates and evaluating additional foreign language formats (Chinese, Vietnamese, Japanese) while adapting ICCS and EU Regulation 2016/1191 Multilingual Standard Forms.

== 개요 ==
'''가족관계등록제도의 개선방안에 관한 연구'''(`JPW-REPORT-201918`)는 대한민국 [[대법원]] 산하 [[사법정책연구원]](JPRI)에서 발간한 공식 사법정책 연구보고서이다(저자: 이혜정 사법정책연구원 연구담당관). 본 보고서는 [[가족관계의 등록 등에 관한 법률]](가족관계등록법)상 등록사항별 증명제도의 운영 현황을 진단하고, 개인정보자기결정권과 공시주의 간의 조화를 도모하며, 해외 8개국(베트남, 일본, 홍콩, 미국, 캐나다, 독일, 영국, 스웨덴)의 신분등록제도 및 국제협약(ICCS 협약, EU 규정 2016/1191)을 비교 분석한다. 또한 전국 12,343명의 등록사무 담당자에 대한 실증 설문조사를 바탕으로 특정증명서 선택항목 확대, 제3자 상세증명서 과도 요구에 대한 제재규정 신설, 영문 및 다국어 증명서 고도화라는 3대 정책 대안을 제시한다.

== 주요 법적 근거 ==

* '''대한민국 헌법''': 제10조(인간의 존엄성과 행복추구권), 제17조(사생활의 비밀과 자유 및 개인정보자기결정권).
* '''가족관계의 등록 등에 관한 법률 (가족관계등록법)''':

== 정책 배경 및 문제점 ==
1. '''제3자의 상세증명서 관행적 과도 요구''': 2016년 개정법이 일반증명서(`일반증명서`)를 원칙으로 명시했음에도 불구하고, 2017~2019년 발급 통계상 상세증명서(`상세증명서`) 비중이 67.4%에 달함. 금융기관, 기업, 학교 등 제3자가 구체적 이유 없이 상세증명서를 요구하는 관행이 지속됨. 2. '''제14조 제5항의 실효성 부재''': 제3자의 최소 정보 요구를 규정한 제14조 제5항에 형벌이나 과태료 등 제재규정이 없어 훈시규정에 그치고 있음. 3. '''특정증명서의 제약''': 현행 특정증명서(`특정증명서`)는 친권·후견 분야(규칙 제21조의2)에 한정되어 있어, 과거 이혼력, 사망한 자녀, 별거 부모 등 불필요한 개인이력 숨김 요구를 수용하지 못함. 4. '''해외 제출용 증명서의 번거로움''': 2019년 12월 27일 영문증명서(`영문증명서`) 도입 전까지, 국민들은 사적 번역, 공증, 아포스티유 발급에 연간 수백억 원의 비용과 시간을 소모함.

== 주요 연구결과 및 정책 제언 ==

* '''특정증명서 선택항목 확대''': 사망자(`사망자`), 등록기준지(`등록기준지`), 본(`본`)의 포함 여부를 신청인이 선택할 수 있도록 하고, 특정 가족 구성원만 선택하거나 과거 혼인·입양 이력의 증명 기간을 제한하는 기능 도입.
* '''통합 특정증명서 신설''': 법률 개정을 통해 '통합 특정증명서'(`통합 특정증명서`) 및 '용도별 증명서'의 법적 근거 마련.
* '''제3자 과도 요구에 대한 제재규정 신설''': 정당한 사유 없이 상세증명서를 강요하거나 목적 외 사용한 제3자에 대해 형벌(징역/벌금) 및 과태료 부과 조항 제정.
* '''외국어 증명서 고도화''': 가족관계 영문증명서의 입증 범위를 확대하고, 중국어·베트남어·일어 등 다국어 증명서 도입 검토 및 ICCS·EU MSF 다국어 표준양식 수용.

== Summary ==
'''A Study on the Reliability Assessment and Experience Rules of Victim's Statement in the Criminal Case of Sexual Violence''' (JPW-REPORT-202002) is an official judicial policy research publication issued by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) under the Supreme Court of Korea. The report examines criminal cases of sexual violence characterized by a scarcity of direct objective evidence, evaluating how courts assess the credibility of victim statements through the application of "experience rules" (경험칙).

The publication comprises two complementary sections:

* '''Part 1''' (authored by Park, Yong Chul): Conducts a comparative legal analysis across common law jurisdictions (United States, United Kingdom, Australia) and Germany, examining jury directions, the "Prompt Outcry / Fresh Complaint" doctrine, and judicial mechanisms designed to eliminate gender bias.
* '''Part 2''' (authored by Lee, Sunmi): Performs an empirical quantitative and qualitative analysis of 474 South Korean lower court rape judgments rendered up to 2016 to evaluate how judges formulate, apply, and modify experience rules in practice.

The report recommends replacing arbitrary societal common sense with scientifically validated propositions of high probability (`고도의 개연성`) and operationalizing the Supreme Court's gender sensitivity doctrine (*성인지 감수성*) on an individualized, victim-specific basis.

== Legal Basis ==
The research and policy frameworks analyzed in the report rely upon the following legal provisions and jurisprudential standards:

=== Constitutional & Statutory Framework ===

* '''Constitution of the Republic of Korea''': Article 11 (Gender Equality) and Article 27 (Right to a Fair Trial & Due Process).
* '''Criminal Procedure Act of South Korea (형사소송법)''':
** Article 307(2): Fact Finding & Proof Beyond Reasonable Doubt.
** Article 308: Principle of Free Evaluation of Evidence (자유심증주의).
** Article 310: Corroboration Rule for Confessions (자백보강법칙).
** Articles 313(1) & 314: Exceptional Admissibility of Hearsay Evidence (특히 신빙할 수 있는 상태).
* '''Criminal Code of South Korea (형법)''': Chapter 32 (Crimes of Rape and Sexual Intercourse, Arts. 297–305).
* '''Special Penal Acts''': Act on Special Cases Concerning the Punishment, etc. of Sexual Crimes; Act on the Protection of Children and Juveniles against Sexual Offences.

=== Precedents & Foreign Statutes ===

* '''Supreme Court Precedents''': Supreme Court Decision 2018Do7709 (Oct 25, 2018; establishing gender sensitivity in adjudication); Decision 4284Hyeong-Sang86 (June 3, 1951; first explicit reference to experience rules); Decisions 2006Do3830 and 2006Do4994.
* '''Comparative Foreign Law''':
** '''United States''': Federal Rules of Evidence (FRE); State Evidence Codes (e.g., 18 Pa. Cons. Stat § 3105 regarding prompt outcry instructions).
** '''United Kingdom''': Criminal Justice & Public Order Act 1994 s. 32 (abolishing mandatory corroboration requirements); Crown Court Compendium Part 20 (Jury Directions).
** '''Australia''': Uniform Evidence Act s. 66(2A) ("Fresh in Memory" test); Victoria Jury Directions Act 2013 s. 37AAA.
** '''Germany''': Strafprozessordnung (StPO) § 261; Federal Court of Justice (BGH) case law on the Null Hypothesis (*제로가설*) in statement psychology.

== Background & Policy Problem ==
Direct objective evidence (such as physical biological traces or third-party eyewitness testimony) is exceptionally rare in sexual violence trials. In an empirical sample of 167 lower court rape judgments examined in this study, third-party eyewitnesses were present at the crime scene in only 1.48% of cases. Consequently, the victim's statement serves as the central direct evidence of guilt.

When evaluating statement credibility under the principle of free evaluation of evidence (CPA Art. 308), judges rely on "experience rules." However, judicial practice has suffered from significant policy problems:

# '''Arbitrariness of Experience Rules''': Judges frequently label subjective personal impressions or unverified societal stereotypes as objective "experience rules."
# '''Inter-Instance Disparities''': Lower courts frequently invoke conflicting propositions regarding delayed reporting, failure to scream, or post-incident contact with the accused. Appellate courts frequently overturn lower court acquittals or convictions due to divergent interpretations of these rules.
# '''The "Average Victim" Stereotype''': Historical adjudication relied on an abstract "average victim" expected to exhibit immediate physical resistance and prompt reporting, ignoring psychological trauma, cognitive freezing, fear of retaliation, and power imbalances.

== Key Findings & Policy Proposals ==

# '''Strict Threshold for Experience Rules''': Valid experience rules operating as legal constraints on free evaluation must reach the threshold of high probability (`고도의 개연성`) or scientific certainty, rather than mere public common sense or societal stereotypes.
# '''Standardized Jury Instructions''': Adopting standardized instructions modeled on the UK Crown Court Compendium Part 20 (14 model directions) and Australia's Victoria Jury Directions Act 2013 to inform fact-finders that delayed reporting or lack of physical injury does not imply consent or fabrication.
# '''Individualized "Specific Victim" Evaluation''': Shifting the judicial evaluation paradigm from an abstract "average victim" to an individualized assessment of "the specific victim" (`바로 그 피해자`), taking into account the individual's specific trauma, age, power relationships, and social context.

== Empirical Data & Case Analysis ==

* '''Sample Scope''': 474 lower court rape (*강간*) judgments rendered up to December 31, 2016 (containing the terms *credibility* [신빙성] and *experience rules* [경험칙]), encompassing 1,188 prosecution facts (`공소사실`).
* '''First-Instance Verdicts''': 81.06% guilty (957 facts) and 17.42% not guilty (213 facts).
* '''Explicit Mention Rate''': Experience rules were explicitly cited in 39.45% of total judgments (36.44% in conviction rulings vs. 50.46% in acquittal rulings).
* '''Delayed Reporting Myth Disproved''': Analysis demonstrated that in cases involving acquainted parties, conviction rates remained consistently high (above 70–75%) regardless of whether the victim reported the crime within 1 month, within 1 year, or after more than 1 year. This empirically disproves the assumption that delayed reporting inherently undermines credibility.

== Key Recommendations ==

# '''Legislative/Judicial Standardization of High Probability Threshold''': Strictly enforcing that any proposition applied as an experience rule must possess high probability (`고도의 개연성`) or scientific verification.
# '''Adoption of Jury Directions in Public Participation Trials''': Standardizing 14 jury direction models in South Korean *국민참여재판* to eliminate jury bias regarding delayed reporting and non-resistance.
# '''Full Operationalization of Gender Sensitivity''': Requiring written court judgments to evaluate the specific psychological and situational context of "the specific victim" (`바로 그 피해자`).

== 개요 ==
'''성폭력 형사사건에서 피해자 진술의 신빙성과 경험칙에 관한 연구'''(JPW-REPORT-202002)는 대한민국 대법원 산하 사법정책연구원(JPRI)이 발간한 공식 사법정책 연구보고서이다. 본 보고서는 물적·직접 증거가 극히 희소한 성폭력 형사재판에서 법원이 자유심증주의(형사소송법 제308조)에 따라 피해자 진술의 신빙성을 평가할 때 활용하는 '경험칙(經驗則)'의 실태와 문제점을 체계적으로 분석하였다.

본 보고서는 두 개의 독립적이면서도 상호보완적인 부분으로 구성되어 있다:

* '''제1부분''' (작성자: 박용철 초빙연구위원): 미국, 영국, 호주 등 영미법계 국가 및 독일의 증거법, '신속한 고소(Prompt Outcry / Fresh Complaint)' 법리, 배심원 설시(Jury Directions), 성인지 감수성 관련 법제를 비교법적으로 연구하였다.
* '''제2부분''' (작성자: 이선미 연구위원): 2016년까지 선고된 국내 강간(强姦) 사건 하급심 판결문 474건을 바탕으로 하급심 법원이 피해자 진술의 신빙성을 판단할 때 경험칙을 어떻게 형성, 적용, 변용하는지 실증적으로 분석하였다.

본 연구는 자의적인 사회적 통념이나 편견을 배제하고, 과학적으로 검증된 '고도의 개연성'을 갖춘 명제만을 경험칙으로 인정하며, 대법원의 성인지 감수성 법리에 따라 개별 피해자의 특수한 상황을 중심으로 신빙성을 평가할 것을 제안하고 있다.

== 법적 근거 ==
본 보고서가 다루는 주요 법적 근거 및 판례 기준은 다음과 같다:

=== 헌법 및 성문 법령 ===

* '''대한민국 헌법''': 제11조(평등권 및 성평등), 제27조(재판을 받을 권리 및 적법절차 원칙).
* '''형사소송법''':
** 제307조 제2항 (증거재판주의 및 합리적 의심 없는 증명).
** 제308조 (자유심증주의).
** 제309조 및 제310조 (자백의 보강법칙).
** 제313조 제1항 및 제314조 (전문증거의 예외적 증거능력 및 특히 신빙할 수 있는 상태).
* '''형법''': 제32장 강간과 추행의 죄(제297조~제305조).
* '''특별형법''': 성폭력범죄의 처벌 등에 관한 특례법, 아동·청소년의 성보호에 관한 법률.

=== 대법원 판례 및 국외 법령 ===

* '''대법원 주요 판례''': 대법원 2018. 10. 25. 선고 2018도7709 판결 (성인지 감수성 평가 기준 확립); 대법원 1951. 6. 3. 선고 4284형상86 판결 (경험칙 용어 최초 사용); 대법원 2006도3830 및 2006도4994 판결.
* '''국외 비교법제''':
** '''미국''': 연방증거규칙(FRE); 주 증거법(예: 18 Pa. Cons. Stat § 3105 피해자 즉시 고소 배심원 지침).
** '''영국''': 1994년 형사사법 및 공공질서법 s. 32 (성범죄 보강증거 요구 폐지); Crown Court Compendium Part 20 (배심원 설시 지침).
** '''호주''': 통일증거법 s. 66(2A) ('기억의 생생함' 요건); 빅토리아주 2013년 배심원지침법 s. 37AAA.
** '''독일''': 형사소송법(StPO) § 261 (자유심증); 독일연방대법원(BGH) 판례 및 진술심리학상의 제로가설(Null Hypothesis).

== 배경 및 정책 과제 ==
성폭력 사건은 범행의 은밀성으로 인해 목격자나 생물학적 증거 등 직접적인 객관적 증거가 존재하지 않는 경우가 대부분이다. 본 연구의 실증분석 대상인 167건의 하급심 강간 판결 분석 결과, 범행 현장에 제3자 목격자가 존재했던 경우는 단 1.48%에 불과했다. 따라서 피해자의 진술은 공소사실을 입증하는 사실상 유일하고 핵심적인 직접증거가 된다.

법원은 자유심증주의에 따라 진술의 신빙성을 판단할 때 '경험칙'을 활용해왔으나, 기존 재판 실무는 다음과 같은 심각한 정책적 문제점을 안고 있었다:

# '''경험칙의 자의성과 불확실성''': 법관 개인의 주관적 인상이나 검증되지 않은 사회적 편견(통념)을 객관적인 '경험칙'으로 포장하여 판결에 응용하는 사례가 빈번함.
# '''심급간·사건간 경험칙의 불일치''': 피해자의 신고 지연, 피해 당시의 미저항, 사건 이후 가해자와의 연락 유지 등을 이유로 하급심이 무죄를 선고하면서 인용한 '경험칙'이 상급심에서 파기되거나 판부판결 간 상충하는 현상이 지속됨.
# ''''평균적 피해자' 프레임의 한계''': 피해 직후 즉시 항의하고 신고하는 '평균적·이상적 피해자'를 전제로 판단함으로써, 피해자의 외상 후 스트레스, 트라우마, 외포 상태, 권력관계에 따른 반응의 다변성을 반영하지 못함.

== 주요 연구 결과 및 정책 제안 ==

# '''경험칙의 법적 엄격성 강화''': 자유심증주의를 제한하는 진정한 의미의 경험칙은 단순한 사회적 통념이나 확률적 추측이 아니라, 과학적·실증적으로 검증된 '고도의 개연성'을 갖춘 명제이어야 함.
# '''표준 배심원 설시(Jury Directions) 모델 도입''': 영국 Crown Court Compendium 및 호주 빅토리아주 배심원지침법을 벤치마킹하여, 국민참여재판에서 배심원들이 '지연 신고'나 '물적 상해의 부재'만을 이유로 피해자 진술의 신빙성을 단정적으로 배척하지 않도록 14개 유형의 표준 설시문 도입 제안.
# ''''바로 그 피해자' 중심의 개별적 평가 전환''': 추상적인 '평균적 피해자'라는 편견에서 벗어나, 사건 당시 구체적 피해자가 처해 있던 나이, 권력관계, 트라우마, 심리적 상태를 입체적으로 분석하는 '바로 그 피해자' 중심의 성인지 감수성 평가 실현.

== 실증 분석 데이터 ==

* '''표본 규모''': 2016년 12월 31일까지 선고된 하급심 강간(强姦) 판결문 중 '신빙성'과 '경험칙' 키워드가 포함된 474건 (총 1,188개 공소사실).
* '''1심 판결 결과''': 유죄 81.06% (957개 공소사실), 무죄 17.42% (213개 공소사실).
* '''경험칙 명시 비율''': 전체 474건 중 39.45%(187건)에서 경험칙 명제 직접 인용 (무죄 판결문에서의 경험칙 인용률이 50.46%로 유죄 판결문의 36.44%보다 높음).
* '''지연 신고에 관한 실증적 반증''': 아는 사람(안면 있음) 관계에서의 성폭력 사건 분석 결과, 최초 신고가 1개월 이내, 1년 이내, 1년 이상 경과한 경우 모두에서 유죄 선고율이 70~75% 이상으로 높게 유지됨. 이는 '진정한 피해자라면 즉시 신고했을 것'이라는 전통적 통념이 실제 재판 결과와 맞지 않는 오류임을 실증적으로 증명함.

== Summary ==
'''A study on the Protection and Participation System for Crime Victims''' (`JPW-REPORT-202412`) is an official judicial policy research publication issued by the [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] (JPRI) under the [[Supreme Court of Korea]]. Authored by Lead Research Fellow Cho, Mi-sun alongside participating researchers Kim, Seong-hwa, Yang, Seung-wook, and Lee, Dan-bi, the report systematically evaluates the legal status, procedural rights, and practical challenges of crime victims across investigation and trial stages in South Korea.

The report examines constitutional foundations, statutory notification rules, record inspection mechanisms, and the victim lawyer system (피해자변호사제도). It conducts comparative analyses across four international jurisdictions (Germany, France, United States, Japan) and international standards (UN, EU, ICC), incorporates empirical survey data from 98 legal practitioners, and formulates legislative amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act and special penal statutes to guarantee victim information rights, expand state-appointed legal assistance across all crime types, and formalize victim participation in court proceedings.

== Background & Policy Problems ==
1. '''Procedural Exclusion & Information Deficit (정보권 보장 미흡)''': Crime victims face steep procedural barriers when tracking police and prosecutorial progress. Existing administrative rules require victims to file manual, proactive requests for status updates rather than establishing automatic digital notifications as default. 2. '''Fragmented Victim Lawyer System (피해자변호사제도 파편화)''': Court-appointed victim lawyers (피해자국선변호사) are restricted to specific statutory offenses (sexual violence, child abuse, stalking) under special laws, leaving victims of general violent crimes or financial fraud without statutory rights to legal representation. Furthermore, victim counsel lacks explicit statutory authority to object to improper questioning during investigations and trials. 3. '''Inconsistent Record Access & Copying (소송기록 열람·등사 편차)''': Trial judges exhibit wide, unpredictable disparities when ruling on victim applications to inspect or copy trial records under CPA Article 294-4, without standardized denial criteria or formal appeal channels. 4. '''Underutilized Trial Statement Rights (재판절차진술권 미흡)''': Although guaranteed by Article 27(5) of the ROK Constitution, standardized judicial procedures are lacking for non-witness victims, and submitted written Victim Impact Statements (VIS) are often returned or overlooked due to procedural ambiguities.

== Key Findings & Policy Proposals ==

* '''Default Automatic Notification via KICS''': Amending Criminal Procedure Act Articles 257 and 259-2 to mandate automatic progress updates via SMS/email through the Korea Information System of Criminal Justice Services (KICS) as the standard default.
* '''Generalizing Victim Legal Assistance''': Codifying a general provision in the Criminal Procedure Act guaranteeing victim legal counsel across all crime types, while expanding court-appointed attorneys for vulnerable victims of violent offenses under the Specific Violent Crimes Act.
* '''Explicit Statutory Right of Objection (이의제기권)''': Enacting explicit statutory rights for victim lawyers to object to improper, secondary-trauma-inducing questioning during investigative interrogations and pre-trial hearings.
* '''Standardized Record Inspection Guidelines & Appeal Procedure''': Amending CPA Article 294-4 to require courts to provide written justifications using standardized refusal checklists when denying record access, and creating an immediate objection/appeal mechanism.
* '''Courtroom Accommodations & VIS Formalization''': Standardizing procedures for receiving Victim Impact Statements, providing designated courtroom seating for victim counsel, and instituting formal attendance checks by trial judges.

== Comparative International Frameworks ==

* '''Germany''': *Nebenklage* (accessory prosecution under StPO § 395) granting victims independent party rights, full file inspection (§ 406e), and state-funded legal assistance (§ 397a).
* '''France''': *Partie civile* allowing civil party status within criminal proceedings with rights to request evidence, ask questions, and receive assistance through the *Bureau d'aide aux victimes*.
* '''United States''': *Crime Victims' Rights Act* (18 U.S.C. § 3771) granting 8 enforceable statutory rights, enforcement via *Writ of Mandamus*, and formal *Victim Impact Statements* during sentencing.
* '''Japan''': *Victim Participation System* (피해자참가제도 under CPA Art. 316-33) enabling court-authorized participation, questioning through prosecutors, and legal aid via *Houterasu* (Japan Legal Support Center).

== 개요 ==
'''형사절차 내 피해자 보호·참가 현황 및 개선방안'''(`JPW-REPORT-202412`)은 대한민국 [[대법원]] 산하 [[사법정책연구원]](JPRI)에서 발간한 공식 사법정책 연구보고서이다(연구책임자: 조미선 연구위원, 공동연구자: 김성화·양승욱·이단비 조사위원). 본 보고서는 수사 및 공판 절차 전반에 걸친 범죄피해자의 법적 지위, 절차적 권리, 실무적 한계를 체계적으로 진단하고 종합적인 개선방안을 제시한다.

보고서는 헌법적 근거, 피해자 통지제도, 소송기록 열람·등사 제도, 피해자변호사제도(피해자변호사제도)를 검토하고, 주요 4개국(독일, 프랑스, 미국, 일본) 및 국제기구(UN, EU, ICC)의 비교법적 모델을 분석하였다. 또한 법조인 98명을 대상으로 한 실증 설문조사 결과를 바탕으로 피해자의 정보권 보장, 피해자변호사 제도의 일반화, 공판절차 참여 형식화를 위한 형사소송법 및 개별 특례법 개정안을 도출하였다.

== 주요 법적 근거 ==

* '''대한민국 헌법''':
** ''제10조'': 인간의 존엄과 가치 및 행복추구권.
** ''제27조제5항'': 범죄피해자의 재판절차진술권.
** ''제30조'': 범죄피해자구조청구권.
* '''형사소송법''':
** ''제258조'': 고소인 등에 대한 처리결과 통지.
** ''제260조'': 재정신청.
** ''제294조의2'': 피해자 등의 진술권.
** ''제294조의4'': 피해자 등의 소송기록 열람·등사.
* '''범죄피해자 보호법''':
** ''제8조제2항'': 피해자에 대한 형사절차 정보 제공.
* '''성폭력범죄의 처벌 등에 관한 특례법''':
** ''제27조'': 피해자변호사의 선임 및 국선변호사 지정.
* '''특정강력범죄의 처벌 등에 관한 특례법''':
** ''신설 제8조의4 (제안)'': 특정강력범죄 피해자에 대한 국선변호사 지원 확대.
* '''국제기준 및 조약''':
** ''유엔 범죄 및 권력남용 피해자를 위한 사법의 기본원칙 선언 (1985년)''.
** ''EU 피해자 권리 지침 (Directive 2012/29/EU)''.
** ''국제형사재판소(ICC) 로마성전 제68조'': 피해자의 보호 및 절차 참여.

== 정책 배경 및 문제점 ==
1. '''정보권 보장 미흡 (절차적 소외)''': 수사 진행 상황 및 재판 일정을 확인하기 위한 절차가 복잡하며, 현행 규정이 피해자의 능동적 신청을 전제로 하고 있어 자동 통지 체계가 미비함. 2. '''피해자변호사제도의 파편화''': 피해자국선변호사 제도가 성폭력, 아동학대, 스토킹 등 일부 성격의 범죄에만 한정되어 있어, 일반 강력범죄나 재산범죄 피해자는 법률지원을 받을 법적 근거가 부재함. 또한 수사 및 공판 과정에서 피해자변호사의 부당한 신문에 대한 이의제기권이 명문으로 규정되어 있지 않음. 3. '''소송기록 열람·등사의 불확실성''': 형사소송법 제294조의4에 따른 소송기록 열람·등사 신청 시 재판장의 성향에 따라 허가 여부의 편차가 크며, 불허가 결정 시 불복할 수 있는 절차가 결여되어 있음. 4. '''재판절차진술권의 형식적 운용''': 헌법 제27조제5항이 재판절차진술권을 보장함에도 불구하고 증인이 아닌 피해자의 의견진술 절차가 표준화되어 있지 않으며, 서면 제출된 피해자영향진술서(VIS)가 충실히 반영되지 못함.

== 주요 연구결과 및 정책 제언 ==

* '''KICS 기반 자동통지 원칙화''': 형사소송법 제257조 및 제259조의2를 개정하여 형사사법정보시스템(KICS)을 통한 수사진행상황 자동 알림(SMS/이메일)을 기본 원칙으로 정립.
* '''피해자변호사 일반 근거 마련''': 형사소송법에 모든 범죄피해자가 변호인을 선임하고 조력을 받을 수 있는 일반 규정을 신설하고, 특정강력범죄 특례법 개정을 통해 국선변호 지원 대상을 확대.
* '''피해자변호사의 이의제기권 명문화''': 수사기관의 조사 및 구속영장 실질심사, 공판신문 과정에서 2차 피해를 유발하는 부당한 신문에 대해 피해자변호사가 이의를 제기할 수 있는 법적 권리 명시.
* '''소송기록 열람·등사 불허사유 서식화 및 불복절차 신설''': 형사소송법 제294조의4를 개정하여 불허가 시 표준화된 체크리스트 형태의 서면 이유를 교부하도록 의무화하고, 즉시이의 또는 불복 절차 마련.
* '''법정 내 피해자변호사 좌석 확보 및 VIS 반영''': 공판정 내 피해자변호사의 전용 좌석을 배치하고 재판장의 출석 확인을 정례화하며, 피해자영향진술서(VIS)의 표준 제출·심리 절차 마련.

== 국외 비교법적 분석 ==

* '''독일''': 부대공소제도(*Nebenklage*, 형사소송법 § 395)를 통해 피해자에게 독립된 당사자적 지위 부여, 제385조 및 제406조의e에 따른 전면적 기록열람권, 제397조의a에 따른 국선변호인 지원.
* '''프랑스''': 사소제도(*Partie civile*)를 통해 형사절차 내 민사 당사자 참가 허용, 증거신청 및 질문권 행사, 피해자지원국(*Bureau d'aide aux victimes*)을 통한 종합 지원.
* '''미국''': 연방 범죄피해자 권리법(*Crime Victims' Rights Act*, 18 U.S.C. § 3771)을 통한 8가지 법적 권리 보장, 구제명령(*Writ of Mandamus*)을 통한 권리 실효성 확보, 양형 단계에서의 피해자영향진술서(*Victim Impact Statement*) 제출 활성화.
* '''일본''': 피해자참가제도(*Victim Participation System*, 일본 형사소송법 제316조의33)를 통한 법원의 참가 결정, 검사에 대한 의견 진술 및 피고인 신문권, 일본사법지원센터(*Houterasu*)를 통한 국선참가변호사 지원.

Policy Analysis == ; Background : Expanding direct and indirect participation by retail investors for wealth accumulation and retirement planning has elevated capital market fairness and investor protection into a core public interest. However, recurring mass financial losses — such as the KIKO currency option crisis, Woori Power Income Fund, DSME accounting fraud, and the Lime and Optimus private equity fund redemption suspensions — highlight systemic vulnerabilities in South Korea's post-hoc collective redress mechanisms. ; Policy Problem : '''Protracted Civil Litigation & Evidentiary Imbalance''': Collective investor lawsuits under general civil procedure take years to resolve (averaging 10 to 53+ months for 1st instance judgments) due to severe evidentiary asymmetry (증거편재), where critical financial engineering, valuation, and sales data are held exclusively by financial institutions. : '''Underutilization of Securities Class Actions''': Over 19 years since its enactment in 2005, only 12 securities class action lawsuits were filed in South Korea (averaging < 0.63 cases/year). Appeals against class certification decisions take an average of 57.54 months — consuming 85% of total trial duration — because immediate appeals automatically suspend main proceedings. : '''Inadequate Regulatory ADR Mechanics''': Financial Dispute Mediation (금융분쟁조정) provides low-cost resolution but lacks legally binding collective enforcement (편면적 구속력 or statutory collective mediation), forcing uncompensated investors back into court if financial institutions reject non-binding recommendations. ; Legal/Policy Gap : Financial law combines private contract law and public regulatory law. While regulatory authorities collect disgorged profits or administrative fines (과징금), these funds revert entirely to the national treasury (국고) rather than compensating victimized investors. ; Objectives : Streamline judicial evidence collection, reduce class certification appellate delays, concentrate common-issue dockets, and establish a statutory mechanism allowing financial regulators to disgorge illicit gains via court actions and distribute them directly to injured investors. ; Implementation & Proposed Reforms : '''Securities Class Action Act Amendments''': Amend Article 15 to specify that immediate appeals against class certification decisions do NOT suspend main court proceedings (excluding suspension of execution), allowing trial courts to conduct evidence gathering while certification is appealed. Introduce modern evidence discovery tools: Material Production Orders (자료제출명령), Deposition/Statement Recording (진술녹취제도), mandatory record transfers from regulatory bodies, and unified financial transaction queries via Korea Exchange (한국거래소 일괄조회). : '''Practical Judicial Management''': Implement "Lead Case / Common Issue Concentration" (한 재판부 관련 사건 병합/집중심리), establish Pre-trial Case Explanation Hearings (사건설명기일), expand Expert Commissioner participation (전문심리위원), and extend judge assignment terms (사무분담 장기화). : '''Capital Markets Act Amendment (Long-term)''': Insert Articles 420-2 and 420-3 to establish an Action for Restitution / Disgorgement of Unjust Enrichment (부당이득환수의 소). This empowers the Financial Services Commission (FSC) to sue non-compliant financial entities in court to disgorge profits or recoup investor losses, appointing court-supervised distribution managers (분배관리인) to disburse funds directly to affected investors. ; Evidence & Empirical Data : '''Civil Lawsuits''': Average 1st instance trial duration ranged from 10.1 months (Woori Power Income) to 53.89 months (DSME). : '''Securities Class Actions''': Out of 12 total filed cases, average class certification resolution took 57.54 months, main case disposition took 67.66 months, and complete distribution took 89.0 months. Attorney fees averaged 22.71% of recovery, while net investor payouts averaged 74.62% of executed recovery. : '''International Benchmarks''': US SEC Fair Funds distributed $903.86 million annually (2017–2023); UK FCA enacted mandatory Consumer Redress Schemes (CONRED) for Arch cru and British Steel Pension cases. == 5. MediaWiki Output == {{Infobox Judicial Policy|name=A Study on the Improvement of the Collective Redress Procedures for Investors|official_name=금융투자자 보호를 위한 집단적 피해구제절차 개선방안|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-202413|issuing_authority=Judicial Policy Research Institute (사법정책연구원)|authors=Kwon Mi-yon (권미연), Kim Seong-hwa (김성화)|publication_date=2024-08-27|report_series=연구총서 2024-13|isbn=979-11-6168-324-9|legal_basis=Capital Markets Act; Financial Consumer Protection Act; Securities Class Action Act; Civil Act; Civil Procedure Act}} '''A Study on the Improvement of the Collective Redress Procedures for Investors''' is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. == Summary == This document is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. It comparatively and empirically analyzes collective redress mechanisms for investors through general civil litigation, securities class actions, and regulatory alternative dispute resolution (ADR). It formulates practical court case-management guidance along with draft amendments to the Securities Class Action Act and the Capital Markets Act. == Legal Basis == The legal frameworks analyzed include: * '''Capital Markets Act (자본시장법)''': Articles 1, 125, 162, 175, 177, 179, and proposed draft Articles 420-2 & 420-3. * '''Financial Consumer Protection Act (금융소비자보호법)''': Articles 1, 17–21, 33, 41, 42, 44. * '''Securities Class Action Act (증권관련집단소송법)''': Articles 3, 11, 12, 15, 17, 30–34, and proposed amendment drafts. * '''Civil Act & Civil Procedure Act of Korea (민법 / 민사소송법)''': Articles 51, 53, 65, 202-2, 344–350, 750. == Background == Growing public participation in financial investment has made capital market fairness a critical public value. However, mass-loss cases such as KIKO, the Woori Power Income Fund, DSME accounting fraud, and the Lime and Optimus fund suspensions demonstrate the slow pace of investor redress through the courts. == Objectives == # Address evidentiary imbalance (증거편재) and shorten the duration of investor lawsuits. # Amend the Securities Class Action Act so that appeals against class certification no longer halt examination of the main case. # Establish an Action for Restitution of Unjust Enrichment (부당이득환수의 소) so regulators can seize illegal profits and distribute them directly to investors. == Scope == * '''Domestic Empirical Study''': Statistical analysis of civil cases, 12 securities class actions (2005–2023), and Financial Dispute Mediation Committee mediations. * '''Four-Country Comparative Study''': United States (SEC Fair Funds & Class Actions), United Kingdom (FCA Redress Schemes & Restitution Orders), Germany (KapMuG & VDuG), and Japan (Consumer Court Procedures Special Measures Act & Designated ADR bodies). == Key Provisions == * '''Removal of Appeal Suspension Effect''': Immediate appeals (즉시항고) against class certification no longer suspend examination of the main case's evidence. * '''Strengthened Evidence Tools''': Adoption of Material Production Orders (자료제출명령), the Deposition/Statement Recording System (진술녹취제도), and integrated data transfer from the Korea Exchange (KRX). * '''Regulator Restitution Action''': The Financial Services Commission (FSC) is empowered to sue violators in court and appoint distribution managers (분배관리인) to disburse funds to victims. == Implementation == Courts adopt integrated case management (Lead Case Concentration), Pre-trial Case Explanation Hearings (사건설명기일), expanded use of Expert Commissioners (전문심리위원), and extended judge assignment terms in corporate/securities divisions. == Policy Issues == * Administrative fines (과징금) and criminal forfeiture proceeds currently go to the national treasury (국고) rather than compensating investor losses. * The lengthy class certification process (averaging 57.54 months) undermines the deterrent function of private enforcement (사적제재). == Reform / Amendments == * Amendment of the Securities Class Action Act (Articles 15, 17, 32, 33, 34). * Amendment of the Capital Markets Act (addition of Articles 420-2 and 420-3). == Relationship to Other Entities == * '''Publisher''': Judicial Policy Research Institute & Supreme Court of Korea. * '''Research Team''': Kwon Mi-yon, Kim Seong-hwa, Yang Seung-wook. * '''Related Regulators''': Financial Services Commission (FSC) & Financial Supervisory Service (FSS). == See Also == * [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] * [[Supreme Court of Korea]] * [[Securities Class Action Act]] * [[Financial Consumer Protection Act]] == Policy Analysis == ; Background : Interest in blockchain-based smart contracts has grown significantly across finance (DeFi), real estate, logistics, insurance, voting, healthcare, and IoT. While proponents claim smart contracts represent a game-changer signaling "the end of classic contract law," critics point to software bugs, immutability risks, hacking, and code rigidity. ; Policy Problem : '''Linguistic & Semantic Limits''': Smart contracts operate via rigid IF-THEN conditional logic in binary code. They cannot encode qualitative, discretionary legal standards such as "good faith," "duty of care of a good manager," "reasonable period," or "force majeure." : '''Immutability vs. Legal Remedies''': Blockchain immutability prevents retroactive cancellation, rescission (해제/해지), or modification of executed contracts when legal defects (mistake, fraud, duress, or incapacity) occur. : '''Privacy Conflicts''': Blockchain transparency and permanent distributed recording directly conflict with Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA) mandates regarding data destruction, correction/erasure rights (잊혀질 권리), and cross-border transfer restrictions. : '''Lack of Statutory Recognition''': Korea's positive law lacks explicit definitions or legal efficacy provisions for smart contracts, creating jurisdictional and enforcement uncertainty. ; Legal/Policy Gap : '''Code vs. Law''': The report refutes Lawrence Lessig's extreme "Code is Law" proposition, establishing that code must operate within positive legal frameworks ("Code has to obey the Law"). : '''Legal Nature''': Smart contracts are legally recognized as special real-execution contracts (의사실현계약) formed when an off-chain offer (code publication) meets a matching acceptance (condition fulfillment). ; Objectives : Establish statutory recognition for smart contracts, harmonize automated execution with civil remedies, protect consumers from automated fraud/mistakes, resolve privacy conflicts, and promote technical standardization. ; Implementation & Proposed Reforms : '''Amendment to Framework Act on Electronic Documents and Transactions''': Insert Paragraph 4 into Article 6 (제6조 제4항), declaring that for smart contracts, the time of sending and receiving an electronic document is presumed to be the time it is recorded on the blockchain. : '''Enactment of Smart Contract Framework Act (스마트계약 기본법률안)''': Introduce a 5-article standalone statute establishing: :# ''Article 1 (Purpose)'': Regulate basic smart contract matters and promote related industries. :# ''Article 2 (Definitions)'': Define "Smart Contract" as a program operating on a distributed, decentralized, shared, and replicated ledger that enables asset acquisition/transfer upon condition fulfillment; define "Blockchain Technology." :# ''Article 3 (Relationship to Other Laws)'': Mutatis mutandis application of Civil Act Part III Chapter 2 (Contracts). :# ''Article 4 (Legal Efficacy)'': Declare that a smart contract shall not be denied legal effect, validity, or enforceability solely because it is in smart contract form or contains smart contract elements. :# ''Article 5 (Standardization)'': Authorize the Minister of Science and ICT to promote standardization research and project funding. : '''Technical & Contractual Safeguards''': Integrate internal cancellation functions (''selfdestruct'' in Solidity, satellite contracts, or reverse transactions), multi-signature oracles, and emergency "kill switches" (as seen in EU Data Act Art. 30). : '''Privacy Guidelines''': Issue administrative data protection guidelines (modeled on Spain's AEPD 2022 framework) requiring privacy impact assessments (GDPR Art. 35) and off-chain personal data storage. ; MediaWiki Output == {{Infobox Judicial Policy|name=A Study on the Legal Issues of Smart Contracts|official_name=스마트계약의 법적 문제에 관한 연구|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-202414|issuing_authority=Judicial Policy Research Institute (사법정책연구원)|authors=Kim Jung-hwan (김정환)|publication_date=2024-09-29|report_series=연구총서 2024-14|isbn=979-11-6168-313-3|legal_basis=ROK Civil Act; Framework Act on Electronic Documents and Transactions; Electronic Signature Act; Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce; Personal Information Protection Act}} '''A Study on the Legal Issues of Smart Contracts''' is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. == Summary == This document is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. It analyzes the concept, technical structure, and legal nature of blockchain-based smart contracts. It evaluates civil law, consumer protection, and personal data protection, and formulates draft amendments to the Electronic Documents Act along with a proposed Smart Contract Framework Act (스마트계약 기본법률안). == Legal Basis == The legal frameworks analyzed include: * '''Civil Act of the Republic of Korea (민법)''': Article 3 (Capacity of Rights), Articles 103, 104, 107–110 (Defects in Intention & Mistake), Article 111 (Effectiveness of Declaration of Intention), Articles 140 & 141 (Cancellation), Article 527 (Binding Force of Offer), and Article 563 (Sales Contract). * '''Framework Act on Electronic Documents and Transactions (전자문서 및 전자거래 기본법)''': Article 2, Article 4(1), Article 5, Article 6 (Time of Sending/Receiving), and Article 17. * '''Electronic Signature Act (전자서명법)''': Article 2 and Article 3. * '''Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce (전자상거래법)''': Articles 2, 10, 13, 17, 20. * '''Personal Information Protection Act (개인정보보호법)''': Articles 2, 15–18, 21, 31, 36, 37, 39-12. == Background == The use of smart contracts is expanding across finance (DeFi), real estate, logistics, insurance, and IoT. However, characteristics such as transparency, code rigidity, immutability, and the risk of bugs/hacking create legal uncertainty requiring positive regulation. == Objectives == # Clarify the legal nature of smart contracts as contracts formed by real execution (의사실현계약). # Reconcile code automation with civil rescission/termination rights and consumer protection. # Draft a Smart Contract Framework Act to provide legal certainty and alignment with international standards (ISO/TC 307). == Scope == * '''Comparative Legal Analysis''': US law (Wyoming, Arizona, Illinois Blockchain Technology Act), Belarus (Decree No. 8), Portugal, Italy (Law 135/2018), the EU Data Act, and Spain's AEPD guidelines. * '''Case Law Analysis''': The Singapore International Commercial Court (SICC) ruling in ''B2C2 Ltd v Quoine Pte Ltd'' [2020] SGHC(I) 3. == Key Provisions == * '''Legal Nature''': Smart contracts are recognized as a special form of contract by real execution (의사실현계약), where the offer is made through code publication and acceptance occurs upon condition fulfillment. * '''Rejection of the "Code is Law" Doctrine''': Code must be subject to positive law ("Code has to obey the Law"). * '''Amendment to the Electronic Documents Act''': Addition of Article 6 Paragraph 4, providing that the time of sending/receiving an electronic smart contract document is the time it is recorded on the blockchain. == Implementation == The government and judiciary recommend using technical functions such as ''selfdestruct'' in Solidity, satellite contracts, verified oracles, and emergency kill switches to lawfully execute contract cancellation or termination. == Policy Issues == * Conflict between blockchain immutability and the obligation to erase personal data (잊혀질 권리) under the Personal Information Protection Act. * The inability of programming languages (such as Solidity) to encode qualitative legal norms such as "good faith" or "valid reason." == Reform / Amendments == * Amendment of Article 6 of the Framework Act on Electronic Documents and Transactions. * Enactment of a Smart Contract Framework Act (스마트계약 기본법률안 — 5 articles). * Development of Personal Information Protection Guidelines for smart contracts by the government. == Relationship to Other Entities == * '''Publisher''': Judicial Policy Research Institute & Supreme Court of Korea. * '''Lead Researcher''': Kim Jung-hwan. * '''Related Ministries''': Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) & Personal Information Protection Commission. == See Also == * [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] * [[Supreme Court of Korea]] * [[Framework Act on Electronic Documents and Transactions]] * [[ISO/TC 307 Blockchain Standards]] == References == == 7. Policy Analysis == ; Background : Human existence as a subject of rights begins at birth. However, to exercise rights, receive public healthcare, enroll in school, or receive state protection, a child's existence must be officially recorded on public registers. Unregistered children exist as "shadow children" (유령아동 / 그림자 아이), vulnerable to illegal online adoption, child trafficking, abuse, and abandonment. Audit Board inspections in 2023 revealed over 6,000 unregistered children born between 2015 and 2022 (2,154 domestic, 4,025 foreign) who existed only as temporary newborn screening numbers (임시신생아번호). ; Policy Problem : '''Passive Parent-Dependent Reporting''': The traditional birth reporting system depended entirely on voluntary reports by parents. If parents failed or refused to report, children remained unrecorded. : '''Strict Presumption of Paternity & Rigid Paternity Rules''': Under Civil Act Article 844, a child born within 300 days of divorce is legally presumed to be the former husband's child, even when biologically belonging to another partner. This created severe barriers for mothers and biological fathers (생부), preventing unwed fathers from registering their biological children without complex litigation. : '''Exclusion of Foreign Children''': Korea's Family Relation Register is strictly limited to Korean nationals (Article 1). Foreign children born in Korea have no public birth register, and undocumented foreign parents avoid embassy reports due to fear of deportation under immigration reporting duties (출입국관리법 통보의무). ; Legal/Policy Gap : '''Supreme Court Order 2020So575 (June 8, 2020)''': Established for the first time that a child's right to birth registration is a constitutional fundamental right derived from Article 10 (human dignity and general personality rights). : '''Constitutional Court Decision 2021Hun-Ma975 (March 23, 2023)''': Declared that failing to provide effective birth registration mechanisms for unwed fathers and children born to married women by non-spousal partners violates the constitutional right to birth registration. : '''Enactment of Birth Notification & Protected Childbirth''': On June 30, 2023, the National Assembly passed the Birth Notification System (출생통보제, Family Relation Registration Act Arts. 44-3 & 44-4), requiring medical institutions to report birth info to HIRA (심평원), which notifies local heads to record births ex-officio (직권기록) if parents do not report within 1 month. Concurrently, the Protected Childbirth System (보호출산제) was enacted to allow crisis mothers to give birth anonymously. Both took effect on July 19, 2024. ; Objectives : Move beyond mere "unregistered child" prevention toward establishing a comprehensive "Right to Birth Registration as a Foundation for Growth." Eliminate discrimination between children born in and out of wedlock, empower biological fathers, protect foreign children as a human right, and modernize administrative forms. ; Implementation & Proposed Statutory Reforms : '''Civil Act Amendments''': :# ''Article 844 (Presumption of Paternity)'': Restrict presumption of paternity to children born during marriage. For marriage termination by death, maintain presumption within 300 days. If remarriage occurs within 300 days of death, presume paternity of the later husband. :# ''Articles 846, 847, 848, 850, 851, 852 (Denial of Paternity)'': Grant independent rights to deny paternity (친생부인권) to adult children and biological fathers (생부), subject to judicial evaluation of biological ties, raising history, and child welfare. :# ''Articles 854-2 & 855-2 (Permissions for Denial/Recognition)'': Delete redundant permission procedures (친생부인의 허가 / 인지의 허가) made obsolete by the new paternity presumption model. : '''Act on Registration of Family Relations Amendments''': :# ''Article 44(2) (Registration Items)'': Eliminate mandatory recording of origin of surname (본) for parents; restrict place of registration (등록기준지) to cases where identification is impossible by resident ID number alone; replace wedlock distinction with statutory presumption check. :# ''Article 46 & 46-2 (Reporting Parties & Unwed Fathers)'': Ease wedlock distinctions; explicitly recognize biological fathers' right to file birth reports with effect of recognition (인지 효력 있는 출생신고) in the main reporting section. :# ''Article 46-3 (Prosecutorial/Local Head Reporting)'': Convert prosecutor/local government head reporting from an optional right (적격자) into a mandatory duty (의무자) when a child's welfare is endangered. :# ''Articles 121 & 122 (Fines)'': Increase late reporting fines from 50,000 / 100,000 KRW to 100,000 / 200,000 KRW; exempt fines when parent-child litigation is pending. : '''Foreign Child Birth Registration Act (Standalone Legislation)''': Enact a standalone law using event-based registration (사건별 편제방식) to register all foreign children born in Korea, issuing official birth certificates (외국인 아동 출생등록부) regardless of parental residence status, with explicit exemption from immigration reporting duties (불법체류자 발견 통보의무 면제). ; Evidence & Empirical Data : '''Public & Official Surveys''': Nationwide survey of 787 citizens (252 paper, 535 online) and 3,189 family register public officials showed 76.6% supporting abolition of in/out-of-wedlock terms. 81.6% of officials and 67% of paper reporters favored maintaining the 1-month reporting deadline. 49.52% supported establishing a foreign child birth registration system, citing universal human rights (76.33%). : '''Divorce & Paternity Statistics''': 87.1% of children born within 300 days of marriage termination (and 91.3% in divorce cases) were proven NOT to be the biological offspring of the former husband through court permission grants (2,131 cases between 2019 and 2023). == 5. MediaWiki Output == {{Infobox Judicial Policy|name=Strategies for Effectively Guarantee Children's Right to Birth Registration|official_name=아동의 출생등록될 권리의 실효적 보장을 위한 방안|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-202415|issuing_authority=Judicial Policy Research Institute (사법정책연구원)|authors=An Won-ju (안원주)|publication_date=2024-09-10|report_series=연구총서 2024-15|isbn=979-11-6168-303-4|legal_basis=ROK Constitution Arts. 10, 37(2); Act on Registration of Family Relations; ROK Civil Act; Special Act on Crisis Pregnancy and Protected Childbirth; UN Convention on the Rights of the Child}} '''Strategies for Effectively Guarantee Children's Right to Birth Registration''' is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. == Summary == This document is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. It analyzes the constitutional right of a child to birth registration (아동의 출생등록될 권리) as a fundamental human right, evaluates the Birth Notification System (출생통보제) and Protected Childbirth System (보호출산제), both effective July 19, 2024, and formulates amendments to the Civil Act, the Act on Registration of Family Relations, and a proposed Foreign Child Birth Registration Act. == Legal Basis == The legal frameworks analyzed include: * '''Constitution of the Republic of Korea''': Article 10 (Human Dignity & General Right of Personality) and Article 37(2). * '''Act on Registration of Family Relations (가족관계의 등록 등에 관한 법률)''': Articles 1, 9, 10, 14, 15, 44, 44-3 (Birth Notification), 44-4 (Ex-Officio Registration), 46, 48, 57, 121, 122. * '''Civil Act of the Republic of Korea (민법)''': Articles 3, 781 (Child's Surname & Origin), 844 (Presumption of Paternity), 846, 847 (Action for Denial of Paternity), 854-2, 855-2, 859, 865. * '''Special Act on Protected Childbirth (위기임신보호출산법)''': Articles 1, 2, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15, 17. * '''International Conventions''': UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC Articles 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 13, 19, 24) and the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR Article 24). == Background == A 2023 audit by the Board of Audit and Inspection found over 6,000 unregistered children (유령아동 / unregistered children) who existed only as temporary newborn screening numbers (임시신생아번호). Cases of exploitation, abuse, and infant death led to Supreme Court Order 2020So575 and Constitutional Court Decision 2021Hun-Ma975, which established birth registration as an absolute constitutional right. == Objectives == # Ensure immediate birth registration for every child born in South Korea, regardless of the parents' marital status or nationality. # Reform the presumption of paternity (친생추정) rules so that a child born after divorce is not automatically attributed to the former husband. # Provide legal certainty and birth registration rights for children of foreign nationals. == Scope == * '''Empirical Study''': A survey of 787 citizens and 3,189 family register officials, along with analysis of 2,131 paternity denial/recognition permission cases (2019–2023). * '''Three-Country Comparative Study''': Germany (''Vertrauliche Geburt'' & BGB § 1592/1600), France (''Accouchement sous x'' & Code civil Art. 326/333), and Japan (Family Register Act & 2024 Civil Code Article 772 amendments). == Key Provisions == * '''Birth Notification System (출생통보제)''': Hospitals are required to send birth information to the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service (HIRA) within 14 days, and local government heads perform ''ex-officio'' registration if parents fail to report within one month. * '''Protected Childbirth System (보호출산제)''': Mothers in crisis may give birth anonymously after undergoing staged counseling. * '''Simplified Forms''': Removes the requirement to record the parents' clan origin (본) and restricts the place of registration (등록기준지). == Implementation == Courts and local governments expand ex-officio verification and require social welfare or police agencies that discover unregistered children to promptly process birth registration reports through a prosecutor or local government head. == Policy Issues == * 87.1% of children born within 300 days of divorce were proven not to be the biological child of the former husband. * Undocumented foreign children risk deportation if their parents report to immigration authorities. == Reform / Amendments == # Amendment of Civil Act Article 844 (restricting the presumption of paternity to births occurring ''during'' marriage). # Granting the right to deny paternity (친생부인권) to adult children and biological fathers (생부). # Enactment of a Foreign Child Birth Registration Act (외국인 아동의 출생등록에 관한 법률) with exemption from immigration reporting obligations (통보의무 면제). == Relationship to Other Entities == * '''Issuing Institution''': Judicial Policy Research Institute & Supreme Court of Korea. * '''Lead Researchers''': An Won-ju, Kim Seong-hwa, Yang Seung-wook, Lee Dan-bi. * '''Related Agencies''': Ministry of Justice (법무부) & Ministry of Health and Welfare (보건복지부). == See Also == * [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] * [[Supreme Court of Korea]] * [[Birth Notification System in South Korea]] * [[UN Convention on the Rights of the Child]] == References == == 7. Policy Analysis == ; Background : Enacted on March 23, 2021, Article 20 of South Korea's Administrative Basic Act established explicit statutory authority for administrative agencies to issue dispositions using fully automated systems, provided the disposition does not involve administrative discretion. This landmark statutory shift catalyzed the deployment of AI in public administration across South Korea. ; Policy Problem : '''The Black Box & Explainability Deficit''': Deep learning and complex machine learning algorithms operate with opaque inner layers ("black box" problem), making it difficult or impossible for affected citizens — and reviewing courts — to trace how specific administrative outputs were derived. : '''Algorithmic Bias & Data Contamination''': AI models trained on historical data risk inheriting or amplifying societal biases (e.g., racial bias in US COMPAS recidivism scores, gender bias in Amazon's recruitment AI, or Google Photos' labeling errors). : '''Constitutional & Statutory Friction''': Fully automated AI decisions challenge traditional principles of due process (right to be heard / hearing rights under Administrative Procedure Act Arts. 21–22), non-delegation ("cyber-delegation" and "data-delegation"), clarity (명확성의 원칙), democratic legitimacy, and individual state compensation liability under State Compensation Act Arts. 2 and 5. ; Legal/Policy Gap : Traditional judicial review theory in civil law jurisdictions divides administrative actions strictly into bound actions (기속행위) and discretionary actions (재량행위). When administrative agencies deploy AI, reviewing courts lack clear standards on whether to defer to algorithmic outputs, evaluate dataset quality, or conduct de novo review. ; Objectives : Reconcile administrative efficiency and speed with the rule of law (법치행정), procedural due process, algorithmic transparency, and effective judicial control over AI administrative dispositions. ; Implementation & Proposed Judicial Review Framework : The report formulates a 3-Tier Judicial Review Standard Framework (3단계 사법심사 모델): :# ''Tier 1 (Bound Dispositions / High Deference / 기속행위)'': Applied when an administrative agency operates within its area of statutory expertise, under clear statutory authority, and uses a transparent, publicly predictable algorithm (e.g., SAFE-i24 for imported food clearance). The court accords high deference to the AI disposition, focusing review on whether statutory requirements were breached and whether the output matched the published algorithm. :# ''Tier 2 (Discretionary Dispositions with Expert Agency / 재량행위)'': Applied when an agency operates in its expert field but under ambiguous statutory terms (involving administrative discretion or undefined legal concepts) OR where the algorithm structure is opaque. The court reviews the disposition under standard human official scrutiny — evaluating proportionality (비례원칙), equality (평등원칙), and prohibition of abuse of discretion. :# ''Tier 3 (Non-Expert Agency / Direct Review / 재량행위 / De Novo)'': Applied when the administrative agency lacks domain expertise in the subject matter or lacks technical competence over the deployed AI algorithm. The court accords zero deference and independently determines the legality and reasonableness of the disposition (De Novo review). : '''Technical Audit Criteria for Courts''': When conducting judicial review of AI actions, courts should audit four technical stages: (a) Dataset Verification (data quality, completeness, and bias), (b) Labeling Verification (accuracy in supervised learning), (c) Algorithm Verification (model structure and transparency), and (d) Explanation Quality Verification (reason-giving adequacy). ; Evidence & Empirical Case Studies : '''Domestic SAFE-i24 (전자심사 24)''': Deployed by MFDS on Sept 14, 2023 under Imported Food Safety Act Art. 20-2, automatically auditing ~260 parameters for repeat food imports, reducing processing time from 48 hours to under 5 minutes. : '''US Deference Jurisprudence''': Reviewed ''Skidmore'' (1944), ''Overton Park'' (1971), ''State Farm'' (1983), ''Chevron'' (1984), ''Mead'' (2001), ''Barnhart'' (2002), and ''Prometheus Radio'' (2021) to extract judicial review principles balancing administrative expertise against arbitrary and capricious actions. : '''US Criminal COMPAS & ''State v. Loomis'' (Wis. 2016)''': Analyzed due process challenges to proprietary risk assessment algorithms; Wisconsin Supreme Court upheld COMPAS sentencing use provided written warnings regarding algorithmic risks are attached for judges. == 5. MediaWiki Output == {{Infobox Judicial Policy|name=Judicial Review of AI-Based Administrative Decision Making|official_name=인공지능에 근거한 행정처분에 대한 사법심사이론 연구|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-202416|issuing_authority=Judicial Policy Research Institute (사법정책연구원)|authors=Seongwook Heo (허성욱)|publication_date=2024-12-11|report_series=연구총서 2024-16|isbn=979-11-6168-240-2|legal_basis=Administrative Basic Act Art. 20; Special Act on Safety Management of Imported Food Art. 20-2; Intelligent Informatization Framework Act Arts. 3, 5; Administrative Procedure Act Arts. 21–24}} '''Judicial Review of AI-Based Administrative Decision Making''' is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. == Summary == This document is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. It comparatively and theoretically analyzes judicial review of administrative dispositions generated by artificial intelligence (AI) under Article 20 of the Administrative Basic Act. It formulates a 3-tier judicial review standard framework. == Legal Basis == The legal frameworks analyzed include: * '''Administrative Basic Act (행정기본법)''': Article 20 (Fully Automated Administrative Actions). * '''Special Act on Safety Management of Imported Food (수입식품안전관리 특별법)''': Article 20-2 (Automated Reception of Import Declarations / 전자심사 24). * '''Intelligent Informatization Framework Act (지능정보화 기본법)''': Article 3 and Article 5. * '''Administrative Procedure Act (행정절차법)''': Articles 21, 22, 23, and 24. * '''State Compensation Act (국가배상법)''': Article 2 and Article 5. == Background == Article 20 of the Administrative Basic Act, effective March 23, 2021, provided the legal basis for government agencies to issue fully automated administrative decisions. Systems such as SAFE-i24 (전자심사 24) cut food import inspection time from 48 hours to 5 minutes. However, the use of AI raises serious challenges regarding transparency, accountability, and citizens' right to challenge decisions. == Objectives == # Address the "black box" (블랙박스) problem and the lack of algorithmic transparency in administrative decisions. # Establish a 3-tier judicial review framework to guide judges in examining the legality of AI-based administrative actions. == Scope == * '''Domestic Case Studies''': The Electronic Review 24 system (Korea's Ministry of Food and Drug Safety) and the Smart Seoul Welfare Service. * '''Foreign Comparative Study''': US administrative law doctrines (''Chevron'', ''Skidmore'', ''State Farm'', ''Overton Park'', ''Mead'', ''Prometheus Radio''), the COMPAS system (''State v. Loomis''), and AI surveillance/CCTV systems in China. == Key Provisions == The 3-Tier Judicial Review Standard Framework (3단계 사법심사 모델): * '''Tier 1 (기속행위 / High Deference)''': The agency has expertise, clear statutory authority, and a transparent/predictable algorithm. The court respects the decision and reviews only for legal violations and algorithm consistency. * '''Tier 2 (재량행위 / Standard Review)''': The agency has expertise but the statutory basis is ambiguous (discretionary), OR the algorithm is not transparent. The court reviews using standard human-official scrutiny (proportionality and equality principles). * '''Tier 3 (재량행위 / De Novo Review)''': The agency lacks domain expertise in AI or the subject matter. The court conducts an independent re-examination (''De Novo''). == Implementation == Courts perform a four-stage technical audit when examining AI decisions: (1) Dataset Verification (data quality & bias), (2) Labeling Verification, (3) Algorithm Verification, and (4) Explanation Quality Verification (explainability). == Policy Issues == * The deep learning "black box" problem, which complicates compliance with the reason-giving obligation under Article 23 of the Administrative Procedure Act. * The risk of historical data bias (such as racial bias in COMPAS or gender bias in recruitment AI). == Reform / Amendments == * Adoption of the 3-Tier Judicial Review Framework by the judiciary. * Amendment of the Administrative Procedure Act and alignment with Algorithmic Accountability rules. == Relationship to Other Entities == * '''Issuing Institution''': Judicial Policy Research Institute & Supreme Court of Korea. * '''Lead Researcher''': Seongwook Heo (허성욱). * '''Related Agencies''': Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (식품의약품안전처) & Seoul Metropolitan Government. == See Also == * [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] * [[Supreme Court of Korea]] * [[Administrative Basic Act]] * [[Electronic Review 24 System]] == References == == 7. Policy Analysis == ; Background : Discussing the "privatization of justice" (사법의 민간화) triggers natural hesitation or apprehension due to historical societal conflicts associated with state asset sales or state enterprise privatizations. However, as state responsibilities expand and judicial caseloads grow, courts face severe budget and manpower constraints, leading to chronic trial delays (재판지연). ; Policy Problem : '''Resource Scarcity & Trial Delays''': The judiciary's budget comprises only 0.33% of South Korea's total national budget in 2024 (down from 0.43% in 2016), while judge quotas (법관 정원) have remained frozen at 3,214 since 2019, forcing Korean judges to handle up to 5.17 times the annual caseload of German judges. : '''Conceptual Confusion''': Previous domestic discussions treated privatization fragmentationally or confused general public-sector enterprise privatization with judicial task delegation. : '''Sectoral Disparities''': Different legal areas (civil, criminal, family, juvenile/child protection) possess distinct constitutional attributes, making uniform privatization models infeasible. ; Legal/Policy Gap : '''Distinction from General Privatization''': Unlike state enterprise privatization focused on transferring ownership and profit-maximization, judicial privatization retains ultimate state guarantee responsibility (''Gewährleistungsverantwortung'') and aims to enhance the fundamental right to a fair trial under Article 27 of the Constitution. : '''Conceptual Typology''': Adopting and expanding Yale Law Professor Judith Resnik's model, the report establishes a 2-tier classification: :# ''External Privatization (외부적 민간화 / Outsourcing)'': Delegating court tasks/functions to non-judicial, private, or external entities through functional entrustment or delegation (e.g., court-annexed mediation, external appraisal, private correctional facilities). :# ''Internal Privatization (내부적 민간화 / Non-Publicity)'': Conducting court-administered procedures in non-public, closed settings to facilitate settlement or efficiency without delegating judicial power outside the court (e.g., court-administered in-house mediation, closed hearings). ; Objectives : The ultimate objective (궁극적 목적) of judicial privatization is "thickly protecting the public's right to a trial through good adjudication" (좋은 재판을 통한 국민의 재판받을 권리의 두터운 보호). The realistic prerequisite (현실적 지향) is creating conditions that allow courts to concentrate on their core judicial function. ; Sectoral Analysis & Recommendations : '''Civil Sector (민사분야)''': Relatively easy to privatize conceptually due to private autonomy (사적자치원칙). Recommends expanding court-annexed ADR, improving appraisal fee structures (감정료), and reforming Expert Commissioner systems (전문심리위원제도). : '''Criminal Sector (형사분야)''': Strictly limited due to the state monopoly on coercive force (국가의 물리적 강제력 독점). However, external participation exists in citizen jury trials (국민참여재판) and German-style criminal plea agreements (''Verständigung'' § 257c StPO). : '''Family, Juvenile & Child Protection Sector (가사, 소년·가정·아동보호분야)''': Possesses strong guardianship/supervisory attributes (후견적·복지적 성격). Offers vast potential for external functional delegation in post-trial counseling, probation, and care placements (e.g., Type 6 & 7 juvenile care facilities, domestic violence counseling), while preserving overall court oversight. ; Core Governance Principle — Dual Complementary Strategy (병행적·동시적 고려) : The report strongly cautions that judicial privatization is NOT a substitute (대체적 관계) for increasing judicial budgets and judge quotas. Rather, judicial privatization and statutory budget/personnel expansion must be pursued parallely and simultaneously (병행적·동시적 고려) as complementary measures. == 5. MediaWiki Output == {{Infobox Judicial Policy|name=A Study on the Private Participation in Justice|official_name=민간의 사법참여에 관한 연구|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-202417|issuing_authority=Judicial Policy Research Institute (사법정책연구원)|authors=You Young Gug (유영국)|publication_date=2024-12-26|report_series=연구총서 2024-17|isbn=979-11-6168-335-5|legal_basis=ROK Constitution Arts. 27, 101(1); Court Organization Act Art. 2(1); Civil Mediation Act; Family Litigation Act; Juvenile Act}} '''A Study on the Private Participation in Justice''' is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. == Summary == This document is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. It comparatively and theoretically analyzes the privatization of justice (사법의 민간화 / private participation in justice), distinguishing between internal privatization (내부적 민간화, based on non-publicity) and external privatization (외부적 민간화, based on outsourcing). It evaluates the civil, criminal, family, and juvenile/child protection sectors, and analyzes the US Rent-a-Judge system, Germany's ''Verständigung'', and France's judge-free divorce procedure. == Legal Basis == The legal frameworks analyzed include: * '''Constitution of the Republic of Korea''': Article 27 (Right to Trial) and Article 101(1) (Judicial Power). * '''Court Organization Act (법원조직법)''': Article 2(1). * '''Civil Procedure Act & Civil Mediation Act (민사소송법 / 민사조정법)''': Articles 1, 164-2~164-8 (Expert Commissioners), Articles 334~341 (Appraisal), and Articles 1~41 of the Civil Mediation Act. * '''Criminal Procedure Act & Act on Criminal Trials with Citizen Participation (형사소송법 / 국민참여재판법)''': Articles 1~3 of the Citizen Participation Act. * '''Family Litigation Act, Juvenile Act, and Domestic/Child Abuse Protection Acts (가사소송법 / 소년법 / 가정폭력처벌법 / 아동학대처벌법)'''. == Background == Growing judicial workloads combined with limited budgets and personnel (the Supreme Court's budget was only 0.33% of the national budget in 2024) have led to trial delays (재판지연). The report formulates judicial privatization as a governance strategy to allow courts to focus on their core functions. == Objectives == # Formulate the concept of judicial privatization (사법의 민간화), distinguishing internal privatization (non-public) from external privatization (functional delegation). # Establish the ultimate objective (궁극적 목적) as "thickly protecting the public's right to a trial through good adjudication" (좋은 재판을 통한 국민의 재판받을 권리의 두터운 보호). # Affirm the principle of parallel and simultaneous consideration (병행적·동시적 고려) — that judicial privatization is NOT a substitute for increasing the number of judges and the judicial budget. == Scope == * '''Domestic Sectoral Study''': The civil sector (ADR, appraisal, expert commissioners), the criminal sector (citizen participation trials), the family sector (mediation, parent education, guardianship), and the juvenile/child sector (Type 6/7 juvenile protection facilities). * '''Foreign Comparative Study''': ** '''United States''': The Rent-a-Judge system (JAMS / Cal. Civ. Proc. Code §§ 638–645.2). ** '''Germany''': The criminal plea agreement (''Verständigung'' § 257c StPO). ** '''France''': Consensual divorce without a judge (''divorce sans juge'' / ''acte déposé au rang des minutes d'un notaire''). == Key Provisions == * '''External Privatization''': Transferring or delegating court tasks to non-judicial institutions outside the court. * '''Internal Privatization''': Conducting proceedings within the court in a closed, non-public setting to expedite resolution without delegating authority externally. * '''State Responsibility Principle''': The state retains ultimate guarantee responsibility (''Gewährleistungsverantwortung'') for the quality and fairness of justice. == Implementation == Courts implement a staged division of tasks: expanding civil mediation and referring child/juvenile protection matters to verified entrusted institutions (수탁기관), while tightening court oversight and supervision. == Policy Issues == * A shrinking share of the judicial budget and a frozen judge quota (3,214 since 2019) that burdens Korean judges with 5.17 times the caseload of their German counterparts. * Risk of declining public trust if privatization proceeds without accountability safeguards. == Reform / Amendments == # Adoption of the Dual Strategy (병행적·동시적 고려): judicial privatization pursued alongside increases in judge quotas and budget. # Reform of the civil sector (adjustment of appraisal fees and expert commissioner incentives). # Strengthening of referral mechanisms in the family and child protection sectors (가사·소년보호 수탁기관). == Relationship to Other Entities == * '''Issuing Institution''': Judicial Policy Research Institute & Supreme Court of Korea. * '''Lead Researcher''': You Young Gug (유영국). * '''Related Ministries''': Ministry of Justice (법무부) & Ministry of Gender Equality and Family (여성가족부). == See Also == * [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] * [[Supreme Court of Korea]] * [[Judith Resnik Privatization Framework]] * [[Court-Annexed Alternative Dispute Resolution]] == References == == 7.
