Policy Analysis == ; Background : Land designated within urban improvement zones is both private property and part of the national spatial infrastructure. When land or buildings in redevelopment or reconstruction zones become subject to court auctions, three distinct legal frameworks collide: urban improvement procedures (정비사업), real estate auction under civil execution (경매), and real estate registration (등기). ; Policy Problem : '''Incomplete Public Disclosure''': The Urban Improvement Act regulates registration procedures after the public notice of transfer (이전고시), but leaves the lengthy multi-year period between building demolition and new building preservation registration without clear disclosure rules. : '''Doctrinal Collision (General Execution vs. Urban Re-Allotment)''': Under general civil law, building demolition results in absolute extinction of ownership (소유권의 절대적 소멸, Civil Act Art. 99). However, under urban re-allotment principles (환권법리), ownership and encumbrances do NOT extinguish upon physical demolition; they persist and transfer to the newly constructed property upon transfer notice (이전고시, Urban Improvement Act Art. 87). This creates severe confusion for execution courts on whether to cancel or suspend auctions on demolished structures. : '''Isolated Land Auctions & Rights Splitting''': When execution courts cancel auctions on demolished buildings and auction the underlying land alone, a buyer acquires only land ownership. This creates severe litigation over whether the buyer acquires association membership (조합원자격), occupancy rights (조합원입주권), or becomes a co-owner with the former building owner, severely depressing auction bid values and impairing mortgagees' recovery. : '''Over-Indebted Cash Settlement Subjects (과다채무자)''': When a property owner is classified as a cash settlement subject (현금청산대상자), but total mortgages and attachments exceed the cash settlement value, re-construction associations cannot clear encumbrances to obtain clean title required for HUG sales guarantees (분양보증). ; Legal/Policy Gap : '''Re-Allotment vs. Purchase-Distribution Models''': For association members, the re-allotment doctrine (환권법리) preserves identity between old and new properties. For non-members/cash settlement subjects, the purchase-distribution doctrine (보류지·체비지 법리) treats new units as freshly created assets (원시취득), extinguishing old encumbrances upon transfer notice. : '''Deficit in Procedural Harmonization''': Korea lacks statutory rules coordinating execution courts with urban improvement projects, whereas Japan's Urban Redevelopment Act (Art. 70) and Supreme Court Adjustment Rules (권리의 변환과 강제집행 등과의 조정에 관한 규칙) mandate procedure commencement registrations (권리변환절차개시등기) and permit court auction suspensions pending re-allotment. ; Objectives : Harmonize urban improvement, civil execution, and registration procedures; protect mortgagees and auction buyers; eliminate incomplete disclosure during building demolition; and provide associations with legal tools to clear over-indebted titles. ; Implementation & Proposed Statutory Reforms : '''Management and Disposal Procedure Commencement Registration (관리처분절차개시등기)''': Enact Article 78-2 in the Urban Improvement Act (도시정비법 제78조의2). Upon management and disposal plan approval (관리처분계획인가), associations must register commencement on property registers. This notifies the public that the property is subject to urban re-allotment, restricts individual piecemeal registrations, and empowers execution courts to suspend isolated auctions pending transfer notice. : '''Blanket Real Estate Clearance System (토지건물일괄말소)''': Amend Registration Rules on Urban Improvement to mandate that old building and land registrations be cancelled simultaneously with new building preservation registration upon transfer notice, preserving encumbrance continuity during construction. : '''Rights & Procedure Adjustment for Over-Indebted Properties''': Enact Article 91-2 (도시정비법 제91조의2). Grants associations a Priority Purchase Right (우선매수권) in court auctions at or above appraised value. For over-indebted cash settlement subjects, allows associations to deposit the appraised cash settlement amount (현금청산금) in court and demand cancellation of mortgages, while court distribution procedures (채권배당절차) distribute the deposited funds among mortgagees. : '''Expansion of Land, etc. Owners Definition''': Amend Article 2(9)(다) of the Urban Improvement Act (도시정비법 제2조 제9호 다목) to explicitly classify owners of underlying land after building demolition as "Land, etc. Owners" (토지등소유자), ensuring that occupancy rights (조합원입주권) naturally attach to the land lot during the demolition phase. ; Evidence & Empirical Data : '''Judicial Statistics & Appraiser Feedback''': Property appraiser surveys revealed that auctioning land alone while excluding demolished building values distorts market value, depresses bid prices, and creates post-auction ownership litigation between land buyers and original building owners. : '''Comparative Japanese Framework''': In Japan, pre-demolition registration of right-conversion commencement (권리변환절차개시등기 under Urban Redevelopment Act Art. 70) and Supreme Court execution rules prevent isolated land sales, requiring auctions to be suspended or transferred to re-allotted shares. == 5. MediaWiki Output == {{Infobox Judicial Policy|name=Understanding Redevelopment, Reconstruction, and Real Estate Auctions|official_name=재개발·재건축의 이해와 부동산 경매 - 도시정비법을 중심으로 -|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-202418|issuing_authority=Judicial Policy Research Institute (사법정책연구원)|authors=Lee Jong-gu (이종구)|publication_date=2024-12-27|report_series=연구총서 2024-18|isbn=979-11-6168-334-8|legal_basis=Urban Improvement Act; Civil Execution Act; Civil Act; Aggregate Buildings Act; Registration Rules on Urban Improvement}} '''Understanding Redevelopment, Reconstruction, and Real Estate Auctions''' is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. == Summary == This document is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. It comparatively and practically analyzes the conflict between civil execution auction procedures (민사집행절차) and urban redevelopment procedures (정비사업절차) under the Urban Improvement Act (도시정비법). It formulates the distinction between the re-allotment doctrine (환권법리) and the purchase-distribution doctrine (보류지·체비지 법리), and proposes enacting a Management and Disposal Procedure Commencement Registration (관리처분절차개시등기) and a Blanket Real Estate Clearance System (토지건물일괄말소). == Legal Basis == The legal frameworks analyzed include: * '''Act on the Improvement of Urban Areas and Residential Environments (도시 및 주거환경정비법 / 도시정비법)''': Articles 2, 35, 39, 63, 64, 73, 74, 78, 81, 86, 87, 88, 91, 129, and proposed Articles 78-2 & 91-2. * '''Civil Execution Act of the Republic of Korea (민사집행법)''': Articles 81, 91, 96, 97, 101, 121, 127, 140, 141, 144, 223–252, 268. * '''Civil Act of the Republic of Korea (민법)''': Article 99 (Concept of Immovable Property), Articles 186, 187, 342, 364, 370 (Real Subrogation of Mortgages). * '''Act on Ownership and Management of Aggregate Buildings (집합건물법)''': Article 20 (Principle Prohibiting Separate Disposal) and Article 47. * '''Registration Rules on Urban Improvement (도시 및 주거환경정비 등기규칙)''': Articles 5, 6, 7, 16. == Background == When property in a redevelopment (재개발) or reconstruction (재건축) area is auctioned by the courts, a clash of legal doctrines occurs. General civil law treats demolition of the old building as an absolute extinguishment of ownership (소유권). By contrast, urban improvement law (환권법리) provides that ownership and encumbrances on the old building do not extinguish but instead automatically transfer to the new building upon the official transfer notice (이전고시). Auctioning the land alone (토지만의 경매) by the courts often creates legal uncertainty, depressed auction prices, and ownership disputes. == Objectives == # Harmonize civil execution auction procedures with the urban improvement schedule to prevent isolated land auctions. # Address the incomplete public disclosure gap (불완전 공시) between demolition of the old building and registration of the new building. # Grant a priority purchase right (우선매수권) to reconstruction associations to take over over-indebted properties (과다채무자). == Scope == * '''Legal & Empirical Analysis''': Supreme Court precedent 95Da10570, a survey by the Korea Association of Property Appraisers (한국감정평가사협회), and execution data provided by Chief Judicial Officer Min Dong-geun. * '''Comparative Japanese Legal Study''': Article 70 of Japan's Urban Redevelopment Act (都市再開発法) on right-conversion procedure commencement registration (권리변환절차개시등기) and Japan's Supreme Court execution adjustment rules. == Key Provisions == * '''Re-Allotment Doctrine (환권법리)''': For association members, rights in the old building are transformed into occupancy rights (조합원입주권), so auctioning land alone without the building is not permitted. * '''Purchase-Distribution Doctrine (보류지·체비지 법리)''': For non-members / cash settlement subjects (현금청산), rights in the new unit are an original acquisition (원시취득), and old encumbrances extinguish upon transfer notice. * '''Procedure Commencement Registration (관리처분절차개시등기 — Proposed Article 78-2)''': Must be registered upon approval of the management and disposal plan (관리처분계획인가) to lock individual registrations and empower courts to suspend isolated auctions. == Implementation == Execution courts suspend isolated land auctions until transfer notice, while associations may use the priority purchase right (우선매수권) or deposit the cash settlement amount (청산금) with the court to clear mortgages exceeding property value. == Policy Issues == * Auctioning land alone (토지만 매각) results in very low bid values, as buyers bear the risk of ownership disputes (매수위험). * Failure to clear encumbrances on over-indebted properties prevents associations from obtaining HUG sales guarantees (주택도시보증공사 분양보증). == Reform / Amendments == # Enactment of Article 78-2 of the Urban Improvement Act (관리처분절차개시등기). # Enactment of Article 91-2 of the Urban Improvement Act (association priority purchase right & cash settlement deposit). # Amendment of Article 2(9)(다) of the Urban Improvement Act (expanding the definition of land owners). # Adoption of the Blanket Clearance System (토지건물일괄말소) for old buildings and land. == Relationship to Other Entities == * '''Issuing Institution''': Judicial Policy Research Institute & Supreme Court of Korea. * '''Lead Researcher''': Lee Jong-gu (이종구). * '''Related Agencies''': Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT), Korea Association of Property Appraisers, & HUG. == See Also == * [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] * [[Supreme Court of Korea]] * [[Act on the Improvement of Urban Areas and Residential Environments]] * [[Civil Execution Act of South Korea]] == References == == 7. Policy Analysis == ; Background : Literacy (문해력) — the ability to read, interpret, and use written language — is essential for exercising rights and participating in judicial proceedings. According to the Ministry of Education's 2020 Adult Literacy Survey (2020년 성인문해능력조사), 8.9 million Korean adults aged 18+ have low literacy skills (Level 1 to 3), including 2.00 million adults at Level 1 (elementary 1st–2nd grade level / 4.5%), 1.85 million at Level 2 (elementary 3rd–6th grade level / 4.2%), and 5.04 million at Level 3 (middle school level / 11.4%). For marginalized groups — such as persons with intellectual or developmental disabilities (281,045 people in Korea), Deaf persons using Korean Sign Language (447,948 hearing-impaired people), children/adolescents (ages 8–15), North Korean defectors, and elderly citizens — traditionally drafted court judgments filled with archaic Sino-Korean legalese (한자어), complex multi-clause sentences, and passive voice create an insurmountable barrier to information accessibility and self-determination (자기결정권). ; Policy Problem : '''Substantive Inequality & Information Exclusion''': When courts deliver judgments in traditional legalese to low-literacy litigants, those litigants cannot independently understand whether they won or lost, why the decision was made, or whether to appeal. Providing identical, unreadable text to low-literacy citizens constitutes indirect discrimination (간접차별) and refusal of reasonable accommodation (정당한 편의 제공 거부) under Article 4 of the Disability Anti-Discrimination Act. : '''First Easy-Read Precedent & Lack of Operational Standards''': On December 2, 2022, the Seoul Administrative Court (Presiding Judge Kang Woo-chan) delivered South Korea's first Easy-Read judgment (서울행정법원 2021구합89381), appending "안타깝지만 원고가 졌습니다" (unfortunately, the plaintiff lost) to Main Ruling Item 1 and inserting a summary box [쉬운 말로 요약한 판결문의 내용] with illustrations. Following UN CRPD Committee recommendations in September 2022 urging South Korea to develop Easy-Read formats across legal proceedings, the National Assembly introduced bill amendments. However, judges lacked concrete drafting standards, visual design templates, or legal guidelines, creating operational confusion and hesitation. ; Legal/Policy Gap : Traditional judicial reform efforts focused on "judgment simplification" (판결서 간이화 / 적정화) for general citizens through plain language. However, plain language (평이한 언어) relies solely on text for moderately literate readers, omitting visual aids and structural design. In contrast, Easy-Read (이지리드) combines simplified text with matched visual illustrations (보조적 이미지), specific typography (12–14+ pt Gothic font, 180–200%+ line spacing, left alignment), and structured page layouts designed specifically for cognitive accessibility. ; Evaluation of Alternative Easy-Read Formatting Options : '''Option 1 — Single Easy-Read Judgment Only (판결서 원본을 이지리드 방식으로만 작성)''': Rejected. Omits essential legal reasoning, eroding the judgment's self-containment (자족성), appellate review function (상급법원 심리기초), and legal certainty regarding res judicata (기판력) and enforcement (집행력). : '''Option 2 — Separate Easy-Read Document Post-Delivery (판결서 원본과 분리된 별도 이지리드 문서 제공)''': Rejected. Creates service timing confusion, risks missing strict appeal deadlines (상소기간), treats Easy-Read as an informal summary without legal standing, and reduces judicial oversight. : '''Option 3 — Dual-Format Embedded Model (판결서 원본 내 이지리드 부분 병기)''': Selected as the Preferred Model. Inserts an Easy-Read text box ([쉬운 말로 요약한 판결문의 내용] / 이해하기 쉬운 판결) at the beginning of the Reason section, preceding the standard full legal text. Ensures zero service delay, binds Easy-Read directly to the official court record, preserves complete legal reasoning for appellate courts, and builds a searchable case law database (코트넷) for future judges. ; Drafting Guidelines & Methodological Standards : '''Text Standards''': Write in polite conversational tone (구어체 존댓말); limit sentences to 1 main idea (1–3 lines max); replace legalese with everyday vocabulary (e.g., replace 임대인/임차인 with 집주인/세입자, 대여 with 빌려주다, 변제 with 갚다, 상해진단서 with 진단서); state the core ruling in active voice at the very top; express dates clearly (2024년 2월 22일 instead of 2024. 2. 22.) and round large numbers (1억 5천만 원 instead of 150,000,000원); include an explicit disclaimer stating that standard legal text prevails in case of interpretation conflict. : '''Visual Standards''': Place simple, clear illustrations or photos directly adjacent to corresponding text (left side preferred); maintain strict character visual consistency across scenes; utilize the 661 court-usable illustration assets developed under JPRI/Supreme Court research; restrict total Easy-Read box length to 5 pages (max 10 pages). ; Empirical Validation & Survey Results : '''Template Development''': Developed 14 model Easy-Read judgment templates: 7 Criminal (assault, theft, voice phishing fraud, sex crimes, child abuse), 3 Civil (building eviction, loan repayment, wage exploitation), 3 Family/Non-Contentious (divorce, child custody, parental rights termination), and 1 Administrative (disability rating rejection). : '''Empirical Comprehension Testing''': Tested 40 participants (15 persons with developmental disabilities, 14 Deaf persons, 11 elementary school students aged 8–11) using 13 paired question sets comparing standard vs Easy-Read text. : '''Key Statistical Findings''': Overall comprehension gain score (차이값) averaged +3.35 points. 80% of participants (32 out of 40) demonstrated measurable comprehension gains (Elementary students: +4.82, Deaf persons: +2.93, Persons with developmental disabilities: +2.67). 82.5% of participants (33 out of 40) explicitly rated the Easy-Read judgment format as easier to understand. == 5. MediaWiki Output == {{Infobox Judicial Policy|name=A Guide to Producing Easy-Read Judgments for Persons with Disabilities|official_name=장애인 등을 위한 이해하기 쉬운(Easy-Read) 판결서 작성방안|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-202419|issuing_authority=Judicial Policy Research Institute (사법정책연구원)|authors=Kweon Hyung-kwoan (권형관), Hong Bo-ram (홍보람), Yang Seung-wook (양승욱), Lee Dan-bi (이단비)|publication_date=2024-12-31|report_series=연구총서 2024-19|isbn=979-11-6168-346-1|legal_basis=ROK Constitution Arts. 10, 11(1), 27(1), 34(5); Disability Anti-Discrimination Act Arts. 4, 21, 26; Developmental Disabilities Act Art. 10(1); UN CRPD Arts. 2, 5, 9, 13, 21}} '''A Guide to Producing Easy-Read Judgments for Persons with Disabilities''' is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. == Summary == This document is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. It formulates practical guidelines, linguistic standards, visual layout rules, and draft Supreme Court regulations for judges to produce Easy-Read judgments (이지리드 판결서) for persons with intellectual/developmental disabilities, Deaf persons, children, and low-literacy citizens. It reviews comparative practice from 8 countries, develops 14 draft model judgments (7 criminal, 3 civil, 3 family, 1 administrative), and demonstrates their effectiveness through empirical testing on 40 participants. == Legal Basis == The legal frameworks analyzed include: * '''Constitution of the Republic of Korea''': Article 10 (Human Dignity & General Personality Rights), Article 11(1) (Equality Principle), Article 27(1) (Right to a Fair Trial), and Article 34(5) (State Protection for Persons with Disabilities). * '''Disability Anti-Discrimination Act (장애인차별금지법)''': Article 4(1) (Direct/Indirect Discrimination & Refusal of Reasonable Accommodation), Article 7 (Right to Self-Determination), Article 21(1) (Access to Information), and Article 26(1), (4), (5), (8) (Reasonable Accommodation in Judicial Proceedings). * '''Act on Guarantee of Rights of Persons with Developmental Disabilities (발달장애인법)''': Article 8(1) and Article 10(1) (Communication Support in Easy-to-Understand Formats). * '''Mental Health Welfare Act (정신건강복지법)''': Article 6(1). * '''International Conventions''': UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UN CRPD Articles 2, 5, 9, 13, 21 & Concluding Observations CRPD/C/KOR/CO/2-3, September 2022); UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC Articles 3, 12); UN International Principles and Guidelines on Access to Justice for Persons with Disabilities (2020). == Background == According to the 2020 Adult Literacy Survey (2020년 성인문해능력조사), 8.9 million South Korean adults have low literacy levels (Level 1–3). For 281,045 persons with developmental disabilities and 447,948 Deaf/hearing-impaired persons, the complex sentence structure and Sino-Korean legal terminology (법률용어) of court judgments has been a major barrier to the right to information access and self-determination (자기결정권). The first Easy-Read judgment, issued by the Seoul Administrative Court on December 2, 2022 (Case 2021Guhap89381), together with UN CRPD recommendations, spurred the need for official drafting guidelines for judges. == Objectives == # Remove communication barriers in the judicial process and ensure substantive equality for vulnerable groups. # Develop draft Supreme Court Regulations (대법원예규) and an Easy-Read judgment drafting guide. # Provide 14 draft Easy-Read judgment models and 661 visual illustration assets to ease judges' drafting workload. == Scope == * '''Comparative Study of 8 Countries & International Bodies''': United Kingdom (Supreme Court ''A Local Authority v JB'' & the "Dear Sam" decision), Germany (''Leichte Sprache'' & BGG § 11), France (FALC & Conseil d'Etat), Spain (Supreme Court Decision STS 339/2023), Colombia (Decision T-573/16), Australia (Style Manual), the United States (Plain Writing Act 2010), Canada, as well as IFLA, the UN, and the EU. * '''Empirical Testing''': A survey of 40 participants (15 persons with developmental disabilities, 14 Deaf persons, 11 elementary school students) using 13 paired comparison question sets (standard text vs. Easy-Read). == Key Provisions == * '''Option 3 Drafting Model (Dual-Format Embedded Model)''': The Easy-Read section is placed in a text box labeled "[쉬운 말로 요약한 판결문의 내용]" at the beginning of the Reason (이유) section within the same official judgment document. * '''Language Standards''': Uses polite conversational language (구어체 존댓말), short active sentences (1 sentence = 1 idea, max 1–3 lines), replaces legal terms with everyday language (e.g., 임대인/임차인 becomes 집주인/세입자, 변제 becomes 갚다), and includes a disclaimer that the standard legal text prevails in case of interpretive conflict. * '''Visual Standards''': Places relevant illustrations/photos to the left of the corresponding text, maintains visual character consistency, uses 12–14+ pt Gothic font with 180–200%+ line spacing, and limits the Easy-Read section to a maximum of 5–10 pages. == Implementation == Judges draft the Easy-Read section independently or with the assistance of an Expert Commissioner (전문심리위원). The Easy-Read judgment is printed double-sided and bound like a booklet for direct delivery to the parties at the time the judgment is read. == Policy Issues == * Judges' concerns about increased workload and the risk of legal inaccuracy. * A lack of verified illustration assets for specialized legal cases. == Reform / Amendments == # Enactment of the Supreme Court Regulation on the Production and Provision of Easy-Read Judgments for Persons with Disabilities (장애인 등을 위한 이해하기 쉬운 판결서 작성 및 제공에 관한 예규(안)). # Enactment of the Supreme Court Rule on Non-Discrimination and Access to Justice for Persons with Disabilities (장애인 차별금지 및 사법접근에 관한 규칙(안)). # Integration of an Easy-Read judgment training module into the Judicial Research and Training Institute (사법연수원) curriculum. # Appointment of Easy-Read Expert Commissioners and establishment of Disability Access to Justice Centers (장애인 사법접근센터). == Relationship to Other Entities == * '''Issuing Institution''': Judicial Policy Research Institute & Supreme Court of Korea. * '''Research Team''': Kweon Hyung-kwoan (권형관), Hong Bo-ram, Yang Seung-wook, Lee Dan-bi. * '''Judicial Figures''': Kang Woo-chan (Presiding Judge, Seoul Administrative Court), Cho Hee-dae (Chief Justice), Lord Stephens (UK Supreme Court). == See Also == * [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] * [[Supreme Court of Korea]] * [[Seoul Administrative Court 2021Guhap89381]] * [[UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities]] == References == == 7. Policy Analysis == ; Background : Service of process (송달) acts as the foundational wheel of judicial proceedings, guaranteeing litigants' constitutional right to a fair trial by informing them of pending actions and enabling defense rights. In criminal cases, service failure creates severe bottlenecks, forcing trial postponements, enabling in absentia trials (불출석 재판), triggering improper detention or bench warrants, and causing witness non-appearance. ; Policy Problem : '''High Service Failure Rates''': Out of 2,690,448 total service attempts in Korean criminal courts in 2023, 452,377 failed (16.8% overall failure rate; rising to 24.1% in summary/약식 cases and 38.3% for witness subpoenas). : '''Predominance of Closed-Door Absenteeism''': 71.1% of all service failures stem from 폐문부재 (door locked / occupant absent during daytime mail delivery), reflecting modern demographic shifts toward single-person households (34.5% in 2022) and daytime employment. : '''Over-Reliance on Traditional Mail''': Mail service accounts for 95.8% of all criminal service attempts, while court bailiff service (집행관 송달) accounts for 2.8%, dispatch service (발송송달) 1.0%, and court constable service (법원경위 송달) only 0.5%. : '''Rampant Illegal Public Notice Reversals''': Because public notice service (공시송달) requirements under Special Expedited Act Article 23 require exhaustive searches of all addresses and phone numbers in the record, lower courts frequently issue invalid public notice orders. An empirical review of 361 Supreme Court decisions identified 161 cases reversed specifically because lower courts failed to call phone numbers or check secondary addresses listed in prosecution records. : '''Administrative Overload''': 42.7% of court clerks (실무관) report spending over 50% of their total working hours on service tasks (printing documents, manual mail envelope stuffing, and address checking). ; Legal/Policy Gap : '''Criminal E-Document Act Constraints''': The Criminal E-Document Act (형사절차전자문서법, effective Oct 20, 2024) mandates user consent for e-service. However, consent obtained during police/prosecution investigation does NOT automatically transfer to court proceedings, forcing courts to revert to paper mail for initial indictment service (공소장부본). Furthermore, the statutory 14-day deemed service period (송달간주기간) is 2–3 times longer than paper mail delivery (3.5–5.7 days), risking strategic trial delays by evasive defendants. : '''Lack of Court Enforcement Power''': Courts face uncooperative police support when executing bench warrants (구인장) or location searches (소재탐지촉탁), resulting in months of idle case suspension. ; Objectives : Elevate service success rates, eliminate structural trial delays, transition to secure digital delivery while accommodating low-literacy groups, prevent invalid public notice reversals, and empower courts with independent enforcement tools. ; Implementation & Proposed Statutory Reforms : '''Mobile Electronic Notification (모바일 전자고지) & Mobile Location Change Reporting''': Implement Connecting Information (CI) code matching via mobile document brokers (Kakao/SMS) to notify defendants of pending service on smartphones before postal dispatch. Introduce a Mobile Location Change Reporting System (모바일 송달장소 신고제도) via court portals or HomeTax-style mobile forms. : '''Integrated Service (통합송달) Expansion''': Extend civil integrated service (통합송달 — combining 1 day, 1 night, and 1 holiday attempt within 20 days) to criminal cases and expand execution authority to court constables (법원경위). : '''Court Police System (법원경찰제도) Enactment''': Amend Article 55-2 of the Court Organization Act to establish an independent Court Police Force (법원경찰대) under judicial command to execute bench warrants, perform location searches (소재탐지), and deliver urgent subpoenas. : '''Pre-Public Notice Prosecution Location Data Submission''': Amend Article 43 of the Criminal Procedure Rules to require prosecutors to submit a final location data report (소재파악 필요자료) from unadmitted investigation files immediately before a judge issues a public notice order. : '''Reformed Service Report Formats''': Modify official service report templates (송달사유통지서/송달사유보고서) to include explicit mandatory checkboxes verifying supplementary service validity (보충송달 적법성 — verifying co-residence and contactability). ; Evidence & Empirical Data : '''Judicial Survey of Judges & Clerks''': Nationwide survey of 325 judges and 218 court clerks found: :* 88.3% of judges supported shortening the 6-month statutory waiting period for public notice service under Special Expedited Act Art. 23 (37.3% favoring 2–3 months, 36.9% favoring 3–4 months). :* 88.3% of judges supported requiring prosecutors to submit location records prior to public notice orders. :* 81.8% of judges supported establishing a Court Police Force (법원경찰제도) for bench warrant execution and location searches. :* 94.5% of clerks reported that service manufacturing (E-Post/mail stuffing) is their most labor-intensive task. == 5. MediaWiki Output == {{Infobox Judicial Policy|name=A Study on Improving Service of Process in Criminal Cases|official_name=형사소송에서의 송달제도 개선에 관한 연구|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-202420|issuing_authority=Judicial Policy Research Institute (사법정책연구원)|authors=Jeon Mun-sik (전문식), Kim Seong-hwa (김성화), Yang Seung-wook (양승욱), Seo Yong-seong (서용성)|publication_date=2024-12-31|report_series=연구총서 2024-20|isbn=979-11-6168-342-3|legal_basis=ROK Criminal Procedure Code; Civil Procedure Act; Special Expedited Act; Criminal E-Document Act (2024); Court Organization Act}} '''A Study on Improving Service of Process in Criminal Cases''' is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. == Summary == This document is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. It empirically and comparatively analyzes criminal service of process (형사송달), diagnoses the main causes of service failure (송달불능) that drive trial delays (재판지연), and formulates reforms covering criminal e-litigation (형사전자소송), mobile electronic notification (모바일 전자고지), integrated service (통합송달), establishment of a Court Police Force (법원경찰제도), and improved service report forms (송달보고서). == Legal Basis == The legal frameworks analyzed include: * '''Criminal Procedure Code of the Republic of Korea (형사소송법)''': Articles 25, 27, 54, 60, 61, 62, 63 (Public Notice Requirements), 64, 65, 76, 81 (Warrant Execution), 151, 152, 266, 344, 345–348, 365, 448, 452, 458. * '''Civil Procedure Act of the Republic of Korea (민사소송법 — applied mutatis mutandis)''': Articles 98, 99, 101, 102, 105, 106 (Supplementary Service), 107, 108, 109, 173, 175, 178, 181, 182, 183, 186, 187, 190, 191, 193, 195. * '''Act on Special Cases Concerning Expedition of Legal Proceedings (소송촉진 등에 관한 특례법 / 소촉법)''': Article 21, Article 23 & Special Rules Articles 18, 19. * '''Act on the Use of Electronic Documents in Criminal Justice Procedures (형사절차전자문서법 — effective October 20, 2024)''': Articles 2, 6(3), 13, 14, 15 & Supreme Court Rule (형사전자문서규칙) Articles 4, 16, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27. * '''Court Organization Act (법원조직법)''': Proposed Article 55-2 (Court Police) and Article 64(3) (Court Constables / 법원경위). == Background == In 2023, out of 2,690,448 total service attempts in Korean criminal courts, 452,377 failed (an overall failure rate of 16.8%; 24.1% in summary cases; and 38.3% for witness subpoenas). 71.1% of failures were caused by 폐문부재 (locked doors / occupant absent during the day). Heavy reliance on physical mail (95.8%) and a high rate of Supreme Court reversals due to illegal public notice service (위법한 공시송달 — 161 cases reversed) drove the need for systemic reform. == Objectives == # Increase the success rate of criminal service of process and eliminate unnecessary trial delays. # Build mobile notification infrastructure (Mobile CI Notification) and a self-service mobile location-change reporting system (모바일 송달장소 신고제도). # Establish a Court Police Force (법원경찰제도) under judicial authority to execute bench warrants (구인장) and conduct location searches (소재탐지). == Scope == * '''Empirical Study''': Statistical analysis for 2018–2023, review of 161 Supreme Court reversal cases, and a nationwide survey of 325 judges and 218 court clerks. * '''Five-Country Comparative Study''': United States (FRCP Rule 4/49 & Process Server System), Germany (StPO § 37, ZPO § 173 & ''Mein Justizpostfach''), Austria (''Ediktsdatei'' & ''JustizOnline''), Switzerland (''justitia.swiss'' / Justitia 4.0), and Japan (Criminal Procedure Rules & 2023 IT Digitization). == Key Provisions == * '''Strengthened Mobile Notification''': Integrates SMS/Kakao-CI systems with the court portal and enables emergency address-change registration via mobile phone. * '''Adoption of Integrated Service (통합송달)''': Extends integrated service (combining daytime, nighttime, and holiday delivery attempts) to criminal cases and grants execution authority to court constables (법원경위). * '''Strict Pre-Public Notice Review''': Requires prosecutors to submit defendant location records (수사기록 소재자료) immediately before a judge issues a public notice order (공시송달). * '''New Report Forms''': Revises service report forms (송달보고서) to require verification of the validity of supplementary service (보충송달 — confirming co-residence and contactability with family members or coworkers). == Implementation == Courts adopt an automated checklist within the judicial computer system to prevent invalid public notice orders (공시송달), and establish a Court Police unit (법원경찰대) to independently carry out field enforcement. == Policy Issues == * The 14-day deemed service period (송달간주) under the Criminal E-Document Act is far longer than paper mail delivery (3.5–5.7 days), risking exploitation by defendants seeking to delay proceedings. * Difficulty transferring e-service consent from the police/prosecution investigation stage to the court trial stage. == Reform / Amendments == # Enactment of Article 55-2 of the Court Organization Act (법원경찰제도). # Amendment of Article 43 of the Criminal Procedure Rules (requiring prosecutors to submit location records before public notice). # Amendment of Article 117 of the Criminal Procedure Rules (requiring defendants' mobile numbers and email addresses to be included in indictments). # Adoption of an e-Post system and integration of Integrated Service (통합송달). == Relationship to Other Entities == * '''Issuing Institution''': Judicial Policy Research Institute & Supreme Court of Korea. * '''Research Team''': Jeon Mun-sik (전문식), Kim Seong-hwa, Yang Seung-wook, Seo Yong-seong. * '''Related Agencies''': Supreme Prosecutors' Office, National Police Agency, & Korea Post (우정사업본부). == See Also == * [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] * [[Supreme Court of Korea]] * [[Public Notice Service in Criminal Cases]] * [[Court Police System]] == References == == 7. Policy Analysis == ; Background : The defendant's presence in criminal trials is both a constitutional fundamental right (guaranteeing defense rights and the right to be heard) and a statutory obligation. Under Korean law, trials in absentia (피고인 불출석 재판) are restricted as narrow exceptions under the Criminal Procedure Act (CPC) and Article 23 of the Act on Special Cases Concerning Expedition, etc. of Legal Proceedings (Special Expedited Act). Following the Constitutional Court's 1998 unconstitutionality decision (97Hun-Ba22), Article 23 was revised in 1999 to exclude crimes punishable by death, life imprisonment, or minimum 10+ years imprisonment. ; Policy Problem : '''Rigid Uniformity & Lack of Defendant-Fault Differentiation''': The current system applies a uniform, strict 6-month wait and complex procedural hurdles (address correction, location search 소재탐지촉탁, detention warrant issuance) regardless of whether the defendant is genuinely unaware of the trial or intentionally evading court appearance / fleeing. : '''Severe Trial Delays & Systemic Abuse''': Defendants intentionally fail to appear at trial or sentencing dates to delay judgment, avoid arrest, or push their crimes past statutory probation expiration periods (집행유예 기간 도과). In 1st instance court-notice (고단) cases, trial in absentia averages 380 days (over double standard cases). : '''Ineffective Appearance Enforcement''': Police execution rates for bench/detention warrants (구인영장/구금영장) for missing defendants are under 20%. : '''Routine Reversals & Recovery of Appeal Rights''': Because courts often miss minor service steps during public notice (공시송달), upper courts routinely grant recovery of appeal rights (상소권회복), forcing appellate courts to retry cases from scratch without ever having seen the defendant in person. ; Legal/Policy Gap : Korea's positive law treats a defendant who never received an indictment bill identically to a defendant who appeared at trial, received full rights warnings, and then intentionally fled before sentencing. ; Objectives : Eliminate defendant incentives to flee; protect victim rights and public judicial power; establish a 4-tier model reflecting defendant fault; and streamline criminal proceedings while safeguarding due process. ; 4-Tier Categorization Model & Proposed Statutory Reforms : '''Type 1 (Indictment Unserved / 공소장 부본 미송달)''': :* Status: Defendant never received the indictment bill and is unaware of prosecution. :* Reform: Shift responsibility to the prosecution. Amend CPC Articles 266 & 328 to stipulate that if the indictment bill remains unserved 2 months after an address correction order is issued to the prosecutor, the prosecution automatically loses its effect, and the court shall issue a Dismissal of Prosecution Decision (공소기각결정) (modeled after Japanese CPC Art. 271). : '''Type 2 (Indictment Served but Never Appeared / 공소장 부본 송달 후 미출석)''': :* Status: Indictment bill served, but defendant never attended any trial date. :* Reform: Maintain Special Expedited Act Article 23(1) 6-month wait and public notice safeguards to protect defense rights. : '''Type 3 (Appeared 1+ Times then Fled/Disappeared / 1회 이상 출석 후 불출석)''': :* Status: Defendant appeared for arraignment/rights warnings, then intentionally fled. :* Reform: Enact Special Expedited Act Article 23(2). Eliminate the 6-month wait; allow trial in absentia after 2 non-consecutive absences following formal rights warnings. Service for subsequent dates shall be executed by mail dispatch (우체에 부치는 방법). : '''Type 4 (Fled at Sentencing Date / 변론종결 후 선고기일 불출석)''': :* Status: Defendant attended full trial until pleadings closed, then fled before sentencing. :* Reform: Enact Special Expedited Act Article 23(3). Allow immediate sentencing in absentia on the 1st unexcused absence date without wait or crime category limits. ; Additional Statutory Reforms : '''CPC Articles 365 & 458 (Summary/Formal Trial & Appeals)''': Amend to allow trial in absentia upon 2 non-consecutive absences (removing the "2 consecutive absences" restriction). : '''CPC Article 277-2 (Arrested Defendants)''': Remove the requirement that "production by prison officers is impossible or extremely difficult," allowing trial in absentia when an arrested defendant refuses appearance without good cause. : '''CPC Article 455 (Formal Trial Request Rejection)''': Allow courts to issue a Decision Rejecting Formal Trial Request (정식재판청구 기각결정) when a defendant fails to appear twice. : '''Protection of Communications Secrets Act Article 15-2''': Mandate telecommunications carrier compliance with court requests for location and communications data to locate missing defendants. ; Evidence & Empirical Data : '''Judicial Survey of 378 Korean Judges''': :* 76% of judges stated the current Special Expedited Act Art. 23 system is improper and causes severe trial delays. :* 93.7% of judges supported establishing a new trial in absentia system for defendants who flee after attending initial trial dates. :* 93% of judges supported relaxing CPC Art. 365 to allow trials in absentia upon 2 non-consecutive absences. :* 91% of judges supported introducing formal trial request rejection decisions for 2-time non-appearances. == 5. MediaWiki Output == {{Infobox Judicial Policy|name=Research on Improvement Measures for Trial in Absentia in Korea|official_name=피고인 불출석 재판 개선방안에 관한 연구|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-202501|issuing_authority=Judicial Policy Research Institute (사법정책연구원)|authors=Ko Dae-seok (고대석), Kim Seong-hwa (김성화), Yang Seung-wook (양승욱)|publication_date=2025-03-25|report_series=연구총서 2025-01|isbn=979-11-6168-349-2|legal_basis=ROK Constitution Arts. 12(1), 27(1); Act on Special Cases Concerning Expedition, etc. of Legal Proceedings Art. 23; ROK Criminal Procedure Act; Protection of Communications Secrets Act Art. 15-2}} '''Research on Improvement Measures for Trial in Absentia in Korea''' is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. == Summary == This document is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. It comparatively and empirically analyzes criminal trial in absentia (피고인 불출석 재판 / 궐석재판), diagnoses structural defects in Article 23 of the Act on Special Cases Concerning Expedition, etc. of Legal Proceedings, and formulates a 4-tier categorization model along with draft amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act and the Special Expedited Act. == Legal Basis == The legal frameworks analyzed include: * '''Constitution of the Republic of Korea''': Article 12(1) (Due Process Principle) and Article 27(1) (Right to a Fair Trial). * '''Act on Special Cases Concerning Expedition, etc. of Legal Proceedings (소송촉진 등에 관한 특례법 / 소촉법)''': Article 23 (Special Rules for First-Instance Trial in Absentia) and Article 23-2 (Retrial / 재심). * '''Criminal Procedure Act of the Republic of Korea (형사소송법)''': Articles 26, 27, 28, 63, 65, 72, 73, 81, 249(2), 266, 276, 277, 277-2, 278, 306, 328, 365, 453, 455, 458, 473. * '''Protection of Communications Secrets Act (통신비밀보호법)''': Proposed Article 15-2 (Telecommunications Carrier Cooperation Obligation). * '''Constitutional Court Decisions''': Decision 97Hun-Ba22 (July 16, 1998 — Unconstitutional) and 2005Hun-Ba21 (July 21, 2005 — Constitutional). == Background == A defendant's presence at a criminal trial is both a constitutional right and obligation. However, the rigid, uniform 6-month deadline in Article 23 of the Special Expedited Act, applied without regard to defendant intent, has been exploited by fleeing defendants to delay proceedings until their probation period (집행유예) expires. This has caused trial delays (averaging 380 days in 고단 cases), wasted judicial resources, and neglect of crime victims' rights. == Objectives == # Eliminate incentives for defendants to flee from trial. # Categorize defendant non-appearance into a 4-Tier Model based on the degree of defendant fault and procedural stage. # Enact draft amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act and the Special Expedited Act to accelerate execution of trial in absentia. == Scope == * '''Empirical Study''': A survey of 378 South Korean judges (76% stated the current system is improper; 93.7% supported in absentia reform for fleeing defendants). * '''Four-Country Comparative Study''': United States (''Parker Warnings'' & FRCP Rule 43), Germany (StPO §§ 230, 231, 231a, 231b, 232, 233, 329), Japan (Japanese CPC Article 271 on the 2-month expiration of prosecutorial authority), and France (CPP Arts. 270, 320, 379-2). == Key Provisions == The 4-Tier Reform Model: * '''Type 1 (공소장 부본 미송달)''': The indictment was never delivered. Proposed amendment to CPC Articles 266 & 328: the court issues a Dismissal of Prosecution Decision (공소기각결정) if the indictment fails to be delivered within 2 months after an address correction order. * '''Type 2 (공소장 부본 송달 후 미출석)''': The indictment was delivered but the defendant never appeared. The 6-month deadline under Special Act Article 23(1) continues to apply. * '''Type 3 (1회 이상 출석 후 불출석)''': The defendant appeared at an initial hearing and received rights warnings, then fled. Proposed Special Act Article 23(2): trial in absentia may proceed after 2 non-consecutive absences without waiting 6 months. * '''Type 4 (변론종결 후 선고기일 불출석)''': The defendant attended until the close of pleadings, then fled on the sentencing date. Proposed Special Act Article 23(3): sentencing may proceed in absentia immediately upon the first unexcused absence. == Implementation == Courts adopt a rights-warning form (Parker Warnings) at the first hearing and use mail dispatch service (우체에 부치는 방법) for notifying defendants of subsequent absences. == Policy Issues == * Police execution rates for detention warrants (구금영장) are below 20%. * A high rate of Supreme Court reversals of in absentia judgments due to minor defects in the public notice (공시송달) procedure. == Reform / Amendments == # Enactment of Special Expedited Act Article 23(2) & (3) (In Absentia Trial for Types 3 & 4). # Amendment of Criminal Procedure Act Articles 266 & 328 (Dismissal of Prosecution Decision for Type 1). # Amendment of Criminal Procedure Act Articles 365 & 458 (relaxing the requirement to 2 non-consecutive absences). # Amendment of Criminal Procedure Act Article 277-2 (relaxing in absentia trial requirements for detained defendants). # Amendment of Criminal Procedure Act Article 455 (Decision Rejecting a Formal Trial Request). == Relationship to Other Entities == * '''Issuing Institution''': Judicial Policy Research Institute & Supreme Court of Korea. * '''Research Team''': Ko Dae-seok (고대석), Kim Seong-hwa (김성화), Yang Seung-wook (양승욱). * '''Related Agencies''': Ministry of Justice (법무부) & Supreme Prosecutors' Office of Korea. == See Also == * [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] * [[Supreme Court of Korea]] * [[Trial in Absentia in South Korea]] * [[Parker Warnings]] == References == == 7. Policy Analysis == ; Background : Advanced technology forms the backbone of South Korea's national competitiveness. As global technology competition intensifies, technology theft targeting Korean semiconductor, display, battery, and automotive innovations has risen sharply — prosecutions increased from 40 cases in 2018 to 73 in 2020 and 53 in 2022. On November 8, 2023, the government launched the inter-agency "Joint Technology Divulgence Response Team" (범정부 기술 유출 합동대응단). However, criminal courts face severe procedural bottlenecks and technical complexities when trying technology theft cases. ; Policy Problem : '''Severe Trial Delays & Chronic Backlog''': 1st instance trial duration for Industrial Technology Protection Act cases averages 23.6 months (unbound) and 21.8 months (bound), compared to 6.2 months for general criminal cases. Over 40.62% of industrial tech cases take over 2 years in 1st instance (vs 3.82% overall criminal average). Average court trial dates reach 12.3 sessions per case. : '''High Acquittal Rates (29.8%)''': The 1st instance acquittal rate for Industrial Technology Protection Act cases reached 29.8% between 2018 and 2022 — nearly 10 times the overall criminal acquittal rate of 3.1%. This stems from judges' difficulty in comprehending complex technical evidence without dedicated technical support. : '''Inadequate Detention Limits''': Under CPC Article 92, the 6-month 1st instance detention limit is far too short for complex tech theft trials involving multiple co-defendants, massive digital forensic discovery, and uncooperative overseas discovery. Defendants frequently obtain bail upon 6-month expiration, creating risks of secondary technology leakage. : '''Secondary Leakage Risks during Trial''': Defendants and defense counsel demand full unredacted discovery (열람·등사) of technical files, risking secondary exposure of non-leaked master R&D databases or national core tech parameters. : '''Leniency Criticism & Disconnect in Sentencing''': Sentencing guidelines historically failed to reflect the strategic economic loss of stolen technologies, leading to public criticism of "slapped wrist" (솜방망이 처벌) suspended sentences. ; Legal/Policy Gap : '''Overlapping Legislation ("Roof-on-Roof" Overlap)''': Protection of technology is fragmented across the Unfair Competition Prevention Act (MOTIE/KIPO), Industrial Technology Protection Act (MOTIE), Defense Technology Protection Act (DAPA/DND), and National High-Tech Strategic Industries Act. This causes prosecutorial confusion and potential double jeopardy or inconsistent statutory application. : '''Snooze-and-Lose Secret Management Requirement''': While 2015 and 2019 Civil Act/Unfair Competition Act amendments relaxed secret management (비밀관리성) from "substantial effort" (상당한 노력) to "reasonable effort" (합리적인 노력) and "managed as secret" (비밀로 관리된), lower courts still apply overly rigid physical access control standards to small-and-medium enterprises (SMEs). ; Objectives : Elevate judicial technical expertise; streamline pre-trial discovery; establish criminal jurisdiction concentration; prevent secondary trial leakage; empower victims in court; extend detention limits; and align sentencing with economic loss. ; Implementation & Proposed Reforms : '''Criminal Jurisdiction Concentration (형사소송 관할집중)''': Enact proposed Article 4-2 of the Criminal Procedure Code. Grant concurrent 1st instance jurisdiction over trade secret/industrial tech crimes to Seoul Central District Court, Suwon District Court, and Daejeon District Court, and exclusive 2nd instance appellate jurisdiction to the Patent Court (특허법원) in Daejeon. : '''Re-Assignment to Three-Judge Panel (재정합의)''': Re-assign single-judge technology theft cases to three-judge panels (합의부) via formal re-assignment decisions to ensure panel-level focus and speed. : '''Expansion of Technical Experts''': Expand Technical Investigators (기술조사관) from Seoul Central District Court to Suwon and Daejeon; actively appoint Expert Commissioners (전문심리위원 under CPC Art. 279-2) to assist judges during hearings. : '''Issue-by-Issue Evidence Examination & Self-Authenticating Official Documents''': Implement mandatory pre-trial preparation hearings (공판준비절차 under CPC Art. 266-5); examine evidence grouped strictly by technical issue rather than document-by-document; treat official National Core Technology Determination Applications as self-authenticating business records under CPC Article 315(3). : '''Criminal Secrecy Orders & Non-Public Trials''': Amend Unfair Competition Act (proposed Arts. 14-4 & 18-4) and Industrial Tech Act to extend civil Secrecy Orders (비밀유지명령) to criminal trial participants (defendants, attorneys, experts) with 5-year imprisonment penalties for breach; enact proposed Art. 14-8 allowing judges to close courtroom hearings (심리의 비공개) during technical evidence presentations. : '''Victim Procedural Participation (피해자참가제도)''': Introduce victim participation rules in the Unfair Competition and Industrial Tech Acts (modeled after German ''Nebenklage'' & Japanese CPC Art. 316-33), permitting corporate victim attorneys to attend pre-trial/trial dates, inspect court files, ask questions via judges, and make closing statements. : '''Extension of Detention Period Limits (구속기간 완화)''': Amend CPC Article 92 to extend 1st and 2nd instance detention period limits from 6 months up to 1 year (in 3-month renewal increments) for complex technology theft cases. : '''Loss-Based Sentencing Reform''': Evaluate the 2024 Revised Sentencing Guidelines (effective July 1, 2024, raising national core tech export sentences up to 12 years); recommend long-term structural adoption of USSG § 2B1.1 loss/intended loss valuation tiers (피해액/손실액 기준 유형 분류) supported by accredited technical valuation institutes. == 5. MediaWiki Output == {{Infobox Judicial Policy|name=A Study on Judicial Procedures and Sentencing in Technology Theft Crimes|official_name=기술 유출 범죄의 심리방식과 양형에 관한 연구|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-202502|issuing_authority=Judicial Policy Research Institute (사법정책연구원)|authors=Kim Chong Kun (김종근), Seo Yong-seong (서용성), Kim Seong-hwa (김성화), Jung Gwan-seon (정관선), Yang Seung-wook (양승욱)|publication_date=2025-03-25|report_series=연구총서 2025-02|isbn=979-11-6168-353-9|legal_basis=Unfair Competition Prevention Act; Industrial Technology Protection Act; National High-Tech Strategic Industries Act; Defense Technology Protection Act; Criminal Act Art. 356; Criminal Procedure Code}} '''A Study on Judicial Procedures and Sentencing in Technology Theft Crimes''' is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. == Summary == This document is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. It empirically and comparatively analyzes trial procedures and sentencing guidelines (양형) in technology theft crime (기술 유출 범죄) cases. It evaluates trade secrets (영업비밀), industrial technology (산업기술), and national core technology (국가핵심기술); diagnoses the causes of trial delays (재판지연) and a high acquittal rate (29.8%); analyzes US, Japanese, German, and French law; and formulates reforms covering jurisdiction concentration (관할집중), criminal secrecy orders (비밀유지명령), victim participation (피해자참가제도), extension of detention periods (구속기간 완화), and loss-based sentencing guideline realignment. == Legal Basis == The legal frameworks analyzed include: * '''Unfair Competition Prevention and Trade Secret Protection Act (부정경쟁방지법)''': Article 2(2), Article 18(1)–(2), Article 18-2, Article 18-3. * '''Act on Prevention of Divulgence and Protection of Industrial Technology (산업기술보호법)''': Article 2(1), Article 9 (National Core Technology), Article 14, Article 36(1)–(8), Article 36-2, Article 37, Article 38. * '''Act on Special Measures for National High-Tech Strategic Industries (국가첨단전략산업법)''': Article 2, Article 15, Article 50(1)–(4). * '''Defense Technology Protection Act (방산기술보호법)''': Article 2, Article 10, Article 21. * '''Criminal Act of the Republic of Korea (형법)''': Article 355(2) & Article 356 (업무상배임 / Business Breach of Trust). * '''Criminal Procedure Code of the Republic of Korea (형사소송법)''': Articles 4, 30, 40, 254(4), 266-5, 279-2, 294-2, 294-4, 315(3), and proposed Article 4-2. * '''Court Organization Act (법원조직법)''': Article 32(1) and Article 54-2. == Background == Advanced technology is a core pillar of South Korea's national competitiveness. Cases of technology leakage abroad have continued to rise (from 40 cases in 2018 to 73 in 2020). First-instance examination of industrial technology cases takes an average of 23.6 months, with an acquittal rate (무죄율) reaching 29.8% (compared to 3.1% for general criminal cases). The limited detention period (6 months) and the risk of secondary leakage during the evidence discovery process have driven the need for comprehensive judicial reform. == Objectives == # Improve judges' technical understanding through the assignment of Technical Investigators (기술조사관) and Expert Commissioners (전문심리위원). # Establish jurisdiction concentration (관할집중) for technology crime cases at the Seoul Central, Suwon, and Daejeon District Courts, and the Patent Court (특허법원). # Prevent secondary leakage of trade secrets through Secrecy Orders (비밀유지명령) and closed hearings (심리의 비공개). # Guarantee victim participation rights (피해자참가제도) and extend the defendant detention period limit (구속기간 완화). # Align sentencing guidelines (양형기준) with the scale of economic loss (intended loss). == Scope == * '''Legal & Empirical Analysis''': Supreme Court precedent 2024Do4098 (the KAIST Professor case), case statistics from 2018–2023, and interviews with judges, prosecutors, and legal directors of major corporations (Samsung, LG, KT). * '''Four-Country Comparative Study''': ** '''United States''': the EEA (18 U.S.C. § 1831/1832), the DTSA, USSG § 2B1.1, and case studies including ''U.S. v. You'', ''U.S. v. Hao Zhang'', ''U.S. v. Hongjin Tan'', and ''U.S. v. Yanjun Xu''. ** '''Japan''': Special Criminal Procedure Rules for Trade Secrets (Articles 23–31 of the Unfair Competition Prevention Act) and case studies involving Nissan, Toshiba/SK Hynix, and Yamazaki Mazak. ** '''Germany''': the 2019 GeschGehG (§ 23) and the ''Nebenklage'' (auxiliary prosecution/공소참가) system. ** '''France''': the EU Trade Secret Directive (2016/943) and the application of ''vol'' (theft) and ''abus de confiance'' (breach of trust). == Key Provisions == * '''Jurisdiction Concentration (Proposed CPC Article 4-2)''': Grants concurrent first-instance jurisdiction to the Seoul Central, Suwon, and Daejeon District Courts, and exclusive appellate jurisdiction to the Patent Court (특허법원). * '''Criminal Secrecy Orders (Proposed Articles 14-4 & 18-4)''': Extends secrecy orders (비밀유지명령) to criminal cases, with penalties of up to 5 years imprisonment for violators. * '''Victim Participation (피해자참가제도)''': Allows victim companies' attorneys to attend hearings, examine case files, and deliver closing statements. * '''Automatic Evidentiary Admissibility (CPC Article 315(3))''': Recognizes National Core Technology determination applications as official business records with automatic evidentiary validity. == Implementation == Courts transfer technology cases from single judges (단독) to three-judge panels (합의부) through a re-assignment decision (재정합의), and conduct evidence examination in stages organized by technical issue (쟁점별 증거조사). == Policy Issues == * Overlapping regulation ("roof-on-roof," 옥상옥) among the Trade Secret Act, Industrial Technology Act, Defense Technology Act, and Strategic Industries Act. * Difficulty in determining economic loss value (기술가치평가) for sentencing purposes. == Reform / Amendments == # Enactment of Criminal Jurisdiction Concentration (형사소송 관할집중). # Enactment of Secrecy Orders and Closed Hearings (비밀유지명령 및 심리의 비공개). # Enactment of the Victim Participation System (피해자참가제도). # Amendment of Article 92 of the Criminal Procedure Code extending the defendant detention period up to 1 year. # Reform of sentencing guidelines based on economic loss value (modeled on USSG § 2B1.1). == Relationship to Other Entities == * '''Issuing Institution''': Judicial Policy Research Institute & Supreme Court of Korea. * '''Lead Researchers''': Kim Chong Kun (김종근), Seo Yong-seong, Kim Seong-hwa, Jung Gwan-seon, Yang Seung-wook. * '''Related Agencies''': MOTIE (산업통상자원부), KIPO (특허청), the Supreme Prosecutors' Office, & the National Police Agency. == See Also == * [[Judicial Policy Research Institute]] * [[Supreme Court of Korea]] * [[Trade Secret Protection in South Korea]] * [[Patent Court of Korea]] == References == == 7. Policy Analysis == ; Background : Criminal cases involving persons with mental disabilities (encompassing intellectual disabilities, autism spectrum disorders, and mental illnesses such as schizophrenia and bipolar disorder) present acute procedural challenges. In South Korea, crimes committed by persons with mental disabilities accounted for 1.1% of total crimes in 2023 (13,915 individuals out of 1,250,885). However, individuals with mental disabilities face double vulnerability: high public fear/stigma following unprovoked acts of violence, combined with systemic procedural exclusion due to an inability to comprehend rights warnings, interrogation questions, or court proceedings. ; Policy Problem : '''Procedural Invisible Barriers & Ineffective Defense Rights''': Unlike physical disabilities, mental disabilities are often hidden or unobserved by police, prosecutors, and judges. Investigative agencies frequently process cases formally relying on family members without understanding the suspect's cognitive limits, leading to coerced or unreliable statements. : '''High Detention Rates''': Arrest/detention rates for suspects with mental disabilities (4.5% in 2023) are nearly double the rate for general suspects (2.3%) due to lack of stable community support or family supervision during investigation. : '''Defunct Trial Suspension Rules (CPC Art. 306)''': Article 306(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code mandates trial suspension when a defendant lacks litigation capacity (사물의 변별 또는 의사의 결정을 할 능력이 없는 상태). However, because Korean law lacks statutory mechanisms for competency restoration treatment (unlike US ''Dusky''/''Sell'' procedures), Article 306 is virtually dead-letter in judicial practice; judges rarely suspend trials to avoid indefinite case stalling. : '''Monopolistic Custody Petitions''': Under the Act on Medical Treatment and Custody, the authority to petition for medical treatment and custody (치료감호) rests exclusively with prosecutors (Art. 4(1)). When courts determine that an acquitted or mentally incapacitated defendant urgently requires institutional medical custody, they cannot issue custody orders if the prosecutor failed to petition. : '''Statement Intermediary Restriction''': The current Statement Intermediary (진술조력인) system under the Sexual Violence Punishment Act and Disability Welfare Act (Art. 59-16) is legally restricted to crime victims. Suspects and defendants with communication difficulties receive no official statement intermediary support. ; Legal/Policy Gap : Korean criminal procedure lacks a unified, cross-stage framework designed specifically to identify mental disabilities at arrest, convey disability data to courts at indictment, provide neutral communication intermediaries during hearings, and deliver state-funded medical treatment orders. ; Objectives : Ensure substantive constitutional equality and procedural due process under UN CRPD Articles 12 and 13; establish early disability identification protocols; expand statement intermediaries to suspects and defendants; revitalize litigation capacity assessments; and reform medical custody and treatment orders. ; Implementation & Proposed Statutory Reforms : '''Harmonized Terminology (Criminal Act Art. 10 Amendment)''': Amend Criminal Act Article 10 to replace the outdated term "심신장애인" with "정신적 장애인," aligning criminal law with the Disability Welfare Act and Developmental Disabilities Act. : '''Simplified Pre-Indictment Psychiatric Evaluation (기소전 간이감정)''': Utilize Professional Investigative Advisers (전문수사자문위원 under CPC Art. 245-2) or Sexual Violence Act expert opinion queries to conduct brief 2-hour pre-indictment evaluations (modeled after Japanese prosecution practice) to verify communication barriers and necessity for procedural support. : '''Mandatory Interrogation Recording & Indictment Attachment''': Mandate audio-visual recording (영상녹화) and stenographic transcripts (속기록) for interrogating suspects with mental disabilities. Require prosecutors to attach a "Suspect Disability Verification Report" (피의자 장애확인 보고서) to the indictment, informing courts of the defendant's disability from the very first hearing without violating the single-document indictment rule (공소장일본주의). : '''Universal Statement Intermediary System (확대된 진술조력인 제도)''': Amend the Criminal Procedure Code to enact proposed Article 244-6 (Intermediary in Investigation) and Article 276-3 (Intermediary in Trial), extending statement intermediaries to all suspects, defendants, and witnesses with communication difficulties. Promulgate matching Supreme Court Rules (진술조력인의 재판절차 참여에 관한 규칙(안)). : '''Clarification of Procedural Support Roles''': Establish clear operational boundaries between Assistants (보조인 — family/guardians exercising legal rights), Persons with Reliable Relationship (신뢰관계인 — emotional support), Communication Assistants (의사소통 보조인력 — ad-hoc sign/device support), and Statement Intermediaries (진술조력인 — certified neutral communication translators). : '''Specialized Disability Trial Divisions (장애인 전문재판부)''': Institutionalize and expand specialized criminal trial divisions for defendants with disabilities (pioneered at Seoul Central District Court in Feb 2024), applying a case weighting factor (가중치) of 1.5 to 2.0x to reflect extended hearing times. : '''Medical Treatment and Custody Act Amendments''': :* Amend Article 4(7) to mandate that prosecutors must comply with a court's request to file a medical treatment and custody petition (법원의 치료감호 청구 요구에 응하여야 한다). :* Amend Article 2-3 to allow Medical Treatment Orders (치료명령) for defendants acquitted due to mental incapacity (심신상실 무죄) or sentenced to fines (벌금형). :* Transition medical treatment order costs to full state funding. ; Evidence & Empirical Data : '''National Disability Crime Statistics (2023)''': Total registered persons with disabilities in Korea stood at 2,641,896 (including 104,197 with mental illness, 239,833 with intellectual disability, and 42,744 with autism). : '''Prosecutorial Disposition Data (2023)''': Out of 13,445 suspect dispositions involving mental disabilities, 54.8% were indicted (4.1% bound trial, 18.0% unbound trial, 32.7% summary order), 36.7% unindicted (32.6% prosecution suspension / 기소유예), and 2.2% transferred to juvenile/family protection. : '''2023 Full Audit of Custody & Treatment Rulings''': Analysis of 168 first-instance Medical Treatment and Custody cases in 2023 showed 133 granted (79.2%) and 35 rejected (20.8%). Out of 35 rejections, 19 defendants were instead sentenced to probation with Medical Treatment Orders (치료명령), demonstrating courts' active preference for community-based medical orders over full institutional custody when appropriate. == 5. MediaWiki Output == {{Infobox Judicial Policy|name=Study on Improvement in Criminal Procedure for Persons with Mental Disabilities|official_name=정신적 장애인에 대한 형사소송절차의 개선방안 연구|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-202503|issuing_authority=Judicial Policy Research Institute (사법정책연구원)|authors=Hyelim Lee (이혜림), Kim Seong-hwa (김성화), Yang Seung-wook (양승욱), Jung Gwan-seon (정관선)|publication_date=2025-04-23|report_series=연구총서 2025-03|isbn=979-11-6168-364-5|legal_basis=ROK Constitution Arts. 11(1), 12, 27(1); Criminal Act Art. 10; Criminal Procedure Code Arts. 29, 33, 244-5, 245-2, 276-2, 306; Disability Welfare Act Art. 2; Developmental Disabilities Act Arts. 8, 12, 13; Disability Anti-Discrimination Act Arts. 4, 26; Medical Treatment and Custody Act; UN CRPD Arts. 5, 12, 13, 14, 21}} '''Study on Improvement in Criminal Procedure for Persons with Mental Disabilities''' is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. == Summary == This document is an official judicial policy research report published by the Judicial Policy Research Institute (JPRI) of South Korea's Supreme Court. It comprehensively, empirically, and comparatively analyzes every stage of criminal procedure (형사소송절차) for suspects and defendants (피의자·피고인) with mental disabilities (정신적 장애, including intellectual disability, autism, and mental illness). It diagnoses communication barriers, high detention rates, and the non-functioning of litigation capacity assessments (소송능력); analyzes the law of 5 countries (US, UK, Germany, France, Japan) and UN CRPD standards; and formulates reforms including simplified pre-indictment psychiatric evaluation (기소전 간이감정), mandatory audio-visual recording (영상녹화), a Suspect Disability Verification Report (피의자 장애확인 보고서) attached to indictments, expansion of statement intermediaries (진술조력인), specialized disability trial divisions (장애인 전문재판부), and amendments to the Medical Treatment and Custody Act (치료감호법). == Legal Basis == The legal frameworks analyzed include: * '''Constitution of the Republic of Korea''': Article 11(1) (Equality Principle), Article 12 (Bodily Freedom & Due Process), and Article 27(1) (Right to a Fair Trial). * '''Criminal Act of the Republic of Korea (형법)''': Article 10 (심신장애 / Mental and Physical Disorder — proposed amendment of the term to 정신적 장애인). * '''Criminal Procedure Code of the Republic of Korea (형사소송법)''': Article 29 (보조인 / Assistant), Article 33 (국선변호인 / Public Defender), Article 244-5 (Special Interrogation Protection), Article 245-2 (Professional Investigative Adviser), Article 276-2 (Special Trial Examination Protection), Article 279-2 (Expert Examiner), Article 306 (공판절차 정지 / Trial Suspension), and proposed Articles 244-6 & 276-3. * '''Act on Welfare of Persons with Disabilities (장애인복지법)''': Article 2, Article 32 (Disability Registration), and Article 59-16. * '''Act on Guarantee of Rights of Persons with Developmental Disabilities (발달장애인법)''': Article 2, Article 8, Article 12 (Procedural Safeguards), and Article 13 (Dedicated Investigators). * '''Disability Anti-Discrimination Act (장애인차별금지법)''': Article 4 and Article 26 (Reasonable Accommodation in Judicial Proceedings). * '''Act on Medical Treatment and Custody (치료감호 등에 관한 법률 / 치료감호법)''': Article 2, Article 2-3, Article 4, Article 7, Article 12, Article 44-3, Article 44-4, Article 44-9. * '''International Conventions and Standards''': UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD Articles 5, 12, 13, 14, 21; General Comments No. 1 & No. 6; Concluding Observations for Korea 2014 & 2022); the UN International Principles and Guidelines on Access to Justice for Persons with Disabilities (2020). == Background == 2023 statistics recorded 13,915 crimes committed by persons with mental disabilities (1.1% of all crime in South Korea). Although this proportion is small, persons with mental disabilities face a detention rate twice as high (4.5% vs. 2.3%), communication isolation during interrogation, and the absence of legal statement intermediaries. Meanwhile, Article 306 of the Criminal Procedure Code, concerning trial suspension (공판절차 정지) due to lack of litigation capacity, has become dead-letter law due to the absence of a capacity restoration program, while judges cannot order medical treatment and custody (치료감호) without a monopolized petition from the prosecutor. == Objectives == # Guarantee due process (적법절차) and substantive equality for suspects/defendants with mental disabilities in accordance with UN CRPD Articles 12 & 13. # Enact a simplified pre-indictment evaluation system (기소전 간이감정) and attach a Suspect Disability Verification Report to indictments. # Expand the Statement Intermediary (진술조력인) system to suspects, defendants, and witnesses under an amended Criminal Procedure Code. # Amend the Medical Treatment and Custody Act to require prosecutors to comply with court requests for treatment orders. == Scope == * '''Empirical & Statistical Study''': Registration data on 2.64 million persons with disabilities, analysis of 13,445 prosecutorial dispositions in 2023, and a full audit of 168 Medical Treatment and Custody rulings in 2023 (133 granted, 35 rejected). * '''Five-Country Comparative Study''': ** '''United States''': Competency to Stand Trial (CTS / ''Dusky'' & ''Sell'' Criteria), the Insanity Defense, and Mental Health Courts. ** '''United Kingdom''': Appropriate Adult (AA / PACE Code C) and Registered Intermediary (''WIS''). ** '''Germany''': ''Verhandlungsfähigkeit'' (StPO) and ''Therapieweisung'' (StGB § 68b). ** '''France''': Exemption from criminal responsibility (Code pénal Art. 122-1) and the judicial representative (''MJPM''). ** '''Japan''': Audio-visual interrogation recording and the 2-hour pre-indictment psychiatric evaluation (기소전 간이감정). == Key Provisions == * '''Simplified Pre-Indictment Evaluation (기소전 간이감정)''': Uses Professional Investigative Advisers (전문수사자문위원, CPC Article 245-2) to evaluate a suspect's communication barriers before indictment. * '''Disability Verification Report (피의자 장애확인 보고서)''': Attached to the indictment (공소장) to inform the trial panel of the defendant's disability from the first day of trial. * '''Statement Intermediary Rules (Proposed CPC Articles 244-6 & 276-3)''': Establishes the right to use a statement intermediary (진술조력인) for suspects and defendants with communication difficulties. * '''Separation of Support Team Roles''': Clarifies the distinction between Assistants (보조인 / legal assistants), Persons with Reliable Relationship (신뢰관계인 / emotional companions), Communication Assistants (의사소통 보조인력 / ad-hoc communication aides), and Statement Intermediaries (진술조력인 / defined neutral communication interpreters). == Implementation == Courts route disability cases to the Specialized Disability Trial Division (장애인 전문재판부), hold pre-trial preparation hearings (공판준비절차) to determine communication needs, and assign dedicated sentencing investigation officers (양형조사관). == Policy Issues == * Absence of a litigation capacity restoration program under Article 306 of the Criminal Procedure Code. * The prosecutor's monopoly on the authority to petition for medical treatment and custody (치료감호), which limits judicial Policy Analysis == ; Background : In a modern welfare state, social security is a core state function, and effective legal remedies for social benefit entitlements must be guaranteed through the judicial system. In South Korea, social security caseloads in courts are exceptionally low compared to advanced welfare states. Annual social security cases filed in German 1st instance Social Courts (Sozialgericht) reached 236,429 cases in 2023 (representing 9.75% of all court cases nationwide), while UK First-tier Tribunals receive ~200,000 cases and French judicial social divisions receive 100,000–200,000 cases annually. By contrast, Korean 1st instance administrative courts handled roughly 20,000 social security cases over an entire decade (2011–2020). In 2023, out of 21,953 total 1st instance administrative cases in South Korea, occupational/industrial accident cases made up only 10.1% (2,226 cases) and national merit cases made up 2.0% (429 cases). ; Policy Problem : '''Severe Barriers to Access to Justice (사법접근권의 제약)''': Plaintiffs in social security litigation are overwhelmingly socially and economically vulnerable individuals (low-income, elderly, disabled, ill, or unemployed). However, complex legal structures, heavy litigation costs (court stamps, service fees, medical appraisal costs), strict procedural formalities, and lack of specialized legal aid cause vulnerable citizens to abandon court remedies or fail to enter the judicial sphere altogether. : '''Structural Asymmetry & Power Imbalance (비대칭적 당사자 관계)''': Social security administrative agencies possess vast institutional resources, specialized expertise, and legal representation. Unrepresented, low-literacy plaintiffs face severe structural inequality in adversarial litigation. : '''Inadequate Remedies under Current Administrative Litigation Act''': :* ''No Action for Mandatory Enforcement (의무이행소송의 부재)'': Korean courts only recognize revocation actions (거부처분 취소소송) and actions for confirmation of illegal omission (부작위위법확인소송). When a plaintiff wins a revocation judgment, the agency can simply issue a new rejection under a slightly modified rationale, forcing the impoverished plaintiff to file endless iterative lawsuits. :* ''Rigid Application of Adversarial Principle (변론주의의 엄격적 적용)'': Supreme Court precedent treats ex officio investigation (Art. 26) as merely supplementary to the adversarial principle. Impoverished plaintiffs who fail to plead specific legal requirements or afford expert medical appraisals routinely lose due to burden of proof. :* ''No Preliminary Injunctions & High Suspensive Effect Bar (가처분 배제 및 집행정지 요건)'': Korean administrative courts reject civil preliminary injunctions (가처분) and require "irreparable harm" (회복하기 어려운 손해) for suspensive effect. Stoppage or clawback of basic livelihood benefits or medical care during multi-year trials threatens the plaintiff's immediate right to survival. ; Legal/Policy Gap : Korea applies general administrative litigation rules indiscriminately to social security disputes, ignoring the inherent public-law, ongoing, and subsistence-oriented nature of social benefit entitlements. ; Objectives : Implement structural procedural reforms to guarantee substantive constitutional equality, lower entry barriers for vulnerable citizens, enforce "equality of arms" (무기대등의 원칙), and deliver complete, gapless legal remedies (공백 없는 권리구제). ; Implementation & Proposed Statutory Reforms : '''Enactment of Mandatory Enforcement Lawsuit (의무이행소송 도입)''': Amend Administrative Litigation Act Articles 4, 38-2 ~ 38-8 to introduce mandatory enforcement lawsuits, empowering courts to directly order administrative agencies to issue specific benefit grants or re-decide applications in compliance with binding judicial findings. : '''Enhancing Access to Justice (원고 사법접근권 강화)''': :* Amend venue rules to permit filing in the court covering the plaintiff's residence, domicile, or place of employment. :* Expand Justice Access Centers (사법접근센터) with specialized personnel to assist unrepresented plaintiffs in drafting oral/written complaints. :* Introduce a Public Defender System for Social Security Litigation (사회보장소송 국선변호사제도) under Administrative Judiciary Rules. :* Make Legal Aid (소송구조) mandatory for recipients of Basic Livelihood, Single-Parent, Basic Pension, and Disability Pension benefits by amending Civil Procedure Act Art. 128 and Court Regulations. : '''Institutionalizing Ex Officio Investigation (직권심리주의 원칙화)''': Amend Administrative Litigation Act Article 26 to establish ex officio investigation as the primary fact-finding principle in social security cases, placing responsibility on judges to investigate technical/medical facts and gather evidence independently. : '''Quasi-Lay Judge System & Expert Participation (준참심제 및 전문가 참여)''': Introduce a Quasi-Lay Judge System (준참심제) under Court Organization Act amendments where 2 expert lay judges (from welfare, labor, medical, and legal associations) participate in hearings and deliberations with advisory impact. As an immediate administrative measure, designate "Social Security Technical Examiners" (사회보장 전문심리위원) and "Social Security Court Investigators" (사회보장사건조사관). : '''Interim Relief & Preliminary Injunctions (가처분 및 집행정지 완화)''': :* Amend Administrative Litigation Act Article 23(2) to relax the suspensive effect threshold from "irreparable harm" to "serious harm" (중대한 손해). :* Enact proposed Article 24-2 to establish Preliminary Injunctions (가처분) to grant temporary provisional benefits during pending trials. : '''Specialized Social Security Divisions & Specialized Court (사회보장 전문재판부 및 사회보장법원)''': Immediately expand specialized social security divisions (사회보장 전문재판부) in district/administrative courts nationwide (pioneered by Seoul Administrative Court in Feb 2025 with 4 collegiate and 11 single-judge panels), paving the way for a standalone Social Security Court (사회보장법원) or integrated Labor and Social Security Court (노동사회법원). ; Evidence & Empirical Data : '''German Social Court Statistics (2023)''': Total cases filed in 1st instance Social Courts (Sozialgericht) reached 236,429. Social security cases accounted for 9.75% of ALL court cases in Germany in 2023 (236,429 out of 2,305,454 total cases across civil, criminal, family, admin, tax, labor, and social courts). : '''German Social Court Judicial Survey''': Survey of German Social Court judges revealed that 75.7% identified social security plaintiffs as having below-average income levels, 60.6% viewed plaintiffs as socially disadvantaged, and ~50% evaluated plaintiffs as lacking education/ability to confront administrative agencies without court assistance. : '''Korean Administrative Court Statistics''': 1st instance administrative social security cases totaled ~20,000 across a 10-year period (2011–2020), averaging ~2,000 cases per year — roughly 1/10th of Germany's caseload relative to population. : '''Korean Welfare Beneficiary Population (Nov 2024)''': Basic Livelihood recipients: 2,666,032; Disability Pension recipients: 351,386; Basic Senior Pension recipients: 6,684,357; Near-poverty / single-parent recipients: 1,006,834. : '''OECD Social Expenditure Data (2022/2023)''': Korea's public social expenditure was 12.3% of GDP in 2023 (Costa Rica level), ranking near the bottom of the OECD (vs OECD average ~21%, France 30.7%, Finland 29.4%, Denmark 28.4%, Germany 25.6%). == 5.
