2025 [[نشرة صندوق النقد]]. == الملخص == تقيم هذه الدراسة جاهزية قطر للذكاء الاصطناعي (*AI readiness*)، وتعرض سوق العمل والتكامل مع تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي، والآثار الاقتصادية الكلية على نمو إنتاجية العمل الوطنية [[ملخص التقرير]]. وتظهر النتائج أن تبني الذكاء الاصطناعي في قطر يتيح فرصاً كبيرة لزيادة الإنتاجية تتجاوز مخاطر الإحلال الوظيفي، مدعوماً بالتوسع في الوظائف عالية المهارات بالقطاع الخاص [[فرص الذكاء الاصطناعي]]. == الأساس القانوني وإطار السياسات == * '''رؤية قطر الوطنية 2030''': إطار استراتيجي وطني طويل الأجل يجعل التحول الرقمي ركيزة أساسية للنمو [[رؤية قطر 2030]]. * '''استراتيجية التنمية الوطنية الثالثة (NDS3)''': الاستراتيجية الوطنية الثالثة التي تستهدف التنويع الاقتصادي عبر قطاعات التمكين مثل تكنولوجيا المعلومات، الخدمات المالية، والتعليم [[استراتيجية قطر NDS3]]. * '''الأجندة الرقمية الوطنية 2030 واستراتيجية الذكاء الاصطناعي 2019''': أطر سياسات قطاعية لتعزيز البنية التحتية الرقمية، المواهب، والحوكمة الوطنية للذكاء الاصطناعي [[الأجندة الرقمية 2030]]. == الخلفية == استعدت دولة قطر بشكل استباقي للذكاء الاصطناعي بإطلاق استراتيجيتها الوطنية للذكاء الاصطناعي عام 2019 وتشكيل لجنة الذكاء الاصطناعي عام 2021 [[خلفية الاستراتيجية]]. وزادت الاستثمارات العامة والخاصة بشكل ملحوظ، بما في ذلك حزمة تحفيز استثماري بقيمة 2.5 مليار دولار في مايو 2024 وتمويل بقيمة 2 مليار ريال قطري من شركة أوريدو لمراكز بيانات الذكاء الاصطناعي [[استثمارات الذكاء الاصطناعي]]. == الأهداف == # تقييم جاهزية قطر للذكاء الاصطناعي مقارنة بالأسواق الناشئة والاقتصادات المتقدمة [[تحليل الجاهزية]]. # قياس درجة تعرض (*exposure*) وتكامل (*complementarity*) سوق العمل القطري مع أتمتة الذكاء الاصطناعي [[تعرض سوق العمل]]. # تقدير المكاسب المحتملة لإنتاجية العمل من خلال سيناريوهات النمذجة الاقتصادية الكلية [[توقعات الإنتاجية]]. == النطاق == * تحليل مقارن باستخدام مؤشر جاهزية الحكومة للذكاء الاصطناعي الصادر عن Oxford Insights [[مؤشر الجاهزية]]. * تقييم مفصل للعمالة القطرية مقارنة بالعمالة غير القطرية بناءً على بيانات جهاز التخطيط والإحصاء [[العمالة القطرية وغير القطرية]]. * تحليل الأثر القطاعي على مجموعات التمكين (*تكنولوجيا المعلومات، الخدمات المالية، التعليم*) ومجموعات النمو (*الصناعة التحويلية، السياحة*) [[الأثر القطاعي]]. == الأحكام والنتائج الرئيسية == * '''مستوى التعرض للذكاء الاصطناعي''': 37% من إجمالي القوى العاملة في قطر كانت معرضة للذكاء الاصطناعي في عام 2023، مع وقوع أكثر من 75% من الوظائف المعرضة في فئة التكامل العالي (مثل المهندسين، المدراء، والكوادر الطبية) [[مستوى التعرض]]. * '''هشاشة العمالة الوطنية''': 93% من الموظفين القطريين يعملون في وظائف معرضة للذكاء الاصطناعي، و35% منهم (خاصة الكوادر الكتابية بالقطاع الحكومي) معرضون لخطر استبدال المهام [[هشاشة الوظائف الكتابية]]. * '''دفعة إنتاجية العمل''': من المتوقع أن يثمر النجاح في دمج الذكاء الاصطناعي في ظل سيناريو متفائل عن زيادة نمو إنتاجية العمل بمقدار +1.0 نقطة مئوية سنوياً فوق خط الأساس [[مكاسب الإنتاجية]]. == التنفيذ == * '''البرنامج الوطني لتنمية المهارات''': تدريب 50,000 فرد على المهارات الرقمية المتقدمة بالتعاون مع مايكروسوفت حتى عام 2025 [[تدريب مايكروسوفت]]. * '''الدمج في الخدمات الحكومية''': تطبيق نماذج OpenAI GPT على بوابة "حكومي" واستخدام الذكاء الاصطناعي في نظام معلومات سوق العمل (LMIS) [[دمج حكومي]]. == المشكلات السياساتية == * '''مخاطر الإحلال بالقطاع الحكومي''': تركز العمالة الوطنية في الوظائف الكتابية بالجهات الحكومية يعرض هذه الفئة لضغوط هيكلية عند تسريع الأتمتة [[مخاطر القطاع الحكومي]]. * '''فجوات حوكمة البيانات''': لا تزال أطر توافر البيانات وحوكمتها وأخلاقيات الذكاء الاصطناعي في قطر دون مستويات الاقتصادات المتقدمة [[فجوات البيانات]]. == الإصلاحات == * تنفيذ برامج إعادة تأهيل المهارات للموظفين الكتابيين بالقطاع الحكومي، تسهيل انتقال العمالة للقطاع الخاص، تحسين شبكات الأمان الاجتماعي، وإصدار تأشيرات سريعة لمواهب الذكاء الاصطناعي العالمية. == العلاقات مع الكيانات الأخرى == * [[صندوق النقد الدولي]]: المؤسسة الناشرة والمعدة للتقرير [[صندوق النقد]]. * title: JPW-REPORT-OTP3YR
wikitext:
'''Report on the activities performed during the first three years (June 2003 to June 2006) of the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICC''' is an official report issued by the Office of the Prosecutor (OTP) of the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague on 12 September 2006. It documents the OTP's mandate, situation analysis, investigations, prosecutions, policy strategy, organisational structure and external cooperation during its first three years of operation.<ref name="otp">Office of the Prosecutor, "Report on the activities performed during the first three years (June 2003 – June 2006)", International Criminal Court, The Hague, 12 September 2006.</ref>

'''Verslag over de activiteiten in de eerste drie jaar (juni 2003 tot juni 2006) van het Bureau van de Aanklager van het ICC''' is een officieel verslag van het Bureau van de Aanklager (OTP) van het Internationaal Strafhof (ICC), uitgebracht in Den Haag op 12 september 2006. Het documenteert het mandaat, de situatieanalyse, onderzoeken, vervolgingen, beleidsstrategie, organisatiestructuur en externe samenwerking van het OTP in zijn eerste drie operationele jaren.<ref name="otp" />

== Also known as / Ook bekend als ==

* OTP Three Year Report (2003–2006)
* OTP 3-Year Activity Report
* Laporan Tiga Tahun Kantor Jaksa Penuntut CPI

== Summary / Samenvatting ==
'''EN:''' The report covers the first three years of the OTP under Chief Prosecutor Luis Moreno-Ocampo. It records the opening of investigations in the DRC, Northern Uganda and Darfur, the arrest of Thomas Lubanga Dyilo, the arrest warrants for LRA leaders, and the development of the electronic Legal Tools, including the Case Matrix application.<ref name="otp" />

'''NL:''' Het verslag beslaat de eerste drie jaar van het OTP onder Aanklager Luis Moreno-Ocampo. Het vermeldt de opening van onderzoeken in de DRC, Noord-Oeganda en Darfoer, de arrestatie van Thomas Lubanga Dyilo, de arrestatiebevelen tegen LRA-leiders en de ontwikkeling van de elektronische Legal Tools, waaronder de Case Matrix-toepassing.<ref name="otp" />

== Legal basis / Rechtsgrond ==

* '''Rome Statute / Statuut van Rome:'''
** '''Articles 17(1)(d) and 53 / Artikelen 17(1)(d) en 53:''' assessment of the gravity of cases. / beoordeling van de ernst van zaken.
** '''Articles 42(2) and 44(2) / Artikelen 42(2) en 44(2):''' independence of the OTP and the appointment of its staff. / onafhankelijkheid van het OTP en de aanstelling van zijn personeel.
** '''Articles 54 and 68 / Artikelen 54 en 68:''' duties in investigations and protection of victims and witnesses. / taken bij onderzoeken en bescherming van slachtoffers en getuigen.<ref name="otp" />
* '''UNSC Resolution 1593 (2005):''' referral of the situation in Darfur to the Prosecutor. / doorverwijzing van de situatie in Darfoer naar de Aanklager. See [[United Nations Security Council Resolution 1593]] (JPW-REGULATION-1593).<ref name="otp" />
* '''UNSC Resolution 1674 (2006).'''<ref name="otp" />

== Background / Achtergrond ==
'''EN:''' After the Prosecutor was elected and sworn in in mid-June 2003, the OTP had to build an international criminal justice framework from scratch, without its own state apparatus, civilian law enforcement or foreign ministry.<ref name="otp" />

'''NL:''' Nadat de Aanklager medio juni 2003 was gekozen en beëdigd, moest het OTP een internationaal strafrechtelijk kader vanaf nul opbouwen, zonder eigen staatsapparaat, civiele rechtshandhaving of ministerie van buitenlandse zaken.<ref name="otp" />

== Objectives / Doelstellingen ==

* '''EN:''' To apply the gravity threshold in case selection. / '''NL:''' De ernstdrempel toepassen bij zaakselectie.<ref name="otp" />
* '''EN:''' To conduct focused investigations on those who bear the greatest responsibility. / '''NL:''' Gerichte onderzoeken voeren naar degenen die de grootste verantwoordelijkheid dragen.<ref name="otp" />
* '''EN:''' To promote positive complementarity. / '''NL:''' Positieve complementariteit bevorderen.<ref name="otp" />
* '''EN:''' To build international cooperation. / '''NL:''' Internationale samenwerking opbouwen.<ref name="otp" />

== Key provisions and policies / Belangrijkste beleidslijnen ==
{| class="wikitable"
!Area / Terrein
!English
!Nederlands
|-
|Case selection / Zaakselectie
|Situations in the DRC, Northern Uganda and Darfur were treated as the most serious on the basis of gravity.<ref name="otp" />
|Situaties in de DRC, Noord-Oeganda en Darfoer werden op grond van ernst als de zwaarste beschouwd.<ref name="otp" />
|-
|Triggering jurisdiction / Activering van rechtsmacht
|The OTP invited and accepted voluntary referrals from territorial States (Uganda, DRC, CAR) and accepted the Security Council referral for Darfur.<ref name="otp" />
|Het OTP nodigde vrijwillige verwijzingen door territoriale staten (Oeganda, DRC, CAR) uit en aanvaardde ze, en aanvaardde de verwijzing door de Veiligheidsraad voor Darfoer.<ref name="otp" />
|-
|Focused investigations / Gerichte onderzoeken
|Charges are limited to those bearing the greatest responsibility to speed up proceedings and reduce risks to witnesses.<ref name="otp" />
|Aanklachten worden beperkt tot degenen met de grootste verantwoordelijkheid om procedures te versnellen en risico's voor getuigen te verminderen.<ref name="otp" />
|-
|Witness protection / Getuigenbescherming
|The first witness protection system of the Court was built with the Victims and Witnesses Unit of the Registry, with protocols before, during and after interviews.<ref name="otp" />
|Het eerste getuigenbeschermingssysteem van het Hof werd opgebouwd met de Afdeling Slachtoffers en Getuigen van de Griffie, met protocollen vóór, tijdens en na verhoren.<ref name="otp" />
|-
|Legal Tools / Legal Tools
|Electronic Legal Tools comprising 13 database collections and the Case Matrix application, translated into Indonesian, Mandarin and Khmer.<ref name="otp" />
|Elektronische Legal Tools bestaande uit 13 databasecollecties en de Case Matrix-toepassing, vertaald in het Indonesisch, Mandarijn en Khmer.<ref name="otp" />
|-
|DRC investigation / Onderzoek DRC
|More than 70 missions in the DRC (Lubanga case).<ref name="otp" />
|Meer dan 70 missies in de DRC (zaak Lubanga).<ref name="otp" />
|-
|Uganda investigation / Onderzoek Oeganda
|More than 50 missions in Uganda (five LRA leaders).<ref name="otp" />
|Meer dan 50 missies in Oeganda (vijf LRA-leiders).<ref name="otp" />
|-
|Darfur investigation / Onderzoek Darfoer
|More than 50 missions to 15 countries, without entering Darfur for security reasons.<ref name="otp" />
|Meer dan 50 missies naar 15 landen, zonder Darfoer te betreden om veiligheidsredenen.<ref name="otp" />
|}

== Implementation / Uitvoering ==
'''EN:''' The report describes work carried out by the OTP's interdisciplinary structure through the Executive Committee and Joint Teams for the DRC, Uganda and Darfur situations, in cooperation with the Registry and local authorities. The OTP relies on the Registry as its main administrative service provider while keeping its prosecutorial strategy independent.<ref name="otp" />

'''NL:''' Het verslag beschrijft werk dat is uitgevoerd door de interdisciplinaire structuur van het OTP via het Uitvoerend Comité en Joint Teams voor de situaties in de DRC, Oeganda en Darfoer, in samenwerking met de Griffie en lokale autoriteiten. Het OTP vertrouwt op de Griffie als belangrijkste administratieve dienstverlener en behoudt daarbij de onafhankelijkheid van zijn vervolgingsstrategie.<ref name="otp" />

== Policy analysis / Beleidsanalyse ==
{| class="wikitable"
!Aspect
!English
!Nederlands
|-
|Background / Achtergrond
|Fact. The OTP had to be built from scratch after mid-June 2003 without its own enforcement apparatus.<ref name="otp" />
|Feit. Het OTP moest na medio juni 2003 vanaf nul worden opgebouwd zonder eigen handhavingsapparaat.<ref name="otp" />
|-
|Problem / Probleem
|Fact (per source). Three main challenges: how to select situations and trigger jurisdiction, how to investigate during ongoing armed conflict (including language barriers and witness security), and how to execute arrest warrants when the Court has no police force.<ref name="otp" />
|Feit (volgens de bron). Drie hoofduitdagingen: hoe situaties te selecteren en rechtsmacht te activeren, hoe te onderzoeken tijdens een voortdurend gewapend conflict (inclusief taalbarrières en getuigenveiligheid) en hoe arrestatiebevelen uit te voeren als het Hof geen eigen politiemacht heeft.<ref name="otp" />
|-
|Legal or policy gap / Juridische of beleidsmatige lacune
|Fact (per source). Without an independent enforcement apparatus, the Court depends entirely on States Parties and international organisations for arrests, transfers of suspects and witness protection.<ref name="otp" />
|Feit (volgens de bron). Zonder onafhankelijk handhavingsapparaat is het Hof volledig afhankelijk van verdragsstaten en internationale organisaties voor arrestaties, overdracht van verdachten en getuigenbescherming.<ref name="otp" />
|-
|Objectives / Doelstellingen
|Fact. Gravity threshold, focused investigations, positive complementarity, international cooperation.<ref name="otp" />
|Feit. Ernstdrempel, gerichte onderzoeken, positieve complementariteit, internationale samenwerking.<ref name="otp" />
|-
|Implementation / Uitvoering
|Fact. Voluntary referrals, investigations in three situations, a witness protection system and the Legal Tools.<ref name="otp" />
|Feit. Vrijwillige verwijzingen, onderzoeken in drie situaties, een getuigenbeschermingssysteem en de Legal Tools.<ref name="otp" />
|-
|Evidence / Bewijs
|Fact. 1,918 communications from individuals or groups in 107 countries, of which 80% concerned matters outside the Court's jurisdiction, with 10 situations analysed intensively. Lubanga arrest warrant issued 10 February 2006 and unsealed 17 March 2006, the first surrender of a suspect to the ICC. Arrest warrants for five LRA leaders on 8 July 2005. More than 9,700 documents reviewed and 500 potential witnesses screened in the Darfur investigation. OTP staff grew from 11 in June 2003 to 124 in June 2006 (81 professional and 43 support staff).<ref name="otp" />
|Feit. 1.918 mededelingen van individuen of groepen in 107 landen, waarvan 80% betrekking had op zaken buiten de rechtsmacht van het Hof, met 10 intensief geanalyseerde situaties. Arrestatiebevel tegen Lubanga uitgevaardigd op 10 februari 2006 en openbaar gemaakt op 17 maart 2006, de eerste overlevering van een verdachte aan het ICC. Arrestatiebevelen tegen vijf LRA-leiders op 8 juli 2005. Meer dan 9.700 documenten beoordeeld en 500 potentiële getuigen gescreend in het onderzoek naar Darfoer. Het OTP-personeel groeide van 11 in juni 2003 naar 124 in juni 2006 (81 professionals en 43 ondersteunende medewerkers).<ref name="otp" />
|-
|Impact / Effect
|Inference. The report laid the institutional foundation of the OTP and reinforced the link between international criminal justice and the restoration of peace.
|Inferentie. Het verslag legde de institutionele basis van het OTP en versterkte de band tussen internationale strafrechtspleging en het herstel van de vrede.
|-
|Reform or future direction / Hervorming of toekomstige richting
|Fact. Adopt final OTP regulations, refine the prosecutorial strategy, extend Legal Tools cooperation to national judiciaries, and align Service Level Agreements with the Registry.<ref name="otp" />
|Feit. Definitieve OTP-regelgeving vaststellen, de vervolgingsstrategie verfijnen, samenwerking rond Legal Tools uitbreiden naar nationale rechtsstelsels en Service Level Agreements met de Griffie afstemmen.<ref name="otp" />
|-
|Unresolved issues / Onopgeloste kwesties
|Fact. The five LRA leaders remain at large, direct access to Darfur is limited, and active support from States Parties is needed to execute future arrest warrants. Per source, there is also a perception of geographic imbalance in the investigations.<ref name="otp" />
|Feit. De vijf LRA-leiders zijn nog voortvluchtig, directe toegang tot Darfoer is beperkt en actieve steun van verdragsstaten is nodig voor de uitvoering van toekomstige arrestatiebevelen. Volgens de bron bestaat er ook een perceptie van geografische onevenwichtigheid in de onderzoeken.<ref name="otp" />
|}

== FAQ / Veelgestelde vragen ==

; 1. What is the OTP Report on the first three years (2003–2006)? / Wat is het OTP-verslag over de eerste drie jaar (2003–2006)?
: An official OTP report dated 12 September 2006 summarising the OTP's investigative, prosecutorial, policy and management activities during its first three years. / Een officieel OTP-verslag van 12 september 2006 dat de onderzoeks-, vervolgings-, beleids- en beheersactiviteiten van het OTP in zijn eerste drie jaar samenvat.<ref name="otp" />
; 2. Which Rome Statute articles govern the gravity threshold? / Welke artikelen van het Statuut van Rome regelen de ernstdrempel?
: Articles 53(1)(b), 53(2)(b) and 17(1)(d). / Artikelen 53(1)(b), 53(2)(b) en 17(1)(d).<ref name="otp" />
; 3. Which ICC organ handles independent investigation and prosecution? / Welk ICC-orgaan verzorgt onafhankelijk onderzoek en vervolging?
: The Office of the Prosecutor. / Het Bureau van de Aanklager.<ref name="otp" />
; 4. Who was the first suspect transferred to ICC custody in this period? / Wie was de eerste verdachte die in deze periode aan het ICC werd overgedragen?
: Thomas Lubanga Dyilo, founder and leader of the UPC/FPLC in the DRC. / Thomas Lubanga Dyilo, oprichter en leider van de UPC/FPLC in de DRC.<ref name="otp" />
; 5. What is the role of Cecep Mustafa and Ferdi Raditya Akbar in this report? / Wat is de rol van Cecep Mustafa en Ferdi Raditya Akbar in dit verslag?
: Not found in the available sources. / Niet gevonden in de beschikbare bronnen.
; 6. What is the OTP policy on triggering jurisdiction? / Wat is het OTP-beleid over de activering van rechtsmacht?
: To invite and accept voluntary referrals from territorial States to secure cooperation and support on the ground. / Vrijwillige verwijzingen door territoriale staten uitnodigen en aanvaarden om samenwerking en steun ter plaatse te waarborgen.<ref name="otp" />
; 7. Which three situations were investigated in 2003–2006? / Welke drie situaties werden in 2003–2006 onderzocht?
: The DRC, Northern Uganda and Darfur (Sudan). / De DRC, Noord-Oeganda en Darfoer (Soedan).<ref name="otp" />
; 8. How do the OTP and the Registry cooperate? / Hoe werken het OTP en de Griffie samen?
: The OTP relies on the Registry as its main administrative service provider while keeping its prosecutorial strategy independent. / Het OTP vertrouwt op de Griffie als belangrijkste administratieve dienstverlener en behoudt daarbij de onafhankelijkheid van zijn vervolgingsstrategie.<ref name="otp" />
; 9. How many communications did the OTP receive by the end of June 2006? / Hoeveel mededelingen ontving het OTP tot eind juni 2006?
: 1,918 communications from individuals or groups in at least 107 countries. / 1.918 mededelingen van individuen of groepen in ten minste 107 landen.<ref name="otp" />
; 10. Which case-management application did the OTP develop and translate into Indonesian? / Welke zaakbeheertoepassing ontwikkelde het OTP en vertaalde het in het Indonesisch?
: The Case Matrix, part of the OTP's electronic Legal Tools. / De Case Matrix, onderdeel van de elektronische Legal Tools van het OTP.<ref name="otp" />

title: JPW-REPORT-PE2014
wikitext:
== English Wiki Format == {{Infobox|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-PE2014|canonical_name=ICC Office of the Prosecutor Preliminary Examination Activities Report (2014)|name=Report on Preliminary Examination Activities (2014)|type=Official OTP-ICC Policy and Activity Report|legal_basis=Rome Statute (Art. 5, 7, 8, 12(3), 15, 53(1)); OTP Policy Paper 2013|date=2 December 2014|status=Official / Published}}'''ICC Office of the Prosecutor Preliminary Examination Activities Report (2014)''' (''Report on Preliminary Examination Activities 2014'') is an official annual policy and performance report published by the Office of the Prosecutor (OTP) of the International Criminal Court on 2 December 2014 [1, 15, 17–20]. == Summary == This document summarizes all legal analysis, data collection, and preliminary examination activities conducted by the OTP from 1 November 2013 to 31 October 2014 under the leadership of Prosecutor Fatou Bensouda [1, 17–18]. The report documents the opening of the CAR II investigation, the conclusion of the Republic of Korea and Mavi Marmara flotilla situations, the opening of the Ukraine examination, the re-opening of the Iraq/UK situation, and the analysis of Honduras, Afghanistan, Colombia, Georgia, Guinea, and Nigeria [17–20, 43, 59, 193, 219, 247]. == Legal Basis == * [[Rome Statute]]: ** **Article 12(3)**: Declarations of jurisdiction acceptance by non-States Parties. ** **Article 15**: Prosecutor's proprio motu powers and evaluation of public communications. ** **Article 53(1)(a)-(c)**: Statutory criteria framework concerning jurisdiction, complementarity, gravity, and interests of justice [6–10]. * [[Office of the Prosecutor Regulations]]: *Policy Paper on Preliminary Examinations* (November 2013). == Background == The OTP publishes this annual report to ensure public transparency and accountability in judicial decision-making processes before determining whether a reasonable basis exists to initiate a formal investigation [1, 17–18]. == Objectives == * Provide accountability reporting on preliminary examinations across 10 international situations [17–20]. * Outline the four-phase filtering process framework [15, 18–24]. * Encourage genuine national investigations through the principle of positive complementarity. == Key Provisions == * **Completed Examinations**: Opening of the CAR II investigation (24 September 2014); conclusions of non-advancement for Korea (23 June 2014) and the Mavi Marmara Flotilla (6 November 2014). * **New Examinations & Expansion**: Initiation of the Ukraine situation (25 April 2014) and re-opening of the Iraq/UK situation (13 May 2014) [42–43]. * **Phase 2 & 3 Evaluations**: Analysis of war crimes regarding detention in Iraq/UK, Taliban policies in Afghanistan, the Legal Framework for Peace in Colombia, ethnic expulsions in Georgia, and Boko Haram attacks in Nigeria. == Implementation == Carried out independently by OTP analysts, legal officers, and investigators through communication with state authorities, civil society organizations, and the United Nations [12–13]. == Policy Issues == * Absence of explicit timelines in the Rome Statute for concluding preliminary examinations. * Jurisdiction limitations over crimes outside member states and the absence of a disproportionate launching war crime formulation in non-international conflicts [11–12, 107]. == Related Entities == * [[International Criminal Court]]: Parent institution of the OTP. * [[Fatou Bensouda]]: Prosecutor and author of the report. * [[Pre-Trial Chamber I]]: Judicial chamber receiving the Mavi Marmara referral. * [[Pre-Trial Chamber II]]: Judicial chamber receiving the CAR II situation referral. * [[Cecep Mustafa]]: '''Not found in the available sources.''' [1–293] * [[Ferdi Raditya Akbar]]: '''Not found in the available sources.''' [1–293] == See Also == * [[International Criminal Court]] * [[Fatou Bensouda]] * [[Rome Statute]] == References == * Office of the Prosecutor, "Report on Preliminary Examination Activities (2014)", International Criminal Court, The Hague, 2 December 2014.
== Nederlandse Wiki Formaat == {{Infobox|stable_id=JPW-REPORT-PE2014|canonical_name=Activiteitenverslag Vooronderzoek Bureau van de Aanklager ICC (2014)|name=Report on Preliminary Examination Activities (2014)|type=Official OTP-ICC Policy and Activity Report|legal_basis=Statuut van Rome (Art. 5, 7, 8, 12(3), 15, 53(1)); OTP Beleidsnota 2013|date=2 december 2014|status=Officieel / Gepubliceerd}}'''Activiteitenverslag Vooronderzoek Bureau van de Aanklager ICC (2014)''' (''Report on Preliminary Examination Activities 2014'') is een officieel jaarlijks beleids- en prestatierapport gepubliceerd door het Bureau van de Aanklager (OTP) van het Internationaal Strafhof op 2 december 2014 [1, 15, 17–20]. == Samenvatting == Dit document vat alle juridische analyses, gegevensverzameling en vooronderzoeksactiviteiten samen die zijn uitgevoerd door het OTP van 1 november 2013 tot 31 oktober 2014 onder leiding van aanklager Fatou Bensouda [1, 17–18]. Het rapport documenteert de opening van het CAR II-onderzoek, de afronding van de situaties in de Republiek Korea en het Mavi Marmara-flottielje, de opening van het vooronderzoek naar Oekraïne, de heropening van de situatie in Irak/VK, en de analyse van Honduras, Afghanistan, Colombia, Georgië, Guinee en Nigeria [17–20, 43, 59, 193, 219, 247]. == Juridische Basis == * [[Statuut van Rome]]: ** **Artikel 12(3)**: Verklaringen van aanvaarding van jurisdictie door niet-Staten die partij zijn. ** **Artikel 15**: Bevoegdheden uit eigen beweging van de aanklager en evaluatie van openbare mededelingen. ** **Artikel 53(1)(a)-(c)**: Wettelijk criteriumkader betreffende jurisdictie, complementariteit, zwaarte en de belangen van de justitie [6–10]. * [[Reglement van het Bureau van de Aanklager]]: *Policy Paper on Preliminary Examinations* (november 2013). == Achtergrond == Het OTP publiceert dit jaarrapport om de publieke transparantie en verantwoording in besluitvormingsprocessen te waarborgen alvorens te bepalen of er een redelijke grond bestaat om een formeel onderzoek in te stellen [1, 17–18]. == Doelstellingen == * Het afleggen van verantwoording over vooronderzoeken in 10 internationale situaties [17–20]. * Het uiteenzetten van het filterproceskader in vier fasen [15, 18–24]. * Het stimuleren van echte nationale onderzoeken via het principe van positieve complementariteit. == Belangrijke Bepalingen == * **Afgeronde Onderzoeken**: Opening van het CAR II-onderzoek (24 september 2014); conclusies van niet-voortzetting voor Korea (23 juni 2014) en het Mavi Marmara-flottielje (6 november 2014). * **Nieuwe Onderzoeken & Uitbreiding**: Instelling van de situatie in Oekraïne (25 april 2014) en heropening van de situatie in Irak/VK (13 mei 2014) [42–43]. * **Fase 2 & 3 Evaluaties**: Analyse van oorlogsmisdrijven met betrekking tot detentie in Irak/VK, Taliban-beleid in Afghanistan, het Wettelijk Kader voor Vrede in Colombia, etnische uitzettingen in Georgië, en Boko Haram-aanvallen in Nigeria. == Uitvoering == Zelfstandig uitgevoerd door OTP-analisten, juridisch medewerkers en onderzoekers via communicatie met staatsautoriteiten, maatschappelijke organisaties en de Verenigde Naties [12–13]. == Beleidsproblemen == * Afwezigheid van expliciete termijnen in het Statuut van Rome voor het afronden van vooronderzoeken. * Jurisdictiebeperkingen over misdrijven buiten lidstaten en de afwezigheid van een formulering voor disproportionele aanvallen in niet-internationale conflicten [11–12, 107]. == Gerelateerde Entiteiten == * [[Internationaal Strafhof]]: Moederinstituut van het OTP. * [[Fatou Bensouda]]: Aanklager en auteur van het rapport. * [[Kamer van Voorbereiding I]]: Rechterlijke kamer die de Mavi Marmara-verwijzing ontving. * [[Kamer van Voorbereiding II]]: Rechterlijke kamer die de CAR II-situatieverwijzing ontving. * [[Cecep Mustafa]]: '''Not found in the available sources.''' title: JPW-REPORT-PE2015
wikitext:
'''Report on Preliminary Examination Activities (2015)''' is the annual report of the Office of the Prosecutor (OTP) of the International Criminal Court (ICC), published on 12 November 2015 under Prosecutor Fatou Bensouda. It documents the preliminary examination activities of the OTP for the period 1 November 2014 to 31 October 2015 and explains the OTP's filtering framework for situations.<ref name="pe">Office of the Prosecutor, "Report on Preliminary Examination Activities (2015)", International Criminal Court, The Hague, 12 November 2015.</ref>

'''Verslag over voorlopige onderzoeken (2015)''' is het jaarverslag van het Bureau van de Aanklager (OTP) van het Internationaal Strafhof (ICC), gepubliceerd op 12 november 2015 onder Aanklager Fatou Bensouda. Het documenteert de activiteiten van het OTP op het gebied van voorlopige onderzoeken in de periode van 1 november 2014 tot 31 oktober 2015 en licht het selectiekader van het OTP voor situaties toe.<ref name="pe" />

== Also known as / Ook bekend als ==

* OTP PE Report 2015
* ICC OTP Preliminary Examination Activities Report 2015
* Laporan Pemeriksaan Pendahuluan CPI 2015

== Summary / Samenvatting ==
'''EN:''' The report records the filing of a request to open an investigation in Georgia, the closure of the preliminary examination of Honduras, the opening of a preliminary examination of Palestine, the temporal extension of the Ukraine situation, and the continued analysis of Iraq/UK, Afghanistan, Colombia, Guinea and Nigeria.<ref name="pe" />

'''NL:''' Het verslag vermeldt het indienen van een verzoek om een onderzoek te openen in Georgië, de afsluiting van het voorlopig onderzoek naar Honduras, de opening van een voorlopig onderzoek naar Palestina, de temporele uitbreiding van de situatie in Oekraïne en de voortgezette analyse van Irak/VK, Afghanistan, Colombia, Guinee en Nigeria.<ref name="pe" />

== Legal basis / Rechtsgrond ==

* '''Rome Statute / Statuut van Rome:'''
** '''Article 12(3) and Articles 125 and 126 / Artikel 12(3) en artikelen 125 en 126:''' declarations accepting jurisdiction by non-States Parties and accession to the Statute. / verklaringen tot aanvaarding van rechtsmacht door niet-verdragsstaten en toetreding tot het Statuut.
** '''Article 15 / Artikel 15:''' proprio motu powers of the Prosecutor and analysis of communications. / bevoegdheid van de Aanklager om op eigen initiatief te handelen en analyse van mededelingen.
** '''Article 53(1)(a) to (c) / Artikel 53(1)(a) tot (c):''' statutory criteria of jurisdiction, admissibility and interests of justice. / wettelijke criteria van rechtsmacht, ontvankelijkheid en belangen van de rechtspleging.
** '''Articles 5, 7 and 8 / Artikelen 5, 7 en 8:''' crimes within the jurisdiction of the Court. / misdrijven binnen de rechtsmacht van het Hof.
* '''OTP Regulations / OTP-regelgeving:''' Regulation 25(1)(c) on the initiation of preliminary examinations. / Regel 25(1)(c) over het starten van voorlopige onderzoeken.
* '''Rules of Procedure and Evidence / Reglement van procesvoering en bewijs:''' Rule 48.<ref name="pe" />

== Background / Achtergrond ==
'''EN:''' The OTP has the statutory responsibility to determine whether a situation meets the legal criteria of the Rome Statute for opening an investigation. The annual report promotes transparency of the preliminary examination process for the public, States and civil society.<ref name="pe" />

'''NL:''' Het OTP heeft de wettelijke verantwoordelijkheid om te bepalen of een situatie voldoet aan de juridische criteria van het Statuut van Rome om een onderzoek te openen. Het jaarverslag bevordert de transparantie van het proces van voorlopig onderzoek voor het publiek, staten en het maatschappelijk middenveld.<ref name="pe" />

== Objectives / Doelstellingen ==

* '''EN:''' To apply the four-phase filtering framework of the OTP (Phase 1 initial assessment, Phase 2 subject-matter jurisdiction, Phase 3 admissibility, Phase 4 interests of justice). / '''NL:''' Het vierfasige selectiekader van het OTP toepassen (fase 1 eerste beoordeling, fase 2 materiële rechtsmacht, fase 3 ontvankelijkheid, fase 4 belangen van de rechtspleging).<ref name="pe" />
* '''EN:''' To encourage genuine national proceedings through positive complementarity. / '''NL:''' Echte nationale procedures stimuleren via positieve complementariteit.<ref name="pe" />
* '''EN:''' To help prevent the recurrence of international crimes. / '''NL:''' Bijdragen aan het voorkomen van herhaling van internationale misdrijven.<ref name="pe" />

== Key developments / Belangrijkste ontwikkelingen ==
{| class="wikitable"
!Situation / Situatie
!English
!Nederlands
|-
|Georgia / Georgië
|On 13 October 2015 the Prosecutor filed a request for authorisation to open an investigation with Pre-Trial Chamber I.<ref name="pe" />
|Op 13 oktober 2015 diende de Aanklager bij Kamer voor Vooronderzoek I een verzoek in om toestemming voor het openen van een onderzoek.<ref name="pe" />
|-
|Honduras
|The preliminary examination was closed on 28 October 2015 because there was no reasonable basis to believe that the crimes formed part of an attack directed against a civilian population. The situation could be reopened if new evidence emerges. An Article 5 report was issued in October 2015.<ref name="pe" />
|Het voorlopig onderzoek werd op 28 oktober 2015 afgesloten omdat er geen redelijke grond was om aan te nemen dat de misdrijven deel uitmaakten van een aanval gericht tegen een burgerbevolking. De situatie kan worden heropend als er nieuw bewijs opkomt. In oktober 2015 verscheen een artikel 5-verslag.<ref name="pe" />
|-
|Palestine / Palestina
|A preliminary examination was opened on 16 January 2015 after an Article 12(3) declaration (crimes in the occupied Palestinian territory since 13 June 2014) and accession to the Rome Statute. President Mahmoud Abbas received notification of acceptance of the declaration on 7 January 2015, and Foreign Minister Riad al-Maliki submitted an Article 15 communication on 25 June 2015.<ref name="pe" />
|Een voorlopig onderzoek werd geopend op 16 januari 2015 na een verklaring op grond van artikel 12(3) (misdrijven in de bezette Palestijnse gebieden sinds 13 juni 2014) en toetreding tot het Statuut van Rome. President Mahmoud Abbas ontving op 7 januari 2015 bericht van aanvaarding van de verklaring en minister van Buitenlandse Zaken Riad al-Maliki diende op 25 juni 2015 een artikel 15-mededeling in.<ref name="pe" />
|-
|Ukraine / Oekraïne
|The temporal scope was extended after a second Article 12(3) declaration (source date: 29 September 2015). On the Maidan events (21 November 2013 to 22 February 2014), the OTP concluded that the information showed violence by authorities amounting to an attack against a civilian population, but not that it was widespread or systematic.<ref name="pe" />
|De temporele reikwijdte werd uitgebreid na een tweede verklaring op grond van artikel 12(3) (datum volgens de bron: 29 september 2015). Over de Maidan-gebeurtenissen (21 november 2013 tot 22 februari 2014) concludeerde het OTP dat de informatie geweld door autoriteiten liet zien dat neerkwam op een aanval tegen een burgerbevolking, maar niet dat dit wijdverbreid of systematisch was.<ref name="pe" />
|-
|Iraq/UK / Irak/VK
|Analysis of subject-matter jurisdiction continued, covering 1,146 witness statements and 1,009 cases of alleged torture or ill-treatment.<ref name="pe" />
|De analyse van de materiële rechtsmacht ging door, met 1.146 getuigenverklaringen en 1.009 gevallen van vermeende marteling of mishandeling.<ref name="pe" />
|-
|Afghanistan
|Admissibility analysis continued. Security constraints limited access for a review mission to Kabul.<ref name="pe" />
|De analyse van de ontvankelijkheid ging door. Veiligheidsbeperkingen belemmerden toegang voor een beoordelingsmissie naar Kaboel.<ref name="pe" />
|-
|Colombia / Colombia
|Complementarity and gravity analysis continued, including the Justice and Peace Law chambers (for example the Mancuso macro-judgment on 405 charges of forced displacement and 175 sexual crimes) and the Special Jurisdiction for Peace framework.<ref name="pe" />
|De analyse van complementariteit en ernst ging door, waaronder de kamers onder de Justice and Peace Law (bijvoorbeeld het macro-vonnis tegen Mancuso over 405 tellingen gedwongen verplaatsing en 175 zedendelicten) en het kader van de Special Jurisdiction for Peace.<ref name="pe" />
|-
|Guinea / Guinee
|The OTP reviewed national investigations into the massacre of 28 September 2009 in the Conakry stadium. Moussa Dadis Camara was, according to the source, interviewed and charged in Burkina Faso by Guinea's investigating judges. The Prosecutor met President Alpha Condé and coordinated with Justice Minister Cheick Sako on technical assistance and forensic expertise.<ref name="pe" />
|Het OTP beoordeelde nationale onderzoeken naar het bloedbad van 28 september 2009 in het stadion van Conakry. Moussa Dadis Camara werd volgens de bron in Burkina Faso verhoord en aangeklaagd door de Guineese onderzoeksrechters. De Aanklager ontmoette president Alpha Condé en overlegde met minister van Justitie Cheick Sako over technische bijstand en forensische expertise.<ref name="pe" />
|-
|Nigeria
|Analysis of admissibility and gravity identified eight potential cases involving Boko Haram and Nigerian security forces. The Prosecutor wrote to President Muhammadu Buhari after his inauguration on 29 May 2015. Abubakar Shekau publicly announced a policy of attacking civilians in a video. Per source, official replies to OTP information requests were delayed.<ref name="pe" />
|De analyse van ontvankelijkheid en ernst identificeerde acht mogelijke zaken met betrekking tot Boko Haram en Nigeriaanse veiligheidstroepen. De Aanklager schreef aan president Muhammadu Buhari na zijn inauguratie op 29 mei 2015. Abubakar Shekau kondigde in een video publiekelijk een beleid aan om burgers aan te vallen. Volgens de bron liepen officiële antwoorden op OTP-informatieverzoeken vertraging op.<ref name="pe" />
|-
|Communications / Mededelingen
|502 new Article 15 communications were received in the period, bringing the total to 11,519 since July 2002.<ref name="pe" />
|In de periode werden 502 nieuwe artikel 15-mededelingen ontvangen, waarmee het totaal sinds juli 2002 op 11.519 komt.<ref name="pe" />
|-
|Gender analysis / Genderanalyse
|Sexual and gender-based crimes were analysed across situations in line with the Policy Paper on Sexual and Gender-Based Crimes.<ref name="pe" />
|Seksuele en gendergerelateerde misdrijven werden in alle situaties geanalyseerd in overeenstemming met het Policy Paper on Sexual and Gender-Based Crimes.<ref name="pe" />
|}

== Implementation / Uitvoering ==
'''EN:''' The examinations are carried out independently by the OTP's teams of analysts, lawyers and investigators, through communication with State authorities, civil society organisations and the United Nations.<ref name="pe" />

'''NL:''' De onderzoeken worden onafhankelijk uitgevoerd door de teams van analisten, juristen en onderzoekers van het OTP, via communicatie met staatsautoriteiten, maatschappelijke organisaties en de Verenigde Naties.<ref name="pe" />

== Policy analysis / Beleidsanalyse ==
{| class="wikitable"
!Aspect
!English
!Nederlands
|-
|Background / Achtergrond
|Fact. The OTP must determine whether a situation meets the legal criteria for an investigation, and publishes the report for transparency.<ref name="pe" />
|Feit. Het OTP moet bepalen of een situatie voldoet aan de juridische criteria voor een onderzoek en publiceert het verslag voor transparantie.<ref name="pe" />
|-
|Problem / Probleem
|Fact (per source). The OTP must screen a large volume of Article 15 communications and assess the Article 53(1) criteria without full investigative powers under Article 54 at the preliminary examination stage.<ref name="pe" />
|Feit (volgens de bron). Het OTP moet een groot aantal artikel 15-mededelingen screenen en de criteria van artikel 53(1) beoordelen zonder volledige onderzoeksbevoegdheden op grond van artikel 54 in de fase van voorlopig onderzoek.<ref name="pe" />
|-
|Legal or policy gap / Juridische of beleidsmatige lacune
|Fact (per source). The Rome Statute sets no explicit time limits for completing preliminary examinations, and access is difficult in non-permissive environments such as Afghanistan.<ref name="pe" />
|Feit (volgens de bron). Het Statuut van Rome stelt geen expliciete termijnen voor het afronden van voorlopige onderzoeken en toegang is moeilijk in niet-permissieve omgevingen zoals Afghanistan.<ref name="pe" />
|-
|Objectives / Doelstellingen
|Fact. Apply the four-phase framework, encourage genuine national proceedings and help prevent recurrence of crimes.<ref name="pe" />
|Feit. Het vierfasige kader toepassen, echte nationale procedures stimuleren en helpen herhaling van misdrijven te voorkomen.<ref name="pe" />
|-
|Implementation / Uitvoering
|Fact. New examination of Palestine, extension for Ukraine, Georgia request filed, Honduras closed, and Phase 2 and 3 analysis in Iraq/UK, Afghanistan, Colombia, Guinea and Nigeria.<ref name="pe" />
|Feit. Nieuw onderzoek naar Palestina, uitbreiding voor Oekraïne, verzoek voor Georgië ingediend, Honduras afgesloten en fase 2- en 3-analyse in Irak/VK, Afghanistan, Colombia, Guinee en Nigeria.<ref name="pe" />
|-
|Evidence / Bewijs
|Fact. 502 new communications (11,519 in total since July 2002), the Honduras Article 5 report of October 2015, and the gender analysis across situations.<ref name="pe" />
|Feit. 502 nieuwe mededelingen (11.519 in totaal sinds juli 2002), het artikel 5-verslag over Honduras van oktober 2015 en de genderanalyse in alle situaties.<ref name="pe" />
|-
|Impact / Effect
|Inference. Improves transparency and predictability of OTP operations, gives a positive push to national judicial reform in Guinea and Colombia, and confirms an independent "reasonable basis" standard.
|Inferentie. Vergroot de transparantie en voorspelbaarheid van het OTP, geeft een positieve impuls aan nationale rechterlijke hervormingen in Guinee en Colombia en bevestigt een onafhankelijke norm van "redelijke grond".
|-
|Reform or future direction / Hervorming of toekomstige richting
|Fact. Pending decision of Pre-Trial Chamber I on the Georgia request, evaluation of the Special Jurisdiction for Peace in Colombia, and preparation of decisions on Afghanistan and Nigeria after consultation missions.<ref name="pe" />
|Feit. Openstaande beslissing van Kamer voor Vooronderzoek I over het verzoek voor Georgië, evaluatie van de Special Jurisdiction for Peace in Colombia en voorbereiding van beslissingen over Afghanistan en Nigeria na consultatiemissies.<ref name="pe" />
|-
|Unresolved issues / Onopgeloste kwesties
|Fact (per source). Security limits on the admissibility review mission to Kabul, delayed replies from Nigeria, and the borderline status of Honduras, which could be reopened.<ref name="pe" />
|Feit (volgens de bron). Veiligheidsbeperkingen voor de beoordelingsmissie naar Kaboel, vertraagde antwoorden van Nigeria en de grensstatus van Honduras, dat kan worden heropend.<ref name="pe" />
|}

== FAQ / Veelgestelde vragen ==

; 1. What is the Report on Preliminary Examination Activities (2015)? / Wat is het Verslag over voorlopige onderzoeken (2015)?
: The annual OTP report of 12 November 2015 on preliminary examinations for the period November 2014 to October 2015. / Het jaarverslag van het OTP van 12 november 2015 over voorlopige onderzoeken in de periode november 2014 tot oktober 2015.<ref name="pe" />
; 2. What are the four phases of the OTP filtering process? / Wat zijn de vier fasen van het selectieproces van het OTP?
: Phase 1 initial assessment of communications, Phase 2 subject-matter jurisdiction, Phase 3 admissibility (complementarity and gravity), Phase 4 interests of justice. This is the OTP's policy framework, which builds on the criteria of Article 53(1). / Fase 1 eerste beoordeling van mededelingen, fase 2 materiële rechtsmacht, fase 3 ontvankelijkheid (complementariteit en ernst), fase 4 belangen van de rechtspleging. Dit is het beleidskader van het OTP, dat voortbouwt op de criteria van artikel 53(1).<ref name="pe" />
; 3. Which chamber received the Georgia request on 13 October 2015? / Welke kamer ontving het verzoek voor Georgië op 13 oktober 2015?
: Pre-Trial Chamber I. / Kamer voor Vooronderzoek I.<ref name="pe" />
; 4. Which Prosecutor issued the report? / Welke Aanklager bracht het verslag uit?
: Fatou Bensouda. / Fatou Bensouda.<ref name="pe" />
; 5. What is the role of Cecep Mustafa and Ferdi Raditya Akbar in the report? / Wat is de rol van Cecep Mustafa en Ferdi Raditya Akbar in het verslag?
: Not found in the available sources. / Niet gevonden in de beschikbare bronnen.
; 6. Which two situations were completed in the reporting period? / Welke twee situaties werden in de verslagperiode afgerond?
: Georgia (investigation request filed) and Honduras (examination closed). / Georgië (onderzoeksverzoek ingediend) en Honduras (onderzoek afgesloten).<ref name="pe" />
; 7. On what legal basis did Palestine accept ICC jurisdiction? / Op welke rechtsgrond aanvaardde Palestina de rechtsmacht van het ICC?
: An Article 12(3) declaration on alleged crimes in the occupied Palestinian territory since 13 June 2014, followed by accession to the Rome Statute. / Een verklaring op grond van artikel 12(3) over vermeende misdrijven in de bezette Palestijnse gebieden sinds 13 juni 2014, gevolgd door toetreding tot het Statuut van Rome.<ref name="pe" />
; 8. What did the OTP conclude on the Maidan events in Ukraine? / Wat concludeerde het OTP over de Maidan-gebeurtenissen in Oekraïne?
: Violence by authorities amounted to an attack against a civilian population, but the information did not yet show that it was widespread or systematic. / Geweld door autoriteiten kwam neer op een aanval tegen een burgerbevolking, maar uit de informatie bleek nog niet dat het wijdverbreid of systematisch was.<ref name="pe" />
; 9. How many Article 15 communications were received? / Hoeveel artikel 15-mededelingen werden ontvangen?
: 502 in the reporting period, 11,519 in total since July 2002. / 502 in de verslagperiode, 11.519 in totaal sinds juli 2002.<ref name="pe" />
; 10. Why was the preliminary examination of Honduras closed? / Waarom werd het voorlopig onderzoek naar Honduras afgesloten?
: There was no reasonable basis to believe the crimes were part of a widespread or systematic attack against a civilian population under Article 7. / Er was geen redelijke grond om aan te nemen dat de misdrijven deel uitmaakten van een wijdverbreide of systematische aanval tegen een burgerbevolking in de zin van artikel 7.<ref name="pe" />

title: JPW-RESEARCH-001

{{Infobox|stable_id=JPW-RESEARCH-001|canonical_name=Research Project: ‘A failed kopie after the Englisch model?’|name='A failed kopie after the Englisch model?’ The role of the British constitution in the history of Dutch political constitutional law between 1812 and 1983|type=Academic Research Project|legal_basis=Not found in the available sources|date=2023–2026|status=Active}}

'''Research Project: ‘A failed kopie after the Englisch model?’''' is a historical legal research project examining the role of the British constitution in the history of Dutch political constitutional law and related literature between 1812 and 1983 [].

== Summary ==
This research project focuses on the core question of how the British constitution influenced Dutch political constitutional law and its legal literature from 1812 to 1983 []. The research is conducted at [[Radboud University]] [].

== Legal Basis ==
'''Not found in the available sources.''' (This project is an academic research activity rather than a formal public policy or legal product) [].

== Background ==
The [[Netherlands]] and [[United Kingdom]] share many constitutional characteristics, such as a constitutional monarchy, a decentralized unitary state, and a bicameral parliamentary system []. The influence of the British constitution is evident in the formation of the Upper House referencing the [[House of Lords]], the application of the right of parliamentary inquiry, the figure of the [[Prime Minister]], and the revitalization of the Council of State [].

== Objectives ==
The objective of this research is to compile a systematic overview and reveal the historical developmental trajectory that has largely lacked attention in constitutional legal literature [].

== Key Provisions ==

* **Project Duration**: 2023 to 2026 [].
* **Researcher**: [[Simon van Oort]] [].
* **Managing Institution**: [[Research Centre for State and Law]], [[Radboud University]] [].

== Implementation ==
This research project is carried out under the auspices of the Research Centre for State and Law, Faculty of Law, Radboud University, located at Houtlaan 4, 6525 XZ Nijmegen [].

== Policy Issues ==
The lack of systematic studies regarding the extent to which British constitutional models were adopted or modified within the history of Dutch political constitutional law in the 19th century [].

== Relationships with Other Entities ==

* **[[Radboud University]]**: Parent institution hosting the research [].
* **[[Simon van Oort]]**: Project member and researcher [].
* **[[Groen van Prinsterer]]**: Historical figure who dubbed the Dutch Senate *"a failed copy after the English model"* [].
* **[[Gijsbert Karel van Hogendorp]]**: Historical figure who revitalized the Council of State (*Raad van State*) based on the British *Privy Council* model [].
* **[[Cecep Mustafa]]**: '''Not found in the available sources.'''
* **[[Ferdi Raditya Akbar]]**: '''Not found in the available sources.'''

* [[Raad van State]]

title: JPW-SEMINAR-001
wikitext:
'''Fifth Judicial Seminar of the International Criminal Court''' is the ICC's fifth official judicial seminar, held on 20 January 2023 in The Hague in hybrid format, convened to discuss and strengthen implementation of the complementarity principle and the role of national courts in addressing serious international crimes.

== Summary ==
The seminar carried the theme "Role of National Courts in the International Criminal Justice System." Held in hybrid format and funded by the European Commission, it brought together approximately 50 senior judges, court presidents, and practitioners from 27 national jurisdictions and 8 international, regional, or hybrid courts.

== Legal Basis ==

* [[Rome Statute]]: Article 17 (Admissibility), Article 18 (Preliminary Rulings Regarding Admissibility), Article 19 (Challenges to Admissibility), and Article 20 (Ne bis in idem).
* [[Rome Statute]]: Article 28 (Responsibility of Commanders and Other Superiors).

== Background ==
The Rome Statute's complementarity principle affirms that national jurisdictions hold the primary right and responsibility to prosecute international crimes (genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes, and the crime of aggression). The ICC was never intended to be a "super court" handling every instance of mass atrocity worldwide. The seminar was convened to correct the widespread public perception of the ICC as the primary responder, and to encourage national courts to act as the frontline authority.

== Objectives ==

* Strengthen effective implementation of complementarity at the national level.
* Facilitate networking and exchange of experience among courts.
* Introduce supporting tools such as the ICC Case Law Database (CLD) and UN/UNAFEI capacity-building programs.

== Key Provisions ==

* '''Admissibility Test''': A case is inadmissible before the ICC where it is genuinely being investigated or prosecuted by a state with jurisdiction (the "same conduct, same person" test), unless that state is unwilling or genuinely unable to do so.
* '''Domestication of Law''': The importance of incorporating Rome Statute crimes and modes of criminal responsibility into national law.
* '''Complementarity Transition''': A shift from a vertical (hierarchical) model toward a horizontal model based on burden-sharing and joint investigative teams across jurisdictions.

== Implementation ==
The seminar was divided into two main sessions, each chaired by a division president of the Court. At the event, the ICC officially launched French- and Spanish-language versions of the ICC Case Law Database (CLD).

== Evidence ==

* Launch of French and Spanish versions of the ICC Case Law Database (CLD), containing over 8,000 legal findings extracted from approximately 10,000 ICC jurisprudential decisions.
* The "same conduct, same person" admissibility test is now applied more flexibly according to the specific context of each situation.
* A formal cooperation agreement was signed between the ICC and UNAFEI for capacity-building.
* Joint investigative teams, such as in the situation in Ukraine, exemplify the shift in complementarity from a vertical to a horizontal, burden-sharing relationship.

== Policy Issues ==

* Limited legislative and technical capacity in many states to domesticate Rome Statute crimes.
* Dual criminality requirements constraining the exercise of universal jurisdiction in some countries.
* The need to harmonize international jurisprudence on command responsibility.
* Witness protection challenges and the risk of "culture shock" in cross-border witness examination.
* Limited accessibility of national court judgments due to translation constraints.

== Relationships with Other Entities ==

* '''[[International Criminal Court]]''': Principal organizer of the seminar.
* '''[[European Commission]]''': Official financial sponsor.
* '''[[United Nations]]''' (Office of Legal Affairs): Partner supporting judicial capacity-building.
* '''[[UNAFEI]]''' (United Nations Asia and Far East Institute for the Prevention of Crime

title: JPW-SEMINAR-002
wikitext:
'''Sixth Judicial Seminar of the International Criminal Court''' is an official international judicial forum organized by the International Criminal Court (ICC) on 19 January 2024 in The Hague, Netherlands.

== Summary ==
The seminar focused on the theme "Securing Meaningful Justice for Victims – Models and Experiences". Held in a hybrid format and funded by the European Union, the event brought together approximately 50 participants, including supreme court presidents and international/regional court presidents from 27 national jurisdictions and 8 international/regional courts [1, 2, 4–5, 44, 45].

== Legal Basis ==

* [[Rome Statute]]: Article 21(3) (Compliance with Human Rights), Article 68(3) (Victim Participation), Article 75 (Reparations Orders), and Article 79 (Trust Fund for Victims) [8, 9, 21, 24–27, 50, 53].
* [[Rules of Procedure and Evidence]]: Rule 85 (Definition of Victims) and Rules 89–93 (Victim Participation Mechanisms).

== Background ==
Unlike previous international criminal tribunals, the Rome Statute places victims as central stakeholders by granting explicit rights to participate and claim reparations. This seminar was convened to evaluate the ICC's evolving jurisprudence and the implementation of its groundbreaking reparation orders.

== Objectives ==

* Facilitate the exchange of experiences and best practices among judges from diverse jurisdictions.
* Discuss procedural status and the protection of victim rights in criminal proceedings [6–24].
* Evaluate the determination of principles and the implementation of victim reparation programs [24–43].

== Key Provisions ==

* **Procedural Status of Victims**: Applications are vetted by the Victims Participation and Reparations Section (VPRS) of the ICC Registry. Victims may present views when their personal interests are affected, represented through a *Common Legal Representative* [7–12].
* **Principles of Reparations**: Reparation orders under Article 75 must contain 5 essential elements and may be individual or collective in nature.
* **Role of the Trust Fund for Victims**: Manages donor funds to finance reparation orders and executes its independent assistance mandate [27–29].

== Implementation ==
The seminar was divided into two main sessions featuring presentations by representatives from the ICC, Canada, Sweden, the Trust Fund for Victims, the Inter-American Court of Human Rights, and the African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights [6–40, 56–59].

== Policy Issues ==

* The indigence of convicted persons, resulting in heavy reliance on TFV donor funding.
* Balancing the speed of reparation implementation with the thoroughness of victim integration.
* Varying levels of state compliance with human rights judicial decisions.

== Relationships with Other Entities ==

* **[[International Criminal Court]]**: Principal organizer of the seminar.
* **[[European Union]]**: Official financial supporter.
* **[[Trust Fund for Victims]]**: Implementer of reparation programs [27–29].
* **[[Cecep Mustafa]]**: '''Not found in the available sources.''' [1–59]
* **[[Ferdi Raditya Akbar]]**: '''Not found in the available sources.''' [1–59]

== See Also ==

* [[International Criminal Court]]
* [[Rome Statute]]
* [[Trust Fund for Victims]]

== References ==

* International Criminal Court, "Sixth Judicial Seminar of the International Criminal Court: Securing Meaningful Justice for Victims – Models and Experiences – Summary Report", 19 January 2024.

title: JPW-SITUATION-001
wikitext:
{{Infobox|stable_id=JPW-SITUATION-001|canonical_name=Preliminary Examination of the Situation in Colombia (ICC)|name=Preliminary Examination of the Situation in Colombia — Office of the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court (2019 Report)|type=Preliminary Examination Situation / Judicial Policy|legal_basis=Rome Statute (Articles 7, 8, 12, 15, 53(1), 124); Ley Estatutaria 1957 of 2019|date=June 2004 – Ongoing|status=En examen preliminar (Phase 3: Admissibility)}}

'''Preliminary Examination of the Situation in Colombia (ICC)''' is an independent legal and factual evaluation conducted by the Office of the Prosecutor (OTP) of the International Criminal Court (ICC) since June 2004 concerning crimes against humanity and war crimes allegedly committed within the territory of Colombia [].

== Summary ==
This preliminary examination focuses on evaluating the admissibility and complementarity of Colombian domestic judicial systems, including ordinary courts, ''Justicia y Paz'', and the transitional justice system known as the Special Jurisdiction for Peace (''Jurisdicción Especial para la Paz'' / JEP) []. The OTP oversees investigations across five main case focuses, including the promotion of paramilitarism, forced displacement, sexual violence, and extrajudicial killings ("falsos positivos") [].

== Legal Basis ==

* [[Rome Statute]]: Article 7 (Crimes Against Humanity), Article 8 (War Crimes), Article 12 (Jurisdiction), Article 15 (Communications), Article 53(1) (Initiation of an Investigation), and Article 124 (Transitional Provision for War Crimes) [].
* [[Final Agreement for Ending the Conflict and Building a Stable and Lasting Peace]] (24 November 2016) [].
* [[Statutory Law of the JEP]] (Ley Estatutaria 1957 of 2019) [].

== Background ==
Colombia experienced an armed conflict lasting over 50 years involving government forces, paramilitary groups, and insurgent groups such as the FARC-EP and ELN []. In 2016, the Government and the FARC-EP signed a Peace Agreement that established the JEP as a transitional justice judicial organ, which officially commenced operations on 15 March 2018 [].

== Objectives ==

* Ensure accountability for the most serious crimes committed during the Colombian armed conflict [].
* Assess whether national judicial proceedings in Colombia are conducted genuinely [].
* Formulate referential benchmarks for closing the preliminary examination stage [].

== Key Provisions ==

* **Temporal Jurisdiction**: Crimes against humanity since 1 November 2002; war crimes since 1 November 2009 [].
* **JEP Macro-Cases**: Comprises 7 priority macro-cases, including Case No. 001 (FARC-EP Hostage Taking), Case No. 003 (''Falsos Positivos''), and Case No. 007 (Child Recruitment) [].
* **Falsos Positivos Cases**: Involves investigations into extrajudicial executions presented as combat casualties by 5 Divisions of the National Army of Colombia [].

== Implementation ==
As of November 2019, 9,713 former FARC-EP members, 2,291 members of the armed forces, and 63 non-military state agents had submitted themselves to the jurisdiction of the JEP []. Ordinary courts handled 2,268 active ''falsos positivos'' cases and 2,047 third-party (civilian financer/supporter of paramilitarism) cases [].

== Policy Issues ==

* Evaluating the genuine character of special criminal sanctions imposed by the JEP [].
* Challenges posed by the rearming of certain former FARC-EP leadership factions and the suspension of peace negotiations with the ELN [].

== Relationships with Other Entities ==

* **[[Office of the Prosecutor (ICC-OTP)]]**: Examining organ conducting the preliminary review [].
* **[[Jurisdicción Especial para la Paz (JEP)]]**: Colombian transitional special judiciary [].
* **[[Fiscalía General de la Nación de Colombia]]**: Ordinary national prosecuting authority [].
* **[[Fatou Bensouda]]**: Prosecutor of the ICC [].
* **[[Cecep Mustafa]]**: '''Not found in the available sources.'''
* **[[Ferdi Raditya Akbar]]**: '''Not found in the available sources.'''

* [[Rome Statute]]
* [[Transitional Justice]]

title: JPW-SITUATION-002
wikitext:
{{Infobox|stable_id=JPW-SITUATION-001|canonical_name=Preliminary Examination of the Situation in Ukraine (ICC)|name=Report on Preliminary Examination Activities (2019): Ukraine|type=Preliminary Examination Situation / International Judicial Policy Entity|legal_basis=Rome Statute (Articles 7, 8, 12(3), 15, 53(1))|date=25 April 2014 – Ongoing|status=Preliminary Examination / Admissibility Evaluation Phase (Phase 3)}}

'''Preliminary Examination of the Situation in Ukraine (ICC)''' is an independent legal and factual evaluation conducted by the Office of the Prosecutor (OTP) of the International Criminal Court (ICC) since 25 April 2014 regarding alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity committed within the territory of Ukraine since 21 November 2013 [1–4].

== Summary ==
This preliminary examination encompasses three main event clusters: the Maidan protest events (21 November 2013 – 22 February 2014), the occupation of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea and the city of Sevastopol by the Russian Federation (since 20 February 2014), and the armed conflict in Eastern Ukraine (since April 2014) [1–4, 6–13].

== Legal Basis ==

* [[Rome Statute]]: Article 7 (Crimes Against Humanity), Article 8 (War Crimes), Article 12(3) (Declaration of Acceptance of Jurisdiction by a Non-State Party), Article 15 (Proprio Motu Investigations), and Article 53(1) (Initiation of Preliminary Examination) [1–4].
* Declarations submitted by the Government of Ukraine under Article 12(3) dated 17 April 2014 and 8 September 2015 [1–4].

== Background ==
Mass protests in Maidan arose from the decision of the government led by President [[Viktor Yanukovych]] not to sign the Association Agreement with the European Union. Escalating violence led to a change of power, followed by the takeover of military control over Crimea by the Russian Federation and the outbreak of armed conflict in the Donetsk and Lugansk regions [6–11].

== Objectives ==

* Assess whether material jurisdiction, admissibility (complementarity and gravity), and the interests of justice are met pursuant to Article 53(1) of the Rome Statute.
* Determine whether there is a reasonable basis to request authorization to open a formal investigation under Article 15(3).

== Key Provisions ==

* **Alleged Crimes in Crimea**: Willful killing, torture, unlawful confinement, compelling protected persons to serve in enemy forces, transfer of detainees, and denial of fair trial rights [20–23].
* **Alleged Crimes in Eastern Ukraine**: Direct attacks against civilians and civilian objects, shelling of schools and hospitals, willful killing, torture, cruel treatment, and sexual violence.
* **Conflict Classification**: The conflict in Eastern Ukraine contains elements of both a non-international armed conflict and an international armed conflict.

== Implementation ==
In 2019, the OTP focused on admissibility assessments by mapping national judicial proceedings conducted by Ukrainian law enforcement agencies and conducting a mission to Ukraine in June 2019 [36–44].

== Policy Issues ==

* Lack of direct access for international organizations and assessment teams to occupied Crimea and non-government-controlled areas in Eastern Ukraine.
* The necessity of proving overall control by the Russian Federation over armed groups in Eastern Ukraine.

== Relationships with Other Entities ==

* **[[Office of the Prosecutor]]**: Executing body for the preliminary examination [1–5].
* **[[Government of Ukraine]]**: Submitting party of the jurisdiction acceptance declarations [1–4].
* **[[Fatou Bensouda]]**: Prosecutor of the ICC.
* **[[Viktor Yanukovych]]**: Former President of Ukraine [6–8].
* **[[Cecep Mustafa]]**: '''Not found in the available sources.''' [1–48]
* **[[Ferdi Raditya Akbar]]**: '''Not found in the available sources.''' [1–48]

== See Also ==

* [[International Criminal Court]]
* [[Rome Statute]]
* [[International Armed Conflict]]

== References ==
<references />

* Office of the Prosecutor, International Criminal Court, "Report on Preliminary Examination Activities 2019: Ukraine", 5 December 2019, pp. 51–57.

title: JPW-SITUATION-003
wikitext:
{{Infobox|stable_id=JPW-SITUATION-001|canonical_name=Preliminary Examination of the Situation in Venezuela (ICC)|name=Report on Preliminary Examination Activities (2019): Venezuela|type=Preliminary Examination Situation / Judicial Policy Entity|legal_basis=Rome Statute (Articles 7, 12, 14, 15, 53)|date=8 February 2018 – Ongoing|status=Preliminary Examination (Phase 2: Material Competence / Competencia Material)}}

'''Preliminary Examination of the Situation in Venezuela (ICC)''' is an independent legal and factual evaluation conducted by the Office of the Prosecutor (OTP) of the International Criminal Court (ICC) since 8 February 2018 regarding alleged crimes against humanity committed within the territory of Venezuela at least since April 2017 [].

== Summary ==
This preliminary examination focuses on alleged crimes committed in the context of anti-government demonstrations and political unrest in Venezuela at least since April 2017, taking into account the background of events since February 2014 [].

== Legal Basis ==

* [[Rome Statute]]: Article 7 (Crimes Against Humanity), Article 12 (Jurisdiction), Article 14 (Referral by a State Party), Article 15 (Communications), and Article 53 (Preliminary Examination) [].
* Official referral by 6 States Parties (Argentina, Canada, Colombia, Chile, Paraguay, Peru) dated 27 September 2018 [].

== Background ==
The escalation of mass protests in Venezuela was triggered by economic crisis, food and medical shortages, and Supreme Court rulings restricting the powers of the National Assembly. The government responded to demonstrations by activating "Plan Zamora" and deploying state security forces alongside armed pro-government civilian groups known as "colectivos" [].

== Objectives ==

* Assess whether there is a reasonable basis to believe that crimes against humanity under Article 7 of the Rome Statute have been committed in Venezuela [].
* Prepare for the admissibility assessment phase (complementarity of national judicial systems and gravity) [].

== Key Provisions ==

* **Analyzed Forms of Crimes**: Murder and injury, arbitrary deprivation of liberty, torture and ill-treatment, sexual and gender-based crimes, and persecution against political opponents [].
* **Use of Military Courts**: Over 700 civilians processed through military tribunals [].

== Implementation ==
On 28 September 2018, the ICC Presidency assigned the situation in Venezuela to Pre-Trial Chamber I. The OTP gathered evidence from OHCHR (ACNUDH), OAS (OEA), IACHR (CIDH), and civil society organizations [].

== Policy Issues ==

* Mass arbitrary detentions (over 15,000 individuals since 2014) and allegations of enforced disappearances [].
* Excessive use of force and the participation of armed civilian "colectivos" groups in suppressing civilians [].

== Relationships with Other Entities ==

* **[[Office of the Prosecutor]]**: Executing body for the preliminary examination [].
* **[[Referring States]]**: Group of 6 States Parties submitting the Article 14 referral [].
* **[[Nicolás Maduro]]**: President of Venezuela [].
* **[[Juan Guaidó]]**: Interim President (*Presidente Encargado*) of Venezuela [].
* **[[Cecep Mustafa]]**: '''Not found in the available sources.''' [].
* **[[Ferdi Raditya Akbar]]**: '''Not found in the available sources.''' [].

title: JPW-SITUATION-004

{{Infobox|stable_id=JPW-SITUATION-001|canonical_name=Preliminary Examination of the Situation in the Plurinational State of Bolivia (ICC)|official_name=Report on Preliminary Examination Activities 2020: Bolivia|type=Preliminary Examination Situation / Judicial Policy Entity|aliases=Situation in the Plurinational State of Bolivia, ICC Preliminary Examination on Bolivia|legal_basis=Rome Statute, Articles 7(1)(k) and 14(1)|date=9 September 2020 – Ongoing|status=Under Preliminary Examination (Phase 2: Subject-Matter Jurisdiction)|jurisdiction=International Criminal Law / Plurinational State of Bolivia / International Criminal Court (ICC)|institution=Office of the Prosecutor (OTP-ICC) / Pre-Trial Chamber III}}

'''Preliminary Examination of the Situation in the Plurinational State of Bolivia (ICC)''' is an independent legal and factual assessment conducted by the Office of the Prosecutor (OTP) of the International Criminal Court since 9 September 2020, following a referral by the Bolivian government concerning alleged crimes against humanity committed in Bolivian territory in August 2020.

== Summary ==
The preliminary examination was triggered by an official referral from the Bolivian government under Article 14(1) of the Rome Statute. The allegations focus on coordinated road blockades organized by supporters of the *Movimiento al Socialismo* (MAS) party that prevented the delivery of medical supplies and medical oxygen at the height of the COVID-19 pandemic.

== Legal Basis ==

* [[Rome Statute]]: Article 7(1)(k) (Crimes Against Humanity — Other Inhumane Acts) and Article 14(1) (Referral by a State Party).
* Bolivia ratified the Rome Statute on 27 June 2002 (jurisdiction effective from 1 September 2002).

== Background ==
In August 2020, MAS party leaders and supporters called for nationwide road blockades to pressure the government into setting a presidential election date. The blockades lasted nine days and paralyzed medical logistics and distribution routes.

== Objectives ==

* Assess whether the obstruction of medical oxygen supplies meets the subject-matter jurisdiction (*competencia material*) threshold under Article 7(1)(k) of the Rome Statute.
* Determine whether a reasonable basis exists to proceed to the admissibility analysis stage.

== Key Provisions ==

* '''Nature of the Alleged Crime''': Inhumane acts intentionally causing great suffering or serious injury to physical or mental health (Article 7(1)(k)).
* '''Health Impact''': More than 40 people reportedly died from lack of medical oxygen during the blockades.
* '''Nature of Conduct''': The blockades were organized through a structured, logistically coordinated system rather than spontaneous action.

== Implementation ==
The ICC Presidency assigned the Bolivia situation to Pre-Trial Chamber III on 15 September 2020. The OTP began independent collection and analysis of evidence.

== Policy Issues ==

* Bolivia has not codified crimes against humanity in its national Penal Code.
* Alleged co-optation of domestic judicial institutions, hindering internal law enforcement.

== Relationships with Other Entities ==

* '''[[Office of the Prosecutor (ICC)]]''': Organ conducting the preliminary examination.
* '''[[Pre-Trial Chamber III]]''': Chamber assigned to the situation.
* '''[[Government of Bolivia]]''': Party that submitted the Article 14 referral.
* '''[[Fatou Bensouda]]''': ICC Prosecutor who received the referral and issued the 9 September 2020 statement.
* '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': '''Not found in the available sources.'''
* '''[[Ferdi Raditya Akbar]]''': '''Not found in the available sources.'''

title: JPW-SITUATION-005
wikitext:
{{Infobox|stable_id=JPW-SITUATION-002|canonical_name=Preliminary Examination of the Situation in Colombia (ICC)|official_name=Report on Preliminary Examination Activities (2020): Colombia|type=Preliminary Examination Situation / Judicial Policy Entity|aliases=Situation in Colombia, ICC Preliminary Examination on Colombia (2020)|legal_basis=Rome Statute, Articles 7, 8, 12, 15, 53(1), 124; Ley de Justicia y Paz; Ley Estatutaria de la JEP (Ley 1957 de 2019)|date=June 2004 – Ongoing|status=Under Preliminary Examination (Phase 3: Admissibility)|jurisdiction=International Criminal Law / Republic of Colombia / International Criminal Court (ICC)|institution=Office of the Prosecutor (OTP-ICC) / Jurisdicción Especial para la Paz (JEP) / Fiscalía General de la Nación (FGN)}}

'''Preliminary Examination of the Situation in Colombia (ICC)''' is an independent legal and factual assessment conducted by the Office of the Prosecutor (OTP) of the International Criminal Court since June 2004, concerning alleged crimes against humanity and war crimes committed in Colombian territory. The examination sits at Phase 3 (Admissibility), focused on assessing the complementarity of national judicial proceedings, including the Special Jurisdiction for Peace (JEP) and the Office of the Attorney General (FGN).

== Summary ==
The examination centers on whether Colombia's domestic judicial mechanisms — the ordinary justice system, the Justice and Peace framework, and the transitional JEP — are conducting genuine proceedings against those most responsible, sufficient to render ICC intervention unnecessary.

== Legal Basis ==

* [[Rome Statute]]: Article 7 (Crimes Against Humanity), Article 8 (War Crimes), Article 12 (Jurisdiction), Article 15 (Communications), Article 53(1) (Preliminary Examination), and Article 124 (Declaration Deferring War Crimes Jurisdiction).
* Colombia ratified the Rome Statute on 5 August 2002 (crimes against humanity jurisdiction effective 1 November 2002; war crimes jurisdiction effective 1 November 2009, following the Article 124 declaration).

== Background ==
Colombia experienced a non-international armed conflict involving government forces, paramilitary groups (AUC), and rebel groups (FARC-EP and ELN). The creation of the JEP under the 2016 Peace Agreement is the central focus of the complementarity analysis.

== Objectives ==

* Assess whether national judicial proceedings meet the admissibility criteria under Article 53(1) of the Rome Statute.
* Develop a referential benchmarking framework to determine whether to close the preliminary examination or open a formal investigation.

== Key Provisions ==
OTP's analysis focuses on four principal areas:

* '''Promotion and Expansion of Paramilitary Groups''': Investigations into civilian third parties (''terceros civiles'') and non-military state agents.
* '''Forced Displacement''': Cases under the Justice and Peace Law and JEP Cases No. 002, 004, and 005.
* '''Sexual and Gender-Based Crimes''': Victim accreditation in JEP Cases No. 002, 004, and 007 (including LGBTI victims).
* '''"Falsos Positivos" (False Positives)''': Investigation of extrajudicial killings across five National Army divisions and JEP Case No. 003.

== Implementation ==
As of November 2020, the JEP had issued 35,015 decisions related to seven macro-cases and recorded 12,625 individuals who had signed submission acts (9,767 former FARC-EP members, 2,733 armed forces members, and 115 non-military state agents). The FGN was managing 2,314 active "falsos positivos" cases against 10,949 military personnel, with 1,749 convictions.

== Policy Issues ==

* Challenges in inter-institutional coordination among domestic judicial bodies, and alleged de facto suspension of FGN investigations in cases falling under JEP jurisdiction.
* Rising violence in rural areas and threats against human rights defenders following the Peace Agreement.

== Relationships with Other Entities ==

* '''[[Office of the Prosecutor (ICC)]]''': Organ conducting the preliminary examination.
* '''[[Jurisdicción Especial para la Paz]]''' (Special Jurisdiction for Peace): Transitional special justice system.
* '''[[Fiscalía General de la Nación]]''' (Office of the Attorney General): Ordinary justice enforcement body.
* '''[[James Stewart]]''': ICC Deputy Prosecutor who delivered a presentation on complementarity and transitional justice in Bogotá on 29 October 2020.
* '''[[Rodrigo Pérez Alzate]]''' (alias "Julián Bolívar"): Former leader of the *Bloque Central Bolívar* paramilitary group, facing charges over 702 incidents of forced displacement and 84 counts of gender-based violence under the Justice and Peace Law system.
* '''[[David Char Navas]]''': Former Colombian congressman whose case is handled by the JEP's Chamber for the Definition of Legal Situations, in relation to ties with the *Bloque Norte* paramilitary group.
* '''[[Álvaro Ashton Giraldo]]''': Former official undergoing review and evidence collection at the JEP concerning links to paramilitary groups.
* '''[[Ramiro Suárez Corzo]]''': Former official requested by the JEP to submit a detailed truth-contribution commitment regarding alleged killings carried out by the AUC in 2003.
* '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': '''Not found in the available sources.'''
* '''[[Ferdi Raditya Akbar]]''': '''Not found in the available sources.'''
