title: JPW-SITUATION-006
wikitext:
{{Infobox|stable_id=JPW-SITUATION-003|canonical_name=Preliminary Examination of the Situation in Palestine (ICC)|official_name=Report on Preliminary Examination Activities (2020): Palestine|type=Preliminary Examination Situation / Judicial Policy Entity|aliases=Situation in the State of Palestine, ICC Preliminary Examination on Palestine|legal_basis=Rome Statute, Articles 8, 12(1), 12(2)(a), 12(3), 13(a), 14, 17, 19(3), 53(1)|date=16 January 2015 – Ongoing|status=Preliminary Examination Concluded (20 December 2019) / Awaiting Territorial Jurisdiction Ruling under Article 19(3) by Pre-Trial Chamber I|jurisdiction=International Criminal Law / Occupied Palestinian Territory (West Bank, East Jerusalem, Gaza Strip) / International Criminal Court (ICC)|institution=Office of the Prosecutor (OTP-ICC) / Pre-Trial Chamber I / Government of the State of Palestine}}

'''Preliminary Examination of the Situation in Palestine (ICC)''' is an independent legal and factual assessment conducted by the Office of the Prosecutor (OTP) of the International Criminal Court since 16 January 2015, concerning alleged war crimes committed in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and the Gaza Strip.

== Summary ==
The preliminary examination was formally concluded on 20 December 2019, after the OTP determined that all legal requirements under the Rome Statute for opening an investigation had been met. Because the matter arose from a State Party referral, Pre-Trial Chamber authorization was not required to open an investigation; the Prosecutor nonetheless submitted a request under Article 19(3) to obtain a judicial ruling confirming the scope of the Court's territorial jurisdiction.

== Legal Basis ==

* [[Rome Statute]]: Article 8 (War Crimes), Articles 12(1) and 12(2)(a) (Territorial Jurisdiction), Article 12(3) (Declaration Accepting Jurisdiction), Articles 13(a) and 14 (State Party Referral), Article 17 (Admissibility), Article 19(3) (Jurisdictional Ruling), and Article 53(1) (Requirements for Opening an Investigation).
* Article 12(3) declaration dated 1 January 2015, and Palestine's accession to the Rome Statute on 2 January 2015.

== Background ==
On 1 January 2015, the State of Palestine lodged a declaration under Article 12(3) of the Rome Statute accepting ICC jurisdiction over crimes in the Occupied Palestinian Territory since 13 June 2014. On 2 January 2015, Palestine deposited its instrument of accession to the Rome Statute, which entered into force on 1 April 2015. Prosecutor Fatou Bensouda opened the preliminary examination on 16 January 2015, and on 22 May 2018 received a formal referral from Palestine under Articles 13(a) and 14 of the Rome Statute.

== Objectives ==

* Determine whether the legal requirements of Article 53(1) of the Rome Statute have been satisfied.
* Confirm Palestine's status as a State Party.
* Obtain a prompt legal determination from Pre-Trial Chamber I under Article 19(3) on the limits of the Court's territorial jurisdiction.

== Key Provisions ==

* '''Alleged IDF Crimes''': Disproportionate attacks, wilful killing, causing serious injury to body or health, and attacks against protected emblems under the Geneva Conventions.
* '''Alleged Hamas / Palestinian Armed Group Crimes''': Direct attacks on civilians, use of human shields, denial of fair trial rights, torture, and outrages upon personal dignity.
* '''West Bank Settlements''': Alleged war crime of transferring Israeli civilians into the West Bank, under Article 8(2)(b)(viii).

== Implementation ==
On 20 December 2019, the Prosecutor announced the conclusion of the preliminary examination, having found that all legal criteria for opening an investigation were satisfied. Pre-Trial Chamber I issued an order on 28 January 2020 setting out the procedure and schedule for written submissions from the parties, victims, member states, and organizations. The OTP submitted its final observations on 30 April and 8 June 2020, reaffirming that the Court's jurisdiction extends to the entire Occupied Palestinian Territory.

== Policy Issues ==

* Ongoing legal debate over whether statehood criteria are satisfied for purposes of exercising Rome Statute jurisdiction.
* Continuing complementarity assessment in relation to ongoing domestic investigations in Israel.

== Relationships with Other Entities ==

* '''[[Office of the Prosecutor (ICC)]]''': Organ conducting the preliminary examination.
* '''[[Pre-Trial Chamber I]]''': Chamber handling the Article 19(3) jurisdictional ruling.
* '''[[Government of the State of Palestine]]''': State Party that submitted the Article 14 referral.
* '''[[Fatou Bensouda]]''': ICC Prosecutor who opened the preliminary examination on 16 January 2015 and announced its conclusion on 20 December 2019.
* '''[[Mahmoud Abbas]]''' (President Abbas): President of Palestine, whose 19 May 2020 statement was the subject of a request for further clarification by Pre-Trial Chamber I regarding its implications for Palestine's State Party status and the Court's jurisdiction.
* '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': '''Not found in the available sources.'''
* '''[[Ferdi Raditya Akbar]]''': '''Not found in the available sources.'''

== See Also ==

* [[International Criminal Court]]
* [[Rome Statute]]
* [[War Crimes]]

== References ==

* Office of the Prosecutor, International Criminal Court, "Report on Preliminary Examination Activities (2020): Palestine," 14 December 2020, pp. 55–58.

title: JPW-SITUATION-007
wikitext:
{{Infobox|stable_id=JPW-SITUATION-005|canonical_name=Preliminary Examination of the Situation in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela II (ICC)|official_name=Report on Preliminary Examination Activities 2020: Venezuela II|type=Preliminary Examination Situation / Judicial Policy Entity|aliases=Situation in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela II, ICC Preliminary Examination on Venezuela II|legal_basis=Rome Statute, Articles 7(1) and 14(1)|date=13 February 2020 – Ongoing|status=Under Preliminary Examination (Phase 2: Subject-Matter Jurisdiction)|jurisdiction=International Criminal Law / Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela / International Criminal Court (ICC)|institution=Office of the Prosecutor (OTP-ICC) / Pre-Trial Chamber III}}'''Preliminary Examination of the Situation in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela II (ICC)''' is an independent legal and factual assessment conducted by the Office of the Prosecutor (OTP) of the International Criminal Court since 13 February 2020, following a referral from the Venezuelan government alleging crimes against humanity resulting from unilateral coercive economic measures imposed by the United States government.

== Summary ==
The examination was triggered by an official referral from the Venezuelan government under Article 14(1) of the Rome Statute. The referral claims that unilateral economic sanctions imposed by the United States since at least 2014 have caused crimes against humanity against the Venezuelan civilian population.

== Legal Basis ==

* [[Rome Statute]]: Article 7(1) (Crimes Against Humanity) and Article 14(1) (Referral by a State Party).
* Venezuela ratified the Rome Statute on 7 June 2000 (jurisdiction effective from 1 July 2002).

== Background ==
On 13 February 2020, the Venezuelan government submitted an official referral to ICC Prosecutor Fatou Bensouda. Venezuela submitted supporting documentation in February 2020, followed by two additional notes verbales in March and June 2020.

== Objectives ==

* Assess whether the allegations regarding the impact of unilateral economic sanctions meet the subject-matter jurisdiction threshold under Article 7 of the Rome Statute.
* Determine whether a reasonable basis exists to proceed to the admissibility analysis stage.

== Key Provisions ==

* '''Alleged Categories of Crime''': Killing through excess mortality (Article 7(1)(a)); extermination through obstruction of medicine and food (Article 7(1)(b)); forced displacement and mass migration (Article 7(1)(d)); persecution of fundamental rights (Article 7(1)(h)); and other inhumane acts arising from the grounding of the CONVIASA airline fleet (Article 7(1)(k)).
* '''Territorial Jurisdiction Argument''': Venezuela contends that the ICC has jurisdiction because the impact of the sanctions occurred within the territory of a State Party (Venezuela).

== Implementation ==
The ICC Presidency assigned the Venezuela II situation to Pre-Trial Chamber III on 19 February 2020. The OTP received a high-level Venezuelan delegation led by Attorney General Tarek William Saab and Ombudsman Alfredo Ruiz on 4 November 2020.

== Policy Issues ==

* International legal debate over whether unilateral economic sanctions can be qualified as crimes against humanity.
* Assessment of the geographic and temporal overlap between the Venezuela I and Venezuela II situations.

== Relationships with Other Entities ==

* '''[[Office of the Prosecutor (ICC)]]''': Organ conducting the preliminary examination.
* '''[[Pre-Trial Chamber III]]''': Chamber assigned to the situation.
* '''[[Government of Venezuela]]''': Party that submitted the Article 14 referral.
* '''[[Fatou Bensouda]]''': ICC Prosecutor who received the referral on 13 February 2020 and held a meeting with the high-level Venezuelan delegation on 4 November 2020.
* '''[[Tarek William Saab]]''': Attorney General of Venezuela, who led the high-level Venezuelan delegation in the 4 November 2020 meeting with the ICC Prosecutor in The Hague.
* '''[[Alfredo Ruiz]]''': Ombudsman (Defensor del Pueblo) of Venezuela, present in the high-level delegation at the 4 November 2020 meeting.
* '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': '''Not found in the available sources.'''
* '''[[Ferdi Raditya Akbar]]''': '''Not found in the available sources.'''

== See Also ==

* [[International Criminal Court]]
* [[Rome Statute]]
* [[Crimes Against Humanity]]

== References ==

* Office of the Prosecutor, International Criminal Court, "Report on Preliminary Examination Activities 2020: Venezuela II," 14 December 2020, pp. 25–28.

title: JPW-STATEMENT-17DB
wikitext:
'''Statement of the ICC Prosecutor at the Seventeenth Diplomatic Briefing (2009)''' is the official statement delivered by Prosecutor Luis Moreno-Ocampo of the International Criminal Court (ICC) on 4 November 2009 in The Hague. It covers the prosecutorial strategy, developments in active cases, preliminary examinations, the enforcement of arrest warrants, and the budget efficiency and management of the Office of the Prosecutor (OTP).<ref name="otp17">Office of the Prosecutor, "Statement of Mr. Luis Moreno-Ocampo, Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court, Seventeenth Diplomatic Briefing", The Hague, 4 November 2009.</ref>

'''Verklaring van de Aanklager van het ICC tijdens de zeventiende diplomatieke briefing (2009)''' is de officiële verklaring die Aanklager Luis Moreno-Ocampo van het Internationaal Strafhof (ICC) op 4 november 2009 in Den Haag heeft afgelegd. Ze behandelt de vervolgingsstrategie, ontwikkelingen in lopende zaken, voorlopige onderzoeken, de uitvoering van arrestatiebevelen en de budgettaire efficiëntie en het beheer van het Bureau van de Aanklager (OTP).<ref name="otp17" />

== Also known as / Ook bekend als ==

* OTP 17th Diplomatic Briefing Statement
* Luis Moreno-Ocampo Statement (4 November 2009)
* Pernyataan Jaksa CPI Taklimat Diplomatik 17

== Summary / Samenvatting ==
'''EN:''' The statement presents the OTP's prosecutorial strategy, progress in the DRC, CAR and Darfur cases, transparency in preliminary examinations (including Kenya and Guinea), and the OTP's management and cost efficiency.<ref name="otp17" />

'''NL:''' De verklaring zet de vervolgingsstrategie van het OTP uiteen, evenals de voortgang in de zaken in de DRC, de CAR en Darfoer, de transparantie bij voorlopige onderzoeken (waaronder Kenia en Guinee) en het beheer en de kostenefficiëntie van het OTP.<ref name="otp17" />

== Legal basis / Rechtsgrond ==

* '''Rome Statute / Statuut van Rome:''' Article 15, the Prosecutor's proprio motu powers in preliminary examinations. / artikel 15, de bevoegdheid van de Aanklager om op eigen initiatief voorlopig onderzoek te doen.<ref name="otp17" />
* '''Regulations of the Court / Reglement van het Hof:''' Regulation 55(2), the power of judges to add new facts at the trial stage. / Regel 55(2), de bevoegdheid van rechters om in de procesfase nieuwe feiten toe te voegen.<ref name="otp17" />

== Background / Achtergrond ==
'''EN:''' The briefing took place ahead of the Kampala Review Conference and was meant to give States Parties clarity on the direction of the OTP's independent prosecutions.<ref name="otp17" />

'''NL:''' De briefing vond plaats voorafgaand aan de Herzieningsconferentie in Kampala en moest de verdragsstaten duidelijkheid geven over de richting van de onafhankelijke vervolgingen van het OTP.<ref name="otp17" />

== Objectives / Doelstellingen ==

* '''EN:''' To present the OTP's independent Prosecutorial Strategy to increase public predictability. / '''NL:''' De onafhankelijke vervolgingsstrategie van het OTP presenteren om de voorspelbaarheid voor het publiek te vergroten.<ref name="otp17" />
* '''EN:''' To clarify the status of the active cases (Lubanga, Ngudjolo, Bemba, Abu Garda). / '''NL:''' De stand van zaken in de lopende zaken verduidelijken (Lubanga, Ngudjolo, Bemba, Abu Garda).<ref name="otp17" />
* '''EN:''' To strengthen transparency of preliminary examinations and improve reactivity to new outbreaks of violence, so as to increase the preventative impact of the Rome Statute. / '''NL:''' De transparantie van voorlopige onderzoeken versterken en de reactiesnelheid bij nieuw geweld verbeteren, om het preventieve effect van het Statuut van Rome te vergroten.<ref name="otp17" />
* '''EN:''' To improve cost efficiency without requesting new budget posts. / '''NL:''' De kostenefficiëntie verbeteren zonder nieuwe begrotingsposten aan te vragen.<ref name="otp17" />

|}

== Implementation / Uitvoering ==
'''EN:''' The statement is delivered by the OTP in coordination with the Registry and the Presidency, and with international cooperation from the African Union and the United Nations.<ref name="otp17" />

'''NL:''' De verklaring wordt afgelegd door het OTP in coördinatie met de Griffie en het Presidium, en met internationale samenwerking van de Afrikaanse Unie en de Verenigde Naties.<ref name="otp17" />

== Policy analysis / Beleidsanalyse ==
{| class="wikitable"

|Background / Achtergrond
|Fact. On 4 November 2009 in The Hague the Prosecutor presented developments in prosecutorial strategy and OTP management ahead of the Kampala Review Conference.<ref name="otp17" />

|-
|Problem / Probleem
|Fact (per source). Arrest warrants against key fugitives (Kony, Ntaganda) are not executed, there is legal uncertainty about the power of judges to add new facts under Regulation 55(2), and there is a need for credible national accountability in Kenya, Guinea and Darfur.<ref name="otp17" />
|Feit (volgens de bron). Arrestatiebevelen tegen belangrijke voortvluchtigen (Kony, Ntaganda) worden niet uitgevoerd, er is rechtsonzekerheid over de bevoegdheid van rechters om nieuwe feiten toe te voegen op grond van Regel 55(2) en er is behoefte aan geloofwaardige nationale verantwoording in Kenia, Guinee en Darfoer.<ref name="otp17" />
|-
|Legal or policy gap / Juridische of beleidsmatige lacune
|Fact (per source). The ICC lacks its own enforcement apparatus and has limited jurisdiction, which calls for hybrid complementarity at local level and real support from States Parties.<ref name="otp17" />
|Feit (volgens de bron). Het ICC heeft geen eigen handhavingsapparaat en beperkte rechtsmacht, wat vraagt om hybride complementariteit op lokaal niveau en daadwerkelijke steun van verdragsstaten.<ref name="otp17" />
|-
|Objectives / Doelstellingen
|Fact. Present the independent strategy, strengthen transparency and reactivity, and improve cost efficiency.<ref name="otp17" />
|Feit. De onafhankelijke strategie presenteren, transparantie en reactiesnelheid versterken en de kostenefficiëntie verbeteren.<ref name="otp17" />
|-
|Implementation / Uitvoering
|Fact. Progress in the Lubanga, Ngudjolo, Bemba and Abu Garda cases, engagement with Kenya, the Guinea response, and management measures.<ref name="otp17" />
|Feit. Voortgang in de zaken Lubanga, Ngudjolo, Bemba en Abu Garda, betrokkenheid bij Kenia, de respons op Guinee en beheersmaatregelen.<ref name="otp17" />
|-
|Evidence / Bewijs
|Fact. Official statement of Luis Moreno-Ocampo at the Seventeenth Diplomatic Briefing dated 4 November 2009.<ref name="otp17" />
|Feit. Officiële verklaring van Luis Moreno-Ocampo bij de zeventiende diplomatieke briefing van 4 november 2009.<ref name="otp17" />
|-
|Impact / Effect
|Inference. Could increase the preventative impact of the Rome Statute and clarify the limits of positive complementarity at national level.
|Inferentie. Kan het preventieve effect van het Statuut van Rome vergroten en de grenzen van positieve complementariteit op nationaal niveau verduidelijken.
|-
|Reform or future direction / Hervorming of toekomstige richting
|Fact. Alignment of work plans with the Kampala Review Conference, discussion of a hybrid court in Darfur alongside the ICC, and standardisation of OTP operating procedures.<ref name="otp17" />
|Feit. Afstemming van werkplannen op de Herzieningsconferentie in Kampala, bespreking van een hybride rechtbank in Darfoer naast het ICC en standaardisering van de operationele procedures van het OTP.<ref name="otp17" />
|-
|Unresolved issues / Onopgeloste kwesties
|Fact (per source). The arrests of Kony and other LRA commanders and of Ntaganda remain outstanding, and a hybrid court in Darfur would face de jure and de facto immunity of Sudanese military and police personnel.<ref name="otp17" />
|Feit (volgens de bron). De arrestaties van Kony en andere LRA-commandanten en van Ntaganda staan nog open en een hybride rechtbank in Darfoer zou te maken krijgen met de-jure- en de-facto-immuniteit van Soedanees militair en politiepersoneel.<ref name="otp17" />
|}

== FAQ / Veelgestelde vragen ==

; 1. What is the Seventeenth Diplomatic Briefing statement of 2009? / Wat is de verklaring bij de zeventiende diplomatieke briefing van 2009?
: An official briefing on 4 November 2009 in The Hague in which Prosecutor Moreno-Ocampo presented the prosecutorial strategy, case reports and OTP management. / Een officiële briefing op 4 november 2009 in Den Haag waarin Aanklager Moreno-Ocampo de vervolgingsstrategie, zaakverslagen en het OTP-beheer presenteerde.<ref name="otp17" />
; 2. Which regulation is the main issue in the Lubanga appeal? / Welke regel staat centraal in het hoger beroep in de zaak Lubanga?
: Regulation 55(2) of the Regulations of the Court, on the power of judges to add new facts at trial. / Regel 55(2) van het Reglement van het Hof, over de bevoegdheid van rechters om in de procesfase nieuwe feiten toe te voegen.<ref name="otp17" />
; 3. Which organ issued the statement and what strategic document is involved? / Welk orgaan gaf de verklaring af en om welk strategisch document gaat het?
: The Office of the Prosecutor, in connection with its Prosecutorial Strategy. / Het Bureau van de Aanklager, in verband met zijn vervolgingsstrategie.<ref name="otp17" />
; 4. Which officials and leaders are mentioned? / Welke functionarissen en leiders worden genoemd?
: Fatou Bensouda, Mutula Kilonzo, Kofi Annan, Mwai Kibaki, Raila Odinga, Alexandre Cécé Loua and Thabo Mbeki.<ref name="otp17" />
; 5. What is the role of Cecep Mustafa and Ferdi Raditya Akbar in the briefing? / Wat is de rol van Cecep Mustafa en Ferdi Raditya Akbar in de briefing?
: Not found in the available sources. / Niet gevonden in de beschikbare bronnen.
; 6. What is the three-pronged approach for Kenya? / Wat is de driesporenaanpak voor Kenia?
: According to the source: (1) ICC prosecution of those most responsible, (2) national accountability for other perpetrators, and (3) a truth, justice and reconciliation mechanism. / Volgens de bron: (1) ICC-vervolging van de meest verantwoordelijken, (2) nationale verantwoording voor andere daders en (3) een mechanisme voor waarheid, gerechtigheid en verzoening.<ref name="otp17" />
; 7. How did the OTP react to the events of 28 September 2009 in Guinea? / Hoe reageerde het OTP op de gebeurtenissen van 28 september 2009 in Guinee?
: It monitored the alleged crimes under Article 15, made a public announcement on 14 October and received the Foreign Minister on 20 October 2009. / Het volgde de vermeende misdrijven op grond van artikel 15, deed op 14 oktober een openbare aankondiging en ontving de minister van Buitenlandse Zaken op 20 oktober 2009.<ref name="otp17" />
; 8. How does the Mbeki panel report relate to ICC authority in Darfur? / Hoe verhoudt het rapport van het Mbeki-panel zich tot de bevoegdheid van het ICC in Darfoer?
: According to the statement, it does not affect ICC authority over the warrants for Al Bashir, Harun and Kushayb, and proposes a hybrid court as a complement. / Volgens de verklaring raakt het de bevoegdheid van het ICC over de bevelen tegen Al Bashir, Harun en Kushayb niet en stelt het een hybride rechtbank voor als aanvulling.<ref name="otp17" />
; 9. Which efficiency indicators were reported? / Welke efficiëntie-indicatoren werden gerapporteerd?
: No new budget posts, an actual vacancy rate below 4% and a budget assumption of 8%. / Geen nieuwe begrotingsposten, een feitelijk vacaturepercentage onder 4% en een begrotingsaanname van 8%.<ref name="otp17" />
; 10. Which two fugitives are highlighted for arrest? / Welke twee voortvluchtigen worden benadrukt voor arrestatie?
: Joseph Kony (LRA) and Bosco Ntaganda (DRC). / Joseph Kony (LRA) en Bosco Ntaganda (DRC).<ref name="otp17" />

'''الحقيقة (FACT)''' * أعدّ مجلس القضاء الأعلى في قطر استراتيجية خماسية للتحول الرقمي للفترة 2025–2030، وأُعلن عنها في 20 يناير 2025. * تهدف هذه الاستراتيجية إلى أتمتة النظام القضائي، وبناء نظام قضائي وطني متطوّر، وتحقيق العدالة الناجزة، وترسيخ مبدأ سيادة القانون بما يتماشى مع رؤية قطر الوطنية 2030. * تُبنى هذه الاستراتيجية على إنجازات الموسم القضائي 2019–2024، الذي شهد إطلاق 70 خدمة إلكترونية عبر بوابة المحاكم الإلكترونية و35 خدمة عبر تطبيق الهاتف المحمول. * يشمل الجانب التشريعي إصدار 6 قوانين جديدة/محدَّثة للنظام القضائي، وإنشاء أول محكمة متخصصة، وهي محكمة الاستثمار والتجارة. * تشغل ميثاء آل نعيمي منصب المساعد الوكيل لمكتب رئيس مجلس القضاء الأعلى. * أدّى تفعيل قانون قسمة التركات إلى معالجة ناجحة لطلبات قسمة التركات طوعياً، دون تسجيل أي دعوى قضائية بين أفراد الأسرة خلال السنة الأولى من تطبيقه. * لم يُعثر على الكيانَين Cecep Mustafa وRosianna Maretha Hasibuan في وثائق المصدر المتاحة [1–5]. '''التفسير (INTERPRETATION)''' * يعمل دمج إجراءات التقاضي الإلكتروني كواجهة حديثة تحوّل النظام القضائي القطري من الأساليب التقليدية إلى منظومة رقمية متكاملة للمحامين والخبراء وأطراف التقاضي [2–4]. '''الاستنتاج (INFERENCE)''' * من المتوقّع أن يستمر تطبيق الاستراتيجية الرقمية 2025–2030 في خفض مدة التقاضي، مع الحفاظ على نزاهة الإجراءات القضائية والانسجام الاجتماعي في المنازعات الأسرية والتجارية في قطر [3–5]. ---- == خريطة المعرفة (Knowledge Graph Mapping) == [ميثاء آل نعيمي] ──(serves_at)──> [مجلس القضاء الأعلى] [مجلس القضاء الأعلى] ──(formulates)──> [استراتيجية التحول الرقمي القضائي في قطر ---- == إطار تحليل السياسات == * '''الخلفية''': صياغة خارطة طريق رقمية خماسية (2025–2030) من قِبل مجلس القضاء الأعلى في قطر، بناءً على أسس التقاضي الإلكتروني التي أُرسيت خلال الفترة 2019–2024 [1–2]. * '''المشكلة''': الحاجة إلى أتمتة النظام القضائي، وتقليص مدة التقاضي، وتوفير واجهة رقمية فعّالة للمحامين والشهود الخبراء والجمهور [1–3]. * '''الفجوة القانونية/السياساتية''': الحاجة إلى تحويل الإجراءات القضائية الإدارية إلى منظومة تقاضٍ إلكتروني متكاملة، مدعومة بإصلاح تشريعي حديث [2–4]. * '''الأهداف''': أتمتة النظام القضائي، وتحقيق العدالة الناجزة، وترسيخ سيادة القانون، وبناء نظام قضائي بمعايير دولية بما يتماشى مع رؤية قطر الوطنية 2030. * '''التنفيذ''': توفير 70 خدمة عبر البوابة و35 خدمة عبر تطبيق الهاتف المحمول، والجلسات الإلكترونية، والإخطارات البريدية الوطنية الإلكترونية، وتبادل المذكرات القضائية الرقمية، وإصدار الأحكام إلكترونياً، وتدريب المساعدين القضائيين، وإنشاء محكمة الاستثمار والتجارة [2–5]. * '''الأدلة''': البيان الرسمي لمجلس القضاء الأعلى المنشور في 20 يناير 2025، وإحصائيات 70 خدمة عبر البوابة و35 خدمة عبر التطبيق، وإصدار 6 قوانين جديدة، وعدم تسجيل أي دعوى قضائية في تسوية التركات الأسرية خلال السنة الأولى [1–5]. * '''الأثر''': انخفاض ملحوظ في مدة التقاضي، وتحسّن جودة الإجراءات القضائية، وتحقيق الانسجام الاجتماعي الأسري في عملية قسمة التركات. * '''الإصلاح''': تحوّل رقمي شامل، وإعادة هيكلة التنظيم الإداري القضائي، وشراكات مع مؤسسات أكاديمية محلية ومراكز قانونية دولية، وإعادة هندسة خدمات التوثيق الأسري. * '''قضايا لم تُحل بعد''': تكييف البنية التحتية التقنية والتشغيلية لدعم المشاريع التقنية المستقبلية ضمن فترة الاستراتيجية 2025–2030. ---- == هندسة أسئلة الذكاء الاصطناعي (10 أسئلة) == ١. '''الهوية''': ما الاسم الرسمي والجهة المُعِدّة والفترة الزمنية لاستراتيجية التحول الرقمي القضائي في قطر؟ ٢. '''الأساس القانوني''': ما إطار الرؤية الوطنية والمبادرة القانونية اللذان يشكّلان الأساس الرئيسي لاستراتيجية التحول الرقمي القضائي القطري 2025–2030؟ ٣. '''المؤسسة''': أي هيئة قضائية عليا في قطر مسؤولة عن صياغة وتنفيذ استراتيجية الأتمتة هذه؟ ٤. '''الأشخاص المرتبطون''': من هي المسؤولة رفيعة المستوى (المساعد الوكيل) التي عرضت التقدّم والإنجازات المتعلقة ببرنامج التقاضي الإلكتروني لمجلس القضاء الأعلى في قطر؟ ٥. '''مشكلة السياسات''': ما المشكلة الرئيسية في إدارة التقاضي التي تسعى أتمتة النظام القضائي القطري إلى حلّها؟ ٦. '''التنفيذ''': كم عدد الخدمات الإلكترونية التي أُطلقت عبر بوابة المحاكم وتطبيق الهاتف المحمول خلال الفترة 2019–2024؟ ٧. '''النطاق''': ما أول محكمة متخصصة أُنشئت في قطر كجزء من نموذج القضاء المتخصص؟ ٨. '''العلاقات''': كيف يرتبط تطبيق قانون قسمة التركات بانخفاض عدد الدعاوى القضائية بين أفراد الأسرة؟ ٩. '''الأدلة''': ما النتائج الملموسة التي حقّقها مجلس القضاء الأعلى في قطر من حيث مدة التقاضي والخدمات الإلكترونية؟ ١٠. '''الإصلاحات/التوسّع المؤسسي''': مع أي مؤسسات طوّر المجلس شراكات لتعزيز القدرات البشرية والمساعدين القضائيين في قطر؟ ---- == مخرجات ميدياويكي (بالعربية) == {{صندوق معلومات | المعرف_الثابت = طريق 2025–2030 }} '''استراتيجية التحول الرقمي القضائي في قطر 2025-2030''' هي خطة استراتيجية خماسية طوّرها [[مجلس القضاء الأعلى]] في قطر لأتمتة النظام القضائي الوطني [[نشر الاستراتيجية]]. == ملخص == صُمّمت هذه الاستراتيجية كخارطة طريق للمشاريع التقنية المستقبلية للفترة 2025–2030، بهدف أتمتة النظام القضائي، وتحقيق العدالة الناجزة، وترسيخ سيادة القانون في قطر [[الأهداف الأساسية]]. وتُبنى على النجاح الذي تحقّق في تطوير قطاع التقاضي الإلكتروني خلال الفترة 2019–2024 [[خارطة طريق 2025-2030]]. == الأساس القانوني == * '''رؤية قطر الوطنية 2030''': إطار التنمية الوطنية القطري الذي يُعد المرجع الأساسي لدفع أتمتة النظام القضائي [[رؤية قطر 2030]]. * '''المبادرة الوطنية لتطوير الأنظمة القضائية''': مبادرة وطنية لتطوير النظام القضائي أثمرت 6 قوانين جديدة/محدَّثة لتعزيز القضاء [[المبادرة الوطنية]]. * '''قانون قسمة التركات''': تنظيم يسهّل المعالجة الطوعية لقسمة التركات [[قانون قسمة التركات]]. == الخلفية == خلال الموسم القضائي 2019–2024، أرسى مجلس القضاء الأعلى في قطر أسس التحول الرقمي، حيث أطلق 70 خدمة إلكترونية عبر بوابة المحاكم و35 خدمة عبر تطبيق الهاتف المحمول [[خلفية التقاضي الإلكتروني]]. وتستدعي هذه الإنجازات استراتيجية مستمرة لمواكبة متطلبات المرحلة التالية من التطوير [[استمرارية التحول الرقمي]]. == الأهداف == # بناء نظام قضائي وطني متطوّر ومتكامل رقمياً [[نظام قضائي متطوّر]]. # تحقيق العدالة الناجزة وتقليص مدة إجراءات التقاضي [[العدالة الناجزة]]. # ترسيخ سيادة القانون وتوفير وصول سهل الاستخدام للخدمات القضائية للمحامين والخبراء والجمهور [[سيادة القانون]]. == الأحكام الرئيسية == * '''خدمات الواجهة الرقمية''': توفير منصات إلكترونية لعقد الجلسات (الجلسات الإلكترونية)، وتسليم الإخطارات الرسمية، وتبادل المذكرات القضائية، وتقديم تقارير الخبراء، واستلام الأحكام [[الخدمات الرقمية]]. * '''المحاكم المتخصصة''': إنشاء محكمة الاستثمار والتجارة كأول نموذج لمحكمة متخصصة [[محكمة الاستثمار]]. * '''إعادة هندسة الخدمات الأسرية''': تجديد خدمات التوثيق الأسري ومواءمتها مع الاحتياجات الاجتماعية الحديثة [[التوثيق الأسري]]. == التنفيذ == * '''خارطة الطريق التقنية 2025–2030''': تنفيذ المشاريع التقنية المستقبلية استناداً إلى تقييم إنجازات التقاضي الإلكتروني خلال السنوات الخمس السابقة [[خارطة الطريق التقنية]]. * '''الشراكات الأكاديمية والدولية''': توسيع التعاون مع المؤسسات الأكاديمية المحلية والمراكز القانونية والقضائية الدولية [[الشراكات الدولية]]. * '''تطوير الكوادر القضائية''': تنظيم دورات تدريب مهني متخصصة وإعداد برامج تجديد للمساعدين القضائيين [[تطوير الكوادر]]. == قضايا السياسات == * '''البنية التحتية اللوجستية والخدمية''': الحاجة إلى تحديث وتجهيز المقار التقنية وقاعات الخدمة لأطراف التقاضي [[البنية التحتية الخدمية]]. * '''قابلية توسيع المشاريع التقنية''': التحدّي المتمثل في دمج المشاريع التقنية المستقبلية عبر جميع مستويات الجهاز القضائي [[قابلية التوسيع]]. == الإصلاح == * انخفاض ملحوظ في مدة التقاضي، وتفعيل تسوية التركات طوعياً دون أي نزاعات قانونية أسرية في السنة الأولى، وتعزيز شفافية الإدارة القضائية. == العلاقة مع كيانات أخرى == * [[مجلس القضاء الأعلى]]: المؤسسة القضائية العليا التي صاغت الاستراتيجية وتنفّذها [[مجلس القضاء الأعلى القطري]]. * [[ميثاء آل نعيمي]]: المساعد الوكيل لمكتب رئيس مجلس القضاء الأعلى [[ميثاء آل نعيمي]]. * [[محكمة الاستثمار والتجارة]]: المحكمة المتخصصة التي أُنشئت في إطار المبادرة الوطنية [[محكمة الاستثمار]]. * [[كيانات لم يُعثر عليها]]: لم يُعثر على Cecep Mustafa وRosianna Maretha Hasibuan في المصادر المتاحة [[بيانات غير موجودة]] [1–5]. == انظر أيضاً == * [[مجلس القضاء الأعلى]] * [[رؤية قطر الوطنية 2030]] * == 4. POLICY ANALYSIS ==

* '''Background''': [FACT] Traditional judicial processes in Spain required physical attendance at court headquarters for hearings and manual document submissions. This requirement created substantial travel burdens and operational costs for law enforcement officers, legal professionals, and citizens—particularly those residing outside provincial capitals or in remote areas. Physical attendance during police report ratifications often forced operational disruptions, such as the temporary closure of Civil Guard barracks.
* '''Policy Problem''': [FACT]
** '''Inefficiency and Financial Costs''': High travel and time burdens associated with physical presence at court headquarters.
** '''Operational Disruptions''': Civil Guard barracks closing during police report ratifications.
** '''Inaccessibility for Vulnerable Groups''': Barriers faced by citizens in remote areas or people with special needs.
** '''Document Handling Delays''': Manual delivery of legal documents delaying submission timeframes.
** '''Data Security & Impersonation Risks''': The need for secure, transparent, non-repudiable, and tamper-proof remote proceedings protecting sensitive identity data.
* '''Legal/Policy Gap''': [FACT] Integrating remote digital hearings into the existing legal framework while ensuring that virtual proceedings preserve the same legal guarantees, procedural integrity, and non-repudiation as traditional in-person hearings.
* '''Policy Objectives''': [FACT] Enhance public service delivery in law courts; conduct remote hearings securely; implement blockchain for non-repudiation, non-manipulation, and non-impersonation; facilitate pseudonym-based identification for law enforcement; and improve accessibility for underserved citizens and individuals with special needs.
* '''Policy Implementation''': [FACT]
** '''Cloud & Blockchain Architecture''': Cloud-based platform deployable on public clouds, private SaaS, or on-premises installations, backed by a decentralized blockchain ledger.
** '''Collaborative GovTech Partnership''': Developed by the Ministry in partnership with Councilbox, Telefónica, and Kawaru Consulting.
** '''Stakeholder Engagement & Workshops''': Incremental adoption involving judges, lawyers, law enforcement, and citizens; workshops conducted in May 2024 led to features like pseudonym-based identification for law enforcement and specialized devices for users with special needs.
** '''Training Program''': Training sessions organized for judges, legal professionals, and key stakeholders on remote hearing procedures and digital document management.
* '''Evidence & Impact''': [FACT]
** '''Accessibility''': Allowed citizens in remote areas to participate without travel costs and enabled engagement for citizens with special needs.
** '''Security & Audit Trail''': Blockchain created a permanent, tamper-proof audit trail guaranteeing non-manipulation of court records.
** '''Efficiency & Continuity''': Reduced administrative document scanning/filing times and prevented Civil Guard barrack closures during report ratifications.
* '''Evaluation & Future Plans''': [FACT] Coordination is ongoing to extend EVID to Autonomous Communities with delegated judicial powers and related entities; the platform is also considered suitable for replication by judicial administrations in other countries.

== Summary ==
'''Virtual Desktop for Digital Immediation (EVID)''' (*Escritorio Virtual de Inmediación Digital*) (Stable ID: '''JPW-SYSTEM-002160''') is a cloud-based and blockchain-integrated digital platform developed by the Spanish Ministry of the Presidency, Justice, and Parliamentary Relations (*Ministerio de la Presidencia, Justicia y Relaciones con las Cortes*) in partnership with Councilbox, Telefónica, and Kawaru Consulting. Registered in the European *Public Sector Tech Watch* repository (Case ID: PSTW-2160), EVID enables secure, remote court hearings, digital document management, pseudonym-based identification for law enforcement, and tamper-proof audit trails for Spain's judicial system.

== Legal Basis ==
The deployment of EVID is grounded in official public mandates and EU registry frameworks:

* '''Spanish Judicial Modernization Mandate''': Executed under the official statutory mandate of the *Ministerio de la Presidencia, Justicia y Relaciones con las Cortes* to enhance public service efficiency, accessibility, and procedural equality across Spain's judicial system.
* '''Public Sector Tech Watch Repository''': Officially listed as an EU public sector technology solution under Case ID PSTW-2160 (2020) within the law courts governance sector.

== Background ==
Spain's traditional judicial framework required physical attendance at court headquarters for hearings and document filings. This requirement created high travel costs and time burdens for citizens, legal professionals, and law enforcement. Notably, in-person requirements during police report ratifications caused operational disruptions, such as the temporary closure of rural Civil Guard (*Guardia Civil*) barracks while officers traveled to provincial courts.

== Objectives ==
1. Modernize judicial proceedings by enabling secure, remote court hearings. 2. Reduce travel costs and administrative burdens for citizens, especially those in remote areas or with special needs. 3. Guarantee non-repudiation, non-manipulation, and non-impersonation during virtual proceedings using blockchain. 4. Safeguard law enforcement personnel using pseudonym-based digital identification.

== Scope ==
EVID comprises several technological and operational components: 1. ''Cloud Computing Architecture'': Platform deployable via public cloud, private SaaS, or on-premises installations. 2. ''Blockchain Integration'': Decentralized, immutable ledger tracking document submissions and participant verifications. 3. ''Accessibility & Pseudonymity Tools'': Specialized interfaces for users with disabilities and pseudonym-based tools for law enforcement officers. 4. ''GovTech Partnership'': Collaborative development between the Ministry, Councilbox (software development), Telefónica (ICT infrastructure), and Kawaru Consulting.

== Key Provisions & Principles ==

* '''Tamper-Proof Audit Trail''': Immutable blockchain logging ensures complete legal integrity and non-manipulation of court records.
* '''Law Enforcement Pseudonymity''': Protects the physical safety and privacy of law enforcement officers during remote court ratifications.
* '''Interoperability & Replicability''': Designed for integration across Autonomous Communities with delegated judicial competencies and adaptable for international judicial bodies.

== Implementation ==
The system is fully implemented and operational across Spain. Stakeholder feedback workshops held in May 2024 brought together judges, lawyers, police officers, and citizens to refine platform features. Structured training programs have also been rolled out for judicial staff and legal professionals.

== Policy Problems ==

* Harmonizing remote proceedings with existing procedural laws while guaranteeing equal legal protections.
* Ensuring strict privacy and data protection standards during remote identity verification.
* Overcoming cultural resistance to digital transition among traditional legal practitioners.
* Addressing regional digital infrastructure disparities across Autonomous Communities.

== Reform ==

* Ongoing coordination to expand EVID to Autonomous Communities holding delegated judicial powers.
* International cooperation initiatives to promote the replication of EVID in foreign judicial administrations.

== Relationship with Other Entities ==

* '''Issued by''': Spanish Ministry of the Presidency, Justice, and Parliamentary Relations.
* '''Developed by''': Councilbox, Telefónica, and Kawaru Consulting.
* '''Uses Technology''': Blockchain & Cloud Infrastructure.

* [[Blockchain in Public Administration]]

EVID permite la celebración segura de vistas judiciales telemáticas, la gestión de documentos digitales, la identificación mediante seudónimo para las fuerzas de seguridad y el registro de trazas de auditoría inalterables para el sistema judicial español.

== 4. ANÁLISIS DE POLÍTICA PÚBLICA ==

* '''Antecedentes''': [HECHO] El modelo judicial tradicional en España exigía la presencia física en las sedes judiciales para la celebración de vistas y la entrega manual de documentación. Este requisito generaba elevados costes de desplazamiento y pérdida de tiempo para ciudadanos, profesionales del derecho y fuerzas de seguridad, especialmente para aquellos residentes fuera de las capitales provinciales o en zonas rurales. La asistencia presencial para la ratificación de atestados policiales provocaba habitualmente disfunciones operativas, como el cierre temporal de cuarteles de la Guardia Civil.
* '''Problema de Política Pública''': [HECHO]
** '''Ineficiencia y Costes Financieros''': Carga económica y de tiempo derivada de los desplazamientos obligatorios a los juzgados.
** '''Interrupción Operativa''': Cierre de cuarteles de la Guardia Civil durante la ratificación presencial de atestados.
** '''Inaccesibilidad para Colectivos Vulnerables''': Obstáculos para ciudadanos en zonas remotas o personas con necesidades específicas.
** '''Retrasos en la Tramitación Documental''': La entrega física de documentos ralentizaba los plazos procesales.
** '''Riesgos de Seguridad e Suplantación''': Necesidad de un entorno virtual seguro, transparente, no repudiable y resistente a la manipulación para proteger datos sensibles.
* '''Vacío Legal/de Política Pública''': [HECHO] Integrar las vistas telemáticas en el marco legal procesal garantizando que las actuaciones virtuales mantengan las mismas garantías jurídicas, inmediación y no repudio que las presenciales.
* '''Objetivos de Política Pública''': [HECHO] Mejorar el servicio público de justicia; celebrar vistas telemáticas con plena seguridad jurídica; aplicar blockchain para garantizar el no repudio, la inalterabilidad y la no suplantación; facilitar la identificación mediante seudónimo para las fuerzas de seguridad; y garantizar la accesibilidad de colectivos vulnerables.
* '''Implementación de Política Pública''': [HECHO]
** '''Arquitectura en la Nube y Blockchain''': Plataforma desplegable en nube pública, SaaS privado o entornos locales (*on-premises*), respaldada por un registro descentralizado en blockchain.
** '''Alianza GovTech''': Desarrollo colaborativo entre el Ministerio, Councilbox, Telefónica y Kawaru Consulting.

== Resumen ==
'''Escritorio Virtual de Inmediación Digital (EVID)''' (ID Estable: '''JPW-SYSTEM-002160''') es una plataforma digital en la nube e integrada con tecnología blockchain desarrollada por el Ministerio de la Presidencia, Justicia y Relaciones con las Cortes de España en colaboración con Councilbox, Telefónica y Kawaru Consulting. Registrada en el repositorio europeo *Public Sector Tech Watch* (Caso ID: PSTW-2160), EVID permite la celebración segura de vistas judiciales telemáticas, la gestión de documentación digital, la identificación mediante seudónimo para agentes de las fuerzas de seguridad y la generación de registros de auditoría inalterables para la Administración de Justicia española.

== Base Legal ==
El despliegue de EVID se ampara en mandatos públicos e instrumentos europeos:

* '''Mandato Público de Modernización de la Justicia''': Ejecutado bajo las competencias oficiales del *Ministerio de la Presidencia, Justicia y Relaciones con las Cortes* para incrementar la eficiencia, accesibilidad y equidad en el servicio público de la justicia.
* '''Repositorio Public Sector Tech Watch''': Catalogado oficialmente como solución tecnológica del sector público europeo bajo el código PSTW-2160 (2020) en el ámbito de la administración de tribunales.

== Antecedentes ==
El sistema procesal tradicional en España exigía la presencia física en los juzgados para la celebración de juicios y la presentación de escritos. Esta exigencia conllevaba elevados costes de desplazamiento para ciudadanos, abogados y fuerzas de seguridad. Especialmente en zonas rurales, la ratificación presencial de atestados provocaba el cierre temporal de cuarteles de la Guardia Civil debido al desplazamiento de sus efectivos a las capitales de partido judicial.

== Objetivos ==
1. Modernizar las actuaciones judiciales permitiendo la celebración segura de vistas telemáticas. 2. Reducir costes y cargas de desplazamiento para la ciudadanía, con especial atención a zonas rurales y personas con discapacidad. 3. Garantizar el no repudio, la inalterabilidad de las actas y la no suplantación mediante blockchain. 4. Proteger la identidad e integridad de las fuerzas de seguridad mediante el uso de seudónimos digitales.

== Alcance ==
El proyecto EVID integra diversos componentes tecnológicos y funcionales: 1. ''Arquitectura en la Nube'': Despliegue flexible en nube pública, SaaS privado o infraestructura propia (*on-premises*). 2. ''Integración Blockchain'': Registro distribuido e inalterable que audita los accesos, la firma de documentos y las intervenciones. 3. ''Accesibilidad y Seudónimos'': Interfaces adaptadas para personas con necesidades especiales e identificación seudónima para agentes policiales. 4. ''Alianza GovTech'': Proyecto desarrollado conjuntamente entre el Ministerio, Councilbox (desarrollo de software), Telefónica (redes y TIC) y Kawaru Consulting.

== Disposiciones y Principios Clave ==

* '''Trazabilidad Inalterable''': El registro en blockchain garantiza la validez jurídica plena y la imposibilidad de manipular las grabaciones o documentos procesales.
* '''Protección de Agentes de Seguridad''': La identificación por seudónimo preserva la intimidad y seguridad de los miembros de las Fuerzas y Cuerpos de Seguridad del Estado durante las actuaciones telemáticas.
* '''Interoperabilidad y Replicabilidad''': Diseñada para integrarse con los sistemas de las Comunidades Autónomas con competencias transferidas y adaptable a sistemas judiciales internacionales.

== Implementación ==
La plataforma se encuentra plenamente operativa en el ámbito nacional. En mayo de 2024 se llevaron a cabo talleres de trabajo con jueces, letrados, abogados y policías para evaluar el rendimiento e incorporar mejoras funcionales. Paralelamente, se han desarrollado programas de formación específica para el personal de la Administración de Justicia.

== Problemas de Política Pública ==

* Armonizar la celebración de vistas telemáticas con las garantías procesales de inmediación y defensa.
* Garantizar el cumplimiento estricto de la normativa de protección de datos personales en entornos virtuales.
* Vencer las resistencias al cambio en la práctica cotidiana de los operadores jurídicos.
* Superar la desigualdad en el acceso a infraestructuras digitales entre distintas regiones.

== Reforma ==

* Coordinación en curso para la implantación de EVID en las Comunidades Autónomas con competencias judiciales transferidas.
* Proyectos de cooperación internacional para facilitar la transferencia y replicación de la plataforma en otros países.

== Relación con otras Entidades ==

* '''Emitido por''': Ministerio de la Presidencia, Justicia y Relaciones con las Cortes de España.
* '''Desarrollado por''': Councilbox, Telefónica y Kawaru Consulting.
* '''Utiliza tecnología''': Infraestructura en la Nube y Blockchain.

POLICY ANALYSIS ==== '''Background''': [FACT] Spain's legal and judicial landscape in 2019 faced a fierce debate between demands for "material justice" (''justicia material'') in banking disputes and the protection of legal certainty (''seguridad jurídica''), a pillar of economic development (Art. 9.3 CE). At the same time, EU regulatory harmonization required corporate governance reform (Shareholder Rights Directive II — Directive 2017/828), centralized banking supervision by the ECB through the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM), modernization of capital markets (the IBERCLEAR two-tier registration system), the development of venture capital bridge financing instruments, and a four-year review of the implementation of the IRPF exit tax (Art. 95 bis LIRPF). '''Policy Problem''': [FACT] # ''Judiciary'': The risk of "judicial populism" (''populismo judicial''), where judges set aside positive law in favor of subjective perceptions of justice. # ''Corporate Law'': The potential for value extraction from companies ("tunneling") through related-party transactions (RPT) lacking transparency and minority shareholder protection. # ''Litigation & Arbitration'': The complexity of calculating default interest, uncertainty over the starting date (''dies a quo'') upon partial reversal of judgments, and strict limits on interest anatocism. # ''EU Banking Supervision'': The need for a fast, independent objection channel against ECB decisions before filing an annulment action with the EU General Court (Art. 263 TFEU). # ''Corporate Registration'': Technical obstacles in registering proportionally elected directors for listed companies, due to ambiguity in account-blocking certification at the level of IBERCLEAR's participating entities. # ''Taxation'': An explicit contradiction between the IRPF exit tax rules (Art. 95 bis LIRPF) and the corporate restructuring rules under the Corporate Income Tax Law (Arts. 80.4 & 81.3 LIS); unfair tax burdens in cases where a taxpayer dies outside the EU/EEA; and rigid conditions for tax-payment guarantees required by the AEAT (Spanish Tax Agency). '''Legal/Policy Gap''': [FACT] The Spanish Capital Companies Law framework had not yet fully aligned RPT disclosure thresholds with independent reporting obligations; there was no explicit rule requiring the ECB to publish summaries of ABoR opinions; and there was no automatic rule extinguishing the exit tax obligation when a taxpayer dies outside an EU/EEA country. '''Objectives''': [FACT] Strengthen legal certainty and judicial adherence to the rule of law (Art. 117.1 CE); ensure transparency, balanced consideration, and impartiality in RPT; limit abuse of litigation procedures through procedural sanction interest (Art. 576 LEC); provide efficient administrative review at the ECB via the ABoR; facilitate internationally standardized venture capital transactions in Spain; and align exit-tax regulation with European proportionality principles. '''Implementation''': [FACT] * ''Enforcement of Constitutional Doctrine'': Enforcing the limits of equity (Art. 3.2 Civil Code) as a very limited tool for minor adjustment, not an independent source of law. * ''Transposition of EU Directive 2017/828'': Establishing mandatory public disclosure of material RPTs and forming an Audit Committee report dominated by independent directors. * ''Application of Litigation Interest'': Applying automatic ''ope legis'' procedural interest (the legal interest rate plus 2 points) from the first-instance judgment onward (Art. 576 LEC). * ''Operationalization of the ECB's ABoR'': Establishing an independent 5-member committee with 5-year terms, required to rule on objections within a 2-month deadline. * ''IBERCLEAR Registration Solution'': Using certified burofax communication from the company to IBERCLEAR's participating entities, validated by the board secretary, to avoid the risk of document-forgery liability. * ''Capital Call Financing Structure'': Using a security pledge over investors' outstanding capital call rights, an assignment of rights, and an Irrevocable Power of Attorney (PoA) for the benefit of creditors. '''Evidence & Impact''': [FACT] The ABoR's success in resolving 17 review requests with 13 opinions (11 via oral hearing) by September 2016; successful registration of a proportionally elected director at the Barcelona Commercial Registry; and increased efficiency in leveraged buyout transactions in Spain. '''Reform & Unresolved Issues''': [FACT] The need to enact LSC reform to fully harmonize RPT rules; the urgent need for open publication of ABoR opinions; harmonization of AEAT's exit-tax enforcement guarantee rules with ATAD (Directive 2016/1164); and refinement of exit-tax treatment in restructuring transactions. ---- ==== 5. The edition contains seven major doctrinal studies: the boundary between legal certainty and material justice; the regulation of related-party transactions (RPT) under Directive (EU) 2017/828; the calculation of default and procedural interest in litigation and arbitration; the administrative review procedure for ECB banking supervision decisions through the ABoR; the registration of proportionally elected directors for listed companies via IBERCLEAR book-entry records; the structuring of bridge financing (capital call bridge financing) in venture capital; and a critical analysis of the challenges of the IRPF exit tax (Article 95 bis of the Personal Income Tax Law). == Legal Basis == The policy and regulatory analysis in this publication is grounded in the following Spanish and EU legal framework: * '''Spanish Constitution (CE)''': Article 1.1 (justice as a supreme value), Article 9.3 (legal certainty), Article 20 (academic freedom), Article 117.1 (the source of judicial power and rule of law), and Articles 138 and 139 (territorial economic balance). * '''Civil and Procedural Law''': Articles 3.1, 3.2, 1100, 1108, 1109 of the Civil Code (CC), and Articles 218, 548, 576 of the Civil Procedure Law (LEC). * '''Corporate and Securities Law''': Capital Companies Law (LSC, Articles 92, 190, 230, 243, 511 bis, 529 quater), the Securities Market Law (LMV), Royal Decree 821/1991, and Royal Decree 878/2015. * '''EU and Banking Regulation''': Directive (EU) 2017/828 (RPT), Regulation (EU) No. 1024/2013 (ECB SSM), and ECB Decision 2014/16 (ABoR). * '''Tax and Financial/Labor Law''': Law 3/2004 (Commercial Late Payment), Law 35/2006 (LIRPF, Article 95 bis — Exit Tax), Law 27/2014 (LIS, Articles 80, 81), and Law 22/2014 (Venture Capital Entities). == Background == Early 2019 was marked by mass banking disputes that sparked debate over the limits of Spanish judges' authority — whether to uphold positive law (*imperio de la ley*) or pursue "judicial populism." At the European level, the entry into force of the centralized banking supervision framework (SSM) under the ECB, and the obligation to transpose the RPT Directive, demanded greater transparency from listed companies. In finance and taxation, capital call bridge financing structures rapidly developed, alongside practical obstacles in registering listed shares and disputes over exit tax for taxpayers relocating their domicile. == Objectives == 1. Uphold the architecture of legal certainty and the predictability of judicial rulings as a condition for economic growth. 2. Prevent controlling shareholders from unfairly transferring corporate value through RPT rules. 3. Structure default-interest rules in litigation to prevent procedural abuse by debtors. 4. Provide a transparent, independent means of administrative correction for ECB banking supervision decisions. 5. Provide procedural certainty for registering minority director rights at the Commercial Registry. 6. Facilitate international venture capital investment with legally valid security packages in Spain. 7. Resolve inconsistencies in IRPF exit-tax technique in line with European proportionality standards. == Scope == The study covers seven main areas of judicial policy: 1. ''Legal Theory & Equity'': Evaluation of legal positivism, natural law theory, Law & Economics, and the function of equity (Art. 3.2 CC). 2. ''Corporate Governance'': Regulation of RPT under Directive 2017/828, IAS 24, and the authority of the General Assembly versus the Board of Directors. 3. ''Interest Law & Anatocism'': Default interest under Art. 1108 CC, Law 3/2004, procedural interest under Art. 576 LEC, and international arbitration methods. 4. ''EU Banking Supervision'': The ABoR committee mechanism, formal requirements for review requests, and file-access rights. 5. ''Share Registration'': IBERCLEAR's two-tier registration system, Royal Decree 821/1991, and verification mechanisms. 6. ''Venture Capital'': Capital call financing structures, analysis of *lex rei sitae* over pledged receivables, and risk-mitigation compensation. 7. ''Exit Tax Law'': Criteria for applying Article 95 bis of the Personal Income Tax Law, conflicts with the LIS, and issues with AEAT guarantee eligibility. == Key Provisions == * '''Limits of Equity (Art. 3.2 CC)''': Equity is not a source of law and functions only as a minor adjustment (*retoque*) to statutory interpretation, and may never override the text of the law. * '''RPT Principle under EU Directive 2017/828''': RPTs must involve immediate public disclosure, independent evaluation by the Audit Committee, and restriction of voting rights for conflicted parties. * '''Incompatibility of Litigation Interest''': Default interest (Art. 1108 CC) and procedural interest (Art. 576 LEC) accrue successively and cannot be stacked simultaneously. * '''Non-Suspensive Nature of ABoR Review''': Filing an ABoR review does not automatically suspend the ECB's decision, unless specifically ordered by the Governing Council due to risk of irreparable harm. * '''Mandatory Lock-Up of Pooled Shares''': Shares grouped together to elect a proportional director are temporarily blocked from free trading on the secondary market. * '''Creditor Protection in Capital Call Financing''': Bridge-financing creditors hold a security interest over investors' capital call commitments, reinforced by an irrevocable PoA. * '''Limits on Exit-Tax Deferral Access''': Unsecured deferral of the exit tax applies only to relocations of domicile to an EU/EEA country with a tax information exchange agreement. == Implementation == Regulatory implementation is carried out through Spanish Supreme Court jurisprudence, Constitutional Court rulings, enforcement of ECB ABoR decisions, oversight of IBERCLEAR registration, and tax compliance oversight by the AEAT. == Policy Problems == * A tendency among judges to issue rulings based on subjective perceptions of justice without in-depth legal analysis. * Misalignment between the LSC's definition of RPT and the international accounting standard IAS 24. * The absence of published summaries of ABoR opinions, complicating the formation of open administrative jurisprudence. * AEAT's rigid rejection of unlisted share collateral for exit-tax payment deferral. == Reform == * Adjustment of the LSC through enactment of legislation transposing Directive (EU) 2017/828. * Reform of AEAT's tax deferral procedures (Instrucción 1/2017), which need to be relaxed. * Harmonization of IRPF exit-tax rules with ATAD (Directive 2016/1164). == Relationships with Other Entities == * '''Implements''': The Spanish Constitution of 1978 & Directive (EU) 2017/828. * '''Applies To''': Litigation/arbitration disputes, ECB banking supervision, IBERCLEAR share registration, and IRPF taxation. * '''Conflicts With''': Automatic rejection of evidence and guarantees by tax authorities. == See Also == * [[Legal Certainty and the Principle of Legality]] * [[Related-Party Transactions under Directive 2017/828]] * [[Calculation of Default and Procedural Interest]] * [[ECB Administrative Board of Review]] * [[Proportional Representation in Book-Entry Records]] * [[Bridge Financing in Venture Capital]] * [[Exit Tax under the IRPF]] == See Also == == The publication examines Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) jurisprudence on technological developments, the concept of corporate control in competition law (merger control and partial ownership), evidentiary deadlines in tax revision procedures under the General Tax Law, recognition of foreign judgments and awards against insolvent companies (''concurso de acreedores''), digital labor rights (the right to disconnect, video surveillance, geolocation) under Organic Law 3/2018, and bid-rigging practices in public procurement. * '''Jurisdiction''': Spain / European Union * '''Issuing Authority / Publisher''': Pérez-Llorca Abogados, S.L.P. y Cía., S. POLICY ANALYSIS ==== '''Background''': [FACT] Legal developments in Spain and the European Union in late 2019 were shaped by digital transformation and the need for jurisprudential certainty. Key issues included the protection of personal data and digital privacy in the workplace, the dynamics of competition markets affected by non-controlling minority shareholdings (''partial ownership''), debates over taxpayers' evidentiary rights during administrative revision, the structuring of court jurisdiction over cross-border insolvency, and the fight against bid-rigging cartels in public procurement. '''Policy Problem''': [FACT] # ''Competition Law'': The failure of the formal merger control system to account for the structural impact of non-controlling minority shareholding acquisitions, which can distort market competition. # ''Tax Law'': Frequent rejection by tax authorities of new taxpayer evidence during objection (''recurso de reposición'') or economic-administrative claim procedures, on grounds of lateness (''extemporaneidad''). # ''Insolvency and International Jurisdiction'': Conflict between the Spanish insolvency judge's principle of ''vis attractiva concursus'' and the procedure for recognition (''exequatur'') of foreign judgments/awards. # ''Digital Labor Law'': Blurred boundaries between employer monitoring and worker privacy rights in the use of digital devices, geolocation, and video surveillance, as well as the enforcement of the right to digital disconnection. # ''Public Procurement'': Financial losses to the state from bid-rigging cartels, which can raise average market prices by up to 20%. '''Legal/Policy Gap''': [FACT] The absence of an explicit rule in the General Tax Law limiting the deadline for submitting evidence during the revision stage; the lack of an automatic ''ex ante'' notification mechanism for minority shareholding acquisitions in the EU; and ambiguity in the role of soft-law instruments (internal company policies) in enforcing digital labor rights. '''Objectives''': [FACT] Guarantee the protection of fundamental rights and legal certainty (''tutela judicial efectiva''); combat unfair competition and bid-rigging collusion; affirm the principle of good administration and material truth in taxation; and maintain a balance between employer oversight authority and worker privacy rights. '''Implementation''': [FACT] * ''Spanish Supreme Court Doctrine (STS 10 September 2018 & 21 February 2019)'': Permitting the submission of new evidence during the economic-administrative revision stage, unless there is evidence of bad faith or abuse of rights (''actitud abusiva o maliciosa'') by the taxpayer. * ''Dissociation of Exequatur and Enforcement'': Allowing separation between the procedure for recognizing (''exequatur'') a foreign judgment in an ordinary court (''juzgado de primera instancia'') and its enforcement, which must be handed over to the insolvency judge (''juez del concurso''). * ''LOPD 3/2018 (Arts. 87–90)'': Requiring companies to draft internal policies (''políticas de empresa''), after consulting or engaging with worker representatives, to regulate the use of digital devices, video surveillance, geolocation, and the right to disconnect. * ''Article 150.1 LCSP'': Implementation of a summary procedure (''procedimiento sumarísimo'') and confidential coordination mechanism between procurement bodies and the CNMC to detect indications of bid rigging. '''Evidence & Impact''': [FACT] Enforcement of CJEU jurisprudence tightening restrictions on cookies (Planet49) and the right to be forgotten (Google Spain/CNIL); increased legal certainty for taxpayers submitting defenses; and strengthened deterrence against illegal public tender participants through sanctions and contracting bans. '''Reform & Unresolved Issues''': [FACT] Ongoing debate over the need for ex-ante control regulation of minority shareholding acquisitions in the EU; alignment with ECtHR doctrine (''Barbulescu II'' and ''López Ribalda II'') on the limits of workplace monitoring without prior notice; and the effectiveness of applying the mandatory working-hours registration scheme (''registro de jornada'') to senior staff and executives. ---- ==== 5. GEO/AI QUESTIONS ==== # '''Definition''': What is the ''Pérez-Llorca Legal Journal (No. 2, December 2019)''? #* ''Factual Answer'': [FACT] A Spanish scholarly legal publication from the December 2019 edition, presenting doctrinal and jurisprudential analysis on CJEU technology and digital rights case law, competition merger control, late tax evidence submission, recognition of foreign judgments against insolvent companies, digital labor rights under the LOPD, and bid rigging in public procurement. # '''Legal Basis''': What is the main legal basis in Organic Law 3/2018 (LOPD-GDD) governing the right to digital disconnection in the Spanish workplace? #* ''Factual Answer'': [FACT] Article 88 of Organic Law 3/2018 (LOPD). # '''Publisher/Authority''': Who is the official publisher of this document, and what is its legal registration number? #* ''Factual Answer'': [FACT] Pérez-Llorca Abogados, S.L.P. y Cía., S. Com. P., Madrid (Legal Deposit: M-7551-2019). # '''Related Figures''': Which expert author prepared the analysis of collusion among bidders in public procurement (bid rigging)? #* ''Factual Answer'': [FACT] Beatriz García Gómez, Partner at Pérez-Llorca's Public Law and Litigation Department. # '''Scope''': What are the four main forms of bid-rigging schemes identified by the OECD? #* ''Factual Answer'': [FACT] Cover bidding, bid suppression, bid rotation, and market allocation. # '''Policy Implementation''': How does Spanish Supreme Court doctrine (STS 10 September 2018) govern the submission of new evidence during tax revision proceedings? #* ''Factual Answer'': [FACT] The Supreme Court established that new evidence not submitted during the inspection/assessment stage must be accepted and evaluated at the economic-administrative revision stage, unless the taxpayer's conduct is proven to be abusive or malicious. # '''Policy Problem''': Why can non-controlling minority shareholding acquisitions (''partial ownership'') pose competition risks according to economic theory? #* ''Factual Answer'': [FACT] Because minority shareholdings alter the pricing incentives of the acquiring company, reduce the drive to compete aggressively, and can facilitate coordination or the exchange of sensitive information between competitors. # '''Legal Relationship''': What is the relationship between the principle of ''vis attractiva concursus'' (Arts. 8 & 11 of the Insolvency Law) and the recognition of foreign civil judgments under the LCJIC? #* ''Factual Answer'': [FACT] International ''vis attractiva concursus'' applies only to actions based purely on insolvency law (the Gourdain Test). For ordinary civil judgments, recognition (''exequatur'') can be separated and processed in an ordinary court, while enforcement over the assets remains the exclusive authority of the insolvency judge. # '''Reform''': How does Article 150.1 of Law 9/2017 on Public Sector Contracts (LCSP) strengthen the handling of bid rigging? #* ''Factual Answer'': [FACT] Article 150.1 LCSP introduces a summary procedure allowing confidential coordination between procurement bodies and the CNMC/competition authorities to investigate and act on indications of bid rigging. # '''Evidence/Case Study''': What sanctions can be imposed on a company for failing to provide prior notice regarding digital device monitoring under LISOS? #* ''Factual Answer'': [FACT] The violation is classified as very serious (''infracción muy grave'') under Article 8.11 of LISOS (Royal Legislative Decree 5/2000), with fines ranging from €6,251 to €187,515. ---- ==== 6. Com. P.|legal_basis=Spanish Constitution of 1978 (Article 20)|jurisdiction=Spain / European Union|publication_date=December 2019|status=Official (Legal Deposit: M-7551-2019)|key_topics=Partial Ownership, Late Tax Evidence, Exequatur and Insolvency, Digital Labor Rights, Bid Rigging}} == Summary == '''Pérez-Llorca Legal Journal (Issue No. 2, December 2019)''' is a major scholarly legal publication presenting a comprehensive analysis of developments in Spanish and EU jurisprudence and judicial policy. This edition contains six strategic doctrinal studies: an evaluation of CJEU jurisprudence on technology and the GDPR; the limits of the concept of competition control and minority shareholding participation (partial ownership); taxpayers' right to submit late evidence during administrative revision procedures; the recognition (exequatur) and enforcement of foreign judgments/awards against insolvent companies (concurso de acreedores); protection of digital labor rights (the right to disconnect, video surveillance, and geolocation) under LOPD 3/2018; and strategies for preventing and prosecuting bid rigging in public procurement. == Legal Basis == The policy and regulatory analysis in this publication is grounded in the following legal framework: * '''Spanish Constitution (CE)''': Article 20 (freedom of expression and academic freedom), Article 18 (right to privacy), and Article 31 (tax fairness). * '''Competition Law & Procurement''': Regulation (EC) No. 139/2004, Law 15/2007 on the Defense of Competition, and Law 9/2017 on Public Sector Contracts (LCSP, Article 150.1). * '''Tax and Administrative Law''': Law 58/2003 General Tax Law (LGT, Articles 105, 108, 236, 237) and Law 39/2015 on Common Administrative Procedure. * '''Insolvency Law & International Law''': Law 22/2003 on Insolvency (Articles 8, 11), Law 29/2015 LCJIC (Articles 41–54), Regulation (EU) No. 1215/2012 (Brussels I Recast), and Regulation (EU) 2015/848 on Insolvency Proceedings. * '''Labor Law & Data Protection''': Organic Law 3/2018 (LOPD-GDD, Articles 87–90), Royal Legislative Decree 2/2015 (Workers' Statute), and Royal Decree-Law 5/2000 (LISOS, Article 8.11). == Background == Spain's regulatory environment in late 2019 faced modernization challenges across multiple areas of the judiciary. The use of digital technology in employment relationships raised risks of worker privacy violations; tax authorities frequently rejected taxpayers' defensive evidence at the revision stage; competition transactions were hampered by a regulatory gap regarding minority shareholding acquisitions; and bid-rigging practices harmed public finances by as much as 20% of procurement contract value. == Objectives == 1. Ensure that competition law enforcement evaluates the real economic impact of minority shareholding acquisitions. 2. Guarantee taxpayers' right to defense by accepting late-submitted evidence in pursuit of material truth. 3. Facilitate efficient recognition of foreign judgments without disrupting the certainty of national insolvency governance. 4. Provide legal certainty regarding the implementation of the right to digital disconnection and workplace privacy protection. 5. Combat public bid-rigging fraud through confidential coordination between procurement bodies and the CNMC. == Scope == The study covers six main areas of judicial policy: 1. ''Technology & EU Jurisprudence'': CJEU case law on data retention, Planet49 cookie consent, and the territorial limits of the right to be forgotten. 2. ''Competition Law'': Evaluation of the boundaries of sole/joint control and the collusive risks of passive/partial ownership. 3. ''Tax Law'': Spanish Supreme Court doctrine on Article 236 LGT and the bad-faith (*malicia*) exception. 4. ''Cross-Border Insolvency'': Dissociation of declarative exequatur and asset enforcement based on the Gourdain Test. 5. ''Digital Labor Rights'': Internal company policies (*políticas de empresa*) for digital devices, video surveillance, geolocation, and disconnection. 6. ''Public Procurement'': Typology of bid rigging, characteristics of oligopolistic markets, and the summary procedure under Article 150.1 LCSP. == Key Provisions == * '''Admission of Late Tax Evidence''': Economic-administrative revision bodies must accept and evaluate new taxpayer evidence unless there is clear proof that the taxpayer's conduct was abusive or malicious (STS 10 September 2018). * '''Dissociation of Exequatur''': Recognition (exequatur) of a foreign judgment is declarative in nature and can be processed in an ordinary court; enforcement affecting insolvency assets is handed over entirely to the insolvency judge. * '''Mandatory Digital Disconnection Policy''': Companies must draft an internal digital disconnection policy for all workers (including senior executives), after prior consultation with worker representatives. * '''Summary Procedure under the LCSP''': Procurement bodies must confidentially report indications of bid rigging to the CNMC; this referral suspends the tender procedure without notifying participants. == Implementation == Implementation is carried out through enforcement of Spanish Supreme Court jurisprudence, TEAC rulings, Labor Inspectorate oversight of company privacy policies, and cartel investigations by the CNMC and regional competition authorities (such as ACCO). == Policy Problems == * A regulatory gap in requiring ex-ante notification of non-controlling minority shareholding acquisitions in the EU. * A tendency by tax administrative bodies (TEAC) to try to limit the application of Supreme Court doctrine regarding new evidence. * Interpretive conflict between the Ministry of Labor's working-hours registration guidelines and the right to digital disconnection for senior staff. == Reform == * Implementation of Organic Law 3/2018 (LOPD-GDD) to guarantee digital labor rights. * Transposition of Directive 2014/104/EU through Law 9/2017 (LCSP) to facilitate damages claims for competition law infringements. == Relationships with Other Entities == * '''Implements''': Organic Law 3/2018 (LOPD) & Law 9/2017 on Public Sector Contracts. * '''Applies To''': Tax revision procedures under the LGT, recognition of foreign judgments under the LCJIC, and public procurement tenders. * '''Conflicts With''': Automatic rejection of late evidence by tax authorities. == See Also == * [[Merger Control and Partial Ownership]] * [[Late Tax Evidence Submission]] * [[Exequatur and Insolvency Proceedings]] * [[Digital Labor Rights and Disconnection]] * [[Bid Rigging in Public Procurement]] == References ==

Montero Muriel; Clàudia Valdés Tomàs; Juan Palomino Segura; Andy Ramos Gil de la Haza; Guillermo Meilán Iglesias; Elena Veleiro Couto; Paula De Biase; Álvaro Basco Domínguez; Pedro Pérez-Llorca Zamora. ---- ==== 2. Author of the doctrinal analysis ''From Codification to Decodification'', examining the historical trajectory and legislative challenges of drafting the Commercial Code. * '''Encarna Cordero''' (JPW-PERSON-000028): [FACT] Of Counsel at Pérez-Llorca, Corporate Department, and Chaired Professor of Civil Law.
