== Summary ==
'''Por los derechos económicos y sociales de las personas refugiadas''' (*For the Economic and Social Rights of Refugees*) is an official human rights policy monograph and advocacy report on the socioeconomic integration and legal protection of refugees in Spain and Europe. Authored by Sophie Muller (UNHCR Representative in Spain / *Representante de ACNUR en España*), it was published in June 2023 by ACNUR/UNHCR Spain in collaboration with the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation (*Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores, Unión Europea y Cooperación — MAEC*). The report presents an empirical and legal analysis of global forced displacement (103 million forcibly displaced persons, including 53.2 million internal displaced persons and 32.5 million refugees) and examines the legal mechanisms required to guarantee sustainable socioeconomic integration rather than mere physical asylum. The monograph systematically evaluates: (1) international legal foundations under the 1951 Geneva Convention on the Status of Refugees and its 1967 Protocol, securing rights to association, self-employment, liberal professions, housing, and education; (2) the UN Global Compact on Refugees (*Pacto Mundial sobre los Refugiados*, UNGA Dec 2018) and World Bank economic impact studies demonstrating that refugee integration strengthens host nation labor markets, tax bases, and social peace; (3) European Union standards under the 2013 Reception Conditions Directive, setting a maximum 9-month exclusion limit for access to the labor market; (4) Spanish national codifications, including Constitutional dignity/health/education rights and Spanish Asylum Act 12/2009 (*Ley 12/2009, de 30 de octubre*), granting refugees equal access to public employment services, healthcare, housing, social assistance, and education; (5) operational administrative barriers in Spain, such as processing delays (*retrasos importantes*), municipal registration obstacles (*empadronamiento*), and commercial banking restrictions (*cuentas bancarias*); and (6) institutional partnership initiatives, including free legal assistance networks organized by the Bar Associations (*Colegios de Abogados*) of Murcia, Madrid, and Almería, refugee-led organizations, and the First Forum in Spain on Refugees (*Primer Foro en España sobre los Refugiados*) held on 20 June 2023 in preparation for the December 2023 Global Refugee Forum in Geneva.

== Legal Basis ==
The international, European, and Spanish statutory provisions analyzed include:

* '''International Treaties & UN Instruments''': 1951 Geneva Convention on the Status of Refugees (*Convención de Ginebra de 1951 sobre el Estatuto de los Refugiados*) and its 1967 Protocol; UN Global Compact on Refugees (*Pacto Mundial sobre los Refugiados*, UNGA Dec 2018).
* '''European Union Directives''': 2013 EU Reception Conditions Directive (*Directiva de Condiciones de Recepción de 2013*).
* '''Spanish Constitutional & Statutory Legislation''': Constitución Española de 1978 (Arts. 10, 27, 43 - human dignity, education, healthcare); Ley 12/2009, de 30 de octubre, reguladora del derecho de asilo y de la protección subsidiaria (Arts. on equal socioeconomic access).

== Background ==
Global forced displacement has reached 103 million people, driven by prolonged conflicts in Syria (nearly 7 million refugees) and the war in Ukraine (over 8 million refugees across Europe). Crucially, 83% of refugees reside in low- and middle-income developing nations, with 8.4 million trapped in protracted exile (>5 years). To move beyond temporary physical shelter toward sustainable protection, the UN Global Compact on Refugees (2018) established economic self-reliance and social rights inclusion as global imperatives based on the 1951 Convention. Sophie Muller published this policy study to assess Spain's progress and identify structural improvements needed to fulfill these standards.

== Objectives ==
1. Transition refugee protection frameworks from basic physical shelter to self-reliant socioeconomic inclusion. 2. Guarantee equal refugee access to employment, education, healthcare, and housing under Ley 12/2009. 3. Eliminate administrative bottlenecks regarding municipal registration (*empadronamiento*) and commercial banking. 4. Expand free legal aid networks through UNHCR partnerships with Spanish Bar Associations (*Colegios de Abogados*). 5. Mobilize public-private commitments through national forums in preparation for global refugee summits.

== Scope ==
The scope of this UNHCR study spans four primary pillars: 1. ''Global Forced Displacement Context'': Analysis of 103 million displaced individuals, Syrian/Ukrainian crises, and host nation distribution. 2. ''International & EU Legal Framework'': 1951 Geneva Convention rights, 2018 Global Compact, and the 9-month maximum labor market exclusion limit under the 2013 EU Reception Directive. 3. ''Spanish Statutory Rights & Administrative Hurdles'': Equal treatment under Asylum Act 12/2009, delays in processing asylum claims, and municipal *empadronamiento* barriers. 4. ''Partnerships & Legal Aid Initiatives'': Collaboration with Bar Associations in Murcia, Madrid, and Almería, community sponsorship, and the June 2023 First Forum in Spain on Refugees.

== Key Provisions & Principles ==

* '''Socioeconomic Rights under the 1951 Convention''': Explicit protection of the rights to association, self-employment (*trabajo por cuenta propia*), practice of liberal professions, housing, and public education.
* '''Labor Access Limit (EU Reception Directive 2013)''': Mandates that asylum seekers must be granted labor market access within a maximum of 9 months from submitting their application.
* '''Equal Treatment under Spanish Ley 12/2009''': Ensures refugees enjoy equal access with Spanish citizens to public employment services, healthcare, social housing, education, and social assistance.
* '''Critical Administrative Bottlenecks''': Identifies that administrative delays, refusal of municipal registration (*empadronamiento*), and banking restrictions represent the primary hurdles to effective refugee integration.
* '''Free Legal Aid Networks''': UNHCR-supported legal guidance programs operated by Bar Associations in Murcia, Madrid, and Almería to help refugees enforce their rights.

== Implementation ==
Implemented by UNHCR Representation in Spain, Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MAEC), Ministry of the Interior, Bar Associations, Municipalities/Local Authorities, and Civil Society Organizations.

== Policy Problems ==

* Long administrative delays in processing asylum applications, leaving applicants without formal documentation.
* Refusal by municipal authorities to grant *empadronamiento* registration, which prevents access to local healthcare and schooling.
* Banking restrictions preventing refugees from opening basic accounts required to receive wages or social assistance.

== Reform ==

* Streamlining administrative procedures to eliminate processing backlogs for Spanish asylum applications.
* Guaranteeing automatic municipal *empadronamiento* for asylum seekers across all Spanish municipalities.
* Expanding free legal assistance networks across all Bar Associations in Spain.
* Mobilizing private sector and university commitments via national refugee forums.

== Summary ==
'''Por los derechos económicos y sociales de las personas refugiadas''' (*For the Economic and Social Rights of Refugees*) is an official human rights policy monograph and advocacy report on the socioeconomic integration and legal protection of refugees in Spain and Europe. Authored by Sophie Muller (UNHCR Representative in Spain / *Representante de ACNUR en España*), it was published in June 2023 by ACNUR/UNHCR Spain in collaboration with the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation (*Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores, Unión Europea y Cooperación — MAEC*). The report presents an empirical and legal analysis of global forced displacement (103 million forcibly displaced persons, including 53.2 million internal displaced persons and 32.5 million refugees) and examines the legal mechanisms required to guarantee sustainable socioeconomic integration rather than mere physical asylum. The monograph systematically evaluates: (1) international legal foundations under the 1951 Geneva Convention on the Status of Refugees and its 1967 Protocol, securing rights to association, self-employment, liberal professions, housing, and education; (2) the UN Global Compact on Refugees (*Pacto Mundial sobre los Refugiados*, UNGA Dec 2018) and World Bank economic impact studies demonstrating that refugee integration strengthens host nation labor markets, tax bases, and social peace; (3) European Union standards under the 2013 Reception Conditions Directive, setting a maximum 9-month exclusion limit for access to the labor market; (4) Spanish national codifications, including Constitutional dignity/health/education rights and Spanish Asylum Act 12/2009 (*Ley 12/2009, de 30 de octubre*), granting refugees equal access to public employment services, healthcare, housing, social assistance, and education; (5) operational administrative barriers in Spain, such as processing delays (*retrasos importantes*), municipal registration obstacles (*empadronamiento*), and commercial banking restrictions (*cuentas bancarias*); and (6) institutional partnership initiatives, including free legal assistance networks organized by the Bar Associations (*Colegios de Abogados*) of Murcia, Madrid, and Almería, refugee-led organizations, and the First Forum in Spain on Refugees (*Primer Foro en España sobre los Refugiados*) held on 20 June 2023 in preparation for the December 2023 Global Refugee Forum in Geneva.

== Legal Basis ==
The international, European, and Spanish statutory provisions analyzed include:

* '''International Treaties & UN Instruments''': 1951 Geneva Convention on the Status of Refugees (*Convención de Ginebra de 1951 sobre el Estatuto de los Refugiados*) and its 1967 Protocol; UN Global Compact on Refugees (*Pacto Mundial sobre los Refugiados*, UNGA Dec 2018).
* '''European Union Directives''': 2013 EU Reception Conditions Directive (*Directiva de Condiciones de Recepción de 2013*).
* '''Spanish Constitutional & Statutory Legislation''': Constitución Española de 1978 (Arts. 10, 27, 43 - human dignity, education, healthcare); Ley 12/2009, de 30 de octubre, reguladora del derecho de asilo y de la protección subsidiaria (Arts. on equal socioeconomic access).

== Background ==
Global forced displacement has reached 103 million people, driven by prolonged conflicts in Syria (nearly 7 million refugees) and the war in Ukraine (over 8 million refugees across Europe). Crucially, 83% of refugees reside in low- and middle-income developing nations, with 8.4 million trapped in protracted exile (>5 years). To move beyond temporary physical shelter toward sustainable protection, the UN Global Compact on Refugees (2018) established economic self-reliance and social rights inclusion as global imperatives based on the 1951 Convention. Sophie Muller published this policy study to assess Spain's progress and identify structural improvements needed to fulfill these standards.

== Objectives ==
1. Transition refugee protection frameworks from basic physical shelter to self-reliant socioeconomic inclusion. 2. Guarantee equal refugee access to employment, education, healthcare, and housing under Ley 12/2009. 3. Eliminate administrative bottlenecks regarding municipal registration (*empadronamiento*) and commercial banking. 4. Expand free legal aid networks through UNHCR partnerships with Spanish Bar Associations (*Colegios de Abogados*). 5. Mobilize public-private commitments through national forums in preparation for global refugee summits.

== Scope ==
The scope of this UNHCR study spans four primary pillars: 1. ''Global Forced Displacement Context'': Analysis of 103 million displaced individuals, Syrian/Ukrainian crises, and host nation distribution. 2. ''International & EU Legal Framework'': 1951 Geneva Convention rights, 2018 Global Compact, and the 9-month maximum labor market exclusion limit under the 2013 EU Reception Directive. 3. ''Spanish Statutory Rights & Administrative Hurdles'': Equal treatment under Asylum Act 12/2009, delays in processing asylum claims, and municipal *empadronamiento* barriers. 4. ''Partnerships & Legal Aid Initiatives'': Collaboration with Bar Associations in Murcia, Madrid, and Almería, community sponsorship, and the June 2023 First Forum in Spain on Refugees.

== Key Provisions & Principles ==

* '''Socioeconomic Rights under the 1951 Convention''': Explicit protection of the rights to association, self-employment (*trabajo por cuenta propia*), practice of liberal professions, housing, and public education.
* '''Labor Access Limit (EU Reception Directive 2013)''': Mandates that asylum seekers must be granted labor market access within a maximum of 9 months from submitting their application.
* '''Equal Treatment under Spanish Ley 12/2009''': Ensures refugees enjoy equal access with Spanish citizens to public employment services, healthcare, social housing, education, and social assistance.
* '''Critical Administrative Bottlenecks''': Identifies that administrative delays, refusal of municipal registration (*empadronamiento*), and banking restrictions represent the primary hurdles to effective refugee integration.
* '''Free Legal Aid Networks''': UNHCR-supported legal guidance programs operated by Bar Associations in Murcia, Madrid, and Almería to help refugees enforce their rights.

== Implementation ==
Implemented by UNHCR Representation in Spain, Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MAEC), Ministry of the Interior, Bar Associations, Municipalities/Local Authorities, and Civil Society Organizations.

== Policy Problems ==

* Long administrative delays in processing asylum applications, leaving applicants without formal documentation.
* Refusal by municipal authorities to grant *empadronamiento* registration, which prevents access to local healthcare and schooling.
* Banking restrictions preventing refugees from opening basic accounts required to receive wages or social assistance.

== Reform ==

* Streamlining administrative procedures to eliminate processing backlogs for Spanish asylum applications.
* Guaranteeing automatic municipal *empadronamiento* for asylum seekers across all Spanish municipalities.
* Expanding free legal assistance networks across all Bar Associations in Spain.
* Mobilizing private sector and university commitments via national refugee forums.

== Relationship with Other Entities ==

* '''Authored by''': Sophie Muller (Representative of UNHCR in Spain).
* '''Issued by''': ACNUR España / UNHCR Representation in Spain.
* '''Analyzes''': 1951 Geneva Convention, UN Global Compact on Refugees (2018), 2013 EU Reception Directive, and Spanish Asylum Act 12/2009.
* '''Evaluates policy of''': MAEC, Bar Associations of Murcia/Madrid/Almería, and World Bank.

== 4. POLICY ANALYSIS ==

* '''Background''': [FACT] The administrative revocation procedure (*procedimiento de revocación*) allows public administrations to modify or leave without effect their own prior administrative acts in favor of citizens when an illegality is detected, even if those acts have become final (*actos firmes*). Under Article 103 of the Spanish Constitution (CE), the Public Administration must serve the general interest with objectivity and act in full submission to the law. Consequently, whenever the Tax Administration becomes aware that a tax assessment or penalty violates the law, it should naturally revoke it. However, in tax practice, revocation was rarely utilized due to Article 219.3 of the Ley General Tributaria (LGT) and Article 10 of the Tax Revision Regulation (RGRVA - RD 520/2005), which strictly provided that the procedure "shall always be initiated ex officio" (*se iniciará siempre de oficio*). Although RGRVA Article 10 allowed taxpayers to "promote" its initiation, it stated that the Tax Administration was under no obligation other than to acknowledge receipt (*acusar recibo*), denying taxpayers standing or judicial remedies. Diego Marín-Barnuevo Fabo (Pérez-Llorca / UAM) published this research monograph analyzing how landmark 2022 Supreme Court decisions fundamentally transformed this paradigm.
* '''Policy Problem''': [FACT]
** '''Ex-Officio Immunity & Denial of Effective Judicial Protection''': Restricting revocation initiation exclusively to ex-officio action created a zone of administrative immunity where the Tax Administration could ignore taxpayer requests pointing out blatant illegalities in firm tax assessments, violating CE Article 24.1 (effective judicial protection) and CE Article 106.1.
** '''Misinterpretation of Administrative Discretion''': The Tax Administration caricatured revocation as a purely discretionary, grace-based power (*potestad graciable*), treating taxpayer petitions as mere informal stimuli requiring no reasoned administrative decision.
** '''Unjust Enrichment & Tax System Injustice''': Forcing taxpayers to maintain unearned tax payments resulting from illegal assessments contradicts CE Article 31, which legitimizes tax collection strictly under statutory law, not via illegal assessments.
** '''Retrospective Impact of Constitutional Annulments''': Thousands of municipal capital gains tax (*plusvalía municipal* / IIVTNU) assessments became firm under statutory rules later declared unconstitutional by STC 59/2017 and STC 182/2021, creating mass taxpayer uncertainty regarding finality vs. restitution.
* '''Legal/Policy Gap''': [FACT] Resolving the contradiction between LGT Article 219.3 (ex-officio initiation) and LGT Article 221.3 (refund of undue payments for firm acts via special revision procedures), establishing that when a taxpayer requests a refund of undue payments, the Tax Administration MUST initiate and resolve the revocation procedure.
* '''Policy Objectives''': [FACT] Guarantee effective judicial protection and good administration in tax matters; establish taxpayer standing to compel Tax Administration decisions on revocation requests; eliminate unearned public enrichment; enforce full administrative submission to constitutional legality (CE Arts. 31, 103, 106.1); and empower administrative courts to grant direct substantive relief without procedural remands.
* '''Policy Implementation & Statutory Mechanics''': [FACT]
** '''1. The Three Statutory Grounds for Tax Revocation (LGT Art. 219.1)''':
*** (i) *Manifest Infringement of the Law (Infracción manifiesta de la ley)*: Requires a clear, obvious, gross, and indisputable legal violation that does not require complex factual or evidentiary inquiry (*"ostentosa, palmaria, evidente, clara, indiscutible"*).
*** (ii) *Supervening Circumstances (Circunstancias sobrevenidas)*: Subsequent legal or factual developments affecting a specific legal situation that demonstrate the unsuitability (*improcedencia*) of the original act (e.g., subsequent judicial annulment of a general regulation or ministerial order underlying the assessment, as in STS 4 Mar 2022).
*** (iii) *Procedural Defenselessness (Indefensión de los interesados)*: Severe procedural defects during management or inspection that deprived the taxpayer of defense rights.
** '''2. Rejection of the "Discretionary Opportunity" Thesis in Tax Law''':
*** Marín-Barnuevo Fabo demonstrates that unlike general administrative law (where revocation may rest on shifting public interest or policy opportunity), LGT Article 219 contains NO opportunity/discretion grounds. All three statutory grounds constitute cases of "qualified illegality" (*anulabilidad cualificada*); once a statutory ground is met, the Tax Administration holds a strict legal duty (*deber de actuación*), not a discretionary option, to revoke.
** '''3. The 2022 Supreme Court Jurisprudential Doctrine (SSTS 9 Feb, 14 Feb, 4 Mar 2022)''':
*** *Iniciación a Instancia de Parte via LGT Art. 221.3*: The Supreme Court ruled that when a taxpayer files a request for refund of undue payments (*devolución de ingresos indebidos*) involving a firm tax act under LGT Art. 221.3 by promoting revocation, the procedure IS initiated at the request of the interested party (*a instancia de parte*).
*** *Duty to Resolve*: The Tax Administration IS OBLIGATED to issue a reasoned resolution or express decision (or face administrative silence) and CANNOT dismiss the request by claiming ex-officio exclusivity under Art. 219.3 or RGRVA Art. 10.
*** *Judicial Review & Direct Merit Rulings*: Administrative silence or explicit refusal is fully subject to judicial review (*control judicial*). Under principles of full jurisdiction (*plenitud de jurisdicción*) and effective judicial protection, administrative courts possessing necessary facts HAVE THE POWER to rule directly on the merits and order the revocation and refund, WITHOUT ordering procedural remand (*retroacción de actuaciones*) to the Tax Administration.
** '''4. Practical Application to Municipal Capital Gains Tax (Plusvalía / IIVTNU)''':
*** *Under Ground 1 (Infracción Manifiesta)*: Rejects revocation for IIVTNU liquidations based on STC 59/2017 because verifying whether a specific transfer suffered a loss requires evidentiary analysis, failing the "manifest/obvious" test.
*** *Under Ground 2 (Circunstancias Sobrevenidas)*: Supports revocation for firm IIVTNU liquidations where no value increase occurred, viewing the constitutional annulment as a supervening circumstance, provided the 4-year prescription period has not expired. However, notes that STC 182/2021 explicitly restricted its retroactive effects, treating non-appealed firm assessments as consolidated situations.
* '''Evidence & Impact''': [FACT] Evaluates Diego Marín-Barnuevo Fabo 2023 study; LGT Arts. 219 & 221.3; RGRVA Art. 10; Spanish Constitution Arts. 9.3, 24.1, 29, 31, 103, 106.1; SSTS 9 Feb 2022, 14 Feb 2022, 4 Mar 2022; STC 59/2017; STC 182/2021; STJUE 21 Oct 2021 (C-80/20); and private equity study by Ander Valverde González-Morejón.
* '''Evaluation & Reform''': [FACT] Concludes that the 2022 Supreme Court doctrine represents a major constitutional advance for taxpayer protection in Spain, dismantling administrative arbitrariness and establishing genuine judicial enforcement over firm illegal tax assessments. Recommends: (1) amending RGRVA Article 10 to formally align its wording with Supreme Court doctrine by acknowledging taxpayer standing to initiate revocation under LGT Art. 221.3; (2) extending taxpayer standing to initiate revocation to cases involving non-monetary tax acts (such as negative tax bases / *bases imponibles negativas*) under the constitutional principle of equality (CE Art. 31); and (3) establishing clear administrative guidelines for applying supervening judicial annulments to firm local tax assessments.

== Summary ==
'''Presente y futuro del procedimiento de revocación en materia tributaria''' (*Present and Future of the Revocation Procedure in Tax Matters*) is an academic research monograph on Spanish tax law, special administrative revision procedures (*procedimientos especiales de revisión*), the revocation of firm tax acts in favor of taxpayers (*revocación de actos tributarios en beneficio de los interesados* under Art. 219 Ley General Tributaria - LGT), taxpayer standing to initiate revocation (*iniciación a instancia de parte*), the prohibition of administrative arbitrariness (*interdicción de la arbitrariedad* under CE Art. 103), and the landmark 2022 Supreme Court jurisprudence (SSTS 9 Feb 2022, 14 Feb 2022, 4 Mar 2022) connecting tax revocation with the refund of undue payments (*devolución de ingresos indebidos* under LGT Art. 221.3). Authored by Diego Marín-Barnuevo Fabo (Of Counsel Fiscal at Pérez-Llorca and Full Professor of Financial and Tax Law at Universidad Autónoma de Madrid), it was published in *Revista Jurídica Pérez-Llorca* (pp. 46–63). The monograph presents a comprehensive legal, exegesis, and comparative analysis of Article 219 LGT and Article 10 of the Tax Revision Regulation (RGRVA - RD 520/2005), which historically restricted revocation to ex-officio initiation (*de oficio*), creating a structural barrier for taxpayers. The study systematically evaluates: (1) the three statutory grounds for tax revocation under LGT Article 219.1—manifest infringement of the law (*infracción manifiesta de la ley*), supervening circumstances demonstrating unsuitability (*circunstancias sobrevenidas*), and procedural defenselessness (*indefensión*); (2) the doctrinal debate contrasting the classical administrative view of discretionary opportunity (*oportunidad/discrecionalidad*) with the tax law doctrine of qualified illegality (*anulabilidad cualificada*) bound by the principle of legality and good administration; (3) the evolution of Supreme Court jurisprudence from rigid ex-officio exclusivity (STS 19 May 2011) to judicial control of discretionary powers (STS 19 Feb 2014) and the landmark 2022 rulings; (4) the 2022 Supreme Court doctrine establishing that when a taxpayer requests a refund of undue payments for a firm tax assessment under LGT Art. 221.3, the Tax Administration IS OBLIGATED to resolve the revocation request and cannot hide behind ex-officio exclusivity; (5) the judicial power of administrative courts to rule directly on the merits (*pronunciamiento sobre el fondo*) and revoke illegal acts without ordering procedural remand (*retroacción*); and (6) the practical application of this doctrine to Municipal Capital Gains Tax (*plusvalía municipal* / IIVTNU) claims following Constitutional Court rulings (STC 59/2017 and STC 182/2021).

The statutory, constitutional, and jurisprudential framework analyzed in the study includes:

* '''Spanish General Tax Legislation''': Ley 58/2003, de 17 de diciembre, General Tributaria (LGT Arts. 213, 216, 217, 219, 220, 221, 244, 252); Real Decreto 520/2005 (RGRVA Art. 10 - Reglamento General de Revisión en Vía Administrativa); Ley 230/1963 General Tributaria (former LGT Art. 8).

== Background ==
The administrative revocation procedure (*procedimiento de revocación*) allows public administrations to modify or leave without effect their own prior administrative acts in favor of citizens when an illegality is detected, even if those acts have become final (*actos firmes*). Under Article 103 of the Spanish Constitution (CE), the Public Administration must serve the general interest with objectivity and act in full submission to the law. Consequently, whenever the Tax Administration becomes aware that a tax assessment or penalty violates the law, it should naturally revoke it. However, in tax practice, revocation was rarely utilized due to Article 219.3 of the Ley General Tributaria (LGT) and Article 10 of the Tax Revision Regulation (RGRVA - RD 520/2005), which strictly provided that the procedure "shall always be initiated ex officio" (*se iniciará siempre de oficio*). Although RGRVA Article 10 allowed taxpayers to "promote" its initiation, it stated that the Tax Administration was under no obligation other than to acknowledge receipt (*acusar recibo*), denying taxpayers standing or judicial remedies. Diego Marín-Barnuevo Fabo published this research monograph analyzing how landmark 2022 Supreme Court decisions fundamentally transformed this paradigm.

== Objectives ==
1. Analyze the legal framework governing the revocation of firm tax acts under LGT Article 219 and RGRVA Article 10. 2. Examine the doctrinal debate contrasting discretionary opportunity (*oportunidad*) with qualified illegality (*anulabilidad cualificada*). 3. Trace the evolution of Supreme Court jurisprudence leading to the landmark 2022 decisions. 4. Explain the 2022 Supreme Court doctrine recognizing taxpayer standing to initiate revocation via refund requests (LGT Art. 221.3). 5. Demonstrate the judicial power of administrative courts to rule directly on the merits (*pronunciamiento sobre el fondo*) without ordering procedural remands. 6. Assess the practical application of tax revocation to Municipal Capital Gains Tax (*plusvalía municipal*) claims post-STC 59/2017 and STC 182/2021.

== Scope ==
The scope of this tax law study spans five core thematic areas: 1. ''Legal Framework & The Three Grounds for Revocation (LGT Art. 219)'': Manifest infringement of the law (*infracción manifiesta*), supervening circumstances (*circunstancias sobrevenidas*), and procedural defenselessness (*indefensión*). 2. ''Doctrinal Interpretation & Legal Nature'': Rejection of the "discretionary opportunity" thesis and confirmation that tax revocation rests on qualified illegality requiring mandatory administrative action. 3. ''Supreme Court Jurisprudential Evolution'': Transition from rigid ex-officio exclusivity (2011) to judicial review of administrative discretion (2014) and prohibition of arbitrariness (2017). 4. ''The 2022 Supreme Court Landmark Doctrine'': Recognition of taxpayer standing to initiate revocation via LGT Art. 221.3, administrative duty to resolve, and judicial power to grant substantive remedies. 5. ''Practical Application to Local Capital Gains Tax (IIVTNU)'': Analysis of *infracción manifiesta* vs. *circunstancias sobrevenidas* in firm IIVTNU liquidations following STC 59/2017 and STC 182/2021.

== Key Provisions & Principles ==

* '''The Three Statutory Grounds for Revocation (LGT Art. 219.1)''': Revocation is permitted only when: (1) the tax act manifestly infringes the law; (2) supervening circumstances demonstrate its unsuitability; or (3) procedural defenselessness occurred.
* '''2022 Supreme Court Standing Doctrine (LGT Arts. 219 & 221.3)''': When a taxpayer requests a refund of undue payments involving a firm act under LGT Art. 221.3 by promoting revocation, the procedure IS initiated at the request of the interested party (*a instancia de parte*). The Tax Administration IS OBLIGATED to issue a reasoned decision.
* '''Definition of Manifest Infringement of Law''': Defined by jurisprudence as a legal violation that is obvious, clear, gross, indisputable, and self-evident (*"ostentosa, palmaria, evidente, clara, indiscutible"*), requiring no complex evidentiary inquiry.
* '''Supervening Circumstances Ground (SSTS 4 Mar 2022)''': Subsequent judicial annulment of a general regulation or ministerial order underlying a tax assessment constitutes a supervening circumstance justifying revocation of the firm assessment.
* '''Direct Judicial Relief Without Remand''': Administrative courts reviewing a refusal to revoke have full jurisdiction to rule directly on the merits and order tax refunds without remanding the case back to the Tax Administration.

== Implementation ==
Applied by State Tax Administration Agency (AEAT), Local Authorities / Municipalities, Supreme Court (Third Chamber), Economic-Administrative Tribunals (TEAC/TEAR), Administrative Courts, and Tax Attorneys.

== Policy Problems ==

* Structural obstacle of LGT Art. 219.3 and RGRVA Art. 10 used by tax authorities to dismiss taxpayer revocation petitions without a decision.
* Unjust public enrichment resulting from retaining tax revenues generated by illegal firm assessments.
* Practical complexity in applying revocation to firm *plusvalía municipal* assessments after Constitutional Court annulments (STC 59/2017 and STC 182/2021).

== Reform ==

* Amending RGRVA Article 10 to align text with 2022 Supreme Court doctrine acknowledging taxpayer standing via LGT Art. 221.3.
* Extending taxpayer standing to initiate revocation for non-monetary firm tax acts (such as negative tax bases) under constitutional equality.
* Reaffirming the Tax Administration's duty to issue express decisions on all revocation petitions under the principle of good administration (*principio de buena administración*).

== 4. ANÁLISIS DE POLÍTICA PÚBLICA ==

* '''Antecedentes''': [HECHO] El procedimiento administrativo de revocación (*procedimiento de revocación*) permite a las administraciones públicas modificar o dejar sin efecto sus propios actos administrativos firmes en beneficio de los ciudadanos cuando se detecte una ilegalidad. Bajo el artículo 103 de la Constitución Española (CE), la Administración Pública debe servir con objetividad los intereses generales y actuar con sometimiento pleno a la ley y al Derecho. En consecuencia, cuando la Administración tributaria tenga conocimiento de que una liquidación o sanción viola la ley, debería proceder a su revocación. Sin embargo, en la práctica tributaria española, la revocación apenas se utilizaba debido al artículo 219.3 de la Ley General Tributaria (LGT) y al artículo 10 del Reglamento General de Revisión en Vía Administrativa (RGRVA - RD 520/2005), los cuales preveían expresamente que el procedimiento "se iniciará siempre de oficio". Aunque el artículo 10 del RGRVA permitía a los contribuyentes "promover" su iniciación, señalaba que la Administración no estaba obligada más que a acusar recibo (*acusar recibo*), negando legitimación y recursos a los ciudadanos. Diego Marín-Barnuevo Fabo publicó esta monografía analizando cómo las sentencias históricas del Tribunal Supremo de 2022 transformaron este paradigma de forma radical.
* '''Problema de Política Pública''': [HECHO]
** '''Inmunidad del Oficio y Denegación de Tutela Judicial Efectiva''': Restringir la iniciación de la revocación exclusivamente a la vía de oficio generaba un ámbito de inmunidad administrativa en el que la Hacienda Pública podía ignorar las peticiones del contribuyente que advertían ilegalidades manifiestas en actos firmes, vulnerando los Arts. 24.1 y 106.1 de la Constitución Española.
** '''Interpretación Errónea de la Discrecionalidad''': La Administración tributaria caracterizaba la revocación como una potestad graciable o de mera oportunidad (*potestad graciable*), tratando las solicitudes de los contribuyentes como meros estímulos informales que no requerían resolución motivada.
** '''Enriquecimiento Injusto e Injusticia del Sistema Tributario''': Obligar a los ciudadanos a soportar pagos tributarios indebidos derivados de liquidaciones ilegales contraviene el Art. 31 de la CE, que legitima la recaudación únicamente cuando se realiza de acuerdo con la ley.
** '''Impacto Retroactivo de Anulaciones Constitucionales''': Miles de liquidaciones del Impuesto sobre el Incremento de Valor de los Terrenos de Naturaleza Urbana (*plusvalía municipal* / IIVTNU) devinieron firmes bajo normas declaradas inconstitucionales por la STC 59/2017 y la STC 182/2021, generando incertidumbre sobre firmeza versus devolución.
* '''Vacío Legal/de Política Pública''': [HECHO] Resolver la contradicción entre el Art. 219.3 LGT (iniciación de oficio) y el Art. 221.3 LGT (devolución de ingresos indebidos de actos firmes mediante procedimientos especiales de revisión), estableciendo que cuando el contribuyente solicita la devolución de ingresos indebidos, la Administración DEBE tramitar y resolver la revocación.
* '''Objetivos de Política Pública''': [HECHO] Garantizar la tutela judicial efectiva y la buena administración en materia tributaria; reconocer la legitimación del contribuyente para exigir resolución motivada; erradicar el enriquecimiento injusto de las arcas públicas; imponer el sometimiento pleno de la Administración a la legalidad constitucional (CE Arts. 31, 103, 106.1); y facultar a los tribunales contencioso-administrativos para estimar directamente el fondo sin retroacción de actuaciones.
* '''Implementación de Política Pública y Mecánica Normativa''': [HECHO]
** '''1. Las Tres Causas Tasadas de Revocación Tributaria (Art. 219.1 LGT)''':
*** (i) *Infracción Manifiesta de la Ley*: Requiere una vulneración patente, clara, indiscutible y ostensible que no precise de una compleja investigación fáctica o probatoria (*"ostentosa, palmaria, evidente, clara, indiscutible"*).
*** (ii) *Circunstancias Sobrevenidas*: Acontecimientos jurídicos o fácticos posteriores que afecten a la situación jurídica y demuestren la improcedencia del acto originario (p. ej., la anulación judicial posterior de una disposición general o orden ministerial que servía de base a la liquidación, como en la STS de 4 de marzo de 2022).
*** (iii) *Indefensión de los Interesados*: Defectos procedimentales graves en la gestión o inspección que hayan privado al contribuyente de sus medios de defensa.
** '''2. Rechazo de la Tesis de la "Oportunidad Discrecional" en Derecho Tributario''':
*** Marín-Barnuevo Fabo demuestra que, a diferencia del Derecho administrativo general (donde la revocación puede responder a razones de oportunidad o interés público cambiante), el Art. 219 de la LGT NO contempla causas de oportunidad. Las tres causas legales constituyen supuestos de "anulabilidad cualificada"; una vez concurrida la causa, la Administración ostenta un deber legal de actuación (*deber de actuación*) y no una opción discrecional.
** '''3. La Doctrina Jurisprudencial del Tribunal Supremo de 2022 (SSTS 9 Feb, 14 Feb, 4 Mar 2022)''':
*** *Iniciación a Instancia de Parte vía Art. 221.3 LGT*: El Tribunal Supremo determinó que cuando el contribuyente insta la devolución de ingresos indebidos de un acto firme al amparo del Art. 221.3 LGT promoviendo la revocación, el procedimiento SE INICIA a instancia de parte (*a instancia de parte*).
*** *Obligación de Resolver*: La Administración tributaria VIENE OBLIGADA a dictar resolución motivada (o incurrir en silencio administrativo) y NO PUEDE inadmitir la petición amparándose en la exclusividad del oficio del Art. 219.3 o del Art. 10 del RGRVA.
*** *Control Judicial y Pronunciamiento sobre el Fondo*: El silencio o rechazo expreso es plenamente fiscalizable por la jurisdicción contencioso-administrativa. En virtud de la plenitud de jurisdicción y la tutela judicial efectiva, los tribunales que dispongan de los elementos de juicio necesarios TIENEN LA FACULTAD de resolver sobre el fondo y ordenar la revocación y devolución, SIN decretar la retroacción de actuaciones a la Administración.
** '''4. Aplicación Práctica a la Plusvalía Municipal (IIVTNU)''':
*** *Por la Causa 1.ª (Infracción Manifiesta)*: Rechaza la revocación de liquidaciones firmes de IIVTNU con base en la STC 59/2017 porque verificar si en una transmisión concreta hubo minusvalía exige prueba contradictoria, no cumpliendo el requisito de "manifiesta/evidente".
*** *Por la Causa 2.ª (Circunstancias Sobrevenidas)*: Admite la revocación para liquidaciones firmes de IIVTNU donde no existió incremento de valor, al considerar la declaración de inconstitucionalidad como circunstancia sobrevenida, siempre que no haya prescripto el plazo de 4 años. No obstante, advierte que la STC 182/2021 limitó expresamente sus efectos retroactivos, considerando las liquidaciones no recurridas como situaciones consolidadas.
* '''Evidencia e Impacto''': [HECHO] Evalúa el estudio de Diego Marín-Barnuevo Fabo de 2023; la LGT (Arts. 219 y 221.3); el RGRVA (Art. 10); la Constitución Española (Arts. 9.3, 24.1, 29, 31, 103, 106.1); las SSTS de 9 de febrero de 2022, 14 de febrero de 2022 y 4 de marzo de 2022; la STC 59/2017; la STC 182/2021; la STJUE de 21 de octubre de 2021 (C-80/20); y la monografía sobre capital riesgo de Ander Valverde González-Morejón.
* '''Evaluación y Propuestas de Reforma''': [HECHO] Concluye que la doctrina del Tribunal Supremo de 2022 representa un avance constitucional decisivo para la protección de los contribuyentes en España, desmontando la arbitrariedad administrativa y garantizando la fiscalización judicial de actos firmes ilegales. Recomienda: (1) modificar el artículo 10 del RGRVA para acomodar su texto a la jurisprudencia del Tribunal Supremo, reconociendo la iniciación a instancia de parte vía Art. 221.3 LGT; (2) extender la legitimación del contribuyente para instar la revocación a actos tributarios no cuantitativos (como la acreditación de bases imponibles negativas) en virtud del principio de igualdad (Art. 31 CE); y (3) fijar directrices administrativas claras para aplicar la anulación judicial sobrevenida a las liquidaciones firmes de tributos locales.

== Resumen ==
'''Presente y futuro del procedimiento de revocación en materia tributaria''' es una monografía de investigación jurídica académica sobre Derecho tributario español, procedimientos especiales de revisión (*procedimientos especiales de revisión*), la revocación de actos tributarios firmes en beneficio de los interesados (*revocación de actos tributarios en beneficio de los interesados* conforme al Art. 219 de la Ley General Tributaria - LGT), la legitimación del contribuyente para iniciar la revocación (*iniciación a instancia de parte*), la interdicción de la arbitrariedad administrativa (*interdicción de la arbitrariedad* del Art. 103 CE) y la jurisprudencia histórica del Tribunal Supremo de 2022 (SSTS 9 Feb 2022, 14 Feb 2022, 4 Mar 2022) que vincula la revocación tributaria con la devolución de ingresos indebidos (*devolución de ingresos indebidos* del Art. 221.3 LGT). Elaborada por Diego Marín-Barnuevo Fabo (Of Counsel Fiscal en Pérez-Llorca y Catedrático de Derecho Financiero y Tributario en la Universidad Autónoma de Madrid), fue publicada en la *Revista Jurídica Pérez-Llorca* (págs. 46–63). La monografía aporta un análisis exegético y doctrinal del artículo 219 LGT y del artículo 10 del RGRVA (RD 520/2005), los cuales restringían históricamente la revocación a la iniciación de oficio (*de oficio*), generando una barrera infranqueable para los contribuyentes. El estudio evalúa: (1) las tres causas tasadas del Art. 219.1 LGT (infracción manifiesta de la ley, circunstancias sobrevenidas e indefensión); (2) la contraposición entre la oportunidad discrecional administrativa y la anulabilidad cualificada del Derecho tributario; (3) la evolución de la jurisprudencia del Tribunal Supremo desde la rigidez de 2011 hasta los fallos de 2022; (4) la doctrina de 2022 que impone el deber de resolver a la Administración cuando el contribuyente insta la devolución de ingresos indebidos de actos firmes vía Art. 221.3 LGT; (5) la facultad de los tribunales contenciosos para resolver sobre el fondo sin decretar la retroacción de actuaciones; y (6) la aplicación práctica a las liquidaciones firmes de la *plusvalía municipal* (IIVTNU) tras las sentencias del Tribunal Constitucional (STC 59/2017 y STC 182/2021).

== Base Legal ==
El marco normativo y jurisprudencial analizado incluye:

* '''Legislación Tributaria General Española''': Ley 58/2003, de 17 de diciembre, General Tributaria (LGT Arts. 213, 216, 217, 219, 220, 221, 244, 252); Real Decreto 520/2005 (RGRVA Art. 10 - Reglamento General de Revisión en Vía Administrativa); Ley 230/1963 General Tributaria.
* '''Disposiciones Constitucionales Españolas''': Constitución Española de 1978 (Art. 9.3 - interdicción de la arbitrariedad; Art. 24.1 - tutela judicial efectiva; Art. 29 - derecho de petición; Art. 31 - deber de contribuir conforme a la ley; Art. 103 - sometimiento pleno a la ley; Art. 106.1 - control judicial).
* '''Procedimiento Administrativo y Jurisdicción''': Ley 39/2015 (LPACAP DA 1ª); Ley 30/1992 (RJAP-PAC DA 5ª); Ley 29/1998 (LJCA Art. 1.1); TRLRHL (Ley de Haciendas Locales Art. 19).
* '''Precedentes Judiciales Clave''':
** ''Tribunal Supremo de España (Sala 3ª / Sección 2ª)'': STS 19 de mayo de 2011; STS 19 de febrero de 2014; SSTS 22 de noviembre de 2016, 22 de febrero de 2017, 28 de febrero de 2017, 13 de junio de 2017; STS 26 de septiembre de 2017; SSTS 9 de febrero de 2022 (Rec. 126/2019), 14 de febrero de 2022 (Rec. 699/2020), 4 de marzo de 2022 (Rec. 865/2020); SSTS 17 de junio de 2021, 18 de enero de 2023.
** ''Tribunal Constitucional de España'': STC 176/1996; STC 9/2005; STC 59/2017 (IIVTNU); STC 182/2021 (IIVTNU).
** ''Tribunal de Justicia de la Unión Europea (TJUE)'': STJUE 21 de octubre de 2021 (C-80/20 - buena administración y devolución del IVA).

== Antecedentes ==
El procedimiento de revocación permite a las administraciones públicas dejar sin efecto sus propios actos firmes cuando incurren en ilegalidad. Bajo el artículo 103 de la Constitución Española, la Administración sirve a los intereses generales con sometimiento pleno a la ley. Sin embargo, en la práctica tributaria, la revocación era inviable porque el Art. 219.3 LGT y el Art. 10 del RGRVA disponían que el procedimiento se iniciaría "siempre de oficio". Cuando el contribuyente solicitaba la revocación, la Administración se limitaba a acusar recibo sin dictar resolución motivada, amparándose en la exclusividad del oficio. Diego Marín-Barnuevo Fabo elaboró esta monografía para analizar cómo la jurisprudencia del Tribunal Supremo de 2022 desmontó esta barrera procedimental.

== Objetivos ==
1. Analizar el régimen jurídico de la revocación de actos tributarios firmes bajo el Art. 219 LGT y el Art. 10 del RGRVA. 2. Examinar el debate doctrinal entre oportunidad discrecional (*oportunidad*) y anulabilidad cualificada (*anulabilidad cualificada*). 3. Trazar la evolución jurisprudencial del Tribunal Supremo hasta los fallos históricos de 2022. 4. Explicar la doctrina del TS de 2022 que reconoce la legitimación del contribuyente para instar la revocación mediante la devolución de ingresos indebidos (Art. 221.3 LGT). 5. Demostrar la potestad de los tribunales contenciosos para pronunciarse sobre el fondo sin decretar la retroacción de actuaciones. 6. Evaluar la aplicación práctica de la revocación a las liquidaciones firmes de la *plusvalía municipal* tras las sentencias del TC.

== Alcance ==
El estudio abarca cinco bloques temáticos principales: 1. ''Marco Legal y Tres Causas Tasadas (Art. 219 LGT)'': Infracción manifiesta de la ley, circunstancias sobrevenidas e indefensión. 2. ''Naturaleza Jurídica y Debate Doctrinal'': Rechazo de la tesis de la oportunidad discrecional y confirmación del deber de actuar ante actos nulos o anulables cualificados. 3. ''Evolución Jurisprudencial del Tribunal Supremo'': Transición desde la rigidez de 2011 hasta el control judicial de la discrecionalidad en 2014 y 2017. 4. ''Doctrina Histórica de las Sentencias de 2022'': Legitimación del contribuyente vía Art. 221.3 LGT, deber de resolver de la Administración y plenitud de jurisdicción de los tribunales. 5. ''Aplicación Práctica a la Plusvalía Municipal (IIVTNU)'': Análisis de la infracción manifiesta versus circunstancias sobrevenidas en liquidaciones firmes post-STC 59/2017 y STC 182/2021.

== Disposiciones y Principios Clave ==

* '''Tres Causas Tasadas de Revocación (Art. 219.1 LGT)''': Solo procede la revocación cuando: (1) el acto infrinja manifiestamente la ley; (2) concurran circunstancias sobrevenidas que determinen su improcedencia; o (3) se haya producido indefensión.
* '''Doctrina TS 2022 de Legitimación (Arts. 219 y 221.3 LGT)''': Cuando el contribuyente insta la devolución de ingresos indebidos de un acto firme al amparo del Art. 221.3 LGT promoviendo la revocación, el procedimiento SE INICIA a instancia de parte. La Administración VIENE OBLIGADA a resolver.
* '''Definición de Infracción Manifiesta''': Vulneración patente, clara, indiscutible y manifiesta (*"ostentosa, palmaria, evidente, clara, indiscutible"*), que no requiere indagación probatoria compleja.
* '''Causa de Circunstancias Sobrevenidas (SSTS 4 Mar 2022)''': La anulación judicial posterior de una disposición general que servía de base a una liquidación tributaria constituye una circunstancia sobrevenida que justifica la revocación del acto firme.
* '''Pronunciamiento sobre el Fondo sin Retroacción''': Los tribunales contencioso-administrativos que revisan la denegación de una revocación tienen plenitud de jurisdicción para resolver sobre el fondo y fijar la devolución sin devolver el expediente a la Administración.

== Implementación ==
Aplicado por la Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Ayuntamientos / Entidades Locales, Tribunal Supremo (Sala 3ª), Tribunales Económico-Administrativos (TEAC/TEAR), Juzgados de lo Contencioso-Administrativo y Abogados Tributaristas.

== Problemas de Política Pública ==

* Barrera procedimental del Art. 219.3 LGT y Art. 10 RGRVA utilizada por la Hacienda Pública para inadmitir peticiones de revocación de los contribuyentes.
* Enriquecimiento injusto de la Administración al retener tributos cobrados mediante liquidaciones firmes pero ilegales.
* Complejidad técnica para aplicar la revocación a las liquidaciones firmes de la *plusvalía municipal* tras las declaraciones de inconstitucionalidad (STC 59/2017 y STC 182/2021).

== Reforma ==

* Modificación del artículo 10 del RGRVA para adaptar su redacción a la doctrina del Tribunal Supremo de 2022 sobre la iniciación a instancia de parte vía Art. 221.3 LGT.
* Extensión de la legitimación del contribuyente para instar la revocación de actos firmes no cuantitativos (como bases imponibles negativas) en virtud del principio de igualdad.
* Consagración del deber de la Administración de dictar resolución motivada ante cualquier solicitud de revocación conforme al principio de buena administración (*principio de buena administración*).

== Relación con otras Entidades ==

* '''Autor''': Diego Marín-Barnuevo Fabo (Pérez-Llorca / UAM).
* '''Publicado por''': Pérez-Llorca.
* '''Analiza''': Ley 58/2003 General Tributaria Arts. 219 y 221.3, RGRVA Art. 10 y Constitución Española Arts. 31, 103, 106.1.
* '''Evalúa la política de''': AEAT, Tribunal Supremo (Sala 3ª), Tribunal Constitucional y Consejo de Estado.

* '''Definition''': [FACT] A specialized academic legal research monograph on European Union financial services regulation, payment services codification, Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (PSD2), Spanish Royal Decree-Law 19/2018 (*Real Decreto-ley 19/2018 de servicios de pago*), Regulatory Technical Standards for Strong Customer Authentication and Common and Secure Open Standards of Communication (RTS SCA & CSC - Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/389), open banking architecture, third-party payment providers (TPPs), Account Information Services (AIS), Payment Initiation Services (PIS), and financial regulatory sandboxes authored by Paula De Biase (Counsel at Pérez-Llorca, Corporate Department, Head of Financial Services Practice) and Álvaro Basco Domínguez (Lawyer at Pérez-Llorca, Corporate Department), published in *Revista Jurídica Pérez-Llorca* (pp. 100–115). # the statutory creation and licensing framework for two new regulated payment services—Account Information Services (AIS / *Servicios de Información sobre Cuentas*) and Payment Initiation Services (PIS / *Servicios de Iniciación de Pagos*)—enabling Third Party Providers (TPPs) to access customer account data via Application Programming Interfaces (APIs / *interfaces de programación de aplicaciones*), replacing legacy screen-scraping techniques;

# the Spanish Financial System Digital Transformation Bill (*Proyecto de Ley de transformación digital del sistema financiero*) establishing a regulatory sandbox for Fintech testing with live clients;
# two-factor Strong Customer Authentication (SCA / *autenticación reforzada / SAC*) requirements under RDL 19/2018 Article 3 and RTS SCA & CSC across Knowledge (*conocimiento*), Possession (*posesión*), and Inherence (*inherencia*) factors;
# statutory SCA exemptions for low-value payments, trusted beneficiaries, recurring transactions, and intra-holder account transfers; and
# the European Banking Authority (EBA) supervisory extension timeline (EBA Opinion of 16 October 2019 setting 31 December 2020 as the migration deadline for e-commerce SCA) and its operational disruption during the COVID-19 pandemic.

== 4. POLICY ANALYSIS ==

* '''Background''': [FACT] Following the 2008 global financial crisis, most European financial regulatory directives adopted a restrictive posture focused on heightened bank supervision and customer transparency. In contrast, Directive (UE) 2015/2366 (PSD2) introduced a paradigm shift by compelling financial institutions to open customer account data to regulated third-party providers (TPPs), giving rise to *open banking*. Spain transposed PSD2 via Royal Decree-Law 19/2018 (*Real Decreto-ley 19/2018 de servicios de pago*) and its regulatory development under Royal Decree 736/2019. Simultaneously, the European Commission enacted Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/389 (RTS SCA & CSC), establishing technical standards for two-factor Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) and secure open communication interfaces (APIs). Paula De Biase and Álvaro Basco Domínguez (Pérez-Llorca) published a specialized monograph analyzing the legal, technical, and strategic challenges of open banking and SCA implementation in Spain.
* '''Policy Problem''': [FACT]
** '''Friction Between Digital Security and User Experience''': Strict mandatory two-factor SCA requirements threaten seamless e-commerce user experiences ("one-click checkout"), creating risks of cart abandonment and transaction failure for online merchants.
** '''Obsolescence of Legacy Screen-Scraping Techniques''': Unregulated data extraction practices (*screen-scraping*) posed severe data protection and security risks, requiring migration to standardized, secure APIs managed by account servicing payment service providers.
** '''Regulatory Authorization Bottlenecks at Banco de España''': Late national transposition and technical complexities delayed regulatory licensing, leaving very few registered TPPs in Spain for AIS and PIS operations.
** '''KYC/AML Ambiguities in Payment Initiation Services (PIS)''': Uncertainty regarding whether TPPs or merchants must perform Anti-Money Laundering (AML) / Know Your Customer (KYC) verification for B2B platforms.
** '''COVID-19 E-Commerce Disruption''': Pandemic-induced shifts toward online commerce collided with the EBA's 31 December 2020 migration deadline for e-commerce SCA, pressuring vulnerable business sectors (e.g., hospitality and catering).
* '''Legal/Policy Gap''': [FACT] Establishing a clear statutory and technical framework under RDL 19/2018 that enables open banking innovation, balances fraud prevention with transaction speed, and streamlines regulatory authorization for Fintech start-ups via simplified registration and sandbox mechanisms.
* '''Policy Objectives''': [FACT] Foster financial market competition and innovation; protect consumers against digital fraud via two-factor authentication; standardize secure communication via open APIs; grant customers sovereignty over their financial data; and provide flexible regulatory pathways for new market entrants.
* '''Policy Implementation & Statutory Mechanics''': [FACT]
** '''1. Regulation of New Payment Services (AIS & PIS)''':
*** ''Account Information Services (AIS / Servicios de Información sobre Cuentas)'': Online services providing aggregated information on payment accounts held across multiple providers, enabling financial management tools and creditworthiness assessments.
*** ''Payment Initiation Services (PIS / Servicios de Iniciación de Pagos)'': Services initiating a payment order at the user's request from an account held at another provider, enabling direct bank transfers for e-commerce transactions without navigating to online banking portals.
** '''2. National Flexibility Options in Spain''':
*** ''Simplified Registration Exception (€3M Threshold)'': Spain implemented a national option under PSD2 allowing payment service providers operating under €3 million in monthly transactions (12-month average) to obtain a simplified registration rather than a full payment institution license (excluding AIS and PIS).
*** ''Regulatory Sandbox Bill (Proyecto de Ley de transformación digital del sistema financiero)'': Establishes a controlled testing environment allowing Fintechs to test innovative financial models with live clients under regulatory supervision prior to formal licensing.
** '''3. Strong Customer Authentication (SCA / SAC) Architecture''':
*** Defined under RDL 19/2018 Article 3 as authentication based on two or more independent factors: (i) *Knowledge* (something only the user knows, e.g., password/PIN); (ii) *Possession* (something only the user possesses, e.g., mobile device/security token); and (iii) *Inherence* (something the user is, e.g., biometrics).
*** Mandatory Triggers: Online account access, electronic payment initiation, and remote actions with fraud risk.
*** Statutory Exemptions under RTS SCA & CSC: Low-value payments, trusted beneficiaries (white lists), recurring transactions, and intra-holder account transfers.
** '''4. Technical Migration & EBA Extension''':
*** RTS SCA & CSC entered into force on 14 September 2019. Recognizing e-commerce adaptation complexities, the EBA granted supervisor flexibility (EBA Opinion of 16 October 2019), establishing a strict migration deadline of 31 December 2020 for e-commerce SCA implementation in Spain and the EU.
* '''Evidence & Impact''': [FACT] Evaluates Paula De Biase & Álvaro Basco Domínguez 2020 study; Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (PSD2); Real Decreto-ley 19/2018; Real Decreto 736/2019; Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/389 (RTS SCA & CSC); EBA Opinion of 16 October 2019; Spanish Regulatory Sandbox Bill; and private equity study by Ander Valverde González-Morejón.
* '''Evaluation & Reform''': [FACT] Concludes that open banking represents an unstoppable structural transformation of the financial system. Notes that while PSD2 opened payment account data, open banking is expanding toward broader financial aggregation (loans, insurance, investments) governed by general privacy and consumer protection laws. Recommends: (1) completing full technical implementation of secure open APIs across all account servicing banks; (2) harmonizing EBA guidance on KYC/AML responsibilities for B2B payment initiation platforms; and (3) enacting the Spanish Financial System Digital Transformation Bill to operationalize the regulatory sandbox for Fintech innovation.

== Summary ==
'''PSD2: Escenario actual tras su implantación y retos jurídicos del “open banking”''' (*PSD2: Current Scenario Following Its Transposition and Legal Challenges of Open Banking*) is an academic research monograph on European Union financial services regulation, payment services codification, Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (PSD2), Spanish Royal Decree-Law 19/2018 (*Real Decreto-ley 19/2018 de servicios de pago*), Regulatory Technical Standards for Strong Customer Authentication and Common and Secure Open Standards of Communication (RTS SCA & CSC - Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/389), open banking architecture, third-party payment providers (TPPs), Account Information Services (AIS), Payment Initiation Services (PIS), and financial regulatory sandboxes. Authored by Paula De Biase (Counsel at Pérez-Llorca, Corporate Department, Head of Financial Services Practice) and Álvaro Basco Domínguez (Lawyer at Pérez-Llorca, Corporate Department), it was published in *Revista Jurídica Pérez-Llorca* (pp. 100–115). The monograph presents a comprehensive legal, technical, and regulatory analysis of the transition from traditional restrictive financial supervision to an open, collaborative banking ecosystem (*open banking*) that balances digital fraud prevention with market opening. The study systematically evaluates: (1) the transposition of PSD2 into Spanish law via Royal Decree-Law 19/2018 and Royal Decree 736/2019; (2) the statutory creation and licensing framework for two new regulated payment services—Account Information Services (AIS / *Servicios de Información sobre Cuentas*) and Payment Initiation Services (PIS / *Servicios de Iniciación de Pagos*)—enabling Third Party Providers (TPPs) to access customer account data via Application Programming Interfaces (APIs / *interfaces de programación de aplicaciones*), replacing legacy screen-scraping techniques; (3) the national flexible exemption establishing a simplified registration regime for payment service providers with monthly operations under €3 million (excluding AIS/PIS); (4) the Spanish Financial System Digital Transformation Bill (*Proyecto de Ley de transformación digital del sistema financiero*) establishing a regulatory sandbox for Fintech testing with live clients; (5) two-factor Strong Customer Authentication (SCA / *autenticación reforzada / SAC*) requirements under RDL 19/2018 Article 3 and RTS SCA & CSC across Knowledge (*conocimiento*), Possession (*posesión*), and Inherence (*inherencia*) factors; (6) statutory SCA exemptions for low-value payments, trusted beneficiaries, recurring transactions, and intra-holder account transfers; and (7) the European Banking Authority (EBA) supervisory extension timeline (EBA Opinion of 16 October 2019 setting 31 December 2020 as the migration deadline for e-commerce SCA) and its operational disruption during the COVID-19 pandemic.

== Legal Basis ==
The statutory and regulatory framework analyzed includes:

* '''European Union Directives & Delegated Regulations''': Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of 25 November 2015 (Second Payment Services Directive / PSD2, amending Directives 2002/65/EC, 2009/110/EC, 2013/36/EU, Regulation (EU) No 1093/2010, and repealing Directive 2007/64/EC); Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/389 of 27 November 2017 (RTS SCA & CSC); EBA Opinion of 16 October 2019 (EBA/OP/2019/11).
* '''Spanish Statutory Codification''': Real Decreto-ley 19/2018, de 23 de noviembre, de servicios de pago y otras medidas urgentes en materia financiera (RDL de Servicios de Pago); Real Decreto 736/2019, de 20 de diciembre, de régimen jurídico de los servicios de pago y las entidades de pago; Proyecto de Ley de transformación digital del sistema financiero (Regulatory Sandbox Bill).

== Background ==
Following the 2008 global financial crisis, European financial directives primarily focused on restricting risk and enforcing bank supervision. Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (PSD2) broke with this trend by compelling account-holding banks to share customer data with authorized third-party providers (TPPs), ushering in the era of open banking. In Spain, RDL 19/2018 transposed this framework into domestic law. However, combining market opening with two-factor Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) created severe technical and legal challenges for payment institutions, card networks, and e-commerce merchants. Paula De Biase and Álvaro Basco Domínguez authored this study to examine these challenges and assess Spain's regulatory readiness.

== Objectives ==
1. Analyze the statutory impact of RDL 19/2018 and PSD2 on Spain's payment services market. 2. Define the licensing and operational framework for AIS (*Servicios de Información sobre Cuentas*) and PIS (*Servicios de Iniciación de Pagos*). 3. Evaluate Spain's national simplified registration exemption for small payment providers (<€3M monthly volume). 4. Examine the regulatory sandbox established under the Financial System Digital Transformation Bill. 5. Detail the technical architecture and statutory exemptions of two-factor Strong Customer Authentication (SCA/SAC). 6. Assess the EBA's supervisory extension to 31 December 2020 for e-commerce SCA implementation.

== Scope ==
The monograph is structured into four main analytical sections: 1. ''Spanish Payment Services Act (RDL 19/2018)'': Transposition of PSD2, statutory definition of AIS and PIS, simplified registration regime, and user protection rules. 2. ''Strong Customer Authentication Architecture (SCA/SAC)'': Two-factor authentication rules (Knowledge, Possession, Inherence), mandatory triggers, and statutory exemption categories. 3. ''Open Banking Architecture & TPP Regulation'': Shift from screen-scraping to standardized open APIs, account aggregation, and KYC/AML compliance in Payment Initiation Services. 4. ''Supervisory Extension & Regulatory Sandbox'': EBA migration timeline (31 December 2020), COVID-19 impact on e-commerce, and live-testing mechanisms under the Spanish Sandbox Bill.

== Key Provisions & Principles ==

* '''Strong Customer Authentication (SCA / SAC - RDL 19/2018 Art. 3)''': Mandatory authentication process requiring two or more independent factors classified under Knowledge (something known), Possession (something held), and Inherence (something the user is, e.g., biometrics).
* '''Regulated AIS and PIS Services''': Account Information Services (AIS) aggregate account data across financial institutions; Payment Initiation Services (PIS) initiate direct payment orders from bank accounts at the user's request.
* '''National Simplified Registration Exemption (€3M Limit)''': Option under Spanish law allowing payment institutions processing less than €3 million monthly (12-month average) to register under simplified requirements, excluding AIS and PIS.
* '''Financial Regulatory Sandbox''': Controlled regulatory environment enabling Fintech startups to test innovative financial products with real customers prior to obtaining formal licenses.
* '''EBA E-Commerce SCA Migration Deadline''': EBA Opinion setting 31 December 2020 as the strict deadline for payment service providers to fully implement two-factor SCA in e-commerce.

== Implementation ==
Applied by Banco de España, European Banking Authority (EBA), Credit Institutions / Banks, Third Party Providers (TPPs / AIS & PIS), Payment Card Networks (Visa, MasterCard, Amex), E-Commerce Merchants, and Fintech Companies.

== Policy Problems ==

* Bureaucratic delays in TPP licensing at Banco de España following late national transposition.
* E-commerce checkout friction and cart abandonment caused by rigid two-factor SCA requirements.
* Legal uncertainty regarding KYC/AML liability allocation between PIS providers and B2B merchants.
* Security and data privacy vulnerabilities associated with legacy screen-scraping practices.

== Reform ==

* Completing full rollout of standardized, secure open APIs across all account-servicing banks.
* Harmonizing EBA guidelines on KYC/AML responsibilities for Payment Initiation Services.
* Enacting the Regulatory Sandbox Bill to facilitate live testing of Fintech innovations in Spain.
* Ensuring full technical compliance with e-commerce SCA before the 31 December 2020 deadline.

== 4. ANÁLISIS DE POLÍTICA PÚBLICA ==

* '''Antecedentes''': [HECHO] Tras la crisis financiera de 2008, la regulación europea se enfocó principalmente en restringir riesgos y reforzar la supervisión bancaria. La Directiva (UE) 2015/2366 (PSD2) rompió esa tendencia al obligar a las entidades bancarias gestoras de cuentas a compartir los datos de sus clientes con terceros proveedores autorizados (TPPs), dando inicio a la era del *open banking*. En España, el RDL 19/2018 traspuso este marco normativo. Sin embargo, compaginar la apertura de mercado con la exigencia de la Autenticación Reforzada de Cliente (*SCA*) de dos factores generó desafíos técnicos e incertidumbres jurídicas para las entidades de pago, redes de tarjetas y comercios electrónicos. Paula De Biase y Álvaro Basco Domínguez elaboraron esta monografía para analizar estos retos e identificar el estado de preparación regulatoria en España.
* '''Problema de Política Pública''': [HECHO]
** '''Fricción entre Seguridad Digital y Experiencia de Usuario''': La exigencia estricta de la SCA de dos factores amenazaba la fluidez en el proceso de compra online ("un solo clic"), incrementando el riesgo de abandono de carrito en el comercio electrónico.
** '''Obsolescencia del Screen-Scraping''': Las prácticas no reguladas de extracción de datos (*screen-scraping*) presentaban graves riesgos de seguridad y protección de datos, exigiendo la transición hacia APIs abiertas y seguras gestionadas por los bancos.
** '''Cuellos de Botella en la Autorización de TPPs''': Los retrasos en la transposición nacional y la complejidad técnica ralentizaron la concesión de licencias por el Banco de España, limitando el número de TPPs operativos para servicios AIS y PIS.
** '''Incertidumbre KYC/AML en Servicios de Iniciación de Pagos (PIS)''': Dudas regulatorias sobre la distribución de responsabilidades en la prevención del blanqueo de capitales (KYC/AML) entre las plataformas PIS y los comercios B2B.
** '''Impacto del COVID-19 en el Comercio Electrónico''': El aumento acelerado de compras online durante la pandemia coincidió con la fecha límite fijada por la EBA (31 de diciembre de 2020) para implantar la SCA en e-commerce, presionando a sectores económicos vulnerables.
* '''Legal/Policy Gap''': [HECHO] Establecer un marco claro bajo el RDL 19/2018 que impulse la innovación en banca abierta, preserve la seguridad contra el fraude digital y articule vías de registro simplificado y *sandbox* regulatorio para las empresas Fintech.
* '''Objetivos de Política Pública''': [HECHO] Fomentar la competencia e innovación en el mercado de pagos; proteger a los consumidores frente al fraude electrónico mediante autenticación de dos factores; estandarizar la comunicación segura vía APIs abiertas; otorgar soberanía al usuario sobre sus datos financieros; y habilitar cauces regulatorios flexibles para nuevos competidores.
* '''Implementación de Política Pública y Mecánica Normativa''': [HECHO]
** '''1. Regulación de Nuevos Servicios de Pago (AIS y PIS)''':
*** ''Servicios de Información sobre Cuentas (AIS)'': Servicios en línea que ofrecen información agregada sobre las cuentas de pago de un usuario en distintas entidades, facilitando la gestión de finanzas personales.
*** ''Servicios de Iniciación de Pagos (PIS)'': Servicios que inician una orden de pago a petición del usuario desde una cuenta abierta en otra entidad, permitiendo transferencias directas para compras online sin acceder a la banca electrónica tradicional.
** '''2. Opción de Flexibilidad Nacional en España''':
*** ''Excepción de Registro Simplificado (Límite 3 M€)'': Opción nacional adoptada por España que permite a las entidades de pago con un volumen mensual de operaciones inferior a 3 millones de euros (media de 12 meses) registrarse bajo requisitos simplificados (excluyendo servicios AIS y PIS).
*** ''Proyecto de Ley de Sandbox Regulatorio'': Entorno de pruebas controlado que permite a las Fintech probar proyectos de tecnología financiera con clientes reales bajo supervisión regulatoria antes de obtener licencias definitivas.
** '''3. Arquitectura de la Autenticación Reforzada de Cliente (SCA / SAC)''':
*** Definida en el Art. 3 del RDL 19/2018 como la autenticación basada en dos o más factores independientes categorizados en: (i) *Conocimiento* (algo que solo el usuario sabe, ej. contraseña/PIN); (ii) *Posesión* (algo que solo el usuario posee, ej. móvil/token); e (iii) *Inherencia* (algo que el usuario es, ej. datos biométricos).
*** Aplicación Obligatoria: Acceso a cuentas en línea, iniciación de pagos electrónicos y acciones remotas con riesgo de fraude.
*** Exenciones Legales bajo las RTS SCA & CSC: Pagos de bajo valor, beneficiarios de confianza (listas blancas), transacciones recurrentes y transferencias entre cuentas del mismo titular.
** '''4. Transición Técnica y Prórroga de la EBA''':
*** Las RTS SCA & CSC entraron en vigor el 14 de septiembre de 2019. Ante la complejidad de adaptación del e-commerce, la EBA emitió su Opinión de 16 de octubre de 2019, fijando como fecha límite definitiva el 31 de diciembre de 2020 para la plena implantación de la SCA en e-commerce.
* '''Evidencia e Impacto''': [HECHO] Evalúa el estudio de Paula De Biase y Álvaro Basco Domínguez de 2020; la Directiva (UE) 2015/2366 (PSD2); el Real Decreto-ley 19/2018; el Real Decreto 736/2019; el Reglamento Delegado (UE) 2018/389 (RTS SCA & CSC); la Opinión de la EBA de 16 de octubre de 2019; el Proyecto de Ley de Sandbox Regulatorio; y la monografía de Ander Valverde González-Morejón.
* '''Evaluación y Propuestas de Reforma''': [HECHO] Concluye que la banca abierta representa una transformación estructural e irreversible del sector financiero. Señala que, si bien la PSD2 abrió las cuentas de pago, el *open banking* se expande hacia la agregación financiera integral (préstamos, seguros, inversiones). Recomienda: (1) completar el despliegue técnico de APIs abiertas y seguras en la totalidad de la banca; (2) armonizar los criterios de la EBA sobre las obligaciones KYC/AML en plataformas de iniciación de pagos; y (3) aprobar definitivamente la Ley de Sandbox Regulatorio para dinamizar la innovación Fintech en España.
