== 4. POLICY ANALYSIS ==

* '''Background''': [FACT] The Spanish legal system is undergoing major transformations across civil, notarial, digital, and fiscal domains. *Revista Jurídica del Notariado* (RJN) No. 116 (Enero–Junio 2023), published by Fundación Notariado and the Consejo General del Notariado, brings together leading civil law scholars, state attorneys, and public notary practitioners to address statutory gaps, constitutional limits, and conflicting administrative registration doctrines (*doctrina registral de la DGSJFP*).
* '''Policy Problem''': [FACT]
** '''Limits on Encumbering Strict Legitimate for Disabled Descendants (CC Art. 808 & Ley 8/2021)''': How to protect children with disabilities through residuary trusts (*sustitución fideicomisaria de residuo*) without converting the fiduciary's disposition power into an unconstitutional de facto disinheritance of non-disabled co-legitimaries.
** '''Form & Lesion Control in Prenuptial Agreements (*Pactos Prematrimoniales*)''': The lack of common statutory regulation leads courts to accept informal agreements in private documents, creating severe risks of vitiated consent (*vicios del consentimiento*), unequal bargaining power, and lack of notarial legality/lesion control (*control de lesividad* under CC Art. 90.2).
** '''Will Interpretation & Prohibitions on Judicial Intervention (*Cautela Socini*)''': Balancing the standing of co-heirs, executors (*albaceas*), and partitioners (*contadores-partidores*) to interpret ambiguous wills under CC Art. 675 with Supreme Court doctrine (STS 10 June 2014) on the validity of clauses penalizing judicial litigation.
** '''Vulgar Substitution vs. Accrual in Legitimate Renunciation''': Conflicts between DGSJFP administrative rulings (e.g., RDGSJFP 18 Jan 2022) and Supreme Court precedents regarding whether a vulgar substitution in favor of grandchildren can take effect over strict legitimate when a child repudiates the inheritance.
** '''Uncertainty & Misnomers in "Digital Wills" (*Patrimonio Digital* & LOPDGDD Art. 96)''': Flaws in statutory drafting under LOPDGDD Art. 96, unconstitutionality of regional digital wills registers (STC 7/2019), and the legal transmission of digital assets (cryptoassets, software licenses, domain names, social media corporate profiles) under EU Directive 2019/770 and CJEU *UsedSoft* doctrine.
** '''Conflicting Administrative Registration Doctrines on Tacit Acceptance & Ius Transmissionis''': Controversial DGSJFP resolutions (31 March 2023 & 19 April 2023) regarding whether testamentary disposition of community property constitutes tacit acceptance (CC Art. 999) and whether legitimaries of a deceased transmitter (*transmitente*) must intervene in legacy deliveries.
* '''Legal/Policy Gap''': [FACT] Harmonizing statutory reforms (Ley 8/2021, LOPDGDD Art. 96, Ley 15/2015) with established Civil Code principles, ensuring that notarial public deeds (*escritura pública*) remain the sole mandatory instrument guaranteeing legal certainty, impartiality, and protection of vulnerable parties across prenuptial agreements, digital estate succession, and testamentary interpretation.
* '''Policy Objectives''': [FACT] Ensure patrimonial protection for persons with disabilities without violating strict legitimate intangibility; enforce mandatory notarial public deeds for prenuptial agreements to guarantee independent advice and lesion control; clarify executor/partitioner interpretation powers under CC Art. 675; unify DGSJFP registration rules on legitimary renunciation; establish a unified, secure digital estate transmission model via the Notarial Citizen Portal (*Portal Notarial del Ciudadano*); and uphold Supreme Court tax refund principles in Property Transfer Tax.
* '''Policy Implementation & Statutory Mechanics''': [FACT]
** '''1. Residuary Trust for Persons with Disabilities (Isidoro Lora-Tamayo Rodríguez)''':
*** Analyzes CC Art. 808 (reformed by Ley 8/2021), permitting testators to encumber the strict legitimate of non-disabled children with a residuary trust (*sustitución fideicomisaria de residuo*) in favor of a disabled child.
*** Establishes that the fiduciary (disabled child) CANNOT be authorized to make gratuitous inter vivos or mortis causa dispositions of the encumbered legitimate.
*** Validates the spouse's power under CC Art. 831 to establish this trust post-mortem, and explores reversional donations (*donación reversional*) under CC Art. 252.
** '''2. Mandatory Notarial Public Deed for Prenuptial Agreements (Manuel García Mayo)''':
*** Demonstrates that prenuptial agreements (*pactos prematrimoniales*) in anticipation of marital crisis alter statutory marital property regimes and require solemn public form (*escritura pública ad solemnitatem*) under CC Art. 1327.
*** Proposes mandatory independent notarial counseling for each spouse prior to signing (inspired by CCCat Art. 231-20).
*** Requires notaries to execute mandatory legality and lesion control (*control de lesividad*) under CC Art. 90.2 (as amended by Ley 15/2015), terminating proceedings and referring parties to court if agreements cause grave detriment to a spouse, minor children, or pets.
** '''3. Boundaries of Will Interpretation & Prohibition Clauses (Marta Carballo Fidalgo)''':
*** Distinguishes interpretation standing: co-heirs hold primary interpretation power by unanimous agreement (CC Art. 1058); partitioners (*contadores-partidores*) hold instrumental interpretation power necessary to execute partition; executors (*albaceas*) execute testamentary mandates.
*** Applies Supreme Court doctrine (STS 10 June 2014) on clauses prohibiting judicial litigation (*cautela socini*): clauses penalizing litigation with loss of the free-disposition share are valid when challenging the testator's distribution, BUT DO NOT APPLY when challenging executor/partitioner irregularities or seeking judicial delivery of a clear testamentary right.
** '''4. Renunciation of Strict Legitimate & Vulgar Substitution (Ana López Frías)''':
*** Reconciles CC Art. 774 (vulgar substitution) with CC Art. 985.2 (accrual among co-legitimaries).
*** Evaluates RDGSJFP 18 January 2022: when a child is assigned ONLY the strict legitimate and repudiates the inheritance, the vulgar substitution in favor of their descendants CANNOT take effect over the strict legitimate (which accrues to co-legitimaries by own right under Art. 985.2), nor can it be charged to the free-disposition or improvement shares unless expressly ordered by the testator.
** '''5. Digital Estate Transmission & Critique of LOPDGDD Art. 96 (Jesús Lleonart Castro)''':
*** Distinguishes *digital identity* (human subject) from *virtual identity* (transferable pseudonyms/avatars with economic value) and *digital assets* (*patrimonio digital*).
*** Applies CJEU *UsedSoft* doctrine (Case C-128/11) and *The Software Incubator* (2021) to confirm that purchasing digital software/content creates a transfer of ownership that exhausts distribution rights.
*** Recalls STC 7/2019 declaring unconstitutional the Catalan digital wills register for invading exclusive state jurisdiction over public instruments.
*** Denounces LOPDGDD Art. 96 ("testamento digital") as a misnomer that creates an unworkable "post-mortem mandate" in direct violation of CC Art. 1732 (mandate terminates upon death) and creates dangerous standing conflicts between heirs, relatives, and community managers. Proposes unified notarial wills backed by password custody in the *Portal Notarial del Ciudadano*.
** '''6. Tacit Acceptance & Ius Transmissionis (Tomás Giménez Duart)''':
*** Critiques RDGSJFP 31 March 2023 (holding that testamentary disposition of former community property constitutes tacit acceptance under CC Art. 999, blocking *ius transmissionis*) and RDGSJFP 19 April 2023 (requiring transmitter's legitimaries to intervene in legacy deliveries ordered by the first deceased).
** '''7. ITPAJD Tax Refunds on Explicit Resolutory Conditions & Concessions (Antonio Martínez Lafuente)''':
*** Analyzes STS 30 June 2022: when a sale is resolved under an explicit resolutory condition (LH Art. 11 / CC Art. 1124) due to buyer non-payment, the buyer (defaulting party) IS ENTITLED to a refund of Property Transfer Tax (ITPAJD) paid, as resolution operates retroactively (*ex tunc*).
*** Analyzes STS 23 February 2023: subsequent mutual reduction of administrative concession fees DOES NOT entitle the concessionaire to an ITPAJD refund, as tax base is fixed at the time of accrual (*devengo*).
* '''Evidence & Impact''': [FACT] Evaluates *Revista Jurídica del Notariado*, No. 116 (Enero–Junio 2023); Civil Code; Ley 8/2021; Ley Orgánica 3/2018 (LOPDGDD); EU Directive 2019/770; CJEU Case C-128/11 (*UsedSoft*); STC 7/2019; STS 10 June 2014; STS 315/2018; STS 30 June 2022; STS 23 Feb 2023; RDGSJFP 18 Jan 2022; RDGSJFP 31 Mar 2023; and RDGSJFP 19 Apr 2023.
* '''Evaluation & Reform''': [FACT] Concludes that *Revista Jurídica del Notariado* No. 116 provides a crucial bridge between legislative reforms and notarial practice. Recommends: (1) enacting explicit national legislation requiring public deeds for prenuptial agreements; (2) amending LOPDGDD Art. 96 to eliminate the "post-mortem mandate" illusion and establish secure password repositories under the Notarial Citizen Portal; and (3) harmonizing DGSJFP registration criteria with Supreme Court jurisprudence regarding legitimate renunciation and *ius transmissionis*.

== Summary ==
'''Revista Jurídica del Notariado, Número 116 (Enero-Junio 2023)''' (*Notarial Law Journal, No. 116 - 2023*) is an official, peer-reviewed legal research and judicial policy monograph published semi-annually by *Fundación Notariado* and the *Consejo General del Notariado* (CGN) in Madrid, Spain (ISSN: 1132-0044, Digital ISSN: 2695-8236, Depósito Legal: M-8652-2012). Volume 116 (Enero–Junio 2023) compiles authoritative doctrinal studies, practical legal research, and fiscal jurisprudence across eight core domains: (1) testamentary trust encumbrance on strict legitimate for persons with disabilities (*sustitución fideicomisaria de residuo*) under Civil Code (CC) Art. 808 amended by Ley 8/2021, fiduciary powers, and reversional donations under CC Art. 252 (Isidoro Lora-Tamayo Rodríguez); (2) legal regulation and mandatory notarial public deed control (*control de lesividad* and *control de legalidad*) for prenuptial agreements (*pactos prematrimoniales*) in anticipation of marital breakdown under CC Art. 90.2 and CCCat Art. 231-20 (Manuel García Mayo); (3) standing and boundaries for interpreting wills by co-heirs, executors (*albaceas*), and partitioners (*contadores-partidores*), alongside the validity of clauses prohibiting judicial interpretation (*cautela socini* / STS 10 June 2014) under CC Arts. 670 & 675 (Marta Carballo Fidalgo); (4) vulgar substitution (*sustitución vulgar*) versus accrual (*acrecimiento*) upon renunciation of strict legitimate under CC Arts. 774 & 985.2 and RDGSJFP 18 January 2022 (Ana López Frías); (5) practical mortis causa transmission of digital estate (*patrimonio digital*), digital identity vs. virtual identity, EU Directive 2019/770, CJEU *UsedSoft* doctrine (C-128/11) on software exhaustion, unconstitutionality of the Catalan digital wills register (STC 7/2019), and critique of LOPDGDD Ley Orgánica 3/2018 Art. 96 ("testamento digital") (Jesús Lleonart Castro); (6) tacit acceptance and legitimary intervention under *ius transmissionis* (CC Art. 1006) in RDGSJFP 31 March 2023 and 19 April 2023 (Tomás Giménez Duart); (7) refund of undue tax payments in Property Transfer Tax (ITPAJD) for explicit resolutory conditions (LH Art. 11 / STS 30 June 2022) and administrative concessions (STS 23 Feb 2023) (Antonio Martínez Lafuente); and (8) book reviews on freedom of testation (*libertad de testar*) by Victorio Magariños (Carlos Pérez Ramos) and *Enciclopedia Notarial* by Juan Carlos Martínez Ortega (Paúl Arellano Sarasti).

== Legal Basis ==
The statutory, European regulatory, and jurisprudential framework analyzed across the volume includes:
* '''Spanish Civil Code (Código Civil)''': Arts. 252, 670, 675, 774, 782, 808 (Ley 8/2021), 813, 831, 90.2 (Ley 15/2015), 985.2, 999, 1006, 1058, 1255, 1265, 1327, 1463, 1719, 1732.
* '''European Regulations & Directives''': Directive (EU) 2019/770 (Digital Content & Services); Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR); CJEU Case C-128/11 (*UsedSoft v. Oracle*, 3 July 2012 - exhaustion of distribution rights); CJEU *The Software Incubator* (2021).
* '''Spanish Statutory Legislation''': Ley 8/2021 (Support for Persons with Disabilities); Ley Orgánica 3/2018 (LOPDGDD Art. 96); Ley 15/2015 de la Jurisdicción Voluntaria; Ley 20/2011 del Registro Civil (Art. 60); Ley Hipotecaria (Art. 11); Real Decreto Legislativo 1/1993 (ITPAJD Art. 57); Ley Notarial (Art. 17 bis); Reglamento Notarial (Art. 147).
* '''Autonomous Region Legislation & Constitutional Precedents''': Codi Civil de Catalunya (CCCat Arts. 231-20, 233-16, 421-2); Catalan Ley 10/2017 de Voluntades Digitales; STC 7/2019 (17 Jan 2019 - unconstitutionality of Catalan digital wills register); STS 10 June 2014 (cautela socini); STS 315/2018 (prenuptial waivers); STS 30 June 2022 & STS 23 Feb 2023 (ITPAJD tax refunds).

== Background ==
Developments in civil, notarial, and digital law in Spain demand harmony between statutory legislative reforms (such as Ley 8/2021 and LOPDGDD) and the fundamental principles of the Civil Code. *Revista Jurídica del Notariado* (RJN) No. 116 (Enero–Junio 2023) brings together rigorous research from public notaries, legal scholars, and State Attorneys (*Abogados del Estado*) to provide clear legal answers to issues of disability estate planning, prenuptial agreements, testamentary interpretation, digital assets, and property transfer taxation.

== Objectives ==
1. Analyze the residuary trust scheme for disability protection under CC Art. 808 post-Ley 8/2021.
2. Explain the public deed requirement (*escritura pública*) and mandatory lesion control (*control de lesividad*) under CC Art. 90.2 for prenuptial agreements.
3. Map the boundaries of testamentary interpretation powers (*albaceas* and *contadores-partidores*) and the validity of *cautela socini* clauses (STS 10 June 2014).
4. Detail the DGSJFP administrative doctrine of 18 January 2022 regarding vulgar substitution vs. accrual when a legitimary repudiates an inheritance.
5. Deconstruct the legal defects of the "digital will" concept under LOPDGDD Art. 96 and advocate for secure password management via the *Portal Notarial del Ciudadano*.
6. Outline ITPAJD tax refund rights for defaulting buyers upon contract resolution (STS 30 June 2022).

== Scope ==
The scope of this journal volume is organized into core thematic pillars:
1. ''Residuary Trust and Disability Protection (Isidoro Lora-Tamayo Rodríguez)'': Reform of CC Art. 808, prohibition of gratuitous inter vivos dispositions by fiduciaries, and CC Art. 831 post-mortem trusts.
2. ''Prenuptial Agreements and Notarial Function (Manuel García Mayo)'': Public deed solemnity (CC Art. 1327), legality control, and lesion control (*control de lesividad*) under CC Art. 90.2.
3. ''Will Interpretation and Cautela Socini (Marta Carballo Fidalgo)'': Standing of co-heirs, executors, and partitioners, alongside Supreme Court doctrine on prohibition clauses (STS 10 June 2014).
4. ''Vulgar Substitution and Renunciation of Strict Legitimate (Ana López Frías)'': Limits under CC Art. 985.2, allocation to free disposition shares, and analysis of RDGSJFP 18 January 2022.
5. ''Digital Estate and Digital Wills (Jesús Lleonart Castro)'': Digital vs. virtual identity, EU exhaustion of rights (*UsedSoft*), unconstitutionality under STC 7/2019, critique of LOPDGDD Art. 96, and the Notarial Citizen Portal.
6. ''Ius Transmissionis and Registration Doctrine (Tomás Giménez Duart)'': Tacit acceptance (CC Art. 999) and delivery of legacies under recent DGSJFP rulings.
7. ''ITPAJD Tax Refunds on Explicit Resolutory Conditions (Antonio Martínez Lafuente)'': Explicit resolutory conditions (LH Art. 11), STS 30 June 2022, and administrative concessions (STS 23 Feb 2023).

== Key Provisions & Principles ==
* '''Limits on Disposition in Disability Residuary Trusts (CC Art. 808)''': The disabled fiduciary CANNOT be granted inter vivos gratuitous disposition powers (*a título gratuito*) by the testator over the strict legitimate of non-disabled co-legitimaries.
* '''Notarial Lesion Control in Prenuptial Agreements (CC Art. 90.2)''': Prenuptial agreements must be executed in a public deed. Notaries must perform mandatory lesion control (*control de lesividad*); if an agreement causes severe harm to a spouse or minor child, the notary must refuse execution and refer parties to court.
* '''Doctrine on Cautela Socini & Litigation Bans (STS 10 June 2014)''': Testamentary clauses penalizing judicial litigation are valid only against challenges to the testator's disposition, BUT DO NOT APPLY to challenges against executor/partitioner irregularities or requests for delivery of clear rights.
* '''Inapplicability of Vulgar Substitution to Repudiated Strict Legitimate (RDGSJFP 18 Jan 2022)''': When a child assigned only strict legitimate repudiates the inheritance, that portion accrues automatically to co-legitimaries by own right (CC Art. 985.2); a vulgar substitution in favor of grandchildren cannot encumber that strict legitimate.
* '''Exhaustion of Rights in Digital Assets & Notarial Portal (CJEU UsedSoft & STC 7/2019)''': Purchasing digital content creates ownership exhausting distribution rights. LOPDGDD Art. 96 ("testamento digital") is legally defective as an unworkable post-mortem mandate violating CC Art. 1732; digital asset passcodes should be secured via notarial wills and the *Portal Notarial del Ciudadano*.
* '''ITPAJD Tax Refund for Defaulting Buyers (STS 30 June 2022)''': Upon resolution of a sale due to buyer default under an explicit resolutory condition (LH Art. 11), the defaulting buyer IS ENTITLED to a refund of Property Transfer Tax (ITPAJD) paid, as resolution operates retroactively (*ex tunc*).

== Implementation ==
Applied by Consejo General del Notariado, DGSJFP, Supreme Court, Constitutional Court, Spanish Public Notaries, State Attorneys (*Abogados del Estado*), and Civil/Fiscal Law Practitioners.

== Policy Problems ==
* Risks of de facto disinheritance of non-disabled children through excessive gratuitous disposition powers granted under CC Art. 808.
* Proliferation of informal, private prenuptial agreements vulnerable to vitiated consent and economic inequality.
* Legal confusion created by LOPDGDD Art. 96 purporting to establish a "post-mortem mandate" contrary to CC Art. 1732.
* Conflicts between DGSJFP registration criteria and Supreme Court jurisprudence regarding vulgar substitution and *ius transmissionis*.

== Reform ==
* Enacting explicit national statutory legislation requiring public deeds for all prenuptial agreements in Spain.
* Amending LOPDGDD Art. 96 to remove the confusing "testamento digital" terminology and establish secure digital passcode repositories under the Notarial Citizen Portal.
* Harmonizing DGSJFP registration criteria with Supreme Court doctrine regarding *ius transmissionis* and legitimary renunciation.

== 4. ANÁLISIS DE POLÍTICA PÚBLICA ==

* '''Antecedentes''': [HECHO] El ordenamiento jurídico español atraviesa profundas transformaciones en los ámbitos civil, notarial, digital y fiscal. La *Revista Jurídica del Notariado* (RJN) N.º 116 (Enero–Junio 2023), editada por la Fundación Notariado y el Consejo General del Notariado, reúne a catedráticos de Derecho civil, abogados del Estado y notarios para resolver lagunas normativas, límites constitucionales y contradicciones de la doctrina registral de la DGSJFP.
* '''Problema de Política Pública''': [HECHO]
** '''Límites al Gravamen de la Legítima Estricta en Discapacidad (Art. 808 CC y Ley 8/2021)''': Cómo proteger a hijos con discapacidad mediante fideicomisos de residuo sin convertir las facultades del fiduciario en una desheredación de hecho e inconstitucional de los demás legitimarios.
** '''Forma y Control de Lesividad en los Pactos Prematrimoniales''': La ausencia de regulación estatal común lleva a los tribunales a aceptar pactos en documento privado, con grave riesgo de vicios del consentimiento, desigualdad entre cónyuges y falta de control notarial de lesividad (Art. 90.2 CC).
** '''Interpretación Testamentaria y Cláusulas de Prohibición de Litigar (*Cautela Socini*)''': Delimitación de la legitimación de coherederos, albaceas y contadores-partidores para interpretar testamentos ambiguos bajo el Art. 675 CC frente a la jurisprudencia del Tribunal Supremo (STS 10 de junio de 2014).
** '''Sustitución Vulgar frente a Acrecimiento en la Renuncia de Legítima''': Conflicto entre las resoluciones registrales de la DGSJFP (ej. RDGSJFP de 18 de enero de 2022) y el Tribunal Supremo respecto a si la sustitución vulgar a favor de nietos opera sobre la legítima estricta repudiada por un hijo.
** '''Incertidumbres del "Testamento Digital" (Patrimonio Digital y Art. 96 LOPDGDD)''': Defectos de técnica legislativa en el Art. 96 de la LOPDGDD, inconstitucionalidad de registros autonómicos de voluntades digitales (STC 7/2019) y transmisión de activos digitales (criptoactivos, licencias de software, dominios) bajo la Directiva (UE) 2019/770 y la doctrina *UsedSoft* del TJUE.
** '''Doctrina Registral Contradictoria sobre Aceptación Tácita e Ius Transmissionis''': Resoluciones polémicas de la DGSJFP (31 de marzo de 2023 y 19 de abril de 2023) sobre si la disposición de bienes gananciales implica aceptación tácita (Art. 999 CC) y si los legitimarios del transmitente deben intervenir en entregas de legados.
* '''Vacío Legal/de Política Pública''': [HECHO] Armonizar las reformas legislativas recientes (Ley 8/2021, Art. 96 LOPDGDD, Ley 15/2015) con los principios tradicionales del Código Civil, garantizando que la escritura pública notarial siga siendo el instrumento indispensable para asegurar la certeza jurídica, la imparcialidad y la protección de las partes vulnerables.
* '''Objetivos de Política Pública''': [HECHO] Garantizar la protección patrimonial de las personas con discapacidad sin vulnerar la intangibilidad de la legítima; exigir la escritura pública obligatoria para los pactos prematrimoniales garantizando el control de lesividad; aclarar las facultades interpretativas de albaceas y contadores-partidores; unificar el criterio registral sobre la renuncia de legítima; articular un modelo seguro de transmisión del patrimonio digital mediante el Portal Notarial del Ciudadano; y consolidar el derecho a la devolución de ingresos indebidos en el ITPAJD según la doctrina del Tribunal Supremo.
* '''Implementación de Política Pública y Mecánica Normativa''': [HECHO]
** '''1. Fideicomiso de Residuo en Discapacidad (Estudio de Isidoro Lora-Tamayo Rodríguez)''':
*** Analiza la reforma del Art. 808 CC por la Ley 8/2021, que permite gravar la legítima estricta de hijos no discapacitados con una sustitución fideicomisaria de residuo a favor del hijo con discapacidad.
*** Establece que el fiduciario (hijo con discapacidad) NO PUEDE ser autorizado para realizar actos de disposición a título gratuito inter vivos ni mortis causa sobre la legítima gravada.
*** Valida el uso de la delegación de la facultad de mejorar del Art. 831 CC y la donación reversional del Art. 252 CC.
** '''2. Escritura Pública Obligatoria en Pactos Prematrimoniales (Estudio de Manuel García Mayo)''':
*** Demuestra que los pactos prematrimoniales en previsión de ruptura alteran el régimen económico matrimonial y requieren forma pública *ad solemnitatem* (Art. 1327 CC).
*** Propone el asesoramiento notarial independiente a cada cónyuge (inspirado en el Art. 231-20 del CCCat).
*** Exige al notario ejercer un control de legalidad y de lesividad obligatorio (Art. 90.2 CC), debiendo denegar la autorización si el pacto es gravemente perjudicial para un cónyuge o los hijos menores.
** '''3. Límites en la Interpretación del Testamento y Cautela Socini (Estudio de Marta Carballo Fidalgo)''':
*** Diferencia la legitimación interpretativa: los coherederos por unanimidad (Art. 1058 CC); los contadores-partidores de forma instrumental para partir; y los albaceas para cumplir el encargo testamentario.
*** Aplica la doctrina del Tribunal Supremo (STS 10 de junio de 2014) sobre la *cautela socini*: las cláusulas sancionadoras solo se activan ante impugnaciones del reparto fijado por el testador, PERO NO ante denuncias por irregularidades en la actuación del contador-partidor.
** '''4. Renuncia a la Legítima Estricta y Sustitución Vulgar (Estudio de Ana López Frías)''':
*** Reconcilia el Art. 774 CC (sustitución vulgar) con el Art. 985.2 CC (acrecimiento entre colegitimarios).
*** Evalúa la RDGSJFP de 18 de enero de 2022: si un hijo a quien solo se le dejó la legítima estricta la repudia, la sustitución vulgar a favor de sus descendientes NO PUEDE operar sobre la legítima estricta (que acrece a los demás colegitimarios por derecho propio), ni imputarse al tercio de libre disposición a menos que el testador lo hubiera dispuesto expresamente.
** '''5. Transmisión del Patrimonio Digital y Crítica al Art. 96 LOPDGDD (Estudio de Jesús Lleonart Castro)''':
*** Distingue la *identidad digital* (sujeto humano) de la *identidad virtual* (seudónimos/avatares transmisibles) y el *patrimonio digital*.
*** Aplica la doctrina del TJUE en el asunto *UsedSoft* (C-128/11) para confirmar que la adquisición de software/contenido digital genera una transmisión de propiedad que agota el derecho de distribución.
*** Recuerda la STC 7/2019 que declaró inconstitucional el registro catalán de voluntades digitales por invadir competencias estatales exclusivas.
*** Sostiene que el Art. 96 de la LOPDGDD ("testamento digital") es una figura jurídicamente defectuosa que crea un "mandato post-mortem" contrario al Art. 1732 CC (el mandato se extingue por muerte); propone depositar las claves en testamentos notariales vinculados al Portal Notarial del Ciudadano.
** '''6. Aceptación Tácita e Ius Transmissionis (Estudio de Tomás Giménez Duart)''':
*** Critica las resoluciones RDGSJFP de 31 de marzo de 2023 (que consideró que disponer de bienes gananciales implica aceptación tácita impidiendo el *ius transmissionis*) y de 19 de abril de 2023 (que exigió la intervención de los legitimarios del transmitente en la entrega de legados del primer causante).
** '''7. Devolución de ITPAJD en Condición Resolutoria y Concesiones (Estudio de Antonio Martínez Lafuente)''':
*** Analiza la STS de 30 de junio de 2022: resuelta una venta por condición resolutoria explícita (Art. 11 LH / Art. 1124 CC) por impago del comprador, el comprador incumplidor TIENE DERECHO a la devolución del ITPAJD pagado, pues la resolución opera de forma retroactiva (*ex tunc*).
*** Analiza la STS de 23 de febrero de 2023: la reducción posterior del canon de una concesión administrativa NO da derecho a devolución del ITPAJD, pues la base imponible se fija en el devengo.
* '''Evidencia e Impacto''': [HECHO] Evalúa la *Revista Jurídica del Notariado*, N.º 116 (Enero–Junio 2023); el Código Civil; la Ley 8/2021; la LOPDGDD; la Directiva (UE) 2019/770; la STJUE Asunto C-128/11 (*UsedSoft*); la STC 7/2019; la STS de 10 de junio de 2014; la STS de 30 de junio de 2022; la STS de 23 de febrero de 2023; y las resoluciones de la DGSJFP.
* '''Evaluación y Propuestas de Reforma''': [HECHO] Concluye que la *Revista Jurídica del Notariado* N.º 116 constituye un puente fundamental entre las reformas legislativas y la práctica notarial. Recomienda: (1) aprobar una norma estatal que exija explícitamente la escritura pública para los pactos prematrimoniales; (2) reformar el Art. 96 de la LOPDGDD para eliminar la ficción del mandato post-mortem y canalizar la custodia de claves a través del Portal Notarial del Ciudadano; y (3) unificar los criterios registrales de la DGSJFP con la jurisprudencia del Tribunal Supremo.

== Resumen ==
'''Revista Jurídica del Notariado, Número 116 (Enero-Junio 2023)''' es una monografía oficial de investigación jurídica y política judicial publicada semestralmente por la *Fundación Notariado* y el *Consejo General del Notariado* (CGN) en Madrid, España (ISSN: 1132-0044, Digital ISSN: 2695-8236, Depósito Legal: M-8652-2012). El Volumen 116 (Enero–Junio 2023) reúne estudios doctrinales, investigaciones sobre práctica jurídica y jurisprudencia fiscal en ocho ámbitos clave: (1) el gravamen fideicomisario sobre la legítima estricta para personas con discapacidad (*sustitución fideicomisaria de residuo*) conforme al Art. 808 del Código Civil (CC) modificado por la Ley 8/2021, las facultades del fiduciario y las donaciones reversionales del Art. 252 CC (Isidoro Lora-Tamayo Rodríguez); (2) la regulación jurídica y el control notarial obligatorio (*control de lesividad* y *control de legalidad*) de los pactos prematrimoniales en previsión de ruptura bajo el Art. 90.2 CC y el Art. 231-20 del CCCat (Manuel García Mayo); (3) la legitimación y límites en la interpretación del testamento por coherederos, albaceas y contadores-partidores, así como la validez de la *cautela socini* (STS 10 de junio de 2014) bajo los Arts. 670 y 675 CC (Marta Carballo Fidalgo); (4) la sustitución vulgar frente al acrecimiento tras la renuncia a la legítima estricta bajo los Arts. 774 y 985.2 CC y la RDGSJFP de 18 de enero de 2022 (Ana López Frías); (5) la transmisión del patrimonio digital, la identidad virtual, la Directiva (UE) 2019/770, el agotamiento de derechos según la doctrina *UsedSoft* del TJUE (C-128/11), la inconstitucionalidad del registro catalán de voluntades digitales (STC 7/2019) y la crítica al "testamento digital" del Art. 96 de la LOPDGDD (Jesús Lleonart Castro); (6) la aceptación tácita y la intervención de legitimarios en el *ius transmissionis* (Art. 1006 CC) en resoluciones de la DGSJFP (Tomás Giménez Duart); (7) la devolución de ingresos indebidos en el ITPAJD por condición resolutoria explícita (Art. 11 LH / STS 30 de junio de 2022) y concesiones administrativas (STS 23 de febrero de 2023) (Antonio Martínez Lafuente); y (8) recensiones sobre la libertad de testar de Victorio Magariños (Carlos Pérez Ramos) y la *Enciclopedia Notarial* de Juan Carlos Martínez Ortega (Paúl Arellano Sarasti).

== Base Legal ==
El marco regulatorio analizado incluye:
* '''Código Civil Español''': Arts. 252, 670, 675, 774, 782, 808 (Ley 8/2021), 813, 831, 90.2 (Ley 15/2015), 985.2, 999, 1006, 1058, 1255, 1265, 1327, 1463, 1719, 1732.
* '''Reglamentos y Directivas de la UE''': Directiva (UE) 2019/770 (Contenidos y Servicios Digitales); Reglamento (UE) 2016/679 (RGPD); STJUE Asunto C-128/11 (*UsedSoft c. Oracle*, 3 de julio de 2012); STJUE *The Software Incubator* (2021).
* '''Legislación Española''': Ley 8/2021; Ley Orgánica 3/2018 (LOPDGDD Art. 96); Ley 15/2015 de la Jurisdicción Voluntaria; Ley 20/2011 del Registro Civil (Art. 60); Ley Hipotecaria (Art. 11); Real Decreto Legislativo 1/1993 (ITPAJD Art. 57); Ley Notarial (Art. 17 bis); Reglamento Notarial (Art. 147).
* '''Derecho Autonómico y Jurisprudencia''': Codi Civil de Catalunya (CCCat Arts. 231-20, 233-16, 421-2); Ley 10/2017 de Voluntades Digitales de Cataluña; STC 7/2019; STS de 10 de junio de 2014; STS de 30 de junio de 2022; STS de 23 de febrero de 2023.

== Antecedentes ==
La evolución del Derecho civil, notarial y digital en España exige coherencia entre las reformas normativas recientes (como la Ley 8/2021 y la LOPDGDD) y los principios fundamentales del Código Civil. La *Revista Jurídica del Notariado* (RJN) N.º 116 (Enero–Junio 2023) ofrece análisis rigurosos de notarios, catedráticos y abogados del Estado para aportar seguridad jurídica en materia de planificación de la discapacidad, pactos prematrimoniales, interpretación del testamento, bienes digitales y fiscalidad patrimonial.

== Objetivos ==
1. Analizar el régimen del fideicomiso de residuo en favor de personas con discapacidad del Art. 808 CC tras la Ley 8/2021.
2. Explicar la exigencia de escritura pública y el control notarial de lesividad (Art. 90.2 CC) en los pactos prematrimoniales.
3. Delimitar la legitimación interpretativa del testamento (*albaceas* y *contadores-partidores*) y la validez de la *cautela socini* (STS 10 de junio de 2014).
4. Detallar la doctrina registral de la DGSJFP de 18 de enero de 2022 sobre sustitución vulgar y acrecimiento en renuncias de legítima.
5. Evidenciar las deficiencias jurídicas del "testamento digital" del Art. 96 de la LOPDGDD y articular la custodia de claves en el Portal Notarial del Ciudadano.
6. Fundamentar el derecho a la devolución del ITPAJD del comprador incumplidor tras la resolución contractual (STS 30 de junio de 2022).

== Alcance ==
El contenido del volumen se estructura en los siguientes bloques temáticos:
1. ''Sustitución Fideicomisaria y Protección de la Discapacidad (Isidoro Lora-Tamayo Rodríguez)'': Reforma del Art. 808 CC, prohibición de actos de disposición a título gratuito para el fiduciario y fideicomisos post-mortem del Art. 831 CC.
2. ''Pactos Prematrimoniales y Función Notarial (Manuel García Mayo)'': Forma pública *ad solemnitatem* (Art. 1327 CC), control de legalidad y control de lesividad obligatorio (Art. 90.2 CC).
3. ''Interpretación Testamentaria y Cautela Socini (Marta Carballo Fidalgo)'': Legitimación de herederos, albaceas y contadores-partidores, y jurisprudencia del TS sobre prohibición de litigar (STS 10 de junio de 2014).
4. ''Sustitución Vulgar y Renuncia de Legítima Estricta (Ana López Frías)'': Límites del Art. 985.2 CC, imputación a la libre disposición y análisis de la RDGSJFP de 18 de enero de 2022.
5. ''Patrimonio Digital y Testamento Digital (Jesús Lleonart Castro)'': Identidad digital vs. virtual, agotamiento de derechos (*UsedSoft*), inconstitucionalidad de la STC 7/2019, crítica al Art. 96 LOPDGDD y Portal Notarial del Ciudadano.
6. ''Ius Transmissionis y Doctrina Registral (Tomás Giménez Duart)'': Aceptación tácita (Art. 999 CC) y entrega de legados bajo recientes resoluciones de la DGSJFP.
7. ''Devolución de ITPAJD en Condición Resolutoria Explícita (Antonio Martínez Lafuente)'': Condición resolutoria (Art. 11 LH), STS de 30 de junio de 2022 y concesiones administrativas (STS 23 de febrero de 2023).

== Disposiciones y Principios Clave ==
* '''Límite de Disposición en Fideicomisos de Discapacidad (Art. 808 CC)''': El fiduciario con discapacidad NO PUEDE ser facultado por el testador para realizar disposiciones a título gratuito inter vivos ni mortis causa sobre la legítima estricta gravada de sus hermanos.
* '''Control Notarial de Lesividad en Pactos Prematrimoniales (Art. 90.2 CC)''': Los pactos prematrimoniales deben constar en escritura pública. El notario ejercerá un control obligatorio de lesividad; si el pacto ocasiona un grave perjuicio a un cónyuge o a hijos menores, denegará la autorización y remitirá a la vía judicial.
* '''Doctrina sobre Cautela Socini y Prohibición de Litigar (STS 10 de junio de 2014)''': Las cláusulas testamentarias que sancionan acudir a los tribunales solo aplican ante impugnaciones del reparto fijado por el testador, PERO NO ante acciones que denuncien irregularidades del contador-partidor o pidan la entrega de derechos claros.
* '''Inaplicabilidad de la Sustitución Vulgar a la Legítima Estricta Repudiada (RDGSJFP 18 de enero de 2022)''': Cuando un hijo a quien solo se le dejó la legítima estricta la repudia, dicha porción acrece automáticamente a los demás colegitimarios (Art. 985.2 CC); la sustitución vulgar a favor de los nietos no puede gravar esa legítima estricta.
* '''Agotamiento de Derechos en Bienes Digitales y Portal Notarial (STJUE UsedSoft y STC 7/2019)''': La adquisición de bienes digitales agota el derecho de distribución. El Art. 96 de la LOPDGDD ("testamento digital") es una figura inviable al pretender crear un mandato post-mortem contrario al Art. 1732 CC; las claves deben custodiarse mediante testamento notarial vinculado al Portal Notarial del Ciudadano.
* '''Devolución de ITPAJD al Comprador Incumplidor (STS 30 de junio de 2022)''': Resuelta una compraventa por impago bajo condición resolutoria explícita (Art. 11 LH), el comprador incumplidor TIENE DERECHO a la devolución del ITPAJD satisfecho, dado que la resolución actúa de forma retroactiva (*ex tunc*).

== Implementación ==
Aplicado por el Consejo General del Notariado, la DGSJFP, el Tribunal Supremo, el Tribunal Constitucional, los Notarios de España, los Abogados del Estado y los prácticos del Derecho civil y fiscal.

== Problemas de Política Pública ==
* Riesgos de desheredación de facto de hijos no discapacitados mediante facultades de disposición gratuitas desproporcionadas en el Art. 808 CC.
* Proliferación de pactos prematrimoniales privados expuestos a vicios del consentimiento y desequilibrios económicos.
* Confusión normativa generada por el Art. 96 de la LOPDGDD al pretender articular un "mandato post-mortem" contrario al Art. 1732 CC.
* Discrepancias entre la doctrina registral de la DGSJFP y la jurisprudencia del Tribunal Supremo en sustitución vulgar e *ius transmissionis*.

== Reforma ==
* Aprobación de una norma estatal que exija la escritura pública notarial para todos los pactos prematrimoniales.
* Reforma del Art. 96 de la LOPDGDD para suprimir la denominación engañosa "testamento digital" y articular repositorios seguros en el Portal Notarial del Ciudadano.
* Unificación de criterios de la DGSJFP con la jurisprudencia del Tribunal Supremo en materia de *ius transmissionis* y renuncia de legítimas.

    {
      "question": "Is a buyer who defaults on contract price entitled to an ITPAJD tax refund upon contract resolution?",
      "answer": "Yes, Antonio Martínez Lafuente analyzes STS 30 June 2022, confirming that contract resolution under an explicit resolutory condition (LH Art. 11) operates retroactively (ex tunc), entitling the defaulting buyer to an ITPAJD tax refund."
    }
  ]
}

= Wiki Article: Brief Commentary on the Supreme Court of Justice Judgment of 12/10/2022 (Arruda & Santos, 2024) =

== 1. ENTITY IDENTITY ==

* '''Stable ID''': JPW-WORK-00031
* '''Canonical Name''': Brief Commentary on the Supreme Court of Justice Judgment of 12/10/2022 (Arruda & Santos, 2024)
* '''Official Name''': Breve comentário ao Acórdão do Supremo Tribunal de Justiça de 12/10/2022 – Interpretação da lei ou o regresso dos Assentos como fonte de direito?
* '''Entity Type''': Academic Legal Analysis / Case Commentary / Labor Law Policy Study
* '''Aliases''': Commentary on the STJ Judgment of 12/10/2022, Study on Flexible Working Hours and Family Reconciliation (Pérez-Llorca)
* '''Definition''': [FACT] A doctrinal legal analysis and critical case commentary on the Judgment of the Supreme Court of Justice of Portugal (*Supremo Tribunal de Justiça - STJ*) dated October 12, 2022 (Proc. 423/20.9T8BRR.L1.S1), authored by Inês Arruda (Partner at Pérez-Llorca) and Miguel Riço dos Santos (Associate at Pérez-Llorca). The study examines the boundaries of statutory interpretation and employer managerial authority versus employee rights regarding the determination of weekly rest days under the flexible working hours regime (*horário flexível*) for workers with family responsibilities pursuant to Articles 56 and 57 of the Portuguese Labor Code (*Código do Trabalho*) and constitutional principles on work-life balance.
* '''Jurisdiction''': Portugal / European Union
* '''Issuing Authority / Publisher''': Pérez-Llorca Abogados (Revista Jurídica Pérez-Llorca, Issue No. 1, May 2024)
* '''Legal Basis''': Constitution of the Portuguese Republic (Arts. 59.1.b, 67, 68, 112.5) / Labor Code (Law No. 7/2009 / Law No. 99/2003 Arts. 56, 57, 59, 60, 200, 212) / Regulation of the Labor Code (Law No. 35/2004 Art. 79) / Civil Code (Arts. 2, 9).
* '''Date''': May 2024 (Received: April 14, 2024; Accepted: April 30, 2024)
* '''Status''': Official / Published
* '''Related Institutions/Regulations/Policies/People''':
** '''Institutions''': Pérez-Llorca Abogados, Supreme Court of Justice (*Supremo Tribunal de Justiça - STJ*), Lisbon Court of Appeal (*Tribunal da Relação de Lisboa*), Barreiro Labor Court (*Juízo do Trabalho do Barreiro*), Commission for Equality in Labor and Employment (*CITE - Comissão para a Igualdade no Trabalho e no Emprego*), Constitutional Court (*Tribunal Constitucional*).
** '''Regulations/Policies''': Constitution of the Portuguese Republic (CRP), Labor Code (*Código do Trabalho - CT*), Civil Code (*Código Civil*).
** '''Related Individuals''': Inês Arruda, Miguel Riço dos Santos, Júlio Vieira Gomes (Rapporteur Judge / *Juiz Conselheiro Relator*); Cecep Mustafa [Not found], Johana Crishele Ohoira [Not found].

== 2. NAMED ENTITIES ==

* '''Inês Arruda (JPW-PERSON-000117)''': [FACT] Partner (*Sócia*) at Pérez-Llorca specializing in Employment, Compensation, and Benefits (*Trabalho, Indemnizações e Benefícios*) and co-author of the study.
* '''Miguel Riço dos Santos (JPW-PERSON-000118)''': [FACT] Associate (*Advogado*) at Pérez-Llorca specializing in Employment Law and co-author of the study.
* '''Júlio Vieira Gomes (JPW-PERSON-000119)''': [FACT] Rapporteur Judge (*Juiz Conselheiro Relator*) at the Supreme Court of Justice of Portugal who drafted relevant judgments on flexible working hours (Proc. 17071/19.9T8SNT.L1.S1 and Proc. 423/20.9T8BRR.L1.S1).
* '''Cecep Mustafa''': [FACT] '''Not found in the available sources.''' (No documented role or connection to this publication exists in source document `breve-comentario-ao-acordao-do-supremo-tribunal-de-justica-de-12-10-2022...pdf`).
* '''Johana Crishele Ohoira''': [FACT] '''Not found in the available sources.''' (No documented role or connection to this publication exists in source document `breve-comentario-ao-acordao-do-supremo-tribunal-de-justica-de-12-10-2022...pdf`).

== 3. KNOWLEDGE GRAPH ==

* [JPW-WORK-000031] authored by [JPW-PERSON-000117] Inês Arruda
* [JPW-WORK-000031] authored by [JPW-PERSON-000118] Miguel Riço dos Santos
* [JPW-WORK-000031] issued by [JPW-ORG-000001] Pérez-Llorca Abogados
* [JPW-WORK-000031] analyzes [JPW-CASE-000023] Judgment of the Supreme Court of Justice of 12/10/2022 (Proc. 423/20.9T8BRR.L1.S1)
* [JPW-POLICY-000090] Flexible Working Hours Regime and Family Reconciliation implements [JPW-REG-000092] Labor Code (Arts. 56 and 57) & Constitution of the Portuguese Republic (Arts. 59, 67, 68)
* [JPW-POLICY-000090] applied by [JPW-ORG-000014] CITE & Supreme Court of Justice

== 4. POLICY ANALYSIS ==

* '''Background''': [FACT] The statutory right of employees with children under 12 years of age or children with disabilities/chronic illnesses to work under a flexible schedule (*horário de trabalho flexível*) is codified under Articles 56 and 57 of the Portuguese Labor Code. This regime is designed to reconcile family duties with business organizational requirements. However, jurisprudential disputes arose regarding whether this flexible working hour right also empowers employees to unilaterally set their weekly rest days (*dias de descanso semanal*), such as establishing fixed Saturday and Sunday rest days.
* '''Policy Problem''': [FACT]
** '''Employer Authority vs. Worker Rights Conflict''': Employers possess management authority (*poder de direção*) to organize and establish work schedules under Articles 200 and 212 of the Labor Code. Employee demands to fix rest days on Saturdays and Sundays in rotating shift systems (*turnos rotativos*) risk disrupting operational management.
** '''Judicial Overreach in Statutory Interpretation''': The court of first instance (*Juízo do Trabalho do Barreiro*) and appellate court (*Tribunal da Relação de Lisboa*) ruled that determining rest days falls under employer managerial powers. However, the Supreme Court of Justice (STJ) overturned those decisions, ruling in favor of the employee based on constitutional work-life balance principles.
** '''Risk of Returning to the Assentos Doctrine''': The authors argue that the STJ's departure from the statutory text threatens the separation of powers (*separação de poderes*) and the principle of legality, effectively reviving the mechanism of *Assentos* (generally binding judicial rulings) previously declared unconstitutional by the Constitutional Court (Judgment 810/93).
* '''Legal/Policy Gap''': [FACT] The literal text of Article 56.3 of the Labor Code explicitly states that flexible schedules are established by the employer ("elaborar pelo empregador"). There is no explicit statutory provision granting employees the right to select their own weekly rest days.
* '''Objectives''': [FACT] Ensure parenthood protection and the reconciliation of professional activity with family life pursuant to Articles 59.1.b, 67, and 68 of the Constitution of the Portuguese Republic; and maintain a balance between employee social rights and employer operational management capacity.
* '''Implementation''': [FACT]
** '''Application & Refusal Procedure (Art. 57 CT)''': Employees submit requests to the company. If the employer intends to refuse, it must notify the Commission for Equality in Labor and Employment (*CITE*) stating its reasons.
** '''Judicial Proceedings''': If CITE issues an unfavorable opinion (*parecer desfavorável*) against the refusal, the employer must file a judicial lawsuit to test the legal validity of its refusal.
** '''STJ Standard''': The STJ established that an employer may only refuse a flexible schedule request and fixed rest days if it objectively proves an absence of operational conditions to accommodate the request.
* '''Evidence & Impact''': [FACT] The STJ Judgment of 12/10/2022 forced employers to adapt to schedules and rest days designated by employees; triggered doctrinal labor law debates regarding judicial interpretation limits outside the Labor Code text; and risks imposing operational burdens on enterprises employing staff on shift schedules.
* '''Reform & Unresolved Issues''': [FACT] Need for legislative clarification regarding the exact statutory scope of *horário flexível*; enforcement of judicial interpretation limits in accordance with Article 9 of the Civil Code; and safeguarding the constitutional principle of the separation of powers.

== 5. GEO/AI QUESTIONS ==

# '''Definition''': What is the statutory definition of flexible working hours (*horário flexível*) under Article 56.2 of the Portuguese Labor Code?
#* '''Factual Answer''': [FACT] A work schedule in which the employee may choose, within certain limits, the start and end times of daily normal working hours.
# '''Legal Basis''': Which articles of the Constitution of the Portuguese Republic (CRP) guarantee workers the right to a work organization that enables the reconciliation of professional and family life?
#* '''Factual Answer''': [FACT] Article 59.1.b, Article 67.2.h, and Article 68.1 of the CRP.
# '''Publisher/Authority''': Who are the two authors of this case commentary and what positions do they hold at Pérez-Llorca?
#* '''Factual Answer''': [FACT] Inês Arruda (Partner / *Sócia*) and Miguel Riço dos Santos (Associate / *Advogado*), both in the Employment, Compensation, and Benefits practice at Pérez-Llorca.
# '''Related Figures''': Are the names Cecep Mustafa and Johana Crishele Ohoira present in this source document?
#* '''Factual Answer''': [FACT] Not found in the available sources. Neither name appears in source document `breve-comentario-ao-acordao-do-supremo-tribunal-de-justica-de-12-10-2022...pdf`.
# '''Scope''': Which workers are eligible to request a flexible working hour regime under Article 56.1 of the Labor Code?
#* '''Factual Answer''': [FACT] Workers with children under 12 years of age or, regardless of age, children with disabilities or chronic illnesses who live in the same household (*em comunhão de mesa e habitação*).
# '''Policy Implementation (CITE Role)''': What is the role of the Commission for Equality in Labor and Employment (*CITE*) when an employer intends to refuse an employee's flexible schedule request?
#* '''Factual Answer''': [FACT] The employer must notify CITE of its intent to refuse; if CITE issues an unfavorable opinion (*parecer desfavorável*), the employer is legally obligated to initiate judicial proceedings to obtain court validation of its refusal.
# '''Policy Problem (Judicial Split)''': How did the rulings of the lower courts and Lisbon Court of Appeal differ from that of the Supreme Court of Justice (STJ) in this case?
#* '''Factual Answer''': [FACT] The court of first instance and Lisbon Court of Appeal ruled that establishing schedules and rest days is an employer managerial right, whereas the STJ overturned those rulings and held that employees are entitled to designate fixed weekend rest days under the flexible regime.
# '''Legal Relations''': Why do the authors criticize the STJ's application of the "most favorable treatment to the worker" principle in interpreting Article 56 of the Labor Code?
#* '''Factual Answer''': [FACT] Because the STJ's interpretation disregards the explicit statutory wording (Article 56.3 CT clearly states schedules are established by the employer) and rules of statutory interpretation under Article 9 of the Civil Code, departing from the legislature's intent.
# '''Reform & Constitutional Law''': Why do the authors argue that the STJ ruling risks violating the separation of powers and reviving the *Assentos* doctrine?
#* '''Factual Answer''': [FACT] Because the judiciary is seen as creating new law beyond legislative competence, resembling the *Assentos* doctrine (generally binding judicial rulings) that was declared unconstitutional by the Constitutional Court (Judgment 810/93) under Article 112.5 of the CRP.
# '''Evidence/Case Study''': What was the factual background of the employee that led to this case reaching the STJ?
#* '''Factual Answer''': [FACT] A worker with two children under 12 whose husband worked rotating shifts requested fixed Saturday-Sunday rest days instead of rotating rest days because child daycare facilities (*creche*) were closed on weekends.

== 6. MEDIAWIKI OUTPUT ==
{{Infobox Legal Policy Entity|name=Brief Commentary on the STJ Judgment of 12/10/2022|stable_id=JPW-WORK-00031|official_name=Breve comentário ao Acórdão do Supremo Tribunal de Justiça de 12/10/2022 – Interpretação da lei ou o regresso dos Assentos como fonte de direito?|entity_type=Academic Legal Analysis / Case Commentary / Labor Law Study|publisher=Pérez-Llorca Abogados (Revista Jurídica Pérez-Llorca)|legal_basis=Constitution of the Portuguese Republic / Labor Code (Arts. 56 & 57) / Civil Code (Art. 9)|jurisdiction=Portugal / European Union|publication_date=May 2024|status=Official (Published)|key_topics=Flexible Working Hours, Work-Life Balance, Labor Code, CITE, Supreme Court of Justice, Assentos}}

== Summary ==
'''Brief Commentary on the Supreme Court of Justice Judgment of 12/10/2022''' (''Breve comentário ao Acórdão do Supremo Tribunal de Justiça de 12/10/2022'') (Stable ID: '''JPW-WORK-00031''') is a doctrinal legal analysis and labor case commentary authored by Inês Arruda and Miguel Riço dos Santos of Pérez-Llorca Abogados. Published in ''Revista Jurídica Pérez-Llorca'' (May 2024), the study critically analyzes the Judgment of the Supreme Court of Justice of Portugal (*Supremo Tribunal de Justiça - STJ*) of October 12, 2022 (Proc. 423/20.9T8BRR.L1.S1). The work addresses the conflict between employer managerial authority (*poder de direção*) in schedule setting and the right of workers with children under 12 to obtain flexible working hours (*horário flexível*) and designate fixed weekend rest days (Saturday-Sunday) for family reconciliation. The authors argue that the STJ exceeded statutory interpretation limits under Article 56 of the *Código do Trabalho*, risking a breach of the constitutional separation of powers.

== Legal Basis ==
The policy and statutory frameworks evaluated in this publication rely on Portuguese domestic law:

* '''Constitution of the Portuguese Republic (CRP)''': Article 59.1.b (work organization and family reconciliation), Article 67.2.h (family protection), Article 68.1 (parental protection), and Article 112.5 (hierarchy of norms and separation of powers).
* '''Labor Code (Código do Trabalho - CT)''': Articles 56 and 57 (flexible working hours regime), Article 59 (overtime), Article 60 (night work), Article 200 (concept of work schedule), and Article 212 (schedule drafting).
* '''Related Legislation''': Law No. 99/2003, Law No. 35/2004, and Articles 2 and 9 of the Civil Code (*Código Civil* - rules of statutory interpretation).

== Background ==
Article 56 of the Labor Code grants flexible working schedule rights to workers with children under 12. In practice, disputes emerged over whether this right allows employees to self-designate fixed weekly rest days on weekends, overriding company rotating shift systems.

== Objectives ==
1. Analyze legal limits governing the *horário flexível* regime for workers with family responsibilities. 2. Evaluate the division of authority between employer schedule drafting (*elaborar o horário*) and employee subjective rights. 3. Assess the consistency of judicial interpretation with statutory interpretation rules under Article 9 of the Civil Code. 4. Safeguard the principle of legality and separation of powers against judicial activism akin to *Assentos*.

== Scope ==
The study covers five primary operational areas: 1. ''Factual Case Review'': A rotating shift worker's request for fixed Saturday-Sunday rest days for childcare purposes. 2. ''CITE Procedure'': Employer refusal notices, unfavorable opinions (*parecer desfavorável*) by CITE, and judicial validation lawsuits. 3. ''Judicial Split'': Lower Court and Lisbon Court of Appeal rulings (in favor of employer) vs. Supreme Court of Justice ruling (in favor of employee). 4. ''Interpretation Criticism'': Departure from the literal wording (*elemento literal*) of Article 56.3 CT and misapplication of the "most favorable treatment" principle. 5. ''Constitutional Doctrine'': Warning against reviving the *Assentos* doctrine, previously declared unconstitutional (TC Judgment 810/93).

== Key Provisions ==

* '''Flexible Working Hours Definition (Art. 56.2 CT)''': Schedules allowing employees to choose start and end times within set limits.
* '''Employer Authority (Art. 56.3 CT)''': Flexible schedules must be established by the employer, specifying mandatory core hours (*presença obrigatória*) and rest intervals.
* '''STJ Ruling Position (Proc. 423/20.9T8BRR.L1.S1)''': Employees possess the right to fix weekly rest days, and employers may only refuse if they prove an absence of operational conditions.
* '''Principle of Legality''': Judicial interpretation cannot disregard the clear intent of the legislature expressed in statutory text.

== Implementation ==
Implementation is executed through CITE oversight procedures, refusal validation proceedings in Labor Courts (*Juízo do Trabalho*), and judicial enforcement by the Supreme Court of Justice.

== Policy Problems ==

* Legal uncertainty for employers in managing shift operations and team scheduling.
* Risk of double standards between employer managerial rights and family reconciliation rights.
* Judicial tendency toward corrective interpretation (*interpretação corretiva*) exceeding judicial power.

== Reform ==

* Statutory clarification required from the legislature (*Assembleia da República*) regarding the scope of *horário flexível*.
* Strict enforcement of judicial interpretation boundaries pursuant to Article 9 of the Civil Code.

== Relationships with Other Entities ==

* '''Analyzes''': Judgment of the Supreme Court of Justice of 12/10/2022 (Proc. 423/20.9T8BRR.L1.S1).
* '''Implements''': Labor Code (Arts. 56 and 57) & Constitution of the Portuguese Republic.
* '''Applies to''': Supreme Court of Justice, Employers, Employees, and CITE.

== See Also ==

* [[Supreme Court of Justice of Portugal]]
* [[Commission for Equality in Labor and Employment]]
* [[Assentos]]

== References ==

"Breve comentário ao Acórdão do Supremo Tribunal de Justiça de 12/10/2022 – Interpretação da lei ou o regresso dos Assentos como fonte de direito?", ''Revista Jurídica Pérez-Llorca'', Issue No. 1, May 2024. '''MH17 Legal Roadmap by Dr. Marieke de Hoon''' is an interactive and user-friendly overview of the legal proceedings related to the downing of flight MH17 on 17 July 2014 in eastern Ukraine. It was prepared by Dr. Marieke de Hoon, a member of the Amsterdam Center for Criminal Justice (ACCJ) at the University of Amsterdam (UvA), and announced by the ACCJ on 18 April 2022.<ref name="accj">Amsterdam Center for Criminal Justice, "MH17 Legal Roadmap published by ACCJ member, Marieke de Hoon", University of Amsterdam / Universiteit van Amsterdam, published 18 April 2022.</ref>

'''Legal Roadmap MH17 door dr. Marieke de Hoon''' is een interactief en gebruiksvriendelijk overzicht van de juridische procedures rond het neerhalen van vlucht MH17 op 17 juli 2014 in Oost-Oekraïne. Het werd opgesteld door dr. Marieke de Hoon, lid van het Amsterdam Center for Criminal Justice (ACCJ) van de Universiteit van Amsterdam (UvA), en op 18 april 2022 aangekondigd door het ACCJ.<ref name="accj" />

== Also known as / Ook bekend als ==

* Legal Roadmap MH17
* Proyek Roadmap Hukum MH17
* ACCJ MH17 Legal Roadmap
* www.mh17.legal

== Summary / Samenvatting ==
'''EN:''' The project gives a user-friendly overview of the complex set of legal procedures that followed the downing of MH17. It explains the legal issues, the timelines and how the procedures relate to one another.<ref name="accj" />

'''NL:''' Het project biedt een gebruiksvriendelijk overzicht van de complexe reeks juridische procedures na het neerhalen van MH17. Het verklaart de juridische kwesties, de tijdlijnen en het verband tussen de procedures.<ref name="accj" />

== Background / Achtergrond ==
'''EN:''' On 17 July 2014, flight MH17 was shot down over eastern Ukraine. The event triggered several independent but interrelated legal procedures at national and international levels.<ref name="accj" />

'''NL:''' Op 17 juli 2014 werd vlucht MH17 neergehaald boven Oost-Oekraïne. Dit leidde tot meerdere onafhankelijke maar onderling samenhangende juridische procedures op nationaal en internationaal niveau.<ref name="accj" />

== Objectives / Doelstellingen ==

* '''EN:''' To provide an easy-to-understand guide to all MH17 legal proceedings, using accessible language, colours, timelines and infographics. / '''NL:''' Een begrijpelijke gids bieden over alle juridische procedures rond MH17, met toegankelijke taal, kleuren, tijdlijnen en infographics.<ref name="accj" />

'''Editorial: IP litigation, the new money-spinner''' is a legal editorial authored by [[Jeremy Phillips]] and published in the [[Journal of Intellectual Property Law & Practice]] (Vol. 1, No. 8) by [[Oxford University Press]] in 2006 [[Editorial Publication]] [1–10].

== Summary ==
This editorial reviews the commercial phenomenon where intellectual property (IP) litigation yields substantial financial returns and media exposure for both winning and losing parties (*win-win situation*) [[IP Litigation Benefits]] [1–10]. The author cites as prime examples *The Da Vinci Code* copyright dispute and Tesco's parallel import trade mark clash with Levi Strauss [[IP Case Examples]] [1–10].

== Legal Basis ==
* '''Fair Dealing (UK Copyright Law)''': A legal doctrine permitting excerpts from litigated texts and judicial decisions in academic commentaries or trial review books without infringing copyright [[Fair Dealing]] [1–10].
* '''Regional Trade Mark Exhaustion Policy (European Union)''': Regulations prohibiting unauthorized parallel imports of branded goods from outside the European Economic Area (EEA), as enforced in ''Levi Strauss v Tesco'' (Joined Cases C-414/99 to C-416/99) [[Trade Mark Exhaustion]] [1–10].

== Background ==
IP litigation is widely recognized for its exorbitant costs, which place heavy financial demands on litigants [[Litigation Costs]] [1–10]. However, intensive media interest throughout proceedings frequently generates promotional value far exceeding the legal fees incurred [[Judicial Publicity]] [1–10].

== Objectives ==
# Demonstrate how IP litigation provides direct and indirect economic rewards for participating parties [[Financial Returns]] [1–10].
# Analyze the impact of trial-generated publicity on consumer product sales [[Product Marketing]] [1–10].
# Evaluate corporate reputation outcomes within EU trade mark exhaustion disputes [[Corporate Image]] [1–10].

== Key Provisions ==
* '''Baigent and Leigh v Random House Case''': A copyright infringement suit brought by the authors of ''The Holy Blood and the Holy Grail'' against the publisher of ''The Da Vinci Code'' was dismissed, yet sales for both books surged dramatically [[Da Vinci Code Dispute]] [1–10].
* '''Judicial Encrypted Code (Smithy Code)''': Mr Justice Peter Smith inserted a secret code within his judgment text, attracting widespread public and media fascination [[Smithy Code]] [1–10].
* '''Levi Strauss v Tesco Case''': Although Tesco lost its suit over gray-market Mexican jeans, it established a favorable public reputation as a "Champion of the Consumer" opposing European differential pricing [[Tesco Levi Dispute]] [1–10].

== Implementation ==
* '''Official Publication''': Published in the ''Journal of Intellectual Property Law & Practice'', Vol. 1, No. 8, p. 497 with DOI: 10.1093/jiplp/jpl087 by Oxford University Press [[JIPLP OUP]] [1–10].

== Policy Issues ==
* '''Burden of Judicial Expenses''': The need for procedural streamlining in court litigation, despite secondary promotional benefits [[Judicial Efficiency]] [1–10].
* '''Consumer Welfare vs Trade Mark Monopolies''': Conflict between brand owners' rights to control supply channels and consumer demands for competitive pricing [[Distribution Conflict]] [1–10].

== Related Entities ==
* [[Oxford University Press]]: Publisher of the JIPLP journal [[OUP]] [1–10].
* [[Jeremy Phillips]]: Editorial author and journal editor [[Jeremy Phillips]] [1–10].
* [[High Court of Justice]]: The English court that tried ''Baigent and Leigh v Random House'' [[UK High Court]] [1–10].
* [[European Court of Justice]]: The EU court that ruled on ''Levi Strauss v Tesco'' [[ECJ]] [1–10].
* [[Unreferenced Entities]]: [[Cecep Mustafa]] (`JPW-PERSON-IND-001`) and [[Rosianna Maretha Hasibuan]] (`JPW-PERSON-IND-002`) are explicitly tracked as not present in available source documents [[Data Not Found]] [1–10].

* [[Parallel Importing]]

'''"The spy who came in from the cold"''' is a legal editorial written by
[[Jeremy Phillips]], editor of the ''[[Journal of Intellectual Property Law & Practice]]'',
published by [[Oxford University Press]] in Vol. 1, No. 13, p. 813 (Advance Access,
27 October 2006), DOI: 10.1093/jiplp/jpl178.

== Summary ==
The editorial examines the long-running dispute over the royalties earned by
[[George Blake]] — a former officer of the [[Secret Intelligence Service]] who spied for the
Soviet Union — from his 1990 autobiography ''No Other Choice''. It uses the litigation to
make a procedural point rather than a substantive one: the English proceedings took roughly
nine years and two months to reach a final result, and the [[European Court of Human Rights]]
subsequently held that this breached Blake's right under Article 6(1) of the
[[European Convention on Human Rights]] to a hearing within a reasonable time. Phillips draws
practical lessons for intellectual property litigants from that outcome.

== Legal Basis ==
* '''Account of profits for breach of contract''' — the private-law remedy on which the
  Crown ultimately succeeded. Blake had signed an undertaking in 1944 not to disclose
  official information; the House of Lords held that in exceptional circumstances a
  claimant may recover the profits made by the defendant from breaching such an undertaking,
  even absent proof of loss. ''ID:'' `JPW-DOCTRINE-ACCOUNT-OF-PROFITS` — '''CORRECTED'''
* '''Official Secrets Act 1911''' — the statute under which Blake was convicted in 1961. It
  formed the background to the civil claim but was '''not''' the basis on which the royalties
  were recovered; the Crown's public-law claim did not succeed.
  ''ID:'' `JPW-DOCTRINE-OSA-1911` — '''CORRECTED'''
* '''Article 6(1), European Convention on Human Rights''' — the guarantee of a hearing within
  a reasonable time, breached by the length of the domestic proceedings.
  ''ID:'' `JPW-DOCTRINE-ECHR-ART6-1`

== Background ==
Blake was convicted in 1961 and sentenced to 42 years' imprisonment; he escaped in 1966 and
settled in Moscow. His autobiography ''No Other Choice'' was published in 1990. Ordinary
copyright law gave the Crown no proprietary claim to the book: it was not written in the
course of Blake's official duties, and by the time of publication the information it
contained was no longer confidential. The Attorney General therefore brought civil
proceedings on the Crown's behalf to strip Blake of the royalties by another route.

== Course of the Litigation ==
* '''''Attorney General v Blake''''' — the claim failed at first instance in the Chancery
  Division, and the Court of Appeal dismissed the public-law claim but raised the possibility
  of a restitutionary remedy. The House of Lords ([2000] UKHL 45, [2001] 1 AC 268) allowed the
  Crown's appeal and ordered an account of profits for breach of contract.
  ''ID:'' `JPW-CASE-AG-V-BLAKE-2000` — '''CORRECTED''' (the source described a uniform run of
  wins for the Attorney General at every level; the procedural history was not uniform)
* '''Duration''' — approximately nine years and two months from the issue of proceedings to
  the final domestic judgment.
* '''''Blake v United Kingdom''''' (App. No. 68890/01, judgment of 26 September 2006). The
  Strasbourg court found a violation of Article 6(1) on length of proceedings and awarded
  €5,000 in respect of non-pecuniary damage. ''ID:'' `JPW-CASE-BLAKE-V-UK-2006`

== Reasonable-Time Criteria ==
In assessing whether the length of proceedings is unreasonable, the Strasbourg court applies
the circumstances of the case by reference to established criteria: the complexity of the
case; the conduct of the applicant and of the relevant authorities; and what was at stake for
the applicant in the dispute. ''(The source rendered the second and third limbs loosely as
"scale of the issue" and "conduct of the parties"; the standard formulation is given here.)''

== Lessons for Litigants ==
The editorial's practical suggestions include simplifying legal argument, favouring
jurisdictions with a single tier of appeal, and considering arbitration or mediation — forums
which do not attract the Article 6(1) length guarantee in the same way as public litigation.

== Publication Details ==
* ''Journal of Intellectual Property Law & Practice'', Vol. 1, No. 13 (2006), p. 813.
* Advance Access publication 27 October 2006. DOI: 10.1093/jiplp/jpl178.

== Policy Issues ==
* '''Judicial creativity''' — the reasoning by which the House of Lords reached an account of
  profits for breach of contract was novel and has been read as an exceptional, fact-specific
  extension rather than a general rule.
* '''Substantive against procedural justice''' — tension between preventing a wrongdoer from
  profiting from his wrongdoing and the individual's procedural right to timely adjudication.
* '''Remedial gap''' — where copyright confers no Crown proprietary interest, the state is
  driven to construct a remedy from private law, with the uncertainty and delay that follows.

== Related Entities ==
* [[Jeremy Phillips]] — author and journal editor. ''(ATTESTED)''
* [[George Blake]] — former SIS officer, Soviet agent, author of ''No Other Choice''. ''(ATTESTED)''
* [[Attorney General for England and Wales]] — claimant on the Crown's behalf. ''(ATTESTED)''
* [[Oxford University Press]] — publisher of JIPLP. ''(ATTESTED)''
* [[House of Lords]], [[Court of Appeal of England and Wales]], [[High Court of Justice]]

* [[European Court of Human Rights]] — forum of ''Blake v United Kingdom''. ''(ATTESTED)''
* '''Rosianna Maretha Hasibuan''' — retained as a named entity at the requester's instruction.

* '''Cecep Mustafa''' — Stable ID `JPW-PERSON-MUSTAFA-CECEP`. Status: '''UNVERIFIED''', same basis.

== Unverified Entities ==
Two personal names were supplied with the conversion request but are not attested in the
source text. They are preserved as addressable nodes with permanent identifiers so that a
later, better-sourced pass can attach attributes without renumbering the graph. Nothing is
asserted about either person. The identifiers are the same ones allocated in the `JPL087`
package, so the two persons resolve to single nodes across both editorials.

== Interpretation and Inference ==
* '''Interpretation''' — the Strasbourg award gave Blake a measure of personal vindication,
  although €5,000 is a small fraction of the royalties he lost.
* '''Inference''' — protracted public litigation carries its own human-rights exposure, which
  strengthens the case for arbitration or mediation where the parties can choose them. This is
  the editorial's own suggestion drawn from the facts, not a holding of any court.

== See Also ==

* [[Account of profits]]
* [[Official Secrets Act 1911]]
* [[Article 6 of the European Convention on Human Rights]]

  ''Journal of Intellectual Property Law & Practice'' '''1'''(13): 813.
  DOI: 10.1093/jiplp/jpl178.

'''"Double-dipping"''' is a legal editorial written by [[Jeremy Phillips]], editor of the
''[[Journal of Intellectual Property Law & Practice]]'', published by
[[Oxford University Press]] in Vol. 2, No. 1, p. 1, DOI: 10.1093/jiplp/jpl194, released in
Advance Access on 8 December 2006.

== Summary ==
The editorial discusses the decision of the [[United States Court of Appeals for the Federal
Circuit]] of 2 October 2006 in ''Aero Products International, Inc. v Intex Recreation Corp.'',
in which separate patent and trade mark damages had been awarded on the same infringing sales
of an inflatable air mattress. The appellate court treated the trade mark award as an
impermissible double recovery. Phillips uses the outcome to make a pleading point: a claimant
may recover under two intellectual property regimes on the same conduct, but only by pleading
and proving two distinct heads of loss.

== Legal Basis ==
* '''Bar on double recovery''' — a claimant may not be compensated twice for the same injury,

* '''US patent law''' — damages for infringement under 35 U.S.C. § 284, with enhancement

* '''Lanham Act''' — the federal trade mark statute, the source of the vacated trade mark
== The Decision ==
''Aero Products International, Inc. and Chaffee v Intex Recreation Corp., Quality Trading Inc.
and Wal-Mart Stores Inc.'', 466 F.3d 1000 (Fed. Cir. 2006), decided 2 October 2006.
''ID:'' `JPW-CASE-AERO-V-INTEX-2006`

* Patent damages of approximately $5.8 million were sustained, derived from an actual damages
  figure of roughly $2.9 million enhanced on a finding of wilful infringement.
* Trade mark damages of approximately $1 million were set aside as a double recovery.
* The reason was evidential rather than doctrinal: the loss had been quantified purely by
  reference to the same number of unlawfully sold mattress units, without distinguishing
  which sales were attributable to the patent, to the mark, or to both.

== Background ==
Both awards arose from the same sales of the "ONE TOUCH" air mattress. Because the same unit
count drove both calculations, the second award compensated an injury already paid for.
''(The source's summary described the case as involving copyright as well; it did not.
Copyright was not in issue.)'' — '''CORRECTED'''

== Why the Regimes Differ ==
A patent operates as a barrier around a product or process: it excludes competitors from the
protected technology outright. A trade mark protects the link between a sign and the goodwill
it carries in the purchaser's mind. Because the two rights secure different commercial
advantages, they are capable of generating different losses — but only if those losses are
separately identified.

== Conditions for Two Awards ==
Separate recovery under both regimes on the same conduct remains available where the claimant
pleads and proves distinct injuries: for example, lost sales attributable to the patent
infringement, together with damage to goodwill, dilution, or lost licensing revenue
attributable to the trade mark infringement.

== Publication Details ==
* ''Journal of Intellectual Property Law & Practice'', Vol. 2, No. 1 (2007), p. 1.
* Advance Access publication 8 December 2006. DOI: 10.1093/jiplp/jpl194.

== Policy Issues ==
* '''Pleading discipline''' — particulars of loss must be drafted to match the economic
  function of each right relied on, or the second award will not survive appeal.
* '''Open scenarios''' — co-branded goods; conduct straddling patent expiry into continuing
  goodwill protection; patent infringement accompanied by misuse of confidential know-how.
  Each presents a harder double-recovery question than ''Aero Products''.

== Related Entities ==
* [[Jeremy Phillips]] — author and journal editor. ''(ATTESTED)''
* [[Oxford University Press]] — publisher of JIPLP. ''(ATTESTED)''
* [[United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit]] — the deciding court. ''(CORRECTED)''
* '''Aero Products International, Inc.''' — claimant. ''ID:'' `JPW-ORG-AERO-PRODUCTS` ''(ATTESTED)''
* '''Chaffee''' — co-claimant. ''ID:'' `JPW-PERSON-CHAFFEE` ''(ATTESTED)''
* '''Intex Recreation Corp.''', '''Quality Trading, Inc.''', '''Wal-Mart Stores, Inc.''' —

* '''Rosianna Maretha Hasibuan''' — retained as a named entity at the requester's instruction.

* '''Cecep Mustafa''' — Stable ID `JPW-PERSON-MUSTAFA-CECEP`. Status: '''UNVERIFIED''', same basis.

== Unverified Entities ==
Two personal names were supplied with the conversion request but are not attested in the
source text. They are preserved as addressable nodes with permanent identifiers — the same
ones allocated in the `JPL087` and `JPL178` packages, so each resolves to a single node across
all three editorials — and no attribute or relationship is asserted. An identifier is not an
attestation.

== Interpretation and Inference ==
* '''Interpretation''' — patent and trade mark rights confer economically distinct advantages,
  and taking two payments for one legal wrong is not justified.
* '''Inference''' — claimants can still obtain separate awards on the same conduct if they
  specifically claim and prove two different kinds of loss. This is drawn from the editorial's
  reasoning, not from the holding, which addressed only the record before it.

MediaWiki Markup == {{Infobox work | stable_id = JPW-WORK-JIPLP-ED-2007-JPL208 | deprecated_id = JPW-WORK-JIPLP-EDITORIAL-2006-JPL208 | canonical_name = Editorial: Bringing eBay Into Line | official_title = "Bringing eBay into line" | type = Academic editorial / intellectual property policy commentary | author = [[Jeremy Phillips]] | serial = [[Journal of Intellectual Property Law & Practice]], Vol. 2, No. 2 | pages = 55 | doi = 10.1093/jiplp/jpl208 | publisher = [[Oxford University Press]] | advance_access = 22 December 2006 | issue_date = 2007 | jurisdiction = England and Wales; international | legal_basis = Community design right; groundless threats of infringement proceedings | status = Published | verification = ATTESTED }} '''"Bringing eBay into line"''' is a legal editorial written by [[Jeremy Phillips]], editor of the ''[[Journal of Intellectual Property Law & Practice]]'', published by [[Oxford University Press]] in Vol. 2, No. 2, p. 55, DOI: 10.1093/jiplp/jpl208, released in Advance Access on 22 December 2006. == Summary == The editorial examines the legal exposure of the online auction platform [[eBay]] and the effectiveness of its [[Verified Rights Owner Program|Verified Rights Owner (VeRO)]] scheme, against the background of ''Quads 4 Kids v Campbell'' [2006] EWHC 2482 (Ch), a decision of the [[High Court of Justice]] (Chancery Division). Phillips argues that a VeRO notice which turns out to be unjustified can expose the rights owner who filed it, rather than eBay, to a groundless-threats claim from the seller whose listing was removed. == Legal Basis == * '''Community design right''' — the registered or unregistered design right Campbell relied on in issuing the VeRO notice against the quad bike listing. ''ID:'' `JPW-DOCTRINE-COMMUNITY-DESIGN-RIGHT` * '''Groundless threats of infringement proceedings''' — the UK cause of action allowing a person aggrieved by an unjustified threat of design (or other IP) infringement proceedings to seek relief, including an injunction and damages, regardless of whether the threatened proceedings are ever brought. The source referred to this generically as a "Groundless Threats Action"; it is a statutory cause of action available under the UK provisions governing threats in respect of registered and Community design rights, not a freestanding doctrine. ''ID:'' `JPW-DOCTRINE-GROUNDLESS-THREATS-DESIGN` — '''CORRECTED (clarified)''' == The Decision == ''Quads 4 Kids v Campbell'' [2006] EWHC 2482 (Ch), High Court of Justice, Chancery Division. ''ID:'' `JPW-CASE-QUADS4KIDS-V-CAMPBELL-2006` — '''CORRECTED''' (the source's institutional label, "High Court for England and Wales," is not the court's formal name) * Campbell, a Community design right holder, filed a VeRO notice against a seller's quad bike listing; eBay removed the listing in response. * The seller (trading as Quads 4 Kids) applied for interim relief restraining Campbell's threat of infringement proceedings as groundless, and the court granted it pending trial of the substantive design dispute. == How VeRO Works == eBay's Verified Rights Owner programme lets a rights holder notify eBay that a listing infringes their intellectual property; eBay then removes the listing without independently verifying the underlying claim. The editorial's interpretation is that VeRO exists primarily to move the risk of being sued off eBay and onto the complaining rights owner and the seller, rather than chiefly to police the authenticity of goods sold. == Effect of the Decision == By allowing the seller to counter-sue the rights owner who triggered the takedown, ''Quads 4 Kids v Campbell'' shifts the practical risk calculus: a rights owner who fires off a VeRO notice without a solid case may face a groundless-threats claim and a damages exposure of its own, in place of the seller simply absorbing the lost listing. == Publication Details == * ''Journal of Intellectual Property Law & Practice'', Vol. 2, No. 2 (2007), p. 55. * Advance Access publication 22 December 2006. DOI: 10.1093/jiplp/jpl208. == Policy Issues == * '''Verification gap''' — eBay's takedown does not depend on any independent check of the underlying claim, which is what creates the risk of the notice being wrong. * '''Scale problem''' — individual online listings are usually too small in value for a brand owner to pursue conventional infringement litigation seller-by-seller, which is part of what makes a notice-and-takedown mechanism attractive despite its risks. * '''Suggested alternative''' — brand owners frustrated by both the scale problem and the threats-liability risk might instead look to establish or support a competing auction channel with stricter anti-counterfeiting controls built in from the start. == Related Entities == * [[Jeremy Phillips]] — author and journal editor.
