'''Copyright, Property Rights, and Supervened Conformed Property Policy Framework for Street Art''' (''Street Art as ‘Supervened’ Conformed Property: Civil Law Issues and Hermeneutic Solutions Between Italy and The United States'') is a comparative civil law and copyright analysis framework (Italy – United States) formulated by Giulia Anselmo in *The Italian Law Journal* (Vol. 10 Nos. 01-02/2024, pp. 517–534)<ref>Anselmo, G. (2024). Street Art as ‘Supervened’ Conformed Property: Civil Law Issues and Hermeneutic Solutions Between Italy and The United States. ''The Italian Law Journal'', 10(1-2), 517–534.</ref>; examining the phenomenon of street art (both commissioned and spontaneous/illicit) and its legal dialectic with property rights and copyright/moral rights<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 517, 518, 519.</ref>; analyzing the US legal regime under the ''Visual Artists Rights Act of 1990 (VARA)'' (17 U.S.C. § 106A & § 113(d)) and the ''5Pointz'' case (''Cohen v. G & M Realty L.P.'')<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 521, 522, 523.</ref>; dissecting the Italian legal regime under Article 936 of the ''Codice Civile'', Articles 1 & 6 of the ''Legge sul Diritto d'Autore'' (L. 633/1941), Articles 10, 50, & 90 of the ''Codice dei Beni Culturali e del Paesaggio'' (D.Lgs. 42/2004), alongside the criminal offense of defacement (''imbrattamento'', Article 639 ''Codice Penale'') and judicial rulings (''Banksy in Venice'', ''Keith Haring Tuttomondo in Pisa'', ''Alice Pasqualini in Bologna'', ''Sqon'', ''Blu'')<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 524, 525, 526, 527.</ref>; and introducing a new hermeneutic concept known as ''supervened conformed property'' (''proprietà conformata sopravvenuta'') and the governance of urban commons / ''dictatio ad patriam''<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 519, 531, 532.</ref>.

== Summary ==
Authored by [[Giulia Anselmo]] (Post-doctoral Researcher at the University of Siena), this work presents a comprehensive comparative analysis of the legal conflicts between property owners and street artists in Italy and the United States<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 517, 519.</ref>. In the United States, an artist's moral rights are protected by the ''Visual Artists Rights Act (VARA) of 1990'' if the artwork has attained "recognized stature," as demonstrated by the $6.75 million statutory damages award in the ''5Pointz'' decision<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 521, 523.</ref>. In Italy, although illegal works are technically subject to criminal defacement charges (''imbrattamento'' under Article 639 CP), courts have increasingly dismissed charges when the work enhances the urban environment (e.g., cases involving ''Banksy'' in Venice and ''Keith Haring'' in Pisa)<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 525, 526, 527.</ref>. The author proposes the novel doctrine of "supervened conformed property" to automatically restrict private property rights in order to safeguard the cultural value and social function of street art for the public benefit<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 532, 533.</ref>.

== Legal Basis ==
* '''Italian Legislation & Constitution''':
** ''Costituzione della Repubblica Italiana'': Article 9 (Protection of Historical and Artistic Heritage), Article 21 (Freedom of Expression), and Article 42 (Property Rights & Social Function)<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 524, 532.</ref>.
** ''Codice Civile Italiano'': Article 936 (Accession / Works Made by a Third Party) and Article 2041 (Unjust Enrichment)<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 524, 525.</ref>.
** ''Legge 22 Aprile 1941 n. 633 (Legge sul Diritto d'Autore)'': Articles 1 and 6 (Principle of Copyright Neutrality)<ref>Anselmo (2024), p. 525.</ref>.
** ''Decreto Legislativo 22 Gennaio 2004 n. 42 (Codice dei Beni Culturali e del Paesaggio)'': Article 10, Article 50 (Divieto di stacco / Prohibition of Detachment), and Article 90 (Scoperta fortunata / Chance Discovery)<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 526, 527, 529, 531, 532.</ref>.
** ''Codice Penale Italiano'': Article 639 (Deturpamento e imbrattamento di cose altrui / Defacement)<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 525, 526.</ref>.
** ''Legge 7 Agosto 1990 n. 241'': Article 20 para. 4 (Silenzio-assenso and Cultural Heritage Exceptions)<ref>Anselmo (2024), p. 531.</ref>.
* '''United States Legislation & Constitution''':
** ''United States Constitution'': First Amendment (Free Speech) & Fifth Amendment (Takings Clause / Property Rights)<ref>Anselmo (2024), p. 521.</ref>.
** ''Visual Artists Rights Act of 1990 (VARA / 17 U.S.C. § 106A & § 113(d))''<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 521, 522.</ref>.
* '''Key Jurisprudence''':
** ''United States'': ''Cohen v. G & M Realty L.P.'' (5Pointz 2018), ''Pollara v. Seymour'' (2001), ''English v. BFC & R East 11th Street LLC'' (1997)<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 521, 522, 523.</ref>.
** ''Italy'': ''Corte di Cassazione Sez. II Penale No. 16371/2016'', ''Tribunale di Bologna No. 674/2016'' (Pasqualini Case), ''Banksy in Venice'' dismissal order (2023), ''Decree No. 335/2013'' (Keith Haring Tuttomondo in Pisa)<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 526, 527.</ref>.

== Core Provisions & Policy Pillars ==
1. '''Comparison of US VARA and Italian Copyright Regimes''': The US relies on the "recognized stature" standard and a mandatory 90-day notification procedure to prevent the destruction of street art integrated into buildings under VARA § 113(d). Italy applies the "Principle of Neutrality" (L. 633/1941), under which copyright subsists upon creation regardless of the legality of the site<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 521, 522, 525, 528.</ref>.
2. '''Shift from Criminal Defacement to Ameliorative Art''': Italian criminal jurisprudence has begun setting aside Article 639 CP charges when street art serves to beautify previously degraded walls, thereby elevating the social and environmental value of urban space<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 526, 527, 528.</ref>.
3. '''Concept of Proprietà Conformata Sopravvenuta''': The author proposes the legal doctrine of supervened conformed property, wherein building owners' property rights are automatically constrained ex novo by law to fulfill their social function (Art. 42 Italian Constitution) and guarantee the public's right to access urban commons and cultural heritage (''dictatio ad patriam'')<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 531, 532, 533, 534.</ref>.

'''Quadro Politico-Giuridico della Street Art come Proprietà Conformata Sopravvenuta''' (''Street Art as ‘Supervened’ Conformed Property: Civil Law Issues and Hermeneutic Solutions Between Italy and The United States'') è un quadro di analisi comparata di diritto civile e diritto d'autore (Italia – Stati Uniti) formulato da Giulia Anselmo su *The Italian Law Journal* (Vol. 10 Nos. 01-02/2024, pp. 517–534)<ref>Anselmo, G. (2024). Street Art as ‘Supervened’ Conformed Property: Civil Law Issues and Hermeneutic Solutions Between Italy and The United States. ''The Italian Law Journal'', 10(1-2), 517–534.</ref>; esamina il fenomeno della *street art* (sia su commissione sia spontanea/illecita) e la sua dialettica giuridica con il diritto di proprietà e il diritto d'autore/diritti morali<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 517, 518, 519.</ref>; analizza il regime giuridico statunitense ai sensi del ''Visual Artists Rights Act of 1990 (VARA)'' (17 U.S.C. § 106A & § 113(d)) e il caso ''5Pointz'' (''Cohen v. G & M Realty L.P.'')<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 521, 522, 523.</ref>; analizza il regime giuridico italiano ai sensi dell'Articolo 936 del ''Codice Civile'', degli Articoli 1 & 6 della ''Legge sul Diritto d'Autore'' (L. 633/1941), degli Articoli 10, 50, & 90 del ''Codice dei Beni Culturali e del Paesaggio'' (D.Lgs. 42/2004), unitamente al reato di imbrattamento (Articolo 639 ''Codice Penale'') e alle decisioni giurisprudenziali (''Banksy a Venezia'', ''Keith Haring Tuttomondo a Pisa'', ''Alice Pasqualini a Bologna'', ''Sqon'', ''Blu'')<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 524, 525, 526, 527.</ref>; e introduce la nuova concezione ermeneutica di ''proprietà conformata sopravvenuta'' e la gestione dei beni comuni urbani / ''dictatio ad patriam''<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 519, 531, 532.</ref>.

== Sintesi ==
A cura di [[Giulia Anselmo]] (Assegnista di ricerca presso l'Università degli Studi di Siena), quest'opera offre un'analisi comparativa approfondita sui conflitti giuridici tra proprietari immobiliari e street artist in Italia e negli Stati Uniti<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 517, 519.</ref>. Negli Stati Uniti, i diritti morali dell'artista sono tutelati dal ''Visual Artists Rights Act (VARA) del 1990'' se l'opera ha raggiunto una notorietà riconosciuta (''recognized stature''), come dimostrato dal risarcimento di 6,75 milioni di dollari nel caso ''5Pointz''<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 521, 523.</ref>. In Italia, sebbene le opere illecite siano astrattamente soggette al reato di imbrattamento (Art. 639 c.p.), la giurisprudenza tende ad assolvere gli artisti qualora l'opera riqualifichi il contesto urbano (es. i casi relativi a ''Banksy'' a Venezia e ''Keith Haring'' a Pisa)<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 525, 526, 527.</ref>. L'autrice propone la nuova categoria dogmatica della "proprietà conformata sopravvenuta" per limitare automaticamente il diritto di proprietà privata a tutela del valore culturale e della funzione sociale dell'opera per la collettività<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 532, 533.</ref>.

== Basi Giuridiche ==
* '''Legislazione e Costituzione Italiana''':
** ''Costituzione della Repubblica Italiana'': Articolo 9 (Tutela del patrimonio storico e artistico), Articolo 21 (Libertà di manifestazione del pensiero), e Articolo 42 (Proprietà privata e funzione sociale)<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 524, 532.</ref>.
** ''Codice Civile Italiano'': Articolo 936 (Accessione / Opere fatte da un terzo con materiali propri) e Articolo 2041 (Arricchimento senza causa)<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 524, 525.</ref>.
** ''Legge 22 Aprile 1941 n. 633 (Legge sul Diritto d'Autore)'': Articoli 1 e 6 (Principio di neutralità del diritto d'autore)<ref>Anselmo (2024), p. 525.</ref>.
** ''Decreto Legislativo 22 Gennaio 2004 n. 42 (Codice dei Beni Culturali e del Paesaggio)'': Articolo 10, Articolo 50 (Divieto di stacco) e Articolo 90 (Scoperta fortunata)<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 526, 527, 529, 531, 532.</ref>.
** ''Codice Penale Italiano'': Articolo 639 (Deturpamento e imbrattamento di cose altrui)<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 525, 526.</ref>.
** ''Legge 7 Agosto 1990 n. 241'': Articolo 20 comma 4 (Silenzio-assenso ed eccezioni per i beni culturali)<ref>Anselmo (2024), p. 531.</ref>.
* '''Legislazione e Costituzione degli Stati Uniti''':
** ''Costituzione degli Stati Uniti d'America'': Primo Emendamento (Libertà di espressione) & Quinto Emendamento (Takings Clause / Diritto di proprietà)<ref>Anselmo (2024), p. 521.</ref>.
** ''Visual Artists Rights Act of 1990 (VARA / 17 U.S.C. § 106A & § 113(d))''<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 521, 522.</ref>.
* '''Giurisprudenza Principale''':
** ''Stati Uniti'': ''Cohen v. G & M Realty L.P.'' (5Pointz 2018), ''Pollara v. Seymour'' (2001), ''English v. BFC & R East 11th Street LLC'' (1997)<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 521, 522, 523.</ref>.
** ''Italia'': ''Corte di Cassazione Sez. II Penale n. 16371/2016'', ''Tribunale di Bologna n. 674/2016'' (Caso Pasqualini), Richiesta di archiviazione caso ''Banksy a Venezia'' (2023), ''Decreto n. 335/2013'' (Keith Haring Tuttomondo a Pisa)<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 526, 527.</ref>.

== Disposizioni Chiave e Pilastri della Politica Giuridica ==
1. '''Comparazione tra il VARA Statunitense e il Diritto d'Autore Italiano''': Gli USA adottano lo standard del "recognized stature" e un preavviso obbligatorio di 90 giorni per impedire la distruzione di opere d'arte incorporate negli edifici ai sensi del VARA § 113(d). L'Italia applica il "Principio di Neutralità" (L. 633/1941), per cui il diritto d'autore nasce al momento della creazione a prescindere dalla liceità del luogo d'installazione<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 521, 522, 525, 528.</ref>.
2. '''Evoluzione dal Reato di Imbrattamento all'Arte Migliorativa''': La giurisprudenza penale italiana ha iniziato a escludere la punibilità ex Art. 639 c.p. qualora la *street art* configuri un abbellimento (*beautification*) di pareti degradate, incrementando il valore sociale dell'ambiente urbano<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 526, 527, 528.</ref>.
3. '''Teoria della Proprietà Conformata Sopravvenuta''': L'autrice delinea la dottrina della proprietà conformata sopravvenuta, in base alla quale le facoltà dominicali del proprietario dell'immobile vengono limitate ex novo dalla legge al fine di garantire la funzione sociale della proprietà (Art. 42 Cost.) e il diritto della collettività di fruire dei beni comuni urbani (''dictatio ad patriam'')<ref>Anselmo (2024), pp. 531, 532, 533, 534.</ref>.

'''Policy Framework for Reducing the Impact of Single-Use Plastic Products and Implementation of Directive (EU) 2019/904 Transposition in Italy and EU Member States''' (''EU Directive 2019/904/EU Single-Use Plastics Policy and National/Regional Transposition Framework'') is an EU environmental law and comparative national/regional analytical framework formulated by Luna Aristei to evaluate the challenges, gaps, and variations in the transposition of Directive (EU) 2019/904 on the reduction of the impact of certain plastic products on the environment (Single-Use Plastics / SUP Directive) <ref>Aristei, L. (2022). A Plastic World. Ups and Downs in the National Application of Directive 2019/904/EU. ''Italian Journal of Public Law'', 14(2), 491–520.</ref>. The framework examines Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) mechanisms, prohibitions on specific single-use plastic items (such as straws, plates, and cotton bud sticks), marking and labeling requirements, the implementation of plastic taxes, pioneering regional regulations in Italy (Marche, Emilia-Romagna, Campania), and the dynamics of Italian administrative jurisprudence (TAR Sicilia, TAR Abruzzo, TAR Puglia, Consiglio di Stato) regarding the boundaries of regional competence and environmental protection <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 491, 496, 498, 505, 513, 514, 516, 518.</ref>.

== Executive Summary ==
Authored by [[Luna Aristei]] (Researcher at Università LUISS Guido Carli, Rome), this study presents a critical evaluation of the implementation of Directive (EU) 2019/904 across the European Union <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 491.</ref>. The author compares transposition performance between virtuous states (Estonia, France, Greece, the Netherlands, Germany) and lagging Member States (Romania, Slovakia) <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 505, 509.</ref>. The framework highlights the pioneering role of Italian regional authorities that introduced anti-plastic restrictions prior to national legislation and examines administrative litigation concerning whether sub-national entities possess authority to establish higher environmental protection standards than national statutes <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 514, 516, 518.</ref>.

== Legal Basis ==
The regulatory framework for single-use plastics reduction across the EU and Italy rests upon supranational directives, national legislation, and regional bylaws:
* '''[[Directive (EU) 2019/904]] (Single-Use Plastics Directive)''': Imposes market bans on items with readily available alternatives (Art. 5), PET bottle recycling targets (Art. 6), mandatory product marking (Art. 7), and EPR schemes (Art. 8) <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 497–499.</ref>.
* '''[[Directive 2008/98/EC]] (Waste Framework Directive)''' & '''Directive (EU) 2018/851''': General framework for waste management and minimum EPR requirements <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 493, 497.</ref>.
* '''Italian National Statutes''':
** ''Law 27 December 2017, No. 205'': Prohibited non-biodegradable plastic cotton bud sticks from 1 January 2019 <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 513.</ref>.
** ''Law 30 December 2018, No. 145'' & ''Law 27 December 2019, No. 160'': Instituted a Plastic Tax (€0.45/kg) on single-use items <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 513.</ref>.
** ''Article 117, paragraph 2, letter s) of the Italian Constitution'': Reserves exclusive legislative power over environmental protection to the State <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 517–518.</ref>.
* '''Italian Regional Enactments''': Regional Law Marche No. 27/2019 <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 514.</ref>; Regional Executive Resolution Emilia-Romagna No. 2000/2019 (#Plastic-freER Strategy) <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 514–515.</ref>; Regional Law Campania No. 26/2019 <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 515.</ref>.

== Background & Transposition Challenges ==
Global plastic production has increased twentyfold since the 1960s and is projected to quadruple by 2050 <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 491.</ref>. An estimated 150,000 to 500,000 tonnes of plastic waste enter EU marine environments annually <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 492.</ref>. In response, the European Commission adopted the European Strategy for Plastics in a Circular Economy (2018) and enacted Directive (EU) 2019/904 <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 493, 498.</ref>. However, the transposition deadline of 3 July 2021 resulted in regulatory fragmentation across Member States due to differing national readiness levels, industrial pushback, and vague quantitative reduction mandates for items like food containers and beverage cups <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 500, 504, 509.</ref>.

== Core Provisions & Comparative Findings ==
* '''Member State Transposition Spectrum''':
# ''Virtuous Performers'': Estonia implemented a deposit-return system for beverage containers and a mandatory €0.50 surcharge on single-use cups <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 505.</ref>; Greece banned single-use plastics in public bodies (Law 4736/2020) <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 505–506.</ref>; France banned single-use plastic plates and straws early (Law No. 398/2018) and set a full phase-out target for 2040 <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 506.</ref>; the Netherlands instituted deposit-return fees on small plastic bottles and cans <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 507.</ref>.
# ''Lagging States'': Romania and Slovakia missed transposition milestones due to industrial opposition and administrative delays <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 509.</ref>.
* '''Italian Administrative Jurisprudence (Consiglio di Stato No. 4273/2019)''':
# Regional Administrative Courts (TAR Sicilia, TAR Puglia) initially struck down municipal anti-plastic ordinances, holding that environmental protection is an exclusive national power <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 516–517.</ref>.
# The Council of State (Consiglio di Stato, Sec. IV, Order No. 4273/2019) reversed TAR Puglia, holding that regional and local authorities may establish higher standards of environmental protection to safeguard sensitive coastal domains <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 518.</ref>.

== Unresolved Policy Issues ==
* '''Italian Plastic Tax Delays''': The €0.45/kg plastic tax enacted under Law 160/2019 faced repeated legislative suspensions (deferred to 1 January 2024 via Law 197/2022) following industrial lobbying over projected revenue declines <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 513.</ref>.
* '''Omission of Civic Education''': Directive (EU) 2019/904 focuses predominantly on market restrictions and producer obligations while failing to harmonize public awareness and civic education, which are vital components of a long-term "Plastexit" strategy <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 500, 501, 519, 520.</ref>.

'''Quadro di Politica Pubblica per la Riduzione dell'Impatto dei Prodotti in Plastica Monouso e Attuazione della Direttiva (UE) 2019/904 in Italia e negli Stati Membri dell'UE''' (''EU Directive 2019/904/EU Single-Use Plastics Policy and National/Regional Transposition Framework'') è un quadro analitico di diritto ambientale europeo e comparato nazionale/regionale formulato da Luna Aristei per valutare le sfide, le lacune e le variazioni di recepimento della Direttiva (UE) 2019/904 sulla riduzione dell'impatto di determinati prodotti in plastica sull'ambiente (Direttiva SUP / Single-Use Plastics) <ref>Aristei, L. (2022). A Plastic World. Ups and Downs in the National Application of Directive 2019/904/EU. ''Italian Journal of Public Law'', 14(2), 491–520.</ref>. Questo quadro esamina i meccanismi di Responsabilità Estesa del Produttore (EPR), i divieti sui prodotti monouso (come cannucce, piatti e bastoncini cotonato), gli obblighi di marcatura, l'introduzione della Plastic Tax, le normative regionali pioniere in Italia (Marche, Emilia-Romagna, Campania) e la dinamica della giurisprudenza amministrativa italiana (TAR Sicilia, TAR Abruzzo, TAR Puglia, Consiglio di Stato) relativa ai limiti delle competenze regionali e alla tutela ambientale <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 491, 496, 498, 505, 513, 514, 516, 518.</ref>.

== Sintesi ==
Scritto da [[Luna Aristei]] (Ricercatrice presso l'Università LUISS Guido Carli di Roma), questo studio presenta una valutazione critica sull'attuazione della Direttiva (UE) 2019/904 nell'Unione Europea <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 491.</ref>. L'autrice confronta i tassi di successo del recepimento tra Stati ad alte prestazioni ("Stati virtuosi" come Estonia, Francia, Grecia, Paesi Bassi e Germania) e Stati in ritardo (come Romania e Slovacchia) <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 505, 509.</ref>. Lo studio evidenzia il ruolo pionieristico dei governi regionali in Italia che hanno introdotto divieti sulla plastica prima della legislazione nazionale e analizza i contenziosi amministrativi riguardanti la competenza regionale nello stabilire standard di tutela ambientale più elevati rispetto alle leggi statali <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 514, 516, 518.</ref>.

== Base Giuridica ==
Il quadro normativo per la riduzione della plastica monouso nell'Unione Europea e in Italia si basa su direttive sopranazionali, leggi nazionali e ordinanze regionali:
* '''[[Direttiva (UE) 2019/904]] (Direttiva SUP)''': Impone restrizioni di mercato per le plastiche facilmente sostituibili (Articolo 5), obiettivi di riciclaggio delle bottiglie in PET (Articolo 6), obblighi di marcatura (Articolo 7) e regimi di Responsabilità Estesa del Produttore (EPR) (Articolo 8) <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 497, 498, 499.</ref>.
* '''[[Direttiva 2008/98/CE]] (Direttiva Quadro sui Rifiuti)''': Regole generali per la gestione dei rifiuti e requisiti minimi EPR <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 493, 497.</ref>.
* '''Legislazione Nazionale Italiana''':
** *Legge 27 dicembre 2017, n. 205*: Ha vietato i bastoncini cotonato in plastica non biodegradabile dal 1° gennaio 2019 <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 513.</ref>.
** *Legge 27 dicembre 2019, n. 160*: Ha introdotto la Plastic Tax (€0,45/kg) sui prodotti monouso <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 513.</ref>.
** *Articolo 117, Comma 2, Lettera s) della Costituzione Italiana*: Attribuisce allo Stato la competenza esclusiva in materia di tutela dell'ambiente <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 517, 518.</ref>.
* '''Legislazione Regionale Italiana''': Legge Regionale Marche n. 27/2019 <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 514.</ref>; Delibera Giunta Regionale Emilia-Romagna n. 2000/2019 (#Plastic-freER) <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 514, 515.</ref>; Legge Regionale Campania n. 26/2019 <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 515.</ref>.

== Contesto e Sfide di Recepimento ==
La produzione e il consumo globale di plastica sono aumentati di 20 volte rispetto agli anni '60 e si prevede che quadruplicheranno entro il 2050 <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 491.</ref>. Tra le 150.000 e le 500.000 tonnellate di rifiuti di plastica finiscono nei mari dell'UE ogni anno, causando un grave degrado marino <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 492.</ref>. La Direttiva SUP è stata approvata nel 2019 per accelerare la transizione verso un'economia circolare <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 493, 498.</ref>. Tuttavia, il termine di recepimento del 3 luglio 2021 ha generato una forte frammentazione giuridica poiché diversi Stati membri hanno riscontrato difficoltà nell'adeguamento industriale <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 504, 509.</ref>.

== Obiettivi ==
* Prevenire e ridurre l'impatto di determinati prodotti in plastica monouso sull'ambiente acquatico e sulla salute umana <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 491, 498.</ref>.
* Promuovere la transizione verso l'economia circolare tramite regimi EPR, obiettivi di riciclaggio e progettazione di prodotti riutilizzabili <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 497, 501, 505.</ref>.
* Ottenere un risparmio di 2,6 milioni di tonnellate di CO2 ed evitare danni ambientali pari a 11 miliardi di euro entro il 2030 <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 498.</ref>.

== Ambito e Risultati Comparativi ==
* '''Variazioni nel Recepimento degli Stati Membri''':
# *Stati Virtuosi*: L'Estonia ha introdotto un contributo minimo di €0,50 sulle tazze monouso <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 505.</ref>; la Grecia ha vietato la plastica monouso negli enti pubblici <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 505, 506.</ref>; la Francia ha istituito regimi EPR per i filtri del tabacco e mira alla graduale eliminazione degli imballaggi monouso entro il 2040 <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 506.</ref>; i Paesi Bassi hanno applicato un deposito di 15 centesimi sulle bottiglie di plastica <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 507.</ref>.
# *Stati in Ritardo*: Slovacchia e Romania hanno ritardato l'adozione delle norme per impreparazione del settore industriale <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 509.</ref>.
* '''Giurisprudenza Amministrativa Italiana (Consiglio di Stato n. 4273/2019)''':
# *TAR Sicilia e TAR Puglia* avevano inizialmente annullato i divieti comunali sulla plastica ritenendoli un'invasione della competenza statale <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 516, 517.</ref>.
# Il *Consiglio di Stato* ha riformato le decisioni cautelari del TAR Puglia, affermando che le Autorità regionali possiedono la legittima potestà di stabilire livelli di tutela ambientale più elevati per la salvaguardia del demanio marittimo <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 518.</ref>.

== Questioni Irrisolte e Criticita ==
* '''Ritardi della Plastic Tax Italiana (€0,45/kg)''': L'applicazione della tassa prevista dalla Legge 160/2019 è stata rinviata più volte a causa dell'opposizione delle associazioni industriali <ref>Aristei (2022), p. 513.</ref>.
* '''Carenza di Educazione Civica''': La Direttiva si concentra principalmente sulle restrizioni dell'offerta, ma trascura programmi di educazione civica armonizzati, fondamentali per una strategia "Plastexit" di successo <ref>Aristei (2022), pp. 500, 501, 519, 520.</ref>.

'''Reforming Justice: A Journey to Fairness in Asia''' is an academic judicial policy monograph authored by Dr. Livingston Armytage (published by Cambridge University Press, 2012, ISBN 978-1-107-01382), which was scientifically reviewed by Sandra Taal (PhD Candidate at the Law Department, Utrecht University).

== Summary ==
This document reviews a critical analysis of the failure of international judicial reform programs in development assistance over the past decades. The book critiques the dominant economic growth-based "institutionalist" approach to legal reform because it has demonstrably failed to alleviate poverty and has not created equitable growth. Armytage reformulates the primary goal of judicial reform from a mere economic instrument to a constitutive theory of justice centered on '''fairness and equity''' and human rights [1–4].

== Legal Basis ==
* '''Not found in the available sources:''' This document is an academic research monograph and scientific book review, not a specific statutory or judicial legislative instrument [1–6].

== Background ==
International development assistance has allocated massive funds for judicial reform worldwide, but the performance has generally been disappointing. This is due to the dominance of the market economy paradigm that views courts instrumentally only as supporters of economic growth, without considering the distributive dimension of justice for the poor.

== Objectives ==
1. Position justice centrally in the concept of equitable development.
2. Shift the reform paradigm from economic/political justification to a humanistic justification that views poverty as a deprivation of opportunity and human rights.
3. Build a performance evaluation framework for judicial reform based on international normative standards.

== Scope & 3 Asian Case Studies ==
The book evaluates reform practices through three main case studies in the Asia-Pacific region:
1. Judicial reform experience at the Asian Development Bank (ADB).
2. AusAID's Law and Justice Sector Program in Papua New Guinea.
3. The experience of reform practitioners across the Asia-Pacific region.

== Key Provisions & Evaluation Framework ==
* '''Failure of the Economic Institutionalist Model:''' [FACT] There is no empirical evidence showing that economic growth-based judicial reform successfully alleviates poverty.
* '''Humanistic Justification:''' [FACT] Judicial reform must focus on promoting equity, fairness, and access to justice for the poor.
* '''Human Rights Evaluation Framework:''' [FACT] Evaluating the effectiveness of judicial reform must be based on the '''principal treaties of international human rights law'''. These treaties provide a universal normative standard recognized by the majority of UN member states.

== Policy Problems ==
1. A lack of judicial reform evaluations conducted methodologically and independently.
2. The failure of international donors to agree on a standardized orthodoxy regarding the measurement of legal development effectiveness.

== Reform / Change ==
Realigns the policy direction of global judicial reform to center on human rights enforcement, distributive equity, and evaluation accountability [3–6].

== Relationships with Other Entities ==
* '''Utrecht University & Cambridge University Press:''' Affiliations of the reviewer (Sandra Taal) and the book publisher.
* '''Asian Development Bank & AusAID:''' Subjects of the case study evaluations.
* '''Cecep Mustafa & [private person]:''' Not found in the available sources [1–6].

'''The Comparative Asian Judicial Systems Policy Framework''' is a comparative judicial governance policy framework reviewed by Markus Zimmer (Executive Editor of the IJCA, 2015) based on the book *Asian Courts in Context*, edited by Jiunn-Rong Yeh and Wen-Chen Chang (National Taiwan University, Cambridge University Press, 2015). It maps the institutional evolution, structure, and judicial administrative reforms across 14 Asian countries/economies (5 advanced and 9 rapidly developing) in response to globalization, the legacy of colonialism, and the dynamics of customary and religious laws [2–8, 16].

== Summary ==
Published by Markus Zimmer in the ''International Journal for Court Administration'' (IJCA), this policy framework analyzes the 600+ page comparative anthology by Jiunn-Rong Yeh and Wen-Chen Chang. The study encompasses 14 Asian judicial systems divided into two groups: advanced economies (Hong Kong, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Taiwan) and rapidly developing economies (Bangladesh, China, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Mongolia, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam). The policy highlights how Asian nations accelerated judicial modernization and established specialized business forums to gain the trust of global investors. Furthermore, the review uncovers the challenges of legal pluralism (the blending of common law, civil law, Sharia, and Hindu Shastra), the fragmentation of forums resulting in a 30-million case backlog in India, and the dynamics of judicial independence versus political indoctrination in China [8, 10, 13–15].

== Legal Basis ==
* '''Act on Basic Provisions of Judicial Power (1964)''': The legal foundation for the establishment of Indonesia's post-colonial national judicial system.
* '''Asian Constitutions''': The official promulgation of the Constitutions of China (1947), Japan (1947), South Korea (1948), India (1950), Singapore (1965), the Philippines (1987), and Mongolia (1992).
* '''Taiwan Fair and Speedy Trial Act (2010)''': Regulations limiting endless cycles of criminal retrials.
* '''Bengal Regulation (1772) & Singapore Constitutional Amendments (1971, 1979, 1993)''': The legal bases for appointing religious advisors in India and Judicial Commissioners in Singapore [10–11].
* '''Not found in the available sources:''' Other specific formal statutory regulations are not mentioned in the source text [FACT].

== Background ==
The economic rise of Asia has driven nations across the continent to restructure their judicial systems. Unlike Western judiciaries that evolved slowly over centuries, Asian judiciaries were shaped rapidly post-decolonization to support global economic growth [2, 6–7].

== Objectives ==
1. Build the trust of the international investment community through specialized commercial, intellectual property, and maritime courts.
2. Fulfill domestic social justice needs through specialized religious, labor, tax, and family courts.
3. Map the interactions between Western colonial law and local customary and religious laws across Asia.

== Scope ==
This policy covers 14 Asian countries/economies situated in East Asia, Southeast Asia, and South Asia.

== Key Provisions ==
* '''Specialization of Business and Social Judicial Forums:'''
** Establishing specialized forums (such as the *Obscene Articles Tribunal* in Hong Kong) to handle highly specific issues [5–6].
* '''Temporary Judge Mechanisms in Singapore:'''
** Appointing *supernumerary judges* and *judicial commissioners* from the ranks of legal practitioners to overcome judge shortages [10–11].
* '''Limitation of Retrials in Taiwan:'''
** Halting endless cycles of appeals and remands through the *Fair and Speedy Trial Act 2010*.
* '''The Pattern of 5-Year Reform Plans in China:'''
** A shift from judicial professionalism (2nd Plan, 2004–2008) toward emphasizing party leadership and social harmony (3rd Plan, 2009) [14–15].

== Implementation ==
* '''Publication of the Anthology (2015):''' The compilation of 14 scientific articles by Jiunn-Rong Yeh and Wen-Chen Chang published by Cambridge University Press [2–4].
* '''Integration of Customary/Religious Law:''' The use of *pandit* and *kazi* advisors within the colonial Indian judicial system up until the 1860s.

== Policy Problems ==
* '''Backlog of 30 Million Cases in India:''' Overlapping jurisdictions across 4 tiers of judicial forums without unifying legislation [11–13].
* '''Politicization of the Judiciary:''' The appointment of a party official without a formal legal background as the Chief Justice in China in 2008 [14–15].

== Reform / Change ==
* Unification of connecting legislation to eliminate overlapping jurisdictions [12–13].
* Restricting the duration of criminal trials to guarantee the right to a speedy trial.

== Relationships with Other Entities ==
* '''National Taiwan University College of Law:''' The home institution of the book's editors (Yeh & Chang).
* '''International Journal for Court Administration (IJCA):''' The publishing journal of the policy review.
* '''[private person]:''' A Law student at Universitas Pembangunan Nasional "Veteran" Jakarta (NIM: 2410611102), specializing in Constitutional Law (Hukum Tata Negara). Cecep Mustafa is not found in the available sources [FACT] [1–16].

'''American Service-Members' Protection Act (ASPA)''' (informally nicknamed ''"The Hague Invasion Act"'') is a United States federal law enacted by the US Congress in August 2002 as an amendment introduced by Senator Jesse Helms to the ''National Defense Authorization Act''. The law was designed to protect US military personnel and government officials from criminal prosecution by the International Criminal Court (ICC), headquartered in The Hague, Netherlands.

== Summary ==
ASPA prohibits all federal, state, and local government bodies (including domestic courts and law enforcement) from cooperating with the ICC. This prohibition covers the extradition of US citizens to the ICC, the transfer of classified intelligence/law enforcement information, and the conduct of investigations by ICC agents on US soil. In addition, ASPA grants the US President special authority to use "all means necessary and appropriate" to free US or allied personnel detained by or at the request of the ICC.

== Legal Basis ==
* '''US Congressional Enactment (August 2002):''' Passed as an amendment introduced by Senator Jesse Helms to the ''National Defense Authorization Act''.
* '''Section 2008 of ASPA:''' Grants executive authority to the US President to authorize action to free US/allied personnel detained at Scheveningen prison, The Hague.
* '''Rome Statute:''' The international treaty establishing the ICC, which the United States has not ratified.

== Background ==
The US government feared that the establishment of the ICC under the Rome Statute could be exploited for politically motivated prosecutions of US soldiers and officials serving abroad. Congress therefore enacted ASPA to shield US personnel from international judicial jurisdiction.

== Objectives ==
1. Protect US military personnel, elected officials, and government officers from ICC criminal jurisdiction.
2. Prevent US domestic law enforcement and courts from cooperating with ICC investigations.
3. Restrict US military aid to ICC member states that have not signed an "Article 98 agreement".

== Scope ==
* '''Cooperation Restrictions:''' Prohibits extradition, transfer of intelligence files, and field investigations by ICC agents within the United States.
* '''Military Aid Restrictions:''' Freezes US military assistance to ICC member states, except for NATO members, major non-NATO allies, Taiwan, or countries that have signed an Article 98 agreement.
* '''Military Authorization ("The Hague Invasion Clause"):''' Grants the US President authority to free US detainees held at Scheveningen prison near The Hague.

== Key Provisions ==
* '''Presidential Waiver Option:''' The US President may waive the military aid ban if deemed essential to US national interests.
* '''Article 98 Agreements:''' Exempts countries that pledge not to surrender US citizens to the ICC from the military aid sanction.

== Policy Problems ==
1. '''Diplomatic Tension with the Netherlands:''' The nickname "The Hague Invasion Act" reflects the potential use of US military force on Dutch sovereign territory (The Hague), conflicting with the Netherlands' international law commitments.
2. '''Obstacle to International Law Enforcement:''' ASPA hampers the ICC, which is supported by 109 nations, in enforcing universal justice.
3. '''Perception of Jurisdictional Imbalance:''' US non-participation risks reinforcing the impression that the ICC targets only developing nations (particularly in Africa).

== Reform / Change ==
* '''Obama Administration Review:''' Under President Barack Obama, foreign policy related to ASPA was placed under review. The Managing Editor of the *International Journal for Court Administration* (Philip M. Langbroek) recommended repealing the law to enhance the ICC's authority and effectiveness without financial burden to the US.

== Relationships with Other Entities ==
* '''US Congress & Senator Jesse Helms:''' Sponsor and drafter of the ASPA legislation.
* '''International Criminal Court (ICC) & Government of the Netherlands:''' Subject of the restrictions and host of the Scheveningen detention facility.
* '''International Journal for Court Administration (IJCA):''' Academic journal (edited by Philip M. Langbroek) that published critical analysis and policy review of ASPA.
* '''Cecep Mustafa & [private person]:''' Not found in the available sources.

'''The Nina Holvast Judicial Assistant and Law Clerk Delegation Framework''' is a judicial administration governance policy framework concerning the delegation of judicial duties to judicial assistants and law clerks. Formulated by Nina Holvast (University of Amsterdam, 2016) in the ''International Journal for Court Administration'' (IJCA), it maps four models of judicial assistants across three jurisdictions (the United States, the Netherlands, and England and Wales). The framework evaluates the impact of organizational structures, terms of office (temporary vs. career), assignment patterns (individual vs. court-wide), and judge types (professional vs. lay judges) on the potential for undue influence in judicial decision-making [1–13].

== Summary ==
Published by Nina Holvast in the ''International Journal for Court Administration'' (IJCA), this policy framework analyzes the vital behind-the-scenes role of judicial assistants in the adjudication process. Holvast evaluates four distinct models of judicial assistants: (1) law clerks in the US Supreme Court and Federal Appellate Courts, (2) judicial staff members/griffiers in Dutch trial courts, (3) magistrates' clerks/court legal advisers in English magistrates' courts, and (4) judicial assistants in the UK Supreme Court and Court of Appeal [12–13]. The study identifies core concerns regarding judgment ghostwriting, monocular perspective filtering, and the erosion of personal judicial responsibility [5–6]. To analyze the risk of undue influence, Holvast formulates six main differentiating factors, including the choice between short-term temporary clerks versus permanent career staff [54–63].

== Legal Basis ==
* '''US Code of Conduct for Federal Judicial Employees & Code of Conduct for Law Clerks of the Supreme Court (1989):''' Ethical regulations and confidentiality guidelines for US federal law clerks.
* '''Dutch Judiciary Organization Act (Wet op de Rechterlijke Organisatie) & Code of Judicial Conduct 2010:''' Regulations concerning confidentiality (Articles 7, 13), oath of office (Article 14), and professional standards for judicial assistants in the Netherlands [27–28].
* '''UK Crime and Disorder Act 1998 & Practice Direction 2000:''' Establishes the pre-trial case management authority of justices' clerks and mandates the delivery of legal advice in open court.
* '''UK Constitutional Reform and Governance Act 2010:''' Recognizes the administrative independence of the UK Supreme Court (including judicial assistants) from ministerial control [48–49].
* '''Not found in the available sources:''' Other specific formal statutory regulations are not mentioned in the source text [FACT].

== Background ==
The caseload crisis since the 1980s forced judicial systems to delegate research and draft preparation tasks to non-judge staff. However, the involvement of assistants in judicial decisions sparked ongoing debates regarding legitimacy and the boundaries of the rule of law.

== Objectives ==
1. Help judges efficiently manage massive caseload backlogs.
2. Maintain the legitimacy and integrity of judgments by limiting assistant-driven undue influence [3, 74–75].
3. Ensure deliberation confidentiality and judicial independence [16, 18, 27–28].

== Scope ==
This policy covers a comparative analysis of apex and trial-level courts in the United States, the Netherlands, and England and Wales [12–13].

== Key Provisions ==
* '''Terms of Office Regulation (Temporary vs. Career):'''
** The use of temporary clerks (1-year terms) as an instrument to curb the accumulation of power versus career clerks possessing deep institutional experience [58–61].
* '''Regulations on Attendance in Judicial Deliberations:'''
** The strict prohibition of law clerks in US Courts of Appeal deliberation rooms versus the mandated presence of assistants in Dutch and English magistrates' courts [31, 65–66].
* '''Assignment Patterns (Individual vs. Court-Wide):'''
** Private individual assignments fostering loyalty to a specific judge versus court-wide assignments supporting consistency across the judiciary [67–71].
* '''Boundaries of Judgment Drafting:'''
** Strict judicial oversight instructions ensuring that judgment texts reflect the official judicial perspective.

== Implementation ==
* '''Application of the US Model:''' Assigning 4 law clerks per Justice in the US Supreme Court for certiorari and bench memos [18–21].
* '''Application of the Dutch Model:''' Assigning griffiers / court secretaries to record court sessions, draft pre-trial memos, and draft judgments [24–33].
* '''Application of the UK Model:''' Assigning 8 judicial assistants in the UK Supreme Court and Court of Appeal for press summaries and petition memos [46, 49–52].

== Policy Problems ==
* '''Judgment Ghostwriting:''' The risk that judges perform only superficial editing on drafts written by inexperienced junior assistants.
* '''Dominance Over Lay Judges:''' The potential for legal advisers to control legal decisions on panels of lay judges lacking formal legal backgrounds [36, 61, 72–73].

== Reform / Change ==
* Formalizing and codifying the roles and limitations of judicial assistants within official judicial regulations.
* Avoiding the direct adoption (cherry-picking) of oversight mechanisms from other jurisdictions without adapting them to local legal traditions.

== Relationships with Other Entities ==
* '''University of Amsterdam:''' The academic institution of Nina Holvast.
* '''International Journal for Court Administration (IJCA):''' The publishing journal for this policy study.
* '''[private person]:''' A Law student at Universitas Pembangunan Nasional "Veteran" Jakarta (NIM: 2410611102), specializing in Constitutional Law, whose academic focus intersects with judicial governance and institutional delegation. Cecep Mustafa is not found in the available sources [FACT] [1–80].

'''The Castelliano, Watanabe & Netto Empirical Impact of Attorneys Policy Framework''' is an empirical judicial policy and civil attorney performance evaluation model formulated by Caio Castelliano de Vasconcelos, Eduardo Watanabe, and Waldir Leôncio Netto in the ''International Journal for Court Administration'' (IJCA), Vol. 9 No. 2 (July 2018). The framework leverages a natural experiment at the Office of the Solicitor General of the Union (SGU - ''Procuradoria-Geral da União'') in Brazil, based on the pure random assignment of cases, to analyze 30,821 judicial decisions handled by 386 Federal Attorneys across 70 specialized teams. It discovers that attorneys significantly influence the win rate in half of the teams (43% at sig < 0.05 and 59% at sig < 0.10) and establishes that there is no statistical correlation between an attorney's experience/seniority and the outcome of civil cases [1–68].

== Summary ==
Published by Caio Castelliano de Vasconcelos, Eduardo Watanabe, and Waldir Leôncio Netto in the IJCA (July 2018), this policy framework fills the severe scarcity of empirical evidence regarding the impact of attorneys in civil litigation. To overcome the methodological hurdle of the case-selection effect (where private attorneys select easy-to-win cases, skewing performance metrics), the study utilizes a natural experiment at the SGU in Brazil, where 30,821 civil cases were assigned purely randomly by an IT system to 386 Federal Attorneys organized into 70 specialized teams. Logistic regression analysis reveals that in approximately half of the teams (43% at sig. < 0.05 and 59% at sig. < 0.10), attorney performance had a statistically significant impact on the win rate, with the maximum odds (Max Odds) of winning varying dramatically—up to 10.98 times higher between attorneys on the same team. Furthermore, Pearson correlation testing proves the absence of a statistical correlation between an attorney's seniority/experience and their civil case win rate, a phenomenon the authors attribute to the trade-off between increasing experience and diminishing workplace motivation over time.

== Legal Basis ==
* '''Brazilian Federal Constitution of 1988:''' The constitutional mandate establishing the ''Advocacia-Geral da União'' (AGU) as the institution responsible for representing the Federal Government.
* '''SGU Internal Regulations & Federal Court IT Random Assignment System:''' The strict internal rules and IT mechanisms that mandate the pure random distribution of civil cases without manual interference from leadership.
* '''Sixth Amendment of the US Constitution (Theoretical Reference):''' The foundational theory regarding the right to legal assistance and fair advocacy representation.
* '''Not found in the available sources:''' Other specific formal statutory regulations are not mentioned in the source text [FACT].

== Background ==
It is highly difficult to isolate a lawyer's pure advocacy skills from the inherent characteristics of a civil case due to the lack of random case assignment in private law firms, leaving the true impact of civil attorneys largely unmeasured in global judicial literature.

== Objectives ==
1. Scientifically isolate and measure the absolute impact of an attorney's work on civil case outcomes by eliminating confounding variables through random assignment.
2. Verify the degree of ''judge sensitivity'' to variations in the quality of civil attorney advocacy.
3. Test the statistical correlation between an attorney's seniority/experience and the case win rate.

== Scope ==
This policy encompasses the empirical evaluation of 30,821 judicial decisions handled by 386 Federal Attorneys within 70 specialized SGU teams across the Federative Republic of Brazil.

== Key Provisions ==
* '''Random Case Assignment Natural Experiment:'''
** Utilizing an IT system's automated random distribution to eliminate confounding variables and the case-selection effect.
* '''Pretreatment Balance Testing (k-means Gap Statistic):'''
** Statistical testing that proved 95.26% of the teams were perfectly homogeneous regarding the distribution of judges, confirming the pure randomness of the sample.
* '''Significant Findings on Judicial Outcomes:'''
** Statistical significance was found in 43% of teams (sig. < 0.05) and 59% of teams (sig. < 0.10), proving that judges are highly sensitive to attorney advocacy in half of all case types.
* '''Independence of Seniority from Case Outcomes:'''
** The lack of a Pearson correlation between attorney seniority and the win rate due to the shifting dynamics of work motivation.

== Implementation ==
* '''SGU Dataset Filtering (2011–2014):''' Processing 93,263 initial defenses down to 30,821 resolved cases to guarantee strict statistical validity.
* '''Application of Logistic Regression Models:''' Calculating the ''goodness of fit'' and the ''Max Odds'' ratio of winning among attorneys within the same specialized team.

== Policy Problems ==
* '''Traditional Case-Selection Bias:''' Private attorneys tend to cherry-pick easily winnable cases, obscuring the measurement of their true pure advocacy skills.
* '''Bureaucratic Reliance on Pure Seniority Criteria:''' Public sector promotion and compensation systems often glorify tenure and seniority without regarding objective performance evidence.

== Reform / Change ==
* Adapting performance-based case assignment processes by allocating the best-performing attorneys to high-value, strategic civil cases.
* Mandating that high-win-rate attorneys share their successful advocacy strategies and defense drafts with their peers to elevate organizational performance.

== Relationships with Other Entities ==
* '''Advocacia-Geral da União (AGU) / SGU:''' The parent institution managing the Federal Attorneys of Brazil.
* '''International Journal for Court Administration (IJCA):''' The academic journal publishing this empirical civil attorney impact study.
* '''National Council of Justice (CNJ Brazil):''' The provider of the ''Justiça em Números'' judicial statistical data.
* '''[private person]:''' A Law student specializing in Constitutional Law (Hukum Tata Negara) at Universitas Pembangunan Nasional "Veteran" Jakarta. The 1988 Brazilian Constitution and the principles of fair advocacy discussed here provide strong comparative frameworks for constitutional studies. Cecep Mustafa is not found in the available sources [FACT] [1–68].

The '''Legal Framework and General Administrative Procedure Model of Austria 1925''' (''Allgemeine Verwaltungsverfahrensgesetz - AVG 1925'') is the first codification of general administrative procedure law in Central Europe. It integrated fifty years of case law from the ''Verwaltungsgerichtshof'' (VwGH) into a package of positive statutes to guarantee citizen participation rights and administrative efficiency <ref>Ferrari Zumbini, A. (2022). The Austrian Model of Administrative Procedure. Origins, Characteristics, Diffusion and the Importance of the Personal Factor. ''Italian Journal of Public Law'', 14(2), 379–397.</ref>.

== Summary ==
Authored and reviewed by [[Angela Ferrari Zumbini]], Associate Professor of Administrative Law at the University of Naples Federico II, this study examines the formation, doctrinal characteristics, and transnational diffusion of AVG 1925 <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), pp. 379, 394–395.</ref>. AVG 1925 codified VwGH jurisprudence developed since 1875, constructing individuals as active subjects of rights (*subjects of rights*) and establishing due process principles (*Rechtsverfahren*) rooted in the nature of things (*Natur der Sache*) <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), pp. 379–384, 388.</ref>.

== Legal Basis ==
This policy framework was enacted through a five-law package on July 21, 1925 (BGBl 274/1925, effective January 1, 1926):
* '''[[Allgemeine Verwaltungsverfahrensgesetz]] (AVG)''': General Administrative Procedure Act <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), pp. 384–385.</ref>.
* '''[[Einführungsgesetz zu den Verwaltungsverfahrensgesetzen]] (EGVG)''': Introductory Act defining application scope and exemptions <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), pp. 384–385.</ref>.
* '''[[Verwaltungsstrafgesetz]] (VSG)''': Administrative Penal Act <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), p. 385.</ref>.
* '''[[Verwaltungsvollstreckungsgesetz]] (VVG)''': Administrative Execution Act <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), p. 385.</ref>.
* '''[[Verwaltungsentlastungsgesetz]] (VEG)''': Act on Administrative Relief and Bureaucratic Workload Reduction <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), p. 385.</ref>.

== Background ==
When the VwGH was established under the Act of October 22, 1875, Austria possessed no general statutory law governing administrative acts <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), pp. 379–380.</ref>. The VwGH utilized its power to annul decisions based on procedural defects to formulate individual protection standards rooted in the nature of things <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), pp. 380–382.</ref>. These judicial principles were systematized by [[Friedrich Tezner]] and incorporated into AVG 1925 to fulfill League of Nations efficiency requirements (*Genfer Reformbeschlüsse 1922*) <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), pp. 381–382, 393–394.</ref>.

== Objectives ==
* Codify VwGH case law into a uniform set of positive statutory rules <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), pp. 384, 388.</ref>.
* Guarantee subjective individual rights protection within public administrative proceedings <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), pp. 385, 388.</ref>.
* Achieve administrative efficiency, speed, simplification, and cost economy (*Zweckmäßigkeit, Raschheit, Einfachheit und Kostenersparnis*) <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), p. 386.</ref>.

== Scope of Application ==
Pursuant to the EGVG, AVG applies to designated public administrative authorities, while excluding taxation, specific public service sectors, and private-law administrative actions (*Privatwirtschaftsverwaltung*) <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), pp. 384–385.</ref>.

== Key Provisions ==
* '''Right to be Heard (Parteiengehör) & Material Truth''': Article 37 AVG defines investigations as tools to uncover material truth (*materielle Wahrheit*) while offering parties a forum to defend legal rights <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), pp. 385–386.</ref>.
* '''Access to Files (Akteneinsicht)''': Article 17 establishes an absolute right for parties to inspect case documents without discretionary refusal <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), p. 391.</ref>.
* '''Decision Timeframes & Administrative Inaction''': Article 73(1) caps decision timelines at 6 months; administrative inertia grants parties an immediate right to hierarchical appeal (Article 73(2)) <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), p. 387.</ref>.
* '''Preference for Oral Proceedings & Speed''': Articles 18 and 40–44 encourage oral hearings and telephonic records to expedite administrative workflow <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), p. 387.</ref>.

== Implementation & Transnational Diffusion ==
The AVG 1925 model was adopted across post-1918 Central European nations through the migration of former VwGH judges and scholars (*personal factor*):
* '''[[Liechtenstein]]''': Transposed AVG draft concepts into the *Landesverwaltungspflegegesetz* (1922) <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), p. 395.</ref>.
* '''[[Poland]]''': Promulgated the Code of Administrative Procedure in 1928 under Polish Supreme Administrative Court President [[Jan Sawicki]] <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), pp. 395–396.</ref>.
* '''[[Czechoslovakia]]''': Formed its Supreme Administrative Court and 1928 procedural code under former VwGH judges [[František Pantůček]] and [[Emil Hácha]] <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), p. 396.</ref>.
* '''[[Yugoslavia]]''': Enacted the General Administrative Procedure Act of 1930 based on VwGH traditions <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), p. 396.</ref>.
* '''[[Italy]]''': Influenced Chamber VI (Temporary) of the Council of State (1919–1923) presided over by [[Guido de Bonfioli Cavalcabò]] <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), pp. 396–397.</ref>.

== Policy Issues & Limitations ==
* '''Marginalization in Comparative Studies''': AVG's archetypal role is frequently neglected in modern Anglo-American comparative law due to the dominance of German doctrine centered on Otto Mayer's concept of administrative act (*Verwaltungsakt*) <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), pp. 394–395.</ref>.
* '''Cassatory Control Limitations''': VwGH was restricted to annulment powers (*cassatory power*) without factual re-evaluation capabilities until the comprehensive judicial reform of 2012 <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), pp. 381–382.</ref>.

== Relations to Other Entities ==
* '''[[Angela Ferrari Zumbini]]''': Author of the underlying academic study <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), pp. 379, 381.</ref>.
* '''[[Verwaltungsgerichtshof]]''': Court that developed the foundational jurisprudence codified in AVG <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), pp. 379–384.</ref>.
* '''[[Friedrich Tezner]]''': Scholar who systematized VwGH jurisprudence <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), pp. 381–382.</ref>.
* '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': ''[[ENTITY IDENTITY UNCERTAIN|Not found in available source materials.]]'' <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), pp. 379–397.</ref>
* '''[[Geovanny Widya Berlianty P]]''': ''[[ENTITY IDENTITY UNCERTAIN|Not found in available source materials.]]'' <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2022), pp. 379–397.</ref>

'''Policy Framework for Concessions Relating to State-Owned Maritime Property Within the Context of Free Movement''' (Italian: ''Kerangka Kebijakan Konsesi Barang Milik Negara Sektor Maritim dalam Konteks Kebebasan Bergerak Eropa'') is an analytical framework of European Union law and Italian administrative law formulated by Prof. Maria Eugenia Bartoloni. It evaluates the legality of automatic extensions (''proroga ex lege'') of concessions of State-owned maritime property for tourism and recreational purposes in light of the landmark ruling of the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) in ''Promoimpresa srl'' (Joined Cases C-458/14 and C-67/15). The study examines two EU law testing parameters (secondary exhaustive harmonisation under the Services Directive 2006/123/EC vs. primary law under Article 49 TFEU) and analyzes the limits of legitimate expectations and Member State discretion <ref>Bartoloni, M.E. (2022). Concessions Relating to State-Owned Maritime Property Within the Context of Free Movement: Reflections on the Promoimpresa Judgment. ''Italian Journal of Public Law'', 14(1), 291–304.</ref>.

== Summary ==
Authored by [[Maria Eugenia Bartoloni]] (Full Professor of European Union Law at University Luigi Vanvitelli), this paper provides an in-depth analysis of EU law criteria regarding the granting of coastal concessions in Italy <ref>Bartoloni (2022), p. 291.</ref>. In the ''Promoimpresa and Melis'' judgment, the CJEU confirmed that the grant of public beach concessions falls under the freedom of establishment pursuant to Article 49 TFEU <ref>Bartoloni (2022), p. 291.</ref>. 

The framework assesses two distinct testing parameters:
# '''Directive 2006/123/EC (Services Directive)''': As secondary harmonised law, Article 12 mandates an impartial and transparent candidate selection procedure where natural resources are scarce <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 296, 298.</ref>.
# '''Article 49 TFEU''': As primary law (''lex generalis''), applicable if the Directive does not apply, requiring a "certain cross-border interest" based on economic value and geographic location <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 299, 300.</ref>.

The study concludes that automatic statutory extensions under Italian national law violate EU law and cannot be justified by claims of legitimate expectations <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 298, 302, 303.</ref>.

== Legal Basis ==
* '''EU Primary Law''':
** ''Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU)'': Article 49 (Freedom of Establishment) <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 291, 292, 302.</ref>; Article 52 (Express Exceptions) <ref>Bartoloni (2022), p. 293.</ref>; Article 56 et seq. (Freedom to Provide Services) <ref>Bartoloni (2022), p. 292.</ref>.
* '''Secondary Law & Harmonisation''':
** ''Directive 2006/123/EC (Services Directive / Bolkestein Directive)'': Articles 9–13, specifically Article 12 (mandatory transparent selection procedure in allocations of scarce natural resources) <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 296, 298.</ref>.
* '''Key CJEU & National Case Law''':
** ''CJEU Joined Cases C-458/14 & C-67/15 Promoimpresa srl & Melis'' (Judgment of 14 July 2016) <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 291, 294.</ref>.
** ''Consiglio di Stato (Adunanza Plenaria Sentenze n. 17 & 18/2021)'' <ref>Bartoloni (2022), p. 291.</ref>.
** ''CJEU Case C-2/74 Reyners'' <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 292, 293.</ref>; ''Case C-120/78 Cassis de Dijon'' <ref>Bartoloni (2022), p. 302.</ref>; ''Case C-593/13 Rina Services'' <ref>Bartoloni (2022), p. 298.</ref>.

== Background ==
For decades, Italian administrative practice for allocating public beach and lake property relied on automatic statutory extensions (''proroga ex lege'') without open tendering <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 291, 298.</ref>. This practice led to protracted legal conflicts with the European Commission because it impeded market entry for operators from other EU Member States and violated internal market principles <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 291, 293, 302.</ref>.

== Objectives ==
1. Eliminate national barriers and discrimination regarding the freedom of establishment in maritime property concessions <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 292, 302.</ref>.
2. Ensure transparency, adequate publicity, and impartial competition in public resource allocations <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 298, 302.</ref>.
3. Clarify the relationship between secondary exhaustive harmonisation (Services Directive) and primary Treaty law <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 294, 299.</ref>.

== Scope ==
The scope covers maritime and lake concessions for tourism and recreational activities in Italy <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 291, 297.</ref>, application of the scarcity of natural resources criterion <ref>Bartoloni (2022), p. 297.</ref>, the doctrines of normative transnationality and certain cross-border interest <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 300, 301.</ref>, and proportionality testing regarding legitimate expectations <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 298, 302, 303.</ref>.

== Key Provisions & Two Testing Parameters ==
1. '''Parameter 1: Secondary Harmonised Rules (Directive 2006/123/EC)''':
* Where resources are scarce, Article 12 mandates transparent competitive selection procedures <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 297, 298.</ref>.
* Because Articles 9–13 constitute exhaustive harmonisation, Member States lose discretion to invoke primary law exceptions (overriding reasons in the public interest) to maintain automatic extensions <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 295, 298, 299.</ref>.
2. '''Parameter 2: Primary Treaty Law (Article 49 TFEU)''':
* Where the Directive does not apply, Article 49 TFEU applies provided there is a "certain cross-border interest" <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 299, 300, 301.</ref>.
* Automatic extensions without transparency constitute de facto discrimination and cannot be justified by incumbent protection or legitimate expectations <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 302, 303.</ref>.

== Implementation & Policy Impact ==
Implementation is executed through the disapplication of non-compliant national statutes by Italian courts and administrative authorities, as affirmed by ''Promoimpresa'' and the Italian Council of State (''Consiglio di Stato Adunanza Plenaria Sentenze n. 17 & 18/2021'') <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 291, 298.</ref>.

== Issues & Policy Challenges ==
1. De facto monopolies restricting market access for non-domestic operators <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 293, 302.</ref>.
2. Repeated legislative resistance enacting automatic extensions (''proroga ex lege'') to protect incumbent concessionaires <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 291, 298, 303.</ref>.

== Legal & Policy Reforms ==
Full enforcement of open public selection procedures where investment protection for incumbent concessionaires may only be considered as part of initial tender evaluation criteria, rather than through automatic extensions <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 298, 303.</ref>.

== Related Entities ==
* '''[[Maria Eugenia Bartoloni]]''': Author & Full Professor of EU Law at University Luigi Vanvitelli <ref>Bartoloni (2022), p. 291.</ref>.
* '''[[Consiglio di Stato]]''': Italian Supreme Administrative Court confirming direct effect of Directive 2006/123/EC <ref>Bartoloni (2022), p. 291.</ref>.
* '''[[Consorzio dei comuni della Sponda Bresciana del Lago di Garda e del Lago di Idro]]''': Public authority involved in the Promoimpresa case <ref>Bartoloni (2022), p. 291.</ref>.
* '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': ''[[ENTITY IDENTITY UNCERTAIN|Not found in available sources.]]'' <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 291–304.</ref>
* '''[[Geovanny Widya Berlianty P]]''': ''[[ENTITY IDENTITY UNCERTAIN|Not found in available sources.]]'' <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 291–304.</ref>

Il '''Quadro di Politica Giuridica sulle Concessioni Demaniali Marittime nel Contesto della Libera Circolazione''' (titolo originale: ''Concessions Relating to State-Owned Maritime Property Within the Context of Free Movement'') è un quadro analitico di diritto dell'Unione Europea e diritto amministrativo italiano formulato dalla Prof.ssa Maria Eugenia Bartoloni. Esso valuta la legittimità delle proroghe automatiche (''proroga ex lege'') delle concessioni di beni demaniali marittimi per finalità turistico-ricreative alla luce della sentenza della Corte di Giustizia dell'Unione Europea (CGUE) nel caso ''Promoimpresa srl'' (Cause riunite C-458/14 e C-67/15). Lo studio esamina due parametri di vaglio del diritto UE (armonizzazione secondaria esaustiva ex Direttiva Servizi 2006/123/CE / Direttiva Bolkestein vs. diritto primario ex Articolo 49 TFUE) ed analizza i limiti della tutela del legittimo affidamento e della discrezionalità degli Stati membri <ref>Bartoloni, M.E. (2022). Concessions Relating to State-Owned Maritime Property Within the Context of Free Movement: Reflections on the Promoimpresa Judgment. ''Italian Journal of Public Law'', 14(1), 291–304.</ref>.

== Sintesi ==
Redatto da [[Maria Eugenia Bartoloni]] (Professoressa Ordinaria di Diritto dell'Unione Europea presso l'Università Luigi Vanvitelli), l'articolo offre un'analisi approfondita dei criteri del diritto UE relativi al rilascio delle concessioni demaniali marittime in Italia <ref>Bartoloni (2022), p. 291.</ref>. Nella sentenza ''Promoimpresa e Melis'', la CGUE ha confermato che il rilascio delle concessioni balneari rientra nell'esercizio della libertà di stabilimento ai sensi dell'Articolo 49 TFUE <ref>Bartoloni (2022), p. 291.</ref>.

L'autrice analizza due distinti parametri di valutazione:
# '''Direttiva 2006/123/CE (Direttiva Servizi)''': In quanto diritto secondario armonizzato, l'Articolo 12 impone una procedura di selezione trasparente ed imparziale tra i candidati qualora la risorsa naturale sia scarsa <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 296, 298.</ref>.
# '''Articolo 49 TFUE''': In quanto diritto primario (''lex generalis''), applicabile qualora la Direttiva non trovi applicazione, il quale richiede la verifica di un "interesse transfrontaliero certo" basato sul valore economico e sulla posizione geografica <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 299, 300.</ref>.

Lo studio conclude che le proroghe automatiche disposte dalla legislazione nazionale italiana violano il diritto dell'UE e non possono essere giustificate da pretese di tutela del legittimo affidamento <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 298, 302, 303.</ref>.

== Basi Giuridiche ==
* '''Diritto Primario dell'Unione Europea''':
** ''Trattato sul Funzionamento dell'Unione Europea (TFUE)'': Articolo 49 (Libertà di stabilimento) <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 291, 292, 302.</ref>; Articolo 52 (Eccezioni espresse) <ref>Bartoloni (2022), p. 293.</ref>; Articolo 56 e ss. (Libera prestazione dei servizi) <ref>Bartoloni (2022), p. 292.</ref>.
* '''Diritto Secondario ed Armonizzazione''':
** ''Direttiva 2006/123/CE (Direttiva Servizi / Direttiva Bolkestein)'': Articoli 9–13, in particolare l'Articolo 12 (procedura di selezione trasparente obbligatoria per l'assegnazione di risorse naturali limitate) <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 296, 298.</ref>.
* '''Giurisprudenza Chiave CGUE e Nazionale''':
** ''CGUE Cause Riunite C-458/14 e C-67/15 Promoimpresa srl & Melis'' (Sentenza del 14 luglio 2016) <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 291, 294.</ref>.
** ''Consiglio di Stato (Adunanza Plenaria Sentenze n. 17 & 18/2021)'' <ref>Bartoloni (2022), p. 291.</ref>.
** ''CGUE C-2/74 Reyners'' <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 292, 293.</ref>; ''C-120/78 Cassis de Dijon'' <ref>Bartoloni (2022), p. 302.</ref>; ''C-593/13 Rina Services'' <ref>Bartoloni (2022), p. 298.</ref>.

== Contesto storico ==
Per decenni, la prassi amministrativa italiana nell'assegnazione delle spiagge pubbliche ha fatto affidamento su proroghe automatiche per legge (''proroga ex lege'') senza procedure ad evidenza pubblica <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 291, 298.</ref>. Tale pratica ha generato contenziosi sistematici con la Commissione Europea, precludendo l'accesso al mercato agli operatori di altri Stati membri e violando i principi del mercato interno <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 291, 293, 302.</ref>.

== Obiettivi ==
1. Eliminare le barriere nazionali e le discriminazioni ostative alla libertà di stabilimento nel settore delle concessioni demaniali marittime <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 292, 302.</ref>.
2. Garantire trasparenza, adeguata pubblicità ed imparzialità nella distribuzione delle risorse pubbliche <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 298, 302.</ref>.
3. Chiarire il rapporto tra armonizzazione secondaria esaustiva (Direttiva Servizi) e diritto primario dei Trattati <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 294, 299.</ref>.

== Ambito di applicazione ==
Lo studio comprende l'analisi delle concessioni marittime e lacustri per finalità turistico-ricreative in Italia <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 291, 297.</ref>, l'applicazione del criterio di scarsità delle risorse naturali <ref>Bartoloni (2022), p. 297.</ref>, i concetti di transnazionalità normativa ed interesse transfrontaliero certo <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 300, 301.</ref>, nonché la valutazione di proporzionalità riguardo al legittimo affidamento <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 298, 302, 303.</ref>.

== Disposizioni Chiave e Due Parametri di Valutazione ==
1. '''Parametro 1: Norme Secondarie Armonizzate (Direttiva 2006/123/CE)''':
* Se le concessioni riguardano risorse naturali scarse, l'Articolo 12 impone una procedura competitiva trasparente <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 297, 298.</ref>.
* Trattandosi di armonizzazione esaustiva, gli Stati membri non possono invocare eccezioni di diritto primario (motivi imperativi di interesse generale) per giustificare proroghe automatiche <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 295, 298, 299.</ref>.
2. '''Parametro 2: Diritto Primario del Trattato (Articolo 49 TFUE)''':
* Laddove la Direttiva non sia applicabile, si applica l'Articolo 49 TFUE purché sussista un "interesse transfrontaliero certo" <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 299, 300, 301.</ref>.
* Le proroghe automatiche prive di trasparenza costituiscono una discriminazione de facto e non possono essere giustificate dalla tutela degli investimenti del concessionario uscente <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 302, 303.</ref>.

== Attuazione ed Impatto ==
L'attuazione avviene tramite la disapplicazione delle norme nazionali incompatibili da parte dei giudici e delle autorità amministrative italiane, in conformità con la sentenza ''Promoimpresa'' e le pronunce del Consiglio di Stato (''Adunanza Plenaria Sentenze n. 17 & 18/2021'') <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 291, 298.</ref>.

== Problematiche e Sfide ==
1. Monopoli de facto e chiusura del mercato per gli operatori esteri <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 293, 302.</ref>.
2. Reiterata resistenza legislativa nazionale volta a rinviare le gare tramite proroghe automatiche (''proroga ex lege'') <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 291, 298, 303.</ref>.

== Riforme Giuridiche e Politiche ==
Piena affermazione dell'obbligo di procedure ad evidenza pubblica, in cui la tutela degli investimenti del concessionario uscente può essere valutata esclusivamente nella formulazione dei criteri di gara iniziali e non tramite proroghe automatiche <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 298, 303.</ref>.

== Entità Correlate ==
* '''[[Maria Eugenia Bartoloni]]''': Autrice e Professoressa Ordinaria di Diritto UE presso l'Università Luigi Vanvitelli <ref>Bartoloni (2022), p. 291.</ref>.
* '''[[Consiglio di Stato]]''': Organo supremo della giustizia amministrativa italiana che ha confermato l'effetto diretto della Direttiva 2006/123/CE <ref>Bartoloni (2022), p. 291.</ref>.
* '''[[Consorzio dei comuni della Sponda Bresciana del Lago di Garda e del Lago di Idro]]''': Ente pubblico coinvolto nella causa Promoimpresa <ref>Bartoloni (2022), p. 291.</ref>.
* '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': ''[[ENTITY IDENTITY UNCERTAIN|Non presente nelle fonti disponibili.]]'' <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 291–304.</ref>
* '''[[Geovanny Widya Berlianty P]]''': ''[[ENTITY IDENTITY UNCERTAIN|Non presente nelle fonti disponibili.]]'' <ref>Bartoloni (2022), pp. 291–304.</ref>
