The '''Latin America Law Reviews on Administrative Law''' (''Tinjauan Hukum Administrasi Amerika Latin'') is a comparative administrative law analytical framework formulated by Silia Gardini in the *Italian Journal of Public Law* (Vol. 13 Issue 2/2021). It examines 14 scientific essays from major Latin American legal journals spanning Chile, Argentina, Cuba, Peru, Colombia, Brazil, Uruguay, Paraguay, and El Salvador. The review analyzes the impact of COVID-19 on public law; emergency regulatory powers (states of exception); methods for legality control of bound and discretionary administrative acts; state patrimonial liability and the culture of anticipation (anticipatory law); regulatory challenges in renewable energy; public contracts governed by private law and contractual nullities; compensation mechanisms in concessions and Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs); urban planning and spatial licensing; functional differentiation between administrative duties and public services; corporate compliance programs for corruption prevention in public procurement; administrative procedure codification based on the Ibero-American Charter; and the financial dynamics of PPP contracts under International Monetary Fund (IMF) conditions.

== Summary ==
Authored by [[Silia Gardini]] (Assistant Professor of Administrative Law at University Magna Graecia Catanzaro), this review provides a comprehensive comparative landscape of contemporary administrative law issues across Latin America. The doctrinal synthesis explores public law adaptations to the COVID-19 pandemic, emergency rulemaking powers in Colombia, judicial scrutiny of administrative discretion in Chile, and the formulation of "anticipatory law" to safeguard public funds. Additionally, the study maps developments in public procurement law, corporate compliance mechanisms to combat corruption in Brazil and Colombia, urban planning permissions, renewable energy transition in Peru, and administrative procedure codifications in Paraguay and El Salvador influenced by Spanish doctrine and CLAD principles.

== Legal Basis ==
* '''Comparative Legal Codifications and Instruments''':
** *Ibero-American Charter of Rights and Obligations of the Citizen in Relation to Innovation in Public Administration (CLAD / XXIII Ibero-American Summit)*.
** *Spanish Administrative Procedure Law (Model of Administrative Procedure)*.
** *Fundamental Right to Good Administration Principle*.
** *Constitutions of Colombia, Cuba (2019), Paraguay, Chile, Argentina, Peru, Uruguay, and Brazil*.
** *Free Trade Agreements, Investment Treaties, and International Human Rights Law*.

== Core Provisions & Key Comparative Issues ==
1. '''Emergency Rules & Scrutiny of Discretion''': Extraordinary emergency rulemaking during public crises must be counterbalanced by rigorous judicial methodologies for inspecting discretionary administrative acts.
2. '''Anticipatory Law & State Liability''': The concept of anticipatory law was developed in Colombia as a conciliation framework designed to mitigate state liability risks and protect public treasuries.
3. '''Corporate Compliance in Procurement''': Implementation of internal self-regulation and corporate compliance programs in Brazil and Colombia serves as an essential requirement to prevent procurement corruption.
4. '''Codification of Administrative Procedure''': Codification efforts in Paraguay and El Salvador integrate principles of legality and rationality derived from Spanish administrative law and the Ibero-American Charter.

Il '''Tinjauan Hukum Administrasi Amerika Latin''' (''Latin America Law Reviews on Administrative Law'') è un quadro analitico di diritto amministrativo comparato formulato da Silia Gardini nell'*Italian Journal of Public Law* (Vol. 13 Issue 2/2021). Esamina 14 saggi scientifici tratti dalle principali riviste giuridiche dell'America Latina (Cile, Argentina, Cuba, Perù, Colombia, Brasile, Uruguay, Paraguay, El Salvador); analizza l'impatto del COVID-19 sul diritto pubblico; i poteri normativi di emergenza (stati di eccezione); i metodi di controllo della legalità sugli atti amministrativi vincolati e discrezionali; la responsabilità patrimoniale dello Stato e la cultura dell'anticipazione (diritto anticipatorio); le sfide regolatorie nelle energie rinnovabili; i contratti pubblici soggetti al diritto privato e le nullità contrattuali; i meccanismi di indennizzo nelle concessioni e nei Partenariati Pubblico-Privati (PPP); le licenze urbanistiche ed edilizie; la differenziazione funzionale tra compiti amministrativi e servizi pubblici; i programmi di conformità aziendale (corporate compliance) per la prevenzione della corruzione negli appalti pubblici; la codificazione del procedimento amministrativo basata sulla Carta Iberoamericana; e le dinamiche finanziarie dei contratti PPP sotto le condizioni del Fondo Monetario Internazionale (FMI).

== Sintesi ==
Redatto da [[Silia Gardini]] (Ricercatrice di Diritto Amministrativo presso l'Università Magna Graecia di Catanzaro), questo studio offre un quadro comparativo sistematico dei temi contemporanei di diritto amministrativo nell'America Latina. Il dibattito dottrinale include l'adattamento del diritto pubblico di fronte alla pandemia di COVID-19, la disciplina dei poteri normativi straordinari in Colombia, il controllo giurisdizionale sulla discrezionalità in Cile, e lo sviluppo del "diritto anticipatorio" per tutelare le risorse pubbliche. Inoltre, la ricerca mappa l'evoluzione della normativa sugli appalti pubblici, l'adozione di programmi di conformità aziendale per contrastare la corruzione in Brasile e Colombia, i titoli abilitativi edilizi, la transizione energetica in Perù, e la codificazione del procedimento amministrativo in Paraguay ed El Salvador influenzata dalla dottrina spagnola e dalla Carta CLAD.

== Base Giuridica ==
* '''Strumenti e Codificazioni Giuridiche Comparate''':
** *Carta Iberoamericana dei Diritti e dei Doveri del Cittadino nei Rapporti con l'Amministrazione Pubblica (CLAD / XXIII Vertice Iberoamericano)*.
** *Legge Spagnola sul Procedimento Amministrativo (Modello Procedimentale)*.
** *Principio del Diritto Fondamentale alla Buona Amministrazione*.
** *Costituzioni di Colombia, Cuba (2019), Paraguay, Cile, Argentina, Perù, Uruguay e Brasile*.
** *Accordi di Libero Scambio, Trattati sugli Investimenti e Diritto Internazionale dei Diritti Umani*.

== Disposizioni Principali e Temi Chiave Comparati ==
1. '''Normazione d'Urgenza e Controllo sulla Discrezionalità''': L'esercizio di poteri normativi straordinari durante le crisi sanitarie deve essere bilanciato da metodologie rigorose di controllo giurisdizionale sulla discrezionalità amministrativa.
2. '''Diritto Anticipatorio e Responsabilità dello Stato''': Il concetto di diritto anticipatorio è stato sviluppato in Colombia come modello di conciliazione preventivo volto a ridurre i rischi di risarcimento del danno a carico del tesoro pubblico.
3. '''Corporate Compliance negli Appalti Pubblici''': L'adozione di programmi interni di autocontrollo e compliance aziendale in Brasile e Colombia costituisce un requisito chiave per prevenire fenomeni corruttivi negli appalti.
4. '''Codificazione del Procedimento Amministrativo''': Le riforme codificatorie in Paraguay ed El Salvador recepiscono i principi di legalità e razionalità derivati dal diritto amministrativo spagnolo e dalla Carta CLAD.

title: Judicial-policy-generative-ai-legal-professions-2024
wikitext:
{{Infobox
| stable_id = judicial-policy-generative-ai-legal-professions-2024
| name = Governance and Impact Framework for Generative AI in the Legal Professions
| type = ICT Governance Policy & Judicial AI Ethics Framework
| issuing_authority = Dr. Francesco Contini (CNR-IRSIG) / IJCA
| legal_basis = EU AI Act; CEPEJ Guidelines 2024; UK Judicial AI Guidance 2023; FBE Guidelines 2023
| date = August 20, 2024
| status = Active Policy Analysis & Comparative Framework
}}

The '''Governance and Impact Framework for Generative AI in the Legal Professions''' (''Unboxing Generative AI for the Legal Professions'') is a policy governance and impact evaluation framework regarding the use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) in judicial administration systems and the legal professions [1, 2, 10–16].

== Summary ==
Published by Dr. Francesco Contini in the ''International Journal for Court Administration'' (2024), this framework analyzes the transformation of the judiciary following the rapid penetration of GenAI since the launch of ChatGPT [1, 6–7]. The policy maps the technical functions of GenAI, evaluates the risks of hallucinations and data confidentiality breaches, and compares two primary regulatory approaches: the bureaucratic/certification approach (''CEPEJ/FBE'') and the professional responsibility and human oversight approach (''Judiciary of England & Wales'') [14–16, 65–70, 87–97, 102–107].

== Legal Basis ==
* '''European Union Artificial Intelligence Act (EU AI Act):''' Classifies LLMs as ''general-purpose AI'' / ''foundation models''.
* '''CEPEJ Guidelines on the Use of Generative AI by Judicial Professionals''' (February 2024) [23, 67, 75–77].
* '''Courts and Tribunals Judiciary AI Guidance for Judicial Office Holders''' (England & Wales, December 2023) [23, 66, 72, 77–79].
* '''European Lawyers in the Era of ChatGPT Guidelines''' (Fédération des Barreaux d’Europe / FBE, June 2023).
* '''Charte pour une utilisation responsable de l'IA générative''' (Predictice, 2023).
* '''Practical Guidance for the Use of Generative AI in the Practice of Law''' (California State Bar, November 2023).
* '''Guidelines for Use of Generative AI in Courts and Tribunals''' (Courts of New Zealand, December 2023).

== Background ==
For over 30 years, legal AI focused on predictive systems (''predictive justice''). However, its development was hindered by the high costs of data cleaning and the limited availability of jurisprudential databases in Europe [3–6]. The emergence of GenAI in November 2022 dramatically disrupted the judicial sector through the availability of public chatbots and direct integration into daily office applications (such as Microsoft 365 Copilot and Google Workspace Gemini) [6–7, 33–34].

== Objectives ==
1. Harness the efficiency of GenAI for document processing and expanding ''access to justice'' [10, 39, 49–52].
2. Prevent judicial risks caused by ''AI hallucinations'' and the submission of fictitious evidence/jurisprudence [15, 19, 60–61, 104].
3. Guarantee data confidentiality, privacy protection, and ''professional secrecy'' [20, 73–78].
4. Reaffirm the principles of ''human oversight'' and personal accountability in court proceedings [2, 15, 85–86, 104–106].

== Scope ==
This governance policy encompasses three levels of analysis [10–13]:
* '''Activity System Level:''' Changes in the practical workflows of judges, lawyers, and ''pro se'' litigants.
* '''Organizational & Judicial Governance Level:''' Implications for self-governing bodies and soft-law regulations.
* '''Economic Level:''' The shift of judicial budgets from local staff to LLM platform license providers (''digital feudalism / techno-feudalism'').

== Key Provisions ==
* '''Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) & Domain Systems:''' The use of RAG architecture and dedicated APIs/GPTs to absorb specific legal knowledge and suppress hallucination rates [25–33, 41–46].
* '''Data Confidentiality & Paid Licenses:''' Prohibition on uploading private data or case files to free public chatbots, and the necessity of contractual clauses forbidding the use of user data for AI model training [20, 26, 73–79].
* '''Output Control & Human Oversight:''' The mandatory requirement for users to verify factual and legal accuracy, as well as the absence of bias, before documents are submitted to the court [15, 81–86, 104–106].

== Implementation ==
* '''Law Firms & Legal Tech:''' Adoption of dedicated systems (such as Lexis+ AI, CoCounsel/Casetext) for summarizing files, drafting contracts, and conducting legal research [38–46].
* '''Public Access to Justice:''' The launch of the ''Guia Prático da Justiça'' (GPJ) chatbot by the Portuguese Ministry of Justice to provide free information on divorce and business registration [51–55].
* '''Judicial Institutions:''' The use of AI by the Spanish Ministry of Justice for document clustering; Italy's development of the National Jurisprudential Database (BDP) abstracts [56–58]; and anecdotal usage by judges in Colombia, India, Pakistan, the UK, and the US [59–64].

== Policy Problems ==
* '''High Hallucination Rates:''' A Stanford University study (Magesh et al., 2024) found that even leading specialized legal AI systems still produce hallucinations at rates of 17% to 33% [47–48, 85].
* '''Divergence in Governance Models:'''
** ''Certification/Authorization Model (CEPEJ/FBE/Predictice):'' Demands pre-use authorization and mandatory disclosure, which risks stifling AI use due to the absence of formal authorizing bodies [91–94, 102].
** ''User Accountability Model (UK Judiciary):'' Emphasizes the personal responsibility of the judge/lawyer for material accuracy without requiring certification or explicit disclosure [91–96, 103–106].
* '''Information Asymmetry & Moral Hazard:''' Inexperienced users or ''pro se'' litigants lack the capacity to verify the accuracy of GenAI outputs, triggering principal-agent problems [86–87, 115–116].

== Reform / Change ==
* Prioritizing the enforcement of ethical and deontological professional obligations (''human empowerment & critical thinking'') over bureaucratic certification.
* Encouraging periodic independent empirical benchmarking regarding the accuracy and hallucination rates of legal GenAI systems.
* Mandating the use of protected licenses (''Enterprise/Paid API'') that guarantee data privacy protection.

== Relationships with Other Entities ==
* '''National Research Council of Italy (CNR-IRSIG):''' Academic affiliation of the lead author (Dr. Francesco Contini).
* '''CEPEJ & Courts and Tribunals Judiciary (UK):''' Publishers of the primary GenAI regulatory guidelines in Europe.
* '''Cecep Mustafa & [private person]:''' Not found in the available sources [1–145].

* [[European Commission for the Efficiency of Justice (CEPEJ)]]

* [[International Journal for Court Administration]]

title: Judicial-policy-german-bvg-recovery-plan-scrutiny-2021
wikitext:
{{Infobox

| name = German Constitutional Court Review of EU Own Resources Decision and Recovery Plan Framework
| type = Constitutional Law Policy & Judicial Review of EU Financial Governance Framework
| issuing_authority = Angela Ferrari Zumbini / University of Naples Federico II / Federal Constitutional Court of Germany / Italian Journal of Public Law
| legal_basis = Basic Law for the Federal Republic of Germany (Arts. 20, 23, 38, 79(3)); BVerfGG § 32; TFEU Arts. 125 & 311; Own Resources Decision 2020/2053; ERatG 2021
| date = 2021 (BVG Decisions 26 March & 15 April 2021; IJPL Vol. 13 Issue 2/2021)
| status = Operational / Applied
}}

'''German Constitutional Court Review of EU Own Resources Decision and Recovery Plan Framework''' (also known as ''BVG Scrutiny of Next Generation EU'') is a judicial policy analysis and constitutional review framework developed by Angela Ferrari Zumbini. It examines the review conducted by the Federal Constitutional Court of Germany (*Bundesverfassungsgericht* / BVG) regarding the German Ratification Act (*ERatG*) of the European Union Own Resources Decision (EU Own Resources Decision 2020/2053) and the post-COVID-19 Next Generation EU (NGEU) Recovery Program. The framework addresses ultra-vires disputes, constitutional identity control (*Identitätskontrolle*), the budgetary sovereignty of the Bundestag, and historical lessons drawn from the League of Nations loan to Austria (1922) <ref>Ferrari Zumbini, A. (2021). The Recovery Plan Under the Scrutiny of the German Constitutional Court: Institutional Implications and a Lesson from the Past. ''Italian Journal of Public Law'', 13(2), 392–415.</ref>.

== Overview ==
Authored by [[Angela Ferrari Zumbini]], Associate Professor of Administrative Law at the [[University of Naples Federico II]], this study analyzes the interim orders issued by the Federal Constitutional Court of Germany (*BVG*) on 26 March and 15 April 2021 concerning the scrutiny of the Own Resources Ratification Act (*ERatG*) <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 392, 393, 399, 401.</ref>. The analysis highlights two primary institutional tensions: internal institutional friction between the BVG and the Bundestag (which had passed the Ratification Act by a majority exceeding 74%), and supranational jurisdictional friction between the BVG and the Court of Justice of the European Union (*CJEU*) concerning the doctrine of *ultra-vires* review <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 392, 393–394, 405–407.</ref>.

== Legal Basis ==
The policy and analytical framework is anchored in both German national constitutional law and European Union treaty law:
* '''[[Basic Law for the Federal Republic of Germany]] (GG)''': Principles of democracy and popular sovereignty (Art. 20(1)&(2), Art. 38(1)), European integration clause (Art. 23(1)), and the eternity clause protecting constitutional identity (Art. 79(3)) <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 398–399, 402–403.</ref>.
* '''[[Federal Constitutional Court Act]] (BVerfGG)''': Provisions governing interim injunctions (§ 32) and enforcement orders (§ 35) <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 395, 399–400.</ref>.
* '''[[Eigenmittelbeschluss-Ratifizierungsgesetz]] (ERatG)''': The German Ratification Act (2021) for the EU Own Resources Decision <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), p. 398.</ref>.
* '''[[EU Own Resources Decision 2020/2053]] & TFEU''': Council Decision of 14 December 2020 alongside Article 125 (no bail-out clause) and Article 311 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 396–397, 399.</ref>.
* '''[[Geneva Protocols 1922]] & [[AVG 1925]]''': International protocols governing the League of Nations financial reconstruction of Austria and the Austrian General Administrative Procedure Act 1925 <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 413–414.</ref>.

== Background & Constitutional Dispute ==
Following the European Council's agreement on the €750 billion Next Generation EU (NGEU) recovery program in July 2020, Germany enacted the ERatG in March 2021 <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 396–398.</ref>. A group of 2,281 German citizens under the *Bündnis Bürgerwille* initiative (led by [[Bernd Lucke]]) filed a constitutional complaint (*Verfassungsbeschwerde*) and an application for an emergency injunction, alleging that EU joint debt issuance violates the budgetary sovereignty of the Bundestag and breaches the no-bailout rule in Art. 125 TFEU <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 398–399.</ref>.

== Objectives ==
* Scrutinize the constitutional boundaries of transferring financial authority to European Union institutions <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 398, 402–403.</ref>.
* Prevent the erosion of the national parliament's budgetary responsibility (*Budgetverantwortung* of the Bundestag) <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 398, 403.</ref>.
* Provide a historical comparative perspective from the 1922 League of Nations financial assistance to Austria regarding administrative reform and good debt management <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 412–415.</ref>.

== Scope ==
The framework encompasses German constitutional law, EU financial governance, supranational judicial relations (BVG vs CJEU), and comparative administrative history <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 392–415.</ref>.

== Key Decisions & Judicial Findings ==
* '''Rejection of Injunction (Order of 15 April 2021)''': The Second Senate of the BVG rejected the application for a preliminary injunction halting ERatG enactment because the constitutional complaint was not "manifestly well-founded" or shown to have a high probability of unconstitutionality, prompting a balancing of consequences (*Folgenabwägung*) <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 401, 404.</ref>.
* '''Weighing of Consequences''': Delaying ratification by 2 to 3 years would cause irreversible economic damage to the EU and recipient states like Italy, whereas financial risks to Germany remained limited and contingent <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), p. 404.</ref>.
* '''Reservation of Ultra-Vires Control''': The Court reasserted its competence to conduct *ultra-vires* review and *Identitätskontrolle* if EU actions exceed treaty mandates <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 403, 405.</ref>.

== Historical Comparative Analysis: Austrian Reconstruction (1922) ==
To ensure the long-term viability of debt-funded recovery schemes, Zumbini highlights the post-WWI reconstruction of Austria via the Geneva Protocols (*Genfer Reformbeschlüsse*, 4 October 1922) <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 412–413.</ref>. International loans were linked to structural administrative reforms, resulting in the enactment of the *Allgemeine Verwaltuntamientoverfahrensgesetz* (AVG 1925)—the world's first codified administrative procedure act—which transformed financial assistance into "good debt" through institutional modernization <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 411, 413–414.</ref>.

== Institutional and Policy Issues ==
* '''Internal Friction''': The review by the BVG of an act passed with over 74% parliamentary approval creates institutional friction with the legislature <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), p. 406.</ref>.
* '''Infringement Proceedings''': The European Commission launched an infringement procedure against Germany on 9 June 2021 following the BVG's *ultra-vires* stance in the 2020 PSPP judgment <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), p. 408.</ref>.

== Entity Relationships ==
* '''[[Angela Ferrari Zumbini]]''': Author of the study, Associate Professor of Administrative Law <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), p. 392.</ref>.

Il '''Quadro di Controllo di Costituzionalità della Corte Costituzionale Tedesca sul Piano di Ripresa dell'UE e sulle Risorse Proprie''' (in inglese ''German Constitutional Court Review of EU Own Resources Decision and Recovery Plan Framework / BVG Scrutiny of Next Generation EU'') è un quadro di analisi delle politiche giudiziarie e di controllo di costituzionalità sviluppato da Angela Ferrari Zumbini. Esso esamina il vaglio della Corte Costituzionale Federale Tedesca (*Bundesverfassungsgericht* / BVG) sulla Legge di Ratifica tedesca (*ERatG*) relativa alla Decisione sulle Risorse Proprie dell'Unione Europea (Decisione UE/Euratom 2020/2053) e sul programma di ripresa *Next Generation EU* (NGEU) post-COVID-19, comprendendo controversie di *ultra-vires*, controllo dell'identità costituzionale (*Identitätskontrolle*), sovranità di bilancio del Bundestag e lezioni storiche derivanti dal prestito della Società delle Nazioni all'Austria (1922) <ref>Ferrari Zumbini, A. (2021). The Recovery Plan Under the Scrutiny of the German Constitutional Court: Institutional Implications and a Lesson from the Past. ''Italian Journal of Public Law'', 13(2), 392–415.</ref>.

== Sintesi ==
Scritto da [[Angela Ferrari Zumbini]], Rettrice/Professoressa Associata di Diritto Amministrativo presso l'[[Università degli Studi di Napoli Federico II]], lo studio analizza le ordinanze cautelari della Corte Costituzionale Federale Tedesca (*BVG*) del 26 marzo e del 15 aprile 2021 relative al controllo sulla Legge di Ratifica della Decisione sulle Risorse Proprie UE (*ERatG*) <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 392, 393, 399, 401.</ref>. L'analisi evidenzia due principali tensioni istituzionali: il conflitto istituzionale interno tra il BVG e il Bundestag (che aveva approvato la legge di ratifica a maggioranza superiore al 74%), e il conflitto giurisdizionale sovranazionale tra il BVG e la Corte di Giustizia dell'Unione Europea (*CGUE*) riguardo alla dottrina del controllo *ultra-vires* <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 392, 393–394, 405–407.</ref>.

== Basi Giuridiche ==
Il quadro analitico si fonda sul diritto costituzionale tedesco e sul diritto dell'Unione Europea:
* '''[[Legge Fondamentale della Repubblica Federale di Germania]] (GG)''': Principi di democrazia e sovranità popolare (Art. 20(1)&(2), Art. 38(1)), clausola di integrazione europea (Art. 23(1)), e clausola di eternità a tutela dell'identità costituzionale (Art. 79(3)) <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 398–399, 402–403.</ref>.
* '''[[Legge sulla Corte Costituzionale Federale]] (BVerfGG)''': Disposizioni sulle ordinanze provvisorie e cautelari (§ 32) e regolamentazione dell'esecuzione (§ 35) <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 395, 399–400.</ref>.
* '''[[Eigenmittelbeschluss-Ratifizierungsgesetz]] (ERatG)''': Legge tedesca di ratifica del 2021 della Decisione sulle Risorse Proprie dell'UE <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), p. 398.</ref>.
* '''[[Decisione Risorse Proprie UE 2020/2053]] & TFUE''': Decisione del Consiglio del 14 dicembre 2020 unitamente all'Articolo 125 (divieto di salvataggio finanziario) e all'Articolo 311 del Trattato sul Funzionamento dell'Unione Europea <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 396–397, 399.</ref>.
* '''[[Protocolli di Ginevra 1922]] & [[AVG 1925]]''': Accordi internazionali per la ricostruzione finanziaria dell'Austria e Legge generale sul procedimento amministrativo austriaco del 1925 <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 413–414.</ref>.

== Contesto e Controversia Costituzionale ==
In seguito all'accordo del Consiglio Europeo del luglio 2020 sul piano di ripresa *Next Generation EU* da 750 miliardi di euro, la Germania ha approvato l'ERatG nel marzo 2021 <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 396–398.</ref>. Un gruppo di 2.281 cittadini tedeschi guidati dall'organizzazione *Bündnis Bürgerwille* (guidata da [[Bernd Lucke]]) ha promosso un ricorso di costituzionalità (*Verfassungsbeschwerde*) e un'istanza cautelare, sostenendo che l'emissione di debito comune UE violi la sovranità di bilancio del Bundestag e il divieto di *bail-out* ex Art. 125 TFUE <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 398–399.</ref>.

== Obiettivi ==
* Esaminare i limiti costituzionali al trasferimento di competenze finanziarie alle istituzioni dell'Unione Europea <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 398, 402–403.</ref>.
* Prevenire l'erosione della responsabilità di bilancio del parlamento nazionale (*Budgetverantwortung* del Bundestag) <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 398, 403.</ref>.
* Offrire una prospettiva storica comparata basata sul sostegno finanziario della Società delle Nazioni all'Austria del 1922 in materia di riforme amministrative e gestione del debito <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 412–415.</ref>.

== Ambito di Applicazione ==
L'ambito comprende il diritto costituzionale tedesco, la governance finanziaria dell'UE, i rapporti giurisdizionali sovranazionali (BVG vs CGUE) e la storia del diritto amministrativo comparato <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 392–415.</ref>.

== Decisioni Chiave e Valutazioni del BVG ==
* '''Rigetto dell'Ingiunzione Cautelare (Ordinanza del 15 aprile 2021)''': Il Secondo Senato del BVG ha respinto la richiesta di sospensione cautelare della promulgazione dell'ERatG poiché il ricorso principale non presentava un'alta probabilità di fondatezza costituzionale, procedendo quindi a una ponderazione delle conseguenze (*Folgenabwägung*) <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 401, 404.</ref>.
* '''Ponderazione delle Conseguenze''': Un ritardo di 2 o 3 anni nella ratifica avrebbe causato danni economici irreversibili per l'UE e per stati beneficiari come l'Italia, mentre i rischi finanziari per la Germania sono stati ritenuti limitati e differiti nel tempo <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), p. 404.</ref>.
* '''Riserva di Controllo Ultra-Vires''': Il BVG ha riaffermato la propria competenza a esercitare il controllo *ultra-vires* e l'*Identitätskontrolle* qualora le decisioni dell'UE eccedano i mandati dei Trattati <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 403, 405.</ref>.

== Analisi Storica Comparata: La Ricostruzione dell'Austria (1922) ==
Per garantire la sostenibilità del debito legato alla ripresa, Zumbini evidenzia il caso della ricostruzione dell'Austria del primo dopoguerra tramite i Protocolli di Ginevra (*Genfer Reformbeschlüsse*, 4 ottobre 1922) <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 412–413.</ref>. I prestiti internazionali furono vincolati a riforme burocratiche strutturali, culminando nell'approvazione della *Allgemeine Verwaltungsverfahrensgesetz* (AVG 1925)—la prima legge generale sul procedimento amministrativo al mondo—trasformando il debito in "debito buono" attraverso la modernizzazione istituzionale <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 411, 413–414.</ref>.

== Questioni Istituzionali e Politiche ==
* '''Frizione Interna''': Il controllo del BVG su un atto approvato a maggioranza qualificata dal Bundestag (>74%) crea tensioni istituzionali tra potere giudiziario e legislativo <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), p. 406.</ref>.
* '''Procedura di Infrazione''': La Commissione Europea ha avviato una procedura di infrazione contro la Germania il 9 giugno 2021 a seguito della posizione assunta dal BVG sul controllo *ultra-vires* nella sentenza PSPP del 2020 <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), p. 408.</ref>.

== Relazioni tra Entità ==
* '''[[Angela Ferrari Zumbini]]''': Autrice dello studio, Professoressa Associata di Diritto Amministrativo <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), p. 392.</ref>.
* '''[[Corte Costituzionale Federale Tedesca]]''': Autorità giudiziaria competente per la valutazione della costituzionalità dell'ERatG <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 393, 401.</ref>.
* '''[[Bundestag]]''': Parlamento Federale Tedesco titolare della sovranità di bilancio <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 394, 398, 406.</ref>.
* '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': ''[[ENTITY IDENTITY UNCERTAIN|Non trovato nelle fonti disponibili.]]'' <ref>Ferrari Zumbini (2021), pp. 392–415.</ref>

title: Judicial-policy-germann-vaa-2025
wikitext:
{{Infobox | stable_id = judicial-policy-germann-vaa-2025 | name = Improving issue representation with candidate-level voting advice applications | type = Comparative Political Science Research Paper & VAA Field Experiment | issuing_authority = Micha Germann et al. / University of Bath / EJPR | legal_basis = Not found in the available sources. | date = 2025 | status = Published / Active }}
'''Improving issue representation with candidate-level voting advice applications''' is an empirical comparative political science research paper authored by Micha Germann (University of Bath), Fernando Mendez (University of Zurich), Jonathan Wheatley (Oxford Brookes University), Constantinos Djouvas (Cyprus University of Technology), Roula Nezi (University of Surrey), and Matthew Wall (Swansea University), published in the ''European Journal of Political Research'' (EJPR) in 2025.
== Summary == This study tests whether candidate-level Voting Advice Applications (VAAs) — which match voters' preferences directly with individual candidates — improve issue representation and policy congruence compared to standard party-level VAAs. Through a randomized field experiment embedded in the MyVoteChoice app during the 2021 Welsh Senedd election (N > 6,500), the study demonstrates that candidate-level VAA recommendations significantly increase both propensity to vote (PTV) and vote intention for the policy-congruent candidate.
== Legal Basis ==
'''Not found in the available sources:''' This document is an academic political science research study and is not based on any specific statutory or judicial legislative instrument [1–70].
'''Welsh Senedd Electoral System (Additional Member System):''' Wales's mixed electoral system, combining 40 First-Past-The-Post constituency seats and 20 regional closed party-list seats.
== Background == Candidate-based electoral systems (such as open-list proportional representation, single transferable vote, or mixed-member systems) have grown increasingly common. However, individual candidates often hold views that diverge from their official party line. Voters frequently struggle to obtain information on individual candidates' policy positions, meaning their votes often fail to reflect their true policy preferences.
== Objectives ==
Test the hypothesis (H): Exposure to candidate-level VAA advice increases policy congruence between candidates and voters' preferences compared to party-level VAA advice.
Determine whether the effect of candidate-level VAAs is driven by substantive policy differences or merely by visual display cues (candidate photos and names).
Assess whether the issue-representation benefits of candidate-level VAAs justify their higher operational cost and complexity.
== Scope == The research consists of a randomized field experiment among voters in the 2021 Welsh Senedd election, using the MyVoteChoice app, which covered 28 policy-issue statements.
== Key Provisions / Findings ==
'''Correlation Between Party and Candidate Advice:''' The correlation between candidate rankings and party rankings was high overall (r = 0.90; r = 0.73 for candidates who took the survey). However, for 30% of voters, the top-ranked candidate differed from the top-ranked party.
'''Increase in Propensity to Vote (PTV):''' Exposure to candidate-level VAA advice increased PTV for the top-matched candidate by '''+0.25 points''' on a 0–10 scale (p < 0.05) compared to party-level advice.
'''Role of Substantive Policy Differences:''' Among candidates who completed the survey (whose positions diverged from party lines), the effect doubled to '''+0.50 points''' (p < 0.001). For non-participating candidates (whose positions defaulted to the party line), the visual display alone produced no significant effect.
'''Increase in Vote Intention:''' Candidate-level VAA advice increased the probability of intending to vote for the top-matched candidate by '''+3 percentage points''' overall (from 60% to 63%, p < 0.05), and by '''+6 percentage points''' (p < 0.01) for candidates who participated in the survey.
'''Candidate Survey Participation Rate:''' The Welsh election recorded a candidate participation rate of 28%, far below Switzerland's smartvote, which achieves 75–85% thanks to a longer institutional tradition and precedent.
== Implementation == The methodology was implemented through linear regression models with candidate fixed effects, standard errors clustered at the user level, and demographic control testing. Replication data and code are stored openly on Harvard Dataverse at https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/47XXEN.
== Policy Issues ==
The high logistical and labor costs of building candidate-level VAAs (contacting candidates, collecting photos/bios, district-specific programming).
Low candidate response rates to pre-election policy surveys in countries lacking a strong VAA tradition.
== Reform / Implications == The study provides experimental evidence that candidate-level VAAs deliver substantive added value in strengthening issue representation within candidate-based electoral democracies.

'''University of Bath, University of Zurich & Oxford Brookes University:''' Home institutions of the authors.
'''European Consortium for Political Research (ECPR):''' Publisher of the EJPR journal.
'''British Academy & UK ESRC:''' Research funding agencies.
'''Harvard Dataverse:''' Repository hosting replication data.
'''Cecep Mustafa:''' Not found in the available sources [1–70].
'''[private person]:''' Not found in the available sources [1–70].

'''A new regime divide? Democratic backsliding, attitudes towards democracy and affective polarization''' is an empirical comparative political science research paper authored by Theresa Gessler (European University Viadrina) and Natasha Wunsch (University of Fribourg), published in the ''European Journal of Political Research'' (EJPR) in 2025.

== Summary ==
This study tests the reverse relationship between democratic backsliding and affective polarization [1, 4, 15–16]. Unlike conventional literature, which treats affective polarization purely as a driver of democratic backsliding, this study demonstrates that prolonged democratic erosion by a government can itself generate a new "regime divide" built around liberal democratic values [1, 5, 19–20, 80]. This divide unites ideologically diverse opposition voters and parties in joint mobilization to defend democracy [1, 6, 67, 80–81].

== Legal Basis ==
* '''Not found in the available sources:''' This document is an academic political science research study and is not based on any specific statutory or judicial legislative instrument [1–119].
* '''2012 Hungarian Constitutional & Electoral Reform:''' Changes to electoral rules enacted by the Fidesz government that strengthened the majoritarian system and reshaped party competition structures.

== Background ==
Earlier studies emphasized that affective polarization increases voters' tolerance for democratic violations committed by their own party's leaders. However, in contexts of prolonged democratic backsliding — such as under Fidesz rule in Hungary since 2010 — commitment to liberal democracy itself becomes a central axis dividing society between government supporters and opposition supporters [1, 7, 19–20, 42].

== Objectives ==
1. Test for the existence of a government-versus-opposition divide in evaluations of party supporters (Hypothesis 1) [23–24, 48, 52].
2. Analyze how commitment to liberal democracy shapes negative evaluations of ruling-party supporters and positive evaluations of opposition supporters (Hypotheses 2a/2b) [27–28, 54, 57].
3. Test the moderating effect of vote intention on the relationship between democratic attitudes and affective polarization (Hypothesis 3) [29–32, 58, 62].

== Scope ==
The research's primary comparative analysis is conducted in Hungary using an original survey (N = 2,000) fielded by Inquiry/YouGov (December 2021 – January 2022), supplemented by secondary analysis in Poland [1, 7, 33–34, 74].

== Key Provisions / Findings ==
* '''Hypothesis 1 Supported (Government–Opposition Divide):''' Opposition supporters rate ruling-party (Fidesz) supporters 3 points lower than the population average on a 0–10 scale (over 50% select the extreme dislike option), while rating all opposition parties significantly more positively [48, 50–52].
* '''Hypotheses 2a/2b Supported (Democracy Divide):''' Liberal democratic commitment is significantly negatively associated with evaluations of Fidesz supporters (b = -0.27, p < 0.001) and positively associated with evaluations of opposition-party supporters (Momentum b = 0.34; Dialogue b = 0.23; LMP b = 0.23; DK b = 0.16).
* '''Exception — Jobbik:''' The democracy-attitude effect is non-significant for the far-right Jobbik party, confirming that parties with questionable democratic commitment are excluded from the democratic in-group.
* '''Hypothesis 3 Supported (Partisan Moderation):''' The positive effect of liberal democratic attitudes on solidarity with opposition supporters is driven specifically by opposition voters; Fidesz voters' evaluations are unaffected by liberal democratic attitudes [58–62].
* '''Role of Backsliding Duration:''' The regime divide reaches full maturity in Hungary after 12+ years of Fidesz rule, producing a single joint 106-district opposition coalition in the 2022 election [66–69, 77, 79], whereas in Poland the process was still developing.

== Implementation ==
The methodology was implemented through OLS linear regression models with interaction terms, demographic and ideological controls, and questionnaire robustness testing [36–38, 50, 53, 56]. The pre-analysis plan is publicly pre-registered on OSF (`https://osf.io/a8utq/`).

== Policy Issues ==
1. Systematic democratic backsliding through the erosion of judicial independence, media freedom, and electoral integrity.
2. Ideological fragmentation that frequently prevents opposition parties from consolidating against an autocratizing incumbent [5, 21–22, 45].

== Reform / Implications ==
The study offers a new, positive perspective on affective polarization, showing that polarization organized around democratic values can function as a bulwark defending democratic institutions [1, 4, 6, 80–81].

| type = Judicial Quality Management Standard & Public Accreditation System
| issuing_authority = Supreme Court of Costa Rica & SINCA-Justicia

'''GICA-Justicia Project''' (and its main product: ''Norma GICA-Justicia 2010: Organización del Despacho Judicial'') is the world's first tailor-made, ISO-9000-like quality management standard and judicial accreditation system specifically designed for judicial environments in Costa Rica. This initiative was developed by the Supreme Court of Costa Rica (''Poder Judicial'') between 2009 and 2010, and scientifically analyzed by Rodrigo Murillo (Bradford School of Management) and Roy Zuniga (INCAE Business School) in the article titled ''"Could Innovation also Emerge from the Public Sector? Creating an ISO-like Judiciary Quality Management Standard"'' published in the ''International Journal for Court Administration'' (IJCA, Vol. 5, No. 2, October 2013).

== Summary ==
The GICA-Justicia Project responded to high public dissatisfaction (reaching 85%) regarding slow judicial services and case backlogs in Costa Rica. The project produced two main instruments: the '''GICA-Justicia Quality Management Model''' (''GJP-Model'') and the '''GICA-Justicia Quality Management Standard''' (''GJP-Standard'' / ''Norma GICA-Justicia 2010''). Unlike international quality models such as RechtspraaQ (Netherlands), IFCE, or CEPEJ which are based on self-assessment, GICA-Justicia adopts an independent third-party accreditation model through the national body ''SINCA-Justicia''.

== Legal Basis ==
* '''Supreme Court Resolution (2009):''' Official decision to launch the GICA-Justicia Project to fill the gap in judicial quality standards.
* '''National Accreditation Bill of 2010:''' Signed by the President of Costa Rica, the State Minister, and the Minister of Justice to establish the independent accreditation body ''SINCA-Justicia'' (''Sistema Nacional de Acreditación y Calidad para la Justicia'').
* '''Organic Law of the Judiciary (''Ley Orgánica del Poder Judicial''):''' Statutory foundation defining the jurisdiction, structure, and administrative competencies of the courts in Costa Rica.

== Background & Policy Problems ==
1. '''Incompatibility of Generic ISO 9001:''' Standard ISO 9001 guidelines do not integrate technical judicial jargon or specific provisions such as vulnerable group protection and alternative dispute resolution.
2. '''Lack of Third-Party Accreditation:''' Most global judicial quality models lack an independent assessment mechanism from a legitimized national accreditation body.
3. '''High Citizen Dissatisfaction (85%):''' National survey results based on an adapted ServQual tool indicated that the public's main complaints pertained to service delivery speed, missed time promises, and the lack of accurate case conclusion reporting [10, 11, 69–71].

== Main Components of the GICA-Justicia Model & Standard ==

=== 1. GICA-Justicia Quality Management Model (GJP-Model) ===
* '''3 Mainstays:''' Public policies in service management, User rights, and Integral system approach.
* '''3 Crosscutting Axes:''' User satisfaction, Organizational commitment, and Good management practices.
* '''3 Continuous Improvement Phases:''' Phase 1 (Redesign), Phase 2 (Accreditation), and Phase 3 (Repeatability/Replication) [75–83].

=== 2. GICA-Justicia Quality Management Standard (Norma GICA-Justicia 2010) ===
Consists of 5 Main Chapters [12–15]:
1. '''QMS Organization:''' Basic QMS principles and transversal guidelines on gender equality, vulnerable populations' accessibility, transparency, ethics, citizen participation, and environmental management.
2. '''Documentation & Communication Management:''' Document hierarchy, version control, and user feedback channels.
3. '''Resources' Management:''' Management of facilities, IT services, and judicial human resource competencies.
4. '''Judicial Process Realization:''' A 4-step process delivery approach (Inputs, Appearances, Resolutions, Outputs) and 4 ancillary activities (Time management, Case/document management, Supportive activities, Alternative Dispute Resolution) [14, 84–87].
5. '''Performance Appraisal & QMS Improvement:''' Performance indicators, internal auditing, non-conformity management, and user satisfaction measurement.

== Accreditation Mechanism & Implementing Agencies ==
* '''SINCA-Justicia:''' An independent national third-party accreditation body consisting of 7 cross-sectoral institutions. It utilizes a weighted scoring scale with an '''80%''' minimum compliance threshold.
* '''CEGECA (''Centro de Gestión de la Calidad''):''' The internal quality management office of the judiciary tasked with coordinating training, pre-audits, and standard replication across district courts.
* '''Pilot Court Results:'''
** ''Juzgado de Violencia Doméstica de Heredia (Domestic Aggression Court):'' Achieved 1,423 / 1,500 points ('''95% compliance''').
** ''Tribunal de Apelación de la Sentencia (Second Court of Appeal):'' Achieved 1,215 / 1,500 points ('''81% compliance''').

== Evaluation Results & Real-World Impacts ==
* '''Case Backlog Drainage:''' Within 6 months after deploying the GJP-Standard, the Second Court of Appeal successfully reduced its case backlog from ~650 cases to '''200 cases''' (its target average).
* '''Systemic Discipline:''' The establishment of written performance indicators, daily work quotas, and official documented procedures.

== Policy Problems & Limitations ==
1. '''Lack of Cost-of-Quality Metrics:''' The standard does not measure the financial cost of processes, meaning a court can be highly effective but financially inefficient.
2. '''Absence of a Public Trust Chapter:''' Unlike the IFCE, the GJP-Standard does not have a dedicated chapter directly measuring public trust.

== Relationships with Other Entities ==
* '''Poder Judicial de Costa Rica, SINCA-Justicia, & CEGECA:''' Developing, accrediting, and managing institutions of judicial quality in Costa Rica.
* '''Cecep Mustafa & [private person]:''' Not found in the available sources [1–89].

'''Policy Framework on EU Regulation of Crypto-Assets and Payment Tokens''' (''Payment Tokens and the Path Towards MiCA'') is a legal policy analysis framework on European Union money and payments law formulated by Gabriella Gimigliano in ''The Italian Law Journal'' (Vol. 08 No. 01/2022, pp. 353–374) <ref>Gimigliano, G. (2022). Payment Tokens and the Path Towards MiCA. ''The Italian Law Journal'', 8(1), 353–374.</ref>. It evaluates the Proposal for Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA Proposal - COM/2020/593 final) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 353, 355.</ref>, assesses token classifications (payment tokens, utility tokens, asset tokens, and hybrid tokens) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 357, 358.</ref>, and examines specific categories including asset-referenced tokens (ART) and electronic money tokens (EMT) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 358, 366.</ref>. Furthermore, it dissects the crypto-asset white paper disclosure requirements (similar to the prospectus regime under Regulation (EU) 2017/1129) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 365.</ref>, evaluates the licensing and supervisory regimes for token issuers and Crypto-Asset Service Providers (CASPs) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 370, 373.</ref>, and addresses MiCA’s limitations concerning Decentralized Finance (DeFi), algorithmic tokens, Decentralised Autonomous Organizations (DAOs), as well as coordination with PSD2 (Directive (EU) 2015/2366) and the E-Money Directive (Directive 2009/110/EC) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 358, 367, 374.</ref>.

== Summary ==
Authored by [[Gabriella Gimigliano]] (PhD, Jean Monnet Chairholder in EU Money Law, and Senior Researcher at the University of Siena), this study analyzes the transition toward regulating payment tokens within EU monetary law <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 353.</ref>. The author analyzes the MiCA Proposal submitted by the European Commission under Article 114 TFEU to ensure internal market harmonization <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 355, 361.</ref>. The article breaks down token categorization criteria, differentiating utility tokens, asset-referenced tokens (ART), and e-money tokens (EMT) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 358.</ref>. Gimigliano examines the strict white paper obligations designed to inform prospective investors <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 365.</ref>, the prohibition of interest on ART and EMT holdings to protect their payment functionality <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 368.</ref>, and the direct supervisory role assigned to the European Banking Authority (EBA) for significant token issuers <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 372.</ref>.

== Legal Basis ==
* '''Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU)''':
** ''Article 114 TFEU'' (Internal Market Harmonization) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 361.</ref>.
** ''Article 128(1) TFEU'' (Legal Tender Status of Euro Banknotes) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 369.</ref>.
* '''EU Regulations & Directives''':
** ''MiCA Regulation Proposal (COM/2020/593 final)'' <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 355.</ref>.
** ''Payment Services Directive 2 (PSD2 - Directive (EU) 2015/2366)'' <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 354, 367.</ref>.
** ''Electronic Money Directive 2009 (Directive 2009/110/EC)'' <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 358, 362.</ref>.
** ''Fifth Anti-Money Laundering Directive (AMLD5 - Directive (EU) 2018/843)'' <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 360.</ref>.
** ''MiFID II (Directive 2014/65/EU)'' & ''Prospectus Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2017/1129)'' <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 357, 365.</ref>.
* '''CJEU Case Law & Official Opinions''':
** ''CJEU Case Law'': ''Case C-264/14 Skatteverket v. David Hedqvist'' (2015) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 369.</ref> & ''Joined Cases C-422/19 & C-423/19 Häring & Dietrich'' (2021) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 369, 370.</ref>.
** ''European Central Bank (ECB)'': ECB Opinion of 19 February 2021 <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 353, 358, 367, 369.</ref>.
** ''European Banking Authority (EBA)'': Report with Advice on Crypto-Assets (2019) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 363, 364.</ref>.

== Key Provisions & Three Pillars of Policy Analysis ==
# '''Token Classification Regime and MiFID Exclusions''': MiCA establishes a catch-all definition for crypto-assets while explicitly excluding financial instruments governed by MiFID II, traditional e-money, and bank deposits <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 357, 358, 359.</ref>. Tokens are categorized into Utility Tokens (Title II), Asset-Referenced Tokens / ART (Title III), and E-Money Tokens / EMT (Title IV) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 358.</ref>.
# '''White Paper Disclosure and Civil Liability''': Issuers are mandated to draft and publish a non-technical summary and a detailed white paper covering the ICO business plan, usage of funds, DLT mechanics, and associated risk factors. Inaccuracies in the white paper give rise to civil liability for the issuer <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 365, 366.</ref>.
# '''Interest Prohibition and EBA Oversight''': Holders of ART and EMT are prohibited from receiving interest or remuneration tied to the duration of holdings (Arts 36 & 45 MiCA) to avoid competing with central bank deposits <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 368.</ref>. Significant token issuers are placed under direct supervision by the European Banking Authority (EBA) subject to enhanced capital requirements <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 372.</ref>.

== Entity Relationships ==
* '''[[Gabriella Gimigliano]]''': Principal Author & Jean Monnet Chairholder at the University of Siena <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 353.</ref>.
* '''[[European Commission]]''': Proposing Authority of the MiCA Regulation <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 353, 359.</ref>.
* '''[[European Central Bank]]''': Monetary Authority issuing legal opinions on MiCA <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 358, 362, 367, 369.</ref>.
* '''[[European Banking Authority]]''': Supervisory Authority over significant token issuers <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 363, 372.</ref>.

'''Quadro Politico della Regolamentazione UE dei Cripto-Asset e dei Token di Pagamento''' (''Payment Tokens and the Path Towards MiCA'') è un quadro di analisi giuridica sul diritto monetario e dei pagamenti dell'Unione Europea formulato da Gabriella Gimigliano su ''The Italian Law Journal'' (Vol. 08 N. 01/2022, pp. 353–374) <ref>Gimigliano, G. (2022). Payment Tokens and the Path Towards MiCA. ''The Italian Law Journal'', 8(1), 353–374.</ref>. L'opera analizza la Proposta di Regolamento relativo ai mercati delle cripto-attività (Proposta MiCA - COM/2020/593 final) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 353, 355.</ref>, valuta la classificazione dei token (payment tokens, utility tokens, asset tokens e hybrid tokens) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 357, 358.</ref>, ed esamina categorie specifiche come gli asset-referenced tokens (ART) e gli e-money tokens (EMT) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 358, 366.</ref>. Inoltre, analizza gli obblighi di pubblicazione del white paper (simili al prospetto informativo previsto dal Regolamento (UE) 2017/1129) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 365.</ref>, valuta i regimi autorizzativi e di vigilanza per gli emittenti e per i prestatori di servizi per le cripto-attività (CASP) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 370, 373.</ref>, ed esamina i limiti della MiCA rispetto alle applicazioni di Finanza Decentralizzata (DeFi), ai token algoritmici, alle Organizzazioni Autonome Decentrate (DAO), nonché il coordinamento con la PSD2 (Direttiva (UE) 2015/2366) e la Direttiva sulla Moneta Elettronica (Direttiva 2009/110/CE) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 358, 367, 374.</ref>.

== Sintesi ==
Scritto da [[Gabriella Gimigliano]] (PhD, Titolare della Cattedra Jean Monnet in EU Money Law e Ricercatrice Senior presso l'Università degli Studi di Siena), questo studio esamina la transizione verso la regolamentazione dei token di pagamento nel quadro del diritto monetario dell'UE <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 353.</ref>. L'autrice analizza la Proposta MiCA presentata dalla Commissione Europea ai sensi dell'Articolo 114 del TFUE al fine di garantire l'armonizzazione del mercato interno <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 355, 361.</ref>. L'articolo definisce i criteri di classificazione dei token, distinguendo tra utility tokens, asset-referenced tokens (ART) ed e-money tokens (EMT) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 358.</ref>. Gimigliano valuta i severi requisiti del white paper intesi a tutelare i potenziali investitori <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 365.</ref>, il divieto di corresponsione di interessi per i possessori di ART ed EMT per preservare la loro funzione di pagamento <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 368.</ref>, e la vigilanza diretta affidata all'Autorità Bancaria Europea (ABE/EBA) sugli emittenti di token significativi <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 372.</ref>.

== Base Giuridica ==
* '''Trattato sul Funzionamento dell'Unione Europea (TFUE)''':
** ''Articolo 114 TFUE'' (Armonizzazione del Mercato Interno) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 361.</ref>.
** ''Articolo 128(1) TFUE'' (Corso Legale delle Banconote in Euro) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 369.</ref>.
* '''Regolamenti e Direttive dell'UE''':
** ''Proposta di Regolamento MiCA (COM/2020/593 final)'' <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 355.</ref>.
** ''Direttiva sui Servizi di Pagamento (PSD2 - Direttiva (UE) 2015/2366)'' <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 354, 367.</ref>.
** ''Direttiva sulla Moneta Elettronica (Direttiva 2009/110/CE)'' <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 358, 362.</ref>.
** ''Quinta Direttiva Antiriclaggio (AMLD5 - Direttiva (UE) 2018/843)'' <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 360.</ref>.
** ''MiFID II (Direttiva 2014/65/UE)'' & ''Regolamento Prospetto (Regolamento (UE) 2017/1129)'' <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 357, 365.</ref>.
* '''Giurisprudenza della CGUE e Pareri Ufficiali''':
** ''Giurisprudenza CGUE'': ''Causa C-264/14 Skatteverket v. David Hedqvist'' (2015) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 369.</ref> & ''Cause Riunite C-422/19 e C-423/19 Häring & Dietrich'' (2021) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 369, 370.</ref>.
** ''Banca Centrale Europea (BCE)'': Parere BCE del 19 febbraio 2021 <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 353, 358, 367, 369.</ref>.
** ''Autorità Bancaria Europea (EBA)'': Report with Advice on Crypto-Assets (2019) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 363, 364.</ref>.

== Disposizioni Chiave e Tre Pilastri dell'Analisi di Politica ==
# '''Regime di Classificazione dei Token ed Esclusioni MiFID''': La MiCA stabilisce una definizione omnicomprensiva per le cripto-attività, escludendo esplicitamente gli strumenti finanziari disciplinati dalla MiFID II, la moneta elettronica tradizionale e i depositi bancari <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 357, 358, 359.</ref>. I token si dividono in Utility Tokens (Titolo II), Asset-Referenced Tokens / ART (Titolo III) ed E-Money Tokens / EMT (Titolo IV) <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 358.</ref>.
# '''Obbligo di White Paper e Responsabilità Civile''': Gli emittenti sono tenuti a redigere e pubblicare una nota di sintesi non tecnica e un white paper dettagliato contenente il piano aziendale della ICO, l'utilizzo dei fondi, le caratteristiche della tecnologia DLT e i fattori di rischio. Eventuali inesattezze comportano la responsabilità civile dell'emittente <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 365, 366.</ref>.
# '''Divieto di Interessi e Vigilanza EBA''': È vietata la concessione di interessi ai possessori di ART ed EMT in base alla durata della detenzione (Artt. 36 & 45 MiCA) al fine di evitare la concorrenza con i depositi bancari della banca centrale <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 368.</ref>. Gli emittenti di token significativi sono soggetti alla vigilanza diretta dell'Autorità Bancaria Europea (EBA) e a requisiti patrimoniali più stringenti <ref>Gimigliano (2022), p. 372.</ref>.

* '''[[Banca Centrale Europea]]''': Autorità Monetaria Emittente di Pareri sulla MiCA <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 358, 362, 367, 369.</ref>.

* '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': ''[[ENTITY IDENTITY UNCERTAIN|Non presente nelle fonti disponibili.]]'' <ref>Gimigliano (2022), pp. 353–374.</ref>

'''Policy Framework and Impact of Global Legal Indicators on Italian Judicial and Administrative Reform''' (''Global Legal Indicators and Domestic Judicial Policy Framework in Italy'') is an analytical framework of judicial policy and legislation formulated by [[Marta Infantino]] to examine the concrete penetration and impact of four major global legal indicators—''[[Freedom in the World]]'' (Freedom House), ''[[Corruption Perceptions Index]]'' (Transparency International), ''[[Trafficking in Persons Report]]'' (US Department of State), and ''[[Doing Business Report]]'' (World Bank)—on the Italian legal system. The framework covers the enactment of anti-corruption legislation ([[ANAC]], Law No. 190/2012, Law No. 3/2019 "Spazza-corrotti"), civil and administrative procedural law reforms (Law No. 27/2012, Law No. 162/2014, Law No. 119/2016), judicial organization ([[Court of Cassation]]), as well as administrative jurisprudence and asylum case law ([[Consiglio di Stato]] Plenary Decision No. 5/2015) <ref>Infantino, M. (2020). Measuring (the Effects of) Measurements: Four Global Legal Indicators in Italy. ''The Italian Law Journal'', 06(02), 431–462.</ref>.

== Overview ==
Authored by [[Marta Infantino]], Associate Professor of Comparative Law at the [[University of Trieste]], this publication presents an empirical analysis regarding how global quantitative indicators penetrate the Italian legal domain <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 431, 432.</ref>. Infantino maps the textual and judicial footprints of four primary indicators across legislative texts, Senate debates, annual speeches by the First Presidents of the Supreme ''Court of Cassation'', and court decisions <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 432, 444–459.</ref>. The research demonstrates that global legal indicators operate as powerful soft law instruments capable of shaping domestic public reform agendas, administrative vocabulary, and judicial reasoning <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 432, 459–461.</ref>.

== Legal Basis & Influenced Domestic Legislation ==
The framework traces legal recognition and statutory implementations driven by global indicators across several instruments:
* '''[[Law 6 November 2012, No. 190]] & [[Law 9 January 2019, No. 3]] ("Spazza-corrotti")''': Establishment of the National Anti-Corruption Authority (''ANAC'') and strengthening of anti-corruption criminal sanctions, directly driven by Italy's ranking in the ''Corruption Perceptions Index'' (CPI) <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 448, 449.</ref>.
* '''[[Law 27 May 2015, No. 69]] & [[Law 17 October 2017, No. 161]]''': Reform of crimes against public administration and Anti-Mafia Code revisions.
* '''[[Law 30 November 2017, No. 179]]''': Whistleblower protection framework.
* '''[[Law 24 March 2012, No. 27]], [[Law 10 November 2014, No. 162]] & [[Law 30 June 2016, No. 119]]''': Civil procedure reforms, establishment of specialized commercial court sections, promotion of Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) and arbitration, and creation of non-possessory security interests (''Patto Marciano''), influenced by the World Bank's ''Doing Business'' report <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 453, 456.</ref>.
* '''[[Legislative Decree 28 January 2008, No. 25]] (Arts. 8, 9, 35)''': Integration of ''Freedom in the World'' (FiW) reports as evidentiary bases for evaluating safe country of origin criteria in asylum seeker assessments <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 445, 446.</ref>.
* '''[[Consiglio di Stato]] (Adunanza Plenaria, Decision No. 5/2015)''': Landmark administrative ruling rejecting uncritical adherence to market-efficiency indicators in administrative procedural law <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 458, 459.</ref>.

== Policy Background & Governance by Indicators ==
The phenomenon of ''governance by indicators'' relies on numerical data and ranking systems to evaluate national legal performance <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 431, 435.</ref>. While criticized for promoting standardized common law models and oversimplifying legal institutional complexity, global benchmarks exert normative pressure (soft law strings attached) affecting investor perceptions, international aid allocation, and domestic legislative priorities <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 435, 449, 455.</ref>.

== Objectives ==
* Map the textual and judicial footprints of global legal indicators within parliamentary debates, statutory enactments, judicial opinions, and legal literature in Italy <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 432, 444.</ref>.
* Identify soft law transmission mechanisms operating between international ranking bodies and domestic legal practice <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 459–461.</ref>.
* Promote a critical methodology among scholars and practitioners to prevent pure managerial rationality from undermining constitutional standards and substantive justice <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 436, 459, 461.</ref>.

== Scope & Detailed Indicator Implementation ==
* '''1. Freedom in the World (FiW)''': Utilized by the National Asylum Commission (''Commissione Nazionale per il Diritto di Asilo'') and civil/cassation courts (e.g., ''Corte di Cassazione'' Decisions No. 30961/2019, 30952/2019, 26731/2019) as evidence of political freedom and security in applicants' countries of origin <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 445, 446.</ref>.
* '''2. Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI)''': Served as a primary justification for enacting Law No. 190/2012 (creating ANAC) and Law No. 3/2019. In Senate debates, Minister of Justice Alfonso Bonafede explicitly cited Italy's 69th rank in the CPI to frame anti-corruption reform as a constitutional imperative under Article 97 of the Italian Constitution <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 448, 449.</ref>.
* '''3. Trafficking in Persons (TiP) Report''': Influenced guidelines issued by the Ministry of the Interior, Parliamentary Anti-Mafia Commission, Ministry of Labor, and trade union NGOs regarding human trafficking and migrant labor exploitation <ref>Infantino (2020), p. 451.</ref>.
* '''4. Doing Business (DB) Report''': Prompted statutory reforms aimed at reducing disposition time in civil litigation (Laws 27/2012, 162/2014, 119/2016). Routinely cited in inaugural judicial year speeches by First Presidents of the ''Corte di Cassazione'' (Giovanni Mammone, Giorgio Canzio, Ernesto Lupo, Vincenzo Carbone) <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 453, 456, 458.</ref>.

== Critical Judicial Counterbalance: Consiglio di Stato Decision No. 5/2015 ==
In Decision No. 5 of 27 April 2015, the Plenary Assembly (''Adunanza Plenaria'') of the ''Consiglio di Stato'' rejected the uncritical subordination of administrative law procedures to the economic metrics of the ''Doing Business'' report. The Court emphasized that administrative justice serves the public interest and rule of law rather than merely optimizing economic indicator scores <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 458, 459.</ref>.

== Entity Relationships ==
* '''[[Marta Infantino]]''': Lead Author / Associate Professor at the University of Trieste <ref>Infantino (2020), p. 431.</ref>.
* '''[[The Italian Law Journal]]''': Publishing Academic Journal <ref>Infantino (2020), p. 431.</ref>.
* '''[[ANAC]] (National Anti-Corruption Authority)''': Italian administrative body established under Law 190/2012 <ref>Infantino (2020), p. 448.</ref>.
* '''[[Alfonso Bonafede]]''': Former Minister of Justice who cited CPI indicators during Senate legislative proceedings <ref>Infantino (2020), p. 449.</ref>.
* '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': ''[[ENTITY IDENTITY UNCERTAIN|Not found in available source data.]]'' <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 431–462.</ref>
* '''[[Geovanny Widya Berlianty P]]''': ''[[ENTITY IDENTITY UNCERTAIN|Not found in available source data.]]'' <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 431–462.</ref>

Il '''Quadro di Politica Giudiziaria e Impatto degli Indicatori Giuridici Globali sulle Riforme Giudiziarie e Amministrative in Italia''' (''Global Legal Indicators and Domestic Judicial Policy Framework in Italy'') è una struttura di analisi della politica giudiziaria e legislativa elaborata da [[Marta Infantino]] per esaminare la penetrazione e l'impatto concreto di quattro principali indicatori giuridici globali—''[[Freedom in the World]]'' (Freedom House), ''[[Corruption Perceptions Index]]'' (Transparency International), ''[[Trafficking in Persons Report]]'' (Dipartimento di Stato degli Stati Uniti) e ''[[Doing Business Report]]'' (Banca Mondiale)—sul sistema giuridico italiano. Il quadro comprende l'introduzione della legislazione anticorruzione ([[ANAC]], Legge n. 190/2012, Legge n. 3/2019 "Spazza-corrotti"), la riforma del diritto processuale civile e amministrativo (Legge n. 27/2012, Legge n. 162/2014, Legge n. 119/2016), l'organizzazione giudiziaria (Corte Suprema di [[Cassazione]]), nonché la giurisprudenza amministrativa e in materia di asilo ([[Consiglio di Stato]], Adunanza Plenaria, Sentenza n. 5/2015) <ref>Infantino, M. (2020). Measuring (the Effects of) Measurements: Four Global Legal Indicators in Italy. ''The Italian Law Journal'', 06(02), 431–462.</ref>.

== Sintesi ==
Scritto da [[Marta Infantino]], Professoressa Associata di Diritto Comparato presso l'[[Università degli Studi di Trieste]], lo studio offre un'analisi empirica su come gli indicatori quantitativi globali penetrino nel contesto giuridico italiano <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 431, 432.</ref>. Infantino ricostruisce le impronte testuali e giurisprudenziali di quattro indicatori chiave nei testi di legge, nei dibattiti del Senato della Repubblica, nelle relazioni annuali dei Primi Presidenti della Corte Suprema di Cassazione e nelle decisioni dei giudici <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 432, 444–459.</ref>. La ricerca dimostra che gli indicatori giuridici globali agiscono come potenti strumenti di ''soft law'', capaci di orientare l'agenda delle riforme pubbliche, il linguaggio amministrativo e le motivazioni delle sentenze <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 432, 459–461.</ref>.

== Base Giuridica e Normativa Nazionale Influenzata ==
Il quadro analizza il riconoscimento normativo e l'attuazione legislativa promossa dagli indicatori attraverso diversi provvedimenti:
* '''[[Legge 6 novembre 2012, n. 190]] e [[Legge 9 gennaio 2019, n. 3]] ("Spazza-corrotti")''': Istituzione dell'Autorità Nazionale Anticorruzione (''ANAC'') e inasprimento delle sanzioni penali anticorruzione, direttamente influenzati dalla posizione dell'Italia nel ''Corruption Perceptions Index'' (CPI) <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 448, 449.</ref>.
* '''[[Legge 27 maggio 2015, n. 69]] e [[Legge 17 ottobre 2017, n. 161]]''': Riforme dei reati contro la Pubblica Amministrazione e revisione del Codice Antimafia.
* '''[[Legge 30 novembre 2017, n. 179]]''': Tutela del dipendente pubblico o privato che segnala illeciti (''Whistleblowing'').
* '''[[Legge 24 marzo 2012, n. 27]], [[Legge 10 novembre 2014, n. 162]] e [[Legge 30 giugno 2016, n. 119]]''': Riforme del processo civile, istituzione delle sezioni specializzate in materia di impresa, promozione della risoluzione alternativa delle controversie (ADR) e dell'arbitrato, e introduzione di garanzie reali non possessorie (''Patto Marciano''), ispirate dal rapporto ''Doing Business'' della Banca Mondiale <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 453, 456.</ref>.
* '''[[Decreto Legislativo 28 gennaio 2008, n. 25]] (Artt. 8, 9, 35)''': Utilizzo dei rapporti ''Freedom in the World'' (FiW) quali fonti probatorie per la valutazione dei Paesi di origine sicuri nelle procedure di asilo <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 445, 446.</ref>.
* '''[[Consiglio di Stato]] (Adunanza Plenaria, Sentenza n. 5/2015)''': Decisione giurisprudenziale fondamentale che rifiuta la subordinazione acritica del diritto processuale amministrativo agli indicatori economici di efficienza <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 458, 459.</ref>.

== Contesto di Politica del Diritto e Governance by Indicators ==
Il fenomeno della ''governance by indicators'' si basa sull'impiego di dati quantitativi e graduatorie per valutare la performance dei sistemi giuridici nazionali <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 431, 435.</ref>. Sebbene ampiamente criticati per la promozione di modelli standardizzati di ''common law'' e per la semplificazione della complessità istituzionale, gli indicatori globali esercitano una pressione normativa (condizionalità di ''soft law'') che incide sulla percezione degli investitori, sull'allocazione dei capitali e sulle priorità legislative interne <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 435, 449, 455.</ref>.

== Obiettivi ==
* Mappare le tracce testuali e giurisprudenziali degli indicatori giuridici globali nei dibattiti parlamentari, nei testi normativi, nelle decisioni giudiziarie e nella dottrina in Italia <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 432, 444.</ref>.
* Identificare i meccanismi di trasmissione del ''soft law'' tra le organizzazioni internazionali e la prassi giudiziaria nazionale <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 459–461.</ref>.
* Promuovere un approccio critico tra giuristi e operatori del diritto per evitare che una pura logica manageriale comprometta i principi costituzionali e la giustizia sostanziale <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 436, 459, 461.</ref>.

== Ambito e Applicazione degli Indicatori Globali ==
* '''1. Freedom in the World (FiW)''': Utilizzato dalla Commissione Nazionale per il Diritto di Asilo e dai giudici ordinari e di legittimità (es. ''Corte di Cassazione'' Sentenze n. 30961/2019, 30952/2019, 26731/2019) per valutare le condizioni di libertà politica e sicurezza nei Paesi d'origine dei richiedenti asilo <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 445, 446.</ref>.
* '''2. Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI)''': Utilizzato come argomentazione centrale per l'approvazione della Legge n. 190/2012 (istitutiva dell'ANAC) e della Legge n. 3/2019. In Senato, il Ministro della Giustizia Alfonso Bonafede ha citato il 69° posto dell'Italia nel CPI per inquadrare la lotta alla corruzione come dovere morale e costituzionale ai sensi dell'Articolo 97 della Costituzione <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 448, 449.</ref>.
* '''3. Trafficking in Persons (TiP) Report''': Ha conformato le linee guida del Ministero dell'Interno, della Commissione Parlamentare Antimafia, del Ministero del Lavoro e delle organizzazioni sindacali sul contrasto alla tratta e al caporalato <ref>Infantino (2020), p. 451.</ref>.
* '''4. Doing Business (DB) Report''': Ha guidato le riforme volte alla riduzione dei tempi della giustizia civile (Legge 27/2012, Legge 162/2014, Legge 119/2016). I dati DB sono regolarmente citati nelle relazioni sull'amministrazione della giustizia dai Primi Presidenti della ''Corte di Cassazione'' (Giovanni Mammone, Giorgio Canzio, Ernesto Lupo, Vincenzo Carbone) <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 453, 456, 458.</ref>.

== Contrappeso Giurisprudenziale: Consiglio di Stato Sentenza n. 5/2015 ==
Con la sentenza n. 5 del 27 aprile 2015, l'Adunanza Plenaria del ''Consiglio di Stato'' ha respinto l'adesione acritica del processo amministrativo agli indici economici del rapporto ''Doing Business''. Il Consiglio di Stato ha riaffermato che la giustizia amministrativa è presidio della legalità e dell'interesse generale, e non può essere asservita a meri parametri di efficienza di mercato <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 458, 459.</ref>.

== Relazioni tra Entità ==

* '''[[The Italian Law Journal]]''': Rivista Scientifica di Pubblicazione <ref>Infantino (2020), p. 431.</ref>.
* '''[[ANAC]] (Autorità Nazionale Anticorruzione)''': Organismo amministrativo indipendente istituito dalla Legge 190/2012 <ref>Infantino (2020), p. 448.</ref>.
* '''[[Alfonso Bonafede]]''': Ex Ministro della Giustizia che ha citato gli indici CPI nei dibattiti parlamentari <ref>Infantino (2020), p. 449.</ref>.
* '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': ''[[ENTITY IDENTITY UNCERTAIN|Non presente nei dati di fonte disponibili.]]'' <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 431–462.</ref>
* '''[[Geovanny Widya Berlianty P]]''': ''[[ENTITY IDENTITY UNCERTAIN|Non presente nei dati di fonte disponibili.]]'' <ref>Infantino (2020), pp. 431–462.</ref>
