The '''Italian Regulation on Confiscated Assets Rehabilitation Framework''' (''Kerangka Pengaturan dan Rehabilitasi Aset Hasil Rampasan Kejahatan Terorganisir Italia'') is the administrative legal structure in Italy that governs the seizure, confiscation, management, allocation, and rehabilitation of real estate assets taken from organized crime (mafia) for social utility and public benefit.

== Summary ==
Authored by [[Stefano D'Alfonso]], Associate Professor of Administrative Law at the [[University of Naples Federico II]], this study evaluates the public law dimensions of allocating and rehabilitating confiscated real estate assets. Unlike many European Union jurisdictions that prioritize asset liquidation through public auctions, the Italian framework establishes social re-use as the primary mechanism to restore legality and generate symbolic educational value within communities.

== Legal Basis ==
This policy framework rests on key national statutory and international legal instruments:
* '''[[Anti-Mafia Code]] (Legislative Decree No. 159/2011)''': The primary codification governing asset preventive measures, confiscation procedures, and allocation protocols (specifically Articles 45, 47, and 48).
* '''[[Law No. 161 of 17 October 2017]]''': Organic reform updating the Anti-Mafia Code and reinforcing ANBSC administrative authority.
* '''[[Rognoni-La Torre Law]] (Law No. 646/1982)''': Foundational statutory legislation introducing asset confiscation targeting organized crime in Italy.
* '''[[Article 117(2)(h) of the Italian Constitution]]''': Establishes the State's exclusive legislative jurisdiction over public order and security.
* '''[[European Union Legal Instruments]]''': Directive 2014/42/EU and Regulation (EU) 2018/1805 regarding mutual recognition of freezing and confiscation orders.

== Background ==
Organized crime severely distorts market competition and legitimate economic activity through illicit capital accumulation. To counter this, Italy developed an ''in rem'' asset recovery mechanism designed to strip criminal organizations of real estate assets and repurpose them to serve public interest and regional development.

== Objectives ==
* Neutralize the socio-economic influence of mafia organizations within their local strongholds.
* Repurpose confiscated properties for social initiatives, public facilities, and victim compensation.
* Promote civic legality and community engagement through the educational value of asset recovery.

== Scope ==
The scope of this framework covers administrative law, criminal preventive measures, public property management, central-local intergovernmental relations, and partnerships with non-profit third-sector entities (*private social sector*).

== Key Provisions & Legal Classification ==
* '''Central Role of ANBSC''': ANBSC leads property administration and determines final asset destinations within 90 days of a final judicial confiscation ruling.
* '''Public Property Classification''': Jurisprudence from the Supreme Court of Cassation and Council of State classifies allocated confiscated real estate as non-available patrimonial assets (*patrimonio indisponibile*), legally binding them to public and social purposes.
* '''Direct vs. Indirect Management''': Receiving municipalities may manage properties directly or grant free concessions to non-profit organizations through transparent public tenders.
* '''NRRP / PNRR Funding Support''': Integration with European Union Next Generation EU funds (PNRR Mission 5 Component 3) to support physical rehabilitation and structural upgrades of allocated properties.

== Implementation ==
Implemented across Italy through inter-institutional coordination involving ANBSC, Regional Prefectures, *Agenzia del Demanio*, local municipalities, and civic anti-mafia networks (such as *Libera*).

== Policy Issues ==
* '''Municipal Budgetary Constraints''': Many local councils lack sufficient capital to restore or maintain degraded confiscated properties.
* '''Municipal Register Transparency Deficits''': Empirical studies indicate that 63.5% of municipalities fail to maintain updated public registers of allocated assets as mandated by the Anti-Mafia Code.

== Reform / Proposed Changes ==
Proposed reforms (*de jure condendo*) emphasize strengthening financial background checks on private buyers during property liquidations, streamlining administrative transfer steps, and securing stable funding streams via EU Cohesion Policies and the PNRR.

== Related Entities ==
* '''[[Stefano D'Alfonso]]''': Author of the Academic Study and Professor of Administrative Law.

| date = 2004 (Enactment of Law No. 215/2004); 2012 (Publication in IJPL Vol. 4 Issue 2/2012)
| status = In Force / Academically Criticized as Inoperative Policy Framework
}}

'''Framework of Government Ethics and Conflict of Interest for Italian Cabinet Members''' (''Legge 20 luglio 2004, n. 215'' / ''Kerangka Kebijakan Konflik Kepentingan Anggota Kabinet Italia'') is an Italian government ethics and administrative law legal framework enacted under Law No. 215/2004 to regulate conflicts of interest among cabinet members (*membri del Governo*). The policy adopts an atypical dynamic definition requiring proof of both personal advantage and actual harm to the public interest (*probatio diabolica*), entrusting monitoring and limited sanctioning powers to the Italian Competition Authority (*Antitrust Authority*) <ref>Mattarella, B.G. (2012). Government Ethics: The Strange Italian “Conflict of Interests”. ''Italian Journal of Public Law'', 4(2), 360–373.</ref>.

== Overview ==
Authored by [[Bernardo Giorgio Mattarella]], Professor of Administrative Law at the [[University of Siena]], the legal study offers a critical analysis of Italian government ethics legislation, specifically Law 20 July 2004 No. 215 (commonly known as the *Frattini Law*) <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 360, 371, 373.</ref>. Mattarella highlights that the Italian statute departs significantly from international standards (such as the [[OECD]] guidelines) by shifting the definition of conflict of interest from a static situation of danger (*crime of danger*) to an actual event of damage (*criminal damage*). This imposes an impossible burden of proof (*probatio diabolica*) that renders its main provisions practically ineffective <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 363, 371, 372.</ref>.

== Legal Basis ==
The statutory and policy foundation includes:
* '''[[Law 20 July 2004, No. 215]]''': The national statute governing the resolution of conflicts of interest for Italian executive office holders <ref>Mattarella (2012), p. 371.</ref>.
* '''[[Code of Behavior for Italian Civil Servants]]''': Public regulations prescribing obligations of disqualification, transparency, and incompatibilities across the administrative civil service <ref>Mattarella (2012), p. 372.</ref>.
* '''[[Italian Local Government Framework]]''': Pre-existing local governance regulations permitting judicial annulment of administrative decisions adopted under conflicts of interest <ref>Mattarella (2012), p. 372.</ref>.
* '''[[OECD Guidelines on Managing Conflict of Interest in the Public Service]] (2004)''': International standard defining conflict of interest as a static situation of risk where private interest can improperly influence public duties <ref>Mattarella (2012), p. 363.</ref>.

== Background & Political Confusion ==
Within Italian political and legal discourse, conflict of interest has historically been conflated with electoral qualifications, political party financing, campaign regulations, and media ownership concentration <ref>Mattarella (2012), p. 364.</ref>. Applying the ancient legal canon "*distingue frequenter*", Mattarella emphasizes that conflict of interest must be strictly separated from media ownership issues to design targeted administrative remedies <ref>Mattarella (2012), p. 364.</ref>.

== Objectives ==
* Prevent the improper influence of private financial interests in cabinet decision-making <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 361, 365.</ref>.
* Balance the protection of public integrity with administrative efficiency and non-discriminatory access to public office <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 365, 366.</ref>.

== Scope ==
Law No. 215/2004 applies exclusively to national cabinet members (Prime Minister, Ministers, Deputy Ministers, Undersecretaries) and explicitly excludes Members of Parliament (MPs) as well as regional and local government officials <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 371, 372.</ref>.

== Key Provisions & Three Ethical Remedies ==
* '''Three Primary Ethical Remedies''':
# *Removal*: The obligation to vacate private positions or sell asset holdings (*duty to sell* / blind trust). Represents the most radical mechanism restricting constitutional rights <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 366, 369.</ref>.
# *Neutralization*: The obligation to recuse or disqualify oneself (*duty to disqualify*) when faced with specific decisions involving personal interest <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 366, 367, 373.</ref>.
# *Exhibition*: The statutory requirement for public financial disclosure (*disclosure*) <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 367, 369, 373.</ref>.
* '''Italian Structural Flaws''': Law No. 215/2004 rejects *removal*, omits public *exhibition* (asset statements submitted to the Antitrust Authority are confidential), and relies on a *disqualification* mechanism burdened by impossible evidentiary rules <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 372, 373.</ref>.

== Policy Issues: Probatio Diabolica & Weak Sanctions ==
* '''Impossible Burden of Proof (Probatio Diabolica)''': To establish a statutory violation, the Italian Competition Authority must prove concrete harm to the public interest (*harm to the public interest*). Because political decision-making naturally balances competing public priorities, an official can easily justify a self-interested decision as serving an alternative public good <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 371, 372.</ref>.
* '''Absence of Deterrent Sanctions''':
** *Corporate Entities*: Financial penalties imposed by the Antitrust Authority are capped at the precise pecuniary gain realized by the business entity, leaving corporate balances unharmed <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 373, 374.</ref>.
** *Cabinet Members*: Sanctions consist merely of confidential reports sent by the Antitrust Authority to the Presidents of Parliamentary Houses (who share the same ruling political majority), involving no personal financial liability or compensatory damages <ref>Mattarella (2012), p. 374.</ref>.

== Entity Relationships ==
* '''[[Bernardo Giorgio Mattarella]]''': Author of the academic study and Professor of Administrative Law <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 360, 368.</ref>.
* '''[[University of Siena]]''': Institutional academic affiliation of the author <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 360, 368.</ref>.
* '''[[Italian Competition Authority]] (Antitrust Authority)''': Designated regulatory and monitoring body for cabinet conflicts of interest <ref>Mattarella (2012), p. 373.</ref>.
* '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': ''Not found in the available sources.'' <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 360–373.</ref>
* '''[[Geovanny Widya Berlianty P]]''': ''Not found in the available sources.'' <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 360–373.</ref>

Il '''Quadro di Kebijakan Konflik Kepentingan Anggota Kabinet Italia''' (''Legge 20 luglio 2004, n. 215'' / ''Framework of Government Ethics and Conflict of Interest for Italian Cabinet Members'') è il quadro normativo di diritto amministrativo ed etica pubblica approvato in Italia con la Legge n. 215/2004 per disciplinare i conflitti di interesse dei componenti del Governo (*cabinet members*). La disciplina adotta una definizione dinamica atipica che richiede la contestuale prova di un vantaggio patrimoniale privato e di un danno concreto all'interesse pubblico (*probatio diabolica*), affidando la vigilanza e limitati poteri sanzionatori all'Autorità Garante della Concorrenza e del Mercato (*Antitrust Authority*) <ref>Mattarella, B.G. (2012). Government Ethics: The Strange Italian “Conflict of Interests”. ''Italian Journal of Public Law'', 4(2), 360–373.</ref>.

== Descrizione ==
Redatto da [[Bernardo Giorgio Mattarella]], Professore Ordinario di Diritto Amministrativo presso l'[[Università degli Studi di Siena]], lo studio analizza criticamente la legislazione italiana in materia di etica pubblica, con particolare riferimento alla Legge 20 luglio 2004 n. 215 (nota come *Legge Frattini*) <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 360, 371, 373.</ref>. Mattarella evidenzia come il legislatore italiano si sia discostato dagli standard internazionali (quali le linee guida [[OECD]]), trasformando la fattispecie del conflitto di interessi da situazione statica di pericolo (*reato di pericolo*) ad evento di danno effettivo (*reato di danno*), introducendo un onere probatorio di fatto diabolico (*probatio diabolica*) che rende inapplicabili le disposizioni principali della legge <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 363, 371, 372.</ref>.

== Base Giuridica ==
Il quadro normativo e regolamentare comprende:
* '''[[Legge 20 luglio 2004, n. 215]]''': Legge ordinaria dello Stato che reca norme per la risoluzione dei conflitti di interessi per i titolari di cariche di Governo <ref>Mattarella (2012), p. 371.</ref>.
* '''[[Codice di comportamento dei dipendenti pubblici]]''': Normativa che stabilisce gli obblighi di astensione, trasparenza e incompatibilità per i funzionari della pubblica amministrazione <ref>Mattarella (2012), p. 372.</ref>.
* '''[[Ordinamento degli Enti Locali in Italia]]''': Disciplina previgente che consente l'annullamento giurisdizionale degli atti amministrativi adottati in presenza di un interesse privato <ref>Mattarella (2012), p. 372.</ref>.
* '''[[Linee guida OECD sulla gestione dei conflitti di interesse]] (2004)''': Standard internazionale che definisce il conflitto di interessi come una situazione statica di rischio di interferenza tra funzioni pubbliche e interessi privati <ref>Mattarella (2012), p. 363.</ref>.

== Contesto e Confusione Politica ==
Nel dibattito politico e giuridico italiano, il tema del conflitto di interessi è stato storicamente sovrapposto alle condizioni di elegibilità, al finanziamento dei partiti, alla regolamentazione della par condicio e alla concentrazione delle proprietà radiotelevisive <ref>Mattarella (2012), p. 364.</ref>. Applicando il principio classico "*distingue frequenter*", Mattarella sottolinea la necessità di scindere il conflitto di interessi dalla proprietà dei media per definire rimedi amministrativi mirati ed efficaci <ref>Mattarella (2012), p. 364.</ref>.

== Obiettivi ==
* Prevenire l'indebita influenza degli interessi finanziari privati nelle decisioni dei membri dell'esecutivo <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 361, 365.</ref>.
* Bilanciare la tutela dell'integrità dell'azione amministrativa con il buon andamento della pubblica amministrazione e il diritto di elettorato passivo <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 365, 366.</ref>.

== Ambito di Applicazione ==
La Legge n. 215/2004 si applica esclusivamente ai componenti del Governo nazionale (Presidente del Consiglio, Ministri, Vice Ministri, Sottosegretari di Stato) e non riguarda i membri del Parlamento né gli amministratori regionali o locali <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 371, 372.</ref>.

== Disposizioni Chiave e i Tre Rimedi Etici ==
* '''Classificazione dei Tre Rimedi Etici''':
# *Rimozione (Removal)*: Obbligo di dismissione di cariche private o vendita di partecipazioni societarie (*duty to sell* / blind trust). Costituisce il rimedio più incisivo sui diritti costituzionali dell'individuo <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 366, 369.</ref>.
# *Neutralizzazione (Neutralization)*: Obbligo di astensione e ricusazione (*duty to disqualify*) in presenza di atti specifici tali da ingenerare conflitto <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 366, 367, 373.</ref>.
# *Trasparenza (Exhibition)*: Obbligo di dichiarazione pubblica delle posizioni patrimoniali e finanziarie (*financial disclosure*) <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 367, 369, 373.</ref>.
* '''Limiti dell'Impianto Normativo Italiano''': La Legge n. 215/2004 rifiuta la *rimozione*, esclude la *trasparenza* verso la collettività (le dichiarazioni presentate all'Autorità Antitrust sono riservate) e si affida ad un meccanismo di *astensione* vincolato a requisiti probatori irrealizzabili <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 372, 373.</ref>.

== Criticità di Politica Pubblica: Probatio Diabolica e Sanzioni Inefficaci ==
* '''Onere della Prova Diabolico (Probatio Diabolica)''': Ai fini della contestazione della violazione, l'Autorità Antitrust deve dimostrare l'esistenza di un danno concreto arrecato all'interesse pubblico (*harm to the public interest*). Poiché le decisioni politiche implicano il bilanciamento di molteplici interessi pubblici, l'organo politico può sempre giustificare il proprio atto dichiarando di aver perseguito un diverso interesse collettivo <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 371, 372.</ref>.
* '''Inadeguatezza del Sistema Sanzionatorio''':
** *Verso l'Impresa*: Le sanzioni pecuniarie comminate dall'Autorità Antitrust sono limitate all'ammontare del profitto conseguito dalla società, evitando così qualsiasi impatto sanzionatorio reale sul bilancio dell'entità commerciale <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 373, 374.</ref>.
** *Verso i Componenti del Governo*: Le sanzioni consistono in una mera segnalazione riservata dell'Autorità Antitrust ai Presidenti delle Camere (espressione della medesima maggioranza politica), priva di responsabilità patrimoniale o risarcitoria diretta <ref>Mattarella (2012), p. 374.</ref>.

== Relazioni tra Entità ==
* '''[[Bernardo Giorgio Mattarella]]''': Autore dello studio accademico e Professore Ordinario di Diritto Amministrativo <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 360, 368.</ref>.
* '''[[Università degli Studi di Siena]]''': Afiliazione accademica dell'autore <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 360, 368.</ref>.
* '''[[Autorità Garante della Concorrenza e del Mercato]] (Antitrust Authority)''': Organo di vigilanza incaricato del controllo sui conflitti di interesse dei membri del Governo <ref>Mattarella (2012), p. 373.</ref>.
* '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': ''Non presente nelle fonti disponibili.'' <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 360–373.</ref>
* '''[[Geovanny Widya Berlianty P]]''': ''Non presente nelle fonti disponibili.'' <ref>Mattarella (2012), pp. 360–373.</ref>

}}

'''The Ethnographic Analysis Framework of Italian Courts of Justice & Communities of Practitioners''' (''Behind the Judges' Desk'') is a policy framework and empirical-ethnographic analysis of judicial administration that investigates the practice of the interpretation of written law "behind the judges' desk" across four labor courts in Italy (Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta). It distinguishes between the dimensions of substance (''merit'') and method/procedure (''method''), and classifies court organizational dynamics into two primary patterns: "condominium" type courts with individualistic judges (''monads/craftsmen'') versus "communities of practitioners" type courts [1, 4, 8, 35–40].

== Summary ==
Published by Luca Verzelloni in the ''International Journal for Court Administration'' (IJCA), this policy framework dissects the daily reality of labor justice in Italy. Based on a two-year ethnographic research study of 16 judges across four district courts, this study proves that legal interpretation is not merely an abstract cognitive activity, but a social practice built through the ''translation'' of rules into daily work procedures. The framework identifies the existence of "condominium" type courts where judges work in isolation, as well as "communities of practitioners" type courts where judges share knowledge and align working methods [1, 4, 8, 35–40].

== Legal Basis ==
* '''Law No. 533/1973 & Articles 409–447 of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure (c.c.p.):''' Procedural law for labor justice that outlines the principles of orality, concentration of hearings, and rapid verdicts.
* '''Article 420 c.c.p.:''' Mandatory provisions for the concentration of hearings, free interrogation of parties, and reconciliation/peace efforts.
* '''Article 429 c.c.p. & Article 281-sexies c.c.p.:''' Obligations for the open reading of the operative part of the sentence (''dispositivi'') and contextual decisions schemes (''decisioni contestuali'').
* '''Law No. 133/2008:''' A 60-day time limit for judges to submit written statements of reasons (''motivazioni'').
* '''Article 47-quarter Royal Decree No. 12/1941 (Italian Judicial Order):''' Duties of the President of the Court Section in facilitating information exchange among judges.

== Background ==
In the eyes of the public, courts are often perceived as "sacred sites," "opaque institutions," or "black boxes" isolated from society. In the Civil Law tradition, the interpretation of abstract written law is often mistakenly considered a purely cognitive activity. However, this research penetrates that institutional facade by applying ethnographic methods behind the judges' desk. It discovered that despite referring to the exact same written laws, judges apply procedural laws in starkly contrasting ways due to differences in local court organizational cultures [1, 4, 35–37].

== Objectives ==
1. Reveal the real practice of legal interpretation behind the judges' desk.
2. Analyze judges' decisions based on two dimensions: ''merit'' (legal substance) and ''method'' (time and procedure management).
3. Drive the transformation of courts from an individualistic "condominium" pattern to "communities of practitioners" [38–40].
4. Identify leadership barriers at the level of the President of the Court Section.

== Scope ==
This policy was evaluated across four labor, social assistance, and welfare courts in Italy:
* '''Tribunal Alpha (Medium-Large, Central Italy):''' Condominium Type; judges work independently without discussion.
* '''Tribunal Beta (Medium-Small, Central Italy):''' Small-Scale Community Type; intensive collaboration between two judges.
* '''Tribunal Gamma (Medium-Large, Southern Italy):''' Severe Condominium Type; chaotic hearings, trials taking up to 5 years.
* '''Tribunal Delta (Very Large, Northern Italy):''' Integrated Communities of Practitioners Type; very fast and collaborative hearings.

== Key Provisions ==
* '''Two Dimensions of Judicial Work:''' The ''Merit'' dimension (technical legal substance) and the ''Method'' dimension (time management, hearing adjournments, and work organization).
* '''Condominium Court Model:''' Courts where judges act as isolated "monads" or "craftsmen" who are unaware of their peers' working methods.
* '''Communities of Practitioners Model:''' Integrated courts where judges routinely discuss, mentor novice judges, and align legal interpretations.
* '''Utilization of Contextual Decisions:''' The use of the ''decisioni contestuali'' instrument to decide simple cases directly during the hearing.

== Implementation ==
* '''Adjournment Practices:''' In Delta, final discussions are adjourned by a maximum of 30 days; in Alpha, by 2–8 months; while in Gamma, by up to 34 months.
* '''Role of the Section President:''' President Brown (Delta) actively facilitates discussion and mentoring, while President Black (Alpha) only works as a regular judge.

== Policy Problems ==
* '''Gap between Positive Law and Living Law:''' The principle of "the law is the same for everyone" is compromised by extreme variations in daily judicial work procedures.
* '''Lack of Section President Management Training:''' Section Presidents are not equipped with court organizational management skills.

== Reform / Change ==
* Institutionalization of routine discussion forums among section judges to align procedural law practices.
* Development of leadership and management training programs for Presidents of Court Sections.

== Relationships with Other Entities ==

* '''International Journal for Court Administration (IJCA):''' Journal publishing the research report.

The '''Italian Emigration Law, Migrants' Rights, and Social Stigma Policy Framework''' (''Kerangka Kebijakan Hukum Emigrasi Italia, Hak-Hak Migran, dan Stigma Sosial'') is a legal-historical and judicial policy analytical framework examining the evolution of Italian emigration law during *La Grande Emigrazione* (1861–1920s), the shift in migrants' legal status to *popolo di mezzo* ("people in the middle"), racial criminal stigmatization, and transnational judicial responses <ref>Spadaro, C. M. (2024). Tra «spartenza» e «restanza»: La Grande Emigrazione tra diritti e stigma sociale. ''Italian Review of Legal History'', 10(2), 61–103.</ref>.

== Summary ==
Authored by [[Carmela Maria Spadaro]], Professor at the [[University of Naples Federico II]], this study analyzes the legal dimensions of the mass migration wave involving 15 to 20 million Italians post-unification <ref>Spadaro (2024), pp. 61, 63.</ref>. Spadaro demonstrates how liberal legal doctrine permitted state absenteeism under the guise of individual liberty (*jus migrandi*), leaving migrants trapped in a state of *minorità giuridica* (loss of rights and legal protection) while suffering racial and criminal stigmatization both domestically and in destination countries such as the United States <ref>Spadaro (2024), pp. 61–62, 65, 71–72.</ref>.

== Legal Basis ==
This framework examines key domestic and international legal instruments:
* '''[[Crispi Law|Legge Crispi 30 dicembre 1888 n. 5866]]''': Early Italian legislation penalizing illegal labor brokers without granting substantive civil rights protections to emigrants <ref>Spadaro (2024), pp. 65, 68.</ref>.
* '''[[Organic Emigration Law of 1901|Legge organica 31 gennaio 1901 n. 23]]''': Comprehensive emigration law establishing the *Commissariato Generale per l'Emigrazione* and setting maritime transport health standards <ref>Spadaro (2024), pp. 69, 70, 102.</ref>.
* '''[[Pica Law|Legge Pica 15 agosto 1863 n. 1409]]''': Anti-brigandage legislation in Southern Italy that triggered forced political exile and displacement <ref>Spadaro (2024), p. 82.</ref>.
* '''[[Immigration Act of 1882|US Immigration Act 1882]] & [[Literacy Act of 1917]]''': Restrictive US federal laws imposing entry restrictions, literacy tests, and racial quotas targeting Italian immigrants <ref>Spadaro (2024), pp. 71, 101.</ref>.

== Background ==
Following Italian unification in 1861, severe economic imbalances between the industrialized North and neglected South sparked a mass exodus <ref>Spadaro (2024), pp. 63, 64.</ref>. Italian regional judicial authorities routinely described emigrants in derogatory terms as idlers or vagrants <ref>Spadaro (2024), pp. 66–67.</ref>. In the United States, Southern Italian immigrants faced systematic racial discrimination, frequently targeted with the slur *dagoes* <ref>Spadaro (2024), pp. 76, 97.</ref>.

== Objectives ==
* Expose the legal mechanisms behind state abandonment of migrant rights in origin and host nations <ref>Spadaro (2024), pp. 61, 71.</ref>.
* Analyze the misuse of positivist criminology ([[Cesare Lombroso]]) in legitimizing judicial prejudice <ref>Spadaro (2024), pp. 67, 76.</ref>.
* Elevate oral folk tradition (*canti di spartenza*) as counter-narrative evidence in legal history <ref>Spadaro (2024), pp. 61, 88, 91.</ref>.

== Scope ==
The framework encompasses Italian public law history, US immigration law, human rights, positivist criminology, and transnational criminal justice <ref>Spadaro (2024), pp. 61–103.</ref>.

== Key Provisions & Judicial Evidence ==
* '''Concept of Popolo di Mezzo''': Emigrants existed in legal limbo without clear protection of citizenship rights <ref>Spadaro (2024), pp. 61, 72–73.</ref>.
* '''1891 New Orleans Lynching''': The murder of 11 Sicilian immigrants following the death of police chief David Hennessy, illustrating mob action fueled by anti-Italian prejudice <ref>Spadaro (2024), pp. 97–98.</ref>.
* '''Sacco and Vanzetti Trial (1920–1927)''': The trial and execution of two Italian anarchists based on political and racial bias, leading to full judicial rehabilitation by Massachusetts Governor [[Michael Dukakis]] on August 23, 1977 <ref>Spadaro (2024), pp. 96, 99–101.</ref>.

== Implementation ==
Enforced through administrative monitoring by the *Commissariato Generale per l'Emigrazione*, passport controls, and the formation of self-protective *Little Italy* enclaves <ref>Spadaro (2024), pp. 102–104.</ref>.

== Policy Issues ==
* '''State Absenteeism''': The misuse of *jus migrandi* doctrine to justify state disengagement, leaving migrants vulnerable to private exploitation <ref>Spadaro (2024), pp. 65, 68, 70.</ref>.
* '''Pseudo-Scientific Racial Bias''': The integration of positivist criminal theories into judicial reasoning to pre-condemn Italian immigrants <ref>Spadaro (2024), pp. 67, 76, 97.</ref>.

== Reform & Proposed Changes ==
Governor Michael Dukakis's 1977 Proclamation underscored the imperative to purge judicial processes of xenophobic and political bias <ref>Spadaro (2024), p. 101.</ref>.

== Related Entities ==
* '''[[Carmela Maria Spadaro]]''': Lead Author and Legal History Professor <ref>Spadaro (2024), p. 61.</ref>.
* '''[[Italian Review of Legal History]]''': Academic Journal of Publication <ref>Spadaro (2024), p. 61.</ref>.
* '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': ''[[ENTITY IDENTITY UNCERTAIN|Not found in available sources.]]'' <ref>Spadaro (2024), pp. 61–103.</ref>
* '''[[Geovanny Widya Berlianty P]]''': ''[[ENTITY IDENTITY UNCERTAIN|Not found in available sources.]]'' <ref>Spadaro (2024), pp. 61–103.</ref>

'''Framework of the Relationship Between the Italian Legal Order and the European Union: Integration, Sovereignty, and Counter-Limits Doctrine''' (''Kerangka Kebijakan Hubungan Tatanan Hukum Italia dan Uni Eropa: Integrasi, Kedaulatan, dan Doktrin Kontra-Limit'') is a public law analytical framework and judicial policy outlining the seven-decade evolution of relations between the Italian national legal order and the legal framework of the European Union (EEC/EU). It covers the constitutional foundations (Articles 10, 11, 35, 81, 97, 117, and 119 of the Italian Constitution), the doctrinal development of the Italian Constitutional Court (''Corte Costituzionale'') from dualist separation (*Granital*, *Frontini*) to judicial dialogue and integration via the preliminary ruling mechanism (Article 267 TFEU), the boundaries of national sovereignty (*controlimiti* or counter-limits doctrine), and the constitutional implications of the Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) and the European Stability Mechanism (ESM) <ref>della Cananea, G. (2023). The Italian Legal Order and the European Union: An Evolving Relationship. ''Italian Journal of Public Law'', 15(2), 167–200.</ref>.

== Overview ==
Authored by [[Giacinto della Cananea]], Professor of Administrative Law at [[Bocconi University of Milan]], the study presents a descriptive and interpretative analysis of how the relationship between the Italian legal system and European integration has developed since World War II <ref>della Cananea (2023), p. 167.</ref>. The analysis traces the transition of the Italian Constitutional Court (ICC) from initial resistance to accepting EU law primacy in a coordinated framework established by the landmark *Granital* decision (1984), while reserving the *controlimiti* (counter-limits) doctrine to safeguard core constitutional principles and non-negotiable human rights <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 171–177.</ref>.

== Legal Basis ==
The policy framework rests upon national constitutional norms, supranational treaties, and landmark jurisprudence:
* '''[[Constitution of the Italian Republic (1948)]]''':
** ''Articles 10 & 11'': Establish alignment with international law and authorize limitations of national sovereignty (*limitations of sovereignty*) on equal terms with other states to ensure peace and justice among nations <ref>della Cananea (2023), p. 169.</ref>.
** ''Article 35'': Protects labor rights beyond national boundaries <ref>della Cananea (2023), p. 169.</ref>.
** ''Article 117 (2001 Constitutional Reform)'': Explicitly obligates state and regional legislative powers to comply with EU legal constraints <ref>della Cananea (2023), p. 179.</ref>.
** ''Articles 81, 97, 119 (2012 Constitutional Reform)'': Enshrine the balanced budget rule and debt sustainability in compliance with EMU framework obligations <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 180, 181.</ref>.
* '''[[Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union]] (TFEU)''': Specifically Article 267 governing preliminary ruling requests <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 174, 175.</ref>.
* '''[[Treaty on European Union]] (TEU)''': Article 4(1) safeguarding national identity <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 188, 191.</ref>.
* '''Jurisprudence of the Italian Constitutional Court''': Judgment No. 14/1964 (*Costa v. ENEL*), Judgment No. 183/1973 (*Frontini*), Judgment No. 170/1984 (*Granital*), Judgment No. 238/2013, Judgment No. 115/2018 (*Taricco II*), Judgment No. 20/2019, and Order No. 117/2019 <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 171–177, 184.</ref>.

== Background & European Political Choice ==
Following the fall of fascism, the 1948 Constitution marked a complete departure from authoritarianism and autarky <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 168, 169.</ref>. Post-war statesmen such as [[Alcide De Gasperi]] and [[Gaetano Martino]] anchored Italian foreign policy in European integration, making Italy a founding member of the European Communities (Paris 1952, Rome 1957) supported by a democratic-liberal coalition <ref>della Cananea (2023), p. 170.</ref>.

== Objectives ==
* Provide a durable constitutional foundation for Italian participation in European integration <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 169, 178.</ref>.
* Ensure consistent application of EU law via structured judicial dialogue between the Italian Constitutional Court and the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 174–177.</ref>.
* Balance fiscal discipline required by the Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) with fundamental social rights guarantees <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 180, 182, 183.</ref>.

== Scope ==
The scope spans Italian constitutional law, supranational judicial doctrines, fiscal rules under the EMU, preliminary reference procedures, state immunity exceptions, and parliamentary debates over ratifying the revised ESM Treaty <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 167–199.</ref>.

== Key Provisions & Judicial Doctrines ==
* '''Granital Doctrine (1984) & Primacy of EU Law''': The ICC recognized the primacy and direct applicability (*disapplication*) of EU law without requiring prior constitutional invalidation by the ICC, while reserving the *controlimiti* doctrine to defend fundamental rights and core constitutional principles <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 172, 173.</ref>.
* '''Judicial Dialogue via Preliminary Reference (Article 267 TFEU)''': Italian ordinary judges became among the most active users of preliminary references (1,326 references from 1953 to 2015) <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 174, 175.</ref>. The ICC itself adopted the practice for inter-institutional disputes (Order No. 104/2008) and administrative sanction proceedings concerning the right to silence (*DB v Consob*, Order No. 117/2019) <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 175, 176.</ref>.
* '''Communitarized State vs. National Identity Defense''': The public policy structure transformed Italy into a communitarized state characterized by shared sovereignty, despite ongoing academic debate regarding technical governance, austerity constraints, and social rights protections <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 188, 191, 192.</ref>.

== Policy Debates & ESM Reforms ==
Political and constitutional debate continues over the Italian Parliament's delay in ratifying the revised European Stability Mechanism (ESM) Treaty, reflecting concerns regarding public debt restructuring risks versus commitments to European financial stability mechanisms <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 195–199.</ref>.

== Entity Relationships ==
* '''[[Giacinto della Cananea]]''': Author of the study and Professor of Administrative Law <ref>della Cananea (2023), p. 167.</ref>.
* '''[[Italian Constitutional Court]] (Corte Costituzionale)''': Guardian of national constitutional order and developer of the counter-limits doctrine <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 171, 173.</ref>.
* '''[[Court of Justice of the European Union]] (ECJ/CJEU)''': Supranational judicial authority in preliminary reference dialogue <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 174, 175.</ref>.
* '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': ''Not found in the available sources.'' <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 167–200.</ref>
* '''[[Geovanny Widya Berlianty P]]''': ''Not found in the available sources.'' <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 167–200.</ref>

Il '''Quadro di Kebijakan Hubungan Tatanan Hukum Italia e Unione Europea''' (''Kerangka Kebijakan Hubungan Tatanan Hukum Italia dan Uni Eropa: Integrasi, Kedaulatan, dan Doktrin Kontra-Limit'') è un quadro analitico di diritto pubblico e politica giudiziaria che ricostruisce l'evoluzione, lungo oltre sette decenni, dei rapporti tra l'ordinamento giuridico nazionale italiano e l'ordinamento dell'Unione Europea (CEE/UE). Il quadro analizza le basi costituzionali (Articoli 10, 11, 35, 81, 97, 117 e 119 della Costituzione Italiana), l'evoluzione dottrinale della Corte Costituzionale italiana dal modello dualista (*Granital*, *Frontini*) all'integrazione e al dialogo giurisdizionale tramite il rinvio pregiudiziale (Articolo 267 TFUE), i limiti alla sovranità statale (dottrina dei *controlimiti*), nonché le implicazioni costituzionali dell'Unione Economica e Monetaria (UEM) e del Meccanismo Europeo di Stabilità (MES) <ref>della Cananea, G. (2023). The Italian Legal Order and the European Union: An Evolving Relationship. ''Italian Journal of Public Law'', 15(2), 167–200.</ref>.

== Descrizione ==
Redatto da [[Giacinto della Cananea]], Professore Ordinario di Diritto Amministrativo presso l'[[Università Bocconi di Milano]], lo studio offre un'analisi descrittiva e interpretativa dell'evoluzione dei rapporti tra l'ordinamento italiano e l'integrazione europea dal secondo dopoguerra a oggi <ref>della Cananea (2023), p. 167.</ref>. L'analisi evidenzia il passaggio della Corte Costituzionale (ICC) dalla iniziale chiusura alla piena affermazione del primato del diritto dell'Unione sancito dalla celebre sentenza *Granital* (1984), salvaguardando al contempo la dottrina dei *controlimiti* a tutela dei principi supremi e dei diritti fondamentali della persona <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 171–177.</ref>.

== Base Giuridica ==
Il quadro di politica costituzionale si fonda su fonti nazionali, trattati comunitari e giurisprudenza di riferimento:
* '''[[Costituzione della Repubblica Italiana (1948)]]''':
** ''Articoli 10 e 11'': Sanciscono l'adeguamento al diritto internazionale e consentono limitazioni di sovranità necessarie ad un ordinamento che assicuri la pace e la giustizia fra le Nazioni <ref>della Cananea (2023), p. 169.</ref>.
** ''Articolo 35'': Tutela il lavoro in tutte le sue forme ed applicazioni oltre i confini nazionali <ref>della Cananea (2023), p. 169.</ref>.
** ''Articolo 117 (Riforma Costituzionale del 2001)'': Impone al legislatore statale e regionale il rispetto dei vincoli derivanti dall'ordinamento comunitario <ref>della Cananea (2023), p. 179.</ref>.
** ''Articoli 81, 97, 119 (Riforma Costituzionale del 2012)'': Introducono il principio del pareggio di bilancio e la sostenibilità del debito pubblico in conformità con le regole dell'UEM <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 180, 181.</ref>.
* '''[[Trattato sul Funzionamento dell'Unione Europea]] (TFUE)''': In particolare l'Articolo 267 relativo al rinvio pregiudiziale <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 174, 175.</ref>.
* '''[[Trattato sull'Unione Europea]] (TUE)''': Articolo 4, comma 1, a tutela dell'identità nazionale degli Stati membri <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 188, 191.</ref>.
* '''Giurisprudenza della Corte Costituzionale''': Sentenza n. 14/1964 (*Costa c. ENEL*), Sentenza n. 183/1973 (*Frontini*), Sentenza n. 170/1984 (*Granital*), Sentenza n. 238/2013, Sentenza n. 115/2018 (*Taricco II*), Sentenza n. 20/2019 e Ordinanza n. 117/2019 <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 171–177, 184.</ref>.

== Contesto e Scelta Politica Europea ==
All'indomani della caduta del fascismo, la Costituzione del 1948 ha segnato una rottura fondamentale con l'autoritarismo e l'autarchia <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 168, 169.</ref>. Statisti del dopoguerra come [[Alcide De Gasperi]] e [[Gaetano Martino]] hanno guidato l'adesione dell'Italia tra i Paesi fondatori delle Comunità Europee (Parigi 1952, Roma 1957), sostenuti da una coalizione democratico-liberale <ref>della Cananea (2023), p. 170.</ref>.

== Obiettivi ==
* Fornire un solido fondamento costituzionale alla partecipazione dell'Italia al processo di integrazione europea <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 169, 178.</ref>.
* Garantire l'applicazione uniforme del diritto dell'Unione attraverso il dialogo giurisdizionale tra la Corte Costituzionale e la Corte di Giustizia dell'Unione Europea (CGUE) <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 174–177.</ref>.
* Bilanciare i vincoli della disciplina di bilancio dell'UEM con la salvaguardia dei diritti sociali e fondamentali della persona <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 180, 182, 183.</ref>.

== Ambito di Applicazione ==
L'ambito comprende il diritto costituzionale italiano, la giurisprudenza europea, le regole di finanza pubblica dell'UEM, i rinvii pregiudiziali alla CGUE, le eccezioni all'immunità degli Stati e il dibattito parlamentare sulla ratifica della riforma del Trattato MES <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 167–199.</ref>.

== Disposizioni Chiave e Dottrine Giudiziarie ==
* '''Dottrina Granital (1984) e Primato del Diritto UE''': La Corte Costituzionale ha riconosciuto il primato e l'applicabilità diretta (*disapplicazione*) del diritto comunitario da parte dei giudici comuni, senza previa dichiarazione d'incostituzionalità, facendo salva la dottrina dei *controlimiti* a tutela dei diritti inalienabili e dei principi fondamentali della Costituzione <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 172, 173.</ref>.
* '''Dialogo Giurisdizionale via Rinvio Pregiudiziale (Art. 267 TFUE)''': I giudici ordinari italiani sono risultati tra i più attivi nell'utilizzo del rinvio pregiudiziale (1.326 rinvii nel periodo 1953–2015) <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 174, 175.</ref>. La stessa Corte Costituzionale si è avvalsa del rinvio pregiudiziale per questioni di legittimità nei giudizi principali (Ordinanza n. 104/2008) e in materia di sanzioni amministrative Consob inerenti al diritto al silenzio (*DB c. Consob*, Ordinanza n. 117/2019) <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 175, 176.</ref>.
* '''Stato Comunitarizzato e Identità Nazionale''': L'ordinamento pubblico italiano si è evoluto nella forma dello Stato comunitarizzato a sovranità condivisa (*shared sovereignty*), pur rimanendo aperto il dibattito accademico circa i limiti della tecnocrazia europea, del rigore di bilancio e della difesa dei diritti sociali <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 188, 191, 192.</ref>.

== Criticità Politiche e Riforma del MES ==
Il dibattito politico e costituzionale rimane aperto sull'iter di ratifica della riforma del Trattato sul Meccanismo Europeo di Stabilità (MES) da parte del Parlamento italiano, posizionando le preoccupazioni sul rischio di ristrutturazione del debito pubblico di fronte agli impegni per la stabilità finanziaria europea <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 195–199.</ref>.

== Relazioni tra Entità ==
* '''[[Giacinto della Cananea]]''': Autore dello studio e Professore Ordinario di Diritto Amministrativo <ref>della Cananea (2023), p. 167.</ref>.
* '''[[Corte Costituzionale]]''': Custode della Costituzione e ideatrice della dottrina dei controlimiti <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 171, 173.</ref>.
* '''[[Corte di Giustizia dell'Unione Europea]] (CGUE)''': Autorità giurisdizionale sopranazionale interlocutrice nel dialogo pregiudiziale <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 174, 175.</ref>.
* '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': ''Non presente nelle fonti disponibili.'' <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 167–200.</ref>
* '''[[Geovanny Widya Berlianty P]]''': ''Non presente nelle fonti disponibili.'' <ref>della Cananea (2023), pp. 167–200.</ref>

title: Judicial-policy-italian-family-law-gender-equality-2023
wikitext:
The '''Gender Equality Framework and Substantive Protection in Italian Family Law''' (officially titled ''Equal and Not. A Feminist Perspective on Italian Family Law'') is a legal policy and judicial analysis framework that evaluates the transformation of gender equality from formal to substantive dimensions within Italian family law <ref>Long, J. (2023). Equal and Not. A Feminist Perspective on Italian Family Law. ''The Italian Law Journal'', 9(2), 533–555.</ref>.

== Overview ==
Formulated by [[Joëlle Long]], Associate Professor of Private Law at the [[University of Turin]], this framework distinguishes between formal equality (gender-neutral legal provisions on paper) and substantive equality (de facto reality, where women continue to bear a disproportionate burden of uncompensated domestic labor) <ref>Long (2023), pp. 533–535.</ref>. The study highlights two critical areas where de facto discrimination against women persists in Italy:
# '''Post-Divorce Economic Decisons and Alimony''': The disregard or minimal economic recognition of domestic work and childcare performed by the wife during the marriage <ref>Long (2023), pp. 536, 542–548.</ref>.
# '''Gender-Based Violence and Domestic Abuse''': The phenomenon of "secondary victimization" within civil and family courts, which frequently mandate mediation or shared custody with abusive partners <ref>Long (2023), pp. 549–553.</ref>.

== Legal Basis ==
This policy framework is rooted in national and international legal instruments:
* '''[[Constitution of the Italian Republic|Constitution of the Italian Republic (1948)]]''': Article 2 (human rights), Article 3 (formal and substantive equality), Article 29 (moral and legal equality of spouses), and Article 117 (compliance with international law/ECHR) <ref>Italian Constitution 1948; Long (2023), pp. 540, 542.</ref>.
* '''[[Italian Civil Code|Italian Civil Code]]''': As amended by Sacchi Law No. 1176/1919 (abolition of marital authority), Family Law Reform Law No. 151/1975 (abolition of the husband's role as head of household, introduction of community property under Art. 159, and family business protections under Art. 230-bis) <ref>Italian Civil Code; Long (2023), pp. 539–540, 542–544.</ref>.
* '''[[Cartabia Reform|Cartabia Reform (Legislative Decree 10 October 2022 No. 149)]]''': Amended the Code of Civil Procedure (*Codice di Procedura Civile*, Art. 473-bis series) by inserting specific rules for handling domestic and gender-based violence <ref>Leg. Dec. 149/2022; Long (2023), pp. 536, 550, 552.</ref>.
* '''[[Istanbul Convention|Council of Europe Convention (Istanbul Convention)]]''': Article 3 (definition of gender violence), Article 31 (custody and visitation rights), and Article 48 (prohibition of mandatory mediation in domestic violence cases) <ref>Istanbul Convention; Long (2023), pp. 549–550.</ref>.

== Background ==
The evolution of Italian family law underwent a long transition from the patriarchal structures of Roman Law and the Napoleonic Code toward formal emancipation <ref>Long (2023), pp. 537–539.</ref>. The Constitutional Court of Italy played a pivotal role through Rulings No. 126/1968 and No. 147/1969, which struck down criminal adultery provisions that discriminated against wives <ref>Long (2023), p. 540.</ref>. Regarding surnames, Ruling No. 131/2022 struck down the automatic transmission of the paternal surname, allowing children to bear the surnames of both parents <ref>Long (2023), pp. 541–542.</ref>.

== Objectives ==
* Integrate feminist and intersectional perspectives into family law analysis and judicial practice <ref>Long (2023), pp. 533, 535–536, 553–554.</ref>.
* Ensure divorce financial settlements account for compensatory contributions based on career sacrifices made for the family <ref>Long (2023), pp. 546–548.</ref>.
* Eliminate secondary victimization of mothers and child victims of domestic abuse during custody determinations <ref>Long (2023), pp. 550–553.</ref>.

== Key Provisions ==
* '''Compensatory Function of Divorce Alimony (Assegno Divorzile)''': Following Court of Cassation *Sezioni Unite* Ruling No. 18287/2018, divorce alimony serves a dual support and compensatory-equalizing function to rebalance financial disparities caused by domestic contributions <ref>Court of Cassation No. 18287/2018; Long (2023), pp. 546–547.</ref>.
* '''Prohibition of Mediation in Abuse Cases''': Under the Cartabia Reform (Arts. 473-bis.42 and 473-bis.43 CPC), family conciliation and mediation are strictly prohibited when there are allegations of domestic or gender-based violence <ref>Long (2023), p. 552.</ref>.
* '''Protection of Victim's Residence''': Judges may order the location of a mother and child's new residence to remain confidential from the perpetrator (Art. 473-bis.13 CPC) <ref>Long (2023), p. 552.</ref>.

== Policy Issues and Evidence ==
* '''Rigid Retrospective Burden of Proof''': Post-2018 jurisprudence often imposes an excessively strict burden of proof ("devil's proof") on women to prove specific past career losses incurred for family care <ref>Long (2023), pp. 547–548.</ref>.
* '''Pseudo-Scientific Labels''': Courts and social services have used pseudo-scientific concepts like *Parental Alienation Syndrome* (PAS) to penalize mothers who seek to protect their children from abusive fathers <ref>Long (2023), p. 551.</ref>.
* '''Empirical Context''': ISTAT data shows 74.7% of new Italian marriages opt for the separation of property regime (''separazione dei beni''), reducing the protective buffer of community property <ref>Long (2023), p. 543.</ref>. The Parliamentary Inquiry Commission on Femicide (2021/2022) highlighted that mothers reporting domestic abuse risk losing custody or facing allegations of alienating the child <ref>Long (2023), p. 551.</ref>.

== Related Entities ==
* '''[[Joëlle Long]]''': Primary Author and Associate Professor of Private Law, University of Turin <ref>Long (2023), p. 533.</ref>.
* '''[[University of Turin]]''': Author's affiliated academic institution <ref>Long (2023), pp. 533, 555.</ref>.
* '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': ''[[ENTITY IDENTITY UNCERTAIN|Not found in the provided sources.]]'' <ref>Long (2023), pp. 533–555.</ref>
* '''[[Geovanny Widya Berlianty P]]''': ''[[ENTITY IDENTITY UNCERTAIN|Not found in the provided sources.]]'' <ref>Long (2023), pp. 533–555.</ref>

title: Judicial-policy-italian-legal-communion-2023
wikitext:
== Overview ==
Formulated by [[Dario Scarpa]], Associate Professor of Private Law at the [[University of Milano-Bicocca]], this framework evaluates the matrimonial property communion rules governed by Articles 177–179 of the ''Codice Civile'' (Italian Civil Code) <ref>Scarpa (2023), pp. 579–580.</ref>. The study rejects rigid categorization dogmatism and establishes that assigning property status as joint ownership (*favor comunionis*) or personal exemption (*favor personae*) must be grounded in an axiological interpretation method. This method balances the constitutional principles of family solidarity (Articles 2 and 29 of the Constitution) with individual equality, personal autonomy, and economic initiative (Articles 3 and 41 of the Constitution) <ref>Scarpa (2023), pp. 579, 581, 583, 585, 592.</ref>.

== Legal Basis ==
This policy framework is rooted in core statutory and constitutional instruments:
* '''[[Constitution of the Italian Republic|Constitution of the Italian Republic (1947/1948)]]''': Article 2 (protection of inviolable rights and social solidarity), Article 3 (formal and substantive equality), Article 29 (moral and legal equality of spouses), Article 30 (duties toward children), and Article 41 (freedom of private economic initiative) <ref>Italian Constitution 1947; Scarpa (2023), pp. 580, 581, 583, 586, 587, 591.</ref>.
* '''[[Italian Civil Code|Italian Civil Code (1942)]]''': Article 160 (indisposability of matrimonial rights and duties), Article 177 (objects of immediate community property), Article 178 (deferred/residual community property), and Article 179 (personal property exemptions) <ref>Italian Civil Code 1942; Scarpa (2023), pp. 579, 580, 582, 589, 593–594.</ref>.
* '''[[Family Law Reform Law (1975)|Family Law Reform Law No. 151/1975 (Riforma del Diritto di Famiglia)]]''': Established the legal communion of property as the default statutory regime, replacing the former default system of separation of property <ref>Scarpa (2023), pp. 581, 589.</ref>.

== Background ==
Prior to the 1975 Family Law Reform in Italy, matrimonial property regimes operated under traditional assumptions that often marginalized the economic participation of women and treated wives as economic subordinates <ref>Scarpa (2023), p. 587.</ref>. The 1975 reform established *comunione legale* as the default statutory regime to embody substantive equality between spouses <ref>Scarpa (2023), pp. 581, 587.</ref>. However, because the explicit statutory list in Articles 177–179 of the Civil Code is incomplete and fragmented, extensive doctrinal debate emerged regarding the boundary between joint family property and personal assets <ref>Scarpa (2023), pp. 579, 581, 595.</ref>.

== Objectives ==
* Provide a constitutional, axiologically oriented hermeneutic framework to resolve statutory ambiguities in matrimonial property division <ref>Scarpa (2023), pp. 579, 581.</ref>.
* Proportionately balance family solidarity with individual economic freedom and personal autonomy for each spouse <ref>Scarpa (2023), pp. 581, 583, 585, 591–593.</ref>.
* Eliminate rigid, formalistic dogmatism in categorizing real-world matrimonial financial assets <ref>Scarpa (2023), pp. 581, 582, 589, 594.</ref>.

== Scope ==
The scope of this framework encompasses civil matrimonial property law, rights over professional assets and acquisitions, third-party and creditor protection, and evolving civil jurisprudence in Italy <ref>Scarpa (2023), pp. 579, 583, 585, 592–594.</ref>.

== Key Provisions & Property Schemes ==
* '''Immediate Communion (Article 177 Italian Civil Code)''': Assets acquired jointly or individually by spouses during marriage automatically fall into joint ownership (*comunione immediata*) <ref>Scarpa (2023), p. 589.</ref>.
* '''Deferred / Residual Communion (Articles 177–178 Italian Civil Code)''': Income derived from personal property or individual professional earnings that remain unspent at the time the legal communion dissolves (*comunione de residuo*) <ref>Scarpa (2023), pp. 589, 593.</ref>.
* '''Personal Property Exemptions (Article 179 Italian Civil Code)''': Property owned prior to marriage, gifts and inheritances received during marriage, strictly personal goods, tools required for professional practice, and compensation received for personal or professional damages (*beni personali*) <ref>Scarpa (2023), pp. 592, 594.</ref>.
* '''Automatic Co-ownership vs. Contract Law''': The automatic vesting of co-ownership rights in a non-participating spouse operates as an exception to general contract principles (*pacta sunt servanda* and the relativity of contracts) in order to fulfill family law policy objectives <ref>Scarpa (2023), pp. 586, 589–590.</ref>.

== Implementation ==
Implemented through landmark decisions of the Italian Constitutional Court (such as Ruling No. 311/1988) and the Italian Court of Cassation *Sezioni Unite* (such as Rulings No. 17952/2007 and No. 9523/2010), which established the nature of legal communion as joint ownership without explicit quotas (*comunione senza quote*) <ref>Scarpa (2023), p. 580.</ref>.

== Policy Issues ==
* '''Tension Between Individual Rights and Community Property''': Overly expansive application of joint ownership risks compressing individual economic initiative and professional independence <ref>Scarpa (2023), pp. 585, 589, 593, 594.</ref>.
* '''Statutory Deficiencies''': The explicit enumerations in Articles 177–179 of the Civil Code are incomplete and struggle to encompass complex contemporary economic transactions <ref>Scarpa (2023), pp. 581, 595.</ref>.

== Proposed Reforms ==
Legal scholars advocate for flexible judicial interpretation wherein judges perform a concrete balancing of interests based on reasonableness and proportionality for each specific property dispute <ref>Scarpa (2023), pp. 581, 582, 591, 592, 595.</ref>.

== Related Entities ==
* '''[[Dario Scarpa]]''': Primary Author and Associate Professor of Private Law at the University of Milano-Bicocca <ref>Scarpa (2023), pp. 579, 580.</ref>.
* '''[[University of Milano-Bicocca]]''': Author's affiliated academic institution <ref>Scarpa (2023), pp. 579, 580.</ref>.
* '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': ''[[ENTITY IDENTITY UNCERTAIN|Not found in the available sources.]]'' <ref>Scarpa (2023), pp. 579–596.</ref>
* '''[[Geovanny Widya Berlianty P]]''': ''[[ENTITY IDENTITY UNCERTAIN|Not found in the available sources.]]'' <ref>Scarpa (2023), pp. 579–596.</ref>

The '''Italian Local Public Services Competition Regulation Framework''' is a regulatory and policy framework governing local public service markets in Italy. Analyzed by Fabio Merusi, it evaluates the implementation of the "competition for the market" model, limitations on in-house company exceptions, and market oversight by the Italian Competition Authority (Antitrust Authority) <ref>Merusi, F. (2012). The Troubled Life of Competition in Local Public Services. ''Italian Journal of Public Law'', 4(1), 38–52.</ref>.

== Summary ==
Authored by [[Fabio Merusi]], Professor of Administrative Law at "Guglielmo Marconi" University, this study examines the regulatory dynamics of Italian local public services following the 2008/2009 reforms and the June 2011 referendum <ref>Merusi (2012), pp. 38, 42.</ref>. Due to the historical fragmentation of Italian municipalities originating from the 1859 Rattazzi Law, European Union law introduced "competition for the market" through periodic tenders rather than direct competition within the market <ref>Merusi (2012), pp. 39–40.</ref>.

== Legal Basis ==
The framework relies on national legislation, constitutional rulings, and popular referendums:
* '''[[Article 23-bis of Law No. 112/2008]]''': Initial provision establishing competitive tendering obligations for local public services <ref>Merusi (2012), pp. 41, 42.</ref>.
* '''[[June 2011 Referendum]] & [[Law No. 148/2011]]''': Popular repeal of Article 23-bis, which was subsequently re-enacted in near-identical form via Legislative Decree No. 138/2011 (Law No. 148/2011) <ref>Merusi (2012), p. 42.</ref>.
* '''[[Article 114 & Repeal of Article 130 of the Italian Constitution]]''': Constitutional foundation for local autonomy, creating legal friction with the Antitrust Authority's ex-ante oversight powers <ref>Merusi (2012), pp. 43–44.</ref>.
* '''[[Constitutional Court Judgment No. 326/2010]]''': Jurisprudence establishing market competition as a horizontal state legislative competence <ref>Merusi (2012), p. 47.</ref>.

== Background ==
Implementing the EU competition model encountered significant structural obstacles in Italy because fragmented local municipalities prevented the formation of viable relevant markets <ref>Merusi (2012), pp. 39–40.</ref>. Consequently, municipalities frequently established controlled joint-stock companies (in-house companies) to bypass competitive tendering and public procurement rules <ref>Merusi (2012), pp. 40, 45–46.</ref>.

== Objectives ==
* Ensure transparency, impartiality, and efficiency in managing local public services of economic interest <ref>Merusi (2012), pp. 41, 46–47.</ref>.
* Restrict direct, non-competitive awards to in-house companies exclusively to exceptional economic or geographical situations <ref>Merusi (2012), pp. 42–43.</ref>.
* Secure high-quality private participation in public-private joint ventures by enforcing a minimum 40% private equity requirement <ref>Merusi (2012), pp. 42, 46.</ref>.

== Scope ==
The scope of this framework includes Italian administrative law, European Union competition law, public procurement rules ([[Legislative Decree 163/2006]]), regional autonomy guarantees, and Constitutional Court jurisprudence <ref>Merusi (2012), pp. 38–52.</ref>.

== Core Provisions & Supervisory Mechanisms ==
* '''Competition for the Market''': Public service operations must be awarded via open competitive tenders, requiring the separation of network ownership from operational management (unbundling) <ref>Merusi (2012), pp. 40, 48.</ref>.
* '''Antitrust Authority Approval''': Municipalities seeking to retain an in-house company must publish market analysis justifications and obtain Antitrust Authority approval, except for services valued under €200,000 <ref>Merusi (2012), pp. 43, 45–46.</ref>.
* '''Private Partner Requirements''': Private partners in joint ventures must be selected through public competitive procedures, perform active managerial roles, and hold at least 40% equity share <ref>Merusi (2012), pp. 42, 49.</ref>.

== Implementation ==
Implementation is carried out through municipal tender drafting, calculating investment amortization schedules to set contract durations, and market supervision by the Antitrust Authority <ref>Merusi (2012), pp. 43, 48–49.</ref>.

== Policy Issues ==
* '''Constitutional Oversight Conflicts''': Ex-ante Antitrust Authority review was challenged as an unconstitutional infringement on local autonomy under Article 114 following the repeal of Article 130 <ref>Merusi (2012), pp. 43–44.</ref>.
* '''Subversion of the 2011 Referendum''': Re-enacting competition rules shortly after the popular referendum created prolonged regulatory instability for service providers <ref>Merusi (2012), p. 52.</ref>.

== Reforms & Modifications ==
The framework drives ongoing reforms to clarify tender termination criteria, resolve asset amortization schedules, and settle property transfer disputes upon contract expiration <ref>Merusi (2012), pp. 48–49.</ref>.

== Entity Relationships ==
* '''[[Fabio Merusi]]''': Author of the Academic Study and Professor of Administrative Law <ref>Merusi (2012), p. 38.</ref>.
* '''[[Italian Competition Authority]]''': Ex-Ante Supervisory Body and Competition Regulator <ref>Merusi (2012), pp. 43, 44.</ref>.
* '''[[Italian Constitutional Court]]''': Judicial Interpreter of State Legislative Competence <ref>Merusi (2012), pp. 47, 52.</ref>.
* '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': ''[[ENTITY IDENTITY UNCERTAIN|Not found in available sources.]]'' <ref>Merusi (2012), pp. 38–52.</ref>
* '''[[Geovanny Widya Berlianty P]]''': ''[[ENTITY IDENTITY UNCERTAIN|Not found in available sources.]]'' <ref>Merusi (2012), pp. 38–52.</ref>

'''The Personalist Principle in the Italian Constitution Framework''' is a value framework and foundational constitutional policy of Italian public law that places the human being as a social and relational person (*persona sociale e relazionale*) possessing axiological, logical, and historical priority over public authority, forming the cornerstone of the 1948 Constitution of the Italian Republic, and directing state action toward guaranteeing the full development (*pieno sviluppo*) of human dignity while enforcing mandatory social, economic, and political solidarity duties <ref>Lamarque, E. (2022). The Italian Constitution: A Personalist Constitution. ''Italian Journal of Public Law'', 14(2), 399–425.</ref>.

== Summary ==
Authored by [[Elisabetta Lamarque]], Associate Professor of Constitutional Law at the [[University of Milano-Bicocca]], this analysis examines the origins, substance, and practical application of the personalist principle embedded in the Italian Constitution of January 1, 1948 <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 399, 400.</ref>. Championed by the Catholic faction in the Constituent Assembly (*Assemblea Costituente*) and adopted through cross-party consensus with Marxist and Socialist factions, the principle explicitly rejects totalitarian statism ("the person for the state") as well as atomistic liberal individualism ("the isolated individual"), establishing that the overarching aim of all state authority is the full development of the concrete person within their natural social relationships <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 400, 403, 410–413, 424–425.</ref>.

== Legal Basis ==
The framework is grounded in primary constitutional provisions and foundational texts:
* '''[[Article 2 of the Italian Constitution]]''': Recognizes and guarantees inviolable human rights, both as an individual and in social formations, while demanding the fulfillment of mandatory political, economic, and social solidarity duties <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 400, 401.</ref>.
* '''[[Article 3 of the Italian Constitution]]''': Guarantees equal social dignity (para. 1) and obligates the Republic to remove socio-economic obstacles limiting freedom and equality to ensure the "full development of the human person" (para. 2) <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 401, 402.</ref>.
* '''[[Article 4 of the Italian Constitution]]''': Establishes work as both a fundamental right and a civic duty underpinning the democratic Republic, aimed at personal fulfillment and social progress <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 402, 403.</ref>.
* '''[[Article 118(4) of the Italian Constitution]]''': Enshrines horizontal subsidiarity, reflecting the social nature of the individual (added via the 2001 constitutional reform) <ref>Lamarque (2022), p. 424.</ref>.

== Background & Constituent Assembly Context ==
Following the defeat of Fascist totalitarianism and WWII, the framers integrated communitarian personalism drawing from [[Thomas Aquinas]], the 1943 *Camaldoli Code*, [[Jacques Maritain]], and [[Emmanuel Mounier]] <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 404, 405, 407.</ref>. Within Sub-Committee I of the Constituent Assembly, Catholic delegates ([[Giuseppe Dossetti]], [[Giorgio La Pira]], [[Aldo Moro]]) reached a convergence with Leftist leaders ([[Palmiro Togliatti]], [[Lelio Basso]]) under the leadership of [[Umberto Tupini]] and [[Meuccio Ruini]], positioning human dignity at the center of the constitutional order <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 407–414.</ref>.

== Objectives ==
* Affirm the pre-existing axiological priority of human rights over state power <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 401, 411.</ref>.
* Replace abstract legal subjecthood with the "concrete/social person" <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 401, 415, 416.</ref>.
* Direct public policy and judicial interpretation toward protecting key relational spaces (family, labor, healthcare) <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 417–420.</ref>.

== Scope ==
Covers Italian constitutional law, comparative legal theory, social legislation, and the case law of the Italian Constitutional Court (*Corte Costituzionale*) <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 399–425.</ref>.

== Key Provisions & Statutory Implementation ==
* '''Recognition of the Concrete Person''': Directs state action toward real individuals in their actual life contexts <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 415, 416.</ref>.
* '''Legislative Application''':
** *Family & Child Law*: Adoption Act (Law 184/1983) and shared custody rules (Art. 155 Civil Code) <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 418, 419.</ref>.
** *Gender & Criminal Law*: Transgender Legal Status Act (Law 164/1982) and sexual violence law reform reclassifying offenses against the person (Law 66/1996) <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 417, 418.</ref>.
** *Medical & Disability Law*: Disability Act (Law 104/1992), Palliative Care Act (Law 38/2010), and Advance Care Planning Act (Law 219/2017) <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 419, 420.</ref>.

== Judicial Evidence (Landmark Jurisprudence) ==
* '''Judgment No. 79/2022''': Affirms the constitutional weight of family relationships and child identity in surrogacy contexts <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 420, 421, 425.</ref>.
* '''Judgment No. 114/2019''': Protects donation freedoms for vulnerable adults as an expression of relational solidarity <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 421, 422.</ref>.
* '''Judgment No. 141/2019''': Holds that paid prostitution is an economic activity that can be restricted to safeguard human dignity <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 424, 425.</ref>.
* '''Judgment No. 322/2007''': Prohibits the instrumentalization of individuals for general criminal deterrence without personal fault <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 422, 423.</ref>.

== Policy Issues & Reforms ==
* '''Horizontal Subsidiarity Reform''': The 2001 constitutional amendment to Article 118(4) fosters autonomous civic initiatives for the common good <ref>Lamarque (2022), p. 424.</ref>.
* '''Limits on Self-Determination''': Clarifies that self-determination claims that sever or harm interpersonal relationships and solidarity obligations lack constitutional protection <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 424, 425.</ref>.

== Related Entities ==
* '''[[Elisabetta Lamarque]]''': Author and Constitutional Law Scholar <ref>Lamarque (2022), p. 399.</ref>.
* '''[[Constituent Assembly of Italy]]''': Framers of the 1948 Constitution <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 400, 403.</ref>.
* '''[[Italian Constitutional Court]]''': Judicial guardian of personalism <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 420–425.</ref>.

'''Il Principio Personalista nella Costituzione Italiana''' è un quadro di valori e un principio fondante del diritto pubblico italiano che pone la persona umana, intesa come essere sociale e relazionale, in una posizione di priorità assiologica, logica e storica rispetto al potere statale. Esso costituisce la pietra angolare della Costituzione della Repubblica Italiana del 1948 e orienta l'azione pubblica verso il pieno sviluppo della dignità umana e l'adempimento dei doveri inderogabili di solidarietà sociale, economica e politica <ref>Lamarque, E. (2022). The Italian Constitution: A Personalist Constitution. ''Italian Journal of Public Law'', 14(2), 399–425.</ref>.

== Sintesi ==
Scritto da [[Elisabetta Lamarque]], Rettrice e Professoressa associata di Diritto Costituzionale presso l'[[Università degli Studi di Milano-Bicocca]], lo studio analizza le origini, la sostanza e l'applicazione pratica del principio personalista nella Costituzione italiana del 1948 <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 399, 400.</ref>. Promosso dal gruppo cattolico nell'Assemblea Costituente e accolto trasversalmente dalle componenti marxiste e socialiste, il principio respinge sia lo statismo totalitario ("la persona per lo Stato") sia l'individualismo liberale astratto ("l'individuo isolato"), stabilendo che il fine supremo dell'ordinamento è il pieno sviluppo della persona concreta inserita nelle sue formazioni sociali <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 400, 403, 410–413, 424–425.</ref>.

== Basi Giuridiche ==
Il quadro normativo si fonda sui principali articoli costituzionali:
* '''[[Articolo 2 della Costituzione Italiana]]''': Riconosce e garantisce i diritti inviolabili dell'uomo, sia come singolo sia nelle formazioni sociali, e richiede l'adempimento dei doveri inderogabili di solidarietà politica, economica e sociale <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 400, 401.</ref>.
* '''[[Articolo 3 della Costituzione Italiana]]''': Sancisce la pari dignità sociale (comma 1) e impone alla Repubblica di rimuovere gli ostacoli di ordine economico e sociale per consentire il "pieno sviluppo della persona umana" (comma 2) <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 401, 402.</ref>.
* '''[[Articolo 4 della Costituzione Italiana]]''': Riconosce il lavoro come diritto e dovere fondamentale su cui si fonda la Repubblica democratica <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 402, 403.</ref>.
* '''[[Articolo 118, quarto comma, della Costituzione Italiana]]''': Consacra il principio di sussidiarietà orizzontale (introdotto con la riforma costituzionale del 2001) <ref>Lamarque (2022), p. 424.</ref>.

== Contesto Storico e Assemblea Costituente ==
Dopo il superamento del totalitarismo fascista, i costituenti integrarono la visione del personalismo comunitario attingendo a [[San Tommaso d'Aquino]], al *Codice di Camaldoli* del 1943, a [[Jacques Maritain]] e a [[Emmanuel Mounier]] <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 404, 405, 407.</ref>. Nella Prima Sottocommissione, i giovani esponenti cattolici ([[Giuseppe Dossetti]], [[Giorgio La Pira]], [[Aldo Moro]]) trovarono una convergenza storica con i leader della sinistra ([[Palmiro Togliatti]], [[Lelio Basso]]), coordinati da [[Umberto Tupini]] e [[Meuccio Ruini]], ponendo la dignità della persona al centro della Carta <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 407–414.</ref>.

== Obiettivi ==
* Affermare la priorità assiologica dei diritti preesistenti della persona rispetto allo Stato <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 401, 411.</ref>.
* Sostituire il soggetto di diritto astratto con la "persona concreta e relazionale" <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 401, 415, 416.</ref>.
* Orientare la legislazione e la giurisprudenza alla tutela delle relazioni interpersonali primarie (famiglia, lavoro, salute) <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 417–420.</ref>.

== Ambito di Applicazione ==
Comprende il diritto costituzionale italiano, la teoria generale del diritto, la legislazione sociale e la giurisprudenza della [[Corte Costituzionale]] <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 399–425.</ref>.

== Attuazione Legislativa ==
* '''Normativa sulla Famiglia e sui Minori''': Legge sull'adozione (L. 184/1983) e affidamento condiviso (Art. 155 Codice Civile) <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 418, 419.</ref>.
* '''Identità di Genere e Diritto Penale''': Rettificazione di attribuzione di sesso (L. 164/1982) e riforma dei reati sessuali recepiti come delitti contro la persona (L. 66/1996) <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 417, 418.</ref>.
* '''Salute e Disabilità''': Legge quadro sulla disabilità (L. 104/1992), cure palliative (L. 38/2010) e disposizioni anticipate di trattamento (L. 219/2017) <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 419, 420.</ref>.

== Giurisprudenza Costituzionale ==
* '''Sentenza n. 79/2022''': Tutela delle relazioni familiari e dell'identità del minore nel contesto della maternità surrogata <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 420, 421, 425.</ref>.
* '''Sentenza n. 114/2019''': Salvaguardia della libertà di donazione per gli adulti vulnerabili come espressione di solidarietà relazionale <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 421, 422.</ref>.
* '''Sentenza n. 141/2019''': Conferma della legittimità delle sanzioni contro il reclutamento della prostituzione a tutela della dignità della persona <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 424, 425.</ref>.
* '''Sentenza n. 322/2007''': Divieto di strumentalizzare la persona per esigenze di prevenzione generale in assenza di colpevolezza <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 422, 423.</ref>.

== Entità Correlate ==
* '''[[Elisabetta Lamarque]]''': Autrice dello studio e costituzionalista <ref>Lamarque (2022), p. 399.</ref>.
* '''[[Assemblea Costituente]]''': Organo redattore della Costituzione del 1948 <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 400, 403.</ref>.
* '''[[Corte Costituzionale]]''': Custode giurisdizionale del principio personalista <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 420–425.</ref>.
* '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': ''[[ENTITÀ NON VERIFICABILE|Non presente nelle fonti disponibili.]]'' <ref>Lamarque (2022), pp. 399–425.</ref>
