'''The Troika’s Portuguese Ministry of Justice Civil Enforcement Evaluation Framework''' is a public policy evaluation and judicial reform framework in Portugal. Analyzed by Pedro Miguel Alves Ribeiro Correia and Susana Antas Videira (2016) in the ''International Journal for Court Administration'' (IJCA), Vol. 8 No. 1, it evaluates the long-term impact on civil enforcement actions based on the May 2011 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Portugal and the Troika (IMF/EC/ECB). The empirical study covers the pre-Troika period (January 2007–May 2011), the Troika period (June 2011–March 2014), and the post-Troika period (April 2014–March 2016), documenting a massive backlog reduction of over 360,000 civil enforcement cases [1–6, 19, 28].

== Summary ==
Published by Pedro Miguel Alves Ribeiro Correia and Susana Antas Videira in the IJCA (October 2016), this policy framework presents an independent empirical evaluation of Portugal's judicial reforms following the Troika (IMF/EC/ECB) financial assistance program [1–4]. Analyzing 111 months of official statistical data (January 2007–March 2016) from the Directorate General for Justice Policy (DGPJ) of the Portuguese Ministry of Justice, the study proves that the successful reduction of the civil enforcement actions backlog continued significantly 24 months after the Troika exited Portugal in March 2014 [4, 19, 34–35]. Kruskal-Wallis statistical testing (p = 0.000) confirmed the elimination of more than 360,000 pending cases since the August 2012 peak, an increase in the clearance rate to a median of 142.3% during the post-Troika period, and a reduction in disposition time by 631 days (1 year and 9 months) [19, 22, 24, 30–32].

== Legal Basis ==
* '''Memorandum of Understanding on Specific Economic Policy Conditionality (MoU May 2011):''' The economic and judicial reform agreement between Portugal and the Troika (IMF, European Commission, ECB).
* '''Código de Processo Civil (Lei n.º 41/2013, June 26, 2013):''' The new Portuguese Civil Procedure Code, which eliminated useless legal formalism and accelerated enforcement procedures.
* '''Decreto-Lei n.º 4/2013 (January 11, 2013):''' Temporary regulatory measures designed to eradicate the backlog of civil cases in the courts.
* '''Not found in the available sources:''' Other specific formal statutory regulations are not mentioned in the source text [FACT].

== Background ==
An explosion of private debt and the 2008 economic crisis triggered a surge in civil enforcement claims in Portugal, accumulating a massive case backlog over two decades due to strict adherence to rigid bureaucratic procedures (the ''Barnard & Hayek adaptation problem'').

== Objectives ==
1. Ensure the timely and effective enforcement of contracts to support economic recovery.
2. Reduce the accumulation of civil enforcement backlogs through the simplification of the Civil Procedure Code and judicial map restructuring.
3. Assess the sustainability of the positive judicial reform results during the post-Troika period (2014–2016).

== Scope ==
This policy covers the evaluation of all civil enforcement actions in Portuguese First-Instance Courts (''Tribunais Judiciais de 1ª Instância'') over a 111-month period.

== Key Provisions ==
* '''Pending Cases Reduction:'''
** Slashing over 360,000 pending cases since the August 2012 peak, reaching a median of 974,527 cases in the post-Troika period (dropping below the 1 million case mark).
* '''Post-Troika Clearance Rate Surge:'''
** An increase in the clearance rate from a median of 76.7% (pre-Troika) to 105.9% (Troika) and 142.3% (post-Troika), with 95.8% of post-Troika months recording values above 100%.
* '''Disposition Time Reduction:'''
** A decrease in disposition time by 631 days (from 2,010 days to 1,379 days).

== Implementation ==
* '''Enactment of the New Civil Procedure Code (2013):''' The elimination of useless formalism, restructuring of the judicial map, and strengthening oversight of enforcement agents.
* '''Kruskal-Wallis Econometric Evaluation (DGPJ Data):''' Processing 111 months of official SIEJ statistical data to verify the statistical significance of performance changes.

== Policy Problems ==
* '''Risk of Post-Adjustment Backlog Reversion:''' Initial concerns that the backlog reduction would stall after the Troika program ended in March 2014.
* '''High Disposition Times:''' A disposition time exceeding 1,300 days remains considerably long for business operations.

== Reform / Change ==
* Replicating this SIEJ statistical data-driven public evaluation model for insolvency cases and corporate recovery procedures.
* Maintaining the policies of civil procedure simplification permanently.

== Relationships with Other Entities ==
* '''Directorate General for Justice Policy (DGPJ):''' The administrator of Portugal's official judicial statistical data (SIEJ).
* '''Troika (IMF / EC / ECB):''' The initiators of the reform conditionality targets in the 2011 MoU.
* '''University of Lisbon (ULisboa - ISCSP & Law Faculty):''' The academic institution of the study's authors (Correia & Videira).
* '''[private person]:''' A Law student at Universitas Pembangunan Nasional "Veteran" Jakarta (NIM: 2410611102), specializing in Constitutional Law (Hukum Tata Negara). The intersection of international memorandums and domestic procedural reform provides a highly relevant comparative model for constitutional legal studies. Cecep Mustafa is not found in the available sources [FACT] [1–41].

| status = Implemented / Active
}}

'''The Portuguese Legal Framework of State Liability for Delayed Justice''' is a legal and jurisprudential framework in the Portuguese Republic that regulates the civil and administrative liability of the State for damages caused by the violation of the right to a judicial decision within a reasonable time.

== Summary ==
Issued through a combination of statutory law (Article 12 of the RRCEE) and the progressive jurisprudence of the Portuguese Supreme Administrative Court (''Supremo Tribunal Administrativo'' - STA), this framework extensively integrates the case law of the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR). The policy allows citizens to swiftly file claims for damages against the State through the application of a judicial presumption of ordinary non-material damage and the adoption of standardized ECtHR compensation benchmarks, thereby satisfying the requirement for an effective domestic remedy in accordance with Article 13 of the ECHR [5, 57, 58, 68–74, 79, 80].

== Legal Basis ==
* '''European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR), Article 6(1):''' The right to a fair and public hearing within a reasonable time.
* '''European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR), Article 13:''' The right to an effective remedy before national authorities.
* '''Constitution of the Portuguese Republic (CRP), Article 20(4):''' The constitutional right to a judicial decision within a reasonable time.
* '''Regime of Extra-Contractual Civil Liability of the State (RRCEE / Law No. 67/2007), Article 12:''' Governs the right to compensation for the violation of the reasonable time requirement [12–14].
* '''RRCEE Articles 7, 8, and 10:''' Outlines the four general cumulative conditions for administrative civil liability [14–18].
* '''Portuguese Civil Code (''Código Civil''), Articles 487(2), 496(1), and 563:''' Establishes the ''bonus pater familias'' standard, non-material damage compensation, and the doctrine of adequate causality (''teoria da causalidade adequada'').

== Background ==
For more than three decades, Portuguese courts have faced lawsuits claiming damages for delayed trials, particularly within administrative and tax jurisdictions. Because Portugal has been condemned approximately 50 times by the ECtHR for violating Article 6(1) of the ECHR, national courts were driven to adopt Strasbourg doctrine to prevent recurring international condemnations and to preserve national legal sovereignty under the principle of subsidiarity.

== Objectives ==
1. Fulfill Portugal's international obligations under Articles 6(1) and 13 of the ECHR.
2. Provide a rapid, effective, and predictable domestic remedy mechanism for affected citizens.
3. Achieve the principle of ''restitutio in integrum'' or an equitable financial compensation for the anguish and frustration caused by judicial delays.

== Scope ==
This policy applies across all Portuguese judicial jurisdictions (civil, criminal, administrative, and tax), with a primary focus on damage claims filed in the Supreme Administrative Court (STA) and the Central Administrative Court (TCA) concerning delays in State judicial services.

== Key Provisions ==
* '''Four Cumulative Conditions for State Liability:'''
# ''Illicit Fact:'' The violation of the duty to administer justice within a reasonable time [14–16].
# ''Fault:'' Assessed based on an individual negligence standard (''bonus pater familias'') or anonymous service failure (''abnormal functioning of service / faute de service'') [16–18].
# ''Damage:'' Encompasses both material (patrimonial) and non-material (non-patrimonial) damages.
# ''Causal Link:'' Causality assessment based on Article 563 of the Civil Code.
* '''Four ECtHR Reasonable Time Criteria:''' The duration of a case is assessed based on: (i) the complexity of the case, (ii) the conduct of the authorities/judges, (iii) the conduct of the parties, and (iv) what is at stake for the applicant.
* '''Calculation of Dead Time (''Tempo Morto''):''' Assessing abnormal halts that obstruct the progress of the trial (punctual perspective).

== Implementation ==
* '''Presumption of Ordinary Non-Material Damage:''' Judges apply a judicial presumption (''presunção judicial'') that delayed justice automatically inflicts ordinary moral damage (anxiety, frustration, postponed life plans) on the applicant without requiring individualized proof [58–60, 63, 65].
* '''Standardization of Compensation (Quantum):''' Judges adopt standardized compensation scales developed by the ECtHR in similar cases (e.g., ''Scordino v. Italy'') to ensure equity in damages awarded [68–74].

== Policy Problems ==
* '''Lack of Specific Statutory Rules:''' Article 12 of the RRCEE does not contain a detailed definition of reasonable time criteria or a compensation formula, making the framework heavily reliant on judicial creation and interpretation.
* '''Burden of Proof for Specific Damages:''' Non-material damage exceeding ordinary levels (such as severe clinical depression) is not protected by legal presumption and must be strictly and independently proven by the plaintiff.

== Reform / Change ==
* Dr. Ricardo Pedro recommends the explicit statutory codification of the ECtHR's reasonable time criteria and compensation mechanisms by the Assembly of the Republic to enhance legal certainty.
* Continuous alignment between the jurisprudence of the Portuguese STA and the ECtHR to maintain the status of RRCEE claims as an ''effective domestic remedy'' under Article 13 of the ECHR.

== Relationships with Other Entities ==
* '''ECtHR (Strasbourg):''' The primary reference for ECHR rights interpretation and the provider of compensation quantum standards.
* '''Supreme Administrative Court (STA):''' The principal national court implementing the presumption of damage and ECtHR criteria.
* '''Lisbon Public Law (CIDP):''' The academic affiliation of the author, Dr. Ricardo Pedro.
* '''Cecep Mustafa & [private person]:''' ''Not found in the available sources.'' [FACT] [1–92].

* [[European Court of Human Rights]]
* [[Supremo Tribunal Administrativo]]
* [[International Journal for Court Administration]]

* Pedro, R. (2024). The Portuguese Legal Framework of State Liability for Delayed Justice: The Relevance of ECtHR Case-Law. ''International Journal for Court Administration'', 15(2), 6. DOI: https://doi.org/10.36745/ijca.486.

'''The Troika’s Portuguese Ministry of Justice Civil Enforcement Policy Framework''' is a public policy evaluation framework and reform model for resolving civil enforcement actions. It was formulated by Prof. Dr. Pedro Miguel Alves Ribeiro Correia and Susana Antas Videira (2015) in the ''International Journal for Court Administration'' (IJCA). The framework is based on the implementation of the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU 2011) between Portugal and the Troika (European Commission, European Central Bank, International Monetary Fund). It combines the new Civil Procedure Code reforms (New CPC 2013), electronic bank account attachment, the extinction of unviable cases, and the deployment of specialized operational teams to empirically reduce the judicial backlog across 217 first-instance courts in Portugal [1–16].

== Summary ==
Published by Prof. Dr. Pedro Miguel Alves Ribeiro Correia and Susana Antas Videira in the ''International Journal for Court Administration'' (IJCA), this policy framework reviews the successful experiment of Portugal's judicial sector reforms under the conditions of the Troika's international financial assistance (2011–2014). Analyzing a 78-month sample (2008–2014) across 217 court districts, the empirical study proves that the reforms introduced by the New Civil Procedure Code (Law 41/2013) and Decree-Law 4/2013 successfully slashed a backlog of over 210,000 cases. Through the automation of debtor bank account attachments (Articles 749(6) & 780 CPC) and the extinction of cases lacking asset prospects (Article 849 CPC), the judicial clearance rate soared from 71.2% to 116.4%, while the disposition time was dramatically reduced by 743 days (more than 2 years) [10–12, 38–40].

== Legal Basis ==
* '''Memorandum of Understanding on Specific Economic Policy Conditionality (MoU 2011):''' The international agreement of May 17, 2011, between Portugal and the Troika (IMF/EC/ECB) mandating judicial sector reforms.
* '''Decreto-Lei n.º 4/2013 (January 11, 2013):''' Government regulations regarding temporary measures to clear the old case backlog [15–16].
* '''Lei n.º 41/2013 (June 26, 2013 - New Civil Procedure Code / CPC):''' New provisions relating to electronic bank account attachment (Articles 749(6) & 780), case extinction (Article 849), and the prohibition of dual filings (Article 85) [9–12].
* '''Not found in the available sources:''' Other specific formal statutory regulations are not mentioned in the source text [FACT].

== Background ==
The global economic crisis triggered widespread over-indebtedness in Portugal, leading to a surge in civil enforcement lawsuits that amassed a backlog of over 1.2 million pending cases by 2012. The Troika's financial bailout required the clearance of this backlog to restore legal certainty for the economy [7–8, 35–37].

== Objectives ==
1. Drastically reduce the civil enforcement backlog [3–5, 8].
2. Automate asset attachment through the national electronic banking system [9–10].
3. Extinguish unviable enforcement actions.
4. Accelerate the disposition time without compromising the legal guarantees for debtors.

== Scope ==
This policy covers the handling of civil enforcement cases across 217 first-instance courts (''concelhos'') throughout Portugal.

== Key Provisions ==
* '''Electronic Bank Account Attachment (Articles 749(6) & 780 CPC):'''
** The Bank of Portugal is mandated to provide debtor account data to enforcement agents for electronic blocking to settle debts.
* '''New Grounds for Case Extinction (Article 849 CPC):'''
** Automatic extinction if no attachable assets are found within 3 months, if salary/income attachments flow directly to the creditor, or if total freezing occurs due to competing creditors [11–13].
* '''Revoking the Enforcement Strength of Private Documents:'''
** Private documents without notarial authentication no longer hold direct enforcement power, serving to protect debtors.
* '''Establishment of Specialized Operational Teams:'''
** The deployment of specialized teams in Lisbon, Porto, Gaia, Maia, and Oeiras to handle debts under €10,000.

== Implementation ==
* '''Implementation of the New CPC (September 2013):''' Operationalization of electronic bank account freezing and automatic case extinction across all district courts.
* '''Mann-Whitney Statistical Evaluation:''' The testing of 6 primary variables that proved a significant reduction in disposition time and procedural balance [37–40].

== Policy Problems ==
* '''Commercial and Family Over-indebtedness:''' The burden of mass debt collection stemming from past credit facilitation [7–8].
* '''Unviable Enforcement Cases:''' Thousands of pending cases lacking debtor assets that overburdened court capacity.

== Reform / Change ==
* Transformation of civil enforcement from a manual bureaucratic system to electronic automation based on banking integration [9–10].

'''Right to Know One's Genetic Origins & Anonymity Regulation Framework in Italy''' (''The Right to Know One’s Genetic Origins: A Right in Need of Regulation'') is a family law and bio-law analytical framework formulated by Sabrina Praduroux. It evaluates an individual's fundamental right to know their genetic and biographical origins within the contexts of anonymous childbirth (''parto anonimo'') and donor insemination (''fecondazione eterologa'') <ref>Praduroux, S. (2021). The Right to Know One’s Genetic Origins: A Right in Need of Regulation. ''The Italian Law Journal'', 7(2), 803–820.</ref>. The framework examines the collision between personal identity rights and the anonymity rights of mothers or donors <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 803, 808, 811.</ref>; analyzes key jurisprudence from the Italian Constitutional Court (''Corte Costituzionale'' Judgment Nos. 278/2013, 162/2014), the Court of Cassation (''Corte di Cassazione'' Plenary Session Judgment No. 1946/2017; Judgment Nos. 15024/2016, 22838/2016, 19824/2020), and the European Court of Human Rights (''Godelli v. Italy'', ''Odièvre v. France'', ''Paradiso and Campanelli v. Italy'') <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 805, 811, 812–815, 817.</ref>; and assesses the judicial branch's role as a "surrogate legislature" arising from parliamentary inaction in Italy <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 813, 814, 820.</ref>.

== Overview ==
Authored by [[Sabrina Praduroux]] (Assistant Professor of Comparative Private Law at the Department of Law, University of Turin), this study maps the legal evolution of the right to personal identity and knowledge of biological origins in Italy <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 803, 808.</ref>. Modern family law has increasingly shifted legal filiation from biological truth toward the intent/will to parent <ref>Praduroux (2021), p. 804.</ref>. Nevertheless, the right to know one's genetic origins has gained strength as an inviolable component of personal identity protected under Article 2 of the Italian Constitution and Article 8 of the ECHR <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 804, 808.</ref>.

The analysis focuses on two primary areas of conflict:
# '''Anonymous Childbirth (Parto Anonimo):''' Legally protected under Italian regulation with a 100-year secrecy rule on maternal records <ref>Praduroux (2021), p. 810.</ref>.
# '''Gamete Donor Anonymity:''' Absolute anonymity rules applying to heterologous medically assisted reproduction <ref>Praduroux (2021), p. 817.</ref>.

Following rulings by the ECtHR (''Godelli v. Italy'') and the Corte Costituzionale (Judgment No. 278/2013), legislative stagnation forced the Court of Cassation (''Corte di Cassazione'') to step in as a "surrogate legislature" to establish procedures for confidential judicial interpellations of anonymous mothers and the expiration of anonymity rights post-mortem <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 811, 813–815.</ref>.

== Legal Basis ==
* '''Constitution of the Italian Republic (Costituzione della Repubblica Italiana)''':
** ''Article 2'': Protection of the inviolable rights of the human person <ref>Praduroux (2021), p. 808.</ref>.
** ''Article 29(1)'': Recognition of the family as a natural society founded on marriage <ref>Praduroux (2021), p. 805.</ref>.
** ''Article 117(1)'': Constitutional review based on international treaty compliance (ECHR) <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 805, 818.</ref>.
* '''Italian Legislation''':
** ''DPR November 3, 2000, No. 396 (Art. 30)'': Right of mothers to give birth anonymously <ref>Praduroux (2021), p. 810.</ref>.
** ''Law May 4, 1983, No. 184 (Art. 28, as amended by Law 149/2001)'': Access to origins for adoptees and anonymous mother exceptions <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 809, 810.</ref>.
** ''Legislative Decree June 30, 2003, No. 196 (Privacy Code, Art. 93(2))'': 100-year secrecy rule for medical records of anonymous mothers <ref>Praduroux (2021), p. 810.</ref>.
** ''Law February 19, 2004, No. 40 & Law December 23, 2014, No. 190'': Heterologous insemination framework and gamete donor registries <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 817, 818.</ref>.
* '''International Instruments & Key Rulings''':
** ''European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR)'': Article 8 (Right to respect for private and family life) <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 804, 808.</ref>.
** ''UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (1989)'': Article 7 (Right to know one's parents) <ref>Praduroux (2021), p. 804.</ref>.
** ''Corte Costituzionale Judgment Nos. 278/2013 & 162/2014'' <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 808, 811, 817.</ref>.
** ''Corte di Cassazione (Plenary Session) Judgment No. 1946/2017'' <ref>Praduroux (2021), p. 813.</ref>.

== Core Provisions & Jurisprudential Pillars ==
1. '''Unconstitutionality of Irreversible Anonymity (Judgment No. 278/2013):''' The Constitutional Court struck down Article 28(7) of Law No. 184/1983 for permanently denying adopted children the ability to check if the birth mother would voluntarily waive anonymity later in life <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 812, 813.</ref>.
2. '''Judiciary as Surrogate Legislature (Judgment No. 1946/2017):''' In response to parliamentary inaction, the Court of Cassation ruled that ordinary judges hold the authority to conduct confidential interpellations to ask birth mothers if they consent to revoking secrecy. If the mother refuses, anonymity remains irrevocable <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 813, 814.</ref>.
3. '''Post-Mortem Expiration of Anonymity Rights (Judgment Nos. 15024/2016 & 19824/2020):''' The right to anonymity is personal and expires upon the mother's death. Descendants are consequently entitled to access biological identity data without infringing upon inheritance rights or family reputation <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 814–816.</ref>.

'''Quadro Politico sul Diritto di Conoscere le Proprie Origini Genetiche e Anonimato in Italia''' (''The Right to Know One’s Genetic Origins: A Right in Need of Regulation'') è un quadro di analisi di diritto di famiglia e biodiritto formulato da Sabrina Praduroux. Il quadro valuta il diritto fondamentale dell'individuo di conoscere le proprie origini genetiche e biografiche nel contesto del parto anonimo e della fecondazione eterologa con donatore <ref>Praduroux, S. (2021). The Right to Know One’s Genetic Origins: A Right in Need of Regulation. ''The Italian Law Journal'', 7(2), 803–820.</ref>; analizza il conflitto tra il diritto all'identità personale e il diritto all'anonimato della madre o del donatore <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 803, 808, 811.</ref>; esamina la giurisprudenza della Corte Costituzionale (Sentenze n. 278/2013, n. 162/2014), della Corte di Cassazione (Sezioni Unite Sentenza n. 1946/2017; Sentenze n. 15024/2016, n. 22838/2016, n. 19824/2020) e della Corte Europea dei Diritti dell'Uomo / CEDU (''Godelli c. Italia'', ''Odièvre c. Francia'', ''Paradiso e Campanelli c. Italia'') <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 805, 811, 812–815, 817.</ref>; e studia il ruolo della giurisprudenza come "legislatore surrogato" a causa dell'inerzia del Parlamento italiano <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 813, 814, 820.</ref>.

== Sintesi ==
Scritto da [[Sabrina Praduroux]] (Ricercatrice di Diritto Privato Comparato presso il Dipartimento di Giurisprudenza dell'Università degli Studi di Torino), lo studio traccia l'evoluzione del diritto all'identità personale e alla conoscenza delle origini biologiche in Italia <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 803, 808.</ref>. Nel diritto di famiglia contemporaneo, la determinazione dello stato di figlio si è progressivamente spostata dalla verità biologica pura verso la volontà di essere genitori <ref>Praduroux (2021), p. 804.</ref>. Tuttavia, il diritto di conoscere le proprie origini genetiche si è consolidato come componente inviolabile dell'identità personale protetta dall'Articolo 2 della Costituzione e dall'Articolo 8 della CEDU <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 804, 808.</ref>.

L'analisi individua due ambiti principali di conflitto:
# '''Parto Anonimo:''' Tutelato dalla normativa italiana con un segreto di 100 anni sui dati cartografici e medici della madre <ref>Praduroux (2021), p. 810.</ref>.
# '''Anonimato del Donatore di Gameti:''' Regola di anonimato assoluto applicata alla procreazione medicalmente assistita di tipo eterologo <ref>Praduroux (2021), p. 817.</ref>.

A seguito delle pronunce della CEDU (''Godelli c. Italia'') e della Corte Costituzionale (Sentenza n. 278/2013), l'inerzia del Parlamento ha spinto la Corte di Cassazione ad agire come "legislatore surrogato", stabilendo le procedure di interpello riservato della madre e la decadenza del diritto all'anonimato post-mortem <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 811, 813–815.</ref>.

== Base Giuridica ==
* '''Costituzione della Repubblica Italiana''':
** ''Articolo 2'': Tutela dei diritti inviolabili dell'uomo <ref>Praduroux (2021), p. 808.</ref>.
** ''Articolo 29, comma 1'': Riconoscimento della famiglia come società naturale fondata sul matrimonio <ref>Praduroux (2021), p. 805.</ref>.
** ''Articolo 117, comma 1'': Controllo di costituzionalità sugli obblighi internazionali (CEDU) <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 805, 818.</ref>.
* '''Legislazione Italiana''':
** ''DPR 3 novembre 2000, n. 396 (Art. 30)'': Diritto della madre di non essere nominata nell'attestazione di nascita <ref>Praduroux (2021), p. 810.</ref>.
** ''Legge 4 maggio 1983, n. 184 (Art. 28, modificato dalla Legge 149/2001)'': Accesso alle informazioni sulle origini del minore adottato <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 809, 810.</ref>.
** ''Decreto Legislativo 30 giugno 2003, n. 196 (Codice della Privacy, Art. 93, comma 2)'': Segreto di 100 anni sulla cartella clinica della madre anonima <ref>Praduroux (2021), p. 810.</ref>.
** ''Legge 19 febbraio 2004, n. 40 e Legge 23 dicembre 2014, n. 190'': Fecondazione eterologa e Registro Donatori <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 817, 818.</ref>.
* '''Strumenti Internazionali e Giurisprudenza''':
** ''Convenzione Europea dei Diritti dell'Uomo (CEDU)'': Articolo 8 (Diritto al rispetto della vita privata e familiare) <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 804, 808.</ref>.
** ''Convenzione ONU sui Diritti dell'Infanzia (1989)'': Articolo 7 (Diritto del fanciullo di conoscere i propri genitori) <ref>Praduroux (2021), p. 804.</ref>.
** ''Corte Costituzionale Sentenze n. 278/2013 e n. 162/2014'' <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 808, 811, 817.</ref>.
** ''Corte di Cassazione (Sezioni Unite) Sentenza n. 1946/2017'' <ref>Praduroux (2021), p. 813.</ref>.

== Principi Giurisprudenziali Fondamentali ==
1. '''Incostituzionalità dell'Anonimato Irreversibile (Sentenza n. 278/2013):''' La Corte Costituzionale ha dichiarato illegittimo l'Art. 28, comma 7, della Legge 184/1983 nella parte in cui non prevede la possibilità per il giudice di verificare la persistenza della volontà di anonimato della madre su richiesta del figlio <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 812, 813.</ref>.
2. '''La Cassazione come Legislatore Surrogato (Sentenza n. 1946/2017):''' Di fronte al silenzio del legislatore, le Sezioni Unite della Cassazione hanno stabilito che il giudice di merito può procedere all'interpello riservato della madre per chiedere la revoca del segreto. Se la madre conferma il diniego, l'anonimato rimane definitivo <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 813, 814.</ref>.
3. '''Estinzione dell'Anonimato con la Morte della Madre (Sentenze n. 15024/2016 e n. 19824/2020):''' Il diritto all'anonimato ha natura personalissima e si estingue con la morte del titolare; di conseguenza, il figlio ha diritto di accedere ai dati biologici maternali post-mortem <ref>Praduroux (2021), pp. 814–816.</ref>.

'''The Development and Role of the Court Administrator in Canada Policy Framework''' is a judicial administration policy framework and comparative study on the evolution of the trial court administrator role in Canada and the United States. Formulated by Pamela Ryder-Lahey (Director of Court Services, Newfoundland) and Prof. Peter H. Solomon, Jr. (University of Toronto), it outlines the transition from traditional court management by judges or local clerks toward an executive partnership model between the Chief Judge and the professional Court Administrator, guided by a public service ethos, caseflow management, and core competencies based on ACCA/NACM standards.

== Summary ==
Published by Pamela Ryder-Lahey and Prof. Peter H. Solomon, Jr. in the ''International Journal for Court Administration'' (IJCA), this policy framework examines the history of court administration modernization in Canada and the United States since the 1970s. Overcoming the weaknesses of traditional systems managed by judges or elected clerks, Canada developed the profession of the court administrator, working within an executive partnership model alongside the Chief Judge. This framework emphasizes that judicial independence is not compromised by executive administration (as affirmed by the Supreme Court of Canada in ''Valente v. The Queen'' 1985), and highlights three core pillars: executive partnership, a user-friendly public service ethos, and integrated caseflow management.

== Legal Basis ==

* '''Supreme Court of Canada Decision: Valente v. The Queen (1985 2 S.C.R. 273):''' Establishes the constitutional standard that judicial independence only requires judicial control over direct adjudicative functions (judge assignments, trial scheduling, courtroom allocation), while operational administrative functions can be managed jointly with the executive branch.
* '''Report of the Ontario Courts Inquiry (Justice Thomas Zuber, 1987):''' Outlines the doctrine of shared responsibility and collaborative meetings between judges and court staff.
* '''Provincial Court Act (Province of Newfoundland and Labrador):''' Regulates the position of court staff as employees of the Department of Justice while simultaneously serving as Officers of the Court.
* '''Not found in the available sources:''' Other specific formal statutory regulations are not mentioned in the source text.

== Background ==
Before 1970, courts in Canada were managed in a fragmented manner ("a fractured mosaic of individual fiefdoms") by judges lacking management training. Surging caseloads drove the adoption of professional trial court administrators trained through academic programs (such as Brock University in 1980) and guided by pioneering literature by Millar & Baar (1981).

== Objectives ==

1. Build an executive partnership model between the Chief Judge and the Court Administrator.
2. Establish user-friendly courts grounded in a public service ethos.
3. Accelerate dispute resolution through caseflow management systems and compulsory mediation.
4. Elevate the professional standards of court administrators through the ACCA/NACM core competencies framework.

== Scope ==
This policy applies to all levels of provincial courts and superior courts in Canada, and serves as a comparative reference for the United States judicial system.

== Key Provisions ==

* '''Executive Partnership Model:'''
 Although formally reporting to the Ministry of Justice (dual subordination), court administrators work on a daily basis in functional equality with the Chief Judge to manage case allocation, staff, and budgets.
* '''Nine ACCA Core Competencies:'''

# Purposes and Responsibilities of Courts.

# Leadership.

# Caseflow Management.

# Information Technology Management.

# Court and Community Communications.

# Human Resource Management.

# Resources, Budget and Finance.

# Education, Training and Development.

# Strategic Planning.

* '''User-Friendly Services and Facilities:'''
 ''Child-Friendly Facilities:'' Dedicated waiting rooms equipped with closed-circuit television (CCTV) and child-sized courtrooms without high podiums.
 ''Self-Service Family Law Centre:'' Free self-service assistance for unrepresented litigants at the Ottawa Courthouse.
 ''Tech-Friendly Courtrooms:'' Provision of direct computer and internet network access for real-time legal precedent research.
* '''Toronto Region Case Management (Superior Court of Justice):'''
 Dispute oversight by a Case Management Master, mandatory mediation within 3 months, and settlement conferences within 6–9 months prior to trial.

== Implementation ==

* '''Newfoundland and Labrador Practice:''' The Director of Court Services manages daily operations alongside the Chief Judge, while consultations with the Deputy Minister of Justice focus strictly on budget submissions.
* '''Ontario Five-Year Plan (2002–2007):''' Implementation of service standards that are evaluated on a periodic basis.

== Policy Problems ==

* '''Dual Subordination:''' The structural position of the court administrator caught between the directives of the Chief Judge and executive ministry regulations.
* '''Civil Delay and Cost of Access:''' The core challenges identified by the CBA Task Force (1995) that prompted the creation of the Canadian Forum on Civil Justice.

== Reform / Change ==

* Institutionalization of compulsory mediation in family and general civil cases.
* Transition of courts from rigid adjudication institutions into public service bodies focused on citizen satisfaction.

== Relationships with Other Entities ==

* '''Association of Canadian Court Administrators (ACCA):''' The professional organization developing competency standards for Canadian court administrators.
* '''Department of Justice / Ministry of the Attorney General:''' The executive body providing funding and provincial court administrative staff.

'''The Selecting and Hiring Psychologically Fit Probation Officers Policy Framework''' is a judicial human resources and psychological evaluation framework formulated by D. Scott Herrmann, Ph.D., ABPP (Superior Court of Arizona) and Scott Bedwell, Ph.D. (PDRI/CEB). Based on the predictive validity testing of the ''PsychEval Personality Questionnaire / Protective Services Report Plus'' (PEPQ / PSR Plus) instrument on 262 probation officer candidates (202 pre-employment candidates and 60 incumbents applying for firearms authorization), it aims to predict the risk of critical incidents, separate the probation function from pure policing, and strengthen accountability standards in court administration risk management.

== Summary ==
Published in the ''International Journal for Court Administration'' (IJCA) Vol. 6 No. 1 (June 2014), this research provides the first empirical predictive evidence regarding the reliability of specialized psychological testing tools for prospective court probation officers. Given the rapid growth of probation services in the US and Europe and the expanding authority for probation officers to carry firearms (operational in 83 of 94 U.S. federal judicial districts), the study emphasizes that police selection instruments cannot be directly equated with probation. Through a logistic regression model on 262 candidates in Arizona, the PEPQ / PSR Plus instrument proved significantly capable of predicting critical incidents and poor performance.

== Legal Basis ==
* '''EEOC Enforcement Guidance on Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA 1995, 1997, 2000):''' Regulates that psychological evaluations measuring pathological dimensions (such as Part II of the PEPQ) are only legally permissible after a candidate receives a conditional offer of employment.
* '''Peace Officer Standards & Training Board (P.O.S.T.) Certification:''' The standard provisions for certifying law enforcement officers in U.S. states.
* '''Federal Judicial Districts Firearms Authorization Policy:''' Provisions in 83 out of 94 federal judicial districts that grant firearms authorization to probation officers.
* '''Other Specific Formal Statutory Regulations:''' Not found in the available sources.

== Background ==
The expansion of probation services in the US and Europe has not been matched by the availability of scientific research on specialized psychological evaluations for probation officers. This gap poses a high risk because the failure to screen out psychologically unfit candidates can endanger the safety of the courts and the public.

== Objectives ==
1. Empirically test the predictive validity of the PEPQ / PSR Plus instrument to screen out unfit probation officer candidates.
2. Identify the functional and philosophical orientation differences between police officers and probation officers.
3. Provide an evidence-based psychological screening standard for court HR managers.

== Scope ==
This policy applies to judicial HR administration units, adult/juvenile probation agencies in the Superior Court of Arizona, the U.S. federal judicial system, and European judiciaries.

== Key Provisions ==
* '''Primary Predictive Indicators of Critical Incidents:'''
** ''Alienation and Perceptual Distortion (AP Scale):'' Each 1-unit increase on the AP scale increases the risk of a critical incident by '''36%'''.
** ''Interpersonal Relations (IR Composite):'' Each 1-unit increase on the IR composite scale decreases the risk of a critical incident by '''62%'''.
** ''Intellectual Efficiency (IE Composite):'' Each 1-unit increase on the IE composite scale decreases the risk of a critical incident by '''50%'''.
* '''Intellectual Protective Effect:''' A high Intellectual Efficiency (IE) score (Sten 9–10) has been proven to buffer and neutralize the negative impact of perceptual distortion risks.
* '''Blind Evaluation Procedure:''' The evaluation involves 325 PEPQ items and a 50-minute clinical interview that does not provide direct feedback to the candidates.

== Implementation ==
* '''Arizona Sample Testing:''' Operationalized on 262 subjects (202 pre-employment candidates and 60 incumbent applicants for firearms authorization) with a critical incident evaluation base rate of 14.9%.
* '''Informed Consent & Ethics:''' All candidates signed informed consent documents for the use of anonymized data in judicial administration research.

== Policy Problems ==
* '''The Danger of Generalizing Police Selection Tools:''' The unsuitability of directly adopting police tests for probation due to the differing functions of rehabilitation versus law enforcement.
* '''Consequences of Selection Failure:''' The risk of severe violations and firearms misuse by unstable probation officers.

== Reform / Change ==
* Mandatory adoption of psychological screening instruments specifically validated for the probation population (''evidence-based selection'').
* Integration of ''fitness for duty'' psychological assessments for incumbents applying for firearms authorization.

* '''International Journal for Court Administration (IJCA):''' The official journal publishing the policy framework.

'''The Public Trust In The Judiciary And Judicial Elections Policy Framework''' is a comparative policy analysis of judicial legitimacy and recruitment formulated by Philip Langbroek (Managing Editor of the IJCA). It compares the transparency issues of lifetime judicial appointments in Continental Europe (the Netherlands, France, Germany), partisan/parliamentary judicial elections in Switzerland (at federal and cantonal levels), business-sponsored judicial elections in U.S. states, and the Arizona hybrid model (''merit selection + performance evaluation + retention elections'') to strengthen public trust and judicial legitimacy [2–7].

== Summary ==
Published by Philip Langbroek in the ''International Journal for Court Administration'' (IJCA) Vol. 5 No. 2 (October 2013), this editorial analyzes judicial legitimacy through a comparison of judicial selection methods in Europe and the United States [1–3]. Sparked by a Dutch politician's proposal to implement 6-year judicial terms or judicial elections following a racism trial, Langbroek examines the flaws of opaque lifetime appointments in Europe and the bias risks of business-sponsored judicial elections in the U.S. [2–3, 6–8]. The policy framework highlights the ''Arizona Model'' as the ideal middle ground between merit-based recruitment and public accountability.

== Legal Basis ==
* '''Constitutions of Continental European States (Netherlands, France, Germany):''' The foundation for lifetime judicial appointments (''appointed for life'') to guarantee judicial independence.
* '''Swiss Federal Constitution (Bundesverfassung):''' Rules regarding the appointment of federal judges by the Parliament for an initial 6-year term with proportional representation based on language and political party [4–5].
* '''Arizona Judicial Recruitment and Retention System:''' A combination of initial merit-based recruitment (''merit selection'') and transparent performance evaluations leading up to ''retention elections'' [7–8].
* '''Other Specific Formal Statutory Regulations:''' Not found in the available sources.

== Background ==
Rising public doubts regarding the independence of judges in the Netherlands prompted discussions on conditional judicial appointments or judicial elections. Although holding judicial elections in Europe is largely considered contrary to the constitutional tradition of lifetime appointments, the lack of transparency in selection committees in the Netherlands and Switzerland has triggered questions regarding public legitimacy.

== Objectives ==
1. Analyze the relationship between judicial recruitment methods, accountability, and public trust in the judiciary.
2. Compare the advantages and disadvantages of lifetime appointments (Netherlands), parliamentary/proportional elections (Switzerland), and direct partisan elections (USA) [3–7].
3. Explore the adoption of the Arizona hybrid model to strengthen European judicial legitimacy.

== Scope ==
This policy covers a comparative study of the judiciaries in the Netherlands, Switzerland, France, Germany, and the United States (specifically Arizona and Wisconsin).

== Key Provisions ==
* '''European Lifetime Appointments:''' Guarantees judicial independence but is criticized because committee selection procedures are "not particularly transparent."
* '''Swiss Proportional System:''' Federal judges are elected by parliament for 6-year terms based on a proportional quota of 4 language groups and political parties [4–5].
* '''Campaign Donor Risks in the U.S.:''' Partisan judicial elections in the U.S. require expensive campaigns; Joana Shepherd's research proves that business-sponsored judges tend to rule in favor of corporate interests [6–8].
* '''The Arizona Hybrid Model:''' Initial merit selection combined with transparent performance evaluations; poorly performing judges usually "quietly resign" before facing a retention election [7–8].

== Implementation ==
* '''Dutch Selection Procedure:''' Administered by a joint committee of the Ministry of Justice and the ''Council for the Judiciary'' via legal exams, psychological assessments, and postgraduate training.
* '''Arizona Supreme Court Presentation in Oñati (2013):''' An exposition on the success of the Arizona system by Chief Justice Rebecca White Berch in Spain [7–8].

== Policy Problems ==
* '''Limited Selection Transparency:''' European public criticism that politicians prioritize recruiting allies ("appointing friends to judicial posts").
* '''Donor Conflict of Interest:''' The erosion of judicial neutrality in the U.S. due to judges' reliance on business campaign contributions [7–8].

== Reform / Change ==
* Adopting a transparent individual judicial performance evaluation system without sacrificing the guarantee of lifetime tenure.
* Conducting fundamental European research regarding the relationship between citizens and judicial institutions.

== Relationships with Other Entities ==
* '''International Journal for Court Administration (IJCA):''' The official journal publishing the policy analysis.
* '''Council for the Judiciary (Netherlands):''' The Dutch judicial management body responsible for judicial quality.
* '''[private person]:''' A Law student at Universitas Pembangunan Nasional "Veteran" Jakarta (NIM: 2410611102), specializing in Constitutional Law (Hukum Tata Negara). Cecep Mustafa is not found in the available sources [1–8].

The '''"Legal Metrics Extracted from Court Decisions: A Focus on Personal Injury Compensation"''' framework (''Kerangka Kebijakan Ekstraksi Metrik Hukum dari Putusan Peradilan dan Evaluasi Proyek Datajust Prancis'') is a jurimetrics and judicial artificial intelligence analytical framework formulated by Christophe Quézel-Ambrunaz and Vincent Rivollier in *The Italian Law Journal* (Vol. 10 Nos. 01-02/2024, pp. 21–42) to evaluate the extraction of legal metrics from judicial decisions in France <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz, C., & Rivollier, V. (2024). Legal Metrics Extracted from Court Decisions. A Focus on Personal Injury Compensation. ''The Italian Law Journal'', 10(1-2), 21–42.</ref>; examines the legal (pseudonymisation, personal data protection) and technical barriers (format heterogeneity, unstructured layout, "black box" judicial reasoning) in implementing judicial open data under the *Digital Republic Act 2016*, Statute 2019-222, and *Decree 2021-1276* <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 22, 23, 26, 27.</ref>; analyzes the failure of the French Ministry of Justice's *Datajust* predictive compensation modeling project (2020–2022) <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 35, 36, 40.</ref>; and evaluates the prospects of digital judicial transformation through the Court of Cassation's automated pseudonymisation algorithms, case file orientation modules (*JuriBERT*), and the unified civil information system reform (*Portalis Project*) <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 41, 42.</ref>.

== Summary ==
Authored by [[Christophe Quézel-Ambrunaz]] and [[Vincent Rivollier]] (Professor and Associate Professor of Law at University Savoie Mont Blanc), this study examines the methodological challenges of extracting quantitative legal metrics from court rulings <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 21, 22.</ref>. Although the *Digital Republic Act 2016* mandates phased judicial open data, French court data faces structural hurdles: unstructured formatting, strict pseudonymisation requirements, procedural constraints under the *principe dispositif*, and a jurisprudential ban prohibiting judges from explicitly citing compensation scales in their opinions <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 22, 27, 28, 39.</ref>. The article dissects the breakdown of the Ministry of Justice's *Datajust* project (2020–2022), which attempted to construct predictive personal injury algorithms <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 35, 38, 40.</ref>. The authors conclude that legal metrics processing is valuable for understanding past judicial trends (*knowledge*), but severely limited for forecasting future litigation outcomes (*predictive justice*) <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 25, 40, 42.</ref>.

== Legal Basis ==
* '''French Statutes and Regulations''':
** *Loi 5 juillet 1985 n° 85-677 (Loi Badinter)*: Article 26 (Public database for traffic accident settlements via AGIRA) <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 23, 32.</ref>.
** *Loi 7 octobre 2016 n° 2016-1321 (Loi pour une République numérique)*: Mandatory judicial open data framework <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 22, 37.</ref>.
** *Statute 23 mars 2019 n° 2019-222* & *Décret 30 septembre 2021 n° 2021-1276*: Technical timeline and procedures for online judgment publication <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), p. 23.</ref>.
** *Décret 27 mars 2020 n° 2020-356*: Regulatory authorization for automated processing under the *Datajust* project <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 35, 37.</ref>.
** *Code de procédure civile*: Article 5 (*Principe dispositif* / disposition principle) <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), p. 28.</ref>.
* '''Key Jurisprudence''':
** *Conseil d’État Ruling n° 346575 (2013)* (Application of the Dintilhac Nomenclature) & *Ruling n° 440376 (2021)* (Legality of the Datajust Decree) <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 34, 36.</ref>.
** *Cour de cassation Rulings n° 11-25.988, 12-25.301, & 18-20.818*: Prohibition against explicitly referencing compensation schedules or benchmark scales in judicial reasoning <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), p. 39.</ref>.

== Core Provisions & Three Pillars of Judicial Jurimetrics ==
1. '''Obstacles to Legal Metrics Extraction''': Court decisions are not structured datasets. Heterogeneous judicial writing styles, structural damage to data tables during computational parsing, and redacting personal identifiers through pseudonymisation inherently restrict AI effectiveness <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 26, 27.</ref>.
2. '''Lessons from the Datajust Failure (2020–2022)''': The *Datajust* project was abandoned after two years due to an inability to capture the complex variables of personal injury victims, lack of methodological transparency, and intense opposition from legal bar associations (*Conseil national des barreaux*) and judicial unions (*Syndicat de la magistrature*) rejecting algorithmic compensation scales <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 38, 39, 40.</ref>.
3. '''Practical AI Applications & Judicial Modernization (JuriBERT & Portalis)''': Successful AI deployment in the French judiciary remains restricted to operational support: automated pseudonymisation algorithms at the *Cour de cassation*, case file routing via *JuriBERT*, and standardizing judgment structures through the *Portalis Project* <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 41, 42.</ref>.

* '''[[Vincent Rivollier]]''': Co-Author & Associate Professor of Law at University Savoie Mont Blanc / CNRS <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), p. 21.</ref>.
* '''[[Ministère de la Justice (France)]]''': French Ministry of Justice, Developer of Datajust and Portalis Projects <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 35, 42.</ref>.
* '''[[Cour de cassation (France)]]''': French Supreme Court for Civil and Criminal Matters, Developer of Pseudonymisation and JuriBERT Algorithms <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 23, 41.</ref>.

Il '''"Legal Metrics Extracted from Court Decisions: A Focus on Personal Injury Compensation"''' (''Kerangka Kebijakan Ekstraksi Metrik Hukum dari Putusan Peradilan dan Evaluasi Proyek Datajust Prancis'') è un quadro analitico di giurimetria e intelligenza artificiale giudiziaria formulato da Christophe Quézel-Ambrunaz e Vincent Rivollier in *The Italian Law Journal* (Vol. 10 Nos. 01-02/2024, pp. 21–42) per valutare l'estrazione di metriche giuridiche (*legal metrics*) dalle decisioni giudiziarie in Francia <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz, C., & Rivollier, V. (2024). Legal Metrics Extracted from Court Decisions. A Focus on Personal Injury Compensation. ''The Italian Law Journal'', 10(1-2), 21–42.</ref>; esamina gli ostacoli giuridici (pseudonimizzazione, protezione dei dati personali) e tecnici (eterogeneità dei formati, strutture non strutturate, "black box" del ragionamento giudiziale) nell'attuazione dell'open data giudiziario ai sensi del *Digital Republic Act 2016*, Statute 2019-222, e *Decree 2021-1276* <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 22, 23, 26, 27.</ref>; analizza il fallimento del progetto di modellazione predittiva del risarcimento del danno alla persona *Datajust* (2020–2022) del Ministero della Giustizia francese <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 35, 36, 40.</ref>; e valuta le prospettive della trasformazione digitale della giustizia attraverso gli algoritmi di pseudonimizzazione automatica della Corte di Cassazione, i moduli di orientamento dei fascicoli (*JuriBERT*), e la riforma del sistema informativo civile unificato (*Portalis Project*) <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 41, 42.</ref>.

== Sintesi ==
Redatto da [[Christophe Quézel-Ambrunaz]] e [[Vincent Rivollier]] (Professore e Professore Associato di Diritto presso l'Università Savoie Mont Blanc), lo studio esamina le sfide metodologiche dell'estrazione di metriche giuridiche quantitative (*legal metrics*) dalle sentenze giudiziarie <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 21, 22.</ref>. Sebbene il *Digital Republic Act 2016* imponga l'open data giudiziario progressivo, i dati giudiziari francesi affrontano ostacoli strutturali: formati non strutturati, obblighi di pseudonimizzazione rigorosi, limiti procedurali legati al *principe dispositif*, nonché il divieto giurisprudenziale che impedisce ai giudici di citare esplicitamente le tabelle risarcitorie nelle motivazioni <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 22, 27, 28, 39.</ref>. L'articolo analizza l'arresto del progetto *Datajust* (2020–2022) del Ministero della Giustizia, volto a costruire algoritmi predittivi per il risarcimento del danno alla persona <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 35, 38, 40.</ref>. Gli autori concludono che l'elaborazione delle metriche giuridiche è utile per comprendere gli orientamenti passati (*knowledge*), ma fortemente limitata nel predire gli esiti delle controversie future (*predictive justice*) <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 25, 40, 42.</ref>.

== Base Giuridica ==
* '''Legislazione e Regolamenti Francesi''':
** *Loi 5 juillet 1985 n° 85-677 (Loi Badinter)*: Articolo 26 (Banca dati pubblica delle transazioni per incidenti stradali tramite AGIRA) <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 23, 32.</ref>.
** *Loi 7 octobre 2016 n° 2016-1321 (Loi pour une République numérique)*: Obbligo di open data per le decisioni giudiziarie <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 22, 37.</ref>.
** *Statute 23 mars 2019 n° 2019-222* & *Décret 30 septembre 2021 n° 2021-1276*: Tempistiche e procedure tecniche di pubblicazione online delle sentenze <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), p. 23.</ref>.
** *Décret 27 mars 2020 n° 2020-356*: Base giuridica per il trattamento automatizzato del progetto *DataJust* <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 35, 37.</ref>.
** *Code de procédure civile*: Articolo 5 (*Principe dispositif* / principio dispositivo) <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), p. 28.</ref>.
* '''Giurisprudenza Chiave''':
** *Conseil d’État Decisione n° 346575 (2013)* (Applicazione della Nomenclatura Dintilhac) & *Decisione n° 440376 (2021)* (Legittimità del Décret Datajust) <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 34, 36.</ref>.
** *Cour de cassation Decisioni n° 11-25.988, 12-25.301, & 18-20.818*: Divieto di menzionare esplicitamente le tabelle risarcitorie nelle motivazioni delle sentenze <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), p. 39.</ref>.

== Disposizioni Principali e Tre Pilastri della Giurimetria Giudiziaria ==
1. '''Ostacoli all'Estrazione delle Metriche Giuridiche''': Le sentenze non costituiscono un set di dati strutturato. La varietà degli stili di redazione giudiziale, il deterioramento delle tabelle dati durante l'elaborazione informatica e l'omissione di identificativi personali mediante pseudonimizzazione limitano l'efficacia dell'IA <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 26, 27.</ref>.
2. '''Insegnamenti dal Fallimento del Progetto Datajust (2020–2022)''': Il progetto *Datajust* è stato abbandonato dopo due anni a causa dell'impossibilità di gestire la complessità delle variabili delle vittime di danni alla persona, della mancanza di trasparenza metodologica e della ferma opposizione degli ordini forensi (*Conseil national des barreaux*) e dei sindacati dei magistrati (*Syndicat de la magistrature*) contrari alla parametrizzazione algoritmica dei risarcimenti <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 38, 39, 40.</ref>.
3. '''Applicazioni Pratiche dell'IA e Modernizzazione Giudiziaria (JuriBERT & Portalis)''': L'uso efficace dell'IA nella giustizia francese rimane circoscritto al supporto operativo: algoritmi di pseudonimizzazione automatica presso la *Cour de cassation*, smistamento dei ricorsi tramite *JuriBERT*, e standardizzazione delle strutture delle sentenze mediante il *Portalis Project* <ref>Quézel-Ambrunaz & Rivollier (2024), pp. 41, 42.</ref>.

| date = 2012 (IJPL Publication Vol. 4 Issue 1/2012); 2011 (Original Book La qualità delle regole)

}}

The '''Quality of Regulation and Good Regulation Tools Policy Framework''' is an analytical policy and administrative law framework developed by Nicoletta Rangone to evaluate instruments aimed at improving the quality of legislation and administrative rules (good/better/smart regulation tools). It encompasses economic-based analytical tools such as Regulatory Impact Assessment (RIA) and the Standard Cost Model (SCM), administrative burden reduction, plain language drafting, and regulatory life cycle management to uphold the principles of the rule of law, efficiency, transparency, and economic competitiveness <ref>Rangone, N. (2012). The Quality of Regulation. The Myth and Reality of Good Regulation Tools. ''Italian Journal of Public Law'', 4(1), 92–121.</ref>.

== Overview ==
Authored by [[Nicoletta Rangone]], Associate Professor of Administrative Law at [[Politecnico di Milano]], this policy study provides a critical assessment of the tools designed to enhance regulatory quality <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 92, 93.</ref>. Rangone emphasizes that good regulation is an essential element of the rule of law, ensuring public participation, transparency, and the obligation of public authorities to give reasons for their decisions <ref>Rangone (2012), p. 93.</ref>. The framework categorizes tools for managing new regulatory flows ("flow tools") and existing regulatory stock ("stock tools"), evaluates the implementation of RIA and SCM in the European Union, the United States, and Italy, and proposes reform directions incorporating insights from behavioural economics <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 100–103, 104–112, 116–118.</ref>.

== Legal Basis ==
The framework and its associated regulatory tools are rooted in national and supranasional legal instruments:
* '''[[Law 133/2008]] (Italy)''': Enacted the administrative burden reduction program (*taglia-oneri*) aimed at cutting red tape costs by up to 25% <ref>Rangone (2012), p. 105.</ref>.
* '''[[Law 106/2011]] (Italy)''': Mandated the application of the Standard Cost Model (SCM) for Italian regions (*regioni*) and independent regulatory authorities <ref>Rangone (2012), p. 105.</ref>.
* '''[[Governmental Regulation n. 170/2008]] (Italy)''': Established oversight mechanisms for Regulatory Impact Assessment (RIA) under the Presidency of the Council of Ministers <ref>Rangone (2012), p. 110.</ref>.
* '''[[Smart Regulation in the European Union]] (COM(2010) 543)''': EU policy framework integrating the oversight of regulatory flows and stock throughout the regulatory life cycle <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 96, 101.</ref>.
* '''[[US Executive Order 13563]] & [[Executive Order 13579]] (2011)''': US Executive Directives mandating periodic regulatory reviews, efficiency, and cost-benefit analysis <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 97, 101, 109.</ref>.
* '''[[Paperwork Reduction Act 1980]] (United States)''': Governs the obligations of US federal agencies to justify information collection burdens imposed on the public <ref>Rangone (2012), p. 104.</ref>.

== Background & Regulatory Life Cycle ==
The drive for regulatory quality emerged from the need to boost economic competitiveness, facilitate market liberalization, and respond to global economic crises <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 95, 96.</ref>. Rangone posits that regulation must be managed across an integrated regulatory life cycle: from ex-ante design and implementation to enforcement, ex-post evaluation, and eventual revision or repeal <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 100, 101.</ref>.

== Objectives ==
* Ensure regulations meet key quality criteria: necessary/targeted, proportional, consistent, written in plain language, and accessible <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 93, 98.</ref>.
* Reduce unnecessary administrative burdens (red tape) without undermining public interest protections <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 98, 104, 107.</ref>.
* Strengthen evidence-based decision-making and public accountability in rule-making <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 94, 112, 113.</ref>.

== Scope ==
The scope encompasses the distinction between "rules" and "principles," economic impact measurement, administrative procedure simplification, and comparative policy evaluation across Italy, the European Union, the OECD, and the United States <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 99, 100, 104–112.</ref>.

== Core Provisions & Regulatory Tools ==
* '''Flow Tools (New Regulations)''':
** *Regulatory Impact Assessment (RIA)*: A comparative ex-ante process evaluating feasible policy options using SMART template objectives and Cost-Benefit Analysis (CBA) or multi-criteria analysis <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 101, 108–112.</ref>.
** *Plain Language Drafting (Légistique Formelle)*: Drafting legal texts with clear, unambiguous syntax and explicit repeals <ref>Rangone (2012), p. 102.</ref>.
* '''Stock Tools (Existing Regulations)''':
** *Standard Cost Model (SCM)*: A quantitative methodology measuring administrative information obligations using the core formula: $\text{Price} = \text{Tariff} \times \text{Time}$; $\text{Quantity} = \text{Number of Entities} \times \text{Frequency}$ <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 104–107.</ref>.
** *Guillotine System & Sunset Clauses*: Periodic inventory mechanism to repeal obsolete rules and automatically set expiration dates for temporary regulations <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 102, 103.</ref>.
** *Codification & Administrative Simplification*: Consolidating existing laws (*a droit constant*) and streamlining procedures through mechanisms such as one-stop shops and "silence is consent" rules <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 103, 111.</ref>.

== Policy Dilemmas & Behavioral Insights ==
* '''Ritualism and Box-Ticking Formalism in RIA''': In jurisdictions like Italy, RIA implementation often suffers from being treated as a ritualistic ex-post justification for political choices already made rather than a genuine evidence-based tool <ref>Rangone (2012), p. 110.</ref>.
* '''Limits of Traditional Rationality Assumptions''': Standard CBA and SCM methodologies assume rational actor behavior, ignoring cognitive biases and bounded rationality in citizen and firm compliance <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 112, 116.</ref>.

== Reforms & Behavioural Law and Economics ==
Rangone advocates for integrating behavioural law and economics into regulatory design (e.g., utilizing default rules and nudges) to account for cognitive heuristics <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 116–118.</ref>. The framework also supports introducing "fitness checks" to measure cumulative regulatory burdens and recognizing regulatory quality as an autonomous public interest <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 108, 113, 114.</ref>.

== Associated Entities ==
* '''[[Nicoletta Rangone]]''': Lead Author and Associate Professor of Administrative Law <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 92, 93.</ref>.
* '''[[Politecnico di Milano]]''': Academic affiliation of the author <ref>Rangone (2012), p. 93.</ref>.
* '''[[Italian Journal of Public Law]]''': Publication venue <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 92, 93.</ref>.

* '''[[Geovanny Widya Berlianty P]]''': ''[[ENTITY IDENTITY UNCERTAIN|Not found in available sources.]]'' <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 92–121.</ref>

Il '''Quadro di Politica sulla Qualità della Regolazione e sugli Strumenti per una Buona Regolazione''' (''Quality of Regulation and Good Regulation Tools Policy Framework'') è un quadro di analisi delle politiche del diritto e del diritto amministrativo sviluppato da Nicoletta Rangone per esaminare gli strumenti volti a migliorare la qualità della regolazione (*good/better/smart regulation tools*), includendo strumenti analitici a base economica come l'Analisi di Impatto della Regolazione (*Regulatory Impact Assessment / AIR*) e il Modello dei Costi Standard (*Standard Cost Model / SCM*), la semplificazione degli oneri amministrativi, la redazione in linguaggio chiaro (*plain language drafting*), e la gestione della regolazione lungo il suo ciclo di vita (*regulatory life cycle*), al fine di attuare i principi dello stato di diritto, dell'efficienza, della trasparenza e della competitività economica <ref>Rangone, N. (2012). The Quality of Regulation. The Myth and Reality of Good Regulation Tools. ''Italian Journal of Public Law'', 4(1), 92–121.</ref>.

== Sintesi ==
Redatto da [[Nicoletta Rangone]], Professoressa Associata di Diritto Amministrativo presso il [[Politecnico di Milano]], questo studio propone un'analisi critica degli strumenti di miglioramento della qualità regolatoria <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 92, 93.</ref>. Rangone sottolinea che una buona regolazione costituisce un elemento essenziale dello stato di diritto (*rule of law*), garantendo la partecipazione pubblica, la trasparenza e l'obbligo di motivazione degli atti amministrativi <ref>Rangone (2012), p. 93.</ref>. Lo studio distingue tra strumenti di gestione dei nuovi flussi normativi (*flow tools*) e strumenti di gestione dello stock normativo esistente (*stock tools*), valuta l'applicazione dell'AIR e del modello SCM nell'Unione Europea, negli Stati Uniti e in Italia, ed evidenzia nuove prospettive di riforma basate sull'economia comportamentale (*behavioural economics*) <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 100–103, 104–112, 116–118.</ref>.

== Basi Giuridiche ==
Il quadro politico e i relativi strumenti regolatori si fondano su fonti normative nazionali e sovranazionali:
* '''[[Legge 133/2008]] (Italia)''': Ha introdotto il programma di riduzione degli oneri amministrativi (*taglia-oneri*) volto a tagliare i costi della burocrazia fino al 25% <ref>Rangone (2012), p. 105.</ref>.
* '''[[Legge 106/2011]] (Italia)''': Ha reso obbligatorio l'uso del Modello dei Costi Standard (SCM) per le Regioni e le autorità indipendenti italiane <ref>Rangone (2012), p. 105.</ref>.
* '''[[D.P.C.M. n. 170/2008]] (Italia)''': Regolamento recante la disciplina della verifica e del controllo dell'AIR sotto la Presidenza del Consiglio dei Ministri <ref>Rangone (2012), p. 110.</ref>.
* '''[[Smart Regulation in the European Union]] (COM(2010) 543)''': Comunicazione UE che integra il controllo sui flussi e sullo stock di regolazione lungo l'intero ciclo di vita normativo <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 96, 101.</ref>.
* '''[[US Executive Order 13563]] & [[Executive Order 13579]] (2011)''': Ordini esecutivi statunitensi sulla revisione periodica della regolamentazione, l'efficienza e l'analisi costi-benefici <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 97, 101, 109.</ref>.
* '''[[Paperwork Reduction Act 1980]] (Stati Uniti)''': Disciplina le procedure per la riduzione degli oneri informativi imposti ai cittadini e alle imprese dalle agenzie federali <ref>Rangone (2012), p. 104.</ref>.

== Contesto e Ciclo di Vita della Regolazione ==
La spinta verso una migliore qualità regolatoria nasce dall'esigenza di rafforzare la competitività economica, liberalizzare i mercati e rispondere alle crisi finanziarie globali <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 95, 96.</ref>. Rangone sostiene che la regolazione debba essere gestita nell'ambito di un ciclo di vita integrato (*regulatory life cycle*): dalla progettazione ex-ante all'attuazione, all'applicazione coattiva, alla valutazione ex-post, fino alla revisione o abrogazione <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 100, 101.</ref>.

== Obiettivi ==
* Garantire che le norme soddisfino i criteri essenziali di qualità: necessarie, proporzionate, coerenti, redatte in linguaggio chiaro e accessibili <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 93, 98.</ref>.
* Ridurre gli oneri amministrativi superflui (*red tape*) senza pregiudicare le tutele di pubblico interesse <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 98, 104, 107.</ref>.
* Rafforzare il processo decisionale basato su evidenze empiriche (*evidence-based decision-making*) e la responsabilità dei regolatori <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 94, 112, 113.</ref>.

== Ambito di Applicazione ==
L'ambito comprende la distinzione tra "regole" e "principi", la misurazione dell'impatto economico, la semplificazione delle procedure amministrative e la valutazione comparata delle politiche in Italia, Unione Europea, OCSE e Stati Uniti <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 99, 100, 104–112.</ref>.

== Disposizioni Principali e Strumenti Regolatori ==
* '''Strumenti di Flusso (Nuove Regole / Flow Tools)''':
** *Analisi di Impatto della Regolazione (AIR / RIA)*: Valutazione comparativa ex-ante delle opzioni regolatorie tramite obiettivi SMART e analisi costi-benefici (CBA) o analisi multi-criterio <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 101, 108–112.</ref>.
** *Linguaggio Chiaro (Plain Language Drafting / Légistique Formelle)*: Redazione formale di testi normativi privi di ambiguità e ricorso ad abrogazioni espresse <ref>Rangone (2012), p. 102.</ref>.
* '''Strumenti di Stock (Regole Esistenti / Stock Tools)''':
** *Modello dei Costi Standard (Standard Cost Model / SCM)*: Metodologia quantitativa per la misurazione degli oneri informativi basata sulla formula: $\text{Prezzo} = \text{Tariffa} \times \text{Tempo}$; $\text{Quantità} = \text{Numero di Entità} \times \text{Frequenza}$ <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 104–107.</ref>.
** *Sistema Guillotine e Clausole Sunset*: Meccanismi periodici per abrogare massivamente norme obsolete e stabilire scadenze automatiche di efficacia per le regolamentazioni <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 102, 103.</ref>.
** *Codificazione e Semplificazione Amministrativa*: Riordino normativo a diritto costante e snellimento delle procedure (es. sportello unico, silenzio-assenso) <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 103, 111.</ref>.

== Dilemmi Politici e Analisi Comportamentale ==
* '''Ritualismo e Formalismo nell'AIR''': In ordinamenti come quello italiano, l'attuazione dell'AIR soffre spesso di un approccio meramente burocratico (*box-ticking*), utilizzato come giustificazione ex-post di decisioni politiche già prese <ref>Rangone (2012), p. 110.</ref>.
* '''Limiti dei Modelli Razionali Tradizionali''': L'analisi costi-benefici e il modello SCM presuppongono una razionalità perfetta degli individui, ignorando le distorsioni cognitive (*cognitive biases*) nell'adempimento delle norme <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 112, 116.</ref>.

== Riforme e Diritto Economico Comportamentale ==
Rangone propone di integrare il diritto economico comportamentale (*behavioural law and economics*) nella redazione delle regole (es. opzioni di *default* e *nudge*) per prevedere le reazioni reali dei destinatari <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 116–118.</ref>. Viene inoltre raccomandata l'introduzione dei *fitness checks* per valutare l'impatto cumulativo della regolazione e il riconoscimento della qualità regolatoria quale interesse pubblico autonomo <ref>Rangone (2012), pp. 108, 113, 114.</ref>.

== Entità Correlate e Persone Focus ==

* '''[[Politecnico di Milano]]''': Affiliazione Accademica dell'Autrice <ref>Rangone (2012), p. 93.</ref>.

The '''Re-Theorizing Public Law Framework''' (officially known as the ''Framework for Re-Theorizing Public Law and the Italian Public-Private Law Divide'') is a policy analysis and public law theory framework designed to evaluate the boundaries of the public-private law divide, the legitimacy of administrative justice, the return of state economic intervention following financial crises, and the integration of legal analysis with social and economic sciences <ref>della Cananea, G. (2012). Editorial: Re-Theorizing Public Law. ''Italian Journal of Public Law'', 4(2), 1–4.</ref>.

== Overview ==
Authored by [[Giacinto della Cananea]], Professor of Administrative Law at the [[University of Rome "Tor Vergata"]], this editorial addresses the ongoing debate over the distinctive nature of public law in Italy, the European Union, and the United Kingdom <ref>della Cananea (2012), pp. 1–3.</ref>. It highlights school-of-thought developments in Italy that deny the distinct character of state actions (such as grants and subsidies) and challenge the dualistic administrative justice system under the assertion that only a monistic judicial review system aligns with the Rule of Law <ref>della Cananea (2012), p. 1.</ref>.

== Legal Basis ==
Rather than relying on specific statutory acts, the framework grounds itself in fundamental legal principles:
* '''[[Rule of Law Principles]]''': Serves as the benchmark for debating the jurisdiction of administrative judges versus monistic judicial review systems <ref>della Cananea (2012), p. 1.</ref>.
* '''[[Basic Standards of Public Life]]''': Encompasses the core principles of legality, fairness, rationality in decision-making, and the quality of public utilities <ref>della Cananea (2012), p. 3.</ref>.

== Background ==
The global economic and financial crisis created new momentum for evaluating the erosion of the traditional boundary between public and private law <ref>della Cananea (2012), p. 2.</ref>. Contrary to predictions regarding the demise of public law, post-crisis developments revealed the "return of the State" as a major investor and owner in key economic sectors, evidenced by massive state financial support for the banking industry <ref>della Cananea (2012), p. 2.</ref>.

== Objectives ==
* Evaluate whether Italian public law satisfies the basic standards of public life recognized across European jurisdictions <ref>della Cananea (2012), p. 3.</ref>.
* Re-theorize 21st-century public law and examine its relationship with private law, economics, and social sciences <ref>della Cananea (2012), pp. 2, 4.</ref>.
* Provide a platform for critical interdisciplinary dialogue via symposia hosted by the ''Italian Journal of Public Law'' <ref>della Cananea (2012), pp. 3, 4.</ref>.

== Scope ==
The scope encompasses Italian public law, administrative jurisdiction, state intervention in the economy, and cross-disciplinary studies between law and economics across Italy, the European Union, and the United Kingdom <ref>della Cananea (2012), pp. 1–4.</ref>.

== Key Provisions & Doctrinal Debates ==
* '''Denial of Authoritative State Actions''': Addressing legal trends in Italy that attempt to minimize or reject grants and subsidies as authoritative acts of public power <ref>della Cananea (2012), p. 1.</ref>.
* '''Challenges to Administrative Courts''': Critiquing arguments against the jurisdiction of administrative judges and the assertion that monistic judicial review is uniquely coherent with the Rule of Law <ref>della Cananea (2012), p. 1.</ref>.
* '''Return of State Intervention''': Demonstrating that financial crises have reinforced the role of the state as an economic actor rather than extinguishing public law <ref>della Cananea (2012), p. 2.</ref>.

== Implementation ==
Operationalized through scientific symposia organized by the ''Italian Journal of Public Law'' (IJPL) to test the fitness of Italian public law for the 21st century, alongside the publication of interdisciplinary quantitative and economic studies on public accounting and regulation <ref>della Cananea (2012), pp. 3, 4.</ref>.

== Policy Issues ==
* '''Erosion of Public and Private Law Boundaries''': Categorization challenges regarding state intervention in modern financial markets <ref>della Cananea (2012), p. 2.</ref>.
* '''Alignment with European Standards''': Ensuring that public accountability, administrative procedures, and public accounts presentation in Italy remain aligned with European integration standards <ref>della Cananea (2012), pp. 3, 4.</ref>.

== Proposed Reforms ==
Recommends gradual adjustments to public rules, administrative procedures, and oversight mechanisms to safeguard public trust in market operators and ensure transparency in public financial reporting <ref>della Cananea (2012), p. 4.</ref>.

== Related Entities ==
* '''[[Giacinto della Cananea]]''': Author and Professor of Administrative Law at the University of Rome "Tor Vergata" <ref>della Cananea (2012), pp. 1, 3.</ref>.
* '''[[Italian Journal of Public Law]]''': Publishing Journal and Host of Academic Symposia <ref>della Cananea (2012), pp. 1, 3, 4.</ref>.
* '''[[Cecep Mustafa]]''': ''[[ENTITY IDENTITY UNCERTAIN|Not found in the available sources.]]'' <ref>della Cananea (2012), pp. 1–4.</ref>

The '''Matrix of Judicial Roles and IT Functional Requirements Framework''' is a judicial ICT policy model and court information processing research framework developed by Dr. Dory Reiling (Judge at the First Instance Court of Amsterdam) based on her dissertation ''Technology for Justice'' (2009). This framework adapts Erhard Blankenburg's matrix of judicial roles to map court caseflow based on two main dimensions—outcome uncertainty (certain vs. uncertain) and party relationship dynamics (zero-sum vs. win-win)—in order to categorize the judicial caseload into four functional groups (Title Provision, Notarial Declaration, Settlement Support, and Judicial Judgment) to determine the most optimal ICT functionalities, accelerate case resolution, and expand access to justice.

== Summary ==
Reiling asserts that the primary obstacle to technology adoption in courts is not the "judges' lack of IT understanding", but rather a lack of understanding regarding how courts process information. Using data from over 900,000 first instance civil cases in the Netherlands (2007), Reiling proves that the work of adjudicating contested cases ('''Group 4 - Judgment''') only covers '''8%''' of the total court caseload. Most court operations consist of registering undefended claims ('''Group 1 - Title''', 35%), formal declarations ('''Group 2 - Notarial''', 30%), and withdrawals/settlements ('''Group 3 - Settlement''', 9%). By identifying the information characteristics in each group, courts can implement automated electronic filing for Title Cases, provide web forms and standard formulas for Notarial Cases, online negotiation platforms for Settlement Cases, and electronic case files (e-files) and decision support systems for Judgment Cases [12–17, 20–25].

== Legal Basis ==
* '''Not found in the available sources:''' This document is an academic research article and policy assessment, not a statutory legislative instrument [1–29].
* '''Procedural Rules Analyzed:''' Dutch Civil Procedure Law (conciliation/settlement mandates); UK Civil Procedure Rules (Money Claim Online / MCOL, Possession Claim Online / PCOL); German Order of Payment Procedure Rules (''Mahnverfahren''); and Adelaide Magistrate's Court Prelodgement Notice Rules (1999).
