== Summary / Ringkasan ==

=== Bahasa Indonesia ===
Surat Edaran Mahkamah Agung (SEMA) Nomor 1 Tahun 2008 (disusun berdasarkan berkas sumber "SEMA NO. 01 TAHUN 2008.pdf") menetapkan kerangka kerja wajib untuk pelaksanaan mediasi di pengadilan dalam sistem peradilan Indonesia. Bertujuan untuk meningkatkan efisiensi operasional pengadilan dan menyelesaikan masalah penumpukan perkara, petunjuk ini mengintegrasikan mekanisme Alternatif Penyelesaian Sengketa (APS/ADR) secara langsung ke dalam proses hukum acara perdata. Regulasi ini mewajibkan hakim pemeriksa perkara untuk secara aktif mendorong dan memandu para pihak yang bersengketa agar mencapai kesepakatan damai yang saling menguntungkan sebelum persidangan formal dilanjutkan. Dengan mengutamakan perdamaian mufakat di atas putusan hakim yang bersifat memutus sepihak, edaran ini mendorong terciptanya lingkungan hukum kolaboratif yang mengedepankan musyawarah untuk mencapai keadilan dalam perkara perdata.

=== English ===
Circular Letter of the Supreme Court (SEMA) Number 1 of 2008 (modeled from the available source "SEMA NO. 01 TAHUN 2008.pdf") establishes a mandatory framework for court-annexed mediation within the Indonesian judicial system. Aimed at increasing the overall efficiency of court operations and resolving the persistent issue of case backlogs, this directive integrates alternative dispute resolution (ADR) directly into the civil litigation process. It mandates that presiding judges actively guide and encourage disputing parties to pursue a mutually beneficial, consensual settlement before a formal court trial commences. By prioritizing amicable agreements over adversarial rulings, the circular promotes a more collaborative, consensus-driven legal environment for achieving justice in civil disputes.

== Scope & Classification / Ruang Lingkup ==

; Sasaran Personel & Pihak

* Hakim Pemeriksa Perkara Perdata pada pengadilan tingkat pertama
* Mediator terdaftar di lingkungan pengadilan
* Para pihak pencari keadilan dan kuasa hukum dalam perkara perdata

; Cakupan Lingkungan Peradilan

* Peradilan Umum (Pengadilan Negeri)
* Peradilan Agama (Pengadilan Agama)
* Seluruh pengadilan tingkat pertama di bawah Mahkamah Agung yang mengadili sengketa keperdataan

; Domain / Kategori

* Hukum Acara Perdata • Mediasi di Pengadilan • Alternatif Penyelesaian Sengketa (APS/ADR) • Perdamaian Para Pihak • Pengurangan Penumpukan Perkara

== Definition / Definisi ==

=== Bahasa Indonesia ===

; Mediasi di Pengadilan (Court-Annexed Mediation)
: Proses penyelesaian sengketa alternatif yang wajib diintegrasikan ke dalam tahapan persidangan formal di pengadilan, di mana pihak ketiga yang netral (mediator) membantu para pihak berperkara untuk mencapai kesepakatan damai guna menyelesaikan sengketa perdata sebelum persidangan dilanjutkan.
; Kesepakatan Damai (Consensual Agreement)
: Hasil penyelesaian sengketa secara sukarela dan saling menguntungkan yang dicapai oleh para pihak melalui perundingan dan mediasi, yang diakui oleh pengadilan sebagai metode terbaik untuk mewujudkan keadilan dalam perkara perdata.

=== English ===

; Court-Annexed Mediation (Mediasi di Pengadilan)
: A mandatory alternative dispute resolution process integrated into formal court proceedings where a neutral third party (mediator) assists litigants in reaching a mutually acceptable, consensual agreement to resolve their civil dispute before a trial proceeds.
; Consensual Agreement (Kesepakatan Damai)
: A voluntary, mutually beneficial settlement reached by disputing parties through negotiation and mediation, which is recognized by courts as the preferred method for resolving civil conflicts.

== Legal Basis / Landasan Hukum ==

=== Bahasa Indonesia ===

* ''[Undang-undang dasar, undang-undang organik, maupun dasar hukum legislatif khusus yang melandasi penerbitan SEMA Nomor 1 Tahun 2008 belum terverifikasi dari sumber yang tersedia / Not verified from available sources]''.

=== English ===

* ''[The specific statutory, constitutional, or organic legislative bases for SEMA Number 1 of 2008 are not verified from available sources]''.

== Core Guidance / Petunjuk Pokok ==

=== Bahasa Indonesia ===
{| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;"
! style="width:30%;" |Prinsip / Mandat
!Petunjuk Teknis & Pedoman Pelaksanaan
|-
|'''Integrasi Mediasi Wajib'''
|Mengintegrasikan mekanisme Alternatif Penyelesaian Sengketa (APS/ADR) secara langsung dan mengikat ke dalam alur proses persidangan perdata formal di pengadilan tingkat pertama.
|-
|'''Kewajiban Aktif Majelis Hakim'''
|Majelis hakim pemeriksa perkara diwajibkan secara aktif mengarahkan, membimbing, dan memfasilitasi para pihak yang bersengketa agar mengupayakan perdamaian yang saling menguntungkan (''win-win solution'').
|-
|'''Syarat Pra-Persidangan (Pre-Trial Stage)'''
|Upaya mediasi wajib ditempuh terlebih dahulu sebagai tahapan awal sebelum pemeriksaan pokok perkara (tahap jawab-jinawab dan pembuktian) dilanjutkan dalam persidangan terbuka.
|-

|-

|}

== Key Facts / Fakta Utama ==

* '''Tujuan Penataan Yudisial:''' Dirancang untuk menekan laju beban perkara (''case backlog'') di pengadilan tingkat pertama dan mengurangi eskalasi upaya hukum kasasi/peninjauan kembali ke Mahkamah Agung.
* '''Integrasi Mediasi Formal:''' Menjadikan mediasi bukan sekadar anjuran moral, melainkan tahapan imperatif di dalam prosedur perkara perdata.
* '''Pejabat Penandatangan & Tanggal Penetapan:''' Informasi pejabat penandatangan dan tanggal pasti penerbitan masih ''[belum terverifikasi dari sumber yang tersedia / not verified from available sources]''.

Sunarto, S.H., M.H. (Ketua Mahkamah Agung RI)|date_enacted=2024-11-05|place_enacted=Jakarta|legal_instrument=Surat Edaran Mahkamah Agung|status=in_force|effective_date=2024-11-05|version=1.0}}

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

=== Bahasa Indonesia ===
Surat Edaran Mahkamah Agung (SEMA) Nomor 1 Tahun 2024, yang ditetapkan pada tanggal 5 November 2024, memberikan pedoman lengkap mengenai penerbitan salinan putusan dan akta cerai secara elektronik (e-AC) di lingkungan peradilan agama dan mahkamah syar'iyah. Kebijakan ini menyempurnakan administrasi yudisial dengan mewajibkan panitera menandatangani dokumen tersebut secara elektronik dan mendistribusikannya melalui Sistem Informasi Pengadilan (SIP). Meskipun regulasi sebelumnya seperti PERMA No. 1 Tahun 2019 jo. PERMA No. 7 Tahun 2022 serta Keputusan KMA No. 363/KMA/SK/XII/2022 telah mengatur persidangan elektronik, SEMA ini mengisi kekosongan hukum bagi perkara konvensional serta penerbitan akta nikah/cerai digital. Ketentuan terdahulu dalam SEMA No. 1 Tahun 1990 dan SEMA No. 1 Tahun 1997 dinyatakan tetap berlaku sepanjang tidak bertentangan dengan surat edaran ini.

=== English ===
Circular Letter of the Supreme Court (SEMA) Number 1 of 2024, issued on November 5, 2024, establishes comprehensive guidelines for the electronic issuance of copies of court decisions and divorce certificates (e-AC) within the Religious Judicature of Indonesia. This policy serves as a modernized administrative framework, enabling court registrars to sign decisions and certificates electronically and distribute them securely via the Court Information System (SIP). While earlier regulations like PERMA No. 1 of 2019 and KMA Decree No. 363/KMA/SK/XII/2022 only covered decisions from electronic trials, SEMA No. 1 of 2024 bridges this gap to include conventional proceedings and digital divorce certification. Preceding guidelines under SEMA No. 1 of 1990 and SEMA No. 1 of 1997 remain in effect to the extent they are not in conflict with this circular.

== Scope & Classification / Ruang Lingkup ==

; Sasaran Institusi

* Pengadilan Tingkat Banding: Pengadilan Tinggi Agama dan Mahkamah Syar'iyah Aceh
* Pengadilan Tingkat Pertama: Pengadilan Agama dan Mahkamah Syar'iyah di seluruh Indonesia
* Instansi Terkait: Direktorat Jenderal Badan Peradilan Agama (Ditjen Badilag), Kementerian Agama RI, dan Kantor Urusan Agama (KUA/PPN)

; Ruang Lingkup Administratif

* Administrasi perkara persidangan elektronik (''e-court'') maupun konvensional
* Penerbitan dan pengesahan Salinan Putusan serta Akta Cerai Elektronik (e-AC)

; Domain / Kategori

* Administrasi Perkara Elektronik • Akta Cerai Elektronik (e-AC) • Tanda Tangan Elektronik • Sistem Informasi Pengadilan (SIP) • Integrasi Data KUA • Legalisasi Dokumen Peradilan

== Definition / Definisi ==

=== Bahasa Indonesia ===

; Salinan Putusan (Copy of Decision)
: Salinan putusan atau penetapan dari pengadilan sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan.
; Akta Cerai (Divorce Certificate)
: Bukti cerai yang diterbitkan oleh pengadilan sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan.
; Akta Cerai Elektronik (e-AC)
: Akta cerai yang diterbitkan secara elektronik.
; Pengadilan (Court)
: Pengadilan agama dan mahkamah syar'iyah.
; Para Pihak (The Parties)
: Penggugat/pemohon/pelawan dan tergugat/termohon/terlawan dalam suatu perkara di Pengadilan.
; Sistem Informasi Pengadilan (SIP)
: Seluruh sistem informasi yang disediakan oleh Mahkamah Agung untuk memberi pelayanan terhadap pencari keadilan yang meliputi administrasi, pelayanan perkara, dan persidangan secara elektronik.
; Legalisasi (Legalization)
: Pengabsahan atas dokumen yang diterbitkan pengadilan dan ditandatangani oleh pejabat yang berwenang.

=== English ===

; Copy of Decision (Salinan Putusan)
: An official copy of a judgment, decision, or decree issued by the court in accordance with prevailing laws and regulations.
; Divorce Certificate (Akta Cerai)
: An official proof of divorce issued by the court pursuant to statutory provisions.
; Electronic Divorce Certificate (Akta Cerai Elektronik / e-AC)
: A divorce certificate officially issued and authenticated in electronic format.
; Court (Pengadilan)
: Appellate and first-instance Religious Courts (Pengadilan Agama) and Sharia Courts (Mahkamah Syar'iyah).
; The Parties (Para Pihak)
: Plaintiff/applicant/opposer and defendant/respondent/opposing party in proceedings before the Court.
; Court Information System (Sistem Informasi Pengadilan / SIP)
: The collection of electronic information platforms provided by the Supreme Court to facilitate judicial administration, case filing, and electronic trial processes.
; Legalization (Legalisasi)
: Official authentication and validation of court documents signed by authorized registry officials.

== Legal Basis / Landasan Hukum ==

=== Bahasa Indonesia ===

* Pasal 84 Undang-Undang Nomor 7 Tahun 1989 tentang Peradilan Agama, sebagaimana telah beberapa kali diubah terakhir dengan Undang-Undang Nomor 50 Tahun 2009.
* Peraturan Mahkamah Agung (PERMA) Nomor 1 Tahun 2019 tentang Administrasi Perkara dan Persidangan di Pengadilan secara Elektronik sebagaimana telah diubah dengan PERMA Nomor 7 Tahun 2022.
* Keputusan Ketua Mahkamah Agung Nomor 363/KMA/SK/XII/2022 tentang Petunjuk Teknis Administrasi dan Persidangan Perkara Perdata, Perdata Agama, dan Tata Usaha Negara di Pengadilan secara Elektronik.
* Surat Edaran Mahkamah Agung (SEMA) Nomor 1 Tahun 1990 tentang Petunjuk Pembuatan Penetapan Eks. Pasal 71 ayat (2) dan Akta Cerai Eks. Pasal 84 ayat (4) Undang-Undang Nomor 7 Tahun 1989 ''(tetap berlaku sepanjang tidak bertentangan)''.
* Surat Edaran Mahkamah Agung (SEMA) Nomor 1 Tahun 1997 tentang Penyempurnaan Pembuatan Akta Cerai Eks Pasal 84 ayat (4) Undang-Undang Nomor 7 Tahun 1989 ''(tetap berlaku sepanjang tidak bertentangan)''.

=== English ===

* Article 84 of Law Number 7 of 1989 on Religious Judicature, as last amended by Law Number 50 of 2009.
* Supreme Court Regulation (PERMA) Number 1 of 2019 on Case Administration and Electronic Court Proceedings, as amended by PERMA Number 7 of 2022.
* Decree of the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court Number 363/KMA/SK/XII/2022 on Technical Guidelines for Electronic Case Administration and Civil, Religious Civil, and State Administrative Proceedings.
* Supreme Court Circular Letter (SEMA) Number 1 of 1990 on Guidelines for the Issuance of Decrees under Article 71 Paragraph (2) and Divorce Certificates under Article 84 Paragraph (4) of Law Number 7 of 1989 ''(remains valid to the extent not contradictory)''.
* Supreme Court Circular Letter (SEMA) Number 1 of 1997 on the Refinement of Divorce Certificate Issuance under Article 84 Paragraph (4) of Law Number 7 of 1989 ''(remains valid to the extent not contradictory)''.

== Core Guidance / Petunjuk Pokok ==

=== Bahasa Indonesia ===
{| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;"
! style="width:30%;" |Aspek / Prosedur
!Petunjuk Teknis & Pedoman Operasional
|-
|'''Penerbitan Salinan Putusan'''
|
* Diterbitkan sesuai undang-undang dan wajib ditandatangani secara elektronik oleh Panitera Pengadilan.
* Panitera yang berhalangan tidak tetap tetap berwenang menandatangani Salinan Putusan secara elektronik.
* Apabila Panitera berhalangan tetap, dokumen ditandatangani secara elektronik oleh Pejabat Pelaksana Tugas (Plt) yang ditunjuk.
* Format dokumen wajib mengikuti ''template'' putusan yang diatur dalam Keputusan Ketua Mahkamah Agung.
|-
|'''Penerbitan Akta Cerai Elektronik (e-AC)'''
|
* Diterbitkan setelah putusan perceraian berkekuatan hukum tetap (BHT) untuk cerai gugat, atau setelah pelaksanaan ikrar talak untuk cerai talak.
* Ditandatangani secara elektronik oleh Panitera Pengadilan (atau Plt jika berhalangan tetap).
* Wajib memuat elemen: (a) nomor penerbitan e-AC; (b) tanggal terbit e-AC; (c) nomor perkara; (d) identitas Para Pihak (nama, umur saat cerai, agama, pekerjaan, alamat); (e) tanggal putusan; (f) jenis perceraian (cerai gugat/cerai talak); (g) perceraian yang keberapa; (h) keadaan bekas istri pada saat perceraian; (i) nomor kutipan akta nikah lengkap beserta KUA penerbit; dan (j) nama serta jabatan penandatangan e-AC.
* Wajib diserahkan kepada Para Pihak melalui SIP paling lambat pada hari kerja berikutnya setelah penerbitan.
* Cetakan e-AC yang digunakan untuk keperluan pernikahan kembali hanya sah dipergunakan untuk satu (1) kali pernikahan saja.
|-
|'''Pengambilan dan Cetak Dokumen'''
|
* Para Pihak dapat mengunduh Salinan Putusan dan e-AC melalui SIP setelah melunasi pembayaran PNBP sesuai ketentuan.
* Apabila Para Pihak membutuhkan versi cetak fisik, pengadilan tempat berperkara maupun pengadilan lainnya dapat mencetakkannya setelah pembayaran PNBP diverifikasi.
|-
|'''Pengiriman Data Perceraian Elektronik'''
|
* Pengadilan berwenang mengirimkan data perceraian dan Salinan Putusan tanpa meterai secara elektronik langsung kepada Pegawai Pencatat Nikah (PPN/KUA).
* Ditjen Badilag menyediakan integrasi basis data perceraian terpusat yang dapat diakses langsung oleh kementerian yang membidangi urusan perkawinan (Kementerian Agama).
|-
|'''Legalisasi Dokumen Elektronik'''
|
* '''Urusan dalam negeri''': Legalisasi fotokopi Salinan Putusan dan cetakan e-AC dapat dilayani oleh seluruh Pengadilan Agama di Indonesia setelah verifikasi elektronik melalui SIP.
* '''Urusan luar negeri''': Legalisasi dilaksanakan oleh Panitera Mahkamah Agung yang didelegasikan wewenangnya kepada Ditjen Badilag melalui mekanisme verifikasi elektronik.
|}

=== English ===
{| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;"
! style="width:30%;" |Aspect / Area
!Technical Directives & Operational Guidance
|-
|'''Issuance of Copies of Decisions'''
|
* Must be issued in accordance with statutory laws and digitally signed by the Court Registrar.
* A Registrar with a temporary absence retains electronic signing authority; upon permanent vacancy/absence, the designated Acting Registrar (Plt) executes the digital signature.
* Visual layout and formatting must conform strictly to standardized templates established by Decree of the Chief Justice.
|-
|'''Issuance of Electronic Divorce Certificates (e-AC)'''
|
* Issued once judgments become final and binding (''inkracht'') in contested divorces (''cerai gugat'') or following the formal divorce pledge (''ikrar talak'') in husband-initiated petitions (''cerai talak'').
* Digitally signed by the Court Registrar (or Plt in permanent vacancy).
* Mandatory contents: issuance number, issuance date, docket number, parties' identities, date of judgment, divorce type, ordinal count, condition of the former wife, marriage certificate details with issuing KUA, and registrar credentials.
* Transmitted to the parties via the SIP portal at the latest on the business day following issuance.
* An e-AC printed for remarriage is strictly restricted to single-use (valid for only one subsequent marriage registration).
|-
|'''Withdrawal and Printing Procedures'''
|
* Parties download certified decision copies and e-AC via SIP upon settlement of required Non-Tax State Revenue (PNBP) fees.
* Hard copies may be requested and issued at the forum court or any other religious court upon PNBP fee clearance.
|-
|'''Electronic Inter-Agency Data Transfer'''
|
* Courts are authorized to dispatch electronic divorce records and unmetered decision copies directly to marriage registrars (PPN/KUA).
* The Directorate General of the Religious Judicature Body (Ditjen Badilag) maintains a centralized portal for divorce database integration accessible to the Ministry of Religious Affairs.
|-
|'''Electronic Legalization Protocols'''
|
* '''Domestic affairs''': Legalization of printed photocopies of decisions and e-AC can be processed by any religious court across Indonesia following electronic SIP verification.
* '''International affairs''': Legalization is executed under the authority of the Supreme Court Registrar, delegated to Ditjen Badilag following electronic validation.
|}

== Key Facts / Fakta Utama ==

* '''Penandatanganan Elektronik Panitera:''' Standardisasi tanda tangan digital bagi Panitera (atau Plt Panitera saat kekosongan tetap) pada salinan putusan dan e-AC.
* '''Pembatasan Satu Kali Nikah:''' Salinan fisik e-AC yang dicetak untuk keperluan pernikahan kembali dibatasi secara hukum hanya berlaku untuk 1 (satu) kali pencatatan pernikahan.
* '''Legalisasi Lintas Pengadilan:''' Legalisasi dalam negeri atas cetakan e-AC dapat dilayani oleh seluruh Pengadilan Agama di Indonesia tanpa harus kembali ke pengadilan asal perkara.
* '''Integrasi Langsung KUA:''' Ditjen Badilag menyediakan jalur data terpadu yang dapat diakses Kementerian Agama/PPN untuk otomatisasi pelaporan perceraian.

== Frequently Asked Questions / FAQ ==

; Q1
: Apakah akta cerai elektronik (e-AC) memiliki kekuatan hukum yang sama dengan akta cerai fisik?
: Ya. Berdasarkan pedoman SEMA Nomor 1 Tahun 2024, e-AC yang ditandatangani secara elektronik memiliki keabsahan hukum penuh dan diserahkan kepada pihak yang bersangkutan melalui Sistem Informasi Pengadilan (SIP).

; Q2
: Bagaimana jika Panitera Pengadilan berhalangan tetap atau posisinya kosong?
: Apabila Panitera berhalangan tetap, Salinan Putusan dan e-AC ditandatangani secara elektronik oleh Pejabat Pelaksana Tugas (Plt) yang ditunjuk secara resmi.

; Q3
: Apakah legalisasi fotokopi akta cerai harus dilakukan di pengadilan tempat perkara diputus?
: Tidak. Untuk urusan dalam negeri, legalisasi fotokopi Salinan Putusan atau cetakan e-AC dapat dilakukan oleh seluruh Pengadilan Agama/Mahkamah Syar'iyah di Indonesia setelah melewati proses verifikasi elektronik pada SIP.

; Q4
: Berapa kali cetakan e-AC dapat digunakan untuk melakukan pernikahan kembali?
: e-AC yang diunduh dan dicetak dari SIP untuk keperluan pernikahan kembali hanya sah dipergunakan untuk 1 (satu) kali pendaftaran pernikahan.

{{Infobox Regulation|entity_id=JPAIS:REGULATION:SEMA-9-2020|title=Surat Edaran Mahkamah Agung Nomor 9 Tahun 2020|short_title=SEMA No. 9 Tahun 2020|aliases=SEMA 9/2020, SEMA Nomor 9 Tahun 2020, Circular Letter of the Supreme Court Number 9 of 2020|country=Indonesia|authority=Mahkamah Agung Republik Indonesia|issuing_authority=JPAIS:ORG:MA-RI|enacting_official=Ketua Mahkamah Agung RI|date_enacted=2020-09-07|legal_instrument=Surat Edaran Mahkamah Agung|status=in_force|effective_date=2020-09-07|version=1.0}}

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

=== Bahasa Indonesia ===
Surat Edaran Mahkamah Agung (SEMA) Nomor 9 Tahun 2020, yang ditetapkan pada tanggal 7 September 2020, memuat perubahan terhadap SEMA Nomor 8 Tahun 2020 tentang pengaturan jam kerja pada masa New Normal. Guna menekan laju penyebaran COVID-19, SEMA ini menginstruksikan pimpinan satuan kerja di wilayah kabupaten/kota berstatus risiko tinggi (zona merah COVID-19) untuk membatasi kehadiran fisik hakim dan aparatur peradilan di kantor (''work from office'') maksimal 25% dari total keseluruhan pegawai. Pengaturan wilayah di luar zona risiko tinggi merujuk pada ketentuan Surat Edaran Menteri Pendayagunaan Aparatur Negara dan Reformasi Birokrasi (PANRB) Nomor 67 Tahun 2020. Ketentuan terdahulu di dalam SEMA Nomor 1 Tahun 2020 beserta perubahan-perubahannya hingga SEMA Nomor 8 Tahun 2020 dinyatakan tetap berlaku sepanjang tidak bertentangan dengan ketentuan ini.

=== English ===
Circular Letter of the Supreme Court (SEMA) Number 9 of 2020, enacted on September 7, 2020, amends SEMA Number 8 of 2020 regarding working-time arrangements during the New Normal period. Designed to curb the rapid transmission of COVID-19, this circular instructs leaders of judicial work units in high-risk zones (COVID-19 red zones) to limit physical office presence (Work from Office) to a maximum of 25% of their total personnel. For areas outside high-risk zones, the applicable rules refer to Circular Letter of the Minister of State Apparatus Empowerment and Bureaucratic Reform (PANRB) Number 67 of 2020. All preceding provisions of SEMA Number 1 of 2020 and its subsequent amendments up to SEMA Number 8 of 2020 remain fully active as long as they do not conflict with this regulation.

== Scope & Classification / Ruang Lingkup ==

; Satuan Kerja Terkait

* Mahkamah Agung Republik Indonesia
* Badan Peradilan di Bawah Mahkamah Agung (Peradilan Umum, Peradilan Agama, Peradilan Militer, Peradilan Tata Usaha Negara)

; Lingkup Geografis

* Satuan kerja pengadilan di wilayah Jabodetabek
* Wilayah kabupaten/kota berstatus risiko tinggi (zona merah COVID-19) di seluruh Indonesia

; Domain / Kategori

* Manajemen ASN Peradilan • Sistem Kerja New Normal • Pembatasan Kehadiran Kantor (WFO/WFH) • Protokol Penanganan Pandemi • Administrasi Peradilan

== Definition / Definisi ==

=== Bahasa Indonesia ===

; Zona Merah COVID-19 (Zona Risiko Tinggi)
: Wilayah kabupaten/kota yang berstatus risiko tinggi penyebaran COVID-19 sesuai dengan ketentuan yang dikeluarkan oleh Satuan Tugas Penanganan COVID-19 dan/atau peraturan Kepala Daerah setempat.
; Pengaturan Giliran Kerja (Work Shifts)
: Pembagian dan penentuan secara selektif bagi hakim dan aparatur peradilan yang melaksanakan tugas dari kantor (''work from office'') dan/atau dari rumah (''work from home'').
; Masa New Normal / Tata Kehidupan Baru (New Normal Period)
: Tatanan sistem kerja aparatur sipil negara dan pelayanan publik dalam masa pandemi COVID-19 sebagaimana diatur oleh pemerintah.

=== English ===

; COVID-19 Red Zone (High-Risk Zone)
: A regency or city designated with high-risk status regarding the transmission of COVID-19 in accordance with provisions from the COVID-19 Handling Task Force and/or local Regional Head regulations.
; Work Shifts (Pengaturan Giliran Kerja)
: The selective scheduling and determination of which judges and court personnel are assigned to work from the office (WFO) and/or work from home (WFH).
; New Normal Period (Masa Tata Kehidupan Baru / New Normal)

== Summary / Ringkasan ==

=== Bahasa Indonesia ===
Keputusan Ketua Mahkamah Agung Republik Indonesia Nomor 15/KMA/SK.HK2/II/2025, yang ditetapkan pada tanggal 10 Februari 2025 oleh Ketua Mahkamah Agung Sunarto, memberlakukan Pedoman Pencegahan dan Penanganan Konflik Kepentingan dalam Penyelesaian Perkara di Mahkamah Agung. Keputusan ini bertujuan untuk menjamin tegaknya kekuasaan kehakiman yang mandiri dan akuntabel serta bebas dari benturan kepentingan. Regulasi ini mewajibkan Hakim Agung, Hakim Ad Hoc, dan Hakim Yustisial untuk mengungkapkan hubungan keluarga (sedarah dan semenda hingga derajat ketiga), afiliasi sosial, serta afiliasi finansial (termasuk kepemilikan saham, aset kripto, dan surat berharga lainnya) melalui pengisian formulir terpusat di Sistem Informasi Pengadilan (SIP). Aturan ini juga mengatur mekanisme pengunduran diri wajib bagi hakim dan panitera pengganti ketika benturan kepentingan teridentifikasi, serta menetapkan peran Ketua Muda Pembinaan dan Ketua Muda Pengawasan untuk melakukan sosialisasi, pemantauan, dan evaluasi berkala minimal satu kali dalam setahun.

=== English ===
Decree of the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court Number 15/KMA/SK.HK2/II/2025, enacted on February 10, 2025, by Chief Justice Sunarto, establishes the comprehensive operational guidelines for the prevention and handling of conflicts of interest within case adjudication at the Supreme Court of Indonesia. Aimed at safeguarding an independent and accountable judiciary free from bias, the decree mandates that Supreme Court Justices, Ad Hoc Judges, and Judicial Judges proactively declare family relationships (consanguinity and affinity up to the third degree), social affiliations, and financial holdings (including stocks, cryptocurrency, and other securities) into the Court Information System (SIP). It sets forth the strict protocols for compulsory recusal (pengunduran diri) when a conflict of interest is identified and delineates the responsibilities of the Chamber Chairpersons for Development and Oversight in managing the dissemination, monitoring, and annual evaluation of this system.

== Scope & Classification / Ruang Lingkup ==

; Subjek Hukum Sasaran

* Hakim Agung pada Mahkamah Agung
* Hakim Ad Hoc pada Mahkamah Agung
* Hakim Yustisial pada Kepaniteraan Mahkamah Agung
* Panitera Pengganti pada Mahkamah Agung

; Ruang Lingkup Institusi

* Mahkamah Agung Republik Indonesia (Pimpinan Mahkamah Agung, Kamar-Kamar Teknis Yudisial, dan Kepaniteraan Mahkamah Agung)

; Domain / Kategori

* Integritas Peradilan • Pencegahan Benturan Kepentingan • Kode Etik dan Pedoman Perilaku Hakim • Penunjukan Majelis Hakim • Pengunduran Diri Hakim (Recusal) • Sistem Informasi Pengadilan (SIP)

== Definition / Definisi ==

=== Bahasa Indonesia ===

; Konflik Kepentingan (Conflict of Interest)
: Kondisi Hakim dalam menangani perkara memiliki atau patut diduga memiliki kepentingan pribadi untuk menguntungkan diri sendiri dan/atau orang lain, hubungan keluarga, afiliasi sosial, afiliasi finansial dengan pihak yang beperkara, atau pernah menangani perkara yang sama pada tingkat peradilan yang berbeda atau dalam profesi lain telah menangani perkara tersebut.
; Hakim (Judge)
: Hakim Agung, Hakim Ad Hoc pada Mahkamah Agung, dan Hakim Yustisial pada Kepaniteraan Mahkamah Agung yang bertugas dalam penanganan perkara di Mahkamah Agung.
; Hubungan Keluarga (Family Relationship)
: Hubungan sedarah atau semenda sampai dengan derajat ketiga atau memiliki hubungan suami atau istri meskipun sudah bercerai dengan hakim, panitera, penuntut umum, advokat, terdakwa, atau para pihak dalam perkara yang sedang atau pernah ditangani.
; Afiliasi Sosial (Social Affiliation)
: Keanggotaan atau keterkaitan Hakim dengan lembaga, organisasi, atau perkumpulan sosial.
; Afiliasi Finansial (Financial Affiliation)
: Keterkaitan antara Hakim dengan entitas bisnis dan keuangan yang memungkinkan Hakim tersebut mendapatkan keuntungan selain tabungan.
; Pengunduran Diri (Recusal)
: Tindakan Hakim mengajukan permohonan pengunduran diri disertai dengan alasan kepada Pimpinan Mahkamah Agung karena ada Konflik Kepentingan dalam menangani perkara.
; Sistem Informasi Pengadilan (SIP)
: Sistem informasi yang disediakan oleh Mahkamah Agung untuk memberi pelayanan terhadap pencari keadilan yang meliputi administrasi, pelayanan perkara, dan persidangan secara elektronik.

=== English ===

; Conflict of Interest (Konflik Kepentingan)
: A state where a judge handling a case has or is reasonably suspected of having personal interests to benefit themselves and/or others, family ties, social affiliations, or financial affiliations with the litigating parties, or has previously handled the same case at a different court level or in another professional capacity.
; Judge (Hakim)
: Supreme Court Justices, Ad Hoc Judges at the Supreme Court, and Judicial Judges at the Supreme Court Registry assigned to case processing at the Supreme Court.
; Family Relationship (Hubungan Keluarga)
: Direct or collateral blood relations (consanguinity) or relations by marriage (affinity) up to the third degree, or marital ties (husband/wife) even if divorced, with judges, registrars, public prosecutors, advocates, defendants, or litigating parties.
; Social Affiliation (Afiliasi Sosial)
: Membership or connection of a judge with non-profit institutions, associations, foundations, or social organizations.
; Financial Affiliation (Afiliasi Finansial)
: Connections between a judge and business or financial entities that permit the judge to obtain benefits beyond personal savings (such as stocks, crypto assets, mutual funds, bonds, deposits, or other securities).
; Recusal / Resignation (Pengunduran Diri)
: The formal action by a judge submitting a written request with specific grounds to the Supreme Court Leadership to withdraw from handling a case due to a conflict of interest.
; Court Information System (Sistem Informasi Pengadilan / SIP)
: The electronic information system provided by the Supreme Court encompassing case administration, public judicial services, and electronic court proceedings.

== Legal Basis / Landasan Hukum ==

=== Bahasa Indonesia ===

* '''Undang-Undang Nomor 14 Tahun 1985 tentang Mahkamah Agung''': Sebagaimana telah beberapa kali diubah terakhir dengan Undang-Undang Nomor 3 Tahun 2009.
* '''Undang-Undang Nomor 28 Tahun 1999 tentang Penyelenggaraan Negara yang Bersih dan Bebas dari Korupsi, Kolusi dan Nepotisme''': Landasan bagi tata laksana pemerintahan yang bersih.
* '''Undang-Undang Nomor 31 Tahun 1999 tentang Pemberantasan Tindak Pidana Korupsi''': Sebagaimana telah diubah dengan Undang-Undang Nomor 20 Tahun 2001.
* '''Undang-Undang Nomor 48 Tahun 2009 tentang Kekuasaan Kehakiman''': Mewajibkan pemeriksaan perkara yang mandiri dan tidak memihak.

* '''Law Number 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court''': As last amended by Law Number 3 of 2009.
* '''Law Number 28 of 1999 on State Administration that is Clean and Free from Corruption, Collusion, and Nepotism''': Regulating general governance and ethical civil service frameworks.
* '''Law Number 31 of 1999 on the Eradication of Criminal Acts of Corruption''': As amended by Law Number 20 of 2001.
* '''Law Number 48 of 2009 on Judicial Power''': Mandating independent and impartial adjudication of cases.

== Core Guidance / Petunjuk Pokok ==

=== Bahasa Indonesia ===
{| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;"
! style="width:30%;" |Aspek / Mekanisme
!Petunjuk Teknis & Pedoman Operasional
|-
|'''Tata Cara Pencegahan dan Pelaporan'''
|
* Pendeteksian konflik kepentingan bertumpu pada pelaporan pengungkapan mandiri yang bersifat wajib. Laporan dilakukan 1 (satu) kali pada saat awal bertugas dan wajib segera diperbarui setiap kali ada perubahan kondisi pribadi.
* Setiap Hakim wajib mengisi formulir laporan pengungkapan (Lampiran II) yang memuat rincian:
** Data pribadi dan riwayat pekerjaan/profesi sebelumnya;
** Hubungan sedarah garis lurus (bapak/ibu, kakek/nenek, buyut, anak, cucu, cicit);
** Hubungan sedarah ke samping (saudara kandung, paman/bibi, keponakan, sepupu, anak keponakan);
** Hubungan pernikahan dan semenda (suami/istri, mertua, menantu, ipar, kakek/nenek mertua, buyut mertua);
** Afiliasi sosial (yayasan, organisasi kemasyarakatan, lembaga nirlaba, asosiasi);
** Afiliasi finansial (saham, aset kripto, reksadana, obligasi, deposito, surat berharga lainnya).
* Laporan yang telah dilengkapi diunggah ke dalam SIP dan disimpan secara rahasia.
|-
|'''Pemanfaatan SIP untuk Penunjukan Majelis'''
|Sistem Informasi Pengadilan (SIP) digunakan untuk menganalisis data pelaporan yang ada sebagai salah satu parameter penunjukan majelis hakim oleh Pimpinan Mahkamah Agung.
|-
|'''Tata Cara Pengunduran Diri (Recusal)'''
|
* Hakim wajib mengundurkan diri apabila terdapat konflik kepentingan dengan mengajukan permohonan tertulis (Lampiran III).
* Apabila disetujui, Ketua Muda Kamar mengeluarkan penetapan majelis hakim yang baru (Lampiran IV) untuk mengganti hakim yang mundur.
* Apabila Panitera Pengganti mengundurkan diri, Panitera Muda Kamar mengeluarkan penetapan (Lampiran V) untuk menunjuk Panitera Pengganti baru.
* Penetapan Pimpinan Mahkamah Agung atas permohonan pengunduran diri bersifat final dan mengikat.
|-
|'''Keberlakuan pada Peradilan di Bawah MA'''
|Penanganan konflik kepentingan untuk badan-badan peradilan di bawah Mahkamah Agung tetap mengacu pada ketentuan yang sudah berlaku masing-masing.
|}

=== English ===
{| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;"
! style="width:30%;" |Aspect / Mechanism
!Technical Directives & Operational Guidance
|-
|'''Reporting & Initial Disclosure'''
|
* Detection of conflicts of interest relies on a mandatory self-disclosure process submitted initially upon assignment and updated immediately whenever personal circumstances change.
* Every Judge must complete the detailed declaration form (Annex II) covering:
** Personal identity and previous professional roles;
** Lineal blood relationships (parents, grandparents, great-grandparents, children, grandchildren, great-grandchildren);
** Collateral blood relationships (siblings, aunts/uncles, nephews/nieces, cousins, first cousins once removed);
** Marital relationships and affinity by marriage (parents-in-law, children-in-law, siblings-in-law, grandparents-in-law, great-grandparents-in-law);
** Social affiliations (foundations, associations, non-profit institutions);
** Financial affiliations (ownership of stocks, crypto assets, mutual funds, bonds, deposits, or other securities).
* Completed disclosure reports are uploaded to the SIP and securely maintained under strict confidentiality.
|-
|'''Case Assignment Automation'''
|SIP features are utilized to assess recorded disclosure data, acting as an automated and managerial parameter when the Supreme Court Leadership assigns panels of judges to specific cases.
|-
|'''Mandatory Recusal Procedure'''
|
* A Judge must submit a formal written application for recusal (Annex III) to the Supreme Court Leadership upon identifying an active conflict of interest.
* If approved, the Chamber Chairperson issues an official decree (Annex IV) appointing replacement panel members.
* If a Substitute Registrar (Panitera Pengganti) recuses themselves, the Chamber Registrar issues a replacement decree (Annex V) to appoint a new Substitute Registrar.
* Determinations by the Supreme Court Leadership regarding any recusal request are final and binding.
|-
|'''Subordinate Courts Administration'''
|Conflict of interest management for judicial bodies under the Supreme Court's hierarchy remains subject to their respective existing rules.
|}

== Key Facts / Fakta Utama ==

* '''Kewajiban Pengungkapan Menyeluruh:''' Hakim diwajibkan mendeklarasikan relasi sedarah dan semenda hingga derajat ketiga, keterlibatan entitas sosial/nirlaba, serta instrumen portofolio finansial (saham, kripto, obligasi, deposito).
* '''Kerahasiaan Data Pengungkapan:''' Seluruh data deklarasi diunggah ke Sistem Informasi Pengadilan (SIP) dan diklasifikasikan secara ketat sebagai dokumen rahasia.
* '''Parameter Penunjukan Majelis:''' Basis data konflik kepentingan SIP diintegrasikan sebagai parameter seleksi pembentukan majelis hakim guna meminimalisasi bias peradilan.
* '''Sifat Putusan Pengunduran Diri:''' Penetapan permohonan pengunduran diri (*recusal*) yang diterbitkan Pimpinan Mahkamah Agung bersifat final, mutlak, dan mengikat.
* '''Fungsi Pembinaan & Pengawasan:''' Sosialisasi regulasi dipimpin oleh Ketua Muda Pembinaan, sedangkan audit dan evaluasi berkala diselenggarakan oleh Ketua Muda Pengawasan minimal satu kali setahun.

== Frequently Asked Questions / FAQ ==

; Q1
: Siapa saja yang wajib melaporkan hubungan keluarga, afiliasi sosial, dan finansial berdasarkan keputusan ini?
: Seluruh Hakim yang bertugas dalam penanganan perkara di Mahkamah Agung, yang mencakup Hakim Agung, Hakim Ad Hoc pada Mahkamah Agung, dan Hakim Yustisial pada Kepaniteraan Mahkamah Agung.

; Q2
: Sejauh mana cakupan hubungan keluarga yang harus diungkapkan oleh Hakim?
: Pengungkapan mencakup hubungan keluarga sedarah dan semenda sampai dengan derajat ketiga, baik garis lurus ke atas/bawah maupun hubungan ke samping, serta hubungan suami/istri meskipun sudah bercerai.

; Q3
: Di mana data laporan pengungkapan hakim disimpan dan apakah publik dapat mengaksesnya?
: Data pengungkapan tersebut wajib diunggah ke dalam Sistem Informasi Pengadilan (SIP), disimpan secara aman, dan bersifat rahasia (tidak untuk diakses publik).

; Q4
: Bagaimana status keputusan Pimpinan Mahkamah Agung terkait permohonan pengunduran diri Hakim?
: Keputusan atau penetapan yang dikeluarkan oleh Pimpinan Mahkamah Agung mengenai permohonan pengunduran diri hakim yang memiliki konflik kepentingan bersifat final dan mengikat.

title: Pemeriksaan Setempat
wikitext:
{{Knowledge|id=PROCEDURE-0005|type=Judicial Procedure|domain=Judicial Process|status=DRAFT|version=1.0|evidence=E0 — Unverified|ai_readiness=2 — Metadata|last_verified=}}

= Pemeriksaan Setempat =
'''Pemeriksaan setempat''' refers to a judicial inspection or observation conducted at a location relevant to a dispute.

The legal basis, procedure, evidentiary status, authority, participants, documentation, and consequences must be determined from applicable Indonesian law and judicial practice.

'''[HUMAN VERIFICATION REQUIRED]'''

== Potential Purpose ==
A site inspection may assist a court in understanding relevant physical circumstances of a dispute.

The inspection should be distinguished from the legal determination of the dispute itself.

== Knowledge Object ==
A structured record may include:

* Case
* Court
* Date
* Location
* Participants
* Object inspected
* Questions examined
* Observations
* Documentation
* Photographs
* Measurements
* Relevant evidence
* Procedural consequences

== Digital Documentation ==
Potential technologies include:

* Geotagged photographs
* Video
* Digital maps
* Measurements
* 3D representations
* GIS
* Digital inspection records

Use of these technologies must comply with applicable legal, privacy, evidentiary, and procedural requirements.

== Evidence Relationship ==
The knowledge model may be represented as:

'''CASE''' → '''REQUIRES FACTUAL CLARIFICATION''' → '''SITE INSPECTION''' → '''OBSERVATION''' → '''DOCUMENTATION''' → '''JUDICIAL ASSESSMENT'''

This model does not itself establish evidentiary effect.

== Mediation Context ==
The potential relationship between site inspection and mediation should be separately analyzed under applicable procedural rules.

'''[LEGAL VERIFICATION REQUIRED]'''

== Pre-Trial Context ==
The potential use of site inspection in pre-trial or preliminary procedures should likewise be established from authoritative sources.

'''[LEGAL VERIFICATION REQUIRED]'''

== AI and Site Inspection ==
AI or computer vision may potentially assist with:

* Image organization
* Object identification
* Change detection
* Mapping
* Document classification

AI output should remain subject to human verification.

* [[Mediation]]
* [[Pre-Trial]]
* [[Digital Evidence]]
* [[Artificial Intelligence and the Judiciary]]

== Sources ==
'''[SOURCE VERIFICATION REQUIRED]'''

title: PERMA No. 1/2019
wikitext:
{{CanonicalID|WIKI-LEGISLATION-PERMA-1-2019-E-COURT}} == Knowledge Metadata == * '''Title:''' Supreme Court Regulation (PERMA) No. 1 of 2019: Electronic Case Administration in Court * '''Canonical Topic:''' PERMA No. 1 of 2019 (Electronic Case Administration and Court Hearings) * '''Topic Type:''' Law / Regulation / Legal Instrument / Procedural Standard * '''Jurisdiction:''' Indonesia * '''Legal Domain:''' Civil Procedure, Legal Informatics, Court Administration, Electronic Commerce Law * '''Status:''' Active / Superseded in part by PERMA No. 7 of 2022 * '''Last Reviewed:''' 2026-08-27 * '''Next Review Recommended:''' 2027-08-27 * '''Primary Sources:''' 1945 Constitution of Indonesia (Art. 24), Law No. 14/1985 on the Supreme Court, Law No. 48/2009 on Judicial Power, Supreme Court Regulation (PERMA) No. 1/2019, Supreme Court Regulation (PERMA) No. 7/2022, State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia. * '''Related Wiki Pages:''' [[Judicial Knowledge Hub]], [[Electronic Court Administration (e-Court)]], [[Supreme Court of Indonesia (Mahkamah Agung RI)]], [[Master System Design Blueprint]], [[SIPP]], [[Direktori Putusan]] == Core Definition == ** Supreme Court Regulation (PERMA) No. 1 of 2019** is the landmark legal instrument that formally established the mandatory framework for electronic case administration (*Administrasi Perkara Secara Elektronik*) and electronic litigation (*e-Litigation*) across the courts of Indonesia. * **Simple Definition:** The pioneering Supreme Court rulebook that officially introduced electronic filing, online summons, and digital trials into the Indonesian court system. * **Legal / Technical Definition:** A binding regulatory enactment issued by the Supreme Court that authorizes electronic case registration (*e-Filing*), electronic fee payment (*e-Payment*), electronic service of process (*e-Summons*), and electronic exchange of trial documents (Answers, Replies, Duplies, and Evidence) in civil, religious, and state administrative litigation. * **Plain-Language Explanation:** It acts as the legal foundation that brought Indonesian courts into the digital age, allowing lawyers and citizens to file lawsuits and conduct parts of their trials online without physically walking into a courthouse. == Why It Matters == * **Revolutionized Access to Justice:** Eliminated geographic and logistical barriers by allowing legal practitioners to file lawsuits and access court dockets remotely 24/7. * **Drastically Reduced Trial Delays:** Shortened bureaucratic paperwork processing times and eliminated physical mail delivery delays for court summons and legal briefs. * **Laid the Legal Foundation for Modern Digital Courts:** Created the statutory authority that enabled subsequent expansions, including remote video hearings and full e-Litigation integration under PERMA No. 7 of 2022. * **Enhanced Administrative Transparency:** Linked e-Court filings directly with internal case tracking systems (SIPP), ensuring every document is digitally timestamped and traceable. == Key Principles == ; Principle of Simple, Fast, and Low-Cost Justice via Electronic Means (Asas Peradilan Sederhana, Cepat, dan Biaya Ringan Secara Elektronik) * **Meaning:** Electronic court administration must actively reduce litigation expenses, paper consumption, and trial durations while preserving full due process. * **Why It Matters:** Modernizes the constitutional mandate of fast and low-cost justice through digital efficiency. * **Legal Basis / Source:** Law No. 48/2009 Art. 2(4); PERMA No. 1/2019 Art. 2. * **Related Concepts:** E-justice, procedural economy, digital transformation. ; Principle of Mutual Consent in e-Litigation (Asas Persetujuan Para Pihak dalam Persidangan Elektronik) * **Meaning:** Transitioning from traditional physical trials to electronic document exchange (*e-Litigation*) generally required the consent of the litigants, particularly for defendants upon their initial appearance. *(Note: Later expanded and streamlined under PERMA No. 7/2022).* * **Why It Matters:** Protects procedural fairness and ensures parties understand digital proceedings. * **Legal Basis / Source:** PERMA No. 1/2019 Arts. 19 & 20. * **Related Concepts:** E-Litigation consent, procedural due process. ; Principle of Authenticity and Legal Equivalence of Electronic Documents (Asas Kesetaraan Hukum Dokumen Elektronik) * **Meaning:** Electronic documents, digital signatures, and electronic records submitted via the e-Court portal possess the same legal validity and evidentiary force as traditional paper documents. * **Why It Matters:** Establishes legal certainty for digital transactions and court filings under national electronic information laws. * **Legal Basis / Source:** PERMA No. 1/2019 Art. 5; Law No. 11/2008 (UU ITE). * **Related Concepts:** Electronic documents, digital signatures, legal equivalence. == Legal / Institutional Framework == 
1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia (Judicial Authority & Modernization)
       ↓
Law No. 48/2009 on Judicial Power & Law No. 14/1985 on the Supreme Court
       ↓
Law No. 11/2008 on Electronic Information and Transactions (UU ITE)
       ↓
Supreme Court Regulation (PERMA) No. 1 of 2019 (Foundational e-Court & e-Litigation Framework)
       ↓
Subsequent Expansion & Integration: PERMA No. 7 of 2022 (Comprehensive e-Case Administration)
       ↓
Operational Implementation Across General, Religious, and State Administrative Courts via SIPP
== Indonesia Section == * **Promulgation & Historical Significance:** Enacted on August 8, 2019, PERMA No. 1/2019 replaced earlier experimental e-filing rules (PERMA No. 3/2018), expanding digital administration nationwide across General Courts, Religious Courts, and State Administrative Courts (*PTUN*). * **Core Services Introduced:** 1. *e-Filing:* Online submission of civil, religious, and administrative lawsuits. 2. *e-Payment:* Integrated electronic court fee calculation and payment via virtual accounts (*e-SKUM*). 3. *e-Summons:* Serving court notices and electronic summons to registered email addresses or portal accounts. 4. *e-Litigation:* Electronic exchange of written answers (*Jawaban*), replies (*Replik*), duplies (*Duplik*), and evidentiary document uploads. * **Nomenclature:** PERMA Nomor 1 Tahun 2019 — *Supreme Court Regulation No. 1 of 2019*; Administrasi Perkara di Pengadilan Secara Elektronik — *Electronic Court Case Administration*. == Comparative Perspective == | Jurisdiction | Foundational E-Court Instrument | Core Digital Services Provided | Mandatory vs. Voluntary Rule | Legal Recognition of Digital Filing | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Indonesia** | **PERMA No. 1 of 2019** (amended by PERMA No. 7/2022) | e-Filing, e-Payment, e-Summons, and e-Litigation document exchange. | Mandatory for registered advocates; available for non-advocate pro se litigants. | Fully recognized under PERMA rules and UU ITE electronic document provisions. | | **United States** | Federal Rules of Civil Procedure Rule 5 & CM/ECF Directives | Electronic filing, docketing, and case management via CM/ECF and PACER. | Mandatory electronic filing for attorneys in almost all federal district courts. | Standardized federal electronic filing rules and digital signature statutes. | | **Singapore** | Supreme Court Practice Directions & eLitigation Rules | End-to-end electronic filing, document management, and virtual hearings. | Mandatory electronic filing via the eLitigation portal for all legal practitioners. | Electronic transactions legislation and court practice directions. | | **European Union** | e-CODEX & National Procedural E-Justice Rules | Cross-border secure electronic document exchange and digital case management. | Varies by member state procedural autonomy under EU e-Justice guidelines. | Harmonized eIDAS regulation governing electronic identification and signatures. | == Core Workflow of PERMA No. 1/2019 == 
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. ADVOCATE REGISTRATION & e-FILING                         │
│ • Lawyers register verified accounts on e-Court portal      │
│ • Upload electronic lawsuit petition and supporting exhibits│
└──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                               │
                               ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 2. e-PAYMENT & e-SKUM GENERATION                            │
│ • System calculates court costs automatically (e-SKUM)      │
│ • Payment settled via integrated banking virtual accounts   │
└──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                               │
                               ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 3. e-SUMMONS & COURT REGISTRATION (SIPP SYNC)               │
│ • SIPP generates case number and issues electronic summons │
│ • Defendant notified via registered electronic channels     │
└──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                               │
                               ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 4. e-LITIGATION DOCUMENT EXCHANGE                           │
│ • Parties upload written answers, replies, and evidence     │
│ • Judge reviews submissions and schedules hearings online   │
└──────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┘
== Important Decisions & Regulatory Milestones == * Decision: Supreme Court Administrative Decree on Universal e-Court Adoption * *Issuing Body:* Mahkamah Agung RI (Office of the Chief Justice) * *Instrument Reference:* Chief Justice Administrative Directives enforcing PERMA 1/2019 * *Legal Principle:* All registered advocates practicing across Indonesian district and religious courts are mandated to utilize the e-Court portal for case filings and document exchanges. * *Why It Matters:* Shifted electronic filing from an optional alternative to the mandatory default standard for legal practitioners. * *Official Source:* Mahkamah Agung Official Circulars. == Key Legislation & Standards == * Instrument: Supreme Court Regulation (PERMA) No. 1 of 2019 * *Number / Year:* PERMA No. 1 of 2019 (subsequently updated and expanded by PERMA No. 7 of 2022) * *Jurisdiction:* Indonesia * *Status:* Active / Integrated into modern e-Court standards * *Relevant Provisions:* Articles 1–32 (Rules governing e-Filing, e-Payment, e-Summons, and e-Litigation procedures). * *Official Source:* Mahkamah Agung Official Gazette. == Timeline == {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" !Date !Milestone / Regulatory Event !Significance |- |'''2018-04-05''' |Promulgation of PERMA No. 3/2018 |Introduced initial experimental electronic filing rules for civil cases in selected courts. |- |'''2019-08-08''' |Promulgation of PERMA No. 1/2019 |Formally established the comprehensive legal framework for e-Court and e-Litigation across multiple court jurisdictions. |- |'''2020-03-15''' |COVID-19 Pandemic Operational Expansion |Accelerated nationwide reliance on PERMA 1/2019 electronic hearings during public health restrictions. |- |'''2022-11-15''' |Promulgation of PERMA No. 7/2022 |Expanded and refined PERMA 1/2019, introducing advanced e-Litigation and digital evidence provisions. |} == Debates & Controversies == * Debate: Mandatory Electronic Filing vs. Digital Access Disparities for Pro Se Litigants * *Position A (Mandatory Digital Efficiency):* Enforcing electronic filing eliminates physical paper backlogs and speeds up court administration. * *Position B (Access to Justice for Non-Advocates):* Citizens representing themselves (*pro se* / *pro litigant*) who lack internet access or technical literacy may struggle with digital portals unless courts provide {{CanonicalID|WIKI-LEGISLATION-LAW-48-2009-JUDICIAL-POWER}} == Knowledge Metadata == * '''Title:''' Law No. 48 of 2009 on Judicial Power: Independence, Institutional Architecture, and Fundamental Adjudication Principles * '''Canonical Topic:''' Law No. 48 of 2009 on Judicial Power (UU Kekuasaan Kehakiman) * '''Topic Type:''' Law / Statute / Master Legal Instrument * '''Jurisdiction:''' Indonesia * '''Legal Domain:''' Constitutional Law, Judicial Administration, Civil & Criminal Procedure, Judicial Ethics * '''Status:''' Stable / Active Master Statutory Framework * '''Last Reviewed:''' 2026-08-27 * '''Next Review Recommended:''' 2027-08-27 * '''Primary Sources:''' 1945 Constitution of Indonesia (Article 24 & Article 25), Law No. 48 of 2009 on Judicial Power (''Lembaran Negara Republik Indonesia Tahun 2009 Nomor 157''), Law No. 14/1985 on the Supreme Court, Law No. 24/2003 on the Constitutional Court. * '''Related Wiki Pages:''' [[Judicial Knowledge Hub]], [[Supreme Court of Indonesia (Mahkamah Agung RI)]], [[Master Institutional Architecture]], [[Strategic Governance Framework]], [[Master Jurisprudential & Legal Theory Framework]], [[Center for Legal and Judicial Policy Strategy (Pustrajak)]] == Core Definition == ** Law No. 48 of 2009 on Judicial Power** (*Undang-Undang Nomor 48 Tahun 2009 tentang Kekuasaan Kehakiman*) is the primary national statutory enactment that operationalizes Chapter IX of the 1945 Constitution, defining the organization, independence, guarantees, and foundational principles governing all state judicial power in Indonesia. * **Simple Definition:** The primary national law passed by parliament that guarantees court independence, defines how the court system is organized, and sets the core ethical and procedural rules that all judges must follow. * **Legal / Technical Definition:** The master statutory instrument regulating the separation of judicial authority between the Supreme Court and the Constitutional Court, establishing the four specialized judicial branches (*Empat Lingkungan Peradilan*), prohibiting external interference, mandating reasoned judgments (Article 50), and enforcing the judicial duty to explore unwritten living law (Article 5). * **Plain-Language Explanation: '''It acts as the legal cornerstone of the entire justice system, ensuring that judges are completely independent, free from political pressure, and bound solely by the law, justice, and the constitution when resolving disputes.''' == Why It Matters == * **Guarantees Absolute Judicial Independence:** Codifies constitutional safeguards ensuring that judges render verdicts free from pressure, influence, or intervention by executive or legislative branches. * **Establishes the Four Judicial Jurisdictions:** Formally structures the specialized court branches (General, Religious, State Administrative, and Military Courts) under the Supreme Court. * **Mandates Substantive Justice and Living Law:** Directs judges not to act as mere mechanical mouthpieces of statutes, but to actively explore unwritten customary norms and community justice values (*hukum yang hidup*). * **Enforces Strict Adjudication Accountability:** Requires every court decision to contain comprehensive legal reasoning and factual evaluations (Article 50), protecting litigants against arbitrary rulings. == Key Principles == ; Principle of Independent Judicial Authority (Asas Kekuasaan Kehakiman yang Merdeka) * **Meaning:** Judicial power is an independent power possessed by state courts to administer justice to uphold law and justice, completely free from interference by other state organs. * **Why It Matters:** Absolute prerequisite for the separation of powers and the protection of civil liberties against state overreach. * **Legal Basis / Source:** 1945 Constitution Art. 24(1); Law No. 48/2009 Arts. 1 & 3. * **Related Concepts:** Judicial independence, separation of powers, anti-interference. ; Principle of Simple, Fast, and Low-Cost Justice (Asas Peradilan Sederhana, Cepat, dan Biaya Ringan) * **Meaning:** Courts must administer justice efficiently, avoiding bureaucratic delays and financial barriers that prevent ordinary citizens from accessing legal remedies. * **Why It Matters:** Combats procedural backlogs and ensures timely, economically viable access to justice. * **Legal Basis / Source:** Law No. 48/2009 Art. 2(4); Access to justice. * **Related Concepts:** Procedural economy, small claims, e-Court efficiency. ; Principle of Duty to Explore Living Law and Prohibit Non Liquet (Asas Kewajiban Menggali Hukum dan Larangan Non Liquet) * **Meaning:** Judges are prohibited from refusing to examine or decide a case on the grounds that the written law is unclear or absent (*non liquet*); instead, they have a statutory duty to explore unwritten customary norms and community values. * **Why It Matters:** Prevents legal vacuums and ensures justice is delivered even in novel or complex disputes. * **Legal Basis / Source:** Law No. 48/2009 Art. 5(1) & (2). * **Related Concepts:** Rechtsvinding, living law (*hukum yang hidup*), judicial gap-filling. == Legal / Institutional Framework == 
1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia (Article 24 - Judicial Power)
       ↓
Law No. 48 of 2009 on Judicial Power (Master Statutory Framework):
- Chapter I: General Provisions & Constitutional Basis
- Chapter II: Principles of Adjudication (Independence, Speed, Equality)
- Chapter III: Organization of Judicial Power (Supreme Court & Constitutional Court)
- Chapter IV: The Four Judicial Jurisdictions (General, Religious, State Admin, Military)
- Chapter V: Guarantees for Judges & Trial Procedures (Article 5 & Article 50)
       ↓
Enforcement across Supreme Court Regulations (PERMA), Chamber Directives, & Court Administration
== Indonesia Section == * **Enactment & Reform Background:** Enacted on October 29, 2009, Law No. 48/2009 replaced earlier post-reform judicial power statutes (Law No. 4/2004 and Law No. 14/1970), consolidating the One-Roof administrative system (*Satu Atap*) and reinforcing the dual apex court model. * **Core Statutory Mandates for Judges:** 1. *Article 5(1):* Judges must explore, follow, and understand legal values and a sense of justice living in society (*hukum yang hidup dalam masyarakat*). 2. *Article 5(2):* Prohibition of *non liquet* — courts cannot refuse to try a case due to unclear or missing statutory law. 3. *Article 50(1):* Every court decision must be accompanied by the legal reasons and considerations (*pertimbangan hukum*) upon which the ruling is based. * **Nomenclature:** Undang-Undang Nomor 48 Tahun 2009 tentang Kekuasaan Kehakiman — *Law No. 48 of 2009 on Judicial Power*; Asas Kekuasaan Kehakiman — *Principles of Judicial Power*. == Comparative Perspective == {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" !Jurisdiction !Master Judicial Power Statute !Constitutional Independence Guarantee !Judicial Gap-Filling Rule !Judge Reasoning Standard |- |'''Indonesia''' |**Law No. 48 of 2009 on Judicial Power** |Guaranteed under 1945 Constitution Art. 24 and Law 48/2009 Arts. 1 & 3. |Explicit statutory duty under Art. 5(1) to explore living law; strict ban on *non liquet*. |Mandatory written legal reasoning (*pertimbangan hukum*) under Art. 50. |- |'''United States''' |U.S. Constitution Article III & Judicial Code (Title 28 U.S.C.) |Lifetime tenure and salary protection for federal Article III judges. |Common law judicial equity, statutory construction, and gap-filling. |Comprehensive written judicial opinions detailing *ratio decidendi*. |- |'''Germany''' |German Judiciary Act (DRiG) & Basic Law (Grundgesetz Art. 97) |Absolute judicial independence (*Richterunabhängigkeit*) guaranteed under Basic Law. |Systematic statutory gap-filling (*richterliche Rechtsfortbildung*). |Structured written judgments following strict German doctrinal methodology (*Urteilstil*). |- |'''France''' |Ordonnance portant loi organique relative à la magistrature |Constitutional Council guarantees of judicial independence for the judiciary (*magistrature*). |Civil Code Article 4 strictly prohibits judges from refusing to judge (*déni de justice*). |Standardized, highly formalized French judicial judgments (*arrêts*). |} == Core Structural Pillars of Law No. 48/2009 == 
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. INSTITUTIONAL INDEPENDENCE & SEPARATION OF POWERS        │
│ • Absolute prohibition of executive/legislative interference│
│ • One-Roof administrative self-governance under Supreme Court│
└──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                               │
                               ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 2. DUAL APEX COURT ARCHITECTURE                             │
│ • Supreme Court (MA RI) overseeing four specialized branches│
│ • Constitutional Court (MKRI) reviewing statutory validity   │
└──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                               │
                               ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 3. FUNDAMENTAL TRIAL SAFEGUARDS                             │
│ • Open public trial pronouncement (*sidang terbuka untuk umum*)│
│ • Right to legal assistance and presumption of innocence    │
└──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                               │
                               ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 4. JUDICIAL REASONING & LIVING LAW MANDATES                 │
│ • Mandatory written legal reasoning (Article 50)            │
│ • Duty to explore unwritten living law and ban non liquet   │
└─────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┘
== Important Decisions & Jurisprudential Milestones == * Decision: Constitutional Court Rulings on Judicial Independence and Ethics * *Issuing Body:* Constitutional Court of Indonesia (Mahkamah Konstitusi) * *Case Reference:* Landmark Constitutional Review Cases on Judicial Authority and Disciplinary Boundaries * *Legal Principle:* Provisions of Law No. 48/2009 must be interpreted to ensure that oversight bodies never infringe upon the core independence of judges in deciding active legal disputes. * *Why It Matters:* Reaffirmed the constitutional limits of administrative and ethical supervision over judicial decision-making. * *Official Source:* Constitutional Court Reports. == Key Legislation & Standards == * Instrument: Law on Judicial Power * *Number / Year:* Law No. 48 of 2009 * *Jurisdiction:* Indonesia * *Status:* In force * *Relevant Provisions:* Articles 1–123 (Independence of judiciary, organization of courts, trial principles, judicial ethics, and transitional provisions). * *Official Source:* State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia. == Timeline == {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" !Date !Milestone / Legislative Event !Significance |- |'''1970-12-18''' |Enactment of Law No. 14/1970 |Indonesia's first comprehensive post-independence statute governing judicial power principles. |- |'''1999-05-03''' |Enactment of Law No. 35/1999 |Initiated the One-Roof structural transfer, shifting court administration to the Supreme Court. |- |'''2004-01-15''' |Enactment of Law No. 4/2004 |Updated judicial power rules following post-Suharto democratic constitutional amendments. |- |'''2009-10-29''' |Enactment of Law No. 48/2009 |The current master statute governing judicial power, consolidating modern procedural and institutional rules. |} == Debates & Controversies == * Debate: Statutory Positivism vs. Judicial Discovery of Living Law * *Position A (Strict Positivist View):* Judges must apply written state law strictly to maintain legal certainty, avoiding unwritten customary laws that lack legislative codification. * *Position B (Sociological & Progressive View):* Under Article 5(1), judges have a progressive duty to recognize unwritten living law (*hukum adat/lokal*), ensuring state law aligns with community conscience. * *Evidence:* Landmark civil and criminal rulings incorporating customary dispute resolution alongside statutory provisions. * *Current Status:* Harmonized under Indonesian jurisprudence: written positive law remains primary, but judges are statutorily empowered to integrate living law and equity where strict statutory application causes injustice. == Rule-of-Law Connection == * *Separation of Powers:* Law No. 48/2009 provides the statutory armor insulating courts from political pressure. * *Due Process:* Guarantees open trials, the presumption of innocence, and mandatory written reasoning. * *Legal Certainty:* Establishes predictable institutional hierarchies and appellate review pathways. == AI & Future of Law == * *AI Compliance Checks in Judgment Writing:* Using AI drafting tools to cross-reference judicial decisions against Article 50 requirements, ensuring every ruling contains robust legal reasoning (*pertimbangan hukum*). * *Living Law Database Integration:* Connecting regional customary legal studies and ethnographic research repositories with the Judicial Knowledge Hub to assist judges in exploring local living law. == Common Misconceptions == * *Myth:* Law No. 48/2009 grants judges absolute immunity to ignore parliamentary statutes if they disagree with them. * *Reality:* Judges are independent in their adjudicative reasoning, but they remain bound by the normative hierarchy; they cannot invalidate statutes unless referred to the Constitutional Court. * *Source:* Law No. 48/2009 Art. 3; Master Normative Hierarchy Standard. * *Myth:* The Supreme Court shares administrative control of lower courts with executive ministries. * *Reality:* Under the One-Roof system codified in Law No. 48/2009, all lower court administration, budgeting, and personnel management are managed exclusively by the Supreme Court. * *Source:* Law No. 48/2009 Chapter III & IV. == Practical Example == * *Scenario:* A remote indigenous community in Kalimantan faces a land dispute governed partly by unwritten customary forestry laws (*hukum adat*) that are not explicitly detailed in the national Civil Code. * *Question:* How must the district court judge handle the case without violating statutory rules? * *Applicable Principle:* Duty to Explore Living Law & Prohibition of Non Liquet (Law No. 48/2009 Art. 5). * *Analysis:* 1. The judge cannot dismiss the lawsuit on the grounds that written statutory law is silent (*non liquet*). 2. Under Article 5(1) of Law No. 48/2009, the judge has an affirmative statutory duty to explore, follow, and understand unwritten living law and customary values. 3. The judge incorporates customary evidence and local expert testimony into the legal reasoning (*pertimbangan hukum*) of the verdict. * *Limitation:* Customary living law applications must not violate fundamental constitutional rights or national statutory public order (*ketertiban umum*). == Key Terms == {| class="wikitable" style="width:100%;" !Term !Definition !Related Term |- |'''Kekuasaan Kehakiman''' |Judicial power; the independent state authority administered by courts to uphold law and justice. |Law No. 48/2009, Separation of Powers |- |'''Non Liquet''' |The illegal judicial refusal to try a case on the grounds that written statutory law is unclear, silent, or absent. |Law 48/2009 Art. 5(2), Gap-Filling |- |'''Pertimbangan Hukum''' |Legal reasoning; the mandatory analytical section of a court judgment detailing factual and statutory justifications. |Law 48/2009 Art. 50, Ratio Decidendi |- |'''Empat Lingkungan Peradilan''' |The four specialized judicial branches operating under the Supreme Court: General, Religious, State Administrative, and Military. |Master Institutional Architecture, Jurisdiction |} == Related Wiki Pages == * [[Judicial Knowledge Hub]] * [[Supreme Court of Indonesia (Mahkamah Agung RI)]] * [[Master Institutional Architecture]] * [[Strategic Governance Framework]] * [[Master Jurisprudential & Legal Theory Framework]] * [[Center for Legal and Judicial Policy Strategy (Pustrajak)]] == Knowledge Relationships == * '''Law No. 48/2009 on Judicial Power''' → *is a* → [[Master Statutory Framework Standard]] * '''Law No. 48/2009 on Judicial Power''' → *operationalizes* → [[1945 Constitution of Indonesia (Article 24)]] * '''Law No. 48/2009 on Judicial Power''' → *governs* → [[Supreme Court of Indonesia (Mahkamah Agung RI)]] & [[Master Institutional Architecture]] * '''Law No. 48/2009 on Judicial Power''' → *mandates principles for* → [[Master Jurisprudential & Legal Theory Framework]] & [[Center for Legal and Judicial Policy Strategy (Pustrajak)]] * '''Law No. 48/2009 on Judicial Power''' → *enforces standards across* → [[Electronic Court Administration (e-Court)]] & [[Judicial Knowledge Hub]] == Sources == === Nomor 157''). # Law No. 14 of 1985 on the Supreme Court, as amended. # Law No. 24 of 2003 on the Constitutional Court, as amended. === Tier 2 — Academic & Institutional Sources === # Mahkamah Agung RI, *Buku Pedoman Teknis Administrasi dan Peradilan Mahkamah Agung*, Mahkamah Agung RI. # Pustrajak Mahkamah Agung RI, *Analisis Perkembangan Kekuasaan Kehakiman dan Negara Hukum di Indonesia*, 2026. affecting judicial independence, or new Supreme Court structural reorganizations. == SEO & AI Metadata == * '''SEO Title:''' Law No. 48/2009 on Judicial Power: Independence & Structure | Hub * '''Meta '''Draft PERMA No. 3 of 2026: Digital Arbitration''' is an active regulatory proposal hosted on the Judicial Knowledge Hub, the secure internal court encyclopedia. 

This proposed regulation seeks to standardize the enforcement and execution of commercial arbitration awards handled entirely on digital communication platforms.

== Proposed clauses under review ==

=== Proposed Paragraph 4.3: Cryptographic Signatures ===
Arbitrators must sign final declarations using secure cryptographic credentials conforming to Section 12 criteria.

== Framework intersection ==
To ensure the authenticity of awards signed under Paragraph 4.3, this draft explicitly intersects with established digital security practices:
* '''Notary Verification:''' Credentials must align with criteria specified under [[Policy: Judicial Policy Portal#SEMA Administrative Circulars|SEMA No. 1 of 2026 (Remote Signature Validation)]].
* '''Data Integrity:''' All digital evidence registries filed during the arbitration lifecycle must preserve a verifiable [[chain of custody]].

|source=Indonesia Judiciary Future Blueprint 2035–2045
|evidence=E2
|status=PROPOSED
}}

=Plain-Language Justice=

Judicial communication should be understandable to its intended users
while preserving legal accuracy.

== Applications ==

* public information;
* service instructions;
* procedural explanations;
* accessibility materials;
* approved summaries.

== Boundary ==

Plain-language explanations must not alter the legal meaning of
authoritative documents.

organizing, streaming, and archiving expert audio legal commentaries, Pustrajak audio policy briefs, judge interviews, and sonic jurisprudential discussions concerning modern judicial reform, court modernization, and comparative law. * **Simple Definition:** The central audio and podcast portal where judges, researchers, and legal experts discuss court reforms, landmark rulings, and legal official audio broadcast station of the judiciary, bringing complex legal research and reform discussions directly to listeners through engaging conversations and expert interviews.''' == Why It Matters == * **Expands Public Legal Accessibility:** Translates dense jurimetric reports, Naskah Akademik drafts, and Supreme Court policy papers into easily digestible audio episodes for legal practitioners and the public. * **Humanizes Institutional Leadership:** Features in-depth interviews with *Hakim Yustisial*, Pustrajak researchers, and visiting international jurists discussing the human side of judicial reform. * **Fosters Audio Legal Education:** Serves as a dynamic educational resource for law students, academics, and court personnel seeking portable professional development. Judicial Reform & Bench Conversations (Podcast Diskusi Pembaruan Peradilan) === * **Core Focus:** Conversational interviews and panel discussions with judges and legal scholars examining landmark chamber rulings and court administrative evolution. * **Key Content:** Discussions on the One-Roof judicial system, chamber jurisprudence harmonization, and trial independence. === 3. Legal Informatics & AI Tech Dialogues (Podcast Informatika Hukum & AI) === * **Core Focus:** Specialized audio episodes exploring the integration of RAG AI research suites, electronic litigation (*e-Court*), and cybersecurity in courts. * **Key Content:** Dialogues on responsible AI governance, cryptographic evidence, and digital court modernization. === 4. Comparative International Dialogues (Podcast Hukum Perbandingan Internasional) === * **Core Focus:** Cross-border audio interviews examining foreign court administration models (such as Japanese mediation series or Singaporean e-litigation) with international experts. * **Key Content:** Insights from JICA and UNODC collaborative training programs and global comparative jurisprudence. == Legal / Institutional Framework ==

Audio Storytelling vs. Formal Institutional Neutrality * *Position A (Casual Storytelling):* Podcasts must be conversational, relaxed, and engaging to capture public interest in otherwise dry legal topics. * *Position B (Formal Neutrality):* Official judicial broadcasts must maintain absolute institutional solemnity and formal legal precision to prevent misrepresentation. * *Evidence:* Public communication trends in modern judiciaries. * *Current Status:* Harmonized under Podcast Hub production guidelines: episodes maintain an engaging, accessible conversational format while strictly upholding professional objectivity and factual legal accuracy. == Rule-of-Law Connection == * *Public Legal Literacy:* Audio broadcasts explain court procedures and reform goals in plain language, languages. == Common Misconceptions == * *Myth:* Podcast episodes constitute binding statutory laws or official Supreme Court trial verdicts. * *Reality:* Podcast episodes provide expert institutional commentary, policy summaries, and educational discussions; they inform public discourse but do not carry binding legal force. * *Source:* Pustrajak Media Standards. * *Myth:* Podcasts replace formal written research papers and academic drafts (*Naskah Akademik*). * *Reality:* Podcasts serve as accessible audio summaries of formal research; listeners seeking complete legal data are directed to the full texts stored in the Research Hub. * *Source:* Master Epistemic Standards. == Practical Example == * *Scenario:* A legal practitioner driving to court wants to catch up on the latest empirical findings regarding Supreme Court electronic filing reforms during their commute. * *Question:* How does the Podcast Hub assist the practitioner? * *Applicable Principle:* Pustrajak Policy Audio Briefs (Podcast Hub). * *Analysis:* 1. The practitioner accesses the Podcast Hub within the Judicial Knowledge Hub on their mobile device. 2. Selects the latest episode summarizing the *Policy Paper Pustrajak 2026* on e-Court case management optimizations. 3. Listens to the concise audio brief during their drive, gaining immediate actionable insights into administrative updates. * *Limitation:* Podcasts deliver fast, portable institutional overviews, but formal litigation filings require review of primary court regulations and procedural rules. == Key Terms == {| class="wikitable" style="width:100%;" !Term !Definition !Related Term |- |'''Podcast Hub''' |The master institutional audio portal organizing commentaries, policy audio briefs, and judge interviews. |Audio, Media |- |'''Sonic Jurisprudence''' |The academic exploration of law, court proceedings, and legal discourse through audio and sound media. |Jurisprudence, Scholarship |- |'''Audio Policy Brief''' |A concise spoken-word summary of complex empirical research and reform recommendations. |Policy Brief, Summary |- |'''Transcript Indexing''' |Converting spoken audio words into searchable text documents indexed within RAG AI search databases. |Search, RAG AI |} == Related Wiki Pages == * * [[ARTICLES]] * [[RESEARCH]] * [[Center for Legal and Judicial Policy Strategy (Pustrajak)]] * [[Supreme Court of Indonesia (Mahkamah Agung RI)]] * [[Rule of Law 2045]] == Knowledge Relationships == * '''Podcast Hub''' → *is categorized under* → * '''Podcast Hub''' → *is managed by* → [[Supreme Court of Indonesia (Mahkamah Agung RI)]] & [[Center for Legal and Judicial Policy Strategy (Pustrajak)]] * '''Podcast Hub''' → *complements* → [[ARTICLES]] & [[RESEARCH]] * '''Podcast Hub''' → *supports goals of* → [[Rule of Law 2045]] * '''Podcast Hub''' → *upholds principles of* → [[Law No. 48/2009 (Judicial Power)]] & [[1945 Constitution of Indonesia (Article 24)]] == Sources == === Tier 1 — Official / Primary Sources === # Legal and Judicial Policy Strategy (Pustrajak) to guide Supreme Court leadership and legislative bodies on strategic judicial reforms. * **Simple Definition:** The central repository for concise, === 1. Backlog & Caseflow Management Briefs (Briefs Manajemen Perkara & SIPP) === * **Core Focus:** Concise analytical evaluations identifying regional court delays, clearance bottlenecks, and resource allocation solutions using SIPP data. * **Key Content:** Targeted strategies for eradicating backlogs and optimizing digital e-Court scheduling. === 2. Legislative & Statutory Reform Briefs (Briefs Pembaruan UU & Peradilan) === * **Core Focus:** Strategic advisory papers evaluating pending national legislation (such as *RUU Jabatan Hakim* and *RUU HPI*) and proposing statutory adjustments. * **Key Content:** Recommendations on judicial appointments, professional standards, and cross-border legal harmonization. === 3. Legal Informatics & AI Governance Briefs (Briefs Informatika Hukum & Tata Kelola AI) === * **Core Focus:** Advisory notes evaluating the secure integration of RAG AI research suites, sovereign cloud infrastructure, and cryptographic evidence standards. * **Key Content:** Guidelines on responsible AI adoption, anti-hallucination safeguards, and digital court security. === 4. Comparative International Policy Briefs (Briefs Perbandingan Internasional) === * **Core Focus:** Strategic digests translating international best practices (such as Japanese *Chotei* mediation or Singaporean e-litigation) into domestic reform options. * **Key Content:** Lessons learned from foreign court modernizations adapted to Indonesian constitutional norms. == Legal / Institutional Framework ==
